definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used before countable or singular nouns referring to people or things that have not already been mentioned
examples: a man/horse/unit
an aunt/egg/hour/X-ray
I can only carry two at a time.
There's a visitor for you.
She's a friend of my father's (= one of my father's friends).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to show that somebody/something is a member of a group or profession
examples: Their new car's a BMW.
She's a Buddhist.
He's a teacher.
Is that a Monet (= a painting by Monet)?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: any; every
examples: A lion is a dangerous animal.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used before uncountable nouns when these have an adjective in front of them, or phrase following them
examples: a good knowledge of French
a sadness that won’t go away

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used in front of two nouns that are seen as a single unit
examples: a knife and fork

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used instead of one before some numbers
examples: A thousand people were there.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used when talking about prices, quantities and rates
examples: SYNONYM per
They cost 50p a kilo.
I can type 50 words a minute.
He was driving at 50 miles an hour.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a person like somebody
examples: She's a little Hitler.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used before somebody’s name to show that the speaker does not know the person
examples: There's a Mrs Green to see you.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used before the names of days of the week to talk about one particular day
examples: She died on a Tuesday.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to leave somebody, especially somebody you are responsible for, with no intention of returning
examples: The baby had been abandoned by its mother.
People often simply abandon their pets when they go abroad.
‘We have been abandoned to our fate,’ said one resident.
The study showed a deep fear among the elderly of being abandoned to the care of strangers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to leave a thing or place, especially because it is impossible or dangerous to stay
examples: SYNONYM leave
Snow forced many drivers to abandon their vehicles.
He gave the order to abandon ship (= to leave the ship because it was sinking).
They had to abandon their lands to the invading forces.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to stop doing something, especially before it is finished; to stop having something
examples: They abandoned the match because of rain.
The plans for reform were quietly abandoned.
She abandoned hope of any reconciliation.
We had to abandon any further attempt at negotiation.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to stop supporting or helping somebody; to stop believing in something
examples: The country abandoned its political leaders after the war.
By 1930 he had abandoned his Marxist principles.
This principle has now been effectively abandoned.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to feel an emotion so strongly that you can feel nothing else
examples: He abandoned himself to despair.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have the skill, intelligence, opportunity, etc. needed to do something
examples: OPPOSITE unable
You must be able to speak French for this job.
A viral illness left her barely able to walk.
We're still able to get visas to come and go from Thailand.
I didn't feel able to disagree with him.
Will you be able to come?
Are you really willing and able to do what is necessary?
They don't even seem able to see what's good about their ideas.
These families are less able to afford a balanced, healthy diet.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: intelligent; good at something
examples: She's the ablest student in the class.
We aim to help the less able in society to lead an independent life.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the deliberate ending of a pregnancy at an early stage
examples: to support/oppose abortion
a woman’s right to abortion
the country's strict abortion laws
I've always been anti-abortion.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a medical operation to end a pregnancy at an early stage
examples: SYNONYM termination
She decided to have an abortion.
Some medical staff wanted the right to refuse to perform abortions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of giving birth to a baby before it is fully developed and able to survive
examples: SYNONYM miscarriage
Higher amounts of caffeine may be associated with increased rates of abortion and low birthweight.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: on the subject of somebody/something; in connection with somebody/something
examples: a book about flowers
Tell me all about it.
What's she so angry about?
There's something strange about him.
There's something about this business that is not quite right.
I don't know what you're on about (= talking about).
There's nothing you can do about it now.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to describe the purpose or an aspect of something
examples: Movies are all about making money these days.
What was all that about? (= what was the reason for what has just happened?)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: busy with something; doing something
examples: Everywhere people were going about their daily business.
And while you’re about it… (= while you’re doing that)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in many directions in a place; here and there
examples: We wandered about the town for an hour or so.
He looked about the room.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in various parts of a place; here and there
examples: The papers were strewn about the room.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: next to a place or person; in the area mentioned
examples: She's somewhere about the office.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: surrounding somebody/something
examples: She wore a shawl about her shoulders.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when asking for information about somebody/something
examples: How about Ruth? Have you heard from her?
I'm having fish. What about you?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to make a suggestion
examples: How about going for a walk?
How about we go for a walk?
What about a break?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at or to a higher place or position than something/somebody
examples: The water came above our knees.
We were flying above the clouds.
the people in the apartment above mine
A captain in the navy ranks above a captain in the army.
They finished the year six places above their local rivals.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: more than something; greater in number, level or age than somebody/something
examples: Inflation is above 6%.
Temperatures have been above average.
We cannot accept children above the age of 10.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: of greater importance or of higher quality than somebody/something
examples: I rate her above most other players of her age.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: too good or too honest to do something
examples: She's not above lying when it suits her.
He's above suspicion (= he is completely trusted).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: louder or clearer than another sound
examples: I couldn't hear her above the noise of the traffic.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: most important of all; especially
examples: Above all, keep in touch.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: having too high an opinion of yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: in addition to something
examples: There are other factors over and above those we have discussed.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: having too high an opinion of yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: in addition to something
examples: There are other factors over and above those we have discussed.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in or to a foreign country
examples: to go/travel/live/study abroad
She worked abroad for a year.
imports of cheap food from abroad
He was famous, both at home and abroad (= in his own country and in other countries).
For a holiday abroad you need a valid passport.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: being talked about or felt by many people
examples: There was news abroad that a change was coming.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: outside; outdoorsWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from a- ‘on’ + broad.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the fact of somebody being away from a place where they are usually expected to be; the occasion or period of time when somebody is away
examples: SEE ALSO leave
The decision was made in my absence (= while I was not there).
We did not receive any news during his long absence.
absence from work
repeated absences from school

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of somebody/something not existing or not being available; a lack of something
examples: I was surprised by the absence of any women on the board of directors.
The case was dismissed in the absence of any definite proof.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that when you are away from somebody that you love, you love them even more

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not present in a situation or place, when it is obvious that you should be there
examples: When it came to cleaning up afterwards, Anne was conspicuous by her absence.
The meeting went well but Nigel was conspicuous by his absence.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not in a place because of illness, etc.
examples: OPPOSITE present
He was absent from work for two weeks.
Local people were conspicuously absent from the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not present in something
examples: OPPOSITE present
Love was totally absent from his childhood.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: showing that you are not really looking at or thinking about what is happening around you
examples: SEE ALSO absently
an absent expression

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: total and complete
examples: I've joined a class for absolute beginners.
absolute confidence/trust/silence/truth
‘You're wrong,’ she said with absolute certainty.
Clean water is an absolute necessity.
Around them the darkness was absolute, the silence oppressive.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used, especially in spoken English, to give emphasis to what you are saying
examples: We must keep costs to an absolute minimum.
This room is an absolute disgrace.
They're talking absolute nonsense.
He must earn an absolute fortune.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: definite and without any doubt
examples: There was no absolute proof.
He taught us that the laws of physics were absolute.
The story offers no clear message, no absolute truth.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (of a legal decision) final
examples: SEE ALSO decree absolute
The divorce became absolute last week.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not limited in any way
examples: absolute power/authority
an absolute ruler/monarchy (= one with no limit to their power)

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: existing or measured independently and not in relation to something else
examples: COMPARE relative
Although prices are falling in absolute terms, energy is still expensive.
Beauty cannot be measured by any absolute standard.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something is completely true
examples: You're absolutely right.
He made it absolutely clear.
I'm not absolutely certain I posted it.
Are you absolutely sure?
Training is absolutely essential in this business.
Don't delay for longer than absolutely necessary.
The place was absolutely packed.
It was absolutely pouring with rain.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something negative
examples: That man does absolutely no work!
There's absolutely nothing more the doctors can do.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used with adjectives or verbs that express strong feelings or extreme qualities to mean ‘extremely’
examples: absolutely delighted/thrilled
We were absolutely devastated at the news.
I absolutely love strawberries.
She absolutely adores you.
absolutely fantastic/amazing
He's an absolutely brilliant cook.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you agree with somebody, or to give somebody permission to do something
examples: ‘They could have told us, couldn't they?’ ‘Absolutely!’
‘Can we leave a little early?’ ‘Absolutely!’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you strongly disagree with somebody, or to refuse permission
examples: ‘Was it any good?’ ‘No, absolutely not.’
‘Can I stay up late?’ ‘Absolutely not!’

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not considered in relation to other things
examples: White-collar crime increased both absolutely and in comparison with other categories.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take in a liquid, gas or other substance from the surface or space around
examples: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air.
Let the rice cook until it has absorbed all the water.
The cream is easily absorbed into the skin.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take in and keep heat, light, energy, sound, etc. instead of reflecting it
examples: Black walls absorb a lot of heat during the day.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to reduce the effect of a physical impact or movement
examples: SEE ALSO shock absorber
This tennis racket absorbs shock on impact.
The bats have graphite shafts that absorb the vibration.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to take something into the mind and learn or understand it
examples: SYNONYM take in
It's a lot of information to absorb all at once.
It took me several days to absorb the fact of her death.
They spent a week in Paris just absorbing the atmosphere.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to interest somebody very much so that they pay no attention to anything else
examples: SYNONYM engross
This work had absorbed him for several years.
His work absorbed him completely.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make something smaller become part of something larger
examples: The country simply cannot absorb this influx of refugees.
The surrounding small towns have been absorbed into the city.
These committees were gradually absorbed into the local government machine.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to use up a large supply of something, especially money or time
examples: The new proposals would absorb $80 billion of the federal budget.
My work absorbs a great deal of my time.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to deal with changes, effects, costs, etc.
examples: The company is unable to absorb such huge losses.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: based on general ideas and not on any particular real person, thing or situation
examples: COMPARE concrete
abstract knowledge/principles
The research shows that pre-school children are capable of thinking in abstract terms.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: existing in thought or as an idea but not having a physical reality
examples: We may talk of beautiful things but beauty itself is abstract.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not representing people or things in a realistic way, but expressing the artist’s ideas about them
examples: COMPARE figurative (2)
the work of American abstract expressionists like Mark Rothko

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: extremely silly; not logical and sensible
examples: SYNONYM ridiculous
That uniform makes the guards look absurd.
Of course it's not true, what an absurd idea.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: things that are or that seem to be absurd
examples: He has a good sense of the absurd.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large quantity that is more than enough
examples: The brochure promised beautiful walks with an abundance of wildlife.
The country has an abundance of natural resources.
We were amazed by the sheer abundance of food.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in large quantities
examples: Fruit and vegetables grew in abundance on the island.
Exotic plants grew there in great abundance.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the use of something in a way that is wrong or harmful
examples: SYNONYM misuse
alcohol/drug abuse
The system of paying cash bonuses is open to abuse (= might be used in the wrong way).
The legal system is open to abuse.
He was arrested on charges of corruption and abuse of power.
What she did was an abuse of her position as manager.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: unfair, cruel or violent treatment of somebody
examples: SEE ALSO child abuse
child abuse
sexual abuse
reported abuses by the secret police
She suffered years of physical abuse.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: rude and offensive remarks, usually made when somebody is very angry
examples: SYNONYM insult
to scream/hurl/shout abuse
a stream/torrent of abuse
The man burst into a torrent of foul-mouthed racist abuse.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with education, especially studying in schools and universities
examples: high/low academic standards
She had a brilliant academic career.
one of this country's most prestigious academic institutions
improving the academic achievement of all students
The university is renowned throughout the world for its academic excellence.
academic research/researchers
We are deeply committed to safeguarding academic freedom.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: involving a lot of reading and studying rather than practical or technical skills
examples: a mixture of vocational and academic courses
people whose skills are practical rather than academic
academic qualifications/subjects

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: good at subjects involving a lot of reading and studying
examples: She wasn't very academic and hated school.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not connected to a real or practical situation and therefore not important
examples: It's a purely academic question.
The whole thing's academic now—we can't win anyway.
Most of his questions were of an academic nature.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a school or college for special training
examples: She trained at the Royal Academy of Music.
a police/military academy

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a type of official organization that aims to encourage and develop art, literature, science, etc.
examples: the Royal Academy of Arts

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a secondary school in Scotland
examples: He went to Ayr Academy.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a private school in the US

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a school in England that is independent of local authority controlWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (denoting the garden where Plato taught): from French académie or Latin academia, from Greek akadēmeia, from Akadēmos, the hero after whom Plato's garden was named.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to happen faster or earlier; to make something happen faster or earlier
examples: Inflation continues to accelerate.
Exposure to the sun can accelerate the ageing process.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to start to go faster
examples: The runners accelerated smoothly around the bend.
The car accelerated to overtake me.
The car purred into life and accelerated away.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a way of pronouncing the words of a language that shows which country, area or social class a person comes from; how well somebody pronounces a particular language
examples: COMPARE dialect
a northern/Dublin/Scottish accent
a strong/broad accent (= one that is easy to notice)
She spoke English with an accent.
The Americans had learned Korean and spoke with a good accent.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the emphasis that you should give to part of a word when saying it
examples: SYNONYM stress
In ‘today’ the accent is on the second syllable.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a mark on a letter to show that it should be pronounced in a particular way
examples: SEE ALSO acute accent
Canapé has an accent on the ‘e’.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a special importance that is given to something
examples: SYNONYM emphasis
In all our products the accent is on quality.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take willingly something that is offered; to say ‘yes’ to an offer, invitation, etc.
examples: OPPOSITE refuse1
He asked me to marry him and I accepted.
Please accept our sincere apologies.
It was pouring with rain so I accepted his offer of a lift.
I am unfortunately unable to accept your kind invitation.
The board of directors accepted our proposal.
She's decided not to accept the job.
Please accept this small token of my appreciation.
He is charged with accepting bribes from a firm of suppliers.
She said she'd accept $15 for it.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to agree to or approve of something
examples: OPPOSITE reject
They accepted the court's decision.
The judge refused to accept his evidence.
He accepted all the changes we proposed.
Are you willing to accept the challenge?
She won't accept advice from anyone.
My article has been accepted for publication.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to take payment in a particular form
examples: This machine only accepts coins.
Credit cards are widely accepted.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to admit that you are responsible or to blame for something
examples: He accepts full responsibility for what happened.
You have to accept the consequences of your actions.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to continue in a difficult situation without complaining, because you realize that you cannot change it
examples: You just have to accept the fact that we're never going to be rich.
to be willing/prepared to accept something
Nothing will change as long as the workers continue to accept these appalling conditions.
They accept the risks as part of the job.
He just refused to accept that his father was no longer there.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel welcome and part of a group
examples: OPPOSITE reject
It may take years to be completely accepted by the local community.
She had never been accepted into what was essentially a man's world.
He never really accepted her as his own child.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to believe that something is true
examples: I don't accept his version of events.
Can we accept his account as the true version?
I accept that this will not be popular.
I am not prepared to accept that this decision is final.
It is generally accepted that people are motivated by success.
Their workforce is widely accepted to have the best conditions in Europe.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to join an organization, attend an institution, use a service, etc.
examples: OPPOSITE reject
The college he applied to has accepted him.
She was disappointed not to be accepted into the club.
The landlord was willing to accept us as tenants.
She was accepted to study music.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: agreed or approved of by most people in a society
examples: Children must learn socially acceptable behaviour.
It is perfectly acceptable for you as an employee to say no.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that somebody agrees is of a good enough standard or allowed
examples: For this course a pass in English at grade B is acceptable.
Air pollution in the city had reached four times the acceptable levels.
We want a political solution that is acceptable to all parties.
It is possible to find a solution that is acceptable to both sides.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not very good but good enough
examples: OPPOSITE unacceptable
The food was acceptable, but no more.
Inspectors found that teaching standards were acceptable, but could be improved.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of accepting a gift, an invitation, an offer, etc.
examples: Please confirm your acceptance of this offer in writing.
He made a short acceptance speech/speech of acceptance.
Invitations have been sent out and 80 acceptances have already been received.
So far we have had one refusal and three acceptances.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of agreeing with something and approving of it
examples: The new laws have gained widespread acceptance.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of allowing somebody to join something or be a member of a group
examples: Your acceptance into the insurance plan is guaranteed.
Social acceptance is important for most young people.
The group is now seeking formal acceptance.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the quality of being willing to accept an unpleasant or difficult situation
examples: acceptance of death/suffering

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the opportunity or right to use something or to see somebody/something
examples: COMPARE visitation
High-speed internet access has become a necessity.
You need a password to get access to the computer system.
access to information/services/resources
access to healthcare/education
They are seeking increased access to markets overseas.
to provide/allow access to something/somebody
to restrict/block access to something/somebody
Journalists were denied access to the President.
Many divorced fathers only have access to their children at weekends (= they are allowed by law to see them only at weekends).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a way of entering or reaching a place
examples: COMPARE egress
The police gained access through a broken window.
Many paths have become overgrown, blocking access.
There is easy access by road.
Disabled visitors are welcome; there is good wheelchair access to most facilities.
The only access to the farmhouse is across the fields.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that can be reached, entered, used, seen, etc.
examples: The remote desert area is accessible only by helicopter.
These documents are not accessible to the public.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that can be reached, entered, used, etc. by somebody who has problems walking
examples: accessible toilets for wheelchair users
The beach should be accessible to everyone.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: easy to understand
examples: Her poetry is always very accessible.
a programme making science more accessible to young people

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: easy to talk to and to get to knowWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from late Latin accessibilis, from Latin access- ‘approached’, from the verb accedere, from ad- ‘to’ + cedere ‘give way, yield’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an unpleasant event, especially in a vehicle, that happens unexpectedly and causes injury or damage
examples: a car/road/traffic accident
He was killed in an accident.
One in seven accidents is caused by sleepy drivers.
The accident happened at 3 p.m.
to have an accident
a serious/minor accident
a fatal accident (= in which somebody is killed)
Every year in the United Kingdom more than 4 000 people die in accidents in the home.
a climbing/riding accident

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that happens unexpectedly and is not planned in advance

an accident of birth/fate/history (= describing facts and events that are due to chance or circumstances)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing or person that is very likely to cause danger or a problem in the future because of the condition it is in or the way they behave
examples: Any one of these nuclear plants may be a disaster waiting to happen.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: people say accidents will happen to tell somebody who has had an accident, for example breaking something, that it does not matter and they should not worry

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in a way that is not planned or organized

Helen got into acting purely by accident.
It happened, whether by accident or design, that Steve and I were the last two people to leave.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a series of unpleasant events caused by bad luck
examples: The whole affair has been a chapter of accidents from start to finish.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: by chance; in a way that was not planned
examples: As I turned around, I accidentally hit him in the face.
The damage couldn't have been caused accidentally.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to provide somebody with a room or place to sleep, live or sit
examples: The hotel can accommodate up to 500 guests.
The aircraft is capable of accommodating 28 passengers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to provide enough space for somebody/something
examples: The garage can accommodate three cars.
The old town hall now accommodates a Folk Museum.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to consider something such as somebody’s opinion or a fact and be influenced by it when you are deciding what to do or explaining something
examples: Our proposal tries to accommodate the special needs of minority groups.
She modified her views so as to accommodate the objections of American feminists.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to help somebody by doing what they want
examples: SYNONYM oblige
I have accommodated the press a great deal, giving numerous interviews.
I’m sure the bank will be able to accommodate you.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to change your behaviour so that you can deal with a new situation better
examples: I needed to accommodate to the new schedule.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a place to live, work or stay in
examples: rented/temporary accommodation

First-class accommodation is available on all flights.

The building plans include much needed new office accommodation.
furnished accommodation

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: somewhere to live or stay, often also providing food or other services
examples: More and more travelers are looking for bed and breakfast accommodations in private homes.
The boat provides reasonable overnight accommodations for four adults.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an agreement or arrangement between people or groups with different opinions that is acceptable to everyone; the process of reaching this agreement
examples: They were forced to reach an accommodation with the rebels.
The two countries should be persuaded to work towards some sort of mutual accommodation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to travel or go somewhere with somebody/something
examples: His wife accompanied him on the trip.
He was accompanied on the visit by his wife.
I must ask you to accompany me to the police station.
Warships will accompany the convoy.
The groups are always accompanied by an experienced mountain guide.
Each young person must be accompanied by an adult.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to happen or appear with something else
examples: Shouts of protest accompanied this announcement.
strong winds accompanied by heavy rain
The text is accompanied by a series of stunning photographs.
Tax cuts have been accompanied by massive increases in public expenditure.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to play a musical instrument, especially a piano, while somebody else sings or plays the main tune
examples: The singer was accompanied on the piano by her sister.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to succeed in doing or completing something
examples: SYNONYM achieve
The first part of the plan has been safely accomplished.
I don't feel I've accomplished very much today.
That's it. Mission accomplished (= we have done what we aimed to do).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an impressive thing that is done or achieved after a lot of work
examples: SYNONYM achievement
It was one of the President's greatest accomplishments.
The series of paintings is quite an accomplishment.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a skill or special ability
examples: Drawing and singing were among her many accomplishments.
He was described as ‘a poet of rare accomplishment’.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the successful completing of something
examples: Money will be crucial to the accomplishment of our objectives.
There is a real sense of accomplishment when everything goes right.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: according to a rule or the way that somebody says that something should be done
examples: in accordance with legal requirements
We acted in accordance with my parents’ wishes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that is appropriate to what has been done or said in a particular situation
examples: We have to discover his plans and act accordingly.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: for that reason
examples: SYNONYM therefore
The cost of materials rose sharply last year. Accordingly, we were forced to increase our prices.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an arrangement that somebody has with a bank, etc. to keep money there, take some out, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO bank account
I don't have a bank account.
I paid the money into my savings account.
a joint account (= one in the name of more than one person)
With internet banking you can manage your account online.
Do you have an account with us?
He opened an account at a bank in Germany.
Interest will be paid monthly into the account holder's current account.
What's your account number please?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an arrangement that somebody has with a company that allows them to use the internet, send and receive messages by email, social media, etc.
examples: an email/a Twitter account
Millions of accounts have been hacked.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a written or spoken description of something that has happened
examples: an eyewitness account (= a description given by somebody who saw what happened)
a first-hand/personal/first-person account
Can you give us an account of what happened?
The diaries contained a detailed account of the writer's experiences in China.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an explanation or a description of an idea, a theory or a process
examples: the Biblical account of the creation of the world

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a written record of money that is owed to a business and of money that has been paid by it
examples: SEE ALSO expense account
to do the accounts
to keep the accounts up to date
the accounts department
She works in Accounts (= the accounts department).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an arrangement with a shop or business to pay bills for goods or services at a later time, for example in regular amounts every month
examples: SEE ALSO charge account
Put it on my account please.
We have accounts with most of our suppliers.
Log in to your account to see how much you have spent.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a bill for goods or services provided over a period
examples: Departing guests should settle their accounts at the office.
It is best to settle the account each month.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a regular customer
examples: The agency has lost several of its most important accounts.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a description of an event that gives you all the details in the order in which they happen
examples: He insisted on giving us a blow-by-blow account of what had happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: according to what other people say
examples: I've never been there, but it's a lovely place, by all accounts.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: according to what you say yourself
examples: By his own account he had an unhappy childhood.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to make somebody explain a mistake, etc. because they are responsible for it

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to do something or perform well, especially in a contest
examples: The team gave a good account of themselves in the match.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: not important
examples: Emotional matters were of no account to them during the war.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: if you buy something or pay on account, you pay nothing or only a small amount immediately and the rest later
examples: Call a cab on account.
Ring for a cab on account.
She bought the furniture she wanted on account.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: because of what you think somebody wants
examples: Please don't change your plans on my account.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: because of somebody/something
examples: She retired early on account of ill health.
The marsh is an area of great scientific interest on account of its wild flowers.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: not for any reason
examples: On no account should the house be left unlocked.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: for yourself
examples: In 2012 Smith set up in business on his own account.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: because you want to and you have decided, not somebody else
examples: No one sent me. I am here on my own account.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: because of the particular thing that has been mentioned
examples: Weather conditions were poor, but he did not delay his departure on that account.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to use something in a good or helpful way
examples: He turned his artistic talents to good account by becoming a sculptor.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to hurt or punish somebody who has harmed or cheated you in the past
examples: ‘Who would do such a thing?’ ‘Maybe someone with an old score to settle.’
An embittered Charlotte is determined to settle accounts with Elizabeth.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to consider particular facts, circumstances, etc. when making a decision about something
examples: The company takes account of environmental issues wherever possible.
Coursework is taken into account as well as exam results.

She hits the ball with great accuracy.

examples: the accuracy of radiocarbon dating

examples: Quantities must be measured accurately.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: You need to hit the ball accurately.

accusations of corruption/cruelty/racism

to achieve an objective/aim

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to succeed in doing something or causing something to happen
examples: SYNONYM accomplish
I haven't achieved very much today.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: SEE ALSO overachieve

an outstanding achievement

He has acquired a reputation for dishonesty.
I have recently acquired a taste for olives.

examples: Abstract art is an acquired taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that is suitable for somebody of your age and not as though you were much younger
examples: Isn’t it time you started acting your age?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to behave in a very confident way that annoys other people, for example by telling them what to do
examples: She was acting as if she owned the place.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to do something for a particular purpose or in order to deal with a situation
examples: It is vital that we act to stop the destruction of the rainforests.
By acting quickly doctors saved her life.
The government was criticized for failing to act decisively.
Initial reports indicated he acted alone.
He claims he acted in self-defence.
We acted in good faith (= believing that we were doing the right thing).
They are acting out of self-interest.
She was not acting for personal gain.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to behave in a particular way
examples: The man was seen acting suspiciously.
I think that most employers act responsibly in these situations.
Decide what your priorities are and act accordingly (= in an appropriate way).
Stop acting like spoilt children!
She was acting as if she'd seen a ghost.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to perform a part in a play or film
examples: Have you ever acted?
He just can't act.
Most of the cast act well.
The play was well acted.
Who's acting the part of Hamlet?
She is acting the role of Juliet.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to pretend by your behaviour to be a particular type of person
examples: SEE ALSO play-act
He's been acting the devoted husband all day.
I decided to act dumb.
to act weird/strange/normal/stupid
He acts all macho, but he’s a real softie underneath.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to perform a particular role or function
examples: She acted as an adviser to the committee.
Can you act as interpreter?
We hope this sentence will act as a deterrent to others.
Culture can act as a powerful catalyst for urban regeneration.
The council is only really acting as an agent.
hormones in the brain that act like natural painkillers

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have an effect on something
examples: Alcohol acts quickly on the brain.
It took a few minutes for the drug to act.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to behave in a stupid way in order to make people laugh, especially in a way that may also annoy them
examples: Quit playing the fool and get some work done!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that is suitable for somebody of your age and not as though you were much younger
examples: Isn’t it time you started acting your age?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to behave in a very confident way that annoys other people, for example by telling them what to do
examples: She was acting as if she owned the place.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of doing something in order to make something happen or to deal with a situation
examples: SEE ALSO affirmative action
The time has come for action if these beautiful animals are to survive.
to threaten/demand/call for action
Firefighters took action immediately to stop the blaze spreading.
Divers were close at hand, ready to go into action if the stunt went wrong.
What is the best course of action in the circumstances?
She began to explain her plan of action to the group.
The men face disciplinary action.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that somebody does
examples: Each of us must take responsibility for our own actions.
They sought to justify their actions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: things that workers do, especially stopping work, to protest to their employers about something
examples: SEE ALSO direct action
Workers voted in favour of strike action.
They called off their action at 7.40 am after the meeting was arranged.
Unions said the action could be suspended early on Friday if talks between the two sides resumed.
The government began taking a hard line against labour actions.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a legal process to stop a person or company from doing something, or to make them pay for a mistake, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO class action
A libel action is being brought against the magazine that published the article.
He is considering taking legal action against the hospital.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: fighting in a battle or war
examples: The possibility of taking military action has not been ruled out.
I never saw action during the war.
soldiers killed in action

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the events in a story, play, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO live action
The action takes place in France.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: exciting events
examples: I like films with plenty of action.
New York is where the action is.
If you want to know where all the action is around here, just ask Jo.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the effect that something such as a chemical has on something
examples: Vitamin D can be made in the body by the action of sunlight on the skin.
The action of the rushing water cleans the gully.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the way a part of the body moves or functions
examples: a study of the action of the liver

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the mechanical parts of a piano, gun, clock, etc. or the way the parts move
examples: SEE ALSO bolt-action

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: what a person actually does means more than what they say they will do

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if somebody/something is in action, they are doing the activity or work that is typical for them
examples: Just press the button to see your favourite character in action.
I've yet to see all the players in action.
I have not yet seen the machines in action.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if you put an idea or a plan into action, you start making it happen or work
examples: The new plan for traffic control is being put into action on an experimental basis.
We need to put these ideas into action.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: not able to work or be used because of injury or damage
examples: Jon will be out of action for weeks with a broken leg.
The photocopier is out of action today.
He is out of action following an ankle injury.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: a share or role in an interesting or exciting activity, especially one that makes money
examples: Foreign firms will all want a piece of the action if the new airport goes ahead.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to suddenly start working or doing something
examples: ‘Let's go!’ he said, springing into action.
The town springs to life (= becomes busy) during the carnival.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to start doing something quickly and with a lot of energy
examples: The ambulance crew swung into action to resuscitate the patient.
The rescue operation swung into action immediately.
The emergency services swung into action as soon as the disaster was reported.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to act in order to avoid danger or an unpleasant situation
examples: The pilot had to take evasive action to avoid a mid-air collision.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make something such as a device or chemical process start working
examples: SEE ALSO voice-activated
The burglar alarm is activated by movement.
The gene is activated by a specific protein.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of making something such as a device or chemical process start working
examples: The activation of several target genes results in two major effects.
to trigger/inhibit/block the activation of something

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: always busy doing things, especially physical activities
examples: OPPOSITE inactive
Staying physically active in later years can also keep you feeling younger.
Before our modern age, people had a more physical and active lifestyle.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: involved in something; making a determined effort and not leaving something to happen by itself
examples: They were both politically active.
his active involvement/participation in the arts
She takes an active part in school life.
He still has an active role in running the company.
an active participant/member
He is an active member of several professional organizations.
At 50, I'm an active participant in my community.
She remained active in politics until her death.
The parents were active in campaigning against cuts to the education budget.
They took active steps to prevent the spread of the disease.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: doing something regularly; functioning
examples: OPPOSITE inactive
Numbers of sexually active teenagers have continued to rise.
These animals are active only at night.
The virus is still active in the blood.
an active volcano (= likely to erupt)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: lively and full of ideas
examples: That child has a very active imagination.
It's important to remain mentally active after retirement.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: working; in use or able to be used
examples: The old watermill was active until 1960.
Ensure the website URL is an active link.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: having or causing a chemical effect
examples: OPPOSITE inactive
What is the active ingredient in aspirin?
drugs that are active against cancers

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: connected with a verb whose subject is the person or thing that performs the action
examples: COMPARE passive
In ‘He was driving the car’, the verb is active.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who works to achieve political or social change, especially as a member of an organization with particular aims
examples: human/civil/animal rights activists
Thousands of environmental activists joined the march to demand action on climate change.
The Prime Minister will face party activists when she addresses the party conference tomorrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that you do for interest or pleasure
examples: leisure/outdoor/recreational activities
The club provides a wide variety of activities including tennis, swimming and squash.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that somebody does in order to achieve a particular aim
examples: SEE ALSO displacement activity
criminal/terrorist/illegal activities
He has decided to focus his time and resources on his business activities.
We met to review progress and to coordinate our activities.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a situation in which something is happening or a lot of things are being done
examples: COMPARE inactivity
Economic activity has taken a downturn this year.
The streets were noisy and full of activity.
Muscles contract and relax during physical activity.
There was no criminal activity involved.
The machines can monitor brain activity.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who performs on the stage, on television or in films, especially as a profession
examples: SEE ALSO actress
Both lead actors (= the ones who play the main parts) are outstanding.
She is one of the country’s leading actors.
a stage/film/movie actor
a Hollywood actor
The movie starred a bunch of relatively unknown young actors.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who plays a part, pretending by their behaviour to be a particular kind of person
examples: I don't know if he really meant the things he said—he was always a good actor.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a participant in an action or process
examples: Employers are key actors within industrial relations.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a woman who performs on the stage, on television or in films, especially as a profession
examples: We will hold auditions to find a talented young actor or actress for the role.
The Oscar-winning actress has taken a break from acting.
In 1940 he married actress Jane Wyman.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a woman who plays a part, pretending by her behaviour to be a particular kind of person
examples: I became a very good actress and they nearly always believed me.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something that is real or exists in fact
examples: NOTE AT presently
James looks younger than his wife but in actual fact (= really) he is five years older.
The actual cost was higher than we expected.
The actual number of unemployed is more than 15 million.
What were his actual words?
A variety of factors could cause our actual results to differ from the expected results.
The story of the film is based on actual events and people.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the most important part of something
examples: The rehearsal was fabulous, the actual performance even better.
The wedding preparations take weeks but the actual ceremony takes less than an hour.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used in speaking to emphasize a fact or a comment, or that something is really true
examples: What did she actually say?
It's not actually raining now.
The book was never actually published.
I'm glad we were actually able to get the message across.
That's the only reason I'm actually going.
There are lots of people there who can actually help you.
I didn't want to say anything without actually reading the letter first.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to show a contrast between what is true and what somebody believes, and to show surprise about this contrast
examples: It was actually kind of fun after all.
The food was not actually all that expensive.
Our turnover actually increased last year.
I couldn't believe it had all actually happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to correct somebody in a polite way
examples: We're not American, actually. We're Canadian.
Actually, it would be much more sensible to do it later.
They're not married, actually.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to get somebody’s attention, to introduce a new topic or to say something that somebody may not like, in a polite way
examples: Actually, I'll be a bit late home.
Actually, I'm busy at the moment—can I call you back?
Well, actually, I think she's done a pretty good job.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very serious or severe
examples: There is an acute shortage of water.
acute pain
the world’s acute environmental problems
Competition for jobs is acute.
The scandal was an acute embarrassment for the President.
He was suffering from acute chest pains.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an acute illness is one that has quickly become severe and dangerous
examples: OPPOSITE chronic
acute appendicitis

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: describing or designed for patients suffering from an acute illness
examples: acute patients
an acute ward

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very sensitive and well developed
examples: SYNONYM keen
Dogs have an acute sense of smell.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: intelligent and quick to notice and understand things
examples: He is an acute observer of the social scene.
Her judgement is acute.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: less than 90°
examples: COMPARE obtuse (2)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a notice, picture or film telling people about a product, job or service
examples: SEE ALSO attack ad
The TV ads were first run last year.
They've produced an ad for a new chocolate bar.
We put an ad on a classifieds website.
A $10 million TV ad campaign
an ad agency

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to change your behaviour in order to deal more successfully with a new situation
examples: SYNONYM adjust
It's amazing how soon you adapt.
The organisms were forced to adapt in order to survive.
Some animals have a remarkable ability to adapt to changing environments.
A large organization can be slow to adapt to change
The company was able to adapt to the conditions and enhance its position.
We have had to adapt quickly to the new system.
It took him a while to adapt himself to his new surroundings.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to change something in order to make it suitable for a new use or situation
examples: SYNONYM modify
These styles can be adapted to suit individual tastes.
The classroom has been specially adapted to take wheelchairs.
Most of these tools have been specially adapted for use by disabled people.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to change a book or play so that it can be made into a play, film, television drama, etc.
examples: Three of her novels have been adapted for television.
The radio play had been adapted from a novel.
They have adapted her original novel beautifully.
It was adapted for the screen from his original play.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the action or process of changing something, or of being changed, to suit a new purpose or situation
examples: the adaptation of buildings for military purposes
The process of adaptation to a new school is difficult for some children.
making adaptations to your home

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a film, television drama or play that is based on a particular book or play but has been changed to suit the new medium
examples: a screen adaptation of Shakespeare’s ‘Macbeth’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of change by which a species becomes better suited to its environment
examples: the adaptation of desert species to the hot conditions
Adaptations in plants occur over thousands of years.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to put something together with something else so as to increase the size, number, amount, etc.
examples: Next add the flour.
The juice contains no added sugar.
As an added bonus, the book includes many black-and-white photographs.
Melt the butter, then add the onion.
The plan has the added (= extra) advantage of bringing employment to rural areas.
Shall I add your name to the list?
They are looking at ways to add further value to their products.
There are a number of ways to add emphasis to words on a web page.
A new wing was added to the building.
Chlorine is added to the water to kill bacteria.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to put numbers or amounts together to get a total
examples: OPPOSITE subtract
He knew how to add and subtract.
Add 9 to the total.
If you add all these amounts together you get a huge figure.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to say something more; to make a further remark
examples: ‘And don't be late,’ she added.
I have nothing to add to my earlier statement.
Do you have anything to add?
He added that they would return a week later.
'The hotel is child-friendly,' she said, adding that special rates apply to children.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to give a particular quality to an event, a situation, etc.
examples: The suite will add a touch of class to your bedroom.
The Easter Festival added a new dimension to Salzburg's musical life.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to introduce another fact that helps to emphasize a point you have already made
examples: Add to this the excellent service and you can see why it's the most popular hotel on the island.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make a bad relationship with somebody worse by offending them even more
examples: Then, to add insult to injury, they told me I couldn't get on the flight.
It adds insult to injury that banks are allowed to increase their charges without our knowledge or consent.
Only 300 people came to the match and to add insult to injury, the floodlights went out during the second half.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the condition of being unable to stop using or doing something as a habit, especially something harmful
examples: cocaine addiction
He is now fighting his addiction to alcohol.
an addiction to TV game shows/social media/gambling

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that is added to something else
examples: All of these technologies are fairly recent additions.
the latest addition to our range of cars
This is a welcome addition to the literature of western art history.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of adding something to something else
examples: Add salt, tasting with every addition.
Pasta's basic ingredients are flour and water, sometimes with the addition of eggs or oil.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a new part that is added to a building
examples: architects who specialize in home additions
The addition should match the architecture of the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the process of adding two or more numbers together to find their total
examples: OPPOSITE subtraction
children learning addition and subtraction

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used when you want to mention another person or thing after something else
examples: In addition to these arrangements, extra ambulances will be on duty until midnight.
There is, in addition, one further point to make.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: more than was first mentioned or is usual
examples: SYNONYM extra
additional resources/funds/security/funding/costs
The government provided an additional £25 million to expand the service.
He provided additional information about this incident.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that is more than was first mentioned or is usual
examples: SYNONYM in addition (to somebody/something)
Additionally, the bus service will run on Sundays, every two hours.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: details of where somebody lives or works and where letters, etc. can be sent
examples: SEE ALSO forwarding address
What's your name and address?
I'll give you my address and phone number.
Is that your home address?
Please note my change of address.
There was no return address on the envelope.
Each entry must include a valid mailing address.
a postal address
Police found him at an address (= a house or flat) in West London.
people with no fixed address (= with no permanent home)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a series of words and symbols that tells you where you can find something using a computer or phone, for example on the internet
examples: SEE ALSO IP address
What's your email address?
The project has a new web address.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a formal speech that is made in front of an audience
examples: tonight’s televised presidential address

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the correct title, etc. to use when you talk to somebodyWord Origin
examples: Middle English (as a verb in the senses ‘set upright’ and ‘guide, direct’, hence ‘write directions for delivery on’ and ‘direct spoken words to’): from Old French, based on Latin ad- ‘towards’ + directus past participle of dirigere, from di- ‘distinctly’ or de- ‘down’ + regere ‘put straight’. The noun is of mid 16th-cent. origin in the sense ‘act of approaching or speaking to someone’.

definitions.definition: details of where somebody lives or works and where letters, etc. can be sent

people with no fixed address (= with no permanent home)

examples: SEE ALSO IP address

The project has a new web address.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: tonight’s televised presidential address
