The noun is of mid 16th-cent. origin in the sense ‘act of approaching or speaking to someone’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: enough in quantity, or good enough in quality, for a particular purpose or need
examples: OPPOSITE inadequate
They'll need an adequate supply of hot water.
The room was small but adequate.
There is a lack of adequate provision for disabled students.
He didn't give an adequate answer to the question.
The space available is not adequate for our needs.
training that is adequate to meet the future needs of industry

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that is enough in quantity, or good enough in quality, for a particular purpose or need
examples: OPPOSITE inadequately
Are you adequately insured?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to stick to something
examples: Once in the bloodstream, the bacteria adhere to the surface of the red cells.
Clean the surface first, or the paint will not adhere.
There was oil adhering to the bird’s feathers.
The tiles may not adhere properly if you do not use the correct glue.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: next to something
examples: The planes landed on adjacent runways.
numbers that are adjacent in the sequence
Our farm land was adjacent to the river.
The vineyards of Verzy lie adjacent to those of Verzenay.
There is a row of houses immediately adjacent to the factory.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to change something slightly to make it more suitable for a new set of conditions or to make it work better
examples: Watch out for sharp bends and adjust your speed accordingly.
This button is for adjusting the volume.
The brakes need to be adjusted.
Adjust your language to the age of your audience.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to get used to a new situation by changing the way you behave and/or think
examples: SYNONYM adapt
They'll be fine—they just need time to adjust.
After a while his eyes adjusted to the dark.
It took her a while to adjust to living alone.
It can be difficult to adjust to being a parent.
You'll quickly adjust yourself to student life.
My eyes were still trying to adjust themselves to the strong sunlight.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move something slightly so that it looks neater or feels more comfortable
examples: SEE ALSO well adjusted
He smoothed his hair and adjusted his tie.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to acknowledge and apologize for something that causes problems or difficulties and ask people to accept and adapt to the situation
examples: The store will be closed this afternoon due to staffing shortages. Kindly adjust.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small change made to something in order to correct or improve it
examples: I've made a few adjustments to the design.
Some adjustment of the lens may be necessary.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a change in the way a person behaves or thinks
examples: She went through a period of emotional adjustment after her marriage broke up.
The process of adjustment to life in another country can be very difficult.
There was a long period of adjustment under the new boss.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to manage and organize the affairs of a company, an organization, a country, etc.
examples: SYNONYM manage
to administer a charity/fund/school
the high cost of administering medical services
The pension funds are administered by commercial banks.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make sure that something is done fairly and in the correct way
examples: to administer justice/the law
The questionnaire was administered by trained interviewers.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to give or to provide something, especially in a formal way
examples: The teacher has the authority to administer punishment.
A taxi driver administered first aid to the victims.
The priest was called to administer the last rites.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to give drugs, medicine, etc. to somebody
examples: Police believe his wife could not have administered the poison.
The dose was administered to the child intravenously.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to kick or to hit somebody/something
examples: He administered a severe blow to his opponent's head.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activities that are done in order to plan, organize and run a business, school or other institution
examples: SEE ALSO business administration
Administration costs are passed on to the customer.
the day-to-day administration of a company
I work in the Sales Administration department.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the government of a country, especially the US
examples: under the Trump administration
Successive administrations have failed to solve the country's economic problems.
A senior administration official has decided to step down.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the management of public affairs
examples: SYNONYM government (2)
The inhabitants of the island voted to remain under French administration.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the process or act of organizing the way that something is done
examples: the administration of justice

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the people who plan, organize and run a business, an institution, etc.
examples: university administrations

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the act of giving a drug to somebody
examples: the administration of antibiotics

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a situation in which the financial affairs of a business that cannot pay its debts are managed by an independent administrator
examples: COMPARE Chapter 11
If it cannot find extra funds, the company will go into administration.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with organizing the work of a business or an institution
examples: an administrative job/assistant/error

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person whose job is to manage and organize the public or business affairs of a company or an institution, or a person who works in an office dealing with records, accounts, etc.
examples: Such organizational decisions are made by the hospital administrators.
For an application form, please contact our administrator.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who manages a computer system and controls who can access it
examples: If you are unable to access the site, contact your system administrator.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person legally appointed (= chosen) to manage the financial affairs of a business that cannot pay its debtsWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Latin, from the verb administrare, from ad- ‘to’ + ministrare ‘wait upon’, from minister ‘servant’, from minus ‘less’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to respect somebody for what they have done or to respect their qualities
examples: I really admire your enthusiasm.
Her work was much admired by critics.
You have to admire the way he handled the situation.
Actually, I greatly admire and respect him.
The school is widely admired for its excellent teaching.
I don't agree with her, but I admire her for sticking to her principles.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to look at something and think that it is attractive and/or impressive
examples: He stood back to admire his handiwork.
I've just been admiring your new car.
Let’s just sit and admire the view.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of accepting somebody into an institution, organization, etc.; the right to enter a place or to join an institution or organization
examples: Hospital admission is not necessary in most cases.
Hospital admissions for asthma attacks have doubled.
the university admissions policy/office
They tried to get into the club but were refused admission.
She failed to gain admission to the university of her choice.
Is there any charge for admission?
There was a steady decline in cinema admissions during the 1960s.
countries applying for admission to the European Union
Last admissions to the park are at 4 p.m.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a statement in which somebody admits that something is true, especially something wrong or bad that they have done
examples: He is a thief by his own admission (= he has admitted it).
an admission of guilt/failure/defeat
The minister's resignation was an admission that she had lied.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the amount of money that you pay to go into a building or to an event
examples: SEE ALSO general admission
admission charges/prices
£5 admission
What's the admission?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to agree, often unwillingly, that something is true
examples: SYNONYM confess
It was a stupid thing to do, I admit.
‘I'm very nervous,’ she admitted reluctantly.
Don't be afraid to admit to your mistakes.
She admits to being strict with her children.
He admitted all his mistakes.
She stubbornly refuses to admit the truth.
Why don't you just admit defeat (= recognize that you cannot do something) and let someone else try?
I hate to admit it, but I think he is right.
Admit it! You were terrified!
I'm almost ashamed to admit it, but I watch this show.
They freely admit (that) they still have a lot to learn.
You must admit that it all sounds very strange.
She readily admits mistakes were made.
I couldn't admit to my parents that I was finding the course difficult.
It was generally admitted that the government had acted too quickly.
The appointment is now generally admitted to have been a mistake.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say that you have done something wrong or illegal
examples: SYNONYM confess
He refused to admit to the other charges.
She admitted to having stolen the car.
She admitted theft.
He refused to admit his guilt.
The hospital has admitted liability for the accident.
She admitted having driven the car without insurance.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to allow somebody/something to enter a place
examples: Each ticket admits one adult.
You will not be admitted to the theatre after the performance has started.
The narrow windows admit little light into the room.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to become a member of a club, a school or an organization
examples: The society admits all US citizens over 21.
Women were only admitted into the club last year.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to take somebody to a hospital or other institution where they can receive special care
examples: Two crash victims were admitted to the local hospital.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to accept that evidence is legally valid and can be presented in court
examples: Judge Neilson refused to admit the evidence because it had been illegally obtained.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a young person who is developing from a child into an adult
examples: adolescents between the ages of 13 and 18 and the problems they face
Stop acting like an adolescent!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take somebody else’s child into your family and become its legal parent(s)
examples: COMPARE foster
a campaign to encourage childless couples to adopt
to adopt a child
She was forced to have her baby adopted.
She adopted three children from the orphanage.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to start to use a particular method or to show a particular attitude towards somebody/something
examples: All three teams adopted different approaches to the problem.
Our study examined the strategies adopted by patients for seeking information.
The police adopted tighter security measures.
to adopt an attitude/stance/position

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to formally accept a suggestion or policy by voting
examples: The government adopted a resolution on disarmament.
The council is expected to adopt the new policy at its next meeting.
The U.N. Security Council unanimously adopted the resolution.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to choose a new name, a country, a custom, etc. and begin to use it as your own
examples: to adopt a name/title/language
Early Christians in Europe adopted many of the practices of the older, pagan religions.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to use a particular manner, way of speaking, expression, etc.
examples: He adopted an air of indifference.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to choose somebody as a candidate in an election; to choose somebody as your representative
examples: She was adopted as parliamentary candidate for Wood Green.
The people adopted him as their patron saint.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of adopting a child; the fact of being adopted
examples: She put the baby up for adoption.
The number of adoptions has fallen markedly since the 1970s.
his adoption into an American family

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the decision to start using something such as an idea, a plan or a name
examples: The widespread adoption of new information technology could save $162 billion a year.
The committee recommended the adoption of new safety procedures.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of choosing somebody as a candidate for an election
examples: his adoption as the Labour candidate
The party announced the formal adoption of George Smith as their election candidate.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a fully grown person who is legally responsible for their actions
examples: SYNONYM grown-up2
Children must be accompanied by an adult.
I simply can't believe that responsible adults allowed a child to wander the streets.
Why can't you two act like civilized adults?
The obesity rate among adults has actually increased.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a fully grown animal
examples: The fish return to the river as adults in order to breed.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: progress or a development in a particular activity or area of understanding
examples: We live in an age of rapid technological advance.
Recent advances in technology have made the procedure safe.
recent advances in medical science
major advances in the field of physics
an advance on the existing techniques
an advance towards a better understanding of God

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the forward movement of a group of people, especially armed forces
examples: We feared that an advance on the capital would soon follow.
enemy advances

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: money paid for work before it has been done or money paid earlier than expected
examples: They offered an advance of £5 000 after the signing of the contract.
The bank will give you an advance of 95% of the purchase price.
She asked for an advance on her salary.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: attempts to start a sexual relationship with somebody
examples: He had made advances to one of his students.
She rejected his sexual advances.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an increase in the price or value of something
examples: Share prices showed significant advances.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: before the time that is expected; before something happens
examples: a week/month/year in advance
The rent is due one month in advance.
Thanks in advance for your help.
We try to plan well in advance.
It would have helped to know in advance that you were coming.
The fee is payable in advance.
People were evacuated from the coastal regions in advance of the hurricane.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: more developed than somebody/something else
examples: Galileo's ideas were well in advance of the age in which he lived.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having the most modern and recently developed ideas, methods, etc.
examples: Scientists are working on highly advanced technology to replace fossil fuels.
It is a technologically advanced society.
Even in advanced industrial societies, poverty persists.
Economically advanced developing countries must make a contribution.
Sweden has a reputation for advanced and stylish design.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: at a high or difficult level
examples: He hopes to pursue an advanced degree in economics.
an advanced student of English
There were only three of us on the advanced course.
special courses for very advanced students

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: at a late stage of development
examples: the advanced stages of the disease
patients with advanced lung cancer

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used in polite expressions to describe somebody as ‘very old’
examples: He was a man of advanced years.
Even at my advanced age I still know how to enjoy myself!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that helps you to be better or more successful than other people
examples: OPPOSITE disadvantage
a distinct/significant/huge advantage
It gives you an unfair advantage (= something that benefits you, but not your opponents).
She had the advantage of a good education.
You will be at an advantage (= have an advantage) in the interview if you have thought about the questions in advance.
The company was able to gain a competitive advantage over its rivals by reducing costs.
Being tall gave him an advantage over the other players.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a quality of something that makes it better or more useful
examples: OPPOSITE disadvantage
Each of these systems has its advantages and disadvantages.
Continuous assessment offers clear advantages for teachers and students.
A small car has the added advantage of being cheaper to run.
Is there any advantage in getting there early?
There are many advantages to online shopping.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the first point scored after a score of 40–40
examples: Advantage Miss Stephens.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to give you an advantage; to change a situation in a way that gives you an advantage
examples: It would be to your advantage to attend this meeting.
Eventually, the new regulations will work to our advantage.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make use of something well; to make use of an opportunity
examples: She took advantage of the children's absence to tidy their rooms.
We took full advantage of the hotel facilities.
I took complete advantage of the situation.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make use of somebody/something in a way that is unfair or dishonest
examples: SYNONYM exploit
He took advantage of my generosity (= for example, by taking more than I had intended to give).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in a way that shows the best of somebody/something
examples: The photograph showed him to advantage.
May was the month to see the garden to best advantage.
The bright lighting showed the jewels to their best advantage.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to use or change a bad situation so that it helps you
examples: Every magician has a trick that goes wrong, but you can turn this to your advantage by pretending it was deliberate and making the audience laugh.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an unusual, exciting or dangerous experience, journey or series of events
examples: her adventures travelling in Africa
adventure stories
Four members of our staff have embarked on the adventure of a lifetime.
They fly around in their rocket ship and go on exciting adventures.
When you're a child, life is one big adventure.
Popper described science as the greatest adventure in the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the quality of being excited and willing to take risks, try new ideas, etc.
examples: a sense/spirit of adventure
I set out across the country looking for adventure.
the adventure travel industry
Travelling by train has always been associated with romance and adventure.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: negative and unpleasant; not likely to produce a good result
examples: adverse change/circumstances/weather conditions
Lack of money will have an adverse effect on our research programme.
They have attracted strong adverse criticism.
This drug is known to have adverse side effects.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell the public about a product or a service in order to encourage people to buy or to use it
examples: If you want to attract customers you need to advertise.
to advertise on TV/online/on social media
to advertise a product/service
a glossy brochure advertising holidays in the Maldives
How to Advertise a Business for Free on the Internet
I bought the camera and case as advertised in the catalogue.
The cruise was advertised as the ‘journey of a lifetime’.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to let people know that something is going to happen, or that a job is available by giving details about it in a newspaper, on a notice in a public place, on the internet, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO re-advertise
Sellers pay upfront to advertise.
We are currently advertising for a new sales manager.
The best jobs are not always advertised in newspapers.
Vacancies are usually advertised on our website.
We advertised the concert quite widely.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show or tell something about yourself to other people
examples: SYNONYM publicize
I wouldn't advertise the fact that you don't have a work permit.
She coughed to advertise her presence.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a notice, picture or film telling people about a product, job or service
examples: SEE ALSO classified advertisement
a newspaper/television advertisement
an online advertisement
You can place an advertisement on a classifieds website.
Television and radio refused to carry advertisements for the album.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an example of something that shows its good qualities
examples: Dirty streets and homelessness are no advertisement for a prosperous society.
He's a walking advertisement for healthy living.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of advertising something and making it public
examples: We are employing an assistant to help with the advertisement of the group’s activities.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activity and industry of advertising things to people on television, in newspapers, on the internet, etc.
examples: Cigarette advertising has been banned.
radio/TV/online advertising
Paid advertising on social media is an assured way to reach out to customers.
The company's print and digital advertising rose compared with the same period a year ago.
a career in advertising
Val works for an advertising agency (= a company that designs advertisements).
A good advertising campaign will increase our sales.
She is a successful advertising executive.
We we.re very happy with our advertising strategy last year.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an opinion or a suggestion about what somebody should do in a particular situation
examples: expert/practical/professional/medical advice
We were advised to seek legal advice.
The service offers information and advice on possible careers.
Ask your teacher's advice on how to prepare for the exam.
Ask your teacher for advice on how to prepare for the exam.
They give good advice to parents about managing difficult behaviour.
We were advised to seek advice from an expert.
Let me give you a piece of advice.
A word of advice. Don't wear that dress.
Take my advice. Don't do it.
Follow your doctor's advice.
I went there on the advice of a friend.
I chose it on his advice.
She went back to work against the advice of her doctor (= her doctor advised her not to).
The centre offers a free and confidential advice service.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell somebody what you think they should do in a particular situation
examples: SEE ALSO ill-advised
I would strongly advise against going out on your own.
They advised me against visiting the troubled south of the country.
The Foreign Office is advising Britons against all non-essential travel to the region.
They advised against the use of military force.
Her mother was away and couldn't advise her.
I'd advise extreme caution.
‘Get there early,’ she advised (them).
Police are advising people to stay at home.
Doctors advised the patient to have surgery.
I'd advise you not to tell him.
Solicitors advised their clients to contact their local councillors.
They advise that a passport be carried with you at all times.
They advise that a passport should be carried with you at all times.
It is strongly advised that you take out insurance.
I'd advise buying your tickets well in advance if you want to travel in August.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give somebody help and information on a subject that you know a lot about
examples: We employ an expert to advise on new technology.
The nurse will advise about getting out of bed, bathing, and diet.
She advises the government on environmental issues.
They can advise customers about safely using and storing pesticides.
The pharmacist will advise which medicines are safe to take.
Your lawyer can advise you whether to take any action.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to officially tell somebody something
examples: SYNONYM inform
Please advise us of any change of address.
to advise somebody of their rights/the situation
You will be advised of the outcome of your application.
Please keep me advised of new developments in this case.
I will contact you later to advise you when to come.
I regret to advise you that the course is now full.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who supports or speaks in favour of somebody or of a public plan or action
examples: SEE ALSO devil’s advocate
an advocate for hospital workers
a staunch advocate of free speech

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who defends somebody in court
examples: Solicitors often appear as advocates in the lower courts.
Those charged should be represented by trained, qualified legal advocates.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: (in Scotland and South Africa) a lawyer who has the right to argue cases in higher courts
examples: SEE ALSO the Lord Advocate

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: made in an artistic way and beautiful to look at
examples: Their furniture was more aesthetic than functional.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: events that are of public interest or political importance
examples: SEE ALSO current affairs
world/international affairs
an expert on foreign affairs (= political events in other countries)
We are expecting a statement from the home affairs (= political events in your own country) spokesman.
internal/external affairs
affairs of state

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an event that people are talking about or describing in a particular way
examples: The newspapers exaggerated the whole affair wildly.
She wanted the celebration to be a simple family affair.
Many people have criticized the way the government handled the affair.
The Whitewater affair was the biggest scandal of the decade.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a sexual relationship between two people, usually when one or both of them are already in a relationship with somebody else
examples: SEE ALSO love affair
She is having an affair with her boss.
an extramarital affair
It's the story of a secret affair between a married teacher and her teenage student.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: matters connected with a person’s private business and financial situation
examples: She manages the family's financial affairs.
I looked after my father's financial affairs.
She wanted to put her affairs in order before she died.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a thing that somebody is responsible for (and that other people should not be interested in)
examples: SYNONYM business
How I spend my money is my affair.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an object that is unusual or difficult to describe
examples: Her hat was an amazing affair with feathers and a huge brim.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a situation
examples: This state of affairs can no longer be ignored.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to produce a change in somebody/something
examples: How will these changes affect us?
The article deals with issues affecting the lives of children.
Thousands of people have been adversely affected (= affected in a negative way) by the decision.
The quality and health of the soil directly affects the quality and health of the plants.
Your opinion will not affect my decision.
The south of the country was worst affected by the drought.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to attack somebody or a part of the body; to make somebody become ill
examples: The disease is more likely to affect women than men.
The condition affects one in five women.
Rub the cream into the affected areas.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel very sad, sorry, etc. about somebody/something
examples: They were deeply affected by the news of her death.
Her death affected him deeply.
Try not to let his problems affect you too much.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to pretend to be feeling or thinking something
examples: She affected a calmness she did not feel.
We are fascinated by the rich and powerful but often affect to despise them.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to use or wear something that is intended to impress other people
examples: SYNONYM put on
I wish he wouldn't affect that ridiculous accent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the feeling of liking or loving somebody/something very much and caring about them
examples: Children need lots of love and affection.
He didn't show his wife any affection.
She was held in deep affection by all her students.
Mr Darcy’s affection for his sister
I have a great affection for New York.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person’s feelings of love
examples: Anne had two men trying to win her affections.
The object of her affections was a young man named Paul.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have enough money to be able to buy or do something
examples: Can we afford a new car?
None of them could afford £50 for a ticket.
I’d give up work if I could afford it.
We can't afford to go abroad this summer.
She never took a taxi, even though she could afford to.
She can well afford to pay for herself.
They couldn't afford to buy a house there.
We can't afford to have children.
He couldn't afford the money to go on the trip.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: if you say that you can’t afford to do something, you mean that you should not do it because it will cause problems for you if you do
examples: We cannot afford to ignore this warning.
They could ill afford to lose any more staff.
The people who suffer most are those who can least afford to lose.
We simply can't afford to take any risks.
She felt she couldn't afford any more time off work.
We cannot afford any more delays.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to provide somebody with something
examples: The tree affords some shelter from the sun.
The legislation aims to afford protection to employees.
Being a college professor affords you the opportunity simply to write and do research.
The programme affords young people the chance to gain work experience.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: cheap enough that people can afford to pay it or buy it
examples: OPPOSITE unaffordable
We offer quality products at affordable prices.
There is a lack of affordable housing in the city.
This model is relatively affordable at just $85.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling fear; frightened because you think that you might be hurt or suffer
examples: Don't be afraid.
It's all over. There's nothing to be afraid of now.
He had always been afraid of death.
They know I'm afraid of heights.
Are you afraid of spiders?
I started to feel afraid of going out alone at night.
She was afraid to open the door.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: worried about what might happen
examples: She was afraid of upsetting her parents.
Tamsin was afraid of making a fool of herself.
Don't be afraid to ask if you don't understand.
The boy wasn’t afraid to say what he believed.
He certainly isn't afraid to speak his mind.
We were afraid (that) we were going to capsize the boat.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: worried or frightened that something unpleasant, dangerous, etc. will happen to a particular person or thing
examples: I'm not afraid for me, but for the baby.
Roger was very afraid for her.
They had already fired three people and he was afraid for his job.
to be afraid for somebody's life/safety

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used as a polite way of telling somebody something that is unpleasant or disappointing, or that you are sorry about
examples: I can't help you, I'm afraid.
I'm afraid we can't come.
I'm afraid that it's not finished yet.
He's no better, I'm afraid to say.
‘Is there any left?’ ‘I'm afraid not.’
‘Will it hurt?’ ‘I'm afraid so.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: later than something; following something in time
examples: We'll leave after lunch.
They arrived shortly after 5.
Not long after that he resigned.
Let’s meet the day after tomorrow/the week after next.
After winning the prize she became famous overnight.
After an hour I went home (= when an hour had passed).
It’s ten after seven in the morning (= 7.10 a.m.).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: next to and following somebody/something in order or importance
examples: Your name comes after mine in the list.
He's the tallest, after Richard.
After you (= Please go first).
After you with the paper (= Can I have it next?).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: behind somebody when they have left; following somebody
examples: Shut the door after you.
I'm always having to clean up after the children (= clean the place after they have left it dirty and untidy).
He ran after her with the book.
She was left staring after him.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in contrast to something
examples: It was pleasantly cool in the house after the sticky heat outside.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: as a result of or because of something that has happened
examples: I'll never forgive him after what he said.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: despite something; although something has happened
examples: I can't believe she'd do that, not after all I've done for her.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show that something happens many times or continuously
examples: SEE ALSO one after another/the other
day after day of hot weather
I've told you time after time not to do that.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: trying to find or catch somebody/something
examples: The police are after him.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the situation that exists as a result of an important (and usually unpleasant) event, especially a war, an accident, etc.
examples: A lot of rebuilding took place in the aftermath of the war.

How does a country cope with the aftermath of war?
The president visited the region in the immediate aftermath of the disaster.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the period of time from 12 o'clock in the middle of the day until about 6 o’clock in the evening
examples: SEE ALSO good afternoon
this/yesterday/tomorrow afternoon

Where were you on the afternoon of May 21?
Heavy snow arrived during the afternoon.
She studies art two afternoons a week.
Georgia was enjoying afternoon tea with her grandmother.
Come over on Sunday afternoon.
The baby always has an afternoon nap.
Are you ready for this afternoon's meeting?
The activities are split into morning and afternoon sessions.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at a later time; after an event that has already been mentioned
examples: Afterwards she was sorry for what she'd said.
Let's go out now and eat afterwards.
Shortly afterwards he met her again.
He took his family to supper at a restaurant, and soon afterwards, he fell ill.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one more time; on another occasion
examples: This must never happen again.
Try again—it takes practice.
Can we start again, please?
Could you say it again, please?
When will I see you again?
Rowling again proves to be a superb storyteller.
I've told you again and again (= many times) not to do that.
I'll have to write it all over again (= again from the beginning).
She tried over and over again (= many times) to get it right.
He has yet again (= as has happened many times before) shown that he cannot be trusted.
Once again (= as had happened several times before), the train was late.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: showing that somebody/something is in the same place or state that they were in originally
examples: We're very happy to be here together again.
He was glad to be home again.
You'll soon feel well again.
She spends two hours a day getting to work and back again.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: added to an amount that is already there
examples: The cost is about half as much again as it was two years ago.
I'd like the same again (= the same amount or the same thing).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that a comment or fact is connected with what you have just said
examples: And again, we must think of the cost.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to introduce a fact or an opinion that contrasts with what you have just said
examples: We might buy it but then again we might not.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when you ask somebody to tell you something or repeat something that you think they have told you already
examples: What was the name again?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: from time to time; occasionally
examples: Every now and again she checked to see if he was still asleep.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody to serve you the same drink as before
examples: Same again, please!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: often; on many or all occasions
examples: You will get a perfect result time after time if you follow these instructions.
Time and again, the girls have shown how strong and determined they can be.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: opposing or disagreeing with somebody/something
examples: the fight against terrorism
We're playing against the league champions next week.
We were rowing against the current.
That's against the law.
She was forced to marry against her will.
Are you for or against the death penalty?
She is against seeing (= does not want to see) him.
I'd advise you against doing that.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not to the advantage or favour of somebody/something
examples: COMPARE for
The evidence is against him.
Her age is against her.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: close to, touching or hitting somebody/something
examples: Put the piano there, against the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in order to prevent something from happening or to reduce the damage caused by something
examples: an injection against rabies
They took precautions against fire.
Are we insured against theft?
He gritted his teeth against the pain.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: with something in the background, as a contrast
examples: His red clothes stood out clearly against the snow.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: You must weigh the benefits against the cost.

What's the rate of exchange against the dollar?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in contrast with something
examples: They got 27 per cent of the vote as against 32 per cent at the last election.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: you are unlikely to succeed because the conditions are not good for youWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from again + -s (adverbial genitive) + -t probably by association with superlatives (as in amongst).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the number of years that a person has lived or a thing has existed
examples: SEE ALSO legal age
You're the same age as my brother.
When I was your age I was already married.
ways of calculating the age of the earth
to reach retirement age
He left school at the age of 18.
He started playing the piano at an early age.
Children can start school from the age of four.
children between the ages of 5 and 10
The children range in age from 5 to 10.

Children over the age of 12 must pay full fare.

Young people of all ages go there to meet.
She needs more friends of her own age.
All ages admitted.
He was tall for his age (= taller than you would expect, considering his age).
She was beginning to feel her age (= feel that she was getting old).
The show appeals to all age ranges.
There’s a big age gap between them (= a big difference in their ages).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a very long time
examples: It'll probably take ages to find a parking space.
I waited for ages.
Carlos left ages ago.
It's been an age since we've seen them.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a particular period of a person’s life
examples: SEE ALSO middle age
in middle/old age
15 is an awkward age.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a particular period of history
examples: SEE ALSO Bronze Age
the nuclear age
We live in an age of globalization.
a study of fashion through the ages

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the state of being old
examples: The jacket was showing signs of age.
White hair is a sign of great age.
Wine improves with age.
the wisdom that comes with age

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a length of time that is a division of an epoch

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that is suitable for somebody of your age and not as though you were much younger
examples: Isn’t it time you started acting your age?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: when a person comes of age, they reach the age when they have an adult’s legal rights and responsibilities
examples: SEE ALSO coming of age
The money will go to the children when they come of age.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: if something comes of age, it reaches the stage of development at which people accept and value it
examples: It was the year that concern for the environment really came of age.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to realize that you are getting old, especially compared with people you are with who are younger than you

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a great age
examples: She finally learned to drive at the grand old age of 70.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: now, in the modern world
examples: Slavery continues to exist, even in this day and age.
Why dress so formally in this day and age?

definitions.label: Meaning 13

examples: She doesn’t look her age; I thought she was ten years younger.

definitions.definition: used in polite expressions to describe somebody as ‘very old’
examples: He was a man of advanced years.

examples: He lived to the ripe old age of 91.

definitions.definition: a list of items to be discussed at a meeting
examples: We have a very full agenda of issues to discuss.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: In our company, quality is high on the agenda.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: SEE ALSO hidden agenda

definitions.definition: a person whose job is to act for, or manage the affairs of, other people in business, politics, etc.
examples: Our agent in New York deals with all US sales.

an insurance agent
Typical agent's fees are around 6 percent of the sale price.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person whose job is to arrange work for an actor, musician, sports player, etc. or to find somebody who will publish a writer’s work
examples: SEE ALSO literary agent
a theatrical/literary agent

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who works secretly to obtain information for a government or other organization
examples: SEE ALSO double agent
He was arrested by federal agents.
an enemy/undercover agent
CIA/FBI agents

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person or thing that has an important effect on a situation
examples: The charity has been an agent for social change.

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: SEE ALSO nerve agent
chemical/biological agents
cleaning/oxidizing agents

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feelings of anger and hate that may result in threatening or violent behaviour
examples: The research shows that computer games may cause aggression.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a violent attack or threats by one person against another person or by one country against another country
examples: SEE ALSO non-aggression
unprovoked military aggression

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: angry, and behaving in a threatening way; ready to attack
examples: SEE ALSO passive-aggressive
Seals have been known to exhibit aggressive behaviour towards swimmers.
He became increasingly aggressive as the evening wore on.
He gets aggressive when he's drunk.
She warned that her dog was aggressive towards strangers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: determined and acting with force in order to succeed
examples: a very aggressive advertising campaign
We need to get more aggressive in our approach.
The firm is extremely aggressive in seeking new markets.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: developing quickly and difficult to treat
examples: Doctors diagnosed her with a rare and aggressive cancer, which was feared to be incurable.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: using all possible treatment options in order to extend somebody’s life
examples: Nicholas was diagnosed with the rare disease in November and has undergone aggressive treatments since then.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used in expressions of time with the simple past tense to show how far in the past something happened
examples: two weeks/months/years ago

She was here just a minute ago.
a short/long time ago
How long ago did you buy it?
It was on TV not (so) long ago.
Scientists think there was water on Mars a long time ago.
He stopped working some time ago (= quite a long time ago).
They're getting married? It's not that long ago (= it's only a short time ago) that they met!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have the same opinion as somebody; to say that you have the same opinion
examples: OPPOSITE disagree
When he said that, I had to agree.
‘That's true’, she agreed.
I totally agree with you!
You can't expect them to agree on everything.
He agreed with them about the need for change.
Many experts agree wholeheartedly with this statement.
I tend to agree with her political views.
All parties agree (that) urgent action is required.
We agreed (that) the proposal was a good one.
‘It's terrible.’ ‘I couldn't agree more!’ (= I completely agree)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to approve of something because you think it is morally right
examples: I don't agree with hitting children as a punishment.
I'm not sure I agree with the government's policy on this.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to say ‘yes’; to say that you will do what somebody wants or that you will allow something to happen
examples: I asked for a pay rise and she agreed.
The government has finally agreed in principle (= agreed in general but not in detail) to the terms of the deal.
Do you think he'll agree to their proposal?
She agreed (that) I could go early.
He reluctantly agreed to pay for the damage.
She agreed to let me go early.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to decide with somebody else to do something or to have something
examples: Can we agree on a date?
The new plan was agreed upon between the two sides.
They met at the agreed time.
Can we agree a price?
We agreed to meet on Thursday.
We couldn't agree what to do.
They left at ten, as agreed.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to officially accept a plan, request, etc.
examples: SYNONYM approve
The company agreed a deal worth $100 million.
Next year's budget has been agreed.
We arranged to meet a few days later and agree terms.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be the same as something
examples: The figures do not agree.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to match a word or phrase in number, gender or person
examples: In ‘Tom likes jazz’, the singular verb ‘likes’ agrees with the subject ‘Tom’.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

Spicy smells wafted through the air.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: We'll get a breath of fresh air at lunchtime.
I'm going outside for a breath of fresh air.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: (to have) plans or dreams that are not likely to happen or come true
examples: As a child he would wander round the boatyards, building castles in the air about owning a boat one day.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to improve a difficult or tense situation by talking about worries, doubts, etc.
examples: This meeting will be an opportunity to clear the air and start the healing process.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

examples: Storms were supposed to clear the air.

definitions.label: Meaning 12

definitions.label: Meaning 13

examples: It isn’t an exact science—it’s a kind of finger in the air thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to feel very happy

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: felt by a number of people to exist or to be happening

definitions.label: Meaning 16

examples: We will be back on air tomorrow morning at 7.

definitions.label: Meaning 17

definitions.label: Meaning 18

definitions.label: Meaning 19

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: full of emotion, excitement, activity, etc.
examples: Ed was alive with happiness.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: continuing to exist
examples: to keep a tradition alive

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: full of living or moving things
examples: The pool was alive with goldfish.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: aware of something; knowing something exists and is important
examples: to be alive to the dangers/facts/possibilities

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: very active, healthy or popular
examples: My mother is still alive and kicking.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: still living and not injured or harmed
examples: The missing student was found alive and well in Newcastle.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: still popular or successful
examples: Singapore's literary scene is alive and well.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to make something interesting
examples: The pictures bring the book alive.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to become interesting and exciting

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to become busy and full of activity
examples: SYNONYM come to life
The city starts to come alive after dark.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to show interest in something and become excited about it
examples: She came alive as she talked about her job.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to criticize or punish somebody severely because you are extremely angry with them
examples: He’ll eat you alive if he ever finds out.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to defeat somebody completely in an argument, a competition, etc.
examples: The defence lawyers are going to eat you alive tomorrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to bite somebody many times
examples: I was being eaten alive by mosquitoes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the whole number of
examples: All horses are animals, but not all animals are horses.
Cars were coming from all directions (= every direction).
All the people you invited are coming.
All my plants have died.
All five men are hard workers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the whole amount of
examples: All wood tends to shrink.
You've had all the fun and I've had all the hard work.
All this mail must be answered.
He has lost all his money.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used with singular nouns showing something has been happening for a whole period of time
examples: He's worked hard all year.
She was unemployed for all that time.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the greatest possible
examples: In all honesty (= being as honest as I can), I can't agree.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: consisting or appearing to consist of one thing only
examples: The magazine was all advertisements.
She was all smiles (= smiling a lot).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: any whatever
examples: He denied all knowledge of the crime.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: and other similar things
examples: I'm bored by history—dates and battles and all that stuff.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: despite
examples: For all its clarity of style, the book is not easy reading.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to say that something is not important or of no interest or value to you/somebody
examples: For all I know she's still living in Boston.

definitions.label: Meaning 10

examples: I didn't think you, of all people, would become a vegetarian.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: in or from all directions; everywhere
examples: We realized we were surrounded on all sides.
Disaster threatens on every side.
She was bombarded with questions from all sides.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a public statement that is made without giving proof, accusing somebody of doing something that is wrong or illegal
examples: SYNONYM accusation
to investigate/deny/withdraw an allegation
Several newspapers made allegations of corruption in the city's police department.
allegations of dishonesty against him
The committee has made serious allegations about interference in its work.
an allegation that he had been dishonest

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to state something as a fact but without giving proof
examples: The prosecution alleges (that) she was driving carelessly.
It is alleged that he mistreated the prisoners.
He is alleged to have mistreated the prisoners.
This procedure should be followed in cases where dishonesty has been alleged.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: expressed as though something is a fact but without giving any proof
examples: crimes allegedly committed during the war

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an agreement between countries, political parties, etc. to work together in order to achieve something that they all want
examples: to form/make an alliance
The Social Democrats are now in alliance with the Greens.
an alliance between education and business to develop the use of technology in schools

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of people, political parties, etc. who work together in order to achieve something that they all want
examples: The Green Alliance was formed to campaign against environmental damage.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give something officially to somebody/something for a particular purpose
examples: A large sum has been allocated for buying new books for the library.
They intend to allocate more places to mature students this year.
More resources are being allocated to the project.
The project is being allocated more resources.
Millions have been allocated to improve students' performance.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of money, space, etc. that is given to somebody for a particular purpose
examples: We have spent our entire allocation for the year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of giving something to somebody for a particular purpose
examples: the allocation of food to those who need it most

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to let somebody/something do something; to let something happen or be done
examples: PAST TENSE, PAST PARTICIPLE OF allow
His parents won't allow him to stay out late.
He allowed his mind to wander.
The law allowed companies to dismiss workers without any reason.
He is not allowed to stay out late.
Students are only allowed to use the equipment under supervision.
This research must be allowed to continue.
He refused to allow himself to be kept quiet.
She won't allow herself to be dictated to.
Eating is not allowed in the classrooms.
He received the maximum sentence allowed by law.
We do not allow eating in the classrooms.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to let somebody have something
examples: You're allowed an hour to complete the test.
I'm not allowed visitors.
I allow myself a treat now and then.
I sometimes allow myself the luxury of a cigar.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to let somebody/something go into, through, out of, etc. a place
examples: No dogs allowed (= you cannot bring them in).
The prisoners are allowed out of their cells for two hours a day.
They weren't allowed into the country.
He was knocking at the door waiting to be allowed in.
You won't be allowed up (= out of bed) for several days.
The crowd parted to allow her through.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make something possible
examples: A ramp allows easy access for wheelchairs.
The system allows people the opportunity to browse a wide selection of books.
The new technology allows users to choose exactly what they watch and when.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make sure that you have enough of something for a particular purpose
examples: How much time would you allow for the trip?
You need to allow three metres of fabric for the dress.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to accept or admit something; to agree that something is true or correct
examples: COMPARE disallow
The judge allowed my claim.
(= in a court of law) ‘Objection!’ ‘I'll allow it.’
He refuses to allow that such a situation could arise.
She was very helpful when my mother was ill—I'll allow you that.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to offer help politely
examples: ‘Allow me,’ he said, taking the tray from her.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to give somebody complete freedom of action; to allow a feeling to be expressed freely
examples: HOMOPHONES AT reign
The designer was given free rein.
The script allows full rein to her larger-than-life acting style.
When I paint I just give my imagination free rein.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of money that is given to somebody regularly or for a particular purpose
examples: SEE ALSO Attendance Allowance
an allowance of $20 a day
a clothing/living/travel allowance
Do you get an allowance for clothing?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the amount of something that is allowed in a particular situation
examples: a baggage allowance of 20 kilos
Roman soldiers received a salt allowance, called salarium, the origin of the word salary.
The recommended daily allowance of vitamin C is 60–90 milligrams.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a small amount of money that parents give their children, usually every week or every month

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an amount of money that can be earned or received before you start paying tax
examples: personal tax allowances

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to consider something, for example when you are making a decision or planning something
examples: The budget made allowance for inflation.
The plan makes no allowance for people working at different rates.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to behave in a way that you would not usually accept, because of a problem or because there is a special reason
examples: You have to make allowances for him because he’s tired.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a country that has agreed to help and support another country, especially in case of a war
examples: our European/NATO allies
a loyal ally of the United States
Portugal is a traditional ally of England.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who helps and supports somebody who is in a difficult situation, especially a politician
examples: a close ally and friend of the prime minister
her most powerful political ally
His sister was his ally against their grandparents.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the group of countries including the UK and the US that fought together in the First and Second World Wars
examples: the Western Allies

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not quite
examples: SYNONYM nearly
I like almost all of them.
They'll eat almost anything.
Almost no one (= hardly anyone) believed him.
The castle is almost entirely surrounded by water.
It's a mistake they almost always make.
The painting is almost certainly a forgery.
Her handwriting is almost impossible to read.
The team faces almost certain defeat in today's match.
The workforce has almost doubled in the past ten years.
I almost forgot your birthday.
Housing has become almost as big a problem as education.
The story seems almost too strange to be true.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: without any other people
examples: Tom is not alone in finding Rick hard to work with.
She did not want to be alone with him.
He was afraid of being alone with his thoughts.
He lives alone.
She was sitting all alone in the hall.
Finally the two of us were alone together.
I don't like going out alone at night.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: without the help of other people or things
examples: SEE ALSO stand-alone
It's hard bringing up children alone.
The assassin said he had acted alone.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: lonely and unhappy or without any friends
examples: Carol felt all alone in the world.
I've been so alone since you went away.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used after a noun or pronoun to show that the person or thing mentioned is the only one
examples: You can't blame anyone else; you alone made the decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used after a noun or pronoun to emphasize one particular thing
examples: The shoes alone cost £200.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to do something without help from anyone
examples: Andrew decided to go it alone and start his own business.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to stop annoying somebody or trying to get their attention
examples: She's asked to be left alone but the press photographers follow her everywhere.
Don't touch me! Leave me alone!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to stop touching, changing, or moving something
examples: I've told you before—leave my things alone!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used after a statement to emphasize that because the first thing is not true or possible, the next thing cannot be true or possible either
examples: There isn't enough room for us, let alone any guests.
I didn’t have any clothes, let alone a passport.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be independent or not connected with other people, organizations or ideas
examples: These islands are too small to stand alone as independent states.
The problems that research is designed to solve do not stand alone, but are part of a wider context.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be not near other objects or buildings
examples: The arch once stood alone at the entrance to the castle.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say that you will have to wait for some time to find out the result of a situation
examples: Only time will tell if the treatment has been successful.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: from one end to or towards the other end of something
examples: They walked slowly along the road.
I looked along the shelves for the book I needed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a line that follows the side of something long
examples: Houses had been built along both sides of the river.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: at a particular point on or next to something long
examples: You'll find his office just along the corridor.

examples: You'll find his office just along the corridor.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: next to or at the side of somebody/something
examples: Nick caught up with me and rode alongside.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: before now or before a particular time in the past
examples: ‘Lunch?’ ‘No thanks, I've already eaten.’
We got there early but Mike had already left.
By 2015, filming of the sequel was already under way.
Much of what he said I knew already.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to express surprise that something has happened so soon or so early
examples: Is it 10 o'clock already?
You're not leaving already, are you?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that a situation or problem exists
examples: I'm already late.
The new company already has an excellent reputation.
There are far too many people already. We can't take any more.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used after a word or phrase to show that you are annoyed
examples: Just stop already, no one feels sorry for you.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that something is annoying or boring and that you want it to stopWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from the adverb all + ready.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in addition; too
examples: She's fluent in French and German. She also speaks a little Italian.
rubella, also known as German measles
I didn't like it that much. Also, it was much too expensive.
Jake's father had also been a doctor (= both Jake and his father were doctors).
She was not only intelligent but also very musical.
He also recently said that he would be leaving at the end of the year.
I probably also have a copy of the list.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become different; to make somebody/something different
examples: Prices did not alter significantly during 2019.
He had altered so much I scarcely recognized him.
His actions that day altered my perception of him.
The landscape has been radically altered by changes in the climate.
He has the power to fundamentally alter the course of history.
She didn't alter her behaviour in any way.
Nothing can alter the fact that we are to blame.
The recipe has been altered to suit American tastes.
Fame hasn't really altered her.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make changes to a piece of clothing so that it will fit you better
examples: We can have the dress altered to fit you.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that you can choose to do or have out of two or more possibilities
examples: The car is too expensive so we're trying to find a cheaper alternative.
There is a vegetarian alternative on the menu every day.
We had no alternative but to fire Gibson.
to offer/provide an alternative
Does this offer a viable alternative to the existing system?
Fruit juice is provided as an alternative to alcoholic drinks.
This treatment is the only alternative for some patients.

to offer/provide an alternative
