definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used for introducing a statement that makes the main statement in a sentence seem surprising
examples: SYNONYM though
Although the sun was shining, it wasn't very warm.
Although small, the kitchen is well designed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to mean ‘but’ or ‘however’ when you are commenting on a statement
examples: I felt he was wrong, although I didn't say so at the time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: (used to emphasize something) completely; in every way
examples: The train went slower and slower until it stopped altogether.
I don't altogether agree with you.
I am not altogether happy (= I am very unhappy) about the decision.
It was an altogether different situation.
I’m not altogether convinced, I’m afraid.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to give a total number or amount
examples: You owe me £68 altogether.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to introduce a summary when you have mentioned a number of different things
examples: The food was good and we loved the music. Altogether it was a great evening.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a chemical element. Aluminium is a light, silver-grey metal used for making pans, etc.
examples: aluminium saucepans/window frames
aluminium foil (= for example, for wrapping food in)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at all times; on every occasion
examples: There's almost always somebody at home in the evenings.
Always lock your car.
She always arrives at 7.30.
The children always seem to be hungry.
Success seems always to be out of reach.
Your ideas are always welcome.
It's not always easy to do the right thing.
We're not always this busy!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: for a long time; since you can remember
examples: Pat has always loved gardening.
This is the way we've always done it.
This painting is very good—Ellie always was very good at art (= so it is not very surprising).
Did you always want to be an actor?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: for all future time
examples: I'll always love you.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if you say a person is always doing something, or something is always happening, you mean that they do it, or it happens, very often, and that this is annoying
examples: She's always criticizing me.
That phone's always ringing.
Why are you always complaining about my cooking?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to suggest a possible course of action
examples: If it doesn't fit, you can always take it back.
If he can't help, there's always John.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: as usually happens or is expected
examples: SYNONYM as usual
As always, Polly was late for school.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody cannot change
examples: Once an actor, always an actor.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: doing something for pleasure or interest, not as a job
examples: an amateur photographer

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: done for pleasure, not as a job
examples: amateur athletics

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not done or made well or with skill
examples: The performance sounded very amateur, I’m afraid.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: doing something for pleasure or interest, not as a job
examples: an amateur photographer

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: done for pleasure, not as a job
examples: amateur athletics

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not done or made well or with skill
examples: The performance sounded very amateur, I’m afraid.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very surprised
examples: an amazed look
an amazed silence
We were all amazed at the number of people who came.
I was amazed at her knowledge of French literature.
We just moved house and are amazed at the amount of junk we have.
We are constantly amazed by the quality and range of the books.
We were amazed by his generosity.
I was banging so loudly I’m amazed (that) they didn’t hear me.
She was amazed how little he had changed.
I was amazed at how well we did.
We were amazed to find that no one was hurt.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very surprising, especially in a way that you like or admire
examples: SYNONYM astonishing
an amazing feat/story/experience
That's amazing, isn't it?
The amazing thing is, he really believes he'll get away with it.
It was truly amazing to see how much work goes into a Broadway musical.
It's amazing how quickly people adapt.
I find it amazing that people can be so irresponsible.
It’s amazing the difference a few polite words make.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very impressive; excellent
examples: SYNONYM fantastic (1)
He makes the most amazing cakes.
I saw the most amazing film yesterday!
That looks pretty amazing, doesn't it?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official who lives in a foreign country as the senior representative there of his or her own country
examples: the British Ambassador to Italy/in Rome
a former ambassador to the UN

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who represents or promotes a particular activity
examples: SEE ALSO brand ambassador
The best ambassadors for the sport are the players.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that you want to do or achieve very much
examples: She had fulfilled her lifelong ambition.
His burning ambition was to study medicine.
political/artistic/career ambitions
At last he had realized his life's ambition.
He had only one ambition in life.
the country's nuclear ambitions (= plans to develop nuclear weapons)
She never achieved her ambition of becoming a famous writer.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the desire or strength of mind to be successful, rich, powerful, etc.
examples: She was driven by personal ambition.
She was intelligent but suffered from a lack of ambition.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: determined to be successful, rich, powerful, etc.
examples: a fiercely ambitious young manager
They were very ambitious for their children (= they wanted them to be successful).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: needing a lot of effort, money or time to succeed
examples: the government’s ambitious plans for social reform
Jogging every morning? That’s very ambitious, isn’t it?
Several interns will be working on three ambitious new projects.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a vehicle with special equipment, used for taking sick or injured people to a hospital
examples: SEE ALSO air ambulance
Call an ambulance!
the ambulance service
The ambulance crew rushed her to the hospital.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to change a law, document, statement, etc. slightly in order to correct a mistake or to improve it
examples: He asked to see the amended version.
The law has been amended to read as follows:…
Parliament will vote to amend the constitution.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small change or improvement that is made to a document or proposed new law; the process of changing a document or proposed new law
examples: to introduce/propose/table an amendment (= to suggest it)
Parliament passed the bill without further amendment.
She made several minor amendments to her essay.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a statement of a change to the Constitution of the US
examples: SEE ALSO Eighteenth Amendment
The 19th Amendment gave women the right to vote.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in the middle of or during something, especially something that causes excitement or fear
examples: He finished his speech amid tremendous applause.
The firm collapsed amid allegations of fraud.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: surrounded by something
examples: The hotel was in a beautiful position amid lemon groves.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: surrounded by somebody/something; in the middle of somebody/something
examples: a house among the trees
They strolled among the crowds.
I found the letter amongst his papers.
It's OK, you're among friends now.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: being included or happening in groups of things or people
examples: A British woman was among the survivors.
He was among the last to leave.
This attitude is common among the under-25s.
‘What was wrong with the job?’ ‘Well, the pay wasn't good, among other things.’
Discuss it among yourselves (= with each other) first.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used when you are dividing or choosing something, and three or more people or things are involved
examples: They divided the money up among their three children.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a quantity of something
examples: I was amazed at the amount he could eat.
Mix the colours in equal amounts.
an amount of money/information/work/time
A certain amount of time has already been spent on the project.
The server is designed to store huge amounts of data.
Try to reduce the amount of energy and water you use at home.
Faculty should increase the amount and quality of feedback they provide.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sum of money
examples: Everyone has paid the same amount.
You will receive a bill for the full amount.
The insurance company will refund any amount due to you.
Small amounts will be paid in cash.
You must pay back the full amount that you owe.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a large quantity of something
examples: There's been any amount of research into the subject.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used for saying that something will have no effect
examples: No amount of encouragement would make him jump into the pool.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: funny and giving pleasure
examples: an amusing story/game/incident
She writes very amusing letters.
I didn't find the joke at all amusing.
She told us about an amusing incident that happened on her way home.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a comparison of one thing with another thing that has similar features; a feature that is similar
examples: The teacher drew an analogy between the human heart and a pump.
There are no analogies with any previous legal cases.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of comparing one thing with another thing that has similar features in order to explain it
examples: learning by analogy
We can understand this theory by analogy with human beings.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to examine the nature or structure of something, especially by separating it into its parts, in order to understand or explain it
examples: The job involves collecting and analysing data.
Researchers have analysed the results in detail using specialist software.
Learn to step back and critically analyse situations.
He tried to analyse his feelings.
The first step is to define and analyse the problem.
The water samples will be analysed for the presence of polluting chemicals.
We need to analyse what went wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to treat or study somebody using psychoanalysisWord Origin
examples: late 16th cent.: influenced by French analyser, from medieval Latin analysis from Greek analusis, from analuein ‘unloose’, from ana- ‘up’ + luein ‘loosen’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the detailed study or examination of something in order to understand more about it; the result of the study
examples: SEE ALSO meta-analysis
statistical/data analysis
a detailed analysis of the data
to perform/conduct an analysis
Further analysis revealed significant regional variations in the results.
We made the decision based on our analysis of the situation.
to be included in/excluded from the analysis

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a careful examination of a substance in order to find out what it consists of
examples: The blood samples are sent to the laboratory for analysis.
the results of a DNA sequence analysis
You can ask for a chemical analysis of your tap water.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a method of treating somebody with mental problems by asking them to talk about past experiences and feelings in order to try to find explanations for their present problems
examples: In analysis the individual resolves difficult emotional conflicts.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say what is most important after everything has been discussed, or considered
examples: In the final analysis, it's a matter of personal choice.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person whose job involves examining facts or materials in order to give an opinion on them
examples: SEE ALSO quantitative analyst
a political/financial analyst
a food/market analyst
He's a senior research analyst at Deutsche Bank.
analysts expect/predict…
City analysts forecast huge profits this year.
According to music industry analysts, music downloads are set to decline by as much as 30 per cent this year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who treats patients using psychoanalysisWord Origin
examples: mid 17th cent.: from French analyste, from the verb analyser, from medieval Latin analysis from Greek analusis, from analuein ‘unloose’, from ana- ‘up’ + luein ‘loosen’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person in your family who lived a long time ago
examples: SYNONYM forebear
His ancestors had come to America from Ireland.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an animal that lived in the past that a modern animal has developed from
examples: a reptile that was the common ancestor of lizards and turtles

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an early form of a machine that later became more developed
examples: SYNONYM forerunner
The ancestor of the modern bicycle was called a penny-farthing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a heavy metal object that is attached to a rope or chain and dropped over the side of a ship or boat to keep it in one place
examples: to drop anchor
We raised the anchor and set sail.
We weighed anchor (= pulled it out of the water).
The ship lay at anchor two miles off the rocky coast.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or thing that gives somebody a feeling of safety
examples: the anchor of the family

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who presents a live radio or television programme and introduces reports by other people; an anchorman or anchorwoman
examples: ABC news anchor Peter Jennings

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: belonging to a period of history that is thousands of years in the past
examples: OPPOSITE modern
Archaeologists are excavating the ruined temples of this ancient civilization.
ancient Greece/Egypt/Rome
the ancient city of Petra

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very old; having existed for a very long time
examples: an ancient oak tree
ancient traditions/culture
the ancient Japanese art of origami
He's ancient—he must be at least fifty!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the people who lived in ancient times, especially the Egyptians, Greeks and RomansWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French ancien, based on Latin ante ‘before’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: also; in addition to
examples: bread and butter
a table, two chairs and a desk
Sue and I left early.
Do it slowly and carefully.
Can he read and write?
I cooked lunch. And I made a cake. (= you are emphasizing how much you have done)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: then; following this
examples: She came in and took her coat off.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used before a verb instead of to, to show purpose
examples: Go and get me a pen please.
I'll come and see you soon.
We stopped and bought some bread.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to introduce a comment or a question
examples: ‘We talked for hours.’ ‘And what did you decide?’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: as a result
examples: Miss another class and you'll fail.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: added to
examples: SYNONYM plus1
5 and 5 makes 10.
What's 47 and 16?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used between repeated words to show that something is repeated or continuing
examples: He tried and tried but without success.
The pain got worse and worse.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used between repeated words to show that there are important differences between things or people of the same kind
examples: I like city life but there are cities and cities.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a spirit who is believed to be a servant of God, and is sent by God to deliver a message or perform a task. Angels are often shown dressed in white, with wings.
examples: SEE ALSO guardian angel

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is very good and kind; a child who behaves well
examples: John is no angel, believe me (= he does not behave well).
Mary’s children are little angels.
I could hardly see Lisa in the role of ministering angel.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used when you are talking to somebody and you are grateful to them
examples: Thanks Dad, you're an angel.
Be an angel and make me a cup of coffee.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who supports a business by investing money in it, especially somebody who supports a new small business with their own money
examples: When will the angels get their money back?
They started the business with the help of $2 million supplied by angel investors.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: people with little experience try to do the difficult or dangerous things that more experienced people would not consider doingWord Origin
examples: Old English engel, ultimately via ecclesiastical Latin from Greek angelos ‘messenger’; superseded in Middle English by forms from Old French angele.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the strong feeling that you have when something has happened that you think is bad and unfair
examples: She had to find a way to express her pent-up anger.
The plan provoked anger among local residents.
the growing anger and frustration of young unemployed people
Jan slammed her fist on the desk in anger.
He was filled with anger at the way he had been treated.
There is much anger over plans to close the hospital.
Local people are seething with anger about the decision.
There is widespread anger at the government following yesterday's announcement.
I feel no anger towards him, only pity.
The people are taking to the streets to vent their anger against the prime minister.
a course in anger management (= controlling your feelings of anger)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the space between two lines or surfaces that join, measured in degrees
examples: SEE ALSO acute angle
a 45° angle
the rocket’s angle of descent

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a corner on the outside or inside of something
examples: It's a modern building, all brick and glass and sharp angles.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the direction that something is leaning or pointing in when it does not go straight up and down or straight across from side to side
examples: The Tower of Pisa leans at an angle
The plane was coming in at a steep angle.
His hair was sticking up at all angles.
His shoulder was bent at an odd angle so it must be broken.
Venus and the Earth orbit the Sun at a slight angle to each other.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a position from which you look at something
examples: The photo was taken from an unusual angle.
The painting changes slightly when seen from different angles.
The variety of camera angles gives her photographs interest.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a particular way of presenting or thinking about a situation, problem, etc.
examples: We need a new angle for our next advertising campaign.
You can look at the issue from many different angles.
You start seeing some solutions when you view something from all angles.
The article concentrates on the human angle (= the part that concerns people's emotions) of the story.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that shows you have strong feelings about something that you dislike very much or about an unfair situation
examples: Some senators reacted angrily to the president's remarks.
He swore angrily.
She angrily rejected any suggestion of a cover-up.
‘This isn't fair!’ she shouted angrily.
The president angrily denounced the coup as illegal.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having strong feelings about something that you dislike very much or about an unfair situation
examples: Her behaviour really made me angry.
I started to get really angry and upset.
The players were attacked by an angry mob.
The comments provoked an angry response from union leaders.
Thousands of angry demonstrators filled the square.
Please don't be angry with me. It wasn't my fault.
I was very angry with myself for making such a stupid mistake.
She felt angry with herself.
I was so angry at the way I had been treated.
The passengers grew angry about the delay.
He felt angry at the injustice of the situation.
The people are very angry over the decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: red and painful, usually because of an infection

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: dark and stormy
examples: the angry sea with its terrible waves

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a creature that is not a bird, a fish, a reptile, an insect or a human
examples: SEE ALSO companion animal
the animals and birds of South America
wild/farm animals
domestic animals such as dogs and cats
the export of live animals for slaughter
Fish oils are less saturated than animal fats.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: any living thing that is not a plant or a human
examples: SEE ALSO dumb animal
This product has not been tested on animals.
The workers were treated like animals.
In court he was banned from keeping animals.
cruelty to animals
animal welfare/cruelty
the animal kingdom

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: any living creature, including humans
examples: COMPARE vegetable
Humans are the only animals to have developed speech.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who behaves in a cruel or unpleasant way, or who is very dirty
examples: The person who did this is an animal, a brute.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a particular type of person, thing, organization, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO party animal
She's not a political animal.
The government that followed the election was a very different animal.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of making films, videos and computer games in which drawings, models or images of people and animals seem to move
examples: computer/cartoon animation

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a film in which drawings, models or images of people and animals seem to move
examples: The electronic dictionary included some animations.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: energy and enthusiasm in the way you look, behave or speak
examples: SEE ALSO suspended animation
His face was drained of all colour and animation.
She talked about her new job with great animation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the joint connecting the foot to the leg; the narrow part of the leg just above the ankle joint
examples: to sprain/break/twist your ankle
She suffered a serious ankle injury in training.
to have a broken/twisted/fractured/sprained ankle
ankle boots (= that cover the ankle)
We found ourselves ankle-deep in water (= the water came up to our ankles).
My ankles have swollen.
The injury required surgery on his right ankle.
He will wear an electronic ankle bracelet, which allows police to track him.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a date that is an exact number of years after the date of an important or special event
examples: on the anniversary of his wife’s death
to celebrate your wedding anniversary
the theatre’s 25th anniversary celebrations
The company is celebrating its 100-year anniversary this year.
Public events will be held to commemorate the anniversary of the end of the Second World War.
They held celebrations to mark the anniversary of Mozart's death.
a yearlong celebration of the 25th anniversary of his company
The context was the occasion of the 450th anniversary of his birth.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell people something officially, especially about a decision, plans, etc.
examples: He officially announced his intention to resign at today's press conference.
They haven't formally announced their engagement yet.
A ring at the doorbell announced Jack's arrival.
We are pleased to announce that all five candidates were successful.
It was announced that new speed restrictions would be introduced.
The company announced its decision to the public in March.
The government yesterday announced to the media plans to create a million new jobs.
She was announced as the winner at last night's ceremony.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give information about something in a public place, especially through a loudspeaker
examples: Has our flight been announced yet?
The winners will be announced in reverse order.
‘Now boarding flight 897, destination Seattle,’ the loudspeaker announced.
They announced that the flight would be delayed.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to say something in a loud and/or serious way
examples: ‘I've given up smoking,’ she announced.
She announced that she'd given up smoking.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to tell somebody your name or somebody else’s name when you or they arrive at a place
examples: Would you announce the guests as they arrive? (= call out their names, for example at a formal party)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to introduce, or to give information about, a programme on the radio or televisionWord Origin
examples: late 15th cent.: from French annoncer, from Latin annuntiare, from ad- ‘to’ + nuntiare ‘declare, announce’ (from nuntius ‘messenger’).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a spoken or written statement that informs people about something
examples: to make an announcement
a formal/an official/a public announcement
The campaign will run public service announcements on radio stations around the country.
We welcome the recent announcement by the Government.
Announcements of births, marriages and deaths appear in some newspapers.
Today's announcement of a peace agreement came after weeks of discussion.
An announcement about her future is expected soon.
We saw an announcement in the national newspaper.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of publicly informing people about something
examples: Announcement of the verdict was accompanied by shouts and cheers.
He was speaking after the announcement of record results for the company.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make somebody slightly angry
examples: SYNONYM irritate
His constant joking was beginning to annoy her.
I’m sure she does it just to annoy me.
I only stay out late to annoy my parents.
It really annoys me when people forget to say thank you.
It annoys me to see him getting ahead of me.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody uncomfortable or unable to relax
examples: SYNONYM bother
He swatted a fly that was annoying him.
The wasps were beginning to annoy me.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: slightly angry
examples: SYNONYM irritated
He was beginning to get very annoyed with me about my carelessness.
I was a little annoyed about the whole thing.
I was a bit annoyed with him.
I was annoyed with myself for giving in so easily.
I bet she was annoyed at having to write it out again.
I was annoyed that they hadn't turned up.
He was annoyed to find himself going red.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: making somebody feel slightly angry
examples: SYNONYM irritating
This interruption is very annoying.
Her most annoying habit was eating with her mouth open.
It's incredibly annoying, but that's life.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening or done once every year
examples: an annual meeting/event/report/conference
The 12th annual Music Festival runs from Friday 25th to Monday 28th October.
Funding will be awarded on an annual basis.
She organized this year's annual Christmas dinner dance.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: relating to a period of one year
examples: an annual income/revenue/budget/fee/salary/turnover
an average annual growth rate of 8%
Our total annual costs have declined.
I have decided to take my annual leave to be with my wife and baby.
annual rainfall

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: once a year
examples: The exhibition is held annually.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: with a name that is not known or that is not made public
examples: an anonymous donor
The money was donated by a local businessman who wishes to remain anonymous.
the largely anonymous perpetrators of terrorist acts

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: written, given, made, etc. by somebody who does not want their name to be known or made public
examples: an anonymous letter

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: without any unusual or interesting features
examples: long stretches of dull and anonymous countryside
new housing estates with their anonymous tower blocks and large barren spaces

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one more; an extra thing or person
examples: COMPARE other
Would you like another drink?
‘Finished?’ ‘No, I've got another three questions to do.’
We've still got another (= a further) forty miles to go.
‘It's a bill.’ ‘Oh no, not another!’
I got another of those calls yesterday.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: different; a different person or thing
examples: Let's do it another time.
We can try that—but whether it'll work is another matter.
The room's too small. Let's see if they've got another one.
I don't like this room. I'm going to ask for another.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing of a very similar type
examples: She's going to be another Madonna (= as famous as her).
There'll never be another like him.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used when you are referring to various types of a thing, without saying exactly what you mean
examples: We've all got problems of one kind or another.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: first one person or thing, and then another, and then another, up to any number or amount
examples: The bills kept coming in, one after another.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that you say, write or do to react to a question or situation
examples: SEE ALSO rejoin2
I rang the bell, but there was no answer.
Can't you give me a definitive answer?
The short answer is no.
The simple answer is that we don't know.
a question and answer session
I can't easily give an answer to your question.
Have you had an answer to your letter?

As if in answer to our prayers, she offered to lend us £10 000.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that you write or say in reply to a question in a test, an exam, an exercise, etc.; the correct reply to a question in a test, etc.
examples: the correct/right answer
Write your answers on the sheet provided.
Do you know the answer (= the right one) to question 12?
The answers are at the back of the book.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a solution to a problem
examples: There is no easy answer.
The answer is simple.
This could be the answer to all our problems.

This may not be the answer for everyone.
She has spent her life looking for answers.
The obvious answer would be to cancel the party.
The answer lies in a combination of factors.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person or thing from one place that may be thought to be as good as a famous person or thing from another place
examples: The new theme park will be Britain's answer to Disneyland.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be confident that you know something, especially when you actually do not
examples: He thinks he knows all the answers.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: You're coming and I won't take no for an answer!

definitions.definition: to expect something
examples: COMPARE unanticipated

Our anticipated arrival time is 8.30.
The eagerly anticipated movie will be released next month.
They anticipate moving to bigger premises by the end of the year.
I don't anticipate it being a problem.
We anticipate that sales will rise next year.
It is anticipated that inflation will stabilize at 3 per cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to see what might happen in the future and take action to prepare for it
examples: We need someone who can anticipate and respond to changes in the fashion industry.
Try and anticipate what the interviewers will ask.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to think with pleasure and excitement about something that is going to happen
examples: We eagerly anticipated the day we would leave school.

definitions.definition: to do something before it can be done by somebody else
examples: SYNONYM forestall

definitions.definition: the state of feeling nervous or worried that something bad is going to happen
examples: SEE ALSO separation anxiety
acute/intense/deep anxiety

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a mental health problem that causes somebody to worry so much that it has a very negative effect on their daily life
examples: Some people are feeling the pressure and suffering from anxiety and depression.
patients suffering from an anxiety disorder

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a worry or fear about something
examples: If you're worried about your health, share your anxieties with your doctor.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a strong feeling of wanting to do something or of wanting something to happen
examples: the candidate’s anxiety to win the vote

the people’s anxiety for the war to end

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling worried or nervous
examples: The bus was late and Sue began to get anxious.
I felt very anxious and depressed about the future.
He seemed anxious about the meeting.
Parents are naturally anxious for their children.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: causing worry; showing worry
examples: The family faces another anxious wait for news.
There were a few anxious moments in the baseball game.
an anxious look/face/expression

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: wanting something very much
examples: She was anxious to finish school and get a job.
He was anxious not to be misunderstood.
There are plenty of graduates anxious for work.
I'm anxious for her to do as little as possible.
She was anxious that he should meet her father.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used with uncountable or plural nouns in negative sentences and questions, after if or whether, and after some verbs such as prevent, ban, forbid, etc. to refer to an amount or a number of something, however large or small
examples: I didn't eat any meat.
Are there any stamps?
I've got hardly any money.
You can't go out without any shoes.
He forbids any talking in class.
She asked if we had any questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used with singular countable nouns to refer to one of a number of things or people, when it does not matter which one
examples: SEE ALSO in any case
Take any book you like.
Any colour will do.
Any teacher will tell you that students learn at different rates.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: It isn't just any day—it's my birthday!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used when adding something to support an idea or argument
examples: It's too expensive and anyway the colour doesn't suit you.
We're not perfect, but it doesn't really matter anyway.
It's too late now, anyway.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: despite something; even so
examples: It's going to happen anyway, so we won't object to it.
I'm afraid we can't come, but thanks for the invitation anyway.
She told them what would happen and they went ahead anyway.
Development money often goes to companies that would have come here anyway.
The water was cold but I took a shower anyway.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used when changing the subject of a conversation, ending the conversation or returning to a subject
examples: So, anyway, back to what I was saying.
Anyway, I'd better go now—I'll see you tomorrow.
Anyway, let's forget about that for the moment.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to correct or slightly change what you have said
examples: I think she's right. I hope so, anyway.
She works in a bank. She did when I last saw her, anyway.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used in negative sentences and in questions instead of somewhere
examples: I can't see it anywhere.
Did you go anywhere interesting?
Many of these animals are not found anywhere else.
He's never been anywhere outside Britain.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in, at or to any place, when it does not matter where
examples: Put the box down anywhere.
An accident can happen anywhere.
I could go anywhere in the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to indicate a range
examples: They cost anywhere from £100 to £500.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: far from; not at all
examples: The job doesn't pay anywhere near enough for me.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: far from; not at all
examples: The job doesn't pay anywhere near enough for me.
Older cars are nowhere near as fuel-efficient as modern cars.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: separated by a distance, of space or time
examples: The two houses stood 500 metres apart.
Their birthdays are only three days apart.
The two sides in the talks are still a long way apart (= are far from reaching an agreement).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not together; separate or separately
examples: We're living apart now.
Over the years, Rosie and I had drifted apart.
She keeps herself apart from other people.
I can't tell the twins apart (= see the difference between them).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: into pieces
examples: The whole thing just came apart in my hands.
When his wife died, his world fell apart.
Within minutes the ship began to break apart.
We had to take the engine apart.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody/something is not included in what you are talking about
examples: Victoria apart, not one of them seems suitable for the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be widely separated; to have no interests that you share
examples: Her own friends were poles apart from his.
In temperament, she and her sister are poles apart.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be completely different in attitudes, opinions, etc.
examples: Although they are twins, they are worlds apart in their attitude to life.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show that you are now being serious after you have said something funny

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to destroy something; to criticize somebody very strongly
examples: countries ripped apart by fighting
The dog had ripped a cushion to shreds.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a building
examples: COMPARE condominium
an apartment building
I was renting a two-bedroom apartment in an old building.
A group of developers wants to build a high-rise apartment complex.
I lived on the ground floor of an apartment block.
They left their fourth-floor apartment on Mott Street and walked to the bus.
a one-room apartment
I moved into a lovely little studio apartment.
He was evicted from his Manhattan apartment.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set of rooms used for a holiday
examples: self-catering holiday apartments
They are staying in a luxury apartment overlooking the beach.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a room in a house, especially a large or famous house
examples: You can visit the whole palace except for the private apartments.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say that you are sorry for doing something wrong or causing a problem
examples: Why should I apologize?
Go and apologize to her.
He wanted to publicly apologize to his victims.
I want to apologize publicly on his behalf to those who have suffered.
He apologized profusely to his family and staff.
I sincerely apologize for the enormous delay in delivery.
We apologize for the late departure of this flight.
I think Mr Peters should withdraw and apologize for his remark.
I apologize unreservedly for any offending remarks I made.
We apologize to our customers for the inconvenience caused.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a word or statement saying sorry for something that has been done wrong or that causes a problem
examples: to offer/make/demand/accept an apology
You owe him an apology for what you said.
We should like to offer our apologies for the delay to your flight today.
We received a letter of apology.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: information that you cannot go to a meeting or must leave early
examples: The meeting started with apologies (= the names of people who said they could not go to the meeting).
She made her apologies and left early.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if you say that you make no apology/apologies for something, you mean that you do not feel that you have said or done anything wrongWord Origin
examples: mid 16th cent. (denoting a formal defence against an accusation): from French apologie, or via late Latin from Greek apologia ‘a speech in one's own defence’, from apo ‘away’+ -logia (see -ology).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of software that you can download to a device such as a smartphone or tablet, for example to look up information or to play a game
examples: SEE ALSO in-app
You first need to install the app on your device.
to download/launch an app
to build/develop an app
Have you got the dictionary app on your phone?
Gaming today is all about mobile app downloads.
app developers
The app is available on/in the app store.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a program designed to do a particular job; a piece of software
examples: SEE ALSO killer app
a database app

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the tools or other pieces of equipment that are needed for a particular activity or task
examples: a piece of laboratory apparatus
Firefighters needed breathing apparatus to enter the burning house.
Science departments say they are lacking basic apparatus.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the structure of a system or an organization, particularly that of a political party or a government
examples: the power of the state apparatus
We cannot do without the apparatus of government in protecting the rights of the individual.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a system of organs in the body
examples: the sensory apparatus

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: easy to see or understand
examples: SYNONYM obvious
Their devotion was apparent.
Then, for no apparent reason, the train suddenly stopped.
It was apparent from her face that she was really upset.
It soon became apparent to everyone that he couldn't sing.
It's readily apparent that she has a gift for this kind of writing.
No damage was apparent from a brain scan.
The consequences of our actions are not immediately apparent to us.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that seems to be real or true but may not be
examples: SYNONYM seeming
My parents were concerned at my apparent lack of enthusiasm for school.
Their affluence is more apparent than real (= they are not as rich as they seem to be).
There is an apparent contradiction between these two approaches.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: according to what you have heard or read; according to the way something appears
examples: Apparently they are getting divorced soon.
I thought she had retired, but apparently she hasn't.
He paused, apparently lost in thought.
The government was apparently unaware of the magnitude of the crisis.
The security forces were apparently taken by surprise.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a deeply felt request for money, help or information that is needed immediately, especially one made by a charity or by the police
examples: to launch a TV appeal for donations to the charity
He made an emotional appeal to voters.
Police are making a fresh appeal to the public for any information that may help them.
The police made an appeal to the public to remain calm.
There was a look of silent appeal on his face.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a quality that makes somebody/something attractive or interesting
examples: SEE ALSO sex appeal
mass/wide/popular/broad/universal appeal
The Beatles have never really lost their appeal.
The prospect of living in a city holds little appeal for me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a formal request to a court or to somebody in authority for a judgement or a decision to be changed
examples: SEE ALSO court of appeal
to lodge an appeal
to file an appeal
an appeal court/judge
an appeals court/judge
They have launched appeals against their convictions.
an appeal against the 3-match ban
an appeal against a decision/sentence/order/ruling
The court dismissed his appeal against the refusal of his asylum claim.
The case was upheld on appeal.
The verdict was later overturned on appeal.
You have the right of appeal to the Constitutional Court.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an indirect suggestion that any good, fair or reasonable person would act in a particular way
examples: I relied on an appeal to his finer feelings.
an appeal to reason

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: attractive or interesting
examples: OPPOSITE unappealing
Spending the holidays in Britain wasn't a prospect that I found particularly appealing.
Brightly coloured packaging made the pens especially appealing to children.
The large salary made their offer even more appealing to him.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: showing that you want people to help you or to show you sympathy
examples: ‘Would you really help?’ he said with an appealing look.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to start to be seen
examples: Three days later a rash appeared.
Symptoms usually start appearing within two to three days.
A cat suddenly appeared out of nowhere.
Smoke appeared on the horizon.
A bus appeared around the corner.
Posters for the gig appeared all over town.
New shoots are just appearing at the base of the plant.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to begin to exist or be known or used for the first time
examples: Scientists are unsure when the virus first appeared.
His work began to appear on the scene in the 1960s.
When did mammals appear on the earth?
This problem first appeared in the inner cities.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to give the impression of being or doing something
examples: SYNONYM seem
She didn't appear at all surprised at the news.
Everything appeared normal at first.
It now appears likely that the school will be closed down.
It appears unlikely that interest rates will fall further.
He appears a perfectly normal person.
The couple appeared to have nothing in common.
The video appears to show a car driving through the wall of a house.
She appeared to be in her late thirties.
They appeared not to know what was happening.
There appears to have been a mistake.
It appears that there has been a mistake.
It would appear that this was a major problem.
The sunset made it appear as if the sea was made of gold.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be published or broadcast
examples: His new book will be appearing in the spring.
It was too late to prevent the story from appearing in the national newspapers.
These allegations appear in a forthcoming documentary.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to take part in a film, play, television programme, etc.
examples: He has appeared in over 60 movies.
She regularly appears on TV.
She is currently appearing as Juliet at the Liverpool Playhouse.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to arrive at a place
examples: By ten o'clock Lee still hadn't appeared.
A man appeared at the door and asked to see her.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be written or mentioned somewhere
examples: Your name will appear at the front of the book.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be present in court in order to give evidence or answer a charge
examples: A man will appear in court today charged with the murder.
She is expected to appear at Dumfries Sheriff Court on Monday.
She appeared on six charges of theft.
They will appear before magistrates tomorrow.
He has been asked to appear as a witness for the defence.
They had all appeared before the court several times.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to act as somebody’s lawyer in court
examples: COMPARE disappear
James Gilbert is the lawyer appearing for the defendant.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the way that somebody/something looks on the outside; what somebody/something seems to be
examples: the physical/outward/external appearance of something
She had never been greatly concerned about her appearance.
The dog was similar in general appearance to a spaniel.
He gave every appearance of (= seemed very much to be) enjoying himself.
Judging by appearances can be misleading.
To all appearances (= as far as people could tell) he was dead.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of somebody/something arriving, especially when it is not expected
examples: The sudden appearance of a security guard caused them to drop the money and run.
I don't want to go to the party, but I suppose I'd better put in an appearance (= go there for a short time).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the moment at which something begins to exist or starts to be seen or used
examples: the early appearance of daffodils in spring
the appearance of organic vegetables in the supermarkets

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an act of appearing in public, especially as a performer, politician, etc., or in court
examples: The Dutch player will make his first appearance for Liverpool this Saturday.
The show featured a guest appearance from Amy Schumer.
The singer's first public appearance was at the age of eight.
She made a cameo appearance in the film.
the defendant’s appearance in court
a court appearance
his appearance before the committee/inquiry

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an act of being published or broadcast
examples: the appearance of claims about the minister’s private life in the press

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to hide the truth about a bad situation and pretend that everything is going well
examples: When she lost all her money she was determined to keep up appearances.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: physical desire for food
examples: He suffered from headaches and loss of appetite.
The walk gave me a good appetite.
Don't spoil your appetite by eating between meals.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a strong desire for something
examples: sexual appetites
The preview was intended to whet your appetite (= make you want more).
The public have an insatiable appetite for scandal.
There is no appetite for (= people do not want) massive federal investment in the US.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to show your approval of somebody/something by clapping your hands (= hitting your open hands together several times)
examples: SYNONYM clap
He started to applaud and the others joined in.
They rose to applaud the speaker.
She was applauded as she came on stage.
The audience applauded loudly.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to express praise for somebody/something because you approve of them or it
examples: We applaud her decision.
His efforts to improve the situation are to be applauded.
The decision to save the company has been warmly applauded.
I applaud her for having the courage to refuse.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a round fruit with shiny red or green skin that is fairly hard and white inside
examples: SEE ALSO Adam’s apple
Peel and core the apples.
an apple pie
apple sauce/juice
a garden with three apple trees
I took a bite of the apple.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a child usually behaves in a similar way to his or her parent(s)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is loved more than any other
examples: She is the apple of her father's eye.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to describe a situation in which two people or things are completely different from each other
examples: They really are apples and oranges.
They are both great but you can't compare apples and oranges.
It’s a totally different situation, it’s apples and oranges.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that something is typical of America

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: one bad person who has a bad effect on others in a groupWord Origin
examples: Old English æppel, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch appel and German Apfel.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that can be said to be true in the case of somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM relevant
Give details of children where applicable (= if you have any).
Much of the form was not applicable (= did not apply) to me.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who makes a formal request for something (= applies for it), especially for a job, a place at a college or university, etc.
examples: There were over 500 applicants for the job.
Successful applicants will receive notification within the week.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a formal (often written) request for something, such as a job, permission to do something or a place at a college or university
examples: a planning/patent/visa application
We have received applications from more than 3 000 students.
You need to complete the online application form.
an application for asylum/a licence
an application for leave to appeal against the conviction
After graduating she made an application to join the BBC.
His application to the court for bail has been refused.
They submitted an application to the council to build two houses.
Further information is available on application to the principal.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the practical use of something, especially a theory, discovery, etc.
examples: The invention would have a wide range of applications in industry.
What are the practical applications of this work?
the application of new technology to teaching

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an act of putting or spreading something, such as paint or medical creams, onto something else
examples: It took three applications of paint to cover the graffiti.
lotion for external application only (= to be put on the skin, not swallowed)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of making a rule, etc. operate or become effective
examples: strict application of the law

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a program designed to do a particular job; a piece of software
examples: SEE ALSO killer app
a database application

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the strength of mind to work hard at something; great effort
examples: Success as a writer demands great application.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a loan, permission for something, a place at a university, etc.
examples: You should apply in person/by letter.
I have decided to apply for this new job.
They have successfully applied for political asylum.
to apply for a visa/passport/grant/licence
The developers applied for planning permission to build over 200 houses.
to apply to a company/university
They may apply to the court for the decision to be reversed.
He has applied to join the army.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to affect or be relevant to somebody/something
examples: Special conditions apply if you are under 18.
The rules applied to employees and their behaviour at work.
What I am saying applies only to some of you.
The policy will apply equally to everyone.
The law applied only to foreign nationals.
The word ‘unexciting’ could never be applied to her novels.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to use something or make something work in a particular situation
examples: to apply political pressure
The challenge allows students to apply economic principles they learn in class.
to apply economic sanctions
to apply a test/method/technique/approach/rule
Each citizen needs to apply the same standards to himself as to others.
The new technology was applied to farming.
Now is the time to apply the insights you have gained from your studies.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to put or spread something such as paint, cream, etc. onto a surface
examples: Apply the cream sparingly to your face and neck.
The glue should be applied to both surfaces.
She combed her hair and carefully applied her make-up.
The paint was applied with a fine brush.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to work at something or study something very hard
examples: You would pass your exams if you applied yourself.
We applied our minds to finding a solution to our problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to press on something hard with your hand, foot, etc. to make something work or have an effect on something
examples: to apply the brakes (of a vehicle)
Pressure applied to the wound will stop the bleeding.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to choose somebody for a job or position of responsibility
examples: They have appointed a new head teacher at my son's school.
She has recently been appointed to the committee.
They appointed him (as) captain of the English team.
She's been appointed British ambassador to the UN.
A lawyer was appointed to represent the child.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to arrange or decide on a time or place for doing something
examples: A date for the meeting is still to be appointed.
Everyone was assembled at the appointed time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a formal arrangement to meet or visit somebody at a particular time, especially for a reason connected with their work
examples: I've got a dental appointment at 3 o'clock.
to book/make/keep an appointment
Do you have an appointment?
She has a doctor's appointment in twenty minutes.
Viewing is by appointment only (= only at a time that has been arranged in advance).
an appointment book
an appointment with my agent/doctor/specialist/consultant
an appointment for a blood test
She made an appointment for her son to see the doctor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of choosing a person for a job or position of responsibility; the fact of being chosen for a job, etc.
examples: They announced the appointments of key security officials.
the appointment of a new captain for the England team
her recent appointment to the post
his appointment as principal
appointments and dismissals

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a job or position of responsibility
examples: a permanent/first appointment
The department wished him success in his new appointment as sales manager.
I would like to congratulate you on your appointment.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person chosen for a job or position of responsibility
examples: Government ministers and other political appointments are frequently replaced.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to recognize the good qualities of somebody/something
examples: Over the years he came to appreciate the beauty and tranquillity of the river.
His talents are not fully appreciated in that company.
Her family doesn't appreciate her.
You can't really appreciate foreign literature in translation.
The sound quality was poor so we couldn't fully appreciate the music.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be grateful for something that somebody has done; to welcome something
examples: I'd appreciate some help.
Your support is greatly appreciated.
Thanks for coming. I appreciate it.
I would appreciate any comments you might have.
Your kindness and generosity is much appreciated.
We really appreciate the extra effort you're making.
I would appreciate it if you paid in cash.
I appreciate having the opportunity to discuss these important issues with you.
I don't appreciate being treated like a second-class citizen.
We would appreciate you letting us know of any problems.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to understand that something is true
examples: SYNONYM realize
What I failed to appreciate was the distance between the two cities.
The experience helped me understand and appreciate some of the difficulties people face.
I don't think you appreciate how expensive it will be.
We didn't fully appreciate that he was seriously ill.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to increase in value over a period of time
examples: Their investments have appreciated over the years.
We wanted a property that would appreciate in value.
The euro continues to appreciate against the dollar.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: pleasure that you have when you recognize and enjoy the good qualities of somebody/something
examples: She shows little appreciation of good music.
The crowd murmured in appreciation.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a full understanding of something, such as a situation or a problem, and of what it involves
examples: I had no appreciation of the problems they faced.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the feeling of being grateful for something
examples: I would like to express my appreciation and thanks to you all.
Please accept this gift in appreciation of all you've done for us.
She never shows any appreciation for our efforts.
The clock was presented to Snell by his colleagues as an appreciation of his work and friendship.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: increase in value over a period of time
examples: OPPOSITE depreciation
an appreciation in the value of the house
capital appreciation

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a piece of writing or a speech in which the strengths and weaknesses of somebody/something, especially an artist or a work of art, are discussed and judged
examples: They were asked to write an appreciation of a poem of their choice.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a way of dealing with somebody/something; a way of doing or thinking about something such as a problem or a task
examples: She took the wrong approach in her dealings with them.
It was time to take a different approach.
an alternative/innovative approach
a traditional/similar approach
The approach they were using no longer seemed to work.
We need to adopt a new approach to the problem.
The therapy takes a holistic approach to health and well-being.
a variety of approaches for the treatment of depression
Will this be a successful approach for providing high-tech offices?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: movement nearer to somebody/something in distance or time
examples: She hadn't heard his approach and jumped as the door opened.
the approach of spring
They felt apprehensive about the approach of war.
The children fell silent at the approach of their teacher.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of speaking to somebody about something, especially when making an offer or a request
examples: The club has made an approach to a local company for sponsorship.
We've received an approach from the director of a rival company.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: attempts to start a personal or sexual relationship with somebody
examples: She resented his persistent approaches.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a path, road, etc. that leads to a place
examples: All the approaches to the palace were guarded by troops.
a new approach road to the port
The approach to the village was very pretty.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the part of an aircraft’s flight immediately before landing
examples: to begin the final approach to the runway
The aircraft had to make a steep approach to the landing strip.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a thing that is like something else that is mentioned
examples: That's the nearest approach to an apology you'll get from him.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if you use the carrot and stick approach, you persuade somebody to try harder by offering them a reward if they do, or a punishment if they do not
examples: The emphasis is on the carrot of incentive rather than the stick of taxes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a way of dealing with somebody/something; a way of doing or thinking about something such as a problem or a task
examples: She took the wrong approach in her dealings with them.
It was time to take a different approach.
an alternative/innovative approach
a traditional/similar approach
The approach they were using no longer seemed to work.
We need to adopt a new approach to the problem.
The therapy takes a holistic approach to health and well-being.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if the police arrest somebody, the person is taken to a police station and kept there because the police believe they may be guilty of a crime
examples: A man has been arrested in connection with the robbery.
A local man has since been arrested on suspicion of murder.
Police arrested three suspects.
He was arrested on corruption charges.
She was arrested and charged with arson.
She was arrested for drug-related offences.
You could get arrested for doing that.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop a process or a development
examples: They failed to arrest the company's decline.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody notice something and pay attention to it
examples: An unusual noise arrested his attention.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if somebody arrests, their heart stops beating
examples: He arrested on the way to the hospital.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act of coming or being brought to a place
examples: OPPOSITE departure (1)
We apologize for the late arrival of the train.
the arrival of the mail in the morning
Our estimated time of arrival is 7.15.
I need to check our arrival time.
Guests receive dinner on arrival at the hotel
She was declared dead on arrival at the hospital.
There are 120 arrivals and departures every day.
daily arrivals of refugees
They are eagerly awaiting the arrival of their new computer.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the part of an airport that you go through when you arrive on a plane
examples: COMPARE departures
I made my way through arrivals.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that comes to a place
examples: The first arrivals at the concert got the best seats.
early/late/new arrivals
We're expecting a new arrival (= a baby) in the family soon.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the time when a new technology or idea is introduced
examples: the arrival of pay TV

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: (of an accident victim or other patient) already dead when arriving at a hospital
examples: She was pronounced dead on arrival.
He didn’t even make it to hospital: DOA.
Many of the casualties were dead on arrival.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: very unlikely to be successful; not working when it is delivered
examples: The bill was dead on arrival in the Senate.
The software was DOA.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to get to a place, especially at the end of a journey
examples: I'll wait until they arrive.
I was pleased to hear you arrived home safely.
to arrive early/late for a meeting
She'll arrive in New York at noon.
The train arrived at the station 20 minutes late.
We didn't arrive back at the hotel until very late.
By the time I arrived on the scene, it was all over.
Pupils may be newly arrived in Britain, with little or no English.
A police officer arrived just in time to see the burglars walking out of the building.
They arrived too late to take any action.
The police arrived to arrest him.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be brought to somebody
examples: A letter arrived for you this morning.
Send your application to arrive by 31 October.
We waited an hour for our lunch to arrive.
The new product will arrive on supermarket shelves (= be available) early next year.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to happen or to come, especially when you have been waiting for it
examples: The wedding day finally arrived.
The baby arrived (= was born) early.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: somebody has become successful
examples: He knew he had arrived when he was shortlisted for the Man Booker prize.
The lad has arrived as a Premiership goalkeeper.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thin stick with a sharp point at one end, which is shot from a bow
examples: a bow and arrow
to fire/shoot an arrow
The road continues as straight as an arrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a mark or sign like an arrow (➞), used to show direction or position
examples: Follow the arrows.
Use the arrow keys to move the cursor.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the use of the imagination to express ideas or feelings, particularly in painting, drawing or sculpture
examples: SEE ALSO clip art
modern/contemporary art
an art critic/historian/lover
Can we call television art?
stolen works of art
Her performance displayed great art.
American art
It's a very beautiful piece of art.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: examples of objects such as paintings, drawings or sculptures
examples: an art gallery/exhibition
a collection of art and antiques

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the skill of creating objects such as paintings and drawings, especially when you study it
examples: She's good at art and design.
He has a master's degree in fine art.
an art teacher/student/college/class

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: art, music, theatre, literature, etc. when you think of them as a group
examples: SEE ALSO performing arts
lottery funding for the arts
What is the relationship between the visual arts and music?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a type of visual or performing art
examples: an exhibition of Peruvian arts and crafts
Dance is a very theatrical art.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the subjects you can study at school or university that are not sciences, such as languages, history or literature
examples: COMPARE science
an arts degree

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an ability or a skill that you can develop with training and practice
examples: a therapist trained in the art of healing
I've never mastered the art of making bread.
Letter-writing is a lost art nowadays.
Appearing confident at interviews is quite an art (= rather difficult).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to learn to do something well and efficiently
examples: I spend so much time travelling that I've got packing down to a fine art.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of writing about a particular subject in a newspaper or magazine, on a website, etc.
examples: to read/write/publish an article
Her tweet follows an article posted online by the ‘Huffington Post’.
I read an interesting article by a well-known scientist on the subject of genetics.
Have you seen that article about young fashion designers?
According to a recent newspaper article, the company is worth over $20 billion.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a separate item in an agreement or a contract
examples: Article 10 of the European Convention guarantees free speech.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a particular item or separate thing, especially one of a set
examples: SYNONYM item
articles of clothing
toilet articles such as soap and shampoo
The articles found in the car helped the police to identify the body.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the words a and an (the indefinite article) or the (the definite article)
examples: Names of countries in English do not usually take an article.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to express or explain your thoughts or feelings clearly in words
examples: She struggled to articulate her thoughts.
It is the school’s duty to articulate its practices to parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to speak, pronounce or play something in a clear way
examples: He was too drunk to articulate properly.
Every note was carefully articulated.
She spoke slowly, articulating each word clearly.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be related to something so that together the two parts form a whole
examples: These courses are designed to articulate with university degrees.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be joined to something else by a joint, so that movement is possible; to join something in this way
examples: bones that articulate with others
a robot with articulated limbs

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: made or produced to copy something natural; not real
examples: an artificial limb/flower/sweetener/fertilizer
artificial lighting/light

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: created by people; not happening naturally
examples: A job interview is a very artificial situation.
the artificial barriers of race, class and gender

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not what it appears to be
examples: SYNONYM fake
artificial emotion

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who creates works of art, especially paintings or drawings
examples: an exhibition of work by contemporary British artists
a graphic artist
a make-up artist
He became a full-time artist in 1929.
In Paris she met a group of young artists: poets, film-makers and painters.
This is an artist's impression of the new stadium.
Whoever made this cake is a real artist.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is a professional singer, dancer, actor, etc.
examples: a recording/solo artist
Among the artistes appearing on our show tonight we have…
He was a true artiste: sensitive, dramatic and tragic.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with art or artists
examples: the artistic works of the period
a work of great artistic merit
an artistic temperament (= behaviour thought to be typical of artists, musicians, etc.)
Love is a time-honoured subject of literary and artistic expression.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: showing a natural skill or pleasure in art, especially being able to paint or draw well
examples: artistic abilities/achievements/skills/talent
She comes from a very artistic family.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: done with skill and imagination; attractive or beautiful
examples: an artistic arrangement of dried flowers
The decor inside the house was very artistic.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the freedom of artists or writers to change facts in order to make a story, painting, etc. more interesting or beautiful

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: pictures and photographs prepared for books, magazines, etc.
examples: Can you let me have the finished artwork for the poster by Friday?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a work of art, especially one in a museum; works of art as a group
examples: 30 original artworks have gone missing from the museum.
a collection of artwork from tribal cultures

definitions.definition: used to describe somebody/something appearing to be somebody/something else
examples: They were all dressed as clowns.
