definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the grey or black powder that is left after something, especially tobacco, wood or coal, has burnt
examples: cigarette ash
black volcanic ash
Ash from the volcano fell over a wide area.
She flicked ash out of the window carelessly.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: what is left after something has been destroyed by burning
examples: The town was reduced to ashes in the fighting.
the glowing ashes of the campfire
The fire had died to cold ashes.
The party had risen, like a phoenix, from the ashes of electoral disaster.
She had seen all her dreams turn to ashes.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the powder that is left after a dead person’s body has been cremated (= burned)
examples: She wanted her ashes to be scattered at sea.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a forest tree with grey bark

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the hard pale wood of the ash tree

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the letter æ, used in Old English, and as a phonetic symbol to represent the vowel sound in cat

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that shows that you are sorry for something that you have doneWord Origin
examples: senses 1 to 3 Old English æsce, aexe, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch as and German Asche.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling shame or feeling embarrassed about somebody/something or because of something you have done
examples: She was deeply ashamed of her behaviour at the party.
Mental illness is nothing to be ashamed of.
We must stop being afraid or ashamed of what we are.
His daughter looked such a mess that he was ashamed of her.
You should be ashamed of yourself for telling such lies.
You ought to be thoroughly ashamed of yourselves.
I feel almost ashamed that I've been so lucky.
The football riots made me ashamed to be English.
You act as if you’re ashamed to be seen with me.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: unwilling to do something because of shame or fear of feeling embarrassed
examples: I'm ashamed to say that I lied to her.
I cried at the end and I'm not ashamed to admit it.
He felt ashamed to let her see him in this state.
You act as if you're ashamed to be seen with me.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to one side; out of the way
examples: She pulled the curtain aside.
Stand aside and let these people pass.
He took me aside (= away from a group of people) to give me some advice.
Leaving aside (= not considering at this stage) the cost of the scheme, let us examine its benefits.
All our protests were brushed aside (= ignored).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be used later
examples: We set aside some money for repairs.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used after nouns to say that except for one thing, something is true
examples: Money worries aside, things are going well.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say or write something in the form of a question, in order to get information
examples: How old are you—if you don’t mind me/my asking?
He asked about her family.
Can I ask a question?
Did you ask the price?
You do what I tell you to, no questions asked.
There are three important questions to ask.
frequently asked questions
‘Where are you going?’ she asked.
‘Are you sure?’ he asked her.
She asked the students their names.
I often get asked that!
I had to ask myself some very difficult questions.
I'd like to ask you a few questions.
Why does everyone keep asking me that?
The interviewer asked me about my future plans.
When specifically asked about the report, she indicated she had not read it.
He asked where I lived.
I had to ask the teacher what to do next.
I was asked if/whether I could drive.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to tell somebody that you would like them to do something or that you would like something to happen
examples: Anyone with information is asked to contact the police.
Parents with young children are asked to attend this meeting.
They were politely asked to leave the shop.
Eric asked me to marry him.
All the students were asked to complete a questionnaire.
I asked whether they could change my ticket.
She asked me if I would give her English lessons.
She asked that she be kept informed of developments.
She asked that she should be kept informed.
If you ask her nicely, she'll give you a hand.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to say that you would like somebody to give you something
examples: Don't be afraid to ask for help.
I am writing to ask for some information about courses.
to ask for a job/a drink/an explanation
Did your friend ask for permission to use the image?
Why don't you ask his advice?
Why don't you ask him for his advice?
Can I ask a favour of you?
Can I ask you a favour?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to request permission to do something
examples: I immediately asked to speak to a supervisor.
I asked to see the manager.
Did you ask to use the car?
I'll ask if it's all right to park here.
She asked her boss whether she could have the day off.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to invite somebody
examples: They've asked me to dinner.
Thank you so much for asking me.
I didn't ask them in (= to come into the house).
We must ask the neighbours round (= to our house).
She's asked him to come to the party.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to request a particular amount of money for something that you are selling
examples: He's asking £2 000 for the car.
How much were they asking for their house?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to expect or demand something
examples: I know I'm asking a great deal.
You're asking too much of him.
I know it's asking a lot to expect them to win again.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to deserve something bad that happens to you or that somebody does to you
examples: ‘You shouldn’t have said that to her.’ ‘Well, she asked for it!’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that is very likely to result in trouble
examples: He was asking for trouble when he insulted their country.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: if you say don’t ask to somebody, you mean that you do not want to reply to their question, because it would be difficult to explain, embarrassing, etc.
examples: ‘And what did he do then?’ ‘Don’t ask!’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: if you say don’t ask me, you mean that you do not know the answer to a question and are annoyed you have been asked
examples: ‘What will the meeting be about?’ ‘Don’t ask me.’

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if you can have something for the asking, it is very easy for you to get it if you ask for it
examples: The job is yours for the asking.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if you say I ask you, you are expressing shock, anger or a strong feeling of dislike about something/somebody
examples: He told me I had to work late on Friday night. I ask you!

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: in my personal opinion
examples: Their marriage was a mistake, if you ask me.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: sleeping
examples: OPPOSITE awake
I waited until they were all fast asleep (= sleeping deeply).
The baby was sound asleep (= sleeping deeply) upstairs.
He was so exhausted that he fell asleep at his desk.
My mother fell asleep at the wheel (= while driving) and crashed into a tree.
She was still half asleep (= not fully awake) when she arrived at work.
The police found him asleep in a garage.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not paying enough attention to what you need to do
examples: They were asleep on the job as the financial crisis deepened.
Let's hope the regulators are not asleep at the wheel.
Someone must have been asleep at the switch to alow this to happen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a particular part or feature of a situation, an idea, a problem, etc.; a way in which it may be considered
examples: The book aims to cover all aspects of city life.
The exhibition will focus on various aspects of life and culture in the Middle East.
the most important aspect of the debate
She felt she had looked at the problem from every aspect.
This was one aspect of her character he hadn't seen before.
We have worked very hard on certain aspects of our game.
The consultancy gives advice to manufacturers on the health and safety aspects of their products.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the appearance of a place, a situation or a person
examples: Events began to take on a more sinister aspect.
the dirty and seedy aspect of the bar

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the direction in which a building, window, piece of land, etc. faces; the side of a building that faces a particular direction
examples: SYNONYM orientation
Our room had a western aspect.
The southern aspect of the school was dominated by the mountain.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the form of a verb that shows, for example, whether the action happens once or repeatedly, is completed or still continuing
examples: SEE ALSO perfect (7)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong desire to have or do something
examples: I didn't realize you had political aspirations.
He has never had any aspiration to earn a lot of money.
What changes are needed to meet women's aspirations for employment?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the action of pronouncing a word with a breath that can be heard, as in the /h/ sound in house in EnglishWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (in sense (2)): from Latin aspiratio(n-), from the verb aspirare, from ad- ‘to’ + spirare ‘breathe’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have a strong desire to achieve or to become something
examples: She aspired to a scientific career.
He aspired to be their next leader.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the murder of an important or famous person, especially for political reasons
examples: The president survived a number of assassination attempts.
the assassination of John F. Kennedy

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the crime of attacking somebody physically
examples: SEE ALSO indecent assault
Both men were charged with assault.
sexual assaults
A significant number of indecent assaults on women go unreported.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of attacking a building, an area, etc. in order to take control of it
examples: SYNONYM attack
An assault on the capital was launched in the early hours of the morning.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of trying to achieve something that is difficult or dangerous
examples: The government has mounted a new assault on unemployment.
a two-year legal assault on alleged tax fraud
Three people died during an assault on the mountain (= while trying to climb it).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an act of criticizing somebody/something severely
examples: SYNONYM attack
The suggested closures came under assault from all parties.
The paper's assault on the president was totally unjustified.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an act that threatens to harm somebody physically, whether or not actual harm is doneWord Origin

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to come together as a group; to bring people or things together as a group
examples: All the students were asked to assemble in the main hall.
She then addressed the assembled company (= all the people there).
to assemble evidence/data
The manager has assembled a world-class team.
He tried to assemble his thoughts.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to fit together all the separate parts of something, for example a piece of furniture
examples: OPPOSITE disassemble
The shelves are easy to assemble.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of people who have been elected to meet together regularly and make decisions or laws for a particular region or country
examples: state/legislative/federal/local assemblies
Power has been handed over to provincial and regional assemblies.
The national assembly has voted to adopt the budget.
the California Assembly
the UN General Assembly
assembly elections
an elected assembly

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the meeting together of a group of people for a particular purpose; a group of people who meet together for a particular purpose
examples: They were fighting for freedom of speech and freedom of assembly.
He was to address a public assembly on the issue.
an assembly point (= a place where people have been asked to meet)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a meeting of the teachers and students in a school, usually at the start of the day, to give information, discuss school events or say prayers together
examples: The deputy head was taking (= leading) school assembly that day.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the process of putting together the parts of something such as a vehicle or piece of furniture
examples: Putting the bookcase together should be a simple assembly job.
a car assembly plant
the correct assembly of the parts

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to state clearly and definitely that something is true
examples: She continued to assert that she was innocent.
The report asserts confidently that the industry will grow.
She continued to assert her innocence.
The German Chancellor was anxious to assert her government's commitment to European unity.
‘That is wrong,’ he asserted.
It is commonly asserted that older people prefer to receive care from family members.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to behave in a confident and determined way so that other people pay attention to your opinions
examples: You’re too timid—you must try to assert yourself more.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make other people recognize your right or authority to do something, by behaving in a determined and confident way
examples: to assert your independence/rights
I was determined to assert my authority from the beginning.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to start to have an effect
examples: Good sense asserted itself.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a statement saying that you strongly believe something to be true
examples: He was correct in his assertion that the minister had been lying.
Do you have any evidence to support your assertions?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of stating, using or claiming something strongly
examples: the assertion of his authority
The demonstration was an assertion of the right to peaceful protest.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a judgement about the nature or quality of somebody/something
examples: Accurately assessing environmental impacts is very complex.
to assess a patient’s needs

She engaged a safety consultant to assess the risks.
Quality of life was assessed using a questionnaire.
The young men were assessed as either safe or unsafe drivers.
I'd assess your chances as low.
The committee assesses whether a building is worth preserving.
We are trying to assess how well the system works.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to calculate the amount or value of something
examples: They have assessed the amount of compensation to be paid.
Damage to the building was assessed at £40 000.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an opinion or a judgement about somebody/something that has been thought about very carefully
examples: SYNONYM evaluation
a detailed assessment of the risks involved
An adequate environmental impact assessment was not carried out on the bypass project.
We conducted the initial assessments defining the scope of work.
The city hired them to do a structural assessment of the damage.
his assessment of the situation

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of judging or forming an opinion about somebody/something
examples: Objective assessment of the severity of the problem was difficult.
Needs assessment is crucial if the hospital is to deliver effective healthcare.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of testing students and making a judgement about their knowledge, ability or progress
examples: SEE ALSO continuous assessment
written exams and other forms of assessment

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an amount that has been calculated and that must be paid
examples: a tax assessment

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is valuable or useful to somebody/something
examples: In his job, patience is an invaluable asset.
Being able to speak a foreign language is a major asset.
I’m not sure if his forcefulness is an asset or a liability.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: immediately; without delay
examples: I want it sent right away.
I told him right off what I thought of him.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: immediately; without delay
examples: SYNONYM at once
I'll do it straight away.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very bad or unpleasant
examples: That's an awful colour.
‘They didn't even offer to pay.’ ‘Oh that's awful.’
I feel awful about forgetting her birthday.
to look/feel awful (= to look/feel ill)
There's an awful smell in here.
The awful thing is, it was my fault.
It sounds awful to say it, but the war was exciting.
The weather conditions were just awful.
It's awful, isn't it?
The weather last summer was awful.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that shocks people very much
examples: SYNONYM terrible
the awful horrors of war
It was only later that we learned the awful truth.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something, especially that there is a large amount or too much of something
examples: It's going to cost an awful lot of money.
There's not an awful lot of room.
I feel an awful lot better than I did yesterday.
I had an awful job persuading him to come (= it was very difficult).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: making you feel embarrassed
examples: There was an awkward silence.
I felt awkward because they obviously wanted to be alone.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: difficult to deal with
examples: SYNONYM difficult
Don't ask awkward questions.
You've put me in an awkward position.
an awkward customer (= a person who is difficult to deal with)
Please don't be awkward about letting him come.
It makes things awkward for everyone when you behave like that.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not convenient
examples: SYNONYM inconvenient
Have I come at an awkward time?
That's a bit awkward for me—could we make it earlier?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: difficult or dangerous because of its shape or design
examples: This box is very awkward for one person to carry.
This tool will reach into awkward corners, such as under kitchen units.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not moving in an easy way; not comfortable
examples: He tried to dance, but he was too clumsy and awkward.
I must have slept in an awkward position—I'm aching all over.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a very young child or animal
examples: SEE ALSO fur baby
The baby's crying!
a newborn baby
My sister's expecting a baby (= she is pregnant).
She had a baby last year.
The baby was born last night.
Mother and baby are doing well.
The baby is due in October.
The baby was delivered by a midwife.
a baby boy/girl
a baby daughter/son/sister/brother
baby food/clothes
a baby monkey/blackbird

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the youngest member of a family or group
examples: He's the baby of the team.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who behaves like a young child and is easily upset
examples: Stop crying and don't be such a baby.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a word used to address somebody, especially your wife, husband or partner, in a way that expresses love but that can be offensive if used by a man to a woman he does not know

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be a plan or project that somebody is responsible for and cares about because they have created it

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how easy it is to do something
examples: I thought it was going to be difficult to get funding for the project, but in the end it was like taking candy from a baby.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to suddenly make somebody responsible for something important that is really your responsibility
examples: He changed to another job and we were left holding the baby.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to sleep very well
examples: He was so tired after all his exertions, he slept like a baby.
I usually sleep like a log.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to lose something that you want at the same time as you are trying to get rid of something that you do not wantWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: probably imitative of an infant's first attempts at speech.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the part of the human body that is on the opposite side to the chest, between the neck and the tops of the legs; the part of an animal’s body that corresponds to this
examples: SEE ALSO bareback
He was lying on his back on the sofa.
Do you sleep on your back or your front?
She was standing with her back to the camera so you can't see her face.
They had their hands tied behind their backs.
They set off with the wind at their backs (= behind them).
your lower/upper back
I have a nagging pain in my lower back.
Most of the victims were shot in the back.
a bad (= painful) back
I pulled (= injured the muscles in) my back playing squash.
She was laid up with severe back pain.
A small boy rode on the elephant's back.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the row of bones in the middle of the back
examples: SYNONYM backbone
She broke her back in a riding accident.
He spent six months recovering from a broken back.
He put his back out (= dislocated something in his back) lifting the crates.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the part or area of something that is furthest from the front
examples: SEE ALSO hardback
She was hit on the back of the head.
He kicked the ball straight into the back of the net.
The man was refusing to go to the back of the queue.
The house has three bedrooms at the front and two at the back.
We could only get seats at the back (= of a room).
There's room for three people in the back (= of a car, etc.).
There's room for three people in back.
Come around the back (= to the area behind the house) and I'll show you the garden.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the part of a piece of paper, etc. that is on the opposite side to the one that has information or the most important information on it
examples: Take a card and write your name on the back.
He scribbled some figures on the back of an envelope.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the last few pages of a book, etc.
examples: The television guide is at the back of the paper.
The answer key is in the back of the book.
The article I mentioned is in that magazine—towards the back I think.
The arts page is usually towards the back of the newspaper.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the part of a chair, etc. against which you lean your back

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to describe furniture that has the type of back mentioned
examples: a high-backed sofa

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a player whose main role is to defend their team’s goal
examples: COMPARE forward

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: if a thought, etc. is at the back of your mind, you are aware of it but it is not what you are mainly thinking about
examples: At the back of my mind was a small, warning voice, telling me it was wrong.
The problem was always at the back of my mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: when somebody's back is turned they are not present and not able to see what is happening
examples: Officers are ready to issue a parking ticket as soon as a driver's back is turned.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a place that is a long way from other houses, towns, etc.
examples: We stayed in some farmhouse in the back of beyond.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to talk about planning or calculating something in a way that is not detailed, exact or complete
examples: We added up our savings on the back of an envelope.
back-of-the-envelope calculations

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if two people stand or sit back to back, they stand or sit with their backs facing or touching each other
examples: SEE ALSO back-to-back
The children sat back to back so they couldn't see each others' drawings.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: if two or more things happen back to back, they happen one after the other
examples: The team had to play three games back to back.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: if you put on a piece of clothing back to front, you make a mistake and put the back where the front should be
examples: COMPARE inside out
I think you've got that sweater on back to front.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be happy that you will not have to deal with or see somebody/something again because you do not like them or it
examples: Was I pleased to see the back of her!
I can’t wait to see the back of that old car.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: without somebody’s knowledge or permission
examples: COMPARE to somebody’s face
Have you been talking about me behind my back?
They went ahead and sold it behind my back.
People say bad things about him behind his back, but never to his face.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to keep asking or telling somebody to do something that they do not want to do, in a way that they find annoying
examples: He’s still on my back about that money I borrowed.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to finish the largest or most important part of a task
examples: I want to break the back of this translation before the weekend.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to realize that you may be blamed or criticized for something later and take action to avoid this
examples: Get everything in writing in order to cover your back.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to annoy somebody
examples: That sort of attitude really gets my back up!

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to stop annoying somebody, for example by criticizing them, or asking them to do something
examples: Just get off my back, will you!

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to protect and support somebody
examples: Don't worry, I've got your back.
I’m loyal and I’ve got your back.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to be in a difficult situation in which you are forced to do something but are unable to make the choices that you would like
examples: We had our backs to the wall with no choice but to sell.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to be aware of everything that is happening around you, even things that seem difficult or impossible to see
examples: You can’t get away with anything in her class. She has eyes in the back of her head.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to be very familiar with somebody/something
examples: This is where I grew up. I know this area like the back of my hand.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: the last in a series of bad events, etc. that makes it impossible for you to accept a situation any longer

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to do something that will cause problems for you in the future

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: immediately after something
examples: They come into this game off the back of a 1–0 defeat to Chelsea.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: as a result of an achievement or a success
examples: The profits growth came on the back of a 26 per cent rise in sales.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: goods that fell off the back of a lorry were probably stolen. People say or accept that they came ‘off the back of a lorry’ to avoid saying or asking where they really came from.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: in bed because you are ill
examples: She's been flat on her back for over a week now.
The UK market was flat on its back (= business was very bad).

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: praise or approval for something that you have done well
examples: He deserves a pat on the back for all his hard work.
Give yourself a pat on the back!

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to praise somebody or yourself for doing something well

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to try to forget about something unpleasant
examples: I tried to push the thought to the back of my mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to use a lot of effort and energy on a particular task

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: anything that somebody has, including the things they really need themselves, that somebody else takes from them or they are willing to give
examples: He was the type of person who would give you the shirt off his back.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: an act that harms somebody, done by a person they thought was a friend
examples: Her refusal to support his campaign was a real stab in the back.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: to do or say something that harms somebody who trusts you
examples: SYNONYM betray

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: to turn so that you are facing in the opposite direction

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: to move so that you are standing or sitting with your back facing somebody/something
examples: When on stage, try not to turn your back on the audience.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: to reject somebody/something that you have previously been connected with
examples: She turned her back on them when they needed her.
Some newspapers have turned their backs on discussion and argument.
She decided to turn her back on Paris and return home.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to protect yourself against danger
examples: She'd better watch her back if she wants to hold onto the top job.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: used to say that something, especially criticism, has no effect on somebody/something
examples: I can't tell my son what to do; it's water off a duck's back with him.

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: used to say that if somebody helps you, you will help them, even if this is unfair to othersWord Origin
examples: Old English bæc, of Germanic origin; related to Middle Dutch and Old Norse bak. The adverb use dates from late Middle English and is a shortening of aback.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an amount of money still owed after some payment has been made
examples: The balance of $500 must be paid within 90 days.
I'll pay the balance later.
The final balance is due six weeks before departure.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the largest part of a group or an amount; the position of advantage or attention

The balance has now shifted from the unions to employers.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an instrument for weighing things, with a bar that is supported in the middle and has dishes hanging from each end

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: (considering) the evidence on both sides of an argument, to find the most likely reason for or result of something
examples: The balance of evidence suggests the Liberal party's decline began before the First World War.
The coroner thought that on the balance of probabilities, the pilot had suffered a stroke just before the crash.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if the future of something/somebody, or the result of something is/hangs in the balance, it is not certain
examples: The long-term future of the space programme hangs in the balance.
Tom’s life hung in the balance for two weeks as he lay in a coma.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to make somebody unsteady and in danger of falling
examples: I was thrown off balance by the sudden gust of wind.
The sudden movement threw him off balance.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make somebody surprised and no longer calm
examples: The senator was clearly caught off balance by the unexpected question.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: after considering all the information
examples: On balance, the company has had a successful year.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to make a situation equal or fair again
examples: For years poorer children have had to put up with a lower quality education, and now is the time to redress the balance.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to manage to find a way of being fair to two things that are opposed to each other; to find an acceptable position that is between two things
examples: We need to strike a balance between these conflicting interests.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to affect the result of something in one way rather than another
examples: In an interview, smart presentation can tip the balance in your favour.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the lowest part of something, especially the part or surface on which it rests or stands
examples: The lamp has a heavy base.
the base of a column/glass

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the main place where you live or stay or where a business operates from

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a place where an army, a navy, etc. operates from
examples: a military/naval base
an air base

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: All we got was base pay—we didn't reach profitability levels to award a bonus.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: SYNONYM basis

These policies give us a solid base for winning the next election.

examples: a drink with a rum base

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a chemical substance, for example an alkali, that can combine with an acid to form a salt

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 10

Be quick!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used when you are describing a situation or saying what you think about it
examples: It was really hot in the sauna.
It's strange how she never comes to see us any more.
He thinks it's clever to make fun of people.
It would be a shame if you lost it.
It's going to be a great match.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: Is there a God?
Once upon a time there was a princess…
I tried phoning but there was no answer.
There's a bank down the road.
Was there a pool at the hotel?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be located; to be in a place
examples: The town is three miles away.
If you're looking for your file, it's on the table.
Mary's upstairs.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say where somebody was born or where their home is
examples: She's from Italy.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to happen at a time or in a place
examples: The party is on Friday evening.
The meetings are always in the main conference room.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to remain in a place
examples: She has been in her room for hours.
They're here till Christmas.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to attend an event; to be present in a place
examples: I'll be at the party.
He'll be here soon (= will arrive soon).

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to talk about time
examples: It's two thirty.
It was late at night when we finally arrived.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to cost
examples: ‘How much is that dress?’ ‘Eighty dollars.’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be equal to
examples: Three and three is six.
How much is a thousand pounds in euros?
Let x be the sum of a and b.
London is not England (= do not think that all of England is like London).

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to visit or call
examples: I've never been to Spain.
He had been abroad many times.
Has the postman been yet?

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to say what something is made of
examples: Is your jacket real leather?

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say who something belongs to or who it is intended for
examples: The money's not yours, it's John's.
This package is for you.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to say how important something is to somebody
examples: Money isn't everything (= it is not the only important thing).
A thousand dollars is nothing to somebody as rich as he is.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: as somebody/something used to be called
examples: Jill Davis that was (= before her marriage)
the Soviet Union, as was

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: the most important part; all that matters
examples: Her career is the be-all and end-all of her existence.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to show that you are surprised and annoyed by something that somebody has done
examples: SEE ALSO go and do something

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody/something stopped somebody/something from happening
examples: If it weren't for you, I wouldn't be alive today.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used to show that you accept that something negative cannot be changed
examples: I never imagined that our company share prices would fall so low, but it is what it is.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to leave somebody/something alone without bothering them/it
examples: Leave her be, she obviously doesn't want to talk about it.
Let the poor dog be (= don't annoy it).

He decided to go to the beach for a swim.
She often spent summer days at the beach.
a sandy beach
a pebble/shingle beach
a beach bar
We rented an airy apartment at a beach resort.

examples: SEE ALSO high beams
narrow beams of light/sunlight
the beam of a torch/flashlight

The car's headlights were on full beam (= shining as brightly as possible and not directed downwards).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a long piece of wood, metal, etc. used to support weight, especially as part of the roof in a building
examples: The cottage had exposed oak beams.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a wooden bar that is used in the sport of gymnastics for people to move and balance on
examples: The gymnast performed a somersault on the beam.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a wide and happy smile
examples: a beam of satisfaction

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not correct; wrong
examples: Your calculation is way off beam.

definitions.definition: a seed, or pod containing seeds, of a climbing plant, eaten as a vegetable. There are several types of bean and the plants that they grow on are also called beans.
examples: SEE ALSO snap bean
green beans
runner beans
beans (= baked beans) on toast
a can/tin of beans
She grows her own broad beans.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a seed from a coffee plant, or some other plants
examples: SEE ALSO jelly bean
cocoa/coffee beans

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having a lot of energy

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: something that is not worth much

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have no money

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to know nothing about a subject
examples: I don’t know beans about making movies.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to tell somebody something that should be kept secret or privateWord Origin
examples: Old English bēan, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch boon and German Bohne.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be able to accept and deal with something unpleasant
examples: SYNONYM stand
The pain was almost more than he could bear.
She bore it all with her usual patience.
She couldn't bear the thought of losing him.
I can't bear having cats in the house.
He can't bear being laughed at.
He can't bear to be laughed at.
I can hardly bear to think about it.
How can you bear to eat that stuff?
I can't bear you doing that.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take responsibility for something
examples: She bore the responsibility for most of the changes.
Do parents have to bear the whole cost of tuition fees?
In the end it's consumers who bear the burden of higher prices.
You shouldn't have to bear the blame for other people's mistakes.
You must bear at least some responsibility for what has happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to support the weight of somebody/something
examples: The ice is too thin to bear your weight.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to show something; to carry something so that it can be seen
examples: The document bore her signature.
He was badly wounded in the war and still bears the scars.
She bears little resemblance to (= is not much like) her mother.
The title of the essay bore little relation to (= was not much connected with) the contents.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to not be suitable for something
examples: Her later work does not bear comparison with her earlier novels (= because it is not nearly as good).
The plan won't bear close inspection (= it will be found to be unacceptable when carefully examined).
The joke doesn't bear repeating (= because it is not funny or may offend people).
His sufferings don't bear thinking about (= because they are so terrible).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have a feeling, especially a negative feeling
examples: He bears no resentment towards them.
He's borne a grudge against me ever since that day.
He's borne me a grudge ever since that day.
She bore him no ill will.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have a particular name
examples: a family that bore an ancient and honoured name

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to carry somebody/something, especially while moving
examples: three kings bearing gifts

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to move, behave or act in a particular way
examples: He bears himself (= stands, walks, etc.) proudly, like a soldier.
She bore herself with dignity throughout the funeral.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to give birth to a child
examples: She was not able to bear children.
She had borne him six sons.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to produce flowers or fruit
examples: These trees take a long time to bear fruit.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to go or turn in the direction mentioned
examples: When you get to the fork in the road, bear right.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be a soldier; to fight

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to have a successful result

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be a cause of difficulty or worry to somebody
examples: Taxation bears heavily on us all.
The burden of the tax bore most heavily on the poor.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to remember somebody/something; to remember or consider that…
examples: You don't have to do anything about it now… just bear it in mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to receive the main force of something unpleasant
examples: Schools will bear the brunt of cuts in government spending.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to provide evidence of the truth of something
examples: The crowd of mourners at his funeral bore witness to the great affection in which he was held.
The ancient temples bear silent witness to the passing dynasties.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to be realized by somebody, especially after a period of time
examples: It was gradually borne in on us that defeat was inevitable.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to use energy, pressure, influence, etc. to try to achieve something or make somebody do something
examples: We must bring all our energies to bear upon the task.
Pressure was brought to bear on us to finish the work on time.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to accept pain or bad luck without complaining
examples: There's nothing we can do about it. We'll just have to grin and bear it.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to have a difficult problem that makes you worried or unhappy but that you have to deal with
examples: We all have our crosses to bear.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an animal, especially one that is large or dangerous, or one that is unusual
examples: wild/savage/ferocious beasts
mythical beasts such as unicorns and dragons

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is cruel and whose behaviour shows a lack of control
examples: SYNONYM animal

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an unpleasant person or thing
examples: The maths exam was a real beast.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a thing of a particular kind
examples: SYNONYM animal
His new guitar is a very expensive beast.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to defeat somebody in a game or competition
examples: He beat me at chess.
She was narrowly beaten by the German in the final.
I beat her by just three points.
Their recent wins have proved they're still the ones to beat (= the most difficult team to beat).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to do or be better than something
examples: Nothing beats home cooking.
You can't beat Italian shoes.
For a break in the sun, Thailand is hard to beat.
They want to beat the speed record (= go faster than anyone before).
This is his latest attempt to beat the world record.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to get control of something
examples: The government's main aim is to beat inflation.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be too difficult for somebody
examples: SYNONYM defeat
It is a problem that beats even the experts.
It beats me (= I don't know) why he did it.
What beats me (= what I don't understand) is how it was done so quickly.
‘Where's she gone?’ ‘Beats me.’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to avoid something
examples: If we go early we should beat the traffic.
We were up and off early to beat the heat.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to hit a person hard and many times in order to hurt them
examples: At that time children were regularly beaten for quite minor offences (= as a punishment).
An elderly man was found beaten to death.
The prisoners were beaten into submission (= they were beaten until they did what was wanted).
They beat him unconscious (= hit him until he became unconscious).
The men took him out into the street and beat him senseless.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to hit something hard several times
examples: Somebody was beating at the door.
Hailstones beat against the window.
Someone was beating a drum.
She was beating dust out of the carpet (= removing dust from the carpet by beating it).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to make, or cause something to make, a regular sound or movement
examples: She's alive—her heart is still beating.
His heart started beating faster.
We heard the drums beating.
The bird was beating its wings (= moving them up and down) frantically.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to mix something with short quick movements with a fork, etc.
examples: Beat the eggs up to a frothy consistency.
Beat the mixture well, until it is light and creamy.
Add three eggs, lightly beaten.
Beat the flour and milk together.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to change the shape of something, especially metal, by hitting it with a hammer, etc.
examples: The gold is beaten out into thin strips.
beaten silver
The metal had been beaten flat.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make a path, etc. by walking somewhere or by pressing branches down and walking over them
examples: a well-beaten track (= one that has been worn hard by much use)
The hunters beat a path through the undergrowth.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to talk about something for a long time without coming to the main point
examples: Stop beating about the bush and tell me what you want.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to defeat or do better than somebody in an activity which they have chosen or in which they think they are strong

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to think very hard about something for a long time
examples: I’ve been beating my brains out all weekend to get this script written.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to show that you feel sorry about something that you have done, especially in public and in an exaggerated way

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to finish a task, race, etc. before a particular time
examples: The player beat the clock and set a new record.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to hit somebody very hard several times and hurt them very much
examples: Get out or I’ll beat the living daylights out of you!

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to waste your effort by trying to do something that is no longer possible

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to speak with enthusiasm in support of somebody/something
examples: She’s really banging the drum for the new system.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to hit somebody/something very hard

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to go away immediately
examples: This is private land, so beat it!

definitions.label: Meaning 22

definitions.label: Meaning 23

definitions.label: Meaning 24

definitions.label: Meaning 25

Beat the flour and milk together.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to change the shape of something, especially metal, by hitting it with a hammer, etc.
examples: The gold is beaten out into thin strips.
beaten silver
The metal had been beaten flat.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make a path, etc. by walking somewhere or by pressing branches down and walking over them
examples: a well-beaten track (= one that has been worn hard by much use)

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to talk about something for a long time without coming to the main point
examples: Stop beating about the bush and tell me what you want.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to defeat or do better than somebody in an activity which they have chosen or in which they think they are strong

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to think very hard about something for a long time
examples: I’ve been beating my brains out all weekend to get this script written.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to show that you feel sorry about something that you have done, especially in public and in an exaggerated way

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to finish a task, race, etc. before a particular time
examples: The player beat the clock and set a new record.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to hit somebody very hard several times and hurt them very much
examples: Get out or I’ll beat the living daylights out of you!

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to waste your effort by trying to do something that is no longer possible

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to speak with enthusiasm in support of somebody/something
examples: She’s really banging the drum for the new system.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to hit somebody/something very hard
examples: He was a dirty player and loved to kick hell out of the opposition.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to go away immediately
examples: This is private land, so beat it!

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: if a lot of people beat a path to somebody’s door, they are all interested in something that person has to sell, or can do or tell them
examples: Top theatrical agents are beating a path to the teenager's door.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to escape without being punished

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to go away or back quickly, especially to avoid something unpleasant
examples: I decided to beat a hasty retreat.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to mark or follow the rhythm of music, by waving a stick, tapping your foot (= hitting it against the floor), etc.
examples: She beat time with her fingers.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to get or do something before somebody else can

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: (to hit somebody until they are) covered with bruises (= blue, brown or purple marks on the body)

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: used to express surprise or anger

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: if you cannot defeat somebody or be as successful as they are, then it is more sensible to join them in what they are doing and perhaps get some advantage for yourself by doing so

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: far away from other people, houses, etc.
examples: They live miles off the beaten track.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: a fact, an argument, etc. that is used in order to blame or punish somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to be difficult to beat
examples: That score is going to take some beating.
For sheer luxury, this hotel takes some beating.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

What a beautiful day!
a beautiful face/baby/voice/garden/beach
beautiful countryside/weather/music

The scenery here is so beautiful.
What a beautiful thing to say!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very good; very kind or showing great skill
examples: Thank you—you have done a beautiful thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of giving pleasure to the senses or to the mind
examples: the beauty of the sunset/of poetry/of his singing

beauty products/treatments (= intended to make a person more beautiful)
She was a contestant in the Miss World beauty pageant.
His voice is a thing of beauty.
The sheer beauty of the scenery took my breath away.
a woman of great beauty

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is beautiful
examples: She had been a beauty in her day.
Isn't she a little beauty?
She was known as a great beauty in her time.
She was still a radiant beauty.
She was an exotic beauty with raven hair.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an excellent example of its type
examples: That last goal was a beauty!
My new car's a real beauty!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an attractive feature
examples: SYNONYM advantage
One of the beauties of living here is that it's so peaceful.
The project will require very little work to start up; that's the beauty of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: people all have different ideas about what is beautiful

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: how a person looks is less important than their characterWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French beaute, based on Latin bellus ‘beautiful, fine’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: for the reason that
examples: I did it because he told me to.
Just because I don't complain, people think I'm satisfied.
Because it was so late, he found it unacceptable to send them all away.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to start to be something
examples: It soon became apparent that no one was going to come.
It is becoming increasingly clear that something has gone seriously wrong.
When did you first become aware of the problem?
It was becoming more and more difficult to live on his salary.
She was becoming confused.

The bill will become law next year.
Over the last five years she has become part of the family.
How can I become a member of the society?
She’s studying to become a teacher.
His job has become his whole life.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be suitable for somebody
examples: Such behaviour did not become her.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to look attractive on somebody
examples: SYNONYM suit
Short hair really becomes you.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to ask what has happened or what will happen to somebody/something
examples: What became of that student who used to live with you?
I dread to think what will become of them if they lose their home.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of furniture for sleeping on
examples: SEE ALSO airbed
a single/double bed
She lay on the bed (= on top of the covers).
He lay in bed (= under the covers).

I'll just put the kids to bed.
It's time for bed (= time to go to sleep).

to make the bed (= arrange the covers in a tidy way)

Having breakfast in bed is a rare treat.
I ran and hid under a bed.
She came over and sat at the foot (= bottom) of the bed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the bottom of a river, the sea, etc.
examples: the ocean bed
oyster beds (= an area in the sea where there are many oysters)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an area of ground in a garden or park for growing flowers, vegetables, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO raised bed
flower beds

ornamental beds of roses

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a layer of something that other things lie or rest on

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a layer of clay, rock, etc. in the ground
examples: SEE ALSO bedrock

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: Their life together hasn't exactly been a bed of roses.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to die because you are old or ill

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be in a bad mood for the whole day for no particular reason

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 10

examples: What's he like in bed?
I caught them in bed together (= having sex).

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to go to bed and stay there because you are ill

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to urinate in your bed by accident
examples: It is quite common for small children to wet their beds.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: you must accept the results of your actionsWord Origin
examples: Old English bed, bedd (noun), beddian (verb), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch bed and German Bett.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a room for sleeping in
examples: the spare/guest bedroom
a hotel with 20 bedrooms
This is the master bedroom (= the main bedroom of the house).
Two double bedrooms overlook the front lawn.
the bedroom window/door
I went into the bedroom and cried.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the number of bedrooms mentioned
examples: a three-bedroomed house
The larger houses are four-bedroom houses.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a black and yellow flying insect that can sting (= touch your skin and make you feel a sharp pain).Bees live in large groups and make honey (= a sweet sticky substance that is good to eat).
examples: SEE ALSO beehive
Bees were buzzing in the clover.
a swarm of bees
a bee sting

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a meeting in a group where people combine work, competition and pleasure
examples: SEE ALSO spelling bee
a sewing bee

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very busy

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an excellent person or thing
examples: She thinks she's the bee's knees (= she has a very high opinion of herself).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the basic facts about sex, especially as told to children

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to think or talk about something all the time and to think that it is very important
examples: Our teacher has a bee in his bonnet about punctuation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: meat that comes from a cow
examples: SEE ALSO chipped beef
roast beef
beef and dairy cattle
minced/ground beef
a joint/fillet/cut of beef
a beef farmer/producer

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a complaint
examples: What's his latest beef?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an alcoholic drink made from malt with hops added to give it taste. There are many types of beer.
examples: a pint/can/bottle of beer
a barrel/glass of beer
beers brewed in Germany
a beer glass/bottle/can
Are you a beer drinker?
The bar has some great beers on tap.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a glass, bottle or can of beer
examples: SEE ALSO craft beer
Shall we have a beer?
David bought us a couple of beers.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: earlier than somebody/something
examples: before lunch
the day before yesterday
The year before last he won a gold medal, and the year before that he won a silver.
She's lived there since before the war.
He arrived before me.
She became a lawyer as her father had before her.
Leave your keys at reception before departure.
Something ought to have been done before now.
We'll know before long (= soon).
Turn left just before (= before you reach) the bank.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody/something is ahead of somebody/something in an order or arrangement
examples: Your name is before mine on the list.
He puts his work before everything (= regards it as more important than anything else).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody/something is in a position in front of somebody/something
examples: COMPARE behind
They knelt before the throne.
Before you is a list of the points we have to discuss.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that something is facing somebody in the future
examples: The task before us is a daunting one.
The whole summer lay before me.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in the presence of somebody who is listening, watching, etc.
examples: He was brought before the judge.
She said it before witnesses.
They had the advantage of playing before their home crowd.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say how somebody reacts when they have to face somebody/something
examples: They retreated before the enemy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to ask somebody for something especially in an anxious way because you want or need it very much
examples: Now you have to beg and plead.
He wants to see them beg for mercy.
They begged him for help.
Forgive me, I beg you!
She begged permission to leave.
I managed to beg a lift from a passing motorist.
Can I beg a favour of you?
‘Give me one more chance,’ he begged (her).
She begged him not to go.
He begged to be told the truth.
She begged that she be allowed to go.
She begged that she should be allowed to go.
Don't leave me here, I beg of you!
I have come to apologize and to beg your forgiveness.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to ask somebody for money, food, etc., especially in the street
examples: London is full of homeless people begging in the streets.
a begging letter (= one that asks somebody for money)
a begging bowl (= used to beg for money with)
The children were begging for food.
They will have to beg for money from tourists.
We managed to beg a meal from the cafe owner.
They went off to beg food.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if a dog begs, it sits on its back legs with its front legs in the air, waiting to be given something

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to ask somebody for permission to do something
examples: I beg leave to add a few comments of my own.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if something is going begging, it is available because nobody else wants it
examples: I’ll have that last cake if it’s going begging.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to ask somebody to forgive you for something you have said or done
examples: He returned to beg her pardon for his sudden outburst.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make somebody want to ask a question that has not yet been answered
examples: All of which begs the question as to who will fund the project.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to talk about something as if it were definitely true, even though it might not be
examples: These assumptions beg the question that children learn languages more easily than adults.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that you are sorry for something you have said or done
examples: I beg your pardon, I thought that was my coat.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody to repeat what they have just said because you did not hear
examples: ‘It's on Duke Street.’ ‘I beg your pardon.’ ‘Duke Street.’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that you are offended by what they have just said or by the way that they have said it
examples: ‘Just go away.’ ‘I beg your pardon!’

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say politely that you do not agree with something that has just been said
examples: ‘At least she is good at her job.’ ‘Oh, I beg to differ.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to start doing something; to do the first part of something
examples: Shall I begin?
Let's begin at page 9.
I'd like to begin with a simple question.
She began by thanking us all for coming.
We began work on the project in May.
I began (= started reading) this novel last month and I still haven't finished it.
He always begins his lessons with a warm-up exercise.
I began piano lessons at the age of six.
She began her speech by praising her opponent.
He began his political career as a student (= when he was a student).
I began to feel dizzy.
Leaves are just beginning to appear.
We have already begun to address the problem.
I was beginning to think you'd never come.
Everyone began talking at once.
We began working on the project in May.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to start to happen or exist, especially from a particular time
examples: When does the concert begin?
Work on the new bridge is due to begin in September.
The lecture begins at 8pm.
The evening began well.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have something as the first part or the point where something starts
examples: Where does Europe end and Asia begin?
Use ‘an’ before words beginning with a vowel.
‘I'm thinking of a country in Asia.’ ‘What does it begin with (= what is the first letter)?’
Each chapter begins with a quotation.
The path begins at Livingston village.
The story begins on the island of Corfu.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to start or make something start for the first time
examples: The school began in 1920, with only ten pupils.
He began a new magazine on post-war architecture.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be something first, before becoming something else
examples: He began as an actor, before starting to direct films.
What began as a minor scuffle turned into a full-scale riot.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to start speaking
examples: ‘Ladies and gentlemen,’ he began, ‘welcome to the Town Hall.’

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make no attempt to do something or have no chance of doing something
examples: I can't begin to thank you enough.
He didn't even begin to understand my problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: you should help and care for your own family, etc. before you start helping other people

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: at first
examples: I found it tiring to begin with but I soon got used to it.
We'll go slowly to begin with.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to introduce the first point you want to make
examples: ‘What was it you didn't like?’ ‘Well, to begin with, our room was far too small.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the time when something starts; the first part of an event, a story, etc.
examples: A story has to have a beginning, middle, and end.

The birth of their first child marked the beginning of a new era in their married life.
We're going to Japan at the beginning of July.

Let's start again from the beginning.
I've read the whole book from beginning to end and still can't understand it.
Our position was quite clear from the very beginning.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the first or early ideas, signs or stages of something
examples: Did democracy have its beginnings in ancient Greece?
The company has grown from humble beginnings.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the first sign of something ending
examples: The scandal was the beginning of the end of his career as a politician.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in order to help somebody
examples: We collected money in behalf of the homeless.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: On behalf of the department I would like to thank you all.
Mr Knight cannot be here, so his wife will accept the prize on his behalf.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in order to help somebody
examples: They campaigned on behalf of asylum seekers.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: because of somebody; for somebody
examples: Don't worry on my behalf.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

He behaved like a true gentleman.

He had always behaved in a friendly manner towards us.
I expect you to behave in a certain way.
She behaved with great dignity.
He behaved as if/though nothing had happened.

examples: OPPOSITE misbehave
Will you kids just behave!
She doesn't know how to behave in public.
The children always behave for their father.
I want you to behave yourselves while I'm away.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: well-/badly behaved children

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to naturally react, move, etc. in a particular way
examples: a study of how metals behave under pressure

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 1

Stay close behind me.
a small street behind the station

Don't forget to lock the door behind you (= when you leave).

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: He's behind the rest of the class in reading.
We're behind schedule (= late).

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: human beings
a strange being from another planet

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: your mind and all of your feelings
examples: I hated him with my whole being.

belief in God/democracy

They share a belief that there is life after death.

definitions.definition: an opinion about something; something that you think is true

definitions.definition: (in a way that is) too great, difficult, etc. to be believed

icy air that was cold beyond belief
