definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: as far as you know
examples: He never made a will, to the best of my knowledge.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to feel certain that something is true or that somebody is telling you the truth
examples: I don't believe you!
The man claimed to be a social worker and the old woman believed him.
Do you really believe her?
Believe me, she's not right for you.
I believed his lies for years.
I find that hard to believe.
Don't believe a word of it (= don't believe any part of what somebody is saying).
People used to believe (that) the earth was flat.
He refused to believe (that) his son was involved in drugs.
I do believe you’re right (= I think something is true, even though it is surprising).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to think that something is true or possible, although you are not completely certain
examples: ‘Where does she come from?’ ‘Spain, I believe.’
‘Does he still work there?’ ‘I believe so/not.’
Police believe (that) the man may be armed.
Experts believe that the diamond is the only one of its kind.
l firmly believe that she is still alive.
There is no reason to believe he is dangerous.
It is believed that the couple have left the country.
It is widely believed that he was forced to resign.
Few people believe the claim that the cost of living has not risen since last year.
The vases are believed to be worth over $20 000 each.
Three sailors are missing, believed drowned.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have the opinion that something is right or true
examples: The party believes (that) education is the most important issue facing the government.
She believes that killing animals for food or fur is completely immoral.
I strongly believe that competition is a good thing.
She truly believes that love can change the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that you are surprised or annoyed at something
examples: She couldn’t believe (that) it was all happening again.
I don't believe I'm doing this!
I can't believe how much better I feel.
I couldn't believe what I was hearing.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have a religious faith
examples: The god appears only to those who believe.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to introduce information that is true but that may surprise people
examples: Believe it or not, he asked me to marry him!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you strongly believe what you are saying
examples: You haven't heard the last of this, believe you me!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that something is definitely not true
examples: ‘She wouldn’t do a thing like that.’ ‘Don’t you believe it!’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to make somebody believe/understand something
examples: I was given to understand that she had resigned.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to say that you are surprised or annoyed about something
examples: I don't believe it! What are you doing here?

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that you think somebody is stupid if they believe that something is true
examples: ‘He promised not to do it again.’ ‘Sure, and if you believe that, you’ll believe anything.’

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to pretend that something is true
examples: RELATED NOUN make-believe

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be very surprised at something you hear/see
examples: I couldn't believe my eyes when she walked in.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody will have to believe that something is true when they see it, although they do not think it is true now

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to show that you are surprised and annoyed about something
examples: And, would you believe, he didn't even apologize!

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that something is definitely true
examples: ‘He’s not a bad player, is he?’ ‘You’d better believe it!’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a hollow metal object, often like a cup in shape, that makes a ringing sound when hit by a small piece of metal inside it; the sound that it makes
examples: A peal of church bells rang out in the distance.
a bicycle bell
His voice came down the line as clear as a bell.
the bell of a trumpet (= the part at the end like a bell in shape)
The church bells rang out.
a bell-shaped flower
Off in the distance a bell tolled two in the morning.
a bell tower
wedding bells
The dancers wore bells on their ankles.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an electrical device which makes a ringing sound when a button on it is pushed; the sound that it makes, used as a signal or a warning
examples: SEE ALSO doorbell
Ring the bell to see if they're in.
The bell's ringing!
The bell went for the end of the lesson.
An alarm bell went off.
Warning bells started ringing in her head as she sensed that something was wrong.
This decision is going to sound a warning bell to other couples.
Saved by the bell! (= a bell that signals the end of something) I thought I'd have to sit here listening to you two argue forever.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if you say that alarm bells are ringing, you mean that people are starting to feel worried and to suspect that something is wrong
examples: The government’s proposal has set alarm bells ringing for people on low incomes.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to call somebody by phone

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to show that you do not believe what somebody has just said

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to sound familiar to you, as though you have heard it before
examples: His name rings a bell but I can't think where we met.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in perfect condition
examples: The doctor said I was as sound as a bell.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be in the right or suitable place
examples: Where do these plates belong (= where are they kept)?
Are you sure these documents belong together?
Several of the points you raise do not belong in this discussion.
A person like that does not belong in teaching.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to feel comfortable and happy in a particular situation or with a particular group of people
examples: I don't feel as if I belong here.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: loved very much
examples: in memory of our dearly beloved son, John
They were glad to be back in their beloved Ireland.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: loved very much by somebody; very popular with somebody
examples: the deep purple flowers so beloved by artists
She was beloved by all who knew her.
She ran one of the little tea rooms so beloved of Londoners at the turn of the century.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at or to a lower level, position or place
examples: They live on the floor below.
I could still see the airport buildings far below.
See below (= at the bottom of the page) for references.
The passengers who felt seasick stayed below (= on a lower deck).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: at a lower rank
examples: This ruling applies to the ranks of Inspector and below.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: lower than zero
examples: The thermometer had dropped to a record 40 below (= −40 degrees).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long narrow piece of leather, cloth, etc. that you wear around the middle part of your body
examples: SEE ALSO black belt
to do up/fasten/tighten a belt
a belt buckle
a studded leather belt
Around his waist he wore a belt.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a continuous band of material that moves round and is used to carry things along or to drive a machine
examples: SEE ALSO conveyor belt

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a narrow area or an area around the edge of something that has particular characteristics
examples: SEE ALSO green belt
the country’s corn/industrial belt
We live in the commuter belt.
a narrow belt of trees
a belt of rain moving across the country
Towns in the country's industrial belt were particularly affected by the recession.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an act of hitting something/somebody hard
examples: She gave the ball a terrific belt.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: unfair or cruel
examples: That was distinctly below the belt!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: taking more actions than are really necessary to make sure that something succeeds or works as it should
examples: a belt-and-braces policy

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have already achieved or obtained something
examples: She already has a couple of good wins under her belt.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to spend less money because there is less available
examples: With price increases on most goods, everyone is having to tighten their belt.
There is a need for further belt-tightening.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long seat for two or more people, usually made of wood
examples: a park bench

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a judge in court or the seat where he/she sits; the position of being a judge or magistrate
examples: His lawyer turned to address the bench.
She has recently been appointed to the bench.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: (in the British parliament) a seat where a particular group of politicians sit
examples: SEE ALSO back bench
There was cheering from the Opposition benches.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the seats where players sit when they are not playing in the game
examples: the substitutes’ bench
He started the game on the bench but finished as the team’s top scorer.
He's sick of spending every game on the bench.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a long heavy table used for doing practical jobs, working with tools, etc.
examples: a carpenter’s bench

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that can be measured and used as a standard that other things can be compared with
examples: Tests at the age of seven provide a benchmark against which the child's progress at school can be measured.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to lean, or make something lean, in a particular direction
examples: He bent and kissed her.
The doctor told me to avoid bending and stretching.
fields of poppies bending in the wind
She suddenly bent over, clutching her stomach.
His dark head bent over her.
She bent forward to pick up the newspaper.
Slowly bend from the waist and bring your head down to your knees.
Keep your feet apart, and bend at the waist
He bent his head and kissed her.
She bent her head towards him.
She was bent over her desk writing a letter.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: if you bend your arm, leg, etc. or if it bends, you move it so that it is no longer straight
examples: Bend your knees, keeping your back straight.
Lie flat and let your knees bend.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to force something that was straight into an angle or a curve
examples: Mark the pipe where you want to bend it.
The knives were bent out of shape.
He bent the wire into the shape of a square.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to change direction to form a curve or an angle; to make something change direction in this way
examples: The road bent sharply to the right.
Glass and water both bend light.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to talk to somebody a lot about something, especially about a problem that you have

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to think very hard about or put a lot of effort into one particular thing
examples: She bent her mind to the problem of escape.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make a great effort, especially in order to be helpful or fair
examples: I've bent over backwards to help him.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to change the rules to suit a particular person or situation
examples: Couldn't they just bend the rules and let us in without a ticket?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to say something that is not completely true
examples: I wasn’t exactly lying when I said I hadn’t seen her—I was just bending the truth a little.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: if you ask for something on bended knee(s), you ask for it in a very anxious and/or humble way (= showing you think you are less important than the person you are asking)
examples: I’d go down on bended knee if I thought she’d change her mind.

definitions.definition: in or to a lower position than somebody/something; under somebody/something

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not good enough for somebody
examples: He considers such jobs beneath him.
They thought she had married beneath her (= married a man of lower social status).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: improving a situation; having a helpful or useful effect
examples: SYNONYM advantageous
A good diet is beneficial to health.
They finally came to a mutually beneficial agreement.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who gains as a result of something
examples: Who will be the main beneficiary of the cuts in income tax?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who receives money or property when somebody dies
examples: She was the sole beneficiary of her father’s will.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an advantage that something gives you; a helpful and useful effect that something has
examples: SEE ALSO cost–benefit
Freedom of information brings great benefits.
health/economic/tax benefits
the benefits of modern medicine
I've had the benefit of a good education.
It was good to see her finally reaping the benefits (= enjoying the results) of all her hard work.
The industry will be one of the first to enjoy the benefits of the recovery.
The company derived substantial benefit from the deal.
He couldn't see the benefit of arguing any longer.
The new regulations will be of benefit to everyone concerned.
It will be to your benefit to arrive early.
The project will have major benefits for the local community.
With the benefit of hindsight (= knowing what we have learnt since), we would do things differently.
Nobody should be sent to prison without the benefit of legal advice.
For maximum benefit, take the tablets before meals.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: money provided by the government to people who need financial help because they are unemployed, ill, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO child benefit
You may be eligible to receive benefits.
The number of people claiming unemployment benefit fell last month.
The aim is to help people who are on benefits (= receiving benefits) to find jobs.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an advantage that you get from a company in addition to the money that you earn
examples: SEE ALSO fringe benefit
Private health insurance is offered as part of the employees' benefits package.
These benefits will now be extended to agency workers.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: money from an insurance company
examples: The insurance plan will provide substantial cash benefits to your family in case of your death.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an event such as a performance, a dinner, etc., organized in order to raise money for a particular person or charity
examples: a benefit match/concert
The proceeds from the benefit will go directly to the refugee camps.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: especially in order to help or be useful to somebody
examples: I have typed out some lecture notes for the benefit of those people who were absent last week.
Don't go to any trouble for my benefit!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to accept that somebody has told the truth or behaved well because you cannot prove that they have not
examples: She may have been lying, but I felt I had to give her the benefit of the doubt.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not able to stand up straight, usually as a result of being old or ill
examples: a small bent old woman
He was bent double with laughter.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: dishonest

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: determined to do something (usually something bad)
examples: SEE ALSO hell-bent
She seems bent on making life difficult for me.
to be bent on destruction/revenge
He's your typical supervillain, bent on world domination.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to become angry, anxious or upset
examples: Don't get bent out of shape about it. It was just a mistake!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: next to or at the side of somebody/something
examples: He sat beside her all night.
a mill beside a stream

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: compared with somebody/something
examples: My painting looks childish beside yours.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to not be important or closely related to the main thing you are talking about
examples: Yes, I know it was an accident, but that's beside the point.
They took my words out of context, but that’s beside the point.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: unable to control yourself because of the strength of emotion you are feeling
examples: He was beside himself with rage when I told him what I had done.
They were beside themselves with excitement.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in addition to somebody/something; apart from somebody/something
examples: We have lots of things in common besides music.
Besides working as a doctor, he also writes novels in his spare time.
I've got no family besides my parents.
I’ve got plenty of other things to do besides talking to you.

definitions.definition: of the most excellent type or quality
examples: That's the best movie I've ever seen!
He wrote his best songs before he was 25.
She was one of the best tennis players of her generation.
Is that your best suit?
They've been best friends (= closest friends) since they were children.
the company’s best-ever results
We want the kids to have the best possible education.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: giving most pleasure; happiest
examples: Those were the best years of my life.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

He's the best man for the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to risk money on a race or an event by trying to predict the result
examples: SEE ALSO betting
You have to be over 16 to bet.
I wouldn't bet on them winning the next election.
Not many people are betting against France retaining their title.
He likes betting on horses and watching table tennis.
He bet $2 000 on the final score of the game.
You shouldn't praise a gambler for betting his life savings if he wins.
She bet me £20 (that) I wouldn't do it.
I bet her (that) the Democrats would not win.
He bet ten dollars (that) he could write a complete story in just six words.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that you are almost certain that something is true or that something will happen
examples: I bet (that) we’re too late.
You can bet (that) the moment I sit down, the phone will ring.
I'm willing to bet (that) the analysts will be wrong.
I’ll bet you (that) he knows all about it.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to risk everything you have on an investment, a bet, etc.
examples: The company bet the farm on the new marketing model, only to find that it wasn’t successful.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that you can understand what somebody is feeling, describing, etc.
examples: ‘I nearly died when he told me.’ ‘I bet!’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that you do not believe what they have just said
examples: ‘I'm going to tell her what I think of her.’ ‘Yeah, I bet!’

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not think that something is very likely
examples: ‘She'll soon get used to the idea.’ ‘I wouldn't bet on it.’

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used instead of ‘yes’ to emphasize that somebody has guessed something correctly or made a good suggestion
examples: ‘Are you nervous?’ ‘You bet!’

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that you are certain that something will happen
examples: You can bet your bottom dollar that he'll be late.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to hurt somebody who trusts you, especially by lying to or about them or telling their secrets to other people
examples: She felt betrayed when she found out the truth about him.
She betrayed his trust over and over again.
I have never known her to betray a confidence (= tell other people something that should be kept secret).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to ignore your principles or beliefs in order to achieve something or gain an advantage for yourself
examples: He has been accused of betraying his former socialist ideals.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to tell somebody or make them aware of a piece of information, a feeling, etc., usually without meaning to
examples: SYNONYM give away
His voice betrayed the worry he was trying to hide.
She was terrified of saying something that would make her betray herself (= show her feelings or who she was).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: of a higher standard or less poor quality; not as bad as something else
examples: We're hoping for better weather tomorrow.
Her work is getting better and better.
He is in a much better mood than usual.
The meal couldn't have been better.
There's nothing better than a long soak in a hot bath.
If you can only exercise once a week, that's better than nothing (= better than taking no exercise at all).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: more suitable or appropriate
examples: Can you think of a better word than ‘nice’?
It would be better for him to talk to his parents about his problems.
You'd be better going by bus.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: more able; showing more skill
examples: She's far better at science than her brother.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: less ill or unhappy
examples: She's a lot better today.
His leg was getting better.
You'll feel all the better for a good night's sleep.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: fully recovered after an illness; in good health again
examples: SEE ALSO well
Don't go back to work until you are better.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: most of something, especially a period of time; more than half of something
examples: He drank the best part of a bottle of Scotch waiting for her to get home.
The journey took her the better part of an hour.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that something should be as big, small, etc. as possible
examples: I love giving parties, the bigger the better.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: you should avoid danger and not take unnecessary risks

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: almost or just the same as; almost or just as bad as
examples: The path was no better than a sheep track.
Charles VII was a bad king and Charles VIII was no better.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: it is better to stop something bad from happening rather than try to deal with the problems after it has happened
examples: Prevention is better than cure, so start looking after your heart now.
Prevention is better than cure, so start taking care of yourself.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to give support to somebody who has been upset and is trying to become calmer
examples: Dry your eyes now. That's better.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to praise somebody who has made an effort to improve
examples: That's much better—you played the right notes this time.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to say that two people can achieve more than one person working aloneWord Origin
examples: Old English betera (adjective), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch beter and German besser, also to best.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in or into the space separating two or more points, objects, people, etc.
examples: Q comes between P and R in the English alphabet.
I sat down between Jo and Diana.
Switzerland lies between France, Germany, Austria and Italy.
The paper had fallen down between the desk and the wall.
My job is somewhere between a secretary and a personal assistant.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in the period of time that separates two days, years, events, etc.
examples: It's cheaper between 6 p.m. and 8 a.m.
Don't eat between meals.
Children must attend school between the ages of 5 and 16.
Many changes took place between the two world wars.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: at some point along a scale from one amount, weight, distance, etc. to another
examples: It weighed between nine and ten kilos.
The temperature remained between 25°C and 30°C all week.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: separating one place from another
examples: the border between Sweden and Norway

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: from one place to another
examples: We fly between Rome and Paris twice daily.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to show a connection or relationship
examples: a difference/distinction/contrast between two things
a link between unemployment and crime
There's a lot of bad feeling between them.
I had to choose between the two jobs.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: shared by two or more people or things
examples: We ate a pizza between us.
This is just between you and me/between ourselves (= it is a secret).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: by putting together the efforts or actions of two or more people or groups
examples: We ought to be able to manage it between us.
China and India between them account for a third of the world's population.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to show that several activities are involved
examples: Between working full-time and taking care of the kids, he didn't have much time for hobbies.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

Employers must consider all candidates impartially and without bias.
Some institutions still have a strong bias against women.
The article examines gender bias in our schools.

definitions.definition: an interest in one thing more than others; a special ability
examples: The course has a strong practical bias.
Leila had a marked scientific bias.
In British universities there was a bias towards pure science.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 27

definitions.label: Meaning 28

examples: If I don't win it's no big deal.

definitions.label: Meaning 14

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.label: Meaning 16

definitions.label: Meaning 21

examples: Gerry’s champing at the bit to go to college.

definitions.label: Meaning 22

examples: We can finish this job on time if everyone does their bit.

definitions.label: Meaning 23

definitions.label: Meaning 25

I don't like that idea one bit.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: used for saying that something that you had expected to happen did not happen
examples: You'd think she'd be tired after the journey but not a bit of it!

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: not any
examples: He didn't take a blind bit of notice of me (= he ignored me).

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: not at all

definitions.label: Meaning 29

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to use your teeth to cut into or through something

Come here! I won't bite! (= you don't need to be afraid)
She bit into a ripe juicy pear.
She was bitten by the family dog.
Stop biting your nails!
He bit off a large chunk of bread/He bit a large chunk of bread off.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to wound somebody by making a small hole or mark in their skin
examples: Most European spiders don't bite.
We were badly bitten by mosquitoes.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if a fish bites, it takes food from the end of a fishing line and may get caught

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have an unpleasant effect
examples: The recession is beginning to bite.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to develop a strong interest in or enthusiasm for something
examples: He's been bitten by the travel bug.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to start to deal with an unpleasant or difficult situation which cannot be avoided
examples: I wasn’t happy with the way my career was going so I decided to bite the bullet and look for another job.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to fail, or to be defeated or destroyed
examples: Thousands of small businesses bite the dust every year.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to die

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to harm somebody who has helped you or supported you

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to shout at somebody in an angry way, especially without reason

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to stop yourself from saying something or from showing an emotion
examples: I bit my lip and forced myself to be calm.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to try to do too much, or something that is too difficult

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to stop yourself from saying something that might upset somebody or cause an argument, although you want to speak
examples: I didn't believe her explanation but I bit my tongue.

definitions.label: Meaning 14

examples: She doesn't blame anyone for her father's death.

Why is he blaming others for his problems?
It's easy to blame the media at times like this.
Police are blaming the accident on dangerous driving.
The violence was blamed in part on militants.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be responsible for something bad
examples: If anyone's to blame, it's me.
Which driver was to blame for the accident?
A spokesman said that bad weather was partly to blame for the delay.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to advise somebody not to do something, when you think they will do it despite your advice
examples: Call her if you like, but don't blame me if she's angry.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that you think that what somebody did was reasonable and the right thing to do
examples: ‘I just slammed the phone down when he said that.’ ‘I don't blame you!’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that you think something is somebody’s own fault
examples: If you lose your job, you'll only have yourself to blame.

the wind’s icy blasts

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: three short blasts on the ship’s siren

He gave a short blast on his trumpet.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: strong criticism
examples: Blast for prison governors in judge’s report.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a very happy experience that is a lot of fun
examples: The party was a blast.
We had a blast at the party.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a piece of advertising or information that is sent to a large number of people at the same time by email
examples: They sent out email blasts and posted information on all their websites.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a person or thing from your past that you see, hear, meet, etc. again in the present

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: with the greatest possible volume or power
examples: She had the car stereo on at full blast.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to lose blood, especially from a wound or an injury
examples: My finger's bleeding.
She slowly bled to death.
He was bleeding from a gash on his head.
The small blood vessels in the nose bleed easily.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: (in the past) to take blood from somebody as a way of treating disease

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to force somebody to pay a lot of money over a period of time
examples: The company seems intent on bleeding us for every penny we have.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to remove air or liquid from something so that it works correctly

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to spread from one area of something to another area
examples: Keep the paint fairly dry so that the colours don't bleed into each other.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to take away all somebody’s money
examples: The big corporations are bleeding some of these small countries dry.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not feel sympathy for somebody
examples: ‘I have to go to Brazil on business.’ ‘My heart bleeds for you!’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to mix two or more substances together
examples: Blend the flour with the milk to make a smooth paste.
Blend together the eggs, sugar and flour.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to form a mixture with something
examples: Oil does not blend with water.
Oil and water do not blend.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to combine with something in an attractive or effective way; to combine something in this way
examples: The old and new buildings blend together perfectly.
Their music blends traditional and modern styles.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to produce something by mixing different types together
examples: blended whisky/tea

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that does not attract any attention; to disappear or hideWord Origin

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to ask God to protect somebody/something
examples: They brought the children to Jesus and he blessed them.
God bless you!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something holy by saying a prayer over it
examples: The priest blessed the bread and wine.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to call God holy; to praise God
examples: We bless your holy name, O Lord.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to express surprise
examples: Bless my soul! Here comes Bill!
‘Where's Joe?’ ‘I'm blessed if I know!’ (= I don't know)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have something good such as ability, great happiness, etc.
examples: She's blessed with excellent health.
We're blessed with five lovely grandchildren.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: said to somebody after they have sneezed

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show that you are pleased with somebody, especially because of something they have done
examples: Sarah, bless her, had made a cup of tea.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when you are leaving somebody, to say that you hope they will be safe, etc.
examples: Goodnight, God bless.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: God’s help and protection, or a prayer asking for this
examples: to pray for God’s blessing
The bishop said the blessing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: approval of or permission for something
examples: The government gave its blessing to the new plans.
He went with his parents' blessing.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that is good or helpful
examples: SEE ALSO mixed blessing
Lack of traffic is one of the blessings of country life.
It's a blessing that nobody was in the house at the time.
Her looks turned out to be more of a curse than a blessing.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: something that seems to be a problem at first, but that has good results in the end
examples: Losing your job might turn out to be a blessing in disguise.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be grateful for the good things in your life

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not able to see
examples: Doctors think he will go blind.
She went blind at the age of ten.
blind and partially sighted people
One of her parents is blind.
She has been legally blind since birth.
The accident left her blind in one eye.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: people who are blind
examples: recorded books for the blind
guide dogs for the blind

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not noticing or realizing something
examples: She is blind to her husband's faults.
I must have been blind not to realize the danger we were in.
They seem to be totally blind to reality.
The government is not blind to the fact that the national debt is increasing.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: seeming to be unreasonable, and accepted without question; seeming to be out of control
examples: blind faith/obedience
It was a moment of blind panic.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: that cannot be controlled by reason
examples: blind chance
the blind force of nature

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: that a driver in a car cannot see, or cannot see around
examples: a blind driveway
a blind bend/corner

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: that does not make a difference between people on the basis of the quality mentioned, or favour one group over another
examples: SEE ALSO colour-blind (2)
In a piece of gender-blind casting, Hamlet is played by British actress Maxine Peake.
We are looking to create a more equitable and race-blind society.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: not able to see well
examples: She’s as blind as a bat without her glasses.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a situation in which people with almost no experience or knowledge give advice to others who also have no experience or knowledge

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: when you love somebody, you cannot see their faults

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: not any
examples: He didn't take a blind bit of notice of me (= he ignored me).
It won't make the blindest bit of difference (= it will make no difference at all).

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to pretend not to notice something bad that is happening, so you do not have to do anything about it
examples: The authorities were either unaware of the problem or they turned a blind eye to it.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large piece of a solid material that is square or rectangular in shape and usually has flat sides
examples: SEE ALSO breeze block
The houses are made of concrete blocks with tin roofs.
a block of ice/wood
The wall was made from massive blocks of stone.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a tall building that contains flats or offices; buildings that form part of a school, hospital, etc. which are used for a particular purpose
examples: a block of flats
a tower block
an office block
She lives in a modern apartment block.
the university’s science block

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the length of one side of a piece of land or group of buildings, from the place where one street crosses it to the next
examples: His apartment is three blocks away from the police station.
They walked a few blocks down the street.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a group of buildings with streets on all sides
examples: She took the dog for a walk around the block.
The downtown area covers four city blocks.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a large area of land

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an area of land for building a house on

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a quantity of something or an amount of time that is considered as a single unit
examples: a block of shares
a block of text in a document
The theatre gives discounts for block bookings (= a large number of tickets bought at the same time).
The three-hour class is divided into four blocks of 45 minutes each.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: something that makes movement or progress difficult or impossible
examples: SYNONYM obstacle
Lack of training acts as a block to progress in a career.
I suddenly had a mental block and couldn't remember his name.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a movement that stops another player from going forward

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the two blocks on the ground that runners push their feet against at the beginning of a race

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: (in the past) the piece of wood on which a person’s head was cut off as a punishment
examples: SEE ALSO chopping block (2)

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a person who is very similar to their mother or father in the way that they look or behave

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be sold, especially at an auction (= a sale in which items are sold to the person who offers the most money)

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to have a lot of experience

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to threaten somebody that you will hit them

examples: Despite his six years in politics, he was still regarded by many as the new kid on the block.

examples: This is a link to the museum's blog.

You can read about my trip in my blog.
He writes a blog about living with diabetes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: pale gold in colour
examples: SEE ALSO dirty blonde
She had long blonde hair.
The child had short blond curls and large blue eyes.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having blonde hair
examples: a small, blond boy
A blonde-haired girl walked in.

examples: SEE ALSO first blood
He lost a lot of blood in the accident.
Blood was pouring out of a cut on her head.
His hands were covered in blood.
to give blood (= to have blood taken from you so that it can be used in the medical treatment of other people)
After the attacks, people donated blood in record numbers.

to draw blood (= to wound a person so that they lose blood)
a drop/pool of blood
There was dried blood on her cheek.
a blood cell/sample
to improve blood flow to the heart
the blood supply to the brain

definitions.definition: having the type of blood mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO blue-blooded
cold-blooded reptiles

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: family origins
examples: She is of noble blood.
There is some Polish blood on his father's side.
I doubt if I have a single drop of aristocratic blood in my veins.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a rich and fashionable man
examples: a young blood

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: feelings of hate or strong dislike

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be angry with somebody and want to hurt or punish them

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be a natural part of your character and of the character of other members of your family

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: family relationships are stronger than any others

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: somebody is very angry and ready to argue or fight

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: very hard work; a lot of effort
examples: The only way to succeed is through old-fashioned blood, sweat and tears.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: when you say that somebody is flesh and blood, you mean that they are a normal human with needs, emotions and weaknesses
examples: Listening to the cries was more than flesh and blood could stand.
She wasn't a ghost. She was flesh and blood.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a person that you are related to
examples: You can’t do that to your own flesh and blood!

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to make you extremely frightened or shocked

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be responsible for somebody’s death
examples: a dictator with the blood of thousands on his hands

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: acting in a way that is deliberately cruel
examples: to kill somebody in cold blood

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: almost impossible to obtain
examples: Getting an apology from him was like getting blood from a stone.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to make somebody extremely angry
examples: The way he treats his employees really makes my blood boil.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to make somebody very frightened or fill them with horror
examples: The sound of laughter in the empty house made my blood run cold.
Our blood ran cold at the thought of how easily we could have been killed.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: new members or employees, especially young ones, with new ideas or ways of doing things
examples: This company badly needs to bring in some new blood.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to kill or wound somebody
examples: Nothing can justify spilling innocent blood.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to show that you are very angry; to speak in an angry way
examples: She looked at him with eyes that spat venom.
She surveyed him coldly with eyes that spat venom.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to make somebody excited
examples: The atmosphere in a theatre never failed to stir her blood.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to work very hard
examples: I sweated blood to get everything ready in time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to send out air from the mouth
examples: You're not blowing hard enough!
The policeman asked me to blow into the breathalyser.
He drew on his cigarette and blew out a stream of smoke.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: when the wind or a current of air blows, it is moving; when it blows, the wind is blowing
examples: PAST TENSE OF blow
The birds were singing and a warm wind was blowing.
A cold wind blew from the east.
It was blowing hard.
It was blowing a gale (= there was a strong wind).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be moved by the wind, somebody’s breath, etc.; to move something in this way
examples: My hat blew off.
The door blew open.
I was almost blown over by the wind.
She blew the dust off the book.
The ship was blown onto the rocks.
The bomb blast blew two passers-by across the street.
The wind blew the door shut.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if you blow a whistle, musical instrument, etc. or if a whistle, etc. blows, you produce a sound by blowing into the whistle, etc.
examples: the sound of trumpets blowing
The referee blew his whistle.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to clear your nose by blowing strongly through it into a tissue or handkerchief
examples: She grabbed a tissue and loudly blew her nose.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to kiss your hand and then pretend to blow the kiss towards somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make or shape something by blowing
examples: to blow smoke rings
to blow bubbles (= for example, by blowing onto a thin layer of water mixed with soap)
to blow glass (= to send a current of air into melted glass to shape it)

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if a fuse blows or you blow a fuse, the electricity stops flowing suddenly because the fuse (= a thin wire) has melted because the current was too strong

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to break open or apart, especially because of pressure from inside; to make a tyre break in this way
examples: The car spun out of control when a tyre blew.
The truck blew a tyre and lurched off the road.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to break something open with explosives
examples: The safe had been blown by the thieves.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make known something that was secret
examples: One mistake could blow your cover (= make your real name, job, intentions, etc. known).
We’re going to blow his operation wide open.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to spend or waste a lot of money on something
examples: He inherited over a million dollars and blew it all on drink and gambling.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to waste an opportunity
examples: She blew her chances by arriving late for the interview.
You had your chance and you blew it.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to show that you are annoyed, surprised or do not care about something
examples: Blow it! We've missed the bus.
Well, blow me down! I never thought I'd see you again.
I'm blowed if I'm going to (= I certainly will not) let him treat you like that.
Let's take a taxi and blow (= never mind) the expense.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to leave a place suddenly
examples: Let's blow this joint.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to kill yourself/somebody by shooting yourself/them in the head
examples: He put a gun to his head and threatened to blow his brains out.
While cleaning his shotgun he had accidentally blown his own brains out.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to vomit

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to help somebody have a fresh, lively state of mind again
examples: A brisk walk should blow the cobwebs away.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to get very angry

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to tell something secret, especially by mistake

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to change your opinion about something often

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to produce a very strong feeling of pleasure or shock
examples: SEE ALSO mind-blowing
Wait till you hear this. It'll blow your mind.
a collection of photographs that will blow your mind

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to get rid of your energy, anger or strong emotions by doing something active or noisy
examples: I went for a long walk to let off steam.
I like blowing off steam and I like saying things that shock people.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to destroy somebody/something completely

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to show that somebody/something is not good by being very much better than it/them
examples: I like my old phone, but this new model blows it out of the water.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to praise your own abilities and achievements
examples: SYNONYM boast

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to try to trick somebody or lie to somebody, particularly by saying something is better than it really is

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to surprise or impress somebody very much

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: used by somebody who does not want to do something because it involves too much effort
examples: Sod that for a lark! I'm not doing any more tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to use bombs or other weapons to destroy somebody/something completely
examples: The plane was blown to pieces when the bomb exploded.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to completely destroy somebody/something with an explosion
examples: The truck was blown to kingdom come.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to get very angry

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: if a plan, etc. blows up in your face, it goes badly wrong in a way that causes you damage or makes you feel embarrassed

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to tell somebody in authority about something wrong or illegal that somebody is doing

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: no problem is so bad that it does not bring some advantage to somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to tell people unpleasant facts about something
examples: Her article lifts the lid on bullying in the workplace.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to breathe quickly and loudly through your mouth after physical effort
examples: Eventually, puffing and blowing, he arrived at the gate.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12

examples: the bare bones of the story

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an extra amount of money that is added to a payment, especially to somebody’s wages or salary as a reward
examples: SEE ALSO no-claims bonus
a £100 Christmas bonus
productivity bonuses
the row over bankers' bonuses
What is actually paid will depend on the bonus payments made at the end of the policy.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: anything pleasant that is extra and more or better than you were expecting
examples: Being able to walk to work is an added bonus of the new job.
As a bonus, club members can get free tickets for all the family.
One of the great bonuses of retirement is having time to spare.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a set of printed pages that are fastened inside a cover so that you can turn them and read them
examples: His desk was covered with piles of books.
hardback/paperback books
a book of short stories

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a written work published in printed or electronic form
examples: to read/write/publish a book
reference/children's/library books
a new book by J. K. Rowling
a book about wildlife
He has written a book on local architecture.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a set of sheets of paper that are fastened together inside a cover and used for writing in
examples: SEE ALSO address book
an exercise book
a notebook

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a set of things that are fastened together like a book
examples: a book of stamps/tickets/matches
a chequebook

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the written records of the financial affairs of a business
examples: to do the books (= to check the accounts)
You need to go over the books again; there’s a mistake somewhere.
She does the books for us.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a section of a large written work
examples: the books of the Bible

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a record of bets made on whether something will happen, somebody will win a race, etc.
examples: They’ve opened a book on who’ll win the Championship.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody is pleased/annoyed with you
examples: I'm in her good books at the moment because I cleared up the kitchen.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to punish somebody for doing something wrong and make them explain their behaviour
examples: We will ensure that people who commit fraud are brought to book through the courts.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: following rules and instructions in a very strict way
examples: She always does everything by the book.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to stop doing something because you no longer believe you will be successful or will find a solution
examples: The police have closed the book on the case (= they have stopped trying to solve it).

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a subject or person that you know nothing about
examples: Nuclear physics is a closed book to most of us.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to change facts or figures dishonestly or illegally
examples: His accountant had been cooking the books for years.
Someone was cooking the books.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say that you should not form an opinion about somebody/something from their appearance only

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: every available method, whether it is honest or not
examples: He'll try every trick in the book to stop you from winning.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be reading
examples: She always has her nose in a book.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: the record of great achievements in history
examples: She has earned her place in the history books.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used when you are giving your opinion
examples: That's cheating in my book.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: (to be) on an organization’s list, for example of people who are available for a particular type of work
examples: We have very few nurses on our books at the moment.
Most of the houses on our books are in the north of the city.
We have fifty people on the books.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: if you describe somebody or their life as an open book, you mean that you can easily understand them and know everything about them

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to understand easily what somebody is thinking or feeling

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to be convenient or useful for you/somebody
examples: Well, if you’re honest and hard-working, that suits our book.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to copy somebody’s behaviour and do things in the same way that they do, because they are successful

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to punish somebody who has committed an offence as severely as possible
examples: ‘Get this man down to the station and throw the book at him!’ yelled Curtis.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an arrangement that you make in advance to buy a ticket to travel somewhere, go to the theatre, etc.
examples: COMPARE reservation
a booking form/hall/clerk
Can I make a booking for Friday?
Early booking is recommended.
No advance booking is necessary.
We can't take any more bookings.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an arrangement for somebody to perform at a theatre, in a concert, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an act of the referee writing a player’s name in a book, as a punishment because an offence has been committed

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sudden increase in trade and economic activity; a period of wealth and success
examples: COMPARE slump
Living standards improved rapidly during the post-war boom.
a boom in car sales
a boom year (for trade, exports, etc.)
a property/housing boom

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a period when something such as a sport or a type of music suddenly becomes very popular and successful
examples: The only way to satisfy the golf boom was to build more courses.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a long pole that the bottom of a sail is attached to and that you move to change the position of the sail

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a loud deep sound
examples: the distant boom of the guns

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a floating barrier that is placed across a river or the entrance to a harbour to prevent ships or other objects from coming in or going out

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a long pole that carries a microphone or other equipment

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a situation in which a period of rapid economic growth is followed by one of sudden decline
examples: High house prices encourage boom and bust and leave the economy vulnerable.
Amid the inevitable boom and bust cycle, families are facing pay cuts and job losses.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make something increase, or become better or more successful
examples: to boost exports/profits
to boost productivity/spending
The movie helped boost her screen career.
to boost somebody’s confidence/morale
Getting that job did a lot to boost his ego (= make him feel more confident).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to steal somethingWord Origin
examples: early 19th cent. (originally US, in sense (4)): of unknown origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong shoe that covers the foot and ankle and often the lower part of the leg
examples: SEE ALSO cowboy boot
walking boots
a pair of heavy walking boots
hiking boots
a pair of black leather boots
She wore black knee-high boots.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the space at the back of a car that you put bags, cases, etc. in
examples: SEE ALSO car boot sale
I'll put the luggage in the boot.
Did you lock the boot?
What have you got in the boot?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a quick hard kick
examples: He gave the ball a tremendous boot.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a device that is attached to the wheel of a car that has been parked illegally, so that it cannot be driven away

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be told that you must leave your job or that a relationship you are having with somebody is over
examples: He should have been given the boot years ago.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be/become too proud of yourself; to behave as if you are more important than you really are

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that a situation has changed so that somebody now has power or authority over the person who used to have power or authority over them

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to invite somebody to take as much as they like of something such as food, drink, etc; help yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to do somebody’s job in an acceptable way when they are not there

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to show too much respect for somebody in authority because you want to please them
examples: SYNONYM crawl

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to kick somebody very hard, especially when they are on the ground

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to attack somebody by criticizing them when they are in a difficult situation
examples: I wonder if the press will put the boot in?

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be very frightened or nervous

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to add a comment to something that you have said
examples: He was a vegetarian, and a fussy one to boot.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: very strong and able to deal successfully with difficult conditions or situations
examples: She’s almost 90 but she’s still as tough as old boots.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the line that divides two countries or areas; the land near this line
examples: I live in a small town in the US, near the Canadian border.
Thousands of illegal immigrants cross the border every day.
They took steps to secure the border.
to seal/close the border
They spent a week in a national park on the border between Kenya and Tanzania.
It is difficult to define the border between love and friendship.
The treaty fixed Denmark's new border with Germany.
They fled across the border.
They live just over the border.
The incident happened on Nevada's northern border.
They were stopped at the border.
There are tensions all along the border.
border crossings
border patrols/security/guards
border controls
a border dispute
a border town/village/county
a border region/area

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a long narrow piece around the edge of something such as a picture or a piece of cloth
examples: a pillowcase with a lace border

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a long narrow area of soil which is planted with flowers, along the edge of the grass
examples: The back garden is mostly lawn with herbaceous borders.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling tired and impatient because you have lost interest in somebody/something or because you have nothing to do
examples: There was a bored expression on her face.
She plays the role of a bored housewife.
She was rather bored with her life in a small town.
The children quickly got bored with staying indoors.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be extremely frightened or bored

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: extremely bored
examples: I remember being bored stiff during my entire time at school.
She enjoys it. Everyone else is bored silly.
He walked along, bored out of his mind.
She was alone all day and bored to death.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not interesting; making you feel tired and impatient
examples: He's such a boring man!
a boring job/book/evening
The movie was dreadfully dull and incredibly boring.
The music eventually gets boring to listen to.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to come out of your mother’s body at the beginning of your life
examples: I was born in 1976.
He was born in a small village in northern Spain.
She was born on 7 February 1874.
The baby was born by Caesarean section on Friday.
She was born into a very musical family.
These children were born into poverty.
He was born of/to German parents.
She was born with a rare heart condition.
She was born with a weak heart.
Her brother was born blind (= was blind when he was born).
John Wayne was born Marion Michael Morrison (= that was his name at birth).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to start to exist
examples: the city where the protest movement was born
She acted with a courage born (out) of desperation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: born in the order, way, place, etc. mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO newborn
firstborn
nobly born
French-born
The part is played by an American-born actress.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to behave or do things in a particular manner because it is part of your character
examples: It's not his fault he's so pompous—he was born that way.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have something as your destiny (= what is certain to happen to you) from birth
examples: He was born to be a great composer.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: born and having grown up in a particular place with a particular background and education
examples: He was born and bred in Boston.
I'm a Londoner, born and bred.
I was born and bred in Texas.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: having rich parents

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when you are very surprised at something you have never heard or seen before
examples: I've never heard such nonsense in all my born days.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to say that you are not stupid enough to believe what somebody is telling you
examples: Oh yeah? I wasn't born yesterday, you know.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to have an easy life without realizing how easy it is
examples: You people without kids don't know you're born.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody is very stupid

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: as if something is natural for you and you have done it many times in the past
examples: She adapted to life on the estate as if to the manner born.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take and use something that belongs to somebody else, and return it to them at a later time
examples: COMPARE lend
Can I borrow your umbrella?
Members can borrow up to ten books from the library at any one time.
I borrowed the tools I needed off my brother.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take money from a person or bank and agree to pay it back to them at a later time
examples: COMPARE lend
How much did you have to borrow to pay for this?
The goal is to borrow funds at a low interest rate.
She borrowed £2 000 from her parents.
I don't like to borrow from friends.
The company had borrowed heavily from state-owned banks.
I had to borrow the money off a friend.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to take words, ideas, etc. from another language, person, etc. and use them as your own
examples: The author borrows heavily from Henry James.
His designs borrow freely from the architecture of ancient Egypt.
Some musical terms are borrowed from Italian.
The villain was—to borrow a phrase from Alex—‘all bark and no bite’.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to still be alive after the time when you were expected to die
examples: He’s been living on borrowed time ever since his last heart attack.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be doing something that other people are likely to soon stop you from doing
examples: According to the latest opinion polls, the government is living on borrowed time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who is in charge of other people at work and tells them what to do
examples: I'll ask my boss if I can have the day off.
I like being my own boss (= working for myself and making my own decisions).
Who's the boss (= who's in control) in this house?
He thinks he's impressing the boss by working through lunch.
He accused his former boss of being arrogant.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is in charge of a large organization
examples: the new boss at IBM
Hospital bosses protested at the decision.
Council bosses have agreed to meet a handful of homeowners today.
He's a notorious crime boss.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make it clear to somebody that you have more power and authority than they haveWord Origin
examples: early 19th cent. (originally US): from Dutch baas ‘master’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used with plural nouns to mean ‘the two’ or ‘the one as well as the other’
examples: Both women were French.
Both the women were French.
Both of the women were French.
I talked to the women. Both of them were French/They were both French.
I liked them both.
We were both tired.
Both of us were tired.
We have both seen the movie.
I have two sisters. Both of them live in London/They both live in London.
Both (my) sisters live in London.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not only… but also…
examples: Both his mother and his father will be there.
For this job you will need a good knowledge of both Italian and Spanish.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to spend time and/or energy doing something
examples: ‘Shall I wait?’ ‘No, don't bother’.
I don't know why I bother! Nobody ever listens!
If that’s all the thanks I get, I won’t bother in future!
It's not worth bothering with (= using) an umbrella—the car's just outside.
I don't know why you bother with that crowd (= why you spend time with them).
He doesn’t bother much about his appearance.
He didn't even bother to let me know he was coming.
He hadn't even bothered to read the crucial documents.
Doctors never bothered to check his blood pressure.
Why bother asking if you're not really interested?
I didn't bother trying to explain my feelings.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to annoy, worry or upset somebody; to cause somebody trouble or pain
examples: The thing that bothers me is…
That sprained ankle is still bothering her (= hurting).
She has been bothered by a leg injury.
‘I'm sorry he was so rude to you.’ ‘It doesn't bother me.’
I don't want to bother her with my problems at the moment.
Does it bother you that she earns more than you?
It bothers me to think of her alone in that big house.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to interrupt somebody; to talk to somebody when they do not want to talk to you
examples: Stop bothering me when I'm working.
Let me know if he bothers you again.
Sorry to bother you, but there's a call for you on line two.
Please stop bothering me with all these questions!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to think that somebody/something is important
examples: I'm not bothered about what he thinks.
‘Where shall we eat?’ ‘I'm not bothered.’ (= I don't mind where we go.)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not want to spend time and/or energy doing something
examples: I should really do some work this weekend but I can't be bothered.
All this has happened because you couldn't be bothered to give me the message.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: in a state of worry or stress because you are under too much pressure, have a problem, are trying to hurry, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to not spend time/effort on something, because it is not important or you are not interested in itWord Origin
examples: late 17th cent. (as a noun in the dialect sense ‘noise, chatter’): of Anglo-Irish origin; probably related to Irish bodhaire ‘noise’, bodhraim ‘deafen, annoy’. The verb (originally dialect) meant ‘confuse with noise’ in the early 18th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a glass or plastic container, usually round with straight sides and a narrow neck, used especially for storing liquids
examples: a wine/beer/milk/water bottle
Put the top back on the bottle.
a plastic/glass bottle
To open the bottle, you twist and pull out the stopper.
He threw his message in a bottle into the North Sea.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the amount contained in a bottle
examples: He drank a whole bottle of wine.
He handed me a bottle of beer.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: alcoholic drink
examples: After his wife died, he really hit the bottle (= started drinking heavily).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a bottle used to give milk to a baby; the milk from such a bottle (used instead of mother’s milk)
examples: It's time for her bottle.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: courage or confidence, for example to do something that is dangerous or unpleasant
examples: SYNONYM nerve
It took a lot of bottle to do that.
I didn’t think she’d have the bottle to ask him.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to do something that has a big effect and after which it is very difficult or impossible to go back to how things were before
examples: When guns were invented, the genie was let out of the bottle.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the lowest part of something
examples: OPPOSITE top
the bottom of the screen/stairs/hill
Footnotes are given at the bottom of each page.
The book I want is right at the bottom (= of the pile).
The wind blew through gaps at the top and bottom of the door.
farmers who lived in the valley bottoms

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the part of something that faces downwards and is not usually seen
examples: The bottom of the pan was all sticky.
The ingredients are listed on the bottom of the box

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the lowest surface on the inside of a container
examples: Line the bottom of the cage with newspaper.
I found some coins at the bottom of my bag.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the ground below the water in a lake, the sea, a swimming pool, etc.
examples: I feel safe as long as I can touch the bottom.
He dived in and hit his head on the bottom.
The boat sank to the bottom of the sea.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the lowest position in a class, on a list, etc.; a person, team, etc. that is in this position
examples: When the list came out, my name was near the bottom.
I was always bottom of the class in math.
a battle between the teams at the bottom of the league
You have to be prepared to start at the bottom and work your way up.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the part of the body that you sit on
examples: SYNONYM backside
We sat on our bottoms on the damp grass.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the lower part of a set of clothes that consists of two pieces
examples: COMPARE top
a pair of pyjama/tracksuit bottoms
a bikini bottom

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the part of something that is furthest from you, your house, etc.
examples: There was a stream at the bottom of the garden.
I went to the school at the bottom of our street.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the lower part of a ship that is below the surface of the water
examples: SYNONYM hull

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: having the type of bottom mentioned
examples: a flat-bottomed boat

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say what somebody/something is really like
examples: Their offer to help was at bottom self-centred.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: high up/low down in the structure of an organization or a society
examples: These workers are at the bottom of the economic heap.
