definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be damaged and separated into two or more parts, as a result of force; to damage something in this way
examples: All the windows broke with the force of the blast.
The bag broke under the weight of the bottles inside it.
She dropped the plate and it broke into pieces.
The boat hit a rock and broke in half.
to break a cup/window
She fell off a ladder and broke her arm.
to break a leg/bone
He broke the chocolate in two.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop working as a result of being damaged; to damage something and stop it from working
examples: My watch has broken.
I think I've broken the washing machine.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to cut the surface of the skin and make it bleed
examples: The dog bit me but didn't break the skin.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to do something that is against the law; to not keep a promise, etc.
examples: I had broken the law and deserved to be punished.
People should not be allowed to break the rules.
to break a promise
to break an agreement/a contract/your word
to break an appointment (= not to come to it)
He was breaking the speed limit (= travelling faster than the law allows).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to stop doing something for a while, especially when it is time to eat or have a drink
examples: Let's break for lunch.
Parliament breaks for recess next week.
We broke early and went for a drink.
Their sleep was broken by noise from the street.
We broke our journey in Oxford (= stopped in Oxford on the way to the place we were going to).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to interrupt something so that it ends suddenly
examples: She broke the silence by coughing.
A tree broke his fall (= stopped him as he was falling).
The phone rang and broke my train of thought.
Someone laughed suddenly and the spell was broken.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make something end by using force or strong action
examples: an attempt to break the year-long siege
Management has not succeeded in breaking the strike.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to end a connection with something or a relationship with somebody
examples: He broke all ties with his parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to manage to get away from or out of a position in which they have been caught
examples: He finally managed to break free from his attacker.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to destroy something or make somebody/something weaker; to become weak or be destroyed
examples: to break somebody’s morale/resistance/resolve/spirit
The government was determined to break the power of the trade unions.
The scandal broke him (= ruined his reputation and destroyed his confidence).
She broke under questioning (= was no longer able to bear it) and confessed to everything.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to win a game in which it is your opponent's turn to serve (= hit the ball across the net first)
examples: Williams broke her opponent's serve five times.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel so sad, lonely, etc. that they cannot live a normal life
examples: The death of his wife broke him completely.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to change suddenly, usually after a period when it has been fine
examples: On the third day the weather broke and they had a violent storm.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to show an opening
examples: The clouds broke and the sun came out.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to come up through the surface of water in the sea, a pool, etc.
examples: When his head broke the surface he took in deep gulps of air.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: when the day or dawn or a storm breaks, it begins
examples: SEE ALSO daybreak
Dawn was breaking when they finally left.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: if a piece of news breaks, it becomes known
examples: There was a public outcry when the scandal broke.
breaking news (= news that is arriving about events that have just happened)

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to be the first to tell somebody some bad news
examples: Who's going to break it to her?
I'm sorry to be the one to break the news to you.
Just break the news to her gently.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: if somebody’s voice breaks, it changes its tone because of emotion
examples: Her voice broke as she told us the dreadful news.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: when a boy’s voice breaks, it becomes permanently deeper at about the age of 13 or 14

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to do something better, faster, etc. than anyone has ever done it before
examples: She had broken the world 100 metres record.
The movie broke all box-office records.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: when waves break, they fall and are dissolved into foam, usually near land
examples: the sound of waves breaking on the beach
The sea was breaking over the wrecked ship.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to find the meaning of something secret
examples: to break a code

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to change a banknote for coins
examples: Can you break a twenty-dollar bill?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an occasion when a vehicle or machine stops working
examples: a breakdown on the motorway
a breakdown recovery service
Most breakdown services give priority to women travelling alone.
The national breakdown organizations are on hand to help motorists 24 hours a day.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a failure of a relationship, discussion or system
examples: The only ground for divorce is the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage.
marriage breakdown
There has obviously been a breakdown in communications between the two sides.
The breakdown of the negotiations was not unexpected.
the breakdown of law and order

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: detailed information that you get by studying a set of figures
examples: First, let's look at a breakdown of the costs.
Please provide us with a breakdown of expenditure by department.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the process of a substance breaking into the parts of which it is made
examples: the breakdown of proteins in the digestive system

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a period of mental illness in which somebody becomes very depressed, anxious and tired, and cannot deal with normal life
examples: She's still recovering from her breakdown.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the first meal of the day
examples: SEE ALSO bed and breakfast
They were having breakfast when I arrived.
She doesn't eat much breakfast.
a big/hearty/light breakfast
a cooked breakfast
Do you want bacon and eggs for breakfast?
We had cereal for breakfast.
a bowl of breakfast cereal
Julianne was sitting in the breakfast room, calmly sipping a cup of tea.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that has been done badly
examples: SYNONYM mess
He's made a real dog's breakfast of these accounts.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an important development that may lead to an agreement or achievement
examples: to make/achieve a breakthrough
a significant breakthrough in negotiations
a major breakthrough in cancer research

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: either of the two round soft parts at the front of a woman’s body that produce milk when she has had a baby
examples: She put the baby to her breast.
breast cancer
The protective benefits of breast milk are numerous for both mother and baby.
She had breast-augmentation surgery.
Getting breast implants entails major surgery.
The book promoted the benefits of breast feeding to child health.
She discovered a lump in her breast.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the similar, smaller part on a man’s body, which does not produce milk

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the top part of the front of your body, below your neck
examples: SYNONYM chest
He cradled the child against his breast.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the part of a piece of clothing that covers your chest
examples: A row of medals was pinned to the breast of his coat.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the front part of a bird’s body
examples: breast feathers
The robin has a red breast.
a robin with a red breast

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: meat from the front part of the body of a bird or an animal
examples: chicken/turkey breasts
breast of lamb

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: having the type of chest or breasts mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO double-breasted
a small-breasted/full-breasted woman
bare-breasted
the yellow-breasted male of the species

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the part of the body where the feelings and emotions are thought to be
examples: a troubled breast

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to show that you feel sorry about something that you have done, especially in public and in an exaggerated way

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to tell the truth about something so that you no longer feel guilty
examples: He made a clean breast of everything and admitted taking the money.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the air that you take into your lungs and send out again
examples: His breath smelt of garlic.
bad breath (= that smells bad)
She was very short of breath (= had difficulty breathing).
Patients develop a cough and shortness of breath.
There was a sharp intake of breath in the courtroom.
We had to stop for breath before we got to the top.
While there is breath left in my body, I will refuse.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an amount of air that enters the lungs at one time
examples: Take a deep breath and try to relax.
He recited the whole poem in one breath.
He sucked in a deep breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a small amount of something; slight evidence of something
examples: a breath of suspicion/scandal

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a slight movement of air
examples: It was a still day, without a breath of wind.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: clean air breathed in after being indoors or in a dirty atmosphere
examples: We'll get a breath of fresh air at lunchtime.
I'm going outside for a breath of fresh air.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a person, thing or place that is new and different and therefore interesting and exciting
examples: The new secretary is a breath of fresh air.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an essential part of a person’s existence
examples: Playing the violin has been the breath of life to her for over 20 years.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to stop breathing for a moment because of fear, shock, etc.
examples: When he said he had resigned, I caught my breath in surprise.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to start to be able to breathe normally again after running or doing exercise that makes you tired

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to stop doing something and rest
examples: She talks all the time and hardly stops to draw breath.
He spoke solidly for twenty minutes, barely pausing to draw breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to live; to be alive
examples: He was as kind a man as ever drew breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to breathe normally again after running or doing exercise that makes you tired
examples: I needed a few minutes to get my breath back after the run.
She paused to catch her breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to stop breathing for a short time
examples: Hold your breath and count to ten.
How long can you hold your breath for?

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be nervous while you are waiting for something that you are anxious about
examples: He held his breath while the results were read out.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: people say don’t hold your breath! to emphasize that something will take a long time or may not happen
examples: She said she'd do it this week, but don't hold your breath!

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: immediately after saying something that suggests the opposite intention or meaning
examples: He praised my work and in the same breath told me I would have to leave.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: the last moment of a person’s life

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: having difficulty breathing after exercise
examples: We were out of breath after only five minutes.
I'm a bit out of breath after my run.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that it is not worth wasting time and effort saying something because it will not change anything
examples: Save your breath—you'll never persuade her.
It's useless talking to him—you may as well save your breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to say something quietly so that people cannot hear
examples: ‘Rubbish!’ she muttered under her breath.
He was whispering rude remarks about her under his breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to be very surprising or beautiful
examples: My first view of the island from the air took my breath away.
The sheer audacity of the man took my breath away.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to say something that nobody takes any notice of
examples: You're just wasting your breath. She never listens.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: feeling very anxious or excited
examples: We waited with bated breath for the winner to be announced.
We waited for the decision with bated breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take air into your lungs and send it out again through your nose or mouth
examples: He breathed deeply before speaking again.
The air was so cold we could hardly breathe.
She was beginning to breathe more easily.
He was breathing heavily after his exertions.
Most people don't realize that they are breathing polluted air.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to send air, smoke or a particular smell out of your mouth
examples: He came up close, breathing alcohol fumes all over me.
She rushed into my office breathing fire and threatening me with a lawyer.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to say something quietly
examples: ‘I'm over here,’ she breathed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if you allow wine to breathe, you open the bottle and let air get in before you drink it

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if cloth, leather, skin, etc. can breathe, air can move around or through it
examples: Cotton clothing allows your skin to breathe.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be full of a particular feeling or quality
examples: Her performance breathed wit and charm.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to feel calm again after something unpleasant or frightening has ended
examples: Once he was safely back in prison, she was able to breathe easily again.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to watch closely what somebody is doing in a way that makes them feel anxious and/or annoyed
examples: I can’t get any work done with you breathing down my neck.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to relax and stop worrying
examples: You can rest easy—I'm not going to tell anyone.
I can sleep easy knowing that she's safely home.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to die

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to improve something by introducing new ideas and making people more interested in it
examples: The results of their research have breathed new life into the debate.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be very enthusiastic about something
examples: He just lives and breathes football.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the action of taking air into the lungs and sending it out again
examples: Her breathing became steady and she fell asleep.
Deep breathing exercises will help you relax.
Heavy (= loud) breathing was all I could hear.
Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus went into the house.
The drug is used to treat breathing difficulties caused by asthma.
Are you having difficulty in breathing?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have sex and produce young
examples: SEE ALSO interbreed
Many animals breed only at certain times of the year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to keep animals or plants in order to produce young ones for a particular purpose
examples: SEE ALSO cross-breed
The rabbits are bred for their long coats.
Greyhounds were originally bred as hunting dogs.
the first panda to be bred in captivity
She's a lovely cat. Will you breed from her?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be the cause of something
examples: Nothing breeds success like success.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to educate somebody in a particular way as they are growing up
examples: SEE ALSO well bred
Fear of failure was bred into him at an early age.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: born and having grown up in a particular place with a particular background and education
examples: He was born and bred in Boston.
I'm a Londoner, born and bred.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have a lot of babies in a short space of time
examples: These rodents breed like rabbits.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: knowing somebody/something very well may cause you to lose respect for them/itWord Origin
examples: Old English brēdan ‘produce (offspring), bear (a child)’, of Germanic origin; related to German brüten, also to brood.

a brick wall

examples: Thanks for looking after the children today—you're a real brick.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: Trying to reason with them was like banging my head against a brick wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: very nervous
examples: She was like a cat on hot bricks before her driving test.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: very nervous
examples: She was like a cat on a hot tin roof before her driving test.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: very heavily; very severely
examples: Disappointment hit her like a ton of bricks.
They came down on him like a ton of bricks (= criticized him very severely).

definitions.definition: to try to work without the necessary material, money, information, etc.Word Origin

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a woman on her wedding day, or just before or just after it
examples: a toast to the bride and groom
The bride wore an elegant gown of ivory satin.
He introduced his new bride.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a structure that is built over a road, railway, river, etc. so that people or vehicles can cross from one side to the other
examples: SEE ALSO suspension bridge
We crossed the bridge over the River Windrush.
The river was spanned by a railway bridge.
The plan incudes a pedestrian bridge connecting the arena with the convention centre.
I don't have time to walk across the bridge.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that provides a connection or contact between two different things
examples: SEE ALSO land bridge
The book serves as a bridge between ancient wisdom and modern science.
Cultural exchanges are a way of building bridges between countries.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the part of a ship where the captain and other officers stand when they are controlling the ship
examples: Who was on the bridge when the collision took place?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a card game for two pairs of players who have to predict how many cards they will win. They score points if they succeed in winning that number of cards and lose points if they fail.
examples: SEE ALSO contract bridge
I enjoy a game of bridge occasionally.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the hard part at the top of the nose, between the eyes

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the part of a pair of glasses that rests on your nose

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a small piece of wood on a guitar, violin, etc. over which the strings are stretched

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a false tooth or false teeth, held permanently in place by being fastened to natural teeth on either side

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to encourage good relationships between two groups, countries, etc.
examples: RELATED NOUN bridge-building
The aim of the project was to build bridges between communities through joint events.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to do something that makes it impossible to return to the previous situation later
examples: Think carefully before you resign—you don't want to burn your bridges.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to worry about a problem when it actually happens and not before

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: lasting only a short time; short
examples: a brief visit/meeting/conversation
Mozart's life was brief.
He said nothing during the brief court appearance.
a brief pause/silence
Susan and Mary were enjoying a brief moment of solitude.
He died after a relatively brief period of suffering.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: using few words
examples: a brief description/summary/overview
Please be brief (= say what you want to say quickly).
I will keep my comments brief.
Section 1 of the book gives a brief history of Mexico.
I made a brief introductory statement and our meeting began.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: short and not covering much of the body
examples: a brief skirt

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in a few words, without details
examples: In brief, the meeting was a disaster.
Now the rest of the news in brief.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: for a short time
examples: He had spoken to Emma only briefly.
She met John briefly on Friday night.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in few words
examples: Briefly, the argument is as follows…
Let me tell you briefly what happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: full of light; shining strongly
examples: bright light/sunshine
a bright room
Her eyes were bright with tears.
a bright morning (= with the sun shining)
All of these stars are bigger and brighter than our sun.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: strong and easy to see
examples: I like bright colours.
a bright yellow dress
Jack's face turned bright red.
This colour is a bit bright, isn't it ?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: giving reason to believe that good things will happen; likely to be successful
examples: This young musician has a bright future.
Prospects for the coming year look bright.
a bright start to the week

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: intelligent; quick to learn
examples: the brightest pupil in the class
Do you have any bright ideas (= clever ideas)?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: cheerful and lively
examples: His eyes were bright and excited.

There are some things money can't buy.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to obtain something by losing something else of great value
examples: Her fame was bought at the expense of her marriage.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to believe that something is true, especially something that is not very likely
examples: You could say you were ill but I don't think they'd buy it (= accept the explanation).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the very best
examples: We make sure our clients get the best that money can buy.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have been killed, especially in an accident or a war

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to get back a country's assets, such as land or property, after they have been owned by another country

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to die

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to do something in order to delay an event, a decision, etc.
examples: The negotiators kept the gunman talking to buy time for the hostages.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

examples: Buying from a catalogue can mean buying a pig in a poke.

definitions.label: Meaning 12

examples: the first-class cabin

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: a log cabin

examples: SEE ALSO filing cabinet
kitchen cabinets
a medicine cabinet
The china was displayed in a glass cabinet.

definitions.definition: a set of wires, covered in plastic or rubber, that carries electricity, phone signals, etc.
examples: fibre-optic cable
a power cable
overhead/underground/undersea cables
a 10 000-volt cable

a length of electric cable
They're digging up the road to lay cables.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: thick strong metal rope used on ships, for supporting bridges, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a system of broadcasting television programmes along wires rather than by radio waves
examples: We can receive up to 500 cable channels.
We just had cable installed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a message sent by electrical signals and printed outWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from an Anglo-Norman French variant of Old French chable, from late Latin capulum ‘halter’.

examples: SEE ALSO cybercafe
There are small shops and pavement cafes around every corner.
an outdoor cafe serving drinks and light meals
They were having lunch at a cafe near the station.
We stopped for a coffee in our favourite cafe.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: early 19th cent.: from French café ‘coffee or coffee house’.

examples: SEE ALSO angel food cake
a piece/slice of cake
to make/bake a cake
a chocolate cake
a birthday cake
a cake tin (= for cooking a cake in)
a cake pan
a plate of cream cakes

examples: SEE ALSO cattle cake

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have the advantages of something without its disadvantages; to have both things that are available

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: It’s an added bonus—the icing on the cake.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a thing that is very easy to do

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: Middle English (denoting a small flat bread roll): of Scandinavian origin; related to Swedish kaka and Danish kage.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to use numbers to find out a total number, amount, distance, etc.
examples: SYNONYM work out
An independent valuer will calculate the value of your property.
That figure was calculated using the standard equation.
Use the formula to calculate the volume of the container.
We haven’t really calculated the cost of the vacation yet.
Benefit is calculated on the basis of average weekly earnings.
Expected cancer rates were calculated from data from the eight surrounding counties.
The daily doses were calculated by a somewhat simpler method.
The ratio is calculated by dividing a company's share price by its earnings per share.
You'll need to calculate how much time the assignment will take.
It has been calculated that at least 47 000 jobs were lost last year.
The sum involved was calculated at $82 million.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to guess something or form an opinion by using all the information available
examples: Conservationists calculate that hundreds of species could be lost in this area.
It is impossible to calculate what influence he had on her life.
It's impossible to calculate the extent of his influence on her.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act or process of using numbers to find out an amount
examples: Cathy did a rough calculation.
By my calculation(s), we made a profit of £20 000 last year.
Our guess was confirmed by calculation.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of using your judgement to decide what the results would be of doing something
examples: Decisions are shaped by political calculations.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: careful planning for yourself without caring about other people
examples: an act of cold calculation

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give somebody/something a particular name; to use a particular name or title when you are talking to somebody
examples: SEE ALSO so-called
They decided to call the baby Mark.
His name's Hiroshi but everyone calls him Hiro.
What's their son called?
I don't know anyone called Scott.
I've forgotten what the firm he works for is called.
What's it called again? Oh yes, a router.
to be commonly/often called something
This group of artists and poets is sometimes called the New York School.
They called their first daughter after her grandmother.
The cheese is called after the town of the same name.
We call each other by our first names here.
The plant is called by different names in different parts of the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to phone somebody
examples: SEE ALSO cold-call
I'll call again later.
I got a message to call home immediately.
I called the office to tell them I'd be late.
People called to ask how they could help.
My brother called me from Spain last night.
Call us toll-free on this number.
Call 0800 33344 for a free copy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to ask somebody/something to come quickly to a particular place by phoning
examples: Someone called the police.
to call an ambulance/a doctor
I'll call a taxi for you.
I'll call you a taxi.
Fire crews were called to the building at 9 p.m.
The doctor has been called to an urgent case.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to describe somebody/something in a particular way; to consider somebody/something to be something
examples: I wouldn't call German an easy language.
Are you calling me a liar?
She now calls Southern California home (= she lives there).
He was in the front room, or the lounge or whatever you want to call it.
I make it ten pounds forty-three you owe me. Let's call it ten pounds.
They call themselves ‘The Gang’.
Would you call it blue or green?
You could hardly call the show perfect, but it was successful.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to claim that you are a particular type of person, especially when other people question whether this is true
examples: Call yourself a friend? So why won't you help me, then?
She's no right to call herself a feminist.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to shout or say something loudly to attract somebody’s attention
examples: I thought I heard somebody calling.
She called out to her father for help.
Someone called to him to wait.
Did somebody call my name?
People in the audience called out requests.
‘See you later!’ she called.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to ask somebody to come by shouting or speaking loudly
examples: Will you call the kids in for lunch?
He heard me call him and came to the door.
Did you call?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to order somebody to come to a place
examples: Several candidates were called for a second interview.
The ambassador was called back to London by the prime minister.
He felt called to the priesthood (= had a strong feeling that he must become a priest).
You may be called to give evidence.
She was called to testify before a Senate subcommittee.
The defence says it plans to call four witnesses.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to order something to happen; to announce that something will happen
examples: to call a meeting/strike
The prime minister has called an election for 8 June.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make a short visit to a person or place
examples: I'll call round and see you on my way home.
Let's call on John.
He was out when I called to see him.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make the noise that is typical for it
examples: The cuckoo called across the trees to its mate.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to predict what the result of something will be
examples: It's a very open game that is very hard to call.
to be difficult/impossible to call
The result of this election is going to be too close to call.
Most media pundits called it for the Conservatives.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to say which side of a coin you think will face upwards after it is thrown
examples: to call heads/tails

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to shout out the steps for people performing a square dance or country dance

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to remember somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM recall
She couldn't call to mind where she had seen him before.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to remind you of somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM recall
The painting brings to mind some of Picasso's early works.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to tell somebody to do what they are threatening to do, because you believe that they will not be cruel or brave enough to do it
examples: She was tempted to call his bluff, hardly able to believe he’d carry out his threat.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to make use of something
examples: Chess is a game that calls into play all your powers of concentration.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to doubt something or make others doubt something
examples: SYNONYM question
His honesty has never been called into question.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to decide or agree to stop doing something
examples: After forty years in politics I think it's time for me to call it a day (= to retire).

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to agree to end a contest, argument, etc. because both sides seem equal

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to decide to stop doing something

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to use offensive words about somebody
examples: Stop calling me names!

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to be the person who controls a situation

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to say exactly what you think without trying to hide your opinion
examples: I believe in calling a spade a spade.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to say or decide that it is time for something to finish

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to make somebody explain a mistake, etc. because they are responsible for it

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to ask people in a meeting to be quiet so that the meeting can start or continue

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to order somebody to obey the formal rules of a meeting; to start a formal meeting
examples: The argument continued until the chairman called them both to order.
The president brought the meeting to order at 9.15 a.m.
As the meeting was brought to order, the councillor immediately stood and began to protest.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: the person who provides the money for something can also control how it is spent

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: called to see somebody in authority because you have done something wrong
examples: I got called on the carpet for being late.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: used to say that you should not criticize somebody for a fault that you have yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: used instead of a name that you cannot remember
examples: She's just gone out with old what-d'you-call-him.

definitions.label: Meaning 10

All remarks should be addressed to the chair.
She takes the chair in all our meetings.
the chair of the committee
He was elected chair of the city council.
The chairs of all the subcommittees will meet on Friday.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the position of being in charge of a department in a university
examples: He holds the chair of philosophy at Oxford.
the department chair

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (especially in the US) a chair in which criminals are killed by having a powerful electric current passed through their bodies; the method of execution that uses this chairWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French chaiere (modern chaire ‘bishop's throne, etc.’, chaise ‘chair’), from Latin cathedra ‘seat’, from Greek kathedra. Compare with cathedral.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the person in charge of a meeting, who tells people when they can speak, etc.
examples: Sir Herbert took it upon himself to act as chairman.
The motion was carried on the casting vote of the chairman.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the person in charge of a committee, a company, etc.
examples: the vice/deputy chairman
the committee/board/party/club chairman
the chairman of the committee/board/party/club
the executive chairman
He then served as chairman of the Civil Aviation Authority.
The chairman of the company presented the annual report.
He became chairman and CEO of the corporation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a new or difficult task that tests somebody’s ability and skill
examples: a tough/major/significant challenge
The role will be the biggest challenge of his acting career.
She still faces many challenges (= has to deal with them).
Destruction of the environment is one of the most serious challenges we face.
The greatest challenge facing the region is unemployment.
Rapid industrialization presents both challenges and opportunities.
Countries need to work together to address the challenge of climate change.
Schools must meet the challenge of new technology (= deal with it successfully).
I’m looking forward to the challenge of my new job.
The gallery has risen to the challenge of exhibiting the works of young artists.
The challenge for the government is to find a way of providing affordable housing.
Digital piracy continues to pose huge challenges to the industry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an invitation or a suggestion to somebody that they should enter a competition, fight, etc.
examples: She accepted his challenge to a debate on the issue.
I'm looking forward to taking on the challenge.
He plans to mount a challenge for the party leadership.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a statement or an action that shows that somebody refuses to accept something and questions whether it is right, legal, etc.
examples: Their legal challenge was unsuccessful.
It was a direct challenge to the president's authority.
The commission reconsidered the rules after a challenge from the television networks.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: difficult in an interesting way that tests your ability
examples: challenging work/questions/problems
I have had a challenging and rewarding career as a teacher.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: done in a way that invites people to disagree or argue with you, or shows that you disagree with them
examples: She gave him a challenging look. ‘Are you really sure?’ she demanded.
Dealing with challenging behaviour in school is never easy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a hall in a public building that is used for formal meetings
examples: SEE ALSO Chamber of Commerce
The members left the council chamber.
the Senate/House chamber

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one of the parts of a parliament
examples: the Lower/Upper Chamber (= in Britain, the House of Commons/House of Lords)
The party has gained more seats in the Chamber of Deputies in the Italian parliament.
Under Senate rules, the chamber must vote on the bill by this Friday.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a room used for the particular purpose that is mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO decompression chamber
a Bronze Age burial chamber

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a space in the body, in a plant or in a machine that is separated from the rest
examples: the chambers of the heart
the rocket’s combustion chamber
the chamber of a gun (= the part that holds the bullets)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a space under the ground that is almost completely closed on all sides
examples: SEE ALSO echo chamber
They found themselves in a vast underground chamber.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a bedroom or private room
examples: Lady Eleanor was found dead in her chamber.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person, team, etc. that has won a competition, especially in a sport
examples: the world/European/national/Olympic champion
the defending champion (= the person who was champion the last time and is trying to be champion again)
the reigning champion (= the person who is champion now)
the world basketball champions
a champion sprinter/boxer/swimmer
He became the youngest US Open champion for 88 years.
the heavyweight champion of the world
a former Italian champion jockey
the Commonwealth Games champion in the 5,000 metres
They were champions at the Winter Olympics in Chamonix.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who fights for, or speaks in support of, a group of people or a belief
examples: She was a champion of the poor all her life.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a competition to find the best player or team in a particular sport
examples: the National Basketball Association Championship
He won a silver medal at the European Championships.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the position of being a champion
examples: They've held the championship for the past two years.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the football (soccer) league in England and Wales that has the second best teams in it, after the Premier League

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a possibility of something happening, especially something that you want
examples: She only has a slim chance of passing the exam.
Is there any chance of getting tickets for tonight?
There's a good chance that he'll be back in time.
There is no chance that he will change his mind.
What chance is there of anybody being found alive?
There is little chance of that happening.
The operation has a fifty-fifty chance of success.
Nowadays a premature baby has a very good chance of survival.
Not wearing a helmet could increase your chance of injury.
The Met Office said there was an 80 per cent chance of severe weather.
Now that he's met the love of his life, he finally has a chance at real happiness.
We believe the plan has a good chance for success.
They are the one team with a chance of beating us.
an outside chance (= a very small one)
The chances are a million to one against being struck by lightning.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a suitable time or situation when you have the opportunity to do something
examples: It was the chance she had been waiting for.
Jeff deceived me once already—I won't give him a second chance.
This is your big chance (= opportunity for success).
We won't get another chance of a holiday this year.
Please give me a chance to explain.
You'll have the chance to ask questions at the end.
The team missed their chance to win the cup.
Tonight is your last chance to catch the play at your local theatre.
He jumped at the chance to go back to Australia.
He realized that this might be his only chance to save himself.
There will be a chance for parents to look around the school.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an unpleasant or dangerous possibility
examples: When installing electrical equipment don't take any chances. A mistake could kill.
The car might break down but that's a chance we'll have to take.
The producers didn't want to take a chance on an unknown actor.
The police were taking no chances with the protesters.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the way that some things happen without any cause that you can see or understand
examples: I met her by chance (= without planning to) at the airport.
Chess is not a game of chance.
It was pure chance that we were both there.
We'll plan everything very carefully and leave nothing to chance.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: happening in a way that was lucky, although it was not planned
examples: As chance would have it, John was going to London too, so I went with him.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have the possibility of succeeding or achieving something
examples: ‘Do you think we'll win?’ ‘I think we're in with a chance.’
He's in with a good chance of passing the exam.
After a poor start, they are now in with a chance of winning the league.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used especially in questions, to ask whether something is true, possible, etc.
examples: Are you in love with him, by any chance?
Are you by any chance Mr Ludd?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: it is likely that…
examples: The chances are you won't have to pay.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: people say chance would be a fine thing to show that they would like to do or have the thing that somebody has mentioned, but that they do not think that it is very likely

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used for saying that you do not believe something is likely to happen
examples: ‘They might let us in without tickets.’ ‘Fat chance of that!’
Fat chance of him helping you!

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a small chance of being successful if a great effort is made
examples: We still have a fighting chance of beating them and winning the Cup.
If you win this round then you still have a fighting chance.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to give somebody/something some opportunity to do something
examples: That dog will give you a nasty bite, given half a chance.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be equally likely to do or not do something
examples: She has more than an even chance of winning tomorrow.
There’s an even chance that the jury will find him guilty.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: there is no possibility
examples: ‘Do you think he'll do it?’ ‘No chance.’

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to have no chance at all

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to have no chance at all
examples: He hasn't a dog's chance of passing the exam.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to have no chance at all
examples: There isn't a snowball's chance in hell that I'll wear that thing!

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: because of the possibility of something happening, although it is unlikely
examples: I didn't think you'd be at home but I just called by on the off chance.
She scanned the crowd on the off chance of seeing someone she knew.
I called in at the office on the off chance that you would still be there.
I rang the company just on the off chance that they might have a vacancy.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: a reasonable chance of success

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to have the possibility of succeeding or achieving something
examples: The driver didn't stand a chance of stopping in time.
He doesn't stand a chance of winning against such an experienced player.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to decide to do something, knowing that it might be the wrong choice
examples: We took a chance on the weather and planned to have the party outside.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to take a risk or to use the opportunities that you have and hope that things will happen in the way that you want
examples: He took his chances and jumped into the water.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: with the hope of using a particular situation in order to gain some advantage for yourselfWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French cheance, from cheoir ‘fall, befall’, based on Latin cadere.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become different
examples: SEE ALSO unchanging
Rick hasn't changed. He looks exactly the same as he did at school.
We examined changing attitudes towards education.
The company failed to adapt to changing circumstances.
Things have changed dramatically since then.
Her life changed completely when she won the lottery.
My attitude to life has changed with age.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something different
examples: Fame hasn't really changed him.
That experience changed my life.
The internet has changed the way people work.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to pass from one state or form into another; to make somebody/something pass from one state or form into another
examples: Wait for the traffic lights to change.
The lights changed from red to green.
The lights changed to green.
Caterpillars change into butterflies.
With a wave of her magic wand, she changed the frog into a handsome prince.
He managed to change the mood from tense to relaxed in minutes.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to stop having one state, position or direction and start having another
examples: Leaves change colour in autumn.
The wind has changed direction.
Our ship changed course.
The fruit changes colour as it ripens.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to replace one thing, person, service, etc. with something new or different
examples: I want to change my doctor.
I didn't change my name when I got married.
That back tyre needs changing.
We change our car every two years.
The law was changed in 2001.
Don't change the subject!
We changed the car for a bigger one.
She changed her name to his.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to exchange positions, places, etc. with somebody else, so that you have what they have, and they have what you have
examples: At half-time the teams change ends.
We asked the waiter if we could change tables.
Can I change seats with you?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to exchange money into the money of another country
examples: I need to change some euros.
to change dollars into yen

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to exchange money for the same amount in different coins or notes
examples: Can you change a £20 note?
The storekeeper changed my dollar bill for four quarters.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to exchange something that you have bought for something else, especially because there is something wrong with it; to give a customer a new item because there is something wrong with the one they have bought
examples: This shirt I bought's too small—I'll have to change it for a bigger one.
Of course we'll change it for a larger size, Madam.
If you bring the dress back with the receipt, you can change it.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to go from one bus, train, etc. to another in order to continue a journey
examples: Where do I have to change?
Change at Reading (for London).
I stopped in Moscow only to change planes.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to put on different or clean clothes
examples: I went into the bedroom to change.
She changed into her swimsuit.
You need to change out of those wet things.
I didn't have time to change clothes before the party.
I didn't have time to get changed before the party (= to put different clothes on).

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to put clean clothes or a clean nappy on a baby
examples: She can't even change a nappy.
The baby needs changing.
There are baby changing facilities in all our stores.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to put clean sheets, etc. on a bed
examples: to change the sheets
Could you help me change the bed?

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to pass to a different owner
examples: The house has changed hands several times.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to change to a different or new activity while you are in the middle of something else; to change from supporting one person or thing to another

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to change a decision or an opinion
examples: Nothing will make me change my mind.
What made you change your mind?

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to be in somebody else’s situation
examples: I'm perfectly happy—I wouldn't change places with anyone.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to express a different opinion or behave in a different way when your situation changes
examples: Wait until it happens to him—he'll soon change his tune.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to start to live or behave in a different way from before
examples: He was in trouble with the police as a teenager but now he’s completely changed his ways.
Your father is unlikely to change his ways now.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to keep changing your mind or what you are doing

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: people cannot change their character, especially if they have a bad character
examples: You didn’t really expect her to be on time, did you? A leopard can’t change its spots.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a television station
examples: SEE ALSO pay channel
a television/TV channel
cable/digital/satellite channels
a news channel
a music/sports/movie channel
to change/switch channels
What's on Channel 4 tonight?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a band of radio waves used for making television or radio broadcasts
examples: radio channels
terrestrial/satellite channels

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a method or system that people use to get information, to communicate, or to send something somewhere
examples: SEE ALSO blue channel
Complaints must be made through the proper channels.
The newsletter is a useful channel of communication between teacher and students.
The company has worldwide distribution channels.
Steps are being taken to implement a ceasefire through diplomatic channels.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a means by which data is communicated and exchanged between elements of a computer system or other system
examples: an audio channel

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a way of expressing ideas and feelings
examples: The campaign provided a channel for protest against the war.
Music is a great channel for releasing your emotions.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a passage that water can flow along, especially in the ground, on the bottom of a river, etc.
examples: drainage channels in the rice fields

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a deep passage of water in a river or near the coast that can be used as route for ships

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a passage of water that connects two areas of water, especially two seas
examples: the Bristol Channel

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the area of sea between England and France, also known as the English Channel
examples: SEE ALSO the English Channel
the Channel Tunnel
cross-Channel ferries
news from across the Channel (= from France)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a complete lack of order
examples: economic/political/domestic chaos
Heavy snow has caused total chaos on the roads.
The house was in chaos after the party.
The country was thrown/plunged into chaos by the president's death.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a separate section of a book, usually with a number or title
examples: to read/write a chapter
He devotes an entire chapter to this topic.
I've just finished Chapter 3.
I read chapter after chapter of the book.
in the previous/next/first/last chapter
in a later chapter
There is a useful summary at the end of the chapter.
the final chapter of her autobiography
the opening chapter of the book
the most interesting chapter in the book
Have you read the chapter on the legal system?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a period of time in a person’s life or in history
examples: a difficult chapter in our country’s history
Her return to Kansas ended a particularly unhappy chapter in her life.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: all the priests of a cathedral or members of a religious community
examples: a meeting of the dean and chapter

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a local branch of a society, club, etc.
examples: the local chapter of the Rotary club

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the exact details of something, especially the exact place where particular information may be found
examples: I can't give chapter and verse, but that's the rough outline of our legal position.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a series of unpleasant events caused by bad luck
examples: The whole affair has been a chapter of accidents from start to finish.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or an animal in a book, play or film
examples: SEE ALSO non-player character
the main character in the film
a major/minor character in the book
Who plays the main character?
He loves to draw and create his own cartoon characters.
Clint Eastwood's character is the most sympathetic in the movie.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a particular type of person in a play, film or TV show
examples: He has developed a skill set from his character work in film,TV and stage.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: all the qualities and features that make a person different from others
examples: SEE ALSO acquired characteristic
to have a strong/weak character
character traits
character defects
The book gives a fascinating insight into Mrs Obama's character.
Generosity is part of the American character.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: strong personal qualities such as the ability to deal with difficult or dangerous situations
examples: Everyone admires her strength of character and determination.
He showed great character returning to the sport after his accident.
Adventure camps are considered to be character-building (= meant to improve somebody's strong qualities).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the way that something is; a particular quality or feature that a thing, an event or a place has
examples: SYNONYM nature
The character of the neighbourhood hasn't changed at all.
I love the delicate character of the light in the evening.
The police pointed out the illegal character of the protest action.
buildings that are very simple in character

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the interesting or unusual quality that a place or a person has
examples: The modern hotels here have no real character.
a face with a lot of character

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a person, particularly an unpleasant or strange one
examples: There were some really strange characters hanging around the bar.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: an interesting or unusual person
examples: She's a character!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the opinion that people have of you, particularly of whether you can be trusted or relied on
examples: She was a victim of character assassination (= an unfair attack on the good opinion people had of her).
a slur/attack on his character
My teacher agreed to be a character witness for me in court.
a character reference (= a letter that a person who knows you well writes to an employer to tell them about your good qualities)

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a letter, sign, mark or symbol used in writing, in printing or on computers
examples: These are the Chinese characters meaning ‘wind’ and ‘water’.
This size of type produces a line 30 characters long.
optical character recognition
The URL contained non-standard characters like question marks.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: typical/not typical of a person’s character
examples: Her behaviour last night was completely out of character.
The lawyer argued that his client's violent behaviour was out of character.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: in the same style as something
examples: The new wing of the museum was not really in character with the rest of the building.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a typical feature or quality that something/somebody has
examples: There were few similarities in the brothers' physical characteristics.
All human languages share some common characteristics.
The two groups of children have quite different characteristics.
Personal characteristics, such as age and sex are taken into account.
genetic characteristics
The need to communicate is a key characteristic of human society.
a defining characteristic of contemporary American culture

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be typical of a person, place or thing
examples: the rolling hills that characterize this part of England
The city is characterized by tall modern buildings in steel and glass.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to describe or show the qualities of somebody/something in a particular way
examples: How would you characterize the mood of the 1990s?
activities that are characterized as ‘male’ or ‘female’ work

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the amount of money that somebody asks for goods and services
examples: SEE ALSO the community charge
admission charges
We have to make a small charge for refreshments.
Delivery is free of charge.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a charge account
examples: Would you like to put that on your charge?
‘Are you paying cash?’ ‘No, it'll be a charge.’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a position of having control over somebody/something; responsibility for somebody/something
examples: She has charge of the day-to-day running of the business.
He took charge of the farm after his father's death.
They left the au pair in charge of the children for a week.
I'm leaving the school in your charge.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person that you have responsibility for and care for

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an official claim made by the police that somebody has committed a crime
examples: criminal charges
a murder/an assault charge
a charge of theft/rape/attempted murder
He will be sent back to England to face a charge of (= to be on trial for) armed robbery.
Both men deny the charges.
They decided to drop the charges against the newspaper and settle out of court.
After being questioned by the police, she was released without charge.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a statement accusing somebody of doing something wrong or bad
examples: SYNONYM allegation
She rejected the charge that the story was untrue.
Be careful you don't leave yourself open to charges of political bias.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the amount of electricity that is put into a battery or carried by a substance
examples: a positive/negative charge

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the act of putting electricity into a battery; the electricity in a battery
examples: He put his phone on charge.
My laptop had run out of charge.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a sudden rush or violent attack, for example by soldiers, wild animals or players in some sports
examples: He led the charge down the field.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the amount of explosive needed to fire a gun or make an explosion
examples: SEE ALSO depth charge

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: the power to cause strong feelings
examples: the emotional charge of the piano piece
a film in which every scene carries an emotional charge

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a task or duty
examples: His charge was to obtain specific information.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to accuse somebody formally of a crime so that there can be a trial in court
examples: Police have brought a charge of dangerous driving against the man.
Many victims of crime are reluctant to press charges against their attackers.
She laid charges against the firm for not complying with the regulations.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to get a strong feeling of excitement or pleasure from something
examples: I get a real charge out of working hard and seeing good results.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be the first to make the effort to do something new
examples: Denmark, Norway and Sweden are united in leading the charge to a cash-free economy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an organization for helping people in need
examples: a registered charity
the UK's largest children's charity
Many charities sent money to help the victims of the famine.
The concert will raise money for local charities.
My parents always supported charities.
a charity for homeless people
a charity for earthquake relief in Pakistan

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: organizations for helping people in need, considered as a group; the money, food, help, etc. that they give
examples: Most of the runners in the London Marathon are raising money for charity.
A portion of the proceeds was donated to charity.
Do you give much to charity?
a charity event (= organized to get money for charity)
All the profits go to charity.
a charity auction/concert/football match
She does a lot of charity work.
to live on/off charity (= to live on money which other people give you because you are poor)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: kind behaviour and sympathy towards other people, especially when you are judging them
examples: Her article showed no charity towards her former friends.
He replied patiently, with more charity than I deserved.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: you should help and care for your own family, etc. before you start helping other peopleWord Origin
examples: late Old English (in the sense ‘Christian love of one's fellows’): from Old French charite, from Latin caritas, from carus ‘dear’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the power of pleasing or attracting people
examples: He was a man of great charm.
The hotel is full of charm and character.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a feature or quality that is pleasant or attractive
examples: her physical charms (= her beauty)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a small object worn on a chain or bracelet that is believed to bring good luck
examples: a lucky charm
a charm bracelet

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an act or words believed to have magic power
examples: SYNONYM spell

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used when you have failed to do something twice and hope that you will succeed the third time

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be immediately and completely successful
examples: Those new pills you gave me worked like a charm.
Her strategy worked like a charm.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very pleasant or attractive
examples: The cottage is tiny, but it's charming.
She's a charming person.
What a charming name.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to show that you have a low opinion of somebody’s behaviour
examples: They left me to tidy it all up myself. Charming, wasn't it?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a diagram, lists of figures, etc. that shows information
examples: SEE ALSO bar chart
Some shares have lost two-thirds of their value since being issued (see chart).
The charts of 138 patients with chronic heart failure were reviewed.
The accompanying chart shows data for eight countries.
a sales chart (= showing the level of a company’s sales)
an astrological chart
a weather chart
comparative charts of prices of food items now and in 2012
Gas prices have risen over the past decade, as shown in the chart below.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a detailed map of the sea
examples: a naval chart

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a list, produced each week, of the songs or albums that have sold the most copies or been downloaded or listened to via streaming the most frequently
examples: The album went straight into the charts at number 1.
to top the charts (= to be the song or album that has sold more copies than all the others)
a chart hit

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: extremely high in level
examples: World demand for the product is off the charts.
Enthusiasm for the project soared off the charts.
The wealth to be found in this town is off the charts.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a written statement describing the rights that a particular group of people should have
examples: the European Social Charter of workers’ rights
a rail passenger’s charter
a charter of rights for people with disabilities

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a written statement of the principles and aims of an organization
examples: SYNONYM constitution
the United Nations Charter

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an official document stating that a government or political leader allows a new organization, town or university to be established and gives it particular rights
examples: The Royal College received its charter as a university in 1967.
Certain towns were allowed to hold weekly markets, by royal charter.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a law or policy that seems likely to help people do something bad
examples: The new law will be a charter for unscrupulous financial advisers.
a blackmailer’s charter

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the hiring of a plane, boat, etc.
examples: a yacht available for charter

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to run, drive, etc. after somebody/something in order to catch them or it
examples: My dog likes chasing rabbits.
The kids chased each other around the kitchen table.
We were chased by a bull while crossing the field.
He chased after the burglar but couldn't catch him.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to force somebody/something to run away
examples: Chase the cat out—we don't want her in the kitchen.
This particular fish chases off any other fish that enters its territory.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to try to obtain or achieve something, for example money, work or success
examples: Too many people are chasing too few jobs nowadays.
The team is chasing its first win in five games.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to try to persuade somebody to have a sexual relationship with you
examples: Kevin's been chasing after Joan for months.
Girls are always chasing him.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to persuade somebody to do something that they should have done already
examples: I need to chase him about organizing the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to rush or hurry somewhere
examples: I've been chasing around town all morning looking for a present for Sharon.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to cut patterns or designs on metal
examples: chased silver

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be very busy but in fact achieve very littleWord Origin
examples: verb senses 1 to 5 Middle English: from Old French chacier (verb), chace (noun), based on Latin captare ‘continue to take’, from capere ‘take’. verb sense 6 late Middle English: apparently from earlier enchase, from Old French enchasser.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to talk in a friendly, informal way to somebody
examples: I'm sorry I can't stop to chat.
My wife and his wife got chatting (= started chatting).
My kids spend hours chatting on the phone to their friends.
Within minutes of being introduced they were chatting away like old friends.
Everyone here chats away to you as though they've known you for decades.
What were you chatting about?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to exchange messages with somebody on the internet, when you can see and reply to messages immediately and have a written conversation
examples: I've been chatting online with my best friend.
I use social media to chat about stuff as well.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: costing little money or less money than you expected
examples: SYNONYM inexpensive
cheap imports/flights
Their cheap prices have helped them pick up new customers.
They're offering incredibly cheap fares to Eastern Europe.
Cycling is a cheap way to get around.
A good education is not cheap.
Electricity is relatively cheap in Ireland.
The device isn't exactly cheap at £500.
A falling dollar will boost the economy by making exports cheaper.
a cheaper alternative/option
Renewable energy is getting cheaper all the time.
The cheapest rates are usually available online.
immigrant workers, used as a source of cheap labour (= workers who are paid very little, especially unfairly)
Game shows are cheap to produce.
Why go by train when it's so cheap to hop on a plane?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: charging low prices
examples: OPPOSITE expensive
a cheap restaurant/hotel
a cheap taxi firm
We found a cheap and cheerful cafe (= one that is simple and charges low prices but is pleasant).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: low in price and quality
examples: cheap perfume/jewellery/shoes
cheap plastic toys that break within seconds
a cheap and nasty bottle of wine

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: unpleasant or unkind and rather obvious
examples: I was tired of his cheap jokes at my expense.
a comedian who is always looking for cheap laughs
to score a cheap political advantage
He couldn't resist taking a cheap shot at his political opponent.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: having a low status and therefore not deserving respect
examples: He's just a cheap crook.
His treatment of her made her feel cheap (= ashamed, because she had lost her respect for herself).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not liking to spend money
examples: Don't be so cheap!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: so good or useful that the cost does not seem too much
examples: To buy all the recommended equipment is expensive, but as an investment for the future it is cheap at the price.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that there is a situation in which it is not thought to be important if people somewhere die or are treated badly

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: spending less money than you usually need to spend to do something
examples: a guide to decorating your house on the cheap
to acquire valuable works of art on the cheap
The school managed to get a couple of computers on the cheap.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to trick somebody or make them believe something that is not true
examples: She is accused of attempting to cheat the taxman.
We will crack down on people who try to cheat the system.
Many people feel cheated by the election process.
He cheated investors out of billions of dollars.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to act in a dishonest way in order to gain an advantage, especially in a game, a competition, an exam, etc.
examples: He cheats at cards.
Have you ever cheated in an exam?
Have you ever cheated on an exam?
You're not allowed to look at the answers—that's cheating.
Anyone caught cheating will be automatically disqualified from the examination.
Why would anyone want to lie or cheat?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have a secret sexual relationship with somebody else
examples: He’s cheating on his wife.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to survive in a situation where you could have diedWord Origin
