definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to examine something to see if it is correct, safe or acceptable
examples: She gave me the minutes of the meeting to read and check.
Check the oil and water before setting off.
Check your work before handing it in.
Customs officers have the right to check all luggage going through customs.
The cars were checked to see whether the faults had been spotted.
Check the container for cracks or leaks.
Be sure to check labels for specific information.
I'll need to check these figures against last year's.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to look at something or ask somebody to find out if something/somebody is present, correct or true or if something is how you think it is
examples: SEE ALSO cross-check
We'll check back in a couple of hours.
We were interrupted by a waiter checking to see if everything was OK.
‘Is Mary in the office?’ ‘Just a moment. I'll go and check.’
Hang on—I just need to check my email.
She's constantly checking her phone—it drives me mad.
Check our website for details.
Go and check (that) I’ve locked the windows.
Check with your doctor before beginning any exercise programme.
She glance around to check whether anyone was watching.
You'd better check with Jane what time she's expecting us tonight.
The data is then checked against a database of criminals.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to put a mark (✓) next to an item on a list, an answer, etc.
examples: Check the box next to the right answer.
To take advantage of this extra bonus offer, simply check the box on your order form.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to control something; to stop something from increasing or getting worse
examples: The government is determined to check the growth of public spending.
She tied some strips of cloth around the wound to check the bleeding.
The active ingredient checks the growth of bacteria.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to stop yourself from saying or doing something or from showing a particular emotion
examples: to check your anger/laughter/tears
She made no effort to check her tears and just let them run down her face.
She wanted to tell him the whole truth but she checked herself—it wasn't the right moment.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to leave coats, bags, etc. in an official place (called a checkroom) while you are visiting a club, restaurant, etc.
examples: Do you want to check your coats?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to leave bags or cases with an official so that they can be put on a plane or train
examples: How many bags are you checking?

Couples were dancing cheek to cheek.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the type of cheeks mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO apple-cheeked
chubby-cheeked/rosy-cheeked/hollow-cheeked

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: either of the buttocks

I think they've got a cheek making you pay to park the car.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: when a liquid, gas or air circulates or is circulated, it moves continuously around a place or system
examples: The condition prevents the blood from circulating freely.
Cooled air is circulated throughout the building.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: if a story, an idea, information, etc. circulates or if you circulate it, it spreads or it is passed from one person to another
examples: Rumours began to circulate about his financial problems.
There's a story circulating around the office that you are about to leave the company.
newspapers circulating among minority communities
Who has been circulating these rumours?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to send goods or information to all the people in a group
examples: They circulated a petition for his release.
The book was circulated widely in Russia.
The document will be circulated to all members.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to move around a group, especially at a party, talking to different peopleWord Origin
examples: late 15th cent. (as an alchemical term meaning ‘distil something in a closed container, allowing condensed vapour to return to the original liquid’): from Latin circulat- ‘moved in a circular path’, from the verb circulare, from circulus ‘small ring’, diminutive of circus ‘ring’.Sense (1) dates from the mid 17th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the movement of blood around the body
examples: Regular exercise will improve blood circulation.
to have good/bad circulation

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the passing or spreading of something from one person or place to another
examples: the circulation of money/information/ideas
A number of forged tickets are in circulation.
The coins were taken out of circulation.
Copies of the magazine were withdrawn from circulation.
putting computer viruses into circulation

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the usual number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold each day, week, etc.
examples: a daily circulation of more than one million
The newspaper has a daily circulation of 20 000.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the movement of something (for example air, water, gas, etc.) around an area or inside a system or machine
examples: Poor air circulation can cause condensation.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the fact that somebody takes part in social activities at a particular time
examples: Anne has been ill but now she's back in circulation.
I was out of circulation for months after the baby was born.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the conditions and facts that are connected with and affect a situation, an event or an action
examples: Police said there were no suspicious circumstances surrounding the boy's death.
Under normal circumstances, your white blood cells are able to fight infections.
The company reserves the right to cancel this agreement in certain circumstances.
In exceptional circumstances, detainees could be denied access to a lawyer.
I know I can trust her in any circumstance.
Due to unforeseen circumstances, we have had to reschedule the concert.
Britain is fortunately not facing the same set of circumstances.
The court will take into account all the circumstances of the case.
Police are investigating the circumstances of the death of a baby boy.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the conditions of a person’s life, especially the money they have
examples: We want to work towards improving the often difficult circumstances in which people find themselves.
The particular circumstances of each individual claimant must be considered.
Grants are awarded according to your personal circumstances.
her family/domestic circumstances

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: situations and events that affect and influence your life and that are not in your control
examples: a victim of circumstance (= a person who has suffered because of a situation that they cannot control)
He had to leave the country through force of circumstance (= events made it necessary).
We were simply thrown together by circumstance on the long journey.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used before or after a statement to show that you have thought about the conditions that affect a situation before making a decision or a statement
examples: Under the circumstances, it seemed better not to tell him about the accident.
She did the job very well in the circumstances.
In the circumstances, you'd better call the police.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something should never happen or be allowed
examples: Under no circumstances should you lend Paul any money.
Don't open the door, in any circumstances.
Under no circumstances should you leave the door unlocked.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: formal and impressive ceremony
examples: Funerals of famous people were conducted with great pomp and circumstance.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the state of being poorer than you were before. People say ‘living in reduced circumstances’ to avoid saying ‘poor’.Word Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French circonstance or Latin circumstantia, from circumstare ‘encircle, encompass’, from circum ‘around’ + stare ‘stand’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to mention something as a reason or an example, or in order to support what you are saying
examples: She cited examples of companies the city has helped relocate or expand.
Citing unnamed sources, the newspaper reports that the two companies are nearing a deal.
There is no reason to doubt the information in the articles cited above.
He cited personal reasons for his decision to resign.
The Bank of England has cited concerns about inflation for the first time in four years.
Their method is similar to those used by many studies cited in this report.
He cited his heavy workload as the reason for his breakdown.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to speak or write the exact words from a book, an author, etc.
examples: SYNONYM quote
He cites no primary sources for his claims.
She cited a passage from the President’s speech.
She is the author most often cited in his work.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to order somebody to appear in court; to name somebody officially in a legal case
examples: He was cited for contempt of court.
She was cited in the divorce proceedings.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to mention somebody officially or publicly because they deserve special praise
examples: He was cited for bravery.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who has the legal right to belong to a particular country
examples: COMPARE subject (6)
The defeat of the president did not change the lives of ordinary citizens for the better.
an economic slowdown that has left millions of our fellow citizens unemployed
She's Italian by birth but is now an Australian citizen.
Polish citizens living in other parts of the European Union
the government's failure to address the concerns of the average citizen
In light of the unrest in the country, the US embassy has urged private citizens to leave.
I became a naturalized American citizen when I was 18.
He said the primary responsibility of a state is to protect its citizens from attack.
This shows that the government respects the rights of citizens.
Some politicians seem to be treating the citizens of this country with contempt.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who lives in a particular place
examples: SEE ALSO active citizen
When you're old, people treat you like a second-class citizen.
There have been meetings of concerned citizens over proposed development plans.
the decent, law-abiding citizens of this city
the citizens of Budapest

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the legal right to belong to a particular country
examples: They were granted full French citizenship.
You can apply for citizenship after five years' residency.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of being a citizen and accepting the responsibilities of it
examples: an education that prepares young people for citizenship

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large and important town
examples: SEE ALSO edge city
Parking is difficult in the city centre.
It is one of the world's most beautiful cities.
Riots occurred in all the major cities.
the country’s capital city
Mexico City has a population of more than 20 million people.
Manchester City Football Club
We live in a big city.
a map of the city of Boston

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a town that has been given special rights by a king or queen, usually one that has a cathedral
examples: the city of York
Ely is a cathedral city in East Cambridgeshire.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a town that has been given special rights by the state government

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: all the people who live in a city
examples: The city turned out to welcome the victorious team home.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the UK’s financial and business centre, in the oldest part of London; the people who work there
examples: a City stockbroker
What is the City's reaction to the cut in interest rates?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used after other nouns to say that a place is full of a particular thing
examples: SEE ALSO cardboard city
It's not exactly fun city here is it?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: officially connected with a town or city
examples: civic buildings/leaders

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with the people who live in a town or city
examples: a sense of civic pride (= pride that people feel for their town or city)
civic duties/responsibilities
The competition would be an opportunity to foster civic pride.
Voting should be a matter of civic duty.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the people who live in a country
examples: SEE ALSO civil war
civil unrest (= that is caused by groups of people within a country)
civil strife/conflict
There were concerns that the economic reforms might lead to civil unrest.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with the state rather than with religion or with the armed forces
examples: the recognition of civil unions for same-sex couples
They were married in a civil ceremony.
civil aviation
We have called in the army to assist the civil authorities in rescue operations.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: involving personal legal matters and not criminal law
examples: COMPARE criminal
a civil court

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: polite in a formal way but possibly not friendly
examples: OPPOSITE uncivil
The less time I have to spend being civil to him the better!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who is not a member of the armed forces or the police
examples: Two soldiers and one civilian were killed in the explosion.
Hundreds of innocent civilians have died in the air strikes.
Further measures are needed to protect civilians.
The group was accused of targeting civilians.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who is not a member of the armed forces or the police
examples: Two soldiers and one civilian were killed in the explosion.
Hundreds of innocent civilians have died in the air strikes.
Further measures are needed to protect civilians.
The group was accused of targeting civilians.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a state of human society that is very developed and organized
examples: the technology of modern civilization
The Victorians regarded the railways as bringing progress and civilization.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a society, its culture and its way of life during a particular period of time or in a particular part of the world
examples: the civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome
diseases that are common in Western civilization

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: all the people in the world and the societies they live in, considered as a whole
examples: Environmental damage threatens the whole of civilization.
Could this be the end of civilization as we know it?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a place that offers you the comfortable way of life of a modern society
examples: It's good to be back in civilization after two weeks in a tent!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say that something is true although it has not been proved and other people may not believe it
examples: He claims (that) he was not given a fair hearing.
I don't claim to be an expert.
She claimed to hate all art.
She's not the saint that many have claimed her to be.
After disappointing box office results, newspapers claimed the show to be a failure
Scientists are claiming a major breakthrough in the fight against cancer.
It was claimed that some doctors were working 80 hours a week.
‘I did not tell any lies,’ she claimed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to state that you have done, gained or achieved something
examples: He claimed victory in the presidential elections before all the results were in.
Nobody has claimed responsibility for the bombing.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to ask for money from the government or a company because you have a right to it
examples: He's not entitled to claim housing benefit.
You might be entitled to claim compensation if you are injured at work.
You could have claimed the cost of the hotel room from your insurance.
She claimed damages from the company for the injury she had suffered.
You can claim on your insurance for that coat you left on the train.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to demand or ask for something because you believe it is your legal right to own or to have it
examples: A lot of lost property is never claimed.
The family arrived in the UK in the 1990s and claimed political asylum.
He is claiming his right to his family's fortune.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to get or take somebody’s attention
examples: A most unwelcome event claimed his attention.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to gain, win or achieve something
examples: She has finally claimed a place on the team.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to cause somebody’s death
examples: The car crash claimed three lives.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make something clearer or easier to understand
examples: to clarify a situation/problem/issue
I hope this clarifies my position.
The law on drugs needs to be clarified.
Talking to someone has helped clarify my feelings.
She asked him to clarify what he meant.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something, especially butter, pure by heating it
examples: clarified butter

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of being expressed clearly
examples: a lack of clarity in the law
The brilliant clarity of his argument could not be faulted.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the ability to think about or understand something clearly
examples: clarity of thought/purpose/vision
With painful clarity she remembered the day he had died.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if a picture, substance or sound has clarity, you can see or hear it very clearly, or see through it easily
examples: the clarity of the sound on the recording

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a short fight between two groups of people
examples: Clashes broke out between police and demonstrators.
Eight people were wounded in a clash with border guards.
Several people were injured in violent clashes with the police.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an argument between two people or groups of people who have different beliefs and ideas
examples: SYNONYM conflict
There has been a head-on clash between the two candidates over education policy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the difference that exists between two things that are opposed to each other
examples: SYNONYM conflict
a clash of interests/opinions/cultures
a personality clash with the boss

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a situation in which two events happen at the same time so that you cannot go to or see them both
examples: a clash in the timetable/schedule

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a loud noise made by two metal objects being hit together
examples: a clash of cymbals/swords

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an occasion when two teams or players compete against each other
examples: Bayern’s clash with Roma in the Champions League

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the situation when two colours, designs, etc. look ugly when they are put togetherWord Origin
examples: early 16th cent.: imitative.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of students who are taught together
examples: We were in the same class at school.
She is the youngest in her class.
He came top of the class.
The whole class was/were told to stay behind after school.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an occasion when a group of students meets to be taught
examples: SYNONYM lesson
I have a history class at 9 o'clock.
I was late for (a) class.
See me after class.
She works hard in class (= during the class).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a series of classes on a particular subject
examples: SYNONYM course
Are you still doing your French evening class?
I've been taking classes in pottery.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a group of students who finish their studies at school, college or university in a particular year
examples: the class of 2020
the freshman/sophomore/junior/senior class

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: one of the groups of people in a society that are thought of as being at the same social or economic level
examples: SEE ALSO middle class
the working/middle/upper class
The party tries to appeal to all classes of society.
His ideas had an appeal among the wealthy, professional classes.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the way that people are divided into different social and economic groups
examples: differences of class, race or gender
The old class system is not appropriate in a modern age.
a society in which class is more important than ability

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: each of several different levels of comfort that are available to travellers in a plane, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO business class
He always travels business class.
The first-class compartment is situated at the front of the train.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a group of people, animals or things that have similar characteristics or qualities
examples: SEE ALSO first-class
It was good accommodation for a hotel of this class.
different classes of drugs
Dickens was in a different class from (= was much better than) most of his contemporaries.
As a jazz singer she's in a class of her own (= better than most others).

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: one of the different groups in a competition
examples: He came first in his class at every event.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: an attractive quality or a high level of skill that is impressive
examples: She has class all right—she looks like a model.
There's a real touch of class about this team.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: one of the levels of achievement in a British university degree exam
examples: a first-/second-/third-class degree

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a group into which animals, plants, etc. that have similar characteristics are divided, below a phylum
examples: COMPARE family

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: the people in society who like to give their opinions on political or social issues
examples: Constitutional reform is popular among the chattering classes.
topics being discussed at the breakfast tables of the chattering classes

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: accepted or deserving to be accepted as one of the best or most important of its kind
examples: a classic film/story/car/game
I grew up listening to classic rock.
a classic novel/study/goal
This classic novel was first published in 1938.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: with all the features you would expect to find; very typical
examples: a classic example of poor communication
This was a classic case of what not to do.
She displayed the classic symptoms of depression.
I made the classic mistake of clapping in a pause in the music!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: attractive, but simple and traditional in style or design; not affected by changes in fashion
examples: a classic grey suit
classic design
a classic look

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: people say That’s classic! when they find something very funny, when they think somebody has been very stupid or when something annoying, but not surprising, happens
examples: She's not going to help? Oh, that's classic!

the classical theory of unemployment
classical and modern ballet/dance

a classical scholar (= an expert in Latin and Greek)
classical architecture

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: classical Arabic

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: simple and attractive
examples: the classical elegance of the design

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act or process of putting people or things into a group or class (= of classifying them)
examples: a style of music that defies classification (= is like no other)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group, class, division, etc. into which somebody or something is put
examples: a document with the security classification ‘confidential’
The material was put into the highest security classification.
Many fairly common human behaviours can fall under the general classification of ‘mental illness’.
The classification ‘science’ covers a great many different subjects.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of putting animals, plants, etc. into groups, classes or divisions according to their characteristics
examples: The classification of bony fish is extremely complicated.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a system of arranging books, tapes, magazines, etc. in a library into groups according to their subject

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to arrange something in groups according to features that they have in common
examples: The books in the library are classified according to subject.
Patients are classified into three categories.
All rural settlements were classified according to their size.
people classified by ethnic group
These can be classified under five headings.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to decide which type or group somebody/something belongs to
examples: Only eleven of these accidents were classified as major.
Would you classify it as a hard drug or a soft drug?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to state that information is officially secret
examples: The government insists on keeping certain documents classified.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a room where a class of children or students is taught
examples: SEE ALSO flipped classroom
classroom activities
classroom teaching/teachers
the use of computers in the classroom

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of words that includes a subject and a verb, and forms a sentence or part of a sentence
examples: SEE ALSO coordinate clause
There are languages that require the subject to come before the object in a clause.
It is the object of the verb of the clause.
Commas are used to separate clauses of sentences.
the second clause in the sentence

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an item in a legal document that says that a particular thing must or must not be done
examples: SEE ALSO escape clause
a confidentiality clause
a key clause of the US Constitution
There is a clause in the contract forbidding tenants to sublet.
the requirements set out in clauses 174 to 176

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not dirty
examples: SEE ALSO squeaky clean
Are your hands clean?
She wiped all the surfaces clean.
It is your responsibility to keep the room clean and tidy.
Keep your room neat and clean.
I can't find a clean shirt (= one I haven't worn since it was washed).
The hotel was spotlessly (= extremely) clean.
The council does a good job keeping the streets clean.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having a clean appearance and living in clean conditions
examples: Cats are very clean animals.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: free from harmful or unpleasant substances
examples: clean water/air
Thousands were left without food or clean drinking water.
clean energy
We all want a cleaner environment but who is going to pay for it?
cleaner cars (= not producing so many harmful substances)
Electric buses are a clean, environmentally friendly way to travel.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: with nothing written on it
examples: a clean sheet of paper

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not offensive or referring to sex; not doing anything that is considered bad or wrong
examples: The entertainment was good clean fun for the whole family.
Keep the jokes clean please!
The sport has a very clean image.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not showing or having any record of doing something that is against the law
examples: a clean driving licence/driver’s license
a clean police record

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not owning or carrying anything illegal such as drugs or weapons
examples: The police searched her but she was clean.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: not having taken drugs or alcohol
examples: He's been clean for three weeks.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: played or done in a fair way and within the rules
examples: It was a tough but clean game.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: having a smooth edge, surface or shape; simple and regular
examples: A sharp knife makes a clean cut.
a modern design with clean lines and a bright appearance

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: done with skill and in an accurate way
examples: The plane made a clean take-off.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: with no changes or mistakes in it
examples: I do my utmost to produce clean copy, but occasionally a mistake slips in.
It backs up data frequently, keeping a clean copy of your work.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: tasting, smelling or looking pleasant and fresh
examples: The wine has a clean taste and a lovely golden colour.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: very clean

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: a report that says somebody is healthy or that something is in good condition
examples: Doctors gave him a clean bill of health after a series of tests and examinations.
The building was given a clean bill of health by the surveyor.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: a complete end to any connection with a person, an organization, a way of life, etc.
examples: She wanted to make a clean break with the past.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: a break in a bone in one place

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: a record of your work or behaviour that does not show any mistakes or bad things that you have done
examples: No government operates with a completely clean sheet.
They kept a clean sheet in the match (= no goals were scored against them).

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to remove all the people or things from an organization that are thought to be unnecessary or need changing
examples: The new manager made a clean sweep of the department.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to win all the prizes or parts of a game or competition; to win an election completely
examples: China made a clean sweep of the medals in the gymnastics events.
The opinion poll suggests a clean sweep for the Democrats.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to admit and explain something that you have kept as a secret
examples: Isn't it time the government came clean about their plans for education?

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to avoid doing anything wrong or illegal
examples: Since leaving prison, he's managed to keep his nose clean.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to tell the truth about something so that you no longer feel guilty
examples: He made a clean breast of everything and admitted taking the money.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to agree to forget about past mistakes or arguments and start again with a relationshipWord Origin
examples: Old English clǣne, of West Germanic origin; related to Dutch and German klein ‘small’.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 10

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12

definitions.label: Meaning 13

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: very clean

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: a complete end to any connection with a person, an organization, a way of life, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: a break in a bone in one place

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: a record of your work or behaviour that does not show any mistakes or bad things that you have done

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to remove all the people or things from an organization that are thought to be unnecessary or need changing
examples: The new manager made a clean sweep of the department.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to win all the prizes or parts of a game or competition; to win an election completely
examples: China made a clean sweep of the medals in the gymnastics events.
The opinion poll suggests a clean sweep for the Democrats.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to admit and explain something that you have kept as a secret
examples: Isn't it time the government came clean about their plans for education?

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to avoid doing anything wrong or illegal
examples: Since leaving prison, he's managed to keep his nose clean.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to tell the truth about something so that you no longer feel guilty
examples: He made a clean breast of everything and admitted taking the money.

definitions.label: Meaning 24

examples: Old English clǣne, of West Germanic origin; related to Dutch and German klein ‘small’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: easy to understand and not confusing
examples: She gave me clear and precise directions.
Are these instructions clear enough?
Your meaning needs to be clear.
You'll do as you're told—is that clear?
She was quite clear about her reasons for leaving.
This behaviour must stop—do I make myself clear (= express myself clearly so there is no doubt about what I mean)?
I hope I made it clear to him that he was no longer welcome here.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: obvious and leaving no doubt at all
examples: This is a clear case of fraud.
She won the election by a clear majority.
His height gives him a clear advantage.
a clear warning of the risks
He left no clear indication of his wishes.
We must send a clear message to young people that cyberbullying will not be tolerated.
There is clear evidence that he was involved with the gang.
They made their intentions abundantly clear.
It was quite clear to me that she was lying.
It is clear from the graph that sales have dropped sharply.
It is not clear what they want us to do.
How he got there was not clear.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not confused; having no doubt
examples: Are you clear about the arrangements for tomorrow?
My memory is not clear on that point.
I'm still not clear what the job involves.
We need a clear understanding of the problems involved.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: thinking in a sensible and logical way, especially in a difficult situation
examples: a clear thinker
You'll need to keep a clear head for your interview.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: easy to see or hear
examples: The photo wasn't very clear.
The voice on the phone was clear and strong.
She was in Australia but I could hear her voice as clear as a bell.
The image was crisp and clear.
The colours in her paintings are very clear and bright.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: that you can see through; transparent
examples: The water was so clear we could see the bottom of the lake.
clear glass
a clear colourless liquid
a sheet of clear cellophane

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: without cloud or mist
examples: a clear blue sky
On a clear day you can see France.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: without spots or marks
examples: clear skin
a clear complexion

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: bright and lively
examples: Her clear blue eyes sparkled.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: free from things that are blocking the way or covering the surface of something
examples: The road was clear and I ran over.
All exits must be kept clear of baggage.
You won't get a clear view of the stage from here.
I always leave a clear desk at the end of the day.
Most roads are now clear of snow.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: if you have a clear conscience or your conscience is clear, you do not feel guilty

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: free from something that is unpleasant
examples: They were still not clear of all suspicion.
We are finally clear of debt.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: not touching something; a distance away from something
examples: The plane climbed until it was clear of the clouds.
Make sure you park your car clear of the entrance.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: whole or complete
examples: Allow three clear days for the letter to arrive.
You must give seven clear days’ notice of the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: that remains when taxes, costs, etc. have been taken away
examples: SYNONYM net
They had made a clear profit of £2 000.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: produced with the central part of the tongue close to the top of the mouth. In many accents of (= ways of pronouncing) English, clear /l/ is used before a vowel, as in leave.
examples: OPPOSITE dark

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to be simple and free from trouble

definitions.label: Meaning 19

examples: Oh well, that's all as clear as mud, then.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: a complete difference or division between two people or groups
examples: Voters want to see clear blue water between the main parties.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: there is no danger of being seen or caught
examples: As soon as the coast was clear, he climbed in through the window.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to remain calm in a difficult situation
examples: She needed to keep a clear head if she was to remain in control.

definitions.label: Meaning 23

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: SYNONYM receptionist

definitions.label: Meaning 3

a clever child

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: He's always been clever at crosswords.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

clever marketing

Just click the link below.
I clicked on the link to the next page of the website.
Click for more images.

The door clicked shut.

Polly clicked her tongue in annoyance.
The corporal clicked his heels.
The police officer clicked a pair of handcuffs around his wrists.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

The clock has stopped.

examples: Staff have been working around the clock to resolve the problems.

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: The player beat the clock and set a new record.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 12

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

The rains came too late to do any good.
Spring came late this year.

Her death came as a terrible shock to us.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 9

His family comes first (= is the most important thing in his life).

definitions.label: Meaning 10

He came to power in 2019.

The trees are coming into leaf.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to become
examples: The handle came loose.

Everything will come right in the end.
This design came to be known as the Oriental style.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to reach a point where you realize, understand or believe something

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to have an orgasm

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be very clever, stupid, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to play the part of a particular type of person; to behave in a particular way
examples: Don't come the innocent with me.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody to repeat something
examples: ‘She's an entomologist.’ ‘Come again?’ ‘An entomologist—she studies insects.’

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to arrive and leave; to move freely
examples: They had a party next door—we heard people coming and going all night.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to be present for a short time and then go away
examples: The pain in my leg comes and goes.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to be easy, natural, etc. for somebody to do
examples: Acting comes naturally to her.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to be unsuccessful; to have no successful result
examples: How sad that all his hard work should come to nothing.
Her plans didn't come to anything.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to introduce something extra that is connected with what has just been said
examples: I don't really trust him—nor his wife, come to that.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: despite any problems or difficulties you may have
examples: He promised to support her come what may.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used to say you do not understand how something can happen and would like an explanation
examples: ‘I think you owe me some money.’ ‘How come?’
If she spent five years in Paris, how come her French is so bad?

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to not be important or successful

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: in the future
examples: They may well regret the decision in years to come.
This will be a problem for some time to come (= for a period of time in the future).

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: when it is a question of something
examples: When it comes to getting things done, he's useless.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: somebody’s ideas, beliefs, personality, etc. that makes them say what they have said
examples: I see where you're coming from (= I understand what you mean).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a play, film or TV show that is intended to be funny, usually with a happy ending; plays, films and TV shows of this type
examples: COMPARE tragedy
a romantic comedy
a black comedy (= a play or film that deals with unpleasant or terrible things in a humorous way)
a slapstick comedy
He moved to Los Angeles to write comedy.
a comedy about an eccentric family
She went on to star in a hit comedy series.
His TV comedy shows ran during the 70s and 80s.
a comedy series/show

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: professional entertainment with jokes, short acts, etc. that is intended to be funny
examples: SEE ALSO stand-up (1)
The show combines theatre with the best of stand-up and sketch comedy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a humorous aspect of something
examples: SYNONYM humour
Her imaginative interpretation of the script brought out the comedy inherent in it.
He didn't appreciate the comedy of the situation.
The visual comedy of this scene is obvious.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being physically relaxed and free from pain; the state of having a pleasant life, with everything that you need
examples: The hotel offers a high standard of comfort and service.
I didn't want to leave the comfort of my bed.
They had enough money to live in comfort in their old age.
Watch the latest movies in the comfort of your own home.
From the comfort of your own armchair, you can witness all the action live.
I dress for comfort rather than elegance.
These tennis shoes are designed for comfort and performance.
He's beginning to find a comfort level with his teammates now.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a feeling of not suffering or worrying so much; a feeling of being less unhappy
examples: SYNONYM consolation
I tried to offer a few words of comfort.
His words were of little comfort in the circumstances.
to take comfort from from somebody’s words
His family can draw some comfort from the fact that the two men accused of his murder have pleaded guilty.
We know that they will find comfort in the knowledge that he died doing the job he loved
The announcement of a few new jobs will provide scant comfort to their many recently redundant employees.
If it's any comfort to you, I'm in the same situation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that helps you when you are suffering, worried or unhappy
examples: SEE ALSO cold comfort
Her being her with me was such a comfort.
The children have been a great comfort to me through all of this.
It's a comfort to know that she is safe.
It was a comfort to her to know that I was never far away.
In some ways it's a comfort that they died together.
It will be a comfort to her family that justice has been done.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a thing that makes your life easier or more comfortable
examples: SEE ALSO creature comforts
The hotel has all modern comforts/every modern comfort.
material comforts (= money and possessions)
She desperately missed her home comforts while camping.
He is someone who would take the comforts of home over the bright lights of Hollywood.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: so near that it is uncomfortable or dangerous
examples: When she leaves the stage, the fans can get a little too close for comfort.
They got the win but it was a tight match, definitely too close for comfort.
