examples: She was committed to a psychiatric hospital.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to send somebody for trial in court
examples: The attackers were committed for trial at Bristol Crown Court.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to learn something well enough to remember it exactly
examples: She committed the instructions to memory.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to write something downWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Latin committere ‘join, entrust’ (in medieval Latin ‘put into custody’), from com- ‘with’ + mittere ‘put or send’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a promise to do something or to behave in a particular way; a promise to support somebody/something; the fact of committing yourself
examples: I'm not ready to make a long-term commitment.
They have failed to honour their commitments.
The company has shown a commitment to diversity over the years.
He questioned the government's commitment to public services.
We're looking for a firm commitment from both sides.
This project demonstrates our commitment to improving the quality of the city's green spaces.
They reaffirmed their commitment to work for peace.
Australia is determined to meet its commitments under the agreement.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the desire to work hard and give your energy and time to a job or an activity
examples: He has demonstrated exceptional commitment and dedication.
commitment to education/democracy/social justice
Not everyone will be happy with this level of commitment.
She was criticized for her lack of commitment.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing that you have promised or agreed to do, or that you have to do
examples: He's busy for the next month with filming commitments.
Women very often have to juggle work with their family commitments.
I don't want to take on any more commitments.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a promise to pay for something, especially regularly; a promise to use resources in order to achieve something
examples: Taking on a mortgage is a huge financial commitment.
the commitment of resources to education
Achieving success at this level requires a commitment of time and energy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of people who are chosen, usually by a larger group, to make decisions or to deal with a particular subject
examples: SEE ALSO conference committee
an executive/advisory/organizing committee
a parliamentary/congressional/Senate committee
The committee has/have decided to close the restaurant.
The committee unanimously approved the plan.
to appoint/establish/form a committee
to chair/head a committee
She's on the planning committee.
He has served on numerous committees.
I have been invited to sit on the committee.
He will be called to give evidence before the committee.
The bill was still in committee (= being considered by a committee) in early December.
a committee of inquiry
a committee of MPs/experts
A special committee to investigate the possible impeachment of the governor meets later today.
the US House of Representatives' committee on foreign affairs
a committee member/chairman
a committee meeting/report
the chairman/chair of a committee
a member/meeting of a committee

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a product or a raw material that can be bought and sold
examples: rice, flour and other basic commodities
a drop in commodity prices
Crude oil is the world's most important commodity.
basic agricultural commodities

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that is useful or has a useful quality
examples: Water is a precious commodity that is often taken for granted in the West.
Time is a very valuable commodity.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening often; existing in large numbers or in many places
examples: OPPOSITE uncommon
a common problem/occurrence/practice
a common feature/theme
the most common type of injury
Breast cancer is the most common form of cancer among women in this country.
Jackson is a common English name.
Some birds that were once a common sight are now becoming rare.
a common spelling mistake
Suicide is the most common cause of death amongst men in this age group.
The disease is very common in young horses.
Allergies to milk are quite common in childhood.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: shared by or belonging to two or more people or by the people in a group
examples: They share a common interest in photography.
to have a common ancestor/enemy
the need to cooperate to achieve a common goal
We are working together for a common purpose.
The various groups all learn Arabic, so they have a common language.
common ownership of the land
This decision was taken for the common good (= the advantage of everyone).
It is, by common consent, Scotland's prettiest coast (= everyone agrees that it is).
basic features that are common to all human languages
This attitude is common to most young men in the armed services.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: ordinary; not unusual or special
examples: Shakespeare's work was popular among the common people in his day.
In most people's eyes she was nothing more than a common criminal.
You'd think he'd have the common courtesy to apologize (= this would be the polite behaviour that people would expect).
It's only common decency to let her know what's happening (= people would expect it).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: found or living in quite large numbers; not rare
examples: the common garden frog
I wanted a recording of the common cuckoo.
The swordfish is not common in European waters.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: typical of somebody from a low social class and not having good manners
examples: She thought he was very common and uneducated.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be something that everyone knows, especially in a particular community or group
examples: Their relationship is common knowledge.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: ordinary; with no special features

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the ability of a powerful or famous person to talk to and understand ordinary people

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be united with somebody about something that you both agree on, believe in or wish to achieveWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French comun (adjective), from Latin communis.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: usually; very often; by most people
examples: Christopher is commonly known as Kit.
the sudden increase in the birth rate after the Second World War, commonly referred to as the ‘baby boom’
avian influenza, commonly called bird flu
This is one of the most commonly used methods.
symptoms commonly associated with HIV
These fats are commonly found in processed foods.
one of the most commonly available substances on the planet

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to share or exchange information, news, ideas, feelings, etc.
examples: We only communicate by email.
They communicated in sign language.
Candidates must be able to communicate effectively.
Dolphins use sound to communicate with each other.
Direct marketing allows a firm to communicate directly with its customers.
In times of uncertainty, a leader must be able to communicate a message of hope.
Language evolved as a means of communicating information between individuals.
He was eager to communicate his ideas to the group.
Her nervousness was communicating itself to the children.
They failed to communicate what was happening and why.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to have a good relationship because you are able to understand and talk about your own and other people’s thoughts, feelings, etc.
examples: His inability to communicate has damaged their relationship beyond repair.
The novel is about a family who can't communicate with each other.
couples who communicate well with one another

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to pass a disease from one person, animal, etc. to another
examples: The disease is communicated through dirty drinking water.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if two rooms communicate, they are next to each other and you can get from one to the other
examples: a communicating door (= one that connects two rooms)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activity or process of expressing ideas and feelings or of giving people information
examples: Good communication between team leaders and members is essential.
attempts to improve communication with customers
The campaign will appear across all communication channels.
helping students develop their communication skills
non-verbal communication such as gestures or facial expressions
We are in regular communication by email.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: methods of sending information, especially phones, radio, computers, etc. or roads and railways
examples: SEE ALSO comms
communications technology
to launch a communications satellite
wireless/electronic/satellite communication
to intercept/disrupt/monitor communications
The new airport will improve communications between the islands.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a message, letter or phone call
examples: a communication from the leader of the party

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with communism
examples: communist ideology

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: governed by or belonging to a Communist party
examples: a Communist country/government/leader

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: all the people who live in a particular area, country, etc. when talked about as a group
examples: SEE ALSO retirement community
The local community supported us from the start.
the international community (= the countries of the world as a group)
It is hoped that the campaign will encourage members of the community to get active.
the problems faced by rural communities
good community relations with the police
community groups/leaders
health workers based in the community (= working with people in a local area)
community parks/libraries (= paid for by the local town/city)
the wider/entire/whole community
She comes from a small island community.
Our aim is to serve the community.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of people who share the same religion, race, job, etc.
examples: the Polish community in London
the business/scientific community
the Muslim/Jewish/Christian community
the gay community
the intelligence community (= all the people whose job is to collect secret information)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the feeling of sharing things and belonging to a group in the place where you live
examples: There is a strong sense of community here.
The town has a strong community spirit.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a group of people who live together and all equally own and share what they have
examples: The nuns live in a closed community.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a group of plants and animals growing or living in the same place or environment
examples: a community fish tank

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or an animal that travels with you or spends a lot of time with you
examples: SEE ALSO animal companion
travelling companions
Geoff was my companion on the journey.
Fear was the hostages' constant companion.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who shares your experiences, especially when these are particularly pleasant or unpleasant
examples: SEE ALSO boon companion
She was a charming dinner companion.
His younger brother is not much of a companion for him.
They're drinking companions (= they go out drinking together).
We became companions in misfortune.
He was an entertaining dinner companion.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person, usually a woman, employed to live with and help somebody, especially somebody old or ill
examples: She lived in the house as a companion to our grandmother.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: one of a pair of things that go together or can be used together
examples: A companion volume is soon to be published.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used in book titles to describe a book giving useful facts and information on a particular subject
examples: A Companion to French Literature

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a business organization that makes money by producing or selling goods or services
examples: SEE ALSO finance company
insurance/oil/tech/technology/pharmaceutical companies
It is the world's largest software company.
He works for the National Bus Company.
Carrington and Company of London
a large/small company
She runs her own TV production company.
to own/start/found a company
Smoking in the workplace is against company policy.
Company profits were 5 per cent lower than last year.
a company executive/director
a company pension

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of people who work or perform together
examples: a theatre/dance, etc. company
the Royal Shakespeare Company
a small touring opera company

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the fact of being with somebody else and not alone
examples: I enjoy Jo's company (= I enjoy being with her).
a pleasant evening in the company of friends
She enjoys her own company (= being by herself) when she is travelling.
The children are very good company (= pleasant to be with) at this age.
He's coming with me for company.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: guests in your house
examples: I didn't realize you had company.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a group of people together
examples: She told the assembled company what had happened.
It is bad manners to whisper in company (= in a group of people).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a group of soldiers that is part of a battalion

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the people that somebody spends time with
examples: Judging by the company he kept, Mark must have been a wealthy man.
John's mother was worried about the company he kept.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be friends with people that others think are bad
examples: They worried about their teenage son getting into bad company.
He got into bad company and got involved in drugs.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: together with or at the same time as somebody/something
examples: She arrived in company with the ship's captain.
The US dollar went through a difficult time, in company with the oil market.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: if you say that somebody is in good company, you mean that they should not worry about a mistake, etc. because somebody else, especially somebody more important, has done the same thing
examples: If you worry about your relationship with your teenage son or daughter, you are in good company. Many parents share these worries.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to stay with somebody so that they are not alone
examples: I'll keep you company while you're waiting.
I'll stay and keep you company.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to leave somebody; to end a relationship with somebody
examples: This is where we part company (= go in different directions).
The band have parted company with their manager.
The band and their manager have parted company.
He parted ways with the team at the end of the season.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to disagree with somebody about something
examples: Weber parted company with Marx on a number of important issues.
The two leaders parted ways on this question.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used after being rude or critical about somebody to say that the people you are talking to are not included in the criticism
examples: The people in this office are so narrow-minded, present company excepted, of course.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to suggest that it is better to be in a group of only two people than have a third person with you as wellWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in senses (2) to (6)): from Old French compainie; related to compaignon, literally ‘one who breaks bread with another’, based on Latin com- ‘together with’ + panis ‘bread’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: similar to somebody/something else and able to be compared
examples: A comparable house in the south of the city would cost twice as much.
The situation in the US is not directly comparable to that in the UK.
Inflation is now at a rate comparable with that in other European countries.
The two machines are comparable in size.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: measured or judged by how similar or different it is to something else
examples: SYNONYM relative
Then he was living in comparative comfort (= compared with others or with his own life at a previous time).
The company is a comparative newcomer to the software market (= other companies have been in business much longer).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with studying things to find out how similar or different they are
examples: a comparative study of the educational systems of two countries
comparative linguistics

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: relating to adjectives or adverbs that express more in amount, degree or quality, for example better, worse, slower and more difficult
examples: COMPARE superlative

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to examine people or things to see how they are similar and how they are different
examples: It is interesting to compare their situation and ours.
We compared the two reports carefully.
The internet allows you to compare prices from a variety of companies.
How can you compare the two things? They are so different!
Compare and contrast the characters of Jack and Ralph.
We compared the results of our study with those of other studies.
My own problems seem insignificant compared with other people's.
I've had some difficulties, but they were nothing compared to yours (= they were not nearly as bad as yours).
Standards in healthcare have improved enormously compared to 40 years ago.
They receive just over three years of schooling, compared to a national average of 7.3.
an increase of over 11% compared to the same period last year
About a third of American adults are obese compared with 24 per cent of Britons

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be similar to somebody/something else, either better or worse
examples: This school compares with the best in the country (= it is as good as them).
This house doesn't compare with our previous one (= it is not as good).
Their prices compare favourably to those of their competitors.
The region's wines compare well with those from elsewhere in Germany.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show or state that somebody/something is similar to somebody/something else
examples: The critics compared his work to that of Martin Amis.
In her early career she was often compared to Ella Fitzgerald.
Some observers compare the situation to that of the early 1980s.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if two or more people compare notes, they each say what they think about the same event, situation, etc.
examples: We saw the play separately and compared notes afterwards.
Let's compare notes on our experiences.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: it is impossible to say that one thing is better than another if the two are completely different
examples: They are both great but you can't compare apples and oranges.
No, you’re trying to compare apples and oranges.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of comparing two or more people or things
examples: For Durkheim, comparison was the most important method of analysis in sociology.
Comparison with other oil-producing countries is extremely interesting.
The education system bears/stands no comparison with (= is not as good as) that in many Asian countries.
I enclose the two plans for comparison.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an occasion when two or more people or things are compared
examples: The films are too different for a fair comparison.
a comparison of the rail systems in Britain and France
a comparison of men’s salaries with those of women
comparisons between Britain and the rest of Europe
a comparison of the brain to a computer (= showing what is similar)
It is difficult to make a comparison with her previous book—they are completely different.
You can draw comparisons with the situation in Ireland (= say how the two situations are similar).
There is no published information that would allow a direct comparison with other regions or countries.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used especially at the beginning of a sentence when the next thing that is mentioned is compared with something in the previous sentence
examples: By comparison, expenditure on education increased last year.
His problems seemed trivial by comparison.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: when compared with somebody/something
examples: The second half of the game was dull by comparison with the first.
The tallest buildings in London are small in comparison with New York's skyscrapers.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to seem less important when compared with something else
examples: Last year's riots pale in comparison with this latest outburst of violence.
Our problems pale into insignificance when compared to theirs.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the difference between two people or things that are being compared
examples: In terms of price there's no comparison (= one thing is much more expensive than the other).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong feeling of sympathy for people or animals who are suffering and a desire to help them
examples: to feel/show compassion
She was known as a hard woman with no compassion, no emotion.
In an overworked doctor, feelings of compassion are soon lost.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to force somebody to do something; to make something necessary
examples: The law can compel fathers to make regular payments for their children.
I feel compelled to write and tell you how much I enjoyed your book.
The court has powers to compel witnesses to attend.
Last year ill health compelled his retirement.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to cause a particular reaction
examples: He spoke with an authority that compelled the attention of the whole crowd.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that makes you pay attention to it because it is so interesting and exciting
examples: Her latest book makes compelling reading.
His eyes were strangely compelling.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: so strong that you cannot resist it
examples: a compelling need/desire
He was a sad man with a compelling need to talk about his unhappiness.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: that makes you think it is true
examples: There is no compelling reason to believe him.
The new studies provide compelling evidence in support of these concepts.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to provide something good to balance or reduce the bad effects of damage, loss, etc.
examples: SYNONYM make up for
Nothing can compensate for the loss of a loved one.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to act in order to balance or correct something wrong or not normal
examples: SYNONYM make up for
In the second experiment, the temperature was raised to compensate for this bias.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to pay somebody money because they have suffered some damage, loss, injury, etc.
examples: Her lawyers say she should be compensated for the suffering she had been caused.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something, especially money, that somebody gives you because they have hurt you, or damaged something that you own; the act of giving this to somebody
examples: SEE ALSO workers' compensation
to claim/award/receive compensation
The employer has a duty to pay full compensation for injuries received at work.
to receive £10 000 in compensation
She received a cash sum by way of compensation.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: money that an employee receives for doing their job
examples: Send your CV and current compensation to Executive Search Consultant.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing or things that make a bad situation better
examples: I wish I were young again, but getting older has its compensations.
The grey streets of London were small compensation for the loss of her beloved Africa.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take part in a contest or game
examples: The games were an outstanding success, with almost 2 400 athletes competing.
He's hoping to compete in the London marathon.
Only 21 bodybuilders competed in the event.
They are competing against teams of full-time professional players.
He is expected to compete for the title of world champion next year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to try to be more successful or better than somebody else who is trying to do the same as you
examples: They simply cannot compete in the international market.
Several companies are competing for the contract.
Young children will usually compete for their mother's attention.
The result is more applicants competing for fewer jobs.
Small independent bookshops find it difficult to compete with the online stores.
For too long UK shipyards have been competing against each other.
We can't compete with them on price.
to compete on quality/cost
There are too many magazines competing to attract readers.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the ability to do something well
examples: SEE ALSO communicative competence
to gain a high level of competence in English
professional/technical competence

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the power that a court, an organization or a person has to deal with something
examples: The judge has to act within the competence of the court.
outside somebody’s area of competence

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a skill that you need in a particular job or for a particular task
examples: The syllabus lists the knowledge and competences required at this level.
You will agree with us a personal learning contract, based on an assessment of personal competences in relation to career objectives.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having enough skill or knowledge to do something well or to the necessary standard
examples: OPPOSITE incompetent
He's very competent in his work.
Make sure the firm is competent to carry out the work.
I don’t feel competent to comment.
She is highly competent at her job.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: of a good standard but not very good
examples: Ron was a competent player—more than that, he was good!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having the power to decide something
examples: The case was referred to a competent authority.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an event in which people compete with each other to find out who is the best at something
examples: a design/an art/a talent competition
an international/a national competition
Hundreds of schools entered the competition.
She's won a prestigious singing competition.
He won fourth place in the competition.
a competition to design the new Parliament building

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a situation in which people or organizations compete with each other for something that not everyone can have
examples: stiff/fierce/intense/tough competition
competition between two similar products
The government said the new laws would enhance competition among banks.
competition for resources/jobs/food, etc.
competition to secure a place on the course
The firm is facing stiff competition from its online rivals.
Public education is run in direct competition with the private sector.
We are in competition with four other companies for the contract.
The programme puts two couples in competition with each other to redecorate one another's homes.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the people who are competing against somebody
examples: We'll be able to assess the competition at the conference.
This car consistently outperforms the competition.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to describe a situation in which people or organizations compete against each other
examples: competitive games/sports
Graduates have to fight for jobs in an increasingly competitive market.
Those businesses are operating in an extremely competitive environment.
The company has succeeded in a highly competitive industry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: trying very hard to be better than others
examples: OPPOSITE uncompetitive
You have to be highly competitive to do well in sport these days.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: as good as or better than others
examples: a shop selling clothes at competitive prices (= as low as any other shop)
to gain a competitive advantage over rival companies
How do we maintain our competitive edge?
What is your strategy for helping the company stay competitive in a global market?
We need to work harder to remain competitive with other companies.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who takes part in a competition
examples: Over 200 competitors entered the race.
the youngest competitor in the event
the most successful South African competitor at the games
There are six remaining competitors for the grand prize of $50 000.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or an organization that competes against others, especially in business
examples: We produce cheaper goods than our competitors.
The company is outperforming its main competitors in the US market.
They are set to become formidable competitors to American companies.
Japan was not a major competitor for scarce resources such as oil.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to produce a book, list, report, etc. by bringing together different items, articles, songs, etc.; to collect information in order to produce a book, list, etc.
examples: We are trying to compile a list of suitable people for the job.
The album was compiled from live recordings from last year's tour.
The figures were compiled from a survey of 2  000 schoolchildren.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to translate instructions from one computer language into another so that a particular computer can understand themWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French compiler or its apparent source, Latin compilare ‘plunder or plagiarize’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about somebody/something
examples: She never complains, but she's obviously exhausted.
‘How are you?’ ‘Oh, I can't complain (= I'm all right).’
Annoyed residents have complained to the police.
Shoppers complained about the lack of toilet facilities.
I'm going to complain to the manager about this.
The defendant complained of intimidation during the investigation.
She complained at the unfairness of it all.
He complained bitterly that he had been unfairly treated.
‘It's not fair,’ she complained.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a reason for not being satisfied; a statement that somebody makes saying that they are not satisfied
examples: a formal complaint
She said the police had immediately investigated the complaint.
I'd like to make a complaint about the noise.
to file/lodge (= make) a complaint
The most common complaint is about poor service.
The Tribunal upheld his complaint of racial discrimination
I believe you have a complaint against one of our nurses.
They said their complaints to the police were often not acted on.
Council bosses said they would respond to complaints from residents.
We received a number of complaints from customers about the lack of parking facilities.
‘Complaints by patients are now at their lowest level,’ she said.
a complaint that he had been unfairly treated
My only complaint is that the website is a little difficult to use.
We have a clear and effective complaints procedure.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of complaining
examples: I can see no grounds for complaint.
The way I was treated gave me no cause for complaint.
I'm planning to write a formal letter of complaint.
Workers were expected to accept pay cuts without complaint.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an illness, especially one that is not serious, and often one that affects a particular part of the body
examples: He has a minor skin complaint.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to add to something in a way that improves it or makes it more attractive
examples: The excellent menu is complemented by a good wine list.
The team needs players who complement each other.
The flavours in the dish complement each other perfectly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: including all the parts, etc. that are necessary; whole
examples: OPPOSITE incomplete
a complete list/sequence/picture/profile
I've collected the complete set.
a complete guide to events in Oxford
the complete works of Tolstoy
You will receive payment for each complete day that you work.
You've made my life complete.
A Chinese New Year celebration would not be complete without fireworks.
No trip to Moscow would be complete without a visit to Lenin's tomb.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: finished
examples: OPPOSITE incomplete
The job is almost complete.
Ther ordering process is nearly complete.
Construction of the new airport is scheduled to be complete by late September.
Work on the office building will be complete at the end of the year.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 2

The condition of the roads is poor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of somebody’s health or how fit they are
examples: He is overweight and out of condition (= not physically fit).
The motorcyclist was in a critical condition (= at risk of dying) in hospital last night.
in a stable/serious condition
You are in no condition (= too ill/sick, etc.) to go anywhere.
She shouldn't be smoking in her condition (= because she is pregnant).
Her condition has deteriorated.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an illness or a medical problem that you have for a long time because it is not possible to cure it
examples: Does your child have any kind of medical condition that we should know about?
She has a serious health condition.
a heart/skin condition
He suffers from a serious heart condition.
The drug is used to treat conditions such as epilepsy.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the circumstances or situation in which people live, work or do things
examples: working/living conditions
economic/market conditions
They were working under appalling conditions.
a strike over pay and conditions
to improve conditions for workers
He grew up in conditions of poverty.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the physical situation that affects how something happens
examples: The plants grow best in cool, damp conditions.
The boat sank in adverse weather conditions.
dry/wet/harsh, etc. conditions
Studies show that the drug may be harmful under certain conditions.
extreme environmental conditions
treacherous driving conditions
Conditions are ideal for sailing today.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a rule or decision that you must agree to, sometimes forming part of a contract or an official agreement
examples: Read the terms and conditions carefully before you sign.
The offer is subject to certain conditions.
They agreed to lend us the car on condition that (= only if) we returned it before the weekend.
The officials spoke on condition of anonymity.
They will give us the money on one condition—that we pay it back within six months.
They agreed under the condition that the matter be dealt with promptly.
Congress can impose strict conditions on the bank.
to satisfy/meet/fulfill a condition
They have agreed to a ceasefire provided their conditions are met.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a situation that must exist in order for something else to happen
examples: Stable political leadership is a necessary condition for economic growth.
conditions for investment/success/development
We are working to create the conditions for peace.
Applicants must agree to teach for three years as a condition of admission to the program.
You can't make a consumer buy something as a condition of getting a loan.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the state of a particular group of people because of their situation in life, their problems, etc.
examples: He spoke angrily about the condition of the urban poor.
Work is basic to the human condition (= the fact of being alive).
We are aiming to improve the condition of the urban poor.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: new or as good as new; in perfect condition
examples: We sell first editions of rare books in mint condition.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: not in any situation; never
examples: You must on no condition tell them what happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to organize and/or do a particular activity
examples: to conduct an experiment/inquiry/investigation/interview
to conduct a survey/poll/study/review
to conduct a test/trial
to conduct research/business
There are concerns about the way in which the firm conducts its acitvities.
The battalion had been preparing to conduct operations in the same area.
Police conducted a thorough search of the building.
The negotiations have been conducted in a positive manner.
They conducted a vigorous campaign for a shorter working week.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to direct a group of people who are singing or playing music
examples: a concert by the London Philharmonic Orchestra, conducted by Marin Alsop
He conducted a programme of Sibelius and Tchaikovsky.
She will conduct works by Brahms and Schumann in tonight's concert.
She sang Gluck's Orfeo at Covent Garden, with Sir Thomas Beecham conducting.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to lead or guide somebody through or around a place
examples: a conducted tour of Athens (= one with a guide, giving information about it)
The guide conducted us around the ruins of the ancient city.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to behave in a particular way
examples: He conducted himself far better than expected.
The report challenges them to examine how they conduct themselves in the workplace.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to allow heat or electricity to pass along or through it
examples: Copper conducts electricity well.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to discuss something with somebody, in order to exchange opinions or get advice
examples: He wanted to confer with his colleagues before reaching a decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give somebody an award, a university degree or a particular honour or right
examples: An honorary degree was conferred on him by Oxford University in 2019.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large official meeting, usually lasting for a few days, at which people with the same work or interests come together to discuss their views
examples: The hotel is used for exhibitions, conferences and social events.
to host/organize a conference
to speak at/address a conference
The conference will be held in Glasgow.
Delegates to the Labour Party's annual conference will be staying in the Grand Hotel.
the national conference of the American Psychiatric Association
We met at an international conference.
The resolution will be debated at the party conference in Brighton.
She is attending a three-day conference on AIDS education.
a conference for health professionals from around the world
a conference room/centre

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a meeting at which people have formal discussions
examples: SEE ALSO press conference
They agreed to convene a peace conference by mid-November.
Her working day consists of conferences with foreign diplomats.
He was in conference with his lawyers all day.
Ministers from all four countries involved will meet at the conference table this week.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a group of sports teams that play against each other in a league
examples: Southeast Conference football champions

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to admit, especially formally or to the police, that you have done something wrong or illegal
examples: After hours of questioning, the suspect confessed.
She confessed to the murder.
He confessed that he had stolen the money.
She confessed to me that she had known his true identity for some time.
We persuaded her to confess her crime.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to admit something that you feel ashamed or embarrassed about
examples: SEE ALSO self-confessed
She was reluctant to confess her ignorance.
I must confess to knowing nothing about golf.
I confess (that) I know nothing about golf.
‘I know nothing about it,’ he confessed.
I confess myself bewildered by their explanation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to tell God or a priest about the bad things you have done so that you can say that you are sorry and be forgiven
examples: They had confessed their sins and done their penance.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to hear somebody confess their sins (= the bad things they have done)Word Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French confesser, from Latin confessus, past participle of confiteri ‘acknowledge’, from con- (expressing intensive force) + fateri ‘declare, avow’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a statement that a person makes, admitting that they are guilty of a crime; the act of making such a statement
examples: After hours of questioning by police, she made a full confession.
His confession was extracted under torture.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a statement admitting something that you are ashamed or embarrassed about; the act of making such a statement
examples: SYNONYM admission
I've a confession to make—I lied about my age.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a private statement to a priest about the bad things that you have done; an occasion when you make such a statement
examples: The priest heard her confession and granted absolution.
I used to go to confession every Saturday as a child.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a statement of your religious beliefs, principles, etc.
examples: a confession of faith

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the feeling that you can trust, believe in and be sure about the abilities or good qualities of somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO consumer confidence
The president's actions hardly inspire confidence.
The players all have confidence in their manager.
He believes his reforms will restore confidence in the financial markets.
The survey revealed a lack of confidence in the government.
She has the utmost confidence in her students' abilities.
Our aim is to increase public confidence in the democratic process.
The university is facing a crisis of confidence about its future role.
The new contracts have undermined the confidence of employees.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a belief in your own ability to do things and be successful
examples: SEE ALSO self-confidence
People often lose confidence when they are criticized.
He gained confidence when he went to college.
Receiving compliments from my work colleagues has boosted my confidence.
The course will help you build your confidence and develop your study skills.
While girls lack confidence, boys often overestimate their abilities.
He suffers from a lack of confidence.
She answered the questions with confidence.
I didn't have any confidence in myself at school.
Winning the award has given me much more confidence in my writing.
The training programmes have given workers the confidence to take on more responsibility.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the feeling that you are certain about something
examples: He said he wished that he shared her confidence.
They could not say with confidence that he would be able to walk again after the accident.
No one can predict with complete confidence what will happen in the financial markets.
She expressed her confidence that they would win.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a feeling of trust that somebody will keep information private
examples: It took a long time to gain her confidence (= make her feel she could trust me).
Eva told me about their relationship in confidence.
This is in the strictest confidence.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a secret that you tell somebody
examples: The girls exchanged confidences.
I could never forgive Mike for betraying a confidence.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be trusted with somebody’s secrets
examples: He is said to be very much in the president's confidence.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to tell somebody secrets and personal information about yourself
examples: She took me into her confidence and told me about the problems she was facing.
She thought she might take Leo into her confidence.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling sure about your own ability to do things and be successful
examples: SEE ALSO self-confident
She was in a relaxed, confident mood.
Beneath his confident and charming exterior, lurked a mass of insecurities.
I was actually fairly confident about my chances.
The teacher wants the children to feel confident about asking questions when they don't understand.
He'd learned to be confident in his ability to handle anything life threw at him.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: feeling certain that something will happen in the way that you want or expect
examples: The Democrats were confident of victory.
The team feels confident of winning.
We are confident about the future.
I'm confident that you will get the job.
He said he remained confident that the dispute could be resolved.
We're pretty confident we can win the case.
She was quietly confident that everything would go as planned.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an arrangement of the parts of something or a group of things; the form or shape that this arrangement produces
examples: The design is based on four configurations of squares.
There was a changing configuration of lights coming from the stadium.
The stars seemed to appear in a different configuration.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the equipment and programs that form a computer system and the way that these are set up to run
examples: Performance will vary depending on your hardware and software configurations.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to keep somebody/something inside the limits of a particular activity, subject, area, etc.
examples: SYNONYM restrict
The work will not be confined to the Glasgow area.
I will confine myself to looking at the period from 1900 to 1916.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to keep a person or an animal in a small or closed space
examples: Keep the dog confined in a suitable travelling cage.
Here the river is confined in a narrow channel.
The soldiers concerned were confined to barracks (= had to stay in the barracks, as a punishment).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have to stay in bed, in a wheelchair, etc.
examples: She was confined to bed with the flu.
He was confined to a wheelchair after the accident.
She's been confined to a wheelchair since having a bad fall.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to state or show that something is definitely true or correct, especially by providing evidence
examples: His guilty expression confirmed my suspicions.
to confirm a diagnosis/report
to confirm results/findings
Rumours of job losses were later confirmed.
We have yet to confirm the identities of the victims.
She said she could not confirm or deny the allegations.
The authorities refused to confirm any details.
Police sources confirmed that ten people had been arrested at the march.
A government official confirmed to the newspaper that Britain was pushing hard for an end to the arms embargo.
Can you confirm what happened?
It has been confirmed that an official complaint was made to the council.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make a position, an agreement, etc. more definite or official; to establish somebody/something clearly
examples: Please write to confirm your reservation (= say that it is definite).
After a six-month probationary period, her position was confirmed.
Has everyone confirmed (that) they’re coming?
It has been confirmed that the meeting will take place next week.
He was confirmed as captain for the rest of the season.
I'm very happy to confirm you in your post.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel or believe something even more strongly
examples: The walk in the mountains confirmed his fear of heights.
This latest tragedy merely confirms my view that the law must be tightened.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to perform the Christian or Jewish ceremony of confirmation
examples: She was baptized when she was a month old and confirmed when she was thirteen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a statement, letter, etc. that shows that something is true, correct or definite
examples: I'm still waiting for confirmation of the test results.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a ceremony at which a person becomes a full member of the Christian Church
examples: a confirmation service

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a Jewish ceremony similar to a bar mitzvah or bat mitzvah but usually for young people over the age of 16Word Origin
examples: Middle English: via Old French from Latin confirmatio(n-), from confirmare ‘make firm, establish’ from con- ‘together’ + firmare ‘strengthen’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a situation in which people, groups or countries disagree strongly or are involved in a serious argument
examples: The violence was the result of political and ethnic conflicts.
a conflict between two cultures
His task will be to resolve potential conflicts between the British and Scottish goverments.
The prime minister wants to avoid conflict with the unions.
The government has done nothing to resolve the conflict over nurses' pay.
She found herself in conflict with her parents over her future career.
John often comes into conflict with his boss.
The terms of the will became a source of conflict within the family.
She has received training in conflict resolution.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a violent situation or period of fighting between two countries
examples: armed/military conflict
The country has experienced internal conflict over the last decade.
Hopes of ending the conflict in the region are fading.
international efforts to find a peaceful solution to the conflict
This isolated state faces the risk of another violent conflict with its neighbour.
They are engaged in a bloody conflict over the disputed territory.
A conflict between the two countries could easily spread across the whole region.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a situation in which there are ideas, opinions, feelings or wishes that are opposed to each other; a situation in which it is difficult to choose
examples: Her diary was a record of her inner conflict.
The story tells of a classic conflict between love and duty.
Many of these ideas appear to be in conflict with each other.
He faced a conflict of loyalties.
a serious conflict of opinion

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a situation in which somebody has two jobs, aims, roles, etc. and cannot treat both of them equally and fairly at the same time
examples: There was a conflict of interest between his business dealings and his political activities.
One member of the planning committee had a conflict of interest as he lived near the proposed road.
There is often a conflict of interests between farmers and conservationists.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to appear and need to be dealt with by somebody
examples: What is to be done about the economic problems confronting the country?
I was suddenly confronted by the task of rewriting the entire book.
The government found itself confronted by massive opposition.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to deal with a problem or difficult situation
examples: SYNONYM face up to
She knew that she had to confront her fears.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to face somebody so that they cannot avoid seeing and hearing you, especially in an unfriendly or dangerous situation
examples: This was the first time he had confronted an armed robber.
Confronted by an angry crowd, the police retreated.
The demonstrators found themselves confronted by a line of police, blocking the road.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make somebody face or deal with an unpleasant or difficult person or situation
examples: He confronted her with a choice between her career or their relationship.
These texts constantly confront the reader with their demanding claims.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have something in front of you that you have to deal with or react to
examples: Most people when confronted with a horse will pat it.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a situation in which there is anger between people or groups who disagree because they have different opinions
examples: She wanted to avoid another confrontation with her father.
Confrontation between employers and unions has resulted in strike action.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make somebody unable to think clearly or understand something
examples: These two sets of statistics are guaranteed to confuse the public.
They confused me with conflicting accounts of what happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to think wrongly that somebody/something is somebody/something else
examples: SYNONYM mix up
People often confuse me and my twin sister.
Be careful not to confuse quantity with quality.
She says that meteors breaking apart can easily be confused for UFOs.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a subject more difficult to understand
examples: His comments only served to confuse the issue further.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: unable to think clearly or to understand what is happening or what somebody is saying
examples: I'm confused—say all that again.
I'm getting really confused now. What has that got to do with it?
He was depressed and in a confused state of mind.
a confused look/expression
teenagers who are confused about their sexuality
People are confused about all the different labels on food these days.
She seemed confused by the question.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not clear or easy to understand
examples: The children gave a confused account of what had happened.
His mind was crowded with confused thoughts.
A confused situation followed the military coup.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: difficult to understand; not clear
examples: The instructions on the box are very confusing.
a confusing situation/experience
confusing messages/signals
a confusing array of options
This is where it all starts to get really confusing.
Beginners may find the terminology confusing.
The new signs will be very confusing for tourists.
All this information can be confusing to the user.
The site is somewhat confusing to navigate.
It would be confusing to have two set of regulations for a single country.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a state of not being certain about what is happening, what you should do, what something means, etc.
examples: The announcement caused a lot of confusion.
There is some confusion about what the correct procedure should be.
There was a confusion as to what to do next.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of making a mistake about who somebody is or what something is
examples: To avoid confusion, please write the children's names clearly on all their school clothes.
confusion between letters of the alphabet like ‘o’ or ‘a’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a situation in which you feel embarrassed because you do not understand something and are not sure what to do
examples: He looked at me in confusion and did not answer the question.
Sacha felt confusion sweeping over her as she read the letter.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a confused situation in which people do not know what action to take
examples: Fighting had broken out and all was chaos and confusion.
Her unexpected arrival threw us into total confusion.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell somebody that you are pleased about their success or achievements
examples: I congratulated them all on their results.
The authors are to be congratulated on producing such a clear and authoritative work.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to feel pleased and proud because you have achieved something or been successful at something
examples: You can congratulate yourself on having done an excellent job.
The organizers are congratulating themselves on attracting record numbers to the event.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of people who are gathered together in a church for a religious service, not including the priest and choir
examples: The congregation stood to sing the hymn.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of people who regularly attend a particular church
examples: members of local congregations

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a group or collection of people, animals or things
examples: Large congregations of birds may cause public harm.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: related to or belonging to a congress or the Congress in the US
examples: a congressional committee/bill
the midterm Congressional elections

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to join together two or more things; to be joined together
examples: The towns are connected by train and bus services.
The island is connected to the mainland by a bridge.
The canal was built to connect Sheffield with the Humber estuary.
The rooms on this floor connect.
a connecting door (= one that connects two rooms)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to join something to the main supply of electricity, gas, water, etc. or to another piece of equipment
examples: OPPOSITE disconnect
We're waiting for the broadband to be connected.
First connect the printer to the computer.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to join a computer or a mobile device to the internet or to a computer network
examples: OPPOSITE disconnect
The device can be hooked up to a mobile phone to connect wirelessly.
Click ‘Continue’ to connect to the internet.
laptops that connect wirelessly to the Net
The system harnesses the processing power of many computers connected by a high-speed network.
Simply connect your device to the camera's Wi-Fi signal.
Many guests leave their laptops connected to the hotel network when they're not in their rooms.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to notice or make a link between people, things, events, etc.
examples: SYNONYM associate
I was surprised to hear them mentioned together: I had never connected them before.
There was nothing to connect him with the crime.
He made a statement connecting the terrorist group to the attack.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to arrive just before another one leaves so that passengers can change from one to the other
examples: His flight to Amsterdam connects with an afternoon flight to New York.
There's a connecting flight at noon.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to put somebody in contact by phone
examples: SYNONYM put through
After a long wait I was connected to customer services.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to form a good relationship with somebody so that you like and understand each other
examples: They met a couple of times but they didn't really connect.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to hit somebody/something
examples: The blow connected and she felt a surge of pain.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: (of two or more things or people) having a link between them
examples: OPPOSITE unconnected
We do not believe that the incidents are connected.
The two issues are closely connected.
market prices and other connected matters
The fall in retail sales is directly connected with the decline in employment.
jobs connected with the environment
Many computer files connected to the case have been erased.
They are connected by marriage.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that connects two facts, ideas, etc.
examples: SYNONYM link
Scientists have established a connection between cholesterol levels and heart disease.
a direct/close/strong connection with something
His resignation must have some connection with the recent scandal.
Consumers are more likely to buy something from a person or shop they feel a personal connection to.
How did you make the connection (= realize that there was a connection between two facts that did not seem to be related)?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of connecting or the state of being connected
examples: a broadband/wireless/Wi-Fi/network connection
I'm having problems with my internet connection.
Connection to the gas supply was delayed for three days.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a point, especially in an electrical system, where two parts connect
examples: A faulty connection caused the machine to stop.
If you break the connection, the light won't come on.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a train, bus or plane at a station or an airport that a passenger can take soon after getting off another in order to continue their journey
examples: I missed the connection by five minutes.
We'll be lucky if we make our connection.
We arrived in good time for the connection to Paris.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a means of travelling to another place
examples: There are good bus and train connections between the resort and major cities.
good connections with New York

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a person or an organization that you know and that can help or advise you in your social or professional life
examples: SYNONYM contact
One of my business connections gave them my name.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: people who are your relatives, but not members of your close family
examples: She is British but also has German connections.
a network of family connections in Italy

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: for reasons connected with somebody/something
examples: A man has been arrested in connection with the murder of the teenager.
I am writing to you in connection with your recent job application.
I am writing in connection with your recent job application.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: for reasons connected with something recently mentionedWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Latin connexio(n-), from connectere, from con- ‘together’ + nectere ‘bind’. The spelling -ct (18th cent.) is from connect, on the pattern of pairs such as collect, collection.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take control of a country or city and its people by force
examples: The Normans conquered England in 1066.
In 330 BC Persia was conquered by Alexander the Great.
conquered peoples/races/territories
The Roman empire offered citizenship to its conquered peoples.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to defeat somebody, especially in a competition, race, etc.
examples: The world champion conquered yet another challenger last night.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to succeed in dealing with or controlling something
examples: The only way to conquer a fear is to face it.
Mount Everest was conquered (= successfully climbed) in 1953.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: The band is now setting out to conquer the world.
This is a British film which could conquer the US market.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the part of your mind that tells you whether your actions are right or wrong
examples: SEE ALSO social conscience
to have a clear/guilty conscience (= to feel that you have done right/wrong)

He won't let it trouble his conscience.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a guilty feeling about something you have done or failed to do
examples: She was seized by a sudden pang of conscience.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: SEE ALSO prisoner of conscience
freedom of conscience (= the freedom to do what you believe to be right)
Emilia is the voice of conscience in the play.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: believing your actions to be fair
examples: SYNONYM honestly
We cannot in all conscience refuse to help.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: making you feel guilty for doing or failing to do something
examples: I'll write and apologize. I've had it on my conscience for weeks.
It’s still on my conscience that I didn’t warn him in time.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make you feel guilty about something; to feel guilty about something
examples: Her conscience pricked her as she lied to her sister.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: aware of something; noticing something
examples: OPPOSITE unconscious

I was vaguely conscious that I was being watched.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: able to use your senses and mental powers to understand what is happening
examples: OPPOSITE unconscious
A patient who is not fully conscious should never be left alone.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: OPPOSITE unconscious
a conscious choice

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: SEE ALSO class-conscious

an image-conscious reality star

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: directly under the control of the person concerned
examples: When you go to sleep, it is only the conscious mind that shuts down.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being able to use your senses and mental powers to understand what is happening
examples: I can't remember any more—I must have lost consciousness.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of being aware of something

his consciousness of the challenge facing him
class-consciousness (= consciousness of different classes in society)

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 1

He is beginning his fourth consecutive term of office.
After six consecutive defeats, the team was almost ready to give up.
Interest rates rose again for the fifth consecutive month.
They achieved their third consecutive year of record sales.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: agreement about something
examples: She was chosen as leader by common consent (= everyone agreed to the choice).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an official document giving permission for something
examples: Your family, in effect, signs the consent for you.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: to encourage the conservation of water/fuel

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to think about something, especially the feelings of other people, and be influenced by it when making a decision, etc.
examples: You should consider other people before you act.

examples: He stood there, considering the painting.

examples: It is my considered opinion that you are wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 6
