definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a change that makes something more accurate than it was before
examples: I've made a few small corrections to your report.
The paper had to publish a correction to the story.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act or process of correcting something
examples: There are some programming errors that need correction.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: punishment
examples: the correction of young offenders

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that is accurate or true, without any mistakes
examples: OPPOSITE incorrectly
Have you spelled it correctly?
Students correctly identified 16 trees species found on their study sites.
If I remember correctly, he was still the prime minister at that point.
They reasoned, correctly, that she was away for the weekend.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a way that is right and suitable, so that something is done as it should be done
examples: OPPOSITE incorrectly
When correctly applied, fake tan is difficult to tell from the real thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a way that follows the accepted standards or rules
examples: He was looking correctly grave.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if two or more facts, figures, etc. correlate or if a fact, figure, etc. correlates with another, the facts are closely connected and affect or depend on each other
examples: The figures do not seem to correlate.
A high-fat diet correlates with a greater risk of heart disease.
The average speed of the vehicles correlates closely with the severity of the accident caused.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to show that there is a close connection between two or more facts, figures, etc.
examples: Researchers are trying to correlate the two sets of figures.
Property values are negatively correlated to the tax rate.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a connection between two things in which one thing changes as the other does
examples: SEE ALSO rank correlation
There is a direct correlation between exposure to sun and skin cancer.
the correlation of social power with wealth

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be the same as or match something
examples: SYNONYM agree
Your account and hers do not correspond.
Your account of events does not correspond with hers.
The written record of the conversation doesn't correspond to (= is different from) what was actually said.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be similar to or the same as something else
examples: The British job of Lecturer corresponds roughly to the US Associate Professor.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to write letters or emails, etc. to somebody and receive letters or emails, etc. from them
examples: She corresponded regularly with her former teacher.
I have corresponded with him in the past.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the letters, emails, etc. a person sends and receives
examples: personal/private correspondence
The editor welcomes correspondence from readers on any subject.
the correspondence column/page (= in a newspaper)
Jane Austen's correspondence with her sister

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the activity of writing letters
examples: I refused to enter into any correspondence (= to exchange letters) with him about it.
We have been in correspondence for months.
We kept up a correspondence for many years.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a connection between two things; the fact of two things being similar
examples: There is a close correspondence between the two extracts.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who reports news from a particular country or on a particular subject for a newspaper or a television or radio station
examples: She's the BBC's political correspondent.
a foreign/war/sports correspondent
our Delhi correspondent

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who writes letters, emails, etc. to another person
examples: She's a poor correspondent (= she does not write regularly).
He was a vivid and witty correspondent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: matching or connected with something that you have just mentioned
examples: SYNONYM equivalent
A change in the money supply brings a corresponding change in expenditure.
Profits have risen by 15 per cent compared with the corresponding period last year.
The Redskins lost to the Cowboys in the corresponding game last year.
Fewer houses are available, but there is no corresponding decrease in demand.
Give each picture a number corresponding to its position on the page.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long narrow passage in a building, with doors that open into rooms on either side
examples: His room is along the corridor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a long narrow piece of land belonging to one country that passes through the land of another country; a part of the sky over a country that planes, for example from another country, can fly through
examples: SEE ALSO air corridor
UN troops will secure the land corridor so that food supplies can reach the trapped civilians.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a long narrow piece of land that follows the course of an important road or river
examples: the electronics industry in the M4 corridor
a now-submerged land corridor between northern Africa and southern Europe

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a passage along the side of some railway trains, from which doors lead into separate compartments

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the higher levels of government, where important decisions are made
examples: She had considerable influence in the corridors of power.
She was a minister with considerable influence in the corridors of power.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: willing to use their power to do dishonest or illegal things in return for money or to get an advantage
examples: It was seen as the only way to overthrow a corrupt regime.
They promised to seek out the corrupt officials who had accepted the bribes.
one of the most notoriously corrupt city councils

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not honest or moral
examples: They had been engaged in corrupt practices.
The whole system is inefficient and corrupt.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: containing changes or faults, and no longer in the original state
examples: corrupt software
The file on the disk seems to be corrupt.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: dishonest or illegal behaviour, especially of people in authority
examples: allegations of bribery and corruption
The new district attorney has promised to fight police corruption.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act or effect of making somebody change from moral to immoral standards of behaviour
examples: He claimed that sex and violence on TV led to the corruption of young people.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the form of a word or phrase that has become changed from its original form in some way; the process by which a word or phrase changes form in this way
examples: The word ‘holiday’ is a corruption of ‘holy day’.
He thought it was possible to secure the language from corruption and decay.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the effect when data is changed by accident in a computer system due to hardware or software failure
examples: A failure of a hard disk can cause unrecoverable data corruption.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the amount of money that you need in order to buy, make or do something
examples: SEE ALSO low-cost
the high/low cost of housing
A new computer system has been installed at a cost of £80 000.
You could buy a used car at a fraction of the cost of a new one.
We did not even make enough money to cover the cost of the food.
Consumers will have to bear the full cost of these pay increases.
The plan had to be abandoned on grounds of cost.
The total cost to you (= the amount you have to pay) is £3 000.
Energy is a major cost for businesses.
He estimates the cost for this project at $150 000.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the total amount of money that needs to be spent by a business
examples: The use of cheap labour helped to keep costs down.
Reducing costs means we can keep prices as low as possible.
We have to find new ways of cutting costs.
The company is focused on lowering its operating costs.
We have had to raise our prices because of rising costs.
Opinion was divided on the potential costs and benefits of the scheme.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the effort, loss or damage that is involved in order to do or achieve something
examples: the terrible cost of the war in death and suffering
the environmental cost of nuclear power
She saved him from the fire at the cost of her own life (= she died).
Victory came at a high cost.
They advanced a few hundred metres, but at a heavy cost in life.
He worked non-stop for three months, at considerable cost to his health.
I felt a need to please people, whatever the cost in time and energy.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the sum of money that somebody is ordered to pay for lawyers, etc. in a legal case
examples: He was ordered to pay £2 000 costs.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: whatever is needed to achieve something
examples: You must stop the press from finding out at all costs.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: under any circumstances
examples: He is determined to win at any cost.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: for only the amount of money that is needed to make or get something, without any profit being added on
examples: goods sold at cost

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to feel the bad effects of a mistake, an accident, etc.
examples: The town is now counting the cost of its failure to provide adequate flood protection.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to know something because of something unpleasant that has happened to you
examples: He's a ruthless businessman, as I know to my cost.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: causing problems or the loss of something
examples: SYNONYM expensive
a costly mistake/failure
Mining can be costly in terms of lives (= too many people can die).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the clothes worn by people from a particular place or during a particular historical period
examples: SEE ALSO national costume
an exhibition of Victorian costumes
She wore a traditional costume of bright pink silk.
a painting of an old woman in Welsh costume

definitions.definition: the clothes worn by actors in a play or film, or worn by somebody to make them look like somebody/something else
examples: The former dancer has also designed the costumes.

They are already planning their costumes for Halloween.

She has four costume changes during the play.
a costume designer

definitions.definition: a piece of clothing worn for swimming, especially the type worn by women and girls
examples: If you’d like a swim, we can lend you a costume.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small house, especially in the country
examples: a thatched cottage
a holiday cottage
James lived in a charming country cottage with roses around the door.

definitions.definition: a plant grown in warm countries for the soft white hairs around its seeds that are used to make cloth and thread
examples: From the age of six she worked in the fields, picking cotton.
bales of cotton
cotton fields/plantations/plants

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the cloth made from the cotton plant
examples: The sheets are 100 per cent pure cotton.
a cotton shirt/skirt
printed cotton cloth
the cotton industry
a cotton mill
a pure cotton T-shirt
shivering in her thin cotton nightdress

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: thread that is used for sewing
examples: sewing cotton
a cotton reel

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a soft mass of white material that is used for cleaning the skin or a wound
examples: Use a cotton ball to apply the lotion.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used as the past tense of ‘can’
examples: She said that she couldn't come.
I couldn't hear what they were saying.
Sorry, I couldn't get any more.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to ask if you can do something
examples: Could I use your phone, please?
Could we stop by next week?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to politely ask somebody to do something for you
examples: Could you babysit for us on Friday?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that something is or might be possible
examples: I could do it now, if you like.
Don't worry—they could have just forgotten to call.
You couldn't have left it on the bus, could you?
‘Have some more cake.’ ‘Oh, I couldn't, thank you (= I'm too full).’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to suggest something
examples: We could write a letter to the director.
You could always try his home number.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to show that you are annoyed that somebody did not do something
examples: They could have let me know they were going to be late!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how strongly you want to express your feelings
examples: I'm so fed up I could scream!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that you need or would like to have something
examples: I could do with a drink!
Her hair could have done with a wash.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of people who are elected to govern an area such as a city or county
examples: SEE ALSO band council
a town council

a member/meeting of the council
the leader of the council
a council member/leader
a council meeting/chamber

cuts to council services

examples: SEE ALSO the Medical Research Council
the Medical Research Council
In Britain, the Arts Council gives grants to theatres.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (especially in the past) a formal meeting to discuss what action to take in a particular situation
examples: The king held a council at Nottingham from 14 to 19 October 1330.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a member of a city or county council
examples: SEE ALSO councilman
Councillor Ann Jones
Talk to your local councillor about the problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: professional advice about a problem
examples: The couple decided to go for relationship counselling.
Some groups offer bereavement counselling.
a student counselling service

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who has been trained to advise people with problems, especially personal problems
examples: I went to see a debt counsellor and she agreed to come to the bank with me.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a lawyer

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is in charge of young people at a summer camp
examples: SEE ALSO guidance counselor

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say numbers in the correct order
examples: Billy can't count yet.
She can count up to 10 in Italian.
to count from 1 to 10

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to calculate the total number of people, things, etc. in a particular group
examples: They're still counting votes in Texas.
I can't count the number of times I've eaten there (= I've eaten there very many times).
The diet is based on counting calories.
She began to count up how many guests they had to invite.
There are twelve weeks to go, counting from today.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to include somebody/something when you calculate a total
examples: We have invited 50 people, not counting the children.
The tour guide was sure one person was missing from the group until she realized she had forgotten to count herself.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be important
examples: SYNONYM matter
It is going to be a close election, so every vote counts.
Every point in this game counts.
With our busy lives today we have less and less time for what really counts.
It's the thought that counts (= used about a small but kind action or gift).
The fact that she had apologized counted for nothing with him.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be officially accepted; to accept something officially
examples: Don't go over that line or your throw won't count.
The goal wouldn't have counted anyway, because the linesman's flag was up for offside.
The home team's manager protested that the run should count.
Applications received after 1 July will not be counted.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to consider somebody/something in a particular way; to be considered in a particular way
examples: For tax purposes that money counts/is counted as income.
I count him among my closest friends.
I count myself lucky to have known him.
She counts herself one of the lucky ones.
I count it a privilege to have served alongside him.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that a total is continuing to increase
examples: The movie's ticket sales add up to $39 million, and counting.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that the total number of somebody/something is very small
examples: She could count on the fingers of one hand the people she actually enjoyed being with.
Although she knew lots of people, she could count her friends on the fingers of one hand.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be grateful for the good things in your life

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to feel the bad effects of a mistake, an accident, etc.
examples: The town is now counting the cost of its failure to provide adequate flood protection.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to imagine that sheep are jumping over a fence and to count them, as a way of getting to sleep

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: you should not be too confident that something will be successful, because something may still go wrong

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to say publicly that you support somebody or you agree with something
examples: Everyone needs to stand up and be counted in order to make them see the strength of our conviction.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not care how many times something happens
examples: I've seen the film five times, but who's counting?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long flat surface over which goods are sold or business is done in a shop, bank, etc.
examples: I asked the woman behind the counter if they had any postcards.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a flat surface in a kitchen for preparing food on
examples: She put her bags down on the kitchen counter.
The kitchen had black marble counter tops.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a small disc used for playing or scoring in some board games
examples: SEE ALSO bargaining counter

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: SEE ALSO bean counter

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: The employers' association was seen as a counter to union power.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: SEE ALSO over-the-counter

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: COMPARE your opposite number

The women's shoe, like its male counterpart, is specifically designed for the serious tennis player.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very many; too many to be counted or mentioned
examples: COMPARE uncountable
I've warned her countless times.
The new treatment could save Emma's life and the lives of countless others.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an area of land that has or used to have its own government and laws
examples: SEE ALSO mother country
European countries
developing countries
It's good to meet people from different parts of the country.
She didn't know what life in a foreign country would be like.
It's the most popular music festival in the country.
House prices are rising across the whole country.
Demonstrations were held in cities around the country.
people from other countries

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: any area outside towns and cities, with fields, woods, farms, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO up-country
I live in the country.
We spent a pleasant day in the country.
The house is at the end of a narrow country lane.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an area of land, especially with particular physical features, suitable for a particular purpose or connected with a particular person or people
examples: SEE ALSO backcountry
The town is surrounded by miles and miles of open country.
This part of Africa is rich farming country.
superb walking country
Explore Thomas Hardy country.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the people of a country; the nation as a whole
examples: They have the support of most of the country.
The rich benefited from the reforms, not the country as a whole.
The whole country is depending on you.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a type of popular music in the style of the traditional music of the southern US, with singing and dance tunes played on violin, guitar and banjo
examples: pop, folk and country

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: directly across fields, etc.; not by a main road
examples: riding across country

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to hold an election to choose a new parliament

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used as a reply when somebody suggests that you should not do something, or when somebody has asked permission or said they are going to do something
examples: It's a free country; I'll say what I like!
Wear what you like. It's a free country.
‘It's a free country!’ he shouted. ‘I can do what I like!’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: land outside towns and cities, with fields, woods, etc.
examples: The surrounding countryside is windswept and rocky.
magnificent views over open countryside
the beautiful countryside of Wales
Everyone should enjoy the right of access to the countryside.
the quieter pace of life in the countryside

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of a number of areas that some countries are divided into, each with its own local government
examples: SEE ALSO Home Counties
rural counties west of the Mississippi
Oxfordshire and neighbouring counties
the southern/northern counties
Orange County
Originally, county boundaries often followed the course of a river.
the most dangerous stretch of road in the county
Most towns and villages throughout the county have experienced a population increase.
Children from schools across the county will be taking part.
Public meetings are being planned at various locations around the county.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sudden change of government that is illegal and often violent
examples: SEE ALSO palace coup
He seized power in a military coup in 2008.
to stage/mount a coup
He was sentenced to death for his part in the attempted coup.
a failed/an abortive coup
She lost her position in a boardroom coup (= a sudden change of power among senior managers in a company).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of achieving something that was difficult to do
examples: Getting this contract has been quite a coup for us.
He pulled off a major diplomatic coup by winning agreement from all the warring factions on a permanent ceasefire.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: two people or things
examples: I saw a couple of men get out.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small number of people or things
examples: We went there a couple of years ago.
a couple of minutes/hours/days/weeks/months
a couple of people/friends/guys
I've seen her a couple of times before.
I'll be with you in a minute. There are a couple of things I have to do first.
We can do it in the next couple of weeks.
The have been some new developments in the past couple of days.
The last couple of years have been difficult.
There are a couple more files to read first.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: two people who are seen together, especially if they are married or in a romantic or sexual relationship
examples: SEE ALSO happy couple
married couples
same-sex/gay/lesbian couples
a young couple
an elderly couple
The royal couple will visit New Zealand next year.
Several couples were on the dance floor.
The couple was/were married in 2016.
We met a couple from Chicago, who were travelling with their three children.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very soon
examples: We’ll be there in a couple of shakes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the ability to do something dangerous, or to face pain or opposition, without showing fear
examples: SYNONYM bravery
He showed great courage and determination.
moral/physical courage
They had the courage to stand up and fight for what they believed in.
He couldn't find the courage to tell his daughters what had happened.
Many said that the women's stories gave them the courage to pursue their goals
I haven't yet plucked up the courage to ask her.
It takes courage to sing in public.
His courage in battle won him a promotion.
She displayed remarkable courage in the face of danger.
I admire your courage in saying what you think.
They fought with courage, but were no match for the enemy.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be/not be brave enough to do what you feel to be right
examples: You need to have the courage of your convictions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to force yourself to be brave enough to do something
examples: I finally screwed up my courage and went to the dentist.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to begin to feel happier and more confident because of something

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make yourself do something that you are afraid of
examples: Taking her courage in both hands, she opened the door and walked in.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a series of lessons or lectures on a particular subject
examples: SEE ALSO access course
a French/chemistry course
He took a course in Russian language and literature.
I want to do a course in art and design.
The department offers short courses in drama, fiction, and poetry.
She teaches a course on internet crime.
My boss has been on a course this week.
You need to go on a management training course.
He has recently completed the five-week course.
The college runs specialist language courses.
I enrolled in a ten-week online course.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a period of study at a college or university that leads to an exam or a qualification
examples: COMPARE programme
What degree course did you choose?
a two-year postgraduate course leading to a master’s degree
He was able to design his own course of study.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a large area of land that is designed for playing golf on
examples: He set a new course record.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an area of land or water where races are held
examples: SEE ALSO assault course
She was overtaken on the last stretch of the course.
Only ten yachts completed the course.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: any of the separate parts of a meal
examples: a four-course dinner
The main course was roast duck.
We had chicken for our main course.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a direction or route followed by a ship or an aircraft
examples: He radioed the pilot to change course.
The plane was off course (= not going in the right direction).
We're on course for our destination.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the general direction in which somebody’s ideas or actions are moving or in which things are developing
examples: The president appears likely to change course on some key issues.
The dollar fell sharply for two days, and then reversed course.
Her career followed a similar course to her sister's.
Politicians are often obliged to steer a course between incompatible interests.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a way of acting in or dealing with a particular situation
examples: There are various courses open to us.
What course of action would you recommend?
It was the best course of action to take in the circumstances.
The wisest course would be to say nothing.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the way something develops or should develop
examples: This was an event that changed the course of history.
The unexpected course of events aroused considerable alarm.
She repeatedly raised the issue during the course of the campaign.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the direction a river moves in
examples: The path follows the course of the river.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a series of medical treatments, tablets, etc.
examples: to prescribe a course of antibiotics
When taking antibiotics it is important to finish the course.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a continuous layer of brick, stone or other building material in a wall
examples: SEE ALSO damp course
A new damp-proof course could cost £1 000 or more.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be in a situation that is almost certain to cause an argument
examples: I was on a collision course with my boss over the sales figures.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be moving in a direction in which it is likely that you will crash into somebody/something
examples: A giant iceberg was on a collision course with the ship.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be just what you would expect to happen or expect somebody to do in a particular situation
examples: SYNONYM norm
Starting early and working long hours is par for the course in this job.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: the act of matching people with suitable jobs or tasks

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: going through a particular process
examples: The new textbook is in course of preparation.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: during
examples: He's seen many changes in the course of his long life.
The company faces major challenges over the course of the next few years.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: when enough time has passed
examples: SYNONYM eventually
It is possible that in the course of time a cure for cancer will be found.
In the course of time, I began to understand.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: at the right time and not before
examples: Your request will be dealt with in due course.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: as things usually happen
examples: SYNONYM normally
In the normal course of things we would not treat her disappearance as suspicious.
In the normal course of events, you should get a reply by Monday.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to allow natural processes to happen, without trying to stop or change them (used especially in the context of illness)
examples: The midwife must judge when to let nature take its course and when to intervene.
When the dog responded so badly to the treatment, we decided to let nature take its course.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: (as) the usual and correct thing to do
examples: We always check people's addresses as a matter of course.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: (to take/find) an acceptable course of action that avoids two extreme positions

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that what you are saying is true or correct
examples: ‘Don't you like my mother?’ ‘Of course I do!’
‘Will you be there?’ ‘Course I will.’

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: used as a polite way of giving somebody permission to do something
examples: ‘Can I come, too?’ ‘Course you can.’
‘Can I have one of those pens?’ ‘Of course—help yourself.’

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: used as a polite way of agreeing with what somebody has just said
examples: ‘I did all I could to help.’ ‘Of course,’ he murmured gently.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: used to show that what you are saying is not surprising or is generally known or accepted
examples: Ben, of course, was the last to arrive.
Of course, there are other ways of doing this.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the fact that you are saying ‘no’
examples: ‘Are you going?’ ‘Of course not.’
‘Do you mind?’ ‘No, of course not.’

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: likely to achieve or do something because you have already started to do it
examples: The American economy is on course for higher inflation than Britain by the end of the year.
Victory in Saturday’s match will put them on course to qualify for the European championships.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to tell a lie or to do something in order to prevent the police, etc. from finding out the truth about a crime

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to develop in the usual way and come to the usual end
examples: When her tears had run their course, she felt calmer and more in control.
With minor ailments the best thing is often to let nature take its course.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to continue doing something until it has finished or been completed, even though it is difficult
examples: Very few of the trainees have stayed the course.
He insists that he will not quit but will stay the course.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the place where legal trials take place and where crimes, etc. are judged
examples: SEE ALSO courthouse
the civil/criminal courts
Her lawyer made a statement outside the court.
Relatives of the dead girl were in court.
She will appear in court tomorrow.
They took their landlord to court for breaking the contract.
The case took five years to come to court (= to be heard by the court).
There wasn't enough evidence to bring the case to court (= start a trial).
The case was settled out of court (= a decision was reached without a trial).
He won the court case and was awarded damages.
She can't pay her tax and is facing court action.
During the court hearing, the prosecutor said she would seek maximum prison sentences.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the people in a court, especially those who make the decisions, such as the judge and jury
examples: SEE ALSO appeal court
Please tell the court what happened.
The court heard how the man collapsed after being stabbed.
The court ruled in favour of her claim.
This is not a case to be decided by the courts.
This evidence was not put before the court.
Airlines could face huge compensation bills following a court ruling on flight delays.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a place where games such as tennis and basketball are played
examples: SEE ALSO clay court
a tennis/squash/basketball court
He won after only 52 minutes on court.
The players are good friends off court and train together.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the official place where kings and queens live
examples: the court of Queen Victoria
He was presented to the queen at court.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the king or queen, their family, and the people who work for them and/or give advice to them
examples: The painting shows the emperor with his court.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an open space that is partly or completely surrounded by buildings and is usually part of a castle, a large house, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used in the names of blocks of flats or apartment buildings, or of some short streets; (in the UK) used in the names of some large houses
examples: The building is situated in a medieval court at the top of Edinburgh's royal mile.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a large open section of a building, often with a glass roof
examples: SEE ALSO food court

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: it is your/somebody’s responsibility to take action next
examples: They've offered me the job, so the ball's in my court now.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to entertain people by telling them interesting or funny things
examples: I met Giles holding court with some tourists in a cafe.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to completely reject an idea, a story, etc. that you think is not worth taking seriously at all
examples: All his attempts at explanation were simply laughed out of court.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to treat somebody with great respect in order to gain favour with them

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to say that something is completely wrong or not worth considering, especially in a trial
examples: The charges were thrown out of court.
Well that's my theory ruled out of court.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: polite behaviour that shows respect for other people
examples: SYNONYM politeness
I was treated with the utmost courtesy by the staff.
We asked them, as a matter of courtesy, if we could photograph their house.
It's only common courtesy to tell the neighbours that we'll be having a party (= the sort of behaviour that people would expect).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a polite thing that you say or do when you meet people in formal situations
examples: an exchange of courtesies before the meeting
The prime minister was welcomed with the usual courtesies.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: with the official permission of somebody/something and as a favour
examples: The pictures have been reproduced by courtesy of the British Museum.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: given as a prize or provided free by a person or an organization
examples: Win a weekend in Rome, courtesy of Fiat.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: as the result of a particular thing or situation
examples: Viewers can see the stadium from the air, courtesy of a camera fastened to the plane.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be polite by doing the thing that is mentioned
examples: Please do me the courtesy of listening to what I'm saying.
She might have done me the courtesy of replying to my letter.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to know when you should do something in order to be polite
examples: You think he'd at least have the courtesy to call to say he'd be late.
You could at least have had the courtesy to let me know.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a child of your aunt or uncle
examples: SEE ALSO country cousin
She's my cousin.
We're cousins.
This is my cousin Richard.
He's a cousin once removed (= separated by one generation of our family).
She's a cousin of the bride.
He claims to be a cousin to the Queen.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is in your wider family but who is not closely related to you
examples: SEE ALSO kissing cousin
She's some sort of cousin, I think.
He's a distant cousin of mine.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a way of describing people from another country who are similar in some way to people in your own country
examples: our American cousins

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a way of describing things that are similar or related in some way
examples: Asian elephants are smaller than their African cousins.
These pigs are close cousins of the wild hog.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to place something over or in front of something in order to hide, protect or decorate it
examples: Cover the chicken loosely with foil.
She covered her face with her hands.
I covered my mouth to stifle a yawn.
He laughed to cover (= hide) his nervousness.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to lie or spread over the surface of something
examples: Snow covered the ground.
Much of the country is covered by forest.
Its head, body, and tail are completely covered with brown fur.
His chest was covered in bruises.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to put or spread a layer of liquid, dust, etc. on somebody/something
examples: The wind blew in from the desert and covered everything with sand.
Soak the dried mushrooms by covering them in boiling water for a few minutes.
The steps were now completely covered with water.
The players were soon covered in mud.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to include something; to deal with something
examples: The lectures covered a lot of ground (= a lot of material, subjects, etc.).
The survey covers all aspects of the business.
The articles cover a wide range of subjects.
Each podcast covers a different topic.
the sales team covering the northern part of the country (= selling to people in that area)
Do the rules cover (= do they apply to) a case like this?
Don't worry. I've got it covered (= I'm dealing with it).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be or provide enough money for something
examples: $100 should cover your expenses.
The show barely covered its costs.
Your parents will have to cover your tuition fees.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to travel the distance mentioned
examples: By sunset we had covered thirty miles.
They walked for a long time and covered a good deal of ground.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to spread over the area mentioned
examples: The reserve covers an area of some 1 140 square kilometres.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to report on an event for television, a newspaper, etc.; to show an event on television
examples: She's covering the party's annual conference.
The BBC will cover all the major games of the tournament.
The media has consistently refused to cover the story.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to do somebody’s work or duties while they are away
examples: I'm covering for Jane while she's on leave.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to invent a lie or an excuse that will stop somebody from getting into trouble
examples: I have to go out for a minute—will you cover for me if anyone asks where I am?

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to protect somebody against loss, injury, etc. by insurance
examples: Are you fully covered for fire and theft?
Does this policy cover my husband to drive?

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to take action in order to protect yourself against being blamed for something
examples: Many firms put money aside to cover themselves against possible legal claims.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to protect somebody by threatening to shoot at anyone who tries to attack them
examples: Cover me while I move forward.
The artillery gave us covering fire (= shot to protect us).

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to aim a gun at a place or person so that nobody can escape or shoot
examples: The police covered the exits to the building.
Don't move—we've got you covered!

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to record a new version of a song that was originally recorded by another band or singer
examples: They've covered an old Rolling Stones number.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to consider and deal with all the things that could happen or could be needed when you are arranging something
examples: I am confident this contract covers all the bases.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to realize that you may be blamed or criticized for something later and take action to avoid this
examples: Get everything in writing in order to cover your back.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to hide the real situation or facts when these are not good or pleasant
examples: She was dressed in loose comfortable clothes that hid a multitude of sins.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to try and hide what you have done, because you do not want other people to find out about it
examples: He had attempted to cover his tracks by making her death appear like suicide.

examples: media/newspaper/press coverage
tonight’s live coverage of the hockey game
There was blanket coverage (= reports everywhere) of the royal divorce.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the range or quality of information that is included in a book or course of study, on television, etc.
examples: magazines with extensive coverage of diet and health topics
The book gives good, general coverage of the subject.
The volume offers incomplete coverage of the history of philosophy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the amount of something that something provides; the extent to which something covers an area or a group of people
examples: Immunization coverage against fatal diseases has increased to 99 per cent in some countries.
The service has a coverage of 90 per cent of the UK population.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: protection that an insurance company provides by promising to pay you money if a particular event happens
examples: insurance coverage
Medicaid health coverage for low-income families

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a layer or amount of something on it
examples: SEE ALSO snow-covered

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having a roof over it
examples: a covered walkway/bridge
a covered area of the stadium with seats

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having a layer of the thing mentioned on or around something
examples: chocolate-covered banana slices

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large animal kept on farms to produce milk or beef
examples: COMPARE bull
to milk a cow
cow’s milk
a herd of dairy cows (= cows kept for their milk)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the female of the elephant, whale and some other large animals
examples: SEE ALSO sea cow

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an offensive word for a woman
examples: You stupid cow!
That interfering old cow has never liked me.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an unpleasant person, thing or situation

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to become very angry or anxious about something
examples: Don't have a cow—it's no big deal.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: for a very long time; forever
examples: You can talk till the cows come home—you’ll never make me change my mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to break without dividing into separate parts; to break something in this way
examples: The ice cracked as I stepped onto it.
He has cracked a bone in his arm.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to break open or into pieces; to break something in this way
examples: A chunk of the cliff had cracked off in a storm.
His face cracked into a smile.
to crack a nut
She cracked an egg into the pan.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to hit something/somebody in a short hard manner
examples: I cracked my head on the low ceiling.
He cracked me on the head with a ruler.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make a sharp sound; to make something do this
examples: A shot cracked across the ridge.
He cracked his whip and galloped away.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if your voice cracks, it changes in depth, volume, etc. suddenly and in a way that you cannot control
examples: In a voice cracking with emotion, he told us of his son's death.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to no longer be able to function normally because of pressure
examples: Things are terrible at work and people are cracking under the strain.
They questioned him for days before he cracked.
The old institutions are cracking.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to find the solution to a problem, etc; to find the way to do something difficult
examples: to crack the enemy’s code
After a year in this job I think I've got it cracked!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to find a way of stopping or defeating a criminal or an enemy
examples: Police have cracked a major drugs ring.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to open a bottle, especially of wine, and drink it

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to tell a joke

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to use your authority or power to make somebody work very hard, usually by treating them in a strict way

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to make jokes
examples: This entertainer can crack wise with the best of them.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to begin immediately and work quickly
examples: SYNONYM get going
There's a lot to be done, so let's get cracking.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: a difficult problem or situation to deal with

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: not as good as people say
examples: He's not nearly such a good writer as he's cracked up to be.

examples: SEE ALSO arts and crafts
traditional crafts like basket-weaving

examples: chefs who learned their craft in top hotels
the writer’s craft

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an accident in which a vehicle hits something, for example another vehicle, usually causing damage and often injuring or killing the passengers
examples: SEE ALSO car crash
a car/plane crash
A man has been arrested in connection with a fatal crash on the M4 motorway.
It is not clear what caused the crash.
A girl was killed yesterday in a crash involving a stolen car.
34 people died in the train crash.
There were no other vehicles involved in the crash.
Mechanical failures were to blame for the crash of the helicopter.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sudden loud noise made, for example, by something falling or breaking
examples: The tree fell with a great crash.
The first distant crash of thunder shook the air.
She heard the crash of shattering glass as the vehicles collided.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a sudden serious fall in the price or value of something; the occasion when a business, etc. fails
examples: SYNONYM collapse
Some economists have been predicting another crash for years.
the 2008 stock market crash
the crash of 2008
a crash in share prices

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a sudden failure of a machine or system, especially of a computer or computer system
examples: Users won't lose important data if a hardware problem causes a crash.
a computer crash
A systems crash in the morning and a bomb scare in the afternoon provided enough excitement for one day.

She crawled under the fence.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: when an insect, a spider, etc. crawls, it moves forward on its legs
examples: There's a spider crawling up your leg.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move forward very slowly
examples: The traffic was crawling along.
The weeks crawled by.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be too friendly or helpful to somebody in authority, in a way that is not sincere, especially in order to get an advantage from them
examples: She's always crawling to the boss.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if you say that somebody comes/crawls out of the woodwork, you mean that they have suddenly appeared in order to express an opinion or to take advantage of a situation
examples: When he won the lottery, all sorts of distant relatives came out of the woodwork.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make you feel afraid or full of horror
examples: Just the sight of him makes my skin crawl.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not sensible; stupid
examples: Are you crazy? We could get killed doing that.
I'd never do anything like that. That's just crazy.
He drove like an idiot, passing in the craziest places.
What a crazy idea!
‘Love makes you do crazy things,’ she said.
I know it sounds crazy but it just might work.
She must be crazy to lend him money.
It's crazy to think he'll ever change.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very angry
examples: Doesn't it make you crazy when people don't reply to your emails?
That noise is driving me crazy.
Marie says he went crazy, and smashed the room up.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: The crowd went crazy when the band came on stage.

He's football-crazy.
I'm not crazy about Chinese food (= I don't like it very much).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: liking somebody very much; in love with somebody
examples: I've been crazy about him since the first time I saw him.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: mentally ill; insane
examples: SEE ALSO stir-crazy
I'd go crazy if I lived here.
She was driven half-crazy by the thought of him in prison.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: very fast, hard, much, etc.
examples: We worked like crazy to get it done on time.

whipped cream
a dollop of fresh cream
scones with cream and jam
I asked for two coffees with cream.
Would you like milk or cream in your coffee?
cream cakes (= containing cream)

examples: a chocolate/peppermint cream

moisturizing cream

a topical antibiotic cream
anti-wrinkle/anti-ageing cream
a cream cleaner

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make something happen or exist
examples: Scientists disagree about how the universe was created.
The main purpose of industry is to create wealth.
The government plans to create more jobs for young people.
Create a new directory and put all your files into it.
Try this new dish, created by our head chef.
The agreement will create new opportunities for the aviation industry.
Severe storms created some travel problems.
the newly created position of executive editor

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to produce a particular feeling or impression
examples: He's eager to create a good impression at work.
The company is trying to create a young energetic image.
The announcement only succeeded in creating confusion.
The reorganization has created a lot of bad feeling.
They've painted it red to create a feeling of warmth.
We work hard to create a pleasant environment for patients, visitors and staff.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to give somebody a particular rank or title
examples: The government has created eight new peers.
He was created a baronet in 1715.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be noticed and have an impact
examples: It's a film that promises to create ripples.
The debate has barely made a ripple here.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act or process of making something that is new, or of causing something to exist that did not exist before
examples: SEE ALSO job creation
Job creation needs to be the top priority.
a period of economic growth and wealth creation
content creation software
the creation of an independent state
The reforms led to the creation of 220 jobs.
The committee proposed the creation of a new Chair of Portuguese for the university.
He had been with the company since its creation in 1989.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that somebody has made, especially something that shows ability or imagination
examples: a literary creation
The cake was a delicious creation of sponge, cream and fruit.
The bright murals in the children’s ward were the creations of the nurses.
What an amazing creation (= a very unusual and new piece of clothing) you’re wearing!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the making of the world, especially by God as described in the Bible

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the world and all the living things in it
examples: They believe that God entrusted the care and use of all creation to mankind.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: involving the use of skill and the imagination to produce something new or a work of art
examples: a course on creative writing (= writing stories, plays and poems)
creative thinking (= thinking about problems in a new way or thinking of new ideas)
the company’s creative team/director
the creative process
She channels her creative energy into her art.
You can get creative with this recipe and add whatever fruit you like.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the skill and ability to produce something new, especially a work of art; showing this ability
examples: She's very creative—she writes poetry and paints.
Do you have any ideas? You're the creative one.
a highly creative artist
a creative genius/talent/mind

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the use of skill and imagination to produce something new or to produce art
examples: Creativity and originality are more important than technical skill.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who has made or invented a particular thing
examples: Walt Disney, the creator of Mickey Mouse

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: GodWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French creatour, creatur, from Latin creator, from creat- ‘created’, from the verb creare ‘to produce’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a living thing, real or imaginary, that can move around, such as an animal
examples: respect for all living creatures
alien/strange/mythical creatures
octopuses and other sea creatures
The dormouse is a shy, nocturnal creature.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person, considered in a particular way
examples: You pathetic creature!
She was an exotic creature with long red hair and brilliant green eyes.
He always goes to bed at ten—he's a creature of habit (= he likes to do the same things at the same time every day).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that depends completely on somebody else and is controlled by themWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in the sense ‘something created’): via Old French from late Latin creatura, from the verb creare ‘to produce’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality that somebody/something has that makes people believe or trust them
examples: SEE ALSO street cred
to gain/lack/lose credibility
The prosecution did its best to undermine the credibility of the witness.
After the recent scandal, the government has lost all credibility.
Newspapers were talking of a credibility gap between what he said and what he did.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that can be believed or trusted
examples: SYNONYM convincing
a credible explanation/witness
It is just not credible that she would cheat.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that can be accepted, because it seems possible that it could be successful
examples: SYNONYM viable
Community service is seen as the only credible alternative to imprisonment.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an arrangement that you make, with a shop for example, to pay later for something you buy
examples: COMPARE hire purchase
to get credit
We bought the dishwasher on credit.
to offer interest-free credit (= allow somebody to pay later, without any extra charge)
Someone with a bad credit history is less likely to be lent money.
a credit agreement
a credit facility
Your credit limit is now £2 000.
He's a bad credit risk (= he is unlikely to pay the money later).
The credit crisis is far from over.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: money that you borrow from a bank; a loan
examples: SEE ALSO consumer credit
The bank refused further credit to the company.
Local lenders are more likely to extend credit (= lend money) to smaller, more marginal borrowers.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the status of being trusted to pay back money to somebody who lends it to you
examples: Her credit isn't good anywhere now.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: money that you have in your bank account; if you or your bank account are in credit, there is money in the account
examples: You have a credit balance of £250.
My account is in credit.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a sum of money paid into a bank account; a record of the payment
examples: OPPOSITE debit
a credit of £50
You'll be paid by direct credit into your bank account.
I have three credits on my bank statement.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the right to use a service up to a certain limit, paid for in advance
examples: My phone's run out of credit.
to add credit to your phone

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a payment that somebody has a right to for a particular reason
examples: SEE ALSO tax credit
The child tax credit is subject to strict income limitations.
Export credits are granted to firms in developing countries to give them a breathing space to pay for goods exported to them.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: praise or approval because you are responsible for something good that has happened
examples: COMPARE blame
to get/deserve/receive/take/claim the credit
He's a player who rarely seems to get the credit he deserves.
We did all the work and she gets all the credit!
I can't take all the credit for the show's success—it was a team effort.
At least give him credit for trying (= praise him because he tried, even if he did not succeed)
Credit will be given in the exam for good spelling and grammar.
His courage brought great credit to his regiment.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a person or thing whose qualities or achievements are praised and who therefore earns respect for somebody/something else
examples: She is a credit to the school.
Your children are a great credit to you.
He's a great credit to the school.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the act of mentioning somebody who worked on a project such as a film or a television programme
examples: She was given a programme credit for her work on the costumes for the play.
The credits (= the list of all the people involved) seemed to last almost as long as the film!
From the opening credits, the movie is non-stop action.
The end credits came as a welcome relief.
We left before the final credits began to roll.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a film, play, television programme, etc. that somebody has worked on
examples: His film credits included ‘The Witches’ and ‘Halloween III’.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a unit of study at a college or university (in the US, also at a school); the fact of having successfully completed a unit of study
examples: SEE ALSO carbon credit
My math class is worth three credits.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if something does credit to a person or an organization, they deserve to be praised for it
examples: Your honesty does you great credit.
Your concern does you credit.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to give somebody the praise they deserve, even if you do not really want to
examples: Give credit where credit is due—what the man does, he does well.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to have achieved something
examples: He's only 30, and he already has four novels to his credit.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to introduce the good points about somebody/something, especially after the bad points have been mentioned
examples: On the credit side, she’s always willing to work very late.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: making somebody deserve praise or respect
examples: To his credit, Jack never told anyone exactly what had happened.
It was to her credit that she managed to stay calm.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move slowly, quietly and carefully, because you do not want to be seen or heard
examples: I crept up the stairs, trying not to wake my parents.
I heard someone creeping around the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move with your body close to the ground; to move slowly on your hands and knees
examples: SYNONYM crawl

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move or develop very slowly
examples: Her arms crept around his neck.
A slight feeling of suspicion crept over me.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to grow along the ground or up walls using long stems or roots
examples: SEE ALSO creeper

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be too friendly or helpful to somebody in authority in a way that is not sincere, especially in order to get an advantage from them

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make you feel afraid or full of horror
examples: Just the sight of him makes my flesh creep.
The story made his flesh creep.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: all the people working on a ship, plane, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO aircrew
crew members
all the men and women in the crew
None of the passengers and crew were injured.
The crew of the plane instructed everyone to remain seated.
a change of crew in Frankfurt

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: all the people working on a ship, plane etc. except the officers who are in charge
examples: the officers and crew

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a group of people with special skills working together
examples: SEE ALSO ground crew
a film/camera/TV crew
a fire/an emergency/a rescue crew
It took ambulance crews more than an hour to free them.
Ten people answer to the crew chief.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a group of people
examples: The people she invited were a pretty motley crew (= a strange mix of types of people).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a team of people who row boats in races
examples: a member of the Cambridge crew

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the sport of rowing with other people in a boat
examples: I’m thinking of going out for crew this semester (= joining the rowing team).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a person or team of people who sail boats in races or for pleasure (usually not including the captain)Word Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French creue ‘augmentation, increase’, feminine past participle of croistre ‘grow’, from Latin crescere. The original sense was ‘band of soldiers serving as reinforcements’; hence it came to denote any organized armed band or, generally, a company of people (late 16th cent.).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: activities that involve breaking the law
examples: SEE ALSO hate crime
This month's figures show an increase in violent crime.
There needs to be a partnership between police and public in the fight against crime.
Stores spend more and more on crime prevention every year.
DNA data is extremely useful in fighting serious crime.
He began to drift into a life of petty crime (= crime that is not very serious).
gun/knife crime
a rise in street crime
the connection between drugs and organized crime
He turned to crime when he dropped out of school.
The crime rate is rising.
crime fiction/novels (= stories about crime)
crime figures/statistics
Victims of crime may be able to obtain compensation.
She’s a crime writer (= she writes stories about crime).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an illegal act or activity that can be punished by law
examples: There is no proof that he committed a crime (= did something illegal).
In his mind he was about to commit the perfect crime.
Arson is a serious crime.
The massacre was a crime against humanity.
Sometimes murder is a crime of passion.
DNA testing can be used to solve old crimes.
An abandoned car was found near the scene of the crime.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an act that you think is morally wrong or is a big mistake
examples: It's a crime to waste so much money.
Not returning phone calls is a grave crime in today's culture.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who commits a crime
examples: SEE ALSO war criminal
a convicted criminal
Police sometimes put themselves in danger when arresting violent criminals.
Society does not know how to deal with hardened criminals (= people who regularly commit crimes and are not sorry for what they do).
a career criminal (= who earns their income through criminal activities)
He admits to being a petty criminal (= who commits crimes that are not very serious).
white-collar criminals
a gang of criminals

examples: SEE ALSO war criminal
