He admits to being a petty criminal (= who commits crimes that are not very serious).
white-collar criminals
a gang of criminals

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a time of great danger, difficulty or doubt when problems must be solved or important decisions must be made
examples: SEE ALSO midlife crisis
an economic/a financial crisis
The government is attempting to solve the debt crisis through spending cuts.
The government is facing a political crisis.
a humanitarian crisis created by war and drought
a housing/an energy crisis
to resolve/solve/address a crisis
The business is still in crisis but it has survived the worst of the recession.
The Labour Party was facing an identity crisis.
an expert in crisis management
We provide help to families in crisis situations.
I know which friends I can turn to in times of crisis.
The party was suffering a crisis of confidence among its supporters (= they did not trust it any longer).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a time when a problem, a bad situation or an illness is at its worst point
examples: Their marriage has reached crisis point.
The fever has passed its crisis.
The team's dismal season has reached crisis point.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a standard or principle by which something is judged, or with the help of which a decision is made
examples: The main criterion is value for money.
She failed to meet the strict selection criteria.
What criteria are used for assessing a student's ability?
The criteria for inclusion in the book are set out clearly in the preface.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who expresses opinions about the good and bad qualities of books, music, etc.
examples: a film/an art/a music critic
Bradley Cooper's gripping performance has been praised by critics.
The critics loved the movie.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who expresses dislike of somebody/something and talks about their bad qualities, especially publicly
examples: She has become one of the ruling party's most outspoken critics.
a harsh/fierce/vocal critic
a critic of private healthcare

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: saying what you think is bad about somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO self-critical
You should just ignore any critical comments.
The supervisor is always very critical.
Some parents are highly critical of the school.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: extremely important because a future situation will be affected by it
examples: SYNONYM crucial
Industry leaders are working together to address this critical issue.
a critical factor in the election campaign
The kidneys play a critical role in overall health.
Reducing levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is of critical importance.
Emails and spreadsheets contain a lot of business-critical information.
Your decision is critical to our future.
Timing is critical for success.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: serious, uncertain and possibly dangerous
examples: SEE ALSO crisis
One of the victims of the fire remains in a critical condition.
The first 24 hours after the operation are the most critical.
a critical care ward
This is a critical moment in our country's history.
He's at a critical point in his life.
a critical step in the process

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: involving making fair, careful judgements about the good and bad qualities of somebody/something
examples: Students are encouraged to develop critical thinking instead of accepting opinions without questioning them.
His latest film attracted enthusiastic critical comment from cinema-goers.
Mike studied the canvas with a critical eye.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: according to the judgement of critics of art, music, literature, etc.
examples: the film director’s greatest critical success
In her day she never received the critical acclaim (= praise from the critics) she deserved.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that says what you think is bad about somebody/something
examples: She spoke critically of her father.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a way that is extremely important because a future situation will be affected by it
examples: a critically important decision

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a way that is serious, uncertain and possibly dangerous
examples: He is critically ill in intensive care.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in a way that involves making fair, careful judgements about the good and bad qualities of somebody/something
examples: I looked at myself critically in the mirror.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in a way that is connected with the judgement of critics of art, music, literature, etc.
examples: a critically acclaimed artist

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of expressing disapproval of somebody/something and opinions about their faults or bad qualities; a statement showing this disapproval
examples: SEE ALSO self-criticism
to draw/face/receive criticism
The plan has attracted criticism from consumer groups.
She sought to deflect criticism by blaming her family.
People in public life must always be open to criticism (= willing to accept being criticized).
Ben is very sensitive—he just can't take criticism.
to offer somebody constructive criticism (= that is meant to be helpful)
I didn't mean it as a criticism.
criticisms levelled at (= aimed at) journalists
There was widespread criticism of the government's handling of the disaster.
My only criticism of the house is that it is on a main road.
He was clearly stung by media criticism of his previous statement.
The former minister is facing growing criticism over his remark.
The government came under heavy criticism over its policies.
We came in for some sharp criticism over this decision.
The actress has come under criticism for her comments about her co-stars.
The film star faced a barrage of criticism for his behaviour.
The actor has recently faced harsh criticism about his weight.
The past five years has seen growing criticism against the regime.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the work or activity of making fair, careful judgements about the good and bad qualities of somebody/something, especially books, music, etc.
examples: She has written several works of literary criticism.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say that you think somebody/something is bad; to say what you do not like or think is wrong about somebody/something
examples: OPPOSITE praise
All you ever do is criticize!
The decision was harshly criticized by environmental groups.
a heavily criticized plan
Journalists who strongly criticize the government can be heavily fined or imprisoned.
She has been sharply criticized for her comments.
The government has been criticized for not taking the problem seriously.
The company has been criticized over its handling of the contract.
The law was widely criticized as racist.
The project has been criticized as a waste of money.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to judge the good and bad qualities of something
examples: We were taught how to criticize poems.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of written criticism of a set of ideas, a work of art, etc.
examples: She wrote a feminist critique of Freud's theories.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a plant that is grown in large quantities, especially as food
examples: SEE ALSO cash crop
Sugar is an important crop on the island.
What are the benefits of growing GM crops?
food crops
crop yield/production
to grow/plant/harvest crops
The crops are regularly sprayed with pesticides.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the amount of grain, fruit, etc. that is grown in one season
examples: SYNONYM harvest
a fall in this year’s coffee crop
Australia's wheat crop is likely to be lower than forecast this year.
We are looking forward to a bumper crop (= a very large one).
We had a very good crop of apples last year.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a group of people who do something at the same time; a number of things that happen at the same time
examples: the current crop of trainees
She is really the cream of the crop (= the best in her group).
a crop of disasters/injuries

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a short whip used by horse riders
examples: a riding crop

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a very short hairstyle
examples: She has her hair cut in a short crop.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: hair that is short and thick
examples: He had a thick crop of black curly hair.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a part of a bird’s throat that has the shape of a bag where food is stored before it passes into the stomachWord Origin
examples: Old English, of Germanic origin; related to German Kropf. From Old English to the late 18th cent. there existed a sense ‘flower head, ear of corn’, giving rise to sense (1) and senses referring to the top of something.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to go across; to pass or stretch from one side to the other
examples: As soon as traffic slowed down enough to safely cross, I started walking.
I waved and she crossed over (= crossed the road towards me).
He crossed over from the other side of the road.
We crossed from Dover to Calais.
She crossed to the other side of the room.
to cross the road/street
to cross the sea/mountains
to cross France by train
The bridge crosses the River Dee.
He was caught trying to cross the border illegally.
More than 150 000 people crossed the bridge that day.
A look of annoyance crossed her face.
They crossed the finishing line together (= in a race).
He crossed over the road and joined me.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to pass across each other
examples: The roads cross just outside the town.
The straps cross over at the back and are tied at the waist.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to put or place something across or over something else
examples: to cross your arms/legs (= place one arm or leg over the other)
She sat with her legs crossed.
a flag with a design of two crossed keys

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to oppose somebody or speak against them or their plans or wishes
examples: She's really nice until you cross her.
He had been crossed in love (= the person he loved was not faithful to him).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make two different types of animal breed (= produce young) together; to mix two types of plant to form a new one
examples: A mule is the product of a horse crossed with a donkey.
He behaved like an army officer crossed with a professor.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to kick or pass a ball to the side across the field
examples: Sissoko crossed from the left.
He could not get to the line to cross the ball.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to draw a line across something
examples: to cross your t’s (= the letters in writing)

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to make the sign of the cross (= the Christian symbol) on your chest

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to do something that is not considered to be acceptable behaviour
examples: He crossed the line by making details of their very private conversation public.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to hope that your plans will be successful (sometimes putting one finger across another as a sign of hoping for good luck)
examples: I'm crossing my fingers that my proposal will be accepted.
Keep your fingers crossed!

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you are telling the truth or will do what you promise
examples: I saw him do it—cross my heart.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to come into your mind
examples: SYNONYM occur to somebody
It never crossed my mind that she might lose (= I was sure that she would win).
The thought never crossed my mind!

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to give somebody money so that they will do you a favour, especially tell your fortune

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: if somebody crosses somebody’s path or their paths cross, they meet by chance
examples: I hope I never cross her path again.
Our paths were to cross again many years later.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to fight or argue with somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to worry about a problem when it actually happens and not before

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to pay attention to the small details when you are finishing a task

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to become confused about what somebody has said to you so that you think they meant something else
examples: We seem to have got our wires crossed. I thought you were coming on Tuesday.

examples: I'm crossing my fingers that my proposal will be accepted.
Keep your fingers crossed!

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you are telling the truth or will do what you promise
examples: I saw him do it—cross my heart.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to come into your mind
examples: SYNONYM occur to somebody
It never crossed my mind that she might lose (= I was sure that she would win).
The thought never crossed my mind!

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to give somebody money so that they will do you a favour, especially tell your fortune

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: if somebody crosses somebody’s path or their paths cross, they meet by chance
examples: I hope I never cross her path again.
Our paths were to cross again many years later.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to fight or argue with somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to worry about a problem when it actually happens and not before

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to pay attention to the small details when you are finishing a task

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to become confused about what somebody has said to you so that you think they meant something else
examples: We seem to have got our wires crossed. I thought you were coming on Tuesday.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large number of people gathered together in a public place, for example in the streets or at a sports game
examples: He pushed his way through the crowd.
A small crowd had gathered outside the church.
Police had to break up the crowd.
Crowds of people poured into the street.
He left the hotel surrounded by crowds of journalists.
Several speakers addressed the crowd at the rally.
a large/huge crowd
The match attracted a capacity crowd of 80 000 (= the maximum number of people who could attend).
The President spoke before a crowd of more than 50 000 in the city's football stadium.
The mayor of Paris was among the crowd that had gathered for the street celebration.
to attract/draw a crowd
I want to get there early to avoid the crowds.
The crowd cheered the winning hit.
Nearly 300 marshals will be involved in crowd control.
crowd trouble
A whole crowd of us (= a lot of us) are going to the ball.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a particular group of people
examples: SEE ALSO in-crowd
Bob introduced her to some of the usual crowd (= people who often meet each other).
the bright young theatrical crowd

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: ordinary people, not special or unusual in any way
examples: We all like to think we stand out from the crowd (= are different from and better than other people).
He prefers to be one of the crowd.
She's quite happy to follow the crowd.
To her I'm just another face in the crowd.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a lot of people or too many people
examples: COMPARE uncrowded
We made our way through the crowded streets.
a crowded bar
The main beach can get really crowded in summer.
London was very crowded.
In the spring the place is crowded with skiers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: full of something
examples: a room crowded with books
We have a very crowded schedule.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an object in the shape of a circle, usually made of gold and precious stones, that a king or queen wears on his or her head on official occasions
examples: The crown was placed upon the new monarch's head.
the emperor's jewel-encrusted crown

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the government of a country, thought of as being represented by a king or queen
examples: land owned by the Crown
a Minister of the Crown
Who's appearing for the Crown (= bringing a criminal charge against somebody on behalf of the state) in this case?
a piece of Crown land

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the position or power of a king or queen
examples: She refused the crown (= refused to become queen).
his claim to the French crown

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a circle of flowers, leaves, etc. that is worn on somebody’s head, sometimes as a sign of victory

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the position of winning a sports competition
examples: She is determined to retain her Wimbledon crown.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the top part of the head or a hat
examples: There were raindrops on his bald crown.
She swept her hair into a bun at the crown of her head.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the highest part of something
examples: the crown of a hill
from the crown of the final bend

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the part of a plant just above and below the ground
examples: Roses bloom on shoots that sprout from the crown of the mother plant.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the top of a tree or other plant
examples: Nests were built high in the crowns of trees.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: an artificial cover for a damaged tooth
examples: SYNONYM cap (6)

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: anything in the shape of a crown, especially as a decoration or a badge

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a unit of money in several European countries
examples: Czech crowns

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: an old British coin worth five shillings (= now 25p)
examples: SEE ALSO half-crown

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: the most attractive or valuable part of something
examples: The Knightsbridge branch is the jewel in the crown of a 500-strong chain of stores.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: extremely important, because it will affect other things
examples: SYNONYM critical
The next few weeks are going to be crucial.
Private security cameras can prove crucial in some investigations.
Parents play a crucial role in preparing their child for school.
This step is a crucial part of the process.
a crucial step/point
He wasn't there at the crucial moment (= when he was needed most).
a crucial element/factor/question/issue
topics of crucial importance
Winning this contract is absolutely crucial to our long term success.
The talks are crucial for the success of the plan.
Early detection is crucial in the fight against cancer.
It is crucial that we get this right.
The summit was crucial in shaping the reform process.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in its natural state, before it has been processed or refined
examples: crude oil/metal

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not changed or corrected
examples: the crude mortality rate
We adjusted crude effects for age, education, height and weight.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: offensive or rude, especially about sex
examples: SYNONYM vulgar
crude jokes/language

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: simple and not very accurate but giving a general idea of something
examples: In crude terms, the causes of mental illness seem to be of three main kinds.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: simply made, not showing much skill or attention to detail
examples: a crude drawing of a face

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a desire to cause physical or mental pain and make somebody suffer
examples: OPPOSITE kind
He was known to be a cruel dictator.
I can't stand people who are cruel to animals.
Her eyes were cruel and hard.
Sometimes you have to be cruel to be kind (= make somebody suffer because it will be good for them later).
an extremely cruel regime

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: causing physical or mental pain and making somebody suffer
examples: a cruel joke/hoax
cruel punishment
It was a cruel irony that he, being gravely ill, would survive his family.
It would be a cruel twist of fate if he escaped only to starve to death once outside.
Her father's death was a cruel blow.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a category of very severe punishment that is banned under US law
examples: This important case confronts the issue of what constitutes cruel and unusual punishment.
Detainees are subjected to malnutrition, forced labor, and to other cruel and unusual punishments.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a journey by sea, visiting different places, especially as a holiday
examples: PLURAL OF crew
I'd love to go on a round-the-world cruise.
a luxury cruise ship

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a journey by sea, visiting different places, especially as a holiday
examples: PLURAL OF crew
I'd love to go on a round-the-world cruise.
a luxury cruise ship

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to press something so hard that it is damaged or injured, or loses its shape
examples: The car was completely crushed under the truck.
Several people were crushed to death in the accident.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to break something into small pieces or into a powder by pressing hard
examples: Add two cloves of crushed garlic.
They crush the olives with a heavy wooden press.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to push or press somebody/something into a small space
examples: Over twenty prisoners were crushed into a small dark cell.
She was crushed against the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make something full of folds or lines; to become full of folds or lines
examples: She crushed the scrap of paper in her hand.
The crisp paper crushed like eggshells in his fingers.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to use violent methods to defeat people who are opposing you
examples: SYNONYM put down
The army was sent in to crush the rebellion.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to destroy somebody’s confidence or happiness
examples: She felt completely crushed by the teacher's criticism.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to do something very well or be very successful
examples: SYNONYM smash it
She got up on stage and absolutely crushed it—the audience was going wild!
His latest film is crushing it at the box office.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to produce tears from your eyes because you are unhappy or hurt
examples: It's all right. Don't cry.
I just couldn't stop crying.
The little boy fell over and started to cry.
The baby was crying for (= because it wanted) its mother.
There's nothing to cry about.
He felt like crying with rage.
She threw her arms around his neck crying tears of joy.
He started to cry real tears.
‘Waaa!’ she cried.
I found him crying his eyes out (= crying very much).
That night she cried herself to sleep.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to shout loudly
examples: She ran to the window and cried for help.
‘You're safe!’ Tom cried in delight.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a loud noise
examples: Seagulls followed the boat, crying loudly.
A pair of eagles cried out to each other as they circled above the trees.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to complain that somebody else has done something wrong or unfair

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to waste time worrying about something that has happened that you cannot do anything about
examples: As the saying goes—it's no use crying over spilt milk.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to call for help when you do not need it, with the result that when you do need it people do not believe you

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show you are angry or surprised
examples: For crying out loud! Why did you have to do that?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to laugh so long and hard that there are tears in your eyes

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be unable to decide how to react to a bad situation

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to describe a person who listens to your problems and gives you sympathy
examples: He was a fatherly shoulder to cry on when things went wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small piece of a substance with many even sides, that is formed naturally when the substance becomes solid
examples: ice/salt crystals

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a clear mineral, such as quartz, used in making jewellery and attractive objects
examples: SEE ALSO rock crystal
crystal earrings

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: glass of very high quality
examples: a crystal chandelier/vase
Every table had been set with fine china and crystal.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a small piece of a mineral that some people believe has the power to bring health or happiness
examples: Smoky Quartz is a powerful healing crystal.
She claims that the crystal awakened her mind power and enabled her to win the race.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a piece of glass or plastic that covers the face of a watch
examples: SEE ALSO liquid crystal display

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a powerful illegal drug, methamphetamine, that looks like small pieces of glassWord Origin

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an action or event that is a signal for somebody to do something

examples: ‘Where is that boy?’ As if on cue, Simon appeared in the doorway.
I can't just cry on cue!

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to copy what somebody else does as an example of how to behave or what to do
examples: Investors are taking their cue from the big banks and selling dollars.

examples: Their son ran away from home and joined a cult.

definitions.definition: to grow plants or crops
examples: SYNONYM grow

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: He purposely tried to cultivate good relations with the press.

examples: She cultivated an air of sophistication.

examples: the culture of silkworms (= for silk)

to do/take a throat culture

a cup and saucer
a plastic/paper cup

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: COMPARE box (10)

definitions.label: Meaning 12

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: nothing is completely certain until it really happens because things can easily go wrongWord Origin
examples: Old English: from popular Latin cuppa, probably from Latin cupa ‘tub’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of furniture with doors and shelves used for storing dishes, food, clothes, etc.
examples: kitchen cupboards
a stationery/linen cupboard
a cupboard door
There's plenty of food in the cupboards.
I found it hidden in the back of a cupboard.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a person or an animal healthy again after an illness
examples: Will you be able to cure him, Doctor?
The doctor managed to cure her of her illness.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make an illness go away
examples: It is better to prevent rather than cure diseases.
Finding it early is the key to curing most cancers.
TB is a serious illness, but it can be cured.
The disease can be cured with antibiotics.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to deal with a problem successfully
examples: I finally managed to cure the rattling noise in my car.
Charities alone can't cure basic social injustices.
He bought some special software that was supposed to cure hard disk problems.
Most of the team's faults could be cured with good coaching.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to stop somebody from behaving in a particular way, especially a way that is bad or annoying
examples: I thought I had finally cured him of this annoying habit.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to treat food or tobacco with smoke, salt or heat, etc. in order to preserve it
examples: SEE ALSO dry-cure
cured ham/bacon

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that what you are going to do will either be very successful or fail completelyWord Origin
examples: Middle English (as a noun): from Old French curer (verb), cure (noun), both from Latin curare ‘take care of’, from cura ‘care’. The original noun senses were ‘care, concern, responsibility’, in particular spiritual care. In late Middle English the senses ‘medical care’ and ‘successful medical treatment’ arose, and hence ‘remedy’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: COMPARE syllabus

Spanish is on the curriculum.
Spanish is in the curriculum.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

to draw/pull/close the curtains (= to pull them across the window so they cover it)
She opened her curtains and looked out.
It was ten in the morning but the curtains were still drawn (= closed).
a pair of curtains
She looked up and saw a face peering through the curtains.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a very thin piece of cloth that you hang at a window and that allows light to enter but stops people outside from being able to see inside

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a piece of cloth that is hung up as a screen in a room or around a bed, for example
examples: SEE ALSO Iron Curtain
a shower curtain

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a piece of thick, heavy cloth that hangs in front of the stage in the theatre
examples: SEE ALSO drop curtain

The curtain goes up to reveal a grand piano at the back of the stage.
There was tremendous applause when the curtain came down (= the play ended).

It's time to face the final curtain (= the end; death).
The curtain has fallen on her long and distinguished career (= her career has ended).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a thing that covers, hides or protects something
examples: a curtain of rain/smoke

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be a situation without hope or that you cannot escape from
examples: When I saw he had a gun, I thought it was curtains for me.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to finish or mark the end of something
examples: His sudden decision to retire brought down the curtain on a distinguished career.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a line or surface that bends gradually; a smooth bend
examples: SEE ALSO bell curve
He admired the delicate curve of her ear.
The pattern was made up of straight lines and curves.
a curve in the road
The driver lost control on a curve and the vehicle hit a tree.
The program automatically plots the curve on a graph.
This figure shows the population curve for the last hundred years.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a ball that moves in a curve when it is thrown to the batter

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that is unexpected and difficult to deal with

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: curving shapes that form part of a woman's body
examples: The supermodel showed off her famous curves in a figure-hugging red dress.
The evening dress hugged her curves beautifully.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in advance of or behind a particular trend
examples: Our expert advice will help you stay ahead of the curve.
We've fallen behind the curve when it comes to developing new digital products.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to manage the rate or quantity of something so that it does not increase too much within a short period of time
examples: These measures are intended to flatten the curve of new infections in order to reduce the load on hospitals.

examples: SEE ALSO protective custody

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an accepted way of behaving or of doing things in a society or a community
examples: It's a local custom.
an ancient custom
a burial/marriage custom
a tribal custom

Widows observed the custom of wearing black

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the way a person always behaves
examples: SYNONYM habit
It was her custom to rise early.
As was his custom, he knocked three times.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the fact of a person or people buying goods or services at a shop or business
examples: Thank you for your custom. Please call again.
We've lost a lot of custom since prices went up.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or an organization that buys goods or services from a shop or business
examples: marketing strategies to target potential customers

one of the shop’s best customers
They know me—I'm a regular customer.
the customer service department
Improving customer satisfaction is a core company strategy.
The firm has excellent customer relations.
How do you attract new online customers?
Our success is measured by how well we serve our customers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used after an adjective to describe a particular type of person
examples: an awkward customer
a cool customer (= somebody who is always calm, even when in trouble)
an ugly customer (= somebody who may become violent)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make an opening or a wound in something, especially with a sharp tool such as a knife or scissors
examples: She cut her finger on a piece of glass.
He cut himself (= his face) shaving.
She suffered from mental health issues and started cutting herself (= deliberately, as a symptom of mental distress).
She had fallen and cut her head open.
She picked up the knife and cut into the meat.
You need a powerful saw to cut through metal.
The canoe cut through the water.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to divide something into two or more pieces with a knife, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO pre-cut
Don't cut the string, untie the knots.
The bus was cut in two by the train.
Now cut the tomatoes in half.
He cut the loaf into thick slices.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make something shorter by cutting
examples: She cuts hair for a living.
to cut the grass/lawn/hedge
the smell of freshly cut grass
He's had his hair cut really short.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to remove something or a part of something, using a knife, etc.
examples: First, cut a long piece of string.
He cut four thick slices from the loaf.
a bunch of cut flowers
I cut them all a piece of birthday cake.
I cut a piece of birthday cake for them all.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make or form something by removing material with a knife, etc.
examples: Workmen cut a hole in the pipe.
The climbers cut steps in the ice.
homemade biscuits cut into heart shapes
Cut a circle of waxed paper to fit the bottom of the pan.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be capable of cutting
examples: This knife won't cut.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be capable of being cut
examples: Sandstone cuts easily.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to reduce something by removing a part of it
examples: to cut costs/prices/spending/taxes
Buyers will bargain hard to cut the cost of the house they want.
a plan to drastically cut emissions
His salary has been cut by ten per cent.
The Bank of England has cut interest rates to 1.5 per cent.
Could you cut your essay from 5 000 to 3 000 words?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to escape from somewhere by cutting the rope, object, etc. that is holding them
examples: The injured driver had to be cut from the wreckage.
Two survivors were cut free after being trapped for twenty minutes.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to design and make a piece of clothing in a particular way
examples: SEE ALSO bias-cut
The swimsuit was cut high in the leg.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to remove something from something
examples: This scene was cut from the final version of the movie.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to delete (= remove) part of a text on a computer screen in order to place it somewhere else
examples: You can cut and paste between different programs.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to stop doing something
examples: Cut the chatter and get on with your work!

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to completely end a relationship or all communication with somebody
examples: SYNONYM sever
She has cut all ties with her family.
He has refused to cut links with these companies.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to prepare a film or tape by removing parts of it or putting them in a different order
examples: SYNONYM edit

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to stop filming or recording
examples: The director shouted ‘Cut!’

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to move quickly from one scene to another
examples: The scene cuts from the bedroom to the street.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to stay away from a class that you should go to
examples: He's always cutting class.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to hurt somebody emotionally
examples: His cruel remarks cut her deeply.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to divide a pack of playing cards by lifting a section from the top, in order to reveal a card to decide who is to play first, etc.
examples: Let's cut for dealer.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to cross another line
examples: The line cuts the circle at two points.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to have a new tooth beginning to appear through the gum
examples: When did she cut her first tooth?

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to make a sound recording on a record, CD, etc.
examples: The Beatles cut their first disc in 1962.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to mix an illegal drug such as heroin with another substance

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to make a quick or sudden escape

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to (not) be as good as is expected or needed
examples: He won't cut it as a professional singer.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: She gives generously to charity without making a song and dance about it.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: Middle English: from Old French dancer (verb), dance (noun), of unknown origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who dances or whose job is dancing
examples: SEE ALSO belly dancer

a ballet dancer
He's a principal dancer with the Royal Ballet.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: moving your body to music
examples: SEE ALSO all-singing, all-dancing

I love Irish dancing.
dancing classes

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the possibility of something happening that will injure, harm or kill somebody, or damage or destroy something
examples: Danger! Keep Out!

Children's lives are in danger every time they cross this road.
in grave/mortal danger
They found themselves in grave danger.
species in imminent danger of extinction
Doctors said she is now out of danger (= not likely to die).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the possibility of something bad or unpleasant happening
examples: There is no danger of a bush fire now.
They reminded residents of the potential dangers of living so near an active volcano.
‘Nicky won't find out, will she?’ ‘Oh, no, there's no danger of that.’
The building is in danger of collapsing.
How many people are in danger of losing their jobs?
There is a danger that the political disorder of the past will return.
Most people are aware of the dangers posed by online fraudsters.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that may cause damage, or harm somebody
examples: SEE ALSO endanger
There are many hidden dangers for small children in the home.
Smoking is a serious danger to health.
Police said the man was a danger to the public.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be so ill that you may die; to no longer be very illWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in the sense ‘jurisdiction or power’, specifically ‘power to harm’): from Old French dangier, based on Latin dominus ‘lord’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: likely to injure or harm somebody, or to damage or destroy something
examples: The situation is extremely dangerous.
Fog and ice are making the roads very dangerous.
potentially dangerous levels of pesticides
It's one of the most dangerous places in the world.
The prisoners who escaped are violent and dangerous.
a conviction for dangerous driving
Poor air quality is particularly dangerous for young children.
It would be dangerous for you to stay here.
The evidence is clear that smoking is dangerous to health.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: likely to cause problems or have a bad result
examples: This ruling sets a dangerous precedent.
Raising income tax is considered politically dangerous.
As always, it's dangerous to generalize.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a situation in which somebody takes risks, usually hoping to gain an advantage
examples: Both gangs are playing a very dangerous game.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a situation or subject that is likely to make somebody angry, or that involves risk
examples: We'd be on dangerous ground if we asked about race or religion.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be brave enough to do something
examples: She said it as loudly as she dared.
He didn’t dare (to) say what he thought.
They daren't ask for any more money.
She dared not breathe a word of it to anybody.
Dare to be different!
There was something, dare I say it, a little unusual about him.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to persuade somebody to do something dangerous, difficult or embarrassing so that they can show that they are not afraid
examples: Go on! Take it! I dare you.
Some of the older boys had dared him to do it.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody strongly not to do something
examples: ‘I'll tell her about it.’ ‘Don't you dare!’
Don't you dare say anything to anybody.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that you are angry about something that somebody has done
examples: How dare you talk to me like that?
How dare she imply that I was lying?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used when you are saying that something is likely
examples: I dare say you know about it already.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: with no or very little light, especially because it is night
examples: OPPOSITE light
a dark room/street/forest/night
What time does it get dark in summer?
Then the theatre went dark.
It was dark outside and I couldn't see much.
The sky was still dark.
Use lights to illuminate dark corners.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not light; closer in shade to black than to white
examples: OPPOSITE light
dark blue/green/red/brown
Darker colours are more practical and don't show stains.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having a colour that is close to black
examples: He wore a dark suit and a plain tie.
dark-coloured wood
The dark clouds in the sky meant that a storm was coming.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: brown or black in colour
examples: Sue has long dark hair.
He was handsome with dark eyes.
Even if you have dark skin, you still need protection from the sun.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: having dark hair, eyes, etc.
examples: a dark handsome stranger

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: mysterious; hidden and not known about
examples: There are no dark secrets in our family.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: evil or frightening
examples: There was a darker side to his nature.
the dark forces of the imagination
My mind was full of dark thoughts.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: unpleasant and without any hope that something good will happen
examples: the darkest days of Fascism
The film is a dark vision of the future.
The theatre stayed open even in the darkest days of the war.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: produced with the back part of the tongue close to the back of the mouth. In many accents of (= ways of pronouncing) English, dark /l/ is used after a vowel, as in ball.
examples: OPPOSITE clear

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a person who does not tell other people much about their life, and who surprises other people by having interesting qualities

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a person taking part in a race, etc. who surprises everyone by winning

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to keep something secret and not tell people about it
examples: He’s got two children? Well he’s kept that dark, hasn’t he!

raw data (= that has not been analysed)

definitions.definition: information that is stored by a computer

I go to the gym every day.
We spent five days in Paris.
I saw Tom three days ago.
We're going away in a few days.

New Year’s Day
Take the medicine three times a day.
They are producing 1.5 million barrels of oil per day.
The helpline is open 24 hours a day.

examples: What a beautiful day!
The sun was shining all day.
I could sit and watch the river all day long.
We spent the day gardening.
He works at night and sleeps during the day.

It's been a long day (= I've been very busy).

I took a half day off yesterday.

in the days of the industrial revolution
back in the early days of computers

in the old days (= in the past)

in his younger days

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: The letter should arrive any day now.

examples: At the end of the day, he'll still have to make his own decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: My dad's always talking about how great everything was back in the day.

definitions.label: Meaning 10

examples: I was a fan back in the days when the band wasn't yet famous.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to decide or agree to stop doing something

definitions.label: Meaning 13

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: easy to see or understand

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: each day repeatedly (used especially when something is boring or annoying)
examples: She hates doing the same work day after day.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: all the time; continuously
examples: The store is open day and night.
The machines are kept running night and day.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: all the time; a little at a time and gradually
examples: Day by day his condition improved.
Morale was sinking day by day.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: every day for a long period of time
examples: Living on junk food day in day out is not good for you.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: the time when somebody will have to deal with the result of something that they have done wrong, or be punished for something bad that they have done

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: a person or thing will not continue to live, exist or be successful for much longer
examples: His days as leader of the party are numbered.
Whatever the protests, the school’s days are numbered and it will be closed down.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to spend the last part of your life in a particular state or place
examples: He ended his days in poverty.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: everyone has good luck or success at some point in their life

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: the time when you have to do something difficult or unpleasant
examples: I’d better go and see the dentist—I can’t put off the evil hour any longer.
If you keep on borrowing, you are only postponing the evil day when you have to pay it all back.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: the amount of fruit or vegetables that some organizations say you should eat in order to be healthy
examples: Start your five a day with a banana for breakfast.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: from the beginning
examples: It's never worked from day one.
This game makes reading and spelling fun from day one.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: with no thoughts or plans for the future
examples: They live from day to day, looking after their sick daughter.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: if a situation changes from day to day, it changes often
examples: A baby's need for food can vary from day to day.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: if a situation changes from one day to the next, it is uncertain and not likely to stay the same each day
examples: I never know what to expect from one day to the next.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: beginning on that day; from that time
examples: From that day forth she gave me endless friendship and encouragement.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: used to say that you prefer a particular thing or person to the one that has just been mentioned
examples: We don't go out much. Give me a quiet night in front of the TV any day!

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: a helpful, kind thing that you do
examples: I took Sarah’s children to school so I’ve done my good deed for the day.
She felt that she had done her good deed for the day.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: an earlier period of time in your life or in history that is seen as better/worse than the present
examples: That was in the bad old days of rampant inflation.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to no longer be successful, powerful, etc.
examples: She's had her day as a supermodel.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: a friendly way of saying goodbye, especially to customers

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to be in poor condition
examples: Our car has seen better days!

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: (used when talking about somebody’s age) at least
examples: He must be 70 if he's a day!

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: used when you are very surprised at something you have never heard or seen before
examples: I've never heard such nonsense in all my born days.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: when you have had time to think calmly about something; in the morning when things are clearer
examples: These things always look different in the cold light of day.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: during the part of somebody’s life when they were most successful, famous, etc.
examples: She was a great dancer in her day.
Things were very different in my grandfather's day.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: when somebody was young
examples: In my day, there were plenty of jobs when you left school.

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: a long time ago in the past
examples: What was life like in the olden days, Gran?

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: now, in the modern world
examples: Slavery continues to exist, even in this day and age.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: used to say that it is too soon to be sure how a situation will develop
examples: It’s early days yet. We don’t know if the play will be a success.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: used when several bad or unpleasant things happen on the same day
examples: My car broke down and then I locked myself out—it's just not my day!

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: after the time when an action could be successful
examples: He started working hard much too late in the day—he couldn't possibly catch up.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: the whole length of the day

definitions.label: Meaning 47

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel very happy on a particular day

definitions.label: Meaning 49

examples: We took a picnic lunch to the river and made a day of it.
They decided to make a night of it and went on to a club.

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: all the time; continuously
examples: The machines are kept running night and day.
The store is open day and night.

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: a person or thing that makes people excited for a short time but does not last very long

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: to refuse to speak to somebody because you do not like or respect them
examples: Since the success of her novel, people shake her hand who once wouldn't have given her the time of day.

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: to not have much time
examples: Come on! We don't have all day!

definitions.label: Meaning 54
definitions.definition: during a particular period of time when somebody lived
examples: the best player of his day

definitions.label: Meaning 55
definitions.definition: of the present time
examples: the political issues of the day

definitions.label: Meaning 56
definitions.definition: that is served on a particular day in a restaurant

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: used to emphasize what you are saying when you are surprised, shocked or annoyed
examples: Oh my days! Is that true?

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: at some time in the future, or on a particular day in the past
examples: One day, I want to leave the city and move to the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: before a long time has passed
examples: One of these days you'll come back and ask me to forgive you.

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: a day when there are a lot of mistakes and a lot of things go wrong

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say or explain what the meaning of a word or phrase is
examples: LANGUAGE BANK AT first
The term ‘mental illness’ is difficult to define.
Life imprisonment is defined as 60 years under state law.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to describe or show the nature or range of somebody/something
examples: The goals of the project are clearly defined.
At that time women's roles were quite narrowly defined.
to be broadly/loosely defined
The difficulty of a problem was defined in terms of how long it took to complete.
It is difficult to define what makes him so popular.
He defines himself as an independent.
We have never defined ourselves in our own right.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make or establish the essential character or somebody/something
examples: For some, the football club defines their identity.
to define the nature/character of somebody/something
The novel told the story of a preacher-poet, who defines himself through his art.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to show clearly a line, shape or edge
examples: The mountain was sharply defined against the sky.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: sure or certain; unlikely to change
examples: Can you give me a definite answer by tomorrow?
No definite conclusions can be drawn from this study.
They have very definite ideas on how to bring up children.
Is it definite that he's leaving?
I've heard rumours, but nothing definite.
I'm not sure—I can find out for definite if you like.
That's definite then, is it?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: easily or clearly seen or understood; obvious
examples: SYNONYM clear
The look on her face was a definite sign that something was wrong.
There was a definite feeling that things were getting worse.
a definite plus/advantage
There was a definite improvement in the sound

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: sure that something is true or that something is going to happen and stating it to other people
examples: I'm definite about this.
He was pretty definite about the price.
She was definite that they weren't coming till next week.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a way of emphasizing that something is true and that there is no doubt about it
examples: I definitely remember sending the letter.
‘Was it what you expected?’ ‘Yes, definitely.’
Do you plan to have children?’ ‘Definitely not!'
Some old people want help; others most definitely do not.
The claim is definitely true.
If you want to know more I'd definitely recommend checking out this guide .

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a way that is certain or that shows that you are certain
examples: The date of the move has not been definitely decided yet (= it may change).
Please say definitely whether you will be coming or not.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an explanation of the meaning of a word or phrase, especially in a dictionary
examples: The dictionary provides clear, simple definitions.
the dictionary definition of this term
a precise/strict definition of a word
We need a good working definition of ‘pollution’.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: what an idea means
examples: What's your definition of happiness?
a broad/narrow definition of the concept
There is no agreed definition of what a comprehensive school should be.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of saying what a word or an idea means
examples: The term ‘partner’ requires careful definition.
Neighbours by definition live close by (= this is what being a neighbour means).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the quality of being clear and easy to see; the ability of a device to give clear images
examples: SEE ALSO high-definition
The clarity and definition of the images are excellent.
The definition of this TV is very good.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to refuse to obey or show respect for somebody in authority, a law, a rule, etc.
examples: I wouldn't have dared to defy my teachers.
Hundreds of people today defied the ban on political gatherings.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be impossible or almost impossible to believe, explain, describe, etc.
examples: a political move that defies explanation
The beauty of the scene defies description.
His face was so odd that it defies description.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to successfully resist something to a very unusual degree
examples: SEE ALSO death-defying
The baby boy defied all the odds and survived (= stayed alive when it seemed certain that he would die).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody should try to do something, as a way of emphasizing that you think it is impossible to do it
examples: I defy anyone not to cry at the end of the film.
I defy you to leave without buying something.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring temperature
examples: Water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit (32°F) or zero/nought degrees Celsius (0°C).
Temperatures are expected to drop below 2 degrees.
Last weekend temperatures reached 40 degrees.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring angles
examples: an angle of ninety degrees (90°)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the amount or level of something
examples: Her job demands a high degree of skill.
The story has been staged several times before, with varying degrees of success.
I agree with you to a certain degree.
The reaction to his decision has been, to some degree, predictable.
These criticisms are, to a degree (= to some extent), well founded.
To what degree can parents be held responsible for a child's behaviour?
Most pop music is influenced, to a greater or lesser degree, by the blues.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the qualification obtained by students who successfully complete a university or college course
examples: SEE ALSO Associate's degree
My brother has a master's degree from Harvard.
She's pursuing a degree in biochemistry.
a four-year degree course
an undergraduate/graduate/doctoral degree
a law/medical degree

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a university or college course, normally lasting three years or more
examples: I'm hoping to do a chemistry degree.
He took a degree in law then joined a law firm.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a level in a scale of how serious something is
examples: SEE ALSO second-degree
murder in the first degree (= of the most serious kind)
first-degree murder
third-degree (= very serious) burns

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: slowly and gradually
examples: By degrees their friendship grew into love.
By slow degrees, the company's turnover dwindled to nothing.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: extremely; to an extreme degree
examples: The children tested her patience to the nth degree.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a period of time when somebody/something has to wait because of a problem that makes something slow or late
examples: Commuters will face long delays on the roads today.
to experience/suffer delays
to avoid/minimize further delays
Increased congestion and traffic delays are expected.
a delay of two hours/a two-hour delay
The strike has led to some delays in train services.
We apologize for the delay in answering your letter.
These issues have caused serious delays to the project.
Flights to New York may be subject to delay.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: failure to do something quickly or at the right time; the act of delaying
examples: There's no time for delay.
Report it to the police without delay (= immediately).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who is chosen or elected to represent the views of a group of people and vote and make decisions for them
examples: Congress delegates rejected the proposals.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who attends a conference
examples: The conference was attended by delegates from 56 countries.
They decided not to send a delegate to the conference.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of people who represent the views of an organization, a country, etc.
examples: the Dutch delegation to the United Nations
a delegation of teachers

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of giving somebody work or responsibilities that would usually be yours
examples: delegation of authority/decision-making

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to remove something that has been written or printed, or that has been stored on a computer
examples: Your name has been deleted from the list.
This command deletes files from the directory.
Mr/Mrs/Ms (delete as appropriate)
Delete the word ‘it’ and insert ‘them’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: done on purpose rather than by accident
examples: SYNONYM intentional
a deliberate act of vandalism
The speech was a deliberate attempt to embarrass the government.
a deliberate lie/deception

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: done slowly and carefully
examples: She spoke in a slow and deliberate way.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: done in a way that was planned, not by chance
examples: SYNONYM intentionally
She's been deliberately ignoring him all day.
an ad campaign that deliberately targets children
She was accused of deliberately misleading Parliament.
to deliberately withhold/conceal information
The fire had been started deliberately.
Her tone was deliberately insulting.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: slowly and carefully
examples: He packed up his possessions slowly and deliberately.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: easily damaged or broken
examples: SYNONYM fragile
delicate china teacups
The eye is one of the most delicate organs of the body.
the delicate ecological balance of the rainforest
Babies have very delicate skin.
a cool wash cycle for delicate fabrics

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not strong and easily becoming ill
examples: a delicate child/constitution
His health had always been delicate.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: small and having a beautiful shape or appearance
examples: his delicate hands

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: made or formed in a very careful and detailed way
examples: the delicate mechanisms of a clock

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: showing or needing careful or sensitive treatment
examples: I admired your delicate handling of the situation.
a delicate problem
The delicate surgical operation took five hours.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: light and pleasant; not strong
examples: SYNONYM subtle
a delicate fragrance/flavour
a river scene painted in delicate watercolours

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a very pleasant taste or smell
examples: Who cooked this? It's absolutely delicious.
to taste/smell/look delicious
a delicious meal/recipe/treat
This dish is delicious with cream.
The food was delicious.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: extremely pleasant
examples: the delicious coolness of the breeze
A delicious shiver of excitement ran through his body.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a feeling of great pleasure
examples: SYNONYM joy
a feeling of sheer/pure delight
The children squealed with delight when they saw the puppy.
She won the game easily, to the delight of all her fans.
He takes (great) delight in (= enjoys) proving others wrong.
She took a simple delight in joys that we could all share.
She couldn't hide her delight at the news.
He expressed his delight at seeing us all again.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that gives you great pleasure
examples: SYNONYM joy
This guitar is a delight to play.
Sample the culinary delights of Morocco.
the delights of living in the country

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very pleased
examples: a delighted smile
I'd be absolutely delighted to come.
‘Can you stay for dinner?’ ‘I’d be delighted (to)!’
I was delighted that you could stay.
She was delighted by the news of the wedding.
They were highly delighted at the court's decision.
I was delighted with my presents.
We are delighted about the decision.
I was so pleased and delighted for him when he started losing weight.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take goods, letters, etc. to the person or people they have been sent to
examples: I get my food delivered from the supermarket to save time.
Leaflets have been delivered to every household.
We promise to deliver within 48 hours.
We deliver to our stores seven days a week.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give or send information or ideas to somebody
examples: Let me deliver the good news first.
The video delivers a clear message about road safety.
Essentially, Web designers must deliver content simply and effectively.
Online training sessions are delivered directly to your desktop.
Our courses are delivered via the internet.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to give a speech, talk, performance, etc. or to make an official statement
examples: She will deliver a major speech on foreign policy tomorrow.
to deliver an address/a lecture/a sermon
The cast delivered the performances of a lifetime.
The jury finally delivered its verdict.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to do what you promised to do or what you are expected to do; to produce or provide what people expect you to
examples: He has promised to finish the job by June and I am sure he will deliver.
She always delivers on her promises.
If you can't deliver improved sales figures, you're fired.
The team delivered a stunning victory last night.
Successive administrations have failed to deliver adequate funding for education.
the failure of successive governments to deliver economic growth
There have been major breakdowns in delivering services to elderly residents.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to take somebody somewhere; to give somebody into somebody else's care or control
examples: She delivered the kids on time at their father's house.
The taxi delivered us to our hotel.
They delivered their prisoner over to the invading army.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to help a woman to give birth to a baby
examples: The baby was delivered by Caesarean section.
The baby was delivered safely on Tuesday night.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to give birth to a baby
examples: The number of women delivering their babies in hospital increased.
She was delivered of a healthy boy.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to throw or aim something
examples: He delivered the blow (= hit somebody hard) with all his force.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to rescue somebody from something bad
examples: SYNONYM save
Deliver us from evil.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to do what you have promised to do or what people expect or want you to do
examples: We expected great things of the England team, but on the day they simply failed to deliver the goods.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: definite, because all the legal documents have been signedWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French delivrer, based on Latin de- ‘away’ + liberare ‘set free’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of taking goods, letters, etc. to the people they have been sent to
examples: SEE ALSO general delivery
Allow 28 days for delivery.
We offer free delivery on orders over $200.
The service guarantees next day delivery.
Please pay for goods on delivery (= when you receive them).
When can you take delivery of (= be available to receive) the car?
A delivery van was waiting in the street outside.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of making a service or information available to people
examples: the delivery of public services
We have invested to improve service delivery.
Digital content delivery, especially music and video, is big business.
an electronic message delivery system

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of giving birth to a baby
examples: an easy/a difficult delivery
a delivery room/ward (= in a hospital, etc.)
a vaginal/caesarean delivery

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the way in which somebody speaks, sings a song, etc. in public
examples: The beautiful poetry was ruined by her poor delivery.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a ball that is thrown, especially in cricket or baseball
examples: a fast delivery

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a system of paying for goods when they are deliveredWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Anglo-Norman French delivree, feminine past participle of delivrer, based on Latin de- ‘away’ + liberare ‘set free’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a very strong request for something; something that somebody needs
examples: a demand for higher pay
demands that the law on gun ownership should be changed
A federal judge rejected their demands.
The management had no intention of meeting union demands.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: things that somebody/something makes you do, especially things that are difficult, make you tired, worried, etc.
examples: Juggling the demands of work and family is never easy.
She shouldn't always give in to his demands.
As a director he makes huge demands on his actors.
Flying makes enormous demands on pilots.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the desire or need of customers for goods or services that they want to buy or use
examples: SEE ALSO print on demand
Demand is exceeding supply.
It is becoming more difficult for us to meet demand.
Consumer demand for organic foods continues to increase rapidly.
We are struggling to satisfy the demand for the product.
We are seeing an increased demand for housing in the area.
increasing/growing/rising demand
to stimulate/boost/increase demand

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: because a lot of people have asked for something
examples: By popular demand, the play will run for another week.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: wanted by a lot of people
examples: Good secretaries are always in demand.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: done or happening whenever somebody asks
examples: SEE ALSO on-demand
Feed the baby on demand.
The service allows you to watch video on demand.
Campaigners insist that abortion should be available on demand.
