definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a system of government in which the people of a country can vote to elect their representatives
examples: SEE ALSO social democracy
parliamentary democracy
the principles of democracy

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a country that has this system of government
examples: Western democracies
I thought we were supposed to be living in a democracy.
We live in a multi-party democracy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: fair and equal treatment of everyone in an organization, etc., and their right to take part in making decisions
examples: the fight for justice and democracy
people who believe in true democracy

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: controlled by representatives who are elected by the people of a country; connected with this system
examples: a democratic country
a democratic system
democratic government
They are aiming to make the institutions of the EU truly democratic.
Exercise your democratic right to vote.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: based on the principle that all members have an equal right to be involved in running an organization, etc.
examples: democratic participation
a democratic decision

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: based on the principle that all members of society are equal rather than divided by money or social class
examples: a democratic society
democratic reforms
In 1776 these were considered dangerously democratic principles.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: connected with the Democratic Party in the US
examples: the Democratic senator from Oregon

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an evil spirit
examples: The people believed the girl was possessed by demons.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that causes a person to worry and makes them unhappy
examples: the demons of jealousy
She's had to battle her personal demons throughout her adult life.
He is plagued by demons which go back to his traumatic childhood.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who does something very well or with a lot of energy
examples: He skis like a demon.
He’s a demon: he gets up early, he works out, he goes home early, he studies, he works out again…

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: alcoholic drinkWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from medieval Latin, from Latin daemon, from Greek daimōn ‘deity, genius’; in sense (1) also from Latin daemonium ‘lesser or evil spirit’, from Greek daemonion, diminutive of daimōn.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to show something clearly by giving proof or evidence
examples: New research convincingly demonstrates that age-related memory loss is not inevitable.
These paintings demonstrate his extraordinary ability as a portrait painter.
The award demonstrated the importance that local people place on road safety.
This new anthology amply demonstrates the range and vitality of modern Scottish poetry.
This study clearly demonstrates how fishing can affect an ecosystem.
Let me demonstrate to you some of the difficulties we are facing.
The theories were demonstrated to be false.
It has been demonstrated that this drug is effective.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to show by your actions that you have a particular quality, feeling or opinion
examples: SYNONYM display
The team demonstrated breathtaking skills.
We want to demonstrate our commitment to human rights.
Students must demonstrate a willingness to work with others.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show and explain how something works or how to do something
examples: Her job involves demonstrating new educational software.
The gallery's experts demonstrated some conservation techniques.
The system was demonstrated to officials from 17 countries.
Let me demonstrate to you how it works.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to take part in a public meeting or march (= an organized walk by many people), usually as a protest or to show support for something
examples: Hundreds of protesters demonstrated outside the court.
students demonstrating against the war
Their objective was to demonstrate peacefully for civil rights.
They are demonstrating in support of free higher education.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a public meeting or a march (= an organized walk by many people) at which people show that they are protesting against or supporting somebody/something
examples: COMPARE march
to take part in/go on a demonstration
to hold/stage a demonstration
mass demonstrations in support of the exiled leader
anti-government demonstrations
a peaceful/violent demonstration

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an act of showing or explaining how something works or is done
examples: We were given a brief demonstration of the computer's functions.
a practical demonstration
a demonstration model (= a model used to show how something works)
Sandra and Nigel provided a demonstration of salsa dance steps.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an act of giving proof or evidence for something
examples: a demonstration of the connection between the two sets of figures
a demonstration of how something that seems simple can turn out to be very complicated

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an act of showing a feeling or an opinion
examples: a public demonstration of affection
a demonstration of support for the reforms

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a statement that something is not true or does not exist; the action of denying something
examples: the prisoner’s repeated denials of the charges against him
The terrorists issued a denial of responsibility for the attack.
There was an official denial that there would be an election before the end of the year.
She shook her head in denial.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an act of refusing to allow somebody to have something they have a right to expect
examples: Pressure groups have drawn attention to the denial of human rights in some areas.
The advertising ban is a denial of freedom of speech.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of refusing to accept that something unpleasant or painful is true
examples: The patient is still in denial.
Some people are in denial about the situation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to strongly criticize somebody/something that you think is wrong, illegal, etc.
examples: She publicly denounced the government's handling of the crisis.
The project was denounced as a scandalous waste of public money.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to tell the police, the authorities, etc. about somebody’s illegal political activities
examples: They were denounced as spies.
Many people denounced their neighbours to the secret police.
Someone in the village must have denounced them to the authorities.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: containing a lot of people, things, plants, etc. with little space between them
examples: a dense crowd/forest
areas of dense population
The forest is quite dense at that point.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: difficult to see through
examples: SYNONYM thick
dense fog/smoke/fumes
The fog was getting very dense.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: stupid
examples: How can you be so dense?
John's all right, but he can be a bit dense sometimes.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: difficult to understand because it contains a lot of information
examples: a dense piece of writing

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: heavy in relation to its size
examples: Less dense substances move upwards to form a crust.
All that is left of the star is a small, dense core.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of being dense; the degree to which something is dense
examples: The population density in this city is very high.
low density forest
an average density of 2.4 people per hectare

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: how thick a solid, liquid or gas is, measured by its mass per unit of volume
examples: SEE ALSO relative density
the density of a gas

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the amount of space available on a disk for recording data
examples: SEE ALSO packing density

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person whose job is to take care of people’s teeth
examples: to see/visit/consult your dentist
the dentist's chair/drill

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a place where a dentist sees patients
examples: I hate going to the dentist.
an appointment at the dentist’s
She couldn’t get treatment because she wasn’t registered with the dentist.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say that something is not true
examples: to deny an allegation/a charge/an accusation
He has denied any involvement in the incident.
The company strongly denies wrongdoing.
to vehemently/strenuously/categorically deny something
A spokesperson refused to either confirm or deny the reports.
She denied that there had been a cover-up.
It can't be denied that we need to devote more resources to this problem.
There's no denying the fact that quicker action could have saved them.
He denies attempting to murder his wife.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to refuse to admit or accept something
examples: She denied all knowledge of the incident.
The department denies responsibility for what occurred.
an anti-environmentalist campaign group that denies climate change

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to refuse to allow somebody to have something that they want or ask for
examples: They were denied access to the information.
Access to the information was denied to them.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to refuse to let yourself have something that you would like to have, especially for moral or religious reasonsWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French deni-, stressed stem of deneier, from Latin denegare, from de- ‘formally’ + negare ‘say no’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to leave a place, especially to start a trip
examples: OPPOSITE arrive
Flights for Rome depart from Terminal 3.
She waited until the last of the guests had departed.
The train departed Amritsar at 6.15 p.m.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to leave your job
examples: the departing president
He departed his job December 16.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to die. People say ‘depart this life’ to avoid saying ‘die’.Word Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French departir, based on Latin dispertire ‘to divide’. The original sense was ‘separate’, also ‘take leave of each other’, hence ‘go away’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a section of a large organization such as a government, business, university, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO police department
the Department of Health
He is a lecturer in the department of psychology at Trinity College, Dublin.
the Treasury Department
a government/university, etc. department
the marketing/sales, etc. department
The children's department (= in a large store) sells a wide range of good quality clothes.
the English department
She used to work in the IT department.
He later served as head of the art history department.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be something that somebody is responsible for or knows a lot about
examples: Don't ask me about it—that's her department.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a particular aspect or quality
examples: He doesn't have much going for him in the brains department, to be honest.
Movies lacking in the story department can still succeed.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act of leaving a place
examples: OPPOSITE arrival
His sudden departure threw the office into chaos.
rumours of her imminent/impending departure
They had received no news of him since his departure from the island.
The day of their departure for London was growing closer.
She postponed her departure to Scotland.
Flights should be confirmed 48 hours before departure.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a plane, train, etc. leaving a place at a particular time
examples: OPPOSITE arrival
arrivals and departures
All departures are from Manchester.
We sat in the departure lounge waiting for our flight to be called.
the departure time/gate
the departures board

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the part of an airport where you go before catching a plane
examples: COMPARE arrivals
There were long delays and queues in departures.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an action that is different from what is usual or expected
examples: Their latest single represents a new departure for the band.
It was a radical departure from tradition.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a place where a journey starts

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an idea, a theory or an event that is used to start a discussion, an activity, etc.
examples: The author takes Freud's dream theories as the point of departure for his essay.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: according to
examples: Starting salary varies from £26 000 to £30 500, depending on experience.
He either resigned or was sacked, depending on who you talk to.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that you are not certain about something because other things have to be considered
examples: ‘Is he coming?’ ‘That depends. He may not have the time.’
I don't know if we can help—it all depends.
I might not go. It depends how tired I am.
‘Your job sounds fun.’ ‘It depends what you mean by “fun”.’
I shouldn't be too late. But it depends if the traffic's bad.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of needing the help and support of somebody/something in order to survive or be successful
examples: OPPOSITE independence
Our relationship was based on mutual dependence.
financial/economic dependence
his dependence on his parents
the dependence of Europe on imported foods

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of being addicted to something (= unable to stop taking or using it)
examples: drug/alcohol dependence
dependence on alcohol

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the fact of one thing being affected by another
examples: the close dependence of soil and landforms

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: needing somebody/something in order to survive or be successful
examples: a woman with several dependent children
You can't be dependent on your parents all your life.
The festival is heavily dependent on sponsorship for its success.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: addicted to something (= unable to stop taking or using it)
examples: to be dependent on drugs

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: affected or decided by something
examples: A child's development is dependent on many factors.
The price is dependent on how many extras you choose.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: secondary to another clause, phrase or word
examples: The word ‘because’ forces the clause to be dependent on some other main clause.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to show an image of somebody/something in a picture
examples: a painting depicting the Virgin and Child
The artist had depicted her lying on a bed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to describe something in words, or give an impression of something in words or with a picture
examples: The novel depicts French society in the 1930s.
The advertisements depicted smoking as glamorous and attractive.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move soldiers or weapons into a position where they are ready for military action
examples: 2 000 troops were deployed in the area.
At least 5 000 missiles were deployed along the border.
Tanks were deployed effectively during the long campaign.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to use something effectively
examples: to deploy arguments/resources
She rejected the arguments that had been deployed against her.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of moving soldiers or weapons into a position where they are ready for military action
examples: the deployment of peacekeeping forces
troop deployments

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of using something effectively
examples: the deployment of resources/staff

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sum of money that is given as the first part of a larger payment
examples: SYNONYM down payment
They normally ask you to pay $100 (as a) deposit.
All deposits are non-refundable.
We've put down a 5% deposit on the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sum of money that is paid by somebody when they rent something and that is returned to them if they do not lose or damage the thing they are renting
examples: SEE ALSO security deposit
to pay a deposit
They'll probably ask you to leave a deposit.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a sum of money that is paid into a bank account
examples: SEE ALSO direct deposit
Deposits can be made at any branch.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (in the British political system) the amount of money that a candidate in an election to Parliament has to pay, and that is returned if he/she gets enough votes
examples: All the other candidates lost their deposits.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a layer of a substance that has formed naturally underground
examples: mineral/gold/coal deposits

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a layer of a substance that has been left somewhere, especially by a river, flood, etc., or is found at the bottom of a liquid
examples: The rain left a deposit of mud on the windows.
fatty deposits in the arteries of the heart
glacial deposits
The floods left a thick deposit of mud over the fields.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: placed in a deposit account
examples: With interest rates so low, there is little point in having cash on deposit.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very sad and without hope
examples: You mustn't let yourself get depressed.
She felt very depressed about the future.
He was really depressed at the thought of going into the office.
She was depressed over the recent death of her mother.
I was depressed by our lack of progress.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: suffering from the medical condition of depression
examples: She became severely depressed.
There is medical evidence to show that he is clinically depressed.
She suffers from sleep disturbance and depressed mood.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: without enough economic activity or jobs for people
examples: They have made little attempt to bring jobs to economically depressed areas.
The shipping trade was badly depressed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: having a lower amount or level than usual
examples: depressed prices

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: making you feel very sad and without enthusiasm
examples: a depressing sight/thought/experience
Looking for a job these days can be very depressing.
These findings make very depressing reading.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a medical condition in which a person feels very sad and anxious and often has physical symptoms such as being unable to sleep, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO postnatal depression
She was diagnosed as having clinical depression.
She suffered from severe depression after losing her job.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of feeling very sad and without hope
examples: There was a feeling of gloom and depression in the office when the news of the job cuts was announced.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a period when there is little economic activity and many people are poor or without jobs
examples: The country was in the grip of (an) economic depression.
the great Depression of the 1930s
He grew up during the Great Depression of the 1930s.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a part of a surface that is lower than the parts around it
examples: SYNONYM hollow
Rainwater collects in shallow depressions on the ground.
From the air, the photos show a shallow depression on the planet's surface.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a weather condition in which the pressure of the air becomes lower, often causing rain
examples: COMPARE anticyclone
an atmospheric depression moving east from the Atlantic

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the distance from the top or surface to the bottom of something; a particular distance down from the surface of something
examples: What's the depth of the water here?
the depth of a cut/wound/crack
Water was found at a depth of 30 metres.
They dug down to a depth of two metres.
Many dolphins can dive to depths of 200 metres.
The oil well extended several hundreds of feet in depth.
The camera must be strong enough to resist the immense water pressure at depth.
Most earthquakes occur at much shallower depths, usually less than 30 kilometres.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the distance from the front to the back of something
examples: The depth of the shelves is 30 centimetres.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the strength and power of feelings
examples: the depth of her love
music of great emotional depth

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: qualities that give somebody/something extra character and make them/it interesting
examples: The separate storylines really add depth and personality to the characters.
This film lacks the complexity or depth of his best movies.
Her paintings reveal hidden depths (= unknown and interesting things about her character).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the quality of knowing or understanding a lot of details about something; the ability to provide and explain these details
examples: SEE ALSO in-depth
a writer of great wisdom and depth
His ideas lack depth.
She has the ability to treat big subjects with breadth and depth.
a job that doesn’t require any great depth of knowledge
Younger students cannot be expected to have great depth of understanding.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the deepest, most extreme or serious part of something
examples: the depths of the ocean
to live in the depths of the country (= a long way from a town)
in the depths of winter (= when it is coldest)
She was in the depths of despair.
He gazed into the depths of her eyes.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the strength of a colour
examples: Strong light will affect the depth of colour of your carpets and curtains.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the quality in a work of art or a photograph that makes it appear not to be flat

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be in water that is too deep to stand in with your head above water
examples: If you can't swim, don't go out of your depth.
I don't like going out of my depth in the sea.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be unable to understand something because it is too difficult; to be in a situation that you cannot control
examples: He felt totally out of his depth in his new job.
The writer seems a little out of her depth when dealing with the emotional issue involved.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: in a detailed, careful and complete way
examples: I haven't looked at the report in depth yet.
an in-depth study
I studied phonology in depth at college.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be or to experience an extreme example of something unpleasant
examples: His latest novel plumbs the depths of horror and violence.
It was at that stage in her life when she plumbed the depths of despair.
The team's poor performances plumbed new depths last night when they lost 10–2.
The story plumbed the depths of tabloid journalism.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: the quality of being strong because you have a great variety of good people, ideas, etc. that can contribute to the success of something
examples: The French team does not have the strength in depth that the Australians have.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who is the next most important person below a business manager, a head of a school, a political leader, etc. and who does the person’s job when he or she is away
examples: I'm acting as deputy till the manager returns.
He was appointed deputy head of the school.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the name for a member of parliament in some countries
examples: Three women were among the 77 deputies elected.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: (in the US) a police officer who helps the sheriff of an areaWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French depute, from late Latin deputatus, past participle of deputare ‘consider to be, assign’, from de- ‘away’ + putare ‘consider’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to come or go down from a higher to a lower level
examples: OPPOSITE ascend
The plane began to descend.
The results, ranked in descending order (= from the highest to the lowest) are as follows…
She descended the stairs slowly.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to slope downwards
examples: OPPOSITE ascend
At this point the path descends steeply.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to arrive and begin to affect somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM fall
Night descends quickly in the tropics.
Calm descended on the crowd.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an action of coming or going down
examples: OPPOSITE ascent
The plane began its descent to Heathrow.
the country’s swift descent into anarchy

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a slope going downwards
examples: OPPOSITE ascent
There is a gradual descent to the sea.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person’s family origins
examples: SYNONYM ancestry
to be of Scottish descent
He traces his line of descent from the Stuart kings.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say what somebody/something is like
examples: The next section describes our findings in detail.
to describe a method/process/situation
Can you describe him to me?
They described for us exactly what happened.
The man was described as tall and dark, and aged about 20.
She describes herself as an artist.
Describe how you did it.
Words cannot describe what I felt at that moment.
Witnesses described seeing strange lights in the sky.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make a movement that has a particular shape; to form a particular shape
examples: The shark described a circle around the shoal of fish.
The road describes a long loop around the town.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of writing or speech that says what somebody/something is like; the act of writing or saying in words what somebody/something is like
examples: Follow the link below for a more detailed description.
a brief description of the software
The name means ‘no trees’ and it is an accurate description of the island.
Police have issued a description of the gunman.
This is a film that defies description (= is difficult or impossible to describe).
the novelist’s powers of description
a personal pain that goes beyond description (= is too great to express in words)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: of some, etc. type
examples: In the bay were boats of every description.
There were flying machines of all descriptions whizzing about.
Their money came from trade of some description.
The trunk was full of medals, coins and things of that description.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be like a particular person or thing
examples: A child answering the description of the missing boy was found safe and well in London yesterday.
We're all looking for quick, healthy meals, and pasta this fits this description.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be too extreme, horrible, etc. to believe/describe
examples: It beggars belief how things could have got this bad.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large area of land that has very little water and very few plants growing on it. Many deserts are covered by sand.
examples: the Sahara Desert
Somalia is mostly desert.
They travelled many miles across burning desert sands.
Occasionally, we passed a desert oasis surrounded by small tracts of grass and shrub.
The town has become a cultural desert (= a place without any culture).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to do something or show qualities that mean a particular reaction, reward or punishment is appropriate
examples: You deserve a rest after all that hard work.
The report deserves careful consideration.
This idea deserves more attention.
One player in particular deserves a mention.
England deserve tremendous credit for the way they played
to deserve praise/respect
What have I done to deserve this?
He finally received the recognition that he so richly deserved.
They didn't deserve to win.
He deserves to be locked up for ever for what he did.
Several other points deserve mentioning.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that you admire somebody because they have done something difficult or unpleasant
examples: She deserves a medal for teaching those 5-year-olds all day!
You really deserve a medal!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that you think somebody has earned the bad things that happen to them
examples: He did wrong, and he got what he deserved.
Let's just say they deserve what's coming to them.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: you should help somebody who has helped youWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French deservir, from Latin deservire ‘serve well or zealously’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the general arrangement of the different parts of something that is made, such as a building, book, machine, etc.
examples: The basic design of the car is very similar to that of earlier models.
special new design features
The system has a fundamental design flaw.
The steel frame is left visible and is part of the overall design concept.
The magazine will appear in a new design from next month.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the art or process of deciding how something will look, work, etc. by drawing plans, making computer models, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO interior design
the design and development of new products
I'm doing a course in art and design.
web/set/product design
a specialist in computer-aided design
a design studio

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a drawing or plan from which something may be made
examples: He has created some new and original designs.
designs for aircraft

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an arrangement of lines and shapes as a decoration
examples: SYNONYM pattern
floral/abstract/geometric designs
The tiles come in a huge range of colours and designs.
The building has intricate geometric designs on several of the walls.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a plan or an intention
examples: It happened—whether by accident or design—that the two of them were left alone after all the others had gone.
It is all part of his grand design.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to want to start a sexual relationship with somebody
examples: He was quite aware of her marital designs on him.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be planning to get something for yourself, often in a way that other people do not approve of
examples: Rumours spread that the Duke had designs on the crown (= wanted to make himself king).

Several pupils were designated as having moderate or severe learning difficulties.
a designated nature reserve
designated seats for the elderly

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to choose or name somebody for a particular job or position
examples: The director is allowed to designate his/her successor.
Who has she designated (as) her deputy?
the man designated to succeed the president

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show something using a particular mark or sign
examples: The different types are designated by the letters A, B and C.

definitions.definition: a person whose job is to decide how things such as clothes, furniture, tools, etc. will look or work by making drawings, plans or patterns
examples: SEE ALSO interior designer
one of the country's top fashion designers
a graphic/web/game designer

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that you would like to have or do; worth having or doing
examples: OPPOSITE undesirable
She chatted for a few minutes about the qualities she considered desirable in a secretary.
Such measures are desirable, if not essential.
The house has many desirable features.
Experience of computers is highly desirable.
It is desirable that interest rates should be reduced.
It is desirable that interest rates be reduced.
It is no longer desirable for such young children to take formal written tests.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: causing other people to feel sexual desire
examples: She suddenly saw herself as a desirable young woman.
He found her intensely desirable.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong wish to have or do something
examples: He now had enough money to satisfy all his desires.
a strong desire for power/revenge
She has a burning desire to be an artist.
I have no desire (= I do not want) to discuss the matter further.
He has expressed a desire to see you.
his father's desire that he become a lawyer

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a strong wish to have sex with somebody
examples: sexual desire
She felt a surge of love and desire for him.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is wished for
examples: When she agreed to marry him, he felt he had achieved his heart's desire.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of furniture like a table, often with drawers (= parts like boxes in it with handles on the front for pulling them open), that you sit at to read, write, work, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO hot-desk
I spend all day sitting at a desk.
The mayor sat behind his desk.
a desk drawer/lamp/calendar
He abandoned a career at sea for a desk job.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a place where you can get information or be served at an airport, a hotel, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO cash desk
There was a long queue at the check-in desk.
The girl behind the reception desk was always on the phone.
We asked the man on the information desk for a map of the city.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an office at a newspaper, television company, etc. that deals with a particular subject
examples: SEE ALSO city desk
the sports desk

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a screen on a computer that shows the icons of programs and files that can be used
examples: desktop icons

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the top of a desk

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a computer with a keyboard, screen and main processing unit that fits on a desk

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling or showing that you have little hope and are ready to do anything without worrying about danger to yourself or others
examples: The prisoners grew increasingly desperate.
Stores are getting desperate after two years of poor sales.
Somewhere out there was a desperate man, cold, hungry, hunted.
I heard sounds of a desperate struggle in the next room.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: giving little hope of success; tried when everything else has failed
examples: He made a desperate bid for freedom.
She clung to the edge in a desperate attempt to save herself.
His increasing financial difficulties forced him to take desperate measures.
Doctors were fighting a desperate battle to save the little girl's life.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: needing or wanting something very much
examples: He was so desperate for a job he would have done anything.
I'm desperate for a cigarette.
to be desperate for money/help/cash/attention
I was absolutely desperate to see her.
She was desperate to escape small town life.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: extremely serious or dangerous
examples: The children are in desperate need of love and attention.
They face a desperate shortage of clean water.
His financial situation was desperate.
He had died in desperate poverty.
American farmers are in desperate straits today.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that shows you have little hope and are ready to do anything without worrying about danger to yourself or others
examples: She looked desperately around for a weapon.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: extremely, especially when talking about bad situations
examples: desperately ill/unhappy/lonely
He grew up desperately poor.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very much, especially when talking about difficult or bad situations
examples: They desperately wanted a child.
He took a deep breath, desperately trying to keep calm.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to show that something happened or is true although something else might have happened to prevent it
examples: SYNONYM in spite of
Her voice was shaking despite all her efforts to control it.
Despite applying for hundreds of jobs, he is still out of work.
She was good at physics despite the fact that she found it boring.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to show that somebody did not intend to do the thing mentioned
examples: SYNONYM in spite of
He had to laugh despite himself.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a place to which somebody/something is going or being sent
examples: popular tourist/holiday destinations like the Bahamas
to arrive at/reach your destination
Our luggage was checked all the way through to our final destination.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to damage something so badly that it no longer exists, works, etc.
examples: The building was completely destroyed by fire.
The earthquake damaged or destroyed countless homes.
Some of the habitat has already been totally destroyed.
They've destroyed all the evidence.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take all the value and pleasure from somebody's life; to ruin (= completely damage) somebody's life or reputation
examples: Failure was slowly destroying him.
She threatened to destroy my reputation.
He wanted revenge on the man who had destroyed his life.
Their lives have been virtually destroyed by this tragedy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to kill an animal deliberately, usually because it is sick or not wanted
examples: The injured horse had to be destroyed.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of destroying something; the process of being destroyed
examples: SEE ALSO self-destruction
the destruction of the rainforests
a tidal wave bringing death and destruction in its wake
The central argument is that capitalism sows the seeds of its own destruction (= creates the forces that destroy it).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: causing destruction or damage
examples: SEE ALSO self-destructive
The war demonstrated the destructive power of modern weapons.
the destructive effects of anxiety
Opencast coal mining is among the most environmentally destructive activities carried out in Wales.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: negative or not helpful
examples: destructive behaviour/impulses/tendencies
destructive emotions that fuel anger and self-pity
They don't think about how damaging and destructive their words are.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small individual fact or item; a less important fact or item
examples: an expedition planned down to the last detail
The Ministry refused to reveal any more details of the attack.
Tell me the main points now; leave the details till later.
The finer details of the plan have still to be worked out.
These are all relatively minor details.
‘We had a terrible time—’ ‘Oh, spare me the details (= don't tell me any more).’

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the small facts or features of something, when you consider them all together
examples: The report was criticized for its lack of detail.
Ensure that your diagrams contain the appropriate level of detail.
This issue will be discussed in more detail in the next chapter.
The making of the movie is explored in minute detail.
The research has been carried out with scrupulous attention to detail.
He had an eye for detail (= noticed and remembered small details).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: information about something
examples: Please provide the following details: name, age and sex.
Can you send me your contact details?
For further details visit our website.
They didn't give any details about the game.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a small part of a picture or painting; the smaller or less important parts of a picture, pattern, etc. when you consider them all together
examples: This is a detail from the 1844 Turner painting.
a huge picture with a lot of fine detail in it

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a group of soldiers given special duties

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to explain something fully
examples: I can't go into details now; it would take too long.
