definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: giving many details and a lot of information; paying great attention to details
examples: a detailed description of the events
For more detailed information visit our website.
a detailed analysis/examination/study
a detailed account/discussion/explanation/investigation
He gave me detailed instructions on how to get there.
The image is clear and richly detailed .

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to keep somebody in an official place, such as a police station, a prison or a hospital, and prevent them from leaving
examples: One man has been detained for questioning.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to delay somebody or prevent them from going somewhere
examples: SEE ALSO detention
I'm sorry—he'll be late; he's been detained at a meeting.
The minister was unavoidably detained in Lisbon on affairs of state.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to discover or notice something, especially something that is not easy to see, hear, etc.
examples: The tests are designed to detect the disease early.
Only 8 per cent of regular cola consumers detected a difference.
The sensor detects changes light level and temperature.
a test that can detect the presence of calcium in the arteries
This is an instrument that can detect very small amounts of radiation.
Do I detect a note of criticism?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of discovering or noticing something, especially something that is not easy to see, hear, etc.; the fact of being discovered or noticed
examples: crime prevention and detection
Last year the detection rate for car theft was just 13 per cent.
Many problems, however, escape detection.
Early detection of cancers is vitally important.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person, especially a police officer, whose job is to investigate crimes and catch criminals
examples: SEE ALSO store detective
a police/homicide/undercover detective
Several objects were taken away by detectives from the anti-terrorist squad.
a detective story/novel
Detective Inspector (Roger) Brown
a detective constable/sergeant/superintendent

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person employed by somebody to find out information about somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO private detective

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being kept in a place, especially a prison, and prevented from leaving
examples: They were sentenced to 12 months' detention in a young offender institution.
police powers of arrest and detention
allegations of torture and detention without trial
a detention camp

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the punishment of being kept at school for a time after other students have gone home
examples: They can’t give me (a) detention for this.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become worse
examples: Her health deteriorated rapidly, and she died shortly afterwards.
They had to cope with deteriorating weather conditions.
The discussion quickly deteriorated into an angry argument.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality that makes you continue trying to do something even when this is difficult
examples: fierce/grim/dogged determination
He fought the illness with courage and determination.
They had survived by sheer determination.
I admire her determination to get it right.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of deciding something officially
examples: SEE ALSO self-determination
factors influencing the determination of future policy

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of finding out or calculating something
examples: Both methods rely on the accurate determination of the pressure of the gas.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to discover the facts about something; to calculate something exactly
examples: SYNONYM establish
An inquiry was set up to determine the cause of the accident.
Try to determine the extent of the problem.
We set out to determine exactly what happened that night.
It is difficult to determine when drama first appeared in India.
It was determined that she had died of natural causes.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something happen in a particular way or be of a particular type
examples: Rural voters in key states will determine the outcome of the election.
Upbringing plays an important part in determining a person's character.
Age and experience will be determining factors in our choice of candidate.
The physical capabilities of a plant determine where it can and cannot live.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to officially decide and/or arrange something
examples: A date for the meeting has yet to be determined.
The court determined (that) the defendant should pay the legal costs.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to decide definitely to do something
examples: They determined to start early.
The government determined on a change of policy.
From that moment, I determined that it should not happen again.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having made a definite decision to do something and not letting anyone prevent you
examples: The opposition to her plan made her more determined than ever.
I'm determined to succeed.
They were quite determined that he wasn't going to do it.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: showing determination
examples: I made a determined effort to stop smoking.
The proposal had been dropped in the face of determined opposition.
They set about their task in determined mood.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very determined to do something
examples: I came here bound and determined to put the last 12 months behind me.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to completely destroy a place or an area
examples: The bomb devastated much of the old part of the city.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel very shocked and sadWord Origin
examples: mid 17th cent.: from Latin devastat- ‘laid waste’, from the verb devastare, from de- ‘thoroughly’ + vastare ‘lay waste’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to gradually grow or become bigger, more advanced, stronger, etc.; to make something do this
examples: The child is developing normally.
Some children develop more slowly than others.
Gradually these settlements developed into cities.
Human beings developed from earlier species of animals.
The place has rapidly developed from a small fishing community into a thriving tourist resort.
The aim is to develop your personal skills.
She developed the company from nothing.
The competition helps entrants develop ideas into business concepts.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to start to have a skill, ability, quality, etc. that becomes better and stronger; to become better and stronger
examples: He's developed a real flair for management.
Their relationship has developed over a number of years.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to think of or produce a new idea, product, etc. and make it successful
examples: The company develops and markets new software.
It takes time to develop new technology.
We are developing products for different parts of the industry.
to develop a strategy/system/programme
to develop a method/model/technique
A new type of painkilling drug has recently been developed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to begin to have something such as a disease or a problem; to start to affect somebody/something
examples: She developed lung cancer at the age of sixty.
Her son developed asthma when he was two.
The car developed engine trouble and we had to stop.
If symptoms develop, seek help quickly.
Problems can develop unexpectedly.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to start to happen or change, especially in a bad way
examples: A crisis was rapidly developing in the Gulf.
We need more time to see how things develop before we take action.
The conflict quickly developed into full-scale war.
The situation is developing into a crisis.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to build new houses, factories, etc. on an area of land, especially land that was not being used effectively before
examples: The site is being developed by a French company.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to build or improve a building or other facilities
examples: The company is developing a chain of hotels.
He is enthusiastic about plans to develop the leisure facilities at the site.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to become economically and socially more advanced
examples: SEE ALSO developed (1)
There have been many attempts to explain why some countries develop whilst others remain in poverty.
China is developing at a pace that is remarkable to behold.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to add further explanation or details to an idea, story or musical theme
examples: SYNONYM elaborate (1)
She develops the theme more fully in her later books.
The piano then takes up the melody and develops it.
He began to develop these ideas in a series of paintings.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to treat film that has been used to take photographs with chemicals so that the pictures can be seen
examples: When Lewis developed the film, he was astonished by what he saw.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the steady growth of something so that it becomes more advanced, stronger, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO self-development
a baby’s development in the womb
This is a perfectly normal stage of development.
the development of basic skills such as literacy and numeracy
The company can offer a number of opportunities for career development.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the growth of the economy of a country or region through increased business activity
examples: Increased tourism will promote job creation and economic development.
International policies should support, not inhibit, sustainable development.
He described women as the backbone of rural development worldwide.
community development projects
a development plan/programme

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of producing or creating something new or more advanced; a new or advanced product or idea
examples: SEE ALSO research and development
the development of new technology
Pete is head of product development.
A more powerful version of this electric bus in currently in development.
A new vaccine is under development.
This drug is an exciting new development.
developments in aviation technology

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a new event or stage that is likely to affect what happens in a continuing situation
examples: Have there been any further developments?
We welcome the recent positive developments.
the latest developments in the war
There have been some interesting new developments in the case.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a piece of land with new buildings on it
examples: SEE ALSO ribbon development
I live in a brand-new housing development.
a mixed residential and business development

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the process of using an area of land, especially to make a profit by building on it, etc.
examples: He bought the land for development.
The city has undergone rapid development.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an object or a piece of equipment that has been designed to do a particular job
examples: SEE ALSO intrauterine device
a tracking/recording/listening device
The new devices will be installed at US airports.
electrical labour-saving devices around the home
This device allows deaf people to communicate by typing messages instead of speaking.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of computer equipment, especially a small one such as a smartphone
examples: SEE ALSO mobile device
You can store thousands of photos on your device.
a portable/wireless device
The waiter takes orders on a hand-held device.
Now connect the device to your computer.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a bomb or weapon that will explode
examples: SEE ALSO IED
A powerful device exploded outside the station.
It was the world's first atomic device.
Two bombers detonated their devices in the busy shopping centre.
The device failed to detonate.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a method of doing something that produces a particular result or effect
examples: Targeted advertising on social media is very successful as a marketing device.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a plan or trick that is used to get something that somebody wants
examples: The report was a device used to hide rather than reveal problems.
This device can be seem as somewhat dishonest.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a form of words that is intended to produce a particular effect in speech or writing
examples: a rhetorical device
Metaphor and symbol are literary devices.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to leave somebody alone to do as they wish, and not tell them what to doWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French devis, based on Latin divis- ‘divided’, from the verb dividere. The original sense was ‘desire or intention’, found now only in leave someone to their own devices (which has become associated with sense (3)).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the most powerful evil being
examples: SYNONYM Satan
belief in the Devil
His strong left-wing views make him the devil incarnate to more extreme Conservatives.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an evil spirit
examples: They believed she was possessed by devils.
He behaved like someone possessed by devils.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who behaves badly, especially a child
examples: SEE ALSO she-devil
a naughty little devil

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to talk about somebody and to emphasize an opinion that you have of them
examples: I miss the old devil, now that he's gone.
She's off to Greece for a month—lucky devil!
James was a handsome devil and rich, too.
They were handsome young devils in their uniforms, weren't they?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: people say Be a devil! to encourage somebody to do something that they are not sure about doing
examples: Go on, be a devil, buy both of them.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that it is easier and wiser to stay in a bad situation that you know and can deal with rather than change to a new situation that may be much worse

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in a difficult situation where there are two equally unpleasant or unacceptable choices

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: very difficult or unpleasant
examples: These berries are the devil to pick because they're so small.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: bad people often seem to have good luck

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: people who do not have enough to do often start to do wrong
examples: She blamed the crimes on the local jobless teenagers. ‘The devil makes work for idle hands,’ she would say.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a very difficult or unpleasant job or time
examples: I've had a devil of a job finding you.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a lot of trouble
examples: There'll be hell to pay when he finds out.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used, in an unfriendly way, to tell somebody to go away

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: very hard, fast, etc.
examples: We ran like the devil.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to do anything, even something really bad or dishonest, in return for money, success or power

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: people say speak/talk of the devil when somebody they have been talking about appears unexpectedly
examples: Well, speak of the devil—here's Alice now!

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used in questions to show that you are annoyed or surprised
examples: What the devil do you think you're doing?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to invent something new or a new way of doing something
examples: SYNONYM think up
A new system has been devised to control traffic in the city.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say exactly what an illness or the cause of a problem is
examples: The test is used to diagnose a variety of diseases.
The illness was diagnosed as cancer.
He has recently been diagnosed with angina.
I quickly diagnosed the problem as a faulty battery.
He was diagnosed (as) a diabetic when he was 64.
He was diagnosed (a) diabetic.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of discovering or identifying the exact cause of an illness or a problem
examples: a diagnosis of lung cancer
They are waiting for the doctor's diagnosis.
An accurate diagnosis was made after a series of tests.
They are using new methods of diagnosis.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to show something using a diagram
examples: The overall structures of these enzymes are diagrammed in Fig 1.
The coach diagrammed defensive plays on his tablet.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a conversation in a book, play or film or in language teaching materials
examples: Learners are asked to listen to three short dialogues.
Practise the dialogue with a partner.
The novel has long descriptions and not much dialogue.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a formal discussion between two groups or countries, especially when they are trying to solve a problem, end a disagreement, etc.
examples: COMPARE monologue
The president told waiting reporters there had been a constructive dialogue.
The government refused to engage in direct dialogue with the terrorists.
There needs to be a closer dialogue between management and staff.
an honest and open dialogue about racial identity in the US
a meaningful dialogue on pay and working conditions

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a clear precious stone of pure carbon, the hardest substance known. Diamonds are used in jewellery and also in industry, especially for cutting glass.
examples: SEE ALSO black diamond
a diamond ring/necklace
She was wearing her diamonds (= jewellery with diamonds in it).
a six carat diamond
a diamond mine
The lights shone like diamonds.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a shape with four straight sides of equal length and with angles that are not right angles
examples: a sweater with a diamond pattern
The eight vehicles assumed a diamond formation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: one of the four suits (= sets) in a pack of cards. The cards are marked with red diamond shapes.
examples: the ten of diamonds
Diamonds are/is trumps.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: one card from the suit called diamonds
examples: You must play a diamond if you have one.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the space inside the lines that connect the four bases; also used to mean the whole baseball fieldWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French diamant, from medieval Latin diamas, diamant-, variant of Latin adamans from Greek adamas, adamant-, ‘untameable, invincible’ (later used to denote the hardest metal or stone, hence diamond), from a- ‘not’ + daman ‘to tame’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a book in which you can write down the experiences you have each day, your private thoughts, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO journal
Do you keep a diary (= write one regularly)?
Peter began writing his diary in October last year.
the diaries of Samuel Pepys
The writer's letters and diaries are being published next year.
I think I'm going to start an online diary.
a travel/sleep/food diary
‘It's all over,’ he wrote in his diary for April 21.
her diary entry for 9 December 2017

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a book or an app with spaces for each day of the year in which you can record things you have to do in the future
examples: I used to keep a desk diary for business appointments.
an appointments diary
I've made a note in my diary.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell somebody what to do, especially in an annoying way
examples: They are in no position to dictate terms (= tell other people what to do).
What right do they have to dictate how we live our lives?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to control or influence how something happens
examples: SYNONYM determine
When we take our vacations is very much dictated by Greg's work schedule.
It's generally your job that dictates where you live now.
The social conventions of the day dictated that she should remain at home with her parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to say words for somebody else to write down or to be recorded
examples: She dictated the letter to her assistant.
OK, you write, I'll dictate.
Just dictate into the machine, we'll transcribe it later.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a political leader who has complete power over a country, especially one who has gained it using military force
examples: The country suffered at the hands of a series of military dictators.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who behaves as if they have complete power over other people, and tells them what to do
examples: Her father was a dictator and the whole family was afraid of him.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a book or electronic resource that gives a list of the words of a language in alphabetical order and explains what they mean, or gives a word for them in a foreign language
examples: a Spanish-English dictionary
a slang dictionary
a dictionary of slang
If you don't know the meaning of a word, look it up in the dictionary.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a book that explains the words that are used in a particular subject
examples: a dictionary of mathematics
I decided to consult a medical dictionary.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a list of words in electronic form, for example stored in a computer’s spellcheckerWord Origin
examples: early 16th cent.: from medieval Latin dictionarium (manuale) or dictionarius (liber) ‘manual or book of words’, from Latin dictio, from dicere ‘to say’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to stop living
examples: My father died suddenly at the age of 48.
At least six people have died in the accident.
That plant's going to die if you don't water it!
He later died in hospital.
They died fighting for their country.
She died peacefully after a long illness.
to die with dignity
to die of/from cancer
He was ready to die for his cause.
I'll never forget it to my dying day (= until I die).
I nearly died when I saw him there (= it was very embarrassing).
to die a natural/slow/horrible/violent death
She died young.
At least they died happy.
He died a hero.
He died a poor man.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop existing; to disappear
examples: The old customs are dying.
His secret died with him (= he never told anyone).
The words died on my lips (= I stopped speaking).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to stop working
examples: My phone died and I had no way to contact you.
The engine spluttered and died.
My car just died on me.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to want something or want to do something very much
examples: I'm dying for a glass of water.
I'm dying to know what happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you are telling the truth or will do what you promise
examples: I saw him do it—cross my heart.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to fail completely
examples: The play got terrible reviews and quickly died a death.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to die because you are old or ill

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to find something extremely funny
examples: I nearly died laughing when she said that.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to die or become ill and fall down in very large numbers
examples: People were dropping like flies in the intense heat.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a situation where you need to act in a very determined way or taking a great risk, because there is no alternative
examples: SEE ALSO do-or-die
At this stage in the competition it's do or die.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: do not stop hoping

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say that things change very slowly

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if you think something is to die for, you really want it, and would do anything to get it
examples: She was wearing a dress to die for.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the food and drink that you eat and drink regularly
examples: SEE ALSO staple diet (1)
to eat a healthy, balanced diet
I loved the Japanese diet of rice, vegetables and fish.
a vegetarian/vegan diet
The traditional Mediterranean diet is fairly high in fat.
to receive advice on diet

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a limited variety or amount of food that you eat for medical reasons or because you want to lose weight; a time when you only eat this limited variety or amount
examples: SEE ALSO the Atkins Diet™
He followed a strict low-fat diet.
I decided to go on a diet (= to lose weight) before my holiday.
She is trying to lose weight through diet and exercise.
diet drinks (= with fewer calories than normal)
Lose pounds with our new diet plan!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a large amount of a limited range of activities
examples: SEE ALSO staple diet (2)
Children today are brought up on a diet of video games and TV on demand.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be different from somebody/something
examples: They hold differing views.
French differs from English in this respect.
French and English differ in this respect.
Ideas on childcare may differ considerably between the parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to disagree with somebody
examples: I have to differ with you on that.
Medical opinion differs as to how to treat the disease.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if two people agree to differ/disagree, they accept that they have different opinions about something, but they decide not to discuss it any longer
examples: We must just agree to differ on this.
In the end we agreed to disagree.
I think you're wrong. Let's just agree to differ.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say politely that you do not agree with something that has just been said
examples: ‘At least she is good at her job.’ ‘Oh, I beg to differ.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the way in which two people or things are not like each other; the way in which somebody/something has changed
examples: OPPOSITE similarity
Americans and Brits speak the same language, but there are big cultural differences.
There are no significant differences between the education systems of the two countries.
He was studying the similarities and differences between humans and animals.
I can never tell the difference (= distinguish) between the twins.
There's no difference in the results.
There is a fundamental difference in approach to conservation in Japan.
She noticed a marked difference in the children on her second visit.
Her work questions notions of gender difference.
What a difference! You look great with your hair like that.
Differences among beetle species may prove to be a key factor.
Despite their differences, the two are great friends.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the amount that something is greater or smaller than something else
examples: SEE ALSO goal difference
We measured the difference in temperature.
The difference between the two numbers gives you the profit.
There's an age difference of six years between the boys (= one is six years older than the other).
There is not much difference in price between the two brands.
I'll lend you £500 and you'll have to find the difference (= the rest of the money that you need).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a disagreement between people
examples: We have our differences, but she's still my sister.
Why don't you settle your differences and be friends again?
There was a difference of opinion over who had won.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to stop not being friendly and become friends again
examples: After not speaking to each other for years, the two brothers decided to bury the hatchet.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a point that somebody wants to suggest is a difference when in fact it is not different at all
examples: His government did not brand them terrorists, but rather ‘an entity that supports terrorism’. That may prove to be a distinction without a difference.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have an important effect on somebody/something; to make somebody feel better
examples: A few kind words at the right time make all the difference.
Just five minutes' exercise a day could make all the difference.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have an effect/no effect on somebody/something
examples: The rain didn't make much difference to the game.
Your age shouldn't make any difference to whether you get the job or not.
Changing schools made a big difference to my life.
What difference will it make if he knows or not?
I don't think it makes a lot of difference what colour it is (= it is not important).
‘Shall we go on Friday or Saturday?’ ‘It makes no difference (to me).’

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that you think the differences between two things are not important
examples: ‘That's not a xylophone, it's a glockenspiel.’ ‘Same difference.’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to agree to forget about your disagreements
examples: We need to sink our differences and present a united opposition to the plan.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: (when discussing a price, etc.) to agree on an amount that is at an equal distance between the two amounts that have been suggested
examples: I offered €200 but he wanted €300. In the end, we split the difference and I paid him €250.
I wanted to leave early and Ian wanted to leave late, so we split the difference and left at noon.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to show that something is interesting or unusual
examples: The traditional backpack with a difference—it's waterproof.
If you want a holiday with a difference, come to Iceland.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how much difference there is between two things
examples: There's a world of difference between liking someone and loving them.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not the same as somebody/something; not like somebody/something else
examples: OPPOSITE similar
American English is significantly different from British English.
It's slightly different to what I'm used to.
He's different than the rest.
It's completely different now than it was a year ago.
People often give very different accounts of the same event.
My son's terribly untidy; my daughter's no different.
The room looks different without the furniture.
Now he spoke in a different and kinder voice.
Let's try a different approach.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: separate and individual
examples: Each chapter deals with a different type of business.
She offered us five different kinds of cake.
We're helping society in many different ways.
The programme was about customs in different parts of the country.
They are sold in many different colours.
I looked it up in three different dictionaries.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: unusual; not like other people or things
examples: ‘Did you enjoy the play?’ ‘Well, it was certainly different!’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be very different
examples: I know which area they live in, but whether I can find their house is a different matter.
That's a whole different matter.
I don't mind lizards, but snakes are a different matter.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a completely different situation or person from the one previously mentioned

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have information or evidence that the opposite is true
examples: He says he doesn't care about what the critics write, but I know different.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to behave in a different way from other people; to have different attitudes or ideas
examples: She was a gifted and original artist who marched to a different drummer.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to have different aims that cannot be achieved together without causing problems
examples: There are different considerations, often pulling in different directions.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to change the way that a situation appears
examples: What you have told us puts a different complexion on the situation.
The joke took on a rather serious complexion when the police became involved.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to change your opinion about somebody/something or your attitude towards somebody/something

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to give some information that is different from what you expect or have been told
examples: These drugs are widely believed to be effective medications. The data, however, tell a different story.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to recognize or show that two things are not the same
examples: SYNONYM distinguish
It's difficult to differentiate between the two varieties.
I can't differentiate one variety from another.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be the particular thing that shows that things or people are not the same
examples: SYNONYM distinguish
The male's yellow beak differentiates it from the female.
features which clearly differentiate this product from other similar ones

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to treat people or things in a different way, especially in an unfair way
examples: SYNONYM discriminate
Rules that differentiate between employees on the basis of gender need to be revised.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to become more specialized during growth and development; to make a cell or tissue more specialized during growth and development
examples: The fertilized egg differentiates into several different cell types.
The receptors are developed and differentiated into sense organs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a different way from somebody/something
examples: OPPOSITE similarly
Boys and girls may behave differently.
He didn't like being treated differently.
What will you do differently next time?
Eddie comes from an older generation that thought differently than we do.
The male bird has a differently shaped head.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not easy; needing effort or skill to do or to understand
examples: The competition judges were given a very difficult task.
a difficult decision/question
Asking for help is extremely difficult for some people.
It's really difficult to read your writing.
Your writing is really difficult to read.
It is difficult to imagine a woman in the 1950s behaving like this.
She finds it very difficult to get up early.
It's difficult for them to get here much before seven.
It has become increasingly difficult for young people to buy a house.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: full of problems; causing a lot of trouble
examples: I found myself in a difficult situation.
difficult conditions/circumstances
I'd had a difficult time and needed a break.
a difficult year/month
My boss is making life very difficult for me.
13 is a difficult age.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not easy to please; not helpful
examples: SYNONYM awkward
a difficult child/customer/boss
Don't pay any attention to her—she's just being difficult.
The singer has a difficult reputation.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have difficulty doing something
examples: You'll have a job convincing them that you're right.
He had a hard job to make himself heard.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a problem; a thing or situation that causes problems
examples: SEE ALSO learning difficulties
the difficulties of English syntax
a patient with breathing difficulties
They encountered numerous difficulties while making the film.
She had been experiencing technical difficulties.
I think we've managed to overcome most of the practical difficulties.
I know the kinds of difficulties faced by parents and teachers.
We've run into difficulties with the new project.
I'm having difficulty with the engine.
He was often in financial difficulties.
He got into difficulty while swimming and had to be rescued.
It was a time fraught with difficulties and frustration.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state or quality of being hard to do or to understand; the effort that something involves
examples: I had considerable difficulty (in) persuading her to leave.
I had no difficulty (in) making myself understood.
He spoke slowly and with great difficulty.
The changes were made with surprisingly little difficulty.
We found the house without difficulty.
They discussed the difficulty of studying abroad.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: how hard something is
examples: Both roles had a high degree of difficulty.
The games have varying levels of difficulty.
questions of increasing difficulty
The walks in the book vary in difficulty.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a hole in the ground or to move soil from one place to another using your hands, a tool or a machine
examples: I think I'll do some digging in the garden.
They dug deeper and deeper but still found nothing.
We could only dig down a few feet.
to dig for gold/treasure
to dig a hole/trench/grave
I've been digging the garden.
They had obviously dug special tunnels beneath the city.
The present entrance was dug through the soft limestone.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to remove something from the ground with a tool
examples: I'll dig some potatoes for lunch.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to search in something in order to find an object in something
examples: I dug around in my bag for a pen.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to approve of or like something very much

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to search for information in a careful and detailed way
examples: You'll need to dig deep into the records to find the figures you want.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to try hard to provide the money, equipment, etc. that is needed
examples: We're asking you to dig deep for the earthquake victims.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to discover and reveal information about somebody that could damage them
examples: They hired private investigators to dig up dirt on their political opponents.
She has come to dig the dirt on her old rival.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to refuse to do something or to change your mind about something
examples: They dug in their heels and would not lower the price.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to spend a lot of your own money on something

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to push your finger or your elbow into somebody’s side, especially to attract their attention

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to do something that will have very harmful results for you

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to get yourself into a bad situation that will be very difficult to get out ofWord Origin
examples: Middle English: perhaps from Old English dīc ‘ditch’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: using a system of receiving and sending information as a series of the numbers one and zero, showing that an electronic signal is there or is not there
examples: COMPARE analogue (1)
a digital camera
digital media/content/platforms
These figures include digital downloads in addition to retail sales.
He quickly realized that all film and video production would go digital.
The system is fully digital, with no analogue components.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with the use of computer technology, especially the internet
examples: communication in the digital age
Digital technology continues to evolve rapidly.
Advertisers are putting more and more money into digital marketing.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: showing information by using figures, rather than with hands that point to numbers
examples: COMPARE analogue (2)
a digital clock/watch
The instrument panel has an easy-to-read digital display.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a calm and serious manner that deserves respect
examples: She accepted the criticism with quiet dignity.
He brings a quiet dignity to the role.
His aristocratic voice gives him an air of dignity and power.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of being given honour and respect by people
examples: the dignity of work
The terminally ill should be allowed to die with dignity.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a sense of your own importance and value
examples: It's difficult to preserve your dignity when you have no job and no home.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: below what you see as your own importance or worth
examples: He clearly regarded manual work as beneath his dignity.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to demand to be treated with the respect that you think that you deserve
examples: Our teacher never stands on her dignity with us, but treats us all as friends and colleagues.
She was never one to stand on her dignity.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a situation that makes problems, often one in which you have to make a very difficult choice between things of equal importance
examples: SYNONYM predicament
I could see no way of resolving this moral dilemma.
The digital era brings new ethical dilemmas for journalists.
They were caught in a real dilemma.
She faced a dilemma about whether to accept the offer or not.
the perennial dilemma between work and family commitments

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a situation in which you have to make a choice between things that are equally unpleasant
examples: The medical profession’s eagerness for scientific advance had impaled it on the horns of a dilemma, forcing an unnatural choice between science and morality.
The dire economic situation had placed the prime minister on the horns of a dilemma.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a measurement in space, for example how high, wide or long something is
examples: SEE ALSO fourth dimension
We measured the dimensions of the kitchen.
computer design tools that work in three dimensions

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the size and extent of a situation
examples: a problem of considerable dimensions

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an aspect, or way of looking at or thinking about something
examples: Her job added a new dimension to her life.
We should also consider the social dimension of unemployment.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become smaller, weaker, etc.; to make something become smaller, weaker, etc.
examples: SYNONYM decrease
The world's resources are rapidly diminishing.
His influence has diminished with time.
The new law is expected to diminish the government's chances.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something seem less important than they really are
examples: I don't wish to diminish the importance of their contribution.
The trial has aged and diminished him.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to refer to a point at which you start achieving less than the value of the time or money you put into something
examples: Our efforts were producing diminishing returns.
In general, the more exercise you take, the greater the health benefit; but beyond a certain level you get diminishing returns.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the main meal of the day, eaten either in the middle of the day or in the evening
examples: SEE ALSO TV dinner
It's time for dinner.
When do you have dinner?
What shall we have for dinner tonight?
As I'm single, I tend to go out to dinner (= eat in a restaurant) a lot.
to go to dinner
I'd like to take you out to dinner tonight.
Let's invite them to dinner tomorrow.
What time do you serve dinner?
It's your turn to cook dinner.
She didn't eat much dinner.
I never eat a big dinner.
Christmas/Thanksgiving dinner
a three-course dinner
a roast/steak/turkey dinner
a family sitting around the dinner table
a dinner plate
He was trying hard to impress his dinner guests.
school dinners (= meals provided at school in the middle of the day)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a large formal social gathering at which dinner is eaten
examples: SEE ALSO rehearsal dinner
The club's annual dinner will be held on 3 June.
The winner will be announced at a gala dinner.
a fund-raising/charity dinner

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing that has been done badly
examples: SYNONYM mess
He's made a real dog's breakfast of these accounts.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: completely defeatedWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French disner (infinitive used as a noun), probably from desjëuner ‘to break fast’, from des- (expressing reversal) + jëun ‘fasting’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to put something quickly into a liquid and take it out again
examples: He dipped the brush into the paint.
Dip your hand in to see how hot the water is.
The fruit had been dipped in chocolate.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to go downwards or to a lower level; to make something do this
examples: SYNONYM fall
The sun dipped below the horizon.
Sales for this quarter have dipped from 38.7 million to 33 million.
The road dipped suddenly as we approached the town.
The plane dipped its wings.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if you dip your headlights when driving a car at night, you make the light from them point down so that other drivers do not have the light in their eyes

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: when farmers dip animals, especially sheep, they put them in a bath of a liquid containing chemicals in order to kill insects, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to spend some of your own money on something
examples: She was forced to dip into her own pocket to pay for the repairs.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to start doing something very carefully to see if it will be successful or not
examples: We decided to dip a toe in the computer games market.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person whose job is to represent his or her country in a foreign country, for example, in an embassy
examples: SEE ALSO Chief Diplomat
Washington's top diplomat in Havana
a Western diplomat in Islamabad

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who shows skill at dealing with other people
examples: You’ll need to be a real diplomat to persuade them to come to some agreement.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with managing relations between countries (= diplomacy)
examples: a diplomatic crisis
Attempts are being made to settle the dispute by diplomatic means.
to break off/establish/restore diplomatic relations with a country

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having or showing skill in dealing with people in difficult situations
examples: SYNONYM tactful
a diplomatic answer
You could try being a little more diplomatic this time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: going in the straightest line between two places without stopping or changing direction
examples: OPPOSITE indirect
the most direct route
This door allows direct access from the kitchen to the garage.
a direct flight (= a flight that does not stop)
There's a direct train to Leeds (= it may stop at other stations but you do not have to change trains).
a direct hit (= a hit that is accurate and does not touch something else first)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: happening or done without involving other people, actions, etc. in between
examples: OPPOSITE indirect
She has been in direct contact with the prime minister.
Clinical depression is thought to have a direct link to brain chemistry.
There is a direct connection between these two phenomena.
He died as a direct result of his employer's actions.
a direct effect/consequence
Many farmers are developing direct access to consumers.
He was cleared of any direct involvement in the case.
Participation in sport brings many benefits, both direct and indirect.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: with nothing between something and the source of the heat or light
examples: The plant should not be placed in direct sunlight.
Grilling involves subjecting the food to direct heat.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: saying exactly what you mean in a way that nobody can pretend not to understand
examples: OPPOSITE indirect
I asked him a direct question: ‘Did you do it?’
He would not give a direct answer.
Her response is refreshingly direct.
Their message is simple and direct: obesity kills.
You'll have to get used to his direct manner.
I prefer a more direct approach.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: clearly showing something
examples: OPPOSITE indirect (1)
There is no direct evidence for the beneficial effects of these herbs.
This information has a direct bearing on (= is closely connected with) the case.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: exact
examples: That's the direct opposite of what you told me yesterday.
a direct quote (= one using a person’s exact words)

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: related through parents and children rather than brothers, sisters, aunts, etc.
examples: OPPOSITE indirect
a direct descendant of the country’s first president
With his death, the direct male line of the House of Capet came to an end.
