definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the general position a person or thing moves or points towards
examples: They headed in the direction of the village.
She pointed in my direction.
They hit a truck coming in the opposite direction.
The road was blocked in both directions.
The aircraft was flying in a northerly direction.
in the right/wrong direction
When the police arrived, the crowd scattered in all directions.
Has the wind changed direction?
I lost all sense of direction (= I didn't know which way to go).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: instructions about how to do something, where to go, etc.
examples: Let's stop and ask for directions.
A farmer gave us directions to the town.
With all pesticides, follow the directions for use carefully.
Simple directions for assembling the model are printed on the box.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the general way in which a person or thing develops
examples: The exhibition provides evidence of several new directions in her work.
I am very unhappy with the direction the club is taking.
He wants to take the company in a different direction.
Do you feel your career is heading/headed in the right direction?
It's only a small improvement, but at least it's a step in the right direction.
The industry will continue to move in the direction of more automation.
Do you think this represents a radical change of direction for the president?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the general position a person or thing comes or develops from
examples: Support came from an unexpected direction.
Let us approach the subject from a different direction.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a purpose; an aim
examples: We are looking for somebody with a clear sense of direction.
Once again her life felt lacking in direction.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the art of managing or guiding somebody/something
examples: She was entrusted with the direction of the project.
All work was produced by the students under the direction of John Williams.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the instructions given by somebody directing a film or play
examples: SEE ALSO stage direction
There is some clever direction and the film is very well shot.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to have different aims that cannot be achieved together without causing problems
examples: There are different considerations, often pulling in different directions.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: without stopping or changing direction
examples: The path leads directly to the river.
He drove her directly to her hotel.
The airline flies directly to Stockholm.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: with nobody or nothing in between
examples: OPPOSITE indirectly
She speaks directly to camera.
She looked directly at us.
We have not been directly affected by the cuts.
directly linked/connected
diseases directly related to smoking
The president was not directly involved.
He was not directly responsible for the accident.
products that are delivered directly to consumers
problems either directly or indirectly caused by human error
Your success in life is not directly proportional to the effort you make.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: exactly in a particular position
examples: directly opposite/below/ahead
They remain directly opposed to these new plans.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: immediately
examples: She left directly after the show.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: soon
examples: SYNONYM shortly
Tell them I'll be there directly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of a group of senior managers who run a company
examples: SEE ALSO executive director
a non-executive director
He's on the board of directors.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person in charge of a film or play who tells the actors and staff what to do
examples: COMPARE producer
a famous film director
He remained active in the theatre as a playwright and director.
the writer and director of the movie ‘Wind River’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is in charge of a particular activity or department in a company, a college, etc.
examples: She was artistic director of the city's photography festival.
He was musical director at the National Theatre.
the deputy/assistant/associate director
the finance/marketing/technical director
the director of marketing/operations/communications
He is assistant director of market research for IDFA.
She recently served as director of the Longwood Arts Project in the Bronx.
the company's regional director in North America
an eminent museum director and curator

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a book or electronic resource containing lists of information, usually in alphabetical order, for example people’s phone numbers or the names and addresses of businesses in a particular area
examples: a telephone/trade directory
a directory of European Trade Associations

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a file containing a group of other files or programs in a computer
examples: SEE ALSO root directory

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a board in an organization or large store listing the names of departments and where to find them
examples: There's a store directory over there.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: any substance that makes something dirty, for example dust, soil or mud
examples: His clothes were covered in dirt.
First remove any grease or dirt from the surface.
The problem with white is that it soon shows the dirt.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: loose earth or soil
examples: He picked up a handful of dirt and threw it at them.
Pack the dirt firmly round the plants.
They lived in a shack with a dirt floor.
I slammed the shovel into the dirt and started to dig.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: unpleasant or harmful information about somebody that could be used to damage their reputation, career, etc.
examples: Do you have any dirt on the new guy?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: solid waste matter from the body
examples: SYNONYM excrement
dog dirt

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to discover and reveal information about somebody that could damage them
examples: They hired private investigators to dig up dirt on their political opponents.
She has come to dig the dirt on her old rival.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to tell people unkind or unpleasant things about somebody, especially about their private life
examples: She loves to dish the dirt on her sisters.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to criticize or say bad things about somebody in public, in a way that is unfair
examples: The paper has dragged his name through the mud.
They feel their agency has been dragged through the mud by the press.
Football's good name is being dragged through the dirt.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to accept bad treatment and being made to feel small or stupid
examples: Her mother ate dirt in poorly-paid jobs just so the family could stay in the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to treat somebody with no respect at all
examples: They treat their workers like dirt.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not clean
examples: dirty hands/clothes/dishes
My thumb had left a dirty mark on the paper.
Try not to get too dirty!
She didn't want to get her dress dirty.
They found him huddled under a dirty old blanket
I always get given the dirty jobs (= jobs that make you become dirty).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with sex in an offensive way
examples: a dirty joke/book
He's got a dirty mind (= he often thinks about sex).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: unpleasant or dishonest
examples: That's a dirty lie!
They discovered her dirty little secret.
She's a dirty player.
He's a great man for doing the dirty jobs (= jobs which are unpleasant because they involve being dishonest or mean to people).
You dirty liar!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not bright
examples: a dirty brown carpet

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: using illegal drugs

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to discuss your personal affairs in public, especially something embarrassing

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: (to do) the unpleasant or dishonest jobs that somebody else does not want to do
examples: Next time you can get somebody else to do your dirty work for you!
He always gets someone else to do the dirty work for him.
The drugs gang used children to do their dirty work for them.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to cheat somebody who trusts you; to treat somebody badly or unfairly
examples: I'd never do the dirty on my friends.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: behaving in an unfair or aggressive way, especially because you want to win
examples: The candidate again got down and dirty with his rival.
The online campaign was getting down and dirty.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: rude and making you feel shocked
examples: The singer got down and dirty at the club last night and made headlines again.
The singers are a down-and-dirty duo from Ohio.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to do physical work
examples: He's not frightened of getting his hands dirty.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to look at somebody in a way that shows you are annoyed with them

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a physical or mental condition that means you cannot use a part of your body completely or easily, or that you cannot learn easily
examples: a physical/mental disability
people with severe learning disabilities

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of not being able to use a part of your body completely or easily; the state of not being able to learn easily
examples: learning to live with disability
He qualifies for help on the grounds of disability.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: unable to use a part of your body completely or easily because of a physical condition, an illness, an injury, etc.; unable to learn easily
examples: physically/mentally disabled
a new home for severely disabled people
He was born disabled.
The museum has special facilities for disabled people.
Does the theatre have disabled access?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: people who are disabled
examples: caring for the sick, elderly and disabled

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to cause problems and tend to stop somebody/something from succeeding or making progress
examples: OPPOSITE advantage
Some pension plans may disadvantage women.
Many people will be greatly disadvantaged by the new tax system.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if two people disagree or one person disagrees with another about something, they have a different opinion about it
examples: Even friends disagree sometimes.
No, I disagree. I don't think it would be the right thing to do.
I must respectfully disagree with my colleague.
Victoria and I obviously disagree on this issue.
He disagreed with his parents on most things.
I'm afraid I disagree with you on that point.
Experts disagree over whether the population will be a burden or a boon in the years ahead.
Jack and Robert disagree about everything.
I strongly disagree with this decision.
to disagree with a statement/view/conclusion/policy
Some people disagree with this argument.
Few would disagree that students learn best when they are interested in the topic.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: if statements or reports disagree, they give different information
examples: The results of the two approaches disagree.
The two reports disagree on the number of people who will be affected by this change.
Clinical diagnoses have frequently been reported to disagree with autopsy results.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if two people agree to differ/disagree, they accept that they have different opinions about something, but they decide not to discuss it any longer
examples: We must just agree to differ on this.
In the end we agreed to disagree.
I think you're wrong. Let's just agree to differ.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a situation where people have different opinions about something and often argue
examples: OPPOSITE agreement
Disagreement arose about exactly how to plan the show.
disagreement on the method to be used
There's no room for disagreement on this point.
There is considerable disagreement over the safety of the treatment.
We are in total disagreement as to how to proceed.
It was a source of disagreement between the two states.
There is disagreement among archaeologists as to the age of the sculpture.
They have had several disagreements with their neighbours.
He shook his head in disagreement.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a difference between two things that should be the same
examples: The comparison shows considerable disagreement between theory and practice.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become impossible to see
examples: SYNONYM vanish
With that, Matt promptly disappeared.
The mirror made the ceiling seem to disappear.
The plane disappeared behind a cloud.
Lisa watched until the train disappeared from view.
Lucy watched his tall figure disappear into the cafe.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop existing
examples: SYNONYM vanish
Her nervousness quickly disappeared once she was on stage.
The problem won't just disappear.
Our countryside is disappearing at an alarming rate.
Wildlife is fast disappearing from our countryside.
These fish have virtually disappeared from their traditional waters.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be lost or impossible to find
examples: SYNONYM vanish
I can never find a pen in this house. They disappear as soon as I buy them.
Then one day he simply disappeared.
A number of his wives mysteriously disappeared.
The child disappeared from his home some time after four.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if a person is disappeared, they are arrested or captured and kept in prison without trial or killed, usually for political reasons
examples: 10 000 people have been disappeared and over 160 000 displaced.
One month later, he was disappeared by the regime.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to remove something secretly or illegally so that it cannot be found
examples: In the last five years, nearly 5 000 companies have been disappeared from the registry.
Soon after the blog post went up, someone disappeared it.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to disappear completely
examples: Keep looking—they can't just have vanished off the face of the earth.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to disappear suddenly in a mysterious way
examples: She can’t just have vanished into thin air.
At a stroke she could make things vanish into thin air.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to go away or be impossible to find when people need or want you
examples: The cat had done a disappearing act.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel sad because something that they hope for or expect to happen does not happen or is not as good as they hoped
examples: Her decision to cancel the concert is bound to disappoint her fans.
I hate to disappoint you, but I'm just not interested.
The movie had disappointed her (= it wasn't as good as she had expected).
I hate to disappoint the children when they've been looking forward to it so much.
His latest novel does not disappoint.
It disappointed me that nobody bothered to say thank you.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to prevent something that somebody hopes for from becoming a reality
examples: The new government had soon disappointed the hopes of many of its supporters.
If he agrees to the deal he will disappoint the expectations of many colleagues.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: upset because something you hoped for has not happened or been as good, successful, etc. as you expected
examples: The singer has promised to refund any disappointed fans.
to be extremely/very/a bit/a little disappointed
They were bitterly disappointed at the result of the game.
Fans of the original film will be sorely disappointed at this remake.
I was disappointed by the quality of the wine.
Andrea was disappointed about the decision.
I'm disappointed about John not coming.
I'm disappointed in you—I really thought I could trust you!
Nick seemed disappointed in her lack of response.
I was very disappointed with myself.
It is hard not to feel disappointed with the end result.
He was disappointed to see she wasn't at the party.
I’m disappointed (that) it was sold out.
She was disappointed not to be chosen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not as good, successful, etc. as you had hoped; making you feel disappointed
examples: a disappointing result/performance/defeat
The team has had a disappointing start to the season.
The outcome of the court case was disappointing for the family involved.
The choices made on election day will always be disappointing to a significant number of voters.
We did a good job but it's still disappointing to only finish second.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the feeling of being sad because something has not happened or been as good, successful, etc. as you expected or hoped
examples: Book early for the show to avoid disappointment.
To our great disappointment, it rained every day of the trip.
He found it difficult to hide his disappointment when she didn't arrive.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is disappointing
examples: a bitter/major disappointment
That new restaurant was a big disappointment.
He's suffered a whole string of disappointments this week.
I always felt I was a disappointment to my father.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an unexpected event, such as a very bad accident, a flood or a fire, that kills a lot of people or causes a lot of damage
examples: SYNONYM catastrophe
the world's worst humanitarian disaster
an environmental/ecological disaster
a rail/mining/tsunami disaster
Thousands died in the disaster.
They provided more than $2.3 billion in disaster relief.
a disaster area/zone
It was taking years for disaster victims to settle and rebuild.
Given the threat of earthquake, we recognized the need for disaster recovery centres.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a very bad situation that causes problems
examples: Losing your job doesn't have to be such a disaster.
Disaster struck when the wheel came off.
Archie has to act quickly to avert disaster.
They could think of no way to avoid the impending disaster.
Many business partnerships end in disaster.
The discovery of the disease among sheep spells financial disaster for farmers.
Letting her organize the party is a recipe for disaster (= something that is likely to go badly wrong).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a complete failure
examples: As a teacher, he's a disaster.
The play's first night was a total disaster.
a complete/total/absolute/unmitigated disaster

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a thing or person that is very likely to cause danger or a problem in the future because of the condition it is in or the way they behave
examples: Any one of these nuclear plants may be a disaster waiting to happen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very bad, harmful or unsuccessful
examples: SYNONYM catastrophic
a disastrous harvest/fire/result
Lowering interest rates could have disastrous consequences for the economy.
It was a disastrous start to the season for the team.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thin flat round object
examples: SEE ALSO tax disc
He wears an identity disc around his neck.
In a total eclipse, the moon completely covers the disc of the sun.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a CD or DVD
examples: SEE ALSO Blu-ray Disc™
This disc contains lots of extra features, including an interview with the director.
This recording is available online or on disc.
The series comes as a two-disc box set with three episodes on each disc.
There are lots of extras on this disc.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a disk for a computer
examples: He inserted the disc into the machine.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a record (= a thin round piece of plastic on which music, etc. is recorded)
examples: SEE ALSO gold disc
I have an old vinyl disc of her singing.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a structure made of cartilage between the bones of the back
examples: SEE ALSO herniated disc

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to get rid of something that you no longer want or need
examples: The room was littered with discarded newspapers.
He had discarded his jacket because of the heat.
She could now discard all thought of promotion.
10 per cent of the data was discarded as unreliable.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to get rid of a card that you do not wantWord Origin
examples: late 16th cent. (originally in the sense ‘reject (a playing card)’): from dis- (expressing removal) + the noun card.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give somebody official permission to leave the police or the armed forces; to make somebody leave the police or the armed forces
examples: He was discharged from the army following his injury.
She was discharged from the police force for bad conduct.
He was found guilty and dishonourably discharged from the army.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to leave hospital because they are well enough to leave
examples: Patients were being discharged from the hospital too early.
All the people involved in the accident have now been discharged from hospital.
She had discharged herself against medical advice.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to leave prison or court
examples: He was conditionally discharged after admitting the theft.
She was formally discharged by the court.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to allow a member of a jury to stop serving in a court case
examples: If the jury cannot agree, it should be discharged.
The judge took the unusual step of discharging the entire jury halfway through the trial.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: when a gas or a liquid discharges or is discharged, or somebody discharges it, it flows somewhere
examples: The river is diverted through the power station before discharging into the sea.
The factory was fined for discharging chemicals into the river.
Raw sewage was discharged from the treatment plant directly into the river.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if part of the body discharges something, a liquid such as pus comes out of it
examples: The wound started discharging pus.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to release force or power
examples: Lightning is caused by clouds discharging electricity.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to do everything that is necessary to perform and complete a particular duty
examples: to discharge your duties/responsibilities/obligations
to discharge a debt (= to pay it)

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to fire a gun, etc.; (of a gun, etc.) to be fired
examples: The police officer accidentally discharged a firearm while unloading it.
They gave a cheer and charged, discharging a volley of arrows as they came.
He knocked her hand down and the gun discharged into the floor.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the practice of training people to obey rules and orders and punishing them if they do not; the controlled behaviour or situation that is the result of this training
examples: OPPOSITE indiscipline
The school has a reputation for high standards of discipline.
Strict discipline is imposed on army recruits.
harsh/rigorous/rigid/iron discipline
She keeps good discipline in class.
to instill/enforce/impose/maintain discipline
Lack of discipline at home meant that many pupils found it difficult to settle in to the ordered environment of the school.
a serious breach of discipline

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a method of training your mind or body or of controlling your behaviour; an area of activity where this is necessary
examples: Yoga is a good discipline for learning to relax.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the ability to control your behaviour or the way you live, work, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO self-discipline
He'll never get anywhere working for himself—he's got no discipline.
Her determination and discipline were admirable.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an area of knowledge; a subject that people study or are taught, especially in a university
examples: The new recruits were drawn from a range of academic disciplines.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give somebody information about something, especially something that was previously secret
examples: SYNONYM reveal
The spokesman refused to disclose details of the takeover to the press.
The report discloses that human error was to blame for the accident.
It was disclosed that two women were being interviewed by the police.
I cannot disclose what we discussed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to allow something that was hidden to be seen
examples: SYNONYM reveal
The door swung open, disclosing a long dark passage.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of making something known or public that was previously secret or private
examples: SYNONYM revelation
the newspaper’s disclosure of defence secrets
The bank will need full disclosure of your financial situation and assets.
The court ruled to prevent public disclosure of the contents of the documents.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: information or a fact that is made known or public that was previously secret or private
examples: SYNONYM revelation
startling disclosures about his private life

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of money that is taken off the usual cost of something
examples: SYNONYM reduction
to get/offer a discount
a 10, 20, 50, etc. per cent discount
Spend over £50 and receive a 15 per cent discount.
Do you qualify for a student discount?
Do you give any discount for students?
If you pay cash you may be able to negotiate a discount.
They're offering a 10% discount on all sofas this month.
You can get a substantial discount off your car insurance.
They were selling everything at a discount (= at reduced prices).
a chance to buy new shares at a discount to the current trading price
We offer special discount rates for families.
a discount voucher/coupon/card
a discount store/retailer (= one that regularly sells goods at reduced prices)
a discount airline/carrier (= an airline that sells cheap tickets)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of money that is taken off the usual cost of something
examples: SYNONYM reduction
to get/offer a discount
a 10, 20, 50, etc. per cent discount
Spend over £50 and receive a 15 per cent discount.
Do you qualify for a student discount?
Do you give any discount for students?
If you pay cash you may be able to negotiate a discount.
They're offering a 10% discount on all sofas this month.
You can get a substantial discount off your car insurance.
They were selling everything at a discount (= at reduced prices).
a chance to buy new shares at a discount to the current trading price
We offer special discount rates for families.
a discount voucher/coupon/card
a discount store/retailer (= one that regularly sells goods at reduced prices)
a discount airline/carrier (= an airline that sells cheap tickets)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to try to prevent something or to prevent somebody from doing something, especially by making it difficult to do or by showing that you do not approve of it
examples: a campaign to discourage smoking among teenagers
I leave a light on when I'm out to discourage burglars.
His parents tried to discourage him from being an actor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel less confident or enthusiastic about doing something
examples: SYNONYM dishearten
Don't be discouraged by the first failure—try again!
The weather discouraged people from attending.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long and serious treatment or discussion of a subject in speech or writing
examples: a discourse on issues of gender and sexuality
He was hoping for some lively political discourse at the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the use of language in speech and writing in order to produce meaning; language that is studied, usually in order to see how the different parts of a text are connected
examples: spoken/written discourse
discourse analysis

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be the first person to become aware that a particular place or thing exists
examples: Cook is credited with discovering Hawaii.
Scientists around the world are working to discover a cure for AIDS.
a newly discovered snake species
They first discovered this protein about five years ago.
She recently discovered two fungi that were new to science.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to find somebody/something that was hidden or that you did not expect to find
examples: Police discovered a large stash of drugs while searching the house.
We discovered this beach while we were sailing around the island.
His body was discovered in the lake near his house.
He was discovered hiding in a shed.
She was discovered dead at her home in Leeds.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to find out about something; to find some information about something
examples: She was determined to discover the truth about her neighbours.
to discover a secret
I've just discovered hang-gliding!
Discover the joys of yoga!
It was a shock to discover (that) he couldn’t read.
We never did discover why she gave up her job.
It was later discovered that the diaries were a fraud.
He was later discovered to be seriously ill.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be the first person to realize that somebody is very good at singing, acting, etc. and help them to become successful and famous
examples: The singer was discovered while still at school.
There's great talent out there just waiting to be discovered.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act or the process of finding somebody/something, or learning about something that was not known about before
examples: Researchers in this field have made some important new discoveries.
New scientific discoveries are being made all the time.
the discovery of antibiotics in the twentieth century
The discovery of a child's body in the river has shocked the community.
the discovery of new talent in the art world
He saw life as a voyage of discovery.
The film takes us on a journey of discovery to different parts of the globe.
She was shocked by the discovery that he had been unfaithful.
In 1974 Hawking made the discovery (= he discovered) that black holes give off radiation.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing, fact or person that is found or learned about for the first time
examples: The drug is not a new discovery—it's been known about for years.
one of the most important scientific discoveries of all time
potentially the biggest archaeological discovery in Norway for fifty years
recent discoveries about sleep

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the freedom or power to decide what should be done in a particular situation
examples: I'll leave it up to you to use your discretion.
How much to tell terminally ill patients is left to the discretion of the doctor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: care in what you say or do, in order to keep something secret or to avoid causing difficulty for somebody or making them feel embarrassed; the quality of being discreet
examples: COMPARE indiscretion
This is confidential, but I know that I can rely on your discretion.
Jane is the soul of discretion (= you can trust her).
Use the utmost discretion when you talk to her.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: according to what somebody decides or wishes to do
examples: Bail is granted at the discretion of the court.
There is no service charge and tipping is at your discretion.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: you should avoid danger and not take unnecessary risksWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in the sense‘ to show good judgement’): via Old French from Latin discretio(n-) ‘separation’ (in late Latin ‘discernment’), from discernere, from dis- ‘apart’ + cernere ‘to separate’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the practice of treating somebody or a particular group in society less fairly than others
examples: SEE ALSO positive discrimination
age/racial/gender/sex discrimination (= because of somebody’s age, race or sex)
discrimination against the elderly
discrimination in favour of the young
They alleged discrimination by the authorities.
to prohibit/outlaw/ban discrimination on the basis of race, gender or sexual orientation
legislation to ban discrimination on the grounds of age

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the ability to judge what is good, true, etc.
examples: SYNONYM discernment
He showed great discrimination in his choice of friends.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the ability to recognize a difference between one thing and another; a difference that is recognized
examples: to learn discrimination between right and wrong
Young children find it difficult to make fine discriminations.
It takes a lot of experience to make such fine discriminations.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to talk about something with somebody, especially in order to decide something
examples: Have you discussed the problem with anyone?
I'm not prepared to discuss this on the phone.
to discuss the issue/matter/topic
to discuss a plan/proposal
They met to discuss the possibility of working together.
We need to discuss when we should go.
We briefly discussed buying a second car.
They discussed the whole family possibly travelling together.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to write or talk about something in detail, showing the different ideas and opinions about it
examples: This topic will be discussed at greater length in the next chapter.
The author discusses the economic impact of these changes.
The article discusses how teachers can use technology in their classrooms.
The novel's main theme is ‘You reap what you sow’. Discuss. (= in an essay question)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a conversation about somebody/something; the process of discussing somebody/something
examples: I discovered something interesting during a family discussion.
We'll continue this discussion some other time.
We had a discussion with them about the differences between Britain and the US.
A lively discussion followed about whether he should be allowed to join the club.
The pair held informal discussions on a number of topics.
The exhibition offers opportunities for frank discussions around sensitive issues.
We want to encourage public discussion of mental health issues.
There was some discussion among reviewers about this film.
The plans have been under discussion (= being talked about) for a year now.
a list of topics for discussion
to stimulate/provoke discussion
to initiate/start/spark a discussion
a panel/group/round-table discussion

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a speech or a piece of writing that discusses many different aspects of a subject
examples: I have chosen to focus my discussion on a single work.
Her article is a discussion of the methods used in research.
See chapter 15 for a detailed discussion of the approach used.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an illness affecting humans, animals or plants, often caused by infection
examples: heart/lung/liver disease
In 19th century England, infectious diseases were the principal cause of death.
chronic diseases such as obesity and diabetes
health measures to prevent the spread of disease
Smoking increases the risk of heart disease.
It is not known what causes the disease.
He suffers from a rare blood disease.
Sailors who ate no fresh food contracted the disease.
It's better to prevent disease by ensuring a clean water supply.
to treat/cure a disease
to spread/transmit a disease
Cattle had to be slaughtered after an outbreak of the disease.
patients with coronary heart disease
cardiovascular/pulmonary/respiratory disease

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that is very wrong with people’s attitudes, way of life or with society
examples: Greed is a disease of modern society.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a flat shallow container for cooking food in or serving it from
examples: SEE ALSO chafing dish
a baking/serving dish
a casserole dish
Bake in a shallow dish for 45 mins.
They helped themselves from a large dish of pasta.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the plates, bowls, cups, etc. that have been used for a meal and need to be washed
examples: I'll do the dishes (= wash them).
My first real job was washing dishes in a restaurant.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: food prepared in a particular way as part of a meal
examples: SEE ALSO side dish
a vegetarian/fish/meat/pasta dish
This makes an excellent hot main dish.
I decided to cook his favourite dish.
to prepare/serve a dish
a savoury dish of curried rice and lamb
I can recommend the chef's dish of the day.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: any object that is like a dish or bowl in shape
examples: SEE ALSO evaporating dish
a soap dish

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a sexually attractive person
examples: What a dish!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not honest; intending to trick people
examples: OPPOSITE honest
Beware of dishonest traders in the tourist areas.
She has been dishonest with voters.
He has been dishonest about his age and academic qualifications.
I don't like him, and it would be dishonest of me to pretend otherwise.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thin flat round object
examples: Red blood cells are roughly the shape of a disk.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a device for storing information on a computer, in the shape of a round flat plate that spins (= turns) to give access to all parts of its magnetic surface, which records information received in electronic form
examples: SEE ALSO hard disk
I'll copy the disk into a file.
The information required can then be retrieved from disk.
I'm running out of disk space on my computer.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to not like somebody/something
examples: OPPOSITE like
Why do you dislike him so much?
She disliked her boss intensely.
There are very few foods that I actively dislike.
I dislike being away from my family.
Much as she disliked going to funerals (= although she did not like it at all), she knew she had to be there.
He disliked her staying away from home.
He disliked it when she behaved badly in front of his mother.
What did you dislike about the movie?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to decide that somebody/something is not important and not worth thinking or talking about
examples: SYNONYM wave something aside/away
to dismiss a suggestion/a claim/an idea
The criticisms were summarily dismissed by the government.
Rob is quick to dismiss the notion that his trip was horrific.
I think we can safely dismiss their objections.
He dismissed the opinion polls as worthless.
His supporters dismissed the allegations as politically motivated.
Vegans are no longer dismissed as cranks.
The suggestion should not be dismissed out of hand (= without thinking about it).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to put thoughts or feelings out of your mind
examples: Dismissing her fears, she climbed higher.
He dismissed her from his mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to officially remove somebody from their job
examples: SYNONYM fire
She claims she was unfairly dismissed from her post.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to send somebody away or allow them to leave
examples: At 12 o'clock the class was dismissed.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to say that a trial or legal case should not continue, usually because there is not enough evidence
examples: The judge dismissed the case for lack of evidence.
to dismiss an appeal/application
The court dismissed all the charges against her.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to end the innings of a player or teamWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from medieval Latin dismiss-, variant of Latin dimiss- ‘sent away’, from the verb dimittere.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of dismissing somebody from their job; an example of this
examples: SEE ALSO constructive dismissal
He still hopes to win his claim against unfair dismissal.
The dismissals followed the resignation of the chairman.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the failure to consider something as important
examples: Her casual dismissal of the threats seemed irresponsible.
Dismissal of the last piece of evidence as unreliable would severely affect our case.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of not allowing a trial or legal case to continue, usually because there is not enough evidence
examples: the dismissal of the appeal

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of sending somebody away or allowing them to leave

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the end of the innings of a player or team

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an illness that causes a part of the body to stop functioning correctly
examples: SEE ALSO attention deficit disorder
a blood/bowel disorder
eating disorders
He was suffering from some form of psychiatric disorder.
This is a rare disorder of the liver.
Most people with acute mental disorder can be treated at home.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an untidy state; a lack of order or organization
examples: OPPOSITE order
The room was in a state of disorder.
His financial affairs were in complete disorder.
Everyone began shouting at once and the meeting broke up in disorder.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: violent behaviour of large groups of people
examples: COMPARE order
an outbreak of rioting and public disorder
Twenty people were arrested after a night of civil disorder.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take the place of somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM replace
Gradually factory workers have been displaced by machines.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to force people to move away from their home to another place
examples: Around 10 000 people have been displaced by the fighting.
If the dam is built it will displace 100 000 people.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move something from its usual position
examples: Check for roof tiles that have been displaced by the wind.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to remove somebody from a job or position
examples: displaced workers

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to take the place of an amount of liquid when put or floating in it, used as a way of measuring size
examples: The ship displaces 58 000 tonnes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to put something in a place where people can see it easily; to show something to people
examples: SYNONYM exhibit
The exhibition gives local artists an opportunity to display their work.
His football trophies were prominently displayed in the kitchen.
She displayed her bruises for all to see.
She proudly displayed her certificate to her parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to show a quality, feeling, skill or type of behaviour; to show signs of something
examples: I have rarely seen her display any sign of emotion.
He displays amazing skill with a golf club.
The supporting cast displays real acting talent.
These statistics display a definite trend.
Many animals in stressful conditions display this behaviour.
From 1811 until his death in 1820, George III displayed symptoms of insanity.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show information
examples: Giant screens displayed images of cheering crowds.
ways of displaying information on screen

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to show a special pattern of behaviour that is intended to attract a female bird or animalWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in the sense ‘unfurl, unfold’): from Old French despleier, from Latin displicare ‘scatter, disperse’ (in medieval Latin ‘unfold’). Compare with deploy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of getting rid of something
examples: SEE ALSO bomb disposal
The council is responsible for waste disposal and street cleaning.
sewage disposal systems
the problems of the ultimate disposal of nuclear waste

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the sale of part of a business, property, etc.
examples: The next step is to think about disposal of your assets.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a machine connected to the waste pipe of a kitchen sink, for cutting food waste into small pieces

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: available for use as you prefer/somebody prefers
examples: He will have a car at his disposal for the whole month.
Well, I'm at your disposal (= I am ready to help you in any way I can).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to arrange things or people in a particular way or position
examples: The visitors disposed themselves in a circle round the statue.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody want to behave in a particular way
examples: a drug that disposes the patient towards sleep
a drug that disposes the patient to sleep

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an argument between two people, groups or countries; discussion about a subject on which people disagree
examples: industrial/pay disputes
a dispute between the two countries about the border
the latest dispute over fishing rights
The union is in dispute with management over working hours.
The cause of the accident was still in dispute (= being argued about).
These are not the issues under dispute.
The matter was settled beyond dispute by the court judgment (= it could no longer be argued about).
His theories are open to dispute (= can be disagreed with).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make it difficult for something to continue in the normal way
examples: Demonstrators succeeded in disrupting the meeting.
Bus services will be disrupted tomorrow because of the bridge closure.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a situation in which it is difficult for something to continue in the normal way; the act of stopping something from continuing in the normal way
examples: We aim to help you move house with minimum disruption to yourself.
disruptions to rail services
The strike caused serious disruptions.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to mix with a liquid and become part of it
examples: Salt dissolves in water.
Heat gently until the sugar dissolves.
The aspirin hasn't dissolved completely yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make a solid become part of a liquid
examples: Dissolve the tablet in water.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to officially end a marriage, business agreement or parliament
examples: Their marriage was dissolved in 1999.
The election was announced and parliament was dissolved.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to disappear; to make something disappear
examples: When the ambulance had gone, the crowd dissolved.
The lights in the windows faded and the house dissolved into darkness again.
His calm response dissolved her anger.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to suddenly start laughing, crying, etc.
examples: When the teacher looked up, the children dissolved into giggles.
Every time she heard his name, she dissolved into tears.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to remove or destroy something, especially by a chemical process; to be destroyed in this way
examples: a new detergent that dissolves stains
All the original calcium had dissolved away.
The limestone has simply dissolved away.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the amount of space between two places or things
examples: SEE ALSO long-distance
a short/long distance
Paul has to drive very long distances as part of his job.
to travel/cover a distance of 200 kilometres
She walked the short distance to her apartment.
Once she was a safe distance from the shop, Gina stopped.
the distance of the earth from the sun
What’s the distance from New York City to Boston?
What’s the distance between New York City and Boston?
The wind carries pollen over considerable distances.
The beach is within walking distance of my house (= you can walk there easily).
The house is within easy commuting distance of town.
In the US, distance is measured in miles.
Our parents live some distance away (= quite far away).
a distance (= long-distance) runner/swimmer

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: being far away in space or in time
examples: SEE ALSO social distance
Distance is no problem on the internet.
These immigrants face problems of geographical distance and cultural isolation.
The car put physical distance between people and their places of work.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a point that is a particular amount of space away from something else
examples: You'll never get the ball in from that distance.
The cat sat and watched us from a safe distance.
Visitors can only view the painting from a distance of three metres.
She followed them at a discreet distance.
A digital camera was positioned at a distance of 1.5 metres from the subject.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a difference or lack of a connection between two things
examples: The distance between fashion and art remains as great as ever.
The government is keen to put some distance between itself and these events (= show that there is no connection between them).
Sociologists must maintain critical distance from the ideas of society at any particular time.
Eddie is, by some distance (= by a great amount), the funniest character in the show.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a situation in which there is a lack of friendly feelings or of a close relationship between two people or groups of people
examples: The coldness and distance in her voice took me by surprise.
There was a growing distance between the two sides of the family.
He worried about the increasing distance between his children and himself.
He felt a sense of distance from the others.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: from a place or time that is not near; from far away
examples: She had loved him at a distance for years.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to continue playing in a competition or sports contest until the end
examples: Nobody thought he would last 15 rounds, but he went the full distance.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: far away but still able to be seen or heard
examples: We saw lights in the distance.
Alice stood staring into the distance.
Five miles of sand stretched away into the distance.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to refuse to be friendly with somebody; to not let somebody be friendly towards you
examples: The manager prefers to keep employees at a distance.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make sure you are not too near somebody/something

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to avoid getting too friendly or involved with a person, group, etc.
examples: She was warned to keep her distance from Charles if she didn't want to get hurt.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: very close
examples: We came within touching distance of winning the cup.
We live within spitting distance of the bus station.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: far away in space or time
examples: the distant sound of music
distant stars/planets
The time we spent together is now a distant memory.
The airport was about 20 kilometres distant.
a star 30 000 light years distant from the Earth
Peace was just a distant hope (= not very likely).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not like something else
examples: SYNONYM remote
Their life seemed utterly distant from his own.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: related to you but not closely
examples: a distant cousin/aunt/relative

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not friendly; not wanting a close relationship with somebody
examples: Pat sounded very cold and distant on the phone.
He became emotionally distant from his friends and family after the illness.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not paying attention to something but thinking about something completely different
examples: There was a distant look in her eyes; her mind was obviously on something else.
He seemed distant and distracted.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a long time ago
examples: stories from the dim and distant past
In the distant past this land was covered in forests.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not a long time in the future but fairly soon
examples: I hope we’ll see each other again in the not too distant future.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: easily or clearly heard, seen, felt, etc.
examples: There was a distinct smell of gas.
His voice was quiet but every word was distinct.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: clearly different or of a different kind
examples: The results of the survey fell into two distinct groups.
Jamaican reggae music is quite distinct from North American jazz or blues.
We are talking about rural areas, as distinct from major cities.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you think an idea or situation definitely exists and is important
examples: SYNONYM definite
Being tall gave Tony a distinct advantage.
I had the distinct impression I was being watched.
A strike is now a distinct possibility.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a clear difference or contrast especially between people or things that are similar or related
examples: distinctions between traditional and modern societies
Philosophers did not use to make a distinction between arts and science.
We need to draw a distinction between the two events.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of separating people or things into different groups
examples: The new law makes no distinction between adults and children (= treats them equally).
All groups are entitled to this money without distinction.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of being something that is special
examples: She had the distinction of being the first woman to fly the Atlantic.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the quality of being excellent or important
examples: a writer of distinction

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a special mark or award that is given to somebody, especially a student, for excellent work
examples: Naomi got a distinction in maths.
He graduated with distinction.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a point that somebody wants to suggest is a difference when in fact it is not different at all
examples: His government did not brand them terrorists, but rather ‘an entity that supports terrorism’. That may prove to be a distinction without a difference.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a quality or characteristic that makes something different and easily noticed
examples: SYNONYM characteristic
clothes with a distinctive style
The male bird has distinctive white markings on its head.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to recognize the difference between two people or things
examples: SYNONYM differentiate
At what age are children able to distinguish between right and wrong?
English law clearly distinguishes between murder and manslaughter.
It was hard to distinguish one twin from the other.
Sometimes reality and fantasy are hard to distinguish.
We can distinguish five meanings of the word ‘mad’.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be a characteristic that makes two people, animals or things different
examples: What was it that distinguished her from her classmates?
The male bird is distinguished from the female by its red beak.
The adult bird can be readily distinguished by its orange bill.
Does your cat have any distinguishing marks?
The power of speech distinguishes human beings from animals.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be able to see or hear something
examples: SYNONYM differentiate
I could not distinguish her words, but she sounded agitated.
She could not distinguish the make and colour of the car in the fading light.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to do something so well that people notice and admire you
examples: She has already distinguished herself as an athlete.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to change the shape, appearance or sound of something so that it is strange or not clear
examples: a fairground mirror that distorts your shape
The loudspeaker seemed to distort his voice.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to change facts, ideas, etc. so that they are no longer correct or true
examples: Newspapers are often guilty of distorting the truth.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take somebody’s attention away from what they are trying to do
examples: SYNONYM divert
You're distracting me from my work.
Don't talk to her—she's very easily distracted.
It was another attempt to distract attention from the truth.
He’s easily distracted from his work
an attempt to distract attention away from the real problems in the country

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a feeling of great worry or unhappiness; great mental pain
examples: The newspaper article caused the actor considerable distress.
She sensed his deep emotional distress.
She was obviously in distress after the attack.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: severe problems caused by not having enough money, food, etc.
examples: SYNONYM hardship
economic/financial distress
The charity aims to relieve poverty and distress caused by natural disasters.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a situation in which a ship, plane, etc. is in danger or difficulty and needs help
examples: a distress signal (= a message asking for help)
It is a rule of the sea to help another boat in distress.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a state of physical pain and effort, especially difficulty in breathing
examples: The patient was suffering serious respiratory distress.
The baby was clearly in distress.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a woman who needs helpWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French destresce (noun), destrecier (verb), based on Latin distringere ‘stretch apart’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give things to a large number of people; to share something between a number of people
examples: The leaflets have been widely distributed.
The newspaper is distributed free.
to distribute fliers/pamphlets/questionnaires
Viruses are often distributed via email.
The organization distributed food to the earthquake victims.
The money was distributed among schools in the area.
The proceeds will be distributed between local charities.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to send goods to shops and businesses so that they can be sold
examples: Who distributes our products in the UK?
Their trademark jeans enjoyed immediate success and were soon distributed worldwide.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to spread something, or different parts of something, over an area
examples: Make sure your weight is evenly distributed.
Cases of the disease are widely distributed through Europe.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the way that something is spread or exists over a particular area or among a particular group of people
examples: SEE ALSO normal distribution
They studied the geographical distribution of the disease.
a more equitable distribution of wealth
an unequal/uneven income distribution
the age distribution of the general population
The map shows the distribution of this species across the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of giving or sharing something out among a number of people
examples: the distribution of food and medicines
the distribution of profit among the partners
When are distributions likely to be made to creditors?
The food was packed up for distribution to outlying communities.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the system of transporting and delivering a product
examples: They have systems in place for marketing, sales and distribution.
We focused on finding new distribution channels for our products.
The company's distribution network includes more than 1  200 retail outlets.
production and distribution systems
a distribution centre/depot/warehouse

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an area of a country or town, especially one that has particular features
examples: SEE ALSO red-light district
the City of London’s financial district
Every city has its central business district.
The house is in a historic district.
Milan's most fashionable shopping district
a poor district of the city
rural/urban districts

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one of the areas that a country, town or state is divided into for purposes of organization, with official boundaries (= borders)
examples: SEE ALSO congressional district
a tax/postal district
a village in the Darjeeling district
a district judge
the district health authority

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to interrupt somebody when they are trying to work, sleep, etc.
examples: I'm sorry to disturb you, but can I talk to you for a moment?
If you get up early, try not to disturb everyone else.
Do not disturb (= a sign placed on the outside of the door of a hotel room, office, etc.)
She awoke early after a disturbed night.
Only the cry of seabirds disturbed the silence.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody worry
examples: The letter shocked and disturbed me.
It disturbed her to realize that she was alone.
It disturbed her to realize that she was missing him already.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move something or change its position
examples: Don't disturb the papers on my desk.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make something function differently from normal
examples: During a magnetic storm, the earth's magnetic field is disturbed.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: making you feel anxious and upset or shocked
examples: a disturbing piece of news
a profoundly disturbing experience

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to jump into water with your head and arms going in first
examples: We dived into the river to cool off.
He dived off the bridge.
Sam walked to the deep end of the pool and dived in.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to swim underwater wearing breathing equipment, collecting or looking at things
examples: SEE ALSO diving
to dive for pearls
The main purpose of his holiday to Greece was to go diving.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to go to a deeper level underwater
examples: The submarine dived to avoid being seen.
The whale dived as the harpoon struck it.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to go steeply down through the air
examples: SEE ALSO nosedive
The seagulls soared then dived.
The plane dived down to attack.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to move or jump quickly in a particular direction, especially to avoid something, to try to catch a ball, etc.
examples: We heard an explosion and dived for cover (= got into a place where we would be protected).
The goalie dived for the ball, but missed it.
It started to rain so we dived into the nearest cafe.
He dived headlong into the ditch.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to fall deliberately when somebody tackles you

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to fall suddenly
examples: SYNONYM plunge
The share price dived from 75p to an all-time low of 50p.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very different from each other and of various kinds
examples: People from diverse cultures were invited to the event.
My interests are very diverse.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a range of many people or things that are very different from each other
examples: SYNONYM variety
the biological diversity of the rainforests
a great/wide/rich diversity of opinion

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the quality or fact of including a range of many people or things
examples: There is a need for greater diversity and choice in education.
The company is working to improve its profile in terms of diversity and inclusion (= offering equal opportunities to people from minority groups).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something change direction
examples: The course of the stream has now been diverted.
Northbound traffic will have to be diverted onto minor roads.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to use money, materials, etc. for a different purpose from their original purpose
examples: More of the budget was diverted into promotions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to take somebody’s thoughts or attention away from something
examples: SYNONYM distract
The war diverted people's attention away from the economic situation.
She managed to divert the baby onto a different activity.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to entertain people
examples: Children are easily diverted.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to separate into parts; to make something separate into parts
examples: SYNONYM split up
The cells began to divide rapidly.
The questions divide into two categories: easy and hard.
After lunch we divided up for group discussions.
I divided the class into four groups.
Divide the dough into four pieces.
The book is divided into 11 sections.
A sentence can be divided up into meaningful segments.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to separate something into parts and give a share to each of a number of different people, etc.
examples: SYNONYM share (3)
They could not agree on how to divide the land.
Jack divided up the rest of the cash.
We divided the work between us.
Profits were divided up among the staff.
The money was divided equally among his sons.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to use different parts of your time, energy, etc. for different activities, etc.
examples: As working parents we think carefully about how we divide our time.
He divides his energies between politics and business.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to separate into two or more parts that lead in different directions
examples: Where the path divides, keep right.
The river divides into several channels.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to separate two people or things
examples: Can it ever be right to divide a mother from her child?
The landowners were divided from the mass of poor peasants who lived in the surrounding area.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be the real or imaginary line or barrier that separates two people or things
examples: SYNONYM separate
A fence divides off the western side of the grounds.
The English Channel divides England from France.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to find out how many times one number is contained in another
examples: 30 divided by 6 is 5 (= 30 ÷ 6 = 5).
It's easy to divide by ten.
The children are learning how to multiply and divide.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be able to be multiplied to give another number
examples: 5 divides into 30 6 times.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to make people disagree
examples: SYNONYM split
to divide the nation/country
This issue has bitterly divided the community.
The building divides opinion (= some people like it and some do not).
The party is deeply divided on this question.
to be evenly/sharply divided over the issue

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to disagree
examples: Communities frequently divided along racial lines.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to keep control over people by making them disagree with and fight each other, therefore not giving them the chance to join together and oppose you
examples: a policy of divide and rule

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to divide something into two equal parts; to divide into two equal parts
examples: The country was split down the middle over the strike (= half supported it, half did not).
Divide the cake down the middle.
It would seem the community has divided down the middle, with some favouring expansion and some dead set against it.

examples: The journey takes about an hour door to door.
a door-to-door salesman

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: at an early stage, especially in a game or competition
examples: Suddenly we lost three home matches early doors.
The team had the game in the bag early doors after tries from Ellis and Wilkins.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to manage to enter an organization, a field of business, etc. that could bring you success
examples: I always wanted to work in TV but it took me two years to get a foot in the door.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to have enough money to avoid going hungry; to stop somebody feeling hungry

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to say that somebody is responsible for something that has gone wrong
examples: The blame for the disaster has been laid firmly at the government’s door.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to make sure that there is still the possibility of doing something
examples: We have left the door open for further talks.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody never to come to your home again
examples: Go! And never darken my door again!

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to provide opportunities for somebody to do something and be successful

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: not inside a building
examples: You should spend more time out of doors in the fresh air.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to ask somebody to leave, because they are no longer welcome

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to shut a door hard when somebody is trying to come in

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to refuse to talk to somebody or meet them, in a rude way

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: directly to somebody’s house
examples: We promise to deliver to your door within 48 hours of you ordering.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of a medicine or a drug that is taken once, or regularly over a period of time
examples: a high/low/lethal dose
Repeat the dose after 12 hours if necessary.
Take a single dose at bedtime to help you sleep.
I always take my daily dose of vitamin C.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an amount of something
examples: A dose of flu kept me off work.
Workers at the nuclear plant were exposed to high doses of radiation.
I can cope with her in small doses (= for short amounts of time).
The film also contains a hefty dose of comedy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very fast and easily
examples: He got through the housework like a dose of salts.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the same bad treatment that you have given to others
examples: Let the bully have a taste of his own medicine.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small round mark, especially one that is printed
examples: SEE ALSO polka dot
There are dots above the letters i and j.
Text and graphics are printed at 300 dots per inch.
The helicopters appeared as two black dots on the horizon.
The island is a small green dot on the map.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a symbol like a full stop used to separate parts of a domain name, a URL or an email address

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the shorter of the two signals that are used in Morse code
examples: COMPARE dash (5)
Telegrams were sent using the complex dots and dashes of Morse code.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a small round mark that appears after a musical note to show that it should last for an extra half of its usual length, or above a musical note to show that it should be played staccato
examples: A dot after a note lengthens its duration by half.
The dot above some notes means they are to be played staccato, the opposite of legato.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: exactly on time or at the exact time mentioned
examples: The taxi showed up on the dot.
Breakfast is served at 8 on the dot.
Please tell him I’ll call him on the dot of twelve.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a very long time ago
examples: I've been going there every summer since the year dot.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: twice as much or as many as usual
examples: a double helping
two double whiskies
a double espresso
a double lesson of English

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having or made of two things or parts that are equal or similar
examples: double doors
a double-page advertisement
‘Otter’ is spelt with a double t.

a high-profile double murder case

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: COMPARE single
a double bed/room
a double garage

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: combining two things or qualities
examples: a double meaning/purpose/aim
It has the double advantage of being both easy and cheap.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to perform two roles or functions at the same time
examples: This device can pull double duty as a decent laptop and an adequate tablet.
She deserves credit for serving double duty as a host and performer.
