definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a feeling of being uncertain about something or not believing something
examples: SEE ALSO self-doubt
a feeling of doubt and uncertainty
New evidence has cast doubt on the guilt of the man jailed for the crime.
He was starting to have some serious doubts.
to have lingering/grave/nagging doubts
The article raised doubts about how effective the new drug really was.
There is some doubt about the best way to do it.
There is no doubt at all that we did the right thing.
There's little doubt in my mind that he's going to go right to the top.
She leaves no doubt as to her own view of Picasso's work.
If you are in any doubt as to whether you should be doing these exercises, consult your doctor.
Medical experts have expressed doubt over how the scientist died.
She knew without a shadow of a doubt that he was lying to her.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be uncertain
examples: The success of the system is not in doubt.
The arrangements for the event still seemed to be in doubt.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a way that shows that something is completely certain
examples: The research showed beyond doubt that smoking contributes to heart disease.
The prosecution was able to establish beyond reasonable doubt that the woman had been lying.
The evidence proves beyond doubt that he is innocent.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to accept that somebody has told the truth or behaved well because you cannot prove that they have not
examples: She may have been lying, but I felt I had to give her the benefit of the doubt.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have reasons why you are not certain about whether something is good or whether something good will happen
examples: I've had my doubts about his work since he joined the firm.
It may be all right. Personally, I have my doubts.
They say they'll be here on time, but I have my doubts about that.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to give advice to somebody who cannot decide what to do
examples: If in doubt, wear black.
If in doubt, consult your doctor.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used when you are saying that something is likely
examples: No doubt she'll call us when she gets there.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when you are saying that something is certainly true
examples: He's made some great movies. There's no doubt about it.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to make something uncertain
examples: The proposed development has been thrown into doubt by the decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used when you are giving your opinion and emphasizing the point that you are making
examples: This meeting has been, without doubt, one of the most useful we have had so far.
Without the slightest doubt this is a remarkable exhibition.
She is without a doubt the best player I know.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to or at a lower place or position
examples: She jumped down off the chair.
He looked down at her.
We watched as the sun went down.
She bent down to pick up her glove.
Mary's not down yet (= she is still upstairs).
The baby can't keep any food down (= in her body).
I stuck the label down with sellotape.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: from a standing position to a sitting or lying position
examples: Please sit down.
He had to go and lie down for a while.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: at a lower level or rate
examples: Prices have gone down recently.
We're already two goals down (= the other team has two goals more).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that the amount or strength of something is lower, or that there is less activity
examples: Turn the music down!
The class settled down and she began the lesson.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: on paper; on a list
examples: Did you get that down?
I always write everything down.
Have you got me down for the trip?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: reading from top to bottom, not from side to side
examples: I can't do 3 down.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to or in the south of a country
examples: They flew down to Texas.
Houses are more expensive down south.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: from an important or famous place, especially a large city, to a smaller or less famous place
examples: We've got people from the head office coming down.
Her daughter's down from Oxford (= Oxford University) for the holidays.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to show the limits in a range or an order
examples: Everyone will be there, from the Principal down.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: having lost the amount of money mentioned
examples: At the end of the day we were £20 down.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: if you pay an amount of money down, you pay that to start with, and the rest later

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say how far you have got in a list of things you have to do
examples: Well, I've seen six apartments so far. That's six down and four to go!

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to or at a local place such as a shop, pub, etc.
examples: I'm just going down to the post office.
I saw him down at the shops.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to tell an animal or person to sit or lie
examples: ‘Down, boy!’ she laughed as the dog jumped up to greet her.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be the responsibility of somebody
examples: It's down to you to check the door.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be caused by a particular person or thing
examples: She claimed her problems were down to the media.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to have only a little money left
examples: I'm down to my last dollar.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to have or catch an illness

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: behaving in an unfair or aggressive way, especially because you want to win
examples: The candidate again got down and dirty with his rival.
The online campaign was getting down and dirty.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: rude and making you feel shocked
examples: The singer got down and dirty at the club last night and made headlines again.
The singers are a down-and-dirty duo from Ohio.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: during a long period of time
examples: Down through the years this town has seen many changes.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: including every small part or detail of something
examples: She organized everything down to the last detail.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to or in Australia and/or New Zealand

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used to say that you are opposed to something, or to a person
examples: The crowds chanted ‘Down with NATO!’

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to be able to do something easily or well
examples: She's young and she hasn't really got it down yet.
The teacher gave us the music to the song and we had two weeks to get it down.
It looked easy once you got the system down.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

I dragged the chair over to the window.
They dragged her from her bed.
He quickly dragged a comb through his hair.
She managed to drag him clear of the wreckage.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take hold of something and pull it
examples: Desperately, Jinny dragged at his arm.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move yourself slowly and with effort
examples: I managed to drag myself out of bed.
She always drags behind when we walk anywhere.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to persuade somebody to come or go somewhere they do not really want to come or go to
examples: I'm sorry to drag you all this way in the heat.

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: They dragged the canal for the murder weapon.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: Click on the file and drag it across.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: RELATED NOUN foot-dragging

definitions.label: Meaning 10

Football's good name is being dragged through the dirt.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: He flung out his arms in a dramatic gesture.

Must you be so dramatic about everything?

examples: Prices have fallen dramatically.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a way that is exciting and impressive
examples: The mountains rose dramatically behind them.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a way that is connected with the theatre or plays
examples: The opera does not compare musically or dramatically with the composer's best work.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: ‘At last!’ she cried dramatically.

definitions.definition: to express a comparison or a contrast; to define the limits of something
examples: to draw a comparison/a parallel/an analogy/a distinction between two events
He attempted to draw a contrast between himself and the prime minister.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to produce a reaction or response
examples: The plan has drawn a lot of criticism.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: Our aim is to draw attention to the plight of these children.

Her gaze was drawn irresistibly to the scene outside.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: The movie is drawing large audiences.

The course draws students from all over the country.
Her screams drew passers-by to the scene.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: The train drew into the station.
The train drew in.

Their car drew alongside ours.

examples: She drew a revolver on me.
He came towards them with his sword drawn.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to make somebody say more about something
examples: Spielberg refused to be drawn on his next movie.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to decide something by picking cards, tickets or numbers by chance
examples: SEE ALSO draw/cast lots (for something/to do something)

He drew the winning ticket.
Names were drawn from a hat for the last few places.
Italy has been drawn against Spain in the first round.
Italy has been drawn to play Spain.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to finish a game without either team winning
examples: England and France drew.

definitions.label: Meaning 16

examples: to draw water from a well

definitions.label: Meaning 18

examples: He drew thoughtfully on his pipe.

examples: One of the police officers drew a bead on the gunman and fired.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to get no response or result
examples: So far, the police investigation has drawn a blank.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to make somebody bleed

examples: She talks all the time and hardly stops to draw breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to live; to be alive
examples: He was as kind a man as ever drew breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to make somebody direct their anger, criticism, etc. at you, so that others do not have to face it

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to start being more careful in your behaviour, especially by spending less money than before
examples: Small businesses have had to pull their horns in during the recession.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to refuse to do something; to set a limit
examples: I don't mind helping, but I draw the line at doing everything myself.
We would have liked to invite all our relatives, but you have to draw the line somewhere.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to make a difference between two closely related ideas
examples: Where do you draw the line between genius and madness?

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to say that something is finished and not worth discussing any more

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to use a method of choosing somebody/something that involves putting a number folded pieces of paper in a bag, one of them with a mark on it. People then take it in turns to take a piece of paper from the bag and the one who takes the paper with the mark on it is chosen.
examples: They drew lots for the right to go first.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to be the person in a group who is chosen or forced to perform an unpleasant duty or task
examples: I drew the short straw and had to clean the toilets.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to use a method of choosing somebody to do or have something in which each person takes a piece of paper, etc. from a container and the one whose paper has a special mark is chosen
examples: We drew straws for who went first.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to stand straight and tall in order to show that you are determined, powerful or important
examples: He drew himself up to his full height and glared at us.

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: (to establish) a clear limit to what you will do or accept
examples: It’s time to draw a line in the sand and stop allowing workplace bullying to continue.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to speak to somebody in private, especially in order to warn or tell them about somethingWord Origin
examples: Old English dragan, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch dragen and German tragen, also to draught.

She teaches drawing at the women's prison in Philadelphia.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a series of images, events and feelings that happen in your mind while you are asleep
examples: COMPARE nightmare
I had a really weird dream last night.
I thought someone came into the bedroom, but it was just a dream.
‘Goodnight. Sweet dreams.’
Don't think about it. You'll only give yourself bad dreams.
a vivid dream about my old school.
a recurrent dream about being late for an exam
I had a dream that we were getting married at the airport.
His dead mother appeared to him in a dream.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a wish to have or be something, especially one that seems difficult to achieve
examples: SEE ALSO pipe dream
Her lifelong dream was to be a famous writer.
He wanted to be rich but it was an impossible dream.
a chance to fulfil a childhood dream
to realize/achieve a dream
If I win, it will be a dream come true.
It was the end of all my hopes and dreams.
The chance to study in Australia had always been a dream for her.

I've finally found the man of my dreams.
Being a TV presenter would be my dream job.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a state of mind or a situation in which things do not seem real or part of normal life
examples: SEE ALSO daydream
She walked around in a dream all day.
She found herself standing in front of the crowded hall and making her speech, as if in a dream.
As if slowly emerging from a dream, she raised her head.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a beautiful or wonderful person or thing
examples: That meal was an absolute dream.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: far more, better, etc. than you could ever have imagined or hoped for

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to work very well
examples: My new car goes like a dream.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to happen without problems, in the way that you had planned
examples: The wedding celebrations went like a dream.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that something they are hoping for is not likely to happen
examples: ‘I'll be a manager before I'm 30.’ ‘In your dreams.’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: so unpleasant that you cannot believe it is true
examples: In broad daylight the events of the night before seemed like a bad dream.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to have a way of life that seems perfect
examples: With her own TV show and a flat in Paris, she is living the dream.

Dragging kids through airports is enough to drive you to drink.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: something that somebody enjoys very much
examples: This degree of chaos is meat and drink to Guy.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: something that is a normal thing to deal with for somebody
examples: This kind of research task is meat and drink to these students.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to operate a vehicle so that it goes in a particular direction
examples: SEE ALSO fly-drive
Can you drive?
Don't drive so fast!
I drove to work this morning.
Shall we drive (= go there by car) or go by train?
to drive a car/vehicle/truck/bus
He drives a taxi (= that is his job).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take somebody somewhere in a car, taxi, etc.
examples: Could you drive me home?
My mother drove us to the airport.
They were driven to an unknown place in the hills.
I don't want to take the bus. Will you drive me?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to travel under the control of a driver
examples: A stream of black cars drove by.
A car drove up to us and a man got out.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to own or use a particular type of vehicle
examples: What car do you drive?
You need a special licence to drive a heavy goods vehicle.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody very angry, crazy, etc. or to make them do something extreme
examples: to drive somebody crazy/mad/nuts/insane
Hunger drove her to steal.
Those kids are driving me to despair.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to force somebody to act in a particular way
examples: The urge to survive drove them on.
You're driving yourself too hard.
He was driven by the desire to understand how things work.
The work is driven by the need for information sharing.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to provide the power that makes a machine work; to operate a device
examples: a steam-driven locomotive
The interface can be used to drive a printer.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to force somebody/something to move in a particular direction
examples: to drive sheep into a field
The enemy was driven back.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to influence something or cause it to make progress
examples: This is the main factor driving investment in the area.
A key factor driving growth was the launch of convenient products.
The dairy products market will also be driven by consumer demand.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to force something to go in a particular direction or into a particular position by pushing it, hitting it, etc.
examples: to drive a nail into a piece of wood

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make an opening in or through something by using force
examples: They drove a tunnel through the solid rock.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to hit a ball with force, sending it forward
examples: to drive the ball into the rough (= in golf)

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to carry something along
examples: Huge waves drove the yacht onto the rocks.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to fall or move rapidly and with great force
examples: The waves drove against the shore.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: extremely clean, pure, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to cause something to fail, for example a plan

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to argue in an aggressive way and force somebody to agree on the best possible price or arrangement

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to make somebody understand or accept something by saying it often, loudly, angrily, etc.
examples: You will really need to drive your point home.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to make somebody so worried, annoyed or upset that they lose control of their behaviour, especially by drinking too much alcohol
examples: The stress drove her to drink and put a strain on her marriage.
Dragging kids through airports is enough to drive you to drink.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to make two people start disliking each other
examples: I don't want to drive a wedge between the two of you.
This was just one of the issues that drove a wedge between them.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to work so hard that you become extremely tired

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: the thing somebody is trying to say
examples: I wish I knew what they were driving at.

definitions.definition: a person who drives a vehicle
examples: SEE ALSO back-seat driver
a bus/train/taxi driver
a car/van driver
an ambulance driver
a good/careful driver
She climbed into the driver's seat.
The accident was the other driver's fault.
Police have warned drivers to take care in the icy conditions.
a learner driver (= one who has not yet passed a driving test)
a student driver
a lorry driver
a truck driver
What he wanted most was to be a racing driver.
The car comes equipped with a driver's airbag.
The driver of the other car walked away from the crash with minor cuts and bruises.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a club with a large head, used for hitting the ball long distances from the tee

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: software that controls the sending of data between a computer and a piece of equipment that is attached to it, such as a printer
examples: I downloaded and installed the drivers.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: one of the main things that influence something or cause it to make progress
examples: Housing is a key driver of the economy.
Young people are widely perceived as the big pop industry drivers.

examples: SEE ALSO drink-driving

careless/reckless driving
a driving lesson/instructor

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to allow something to fall by accident; to fall by accident
examples: Be careful not to drop that plate.
I accidentally dropped my glasses into the water.
The climber slipped and dropped to his death.
His arms dropped limply to his sides.
Her mouth dropped open in disbelief.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something fall deliberately; to let yourself fall
examples: You can never be sure whether the planes will be dropping bombs or food parcels.
Medical supplies are being dropped into the stricken area.
She lifted the bag then dropped it down again.
He dropped his trousers (= undid them and let them fall).
He dropped his pants.
Catch me when I drop.
I dropped to my knees beside her.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to fall down or be no longer able to stand because you are extremely tired
examples: I feel ready to drop.
She expects everyone to work till they drop.
He staggered in and dropped into a chair.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to become or make something weaker, lower or less
examples: SYNONYM fall
The temperature has dropped considerably.
At last the wind dropped.
Error rates have dropped dramatically.
His voice dropped to a whisper.
The Dutch team have dropped to fifth place.
The price of shares dropped by 14p.
Shares dropped in price by 14p.
The dollar dropped sharply against the euro.
You must drop your speed in built-up areas.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to fail to win something
examples: It's a long time since we dropped a game.
They didn't drop any points until halfway through the season.
She dropped the second set but came back to win the match.
He dropped his serve (= failed to win games in which it was his turn to hit the ball first) twice in the first set.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to look down
examples: Her eyes dropped to her lap.
She smiled and let her eyes drop again.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to slope steeply downwards
examples: In front of them the valley dropped sharply away from the road.
The land dropped steeply away into a small valley.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to stop so that somebody can get out of a car, etc.; to deliver or leave something in a particular place, especially on the way to somewhere else
examples: RELATED NOUN drop-off (2)
Can you drop me near the bank?
You left your jacket, but I can drop it off on my way to work tomorrow.
Just drop it in the mail when you have time.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to send a short letter or email to somebody
examples: Drop me a line when you get there.
Don't hesitate to drop me an email or give me a call.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to put some text, an icon, etc. into a file, folder or place on a computer screen, using the mouse
examples: You can easily drag and drop files onto your memory stick.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to leave somebody/something out by accident or deliberately
examples: She's been dropped from the team because of injury.
He spoke with a cockney accent and dropped his aitches (= did not pronounce the letter ‘h’ at the start of words).
She was unceremoniously dropped by her record label.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to stop seeing somebody socially
examples: She's dropped most of her old friends.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to stop doing or discussing something; to not continue with something
examples: I dropped German (= stopped studying it) when I was 14.
Drop everything and come at once!
Look, can we just drop it (= stop talking about it)?
I think we'd better drop the subject.
The police decided to drop the charges against her.
Let's drop the formalities—please call me Mike.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to say or do something in order to show somebody, in an indirect way, what you are thinking
examples: SEE ALSO name-drop

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to let a stitch go off the needle

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: people stop buying or using the products of a particular industry
examples: The bottom has fallen out of the travel market.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to die or become ill and fall down in very large numbers
examples: People were dropping like flies in the intense heat.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to tell the police or people in authority that somebody has done something wrong
examples: If he finds out who dropped the dime on him, they're in trouble.
I'm worried if I drop a dime on this guy, he'll get fired, which I don't think he really deserves.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to make a mistake and cause something that you are responsible for to fail
examples: Let’s not drop the ball on this.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to say something that offends or embarrasses somebody, although you did not intend to

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to suddenly not be able to think clearly; to act in a stupid way because you have lost control over yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to die suddenly and unexpectedly

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody, rudely, to stop annoying you, interfering, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO drop-dead

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to stop being careful and preparing yourself for possible danger or difficulty
examples: You can never drop your guard with a two-year-old.
Even when he's winning, he never drops his guard.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to put somebody in an embarrassing situation, especially by telling a secret that you should not have told

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to make something the responsibility of another person
examples: They dropped the problem firmly back in my lap.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to mention famous people you know or have met in order to impress others
examples: RELATED NOUN name-dropping
She found him rather irritating to talk to; all he did was drop names.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: somebody has the opportunity to do something pleasant without having made any effort
examples: My dream job just fell into my lap.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody suddenly looked surprised, shocked or disappointed

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to do or say nothing more about somebody/something
examples: I suggest we let the matter drop.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to mention somebody/something in a conversation, by accident or as if by accident
examples: He let it drop that the prime minister was a close friend of his.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody has finally understood or realized something that they had not understood or realized before
examples: I had to explain the joke to her a couple of times before the penny dropped.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: it was extremely quiet
examples: The audience was so quiet you could have heard a pin drop.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long period of time when there is little or no rain
examples: Farmers are facing ruin after two years of severe drought.
one of the worst droughts on record
The country’s entire grain harvest has been hit by drought.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a long period of time when there is a lack of something that is needed or wanted
examples: The team is desperate to end a ten-game goal drought.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to die because you have been underwater too long and you cannot breathe; to kill somebody by holding them underwater
examples: Two children drowned after falling into the river.
He had attempted to rescue the drowning man.
She tried to drown herself.
They had drowned the unwanted kittens.
He was drowned at sea.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something very wet; to completely cover something in water or another liquid
examples: SYNONYM drench
The fruit was drowned in cream.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be louder than other sounds so that you cannot hear them
examples: She turned up the radio to drown out the noise from next door.
His words were drowned out by jeers and whistling.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to get drunk in order to forget your problems
examples: She opened a bottle of wine to drown her sorrows.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an illegal substance that some people smoke, inject, etc. for the physical and mental effects it has
examples: SEE ALSO class A drug
He does not smoke or take drugs.
to use/abuse drugs
I don't do drugs (= use them).
to smuggle/supply/sell drugs
He was charged with possessing drugs.
illegal/illicit drugs
She looked like she was on drugs (= had taken drugs).
I found out he was on drugs (= took them regularly).
a drug dealer/trafficker/smuggler
drug use/abuse
She was a drug addict.
The actor struggled with drug addiction.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a substance used as a medicine or used in a medicine
examples: SEE ALSO designer drug
to prescribe/administer a drug
a prescription drug (= one that must be prescribed by a doctor)
anti-inflammatory/antiviral/painkilling drugs
a new cancer drug
a major drug company
He's taking drugs for depression.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a musical instrument made of a hollow round frame with plastic or skin stretched tightly across one or both ends. You play it by hitting it with sticks or with your hands.
examples: SEE ALSO bass drum
to play the drum
I used to play drums in a band.
Tony Cox on drums
a slow drum beat
There was a great crash and then a long roll of drums.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a large container for oil or chemicals that is like a cylinder in shape
examples: a 50 gallon drum
an oil drum
Hazardous waste is stored in drums until it can be disposed of.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing that is like a drum in shape, especially part of a machine
examples: The mixture flows to a revolving drum where the water is filtered out.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to speak with enthusiasm in support of somebody/something
examples: She’s really banging the drum for the new system.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to behave in a different way from other people; to have different attitudes or ideas
examples: She was a gifted and original artist who marched to a different drummer.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having drunk so much alcohol that it is impossible to think or speak clearly
examples: OPPOSITE sober
She was too drunk to remember anything about the party.
His only way of dealing with his problems was to go out and get drunk.
They got drunk on vodka.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very excited, tired, etc. because of a particular emotion or situation
examples: SEE ALSO punch-drunk
drunk with success
She was almost drunk with all these new impressions.
drunk with fatigue

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: extremely drunk
examples: He came home blind drunk, as usual.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: behaving in a noisy or violent way in a public place because you are drunk
examples: Police arrested him for being drunk and disorderly.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: very drunk

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: extremely drunk and noisy
examples: He rolled home roaring drunk at 3 o’clock in the morning.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not wet or sticky; without water or moisture
examples: SEE ALSO bone dry
Is my shirt dry yet?
Store onions in a cool dry place.
I'm afraid this cake has turned out very dry.
Some plants grow better in dry soil.
When the paint is completely dry, apply another coat.
We managed to stay dry by huddling in a doorway.
Her mouth felt as dry as a bone (= completely dry).
It was high summer and the rivers were dry (= had no water in them).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: with very little rain
examples: weeks of hot, dry weather
the dry season
I hope it stays dry for our picnic.
There is every prospect of the weather remaining dry this week.
Rattlesnakes occur in the warmer, drier parts of North America.
The day will start bright and mainly dry.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: without the natural oils that makes it soft and healthy
examples: a shampoo for dry hair

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: that does not produce any phlegm (= the thick liquid that forms in the nose and throat)
examples: a dry hacking cough

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: eaten on its own without any butter, jam, etc.
examples: Breakfast consisted of dry bread and a cup of tea.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not sweet
examples: a crisp dry white wine
a dry sherry

examples: He was a man of few words with a delightful dry sense of humour.
He quickly built up a reputation for his dry wit.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: a dry voice
‘He may not last the night,’ she said in a dry tone.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 10

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12

definitions.label: Meaning 13

definitions.label: Meaning 14

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.label: Meaning 16

definitions.label: Meaning 17

examples: By earning millions from racing and giving pennies back, the bookmakers are sucking the sport dry.

definitions.label: Meaning 18

examples: There wasn't a dry eye in the house when they announced their engagement.

Native resources of scientific talent and ingenuity have not run dry.

When the paint is completely dry, apply another coat.

Her mouth felt as dry as a bone (= completely dry).

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: weeks of hot, dry weather

I hope it stays dry for our picnic.
There is every prospect of the weather remaining dry this week.
Rattlesnakes occur in the warmer, drier parts of North America.

definitions.definition: to give somebody/something a particular name, often in a humorous or critical way
examples: The media dubbed anorexia ‘the slimming disease’.

examples: COMPARE subtitle
an American movie dubbed into Italian

examples: verb sense 1 late Old English (in the sense ‘make a knight’): from Old French adober ‘equip with armour’, of unknown origin. verb senses 2 to 3 1920s: abbreviation of double.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: caused by somebody/something; because of somebody/something
examples: The team's success was largely due to her efforts.
He argues that climate change is mainly due to the actions of industrialized countries.
The increase in reported cases is partly due to growing public awareness of the disease.
This increase is due in part to the strong economy.
Most of the problems were due to human error.
The delay to the flight was due to the fact that there was ice on the runway.
The project had to be abandoned due to a lack of government funding.
Due to staff shortages, we are unable to offer a full buffet service on this train.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: arranged or expected
examples: When's the baby due?
The next train is due in five minutes.
My essay's due next Friday (= it has to be given to the teacher by then).
Rose is due to start school in January.
The band's first album is due for release later this month.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: when a sum of money is due, it must be paid immediately
examples: Payment is due on 1 October.
Membership fees are now due for the coming year.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: owed to somebody as a debt, because it is their right or because they have done something to deserve it
examples: Have they been paid the money that is due to them?
Our thanks are due to the whole team.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: owed something; deserving something
examples: I'm still due 15 days' leave.
She's due for promotion soon.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: that is suitable or right in the circumstances
examples: COMPARE undue
After due consideration, we have decided to appoint Mr Davis to the job.
Due allowance should be made for inexperience.
He was charged with driving without due care and attention.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to give somebody the praise they deserve, even if you do not really want to
examples: Give credit where credit is due—what the man does, he does well.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: at the right time and not before
examples: Your request will be dealt with in due course.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used when you are going to disagree, usually quite strongly, with somebody
examples: With all due respect, the figures simply do not support you on this.
With all due respect, I think you've misunderstood what he said.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not interesting or exciting
examples: SYNONYM dreary
Life in a small town could be deadly dull.
The countryside was flat, dull and uninteresting.
The first half of the game was pretty dull.
There's never a dull moment when John's around.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not bright or shiny
examples: a dull grey colour
dull, lifeless hair
Her eyes were dull.
The fire died down to a dull glow.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not bright, with a lot of clouds
examples: SYNONYM overcast
It was a dull, grey day.
The town seemed deserted in the dull afternoon light.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not clear or loud
examples: The gates shut behind him with a dull thud.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not very severe, but continuous
examples: a dull ache/pain

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: slow in understanding
examples: SYNONYM stupid
a dull pupil

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not busy; slow
examples: Don't sell into a dull market.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: it is not healthy to spend all your time working; you need to relax too

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: extremely boring
examples: I always found history as dull as ditchwater.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: stupid
examples: That was a pretty dumb thing to do.
If the police question you, act dumb (= pretend you do not know anything).
In her early movies she played a dumb blonde.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: unable to speak
examples: She was born deaf and dumb.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: temporarily not speaking or refusing to speak
examples: We were all struck dumb with amazement.
We sat there in dumb silence.
She stood in the doorway, dumb with rage.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to get rid of something you do not want, especially in a place that is not suitable
examples: Too much toxic waste is being dumped at sea.
The dead body was just dumped by the roadside.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to get rid of somebody/something or leave them for somebody else to deal with
examples: He's got no right to keep dumping his problems on me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to get rid of goods by selling them at a very low price, often in another country

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to put something/somebody down in a careless or untidy way
examples: Just dump your stuff over there—we'll sort it out later.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to end a romantic relationship with somebody
examples: Did you hear he's dumped his girlfriend?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to copy information and move it somewhere to store it

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make something the responsibility of another person
examples: They dropped the problem firmly back in my lap.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy
the goal-scoring duo of Coates and Winterbotham

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a performance by two musicians or singers; a piece of music for two players or singersWord Origin
examples: late 16th cent. (in sense (2)): via Italian from Latin duo ‘two’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the length of time that something lasts or continues
examples: The school was used as a hospital for the duration of the war.
a contract of three years’ duration

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: until the end of a particular situation, especially a war
examples: His wife and children had gone for the duration to the Lake District to escape the bombs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: all through a period of time
examples: during the 1990s
There are extra flights to Colorado during the winter.
Please remain seated during the performance.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: at some point in a period of time
examples: He was taken to the hospital during the night.
I only saw her once during my stay in Rome.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a fine powder that consists of very small pieces of sand, earth, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO cosmic dust
A cloud of dust rose as the truck drove off.
Fine particles of dust will get everywhere.
The workers wear masks to avoid inhaling the dust.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fine powder of dirt that forms in buildings, on furniture, floors, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO dusty
The books were all covered with dust.
There was a thick layer of dust on the table.
There wasn't a speck of dust anywhere in the room.
She is allergic to house dust.
That guitar's been sitting gathering dust (= not being used) for years now.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a fine powder that consists of very small pieces of a particular substance
examples: SEE ALSO angel dust
coal dust

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: Thousands of small businesses bite the dust every year.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to die

examples: Play your guitar that's gathering dust, or pull out the old tennis racket for a match.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to leave somebody far behind

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to wait for a situation to become clear or certain
examples: He waited for the dust to settle after the election before making any new decisions.

examples: It is my duty to report it to the police.

your duties as a parent

a civic/patriotic/moral duty

I’ll have to go, I’m afraid—duty calls (= there is a duty I need to go and do).
a breach/dereliction of duty

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the work that is your job
examples: SEE ALSO active duty
Report for duty at 8 a.m.
He was the duty manager that day.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: tasks that are part of your job
examples: SEE ALSO heavy-duty
I spend a lot of time on administrative duties.
The princess has taken on her mother's official duties.
to perform/fulfil/discharge your duties
Your duties will include greeting visitors and answering the phone.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a tax that you pay on things that you buy, especially those that you bring into a country
examples: customs/excise/import duties
duty on wine and beer
The US imposed a duty on imports from China.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to a higher standard or level than is required for a job or task
examples: She went above and beyond the call of duty in her efforts to save his life.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: something that you feel you must do; a responsibility which cannot be ignored
examples: He felt it was his bounden duty to tell the police what he knew.
We have a bounden duty to respond to this call for help.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to perform two roles or functions at the same time
examples: This device can pull double duty as a decent laptop and an adequate tablet.
She deserves credit for serving double duty as a host and performer.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: while doing a job
examples: A policeman was injured in the line of duty yesterday.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: working/not working at a particular time
examples: SEE ALSO off-duty
Who's on duty today?
What time do you go off duty?
You're not allowed to drink alcohol on duty.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a disk on which large amounts of information, especially films, photographs and video, can be stored, for use on a DVD player or computer (the abbreviation for ‘digital versatile disc’ or ‘digital videodisc’)
examples: Let's just stay in and watch a DVD.
a DVD recorder
a DVD drive
Is it available on DVD yet?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a lot of energy and a strong personality
examples: a dynamic leader
He was a dynamic young advertising executive.
She has a dynamic personality.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: always changing and making progress
examples: OPPOSITE static

These countries are characterized by highly dynamic economies.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: producing movement
examples: OPPOSITE static

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: SYNONYM keen
eager crowds outside the stadium
Small eager faces looked up and listened.
She is eager for (= wants very much to get) her parents' approval.
Everyone in the class seemed eager to learn.
They're eager to please (= wanting to be helpful).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: either of the organs on the sides of the head that you hear with
examples: SEE ALSO cauliflower ear
the left/right ear
He put his hands over his ears.
She's had her ears pierced.
The elephant flapped its ears.
She whispered something in his ear.
He was now screaming in my ear.
He was always there with a sympathetic ear (= was always willing to listen to people).
an ear infection

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the type of ears mentioned
examples: a long-eared owl

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an ability to recognize and copy sounds well
examples: She has always had an ear for languages.
You need a good ear to master the piano.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the top part of a grain plant, such as wheat, that contains the seeds
examples: ears of corn

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be waiting with interest to hear what somebody has to say
examples: ‘Do you know what he said?’ ‘Go on—I'm all ears.’

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to talk to somebody a lot about something, especially about a problem that you have

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be forced to leave (a job, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to have a lot of something to deal with
examples: We're up to our ears in work.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to hit somebody with your hand on the side of their head as a punishment

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to look at or listen to something/somebody carefully and with a lot of attention

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: somebody hears about something, especially when other people already know about it
examples: News of his affair eventually reached her ears.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a person thinks that other people are talking about them, especially in an unkind way
examples: ‘I bumped into your ex-wife last night.’ ‘I thought I could feel my ears burning!’

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a person is trying to listen to somebody else’s conversation

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: pleasant to listen to
examples: Their music is all very easy on the ear.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: pleasant to listen to or look at
examples: The room was painted in soft pastels that were easy on the eye.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be ignored or not noticed by other people
examples: Her advice fell on deaf ears.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to hit somebody/be hit on the head as a punishment
examples: You’ll get a thick ear if you’re not careful!

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to be forgotten quickly
examples: Everything I tell them just goes in one ear and out the other.
I knew that my words were going in one ear and out the other.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to have a lot of something, especially more than you need
examples: That man has money coming out of his ears.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to be able to give somebody advice, influence them, etc. because they trust you
examples: He had the ear of the monarch.
This was the woman who had the ear of the President.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to speak to somebody privately about something
examples: Can I have a word in your ear about tomorrow's presentation?

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to listen out for somebody/something that you might hear

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to listen or look out for somebody/something that you might hear or see

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to make sure that you always find out about the most recent developments in a particular situation
examples: The agent had no suitable properties on his books but promised to keep an ear to the ground for us.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to listen in a patient and kind way to somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to do something badly; to make a mess of something

definitions.label: Meaning 27

examples: I couldn't believe my ears when I heard the news.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to be very surprised at something you hear/see
examples: I couldn't believe my eyes when she walked in.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to play music by remembering how it sounds rather than by reading it
examples: She usually plays the guitar by ear, rather than reading the music.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to decide how to deal with a situation as it develops rather than by having a plan to follow
examples: I’m not sure how many people are expected—we’ll just have to play it by ear.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to raise the ears

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to listen carefully because you have just heard something interesting; to listen out for something you might hear
examples: Her ears pricked up at the sound of his name.
I walked along, ears pricked for the slightest noise.

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to make you feel that you can still hear something
examples: His warning was still ringing in my ears.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to refuse to listen to something
examples: She decided to shut her ears to all the rumours.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to be smiling, etc. a lot because you are very pleased about something
examples: He was beaming from ear to ear.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: to ignore or refuse to listen to somebody/something

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: used to warn people to be careful what they say because other people may be listening

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: young and without much experience
examples: SYNONYM naive

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: if somebody sends a person away with a flea in their ear, they tell them angrily to go away

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: without giving your full attention to what is being said, etc.
examples: He listened to her with only half an ear as he watched TV.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: near the beginning of a period of time, an event etc.
examples: the early morning
my earliest memories

the early 1990s
in the early years of the twentieth century
in the early days of space exploration (= when it was just beginning)

The earliest possible date I can make it is the third.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: arriving, or done before the usual, expected or planned time
examples: SEE ALSO early night

The bus was ten minutes early.
an early breakfast
He learnt to play the piano at an early age.

to encourage development/investment/growth
The government should encourage the use of renewable energy sources.
They claim that some computer games encourage violent behaviour in young children.
Music and lighting are used to encourage shoppers to buy more.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of encouraging somebody to do something; something that encourages somebody
examples: OPPOSITE discouragement
a few words of encouragement
He needs all the support and encouragement he can get.
With a little encouragement from his parents he should do well.
She was given every encouragement to try something new.
Her words were a great encouragement to them.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that gives somebody support, courage or hope
examples: OPPOSITE discouraging
This month's unemployment figures are not very encouraging.
You could try being a little more encouraging!
Despite the encouraging findings, we remain cautious.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the final part of a period of time, an event, an activity or a story
examples: SEE ALSO back end (1)
It's the end of an era.
the end of the book
at the end of the week
There’ll be a chance to ask questions at the end.
He wants the reports by the end of the month.
She remained active as an artist to the end of her life.
I was getting bored towards the end of the talk.
We didn't leave until the very end.
I'm staying until the end of this week.
We had to hear about the whole journey from beginning to end.
He is nearing the end of his career.
Our end-of-season sale starts next week.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a situation in which something does not exist any more
examples: It was the end of all his dreams.
That was by no means the end of the matter.
The war was finally at an end.
The meeting came to an end (= finished).
The coup brought his corrupt regime to an end.
This latest attack could spell the end of the peace process.
They have called for an end to violence.
an end to the conflict/war
Let’s put an end to (= stop) these rumours once and for all.
There's no end in sight to the present crisis.
Cheap air travel marked the end of the golden age of the British seaside holiday.
The release of ‘The Jazz Singer’ signalled the end of the silent movie era.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the part of an object or a place that is the furthest away from its centre
examples: SEE ALSO big end
I joined the end of the queue.
Go to the end of the line!
Turn right at the end of the road.
His office is the room at the other end of the corridor.
That's his wife sitting at the far end of the table.
You've got something on the end of your nose.
Tie the ends of the string together.
the front/rear end of a cow/tractor
These two products are from opposite ends of the price range.
We've travelled from one end of Mexico to the other.
They live in the end house.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an aim or a purpose
examples: They are prepared to use violence in pursuit of their ends.
She is exploiting the current situation for her own ends.
He joined the society for political ends.
With this end in view (= in order to achieve this) they employed 50 new staff.
We are willing to make any concessions necessary to this end (= in order to achieve this).
They are working towards common ends.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a part of an activity with which somebody is involved, especially in business
examples: SEE ALSO business end (2)
We need somebody to handle the marketing end of the business.
Are there any problems at your end?
I have kept my end of the bargain.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: either of two places connected by a phone call, journey, etc.
examples: I answered the phone but there was no one at the other end.
Jean is going to meet me at the other end.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: one of the two halves of a sports field
examples: The teams changed ends at half-time.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a small piece that is left after something has been used
examples: SEE ALSO bin-end
a cigarette end

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a person’s death. People say ‘end’ to avoid saying ‘death’.
examples: She came to an untimely end (= died young).
I was with him at the end (= when he died).
He met his end (= died) at the Battle of Waterloo.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a lineman who is nearest to the side of the field
examples: SEE ALSO tight end
a defensive end
He does as good a job as any end in football at helping his teammates.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to introduce the most important fact after everything has been considered
examples: At the end of the day, he'll still have to make his own decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: having nothing to do and not knowing what you want to do
examples: Come and see us, if you're at a loose end.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: something unpleasant that happens to somebody, for example punishment or a violent death, usually because of their own actions
examples: He'll come to a sticky end one of these days if he carries on like that.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to have almost nothing left of something
examples: I'm at the end of my patience.
They are at the end of their food supply.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to feel that you cannot deal with a difficult situation any more because you are too tired, worried, etc.
examples: You’d better let her know you’re safe. She’s at the end of her tether.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be the person that an action, etc. is directed at, especially an unpleasant one
examples: She found herself on the receiving end of a great deal of criticism.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to be so worried by a problem that you do not know what to do next
examples: She was at her wits’ end wondering how she’d manage it all in the time.
I'm at my wits' end trying to cope with his moods.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: when you say that people or situations are the end, you mean that you are annoyed with them

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: the first sign of something ending
examples: The scandal was the beginning of the end of his career as a politician.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to become very tired by trying to do too many things and going to bed late and getting up early

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: a thing that is itself important and not just a part of something more important
examples: For her, shopping had become an end in itself.
For her, travelling had become an end in itself rather than a means of seeing new places.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: bad or unfair methods of doing something are acceptable if the result of that action is good or positive
examples: He defended a morality in which the end justifies the means.
That's only OK if you believe that the end justifies the means.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: (to reach) the point at which something can no longer continue in the same way
examples: A defeat in the second round marked the end of the line for last year's champion.
The loss of this contract could signal the end of the line for the shipyard.
This latest disagreement could mean the end of the road for the band.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used when you are stating that there is nothing more that can be said or done about something
examples: If she doesn’t agree, I won’t go ahead. End of story.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: in a line, with the ends touching
examples: They arranged the tables end to end.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to have sex

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to be the person in a group who is chosen or forced to perform an unpleasant duty or task

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to understand something in the wrong way

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to suddenly become very angry or emotional

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to do everything possible, even if it is difficult, in order to get or achieve something
examples: I'd go to the ends of the earth to see her again.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: after a long period of time or series of events
examples: He tried various jobs and in the end became an accountant.
In the end, they decided to spend Christmas at home.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: after everything has been considered
examples: You can try your best to impress the interviewers but in the end it's often just a question of luck.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to start or be made to start a new and difficult activity that you are not prepared for
examples: Junior hospital doctors are thrown in at the deep end in their first jobs.
The company believes in throwing new employees in at the deep end with no training.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to continue to be cheerful in a difficult situation

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: something that shows you are nearly at the end of a long and difficult time or situation
examples: For the first time since the start of his treatment, we can now see light at the end of the tunnel.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to earn just enough money to be able to buy the things you need
examples: Many families struggle to make ends meet.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to shock or frighten somebody
examples: a chilling tale that will make your hair stand on end

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: a thing or an action that is not interesting or important in itself but is a way of achieving something else
examples: He doesn't particularly like the work but he sees it as a means to an end.
I don't enjoy studying computing—it's just a means to an end.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: very much
examples: It upset me no end to hear they'd split up.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: a lot of something
examples: We had no end of trouble getting them to agree.

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: not the worst thing that could happen to somebody
examples: Failing one exam is not the end of the world.
It won't be the end of the world if you don't get the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: to keep being reminded of something because somebody is always talking to you about it
examples: If we don't get her a dog we'll never hear the end of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: in a position standing upright rather than lying flat
examples: It'll fit if you stand it on end.
Stand the box on end.
Stand it on end.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: for the stated length of time, without stopping
examples: He would disappear for weeks on end.

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: to kill yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: a situation in which somebody is treated badly or unfairly

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: the place or position of greatest difficulty or responsibility
examples: He started work at the sharp end of the business, as a salesman.

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: an event or action that is the beginning of something more serious and/or unpleasant
examples: The introduction of a tax on workplace parking is seen by many as the thin end of the wedge.

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: continuing until you have done everything you can, or until something is completely finished, despite difficulties and problems
examples: They were prepared to fight to the bitter end for their rights.
We will fight this case to the bitter end.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an attempt to do something, especially something new or difficult
examples: There have been great advances in the field of scientific endeavour.
Please make every endeavour to arrive on time.
The manager is expected to use his or her best endeavours to promote the artist's career.
The public bombarded the company with complaints in an endeavour to have the price increases revoked.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the last part of a story, film, etc.
examples: OPPOSITE opening
His stories usually have a happy ending.
Friends don't spoil the endings of films for their friends.
It's a beautiful ending to the scene.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of finishing something; the last part of something
examples: Today is the anniversary of the ending of the Pacific War.
It was the perfect ending to the perfect day.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the last part of a word, that is added to a main part
examples: verb endings
a masculine/feminine ending

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very large in size or amount and seeming to have no end
examples: SYNONYM limitless
endless patience
endless opportunities for making money
The possibilities are endless.
an endless list of things to do
We don't have an endless supply of money, you know.
I've had enough of their endless arguing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: continuing for a long time and seeming to have no end
examples: an endless round of parties and visits
The journey seemed endless.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having the ends joined together so it forms one piece
examples: an endless loop of tape

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say publicly that you support a person, statement or course of action
examples: I wholeheartedly endorse his remarks.
Members of all parties endorsed a ban on land mines.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say in an advertisement that you use and like a particular product so that other people will want to buy it
examples: I wonder how many celebrities actually use the products they endorse.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to put details of a driving offence on somebody’s driving record
examples: You risk having your licence endorsed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to write your name on the back of a cheque so that it can be paid into a bank accountWord Origin
examples: late 15th cent. (in the sense ‘write on the back of’; formerly also as indorse): from medieval Latin indorsare, from Latin in- ‘in, on’ + dorsum ‘back’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a public statement or action showing that you support somebody/something
examples: The election victory is a clear endorsement of their policies.
a letter of endorsement
This is hardly a ringing endorsement of the plan.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a statement made in an advertisement, usually by somebody famous or important, saying that they use and like a particular product
examples: We are happy to give the product our full endorsement.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: details of a driving offence recorded on somebody’s driving licence
examples: How many endorsements can you have before you lose your licence?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to experience and deal with something that is painful or unpleasant without giving up
examples: SYNONYM bear
They had to endure a long wait before the case came to trial.
She could not endure the thought of parting.
The pain was almost too great to endure.
a love that endures all things and never fails
He had to endure the racist taunts of the crowd.
He can't endure being defeated.
He can't endure to be defeated.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to continue to exist for a long time
examples: SYNONYM last1
a success that will endure
The torn flag has endured as a symbol of freedom.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who hates somebody or who acts or speaks against somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO enmity
She didn't have an enemy in the world.
He has a lot of enemies in the company.
After just one day, she had already made an enemy of her manager.
They united in the face of a common enemy.
They used to be friends but they are now sworn enemies (= are determined not to become friends again).
James Moriarty was Sherlock Holmes's mortal enemy.
It is rare to find a prominent politician with few political enemies.
The state has a duty to protect its citizens against external enemies.
Birds are the natural enemies of many insect pests (= they kill them).
The enemy of my enemy is my friend.
‘We will defeat the enemies of freedom,’ said the president.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a country or group that you are fighting a war against; the soldiers, etc. of this country or group
examples: The enemy was/were forced to retreat.
to fight/defeat the enemy
enemy forces/combatants
The men came under enemy fire.
They were dropped by parachute behind enemy lines (= in the area controlled by the enemy)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: anything that harms something or prevents it from being successful
examples: Poverty and ignorance are the enemies of progress.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be the cause of your own problems
examples: Her indecisiveness makes her her own worst enemy.
Some dancers become their own worst enemies, criticizing themselves for every imperfection.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the strength, effort and enthusiasm required for physical or mental activity, work, etc.
examples: It's a waste of time and energy.
She's always full of energy.
I don't seem to have any energy these days.
nervous energy (= energy produced by feeling nervous)
For five years, she devoted considerable energy to photography.
He expends great energy trying to help them.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the physical and mental effort that you use to do something
examples: She put all her energies into her work.
He focused his energies on preparing the lectures.
Provide a means of channelling your child's creative energies.
I will put all my energies into improving the situation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a source of power, such as fuel, used for driving machines, providing heat, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO alternative energy
solar/wind/renewable energy
to save/conserve energy
to generate/produce energy
The £500 million programme is centred around energy efficiency and renewable power sources.
the country's total energy consumption
an energy crisis (= for example when fuel is not freely available)
energy conservation

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the ability of matter or radiation to work because of its mass, movement, electric charge, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO potential energy
potential/kinetic/electrical energy

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person who is full of energy and enthusiasmWord Origin
examples: mid 16th cent. (denoting force or vigour of expression): from French énergie, or via late Latin from Greek energeia, from en- ‘in, within’ + ergon ‘work’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make sure that people obey a particular law or rule
examples: It's the job of the police to enforce the law.
The legislation will be difficult to enforce.
United Nations troops enforced a ceasefire in the area.
The creditor should be at liberty to enforce his rights against the company's property.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something happen or force somebody to do something
examples: You can't enforce cooperation between the players.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of making people obey a particular law or rule
examples: strict enforcement of regulations
law enforcement officers

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to succeed in attracting and keeping somebody’s attention and interest
examples: It is a movie that engages both the mind and the eye.
Their pleas failed to engage any sympathy.
to engage the public/audience/viewer/reader
It was difficult to engage the students at first.
The party is attempting to engage young voters politically.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to employ a person, company, etc. to do a particular job

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 1
