examples: The appointment of a woman was one in the eye for male domination.

definitions.label: Meaning 64
definitions.definition: to be in love with only one particular person
examples: He's only ever had eyes for his wife.

definitions.label: Meaning 65
definitions.definition: to realize or make somebody realize the truth about something
examples: Travelling really opens your eyes to other cultures.

definitions.label: Meaning 66
definitions.definition: to be very attractive to look at

definitions.label: Meaning 67
definitions.definition: to hide your real actions or intentions from somebody by making them believe something that is not true

definitions.label: Meaning 68
definitions.definition: to think about or see something the way that another person sees it
examples: Try looking at it through her eyes for a change.
Events are seen through the eyes of a Polish refugee.

definitions.label: Meaning 69
definitions.definition: to see something by accident or not very clearly because you see it from the side of your eye and are not looking straight at it
examples: Out of the corner of her eye, she saw him coming closer.

definitions.label: Meaning 70
definitions.definition: to pretend that you have not noticed something so that you do not have to deal with it
examples: You can't just close your eyes to his violence.
They seem intent on shutting their eyes to the problems of pollution.

definitions.label: Meaning 71
definitions.definition: a person or thing that you are pleased to see; something that is very pleasant to look at

definitions.label: Meaning 72
definitions.definition: to stop giving your attention to what is most important

definitions.label: Meaning 73
definitions.definition: a person or thing is more complicated or interesting than you might think at first

definitions.label: Meaning 74
definitions.definition: to pretend not to notice something bad that is happening, so you do not have to do anything about it
examples: The authorities were either unaware of the problem or they turned a blind eye to it.

definitions.label: Meaning 75
definitions.definition: being watched carefully by somebody
examples: The children played under the watchful eye of their father.
I want you under my eye.

definitions.label: Meaning 76
definitions.definition: if a person does not know about something that they would normally think was bad, then it cannot hurt them
examples: What does it matter if I use his flat while he’s away? What the eye doesn’t see…!

definitions.label: Meaning 77
definitions.definition: with the hope of using a particular situation in order to gain some advantage for yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 78
definitions.definition: fully aware of the possible problems or results of a particular course of action
examples: I went into this with my eyes open so I guess I only have myself to blame.

definitions.label: Meaning 79
definitions.definition: very easily, without thinking about it
examples: I've made this trip so often, I could do it with my eyes shut.

definitions.label: Meaning 80
definitions.definition: with the intention of doing something
examples: He bought the warehouse with an eye to converting it into a hotel.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: material made by weaving wool, cotton, silk, etc., used for making clothes, curtains, etc. and for covering furniture
examples: They sell a wide variety of printed cotton fabric.
furnishing fabrics

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the basic structure of a society, an organization, etc. that enables it to function successfully
examples: a trend which threatens the very fabric of society

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the basic structure of a building, such as the walls, floor and roof
examples: The city retains much of its historic fabric.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: extremely good
examples: They put on a fabulous performance.
Jana is a fabulous cook.
The food looks fabulous.
I want an outfit that'll make me look fabulous.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very great
examples: fabulous wealth/riches/beauty

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: appearing in fables
examples: fabulous beasts

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the front part of the head, where the eyes, nose and mouth are
examples: SEE ALSO full face
a pretty/pale/round face
He buried his face in his hands.
to hide/cover your face
You should have seen the look on her face when I told her!
The expression on his face never changed.
She was red in the face with embarrassment.
At that time, her face was on the covers of all the magazines.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an expression that is shown on somebody’s face
examples: SEE ALSO game face
a smiling/happy/sad face
Her face lit up (= showed happiness) when she spoke of the past.
His face fell (= showed disappointment, sadness, etc.) when he read the headlines.
I could tell by his face it hadn't gone well.
Sue's face was a picture (= she looked very surprised, angry, etc.) as she listened to her husband's speech.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to refer to a person of the type mentioned
examples: She looked around for a familiar face.
He's a fresh face (= somebody new) at the company.
It's nice to see some new faces here this evening.
The movie is full of famous faces.
a well-known face on our television screens
I'm tired of seeing the same old faces every time we go out!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: having the type of face or expression mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO baby-faced
pale-faced
a freckle-faced boy
grim-faced
a sad-faced woman

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a side or surface of something
examples: SEE ALSO coalface
the north face of the mountain
the dark face of the moon
A steep path zigzags down the cliff face.
We could see tiny figures climbing the rock face.
Ivy covered the front face of the house.
A banner hung across the face of the building.
How many faces does a cube have?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the front part of a clock or watch
examples: a dial like the face of a clock

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the particular character of something
examples: the changing face of Britain
This discovery changed the whole face of science.
bureaucracy with a human face

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a particular aspect of something
examples: Social deprivation is the unacceptable face of capitalism.
He has become the public face of the company.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to describe something that you have failed to see, even though it was obvious and should have been easy to see
examples: The answer was staring us in the face but we never saw it until it was too late.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be certain to happen
examples: Defeat was staring them in the face.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be unable to avoid something
examples: They were staring defeat in the face.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be very obvious to other people from the expression on somebody’s face
examples: Guilt was written all over his face.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if a plan, etc. blows up in your face, it goes badly wrong in a way that causes you damage or makes you feel embarrassed

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to do something when you are angry that is meant to harm somebody else but that also harms you

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to disappear completely
examples: Keep looking—they can't just have vanished off the face of the earth.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to try to do something as hard and as long as you possibly can but without success
examples: You can argue till you're blue in the face, but you won't change my mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody will/will not get a particular job or position because they have/do not have the appearance, personality, etc. that the employer wants, even when this should not be important
examples: If your face fits, you'll get the job.
It doesn't matter how well qualified you are; if your face doesn't fit, you don't stand a chance.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: somebody looks very angry
examples: Mr Hibbs came in with a face like thunder.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: close to and looking at somebody
examples: The two have never met face to face before.
The room fell silent as she came face to face with the man who had tried to kill her.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: in a situation where you have to accept that something is true and deal with it
examples: She was at an early age brought face to face with the horrors of war.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: with your face and stomach facing upwards/downwards
examples: She lay face down on the bed.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: with the front part or surface facing upwards/downwards
examples: Place the card face up on the pile.
She placed the cards face down on the table.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to fall so that you are lying on your front

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to fail completely, usually in an embarrassing way
examples: His next television venture fell flat on its face.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to eat a lot of food or too much food

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to oppose or be the opposite of something that is usual or expected
examples: Such a proposal is flying in the face of common sense.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to do something that other people think is rude or shows a lack of respect, without feeling embarrassed or ashamed
examples: I don't know how you have the face to complain after everything they've done for you!

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to be made to look stupid
examples: They were left with egg on their faces when only ten people showed up.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: annoying somebody by criticizing them or telling them what to do all the time
examples: Why are you always in my face?

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: despite problems, difficulties, etc.
examples: She showed great courage in the face of danger.
The campaign continued in the face of great opposition.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: as a result of something
examples: He was unable to deny the charges in the face of new evidence.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to show in a very obvious way that you have no respect for somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to be forced to change from feeling pleased or satisfied to feeling disappointed or annoyed
examples: He’ll be laughing on the other side of his face when he reads my letter.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: (to have) an unhappy or disappointed expression
examples: He took one look at her long face and said ‘What’s wrong?’
The news for the company isn't good, judging from the long faces in the boardroom.

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to look straight at somebody without feeling embarrassed or ashamed
examples: Can you look me in the eye and tell me you're not lying?
She looked her father straight in the eye and answered his question truthfully.
I'll never be able to look her in the face again!

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to be less respected or look stupid because of something you have done
examples: Many leaders don't want to lose face by admitting failures.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: the state of being less respected by other people or looking stupid because of something you have done
examples: Failure to pass the exams means a massive loss of face for the students and their parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you have particular skills or qualities
examples: ‘I didn't know you could play the piano.’ ‘I'm not just a pretty face, you know!’

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: used to say that something seems to be good, true, etc. but that this opinion may need to be changed when you know more about it
examples: On the face of it, it seems like a great deal.
What may, on the face of it, seem obvious often turns out to be far more complicated.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: very obvious

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: to produce an expression on your face to show that you do not like somebody/something or in order to make somebody laugh
examples: What are you pulling a face at now?
Do you think it’s funny to make faces behind my back?

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: to put on make-up

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to pretend that you feel confident and happy when you do not
examples: I had to put on a brave face and try to show him that I wasn’t worried.
She put a brave face on her illness.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: to avoid or help somebody avoid being embarrassed
examples: She was fired, but she saved face by telling everyone she'd resigned.

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: to be determined to oppose somebody/something
examples: Her father had set his face against the marriage.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: to appear among your friends or in public
examples: She stayed at home, afraid to show her face.

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: to shut a door hard when somebody is trying to come in

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: to refuse to talk to somebody or meet them, in a rude way

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: a rude way of telling somebody to be quiet or stop talking

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: an action that seems to be intended as a deliberate way of offending and showing lack of respect for somebody
examples: The closure of the school is a slap in the face to the local community.

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: if you keep a straight face, you do not laugh or smile, although you find something funny
examples: SEE ALSO straight-faced

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: if you say something to somebody’s face, you say it to them directly rather than to other people
examples: COMPARE behind somebody’s back
He’s a liar, and I’ve told him so to his face many times.

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: used to refer to a person whose name you cannot remember
examples: Are you still working for what's her face?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make an action or a process possible or easier
examples: The new trade agreement should facilitate more rapid economic growth.
Structured teaching facilitates learning.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: buildings, services, equipment, etc. that are provided for a particular purpose
examples: leisure/sports facilities
medical/recreational/educational facilities
shopping/banking/cooking facilities
Recycling facilities are provided.
The school is upgrading its outdoor play facilities.
They provide facilities management services to corporations, hospitals and universities.
There are not enough facilities for families with young children.
All rooms have private facilities (= a private bathroom).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a place, usually including buildings, used for a particular purpose or activity
examples: the world’s largest nuclear waste facility
a new healthcare facility
a production/manufacturing/research/storage facility
a detention/correctional facility (= a prison)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a special feature of a machine, service, etc. that makes it possible to do something extra
examples: a bank account with an overdraft facility
This facility allows the user to input text in various forms onto the screen and thus create a true newspaper page.
a facility for checking spelling

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a natural ability to learn or do something easily
examples: She has a facility for languages.
He plays the piano with surprising facility.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that is known to be true, especially when it can be proved
examples: First, some basic facts about healthy eating.
Isn't it a fact that the firm is losing money?
It's a well-known fact that dogs have an acute sense of smell.
I know for a fact (= I am certain) that she's involved in something illegal.
The report is based on hard facts (= information that can be proved to be true).
Get your facts right (= make sure your information is correct) before you start making accusations.
It's about time you learnt to face (the) facts (= accepted the truth about the situation).
We didn't get on well, and that's a fact.
The judge instructed both lawyers to stick to the facts of the case.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: things that are true rather than things that have been invented
examples: The story is based on fact.
Is the account fact or fiction?
This is simply historical fact.
It's important to distinguish between fact and opinion.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to refer to a particular situation that exists
examples: I could no longer ignore the fact that he was unhappy.
We don't hide the fact that we've made mistakes.
I did everything I could, and she acknowledged the fact.
Students are already highly media-literate and the curriculum needs to reflect this fact.
The very fact that this happened more than once shows there is a problem.
Despite the fact that she was wearing a seat belt, she was thrown sharply forward.
Due to the fact that they did not read English, the prisoners were unaware of what they were signing.
She was happy apart from the fact that she could not return home.
Voluntary work was particularly important in view of the fact that women were often forced to give up paid work on marriage.
We want to celebrate the simple fact of their being here.
The mere fact of being poor makes such children criminals in the eyes of the police.
The fact remains that we are still two teachers short.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: after something has happened or been done, when it is too late to prevent it or change it
examples: On some vital decisions employees were only informed after the fact.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to add a comment on something that you have just said, usually adding something that you think the other person will be interested in
examples: It's a nice place. We've stayed there ourselves, as a matter of fact.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to disagree with something that somebody has just said
examples: SYNONYM actually
‘I suppose you'll be leaving soon, then?’ ‘No, as a matter of fact I'll be staying for another two years.’

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a statement, especially one that is the opposite of what has just been mentioned
examples: A new car would be wonderful but the fact of the matter is that we can't afford one.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a situation that cannot be changed, especially one that is unpleasant
examples: Illness is just a fact of life.
It’s a fact of life that some people will always be racist.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: accurate and detailed information
examples: I've asked to see all the facts and figures before I make a decision.
All the facts and figures were presented at the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the details about sex and about how babies are born, especially as told to children

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: it is not necessary to give any further explanation about something because the information that is available already proves that it is true

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to give extra details about something that has just been mentioned
examples: I used to live in France; in fact, not far from where you're going.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a statement, especially one that is the opposite of what has just been mentioned
examples: I thought the work would be difficult. In actual fact, it's very easy.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say what is true in a situation
examples: In point of fact, she is their adopted daughter.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to reply to a statement that you find interesting or surprising, or that you do not believe
examples: ‘She says I'm one of the best students she's ever taught.’ ‘Is that a fact?’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small group of people within a larger one, whose members have some different aims and beliefs to those of the larger group
examples: There are rival factions within the administration.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: opposition, disagreement, etc. that exists between small groups of people within an organization or political party
examples: a party divided by faction and intrigue

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: films, books, etc. that combine fact with fiction (= imaginary events)Word Origin
examples: senses 1 to 2 late 15th cent. (denoting the action of doing or making something): via French from Latin factio(n-), from facere ‘do, make’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of several things that cause or influence something
examples: SEE ALSO wow factor
Obesity is a major risk factor for heart disease.
the key/crucial/deciding factor
Criminality is associated with a range of individual, family and environmental factors.
The result will depend on a number of different factors.
The closure of the mine was the single most important factor in the town's decline.
We have identified a few key factors in the project's success.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a number that divides into another number exactly
examples: SEE ALSO highest common factor
1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12 are the factors of 12.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the amount by which something increases or decreases
examples: The real wage of the average worker has increased by a factor of over ten in the last 70 years.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a particular level on a scale of measurement
examples: SEE ALSO chill factor
a suntan lotion with a protection factor of 10
The wind-chill factor will make it seem colder.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a substance in the blood that helps the clotting process. There are several types of this substance.
examples: SEE ALSO clotting factor
Haemophiliacs have no factor 8 in their blood.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the feeling of confidence in the future that is shared by many people
examples: After the recession, people were waiting for the return of the feel-good factor before starting to spend money again.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a building or group of buildings where goods are made, mainly by machine
examples: a car factory
The factory closed down ten years ago.
She works in the local textile factory.
factory workers

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or organization that continuously produces a large quantity of a particular thing
examples: This record label has become a real hit factory (= one that produces a lot of successful songs).
These universities are becoming colourless degree factories, with no sense of what higher learning is really about.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a department or group of related departments in a college or university
examples: the Faculty of Law
students who are doing degrees in the Arts Faculty
the Faculty of Arts

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: all the teachers in a faculty of a college or university
examples: the Law School faculty
a faculty meeting
faculty members

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: all the teachers of a particular university or college
examples: faculty members
She joined the faculty of the University of Maryland.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: any of the physical or mental abilities that a person is born with
examples: the faculty of sight
She retained her mental faculties (= the ability to think and understand) until the day she died.
to be in full possession of your faculties (= be able to speak, hear, see, understand, etc.)
intellectual/critical/artistic faculties

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a particular ability for doing something
examples: the faculty of understanding complex issues
He had a faculty for seeing his own mistakes.
our faculty for picking up speech even in noisy environments

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become or to make something become paler or less bright
examples: The curtains had faded in the sun.
All colour had faded from the sky.
The sun had faded the curtains.
He was wearing faded blue jeans.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to disappear gradually
examples: Her smile faded.
Hopes of reaching an agreement seem to be fading away.
The laughter faded away.
The smile faded from his face.
His voice faded to a whisper (= gradually became quieter).
All other issues fade into insignificance compared with the struggle for survival.
Summer was fading into autumn.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if a sports player, team, actor, etc. fades, they stop playing or performing as well as they did before
examples: Black faded on the final bend.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be disappearing quickly
examples: Hopes of a peace settlement were fading fast.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that does not attract any attention; to disappear or hideWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in the sense ‘grow weak’): from Old French fader, from fade ‘dull, insipid’, probably based on a blend of Latin fatuus ‘silly, insipid’ and vapidus ‘vapid’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to not be successful in achieving something
examples: OPPOSITE succeed (1)
Many diets fail because they are boring.
Ultimately all their efforts failed.
a policy/plan fails
I failed in my attempt to persuade her.
He failed in his bid for the presidency.
The department failed to meet its sales targets.
They promised a lot, but utterly failed to deliver.
The song can't fail to be a hit (= definitely will be a hit).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to not pass a test or an exam; to decide that somebody/something has not passed a test or an exam
examples: OPPOSITE pass
What will you do if you fail?
He failed his driving test.
Students who fail the exam can retake it.
She was disqualified after failing a drugs test.
The restaurant failed a hygiene inspection.
The examiners failed over half the candidates.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to not do something
examples: People failed to recognize her talent.
His article fails to mention that he actually supported this change.
If you fail to comply, you can be fined.
The government has failed to provide the needed resources.
Such comments never failed to annoy him.
I fail to see (= I don't understand) why you won't even give it a try.
She cannot fail to (= must) be aware of the situation.
They failed in their duty to protect the public.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to stop working
examples: The brakes on my bike failed half way down the hill.
The air-conditioning system failed on the hottest day of the year.
Sadly, his kidneys had failed.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to become weak
examples: Her eyesight is failing.
The light began to fail.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to disappoint somebody; to be unable to help when needed
examples: When he lost his job, he felt he had failed his family.
She tried to be brave, but her courage failed her.
Words fail me (= I cannot express how I feel).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to not be enough when needed or expected
examples: The crops failed again last summer.
The rains had failed and the rivers were dry.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be unable to continue
examples: Several banks failed during the recession.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to suggest something that somebody can do if nothing else they have tried is successful
examples: If all else fails, you can always sell your motorbike.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: so important to the economy of a country that when it finds itself in financial trouble, the government or central bank must act to save it
examples: Shouldering the huge costs of rescuing banks that are too big to fail has been left to taxpayers.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not successful
examples: a failed writer
a failed coup

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: lack of success in doing or achieving something
examples: OPPOSITE success
The success or failure of the plan depends on you.
She is still coming to terms with the failure of her marriage.
The attempt was doomed to failure.
All my efforts ended in failure.
the problems of economic failure and increasing unemployment
Their bid to win the contract resulted in abject failure.
The decision to withdraw funding represents a failure of imagination.
the intelligence failures that preceded the terrorist attacks

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is not successful
examples: OPPOSITE success
The whole thing was a complete failure.
A team learns from experience, both successes and failures.
He was a failure as a teacher.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an act of not doing something, especially something that you are expected to do
examples: Failure to comply with the regulations will result in prosecution.
the city's failure to provide an efficient public transport system
the government's failure to carry out reforms in the energy sector
His confession followed repeated failures to appear in court.
the failure of the United Nations to maintain food supplies
a report on the failure by the police to protect her

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the state of not working correctly or as expected; an occasion when this happens
examples: patients suffering from heart/kidney/liver failure
renal/respiratory failure
Production has been hampered by mechanical failure.
A power failure plunged everything into darkness.
The cause of the crash was given as engine failure.
Poor maintenance caused the failure of two electricity generators.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a situation in which a business has to close because it is not successful
examples: There has been an alarming increase in business failures.
Are we going to see more closures or failures in the ISP business?
Business failures rose by 30% in 2018.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a situation in which crops do not grow correctly and do not produce food
examples: Bad weather has resulted in crop failure.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: acceptable and appropriate in a particular situation
examples: OPPOSITE unfair
a fair deal/wage/price
The punishment was very fair.
In the end, a draw was a fair result.
I give you fair warning, I’m not always this generous.
We wanted to resolve this matter in a way that would be fair to her.
Was it really fair to him to ask him to do all the work?
Moving to a new city wouldn't have been fair on the kids.
It's not fair on the students to keep changing the timetable.
It's only fair to add that they were not told about the problem until the last minute.
I think it is fair to say that they are pleased with this latest offer.
It's fair that they should give us something in return.
To be fair, she behaved better than we expected.
‘You should really have asked me first.’ ‘Right, okay, fair comment.’

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: treating everyone equally and according to the rules or law
examples: OPPOSITE unfair
She has always been scrupulously fair.
They are fair and decent employers.
demands for a fairer distribution of wealth
his vision of a fairer, kinder society
The new tax is fairer than the old system.
We have to be fair to both players.
to receive a fair trial
For the first time, free and fair elections will be held.
It's not fair! He always gets more than me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: pale in colour
examples: a fair complexion
Kate had dark hair and fair skin.
She has long fair hair.
All her children are fair (= they all have fair hair).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: quite large in number, size or amount
examples: A fair number of people came along.
There's been a fair amount of research on this topic.
a fair-sized town
We've still got a fair bit (= quite a lot) to do.
My birthday’s still a fair way off (= it’s still a long time until my birthday).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: quite good
examples: There's a fair chance that we might win this time.
It's a fair bet that they won't turn up.
I have a fair idea of what happened.
His knowledge of French is only fair.
Scoring twenty points was a fair achievement.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: bright and not raining
examples: SYNONYM fine
It was a fair and breezy day.
The day was set fair with the spring sun shining down.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not too strong and blowing in the right direction
examples: They set sail with the first fair wind.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: beautiful
examples: a fair maiden

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: in some situations any type of behaviour is acceptable to get what you want

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to be reasonable in their judgement of somebody/something
examples: Be fair! She didn't know you were coming.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: using dishonest methods if honest ones do not work
examples: She’s determined to win, by fair means or foul.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a reasonable opportunity to show that you can do something
examples: I felt we weren't given a fair crack of the whip.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to say that an idea or suggestion seems reasonable
examples: ‘We'll meet at 8.’ ‘Fair enough.’
If you don't want to come, fair enough, but let Bill know.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: a fairly large number
examples: I've been there a fair few times.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody to be reasonable
examples: I just wanted to say, ‘Hey mate, fair go!’

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: (to allow somebody) the opportunity to give their opinion of something before deciding if they have done something wrong, often in court
examples: I'll see that you get a fair hearing.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to ask for fair treatment or to claim that a situation is fair
examples: Fair's fair—we were here first.
Fair's fair—you can't expect them to cancel everything just because you can't make it.
Come on, fair's fair—you’ve had your chance, now let me try.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: (to give somebody/get) fair treatment that gives you the same chance as somebody else
examples: Are minority students getting a fair shake at college?
We need a government that cares about equity and a fair go for all.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: (more than) an amount of something that is considered to be reasonable or acceptable
examples: He has more than his fair share of problems.
I've had my fair share of success in the past.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: not particularly good or bad
examples: ‘How are you feeling today?’ ‘Oh, fair to middling.’

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used by somebody who is caught doing something wrong, to say that they admit that they are wrongWord Origin
examples: adjective Old English fæger ‘pleasing, attractive’, of Germanic origin; related to Old High German fagar.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to some extent but not very
examples: fairly simple/easy/straightforward
This is a fairly common problem.
It's fairly obvious what's going on here.
It's fairly clear that there is still room for improvement.
That's a fairly typical reaction.
I know him fairly well, but I wouldn't say we were really close friends.
We'll have to leave fairly soon (= before very long).
I'm fairly certain I can do the job.
He was fairly sure he was right.
I think you'll find it fairly difficult (= you do not want to say that it is very difficult).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a fair and reasonable way; honestly
examples: He has always treated me very fairly.
Her attitude could fairly be described as hostile.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something that you are saying
examples: The time fairly raced by.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: honestly and according to the rules

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in a direct way that is easy to understand

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: exactly in the place you were aiming for

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of treating people equally or in a way that is reasonable
examples: The fairness of the judicial system is being questioned.
She has a strong sense of justice and fairness.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a pale colour of skin or hair
examples: A tan emphasized the fairness of her hair.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to introduce a statement that defends somebody who has just been criticized, or that explains another statement that may seem unreasonable
examples: In all fairness to him, he did try to stop her leaving.
I have in fairness to say that, as yet, there is no hard evidence to support these charges.
In all fairness to him, I should say that most of his story is true.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: trust in somebody’s ability or knowledge; trust that somebody/something will do what has been promised
examples: If the company can retain its customers' faith, it could become the market leader.
I have faith in you—I know you'll do well.
We've lost faith in the government's promises.
Her friend's kindness has restored her faith in human nature.
I wouldn't put too much faith in what she says.
He has blind faith (= unreasonable trust) in doctors' ability to find a cure.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: strong religious belief
examples: to have faith
to lose your faith
Faith is stronger than reason.
a woman of strong religious faith
He started questioning his faith in God.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a particular religion
examples: the Christian/Catholic/Islamic/Muslim/Jewish faith
The children are learning to understand people of different faiths.
people of all faiths and none

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the intention to do something right/wrong
examples: They handed over the weapons as a gesture of good faith.
The judge did not find any bad faith on the part of the defendants.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to break/keep a promise that you have made to somebody; to stop/continue supporting somebody
examples: As club manager he was not prepared to keep faith with the players who had failed him.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: knowing that what you are doing is wrong
examples: They had entered into the contract in bad faith.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: believing that what you are doing is right; believing that something is correct
examples: We printed the report in good faith but have now learnt that it was incorrect.
He bought the painting in good faith (= he did not know that it had been stolen).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a belief in something that is not known or has not been done before
examples: These reforms are totally untested and will require a leap of faith on the part of teachers.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to rely on somebody/something completely for success or help
examples: She did not pin much faith on their chances of success.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not what somebody claims it is; appearing to be something it is not
examples: SYNONYM counterfeit
There were a few stalls selling fake designer clothing.
The caller appeared to have a fake American accent.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: made to look like something else
examples: SYNONYM imitation
a fake fur jacket
Don't go out in the sun—get a fake tan from a bottle.
We sprayed fake snow over the trees to make it look like winter.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to drop down from a higher level to a lower level
examples: The rain was falling steadily.
They were injured by falling rocks.
Several of the books had fallen onto the floor.
The label must have fallen off.
The leaves were falling from the trees.
The seeds fall to the ground and germinate.
One of the kids fell into the river.
He fell 20 metres onto the rocks below.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to suddenly stop standing
examples: SEE ALSO fallen
She slipped on the ice and fell.
A tree fell, just missing his car.
I fell over and cut my knee.
The house looked as if it was about to fall down.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to decrease in amount, number or strength
examples: Prices continued to fall on the stock market today.
The temperature fell sharply in the night.
Falling birth rates could have an impact on future economic growth.
Reputations rise and fall for a variety of reasons.
Their profits have fallen by 30 per cent.
Share prices fell 30p.
Petroleum sales fell almost 11 per cent.
The dollar fell slightly against the yen.
Her voice fell to a whisper.
Unemployment fell to its lowest level in 30 years.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to pass into a particular state; to begin to be something
examples: He had fallen asleep on the sofa.
She fell ill soon after and did not recover.
The room had fallen silent.
When the rent fell due, she couldn't pay.
The book fell open at a page of illustrations.
I had fallen into conversation with a man on the train.
The house had fallen into disrepair.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to hang down
examples: Her hair fell over her shoulders in a mass of curls.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to slope downwards
examples: The land falls away sharply towards the river.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be defeated or captured
examples: The coup failed but the government fell shortly afterwards.
Troy finally fell to the Greeks.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to die in battle; to be shot
examples: a memorial to those who fell in the two world wars

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to come quickly and suddenly
examples: SYNONYM descend
A sudden silence fell.
Darkness falls quickly in the tropics.
An expectant hush fell on the guests.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to happen or take place
examples: My birthday falls on a Monday this year.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to move in a particular direction or come in a particular position
examples: My eye fell on (= I suddenly saw) a curious object.
Which syllable does the stress fall on?
A shadow fell across her face.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to belong to a particular class, group or area of responsibility
examples: Out of over 400 staff there are just seven that fall into this category.
This case falls outside my jurisdiction.
This falls under the heading of scientific research.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: wrong; not correct or true
examples: A whale is a fish. True or false?
Predictions of an early improvement in the housing market proved false.
She gave false information to the insurance company.
He used a false name to get the job.
His career was ruined by false accusations.
The allegations are completely false.
This claim is simply false.
The law can punish knowingly false statements.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not natural
examples: SYNONYM artificial
false teeth/eyelashes
a false beard

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not real or what somebody claims it is, but made to look real to cheat people
examples: He had been travelling with a false passport.
The case had a false bottom where documents or even a small radio could be hidden.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: wrong or not accurate, because it is based on something that is not true or correct
examples: a false argument/assumption/belief
to give a false impression of wealth
to lull somebody into a false sense of security (= make somebody feel safe when they are really in danger)
They didn't want to raise any false hopes, but they believed her husband had escaped capture.
Buying a cheap computer is a false economy (= will not actually save you money).
If you don't do the test right, it can lead to false positives.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not real or sincere
examples: false modesty
She flashed him a false smile of congratulation.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not faithful
examples: a false lover

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: by pretending to be something that you are not, in order to gain some advantage for yourself
examples: She was accused of obtaining money under false pretences.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to give the impression of being sincere/true or not sincere/true
examples: It may seem a strange story but it rings true to me.
His expressions of support rang rather hollow.
His promise rang hollow.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being known and talked about by many people
examples: SEE ALSO famous
to achieve/win instant fame
Daisy Ridley of ‘Star Wars’ fame (= famous for ‘Star Wars’)
The town's only claim to fame is that there was once a riot there.
She went to Hollywood in search of fame and fortune.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a short period of being famous
examples: Everybody wants their fifteen minutes of fame.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to suddenly become famous, especially as a singer or actor
examples: He shot to fame almost overnight.
She shot to stardom in a Broadway musical.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: well known to you; often seen or heard and therefore easy to recognize
examples: OPPOSITE unfamiliar
to look/sound/seem familiar
I couldn’t see any familiar faces in the room.
He's a familiar figure in the neighbourhood.
Then she heard a familiar voice.
The cast contains a number of familiar names.
The song was vaguely familiar.
The smell is very familiar to everyone who lives near a bakery.
Violent attacks are becoming all too familiar (= sadly familiar).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: knowing something very well
examples: OPPOSITE unfamiliar
an area with which I had been familiar since childhood
You will soon become familiar with the different activities.
Are you familiar with the computer software they use?
She would have been familiar with the work of this 18th-century German philosopher.
Ishii is clearly intimately familiar with his script and characters.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very informal, sometimes in a way that is unpleasant
examples: You seem to be on very familiar terms with your tutor.
After a few drinks her boss started getting too familiar for her liking.
He was being overly familiar with Gloria.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group consisting of one or two parents and their children
examples: SEE ALSO blended family
I introduced Neil to the other members of my family.
The event promises games and fun for the entire family.
This is a summer movie for the whole family.
Every family has its own story to tell.
All my family enjoy skiing.
one-parent/single-parent families
Taking a family of four to the cinema is expensive.
families with young children
He's a friend of the family (= he is known and liked by the parents and the children).
From early childhood he was a mystery to the rest of his family.
He barely earns enough money to pay his rent and feed his family.
She works tirelessly to provide for her family.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group consisting of one or two parents, their children and close relations
examples: SEE ALSO extended family
All our family came to Grandad's eightieth birthday party.
The support of family and friends is vital.
We've only told the immediate family (= the closest relations).
the royal family (= the children and close relations of the king or queen)
I always think of you as one of the family.
There are a lot of girls in our family.
Nobody outside his family knew that he had a daughter.

examples: the lifestyles of the rich and famous

a fan heater
a fan blowing cold air

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: SYNONYM feel like

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: SYNONYM great

You look fantastic!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very large; larger than you expected
examples: SYNONYM enormous

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: SYNONYM weird
fantastic dreams of forests and jungles

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: impossible to put into practice; impossible to believe
examples: a fantastic scheme/project

The plot gets increasingly fantastic as the film goes on.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a pleasant situation that you imagine but that is unlikely to happen
examples: He spoke of his childhood fantasies about becoming a famous football player.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a product of your imagination
examples: Her books are usually escapist fantasies.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of imagining things; a person’s imagination
examples: This is a work of fantasy.
Stop living in a fantasy world.
I live in the real world, not fantasy land.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a type of story that is set in a world, or a version of our world, that does not really exist and involves magic, monsters, etc.
examples: She wrote a series of fantasy novels filled with wizards, witches and dragons.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a competition in which you choose players to make your own imaginary team, and score points according to the performance of the real players
examples: SEE ALSO fantasy football

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long distance away
examples: We didn't go far.
Have you come far?
It's not far to the beach.
There's not far to go now.
It's too far to walk.
The restaurant is not far from here.
countries as far apart as Japan and Brazil
He looked down at the traffic far below.
Far away in the distance, a train whistled.
The farther north they went, the colder it became.
a concert of music from near and far
Legends are usually far removed from the reality.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used when you are asking or talking about the distance between two places or the distance that has been travelled or is to be travelled
examples: How far is it to your house from here?
How far is Boston from New York?
How much further is it?
I'm not sure I can walk so far.
We'll go by train as far as London, and then take a bus.
We didn't go as far as the others.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a long time from the present; for a large part of a particular period of time
examples: The band had their first hit as far back as 2012.
To answer that question we need to go further back in time.
Let's try to plan further ahead.
We worked far into the night.
The film takes place in a future not too far distant.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very much; to a great degree
examples: That's a far better idea.
The damage was far worse than I'd expected.
a drug that gives heart attack victims a far greater chance of survival
There are far more opportunities for young people than there used to be.
She always gives us far too much homework.
The results far exceeded my expectations.
The benefits far outweigh the cost.
The recent heat and continued drought further reduced yields.
It had been a success far beyond their expectations.
He's fallen far behind in his work.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used when you are asking or talking about the degree to which something is true or possible
examples: How far can we trust him?
His parents supported him as far as they could.
Plan your route in advance, using main roads as far as possible.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to talk about how much progress has been made in doing or achieving something
examples: How far have you got with that report?
Half an hour later Duncan was no farther in his quest.
I read as far as the third chapter.
We’ve got as far as collecting our data but we haven’t analysed it yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to the horizon (= where the sky meets the land or sea)
examples: The bleak moorland stretched on all sides as far as the eye could see.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to give your personal opinion on something
examples: As far as I am concerned, you can do what you like.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to say that you think you know, remember, understand, etc. something but you cannot be completely sure, especially because you do not know all the facts
examples: SEE ALSO AFAIK
As far as we knew, there was no cause for concern.
As far as I can see, you've done nothing wrong.
She lived in Chicago, as far as I can remember.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to give facts or an opinion about a particular aspect of something
examples: She's doing fine as far as French is concerned, it's her German I'm worried about.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to a limited degree, usually less than is enough
examples: It's a good plan as far as it goes, but there are a lot of things they haven't thought of.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: by a great amount
examples: The last of these reasons is by far the most important.
Amy is the smartest by far.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to continue doing something beyond reasonable limits

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: far away from home; to or in places that are not near
examples: You can hire a car if you want to explore further afield.
Journalists came from as far afield as China.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: by a very great amount
examples: She's far and away the best player.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: over a large area
examples: They searched far and wide for the missing child.
People came from far and wide for the show.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used when you are just about to disagree with somebody or to criticize them and you would like them to think that you do not really want to do this
examples: Far be it from me to interfere in your affairs but I would like to give you just one piece of advice.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: almost the opposite of something or of what is expected
examples: It is far from clear (= it is not clear) what he intends to do.
Computers, far from destroying jobs, can create employment.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: used to say that the opposite of what somebody says is true
examples: ‘You're not angry then?’ ‘Far from it. I've never laughed so much in my life.’

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: not happening often

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to be very successful in the future
examples: She is very talented and should go far.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to achieve all that is wanted
examples: The new legislation is welcome but does not go far enough.
Do these measures go far enough?
Stop it now. The joke has gone far enough (= it has continued too long).

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to be willing to go to extreme or surprising limits in dealing with something
examples: I wouldn't go as far as to say that he's a liar (= but I think he may be slightly dishonest).
In June 2009 he went so far as to offer his resignation.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to behave in an extreme way that is not acceptable
examples: He's always been quite crude, but this time he's gone too far.
I never thought she'd go this far.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to the degree that
examples: That's the truth, in so far as I know it.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: almost correct
examples: Your guess wasn't far out at all.
They weren't far out with their estimate of 100 000.
You're not far wrong when you say he's the richest guy in town.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to not be enough to buy a lot of things
examples: Five pounds doesn't go very far these days.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to not be enough for what is needed
examples: Four bottles of wine won't go far among twenty people.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: until now; up to this point
examples: What do you think of the show so far?
Detectives are so far at a loss to explain the reason for his death.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: only to a limited degree
examples: I trust him only so far.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: used to say that things have been successful until now and you hope that they will continue to be successful, but you know that the task, etc. is not finished yet

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: used to comment on something that was almost successful but in fact failedWord Origin

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a popular style of clothes, hair, etc. at a particular time or place; the state of being popular
examples: the latest fashion trends
the new season’s fashions
Jeans are always in fashion.
Long skirts have come into fashion again.
Some styles never go out of fashion.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the business of making or selling clothes in new and different styles
examples: They all want to work in fashion.
household names in the world of fashion and design
a fashion magazine
the fashion industry

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a popular way of behaving, doing an activity, etc.
examples: This theory, though recent, is more than a passing fashion.
Fashions in art and literature come and go.
He seemed to endorse the current fashion for neoliberal economics.
The fashion at the time was for teaching mainly the written language.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to some extent, but not very well
examples: I can play the piano, after a fashion.
‘Do you speak French?’ ‘After a fashion.’
So they became friends, after a fashion.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in the style of somebody/something
examples: The new library is very much after the fashion of Nash.
She spoke in French after the fashion of the court.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: in a particular way
examples: How could they behave in such a fashion?
I strive to get my work done in a timely fashion.
The troops embarked in an orderly fashion.
Each chapter is structured in a similar fashion.
She was proved right, in dramatic fashion, when the whole department resigned.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that somebody is doing something or using something a lot
examples: SEE ALSO parrot-fashion
She's been spending money like it's going out of fashion.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: following a style that is popular at a particular time
examples: fashionable clothes/ideas/styles
He was laughed at by his more fashionable friends.
It's becoming fashionable to have long hair again.
Such thinking is currently fashionable among right-wing politicians.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used or visited by people following a current fashion, especially by rich people
examples: OPPOSITE unfashionable
a fashionable address/resort/restaurant
She lives in a very fashionable part of London.
The shop moved to a more fashionable address.
The play is a satire on fashionable society in Victorian times.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: moving or able to move quickly
examples: a fast car/horse
He's just become the world's fastest runner.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: happening in a short time or without delay
examples: We've recorded the fastest rate of increase for several years.
We can guarantee a fast response time.
Technology was expanding at a fast pace.
a period of fast economic growth

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: able to do something quickly
examples: a fast learner
Are you a fast reader with the ability to retain the key points?
These are complex programs needing very large and fast computers.
a fast internet connection

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: producing or allowing quick movement
examples: SEE ALSO fast lane
It's a very fast road and people do not realize what speed they are doing.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: showing a time later than the true time
examples: I'm early—my watch must be fast.
That clock's ten minutes fast.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: very sensitive to light, and therefore useful when taking photographs in poor light or of something that is moving very quickly

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: safely fixed in position
examples: He made the boat fast.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: not likely to change or to come out when washed
examples: SEE ALSO colour fast

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be quick to understand or react in a new situation
examples: You can't fool him—he's always fast on the draw.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be quick at pulling out a gun in order to shoot it

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be quick to understand or react in a new situation
examples: You can't fool him—he's always quick on the draw.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be quick at pulling out a gun in order to shoot it

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: full of rapid action and sudden changes
examples: In his latest movie, the action is fast and furious.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: a person who can talk very quickly and easily, but who cannot always be trusted
examples: As a politician, she had the reputation for being a real fast talker.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: a person who knows how to get what they want quickly, especially when beginning a sexual relationship with somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: that cannot be changed in any circumstances
examples: There are no hard and fast rules about this.
This situation isn’t hard and fast.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to earn money quickly and easily
examples: This is a long-term project. We are not out to make a quick buck.

definitions.label: Meaning 18

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to close or join together the two parts of something; to become closed or joined together
examples: SYNONYM do up
Fasten your seat belts, please.
Emma shivered and fastened the top button of her coat.
He fastened up his coat and hurried out.
The garment is fastened with a sash.
The dress fastens at the back.
a short yellow skirt which fastens up the side.
The gown fastens down the front with Velcro.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to close something so that it will not open; to be closed in this way
examples: OPPOSITE unfasten
Fasten the gates securely so that they do not blow open.
Make sure all the exits are securely fastened.
The window wouldn't fasten.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to fix something in a particular position
examples: He fastened back the shutters.
Use the special kit provided to fasten the child seat in the car.
A gold locket was fastened around Eleanor's neck.
Each bundle of 100 votes was rolled up and fastened with a rubber band.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to attach or tie one thing to another thing
examples: He fastened the papers together with a paper clip.
She fastened the rope to a tree.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if you fasten your arms around somebody, your teeth into something, etc., or if your arms, teeth, etc. fasten around, into, etc. somebody/something, you hold the person/thing strongly with your arms, etc.
examples: The dog fastened its teeth in his leg.
His hand fastened on her arm.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if you fasten your eyes on somebody/something or your eyes fasten on somebody/something, you look at them for a long time
examples: He fastened his gaze on her face.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having too much flesh on it and weighing too much
examples: NOTE AT thin
a big fat man/woman
You'll get fat if you eat so much chocolate.
He grew fatter and fatter.
I was ashamed of my fat flabby legs.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: containing a lot of fat
examples: fat bacon/sausages

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: thick or wide
examples: a fat volume on American history
a big fat envelope stuffed with banknotes

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: large in quantity; worth a lot of money
examples: a fat sum/profit
He gave me a nice fat cheque.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used for saying that you do not believe something is likely to happen
examples: ‘They might let us in without tickets.’ ‘Fat chance of that!’
Fat chance of him helping you!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not at all good or useful
examples: Paul can't drive so he was a fat lot of use when I broke my arm.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: causing or ending in death
examples: COMPARE mortal
a fatal accident/blow/illness
a potentially fatal form of cancer
If she gets ill again it could prove fatal.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: causing disaster or failure
examples: a fatal error/mistake
Any delay would be fatal.
There was a fatal flaw in the plan.
It'd be fatal to try and stop them now.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the things, especially bad things, that will happen or have happened to somebody/something
examples: The fate of the three men is unknown.
She sat outside, waiting to find out her fate.
The court will decide our fate/fates.
Each of the managers suffered the same fate.
The government had abandoned the refugees to their fate.
From that moment our fate was sealed (= our future was decided).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the power that is believed to control everything that happens and that cannot be stopped or changed
examples: Fate was kind to me that day.
By a strange twist of fate, Andy and I were on the same plane.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a terrible thing that could happen
examples: At the last minute the hero saves her from a fate worse than death.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to do something too confidently in a way that might mean that your good luck will come to an end
examples: She felt it would be tempting fate to try the difficult climb a second time.
It would be tempting fate to say that we will definitely win the game.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a male parent of a child or an animal; a person who is acting as the father to a child
examples: SEE ALSO godfather
My father died in 2017.
Ben's a wonderful father.
Our new boss is a father of three (= he has three children).
You've been like a father to me.
He was a wonderful father to both his natural and adopted children.
I never met my biological father.
Father, I cannot lie to you.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person’s ancestors (= people who are related to you who lived in the past)
examples: SEE ALSO forefather
the land of our fathers

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the first man to introduce a new way of thinking about something or of doing something
examples: SEE ALSO founding father
Henry Moore is considered to be the father of modern British sculpture.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used by Christians to refer to God
examples: Father, forgive us.
God the Father

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the title of a priest, especially in the Roman Catholic Church and the Orthodox Church
examples: SEE ALSO Holy Father
Father Dominic

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: from one generation of a family to the next

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that a son’s character or behaviour is similar to that of his father

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: very much older than somebody (especially used to suggest that a romantic or sexual relationship between the two people is not appropriate)

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: we believe a thing because we want it to be trueWord Origin
examples: Old English fæder, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch vader and German Vater, from an Indo-European root shared by Latin pater and Greek patēr.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the responsibility for something wrong that has happened or been done
examples: SEE ALSO no-fault
Why should I say sorry when it's not my fault?
It's nobody's fault.
He believes that the product’s poor image is partly the fault of the press.
It was his fault that we were late.
It's your own fault for being careless.
He would not admit fault for the collision.
I think the owners are at fault (= responsible) for not warning us.
Many people live in poverty through no fault of their own.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a bad or weak aspect of somebody’s character
examples: SYNONYM shortcoming
He's proud of his children and blind to their faults.
I love her for all her faults (= in spite of them).
I think my worst fault is impatience.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that is wrong or not perfect; something that is wrong with a machine or system that stops it from working correctly
examples: SYNONYM defect
The book's virtues far outweigh its faults.
a mechanical/technical fault
The fire was caused by an electrical fault.
The system, for all its faults, is the best available at the moment.
a major fault in the design
We're trying to correct the faults in the program.
a common fault with this type of machine
The film is not without fault.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a mistake made when serving
examples: SEE ALSO double fault
He has served a number of double faults in this set.
Even tennis champions sometimes serve double faults.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a place where there is a break that is longer than usual in the layers of rock in the earth’s crust
examples: the San Andreas fault
a fault line

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to look for and discover mistakes in somebody/something; to complain about somebody/something
examples: My mother did nothing but find fault with my manners.
She was always finding fault with his manners.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody has a lot, or even too much, of a particular good quality
examples: She is generous to a fault.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that you do to help somebody
examples: Could you do me a favour and pick up Sam from school today?
Can I ask a favour?
I would never ask for any favours from her.
I'll ask Steve to take it. He owes me a favour.
Thanks for helping me out. I'll return the favour (= help you because you have helped me) some time.
I'm going as a favour to Ann, not because I want to.
Do yourself a favour (= help yourself) and wear a helmet on the bike.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: approval or support for somebody/something
examples: Artists sought the favour of wealthy patrons.
The suggestion to close the road has found favour with (= been supported by) local people.
to gain/win/lose favour with somebody
The programme has lost favour with viewers recently.
The policy is gaining favour among voters.
She's not in favour with (= supported or liked by) the media just now.
It seems Tim is back in favour with the boss (= the boss likes him again).
Reality TV has begun to fall out of favour with viewers.
an athlete who fell from favour after a drugs scandal
The government looks with favour upon (= approves of) the report's recommendations.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: treatment that is generous to one person or group in a way that seems unfair to others
examples: SYNONYM bias
As an examiner, she showed no favour to any candidate.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a small gift given to children at a party

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: agreement to have sex with somebody
examples: demands for sexual favours

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: you are likely to succeed because the conditions are good and you have an advantage

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to try to get somebody to like or support you by praising or helping them a lot
examples: He’s always trying to curry favour with the boss.
He tried to curry favour with the teachers.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used in reply to a question that you think is silly
examples: ‘Do you think they'll win?’ ‘Do me a favour! They haven't got a single decent player.’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to do something that is not helpful to somebody or that gives a bad impression of them
examples: You're not doing yourself any favours, working for nothing.
The orchestra did Beethoven no favours.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: if you are in favour of somebody/something, you support and agree with them/it
examples: He argued in favour of a strike.
There were 247 votes in favour (of the motion) and 152 against.
I'm all in favour of (= completely support) equal pay for equal work.
Most of the ‘don't knows’ in the opinion polls came down in favour of (= eventually chose to support) the Democrats.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: in exchange for another thing (because the other thing is better or you want it more)
examples: He abandoned teaching in favour of a career as a musician.
Early in his musical career he abandoned blues in favour of jazz.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if something is in somebody’s favour, it gives them an advantage or helps them
examples: The exchange rate is in our favour at the moment.
She was willing to bend the rules in Mary's favour.
The golf tournament went in the Americans' favour.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a decision or judgement that is in somebody’s favour benefits that person or says that they were right
examples: The court decided in Ms Smith’s favour and she received compensation for unfair dismissal.
The High Court found in favour of the plaintiffs.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: in a fair way
examples: They undertook to make their judgement without fear or favour.

Terror attacks are a tool to instil fear in the public.

Women should be able to work without fear of harassment.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a feeling of concern about somebody's safety or about something bad that might happen

Alan spoke of his fears for the future.
the fear that he had cancer
The announcement sparked fears that interest rates will rise.
The government announced the new measures amid growing security fears.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to avoid the danger of something happening
examples: We spoke quietly for fear of waking the guards.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: feeling frightened that you might be killed

examples: ‘Are you coming climbing?’ ‘No fear!’
