definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the bad feeling that you have when you are in danger or when a particular thing frightens you
examples: Her eyes showed no fear.
The child was shaking with fear.
I suddenly felt gripped by fear.
She nearly went crazy with fear and anxiety.
The attacks created a climate of fear.
Terror attacks are a tool to instil fear in the public.
He managed to overcome his fears.
Fear of crime can affect people's lives.
We lived in constant fear of losing our jobs.
Women should be able to work without fear of harassment.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a feeling of concern about somebody's safety or about something bad that might happen
examples: The doctor's report confirmed our worst fears.
Police tried hard to allay the fears of local residents.
her fears for her son’s safety
Alan spoke of his fears for the future.
the fear that he had cancer
The announcement sparked fears that interest rates will rise.
The government announced the new measures amid growing security fears.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to avoid the danger of something happening
examples: We spoke quietly for fear of waking the guards.
I had to run away for fear (that) he might one day kill me.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: feeling frightened that you might be killed

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that you definitely do not want to do something
examples: ‘Are you coming climbing?’ ‘No fear!’

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an action or a piece of work that needs skill, strength or courage
examples: PLURAL OF foot
The tunnel is a remarkable feat of engineering.
to accomplish/achieve/perform astonishing feats
That was no mean feat (= it was difficult to do).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of the many soft light parts covering a bird’s body
examples: a peacock feather
tail/flight/wing feathers
a feather pillow (= one containing feathers)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: people of the same sort (are found together)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an action that you can be proud of

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to annoy or upset somebody or a group of people
examples: The senator's speech ruffled a few feathers in the business world.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel less angry or offended

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to express surpriseWord Origin
examples: Old English fether, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch veer and German Feder, from an Indo-European root shared by Sanskrit patra ‘wing’, Latin penna ‘feather’, and Greek pteron, pterux ‘wing’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something important, interesting or typical of a place or thing
examples: SEE ALSO water feature
An interesting feature of the city is the old market.
geographical features
Teamwork is a key feature of the training programme.
I've added some new features to my website.
new safety/security features
There are a number of special features included on the disc.
The main bonus feature on the DVD is a lengthy interview with the director.
The most distinctive feature of this track is the trumpet sound.
The one redeeming feature (= good thing about it) of the plan was its low cost.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a part of somebody’s face such as their nose, mouth and eyes
examples: facial features
his strong handsome features
Her eyes are her most striking feature.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a special article or programme about somebody/something
examples: In today's programme we have a special feature on education.
There are in-depth feature articles in every issue.
She is a feature writer for the ‘Evening Standard’.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the main film in a cinema programmeWord Origin

The meeting is on February fifth.
We went to Japan last February.
I arrived at the end of February.
last February's election

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a system of government in which the individual states of a country have control over their own affairs, but are controlled by a central government for national decisions, etc.
examples: a federal republic

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: (within a federal system, for example the US and Canada) connected with national government rather than the local government of an individual state
examples: a federal law
state and federal income taxes

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of money that you pay for professional advice or services
examples: SEE ALSO contingency fee
Employees are reimbursed for any legal fees incurred when they relocate.
fee-paying schools (= that you have to pay to go to)

Students take out loans to cover tuition fees.

Users can block ads for a small monthly fee.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an amount of money that you pay to join an organization, or to do something
examples: a membership/subscription fee
There is no entrance fee to the gallery.
the TV licence fee
You have to pay a fee to enter the race.
The registration fee for the event is £35.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give food to a person or an animal
examples: SEE ALSO bottle-feed
Have you fed the cat yet?
The baby can't feed itself yet (= can't put food into its own mouth).
It's important to feed children a well-balanced diet.
He has to be fed liquids through a tube in his stomach.
The cattle are fed (on) barley.
The barley is fed to the cattle.
The animals are fed with hay and grass.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to eat food
examples: SEE ALSO feed on/off something
Slugs and snails feed at night.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to provide food for a person or group of people
examples: They have a large family to feed.
There's enough here to feed an army.
Have they been feeding you well?
They struggled to feed and clothe the children.
Having another mouth (= person) to feed can be a strain.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to give a plant a special substance to make it grow
examples: Feed the plants once a week.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to give advice, information, etc. to somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO drip-feed
We are constantly fed gossip and speculation by the media.
The media were being fed with accusations and lies.
Gossip and speculation are constantly fed to us by the media.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to supply something to somebody/something
examples: The lake is fed by a river.
The electricity line is fed with power through an underground cable.
Power is fed into the electricity line through an underground cable.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to put or push something into or through a machine
examples: He fed the meter with coins.
He fed coins into the meter.
The information was fed into the data store.
The fabric is fed through the machine.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to satisfy a need, desire, etc. and keep it strong
examples: For drug addicts, the need to feed the addiction takes priority over everything else.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to harm somebody who has helped you or supported you

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to experience a particular feeling or emotion
examples: The bus ride made me feel sick.
Are you feeling comfortable?
She sounded more confident than she felt.
I was feeling guilty.
You'll feel better after a good night's sleep.
I feel sorry for him.
I feel bad about leaving you like this.
She felt betrayed.
How are you feeling today?
I know exactly how you feel (= I feel sympathy for you).
We all felt the same way.
Luckily I was feeling in a good mood.
I felt the need to explain.
I felt a sense of relief.
I felt like a complete idiot.
She made me feel like a child by doing everything for me.
I feel as if nobody cares.
She felt as though she was going to cry.
to feel an idiot/a fool

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to notice or be aware of something because it is touching you or having a physical effect on you
examples: SYNONYM sense
I could feel the warm sun on my back.
She felt a sharp pain in her hand.
She could not feel her legs.
I can’t feel his pulse.
He felt a hand on his shoulder.
You may feel a slight pressure in your chest.
He felt a hand touching his shoulder.
She could feel herself blushing.
He felt the sweat running down his face.
I felt something crawl up my arm.
We felt the ground give way under our feet.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to become aware of something even though you cannot see it, hear it, etc.
examples: SYNONYM sense
Can you feel the tension in this room?
They all feel pressure from managers to make a sale.
I definitely felt the importance of the occasion.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to give you a particular feeling or impression
examples: This situation doesn't feel right.
You need to go somewhere that feels safe.
My mouth felt completely dry.
It felt strange to be back in my old school.
The place still feels like a small fishing village.
The interview only took ten minutes, but it felt like hours.
I've lived here for years, but it still doesn't feel like home.
It feels like rain (= seems likely to rain).
It's three degrees right now, but with the wind chill factor it feels like minus 12.
How does it feel to be alone all day?
Her head felt as if it would burst.
It felt as though he had run a marathon.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have a particular physical quality that you become aware of by touching
examples: The water feels warm.
Its skin feels really smooth.
This wallet feels like leather.
Your hands feel like ice.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to deliberately move your fingers over something in order to find out what it is like
examples: Can you feel the bump on my head?
Try to tell what this is just by feeling it.
People like to touch and feel the fabric before they buy.
Feel how rough this is.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to think or believe that something is the case; to have a particular opinion or attitude
examples: We all felt (that) we were unlucky to lose.
We've always felt this was our home.
I felt (that) I had to apologize.
I feel I could continue playing until I am 35.
This is something I feel strongly about.
How do you feel about inviting the children too?
I didn't know you felt like that about it.
She felt it her duty to tell the police.
I feel it a great honour to be chosen.
She felt it to be the best course of action to remain.
Why did you feel it necessary to do that?
I felt it advisable to do nothing.
We felt it to be unfortunate.
This decision is, I feel, a huge mistake.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to experience the effects or results of something, often strongly
examples: He feels the cold a lot.
Cathy was really feeling the heat.
We're all starting to feel the pressure at work.
I was OK after my run, but I'll feel it tomorrow.
She felt her mother's death very deeply.
The effects of the recession are being felt everywhere.
We all felt the force of her arguments.
Her loss has been keenly felt.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to search for something with your hands, feet, etc.
examples: She felt in her bag and pulled out a pen.
If you feel under the desk you'll find a hook.
She felt for the step with her foot.
I had to feel about in the dark for the light switch.
He felt in his pockets for some money.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be pleased because somebody has made you feel important or special
examples: He was flattered by her attention.
I felt flattered at being asked to give a lecture.
She was flattered to hear that he had been asking about her.
I suppose we should be flattered that he agreed to come at all.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be or feel unfairly treated
examples: She has every right to feel hard done by—her parents have given her nothing.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to feel proud and happy
examples: I was honoured to have been mentioned in his speech.
‘Would you be my best man?’ ‘I’d be honoured.’

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to feel weak because you are nervous

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to realize that you are getting old, especially compared with people you are with who are younger than you

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that they are allowed to do something
examples: Feel free to ask questions if you don't understand.
‘Can I use your phone?’ ‘Feel free.’

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to feel happy, confident, etc.
examples: It makes me feel good to know my work is appreciated.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to be certain about something even though you do not have any direct proof and cannot explain why you are certain
examples: I know I'm going to fail this exam—I can feel it in my bones.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to want to have or do something
examples: I feel like a drink.
We all felt like celebrating.
He felt like bursting into tears.
We'll go for a walk if you feel like it.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to not have enough money
examples: Lots of people who have lost their jobs are starting to feel the pinch.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to move along carefully, for example when it is dark, by touching walls, objects, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to be careful about how you do things, usually because you are in a situation that you are not familiar with
examples: She was new in the job, still feeling her way.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to feel that you must do something because of your sense of moral duty
examples: COMPARE duty-bound
She felt honour-bound to attend as she had promised to.
He felt honour bound to help her.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to look or feel very ill or tired

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to look/feel extremely good
examples: Wow, you look like a million dollars.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to look or feel stupid, weak, ashamed, etc.
examples: There’s no need to make me look small in front of all these people.
I felt really small when I realized how much time he’d spent on it.

definitions.label: Meaning 26

examples: She’s only been here a couple of weeks but she is already making her presence felt.
She certainly made her presence felt in the boardroom.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: not to feel as well or lively as usual
examples: I’m not feeling up to the mark at the moment.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to not feel healthy and well
examples: I’m not quite feeling myself today.

definitions.definition: the idea or belief that a particular thing is true or a particular situation is likely to happen

I got the feeling he didn't like me much.
I had this nagging feeling that I had forgotten something.
He suddenly had the feeling of being followed.
I have a bad feeling about this (= I have the impression it is not going to go well).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: sympathy or love for somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO fellow feeling
He never told her his feelings.
You have no feeling for the sufferings of others.
I still have feelings for her (= feel attracted to her in a romantic way).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the ability to feel physically
examples: I've lost all feeling in my legs.
Feeling gradually began to return to my frozen feet.
Will she ever get the feeling back in her fingers?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the ability to understand somebody/something or to do something in a sensitive way
examples: He played the piano with great feeling.
She has a wonderful feeling for colour.
He had developed a feeling for when not to disturb her.
He had great design sense, and a great feeling of proportion.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the atmosphere of a place, situation, etc.
examples: They have managed to recreate the feeling of the original theatre.
The house had a feeling of neglect about it.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: anger between people, especially after an argument
examples: There was a lot of bad feeling between the two groups of students.
I don't want any bad feelings between us.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used after you have been arguing with somebody or have beaten them in a contest but you would still like to be friendly with them
examples: It looks like I'm the winner again. No hard feelings, Dave, eh?
Someone has to lose. No hard feelings, eh?

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: an unpleasant feeling that you get when you realize that something bad has happened or is going to happen
examples: I had a horrible sinking feeling when I saw the ambulance outside the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be careful not to do or say anything that might upset somebody
examples: I kept off the subject of divorce so as to spare her feelings.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to describe somebody who is the same as you in some way, or in the same situation
examples: fellow citizens/students
my fellow passengers on the train

Thousands of their fellow countrymen are dead.
We sometimes appear to care more for animals than for our fellow human beings.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: SEE ALSO chain-link fence
The two women chatted over the garden fence.
Security guards with dogs patrolled the perimeter fence.
The footpath was blocked by a barbed wire fence.
The house was surrounded by a white picket fence.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a structure that horses must jump over in a race or a competition

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a criminal who buys and sells stolen goods

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: said about people who never seem happy with what they have and always think they could be happier in a different place or situation

definitions.definition: to find a solution when you disagree with somebody
examples: RELATED NOUN fence-mending
The White House already is struggling to mend fences with Europe.
Is it too late to mend fences with your ex-wife?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to refer to either of two opposite opinions on an issue
examples: The two countries are often on opposite sides of the fence when it comes to climate change.
There are arguments on both sides of the aisle.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to avoid becoming involved in deciding or influencing something
examples: He tends to sit on the fence at meetings.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a series of performances of music, plays, films, etc., usually organized in the same place once a year; a series of public events connected with a particular activity or idea
examples: a film/music festival
the Edinburgh Festival
the Cannes Film Festival
The pub is holding its annual beer festival later this week.
a rock festival (= where bands perform, often outdoors and over a period of several days)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a day or period of the year when people stop working to celebrate a special event, often a religious one
examples: The family always celebrates the Jewish festivals.
the pilgrims who arrived on major festivals
festivals held in honour of local saints
Holi, the Hindu festival to welcome spring

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a medical condition in which a person has a temperature that is higher than normal
examples: COMPARE temperature
He has a high fever.
Aspirin should help reduce the fever.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a type of disease in which somebody has a high temperature
examples: SEE ALSO breakbone fever
She caught a fever on her travels in Africa, and died.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a state of nervous excitement
examples: He waited for her arrival in a fever of impatience.
She was in a fever of anxiety about him.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: great interest or excitement about something
examples: SEE ALSO spring fever
Election fever suddenly gripped the nation.
World Cup fever has gripped the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: We've had a few replies.
I need a few things from the store.

There seem to be fewer tourists around this year.
Very few students learn Latin now.

definitions.definition: not happening oftenWord Origin

examples: SYNONYM roughage
dietary fibre
Dried fruits are especially high in fibre.
a high-/low-fibre diet
He has been advised to increase his fibre intake.
bran fibre

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a material such as cloth or rope that is made from a mass of natural or artificial threads
examples: SEE ALSO glass fibre
nylon and other man-made fibres
Wear underwear that is made from natural fibres.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: one of the many thin threads that form body tissue, such as muscle, and natural materials, such as wood and cotton
examples: cotton/wood/nerve/muscle fibres

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a type of literature that describes imaginary people and events, not real ones
examples: OPPOSITE non-fiction
a work of popular fiction
historical/romantic/crime fiction
to write/read fiction
a crime fiction writer

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that is invented or imagined and is not true
examples: Don't believe what she says—it's pure fiction!
For years he managed to keep up the fiction that he was not married.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that things that actually happen are often more surprising than stories that are inventedWord Origin

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an area of land in the country used for growing crops or keeping animals in, usually surrounded by a fence, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO cornfield

People were working in the fields.
We saw golden fields of wheat.
He planted a field of beans.

The house overlooks the sugar cane fields.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an area of land used for the purpose mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO airfield
a landing field

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a large area of land covered with the thing mentioned; an area from which the thing mentioned is obtained
examples: SEE ALSO coalfield
The territory is covered with snow, bare rock and ice fields.
Prisoners were sent to work in the gas fields in the north.
the discovery of the oil and gas fields in the North Sea

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an area of land used for playing a sport on
examples: SEE ALSO centre field
a football/soccer/sports field
a baseball/cricket/rugby field
Every player on the field did their best today.
Players need discipline both on and off the field (= when they are playing and also in their free time).
There was huge excitement as the teams came onto the field.
Today they take the field (= go on to the field to play a game) against county champions Essex.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the team that is trying to catch the ball rather than hit it
examples: He took the ball early and hit it through a gap in the field.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: all the people or animals competing in a particular sports event
examples: The strong field includes three world record holders.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an area of land where a battle is fought
examples: SEE ALSO battlefield
a medal for bravery in the field
to die on the field of battle
a field ambulance/kitchen

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a particular subject or activity that somebody works in or is interested in
examples: SYNONYM area (4)
Child development is such an interesting field.
Genetic science has developed dramatically since I entered the field 40 years ago.
All of them are experts in their chosen field.
He was awarded a Nobel Prize for his work in this field.
She works in the field of adult education.
I enjoy meeting people in other fields of business.
This discovery has opened up a whole new field of study.
‘How big was the bomb, if it did all that damage?’ ‘I don’t know. Not my field’ (= that is not one of the subjects I know about).

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the fact of people doing practical work or study, rather than working in a library or laboratory
examples: SEE ALSO field trip
a field study/experiment
field recordings/observations
Her findings were based on extensive field and laboratory work.
We then tested the questionnaire in field conditions.
tests carried out in the field

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: all the people or products competing in a particular area of business
examples: They lead the field in home entertainment systems.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: an area within which the force mentioned has an effect
examples: SEE ALSO force field
the earth’s gravitational field
an electromagnetic field
Weak electric fields are emitted by all living organisms.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: part of a record that is a separate item of data
examples: You will need to create separate fields for first name, surname and address.
the use of keys to move between fields

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to enable somebody to be successful in a particular area of activity because other people or groups have given up competing with them
examples: The complete disarray of the opposition parties leaves the field clear for the government to implement urgent reforms.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to create a situation where everyone has the same opportunities

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to have sexual relationships with a lot of different peopleWord Origin
examples: Old English feld (also denoting a large tract of open country; compare with veld), of West Germanic origin; related to Dutch veld and German Feld.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: angry and aggressive in a way that is frightening
examples: a fierce dog
Two fierce eyes glared at them.
He suddenly looked fierce.
She spoke in a fierce whisper.
The more she struggled, the fiercer he became.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: showing strong feelings or a lot of activity, often in a way that is violent
examples: fierce loyalty
the scene of fierce fighting
He launched a fierce attack on the Democrats.
Competition from abroad became fiercer in the 1990s.
His wife is his fiercest critic.
The bill was passed despite fierce opposition.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very strong in a way that could cause damage
examples: fierce wind
the fierce heat of the flames

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very much; more than usual
examples: I sure do miss you something fierce!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a team of Rugby Union players
examples: He's in the first fifteen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: 5th
examples: Today is the fifth (of May).
the fifth century BC
It's her fifth birthday.
My office is on the fifth floor.
It's the fifth time that I've been to America.
Her mother had just given birth to another child, her fifth.
the world’s fifth-largest oil exporter
He finished fifth in the race.
Edward V (= Edward the Fifth)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: numbers, years or temperatures from 50 to 59
examples: She was born in the fifties.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: between the ages of 50 and 59
examples: He retired in his fifties.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take part in a war or battle against an enemy
examples: soldiers trained to fight
He fought in Vietnam.
My grandfather fought against the Fascists in Spain.
to fight a war/battle
They gathered soldiers to fight the invading army.
They fought for control of the island.
Didn't we fight a war for freedom?
They were fighting over disputed land.
Future wars will be fought over water supplies.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to struggle physically with somebody
examples: My little brothers are always fighting.
He taught me how to fight with a sword.
Riot police fought with demonstrators.
He sometimes fights with other children in the playground.
She fought her attacker, eventually forcing him to flee.
Children will fight even over small things.
dogs fighting over scraps of food
They were fighting each other over a toy.
Paris offers to fight Menelaus for Helen's hand.
She fought hard against his strong grip.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have an argument with somebody about something
examples: I remember lying in bed listening to my parents fighting.
It's a trivial matter and not worth fighting about.
Scholars have long fought over this point.
I'm always fighting with my sister.
It's normal for couples to fight.
The thing we fight about most is money.
We've fought over many issues, but always respected one another.
Let's not fight over the details.
He was well-liked by his peers, but often fought with his teachers.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to try hard to stop, deal with or oppose something bad or something that you disagree with
examples: We will continue to fight for as long as it takes.
She fought bravely, but died of the disease.
to fight terrorism/crime/corruption/poverty
Vitamin C helps your body to fight disease.
Workers are fighting the decision to close the factory.
The fire crews had problems fighting the blaze.
She fought a long battle against cancer.
They are committed to fighting against racism.
She spent her life fighting for the poor.
We must fight hatred with love.
She'll fight like a tiger to protect her children.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to try very hard to get something or to achieve something
examples: We fought for years before we got the recognition we deserved.
Women fought for the right to vote.
He's still fighting for compensation after the accident.
Doctors fought for more than six hours to save his life.
She fought hard to get this film made.
She gradually fought her way to the top of the company.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to take part in a contest against somebody
examples: to fight an election/a campaign
She's fighting for a place in the national team.
There are twelve parties fighting the election.
The second half was fiercely fought, but neither side managed to score.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to take part in a boxing match
examples: Doctors fear he may never fight again.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to try to get what you want in court
examples: He fought his wife for custody of the children.
I'm determined to fight the case.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to defend your/somebody’s position against other people

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to use similar methods in a fight or an argument to those your opponent is using

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make a great effort to stay alive, especially when you are badly injured or seriously ill
examples: A young cyclist is fighting for his life after the accident.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be able to win an argument or get what you want without anyone’s help
examples: I wouldn't get involved—he's old enough to fight his own battles.
My parents believed in leaving me to fight my own battles.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be unwilling to accept something or do something, and to try to avoid it
examples: Successive governments have fought shy of such measures.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to fight until one of the two people or groups is dead, or until one person or group defeats the other
examples: The soldiers were prepared to fight to the death if they had to.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to fight in a very determined way for what you want
examples: The residents are fighting tooth and nail to stop the new development.
She fought tooth and nail to keep custody of the children.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to say that although you have failed or had a bad experience, you will continue

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: (to try to do) something that you will probably never succeed in doing
examples: I’m fighting a losing battle against the mess in this house!

The children were nowhere to be seen.
A peace settlement is nowhere in sight (= is not likely in the near future).

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to accept somebody as they are without expecting them to behave in a special way or have special qualitiesWord Origin
examples: Old English findan, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch vinden and German finden.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: information that is discovered as the result of research into something
examples: Our research findings indicate that pregnant women benefit from this treatment.
These findings suggest that there is no direct link between unemployment and crime.
This result confirms the findings of many previous studies.
to report/present/publish your findings
I'll now summarize the key findings from these studies.
An interesting finding of the survey was that older people were happier than younger people.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a decision made by the judge or jury in a court case
examples: SEE ALSO fact-finding
The appeal court upheld a finding that the agreement was unlawful.
The court made a finding in favour of the defendant.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in good health
examples: ‘How are you?’ ‘Fine, thanks.’
I was feeling fine when I got up this morning.
‘How’s your throat?’ ‘It’s fine as long as I don’t cough.’

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: of high quality; good
examples: a very fine performance
fine clothes/wines/workmanship
It's a particularly fine example of Saxon architecture.
the finest collection of paintings in Europe
She's a fine actor and an even finer dancer.
Jim has made a fine job of the garden.
people who enjoy the finer things in life (= for example art, good food, etc.)
It was his finest hour (= most successful period) as manager of the England team.
This movie features some of her finest work.
He tried to appeal to their finer feelings (= feelings of duty, love, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that an action, a suggestion or a decision is acceptable
examples: ‘I'll leave this here, OK?’ ‘Fine.’
‘Bob wants to know if he can come too.’ ‘That's fine by me.’
If you don't agree, that's fine with him.
She has been virtually ignoring me but I'm fine with that.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say you are satisfied with something
examples: Don't worry. Your speech was fine.
Other than a few damp spots, the place looked fine.
to sound/seem fine
You go on without me. I'll be fine.
‘Can I get you another drink?’ ‘No, thanks. I'm fine.’
Never mind, Jake. Everything will be just fine.
Your hair is perfectly fine the way it is.
This paper's not very good quality, but it's fine for rough work.
You're a fine one to talk! (= you are not in a position to criticize, give advice, etc.)
This is a fine (= terrible) mess we're in!

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: bright and not raining
examples: a fine day/evening
I hope it stays fine for the picnic.
It was a fine sunny morning.
That summer saw weeks of fine dry weather.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: pleasant to look at
examples: a fine view
a fine-looking woman
a fine figure of a man
The boy looks mighty fine in a uniform.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: made of very small grains
examples: fine sand
Use a finer piece of sandpaper to finish.
The top 8 inches of earth is very fine, made up of river sediment.
Dip in beaten egg then fine dry breadcrumbs before frying in olive oil.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: attractive and small or thin
examples: SYNONYM delicate
fine bone china
She has inherited her mother's fine features (= a small nose, mouth, etc.).

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: very thin or narrow; made of very thin or narrow wires or threads
examples: His fine blond hair came down almost to his shoulders.
a fine thread
I need a brush with a fine tip.
a fine sieve/mesh

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: difficult to see or describe
examples: SYNONYM subtle
You really need a magnifying glass to appreciate all the fine detail.
There's no need to make such fine distinctions.
There's a fine line between love and hate (= it is easy for one to become the other).
We still have to iron out the finer details.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: that you have a lot of respect for
examples: He was a fine man.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: sounding important and impressive but unlikely to have any effect
examples: His speech was full of fine words which meant nothing.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: containing only a particular metal and no other substances that reduce the quality
examples: fine gold

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: people say chance would be a fine thing to show that they would like to do or have the thing that somebody has mentioned, but that they do not think that it is very likely

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: the more complicated or detailed aspects of something
examples: She seems at ease discussing the finer points of foreign policy.
He learnt the finer points of cricket during a trip to London.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: healthy; in good condition
examples: The team is in fine fettle.
Park Foods is in fine fettle after selling off all non-core businesses.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something that is expressed clearly and directly, especially a criticism
examples: Not to put too fine a point on it, I think you are lying.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to be in a difficult or dangerous situation where you could easily make a mistake
examples: He was walking a fine line between being funny and being rude.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of the four long thin parts that stick out from the hand (or five, if the thumb is included)
examples: SEE ALSO butterfingers
She ran her fingers through her hair.
Hold the material between finger and thumb.
He was about to speak but she raised a finger to her lips.
The old man wagged his finger at the youths.
Tina curled her slender fingers into a fist.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the type of fingers mentioned; having or using the number of fingers mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO light-fingered
long-fingered
nimble-fingered
a four-fingered chord

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the part of a glove that covers the finger

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a long narrow piece of bread, cake, land, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO fish finger
chocolate fingers
a finger of toast
a narrow finger of land pointing out into the sea

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that the total number of somebody/something is very small
examples: She could count on the fingers of one hand the people she actually enjoyed being with.
Although she knew lots of people, she could count her friends on the fingers of one hand.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be awkward with your hands so that you drop things or are unable to do something

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to suffer as a result of doing something without realizing the possible bad results, especially in business
examples: He got his fingers badly burnt dabbling in the stock market.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to hope that your plans will be successful (sometimes putting one finger across another as a sign of hoping for good luck)
examples: I'm crossing my fingers that my proposal will be accepted.
Keep your fingers crossed!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to refer to an estimate or method of doing something that is not very accurate or scientific and partly based on guessing
examples: It isn’t an exact science—it’s a kind of finger in the air thing.
‘It’s all a bit finger in the air,’ admitted a spokesman.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: if the finger of blame/suspicion points or is pointed at somebody, they are suspected of having committed a crime, being responsible for something, etc.
examples: The inquiry pointed the finger of blame at the driver of the crashed coach.
The finger of suspicion was pointed at the chicken served for lunch.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to start doing some work or making an effort
examples: You're going to have to pull your finger out if you want to pass this exam.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to raise your middle finger in the air with the back part of your hand facing somebody, done to be rude to somebody or to show them that you are angry

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be involved in a lot of different activities and have influence over them, especially when other people think that this is annoying

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to always be aware of the most recent developments in a particular situation

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be stealing money from the place where you work

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be likely to steal something

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to touch somebody with the intention of hurting them physically
examples: I never laid a finger on her.
If you lay a finger on me, I’ll call the police.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to miss or fail to use an opportunity
examples: Don't let the chance to work abroad slip through your fingers.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to do nothing to help somebody
examples: The children never lift a finger to help around the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to accuse somebody of doing something
examples: RELATED NOUN finger-pointing
The article points an accusing finger at the authorities.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to (not) be able to identify what is wrong or different about a particular situation
examples: There was something odd about him but I couldn't put my finger on it.
You've put your finger on something there—we'll need to investigate that.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to form the shape of a V with the two fingers nearest your thumb and raise your hand in the air with the back part of it facing somebody, done to be rude to them or to show them that you are angry
examples: SEE ALSO V-sign
She enjoys sticking two fingers up to convention.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to make a sharp noise by moving your second or third finger quickly against your thumb, to attract somebody’s attention, or to mark the beat of music, for example
examples: He snapped his fingers for the waiter to bring more wine.
He snapped his fingers and the waiter came running.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to work very hardWord Origin
examples: Old English, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch vinger and German Finger.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to stop doing something or making something because it is complete
examples: Haven't you finished your homework yet?
She finished law school last year.
You only get points if you finish the race.
I thought you'd never finish!
We've just finished the project.
Let me just finish what I'm doing.
Be quiet! He hasn't finished speaking.
He finished by telling us about his trip to Spain.
‘And that was all,’ she finished.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to come to an end; to bring something to an end
examples: The play finished at 10.30.
The symphony finishes with a flourish.
The evening finished with a few songs.
A cup of coffee finished the meal perfectly.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to eat, drink or use what remains of something
examples: I quickly finished my tea.
He finished off his drink with one large gulp.
We might as well finish up the cake.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be in a particular state or position at the end of a race or a competition
examples: She was delighted to finish second.
He finished 12 seconds outside the world record.
The team finished the season in ninth position.
The dollar finished the day slightly down.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody so tired or impatient that they cannot do any more
examples: Climbing that hill really finished me off.
A lecture from my parents now would just finish me.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the flames, light and heat, and often smoke, that are produced when something burns
examples: Most animals are afraid of fire.
When did people start to cook with fire?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: flames that are out of control and destroy buildings, trees, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO bush fire
Several youths had set fire to the police car (= had made it start burning).
The car was on fire.
A candle had set the curtains on fire.
These thatched roofs frequently catch fire (= start to burn).
Forest fires raged all over Australia.
Five people died in a house fire.
Fires were breaking out everywhere.
A fire had started in the kitchen.
He was accused of deliberately starting a fire.
Fire can spread very quickly.
The fire burned for three days before it was finally contained.
The warehouse was destroyed by fire.
It took two hours to put out the fire (= stop it burning).
Fire crews arrived and began to fight the flames.
We have to comply with fire safety regulations.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a pile of burning fuel, such as wood or coal, used for cooking food or heating a room
examples: SEE ALSO bonfire
They cook on an open fire.
a log/coal/wood fire
Sam had lit a fire to welcome us home.
to make/build a fire
Come and get warm by the fire.
We sat in front of a roaring fire.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a piece of equipment for heating a room
examples: SEE ALSO heater
a gas/an electric fire
Shall I put the fire on?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: shots from guns
examples: SEE ALSO friendly fire
The gunmen opened fire on (= started shooting at) the police.
Their vehicle came under fire (= was being shot at).
The men were under heavy fire (= being shot at many times).
He was hit by enemy fire.
a burst of machine-gun fire
artillery/rocket/mortar fire
to return fire (= to fire back at somebody who is shooting at you)
He ordered his men to hold their fire (= not to shoot).
Protesters exchanged fire with the guards (= they shot at each another).
A young girl was in the line of fire (= between the person shooting and what he/she was shooting at).
I’ll give you covering fire while you try to escape.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: strong criticism
examples: She directed her fire against the new education policy.
The health minister has come under fire from all sides.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: very strong emotion, especially anger or enthusiasm
examples: Her eyes were full of fire.
The fire seemed to die in him when his wife died.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a person who is full of energy and enthusiasm

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a difficult introduction to a new job or activity

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make somebody direct their anger, criticism, etc. at you, so that others do not have to face it

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to use similar methods in a fight or an argument to those your opponent is using

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a very strong desire to achieve something
examples: You need fire in your belly if you want to make it in the music business.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to become friends quickly and have a very friendly relationship

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to delay or be delayed in taking action
examples: The project had hung fire for several years for lack of funds.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be involved in several activities or areas of business at the same time, hoping that at least one will be successful

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: if something bad is being said about somebody/something, it usually has some truth in it

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: giving you a painful burning feeling
examples: He couldn't breathe. His chest was on fire.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: from a bad situation to one that is worse

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to act in a way that is not sensible and take dangerous risks

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to be very successful and admired by other people
examples: He's never going to set the world on fire with his paintings.

a close-fitting dress

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be of the right size, type or number to go somewhere
examples: I'd like to have a desk in the room but it won't fit.
All the kids will fit in the back of the car.

His arms fitted snugly around me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to put clothes on somebody and make them the right size and shape
examples: I'm going to be fitted for my wedding dress today.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to put or fix something somewhere
examples: They fitted a smoke alarm to the ceiling.
uPVC windows have been fitted throughout the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to put or join something in the right place
examples: The glass fits on top of the jug to form a lid.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to agree with, match or be suitable for something; to make something do this
examples: Something doesn't quite fit here.

The words fit perfectly with the music.
The facts certainly fit your theory.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something suitable for a particular job or situation
examples: His experience fitted him perfectly for the job.

Natural selection will see to it that animals are well fitted to survive in their environment.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be like a particular person or thing
examples: A child answering the description of the missing boy was found safe and well in London yesterday.

definitions.label: Meaning 10

examples: On paper, several of the applicants fit the bill.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

examples: The dress fits me like a glove.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to repair or correct something
examples: The car won't start—can you fix it?
I've fixed the problem.
Businesses and government have spent billions of dollars to find and fix the bug.
We need to get the TV fixed.
If you suspect that you have a fuel leak have it fixed as soon as possible.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to decide on a date, a time, an amount, etc. for something
examples: SYNONYM set
Has the date of the next meeting been fixed?
Their prices are fixed until the end of the year (= will not change before then).
A second trial date was fixed for 7th December.
They fixed the rent at £200 a week.
Crop prices were fixed at $ 1.98 per bushel for corn.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to arrange or organize something
examples: I'll fix a meeting.
You have to fix visits up in advance with the museum.
Just give me a list of your friends, and I'll fix things up for them.
Don't worry, I'll fix it with Sarah.
I’ve fixed up (for us) to go to the theatre next week.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to put something in a place so that it will not move
examples: to fix a shelf to the wall
to fix a post in the ground

He noted every detail so as to fix the scene in his mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to discover or say the exact position, time, etc. of something
examples: We can fix the ship's exact position at the time the fire broke out.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to provide or prepare something, especially food
examples: Can I fix you a drink?
I'm just going to fix myself some breakfast.
Can I fix a drink for you?
I'll fix supper.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make something such as your hair or face neat and attractive
examples: I'll fix my hair and then I'll be ready.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to arrange the result of something in a way that is not honest or fair
examples: I'm sure the race was fixed.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to punish somebody who has harmed you and stop them doing you any more harm
examples: Don't worry—I'll fix him.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to treat film for cameras, etc. with a chemical so that the colours do not change or become less bright

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make an animal unable to have young by means of an operation

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to intend to do something

definitions.label: Meaning 13

definitions.label: Meaning 23

definitions.label: Meaning 24

definitions.label: Meaning 26

examples: He seems to fly off the handle about the slightest thing these days.

definitions.label: Meaning 29

examples: As soon as the kids arrived, order went out of the window.

definitions.label: Meaning 30

definitions.label: Meaning 1

‘Look at me,’ he says, focusing the camera.

My gaze was focused elsewhere at the time.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: A laser focuses a beam of light.
She used her glasses to focus the sun's rays on the twigs and spark a fire.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to shine on somebody/something
examples: Suddenly a spotlight focused on us.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to come or go after or behind somebody/something
examples: Follow me please.
He followed her into the house.
They were followed down the street by a bunch of photographers.
Wherever she led, they followed.
Sam walked in, with the rest of the boys following closely behind.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to come or go after or behind somebody in order to watch where they go and what they do
examples: I think we're being followed.
Police followed the car along Station Road where it mounted the kerb again.
As she walked home, she had the feeling she was being followed.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to come after something/somebody else in time or order; to happen as a result of something else
examples: I remember little of the days that followed the accident.
A period of unrest followed the president's resignation.
The first two classes are followed by a break of ten minutes.
The main course was followed by fresh fruit.
I'll have soup and fish to follow.
A detailed news report will follow shortly.
There followed a short silence.
The opening hours are as follows…
A new proposal followed on from the discussions.
the workers' revolts that followed in the wake of the student uprising

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to do something after something else
examples: Give your contact details and follow this with a brief profile of yourself.
They follow up their March show with four UK dates next month.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to accept advice, instructions, etc. and do what you have been told or shown to do
examples: to follow rules/procedures/guidelines
They said they were just following orders.
He has trouble following simple instructions.
Why didn't you follow my advice?
Turn right and follow signs to Dundee.
I never follow a recipe completely.
He followed a strict diet.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to accept somebody/something as a guide, a leader or an example; to copy somebody/something
examples: I encourage others to follow our example.
The Senate is expected to follow the lead of the House.
We believe it is in our best interests to follow the path of economic openness and growth.
The movie follows the book faithfully.
They followed the teachings of Buddha.
He always followed the latest fashions (= dressed in fashionable clothes).
Where one airline leads, others follow.
Laura followed her mother into the medical profession (= became a doctor like her mother).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to click on a link in a website
examples: Follow the links to sign up for the webinar.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to go along a road, path, etc.
examples: Follow this road until you get to the school, then turn left.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to go in the same direction as something or parallel to something
examples: The lane follows the edge of a wood for about a mile.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be the logical result of something
examples: I don't see how that follows from what you've just said.
Several conclusions follow on from his statement.
If a = b and b = c it follows that a = c.
It does not necessarily follow that sleep loss would cause these symptoms.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to understand an explanation or the meaning of something
examples: Sorry, I don't follow.
Do you follow me?
I couldn't really follow his argument.
The plot is almost impossible to follow.
to be easy/difficult/hard to follow

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to watch or listen to somebody/something very carefully
examples: The children were following every word of the story intently.
Her eyes followed him everywhere (= she was looking at him all the time).

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to take an active interest in something and be aware of what is happening; to support a sports team
examples: We've been following this story for months.
Have you been following the basketball championships?
Millions of people followed the trial on TV.
In his leisure time he follows West Ham United.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to choose to regularly receive messages from a person, company, etc. using a social media service
examples: I don’t follow many celebrities on Twitter any more.

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.label: Meaning 16

definitions.label: Meaning 17

examples: She works in television, following in her father's footsteps.

definitions.label: Meaning 18

definitions.label: Meaning 19

definitions.label: Meaning 20

definitions.label: Meaning 21

definitions.label: Meaning 22

definitions.label: Meaning 1

In the following nights, Lucy slept poorly.

examples: I waited all day in the fond hope that she would change her mind.

to grow/cook/serve/eat food

baby food (= prepared especially for babies)
cat/dog/pet food (= for a cat/dog/pet to eat)

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: SYNONYM jester

examples: Quit playing the fool and get some work done!

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that something is very easy to do
examples: Any fool could tell she was lying.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: She's nobody's fool when it comes to dealing with difficult patients.
She's nobody's fool. She had the car checked by a mechanic before buying it.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 8

She was angry at having been made a fool of.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to do something stupid that makes other people think that you are a fool
examples: I made a complete fool of myself in front of everyone!

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that you think that somebody was stupid to do something, especially when it causes them problems
examples: ‘He's not an easy person to live with.’ ‘More fool her for marrying him!’

definitions.label: Meaning 13

examples: She was a forceful personality who didn't suffer fools gladly.

I've been on my feet (= standing or walking around) all day.

walking around the house in bare feet (= not wearing shoes or socks)
We were stamping our feet (= hitting them on the ground) to keep warm.
Please wipe your feet (= your shoes) on the mat.
The hot sand burned the soles of my feet.

a foot pump (= operated using your foot, not your hand)
a foot passenger (= one who travels on a ferry without a car)

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: What are the correct legal formulae for this kind of letter?
The minister keeps coming out with the same tired formulas.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to create or prepare something carefully, giving particular attention to the details
examples: to formulate a policy/theory/plan/proposal
The compost is specially formulated for pot plants.
This new kitchen cleaner is formulated to cut through grease and dirt.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to express your ideas in carefully chosen words
examples: She has lots of good ideas, but she has difficulty formulating them.
He struggled to formulate an answer.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: away from a place; out
examples: They set forth at dawn.
Huge chimneys belched forth smoke and grime.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: towards a place; forwards
examples: Water gushed forth from a hole in the rock.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used at the end of a list to show that it continues in the same way
examples: We discussed everything—when to go, what to see and so on.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: from one place to another and back again repeatedly
examples: ferries sailing back and forth between the islands

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: beginning on that day; from that time
examples: From that day forth she gave me endless friendship and encouragement.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: going to happen, be published, etc. very soon
examples: the forthcoming elections
a list of forthcoming books
the band’s forthcoming UK tour

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: ready or made available when needed
examples: Financial support was not forthcoming.
Help was immediately forthcoming.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: willing to give information about something
examples: OPPOSITE unforthcoming
She's never very forthcoming about her plans.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having or bringing an advantage, an opportunity, a piece of good luck, etc.
examples: SYNONYM lucky
Remember those less fortunate than yourselves.
I have been fortunate enough to visit many parts of the world as a lecturer.
I was fortunate in having a good teacher.
It was very fortunate for him that I arrived on time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: by good luck
examples: SYNONYM luckily
I was late, but fortunately the meeting hadn't started.
The documents fortunately survived the fire.
Fortunately or unfortunately, those times have passed.
Fortunately for him, he was very soon offered another job.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large amount of money
examples: He made a fortune in real estate.
Her father made his fortune selling electronics.
She inherited a share of the family fortune.
A car like that costs a small fortune (= a lot of money).
You don't have to spend a fortune to give your family tasty, healthy meals.
She is hoping her US debut will be the first step on the road to fame and fortune.
He amassed a fortune of nearly $2 billion.
She devoted a large part of her personal fortune to ensuring the company's survival.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: chance or luck, especially in the way it affects people’s lives
examples: I have had the good fortune to work with some brilliant directors.
By a stroke of fortune he found work almost immediately.
Fortune smiled on me (= I had good luck).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the good and bad things that happen to a person, family, country, etc.
examples: The share price tends to follow the changing fortunes of the film industry.
the fortunes of war
The company suffered a great reversal of fortune when public taste changed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person’s fate or future
examples: She can tell your fortune by looking at the lines on your hand.
They went to have their fortunes read.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: something that you have, or have promised to do, that could cause trouble or worry in the future

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to try to find a way to become rich, especially by going to another place
examples: Many emigrated to Australia to seek their fortune.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
examples: SEE ALSO Top 40

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: numbers, years or temperatures from 40 to 49

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: between the ages of 40 and 49

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an event or medium where people can exchange opinions and ideas on a particular issue; a meeting organized for this purpose
examples: SEE ALSO discussion forum (2)
to hold an international forum on drug abuse
Television is now an important forum for political debate.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a website or web page where users can put comments about a particular issue or topic and reply to other users' comments
examples: SEE ALSO discussion forum (1)
an internet forum
It's a forum where mothers can exchange advice, support and gossip.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: (in ancient Rome) a public place where meetings were heldWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (in sense (2)): from Latin, literally ‘what is out of doors’, originally denoting an enclosure surrounding a house; related to fores ‘(outside) door’. Sense (1) dates from the mid 18th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: towards a place or position that is in front
examples: OPPOSITE back
She leaned forward and kissed him on the cheek.
He took two steps forwards.
They ran forward to welcome her.
The procession slowly moved forward.
Turn your wrists so that your palms face forward.
He stands by the fire, rocking backward and forward.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: towards the future; ahead in time
examples: SEE ALSO flash-forward
Looking forward, we hope to expand our operations in several of our overseas branches.
The next scene takes the story forwards five years.
The series moves back and forward through time.
from this day forward

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: towards a good result
examples: OPPOSITE backwards
We consider this agreement to be an important step forward.
Cutting our costs is the only way forward.
We are not getting any further forward with the discussion.
The project will go forward (= continue) as planned.
The 21st century has seen trade between the two countries leap forward.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: earlier; sooner
examples: It was decided to bring the meeting forward two weeks.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in or towards the front part of a ship or plane
examples: The main cabin is situated forward of (= in front of) the mast.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: from one place or position to another and back again many times
examples: She rocked backwards and forwards on her chair.
The film skips backwards and forwards through time.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in the future, starting from now
examples: We have a very solid financial position going forward.
The strategy going forward is still undecided.
Moving forward, we need to have a real plan.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to make a great effort to do something, especially if it is difficult or you are feeling tired

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to change the time shown by clocks, usually by one hour, when the time changes officially, for example at the beginning and end of summer
examples: Remember to put your clocks back tonight.
