definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the parts of a dead animal or a plant that have become hard and turned into rock
examples: fossils over two million years old

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an old person, especially one who is unable to accept new ideas or adapt to changesWord Origin
examples: mid 16th cent. (denoting a fossilized fish found, and believed to have lived, underground): from French fossile, from Latin fossilis ‘dug up’, from fodere ‘dig’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to encourage something to develop
examples: SYNONYM encourage
The club's aim is to foster better relations within the community.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take another person’s child into your home for a period of time, without becoming his or her legal parents
examples: COMPARE adopt
They have fostered over 60 children during the past ten years.
We couldn't adopt a child, so we decided to foster.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to start something, such as an organization or an institution, especially by providing money
examples: SYNONYM establish
to found a club/company/school
Her family founded the college in 1895.
the founding members of the European Union
He was a founding editor of the journal.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be the first to start building and living in a town or country
examples: The town was founded by English settlers in 1790.
French settlers founded New Orleans.
the founding generation of immigrants

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to base something on something
examples: SEE ALSO ill-founded
Their marriage was founded on love and mutual respect.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to melt metal and pour it into a mould; to make objects using this process
examples: PAST TENSE, PAST PARTICIPLE OF find

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a principle, an idea or a fact that something is based on and that it grows from
examples: Respect and friendship provide a solid foundation for marriage.
He laid the foundation of Japan's modern economy.
These stories have no foundation (= are not based on any facts).
The rumour is totally without foundation (= is not based on any facts).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an organization that is established to provide money for a particular purpose, for example for scientific research or charity
examples: The money will go to the San Francisco AIDS Foundation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of starting a new institution or organization
examples: SYNONYM establishment
The organization has grown enormously since its foundation in 1955.
She used the money to go towards the foundation of a special research group.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a layer of stone, concrete, etc. that forms the solid underground base of a building
examples: The builders are now beginning to lay the foundations of the new school.
The explosion shook the foundations of the houses nearby.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a skin-coloured cream that is put on the face under other make-up

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to cause people to question their basic beliefs about something
examples: This issue has shaken the foundations of French politics.
an event which rocked the foundations of British politics
The scandal rocked the legal establishment to its foundations.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who starts an organization, institution, etc. or causes something to be built
examples: the founder and president of the company
a wife and husband who are joint founders of the company

definitions.label: Meaning 1
examples: There are only four cookies left.
four of Sweden’s top financial experts
Ten people were invited but only four turned up.
Can you lend me four dollars?
a four-month contract
Look at page four.
Five and four is nine.
Three fours are twelve.
I can't read your writing—is this meant to be a four?
The bulbs are planted in threes or fours (= groups of three or four).
We moved to America when I was four (= four years old).
Shall we meet at four (= at four o'clock), then?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of four people or things
examples: SEE ALSO Final Four
to make up a four at tennis
a coach and four (= four horses)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a hit that scores four runs (= points)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a team of four people who row a long narrow boat in races; the boat that they row

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: bent over with hands and knees on the ground
examples: We were crawling around on all fours.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when you are talking about keeping something secret
examples: Don't let this go further than these four walls (= Don't tell anyone else who is not in the room now).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: 14Word Origin
examples: Old English fēowertīene (from four and -teen).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: 4th
examples: Today is the fourth (of May).
the fourth century BC
It's her fourth birthday.
My office is on the fourth floor.
It's the fourth time that I've been to America.
Her mother had just given birth to another child, her fourth.
the world’s fourth-largest oil exporter
He finished fourth in the race.
Edward IV (= Edward the Fourth)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small part or amount of something
examples: Only a small fraction of a bank's total deposits will be withdrawn at any one time.
She hesitated for the merest fraction of a second.
He raised his voice a fraction.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a division of a number, for example ⅝
examples: SYNONYM rational number
How do you express 25% as a fraction?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a quantity of liquid that has been collected as a result of a process that separates the parts of a liquid mixture
examples: The third fraction contains alchohols with boiling points of 120–130℃.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: easily broken or damaged
examples: fragile china/glass/bones
Be careful not to drop it; it’s very fragile.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: weak and uncertain; easy to destroy or harm
examples: a fragile alliance/ceasefire/relationship
The economy remains extremely fragile.
In her job she was used to dealing with actors’ fragile egos.
fragile habitats threatened by pollution

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: thin or light and often beautiful
examples: fragile beauty
The woman's fragile face broke into a smile.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not strong and likely to become ill
examples: Her father is now 86 and in fragile health.
I'm feeling a bit fragile after last night (= not well, perhaps because of drinking too much alcohol).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small part of something that has broken off or comes from something larger
examples: Police found fragments of glass near the scene.
The shattered vase lay in fragments on the floor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a single part of something; a part that is not complete
examples: I overheard a fragment of their conversation.
She could recall only fragments of his poetry.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong border or structure of wood, metal, etc. that holds a picture, door, piece of glass, etc. in position
examples: a picture/photo frame
aluminium window frames
I'm going to paint the door frame white.
She leaned against the frame of the door.
pictures in gold frames

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the supporting structure of a piece of furniture, a building, a vehicle, etc. that gives it its shape
examples: SEE ALSO A-frame
a bicycle frame
The bed frame is made of pine.
the frame of an aircraft/a car/a bicycle
In the 1920s, federal office buildings were typically built with steel frames encased in concrete or granite.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a structure of plastic or metal that holds the lenses in a pair of glasses
examples: gold-rimmed frames

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the form or structure of a person or animal’s body
examples: to have a small/slender/large frame
The bed was shorter than his six-foot frame.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the general ideas or structure that form the background to something
examples: SEE ALSO time frame
In this course we hope to look at literature in the frame of its social and historical context.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: one of the single photographs that a film or video is made of
examples: SEE ALSO freeze-frame

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a single picture in a comic strip

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: one of the separate areas on an internet page that you can scroll through (= read by moving the text up or down)

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a small wooden or metal frame covered with glass that you grow seeds or small plants in to protect them from cold weather

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a single section of play in the game of snooker, etc., or in bowling
examples: He won the first frame easily.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: be taking part/not taking part in something
examples: We won our match, so we're still in the frame for the championship.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be wanted/not wanted by the police because you are/are not suspected of having committed a crime
examples: He was always in the frame for the killing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the parts of a building or an object that support its weight and give it shape
examples: built on a wooden framework
The ship's elaborate metal framework was exposed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set of beliefs, ideas or rules that is used as the basis for making judgements, decisions, etc.
examples: a theoretical/conceptual framework
The report provides a framework for further research.
We are currently exploring new approaches within existing frameworks of practice and thinking.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the structure of a particular system
examples: the basic framework of society
a regulatory/legislative framework
We need to establish a legal framework for the protection of the environment.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: formal permission given by a company to somebody who wants to sell its goods or services in a particular area; formal permission given by a government to somebody who wants to operate a public service as a business
examples: a franchise agreement/company
a catering/rail franchise
In the reorganization, Southern Television lost their franchise.
to operate a business under franchise

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a business or service run under franchise
examples: They operate franchises in London and Paris.
He's got a job as manager of a burger franchise.
He runs a local pizza franchise.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the right to vote in a country’s elections
examples: universal adult franchise
The 1918 Reform Act extended the franchise to women over 30.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a set of films in which the same characters appear in related stories
examples: Disney has successfully revived the ‘Star Wars’ franchise, with four films already released and more in the works.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in an honest and direct way that people might not like
examples: He spoke frankly about the ordeal.
They frankly admitted their responsibility.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to show that you are being honest about something, even though people might not like what you are saying
examples: Frankly, I couldn't care less what happens to him.
Quite frankly, I'm not surprised you failed.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the crime of cheating somebody in order to get money or goods illegally
examples: SEE ALSO wire fraud
She was charged with credit card fraud.
It was said that the property had been obtained by fraud.
He helped prevent a $100 million fraud.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who pretends to have qualities, abilities, etc. that they do not really have in order to cheat other people
examples: He's nothing but a liar and a fraud.
She felt a fraud accepting their sympathy (= because she was not really sad).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that is not as good, useful, etc. as people claim it isWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French fraude, from Latin fraus, fraud- ‘deceit, injury’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: without particular plans or arrangements; not busy
examples: Are you free on Saturday? We're having a barbecue.
We try to keep Sundays free.
If Sarah is free for lunch I'll take her out.
Keep Friday night free for my party.
What do you like to do in your free time (= when you are not working)?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not being used
examples: He held out his free hand and I took it.
Is this seat free?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: costing nothing
examples: Admission is free.
free software/tickets
We even offer a free web design service.
We''ll give you a fabulous free gift with each copy you buy.
Use of the pool is free to members.
Updates are free for registered users.
You can't expect people to work for free (= without payment).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not under the control or in the power of somebody else; able to do what you want
examples: I have no ambitions other than to have a happy life and be free.
Students have a free choice of modules in their final year.
You are free to leave at any time.
The government wants to leave companies free to make their own decisions.
The organization wants to remain free from government control.
We want an independent state free of foreign interference.
‘Can I sit here?’ ‘Please, feel free (= of course you can).’
Feel free to email me if you have any questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not limited or controlled by anyone else
examples: A true democracy needs free speech and a free press.
He called for free and fair elections.
They gave me free access to all the files.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not a prisoner or slave
examples: He walked out of jail a free man.
The hostages were all set free.
The hacker is currently free on bail.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not tied up or in a cage
examples: The researchers set the birds free.
Our livestock is free to roam.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: clear; not blocked
examples: Ensure there is a free flow of air around the machine.
the free movement of traffic

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: not containing or affected by something harmful or unpleasant
examples: free from artificial colours and flavourings
Everyone deserves to live free from fear.
free of defects/problems/symptoms
Beef producers want their herds free of disease.
It was several weeks before he was completely free of pain.
We've managed to keep the garden free of weeds this year.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: without the thing mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO duty-free
pure, additive-free ingredients
a trouble-free life
After six months of treatment he is cancer-free.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: not attached to something; not stuck somewhere and unable to move
examples: Pull gently on the free end of the rope.
She finally managed to pull herself free.
They tied him up but he managed to get free.
They had to be cut free from their car after the accident.
The boat had broken free of its moorings.
They swam free of the wreckage.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: ready to give something, especially when it is not wanted
examples: He's too free with his opinions.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a free translation is not exact but gives the general meaning
examples: COMPARE literal

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to have done something successfully, especially when it was difficult
examples: I could see the finish line and thought I was home free.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: informal; relaxed
examples: Life was never going to be so free and easy again.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: if you give somebody a free pass or somebody gets a free pass, they are not punished for something bad they have done, or they are given permission to do something bad
examples: This time he gets a free pass but if he does it again, he’ll be sent to jail.
Just because someone has expensive designer gear, it doesn't mean they have a free pass to be mean to my staff.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to get, have, etc. the opportunity to do what you want to do and to make your own decisions
examples: I was given a free hand in designing the syllabus.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to get or take something without paying because somebody else is paying for it

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to give somebody complete freedom of action; to allow a feeling to be expressed freely
examples: The designer was given free rein.
The script allows full rein to her larger-than-life acting style.
When I paint I just give my imagination free rein.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used as a reply when somebody suggests that you should not do something, or when somebody has asked permission or said they are going to do something
examples: It's a free country; I'll say what I like!
Wear what you like. It's a free country.
‘It's a free country!’ he shouted. ‘I can do what I like!’

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used to say that it is not possible to get something for nothing

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to be allowed to leave court, etc., without receiving any punishment
examples: She was acquitted and walked free from court.

Used as a general term of abuse in Middle English, the term was applied specifically to the Dutch in the 17th cent.; its application to the French (late 18th cent.) is partly alliterative, partly from the reputation of the French for eating frogs' legs.

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: The shares gained 14p to 262p.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: At last she gained the shelter of the forest.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: If the price goes up again, he may decide that the game’s not worth the candle.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.definition: if you buy cooked food to go in a restaurant or shop, you buy it to take away and eat somewhere else
examples: Two pizzas to go.

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: the way somebody behaves towards other people will affect the way those people behave towards them in the future

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: something that is not fashionable now will become fashionable again in the future

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: used to ask what action somebody should take, especially in order to improve the difficult situation that they are in

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: used by a soldier who is guarding a place to order somebody to say who they are
examples: Halt, who goes there?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a frame with a net into which players must kick or hit the ball in order to score a point
examples: He headed the ball into an open goal (= one that had nobody defending it).
Nicky Roberts was outstanding in goal (= as goalkeeper).
The goalkeeper was injured so a defender had to go in goal.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of kicking or hitting the ball into the goal; a point that is scored for this
examples: SEE ALSO drop goal
She scored twenty goals in her first season.
United conceded two goals in the first half.
Liverpool won by three goals to one.
The winning goal came in the 71st minute.
a penalty goal

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that you hope to achieve
examples: SYNONYM aim
to achieve/accomplish/reach a goal
My job is to help businesses meet their goals.
You need to set yourself some long-term goals.
Their goal was to eradicate malaria.
Their primary goal is to make a profit.
Our ultimate goal must be the preservation of the environment.
We are all working towards a common goal.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the being or spirit that is worshipped and is believed to have created the universe
examples: Do you believe in God?
Good luck and God bless you.
Christians believe that Jesus is the Son of God.
I swear by Almighty God that the evidence I shall give… (= in a court of law)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: (in some religions) a being or spirit who is believed to have power over a particular part of nature or who is believed to represent a particular quality
examples: SEE ALSO goddess
Greek gods
the sun/rain god
Mars was the Roman god of war.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is loved or admired very much by other people
examples: SEE ALSO goddess
To her fans she's a god.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: something to which too much importance or attention is given
examples: Money is his god.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the seats that are high up at the back of a theatre
examples: We could only afford to sit in the gods.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an event caused by natural forces beyond human control, such as a storm, a flood or an earthquake

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a feeling of surprise or that you are determined to do something

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when you are expressing anger and the fact that you are impatient
examples: For the love of God, tell me what he said!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to emphasize what you are saying when you are surprised, shocked or annoyed
examples: God, what a stupid thing to do!

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used when you are leaving somebody, to say that you hope they will be safe, etc.
examples: Goodnight, God bless.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that you hope that something will not happen
examples: ‘Maybe you'll end up as a lawyer, like me.’ ‘God forbid!’

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say that you are afraid somebody will be in danger or that something bad will happen to them
examples: God help us if this doesn't work.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you do not know something
examples: God knows what else they might find.
‘Where are they?’ ‘Goodness knows.’

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the truth of what you are saying
examples: She ought to pass the exam—goodness knows she's been working hard enough.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to show respect when you are talking about somebody who is dead

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: a person who thinks that they are particularly good at something or who thinks that somebody will find them particularly attractive
examples: He seems to think he's God's gift to women.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to say that you hope that things will happen as you have planned and that there will be no problems
examples: I'll be back next week, God willing.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that you are frightened of the idea of something happening
examples: Heaven forfend that students are encouraged to think!

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that what you are saying is true
examples: SEE ALSO honest-to-goodness
Honest to God, Mary, I'm not joking.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used especially in questions to show that you are angry, surprised or shocked
examples: What in God's name was that noise?
Where in the name of Heaven have you been?

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: if the result of something is in the lap of the gods, you do not know what will happen because it depends on luck or things you cannot control

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: a religious man, especially a priest or a clergyman

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to behave as if you control events or other people’s lives
examples: It is unfair to ask doctors to play God and end someone's life.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used to say that you very much hope or wish that something will happen or not happen
examples: Please God, don't let him be dead.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to make somebody very frightened, especially in order to make them do something

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: used to swear that what you are saying is true, especially in a court of law

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: used to say that you are pleased about something
examples: Thank God you're safe!
‘Thank goodness for that!’ she said with a sigh of relief.
Thank heavens I've found my keys.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: used to say that you could easily have been in the same difficult or unpleasant situation that somebody else is in

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: used after a verb to emphasize a particular hope, wish, etc.
examples: I wish to God you'd learn to pay attention!

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: used to show surprise, lack of belief, etc.Word Origin
examples: Old English, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch god and German Gott.

definitions.label: Meaning 15

examples: Good old Jack!

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used in exclamations
examples: Good heavens!

definitions.label: Meaning 17

definitions.label: Meaning 19

definitions.label: Meaning 20

examples: a good story/joke
That's a good one!

definitions.label: Meaning 21

examples: You're good for (= you will live) a few years yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: acceptable for something
examples: The ticket is good for three months.

definitions.label: Meaning 23

examples: The flour is ground using traditional methods.

definitions.definition: to press or rub something into a surface
examples: He ground his cigarette into the ashtray.

examples: Parts of the machine were grinding together noisily.

The climber slipped and lost her grip.
She struggled from his grip.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: The home team took a firm grip on the game.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: Don't let him persuade you—stand your ground.

definitions.label: Meaning 26

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give a written promise to replace or repair a product free if it goes wrong
examples: All our electrical goods are fully guaranteed.
This iron is guaranteed for a year against faulty workmanship.

definitions.definition: to make something certain to happen
examples: Tonight's victory guarantees the team's place in the final.
These days getting a degree doesn't guarantee you a job.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be certain that something will happen

definitions.label: Meaning 5

His father agreed to guarantee the bank loan.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be certain to have a particular result
examples: If we try to keep it a secret, she's guaranteed to find out.
That kind of behaviour is guaranteed to make him angry.

prison/border guards

The prisoner slipped past the guards on the gate and escaped.
A guard was posted outside the building.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act or duty of protecting property, places or people from attack or danger; the act or duty of preventing prisoners from escaping
examples: a sentry on guard (= at his or her post, on duty)
to be on guard duty

The terrorist was kept under police guard.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a group of people, such as soldiers or police officers, who protect somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO advance guard
the captain of the guard
the changing of the guard (= when one group replaces another)

examples: the Scots Guards
a Guards officer

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: conductor (= a person who is in charge of a train and travels with it, but does not drive it)

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: SEE ALSO pulling guard

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: either of two equal parts into which something is or can be divided
examples: SEE ALSO halve
two and a half kilos (= 2½)

in the first half of the 20th century
The second half of the book is more exciting.
The two halves of the city were reunited in 1990.
the left half of the brain
the lower half of the window
the northern half of the country
I've divided the money in half.
We'll need to reduce the weight by half.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: either of two periods of time into which a sports game, concert, etc. is divided
examples: No goals were scored in the first half.
She played well in the second half of the match.
He made two superb saves in the first two minutes of the half.
We had a few chances to score in both halves.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: one of the defending players in hockey or rugby whose position is between those who play at the front of a team and those who play at the back
examples: SEE ALSO scrum half

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the position a half back plays at (also called a tailback in american football)

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: half a pint (= 0.568 of a litre in the UK and some other countries, and 0.473 of a litre in the US) of beer or a similar drink
examples: Two halves of bitter, please.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: bigger, better, more important, etc. than usual
examples: That was a game and a half!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to do whatever you do completely and to the greatest possible degree
examples: You're expecting twins? Well, you never did do anything by halves.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to share the cost of something equally with somebody
examples: We go halves on all the bills.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used in negative sentences to say that a situation is worse or more complicated than somebody thinks
examples: ‘It sounds very difficult.’ ‘You don't know the half of it.’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that you think you will do something, although you are not sure
examples: I've half a mind to come with you tomorrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say that there is not much real difference between two possible choices

definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that you feel sorry for them
examples: ‘Failed again, I'm afraid.’ ‘Oh, hard luck.’

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: a difficult problem or situation to deal with

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: a person or event that is so good or successful at something that it will be difficult for anyone/anything else coming after them to be as good or successful
examples: She has been an excellent principal and will be a hard act to follow.
Their contribution will prove a tough act to follow.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: by having an unpleasant experience or by making mistakes
examples: She won't listen to my advice so she'll just have to learn the hard way.
He learned about the dangers of drugs the hard way.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to have difficulty doing something
examples: You'll have a job convincing them that you're right.
He had a hard job to make himself heard.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to use more time or energy on a task than is necessary

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: used after you have been arguing with somebody or have beaten them in a contest but you would still like to be friendly with them
examples: It looks like I'm the winner again. No hard feelings, Dave, eh?
Someone has to lose. No hard feelings, eh?

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to make yourself seem more attractive or interesting by not immediately accepting an invitation to do something

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to consider a problem or possibility very carefully and without hurrying
examples: We need to take a long, hard look at all the options.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: needing too much effort
examples: I can't be bothered making a hot meal—it's too much like hard work.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: almost no; almost not; almost none
examples: There's hardly any tea left.
Hardly anyone has bothered to reply.
She hardly ever calls me (= almost never).
We hardly know each other.
I had hardly seen my father since that day.
It hardly seems fair to put all the blame on him.
Hardly a day goes by without my thinking of her (= I think of her almost every day).
At the time, I hardly spoke any French.
There was hardly a cloud in the sky.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used especially after ‘can’ or ‘could’ and before the main verb, to emphasize that it is difficult to do something
examples: I can hardly keep my eyes open (= I'm almost falling asleep).
I could hardly believe it when I read the letter.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to suggest that something is unlikely or unreasonable or that somebody is silly for saying or doing something
examples: He is hardly likely to admit he was wrong.
It's hardly surprising she was fired; she never did any work.
It's hardly the time to discuss it now.
You can hardly expect her to do it for free.
‘Couldn't you have just said no?’ ‘Well, hardly (= of course not), she's my wife's sister.’
He’s 24—hardly a baby.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that something has just begun, happened, etc.
examples: We can't stop for coffee now, we've hardly started.
We had hardly sat down to supper when the phone rang.
Hardly had she spoken before she regretted it bitterly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the machines and electronic parts in a computer or other electronic system
examples: COMPARE software

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: tools and equipment that are used in the house and garden
examples: a hardware shop/store

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the equipment, machines and vehicles used to do something
examples: tanks and other military hardware

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: damage or injury that is caused by a person or an event
examples: SEE ALSO actual bodily harm
He would never frighten anyone or cause them any harm.
The accused clearly intended to inflict harm on him.
He may look fierce, but he means no harm.
No definite harm to human health has been determined.
The court case will do serious harm to my business.
The accident could have been much worse; luckily no harm was done.
Don't worry, we'll see that the children come to no harm.
I can't say I like Mark very much, but I don't wish him any harm.
Hard work never did anyone any harm.
Look, we're just going out for a few drinks, where's the harm in that?
The treatment they gave him did him more harm than good.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to suggest that it would be a good idea for somebody to do something
examples: It wouldn't do you any harm to smarten yourself up.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody not to worry because they have caused no serious damage or injury
examples: Forget it, Dave, no harm done.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in a safe place where somebody/something cannot be hurt or injured or do any damage to somebody/something
examples: She put the knife in a drawer, out of harm’s way.
I prefer the children to play in the garden where they’re out of harm’s way.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that something is a good idea and will not cause any problems
examples: He may say no, but there's no harm in asking.
It does no harm to ask.

social/racial harmony

passionate lyrics and stunning vocal harmonies

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to collect money from a number of people, for example to buy a present for somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 14

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.label: Meaning 23

definitions.label: Meaning 26

definitions.label: Meaning 27

definitions.label: Meaning 28

examples: We had some friends to dinner last night.

definitions.label: Meaning 29

definitions.label: Meaning 38

definitions.label: Meaning 29

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that you are afraid somebody will be in danger or that something bad will happen to them
examples: God help us if this doesn't work.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to swear that what you are saying is true, especially in a court of lawWord Origin
examples: Old English helpan (verb), help (noun), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch helpen and German helfen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make it easier or possible for somebody to do something by doing something for them or by giving them something that they need
examples: What can I do to help?
I was only trying to help!
He always helps with the housework.
They are trying their best to do a good job and help others.
Jo will help us with some of the organization.
Following these steps will help in protecting our environment.
Come and help me lift this box.
This charity aims to help people to help themselves.
The college's aim is to help students achieve their aspirations.
She helped organize the party.
Some history may help to explain why this is.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to improve a situation; to make it easier for something to happen
examples: The support of our families has helped enormously.
It helped being able to talk about it.
It certainly helped that her father is a duke!
The money raised will help towards (= partly pay for) the cost of organizing the championships.
It doesn't really help matters knowing that everyone is talking about us.
This should help to reduce the pain.
We need new measures to help fight terrorism.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to help somebody move or do some other action by letting them lean on you, guiding them, etc.
examples: She helped him to his feet.
We were helped ashore by local people.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to give yourself/somebody food, drinks, etc.
examples: If you want another drink, just help yourself.
Can I help you to some more salad?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to take something without permission
examples: SYNONYM steal
He'd been helping himself to the money in the cash register.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that it is impossible to prevent or avoid something
examples: I can't help thinking he knows more than he has told us.
He can’t help being ugly.
She couldn't help but wonder what he was thinking.
It couldn't be helped (= there was no way of avoiding it and we must accept it).
He never does more work than he can help (= he does as little as possible).
I always end up having an argument with her, I don't know why, I just can't help it.
I couldn't help it if the bus was late (= it wasn't my fault).
She burst out laughing—she couldn't help herself (= couldn't stop herself).
She won’t be invited again, not if I can help it (= if I can do anything to prevent it).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to help somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: able to improve a particular situation

helpful hints/tips/suggestions/comments

You may find it helpful to read this before making any decisions.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: willing to help somebody
examples: I called the police but they weren't very helpful.
The staff couldn't have been more helpful.
She’s one of the most helpful people I know.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: for this reason
examples: We suspect they are trying to hide something, hence the need for an independent inquiry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a number of days, etc. from now
examples: The true consequences will only be known several years hence.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used as the object of a verb, after the verb be or after a preposition to refer to a woman or girl who has already been mentioned or is easily identified
examples: COMPARE she
We're going to call her Sophie.
Please give her my regards.
The manager will be free soon—you can wait for her here.
That must be her now.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used as the object of a verb, after the verb be or after a preposition to refer to a woman or girl who has already been mentioned or is easily identified
examples: COMPARE she

That must be her now.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a plant whose leaves, flowers or seeds are used to add taste to food, in medicines or for their pleasant smell. parsley, mint and oregano are all herbs.
examples: a herb garden
an herb garden

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a plant with a soft stem that dies down after floweringWord Origin
examples: Middle English: via Old French from Latin herba ‘grass, green crops, herb’. Although herb has always been spelled with an h, pronunciation without the h was usual until the 19th cent. and is still standard in the US.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used after a verb or preposition to mean ‘in, at or to this position or place’
examples: I live here.
Put the box here.
Click here for more details.
Let's get out of here.
Come over here.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used when you are giving or showing something to somebody
examples: Here's the money I promised you.
Here's a dish that is simple and quick to make.
Here is your opportunity.
Here comes the bus.
I can't find my keys. Oh, here they are.
Here we are (= we've arrived).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to show your role in a situation
examples: I'm here to help you.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: now; at this point
examples: The countdown to Christmas starts here.
Here the speaker paused to have a drink.
My friend here saw it happen.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: here; to here
examples: Come by here now!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the present time; at the present time
examples: our obsession with the here and now
We're going to settle this here and now.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in various places
examples: Papers were scattered here and there on the floor.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when you are telling people that you are just going to do something exciting, dangerous, etc.
examples: ‘Here goes,’ said Grace and took a deep breath.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to wish somebody health or success, as you lift a glass and drink a toast
examples: Here's to your future happiness!

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: in many different places; all around

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: said when something is starting to happen
examples: ‘Here we go,’ thought Fred, ‘she's sure to say something.’

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: said when something is starting to happen again, especially something bad

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used when you are giving something to somebody
examples: Here you are. This is what you were asking for.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used when you are giving something to somebody
examples: Here you go. Four copies, is that right?

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: not important
examples: SYNONYM irrelevant
What might have happened is neither here nor there.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: going or leaving
examples: As soon as I get my money I'm out of here!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the history, traditions, buildings and objects that a country or society has had for many years and that are considered an important part of its character
examples: Spain’s rich cultural heritage
The building is part of our national heritage.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to describe a traditional product, brand, type of animal or plant variety, especially one that is old-fashioned, rare and of high quality
examples: Cotswold sheep are considered a heritage breed in Canada.
Heritage carrots are not always orange in colour.
They work with some of Britain's oldest heritage brands, including Jaguar, Harrods and the BBC.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person, especially a man, who is admired by many people for doing something brave or good
examples: SEE ALSO folk hero
a war hero (= somebody who was very brave during a war)
a hero of the First World War
one of the country’s national heroes
His charity work has made him something of a local hero.
The Olympic team were given a hero's welcome on their return home.
Scientists like her are typically unsung heroes (= people who are not praised or famous but deserve to be).
He was hailed as a hero after the rescue.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the main male character in a story, novel, film, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO anti-hero
The hero of the novel is a ten-year old boy.
action heroes like Bruce Willis

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person, especially a man, that you admire because of a particular quality or skill that they have
examples: my childhood hero
He became a hero to millions for his decision to oppose the government's reforms.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a long bread roll split open along its length and filled with various types of foodWord Origin
examples: Middle English (with mythological reference): via Latin from Greek hērōs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: of or belonging to her
examples: His eyes met hers.
The choice was hers.
a friend of hers

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used when the woman or girl who performs an action is also affected by it
examples: She hurt herself.
She must be very proud of herself.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the female subject or object of a sentence
examples: She told me the news herself.
Jane herself was at the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be in a normal state of health or happiness
examples: She didn't seem quite herself this morning.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not influenced by other people
examples: She needed space to be herself.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: alone; without anyone else
examples: She lives by herself.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: without help
examples: She runs the business by herself.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: for only her to have or use; not shared
examples: She wants a room all to herself.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be slow to speak or act because you feel uncertain or nervous
examples: She hesitated before replying.
He seemed to hesitate a second.
When she hesitated over her order, the waiter gave her an impatient look.
I didn't hesitate for a moment about taking the job.
She stood there, hesitating over whether or not to tell him the truth.
‘I'm not sure,’ she hesitated.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be worried about doing something, especially because you are not sure that it is right or appropriate
examples: Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any queries.
If you'd like me to send you the book, then please don't hesitate to ask.
She never hesitated to speak her mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if you delay in doing something you may lose a good opportunityWord Origin
examples: early 17th cent.: from Latin haesitat- ‘stuck fast, left undecided’, from the verb haesitare, from haerere ‘stick, stay’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to attract somebody’s attention or to express interest, surprise or anger
examples: Hey, can I just ask you something?
Hey, leave my things alone!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say hello
examples: SYNONYM hi
Hey, Jake! How are you doing?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to show that you do not really care about something or that you think it is not important
examples: That's the third time I've been late this week—but hey!—who's counting?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used at the end of a statement, to show that you have finished speaking, or to form a question or invite somebody to reply
examples: Thanks for your help, hey.
My new bike's nice, hey?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that something does not matter or that you do not care about it
examples: This is probably a bad idea, but what the hey!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to say hello
examples: Hi guys!
Hi, there! How're you doing?
Say hi to her from me.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that is hidden is kept or located in a place where it cannot be seen
examples: Hidden dangers lurk in the ocean depths.
A reporter wearing a hidden camera got footage of the abuse.
This tiny museum is a hidden treasure of the city's Old Quarter.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: secret
examples: She felt sure the letter had some hidden meaning.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to put or keep somebody/something in a place where they/it cannot be seen or found
examples: SYNONYM conceal
He hid the letter in a drawer.
I keep my private papers hidden.
They hid me from the police in their attic.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to go somewhere where you hope you will not be seen or found
examples: Quick, hide!
I hid under the bed.
We hid from our pursuers in an empty house.
She hides herself away in her office all day.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to cover somebody/something so that they/it cannot be seen
examples: SYNONYM conceal
He hid his face in his hands.
The house was hidden by trees.
The brim of his hat hid half his face.
No amount of make-up could hide her age.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to keep something secret, especially your feelings
examples: SYNONYM conceal
They didn't try to hide the fact that the film was a remake.
I have never tried to hide the truth about my past.
She struggled to hide her disappointment.
They claim that they have nothing to hide (= there was nothing wrong or illegal about what they did).
His brusque manner hides a shy and sensitive nature.
I could not hide my joy at seeing him again.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to refuse to admit that a problem exists or refuse to deal with it

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to hide the real situation or facts when these are not good or pleasant
examples: She was dressed in loose comfortable clothes that hid a multitude of sins.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to not let people know that you are good at something

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that whatever you do, you cannot escape the consequences of your actionsWord Origin
examples: verb Old English hȳdan, of West Germanic origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a system, especially in a society or an organization, in which people are organized into different levels of importance from highest to lowest
examples: the social/political hierarchy
She's quite high up in the management hierarchy.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the group of people in control of a large organization or institution
examples: It was on orders from the party hierarchy that she dropped the investigation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a system that ideas or beliefs can be arranged into according to their importance
examples: a hierarchy of needs

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: measuring a long distance from the bottom to the top
examples: OPPOSITE low
What's the highest mountain in the US?
The house has a high wall all the way round it.
shoes with high heels
He has a round face with a high forehead.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to talk about the distance that something measures from the bottom to the top
examples: How high is Everest?
It's only a low wall—about a metre high.
The grass was waist-high.
knee-high boots

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: at a level that is a long way above the ground or above the level of the sea
examples: a high branch/shelf/window
The rooms had high ceilings.
streaks of high cloud
They were flying at high altitude.
the grasslands of the high prairies

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: greater or better than normal in quantity or quality, size or degree
examples: a high price/cost/speed/temperature
a high rate of inflation
high levels of pollution
Demand is high at this time of year.
high-quality goods
a high risk of injury
a high standard of craftsmanship
A high proportion of our staff are female.
Originally, an even higher percentage of land was wetlands.
A high degree of accuracy is needed.
The cost in terms of human life was high.
Sales were significantly higher than in previous years.
The tree blew over in the high winds.
We had high hopes for the business (= we believed it would be successful).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: containing a lot of a particular substance
examples: OPPOSITE low
a high potassium content
a high-fat diet
foods that are high in fat
Oranges are high in vitamin C.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: near the top in rank, status or importance
examples: OPPOSITE low
She has held high office under three prime ministers.
The case was referred to a higher court.
the distinction between high art and popular art
Job security is high on his list of priorities.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: of great value
examples: to play for high stakes
My highest card is ten.
At the moment, the euro is high against the dollar, which makes for a good exchange rate.
The high dollar is still a major problem for importers.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: when a river or the tide is high, the water reaches a long way up the river bank, beach, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO high tide
The river was very high and threatening to flood.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: morally good
examples: a man of high ideals/principles

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: showing a lot of approval or respect for somebody
examples: OPPOSITE low
She is held in very high regard by her colleagues.
You seem to have a high opinion of yourself!

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: at the upper end of the range of sounds that humans can hear; not deep or low
examples: OPPOSITE low
She has a high voice.
That note is definitely too high for me.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to describe the middle or the most attractive part of a period of time
examples: high noon
high summer

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: beginning to go bad and having a strong smell

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: behaving in an excited way because of the effects of alcohol or drugs
examples: He was high on drugs.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: produced with the mouth in a relatively closed position

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that shows you think you are better than other people

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: friends, people, etc. in positions of power and influence
examples: He has friends in high places.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to enjoy yourself very much

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: despite any difficulties
examples: I was determined to go, come hell or high water.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: in a position out of the water
examples: Their yacht was left high and dry on a sandbank.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: in a difficult situation, without help or money

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: behaving as though you think you are more important than other people

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: behaving in a very excited way, especially because of being strongly affected by alcohol or drugs

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: the amount of attention somebody/something has from the public
examples: This issue has had a high profile in recent months.
I advised her to keep a low profile for the next few days (= not to attract attention).
The story was given a low profile in today's papers.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: in an angry or offended mood, and showing other people that you are angry
examples: He stomped out of the room in high dudgeon.
She stormed out in high dudgeon.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: used to say that you think somebody should do something soon
examples: It's about time you cleaned your room!

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: of a high quality or degree; of the highest quality or greatest degree
examples: The job requires diplomatic skills of a high order.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to have a strong unpleasant smell

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to seem to be very dishonest or morally unacceptable

His death didn't really hit me at first.
A tornado hit on Tuesday night.
Rural areas have been worst hit by the strike.
Spain was one of the hardest hit countries.
It hit him very hard when Rosie left.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to attack somebody/something
examples: We hit the enemy when they least expected it.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to reach a place
examples: Follow this footpath and you'll eventually hit the road.
The President hits town tomorrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to reach a particular level
examples: Temperatures hit 40° yesterday.
The euro hit a record low in trading today.
We hit top form (= played our best) in yesterday’s match.
The film doesn't always hit its targets (= succeed in what it is attempting to do).

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to experience something difficult or unpleasant
examples: We seem to have hit a problem.
Everything was going well but then we hit trouble.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to come suddenly into your mind
examples: The idea hit me like a tornado.
I couldn't remember where I'd seen him before, and then it suddenly hit me.
That's when it really hit me that we were in deep trouble.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to become widely available for sale
examples: the latest board game to hit the market
to hit the shops/stores/shelves
Her shocking autobiography is about to hit the streets.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be an important item of news in the mediaExtra Examples
examples: He always manages to grab the headlines.
The hospital hit the headlines when a number of suspicious deaths occurred.
The story was important enough to make the headlines.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be very successful
examples: The band has hit big in the US.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: if a plan, somebody’s career, etc. hits the buffers, it suddenly stops being successful
examples: The former tennis star’s comeback trail hit the buffers yesterday when she lost in straight sets.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to fall to the ground

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to affect somebody very deeply
examples: The business over the lawsuit had really knocked her for six.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to start doing something and continue very quickly and successfully

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to go to bed
examples: I decided to hit the sack and have an early night.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: if a remark, etc. hits/strikes home, it has a strong effect on somebody, in a way that makes them realize what the true facts of a situation are
examples: Her face went pale as his words hit home.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to be very obvious to somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to start doing something, such as playing music
examples: Hit it, Louis!

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to have a good friendly relationship with somebody
examples: We hit it off straight away.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to make or win a lot of money quickly and unexpectedly

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to succeed/fail in achieving or guessing something
examples: He blushed furiously and Robyn knew she had hit the mark.
The film misses the mark because it just isn't believable.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to say something that is exactly right

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to mention a subject that makes somebody feel angry, upset, embarrassed, etc.
examples: You touched a raw nerve when you mentioned his first wife.
My remarks about divorce had unwittingly touched a raw nerve.
The article struck a raw nerve as it revived unpleasant memories.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to suddenly be in a successful situation, especially one that makes you rich
examples: The band really hit pay dirt with their last album.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to do, say or write something that is suitable/not suitable for a particular occasion
examples: It is a bizarre tale and the author hits just the right note of horror and disbelief.
Unfortunately, the president struck the wrong note in his speech, ignoring the public mood.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to start a journey
examples: The following spring I hit the road.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to suddenly become very angry

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: if something hits the spot it does exactly what it should do

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to begin to do something with confidence and at a good speed after a slow, uncertain start
examples: After a nervous start, he finally hit his stride in the second set.
The team took time to hit stride.
The show finally hit its stride in the second season.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to reach a point when you cannot continue or make any more progress
examples: We hit a wall and we weren't scoring.
I’ve hit a wall with my marathon training.
What do you do when you hit the wall at work?

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to continue to hurt somebody when they are already defeated

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: to affect somebody where they will feel it most

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: to hit the wooden frame of the goal in the game of football (soccer), instead of scoring a goal
examples: She hit the woodwork twice before scoring.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: to be so surprised by something that you do not know how to react

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: when somebody in authority finds out about something bad or wrong that somebody has done
examples: When the shit hits the fan, I don't want to be here.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an activity that you do for pleasure when you are not working
examples: Do you have any hobbies?
Her hobbies include swimming and gardening.
Why don't you take up a new hobby?
My favourite hobby is definitely scuba diving.
I only play jazz as a hobby.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a game played on a field by two teams of 11 players, with curved sticks and a small hard ball. Teams try to hit the ball into the other team’s goal.
examples: to play hockey
a hockey stick/pitch/player/team

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a game played on ice, in which players use long sticks to hit a hard rubber disc (called a puck) into the other team’s goal
examples: SEE ALSO street hockey
She plays hockey in the winter.
a hockey stick/puck/rink/player/team
Every Saturday night people would sit in front of their television sets watching hockey.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have somebody/something in your hand, arms, etc.
examples: She was holding a large box.
They were holding hands (= the right hand of one person holding the left hand of the other).
I held the mouse by its tail.
The girl held her father's hand tightly.
He was holding the baby in his arms.
The winning captain held the trophy in the air.
The lovers held each other close.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to put your hand on part of your body, usually because it hurts
examples: She groaned and held her head.
The prisoner held his head in his hands.
She started to dance, holding her hands rapturously to her chest.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to keep somebody/something in a particular position
examples: Hold your head up.
Hold this position for a count of 10.
The wood is held in position by a clamp.
People held handkerchiefs over their mouths.
I had to hold my stomach in (= pull the muscles flat) to zip up my jeans.
I'll hold the door open for you.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to support the weight of somebody/something
examples: I don't think that branch will hold your weight.
She let him hold most of her weight as he led her upstairs.
Several pieces of wood joined together can hold more weight than just one piece.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have enough space for something/somebody; to contain something/somebody
examples: This barrel holds 25 litres.
The plane holds about 300 passengers.
The inner box holds the cheese and has holes in it.
Each 180-litre container will hold up to three black bags of rubbish.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have or offer something; to be going to bring something
examples: I don't know what the future holds.
This research holds the key to understanding life.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have a meeting, competition, conversation, etc.
examples: Each month she holds a meeting with her entire staff.
The British Foreign Minister held talks with the leaders of the two countries.
He has already held discussions with Irish shareholders.
It's impossible to hold a conversation with all this noise.
The next conference will be held in Ohio.
The country is holding its first free elections for 20 years.
to hold an event/a party/a competition

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to have something you have gained or achieved
examples: Who holds the world record for the long jump?
She held the title of world champion for three years.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to have a particular job or position
examples: How long has he held office?
Mrs Thatcher held the post of prime minister longer than anyone else last century.
Men still hold most positions of power in this country.
The company has held the advertising contract since 2005.
The professor will hold a seat on the advisory board.
Labour's John Taylor and Mary Smith both held seats in this constituency.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to keep somebody and not allow them to leave
examples: Police are holding two men in connection with last Thursday's bank raid.
He was held prisoner for two years.
Eight people were held hostage for four months.
She was held captive in a castle.
She was arrested and held in custody in a police station.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to keep somebody’s attention or interest
examples: There wasn't much in the museum to hold my attention.
These discussions held little interest for Lucy.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to keep something at the same level, rate, speed, etc.; to stay at the same level, rate, etc.
examples: Hold your speed at 70.
Interest rates have been held at 8% for a year now.
They are trying to hold public spending to £300 billion.
The company's shares held at £3.47.
In trading today the dollar held steady against the yen.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to keep something so that it can be used later
examples: Employees do not have access to personal records held on computer.
Our solicitor holds our wills.
We can hold your reservation for three days.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to wait until you can speak to the person you have phoned
examples: That extension is busy right now. Can you hold?
She asked me to hold the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to own or have something
examples: Employees hold 30% of the shares.
He was born in South Africa but he holds a British passport.
Applicants must hold a full driving licence.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to defend something against attack; to have control of something
examples: The rebels held the radio station.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to remain strong and safe or in position
examples: They were afraid the dam wouldn't hold.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to remain the same
examples: How long will the fine weather hold?
If their luck holds, they could still win the championship.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to have a belief or an opinion about somebody/something
examples: He holds strange views on education.
She is held in high regard by her students (= they have a high opinion of her).
to be held in high esteem
He has very firmly held religious beliefs.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to consider that something is true
examples: I still hold that the government's economic policies are mistaken.
Parents will be held responsible for their children's behaviour.
These vases are held to be the finest examples of Greek art.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to be in close contact with the road and easy to control, especially when driven fast

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to continue to move in a particular direction

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to make a note continue for a particular time

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: be able to drink a reasonable amount of alcohol without becoming drunk
examples: I can hold my drink as well as anyone.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to win a game in which you are serving
examples: Zverev held serve to take the set.
Halep held to love.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to stop doing something or not to do something
examples: Hold your fire! (= don't shoot)
Hold the front page! (= don't print it until a particular piece of news is available)
Give me a hot dog, but hold the (= don't give me any) mustard.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to be true
examples: The same argument does not hold good in every case.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody to wait, or not to move
examples: Hold it a second—I don't think everyone's arrived yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to hold somebody/something very tightly because you are afraid

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: a person cannot be prevented from doing something
examples: Once she gets on to the subject of politics there's no holding her.
