definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a hollow space in something solid or in the surface of something
examples: SEE ALSO f-hole
He dug a deep hole in the garden.
The bomb blew a huge hole in the ground.
Water had collected in the holes in the road.
She drilled a small hole in the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a space or opening that goes all the way through something
examples: SEE ALSO black hole
We drilled a hole through the wall.
The car was riddled with bullet holes.
The old blankets were full of holes.
There were holes in the knees of his trousers.
There's a gaping hole in the ceiling and rain is pouring onto my desk.
She punched two holes in each sheet of paper.
The children climbed through a hole in the fence.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the home of a small animal
examples: COMPARE foxhole
a mouse hole
The story begins with Alice falling down a rabbit hole.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an unpleasant place to live or be in
examples: SYNONYM dump
I am not going to bring up my child in this hole.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a hollow in the ground that you must get the ball into; one of the sections of a golf course with the tee at the beginning and the hole at the end
examples: The ball rolled into the hole and she had won.
an eighteen-hole golf course
He liked to play a few holes after work.
She won the first hole.
She won by one hole.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a fault or weakness in something such as a plan, law or story
examples: SEE ALSO loophole
I don't believe what she says—her story is full of holes.
He was found not guilty because of holes in the prosecution case.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a place or position that needs to be filled because somebody/something is no longer there
examples: After his wife left, there was a gaping hole in his life.
Buying the new equipment left a big hole in the company's finances.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a secret advantage, for example a piece of information or a skill, that you are ready to use if you need to

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: if money burns a hole in your pocket, you want to spend it as soon as you have it

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to get yourself into a bad situation that will be very difficult to get out of

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: in a difficult situation
examples: He had got himself into a hole and it was going to be difficult to get out of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: owing money
examples: We start the current fiscal year $30 million in the hole.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to use up a large amount of something that you have, especially money
examples: School fees can make a big hole in your savings.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to find the weak points in something such as a plan, suggestion, etc.
examples: It was easy to pick holes in his arguments.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: a person who does not feel happy or comfortable in a particular situation, or who is not suitable for itWord Origin
examples: Old English hol (noun), holian (verb), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch hol (noun) ‘cave’, (adjective) ‘hollow’, and German hohl ‘hollow’, from an Indo-European root meaning ‘cover, conceal’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a period of time when you are not at work or school
examples: COMPARE leave (1)
the school/summer/Christmas holidays
She spent her holiday decorating the flat.
I'm afraid Mr Walsh is away on holiday this week.
The package includes 20 days' paid holiday a year.
holiday pay
a holiday job (= done by students during the school holidays)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a period of time spent travelling or resting away from home
examples: SEE ALSO busman’s holiday
a camping/skiing/walking holiday
an adventure holiday
a foreign/an overseas holiday
a family holiday
a two-week holiday in the sun
to have/take a holiday
They met while on holiday in Greece.
We went on holiday together last summer.
Where are you going for your holidays this year?
a holiday cottage/home
a holiday destination/resort

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a day when most people do not go to work or school, especially because of a religious or national celebration
examples: SEE ALSO August Bank Holiday
The president's birthday was declared a national holiday.
Today is a holiday in Wales.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the time from late November to early January that includes Thanksgiving, Christmas, Hanukkah and New Year
examples: Happy Holidays!
Thanksgiving is the traditional start of the holiday season for most Americans.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a hole or empty space inside
examples: a hollow ball/centre/tube/tree
a hollow metal cylinder
The tree trunk was hollow inside.
Her stomach felt hollow with fear.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: sinking deeply into the face
examples: hollow eyes/cheeks
hollow-eyed from lack of sleep

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: making a low sound like that made by an empty object when it is hit
examples: a hollow groan

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not sincere
examples: I've had enough of their hollow promises.
She gave a slightly hollow laugh.
Their appeals for an end to the violence had a hollow ring.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: without real value
examples: He won something of a hollow victory when his opponent was forced to withdraw with a serious injury.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to give the impression of not being sincere or true
examples: His expressions of support rang rather hollow.
His promise rang hollow.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to give the impression of being sincere/true or not sincere/true
examples: It may seem a strange story but it rings true to me.
His expressions of support rang rather hollow.
His promise rang hollow.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with God or a particular religion
examples: OPPOSITE unholy
the Holy Bible
holy books/scriptures
the holy city of Mecca
Islam’s holiest shrine
a holy day/month
a holy war (= one fought to defend the beliefs of a particular religion)
holy ground

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: good in a moral and religious way
examples: OPPOSITE unholy
a holy life/man

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you are surprised, afraid, etc.
examples: Holy cow! What was that?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the house or flat that you live in, especially with your family
examples: SEE ALSO at-home
Old people prefer to stay in their own homes.
His children were upset when he sold the family home.
While travelling she missed the comforts of home.
She leaves home at 7 every day.
He left home (= left his parents and began an independent life) at sixteen.
The floods forced many people to flee their homes.
I'll call you from home later.
stray dogs needing new homes

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a house or flat, etc., when you think of it as property that can be bought and sold
examples: SEE ALSO mobile home
a holiday/summer home
A lot of new homes are being built on the edge of town.
He'd always dreamed of owning his own home.
Buying a home can be a complicated business.
The number of homes sold in January fell by 13% on the previous month.
Private home ownership is increasing faster than ever.
They applied for a home improvement loan.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the town, district, country, etc. that you come from, or where you are living and that you feel you belong to
examples: I often think about my friends back home.
Jane left England and made Greece her home.
Jamaica is home to over two million people.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to refer to a family living together, and the way it behaves
examples: SEE ALSO broken home
She came from a violent home.
They wanted to give the boy a secure and loving home.
He had always wanted a real home with a wife and children.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a place where people who cannot care for themselves live and are cared for by others
examples: SEE ALSO care home
a children’s home
an old people’s home
a retirement home
a home for the mentally ill
She has lived in a home since she was six.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a place where pets with no owner are taken care of
examples: a dogs’/cats’ home

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the place where a plant or animal usually lives; the place where somebody/something can be found
examples: This region is the home of many species of wild flower.
The tiger's home is in the jungle.
Beverly Hills is the home of the stars.
The Rockies are home to bears and mountain lions.
Arizona is home to the Grand Canyon and the Petrified Forest.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a place where an object is kept
examples: We haven't found a home for all our books yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the place where something was first discovered, made or invented
examples: New Orleans, the home of jazz
Greece, the home of democracy
Andalusia, the home of flamenco

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: in a person’s own house, flat, etc.
examples: I called round last night, but you weren't at home.
Oh no, I left my purse at home.
He lived at home (= with his parents) until he was thirty.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: comfortable and relaxed

examples: Many refugees have been forced to flee their homeland.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: (in the Republic of South Africa under the apartheid system in the past) one of the areas with some self-government that were intended for a group of black African people to live in
examples: the Transkei homeland

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having no home, and therefore typically living on the streets
examples: The scheme has been set up to help homeless people.
The local authority ruled that he had made himself intentionally homeless and was therefore not entitled to be rehoused.
Three hundred people were left homeless by the earthquake.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: people who have no home
examples: helping the homeless

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: work that is given by teachers for students to do at home
examples: I always do my homework on the bus.
physics/geography/French, etc. homework
I still haven't done my geography homework.
How much homework do you get?
I have to write up the notes for homework.
I have to finish this homework assignment.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: work that somebody does to prepare for something
examples: You could tell that he had really done his homework (= found out all he needed to know).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: always telling the truth, and never stealing or cheating
examples: OPPOSITE dishonest
an honest man/woman
They were honest, hard-working people, trying to farm on their own two feet.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not hiding the truth about something
examples: Are you being completely honest about your feelings?
Thank you for being so honest with me.
Give me your honest opinion.
He made an honest mistake and deserves a second chance.
He gave an honest answer to a difficult question.
We need to have more open and honest discussions about mental health.
The meeting was described as ‘a frank and honest exchange of views’.
To be honest (= what I really think is), it was one of the worst books I've ever read.
I'll be honest, I really don't agree with what she did.
Let's be honest, she's only interested in Mike because of his money.
The film has won accolades for being both brutally honest and very funny.
If I am perfectly honest, I wasn't expecting much from this album.
I just want the honest truth.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: showing an honest mind or attitude
examples: She's got an honest face.
She seems honest enough.
an honest mistake

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: earned or resulting from hard work
examples: He hasn't done an honest day's work in his life.
It's quite a struggle to make an honest living.
She claimed she was just trying to earn an honest penny.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you are not lying
examples: I didn't mean it, honest!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that what you are saying is true
examples: SEE ALSO honest-to-goodness
Honest to God, Mary, I'm not joking.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to marry a woman after having had a sexual relationship with her, especially if she is pregnantWord Origin
examples: Middle English (originally in the sense ‘held in or deserving of honour’): via Old French from Latin honestus, from honos, honor.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of being honest
examples: She answered all my questions with her usual honesty.
His honesty is not in question.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to state a fact or an opinion that, though true, may seem disappointing
examples: The book isn't, in all honesty, as good as I expected.
In all honesty, the book was not as good as I expected.
Who in honesty can blame her?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: great respect for somebody
examples: SEE ALSO maid of honour
the guest of honour (= the most important one)
the seat/place of honour (= given to the most important guest)
They stood in silence as a mark of honour to her.
This biography does great honour to the poet's achievements.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that you are very pleased or proud to do because people are showing you great respect
examples: SYNONYM privilege
It was a great honour to be invited here today.
It is a great honour to represent my country at the Olympics.
It was my honour and privilege to be Helen's friend.
The city has the dubious honour (= something that does not make you pleased or proud) of being the road rage capital of Europe.
He shared the honour of being the season's top scorer with Andy Cole.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of knowing and doing what is morally right
examples: a man of honour
Proving his innocence has become a matter of honour.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a good reputation; respect from other people
examples: COMPARE dishonour
upholding the honour of your country
The family honour is at stake.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person or thing that causes others to respect and admire something/somebody
examples: She is an honour to the profession.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an award, official title, etc. given to somebody as a reward for something that they have done
examples: SEE ALSO roll of honour
the New Year’s Honours list (= in Britain, a list of awards and titles given on January 1 each year)
to receive/win the highest honour
to bestow an honour on somebody
She received nearly every honour bestowed upon a poet.
He received numerous honours, including the OBE in 1961.
He was buried with full military honours (= with a special military service as a sign of respect).
He wears his scars like badges of honour (= rewards that you can see).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a university course that is of a higher level than a basic course (in the US also used to describe a class in school that is at a higher level than other classes)
examples: an honours degree/course
a First Class Honours degree
I took an honors class in English.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if you pass an exam or graduate from a university or school with honours, you receive a special grade for having achieved a very high standard
examples: He passed with second-class honours.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a title of respect used when talking to or about a judge or a US mayor
examples: No more questions, Your Honour.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the cards that have the highest value

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to do something to make somebody feel very proud and pleased
examples: Would you do me the honour of dining with me?

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to perform a social duty or ceremony, such as pouring drinks, making a speech, etc.
examples: Would you do the honours and draw the winning ticket?

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be given the opportunity to do something that makes you feel proud and happy
examples: May I have the honour of the next dance?
It was Tevez who had the honour of scoring the first goal.
She had the honour of being the first living artist to have her work exhibited in the Louvre.
I had the rare honour of being allowed into the artist's studio.
Max was given the dubious honour (= it may not really have made him feel proud and happy) of organizing the children's party.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say that even criminals have standards of behaviour that they respect

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to feel that you must do something because of your sense of moral duty
examples: COMPARE duty-bound
She felt honour-bound to attend as she had promised to.
He felt honour bound to help her.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: no particular person, team, etc. is doing better than the others in a competition, an argument, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: in order to show great respect for somebody/something
examples: a ceremony in honour of those killed in the explosion
A banquet was held in her honour.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to promise very seriously that you will do something or that something is true
examples: I swear on my honour that I knew nothing about this.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to be trusted to do something
examples: You're on your honour not to go into my room.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the time when something important happens

She thought her last hour had come.
Don't desert me in my hour of need.
She helped me in my hour of need.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the time when it is exactly 1 o’clock, 2 o’clock, etc.

ten minutes past the hour
There's a bus every hour on the hour

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when giving the time according to the 24-hour clock, usually in military or other official language

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: any time, especially a time that is not usual or suitable

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: at the last possible moment; just in time

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: very early, especially when this is annoying
examples: The job involved getting up at some unearthly hour to catch the first train.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: very early or very late and therefore annoying
examples: I apologize for calling you at this ungodly hour.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: the time when you have to do something difficult or unpleasant

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: if you keep regular, strange, etc. hours, the times at which you do things (especially getting up or going to bed) are regular, strange, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to spend time doing something that is not important while you are waiting for something else to happen
examples: We killed time playing cards.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: the period of time very early in the morning, soon after midnight
examples: We worked well into the small hours.

The party continued well into the early hours.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a building for people to live in, usually for one family
examples: SEE ALSO Buck House
We live in a two-bedroom house.
It was so hot outside we stayed in the house.
He went into the house.
I had to get out of the house.
A light was on inside the house.
There was a police van parked outside the house.
Let's have a party at my house.
We need to build more houses in a way that respects the needs of the environment.
Investors were buying houses to rent them out.
What time do you leave the house in the morning (= to go to work)?
We're moving house (= leaving our house and going to live in a different one).
House prices (= prices of houses and flats) in London are still rising.
We went on a tour of the house and grounds (= for example, at a country house, open to the public).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: all the people living in a house
examples: SYNONYM household
Be quiet or you'll wake the whole house!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a building used for a particular purpose, for example for holding meetings in or keeping animals or goods in
examples: SEE ALSO doghouse
an opera house
a henhouse

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used in the names of office buildings
examples: SEE ALSO Bush House

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a company involved in a particular kind of business; an institution of a particular kind
examples: SEE ALSO clearing house
a fashion/banking/publishing house
a religious house (= a convent or a monastery)

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a restaurant
examples: SEE ALSO free house
a steakhouse
a coffee house
a bottle of house wine (= the cheapest wine available in a particular restaurant, sometimes not listed by name)

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a group of people who meet to discuss and make the laws of a country
examples: SEE ALSO lower house
Legislation requires approval by both houses of parliament.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the House of Commons or the House of Lords in the UK; the House of Representatives in the US

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a group of people discussing something in a formal debate
examples: I urge the house to vote against the motion.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the part of a theatre where the audience sits; the audience at a particular performance
examples: SEE ALSO front of house
playing to a full/packed/empty house (= to a large/small audience)
The spotlight faded and the house lights came up.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: (in some British schools) an organized group of students of different ages who compete against other groups in sports competitions, etc. and who may, in boarding schools, live together in one building

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: an old and famous family
examples: the House of Windsor (= the British royal family)

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a type of electronic dance music with a fast beat

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to make everyone laugh or cheer, especially at a performance in the theatre

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to remove people or things that are not necessary or wanted
examples: The new manager said he wanted to clean house.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to make your house clean

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to eat a lot of somebody else’s food
examples: How much longer is he staying? He’s eating us out of house and home.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to become friends quickly and have a very friendly relationship

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to do something or ask a question in a very complicated way instead of in a simple, direct way
examples: You did go all round the houses didn’t you? Why not get straight to the point?

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to cook, clean and do all the other jobs around the house
examples: She kept house for her elderly parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used to say that everyone was very emotional about something
examples: There wasn't a dry eye in the house when they announced their engagement.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: drinks or meals that are on the house are provided free by the pub or restaurant and you do not have to pay
examples: Have a drink on the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: you should not criticize other people, because they will easily find ways of criticizing you

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to play at being a family in its home
examples: The children were playing house, giving dinner to their dolls.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to organize your own business or improve your own behaviour before you try to criticize somebody else

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: very safe

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to make a place your home
examples: They set up house together in a small flat in Brighton.

examples: SEE ALSO affordable housing

temporary/permanent housing

examples: Tenants may only keep pets with the written consent of the housing department.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: a car’s rear axle housing

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in what way or manner
examples: COMPARE however
How does it work?

I'll show you how to load the software.

Do you remember how (= that) the kids always loved going there?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to ask about somebody’s health or how well things are going for them
examples: How are you?
How are you feeling now?
Hey, how are you doing?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to ask whether something is successful or fun
examples: How was your trip?
How did they play?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used before an adjective or adverb to ask about the amount, degree, etc. of something, or about somebody’s age
examples: How often do you go swimming?

How much are those earrings (= What do they cost)?
How many people were there?
How old is she?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to express surprise, pleasure, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: SYNONYM however

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used when asking for information about somebody/something
examples: I'm not going. How about you?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to make a suggestion
examples: How about a break?
How about going for a meal?
How about we go for a meal?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to show that you think somebody’s behaviour is very bad or are very surprised by it
examples: Ben! How could you? After all they've done for us!
Ugh! How can you eat that stuff?

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to say you do not understand how something can happen and would like an explanation
examples: ‘I think you owe me some money.’ ‘How come?’
If she spent five years in Paris, how come her French is so bad?

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used as a formal greeting when you meet somebody for the first time. The usual reply is also How do you do?

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to ask the reason for something
examples: ‘I left work early today.’ ‘How's that (= Why)?’

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used when asking somebody’s opinion of something
examples: I'll tuck your sheets in for you. How's that? Comfortable?
Two o'clock on the dot! How's that for punctuality!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to introduce a statement that contrasts with something that has just been said
examples: LANGUAGE BANK AT nevertheless
He was feeling bad. He went to work, however, and tried to concentrate.
We thought the figures were correct. However, we have now discovered some errors.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used with an adjective or adverb to mean ‘to whatever degree’
examples: He wanted to take no risks, however small.
She has the window open, however cold it is outside.
However carefully I explained, she still didn't understand.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in whatever way
examples: However you look at it, it's going to cost a lot.
It's easy to reach the city centre, however you choose to travel.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: extremely large in size or amount; great in degree
examples: SYNONYM enormous

Huge amounts of data were lost.
I wasn't a huge fan of the movie.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very successful
examples: I think this band is going to be huge.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

a terrible loss of human life
human development/activity/behaviour

one of the greatest leaders in human history

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: showing the weaknesses and desires that are typical of people, which means that other people should not criticize the person too much
examples: human weaknesses/failings
It's only human to want the best for your children.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having the same feelings and emotions as most ordinary people
examples: He's really very human when you get to know him.

The public is always attracted to politicians who have the human touch (= the ability to make ordinary people feel relaxed when they meet them).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who is involved in a subject, issue, etc. and makes it easier for ordinary people to understand and have sympathy with it
examples: He is the human face of party politics.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: kind behaviour, considered to be natural to humans

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: that considers the needs of ordinary people
examples: This was science with a human face.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: the early nineteen hundreds (= written ‘early 1900s’)

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (in the UK) to go after and kill foxes as a sport, riding horses and using dogs. Fox hunting with dogs has been illegal in England and Wales since 2005, but people still ride out with dogs following a scent trail, without an actual fox.
examples: They hunt when they stay with friends in Ireland.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to go after wild animals in order to catch or kill them for food, sport or to make money
examples: Lions sometimes hunt alone.
Whales are still being hunted and killed in the Arctic.
Cavemen had to hunt for their food.
They watched the bald eagles hunting for fish.
The animals are hunted for their fur.
Turtles are illegally hunted for their eggs, meat and shells.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to look for something that is difficult to find
examples: SYNONYM search
She is still hunting for a new job.
I've hunted everywhere but I can't find it.
After spending half an hour hunting through the boxes, he had still found nothing.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to look for somebody in order to catch them or harm them
examples: Police are hunting an escaped criminal.
Two police forces are still hunting the killer of three-year-old Lucy Black.
Detectives are hunting for thieves who broke into a warehouse yesterday.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (in the UK) to go after and kill foxes as a sport, riding horses and using dogs. Fox hunting with dogs has been illegal in England and Wales since 2005, but people still ride out with dogs following a scent trail, without an actual fox.
examples: They hunt when they stay with friends in Ireland.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: going after and killing wild animals as a sport or for food
examples: He goes hunting every weekend.
Since 1977 otter hunting has been illegal.
In 1966, the commercial hunting of blue whales was banned.
In the tiger, evolution has produced a perfect hunting machine.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sport in which foxes are hunted by specially trained dogs and by people on horses. Fox hunting with dogs is now illegal in the UK.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of looking for something
examples: SEE ALSO bargain hunting
How's the job-hunting going?
Archaeologists have called for a ban on treasure hunting in the region.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a violent storm with very strong winds, especially in the western Atlantic Ocean
examples: COMPARE cyclone
A powerful hurricane hit the Florida coast.
Hurricane Sandy devastated the area.
The hurricane season does not end until November.
hurricane victims
hurricane-force winds
The proceeds will go to hurricane relief.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move or act quickly because there is not much time
examples: SYNONYM rush
You'll have to hurry if you want to catch that train.
We need to hurry or we'll be late for school.
The kids hurried to open their presents.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move quickly in a particular direction
examples: SYNONYM rush
He picked up his bags and hurried across the courtyard.
She hurried away without saying goodbye.
She hurried after Gary to apologize to him.
She hurried down the street.
I hurried home to tell him the news.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody do something more quickly
examples: SYNONYM rush
I don't want to hurry you but we close in twenty minutes.
She was hurried into making an unwise choice.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to deal with something quickly
examples: SYNONYM rush
Her application was hurried through.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to do something too quickly
examples: SYNONYM rush
A good meal should never be hurried.

examples: He hurt his back playing squash.
Strong light hurts my eyes.
Did you hurt yourself?
Stop it. You're hurting me.
No one was seriously hurt in the accident.
My back is really hurting me today.
My shoes hurt—they're too tight.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to feel painful
examples: My feet hurt.
My head hurts.
Ouch! That hurt!
It hurts when I bend my knee.
It hurts if I move my neck.
It hurts to breathe.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody unhappy or upset
examples: What really hurt was that he never answered my letter.
I'm sorry, I didn't mean to hurt you.
I didn't want to hurt his feelings.
It always hurts to lose, especially in the final.
It hurt me to think that he would lie to me.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to feel unhappy or upset
examples: I know you're hurting and I want to help you.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have a bad effect on somebody/something
examples: Hard work never hurt anyone.
Many people on low incomes will be hurt by the government's plans.
High interest rates are hurting the local economy.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be in a difficult situation because you need something, especially money
examples: His campaign is already hurting for money.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to affect somebody where they will feel it most

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: It wouldn't hurt you to help with the housework occasionally.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the man that somebody is married to; a married man
examples: SEE ALSO house husband
This is my husband, Steve.
How did you meet your husband?
She's finally decided to leave her husband.
She lost her husband (= he died) recently.
her late husband
his husband of four years
It had been a shock to find himself a husband and father.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a man and woman who are married to each other
examples: They lived together as husband and wife (= as if they were married) for years.
a husband-and-wife team

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a chemical element. Hydrogen is a gas that is the lightest of all the elements. It combines with oxygen to form water.Word Origin
examples: late 18th cent.: coined in French from Greek hudro- ‘water’ + -genēs ‘-born, of a specified kind’, from gen- (root of gignomai ‘be born, become’, genos ‘a kind’).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an idea or explanation of something that is based on a few known facts but that has not yet been proved to be true or correct
examples: SYNONYM theory
to formulate/confirm a hypothesis
a hypothesis about the function of dreams
There is little evidence to support these hypotheses.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: guesses and ideas that are not based on certain knowledge
examples: SYNONYM speculation
It would be pointless to engage in hypothesis before we have the facts.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used as the subject of a verb when the speaker or writer is referring to himself/herself
examples: SEE ALSO me
I think I'd better go now.
When they asked me if I wanted the job, I said yes.
He and I are old friends.
I'm not going to fall, am I?
I'm taller than her, aren't I?
Jen and I went to London yesterday.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: water that has frozen and become solid
examples: SEE ALSO icy
There was ice on the windows.
The lake was covered with a sheet of ice.
the body of a man perfectly preserved in a block of ice
My hands are as cold as ice.
substantial loss of sea ice in the Arctic Ocean

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a frozen surface that people skate on
examples: Both teams are on the ice, waiting for the whistle.
The dancers came out onto the ice.
People were skating on the ice.
They held hands as they glided across the ice.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a piece of ice used to keep food and drinks cold
examples: I'll have lemonade please—no ice.
a glass of water with ice and lemon
She ordered a vodka and ice.
The glass was filled with green liquid and crushed ice.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an ice cream
examples: SEE ALSO choc ice
Drinks, ices and popcorn are all on sale in the foyer.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a type of sweet food that consists of ice that has been crushed (= broken into very small pieces) and given a sweet taste

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be taking a risk

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed, especially at the beginning of a meeting, party, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO icebreaker (2)
Jim organized a few party games to break the ice when people first arrived.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to have no influence or effect on somebody
examples: His excuses cut no ice with me.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: kept cold by being surrounded by ice
examples: All the food is laid out and the champagne is on ice.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: not being dealt with now; waiting to be dealt with at a later time
examples: We've had to put our plans on ice for the time being.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: performed by skaters on an ice rink
examples: Cinderella on ice

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small symbol on a computer or smartphone screen that represents a program or a file
examples: Click on the printer icon with the mouse.
Tap the app icon on your phone to open it.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a famous person or thing that people admire and see as a symbol of a particular idea, way of life, etc.
examples: Madonna and other pop icons of the 1980s
a feminist/gay icon (= somebody that feminists/gay people admire)
Sandra has become a style icon, for the fashion world particularly.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a painting or statue of a holy person that is also thought of as a holy objectWord Origin
examples: mid 16th cent. (in the sense ‘simile’): via Latin from Greek eikōn ‘likeness, image’. Current senses date from the mid 19th cent. onwards.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the part of the unconscious mind where many of a person’s basic needs, feelings and desires are supposed to exist
examples: COMPARE ego

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a plan, thought or suggestion, especially about what to do in a particular situation
examples: It would be a good idea to call before we leave.
That's a great idea!
I’ve had a brilliant idea!
I knew this was a bad idea.
The latest big idea is to make women more interested in sport.
The surprise party was Jane's idea.
He already had an idea for his next novel.
We’re having a meeting to try to come up with ideas for fund-raising.
The idea of a new museum was first discussed two years ago.
I like the idea of living on a boat.
We've been toying with the idea of (= thinking about) getting a dog.
Her family expected her to go to college, but she had other ideas.
I don't know what to do, but I'm open to ideas.
It might be an idea (= it would be sensible) to try again later.
It seemed like a good idea at the time, and then it all went horribly wrong.
Ben is the ideas man and the others do the day-to-day work.
Ben is the idea man.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a picture or an impression in your mind of what somebody/something is like
examples: The brochure should give you a good idea of the hotel.
I had some idea of what the job would be like.
This film changed the very idea of what an outer space movie could be.
She doesn't seem to have any idea of what I'm talking about.
An evening at home watching TV is not my idea of a good time.
If this is your idea of a joke, then I don’t find it very funny.
I don't want anyone getting the wrong idea (= getting the wrong impression about something).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an opinion or a belief about something
examples: the experiences that shaped her ideas
He has some very strange ideas about education.
Her ideas on the family are pretty old-fashioned.
These photographs challenge conventional ideas of beauty.
She rejects the idea that product quality has suffered.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a feeling that something is possible or is true
examples: Where on earth did you get that idea?
What gave you the idea that he'd be here?
I have a pretty good idea where I left it—I hope I'm right.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the aim or purpose of something
examples: You'll soon get the idea (= understand).
What's the idea of the game?
The whole idea of going was so that we could meet her new boyfriend.
They buy other people's tickets with the idea of reselling them.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to start behaving in a more acceptable way, so that work gets done better, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to give somebody hopes about something that may not be possible or likely; to make somebody act or think in an unreasonable way
examples: Who's been putting ideas into his head?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you do not know something
examples: ‘What's she talking about?’ ‘I've no idea.’
He hasn't the faintest idea how to manage people.
I had no idea she’d had such a difficult life.
I don’t have any idea where he is.
I haven't got the faintest idea what she meant.
He hadn't had the slightest idea about what had been going on.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to have found a very good or successful way of living, doing something, etc.
examples: He's certainly got the right idea—retiring at 55.
The party had the right idea, but failed to win over the voters.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to reply in a positive way to a suggestion that somebody has made
examples: Hey, that's an idea! And we could get a band, as well.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to encourage people and to tell them that they are doing something right
examples: That's the idea! You're doing fine.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to show that something is hard for somebody else to imagine
examples: You've no idea how much traffic there was tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: perfect; most suitable
examples: an ideal location/place
This beach is ideal for children.
She's the ideal candidate for the job.
The trip to Paris will be an ideal opportunity to practise my French.
The prime minister admitted the current situation was ‘not ideal’ (= was bad).
It was not the ideal solution to the problem.
Harvesting is being done in less than ideal conditions.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: existing only in your imagination or as an idea; not likely to be real
examples: the search for ideal love

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that something is what you would like to happen or what should happen, but you know it cannot
examples: In an ideal world we would be recycling and reusing everything.

Her dress is almost identical to mine.
The name on the ticket should be identical with the one in the passport.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the same
examples: This is the identical room we stayed in last year.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of showing, proving or recognizing who or what somebody/something is
examples: SEE ALSO self-identification
The identification of the crash victims was a long and difficult task.
Accurate identification of these birds is difficult.
Each product has a number for easy identification.
The vehicle's identification number is stamped on the engine.
Biometric identification methods include fingerprints and facial recognition scanners.
Only one witness could make a positive identification.
The hospital had mixed up the patients' identification tags.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of recognizing that something exists, or is important
examples: The early identification of children with special educational needs is very important.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: official papers or a document that can prove who you are
examples: Can I see some identification, please?
To vote, Florida law requires a photo identification with a signature.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a strong feeling of sympathy, understanding or support for somebody/something
examples: her emotional identification with the play’s heroine
their increasing identification with the struggle for independence

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the process of making a close connection between one person or thing and another
examples: the voters’ identification of the Democrats with high taxes

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to recognize somebody/something and be able to say who or what they are
examples: She was able to identify her attacker.
Passengers were asked to identify their own suitcases before they were put on the plane.
Many of those arrested refused to identify themselves (= would not say who they were).
The bodies were identified as those of two suspected drug dealers.
two species of waterbirds that can be identified by their distinctive beaks

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to find or discover somebody/something
examples: First of all we must identify the problem areas.
Scientists have identified the gene responsible for the disease.
As yet they have not identified a buyer for the company.
to identify a need/factor/source/cause
They are trying to identify what is wrong with the present system.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make it possible to recognize who or what somebody/something is
examples: In many cases, the clothes people wear identify them as belonging to a particular social class.
a serial number that uniquely identifies the disk

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: who or what somebody/something is
examples: SEE ALSO mistaken identity
The police are trying to discover the identity of the killer.
to establish/reveal/confirm the identity of somebody/something
Their names have been changed for the purposes of this article to protect their identities.
Their identities were kept secret.
Do you have any proof of identity?
The thief used a false identity.
He falls in love with her but can't reveal his true identity.
Each object in the collection has a unique identity number.
She went through an identity crisis in her teens (= was not sure of who she was or of her place in society).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the characteristics, feelings or beliefs that make people different from others
examples: SEE ALSO gender identity
national/cultural/personal identity
ethnic/racial identity
The region's sense of identity remained strong.
a plan to strengthen the corporate identity of the company
Scotland has never lost its identity as a separate nation.
She was searching for a clearer conception of her identity as a writer.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the state or feeling of being very similar to and able to understand somebody/something
examples: The two companies started working together as a result of a clear identity of interests.
He feels a strong sense of identity with his fellow men.
There's a close identity between fans and their team.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: based on or connected with an ideology
examples: ideological differences
This was rejected for ideological reasons.
His agenda has been purely ideological.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a set of ideas that an economic or political system is based on
examples: Marxist/capitalist ideology

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set of beliefs, especially one held by a particular group, that influences the way people behave
examples: the ideology of gender roles
alternative ideologies

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a very stupid person
examples: SYNONYM fool
When I lost my passport, I felt such an idiot.
Not that switch, you idiot!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person with very low intelligence who cannot think or behave normallyWord Origin
examples: Middle English (denoting a person of low intelligence): via Old French from Latin idiota ‘ignorant person’, from Greek idiōtēs ‘private person, layman, ignorant person’, from idios ‘own, private’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to say that one thing can, will or might happen or be true, depending on another thing happening or being true
examples: If you see him, give him this note.
I'll only stay if you offer me more money.
If necessary I can come at once.
You can stay for the weekend if you like.
If anyone calls, tell them I'm not at home.
If he improved his IT skills, he'd (= he would) easily get a job.
You would know what was going on if you'd (= you had) listened.
They would have been here by now if they'd caught the early train.
If I was in charge, I'd do things differently.
If I were in charge…

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: when; whenever; every time
examples: If metal gets hot it expands.
She glares at me if I go near her desk.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used after ask, know, find out, wonder, etc. to introduce one of two or more possibilities
examples: SYNONYM whether
Do you know if he's married?
I wonder if I should wear a coat or not.
He couldn't tell if she was laughing or crying.
Listen to the tune and see if you can remember the words.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used after verbs or adjectives expressing feelings
examples: I am sorry if I disturbed you.
I'd be grateful if you would keep it a secret.
Do you mind if I turn the TV off?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to admit that something is possible, but to say that it is not very important
examples: If she has any weakness, it is her Italian.
So what if he was late. Who cares?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody to listen to your opinion
examples: If you ask me, she's too scared to do it.
If you think about it, those children must be at school by now.
If you remember, Mary was always fond of animals.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used before an adjective to introduce a contrast
examples: He's a good driver, if a little over-confident.
We'll only do it once—if at all.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used with will or would to ask somebody politely to do something
examples: If you will sit down for a few moments, I'll tell the manager you're here.
If you would care to leave your name, we'll contact you as soon as possible.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used before could, may or might to suggest something or to interrupt somebody politely
examples: If I may make a suggestion, perhaps we could begin a little earlier next week.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: despite the possibility that; no matter whether
examples: I'll get there, even if I have to walk.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: despite the fact that; even though
examples: He is a great leader, even if he has many enemies.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say something about an event that may or may not happen
examples: If and when we ever meet again I hope he remembers what I did for him.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to express an opinion about something, or after a negative statement to suggest that the opposite is true
examples: I'd say he was more like his father, if anything.
She's not thin—if anything she's on the plump side.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to give somebody advice
examples: If I were you I'd start looking for another job.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to introduce a different suggestion, after a sentence with if
examples: I'll go if you're going. If not (= if you are not), I'd rather stay at home.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used after a yes/no question to say what will or should happen if the answer is ‘no’
examples: Are you ready? If not, I'm going without you.
Do you want that cake? If not, I'll have it.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to suggest that something may be even larger, more important, etc. than was first stated
examples: They cost thousands if not millions of pounds to build.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that you wish something was true or that something had happened
examples: If only I were rich.
If only I knew her name.
If only he'd remembered to send that letter.
If only I had gone by taxi.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: if that is the case
examples: Do you do research in your studies? If so, what research methods do you use?

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used to say that something that is happening is surprising
examples: I'm surprised they've invited me to their wedding—it's not as if I know them well.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used to state the only situation in which something can happen
examples: Only if a teacher has given permission is a student allowed to leave the room.
Only if the red light comes on is there any danger to employees.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a lack of knowledge or information about something
examples: They fought a long battle against prejudice and ignorance.
I hate to admit my ignorance, but how does it work?
He showed a remarkable ignorance of the facts.
widespread ignorance about the disease
She was kept in ignorance of her husband's activities.
Children often behave badly out of ignorance.
Many lives are lost through ignorance.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of not knowing about something and so being unable to worry about it
examples: We preferred to remain in blissful ignorance of what was going on.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if you do not know about something, you cannot worry about it
examples: Some doctors believe ignorance is bliss and don't give their patients all the facts.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to pay no attention to something
examples: SYNONYM disregard
He ignored all the ‘No Smoking’ signs and lit up a cigarette.
I made a suggestion but they chose to ignore it.
We cannot afford to ignore their advice.
to ignore a warning/a problem/an issue
She deliberately ignored my question and changed the subject.
We can't ignore the fact that there is a huge problem here.
His work was largely ignored and forgotten for 30 years.
Much of social science research simply ignores these sectors.
The government has completely ignored the wishes of the public.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to pretend that you have not seen somebody or that somebody is not there
examples: OPPOSITE acknowledge (4)
She ignored him and carried on with her work.
If he tries to start an argument, just ignore him.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: suffering from an illness or disease; not feeling well
examples: Her father is seriously ill in St Luke's hospital.
chronically ill patients
He is still critically ill in hospital.
Uncle Harry is terminally ill with cancer (= he will die from his illness).
the mentally ill (= people with a mental illness)
She was taken ill suddenly.
We both started to feel ill shortly after the meal.
veterans who became ill after fighting in the Gulf War
He fell ill and died soon after.
I can't eat bananas as they make me ill.
He'd been ill with cancer for months.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: bad or harmful
examples: SEE ALSO ill health
She suffered no ill effects from the experience.
a woman of ill repute (= with a bad reputation, especially because of her sexual behaviour)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: that brings, or is thought to bring, bad luck
examples: a bird of ill omen

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: anger between people, especially after an argument
examples: There was a lot of bad feeling between the two groups of students.
I don't want any bad feelings between us.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: feeling uncomfortable and embarrassed
examples: I felt ill at ease in such formal clothes.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: anger between people, especially after an argument
examples: There was a lot of ill feeling between the two groups of students.
I don't want any ill feelings between us.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: no problem is so bad that it does not bring some advantage to somebodyWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in the senses ‘wicked’, ‘malevolent’, ‘harmful’, and ‘difficult’): from Old Norse illr ‘evil, difficult’, of unknown origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not allowed by the law
examples: OPPOSITE legal
illegal immigrants/aliens
She promised to crack down on illegal immigration.
dealing in illegal drugs
These illegal activities landed him in jail several times.
It's illegal to drive through a red light.
It is illegal for anyone under 18 to possess fireworks in a public place.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being physically or mentally ill
examples: patients with severe mental illness
The virus can cause illness in humans.
I missed a lot of school through illness last year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a type or period of illness
examples: serious/severe/chronic illnesses
a terminal illness
childhood illnesses
He died after a long illness.
She suffers from a debilitating illness.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a false idea or belief, especially about somebody or about a situation
examples: She's under the illusion that (= believes wrongly that) she'll get the job.
The new president has no illusions about the difficulties facing her country (= she knows that the country has serious problems).
I have no illusions about her feelings for me (= I know the truth is that she does not love me).
He could no longer distinguish between illusion and reality.
I don’t want to have my illusions shattered!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that seems to exist but in fact does not, or seems to be something that it is not
examples: SEE ALSO optical illusion
Mirrors in a room often give an illusion of space.
The idea of absolute personal freedom is an illusion.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to use pictures, photographs, diagrams, etc. in a book, etc.
examples: She illustrated her own books.
His lecture was illustrated with photos taken during the expedition.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make the meaning of something clearer by using examples, pictures, etc.
examples: LANGUAGE BANK AT evidence
To illustrate my point, let me tell you a little story.
Last year's sales figures are illustrated in Figure 2.
He is showing these silent films to help illustrate his story of survival.
Each topic is illustrated with concrete examples of economic practice.
Here's an example to illustrate what I mean.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show that something is true or that a situation exists
examples: SYNONYM demonstrate
The incident illustrates the need for better security measures.
This story illustrates how little has changed.
These data illustrate that many parents are not aware of the risks.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a drawing or picture in a book, magazine, for decoration or to explain something
examples: 50 full-colour illustrations
detailed illustrations of animals, birds and plants
a volume of Chaucer with illustrations by Edward Burne-Jones
He produced illustrations for children's books.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of illustrating something
examples: the art of book illustration

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a story, an event or an example that clearly shows the truth about something
examples: The statistics are a clear illustration of the point I am trying to make.
I use this case as an illustration.
Let me, by way of illustration, quote from one of her poems.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a picture, photograph or statue that represents somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO graven image
Most simple leaflets will include text and images.
We already have more than 22  000 digital images on file.
The visual image is steadily replacing the written word.
Images of deer and hunters decorate the cave walls.
Consider the images of war that fill the pages of our newspapers.
a wooden image of the Hindu god Ganesh
An exhibition of images of St Nicholas is on display in the cathedral.
In the Bible it states that humans were created in the image of God.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a picture of somebody/something seen in a mirror, through a camera, or on a television, computer, phone, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO mirror image
He stared at his own image reflected in the water.
Slowly, an image began to appear on the screen.
Click on the image for a larger version.
Police will study the images from CCTV cameras.
The camera captured an image of the suspect and his car.
The satellite provides high-resolution images of the Earth's surface.
The image quality is too low.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the impression that a person, an organization, a product, etc. gives to the public
examples: His public image is very different from the real person.
The advertisements are intended to improve the company's image.
Image is very important in the music world.
It was years before the country was able to project an image of stability again.
The campaign aims to create a new image for the city.
stereotyped images of women in children’s books
to have a positive/negative image
The company changed its name on the advice of an image consultant.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a mental picture that you have of what somebody/something is like or looks like
examples: SEE ALSO after-image
images of the past
I had a mental image of what she would look like.
Dieting always seems to conjure up images of endless cottage cheese salads.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a word or phrase used with a different meaning from its normal one, in order to describe something in a way that produces a strong picture in the mind
examples: Her writings are full of poetic images of the countryside.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to look very like somebody/something else
examples: SEE ALSO spitting image
He's the image of his father.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: language that produces pictures in the minds of people reading or listening
examples: SEE ALSO metaphor
poetic imagery

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: pictures, photographs, etc.
examples: satellite imagery (= for example, photographs of the earth taken from space)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: existing only in your mind or imagination
examples: The equator is an imaginary line around the middle of the earth.
I had an imaginary friend when I was a child.
As children they invented the imaginary world of Gondal.
We must listen to their problems, real or imaginary.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the ability to create pictures in your mind; the part of your mind that does this
examples: a vivid/fertile imagination
He has no imagination.
It doesn't take much imagination to guess what she meant.
I won't tell you his reaction—I'll leave that to your imagination.
Don't let your imagination run away with you (= don't use too much imagination).
The new policies appear to have captured the imagination of the public (= they find them interesting and exciting)
His stories really stretch children’s imaginations.
Nobody hates you—it's all in your imagination.
This is an image which persists in the popular imagination.
Use your imagination! (= used to tell somebody that they will have to guess the answer to the question they have asked you, usually because it is obvious or embarrassing)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that you have imagined rather than something that exists
examples: She was no longer able to distinguish between imagination and reality.
Is it my imagination or have you lost a lot of weight?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the ability to have new and exciting ideas
examples: His writing lacks imagination.
With a little imagination, you could turn this place into a palace.
We are looking for someone with ingenuity and imagination.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to allow more of somebody’s body to be seen than usual
examples: Her tight-fitting dress left nothing to the imagination.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say strongly that something is not true, even if you try to imagine or believe it
examples: She could not, by any stretch of the imagination, be called beautiful.
By no stretch of the imagination could the trip be described as relaxing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to form a picture in your mind of what something might be like
examples: The house was just as she had imagined it.
Imagine my surprise when I opened the door to find him standing there.
I can't imagine life without the children now.
It's hard to imagine a more cynical political strategy.
Close your eyes and imagine (that) you are in a forest.
Can you imagine what it must be like to lose your job after 20 years?
Imagine earning that much money!
She imagined walking into the office and handing in her resignation.
I can just imagine him saying that!
I had imagined her to be older than that.
He loved to imagine himself as the hero.
I find it difficult to imagine her a grandmother.
I can imagine him really angry.
‘He was furious.’ ‘I can imagine.’

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to believe something that is not true
examples: He’s always imagining (that) we’re talking about him behind his back.
There's nobody there. You're imagining things.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to think that something is probably true
examples: SYNONYM suppose
‘Can we still buy tickets for the concert?’ ‘I imagine so.’
I don’t imagine (that) they’ll refuse.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening or done without delay
examples: SYNONYM instant
an immediate reaction/response
to take immediate action
RAM stores information for immediate access.
This decision will have an immediate impact on students.
The company announced the immediate availabilty of an updated version of the software.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: existing now and needing attention quickly
examples: Our immediate concern is to help the families of those who died.
The effects of global warming, while not immediate, are potentially catastrophic.
The hospital says she's out of immediate danger.
weapons of mass destruction that were an immediate threat to international security
The report focuses on some of the more immediate problems facing us.
He said there was no immediate need to appeal for international assistance.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: next to or very close to a particular place or time
examples: in the immediate vicinity
in the immediate aftermath of the war
The prospects for the immediate future are good.
The director is standing on her immediate right.
my immediate predecessor in the job (= the person who had the job just before me)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: nearest in relationship or rank
examples: The funeral was attended by her immediate family (= her parents, children, brothers and sisters) only.
He is my immediate superior (= the person directly above me) in the company.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: having a direct effect
examples: The immediate cause of death is unknown.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: starting now
examples: She has resigned with immediate effect.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: without delay
examples: SYNONYM at once
She answered almost immediately.
They immediately began arguing.
The point of my question may not be immediately apparent.
It is immediately clear that he is out of his depth.
Details were not immediately available.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: next to or very close to a particular place or time
examples: Turn right immediately after the church.
the land immediately adjacent to the river
the years immediately before the war
in the two weeks immediately prior to the exam
Who is immediately above a colonel in rank?
the period immediately following her birth
The film takes place in the days immediately preceding the invasion.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: closely and directly
examples: Counselling is being given to those most immediately affected by the tragedy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: extremely large or great
examples: SYNONYM enormous
There is still an immense amount of work to be done.
The benefits are immense.
a project of immense importance
To my immense relief, he didn’t notice my mistake.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who has come to live permanently in a country that is not their own
examples: COMPARE emigrant
illegal/undocumented immigrants
immigrants from other European countries
immigrants to the United States
immigrant workers/communities/groups

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of coming to live permanently in a country that is not your own; the number of people who do this
examples: COMPARE emigration
illegal/legal immigration
laws restricting immigration into the US
There was a sudden increase in immigration from Eastern Europe.
immigration policy/reform

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the place at a port, an airport, etc. where the passports and other documents of people coming into a country are checked
examples: We landed at Heathrow and went through customs and immigration.
immigration officers

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: likely to happen very soon
examples: the imminent threat of invasion
The system is in imminent danger of collapse.
An announcement about his resignation is imminent.
An attack seems imminent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that cannot catch or be affected by a particular disease or illness
examples: Adults are often immune to German measles.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not affected by something, especially something that you might expect to be harmful
examples: You'll eventually become immune to criticism.
Few men are immune to her charms.
Our business is far from immune to economic conditions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: protected from something and therefore able to avoid it
examples: SYNONYM exempt
No one should be immune from prosecution.
Not even the President’s wife was immune from criticism by the press.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the powerful effect that something has on somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO low-impact
a positive/a negative/an adverse impact
a significant/major/huge impact
to have/make an impact
to reduce/minimize the impact of something
the environmental impact of tourism
the economic impact of leaving the European Union
Her speech made a profound impact on everyone.
She has had a lasting impact on the lives of many of her students.
The project's impact on the environment should be minimal.
The report assesses the impact of the disease on mortality and population growth.
It is too early to notice any impact from the recent changes to the rules.
an environmental impact assessment
a victim impact statement

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of one object hitting another; the force with which this happens
examples: craters made by meteorite impacts
The impact of the blow knocked Jack off balance.
A well-designed sports shoe should absorb the impact on the 28 bones in each foot.
The bomb explodes on impact (= when it hits something).
The car is fitted with side impact bars (= to protect it from a blow from the side).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the powerful effect that something has on somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO low-impact
a positive/a negative/an adverse impact
a significant/major/huge impact

to reduce/minimize the impact of something
