A well-designed sports shoe should absorb the impact on the 28 bones in each foot.
The bomb explodes on impact (= when it hits something).
The car is fitted with side impact bars (= to protect it from a blow from the side).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: annoyed by somebody/something, especially because you have to wait for a long time
examples: I'd been waiting for twenty minutes and I was getting impatient.
The children were growing impatient.
Try not to be too impatient with her.
Sarah was becoming increasingly impatient at their lack of interest.
An impatient driver behind me sounded his horn.
He waved them away with an impatient gesture.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: wanting to do something soon; wanting something to happen soon
examples: She was clearly impatient to leave.
impatient for change

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: unable or unwilling to accept something unpleasant
examples: impatient of criticism

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make something that has been officially decided start to happen or be used
examples: SYNONYM carry out
to implement changes/decisions/policies/reforms
A new work programme for young people will be implemented.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of making something that has been officially decided start to happen or be used
examples: the implementation of the new system

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a possible effect or result of an action or a decision
examples: They failed to consider the wider implications of their actions.
The development of the site will have implications for the surrounding countryside.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that is suggested or indirectly stated (= something that is implied)
examples: The implication in his article is that being a housewife is greatly inferior to every other occupation.
He criticized the Director and, by implication, the whole of the organization.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the fact of being involved, or of involving somebody, in something, especially a crime
examples: SYNONYM involvement
He resigned after his implication in a sex scandal.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to suggest that something is true or that you feel or think something, without saying so directly
examples: Are you implying (that) I am wrong?
I disliked the implied criticism in his voice.
His silence seemed to imply agreement.
High-yield bonds, as the name implies, offer a high rate of interest.
It was implied that we were at fault.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make it seem likely that something is true or exists
examples: SYNONYM suggest
The survey implies (that) more people are moving house than was thought.
It was implied in the survey that…
Popularity does not necessarily imply merit.
The fact that she was here implies a degree of interest.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make something necessary in order to be successful
examples: SYNONYM mean
The project implies an enormous investment in training.
Sustainable development implies a long-term perspective.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a product or service that is brought into one country from another
examples: OPPOSITE export
food imports from abroad
cheap imports into the United States

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of bringing a product or service into one country from another
examples: OPPOSITE export
The report calls for a ban on the import of hazardous waste.
imports of oil
import duties/tariffs
import controls/restrictions/quotas
an import licence
A restricted import quota was set for meat products.
the UK's net imports of food
Most of their oil revenues are used to finance imports of consumer and capital goods.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: importance
examples: matters of great import

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the meaning of something, especially when it is not immediately clear
examples: It is difficult to understand the full import of this statement.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a product or service that is brought into one country from another
examples: OPPOSITE export

cheap imports into the United States

definitions.definition: importance
examples: matters of great import

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the meaning of something, especially when it is not immediately clear
examples: It is difficult to understand the full import of this statement.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of being important
examples: SEE ALSO self-importance
She stressed the importance of careful preparation.
to emphasize/highlight the importance of something
He understands the importance of getting the details right.
They attach great importance to the project.
the relative importance of the two ideas
It's a matter of the utmost importance to me.
to be of paramount/vital importance
State your reasons in order of importance.
He was very aware of his own importance (= of his status).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a great effect on people or things; of great value
examples: SEE ALSO all-important
an important issue/question/point/factor
We have an important decision to make.
Money played an important role in his life.
Listening is an important part of the job.
one of the most important collections of American art
The important thing is to keep trying.
The centre is extremely important to many local people.
Banks are vitally important to the economy.
Many chemicals are important for our health.
It is important to follow the manufacturer's instructions.
It is important to note that total government funding has increased.
It's important to remember that our figures are averages only.
It is important that he attend every day.
It is important that he should attend every day.
It's very important to me that you be there.
It's very important to me that you should be there.
It is important for him to attend every day.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having great influence or authority
examples: SEE ALSO self-important
an important member of the team
He likes to feel important.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to introduce a new law, rule, tax, etc.; to order that a rule, punishment, etc. be used
examples: The UN Security Council imposed sanctions in 1992.
to impose a penalty/fine/sentence/ban
A new tax was imposed on fuel.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to force somebody/something to have to deal with something that is difficult or unpleasant
examples: He described the limitations imposed by his disease.
This system imposes additional financial burdens on many people.
to impose restrictions/constraints/obligations on somebody/something
The time limits are imposed on us by factors outside our control.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody accept the same opinions, wishes, etc. as your own
examples: She didn't want to impose her values on her family.
It was noticeable how a few people managed to impose their will on the others.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to expect somebody to do something for you or to spend time with you, when it may not be convenient for them
examples: ‘You must stay for lunch.’ ‘Well, thanks, but I don’t want to impose…’
Everyone imposes on Dave's good nature.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something accept or be aware of your presence or ideas
examples: European civilization was the first to impose itself across the whole world.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that cannot exist or be done; not possible
examples: OPPOSITE possible
almost/virtually/nearly impossible
Only a year ago and this would have seemed impossible.
Getting any kind of decent job was proving impossible.
an impossible dream/goal
Going downstairs would be impossible for him with his sprained ankle.
The outcome is impossible to predict.
It's impossible to prove.
Cheap rental accommodation was impossible to find.
It's impossible to say which is the best.
It is impossible to tell whether it will actually work.
I find it impossible to lie to her.
It's impossible for me to be there before eight.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very difficult to deal with
examples: I've been placed in an impossible position.
Honestly, you're impossible at times!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing that is or seems impossible
examples: to attempt the impossible

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a difficult or impossible task
examples: Many regard this task as mission impossible.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if a person or thing impresses you, you admire them or it
examples: SEE ALSO impressed
We interviewed a number of candidates but none of them impressed us.
The Grand Canyon never fails to impress people.
The Grand Canyon never fails to impress.
His sincerity impressed her.
He impressed her with his sincerity.
It impressed me that she remembered my name.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody understand how important, serious, etc. something is by emphasizing it
examples: He impressed on us the need for immediate action.
Their responsibilities are impressed on them during training.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have a great effect on something, especially somebody’s mind, imagination, etc.
examples: Her words impressed themselves on my memory.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: admiring somebody/something because you think they are particularly good, interesting, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO unimpressed
I must admit I am impressed.
We were all impressed by her enthusiasm.
He was particularly impressed by her essay.
She was suitably impressed (= as impressed as somebody had hoped) with the painting.
He was impressed at the way the team had played.
We were impressed to see how well they'd done already.
I was impressed that she remembered my name.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an idea, a feeling or an opinion that you get about somebody/something, or that somebody/something gives you
examples: My first impression of him was favourable.
She gives the impression of being very busy.
I did not get the impression that they were unhappy about the situation.
I had the impression that it was all done in a hurry.
My impression is that there are still a lot of problems.
Try and smile. You don't want to give people the wrong impression (= that you are not friendly).
He does not want to give a false impression of progress.
If you want to create the right impression, I suggest you wear a suit.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the effect that an experience or a person has on somebody/something
examples: You'll have to play better than that if you really want to make an impression (= to make people admire you).
His trip to India made a strong impression on him.
My words made no impression on her.
The whole business left a lasting impression on Margaret.
The new player failed to make an immediate impression on the team.
I don't think this argument made any impression upon the brothers.
The events left an indelible impression on all those who witnessed them.
The stillness and silence leave a deep impression on visitors.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a drawing showing what a person looks like or what a place or a building will look like in the future
examples: This is an artist's impression of the new stadium.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a clever or funny copy of the way a person acts or speaks
examples: SYNONYM impersonation
He did an impression of Tom Hanks.
She did her Marilyn Monroe impression.

examples: You risk incurring bank charges if you exceed your overdraft limit.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

The original sense ‘index finger’ (the finger with which one points), came to mean ‘pointer’ (late 16th cent.), and figuratively something that serves to point to a fact or conclusion; hence a list of topics in a book (“pointing” to their location).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to mention something, especially in an indirect way
examples: In his letter he indicated to us (that) he was willing to cooperate.
He indicated his willingness to cooperate.
Has she indicated yet whether she would like to be involved?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make somebody notice somebody/something, especially by pointing or moving your head
examples: ‘What are they doing here?’ he asked, indicating her bags in the hallway.
She took out a map and indicated the quickest route to us.
He indicated where the furniture was to go.
She indicated that I was to sit down.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to represent information without using words
examples: Arrows indicate the direction of flow.
The results are indicated in Table 2.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to give information in writing
examples: You are allowed 20  kg of baggage unless indicated otherwise on your ticket.
As indicated above, this chapter deals with the practical implications of the research.
Please indicate clearly which colour you require.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to show a particular measurement
examples: When the temperature gauge indicates 90°F or more, turn off the engine.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to show that your vehicle is going to change direction, by using lights or your arm
examples: SYNONYM signal
Always indicate before moving into another lane.
He indicated left and then turned right.
She indicated that she was turning right.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be necessary or recommended
examples: A course of chemotherapy was indicated.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a remark or sign that shows that something is happening or what somebody is thinking or feeling
examples: They gave no indication of how the work should be done.
He shows every indication (= clear signs) of wanting to accept the post.
There are clear indications that the economy is improving.
All the indications are that the deal will go ahead as planned.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a symptom that suggests that particular medical treatment is necessary
examples: There was no clinical indication for such a test.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sign that shows you what something is like or how a situation is changing
examples: The economic indicators are better than expected.
These atmospheric waves are a reliable indicator of weather changes.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a device on a machine that shows speed, pressure, etc.
examples: a depth indicator

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a light on a vehicle that flashes to show that the vehicle is going to turn left or right
examples: Her right-hand indicator was flashing.
She flicked on her indicator light and passed the lorry.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sign that a system, society, etc. is very bad or very wrong
examples: The poverty in our cities is a damning indictment of modern society.
This research is a terrible indictment on the medical profession.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an official statement accusing somebody of a crime
examples: She was convicted on an indictment for conspiracy.
The federal district court dismissed the indictment.
The government announced a federal indictment against him.
They issued an indictment against them.
Two men were named in the indictment.
War crimes indictments were handed down by a UN-backed court.
an indictment charging theft
There is sufficient evidence against him to support an indictment for murder.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of officially accusing somebody of a crime
examples: This led to his indictment on allegations of conspiracy.
He faces indictment for perjury.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: belonging to a particular place rather than coming to it from somewhere else
examples: SYNONYM native
the indigenous peoples/languages of the area
The kangaroo is indigenous to Australia.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening not as the main aim, cause or result of a particular action, but in addition to it
examples: the indirect effects of the war
to find something out by indirect methods
The building collapsed as an indirect result of the heavy rain.
There would be some benefit, however indirect, to the state.
indirect costs (= costs that are not directly connected with making a product, for example training, heating, rent, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not done directly; done through somebody/something else
examples: territories under the indirect control of the British

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: avoiding saying something in a clear and obvious way
examples: The comment was an indirect attack on the prime minister.
The president made an indirect reference to the subject in his speech.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not going in a straight line
examples: an indirect route
The plant prefers indirect sunlight.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person considered separately rather than as part of a group
examples: The competition is open to both teams and individuals.
Treatment depends on the individual involved.
He has persuaded private individuals (= ordinary people rather than companies, etc.) to donate to the collection.
There is no single individual who is to blame.
Wealthy individuals currently account for about 75 per cent of hedge fund investment, and institutions make up the other 25 per cent.
We are concerned to protect the rights of the individual.
Every child is treated here as an individual.
Symptoms of depression vary among individuals.
Differences between individuals affect their susceptibility to disease.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a single member of a class of things
examples: They live in a group or as individuals, depending on the species.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is original and very different from others
examples: She's grown into quite an individual.
She saw the artist as a unique individual, possessing a heightened awareness of reality.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person of a particular type, especially a strange one
examples: an odd-looking individual
So this individual came up and demanded money.
This scruffy-looking individual wandered into the office.

Let's go indoors.
I was indoors watching TV when I heard shouting in the street.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: Nothing would induce me to take the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to cause something
examples: drugs that induce sleep
a drug-induced coma
Hearing loss is often induced by exposure to loud noise.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a woman start giving birth to her baby by giving her special drugs; to make a baby start being born by giving the mother special drugs
examples: an induced labour
We'll have to induce her.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to allow yourself to have or do something that you like, especially something that is considered bad for you
examples: They went into town to indulge in some serious shopping.

I indulged myself with a long hot bath.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to satisfy a particular desire, interest, etc.
examples: The inheritance enabled him to indulge his passion for art.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be too generous in allowing somebody to have or do whatever they like
examples: She did not believe in indulging the children with presents.
His questions were annoying but it was easier to indulge him than try and protest.
Her father had always indulged her every whim.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to take part in an activity, especially one that is illegalWord Origin
examples: early 17th cent. (in the sense ‘treat with excessive kindness’): from Latin indulgere ‘give free rein to’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with industry
examples: SEE ALSO agro-industrial
an industrial dispute
industrial unrest
an industrial accident
Industrial production fell in December by 1.4 per cent.
policy with regard to future industrial development
India has a large industrial sector.
a huge industrial complex
the country's industrial base

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used by industries
examples: industrial chemicals

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having many industries
examples: SEE ALSO post-industrial
an industrial city/town
an industrial society
the world’s leading industrial nations

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very great in extent or amount
examples: They had made industrial quantities of food.
They were guilty of fraud on an industrial scale.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the production of goods from raw materials, especially in factories
examples: SEE ALSO captain of industry
the needs of British industry
the Department of Trade and Industry
She got a job in industry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the people and activities involved in producing a particular thing, or in providing a particular service
examples: SEE ALSO agro-industry
the steel/oil/auto industry
the music/film/tourism industry
We need to develop local industries.
She later worked in the banking industry.

industry insiders/analysts/experts
the Kardashian industry (= the large number of people involved in making the Kardashian family successful)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of working hard
examples: We were impressed by their industry.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the unfair difference between groups of people in society, when some have more wealth, status or opportunities than others
examples: OPPOSITE equality
We need to tackle inequality of opportunity wherever we find it.
economic inequalities between different areas
Gender and racial inequality are still widespread throughout society.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that you cannot avoid or prevent
examples: SYNONYM unavoidable
It was an inevitable consequence of the decision.
It was inevitable that there would be job losses.
A rise in the interest rates seems inevitable.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: happening so often that you always expect it
examples: the English and their inevitable cups of tea

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that is certain to happen
examples: You have to accept the inevitable.
The inevitable happened—I forgot my passport.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: as is certain to happen
examples: Inevitably, the press exaggerated the story.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: as you would expect
examples: Inevitably, it rained on the day of the wedding.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: well known for being bad or evil
examples: SYNONYM notorious

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: a nursery for infants under two
their infant son

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a child at school between the ages of four and seven
examples: an infant school

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make somebody share a particular feeling
examples: She infected the children with her enthusiasm for music.

a fungal infection of the skin

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to suggest indirectly that something is true
examples: Are you inferring (that) I’m not capable of doing the job?

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: His early work shows the influence of Cézanne and Matisse.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 1

informal discussions/talks

examples: the informal economy/sector

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: SYNONYM directory assistance

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: For your information, I don't even have a car.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: This book is a mine of information on the Romans.

The questionnaire results proved to be a rich mine of empirical data.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the basic systems and services that are necessary for a country or an organization to run smoothly, for example buildings, transport and water and power suppliesWord Origin
examples: early 20th cent.: from French (see infra-, structure).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of the things from which something is made, especially one of the foods that are used together to make a particular dish
examples: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl.
Our skin cream contains only natural ingredients.
The only active ingredient in this medicine is aspirin.
Avocado is the main ingredient of the Mexican dish.
Coconut is a basic ingredient for many curries.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one of the things or qualities that are necessary to make something successful
examples: It has all the ingredients of a good mystery story.

Determination is one of the essential ingredients for success.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or an animal that lives in a particular place
examples: the oldest inhabitant of the village
It is a town of about 10 000 inhabitants.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that is a basic or permanent part of somebody/something and that cannot be removed

the difficulties inherent in a study of this type

an inherent weakness in the design of the machine

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to receive money, property, etc. from somebody when they die

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: The managing director's presence inhibited them from airing their problems.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

an initial phase/period
an initial assessment/investigation/report

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at the beginning

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make something begin

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: Many of them had been initiated into drug use at an early age.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody a member of a particular group, especially as part of a secret ceremony
examples: Hundreds are initiated into the sect each year.

new initiatives to improve animal welfare
a government initiative to combat unemployment
a joint initiative by the Scottish and UK governments
an initiative for peace and human rights

examples: The fruit is injected with chemicals to reduce decay.

definitions.definition: a large sum of money that is spent to help improve a situation, business, etc.
examples: The theatre faces closure unless it gets an urgent cash injection.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an act of forcing a liquid or other substance into something
examples: SEE ALSO fuel injection
a fuel injection system

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to harm yourself or somebody else physically, especially in an accident
examples: He injured his knee playing hockey.
Three people were killed and five injured in the crash.
She injured herself during training.
She was seriously injured in a riding accident.
During the Second World War he was badly injured by a bomb.
He was hit by an unmarked police car and severely injured.
The man was critically injured after falling from a ladder.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to damage somebody’s reputation, interests, feelings, etc.
examples: This could seriously injure the company's reputation.
espionage activity that was likely to injure the national interest

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: physically hurt; having an injury
examples: OPPOSITE uninjured
His injured leg prevented him from walking.
Luckily, she isn't injured.
Carter is playing in place of the injured O'Reilly.
The boy and another seriously injured person were evacuated by air ambulance
He tried to pull his critically injured friend from the burning vehicle.
He was conscious, but severely injured.
her badly injured ankle

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the people injured in an accident, a battle, etc.
examples: Ambulances took the injured to a nearby hospital.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: upset or offended because something unfair has been done
examples: an injured look/tone
injured pride

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: harm done to a person’s or an animal’s body, for example in an accident
examples: SEE ALSO personal injury
Two people sustained minor injuries.
One of the girls suffered serious injuries.
He was lucky to escape injury.
The passengers escaped with only minor injuries.
As a result of the accident, several passengers sustained serious head injuries.
One youth was treated for injuries to his arm.
He died from multiple injuries caused by the accident.
There were no injuries in the crash (= no people injured).
No damage or injuries were reported.
These new guidelines will help save lives and prevent injury.
Taking a few simple precautions will reduce your risk of injury.
This could result in serious injury or even death.
Two players are out of the team because of injury.
Don't do that. You'll do yourself an injury (= hurt yourself).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: damage to a person’s feelings
examples: Damages may be awarded for emotional injury.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a bad relationship with somebody worse by offending them even more
examples: Then, to add insult to injury, they told me I couldn't get on the flight.
It adds insult to injury that banks are allowed to increase their charges without our knowledge or consent.
Only 300 people came to the match and to add insult to injury, the floodlights went out during the second half.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the fact of a situation being unfair and of people not being treated equally; an unfair act or an example of unfair treatment
examples: OPPOSITE justice
We are committed to fighting against poverty and injustice.
a burning sense of injustice
Social and political injustice seemed to be getting worse rather than better.
She was enraged at the injustice of the remark.
The report exposes the injustices of the system.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to judge yourself/somebody unfairly
examples: We may have been doing him an injustice. This work is good.
Perhaps I'm doing you an injustice.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: coloured liquid for writing, drawing and printing
examples: SEE ALSO Indian ink
written in ink
different coloured inks
a pen and ink drawing

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of the people living in an institution such as a prison or a psychiatric hospital
examples: The jail has 500 inmates.
He was attacked by a fellow inmate.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: inside; towards or close to the centre of a place
examples: OPPOSITE outer
an inner courtyard
inner London

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: private and secret; not expressed or shown to other people
examples: She doesn't reveal much of her inner self.
the inner workings of the mind
An inner voice told him that what he was doing was wrong.
He has to fight an inner turmoil even to step onto a plane.
a character who makes us wish to know more about his inner life
It's time to get in touch with your inner geek (= the part of you that likes geeky things, even though you pretend not to).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not guilty of a crime, etc.; not having done something wrong
examples: OPPOSITE guilty
They have imprisoned an innocent man.
She was found innocent of any crime.
I was convinced that he was innocent of killing his wife.
He was the innocent party (= person) in the breakdown of the marriage.
There must be an innocent explanation for her behaviour.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: suffering harm or being killed because of a crime, war, etc. although not directly involved in it
examples: an innocent bystander
innocent victims of the bomb blast
Thousands of innocent civilians have been killed in this conflict.
He expressed outrage at the loss of innocent lives.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having little experience of the world, especially of sexual matters, or of evil or unpleasant things
examples: SYNONYM naive
He prefers to see his teenage daughter as an innocent young child.
She is very naive and innocent.
He looked so sweet and innocent.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not intended to cause harm or upset somebody
examples: SYNONYM harmless
It was all innocent fun.
It was a perfectly innocent remark.
The circumstance could be altogether innocent, but suspicions have been raised.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the introduction of new things, ideas or ways of doing something
examples: an age of technological innovation
The company is very interested in product design and innovation.
Too strict a regulatory system will stifle innovation.
innovation in engineering

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a new idea, way of doing something, etc. that has been introduced or discovered
examples: technological innovations designed to save energy
recent innovations in steel-making technology

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: introducing or using new ideas, ways of doing something, etc.
examples: There will be a prize for the most innovative design.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: time, knowledge, ideas, etc. that you put into work, a project, etc. in order to make it succeed; the act of putting something in
examples: I'd appreciate your input on this.
Her specialist input to the discussions has been very useful.
Barley is one of the main inputs to the process of distillation.
Growing anything in this soil will require heavy inputs of nutrients.
There has been a big input of resources into the project from industry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of putting information into a computer; the information that you put in
examples: data input
The software will accept input from a variety of other programs.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a place or means for electricity, data, etc. to enter a machine or system
examples: an input lead
Where is the audio input on the computer?
inputs for the printers

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official process to find out the cause of something or to find out information about something
examples: a murder inquiry
a public inquiry into the environmental effects of the proposed new road
to hold/conduct/launch an inquiry into the affair

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a request for information about somebody/something; a question about somebody/something
examples: inquiries from prospective students about courses
We received over 300 inquiries about the job.
Greetings and inquiries about family members tend to be in the local dialect.
mkaI'll have to make a few inquiries and get back to you.
For further inquiries, please call…
All inquiries should be addressed to the customer services department.
Two men have been helping police with their inquries (= are being questioned about a crime, but have not been charged with it).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of asking questions or collecting information about somebody/something
examples: scientific inquiry
The police are following several lines of inquiry.
a commission/committee of inquiry

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a place where you can get information
examples: Ask at inquiries to see if your bag has been handed in.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: any small creature with six legs and a body divided into three parts. Insects usually also have wings. ants, bees and flies are all insects.
examples: SEE ALSO stick insect
Most birds spend most of the day eating insects.
There are about 30 million species of insects in the world.
insect species
insect repellent (= a chemical that keeps insects away)
an insect bite
The pesticide is lethal to all insect life.
methods to ensure the plants are as free of disease and insect pests as possible

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to put something into something else or between two things
examples: Insert coins into the slot and press for a ticket.
They inserted a tube in his mouth to help him breathe.
She picked up a knife and inserted it between the top of the drawer and the desk.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to add something to a piece of writing
examples: Position the cursor where you want to insert a word.
The program will automatically insert the replacement text.
Later, he inserted another paragraph into his will.
The English translation is inserted between the lines of text.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of putting something inside something else; a thing that is put inside something else
examples: An examination is carried out before the insertion of the tube.
Acupuncture involves the insertion of needles into specific points of the body.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that is added to a book, piece of writing, etc.; the act of adding something
examples: the insertion of an extra paragraph

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: on or to the inner part of something/somebody; within something/somebody
examples: OPPOSITE outside
Go inside the house.
Inside the box was a gold watch.
For years we had little knowledge of what life was like inside China.
You'll feel better with a good meal inside you.
Inside most of us is a small child screaming for attention.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in less than the amount of time mentioned
examples: COMPARE outside (4)
The job is unlikely to be finished inside (of) a year.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who knows a lot about a group or an organization, because they are part of it
examples: COMPARE outsider
The situation was described by one insider as ‘absolute chaos’.
an insider’s view of the movie industry

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an understanding of what something is like
examples: There are many valuable insights in her book.
His work offers several useful insights.
The book gives us fascinating insights into life in Mexico.
I hope you have gained some insight into the difficulties we face.
She has some interesting insights on the principles that have guided US foreign policy.
The book provides important insights about the doctor-patient relationship.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the ability to see and understand the truth about people or situations
examples: He has insight, vision and a deep humanity.
She was a writer of great insight.
With a flash of insight I realized what the dream meant.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to demand that something happen or that somebody agree to do something
examples: I didn't really want to go but he insisted.
Stay and have lunch. I insist!
‘Please come with us.’ ‘Very well then, if you insist.’
She insisted on him wearing a suit
She insisted on his wearing a suit
He insists that she come.
He insists that she should come.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to state clearly that something is true, especially when other people do not believe you
examples: He insisted on his innocence.
He insisted (that) he was innocent.
The government has always insisted that this was not the case.
‘It's true,’ she insisted.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to look closely at something/somebody, especially to check that everything is as it should be
examples: SYNONYM examine
The teacher walked around inspecting their work.
Make sure you inspect the goods before signing for them.
The plants are regularly inspected for disease.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to officially visit a school, factory, etc. in order to check that rules are being obeyed and that standards are acceptable
examples: Public health officials were called in to inspect the premises.
The Tourist Board inspects all recommended hotels at least once a year.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official visit to a school, factory, etc. in order to check that rules are being obeyed and that standards are acceptable
examples: Regular inspections are carried out at the prison.
The head went on a tour of inspection of all the classrooms.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of looking closely at something/somebody, especially to check that everything is as it should be
examples: SYNONYM examination
The documents are available for inspection.
Engineers carried out a thorough inspection of the track.
Following an 8 a.m. pitch inspection by the referee, today's game has been called off due to a waterlogged pitch.
On closer inspection, the notes proved to be forgeries.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an officer of middle rank in the police force
examples: SEE ALSO chief inspector
Inspector Maggie Forbes
He reached the rank of inspector.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person whose job is to visit schools, factories, etc. to check that rules are being obeyed and that standards are acceptable
examples: a school/health/safety inspector

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: (in the UK) a person whose job is to check tickets on a bus or trainWord Origin
examples: early 17th cent.: from Latin, from inspicere (from in- ‘in’ + specere ‘look at’).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process that takes place when somebody sees or hears something that causes them to have exciting new ideas or makes them want to create something, especially in art, music or literature
examples: Dreams can be a rich source of inspiration for an artist.
Both poets drew their inspiration from the countryside.
Her work lacks inspiration (= it does not contain any exciting new ideas).
Looking for inspiration for a new dessert? Try this recipe.
She had the time and the inspiration to develop her talent.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is the reason why somebody creates or does something
examples: He says my sister was the inspiration for his heroine.
Clark was the inspiration behind Saturday's victory.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that makes you want to be better, more successful, etc.
examples: Her charity work is an inspiration to us all.
She became an inspiration and a role model for a new generation of women.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a sudden good idea
examples: He had an inspiration: he'd give her a dog for her birthday.
It came to me in a flash of inspiration.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give somebody the desire, confidence or enthusiasm to do something well
examples: The actors' enthusiasm inspired the kids.
The actors inspired the kids with their enthusiasm.
His superb play inspired the team to a thrilling 5–0 win.
By visiting schools, the actors hope to inspire children to put on their own productions.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give somebody the idea for something, especially something artistic or that shows imagination
examples: The choice of decor was inspired by a trip to India.
His tragic story later inspired a Hollywood film.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody have a particular feeling or emotion
examples: Henry did not inspire confidence as a figure of authority.
Her work didn't exactly inspire me with confidence.
As a general, he inspired great loyalty in his troops.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to fix equipment or furniture into position so that it can be used
examples: They're planning to install a new drainage system.
Make sure the equipment is properly installed.
A hidden camera had been installed in the room.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to put a new program onto a computer
examples: to install software/an app
Do not download and install programs from websites that you are unfamiliar with.
Be selective about the apps you install on your device.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to put somebody in a new position of authority, often with an official ceremony
examples: He was installed as President last May.
She was recently installed as president of the National Medical Association.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make somebody/yourself comfortable in a particular place or position
examples: We installed ourselves in the front row.
She saw her guests safely installed in their rooms and then went downstairs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of fixing equipment or furniture in position so that it can be used
examples: installation costs
Installation of the new system will take several days.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of equipment or a machine that has been fixed in position so that it can be used
examples: a heating installation

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of putting a new program onto a computer
examples: installation of the software

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a place where specialist equipment is kept and used
examples: a military installation

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the act of placing somebody in a new position of authority, often with a ceremony
examples: the installation of the new chancellor

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a piece of modern sculpture that is made using sound, light, etc. as well as objectsWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from medieval Latin installatio(n-), from the verb installare, from in- ‘into’ + stallum ‘place, stall’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a particular example or case of something
examples: The report highlights a number of instances of injustice.
He admitted two instances of taking money from the till.
There have been several instances of that happening.
In most instances, there will be no need for further treatment.
In rare instances, viral infections in the mother may be passed to the unborn child.
I would normally suggest taking time off work, but in this instance I'm not sure that would do any good.
Students described many instances in which they had felt uncomfortable speaking in class.
This is one of the few instances where the director does not succeed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: for example
examples: What would you do, for instance, if you found a member of staff stealing?
Murder, petty theft and tax evasion, for instance, all have different motives and consequences.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: as the first part of a series of actions
examples: In the first instance, notify the police and then contact your insurance company.
In the first instance, a letter from your employer may be all you need.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening immediately
examples: SYNONYM immediate
This account gives you instant access to your money.
The show was an instant success.
People today seem to want instant gratification.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that can be made quickly and easily, usually by adding hot water
examples: instant coffee

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: immediately
examples: Her voice is instantly recognizable.
The driver was killed instantly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in the place of somebody/something
examples: Lee was ill so I went instead.
He didn't reply. Instead, he turned on his heel and left the room.
She said nothing, preferring instead to save her comments till later.
She might have pursued a successful career in business, but she chose instead to become a nun.
The UN resisted any tougher sanctions, opting instead for more time to give talks a chance.
While the Conservatives put the emphasis on the economy, Labour focused instead on public services.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a natural quality that makes people and animals tend to behave in a particular way using the knowledge and abilities that they were born with rather than thought or training
examples: SEE ALSO herd instinct
She did not seem to have any of the usual maternal instincts.
Children do not know by instinct the difference between right and wrong.
His first instinct was to run away.
Horses have a well-developed instinct for fear.
Even at school, he showed he had an instinct for (= was naturally good at) business.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a feeling that makes you do something or believe that something is true, even though it is not based on facts or reason
examples: SYNONYM intuition
I've always trusted my instincts in the past.
It's best to follow your first instincts in matters like this.
Her instincts about him had been right.
He had a gut instinct for when people were lying to him.
I acted purely on instinct.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an organization that has a particular purpose, especially one that is connected with education or a particular profession; the building used by this organization
examples: SEE ALSO collegiate institute
The report was compiled by Germany's five leading economic research institutes.
The course is offered at six colleges and institutes of higher education.
He is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants.
She was a senior researcher at the institute.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large important organization that has a particular purpose, for example a university or bank
examples: The deal is backed by one of the country's largest financial institutions.
He has worked as a visiting lecturer for various educational institutions.
The system is targeted mainly at academic and research institutions.
the Smithsonian Institution
The region boasts several institutions of higher education.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a building where people with special needs are taken care of, for example because they are old or mentally ill
examples: They had him committed to a mental institution.
We want this to be like a home, not an institution.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a custom or system that has existed for a long time among a particular group of people
examples: He claimed this threatened ‘the sacred institution of marriage’.
Fish and chips became a national institution in Britain.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of starting or introducing something such as a system or a law
examples: the institution of new safety procedures

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person who is well known because they have been in a particular place or job for a long time
examples: You must know him—he's an institution around here!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with a large important organization, for example a university or bank
examples: institutional investors

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in or like a building where people with special needs are taken care of
examples: institutional care
The rooms are rather drab and institutional.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: established as a normal part of an organization or culture
examples: institutional racism

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell somebody to do something, especially in a formal or official way
examples: SYNONYM direct
The letter instructed him to report to headquarters immediately.
You will be instructed where to go as soon as the plane is ready.
She arrived at 10 o'clock as instructed.
He instructed that a wall be built around the city.
He instructed that a wall should be built around the city.
‘Put it there,’ she instructed (them).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to teach somebody something, especially a practical skill
examples: All our staff have been instructed in sign language.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to give somebody information about something
examples: We have been instructed that a decision will not be made before the end of the week.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to employ somebody to represent you in a legal situation, especially as a lawyerWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (in sense (2)): from Latin instruct- ‘constructed, equipped, taught’, from the verb instruere, from in- ‘upon, towards’ + struere ‘pile up’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: detailed information on how to do or use something
examples: SYNONYM direction
Follow the instructions on the packet carefully.
Always read the instructions before you start.
Step-by-step instructions are provided.
The plant comes with full instructions on how to care for it.
The tin or packet should be clearly labelled with instructions for use.
The website has easy instructions for making dozens of costumes for children.
According to the instructions, you can get started in one hour.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that somebody tells you to do
examples: SYNONYM order
Climbers should always follow the instructions of their guide.
to ignore/carry out somebody's instructions
Police are awaiting instructions from senior officers before proceeding.
His instructions to his staff were very clear.
She gave him detailed instructions on the procedure to be followed.
The government has issued specific instructions on reducing waste disposal.
He said he received his instructions for the attack on the embassy by telephone.
He left strict instructions that the box should only be opened after his death.
I have explicit instructions not to let anyone else in.
I'm under instructions to keep my speech short.
He phoned you on my instructions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a piece of information that tells a computer to perform a particular operation
examples: The chip runs at speeds of up to 100MHz and executes two instructions per clock cycle.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of teaching something to somebody
examples: Religious instruction is banned in all state schools in the country.
the language/medium of instruction used in the school
She had no formal instruction in music.
basic instruction on using the internet
driver under instruction (= being taught how to drive)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person whose job is to teach somebody a practical skill or sport
examples: a fitness/driving/ski instructor
a qualified/certified instructor
He worked for a time as an aerobics instructor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a teacher below the rank of assistant professor at a college or university

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an object used for producing musical sounds, for example a piano or a drum
examples: SEE ALSO stringed instrument
to play an instrument
Is he learning an instrument?
percussion/brass/string instruments
an instrument maker

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a tool or device used for a particular task, especially for specialist or scientific work
examples: SEE ALSO blunt instrument (1)
surgical/optical/scientific instruments
Scientists then began using powerful instruments to peer through the planet's dense atmosphere.
syringes, needles or other sharp instruments
medieval instruments of torture such as the rack and the wheel
Instruments for diagnosis and surgery have become hugely more sophisticated.
the world's most powerful instrument for detecting gamma rays

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a device used for measuring speed, distance, temperature, etc. in a vehicle or on a machine
examples: data gathered by instruments aboard the satellite
the flight instruments
There was a warning light flashing on the instrument panel.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: something that is used by somebody in order to achieve something; a person or thing that makes something happen
examples: SEE ALSO blunt instrument (2)
The law is not the best instrument for dealing with family matters.
an instrument of change

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person who is used and controlled by somebody/something that is more powerful
examples: an instrument of fate
The despot claimed to be the chosen instrument of divine providence.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a formal legal document
examples: SEE ALSO statutory instrument
credit instruments issued by banks

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: important in making something happen
examples: The Conservation Trust performs an instrumental role in the protection of rural environments.
He was instrumental in bringing about an end to the conflict.
They were highly instrumental in bringing the business to Newtown.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: made by or for musical instruments
examples: instrumental music
The songs are largely instrumental.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in the form that a noun, pronoun or adjective has when it refers to a thing that is used to do something
examples: COMPARE ablative
the instrumental case

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not large, strong or important enough for a particular purpose
examples: SYNONYM inadequate
insufficient time
The management paid insufficient attention to working conditions.
There are fears that the existing flood barrier may prove insufficient.
I’m afraid we have insufficient evidence.
His salary is insufficient to meet his needs.
The plan was to refurbish the whole building but the funds raised were insufficient for the purpose.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a remark or an action that is said or done in order to offend somebody
examples: The crowd were shouting insults at the police.
His comments were seen as an insult to the president.
The questions were an insult to our intelligence (= too easy).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make a bad relationship with somebody worse by offending them even more
examples: Then, to add insult to injury, they told me I couldn't get on the flight.
It adds insult to injury that banks are allowed to increase their charges without our knowledge or consent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to translate one language into another as it is spoken
examples: He took me with him to interpret in case no one spoke English.
She couldn't speak much English so her children had to interpret for her.
Interpreters must interpret everything that is said in the interaction.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to perform a piece of music, a role in a play, etc. in a way that shows your feelings about its meaning
examples: He interpreted the role with a lot of humour.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the particular way in which something is understood or explained
examples: Her evidence suggests a different interpretation of the events.
It is not possible for everyone to put their own interpretation on the law.
Dreams are open to interpretation (= they can be explained in different ways).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the particular way in which somebody chooses to perform a piece of music, a role in a play, etc.
examples: a modern interpretation of ‘King Lear’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say or do something that makes somebody stop what they are saying or doing
examples: Sorry to interrupt, but there's someone to see you.
Would you mind not interrupting with questions all the time?
I hope I'm not interrupting you.
They were interrupted by a knock at the door.
The President's speech was constantly interrrupted with boos and jeers.
‘I have a question,’ she interrupted.
‘Just listen for a moment,’ he interrupted her angrily.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop something for a short time
examples: The game was interrupted several times by rain.
We interrupt this programme to bring you an important news bulletin.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to stop a line, surface, view, etc. from being even or continuous
examples: There were no other buildings to interrupt the view of the valley.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a period of time between two events
examples: The interval between major earthquakes might be 200 years.
He knocked on the door and after a brief interval it was opened.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a short period of time separating parts of a play, film or concert
examples: There will be an interval of 20 minutes after the second act.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a short period during which something different happens from what is happening the rest of the time
examples: She's delirious, but has lucid intervals.
The day should be mainly dry with sunny intervals.
The intervals between his various illnesses grew shorter and shorter.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a difference in pitch (= how high or low a note sounds) between two notes
examples: an interval of one octave

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: with time between
examples: Buses to the city leave at regular intervals.
The runners started at 5-minute intervals.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: with spaces between
examples: Flaming torches were positioned at intervals along the terrace.
The flags were spaced at two-metre intervals.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become involved in a situation in order to improve or help it
examples: She might have been killed if the neighbours hadn't intervened.
The President intervened personally in the crisis.
She went over to intervene between the two men.
They would not intervene against the rebels themselves.
attempts to intervene with the authorities on the prisoners' behalf
They intervened to halt the attack.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to interrupt somebody when they are speaking in order to say something
examples: ‘But,’ she intervened, ‘what about the others?’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to happen in a way that delays something or prevents it from happening
examples: They were planning to get married and then the war intervened.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to exist between two events or places
examples: I saw nothing of her during the years that intervened.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: action taken to improve or help a situation
examples: calls for government intervention to save the steel industry
In the second group of states, direct intervention in the economy was limited.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: action by a country to become involved in the affairs of another country when they have not been asked to do so
examples: SEE ALSO non-intervention
armed/military intervention
NATO intervention in the troubled region

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: action taken to improve a medical condition or illness
examples: a medical/surgical intervention
Most patients make a recovery without further intervention.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of interrupting somebody when they are speaking in order to say something
examples: People resented his repeated interventions in the debate.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an occasion when a group of people meet to take action with a friend or family member who has an addiction to drugs or alcohol, in order to help them recover
examples: Her daughters staged an intervention.
Family intervention is an essential component of treatment for adolescent drug abuse.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a formal meeting at which somebody is asked questions to see if they are suitable for a particular job, or for a course of study at a college, university, etc.
examples: COMPARE exit interview
a job interview
She's been called for (an) interview.
He has an interview next week for the manager's job.
I got an interview with a PR company for a trainee position.
In the interview they asked me about my future plans.
He came across very well at the interview.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a meeting (often a public one) at which a journalist asks somebody questions in order to find out their opinions
examples: a television/TV/radio/newspaper interview
to do/give an interview (= to agree to answer questions)
to conduct an interview (= to ask somebody questions in public)
The interview was published in all the papers.
Yesterday, in an interview on German television, the minister denied the reports.
an in-depth interview with the new governor
an exclusive interview about her new book
The film begins with an interview by two local student reporters.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a private meeting between people when questions are asked and answered
examples: a telephone/phone interview
She's had an interview with the careers adviser.
He gave a very full account in long interviews with experienced police officers.
Interviews and questionnaires are the most important tools in market research.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a formal meeting at which somebody is asked questions to see if they are suitable for a particular job, or for a course of study at a college, university, etc.
examples: COMPARE exit interview
a job interview
She's been called for (an) interview.
He has an interview next week for the manager's job.
I got an interview with a PR company for a trainee position.
In the interview they asked me about my future plans.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a meeting (often a public one) at which a journalist asks somebody questions in order to find out their opinions
examples: a television/TV/radio/newspaper interview
to do/give an interview (= to agree to answer questions)
to conduct an interview (= to ask somebody questions in public)
The interview was published in all the papers.
