definitions.definition: a private meeting between people when questions are asked and answered
examples: a telephone/phone interview
She's had an interview with the careers adviser.
He gave a very full account in long interviews with experienced police officers.
Interviews and questionnaires are the most important tools in market research.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a close and friendly relationship
examples: intimate friends
We're not on intimate terms with our neighbours.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: private and personal, often in a sexual way
examples: The article revealed intimate details about his family life.
the most intimate parts of her body

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: encouraging close, friendly relationships, sometimes of a sexual nature
examples: an intimate restaurant
He knew an intimate little bar where they would not be disturbed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very detailed
examples: an intimate knowledge of the English countryside

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: very close
examples: an intimate connection between class and educational success

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: having a sexual relationship with somebodyWord Origin
examples: adjective early 17th cent. (as a noun): from late Latin intimatus, past participle of Latin intimare ‘impress, make familiar’, from intimus ‘inmost’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to a position in or inside something
examples: Come into the house.
She dived into the water.
He threw the letter into the fire.
She turned and walked off into the night.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in the direction of something
examples: Speak clearly into the microphone.
Driving into the sun, we had to shade our eyes.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to a point at which you hit somebody/something
examples: The truck crashed into a parked car.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to a point during a period of time
examples: She carried on working late into the night.
He didn't get married until he was well into his forties.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to show a change in state
examples: The fruit can be made into jam.
Can you translate this passage into German?
They came into power in 2008.
She was sliding into depression.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to show the result of an action
examples: He was shocked into a confession of guilt.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: about or in connection with something
examples: an inquiry into safety procedures

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when you are dividing numbers
examples: 3 into 24 is 8.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be interested in something in an active way
examples: He's into surfing in a big way.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to owe somebody money or be owed money by somebody
examples: By the time he'd fixed the leak, I was into him for $500.
The bank was into her for $100 000.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very interesting because of being unusual or not having an obvious answer
examples: These discoveries raise intriguing questions.
an intriguing possibility
He found her intriguing.
It all sounds very intriguing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell two or more people who have not met before what each other’s names are; to tell somebody what your name is
examples: Allow me to introduce my mother.
The lead singer introduced each member of the band.
He introduced me as a new member of the company.
He introduced me to a Greek girl at the party.
She was introduced to me as a well-known novelist.
Sue and Jo were introduced by a mutual friend.
We have met before, but we haven't been formally introduced.
Can I introduce myself? I'm Helen Robins.
The chairperson introduced herself and opened the discussion.
‘Kay, this is Steve.’ ‘Yes, I know—we've already introduced ourselves.’
She made sure she introduced herself to all her new colleagues.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be the main speaker in a television or radio show, who gives details about the show and who presents the people who are in it; to tell the audience the name of the person who is going to speak or perform
examples: The next programme will be introduced by Mary David.
It is my pleasure to introduce my first guest on the show tonight…

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to mention something for the first time in a piece of writing
examples: Introduce the topic and briefly state your own opinion.
Each new idea should be introduced in a new paragraph.
In Chapter 3 the author introduces the concept of the learner-centred classroom to readers.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make somebody learn about something or do something for the first time
examples: The first lecture introduces students to the main topics of the course.
He was first introduced to drugs by his elder brother.
She has developed her love of archery since being introduced to the sport by a workmate.
It was she who first introduced the pleasures of sailing to me.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make something available for use, discussion, etc. for the first time
examples: SYNONYM bring somebody/something in
The company has recently introduced a new warehouse management system.
Legislation will be introduced to ensure free bus travel for all pensioners.
The new law was introduced in 2007.
Psychologists first introduced the term in the early 1990s.
to introduce measures/reforms
We are going to introduce a few changes to the system.
The government plans to gradually introduce the latest technology into all schools.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be the start of something new
examples: Bands from London introduced the craze for this kind of music.
A slow theme introduces the first movement.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to bring a plant, an animal or a disease to a place for the first time
examples: Some new species were introduced accidentally to Australia from Europe.
Vegetation patterns changed when goats were introduced to the island.
Diseases were inadvertently introduced into the environment by settlers.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to formally present a new law so that it can be discussed
examples: to introduce a bill (before Parliament)

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to put something into something
examples: Particles of glass had been introduced into the baby food.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to cause something to contain errors
examples: Measurement error could have been introduced by respondents' recall errors.
The analyst's rankings rely on subjective information, which may introduce a bias into the rankings.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the first part of a book or speech that gives a general idea of what is to follow
examples: COMPARE preface
a book with an excellent introduction and notes
Can you write a brief introduction to the text?
The English edition has an introduction by Herbert Read.
His mother is mentioned in the introduction.
By way of introduction, let me give you the background to the story.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of making one person formally known to another or a group of others, in which you tell them the person's name
examples: Introductions were made and the conversation started to flow.
Our speaker today needs no introduction (= is already well known).
I was hoping to get an introduction to his good-looking colleague.
a letter of introduction (= a letter which tells somebody who you are, written by somebody who knows both you and the person reading the letter)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of bringing something into use or existence for the first time, or of bringing something to a place for the first time
examples: the introduction of new manufacturing methods
the introduction of compulsory military service
the 1 000th anniversary of the introduction of Christianity to Russia
We can now begin commercial introduction of the product into the United States.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a thing that is brought into use or introduced to a place for the first time
examples: The book lists plants suitable for the British flower garden, among them many new introductions.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person’s first experience of something
examples: This album was my first introduction to modern jazz.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a book or course for people beginning to study a subject
examples: ‘Global Politics: An Introduction’
It's a useful introduction to an extremely complex subject.
‘An Introduction to Astronomy’
The course provides a brief introduction to philosophy.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a short section at the beginning of a piece of music
examples: an eight-bar introduction
After a lengthy musical introduction, the dancers finally appear.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to enter a country, town, etc. using military force in order to take control of it
examples: Troops invaded on August 9th that year.
When did the Romans invade Britain?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to enter a place in large numbers, especially in a way that causes damage or problems
examples: Demonstrators invaded the government buildings.
As the final whistle blew, fans began invading the field.
The cancer cells may invade other parts of the body.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to affect something in an unpleasant or annoying way
examples: Do the press have the right to invade her privacy in this way?
You feel tense with worrying thoughts constantly invading your sleep.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of an army entering another country by force in order to take control of it
examples: the German invasion of Poland in 1939
the threat of invasion
an invasion force/fleet

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of a large number of people or things arriving somewhere, especially people or things that are unpleasant
examples: SEE ALSO pitch invasion
the annual tourist invasion
Farmers are struggling to cope with an invasion of slugs.
Robberies and home invasions are grim facts of daily life.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an act or a process that affects somebody/something in a way that is not welcome
examples: The actress described the photographs of her as an invasion of privacy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to produce or design something that has not existed before
examples: SEE ALSO reinvent
Who invented the steam engine?
I wish mobile phones had never been invented!
The term ‘sociology’ was invented by Auguste Comte.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say or describe something that is not true, especially in order to trick people
examples: What excuse did he invent this time?
Many children invent an imaginary friend.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing or an idea that has been invented
examples: Fax machines were a wonderful invention at the time.
He failed to patent his invention and never made a penny from it.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of inventing something
examples: Such changes have not been seen since the invention of the printing press.
After the war, Westinghouse devoted himself to invention.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of inventing a story or an idea and pretending that it is true; a story invented in this way
examples: This story is apparently a complete invention.
Most of what she says is pure invention.
What would he tell his parents? Some invention and quick thinking—that’s what was needed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the ability to have new and interesting ideas
examples: John was full of invention—always making up new dance steps and sequences.
Her powers of invention were somewhat limited.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a difficult new problem forces people to think of a solution to itWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in the sense ‘finding out, discovery’): from Latin inventio(n-), from invenire ‘discover’, from in- ‘into’ + venire ‘come’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to buy property, shares in a company, etc. in the hope of making a profit
examples: Now is a good time to invest.
She advised us to invest in the property market.
If you want to invest your money, you are probably better off with bonds.
He invested his life savings in his daughter's business.
She personally invested $980 000 in the company.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to spend money on something in order to make it better or more successful
examples: The company plans to invest still further.
The government has invested heavily in public transport.
The industry has failed to invest in new product development.
Tokyo instead invested on infrastructure.
The rest of the required funds will be invested by the council.
The college is to invest $2 million in a new conference hall.
In his time managing the club he has invested millions on new players.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to spend time, energy, effort, etc. on something that you think is good or useful
examples: She had invested all her adult life in the relationship.
He had invested so much personal energy turning the company around.
Are you willing to invest the time and effort necessary to make the scheme work?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to give somebody power or authority, especially as part of their job
examples: SEE ALSO investiture
The new position invested her with a good deal of responsibility.
The interview was broadcast on the same day he was invested as President.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to carefully examine the facts of a situation, an event, a crime, etc. to find out the truth about it or how it happened
examples: The FBI has been called in to investigate.
the senior investigating officer
‘What was that noise?’ ‘I'll go and investigate.’
Detectives are currently investigating possible links between the murders.
to investigate a crime/a complaint/an incident
The allegations have not yet been thoroughly investigated.
The report calls for a commission to investigate the matter further.
The case will be investigated in detail to determine whether the claims are true.
Police are investigating what happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to try to find out information about somebody’s character, activities, etc.
examples: This is not the first time he has been investigated by the police for fraud.
She is being investigated over allegations of illegal business dealings.
They were investigated on suspicion of drug smuggling.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to find out information and facts about a subject or problem by study or research
examples: The study investigates the effects of feeding a high energy diet to cows.
Researchers are investigating how foreign speakers gain fluency.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official examination of the facts about a situation, crime, etc.
examples: a criminal/murder/police investigation
an accident investigation team
The president has promised a full investigation.
The authorities have launched an investigation to determine why the ferry sank.
She remains under investigation for fraud.
He is under investigation for assaulting a teenager.
The police are conducting ongoing investigations into the man's death.
Officials are calling for an investigation into the incident.
On investigation, the noise turned out to be only a door banging.
He is suspended pending a thorough investigation (= until an investigation has happened) of the allegations.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a scientific or academic examination of the facts of a subject or problem
examples: SYNONYM enquiry
Further investigation revealed a flaw in this theory.
Refer patients with these symptoms for further investigation.
the results of a preliminary investigation into stress at work

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who examines a situation such as an accident or a crime to find out the truth
examples: air safety investigators
a private investigator (= a detective)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of investing money in something
examples: SEE ALSO foreign direct investment
foreign/private investment
capital/business/property investment
to attract/encourage investment
This country needs investment in education.
This initiative involves considerable long-term investment by the university.
an investment trust/fund/firm
investment opportunities/decisions/strategies

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the money that you invest, or the thing that you invest in
examples: a minimum investment of $10 000
a substantial/significant/major investment
Our investments are not doing well.
We bought the house as an investment (= to make money).
The area is trying to attract £11 million of private investment to stimulate the local economy.
a high return on investment
investment returns/income
Bonds should be part of your investment portfolio.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing that is worth buying because it will be useful or helpful
examples: A microwave is a good investment.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of giving time or effort to a particular task in order to make it successful
examples: The project has demanded considerable investment of time and effort.
parents' emotional investment in their children

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or an organization that invests money in something
examples: SEE ALSO angel (4)
small investors (= private people)
institutional investors

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that cannot be seen
examples: OPPOSITE visible
a wizard who could make himself invisible
She felt invisible in the crowd.
stars invisible to the naked eye

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with a service that a country provides, such as banks or tourism, rather than goods
examples: invisible earnings

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a spoken or written request to somebody to do something or to go somewhere
examples: to issue/extend an invitation
to accept/turn down/decline an invitation
I received an invitation to the party
She repeated her invitation for dinner at her place.
We got a wedding invitation from Alex and Chris.
I have an open invitation (= not restricted to a particular date) to visit my friend in Japan.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of inviting somebody or of being invited
examples: He produced an official letter of invitation.
Admission is by invitation only.
A concert was held at the invitation of the mayor.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a card or piece of paper that you use to invite somebody to something
examples: We've already sent out the invitations.
Have you ordered the wedding invitations yet?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: something that encourages somebody to do something or encourages something to happen, usually something bad
examples: Leaving the doors unlocked is an open invitation to burglars.
Putting the kids in charge was an invitation to disaster.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to ask somebody to come to a social event
examples: Have you been invited to their party?
She very kindly invited me to lunch.
I'd have liked to have gone but I wasn't invited.
My mother invited a few friends that she hadn't seen for 20 years.
Let's invite them all for dinner.
They have invited me to go to Paris with them.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to ask somebody formally to go somewhere or do something; to make a formal or polite request for something
examples: The bishop invited representatives from all the parishes in the diocese.
Successful candidates will be invited for interview next week.
Clarke was not invited to the meeting.
The ministry had invited tenders for the demolition of the buildings.
He invited questions from the audience.
Readers are invited to email their comments to us.
He was invited to attend the Paris Peace Conference in 1919.
Audience members are invited to participate in the discussion.
In 1956 she was invited to join the Bolshoi Ballet as a soloist.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make something, especially something bad or unpleasant, likely to happen
examples: SYNONYM ask for
Such comments are just inviting trouble.
Such harsh punishments invited prisoners to respond with defiance.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to mention or use a law, rule, etc. as a reason for doing something
examples: It is unlikely that libel laws will be invoked.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to mention a person, a theory, an example, etc. to support your opinions or ideas, or as a reason for something
examples: She invoked several eminent scholars to back up her argument.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to mention somebody’s name to make people feel a particular thing or act in a particular way
examples: His name was invoked as a symbol of the revolution.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make a request (for help) to somebody, especially a god

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody have a particular feeling or imagine a particular scene
examples: SYNONYM evoke
The opening paragraph invokes a vision of England in the early Middle Ages.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to begin to run a program, etc.
examples: This command will invoke the HELP system.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make evil appear by using magicWord Origin
examples: late 15th cent.: from French invoquer, from Latin invocare, from in- ‘upon’ + vocare ‘to call’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if a situation, an event or an activity involves something, that thing is an important or necessary part or result of it
examples: SYNONYM entail
Any investment involves an element of risk.
The process involves using steam to sterilize the instruments.
The test will involve answering questions about a photograph.
The job involves me travelling all over the country.
The job involves my travelling all over the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: if a situation, an event or an activity involves somebody/something, they take part in it or are affected by it
examples: There was a serious incident involving a group of youths.
cases involving the care of young children

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody take part in something
examples: We want to involve as many people as possible in the celebrations.
Parents should involve themselves in their child's education.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to say or do something to show that somebody took part in something, especially a crime
examples: SYNONYM implicate
His confession involved a number of other politicians in the affair.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: taking part in something; being part of something or connected with something
examples: OPPOSITE uninvolved
Some people tried to stop the fight but I didn't want to get involved.
It can be helpful to talk about your worries to someone who is not directly involved.
He became actively involved in politics.
How many vehicles were involved in the crash?
They were involved in a road accident.
Several people have been involved with the project from the beginning.
We'll make our decision and contact the people involved.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: giving a lot of time or attention to somebody/something
examples: OPPOSITE uninvolved
She was deeply involved with the local hospital.
You're too emotionally involved with the situation.
You shouldn't allow yourself to become so heavily involved.
He's a very involved father (= he spends a lot of time with his children).
I was so involved in my book I didn't hear you knock.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having a close personal relationship with somebody
examples: OPPOSITE uninvolved
They're not romantically involved.
She became personally involved with her boss.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: complicated and difficult to understand
examples: SYNONYM complex
an involved plot

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of taking part in something or dealing with somebody
examples: SYNONYM participation
US involvement in European wars
When she was promoted, she missed the day-to-day involvement with customers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of giving a lot of time and attention to something you care about
examples: The new album came out of her growing involvement with contemporary music.
the involvement of parents in their children's education

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a close relationship with somebody, especially a romantic or sexual relationship with somebody that you are not married to
examples: He spoke openly about his involvement with the singer.
Nurses usually try to avoid emotional involvement with patients.
Her husband's involvement with another woman led to their divorce.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

iron gates/bars/railings
a hut with a corrugated iron roof
the iron and steel industries
iron ore (= rock containing iron)
foods that are rich in iron
patients with iron deficiency (= not enough iron in their blood)
iron tablets (= containing iron prepared as a medicine)

definitions.label: Meaning 3

to clap somebody in irons

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: showing that you really mean the opposite of what you are saying; expressing irony
examples: an ironic comment

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: strange or funny because it is very different from what you expect
examples: SEE ALSO irony
It's ironic that she became a teacher—she used to hate school.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that shows that you really mean the opposite of what you are saying; in a way that expresses irony
examples: He smiled ironically.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a way that is strange or funny because it is very different from what you expect
examples: Ironically, the book she felt was her worst sold more copies than any of her others.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the funny or strange aspect of a situation that is very different from what you expect; a situation like this
examples: It was one of life's little ironies.
The irony is that when he finally got the job, he discovered he didn't like it.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the use of words that say the opposite of what you really mean, often as a joke and with a tone of voice that shows this
examples: ‘England is famous for its food,’ she said with heavy irony.
There was a note of irony in his voice.
She said it without a hint/trace of irony.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not important to or connected with a situation
examples: OPPOSITE relevant
totally/completely/largely irrelevant
irrelevant remarks
Whether I believe you or not is irrelevant now.
That evidence is irrelevant to the case.
Many people consider politics irrelevant to their lives.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of land that is completely surrounded by water
examples: SEE ALSO desert island
a small/tiny island
a remote island off the coast of Scotland
the islands in the Baltic Sea
the Virgin Islands
the resort island of Bali
We spent a week on the Greek island of Kos.
an island nation/state
No place on the planet can remain an island of affluence in a sea of suffering.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an area in the middle of a road where you can stand and wait for cars to go past until it is safe for you to cross
examples: SEE ALSO safety island

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to separate somebody/something physically or socially from other people or things
examples: Patients with the disease should be isolated.
Engineers isolated the gas supply to the house.
He was immediately isolated from the other prisoners.
This decision will isolate the country from the rest of Europe.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to separate a part of a situation, problem, idea, etc. so that you can see what it is and deal with it separately
examples: It is possible to isolate a number of factors that contributed to her downfall.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to separate a single substance, cell, etc. from others so that you can study it
examples: Researchers are still trying to isolate the gene that causes this abnormality.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: far away from any others
examples: SYNONYM remote
isolated rural areas

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: without much contact with other people or other countries
examples: I felt very isolated in my new job.
Elderly people easily become socially isolated.
The decision left the country isolated from its allies.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: single; happening once
examples: The police said the attack was an isolated incident.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of separating somebody/something; the state of being separate
examples: geographical isolation
an isolation hospital/ward (= for people with infectious diseases)
The country has been threatened with complete isolation from the international community unless the atrocities stop.
He lives in splendid isolation (= far from, or in a superior position to, everyone else).
the isolation of the polio virus

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of being alone or lonely
examples: Many unemployed people experience feelings of isolation and depression.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: separately; alone
examples: To make sense, these figures should not be looked at in isolation.
Words are pronounced differently in isolation from how they are pronounced in context.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an important topic that people are discussing or arguing about
examples: SEE ALSO side issue
a key/major issue
This is a big issue; we need more time to think about it.
Teacher education has become a political issue.
They discussed a number of important environmental issues.
They are talking about issues relating to the safety of children online.
Her work deals with issues of race and identity.
to explore/debate/examine an issue
The union plans to raise the issue of overtime.
We really need to focus on the key issues and not get sidetracked.
You're just avoiding the issue.
Don't confuse the issue.
The meeting included discussion of a range of issues.
What you say is interesting, but it does not affect the question at issue here.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a problem or worry that somebody has with something
examples: SEE ALSO non-issue
If you have any issues, please call this number.
The community is working together to address social issues and problems.
All technical issues have now been resolved.
Miller decided to tackle the issue head on.
Serious issues arose during the development of the new product.
Money is not an issue.
I'm not bothered about the cost—you're the one who's making it an issue.
She's always on a diet—she has issues about food.
Young people sometimes struggle with issues around body image.
He still has some issues with women (= has some problems dealing with them).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: one of a regular series of magazines or newspapers
examples: SEE ALSO back issue
the July issue of ‘What Car?’
The article appeared in issue 25.
an article in the current issue of ‘Newsweek’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a number or set of things that are supplied and made available at the same time
examples: SEE ALSO standard issue
The company is planning a new share issue.
a special issue of stamps

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the act of supplying or making available things for people to buy or use
examples: SEE ALSO rights issue
I bought a set of the new stamps on the date of issue.
the issue of blankets to the refugees

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the act of formally making something known to people
examples: the issue of a joint statement by the French and German foreign ministers

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: children of your own
examples: He died without issue.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be the most important part of the subject that is being discussed
examples: What is at issue is whether she was responsible for her actions.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to do something to make people take a decision quickly

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to start disagreeing or arguing with somebody about something
examples: I must take issue with you on that point.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to refer to an animal or a thing that has already been mentioned or that is being talked about now
examples: ‘Where's your car?’ ‘It's in the garage.’
Did you see it?
The other room has two beds in it.
Look! It's going up that tree.
We have $500. Will it be enough for a deposit?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to refer to a baby, especially one whose sex is not known
examples: Her baby's due next month. She hopes it will be a boy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to identify a person
examples: It's your mother on the phone.
Hello, Peter, it's Mike here.
Hi, it's me!
Was it you who put these books on my desk?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used in the position of the subject of a verb when you are talking about time, the date, distance, the weather, etc.
examples: It's ten past twelve.
It's our anniversary.
It's two miles to the beach.
It's a long time since they left.
It was raining this morning.
It's quite warm at the moment.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to refer to a fact or situation that is already known or happening
examples: When the factory closes, it will mean 500 people losing their jobs.
Yes, I was at home on Sunday. What about it? (= Why do you ask?)
Stop it, you're hurting me!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used in the position of the subject or object of a verb when the real subject or object is at the end of the sentence
examples: Does it matter what colour it is?
It's impossible to get there in time.
It's no use shouting.
She finds it boring at home.
It appears that the two leaders are holding secret talks.
I find it strange that she doesn't want to go.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used when you are talking about a situation
examples: If it's convenient I can come tomorrow.
It's good to talk.
I like it here.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to emphasize any part of a sentence
examples: It's Jim who's the clever one.
It's Spain that they're going to, not Portugal.
It was three weeks later that he heard the news.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: exactly what is needed
examples: SEE ALSO its
In this business, either you've got it or you haven't.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: this/that is the important point, reason, etc.
examples: That's just it—I can't work when you're making so much noise.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: this/that is the end
examples: I'm afraid that's it—we've lost.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: the expected event is just going to happen
examples: Well, this is it! Wish me luck.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: this is the main point
examples: ‘You're doing too much.’ ‘Well, this is it. I can't cope with any more work.’

examples: Turn the box on its side.
Have you any idea of its value?

examples: The cat was washing itself.
Does the computer turn itself off?

There's no need for the team to feel proud of itself.

definitions.definition: used to emphasize an animal, a thing, etc.
examples: The village itself is pretty, but the surrounding countryside is rather dull.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be an example of complete patience, etc.
examples: The manager of the hotel was courtesy itself.

definitions.definition: automatically; without anyone doing anything
examples: The machine will start by itself in a few seconds.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: alone
examples: The house stands by itself in an acre of land.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: considered separately from other things; in its true nature
examples: In itself, it's not a difficult problem to solve.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: The company doesn't have the market to itself.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5

last January's election

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 8

Local residents have joined battle with the council over the lack of parking facilities.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 10

The two companies have joined forces to form a new consortium.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to work together in doing something
examples: Education has been reluctant to join hands with business.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: involving two or more people together
examples: a joint account (= a bank account in the name of more than one person, for example a husband and wife)

They finished in joint first place.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

I can't tell jokes.
She's always cracking jokes.
They often make jokes at each other's expense.
I didn't get the joke (= understand it).
I wish he wouldn't tell dirty jokes (= about sex).
a sick joke (= about death, disease, etc.)

Have you heard the joke about the elephant and the mouse?

definitions.definition: a person, thing or situation that is silly or annoying and cannot be taken seriously

This can't really be happening—it must be some kind of cruel joke.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to become annoying and no longer acceptable
examples: His teasing is getting beyond a joke.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be difficult or unpleasant
examples: It's no joke trying to find a job these days.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: ‘Quick, jump!’ he shouted.

He killed himself by jumping off a bridge.
She has jumped 2.2 metres.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to pass over something by jumping
examples: SYNONYM leap
He jumped over the wall to get away.
Can you jump that gate?
He jumped the stream and carried on up the hill.
His horse fell as it jumped the last hurdle.
I jumped my horse over all the fences.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move quickly and suddenly
examples: He jumped to his feet when they called his name.
She jumped up and ran out of the room.
Do you want a ride? Jump in.
He jumped out of the car and disappeared into the building.
When she heard the news, she immediately jumped on a plane to France.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make a sudden movement because of surprise, fear or excitement
examples: A loud bang made me jump.
Her heart jumped when she heard the news.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to rise suddenly by a large amount
examples: SYNONYM leap
Prices jumped by 60% last year.
Sales jumped from $2.7 billion to $3.5 billion.
Your interest rate might suddenly jump at the end of the fixed period.
The FTSE 100 benchmark index jumped 199.9 points.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to change suddenly from one subject to another
examples: I couldn't follow the talk because he kept jumping about from one topic to another.
The story then jumps from her childhood in New York to her first visit to London.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to leave out something and pass to a further point or stage
examples: You seem to have jumped several steps in the argument.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to move suddenly and unexpectedly, especially out of the correct position
examples: The needle jumped across the dial.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to attack somebody suddenly
examples: The thieves jumped him in a dark alleyway.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to get on a vehicle very quickly, especially in a way that is dangerous or illegal
examples: to jump a bus

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to start the engine of a car by connecting the battery to the battery of another car with jump leads

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to put a lot of energy into starting a process or an activity or into making it start more quickly

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be very lively
examples: The bar's jumping tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be very angry or excited about something
examples: The local residents are jumping up and down complaining about the noise.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to join others in doing something that is becoming fashionable because you hope to become popular or successful yourself
examples: politicians eager to jump on the environmental bandwagon

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to fail to appear at your trial after you have paid money to be allowed to go free until the trial
examples: He skipped bail and went on the run for two weeks.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to start or be made to start a new and difficult activity that you are not prepared for
examples: Junior hospital doctors are thrown in at the deep end in their first jobs.

definitions.label: Meaning 18

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to do something too soon, before the right time

definitions.label: Meaning 20

definitions.label: Meaning 21

examples: She nearly jumped out of her skin when she saw me.

definitions.label: Meaning 22

the world junior tennis championships

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: (especially in the US) used after the name of a man who has the same name as his father, to make it clear who is being referred to
examples: COMPARE the younger

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: for children under the age of 11 or 13
examples: a junior school

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: connected with the year before the last year in a high school or college
examples: I spent my junior year in France.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the authority that an official organization has to make legal decisions about somebody/something
examples: The English court had no jurisdiction over the defendants.
The Court of Appeal exercised its jurisdiction to order a review of the case.
These matters do not fall within our jurisdiction.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an area or a country in which a particular system of laws has authority
examples: Practice varies between different European jurisdictions.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of members of the public who listen to the facts of a case in a court and decide whether or not somebody is guilty of a crime, or whether a claim has been proved
examples: SEE ALSO grand jury
members of the jury
The jury has/have returned a verdict of guilty.
to be/sit/serve on a jury
the right to trial by jury

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of people who decide who is the winner of a competition
examples: He was on the jury for this year's Booker Prize.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used when you are saying that something is still not certain
examples: The jury is still out on whether wine can be good for you.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: only
examples: There is just one method that might work.
I decided to learn Japanese just for fun.
I waited an hour just to see you.
‘Can I help you?’ ‘No thanks, I'm just looking.’ (= in a shop)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: simply
examples: It was just an ordinary day.
I just want to help.
I just think you should wait a bit.
We'll just have to hope for the best.
I'm just saying there are risks involved.
I'm just glad you're OK.
That's just plain stupid.
I can't just drop all my commitments.
This essay is just not good enough.
I didn't mean to upset you. It's just that I had to tell somebody.
This is not just another disaster movie—it's a masterpiece.
It has to be green—and not just any green, but a very precise shade of olive.
Just because you're older than me doesn't mean you know everything.
It just kind of happened.
If she doesn't like, that's just too bad.
I'm just so sick of this.
They just never give up.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: by a small amount
examples: You've just missed her.
They just made it, boarding the aircraft minutes before take-off.
I only just caught the train.
Inflation fell to just over 4 per cent.
The painting sold for just under £6 million.
I got here just after nine.
They must have got there just before I did.
He visited Guatemala just prior to his death.
They're now the largest party, through just short of an overall majority.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that you/somebody did something or something happened very recently
examples: I've just heard the news.
When you arrived, he had only just left.
She has just been telling us about her trip to Rome.
I just saw him a moment ago.
She was just here.
Just last week it was snowing and now it's 25 degrees.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: at this/that moment; now
examples: I'm just finishing my book.
I was just beginning to enjoy myself when we had to leave.
I'm just off (= I am leaving now).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: exactly
examples: This jacket is just my size.
With him, everything always has to to be just right.
This gadget is just the thing for getting those nails out.
Just my luck (= the sort of bad luck I usually have). My phone needs recharging.
You're just in time.
She looks just like her mother.
It's just what I wanted!
It's just as I thought.
It's just on six (= exactly six o'clock).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: at the same moment as
examples: The clock struck six just as I arrived.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: no less than; equally
examples: She's just as smart as her sister.
You can get there just as cheaply by plane.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: going to do something only a few moments from now or then
examples: The water's just about to boil.
I was just going to tell you when you interrupted.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: really; completely
examples: The food was just wonderful!
The trip was just amazing!
Relax—you're doing just fine.
I can just imagine his reaction.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used in orders to get somebody’s attention, give permission, etc.
examples: Just listen to what I'm saying, will you!
Just help yourselves.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to make a polite request, excuse, etc.
examples: Could you just help me with this box, please?
I've just got a few things to do first.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to show a slight possibility that something is true or will happen
examples: Try asking Mike—he might just know the answer.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to agree with somebody
examples: ‘He's very pompous.’ ‘Isn't he just?’

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to say that you/somebody would have been in the same position if you had done something else, because you got little benefit or pleasure from what you did do
examples: The weather was so bad we might just as well have stayed at home.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: because of the possibility of something happening
examples: You'd better take the keys in case I'm out.
You probably won't need to call—but take my number, just in case.
In case (= if it is true that) you’re wondering why Jo’s here—let me explain…

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: it is a good thing
examples: It is just as well that we didn't leave any later or we'd have missed him.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that you would equally well like to do something as do something else that has been suggested
examples: I'd just as soon stay at home as go out tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: almost; very nearly
examples: I've met just about everyone.
‘Did you reach your sales target?’ ‘Just about.’

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: approximately
examples: She should be arriving just about now.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: suddenly, without warning or explanation

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody to wait for a short time
examples: ‘Is Mr Burns available?’ ‘Just a second, please, I'll check.’

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: at this moment
examples: Come and see me later—I'm busy just now.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: during this present period
examples: Business is good just now.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: only a short time ago
examples: I saw her just now.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: later; in a short period of time

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: done or arranged very accurately or carefully
examples: He liked polishing the furniture and making everything just so.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: at that moment
examples: Just then, someone knocked at the front door.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: exactly what is needed in a particular situation
examples: That cup of tea was just the ticket.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: used when commenting on a situation to suggest that you could say something more or worse but prefer not to
examples: Let's just say he wasn't very happy about the decision (= he was very unhappy or angry about it).

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: not now but probably quite soon
examples: I can't give you the money just yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the fair treatment of people
examples: OPPOSITE injustice
She spent her life fighting for social justice and equality for women.
He pledged to seek justice for the victims of the tragedy.
Children often have a highly developed sense of justice.
laws based on the principles of natural justice

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the quality of being fair or reasonable
examples: OPPOSITE injustice
Who can deny the justice of their cause?
He demanded, not without justice, that he should be allowed to express his views.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the legal system used to punish people who have committed crimes
examples: the criminal justice system
The European Court of Justice
the administration/obstruction of justice
They were accused of attempting to pervert the course of justice.
They were accused of attempting to obstruct justice.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a judge in a court (also used before the name of a judge)
examples: SEE ALSO chief justice

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used before the name of a judge in a court of appeal
examples: Mr Justice Davies

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to arrest somebody for a crime and put them on trial in court

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to treat or represent somebody/something fairly, especially in a way that shows how good, attractive, etc. they are
examples: That photo doesn't do you justice.
He didn’t play as well as he can, but to do him justice, it was his first game since his injury.
The review did not do justice to her talents.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to deal with somebody/something correctly and completely
examples: You cannot do justice to such a complex situation in just a few pages.
I didn’t feel well and wasn’t able to do justice to the meal she had cooked (= I could not eat all the food).

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to do something as well as you can in order to show other people how good you are
examples: She didn't do herself justice in the exam.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to tell a lie or to do something in order to prevent the police, etc. from finding out the truth about a crimeWord Origin
examples: late Old English iustise ‘administration of the law’, via Old French from Latin justitia, from justus, from jus ‘law, right’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a good reason why something exists or is done
examples: I can see no possible justification for any further tax increases.
I could find no real justification for the proposed reorganization.
He was getting angry—and with some justification.
She was arrested entirely without justification.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: as an explanation of why something exists or why somebody has done something
examples: All I can say in justification of her actions is that she was under a lot of pressure at work.
the argument which he put forward in justification

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to show that somebody/something is right or reasonable
examples: How can they justify paying such huge salaries?
The results of the inquiry did not justify them departing from their existing policy.
Her success had justified the faith her teachers had put in her.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give an explanation or excuse for something or for doing something
examples: SYNONYM defend
The senator made an attempt to justify his actions.
The Prime Minister has been asked to justify the decision to Parliament.
You don't need to justify yourself to me.
He sought to justify taking these measures by citing the threat of a terrorist attack.
The press release was intended to justify them sacking her.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to arrange lines of printed text so that one or both edges are straight

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: bad or unfair methods of doing something are acceptable if the result of that action is good or positive
examples: He defended a morality in which the end justifies the means.
That's only OK if you believe that the end justifies the means.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: wanting to do something or wanting something to happen very much
examples: SYNONYM eager
John was very keen to help.
His father was keen for him to go to university.
He is keen for the deal to proceed.
We are keen that our school should get involved too.
I wasn't too keen on going to the party.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: enthusiastic about an activity or idea, etc.
examples: a keen sportsman/gardener
one of the keenest supporters of the team
She was a star pupil—keen, confident and bright.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: liking somebody/something very much; very interested in somebody/something
examples: They've been on a few dates together and Naomi seems really keen.
Tom's very keen on Anna.
He's particularly keen on football.
Sally's quite keen on the idea.
She's not keen on being told what to do.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: quick to understand
examples: SYNONYM sharp
a keen mind/intellect

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: strong or deep
examples: a keen sense of tradition
He took a keen interest in his grandson's education.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: highly developed
examples: SYNONYM sharp
Dogs have a keen sense of smell.
My friend has a keen eye for (= is good at noticing) a bargain.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: involving people competing very hard with each other for something
examples: There is keen competition for places at the college.
They were keen rivals.
It was the subject of keen debate.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: kept low in order to compete with other prices
examples: SYNONYM competitive
The company hopes its keen pricing policy will increase sales.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: extremely cold

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: having a sharp edge or point
examples: SYNONYM sharp

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: wanting very much to do well at something; enthusiastic

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: liking something/somebody very much; very interested in something
examples: He's mad keen on planes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to continue to have something and not give it back or throw it away
examples: He kept all her letters.
She handed the waiter a hundred dollar bill and told him to keep the change.
Always keep a backup of the file.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to put or store something in a particular place
examples: Keep your passport in a safe place.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to save something for somebody
examples: Please keep a seat for me.
The man in the shop said he'd keep it for me until Friday.
Please keep me a seat.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to stay in a particular condition or position; to make somebody/something do this
examples: We huddled together to keep warm.
I could not keep silent any longer.
The notice said ‘Keep off (= Do not walk on) the grass’.
Keep left along the wall.
The doctors worked miracles to keep him alive.
Winning the contract means they can now keep the factory open.
She kept the children amused for hours.
Keep your PIN safe.
He kept his coat on.
Don't keep us in suspense—what happened next?
She had trouble keeping her balance.
I'm very sorry to keep you waiting.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to continue doing something; to do something repeatedly
examples: Keep smiling!
Why does everyone keep saying that?
Things just keep getting worse.
Don't keep on interrupting me!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to know something and not tell it to anyone
examples: Can you keep a secret?
She kept her past secret from us all.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to do what you have promised to do; to go where you have agreed to go
examples: She kept her promise to visit them.
Mary kept her word and Henry was never informed.
He failed to keep his appointment at the clinic.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to write down something as a record
examples: She kept a diary for over twenty years.
We keep a record of all complaints that we receive.
Keep a note of where each item can be found.
I kept a weekly account of my workload and activities.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to own and care for animals
examples: to keep bees/goats/hens
My grandmother kept chickens in her back yard.
Residents are not allowed to keep pets.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to own and manage a shop or restaurant
examples: Her father kept a grocer's shop.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to provide what is necessary for somebody to live; to support somebody by paying for food, etc.
examples: He scarcely earns enough to keep himself and his family.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to delay somebody
examples: SYNONYM hold up
You're an hour late—what kept you?
I won't keep you long. I've just got a couple of quick questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to ask or talk about somebody’s health
examples: How is your mother keeping?
We're all keeping well.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to remain in good condition
examples: Finish off the pie—it won't keep.
Milk and cream should keep quite well in a fridge.
‘I'd love to hear about it, but I'm late already.’ ‘That's OK—it'll keep (= I can tell you about it later).’

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to protect somebody from something
examples: May the Lord bless you and keep you (= used in prayers in the Christian Church).
His only thought was to keep the boy from harm.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to guard or protect the goal or wicket
examples: SEE ALSO goalkeeper

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to make an effort to live normally when you are in a difficult situation or when you have experienced great pain and difficulty
examples: You just have to keep yourself busy and keep going.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to encourage somebody to continue doing something
examples: Keep going, Sarah, you're nearly there.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to be enough for somebody until they get what they are waiting for
examples: Have an apple to keep you going till dinner time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of metal with a special shape used for locking a door, starting a car, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO Allen key™
to put/turn the key in the lock
He inserted the key in the lock and let himself into the house.
the car keys
a set/bunch of keys
the spare key to the front door
We'll have a duplicate key cut (= made).
Luckily Dad has keys for my house.
There's a special key for winding up this clock.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that makes you able to understand or achieve something
examples: SYNONYM secret
Persistence is the key if you want to get a job.
The key to success is preparation.
First-time voters could hold the key to the election result.
The driver of the car probably holds the key to solving the crime.
Language is the key to understanding those around you.
The key is, how long can the federal government control the inflation rate?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: any of the buttons that you press to operate a computer, phone or typewriter
examples: SEE ALSO Alt key
Press the return key to enter the information.
You can use the arrow keys on the keyboard instead.
He began tapping on the keys of his laptop.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: any of the wooden or metal parts that you press to play a piano and some other musical instruments
examples: His hands flew over the piano keys.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a set of related notes, based on a particular note. Pieces of music are usually written mainly using a particular key.
examples: COMPARE scale
a sonata in the key of E flat major
This piece changes key many times.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a set of answers to exercises or problems
examples: Check your answers in the key at the back of the book.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an explanation of the symbols used on a map or plan
examples: You can find the symbols in the key at the bottom of the page.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: locked up safely somewhere; in prison
examples: We keep our valuables under lock and key.
I will not rest until the murderer is under lock and key.
Prisoners are kept under lock and key 24 hours a day.

examples: SYNONYM secret
Persistence is the key if you want to get a job.
The key to success is preparation.
First-time voters could hold the key to the election result.
The driver of the car probably holds the key to solving the crime.
Language is the key to understanding those around you.
The key is, how long can the federal government control the inflation rate?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: any of the buttons that you press to operate a computer, phone or typewriter
examples: SEE ALSO Alt key
Press the return key to enter the information.
You can use the arrow keys on the keyboard instead.
He began tapping on the keys of his laptop.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: any of the wooden or metal parts that you press to play a piano and some other musical instruments
examples: His hands flew over the piano keys.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a set of related notes, based on a particular note. Pieces of music are usually written mainly using a particular key.
examples: COMPARE scale
a sonata in the key of E flat major
This piece changes key many times.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a set of answers to exercises or problems
examples: Check your answers in the key at the back of the book.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an explanation of the symbols used on a map or plan
examples: You can find the symbols in the key at the bottom of the page.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: locked up safely somewhere; in prison
examples: We keep our valuables under lock and key.
I will not rest until the murderer is under lock and key.
Prisoners are kept under lock and key 24 hours a day.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the set of keys for operating a computer or typewriter, or the set of letters that you can touch to write on a smartphone or tablet
examples: The program locks the keyboard until a password is given.
keyboard shortcuts

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the set of black and white keys on a piano or other musical instrument
examples: a piano keyboard

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an electronic musical instrument that has keys like a piano and can be made to play in different styles or to sound like different instruments
examples: COMPARE synthesizer
She plays keyboard and guitar.
He played the song on his keyboard.
The recording features Herbie Hancock on keyboard.
She sat down at the keyboard and started to play.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to hit somebody/something with your foot
examples: Stop kicking—it hurts!
She was punched and kicked by her attackers.
The boys were kicking a ball around in the yard.
Vandals had kicked the door down.
She had to kick the door open because her hands were full.
She kicked at the loose pebbles by the roadside.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move your legs as if you were kicking something
examples: The child was dragged away, kicking and screaming.
The dancers kicked their legs in the air.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be annoyed with yourself because you have done something stupid, missed an opportunity, etc.
examples: He'll kick himself when he finds out he could have had the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to score points by kicking the ball
examples: SEE ALSO drop-kick
to kick a penalty/goal
He kicked 23 points, ensuring victory for New Zealand.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to stop doing something harmful that you have done for a long time
examples: He had been smoking for 15 years and wanted to kick the habit.
to kick the drug/booze

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: very active, healthy or popular
examples: My mother is still alive and kicking.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to hit somebody/something very hard
examples: He was a dirty player and loved to kick hell out of the opposition.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to act in a way that is aggressive or full of energy

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to succeed or win in an impressive way

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to punish or defeat somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to die

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to delay dealing with a problem
examples: This is another attempt to kick the can down the road and leave it to the next generation.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to have nothing to do while you are waiting for somebody/something
examples: We were kicking our heels, waiting for some customers.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: if you drag somebody kicking and screaming to do something, they only do it with great protests because they don't really want to do it at all
examples: The president had to be dragged kicking and screaming to the signing ceremony.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to treat somebody badly or fail to give them help when they need it

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to reject something or treat it as not important; to stop dealing with a problem
examples: He tends to deal with disputes by kicking them into the long grass.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to start to behave badly and refuse to accept any discipline or control

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to test the quality of something to see whether it is suitable for you before you buy it

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to complain loudly about something
examples: They’ll usually give you your money back if you threaten to kick up a stink.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to be relaxed and enjoy yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to move somebody to a job that seems to be more important but that actually has less power or influence

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to continue to hurt somebody when they are already defeated, etc.Word Origin
examples: late Middle English: of unknown origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a child or young person
examples: SEE ALSO boomerang kid
Do you have any kids?
How are the kids (= your children)?
A bunch of kids were hanging around outside.
a gang/group of kids
college/school kids
street kids who rely on their ingenuity to keep alive
You're acting like a little kid!
I remember reading with my grandmother as a young kid of 6.
I'm looking forward to getting home to the wife and kids.
Here are some fun ways to teach your kids about healthy eating.
The kids love playing outside in the mud.
The game is aimed at kids of all ages.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a young goat

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: soft leather made from the skin of a young goat
examples: a pair of white kid gloves

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to deal with somebody in a very careful way so that you do not offend or upset them
examples: Treat her with kid gloves—she's very sensitive.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: something that is so easy to do or understand that it is thought to be not very serious or only suitable for children
examples: That was kids' stuff compared with what lies ahead.
The movie is pure kids' stuff from beginning to end.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a person who is new to a place, an organization, etc.
examples: Despite his six years in politics, he was still regarded by many as the new kid on the block.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take somebody away illegally and keep them as a prisoner, especially in order to get money or something else for returning them
examples: SYNONYM abduct
Two businessmen have been kidnapped by terrorists.
The terrorists were planning to kidnap one of the president’s sons.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: either of the two organs in the body that remove waste products from the blood and produce urine
examples: a kidney infection

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the kidneys of some animals that are cooked and eaten
examples: steak and kidney pie

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something die
examples: Cancer kills thousands of people every year.
Tiredness while driving can kill.
Dozens of civilians were killed or injured in the attack.
She was nearly killed by a car bomb.
Both members of the crew were killed instantly when the missile hit their aircraft.
Three soldiers were killed in action (= while fighting) yesterday.
She tried to kill me!
The terrorists threatened to kill the hostages.
I bought a spray to kill the weeds.
My mother will kill me (= be very angry with me) when she finds out.
He tried to kill himself with sleeping pills.
Don't kill yourself trying to get the work done by tomorrow. It can wait.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to destroy something or make it less good; to make something stop
examples: to kill a rumour
She claims that social media kills relationships.
The defeat last night killed the team's chances of qualifying.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to switch off a light or engine; to stop a computer program or process
examples: She killed the engine and climbed out.
The only way to kill the process is to reboot the computer.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to cause somebody pain
examples: My feet are killing me.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody laugh a lot
examples: Stop it! You're killing me!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody not to ask questions or try to find out about things that do not involve them

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: wearing the kind of clothes that will make people notice and admire you

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to have nothing to do or not be busy

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to describe the very angry or unpleasant way somebody is/was looking at you
examples: If looks could kill, she thought, seeing the expression that came over his face when he saw her, she’d be dead on the pavement.
I don’t know what I’ve done to upset him, but if looks could kill…

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to destroy something that would make you rich, successful, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that what you are going to do will either be very successful or fail completely

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to spend time doing something that is not important while you are waiting for something else to happen
examples: We killed time playing cards.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to achieve two things at the same time with one action

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be so kind to somebody/something that you in fact harm them

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to laugh a lot
examples: He was killing himself laughing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act of killing somebody deliberately
examples: SYNONYM murder
Their leader condemned the torture and killing of innocent civilians.
The mass killing (= killing of a large number of people) occurred when soldiers opened fire on protesters.
a verdict of unlawful killing
He is responsible for the brutal killing of thousands of animals.
No motive for the killing has yet been established.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make a lot of money quickly
examples: She made a killing on the stock market.
Investors are set to make a killing from the sell-off.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring distance; 1 000 metres
examples: The industrial estate is 6 kilometres from the city centre.
She had been driving at 110 kilometres per hour.
Monaco is only two square kilometres in size.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of people or things that are the same in some way; a particular variety or type
examples: three kinds of cakes/cake
What kind of house do you live in?
They sell all kinds of things.
I need to buy paper and pencils, that kind of thing.
His diet's terrible—burgers, chips, pizzas, that kind of stuff.
I'm the kind of person who hates to do anything wrong.
We have the same kind of car.
I'll never have that kind of money (= as much money as that).
She isn't that kind of girl.
This kind of exercise is very popular.
Exercises of this kind are very popular.
music of all/various/different kinds
The school is the first of its kind in Britain.
Would you like a drink of some kind?
The regions differ in size, but not in kind.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: consisting of goods or services, not money
examples: As well as his salary, he gets benefits in kind.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: with the same thing
examples: She insulted him and he responded in kind.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that something you are saying is not exact
examples: I had a kind of feeling this might happen.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: slightly; in some ways
examples: That made me feel kind of stupid.
I like him, kind of.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that the situation is very different from what has been said
examples: ‘I was terrible!’ ‘You were nothing of the kind.’

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not as good as it could be
examples: You're making progress of a kind.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: very similar
examples: They're two of a kind—both workaholics!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the only one like this
examples: SYNONYM unique
My father was one of a kind—I'll never be like him.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: something like what has been said
examples: ‘He's resigning.’ ‘I'd suspected something of the kind.’
