definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the male ruler of an independent state that has a royal family
examples: SEE ALSO pearly king
the kings and queens of England
the French king
to be crowned king
King George V

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person, an animal or a thing that is thought to be the best or most important of a particular type
examples: the king of comedy
The lion is the king of the jungle.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used in compounds with the names of animals or plants to describe a very large type of the thing mentioned
examples: a king penguin

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the most important piece used in the game of chess, that can move one square in any direction

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a playing card with the picture of a king on it

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a very large amount of money

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the person considered to be the best, most famous or successful in a particular place or area of activityWord Origin
examples: Old English cyning, cyng, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch koning and German König, also to kin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a country that has a king or queen as head of state (= official leader of the country)
examples: the United Kingdom
the kingdom of God (= heaven)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an area controlled by a particular person or where a particular thing or idea is important

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: one of the three traditional divisions of the natural world
examples: the animal, vegetable and mineral kingdoms

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: one of the five major groups into which all living things are organized

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to completely destroy somebody/something with an explosion
examples: The truck was blown to kingdom come.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: forever
examples: He’ll talk till kingdom come if you let him.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to touch somebody with your lips as a sign of love or sexual desire or when saying hello or goodbye
examples: SEE ALSO air-kiss
They stood in a doorway kissing (= kissing each other).
Do people in Britain kiss when they meet?
Go and kiss your mother goodnight.
He bent forward to kiss her cheek.
She kissed him on both cheeks.
He lifted the trophy up and kissed it.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to gently move or touch something
examples: The sunlight kissed the warm stones.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a way of referring to somebody talking publicly, usually for money, about a past sexual relationship with somebody famous

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be very nice to somebody in order to persuade them to help you or to give you something

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to take away the pain of an injury by kissing it
examples: Come here and let me kiss it better.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to accept that you will lose something or be unable to do something
examples: Well, you can kiss goodbye to your chances of promotion.

examples: SEE ALSO toolkit
a first-aid kit
a drum kit

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set of parts ready to be made into something
examples: a kit for a model plane
She built the doll’s house from a kit.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a set of clothes and equipment that you use for a particular activity
examples: sports kit
The soldiers packed tents and kits to move to new positions.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to take your clothes off

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: everything
examples: I had new clothes, a new hairstyle—the whole caboodle.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a room in which meals are cooked or prepared
examples: SEE ALSO soup kitchen
We ate at the kitchen table.
the kitchen floor/window/door
a stainless steel kitchen sink
He stabbed her with a kitchen knife.
The house has a fully fitted kitchen with custom-built units.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a very large number of things, probably more than is necessary
examples: We seem to take everything but the kitchen sink when we go camping.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to stop trying to do something if they find it too difficult, especially in order to suggest that they are less able than other peopleWord Origin
examples: Old English cycene, of West Germanic origin; related to Dutch keuken and German Küche, based on Latin coquere ‘to cook’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the joint between the top and bottom parts of the leg where it bends in the middle
examples: a knee injury
I had knee surgery three years ago.
Bend your knees until you feel your thigh muscles working.
I grazed my knee when I fell.
He went down on one knee and asked her to marry him.
She was on her knees scrubbing the kitchen floor.
Everyone was down on (their) on (their) hands and knees (= crawling on the floor) looking for the ring.
He fell to his knees and begged for mercy.
My knees were knocking (= I was frightened).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the part of a piece of clothing that covers the knee
examples: I brushed the dust from the knees of my trousers.
These jeans are torn at the knee.
a knee patch

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the top surface of the upper part of the legs when you are sitting down
examples: SYNONYM lap
Come and sit on Daddy's knee.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: when you were very young
examples: I learnt these songs at my mother's knee.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an excellent person or thing
examples: She thinks she's the bee's knees (= she has a very high opinion of herself).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to defeat somebody, especially in a war

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to badly affect an organization, etc. so that it can no longer function
examples: The strikes brought the industry to its knees.
The fuel shortage brought the country to its knees within weeks.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if you ask for something on bended knee(s), you ask for it in a very anxious and/or humble way (= showing you think you are less important than the person you are asking)
examples: I’d go down on bended knee if I thought she’d change her mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to punish somebody by making them lie on top of your knee and hitting their bottom

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: hardly able to stand because of emotion, fear, illness, etc.
examples: His sudden smile made her go weak at the knees.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sharp blade (= metal edge) with a handle, used for cutting or as a weapon
examples: SEE ALSO bowie knife
knives and forks
a sharp knife
a bread knife (= one for cutting bread)
The aim is to deter young people from carrying knives.
He had been stabbed repeatedly with a kitchen knife.
a plan to tackle knife crime
She was murdered in a frenzied knife attack.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the situation has become so bad that people are preparing to make one person take the blame, for example by taking away their job
examples: The knives are out for the chancellor.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: easily; without meeting any difficulty

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to behave towards somebody in an unfriendly way and try to harm them

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to say or do something unkind deliberately; to make somebody who is unhappy feel even more unhappy
examples: Marcia laughed as she twisted the knife still deeper.
Just to twist the knife, the filmmakers have provided a surprise ending.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: having a medical operation
examples: He is to go under the surgeon's knife again on Thursday.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to hit a door, etc. in order to attract attention
examples: SYNONYM rap
He knocked three times and waited.
I knocked on the door and went straight in.
Somebody was knocking on the window.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to hit something hard, often by accident
examples: Be careful you don't knock your head on this low beam.
Her hand knocked against the glass.
She dropped the pile of books when he accidentally knocked her shoulder.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to hit something so that it moves or breaks
examples: He'd knocked over a glass of water.
I knocked the nail into the wall.
They had to knock the door down to get in.
He had knocked one of the pictures off the wall.
The boys were knocking (= kicking) a ball around in the back yard.
The criticism had knocked (= damaged) her self-esteem.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to put somebody/something into a particular state by hitting them/it
examples: The blow knocked me flat.
He was knocked senseless by the blow.
She knocked my drink flying.
The two rooms had been knocked into one (= the wall between them had been knocked down).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make a hole in something by hitting it hard
examples: They managed to knock a hole in the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if your heart knocks, it beats hard; if your knees knock, they shake, for example from fear
examples: My heart was knocking wildly.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make a regular sound of metal hitting metal, especially because there is something wrong

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to criticize somebody/something, especially when it happens unfairly
examples: The newspapers are always knocking the England team.
It may sound pretty childish, but don't knock it until you've tried it.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to force people to stop arguing and behave in a sensible way

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to hit somebody very hard several times and hurt them very much
examples: Get out or I’ll beat the living daylights out of you!

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to hit somebody/something very hard
examples: He was a dirty player and loved to kick hell out of the opposition.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to surprise or impress somebody very much

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to train somebody so that they do a particular job, task, etc. well
examples: It took him just two weeks to knock the new recruits into shape.
Leave the boy with me—I'll soon knock him into shape!

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to make something more acceptable, organized or successful
examples: I've got all the information together but it still needs knocking into shape.
It shouldn’t take long to get the company back into shape.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to affect somebody very deeply
examples: The business over the lawsuit had really knocked her for six.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to threaten somebody that you will hit them

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to impress somebody very much
examples: You look fabulous—you'll knock 'em dead tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to be very much better than somebody/something
examples: She knocks the rest of the cast into a cocked hat.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to stop making a noise, annoying you, etc.
examples: Knock it off, kids—I’m trying to work.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to make somebody lose their position as somebody/something successful or admired
examples: A lot of teams are looking to knock us off our perch.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to stop something from happening; to stop doing something
examples: The recession knocked on the head any idea of expanding the company.
By eleven o’clock we were all tired so we knocked it on the head.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used when talking about your previous good luck or your hopes for the future, to avoid bringing bad luck
examples: I've been driving for over 20 years and never had an accident—knock on wood!

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to surprise or shock somebody so much that they are unable to react immediately

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to try and persuade somebody to stop behaving in a stupid way, sometimes using rough or violent methods
examples: Try and talk some sense into her before she makes the wrong decision.
Where would I be without you to knock some sense into my head?

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to be very much better than somebody/something
examples: She knocks spots off all the other candidates.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to make somebody lose their confidence and enthusiasm

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to hit a door, etc. in order to attract attention
examples: SYNONYM rap
He knocked three times and waited.
I knocked on the door and went straight in.
Somebody was knocking on the window.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to hit something hard, often by accident
examples: Be careful you don't knock your head on this low beam.
Her hand knocked against the glass.
She dropped the pile of books when he accidentally knocked her shoulder.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to hit something so that it moves or breaks
examples: He'd knocked over a glass of water.
I knocked the nail into the wall.
They had to knock the door down to get in.
He had knocked one of the pictures off the wall.
The boys were knocking (= kicking) a ball around in the back yard.
The criticism had knocked (= damaged) her self-esteem.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to put somebody/something into a particular state by hitting them/it
examples: The blow knocked me flat.
He was knocked senseless by the blow.
She knocked my drink flying.
The two rooms had been knocked into one (= the wall between them had been knocked down).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make a hole in something by hitting it hard
examples: They managed to knock a hole in the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if your heart knocks, it beats hard; if your knees knock, they shake, for example from fear
examples: My heart was knocking wildly.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make a regular sound of metal hitting metal, especially because there is something wrong

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to criticize somebody/something, especially when it happens unfairly
examples: The newspapers are always knocking the England team.
It may sound pretty childish, but don't knock it until you've tried it.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to force people to stop arguing and behave in a sensible way

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have information in your mind as a result of experience or because you have learned or been told it
examples: SEE ALSO well known (2)
No one knows the answer.
I need to know your name.
The truth about what happened is not yet known.
All I know is that she used to work in a bank (= I have no other information about her).
I know (that) people’s handwriting changes as they get older.
We know from experience that turning a hobby into a business is not easy.
I know for a fact (that) he didn't go to the party.
‘There's no one in.’ ‘How do you know?’
‘You've got a flat tyre.’ ‘I know.’
‘What's the answer?’ ‘I don't know.’
As you know, Emma and I are old friends.
‘Isn’t that his car?’ ‘I wouldn’t know./How should I know?’ (= I don’t know and I am not the person you should ask.)
‘What are you two whispering about?’ ‘You don't want to know’ (= because you would be shocked or wouldn't approve).
It is widely known that CFCs can damage the ozone layer.
I knew where he was hiding.
No one knows for sure who did it.
You know about Amanda's baby, don't you?
I don't know about you, but I'm ready for something to eat.
I know next to nothing (= know almost nothing) about opera.
I know of someone who can help us.
‘Is anyone else coming?’ ‘Not that I know of.’
Does he know to come here (= that he should come here) first?
We know her to be honest.
Strobe lights are known to cause seizures.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to realize, understand or be aware of something
examples: As soon as I walked in the room I knew (that) something was wrong.
She knew she was dying.
‘Martin was lying all the time.’ ‘I should have known.’
I knew perfectly well what she meant.
I know exactly how you feel.
This case is hopeless and he knows it (= although he will not admit it).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to feel certain about something
examples: SEE ALSO don’t-know
He knew (that) he could trust her.
I know it's here somewhere!
I know things will turn out all right.
I don't know that I can finish it by next week.
I just knew that it was something I wanted to do.
‘You were right—someone's been spreading rumours about you.’ ‘I knew it!’
‘She's the worst player in the team.’ ‘Oh, I don't know (= I am not sure that I agree)—she played well yesterday.’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be familiar with a person, place, thing, etc.
examples: I've known David for 20 years.
Do you two know each other (= have you met before)?
She was a secretary when I first knew her.
She's very nice when you get to know her.
Knowing Ben, we could be waiting a long time (= it is typical of him to be late).
This man is known to the police (= as a criminal).
I don’t know anyone in Oxford.
I know Paris well.
Do you know the play (= have you seen or read it before)?
How many of your neighbours do you know by name?
The new rules could mean the end of football as we know it (= in the form that we are familiar with).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have learned a skill or language and be able to use it
examples: Do you know any Japanese?
Do you know how to use spreadsheets?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to think that somebody/something is a particular type of person or thing or has particular characteristics
examples: SEE ALSO well known (1)
He has become widely widely known as an expert in child psychology.
It's known as the most dangerous part of the city.
She is best known for her work on the human brain.
He is internationally known for his work with vaccines.
He's known to be an outstanding physicist.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to give somebody/something a particular name or title
examples: Iran was formerly known as Persia.
The drug is commonly known as Ecstasy.
Peter Wilson, also known as ‘The Tiger’
He was known as Bonzo to his friends.
The country was not yet known by the name of England.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be able to recognize somebody/something
examples: I couldn't see who was speaking, but I knew the voice.
She knows a bargain when she sees one.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to understand the difference between one person or thing and another
examples: SYNONYM distinguish (1)
I hope we have taught our children to know right from wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to have seen, heard or experienced something
examples: I’ve never known it (to) snow in July before.
He has been known to spend all morning in the bathroom.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to have personal experience of something
examples: He has known both poverty and wealth.
She may be successful now, but she has known what it is like to be poor.
She thought she would never know the joy of seeing a child grow up in her care.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say that you think you know, remember, understand, etc. something but you cannot be completely sure, especially because you do not know all the facts
examples: SEE ALSO AFAIK
As far as we knew, there was no cause for concern.
As far as I can see, you've done nothing wrong.
She lived in Chicago, as far as I can remember.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: very quickly or suddenly
examples: We were whisked off in a taxi before we knew where we were.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to have no way of realizing or being aware that you have done something wrong
examples: ‘I'm sorry, I called when you were in bed.’ ‘Don't worry—you weren't to know.’

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to say that it is easier and wiser to stay in a bad situation that you know and can deal with rather than change to a new situation that may be much worse

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you do not know something and that it is not important to you
examples: She could be dead for all I know.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you do not know something
examples: God knows what else they might find.
‘Where are they?’ ‘Goodness knows.’

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the truth of what you are saying
examples: She ought to pass the exam—goodness knows she's been working hard enough.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to be confident that you know something, especially when you actually do not
examples: He thinks he knows all the answers.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to know something perfectly so that you can repeat it at any time without having to think about it
examples: He had all the answers off pat.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to be in poor condition
examples: Our car has seen better days!

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to criticize somebody’s behaviour
examples: I don't know how you can say things like that.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody the true facts about a situation, especially when these are not known by other people
examples: If the truth be known, I was afraid to tell anyone.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used to agree with somebody or to show sympathy
examples: ‘What a ridiculous situation!’ ‘I know.’

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: used to introduce a new idea or suggestion
examples: I know, let's see what's on at the theatre.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: used to criticize somebody by saying that they should realize or understand something
examples: You know as well as I do that you're being unreasonable.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to know somebody/something extremely well
examples: She must know the play backwards by now.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to know what should be done, etc. better than other people
examples: The doctor told you to stay in bed, and she knows best.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to be sensible enough not to do something
examples: He knows better than to judge by appearances.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to recognize somebody without knowing them well

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to have information or evidence that the opposite is true
examples: He says he doesn't care about what the critics write, but I know different.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to be very aware of a fact and unable to deny or ignore it
examples: He knew full well what she thought of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to be very familiar with somebody/something
examples: This is where I grew up. I know this area like the back of my hand.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to have very clear and definite ideas about what you want to do

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to know a lot about a particular subject or job

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to know/tell somebody some useful, interesting or surprising information about somebody/something
examples: She's been married five times, so she knows a thing or two about men!

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to know something because of something unpleasant that has happened to you
examples: He's a ruthless businessman, as I know to my cost.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: to be familiar with a place, subject, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: to have knowledge about something from your own experience
examples: I’ve lived in China, so I know what I’m talking about.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: to know where you can get an advantage for yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: to make sure that people are informed about something, especially by getting somebody else to tell them
examples: The President has let it be known that he does not intend to run for election again.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: to tell somebody about something
examples: I don't know if I can come, but I'll let you know tomorrow.
Let me know how I can help.
Please let me know if there's anything I can do to help.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: used to emphasize what you are saying
examples: Lord knows, I tried to teach her.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not know the answer to something
examples: ‘Why did she say that?’ ‘Lord knows!’

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: to introduce yourself to somebody
examples: I made myself known to the hotel manager.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: to behave badly, usually because you have not been taught the correct way to behave
examples: Don’t blame the children—they don’t know any better.

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: to be very stupid; to have absolutely no skill

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: to know nothing about a subject
examples: I don’t know beans about making movies.

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: to know nothing at all about somebody/something
examples: I’m afraid I don’t know the first thing about cars.

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: to know nothing at all about something/somebody
examples: We’ve lived next to him for years, but we still don’t know the first thing about him.

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: to not know at all who somebody is

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: to be so surprised by something that you do not know how to react

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: to feel very embarrassed and not know how to react

definitions.label: Meaning 54
definitions.definition: to be so excited or confused that you cannot behave or think in a sensible way

definitions.label: Meaning 55
definitions.definition: to have an easy life without realizing how easy it is
examples: You people without kids don't know you're born.

definitions.label: Meaning 56
definitions.definition: to take no interest in something because you do not care about it or it is too much trouble
examples: I've tried to ask her advice, but she doesn't want to know (= about my problems).
‘How much was it?’ ‘You don't want to know’ (= it is better if you don't know).

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: old enough to behave in a more sensible way than you actually did

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: to show somebody/know/learn how a particular job should be done

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: used to say that it is impossible to say what might happen
examples: There's no knowing how he'll react.

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody knows nothing about the subject you are talking about
examples: What does he know about football, anyway?

definitions.label: Meaning 61
definitions.definition: used to express surprise
examples: Well, what do you know? Look who's here!

definitions.label: Meaning 62
definitions.definition: (know) what things are useful, important, etc.
examples: She certainly knows what's what.

definitions.label: Meaning 63
definitions.definition: used when you are thinking of what to say next
examples: Well, you know, it's difficult to explain.

definitions.label: Meaning 64
definitions.definition: used to show that what you are referring to is known or understood by the person you are speaking to
examples: Guess who I've just seen? Maggie! You know—Jim's wife.
You know that restaurant round the corner? It's closed down.

definitions.label: Meaning 65
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something that you are saying
examples: I'm not stupid, you know.

definitions.label: Meaning 66
definitions.definition: used to introduce an interesting or surprising opinion, piece of news, etc.
examples: You know something? I've never really enjoyed Christmas.

definitions.label: Meaning 67
definitions.definition: used to refer to somebody/something without mentioning a name

definitions.label: Meaning 68
definitions.definition: used to say that you can never be certain about what will happen in the future, especially when you are suggesting that something good might happenWord Origin
examples: Old English cnāwan (earlier gecnāwan) ‘recognize, identify’, of Germanic origin; from an Indo-European root shared by Latin (g)noscere, Greek gignōskein, also by can and ken.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the information, understanding and skills that you gain through education or experience
examples: SEE ALSO carnal knowledge
scientific/technical knowledge and skills
intimate/first-hand/basic knowledge
a thirst for knowledge
It will be an opportunity to gain knowledge and experience.
She has acquired a detailed knowledge of the subject.
They enjoy sharing their knowledge of the business.
He had no prior knowledge of the language before visiting the country.
He has a wide knowledge of painting and music.
There is a lack of knowledge about the tax system.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of knowing about a particular fact or situation
examples: He denied all knowledge of the affair.
She sent the letter without my knowledge.
The film was made with the Prince's full knowledge and approval.
I was happy in the knowledge that I had done my best.
I went to sleep secure in the knowledge that I was not alone in the house.
They could relax safe in the knowledge that they had the funding for the project.
Their delight in the win was tempered by the knowledge that the competition would only get fiercer.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: information, considered as a resource to be used and supplied in industry, rather than producing goods
examples: the shift toward a knowledge economy
Knowledge workers are driving our economy today.
the emergence of consultancy as a knowledge industry
knowledge capital/assets
The successful candidate will have experience in data and knowledge management.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be something that everyone knows, especially in a particular community or group
examples: Their relationship is common knowledge.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to become known by somebody
examples: It has come to our knowledge that you have been taking time off without permission.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: as far as you know
examples: He never made a will, to the best of my knowledge.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: from the information you have, although you may not know everything
examples: ‘Are they divorced?’ ‘Not to my knowledge.’
She never, to my knowledge, considered resigning.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a laboratory
examples: SEE ALSO crime lab
a computer/research lab
the school science labs
She'd been working in the lab all day.
a lab technician
a lab coat (= a white coat worn by scientists, etc. working in a laboratory)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of paper, etc. that is attached to something and that gives information about it
examples: SYNONYM tag
Always read the label carefully.
price/address labels
The washing instructions are on the label.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a word or phrase that is used to describe somebody/something in a way that seems too general, unfair or not correct
examples: I hated the label ‘housewife’.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the name or trademark of a fashion company
examples: SEE ALSO white label
today's major fashion labels
She plans to launch her own designer clothes label.
He's really fashion-conscious and will only wear labels (= clothes with a designer label).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a company that produces and sells music, CDs, etc.
examples: the Virgin record label
It's his first release for a major label.

definitions.definition: a room or building used for scientific research, experiments, testing, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO language laboratory
a clinical/research laboratory
to send a specimen to the laboratory for analysis
The effects of weathering can be simulated in the laboratory.
laboratory experiments/tests
The athletes' reflexes were tested under laboratory conditions.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: work, especially physical work
examples: SEE ALSO bonded labour
manual labour (= work using your hands)
The price will include the labour and materials.
The company wants to keep down labour costs.
The workers voted to withdraw their labour (= to stop work as a means of protest).
a fair division of labour between men and women

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a task or period of work
examples: He was so exhausted from the day's labours that he went straight to bed.
People look forward to enjoying the fruits of their labours during retirement.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the people who work or are available for work in a country or company
examples: SEE ALSO child labour
forced/slave labour
a shortage of labour
Companies are making huge profits by exploiting cheap labour in poor countries.
There is a growing demand for skilled labour.
New labour laws make it more difficult for employers to sack workers.
good labour relations (= the relationship between workers and employers)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the period of time or the process of giving birth to a baby
examples: Jane was in labour for ten hours.
She went into labour early.
labour pains
It was a difficult labour.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the British Labour Party
examples: He always votes Labour.
Labour was/were in power for many years.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a hard task that you do because you want to, not because it is necessary
examples: Writing the book was a labour of love.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of not having something or not having enough of something
examples: SYNONYM dearth
a lack of understanding/knowledge
Passengers complained about the lack of information when flights were cancelled.
Her enthusiasm compensated for her apparent lack of experience.
He was suffering from a complete lack of confidence.
There was no lack of volunteers.
The project was abandoned because of a total lack of support.
He was released due to lack of evidence.
The trip was cancelled through lack of interest.
Fans of classic comedy should be happy with this disc, despite the lack of extras.
Money and the fear of its lack are present in many of his poems.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that although somebody has not succeeded in something, they have tried very hard
examples: They haven't won a game yet, but it isn't for want of trying.
They lost the game, but not for lack of trying.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a boy or young man
examples: COMPARE lass
Things have changed since I was a lad.
He's a nice lad.
Hurry up, lad.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of friends that a man works with or spends free time with
examples: to go to the pub with the lads
I tried to fit in and be one of the lads.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a lively young man, especially one who is very interested in women and having sex, drinks a lot of alcohol and enjoys sport
examples: SEE ALSO laddish
Tony was a bit of a lad—always had an eye for the women.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who works in a stableWord Origin
examples: Middle English: of unknown origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of equipment for climbing up and down a wall, the side of a building, etc., consisting of two lengths of wood or metal that are joined together by steps or rungs
examples: SEE ALSO rope ladder
to climb up/fall off a ladder

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a series of stages by which you can make progress in your life or career
examples: to move up or down the social ladder
the career ladder
to get onto the property ladder (= buy your first home)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a long, thin hole in tights or stockings where some threads have broken
examples: I've got a ladder in my new tights.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a competition in a particular sport or game in which teams or players are arranged in a list and they can move up the list by defeating one of the teams or players above
examples: He’s third on the tennis ladder at work.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a word used to mean ‘woman’ that some people, especially older people, consider is more polite
examples: SEE ALSO bag lady
There's a lady waiting to see you.
an old/elderly lady
He was with an attractive young lady.
And who is this lovely lady?
the lady with the red hair
the lady in the designer dress
the ladies’ golf championship
a tea lady (= a woman who serves tea in an office)
She's a tough lady.
a lady doctor/golfer

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a woman who is polite and well educated, has excellent manners and always behaves well
examples: COMPARE gentleman
His wife was a real lady.
You could at least try to behave like a lady.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used when speaking to or about a girl or woman, especially somebody you do not know
examples: Can I take your coats, ladies?
Could I have your attention, ladies and gentlemen?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an informal way to talk to a woman, showing a lack of respect
examples: Listen, lady, don't shout at me.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: (in the UK) a woman belonging to a high social class
examples: the lords and ladies of the court
a lady’s maid

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: (in the UK) a title used by a woman who is a member of the nobility, or by somebody who has been given the title ‘lady’ as an honour. The wives and daughters of some members of the nobility and the wives of knights are also called ‘Lady’.
examples: COMPARE lord
Lady Howe
Lady Jane Grey

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a toilet for women in a public building or place
examples: Could you tell me where the ladies is?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a title used to refer to Mary, the mother of Christ, especially in the Roman Catholic Church
examples: Our Lady of Lourdes

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a man/woman who does not have to work

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used for saying that a situation may still change, for example that a contest, election, etc. is not finished yet, and somebody still has a chance to win itWord Origin
examples: Old English hlǣfdīge (denoting a woman to whom homage or obedience is due, such as the wife of a lord, also specifically the Virgin Mary), from hlāf ‘loaf’ + a Germanic base meaning ‘knead’, related to dough; compare with lord.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large area of water that is surrounded by land
examples: SEE ALSO ribbon lake
We swam in the lake.
There were a number of boats on the lake.
We stayed in a hotel on the edge of Lake Ontario.
a wine lake (= a large supply of wine that is not being used)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a device that uses electricity, oil or gas to produce light
examples: SEE ALSO arc lamp
a desk/bedside lamp
a street lamp
an oil lamp
a paraffin lamp
a kerosene lamp
a fluorescent/halogen lamp
to switch on/turn off a lamp

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an electrical device that produces rays of heat and that is used for medical or scientific purposes
examples: SEE ALSO blowlamp
an infrared/ultraviolet lamp
The specimen was viewed under an ultraviolet lamp.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the surface of the earth that is not sea
examples: SEE ALSO dry land
The new project will reclaim the land from the sea.
It was good to be back on land.
Some animals can live both on land and in water.
We travelled by land, though flying would have been cheaper.
It's impossible to reach this beach by land because of the high cliffs.
We can organize air transport, land transport and all accommodation for your trip.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an area of ground, especially of a particular type or used for a particular purpose
examples: SYNONYM terrain
agricultural/arable/fertile land
Changes in land use can have significant effects on the local wildlife.
a piece/plot of land
They are not permitted to build on the surrounding green belt land (= open land around a city).
The land rose to the east.
Some of the country's richest grazing lands are in these valleys.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the area of ground that somebody owns, especially when you think of it as property that can be bought or sold
examples: SEE ALSO no man’s land
public/private land
to own/buy/purchase/sell land
He acquired a parcel of several acres of land.
The college owns vast tracts of land.
land ownership/acquisition
Land values in the area are falling.
During the war their lands were occupied by the enemy.
Ancient tribes were forced off their ancestral lands.
The adjoining plot of land belongs to the local council.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to refer to the countryside and the way people live in the country as opposed to in cities
examples: At the beginning of the 20th century almost a third of the population lived off the land (= grew or produced their own food).
Many people leave the land to find work in towns and cities.
Her family had farmed the land for generations.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to refer to a country or region in a way that involves the emotions or the imagination
examples: SEE ALSO cloud cuckoo land
She longed to return to her native land.
They dreamed of travelling to foreign lands.
faraway lands beyond the sea
America is the land of freedom and opportunity.
the land of the fairies/elves/giants

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: alive; not sleeping; no longer ill
examples: I’m glad to see you’re back in the land of the living. We were worried about you.
By lunchtime I’d returned to the land of the living.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: sleeping
examples: Pete and Jo were still in the land of Nod, so I went out for a walk in the morning sunshine.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a place where life is pleasant and easy and people are very happy
examples: He dreamed of emigrating to Canada—the land of milk and honey.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the way the land in an area is formed and what physical characteristics it has
examples: The castle was hidden by the lie of the land.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the way a situation is now and how it is likely to develop
examples: Check out the lie of the land before you make a decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to have enough money to be able to afford expensive things, food, drink, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to find out about a situation
examples: Let's wait and see how the land lies before we do anything.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to collect information before deciding what to doWord Origin
examples: Old English, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch land and German Land.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act of bringing an aircraft or a spacecraft down to the ground after a journey
examples: OPPOSITE take-off
a perfect/smooth/safe landing
the first Apollo moon landing
The pilot was forced to make an emergency landing.
a landing site
the first successful lunar landing

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the area at the top of a set of stairs where you arrive before you go into an upstairs room or move onto another set of stairs
examples: Go up to the first-floor landing and it’s the door on the right.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an act of bringing soldiers to land in an area that is controlled by the enemy

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a flat wooden platform on the water where boats let people get on and off, and load and unload goods
examples: SYNONYM jetty

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or company from whom you rent a room, a house, an office, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO absentee landlord
a buy-to-let landlord (= who buys houses and flats in order to rent them out)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a man who owns or manages a pub or a guest house
examples: COMPARE landlady

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something, such as a large building, that you can see clearly from a distance and that will help you to know where you are
examples: The Empire State Building is a familiar landmark on the New York skyline.
The tower was once a landmark for ships.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an event, a discovery, an invention, etc. that marks an important stage in something
examples: SYNONYM milestone
The ceasefire was seen as a major landmark in the fight against terrorism.
a landmark decision/ruling in the courts

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a building or a place that is very important because of its history, and that should be preserved
examples: SYNONYM monument
The residents are seeking landmark status for the building.
The building has been designated a historical landmark by the Commission.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: everything you can see when you look across a large area of land, especially in the country
examples: the woods and fields that are typical features of the English landscape
an urban landscape
the bleak/barren/rugged landscape of the area
The mountains dominate the landscape.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a painting of a view of the countryside; this style of painting
examples: COMPARE townscape
an artist famous for his landscapes
She specializes in landscapes.
a landscape painter/painting

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the characteristic features of an area of activity
examples: We can expect changes in the political landscape.
Their songs altered the landscape of popular music.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the way of printing a document in which the top of the page is one of the longer sides
examples: COMPARE portrait (3)
Select the landscape option when printing the file.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an object, especially an ugly building, that makes a place less beautiful
examples: The power station is a blot on the landscape.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a narrow road in the country
examples: SEE ALSO memory lane
winding country lanes
We drove along a muddy lane to reach the farmhouse.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a city street
examples: Park Lane
The quickest way is through the back lanes behind the bus station.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a section of a wide road, that is marked by painted white lines, to keep lines of traffic separate
examples: SEE ALSO bicycle lane
the inside/middle lane
the northbound/southbound lane
to change lanes
She signalled and pulled over into the slow lane.
a four-lane highway

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a narrow marked section of a track or a swimming pool that is used by one person, for example when taking part in a race
examples: The Australian in lane four is coming up fast from behind.
Obi, the record holder, is in lane 3.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a route used by ships or aircraft on regular journeys
examples: SEE ALSO air lane
one of the world’s busiest shipping/sea lanes

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: (in tenpin bowling) a narrow section of floor along which the ball is bowled
examples: a 20-lane bowling alley

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: where things are most exciting and where a lot is happening
examples: He had a good job, plenty of money and he was enjoying life in the fast lane.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the system of communication in speech and writing that is used by people of a particular country or area
examples: SEE ALSO first language
the English language
It takes a long time to learn to speak a language well.
All the children must learn a foreign language.
German is my native language.
Is English an official language in your country?
The novel has been translated into over twenty languages.
She has a good command of the Spanish language.
Good language skills are essential in this job.
They fell in love in spite of the language barrier (= the difficulty of communicating when people speak different languages).
Why study Latin? It's a dead language (= no longer spoken by anyone).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the use by humans of a system of sounds and words to communicate
examples: SEE ALSO artificial language
a qualification in language teaching
a study of language acquisition in two-year-olds
Language is constantly evolving.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a particular style of speaking or writing
examples: SEE ALSO bad language
spoken/written language
literary/poetic language
foul language (= words that people may consider offensive)
The poem uses distinctly modern language.
His strength is that he addresses his readers in plain language.
the language of science

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a way of expressing ideas and feelings using movements, symbols and sound
examples: SEE ALSO body language
the language of mime
the language of dolphins/bees

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a system of symbols and rules that is used to operate a computer
examples: SEE ALSO assembly language
a programming language

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be careful about what you say in order not to upset or offend somebody
examples: Watch your language, young man!
The referee told the players to mind their language.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be able to communicate easily with another person because you share similar opinions and experienceWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French langage, based on Latin lingua ‘tongue’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the top part of your legs that forms a flat surface when you are sitting down
examples: There's only one seat so you'll have to sit on my lap.
She sat with her hands in her lap.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one journey from the beginning to the end of a track used for running, etc.
examples: the fastest lap on record
She has completed six laps.
He was overtaken on the final lap.
to do a lap of honour (= go around the track again to celebrate winning)
to do a victory lap

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a section of a journey, or of a piece of work, etc.
examples: They're off on the first lap of their round-the-world tour.
We've nearly finished. We're on the last lap.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make something the responsibility of another person
examples: They dropped the problem firmly back in my lap.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: somebody has the opportunity to do something pleasant without having made any effort
examples: My dream job just fell into my lap.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if the result of something is in the lap of the gods, you do not know what will happen because it depends on luck or things you cannot control

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in easy, comfortable conditions, and enjoying the advantages of being rich
examples: We spent two weeks in the hotel living in the lap of luxury.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small computer that can work with a battery and be easily carried
examples: SYNONYM notebook
I opened my laptop and started typing.
She was still working on her laptop.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: big in size or quantity
examples: a large group/city/area/crowd/family
a large number of people
There were some very large amounts of money involved.
Drought hit large parts of the country.
A large proportion of old people live alone.
The company has grown large enough to employ over 100 people.
The kitchen is relatively large for a modern apartment.
That's too large to fit in my suitcase!
The population is slightly larger than that of Canada.
Women usually do the larger share of the housework.
Seoul is one of the world's largest cities.
Who's the rather large (= fat) lady in the hat?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to describe one size in a range of sizes of clothes, food, products used in the house, etc.
examples: Would you like small, medium or large?
Do you have these jeans in a larger size?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: wide in range and involving many things
examples: a large and complex issue
Some drugs are being used on a much larger scale than previously.
The studies are often large in scope, with budgets to match.
If we look at the larger picture of the situation, the differences seem slight.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: as a whole; in general
examples: the opinion of the public at large

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not captured; free
examples: Her killer is still at large.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when you are saying something that is generally, but not completely, true
examples: By and large, I enjoyed my time at school.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to enjoy yourself, especially by dancing and drinking alcohol

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to a great extent
examples: Their success is due in large part to their determination.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to show surprise at seeing somebody/something
examples: I hadn’t seen her for fifteen years and then there she was, (as) large as life.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: looking or behaving in a way that is more interesting or exciting than other people, and so is likely to attract attention
examples: SYNONYM flamboyant
He's a larger than life character.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be frightening and make you worried because something seems hard to avoid
examples: The prospect of war loomed large.
The issue looms large in political campaigns nationwide.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: easy to see or understand
examples: Mistrust was writ large on her face.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: being a large or obvious example of the thing mentioned
examples: This is deception writ large.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: involving many people or things, especially over a wide area
examples: Large areas of the forest will be cleared for ranching as part of a large-scale development plan.
the large-scale employment of women

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: drawn or made to a scale that shows a small area of land or a building in great detail
examples: OPPOSITE small-scale

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to a great extent; mostly or mainly
examples: The manager was largely responsible for the team’s victory.
The popularity of the book is largely due to the fantastic illustrations.
Women aged 35 to 50 are largely ignored by mainstream cinema.
The decision was based largely on consumer feedback.
He resigned largely because of the stories in the press.
It was largely a matter of trial and error.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a device that gives out light in which all the waves oscillate (= change direction and strength) together, typically producing a powerful beam of light that can be used for cutting metal, in medical operations, etc.
examples: a laser beam
a laser navigation device
The barcodes on the products are read by lasers.
a laser show (= lasers used as entertainment)
She's had laser surgery on her eye.
laser treatment/therapy

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: arriving, happening or done after the expected, arranged or usual time
examples: OPPOSITE early
I'm sorry I'm late.
She's late for work every day.
My flight was an hour late.
We apologize for the late arrival of this train.
Interest will be charged for late payment.
Because of the cold weather the crops are later this year.
Here is a late news flash.
Some children are very late developers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: near the end of a period of time, a person’s life, etc.
examples: OPPOSITE early
in the late afternoon
in late summer
young people in their late teens (= aged 18 or 19)
She married in her late twenties (= when she was 28 or 29).
The school was built in the late 1970s.
The concert was cancelled at a very late stage.
United sealed the win with two late goals.
Shakespeare's late plays
a late Victorian house

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: near the end of the day
examples: OPPOSITE early
Let's go home—it's getting late.
Look at the time—it's much later than I thought.
What is the latest time I can have an appointment?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: no longer alive
examples: She spoke of her late husband with passion.
The event was organized in memory of the late Stephen Hawking.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: happening after the time when it is possible to do something
examples: It's too late to save her now.
Buy now before it's too late.
I’m afraid you’re too late to apply for the job.
The doctors did all they could, but it was too late.
It's getting too late to do anything today.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: recently; in the recent past
examples: Have you seen her lately?
It's only lately that she's been well enough to go out.
I haven't been sleeping well just lately.
She had lately returned from India.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at a time in the future; after the time you are talking about
examples: OPPOSITE early
See you later.
I met her again three years later.
His father died later that year.
We're going to Rome later in the year.
She later became a doctor.
I discovered later that she'd known all about it from the beginning.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a way of saying goodbye, used by young people
examples: Later, guys!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: at a time in the future; after the time you are talking about
examples: I'm going out later on.
Much later on, she realized what he had meant.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: by a particular time and not after it
examples: Please arrive no later than 8 o'clock.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: at some time in the future, even if you are not sure exactly when
examples: Sooner or later you will have to make a decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: after a short time rather than after a long time
examples: We urged them to sort out the problem sooner rather than later.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the most recent or newest
examples: the latest craze/fashion/trend
his latest book/film/album
the latest polls/reports
Have you heard the latest news?
the latest unemployment figures
The government declined to comment on the latest developments.
the latest version of the software
The latest round of talks was productive.

examples: SYNONYM shoot up
The shares leapt in value from 476p to close at 536p.
The company saw pre-tax profits leap to £14.5 million in 2004.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody has a sudden feeling of happiness or excitement
examples: My heart leapt at the news.
Her heart leaped with joy.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make a decision about somebody/something too quickly, before you know or have thought about all the facts
examples: There I go again—jumping to conclusions.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to advise somebody to think about the possible results or dangers of something before doing itWord Origin
examples: Old English hlēapan (verb), hlȳp (noun), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch lopen, German laufen (verb), and Dutch loop, German Lauf (noun), all meaning ‘run’, also to lope.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to jump high or a long way
examples: A dolphin leapt out of the water.
We leaped over the stream.
The horse leapt a five-foot wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move or do something suddenly and quickly
examples: She leapt out of bed.
He leaped across the room to answer the door.
I leapt to my feet (= stood up quickly).
They leapt into action immediately.
She was quick to leap to my defence (= speak in support of me).
The photo seemed to leap off the page (= it got your attention immediately).
His name leapt out at me (= I saw it immediately).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to gain knowledge or skill by studying, from experience, from being taught, etc.
examples: to learn a language/skill/trade
He had the opportunity to learn English in Australia.
I learned a lot from my father.
Everyone in the class had the opportunity to learn from each other.
You can learn a great deal just from watching other players.
She's very keen to learn about Japanese culture.
The book is about how children learn.
She received no training but quickly learnt on the job (= while doing the job).
He's learning to play the trumpet.
Most people learn to read as children.
Today we learnt how to use the new software.
Students need to learn what to do in an emergency.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to study and repeat something in order to be able to remember it
examples: SYNONYM memorize
I learnt the poem by heart.
We have to learn one of Hamlet's speeches for school tomorrow.
You'll have to learn your lines by next week.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to gradually change your attitudes about something so that you behave in a different way
examples: Some people never learn, do they?
I'm sure she'll learn from her mistakes.
Why do people so often fail to learn from experience?
He’ll just have to learn (that) he can’t always have his own way.
They soon learn that bad behaviour is a sure-fire way of getting attention.
They soon learned to love living in the countryside.
I soon learned not to ask too many questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to become aware of something by hearing about it from somebody else
examples: SYNONYM discover
I first learnt of his death many years later.
We only learned about the problems in May of this year.
We were very surprised to learn (that) she had got married again.
We only learned who the new teacher was a few days ago.
How did they react when they learned the news?
It has been learned that 500 jobs are to be lost at the factory.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to know something because of something unpleasant that has happened to you
examples: He's a ruthless businessman, as I know to my cost.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to find out how to behave by learning from your mistakes or from unpleasant experiences, rather than from being told

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to learn what to do or not to do in the future because you have had a bad experience in the past

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to show somebody/know/learn how a particular job should be done

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to express surprise at something new or unexpected you have been toldWord Origin
examples: Old English leornian ‘learn’ (in Middle English also ‘teach’), of West Germanic origin; related to German lernen, also to lore.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of learning something
examples: SEE ALSO blended learning
lifelong/adult learning
new methods to facilitate language learning
Field trips provide an opportunity for experiential learning.
teaching and learning
The school aims to provide a supportive learning environment.
Last season was a learning experience for the team.
The learning process is slightly different in each individual.
A large part of children's learning takes place in the home.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: knowledge that you get from reading and studying
examples: SEE ALSO book learning
a woman of great learning

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that you learn, especially from your experience of working on something
examples: We will be sharing key learnings from our project.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: smallest in size, amount, degree, etc.
examples: He's the best teacher, even though he has the least experience.
She never had the least idea what to do about it.
He gave (the) least of all towards the wedding present.
How others see me is the least of my worries (= I have more important things to worry about).
It's the least I can do to help (= I feel I should do more).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used after amounts to show that the amount is the lowest possible
examples: It'll take a year, at the very least.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not at all
examples: Really, I'm not in the least tired.
‘Do you mind if I put the television on?’ ‘No, not in the least.’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not at all
examples: Normally I'm not the least bit shy.
He wasn't the slightest bit interested in answering our questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: without making something seem better, worse, more serious, etc. than it really is
examples: I was surprised, to say the least.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: material made by removing the hair or fur from animal skins and preserving the skins using special processes
examples: SEE ALSO chamois (2)
a leather jacket
The soles are made of leather.
a leather-bound book
I'm looking for a pair of boots in dark brown leather.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: clothes made from leather, especially those worn by people riding motorcycles
examples: a biker in black leathers

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: as quickly as possible
examples: to ride hell for leather

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to go away from a person or a place
examples: Come on, it's time we left (= time for us to leave).
She left without saying goodbye.
The plane leaves for Dallas at 12.35.
What time do you have to leave for work?
The plane leaves Heathrow at 12.35.
I hate leaving home.
She left the house around 8 this morning.
The whole family was forced to leave the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop living at a place, belonging to a group, working for an employer, etc.
examples: My assistant is threatening to leave.
He didn't leave home until he was 30.
She left school at 16.
I went to see him, but was told he had left town.
The Mayor left office in 2018.
Why did you leave your last job?
People leave for better-paid jobs elsewhere.
Many of her relatives had left Ireland for America.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to leave your wife, husband or partner permanently
examples: I was afraid you'd leave if you knew the truth.
I'll never leave you.
She left him for a colleague.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to go away from a place without taking something/somebody with you
examples: I'll have to go back—I've left my jacket.
They left the children and went out for the evening.
I've left my bag on the bus.
You can leave your things here.
He wasn't well, so we had to leave him behind.
Don't leave any of your belongings behind.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make or allow somebody/something to remain in a particular condition, place, etc.
examples: Leave the door open, please.
The bomb blast left 25 people dead.
His help left her free to focus on her research.
Don't leave her waiting outside in the rain.
We were left feeling rather disappointed.
Leave the rice to cook for 20 minutes.
He ate up his vegetables but left the chicken.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to remain to be used, sold, etc.
examples: Is there any coffee left?
He's spent all the money—there's nothing left.
You still have a few minutes left.
How many tickets do you have left?
They are fighting to save what is left of their business.
Not much is left of the old town.
The only course of action left to me was to notify her employer.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make something happen or remain as a result
examples: Red wine leaves a stain.
The Romans left their mark on Britain.
Leave room on the spreadsheet to add the results later.
They've left a space here where you can put your name.
She left me with the impression that she was unhappy.
I'm afraid you leave me no choice.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to deliver, write or record something to be seen or heard later
examples: Lots of people had left comments under the post.
Someone called, but they didn't leave a message.
Someone left this note for you.
Someone left you this note.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to not do something or deal with something immediately
examples: Leave the dishes—I'll do them later.
Why do you always leave everything until the last moment?
Let's leave that topic for another day.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to take care of something
examples: You can leave the cooking to me.
They didn't leave anything to chance (= everything was planned carefully).
‘Where shall we eat?’ ‘I’ll leave it entirely (up) to you (= you can decide).’
I leave it to you to decide what order to do things in.
She left her assistant in charge.
Leave it with me—I'm sure I can sort it out.
They left me with all the clearing up.
Can I leave you to lock up the shop?
I was left to cope on my own.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to give something to somebody when you die
examples: SYNONYM bequeath
He left a large estate.
She left £1 million to her daughter.
She left her daughter £1 million.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to have family who continue to live after your death
examples: He leaves a wife and two children.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to have a particular amount left over
examples: Seven from ten leaves three.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be alone
examples: I didn’t know anyone in New York, so I was left to myself to explore.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be allowed to do what you want
examples: Left to himself, the dog will eat anything and everything.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not care if somebody accepts or rejects your offer

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody does not have a strong opinion about something
examples: Dancing? I can take it or leave it.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to stop annoying somebody or trying to get their attention
examples: SYNONYM leave/let somebody alone
Why can’t you stop texting me and just leave me be?

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to stop holding on to something
examples: SYNONYM let go
Leave go of my arm—you're hurting me!

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to say or do nothing more about something
examples: We'll never agree, so let's just leave it at that.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to stop doing somethingWord Origin
examples: verb Old English lǣfan ‘bequeath’, also ‘allow to remain, leave in place’ of Germanic origin; related to German bleiben ‘remain’.

definitions.definition: a talk that is given to a group of people to teach them about a particular subject, often as part of a university or college course
examples: to go to/attend a lecture
to give/deliver a lecture
I have a lecture at nine tomorrow.
a series of lectures on Jane Austen
a course of lectures on art history
an illustrated lecture about the planet Mars
a book based on her lectures to students
a lecture to the Darwin Society
a lecture by Professor Snow
She spoke about the environmental problems of the future in a lecture at Georgetown University.
There were very few students at his lecture that morning.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a long, angry talk that somebody gives to one person or a group of people because they have done something wrong
examples: I know I should stop smoking—don't give me a lecture about it.

examples: SEE ALSO bow legs
Sit on the floor, stretching your legs out in front of you.
your left/right leg
I broke my leg playing football.
She has a broken leg.
He lost a leg in a motorcycle accident.
She had to have her leg amputated.
How many legs does a centipede have?
The bear rose up on its hind legs.
a wooden leg
He dribbled the ball between the defender's legs.
I had a big bruise on my leg.
a leg injury

definitions.label: Meaning 2
