examples: Have you ever tried frogs' legs?
chicken legs
roast leg of lamb

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the part of a pair of trousers that covers the leg
examples: a trouser/pant leg
He rolled up the legs of his jeans.
These jeans are too long in the leg.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: one of the long thin parts on the bottom of a table, chair, etc. that support it
examples: a table/chair leg
He tripped over the leg of the chair.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: having the number or type of legs mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO cross-legged
a three-legged stool
a long-legged insect

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: one part of a journey or race
examples: SYNONYM section
The final leg of the trip was by donkey.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: one of a pair of matches played between the same opponents in a sports competition, which together form a single round (= stage) of the competition
examples: The Spanish team won the third leg.
I really believe we can turn around that 4–2 first leg deficit and win this game.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: as quickly as you can

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be going to die or stop functioning very soon; to be very weak or in bad condition

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to wish somebody good luck, especially to an actor before they go on stage

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to cost/pay a lot of money

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to have sex

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if you say that a news story, etc. has legs, you mean that people will continue to be interested in it for a long time

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be in a position where you are unable to prove something or explain why something is reasonable
examples: Without written evidence, we don't have a leg to stand on.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to play a joke on somebody, usually by making them believe something that is not true

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to start to do something or to hurry

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to go for a short walk after sitting for some time
examples: It was good to get out of the car and stretch our legs.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to talk too much, especially about things that are boring or not important

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: feeling ashamed or unhappy because you have been defeated or punishedWord Origin
examples: Middle English (superseding shank): from Old Norse leggr (compare with Danish læg ‘calf (of the leg)’), of Germanic origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: money or property that is given to you by somebody when they die
examples: SYNONYM inheritance
They each received a legacy of $5 000.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a situation that exists now because of events, actions, etc. that took place in the past
examples: Future generations will be left with a legacy of pollution and destruction.
The problems were made worse by the legacy of centuries of neglect.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that somebody has done successfully and that has positive effects even after they retire or die
examples: She was an active anti-bullying campaigner, and after she died her family set up a charity to ensure that her legacy lives on.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the idea that something created for an event in the past can be used in a different way in the future
examples: In the UK, the Olympic legacy lives on most strongly in East London where the Olympic Park is located.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the law
examples: the legal profession/system
to take/seek legal advice
a legal adviser/expert/team
legal fees/costs
They are currently facing a long legal battle in the US courts.
Campaigners have have threatened to mount a legal challenge on human rights grounds.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: allowed or required by law
examples: OPPOSITE illegal
legal rights/obligations
The legal status of refugees was defined in the Refugee Convention of 1951.
The driver was more than three times over the legal limit (= the amount of alcohol you are allowed to have in your body when you are driving).
Should euthanasia be made legal?
substances such as alcohol and nicotine that are legal for adults
Many of these products are actually legal to use in the United States.
It is now perfectly legal to gamble online in Nevada.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a story from ancient times about people and events, that may or may not be true; this type of story
examples: SYNONYM myth
The film is based on the legend of Robin Hood.
the heroes of Greek legend
Legend has it that the lake was formed by the tears of a god.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a very famous person, especially in a particular field, who is admired by other people
examples: a jazz/screen/sporting legend
She was a legend in her own lifetime.
Many of golf's living legends were playing.
a legend in the world of music
movie stars who become living legends

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the explanation of a map or a diagram in a book
examples: SYNONYM key

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a piece of writing on a sign, a label, a coin, etc.Word Origin
examples: Middle English (in the sense ‘story of a saint's life’): from Old French legende, from medieval Latin legenda ‘things to be read’, from Latin legere ‘read’. Sense (1) dates from the early 17th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very famous and talked about a lot by people
examples: a legendary figure
the legendary Bob Dylan
Her patience and tact are legendary.
His dedication and Christian charity had made him a legendary figure.
We once received a visit from the legendary Orson Welles.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: mentioned in stories from ancient times
examples: legendary heroes

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a law or a set of laws passed by a parliament
examples: an important piece of legislation
New legislation on the sale of drugs will be introduced next year.
They are calling for tough legislation to tackle this problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of making and passing laws
examples: Legislation will be difficult and will take time.
The terrorist attack prompted knee-jerk legislation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the act of making and passing laws
examples: a legislative assembly/body/council
legislative powers

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group of people who have the power to make and change laws
examples: COMPARE executive
a democratically elected legislature
the national/state legislature

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: for which there is a fair and acceptable reason
examples: SYNONYM valid
a legitimate grievance
It seemed a perfectly legitimate question.
Politicians are legitimate targets for satire.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: allowed and acceptable according to the law
examples: SYNONYM legal
the legitimate government of the country
Is his business strictly legitimate?
The legitimate government was reinstated after the uprising.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: born when its parents are legally married to each other
examples: OPPOSITE illegitimate

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: time when you are not working or studying; free time
examples: These days we have more money and more leisure to enjoy it.
Make the most of your leisure time!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: activities that you enjoy in your free time
examples: These days we have increased opportunities for leisure.
leisure activities/pursuits
public parks and leisure facilities
the leisure industry (= the business of providing leisure activities)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: with no particular activities; free
examples: Spend the afternoon at leisure in the town centre.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: without hurrying
examples: Let's have lunch so we can talk at leisure.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: when you have the time to do something without hurrying
examples: I suggest you take the forms away and read them at your leisure.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a man/woman who does not have to workWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French leisir, based on Latin licere ‘be allowed’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a yellow citrus fruit with juice that has a bitter, sharp taste. Slices of lemon and lemon juice are used in cooking and drinks.
examples: Add a squeeze of lemon juice.
Squeeze the juice of half a lemon over the fish.
a gin and tonic with ice and lemon
lemon tea
a lemon tree
Garnish the fish with wedges of lemon.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: lemon juice or a drink made from lemon
examples: SEE ALSO bitter lemon

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a pale yellow colour

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a thing that cannot be used because it does not work as it should
examples: SYNONYM dud

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a stupid personWord Origin
examples: Middle English: via Old French limon (in modern French denoting a lime) from Arabic līmūn (a collective term for fruits of this kind); compare with lime (the fruit).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give something to somebody or allow them to use something that belongs to you, which they have to return to you later
examples: They will lend equipment free of charge.
I've lent the car to a friend.
The gallery has been willing to lend out works of art in the past.
The charity lends out toys to children with special needs and disabilities.
Can you lend me £10?
Can you lend me your car this evening?
Has he returned that book you lent him?
She very kindly lent me her bicycle.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give money to somebody on condition that they pay it back over a period of time and pay interest on it
examples: The bank lends money at very cheap rates.
They refused to lend us the money.
The bank refused to lend the money to us.
Banks are less willing to lend in these uncertain times.
There are a large number of financial providers lending to businesses across the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to give a particular quality to a person or a situation
examples: The setting sun lent an air of melancholy to the scene.
Her presence lent the occasion a certain dignity.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to give or provide help, support, etc.
examples: I was more than happy to lend my support to such a good cause.
He came along to lend me moral support.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to help somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make something seem true or likely
examples: Most of the available evidence lends colour to this view.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to listen in a patient and kind way to somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to help somebody with something
examples: I went over to see if I could lend a hand.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to let it be known in public that you support or agree with something
examples: I am more than happy to lend my name to this campaign.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to have a place named after you

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make something seem more likely to be true or real
examples: This latest evidence lends support to her theory.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the size or measurement of something from one end to the other
examples: COMPARE breadth
Measure the length of the line from A to B.
to estimate/calculate/increase/reduce the length of something
The river is 300 miles in length.
The snake usually reaches a length of 100 cm.
Safety barriers will be installed along the full length of the road.
He ran the entire length of the beach.
Look at the length of that queue!
He has to hold newspapers at arm's length to focus on the print.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the quality of being long
examples: Did you see the length of his hair?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the amount of time that something lasts
examples: The average length of each song on the album is six minutes.
These changes will shorten the length of time spent waiting for test results.
She got a headache if she had to read for any length of time (= for a long time).
Size of pension depends partly on length of service with the company.
Each class is 45 minutes in length.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the amount of writing in a book, or a document, etc.; the amount of time that a film lasts
examples: SEE ALSO feature-length
There is a maximum length of 2 500 words.
The document is over 800 pages in length.
Her novels vary in length.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: having the length mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO full-length
shoulder-length hair

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the distance from one end of a swimming pool to the other
examples: COMPARE width
He swims 50 lengths a day.
I did 20 lengths today.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the size of a horse or boat from one end to the other, when it is used to measure the distance between two horses or boats taking part in a race
examples: The horse won by two clear lengths.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a long, thin piece of something
examples: a length of rope/string/wire
The timber is sold in lengths of 2, 5 or 10 metres.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: for a long time and in detail
examples: He quoted at length from the report.
We have already discussed this matter at great length.
He told me at length about his new job.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: after a long time
examples: ‘I'm still not sure,’ he said at length.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to put a lot of effort into doing something, especially when this seems extreme
examples: She goes to extraordinary lengths to keep her private life private.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to avoid having a close relationship with somebody
examples: He keeps all his clients at arm's length.
She kept him at arm's length until he stopped smoking.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: in or to all parts of a place
examples: They have travelled the length and breadth of Europe giving concerts.
They travelled the length and breadth of the land.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very long, and often too long, in time or size
examples: lengthy delays
I had to go through the lengthy process of obtaining a visa.
a lengthy explanation

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a curved piece of glass or plastic that makes things look larger, smaller or clearer when you look through it
examples: a pair of glasses with tinted lenses

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of equipment that is part of a camera, containing one or more lenses
examples: SEE ALSO fisheye
a camera with an adjustable lens
a view of Mount Kilimanjaro as seen through Eddie's camera lens
a lens cap/cover
a long-lens shot of a rare bird

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a contact lens (= a small round piece of thin plastic that you put on your eye to help you see better)
examples: Have you got your lenses in?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the clear part of the eye, behind the pupil, that focuses light so that you can see clearlyWord Origin
examples: late 17th cent.: from Latin, ‘lentil’ (because of the similarity in shape).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: sexually attracted to other women; connected with lesbians
examples: the lesbian and gay community
a lesbian relationship
The singer has become a lesbian icon.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used with uncountable nouns to mean ‘a smaller amount of’
examples: less butter/time/importance
He was advised to smoke fewer cigarettes and drink less beer.
We have less to worry about now.
They say we should exercise and eat less of some kinds of fat.
We'll be there in less than no time (= very soon).
The victory was nothing less than a miracle.
It is less of a problem than I'd expected.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: smaller and smaller amounts; at a rate that is decreasing
examples: As time passed, she saw less and less of all her old friends at home.
There used to be TV shows that everyone would watch at the same time and talk about the next day, but that happens less and less.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: including only what is essential can create a more effective product or result
examples: His simple, elegant paintings reflect his principle that less is more.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to suggest that something is surprising or impressive
examples: She's having lunch with the Director, no less.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a large amount
examples: The guide contains details of no less than 115 hiking routes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not as great in size, amount or importance as something/somebody else
examples: people of lesser importance
They were all involved to a greater or lesser degree (= some were more involved than others).
The law was designed to protect wives, and, to a lesser extent, children.
He was encouraged to plead guilty to the lesser offence.
He doesn’t even acknowledge us lesser mortals (= people who are not as important or powerful).
A lesser woman would have given up.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used in the names of some types of animals, birds and plants that are smaller than similar kinds
examples: a lesser black-backed gull

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the less unpleasant of two unpleasant choicesWord Origin
examples: Middle English: a double comparative, from less + -er.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a period of time in which somebody is taught something
examples: COMPARE class
She gives piano lessons.
I’m having driving lessons.
He took lessons in Thai cookery.
a history lesson on the Roman Empire
Beethoven's lessons with Haydn continued until 1794.
His parents paid for lessons from local dance teachers.
Lessons for beginners can be arranged.
Our first lesson on Tuesdays is French.
What did we do last lesson?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that is intended to be learned
examples: The coursebook is divided into 30 lessons.
Other countries can teach us a lesson or two on industrial policy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an experience, especially an unpleasant one, that somebody can learn from so that it does not happen again in the future
examples: SEE ALSO object lesson
The accident taught me a lesson I'll never forget.
There are lessons to be learned from this mistake.
The narrative presents the hero with a series of life lessons.
It is dangerous to ignore the lessons of history.
Let that be a lesson to you (= so that you do not make the same mistake again).
Their openness was a terrific lesson to me.
The film offers an important lesson on the value of friendship.
That's one of the lessons about being in a relationship that I hope not to forget.
He said that the election results were a lesson in humility for the party.
This experience has provided many valuable lessons in caring for the marine habitat.
The lesson for the leaders of Western governments is clear.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a passage from the Bible that is read to people during a church service in the Church of England
examples: SYNONYM reading (7)
The first lesson is taken from St John’s Gospel.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to learn what to do or not to do in the future because you have had a bad experience in the pastWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French leçon, from Latin lectio ‘choosing, reading’, from the verb legere.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used for making suggestions or as a polite way of telling people what you want them to do
examples: ‘Shall we check it again?’ ‘Yes, let's.’
Let's go to the beach.
Right, let's begin.
Let us review these points in more detail.
Let's not tell her what we did.
Don't let's tell her what we did.
Now let's not be silly about this.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used for offering help to somebody
examples: Let me help you with that.
Here, let me do it.
Let us get those boxes down for you.
'Please, let me,' she said, opening the door.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used for making requests or giving instructions
examples: Let me have your report by Friday.
Let me know (= tell me) how I can help.
Please let us know your decision as soon as possible.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to do something or something to happen without trying to stop it
examples: Let them splash around in the pool for a while.
Don't let her upset you.
Let your body relax.
I'll let others decide whether the play was a success or not.
Will you let me finish?
He'd eat chocolate all day long if I let him.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to give somebody permission to do something
examples: They won't let him leave the country.
In some countries they let you drive at 15.
They refused to let us cross the border.
I wanted to go but my parents wouldn't let me.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to allow somebody/something to go somewhere
examples: to let somebody into the house
This lets more water into the soil.
I'll give you a key so that you can let yourself in.
A decision was made to let in more refugees.
Please let me past.
The cat wants to be let out.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show that you are not afraid or worried about somebody doing something
examples: If he thinks he can cheat me, just let him try!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to express a strong wish for something to happen
examples: Let her come home safely!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to introduce what you are going to say or do
examples: Let me give you an example.
Let me just finish this and then I'll come.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to say that you are supposing something to be true when you calculate something
examples: Let line AB be equal to line CD.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to use a house, room, etc. in return for regular payments
examples: SEE ALSO buy-to-let
I let the spare room.
They decided to let out the smaller offices at low rents.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to stop trying to change the behaviour or state of somebody/something
examples: I know I'm being grumpy, but I'm really tired so just let me be.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to mention something in a conversation, by accident or as if by accident
examples: SYNONYM drop
She let fall a further heavy hint.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to be free
examples: SYNONYM free
Will they let the hostages go?
He's finally been let go.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to make somebody have to leave their job
examples: They're having to let 100 employees go because of falling profits.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to stop holding somebody/something
examples: Don't let the rope go.
Don't let go of the rope.
Let go! You're hurting me!

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to give up an idea or an attitude, or control of something
examples: It's time to let the past go.
It's time to let go of the past.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to stop taking care of a house, garden, etc.
examples: I'm afraid I've let the garden go this year.
Let the house go in order to spend time with the kids.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to attack somebody physically or with words

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to say or do no more about something
examples: I don't entirely agree, but I'll let it go at that.
I thought she was hinting at something, but I let it go.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used when you are thinking or trying to remember something
examples: Now let me see—where did he say he lived?

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used when commenting on a situation to suggest that you could say something more or worse but prefer not to
examples: Let's just say he wasn't very happy about the decision (= he was very unhappy or angry about it).

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: used when making a suggestion or giving an example
examples: I can let you have it for, well let's say £100.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to behave in a relaxed way without worrying about what people think of your behaviour
examples: Come on, enjoy yourself, let yourself go!

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to stop being careful about how you look and dress, etc.
examples: He has let himself go since he lost his job.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: available for rent
examples: The website advertises flats to let in the local area.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: causing or able to cause death
examples: SYNONYM deadly
She had been given a lethal dose of poison.
Any sharp pointed instrument is potentially a lethal weapon.
The closure of the factory dealt a lethal blow to the town.
The snake’s venom is rarely lethal to humans.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: causing or able to cause a lot of harm or damage
examples: You and that car—it's a lethal combination!
The group claims that a lethal cocktail of pollutants is being poured into Scotland's rivers and estuaries.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a written, typed or printed message that is put in an envelope or attached to an email and sent to somebody
examples: SEE ALSO air letter
to write/send (somebody) a letter
to receive/get a letter
to post a letter
to mail a letter
a thank-you/resignation/rejection letter
In a letter to members, the Chairman explained the changes.
I wrote a letter to the editor of our local paper.
You may need a letter from your doctor.
a letter of recommendation/complaint/apology
You will be notified by letter.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a written or printed sign representing a sound used in speech
examples: SEE ALSO capital letter
'B' is the second letter of the alphabet.
How many letters are in the Greek alphabet?
the letter A/B/C
I'm thinking of a word that begins with the letter M.
She typed the word ‘HISTORY’ in capital letters.
The slogan is printed in bold letters across the top.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a sign in the shape of a letter that is sewn onto clothes to show that a person plays in a school or college sports team

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the exact words of a law or rule rather than its general meaning
examples: They insist on sticking to the letter of the law.
We might be guilty of slightly bending the letter of the law.
In spite of the difficulties it would cause her family, the judge stuck to the letter of the law and jailed her.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: doing/following exactly what somebody/something says, paying attention to every detail
examples: I followed your instructions to the letter.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the height of something in relation to the ground or to what it used to be
examples: SEE ALSO eye level
The cables are buried one metre below ground level.
The floodwater nearly reached roof level.
The river has fallen to its lowest level since 2012.
the level rose/dropped/decreased/increased
On the second floor you are on a level with (= at the same height as) the treetops.
The tables are not on a level (= the same height).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a floor of a building; a layer of ground
examples: SEE ALSO split-level
a multi-level parking lot
Take the elevator to Level Four.
The restaurant is on the level below this one.
The library is all on one level.
Archaeologists found pottery in the lowest level of the site.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the amount of something that exists in a particular situation at a particular time
examples: a low level of support for the proposed changes
Increase your level of activity to burn more calories.
to raise/reduce the level of something
They have achieved higher levels of efficiency.
A change of course may be needed if the current level of violence continues.
low/high/elevated blood cholesterol levels
a reduction/a rise/a decrease/an increase/a change in energy levels
Profits were at the same level as the year before.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a particular standard or quality
examples: SEE ALSO A level
The hotel's level of service is consistently high.
The participants had different levels of education.
He studied French to degree level.
What is the level of this course?
It is difficult to maintain this level of performance.
She has played tennis at a high level.
Both players are on a level (= of the same standard).
I refuse to sink to their level (= behave as badly as them).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a position or rank in a scale of size or importance
examples: SEE ALSO high-level
the upper levels of government
Discussions are currently being held at national level.
at local/international level

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a particular way of looking at, reacting to or understanding something
examples: On a more personal level, I would like to thank Jean for all the help she has given me.
Fables can be understood on various levels.
At a conscious level, I was quite satisfied with my life.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: one of a series of stages in a computer game. Players progress from easy to more advanced levels within the game.
examples: a computer game with 15 levels
Players advance to the next level by collecting all the pieces and constructing the spaceship.
Each level is randomly generated so each game is different.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a device used to test whether a surface is level, consisting of a glass tube partly filled with liquid with a bubble of air inside. The position of the bubble indicates whether the surface is level.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: honest; legal
examples: SYNONYM above board
I'm not convinced he's on the level.
Are you sure this deal is on the level?

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: as good, bad, important, etc. as somebody/something else
examples: This place is on a level with the best French restaurants.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: as good, bad, important, etc. as somebody/something else
examples: This place is on a par with the best French restaurants.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the greatest or smallest amount of something that is allowed
examples: SYNONYM restriction
They imposed a strict spending limit.
His speed was double the legal limit.
Do not exceed the recommended limit of 6g of salt per day.
The EU has set strict limits on levels of pollution.
to keep government spending within acceptable limits
You can't drive—you're over the limit (= you have drunk more alcohol than is legal when driving).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a point at which something stops being possible or existing
examples: She knew the limits of her power.
to set/define the limits of something
to push/test the limits of something
It's a movie that stretches the limits of believability.
His arrogance knew (= had) no limits.
There is a limit to the amount of pain we can bear.
The team performed to the limit of its capabilities.
to push/test somebody/something to the limit
I knew I had reached my limit and couldn't do any more.
They've done their best within the limits of their capability.
I saw things beyond the limits of my ability to describe.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the furthest edge of an area or a place
examples: SEE ALSO off-limits
We were reaching the limits of civilization.
the city limits (= the imaginary line which officially divides the city from the area outside)
islands on the outer limit of the continent

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be extremely annoying

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to attempt to go beyond what is allowed or thought to be possible
examples: We aim to push the boundaries of what we can achieve.
She pushes her physical limits through various endurance challenges.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: there is no limit to what somebody can achieve, earn, do, etc.
examples: With a talent like his, the sky's the limit.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to some extent
examples: I'm willing to help, within limits.
The children can do what they like, within limits.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: without a point at which something has to stop
examples: The debt is rising without limit.
She's a free spirit and lives her life without limits.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: SYNONYM restraint
to impose limitations on imports
Disability is a physical limitation on your life.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a limit on what somebody/something can do or how good they or it can be
examples: This technique is useful but it has its limitations.
She has serious limitations as a poet.
He was well aware of his own limitations.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not very great in amount or extent
examples: We are doing our best with the limited resources available.
a limited budget/range
Students were unhappy with the limited space available for study.
This animal's intelligence is very limited.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having a particular limit of time, numbers, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO Ltd
This offer is for a limited period only.
There are only a limited number of jobs available.
Entry is limited to 150 people.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long, thin mark on a surface
examples: SEE ALSO bar line
a straight/solid/dotted/dashed line
a wavy/diagonal line
a vertical/horizontal line
parallel lines

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a long, thin mark on the ground to show the limit or border of something, especially of a playing area in some sports
examples: SEE ALSO finishing line
The first to cross the line wins the race.
They were all waiting on the starting line.
She crossed the centre line and hit an oncoming truck.
The ball was over the line.
Your feet must be behind the line when you serve (= in tennis).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a mark like a line on somebody’s skin that people usually get as they get older
examples: SYNONYM wrinkle
He has fine lines around his eyes.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a row of people or things next to each other or behind each other
examples: SEE ALSO chorus line
They formed a line and marched forward.
The children all stood in a line.
They were stuck in a line of traffic.
a straight/long line of trees

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a queue of people
examples: A line formed at each teller window.
to stand/wait in line
If you want a ticket, get in line.
There's a line for the women's bathroom.
They have to stand in line for groceries.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a phone connection; a particular phone number
examples: SEE ALSO fixed-line
The phone lines were jammed (= very busy) with people calling to complain.
I tried to call but the line was busy.
I was talking to John when the line suddenly went dead.
Lines are open from 7.30 am until midnight seven days a week.
If you hold the line (= stay on the phone and wait), I'll see if she is available.
It's your mother on the line.
Your bill includes line rental.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a railway track or other transport route; a section of a transport system or route
examples: SEE ALSO main line
The train was delayed because a tree had fallen across the line.
a rail line
a railway line
the East Coast line
We got off the bus near the end of the line at San Gerardo.
Streetcar lines carried passengers to ever more distant areas of the city.
We live on the Northern Line.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the direction that somebody/something is moving or located in
examples: Just keep going in a straight line.
The town is in a direct line between London and the coast.
Be careful to stay out of the line of fire (= the direction somebody is shooting in).
They followed the line of the river for three miles.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a route from one place to another especially when it is used for a particular purpose
examples: Their aim was to block guerrilla supply lines.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a row of words on a page or the empty space where they can be written; the words of a song or poem or other piece of writing
examples: SEE ALSO bottom line
Look at line 5 of the text.
Write the title of your essay on the top line.
I can only remember the first two lines of that song.
She quoted a few lines of Shakespeare.
A team of programmers wrote 200 000 lines of code (= computer programming language).
Avoid a line break (= starting a new line) in the middle of a word.

examples: to learn your lines
I keep forgetting my lines.
The way she delivers the line is hilarious.

It was a small part with few lines.
Actors always want more lines.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a punishment in which a child has to write out a particular sentence a number of times
examples: The teacher gave me 100 lines.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a remark, especially when somebody says it to achieve a particular purpose
examples: Don't give me that line about having to work late again.
That's the worst chat-up line I've ever heard.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: a long piece of rope, string, etc., especially when it is used for a particular purpose
examples: SEE ALSO clothes line
They dropped the sails and threw a line to a man on the dock.
Towels were hanging on the line (= clothes line).
He had a fish on his line.
150 feet of nylon line

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: a pipe or thick wire that carries water, gas or electricity from one place to another
examples: SEE ALSO power line
water/gas/sewage lines
Telephone lines were brought down in the storm.
There were two fuel lines coming into the engine.
The telegraph lines connecting the two cities had been cut.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: an imaginary limit or border between one place or thing and another
examples: SEE ALSO coastline
a district/county line
lines of longitude and latitude

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: the division between one area of thought or behaviour and another or between one group of people and another

We want to cut across lines of race, sex and religion.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: an attitude or a belief, especially one that somebody states publicly
examples: SEE ALSO hard line
The company line is that discrimination in any form is not tolerated.
He supported the official line on education.
The government is taking a firm line on terrorism.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: a method or way of doing or thinking about something
examples: SEE ALSO first-line
His research follows quite different lines.
I don't follow your line of reasoning.
a line of thought/thinking
She decided to try a different line of argument (= way of persuading somebody of something).
somebody’s first line of attack/defence
The police are pursuing a new line of inquiry (= way of finding out information).

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: a series of people, things or events that follow one another in time
examples: to pass something down through the male/female line
She came from a long line of doctors.
This novel is the latest in a long line of thrillers that he has written.
That was the first in a whole line of mistakes and bad decisions.
The book traces a historical line from Beethoven to the present day.
The muddle seems to have happened further down the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: a series of people in order of importance
examples: SEE ALSO line manager
a line of command
There is some benefit to having a clear line of authority.
Orders came down the line from the very top.
He is second in line to the chairman.
to be next in line to the throne

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: the edge, outline or shape of somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO A-line
He traced the line of her jaw with his finger.
a beautiful sports car with sleek lines
I prefer simple lines in skirts and trousers.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: a system of making something, in which the product moves from one worker to the next until it is finished
examples: SEE ALSO assembly line

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: a type or area of business, activity or interest
examples: SEE ALSO sideline
My line of work pays pretty well.
What line of business are they in?
You can't do much in the art line without training.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: a type of product
examples: Some lines sell better than others.
new product lines
We are starting a new line in casual clothes.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: a company that provides transport for people or goods
examples: SEE ALSO airline
a shipping/bus line
the White Star Line

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: a row or series of military defences where the soldiers are fighting during a war
examples: SEE ALSO front line
They were trapped behind enemy lines (= in the area controlled by the enemy).

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: an amount of cocaine that is spread out in a thin line, ready to take

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: connected with the income that a company receives and the costs it has to pay in its daily business, which affect the profit it makes
examples: COMPARE below the line (1)
All these costs are above the line and directly hit profits.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: connected with advertising in the mass media
examples: COMPARE below the line (2)
They planned an advertising campaign with both above-the-line and social media components.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: at some point during an activity or a process
examples: Somewhere along the line a large amount of money went missing.
We'll make a decision on that further down the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: in the way that is mentioned
examples: The new system will operate along the same lines as the old one.
They voted along class lines.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: similar to the way or thing that is mentioned
examples: Those aren't his exact words, but he said something along those lines.
The hotel was built along the lines of a French chateau.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: used to say that people or groups have shown which side they intend to support in an argument or contest that is going to begin

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to be working or functioning
examples: SEE ALSO online
The new working methods will come on line in June.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to be in a position where you can be shot at
examples: attempts to prevent civilians from being in the firing line

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to be in a position where people can criticize or blame you
examples: The employment secretary found himself in the firing line over recent job cuts.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: connected with unusual costs or income that a company pays or receives, that are not part of its daily business and are taken away or added after calculating profits
examples: COMPARE above the line (1)
There was a £4 million extraordinary charge below the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: connected with advertising by means of direct mail, email, social media, events, etc.
examples: COMPARE above the line (2)
We are planning social networking, digital marketing and below-the-line activities across the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: connected with a section at the end of an online article or blog post where readers can put comments
examples: There were numerous comments below the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: to behave or make somebody/something behave in the same way as other people or how they should behave
examples: The other members of the board must be brought into line.
The actions of investors do not always fall into line with financial theory.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: to do something that is not considered to be acceptable behaviour
examples: He crossed the line by making details of their very private conversation public.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to go to the front of a line of people without waiting for your turn
examples: Somebody cut in line in front of me.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: to say that something is finished and not worth discussing any more

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: (to reach) the point at which something can no longer continue in the same way
examples: A defeat in the second round marked the end of the line for last year's champion.
The loss of this contract could signal the end of the line for the shipyard.
This latest disagreement could mean the end of the road for the band.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: strong control or discipline
examples: Those children need a firm hand to make them behave.

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: completely
examples: What I said was not true, but he fell for it (= believed it) hook, line and sinker.

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: in a position that forms a straight line with something
examples: An eclipse happens when the earth and moon are in line with the sun.

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: likely to get something
examples: She is in line for promotion.

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: while doing a job
examples: A policeman was injured in the line of duty yesterday.

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: similar to something or so that one thing is closely connected with another
examples: Annual pay increases will be in line with inflation.

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: to tell somebody clearly what you think, especially when they will not like what you say
examples: The manager laid it on the line—some people would have to lose their jobs.

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: (to establish) a clear limit to what you will do or accept
examples: It’s time to draw a line in the sand and stop allowing workplace bullying to continue.

definitions.label: Meaning 54
definitions.definition: (to choose, etc.) the easiest way of doing something

definitions.label: Meaning 55
definitions.definition: at risk
examples: If we don't make a profit, my job is on the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 56
definitions.definition: not forming a straight line

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: different from something
examples: London prices are way out of line with the rest of the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: behaving in a way that is not acceptable or right

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that people think is not acceptable
examples: She realized she had overstepped the mark and quickly apologized.

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: to tell somebody a story or make an excuse that is not true

definitions.label: Meaning 61
definitions.definition: to look for or discover a meaning in something that is not openly stated
examples: Reading between the lines, I think Clare needs money.

definitions.label: Meaning 62
definitions.definition: to sign a document to show that you have agreed to buy something or do something
examples: Just sign on the dotted line and the car is yours.

definitions.label: Meaning 63
definitions.definition: to behave badly or break the rules
examples: His boss warned him that if he stepped out of line once more he would be fired.

definitions.label: Meaning 64
definitions.definition: to say or do what somebody in authority tells you to say or do, even if you do not share the same opinions, etc.
examples: One or two of them refused to toe the line.
MPs rarely fail to toe the party line.

definitions.label: Meaning 65
definitions.definition: to be in a difficult or dangerous situation where you could easily make a mistake
examples: He was walking a fine line between being funny and being rude.
She often seems to tread a thin line between success and failure.

definitions.definition: connected with the income that a company receives and the costs it has to pay in its daily business, which affect the profit it makes
examples: COMPARE below the line (1)
All these costs are above the line and directly hit profits.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: connected with advertising in the mass media
examples: COMPARE below the line (2)
They planned an advertising campaign with both above-the-line and social media components.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: at some point during an activity or a process
examples: Somewhere along the line a large amount of money went missing.
We'll make a decision on that further down the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: in the way that is mentioned
examples: The new system will operate along the same lines as the old one.
They voted along class lines.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: similar to the way or thing that is mentioned
examples: Those aren't his exact words, but he said something along those lines.
The hotel was built along the lines of a French chateau.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: used to say that people or groups have shown which side they intend to support in an argument or contest that is going to begin

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to be working or functioning
examples: SEE ALSO online
The new working methods will come on line in June.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to be in a position where you can be shot at
examples: attempts to prevent civilians from being in the firing line

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to be in a position where people can criticize or blame you
examples: The employment secretary found himself in the firing line over recent job cuts.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: connected with unusual costs or income that a company pays or receives, that are not part of its daily business and are taken away or added after calculating profits
examples: COMPARE above the line (1)
There was a £4 million extraordinary charge below the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: connected with advertising by means of direct mail, email, social media, events, etc.
examples: COMPARE above the line (2)
We are planning social networking, digital marketing and below-the-line activities across the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: connected with a section at the end of an online article or blog post where readers can put comments
examples: There were numerous comments below the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: to behave or make somebody/something behave in the same way as other people or how they should behave
examples: The other members of the board must be brought into line.
The actions of investors do not always fall into line with financial theory.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: to do something that is not considered to be acceptable behaviour
examples: He crossed the line by making details of their very private conversation public.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to go to the front of a line of people without waiting for your turn
examples: Somebody cut in line in front of me.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: to say that something is finished and not worth discussing any more

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: (to reach) the point at which something can no longer continue in the same way
examples: A defeat in the second round marked the end of the line for last year's champion.
The loss of this contract could signal the end of the line for the shipyard.
This latest disagreement could mean the end of the road for the band.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: strong control or discipline
examples: Those children need a firm hand to make them behave.

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: completely
examples: What I said was not true, but he fell for it (= believed it) hook, line and sinker.

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: in a position that forms a straight line with something
examples: An eclipse happens when the earth and moon are in line with the sun.

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: likely to get something
examples: She is in line for promotion.

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: while doing a job
examples: A policeman was injured in the line of duty yesterday.

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: similar to something or so that one thing is closely connected with another
examples: Annual pay increases will be in line with inflation.

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: to tell somebody clearly what you think, especially when they will not like what you say
examples: The manager laid it on the line—some people would have to lose their jobs.

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: (to establish) a clear limit to what you will do or accept
examples: It’s time to draw a line in the sand and stop allowing workplace bullying to continue.

definitions.label: Meaning 54
definitions.definition: (to choose, etc.) the easiest way of doing something

definitions.label: Meaning 55
definitions.definition: at risk
examples: If we don't make a profit, my job is on the line.

definitions.label: Meaning 56
definitions.definition: not forming a straight line

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: different from something
examples: London prices are way out of line with the rest of the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: behaving in a way that is not acceptable or right

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that people think is not acceptable
examples: She realized she had overstepped the mark and quickly apologized.

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: to tell somebody a story or make an excuse that is not true

definitions.label: Meaning 61
definitions.definition: to look for or discover a meaning in something that is not openly stated
examples: Reading between the lines, I think Clare needs money.

definitions.label: Meaning 62
definitions.definition: to sign a document to show that you have agreed to buy something or do something
examples: Just sign on the dotted line and the car is yours.

definitions.label: Meaning 63
definitions.definition: to behave badly or break the rules
examples: His boss warned him that if he stepped out of line once more he would be fired.

definitions.label: Meaning 64
definitions.definition: to say or do what somebody in authority tells you to say or do, even if you do not share the same opinions, etc.
examples: One or two of them refused to toe the line.
MPs rarely fail to toe the party line.

definitions.label: Meaning 65
definitions.definition: to be in a difficult or dangerous situation where you could easily make a mistake
examples: He was walking a fine line between being funny and being rude.
She often seems to tread a thin line between success and failure.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to stand in a line or row; to form a queue
examples: Line up, children!
Cars lined up waiting to board the ship.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to arrange people or things in a straight line or row
examples: The suspects were lined up against the wall.
He lined the bottles up along the shelf.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to arrange for an event or activity to happen, or arrange for somebody to be available to do something
examples: Mark had a job lined up when he left college.
I've got a lot lined up this week (= I'm very busy).
She's lined up a live band for the party.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to move one thing into a correct position in relation to another thing
examples: To get good TV reception, the dish must be accurately lined up with the satellite.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: of or in lines
examples: In his art he broke the laws of scientific linear perspective.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: going from one thing to another in a single series of stages
examples: OPPOSITE non-linear
Students do not always progress in a linear fashion.
The author abandons the conventions of linear narrative and normal chronology.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: of length
examples: linear measurement (= for example metres, feet, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: able to be represented by a straight line on a graph
examples: linear equations

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: broadcast and watched at regular times according to a schedule
examples: COMPARE on-demand
People are watching linear TV much less these days, preferring on-demand platforms like Netflix.
the simplicity of traditional linear channel programming

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to continue to exist for longer than expected
examples: The faint smell of her perfume lingered in the room.
The civil war lingered on well into the 1930s.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stay somewhere for longer because you do not want to leave; to spend a long time doing something
examples: She lingered for a few minutes to talk to Nick.
We lingered over breakfast on the terrace.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to continue to look at somebody/something or think about something for longer than usual
examples: His eyes lingered on the diamond ring on her finger.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to stay alive but become weaker
examples: He lingered on for several months after the heart attack.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a connection between two or more people or things
examples: SEE ALSO missing link
Police suspect there may be a link between the two murders.
There is evidence for a strong causal link between exposure to sun and skin cancer.
to establish/find a link
These photographs are a direct link with the past.
Many of them had no previous links to terrorism.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a relationship between two or more people, countries or organizations
examples: to establish trade links with Asia
Producers are forging direct links with consumers.
The department tries to maintain close links with industry.
Social workers provide a vital link between hospital and community.
The agreement will strengthen the links between the two countries.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a means of travelling or communicating between two places
examples: a high-speed rail link
a video link
The canal was an important transport link between England and Wales.
The driver has a radio link to base.
We're trying to establish a link via satellite.
The speech was broadcast via a satellite link.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a place in an electronic document that is connected to another electronic document or to another part of the same document
examples: You can find all the details by clicking this link.
Follow the links to watch our exclusive trailer.
I've posted a link to the article, for those who are interested.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: each ring of a chain
examples: SEE ALSO cufflink
The chain was too long so I removed a few of the links.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a chain of long thin sausages; an individual long thin sausage
examples: You need four Italian sausage links.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: one of the stages in a process or a line of argument
examples: Food production, processing and marketing are different links in the chain from farmer to consumer.
Death is the last link in the chain.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the point at which a system or an organization is most likely to fail
examples: She went straight for the one weak link in the chain of his argument.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large, powerful animal of the cat family that hunts in groups and lives in parts of Africa and southern Asia. Lions have yellow-brown fur and the male has a mane (= long, thick hair round its neck).
examples: COMPARE lioness
The lion shook its mane and roared.
a pride of lions (= a group of them)
Over the past two months, 13 lions have been killed by poachers.
He had once been chased and almost eaten by a lion.
Young Masai men gather for traditional lion hunts.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a difficult situation in which you have to face a person or people who are unfriendly or aggressive towards you

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the largest or best part of something when it is divided

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to go to see an important or powerful person to tell them that you disagree with them, that you want something, etc.Word Origin
examples: Middle English: from Anglo-Norman French liun, from Latin leo, leon-, from Greek leōn, leont-.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: either of the two soft edges at the opening to the mouth
examples: SEE ALSO cleft lip
The assistant pursed her lips.
your upper/lower/top/bottom lip
She kissed him on the lips.
He raised the bottle to his lips and took a large swig from it.
She always has a cigarette dangling from her lips.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the type of lips mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO tight-lipped
thin-lipped
thick-lipped

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the edge of a container or a hollow place in the ground
examples: SYNONYM rim
He ran his finger around the lip of the cup.
Lava bubbled a few feet below the lip of the crater.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: words spoken to somebody that are rude and show a lack of respect for that person
examples: SYNONYM cheek
Don't let him give you any lip!
I’ve just about had enough of your lip!

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to stop yourself from saying something or from showing an emotion
examples: I bit my lip and forced myself to be calm.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to move your tongue over your lips, especially before eating something good

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to show that you are excited about something and want it to happen soon
examples: They were licking their lips at the thought of clinching the deal.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that you will not repeat somebody’s secret to other people

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: if words do not pass your lips, you say nothing

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: if food or drink does not pass your lips, you eat or drink nothing

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: if something is on everyone’s lips, they are all talking about it

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to listen carefully to what you are saying
examples: Read my lips: no new taxes (= I promise there will be no new taxes).

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to keep calm and hide your feelings when you are in pain or in a difficult situation
examples: He was taught to keep a stiff upper lip and never to cry in public.
Their reaction contrasts sharply with the stiff upper lip of the English.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: nothing is completely certain until it really happens because things can easily go wrongWord Origin
examples: Old English lippa, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch lip and German Lippe, from an Indo-European root shared by Latin labia, labra ‘lips’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a substance that flows freely and is not a solid or a gas, for example water or oil
examples: SEE ALSO washing-up liquid
She poured the dark brown liquid down the sink.
restrictions on passengers carrying liquids in their hand luggage
a flammable liquid
the transition from liquid to vapour

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a series of names, items, figures, etc., especially when they are written or printed
examples: SEE ALSO A-list
The guest list includes numerous celebrities.
Is your name on the list?
I'll add you to the email list.
Her novel shot to the top of the bestseller list.
He plays drums, guitar, piano, flute, the list goes on.
a list of names/candidates/questions
I made a list of things to do.
They compiled a list of all the items they'd need.
to draw up a list
Going to the bank tops my list of priorities today.
Having to wait hours came high on the list of complaints.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of a ship leaning to one side
examples: The ship had a noticeable list to the starboard side.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be so ill that you may die; to no longer be very illWord Origin
examples: noun sense 1 Middle English (originally referring to the edge put on fabric to stop it unravelling): from Old English liste ‘border’, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch lijst and German Leiste. The current senses are late 16th cent., from French liste, of Germanic origin. noun sense 2 early 17th cent.: of unknown origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to pay attention to somebody/something that you can hear
examples: Listen! What's that noise? Can you hear it?
Sorry, I wasn't really listening.
He had been listening at the door.
to listen to music/the radio
to listen to a song/an album
I listened carefully to her story.
He was listening intently to what she was saying.
You haven’t been listening to a word I’ve said!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to take notice of what you are going to say
examples: Listen, there's something I have to tell you.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to take notice of what somebody says to you so that you follow their advice or believe them
examples: I tried to warn her, but she wouldn't listen.
None of this would have happened if you'd listened to me.
The government is willing to listen to any concerns that people have.
Why won't you listen to reason?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who listens
examples: a good listener (= somebody who you can rely on to listen with attention or sympathy)
a sympathetic/willing listener
an attentive listener

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person listening to a radio programme or podcast
examples: radio listeners
Regular listeners will know this is the Year of Czech Music.
Listeners to Radio 4 have plenty to look forward to this week.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a list, especially an official or published list of people or things, often arranged in alphabetical order
examples: a comprehensive listing of all airlines

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: information online or in a newspaper or magazine about what films, plays, etc. are being shown in a particular town or city
examples: a listings website/magazine

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a position or an item on a list
examples: The company is seeking a stock exchange listing (= for trading shares).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the ability to read and write
examples: OPPOSITE illiteracy
a campaign to promote adult literacy
basic literacy skills
Most of the students here need help with literacy and numeracy.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: knowledge or skills in a specific area
examples: SEE ALSO computer literacy
financial/health literacy
We’re looking to hire an assistant with a high level of digital literacy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a literal way
examples: SYNONYM exactly
The word ‘planet’ literally means ‘wandering body’.
When I told you to ‘get lost’ I didn't expect to be taken literally.
Idioms usually cannot be translated literally into another language.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the truth of something that may seem surprising
examples: There are literally hundreds of prizes to win.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a word or phrase, even if it is not actually true in a literal sense
examples: I literally jumped out of my skin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with literature
examples: literary criticism/theory

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: suitable for or typical of a work of literature
examples: It was Chaucer who really turned English into a literary language.
She was one of the great literary figures of her age.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: liking literature very much; studying or writing literature
examples: a literary man

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: pieces of writing that are valued as works of art, especially novels, plays and poems (in contrast to technical books and newspapers, magazines, etc.)
examples: SEE ALSO comparative literature
English/American/French literature
children's literature
great works of literature
For most people, the desire to study literature begins with a love of reading.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: pieces of writing or printed information on a particular subject
examples: sales literature
a review of the scientific literature on the topic
I've read all the available literature on keeping rabbits.
I picked up some literature about pensions.
Chapter 1 reviews the literature and discusses the main types of sources available.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring volume, equal to 1.76 British pints or 2.11 American pints
examples: 3 litres of water
a litre bottle of wine
a car with a 3.5 litre engine

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: small pieces of rubbish such as paper, cans and bottles, that people have left lying in a public place
examples: There will be fines for people who drop litter.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a number of things that are lying in an untidy way
examples: The floor was covered with a litter of newspapers, clothes and empty cups.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a dry substance that is put in a shallow open box for pets, especially cats, to use as a toilet when they are indoors
examples: cat litter
kitty litter
a litter tray
a litter box

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a number of baby animals that one mother gives birth to at the same time
examples: a litter of puppies
the runt (= the smallest and weakest baby) of the litter
‘Chief’ was born six years ago, one of a litter of 11.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the substance, especially straw, that is used for farm animals to sleep on

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a kind of chair or bed that was used in the past for carrying important peopleWord Origin
examples: Middle English (originally referring to a structure used to carry people carried on men's shoulders or by animals): from Old French litiere, from medieval Latin lectaria, from Latin lectus ‘bed’. Senses 1 and 2 date from the mid 18th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not big; small; smaller than others
examples: a little house
a little group of tourists
a little old lady
We passed through several nice little towns.
It was a tiny little room.
‘Which do you want?’ ‘I'll take the little one.’
She gave a little laugh.
We should manage, with a little bit of luck.
Here's a little something (= a small present) for your birthday.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: young
examples: a little boy/girl
He's just a little kid.
my little brother/sister (= younger brother/sister)
The little ones were already in bed.
cute little baby animals
I lived in America when I was little.
He's still very little and doesn't understand yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: short
examples: A little while later the phone rang.
Shall we walk a little way?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used after an adjective to show approval, sympathy or dislike, especially in a patronizing way (= one that suggests that you think you are better than somebody)
examples: The poor little thing! It's lost its mother.
What a nasty little man!
She's a good little worker.
He'd become quite the little gentleman.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not important; not serious
examples: I can't remember every little detail.
Sometimes it's the little things that count.
You soon get used to the little difficulties.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: something large and successful often begins in a very small way

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody told you something but you do not want to say who it was

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: it is not surprising
examples: It is little wonder (that) she was so upset.
No wonder you're tired—you've been walking for hours.
No wonder you're still single—you never go out!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that is being carried (usually in large amounts) by a person, vehicle, etc.
examples: The trucks waited at the warehouse to pick up their loads.
The women came down the hill with their loads of firewood.
These backpacks are designed to carry a heavy load.
A lorry shed its load (= accidentally dropped its load) on the motorway.
The company's debt load could drag it into bankruptcy.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the total amount of something that something can carry or contain
examples: a busload of tourists
They ordered three truckloads of sand.
He put half a load of washing in the machine.
The plane took off with a full load.
Maximum load, including passengers, is 800 pounds.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the amount of weight that is pressing down on something
examples: a load-bearing wall
Modern backpacks spread the load over a wider area.
The table creaked under its heavy load.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a large number or amount of people or things; plenty
examples: She's got loads of friends.
He wrote loads and loads of letters to people.
Uncle Jim brought a whole load of presents for the kids.
We saw a load of houses before we bought this one.
They all had loads of fun at the park.
In my job I get the chance to meet loads of different people.
There's loads to do today.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something is wrong, stupid, bad, etc.
examples: You're talking a load of rubbish.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an amount of work that a person or machine has to do
examples: SEE ALSO caseload
Teaching loads have increased in all types of school.
Extra warmth from sunlight can put an additional load on the air-conditioning system.
We're trying to spread the load by employing more staff.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a feeling of responsibility or worry that is difficult to deal with
examples: SYNONYM burden
She thought she would not be able to bear the load of bringing up her family alone.
Knowing that they had arrived safely took a load off my mind.
Many companies are burdened by high debt loads.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the amount of electrical power that is being supplied at a particular time

definitions.definition: to find the exact position of somebody/something
examples: The mechanic located the fault immediately.
Rescue planes are trying to locate the missing sailors.
I twisted my head to either side, attempting to immediately locate and identify the horrible stench.
We tried to locate the source of the sound.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to put or build something in a particular place
examples: They located their headquarters in Swindon.
Locating offices directly next to the labs is preferred by most researchers.

a small, centrally located hotel

the country's strategic geographical/geographic location

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: A mountain in the Rockies became the location for a film about Everest.
