the exotic locations they filmed in
He went to the restaurant to scout a location for his next film.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of finding the position of somebody/something
examples: Location of a suitable site may take some time.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: A domain name is the location of your website on the internet.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to fasten something with a lock; to be fastened with a lock
examples: OPPOSITE unlock (1)
Did you lock the door?
David locked the car and slipped the key into his pocket.
The gates are locked at 6 o'clock.
a locked cabinet
This suitcase doesn't lock.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to put something in a safe place and lock it
examples: She locked her passport and money in the safe.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to become or make something become fixed in one position and unable to move
examples: The brakes locked and the car skidded.
He locked his helmet into position with a click.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be involved in a difficult situation, an argument, etc.
examples: The two sides are locked into a bitter dispute.
She felt locked in a loveless marriage.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be held very tightly by somebody
examples: They were locked in a passionate embrace.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: These files are locked to protect confidentiality.
My phone is locked and I've forgotten the password.
Make sure you lock your screen if you leave your desk.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to get involved in an argument with somebody
examples: The company has locked horns with the unions over proposed pay cuts.

examples: Linking the proposals in a single package did have a certain logic.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the science of thinking about or explaining the reason for something using formal methods
examples: the rules of logic

definitions.definition: seeming natural, reasonable or sensible

a logical thing to do in the circumstances
What 's the next logical step?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: following or able to follow the rules of logic in which ideas or facts are based on other true ideas or facts
examples: a logical argument

definitions.definition: a printed design or symbol that a company or an organization uses as its special sign
examples: All over the world there are red and white paper cups bearing the company logo.

examples: She lives alone and often feels lonely.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: all those lonely nights at home watching TV
a lonely childhood

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: SYNONYM isolated

It's a long way away.
He had long, thin fingers.
a lush meadow of long grass

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used for asking or talking about particular lengths or distances
examples: How long is the River Nile?
The table is six feet long.
The report is only three pages long.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: lasting or taking a great amount of time or more time than usual
examples: OPPOSITE short

There was a long silence before she spoke.
I like it now the days are getting longer (= it stays light for more time each day).
a long book/film/list (= taking a lot of time to read/watch/deal with)
Nurses have to work long hours (= for more hours in the day than is usual).

to have a long life/career

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used for asking or talking about particular periods of time
examples: SEE ALSO age-long

I think it's only three weeks long.
How long a stay did you have in mind?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: seeming to last or take more time than it really does because, for example, you are very busy or not happy
examples: OPPOSITE short
I'm tired. It's been a long day.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: covering all or most of your legs or arms
examples: OPPOSITE short
She usually wears long skirts.
a long-sleeved shirt

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: having a lot of a particular quality
examples: The government is long on ideas but short on performance.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a long vowel is pronounced for a longer time than other vowels
examples: OPPOSITE short
Compare the long vowel in ‘beat’ and the short vowel in ‘bit’.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: very long
examples: There's a list of repairs as long as your arm.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: not longer than the particular time given
examples: It will take an hour at the longest.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: after a long time
examples: SYNONYM finally
At long last his prayers had been answered.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: by a great amount
examples: He was the best by a long way.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to have known each other for a long time
examples: We go back a long way, he and I.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to last a long time
examples: She seems to make her money go a long way.
A small amount of this paint goes a long way (= covers a large area).
I find that a little of Jerry's company can go a long way (= I quickly get tired of being with him).

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to help very much/a little in achieving something
examples: The new law goes a long way towards solving the problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to have made a lot of progress
examples: We've come a long way since the early days of the project.
The study of genes has come a long way in recent years.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to need to make a lot of progress before you can achieve something
examples: She still has a long way to go before she's fully fit.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that there is no definite answer to a question
examples: ‘How long will it take?’ ‘How long's a piece of string?’

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: relating to a longer period in the future
examples: This measure inevitably means higher taxes in the long run.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used to describe what will happen a long, short, etc. time in the future
examples: Such a development seems unlikely, at least in the short term (= it will not happen for quite a long time).
In the longer term, children of depressed mothers are more likely to suffer from childhood depression.
In the long term, our efforts will pay off.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: it makes no real difference which of two possible choices you make

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to say that the reasons for something are complicated and you would prefer not to give all the details

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to reject something or treat it as not important; to stop dealing with a problem
examples: He tends to deal with disputes by kicking them into the long grass.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used when you are telling somebody the essential facts about something or what effect it will have, without explaining all the details

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: the power and/or authority of something
examples: There is no escape from the long arm of the law.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: (to have) an unhappy or disappointed expression
examples: He took one look at her long face and said ‘What’s wrong?’
The news for the company isn't good, judging from the long faces in the boardroom.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: old or too old

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: an attempt or a guess that is not likely to be successful but is worth trying
examples: It's a long shot, but it just might work.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: used when you are saying that you will get to the point of what you are saying quickly, without including all the details
examples: To cut a long story short, we didn’t get home until 3 in the morning!
Anyway, long story short: we had this argument and I haven't seen him since.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: used to say hello to somebody you have not seen for a long time

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: not nearly; not at all
examples: It's not over yet—not by a long chalk.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to consider a problem or possibility very carefully and without hurrying
examples: We need to take a long, hard look at all the options.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to consider what is likely to happen or be important over a long period of time rather than only considering the present situation
examples: As pension funds are investing for members’ retirements, they can take the long view.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: measuring or covering a great length or distance, or a greater length or distance than usual
examples: OPPOSITE short
She had long dark hair.
He walked down the long corridor.
It was the world's longest bridge.
a long journey/walk/drive/flight
We're a long way from anywhere here.
It's a long way away.
He had long, thin fingers.
a lush meadow of long grass

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used for asking or talking about particular lengths or distances
examples: How long is the River Nile?
The table is six feet long.
The report is only three pages long.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: lasting or taking a great amount of time or more time than usual
examples: OPPOSITE short
He’s been ill (for) a long time.
There was a long silence before she spoke.
I like it now the days are getting longer (= it stays light for more time each day).
a long book/film/list (= taking a lot of time to read/watch/deal with)
Nurses have to work long hours (= for more hours in the day than is usual).
He stared at them for the longest time (= for a very long time) before answering.
Chicago has a long history of country music.
to have a long life/career

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used for asking or talking about particular periods of time
examples: SEE ALSO age-long
How long is the course?
I think it's only three weeks long.
How long a stay did you have in mind?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: seeming to last or take more time than it really does because, for example, you are very busy or not happy
examples: OPPOSITE short
I'm tired. It's been a long day.
We were married for ten long years.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: covering all or most of your legs or arms
examples: OPPOSITE short
She usually wears long skirts.
a long-sleeved shirt

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: having a lot of a particular quality
examples: The government is long on ideas but short on performance.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a long vowel is pronounced for a longer time than other vowels
examples: OPPOSITE short
Compare the long vowel in ‘beat’ and the short vowel in ‘bit’.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: very long
examples: There's a list of repairs as long as your arm.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: not longer than the particular time given
examples: It will take an hour at the longest.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: after a long time
examples: SYNONYM finally
At long last his prayers had been answered.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: by a great amount
examples: He was the best by a long way.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to have known each other for a long time
examples: We go back a long way, he and I.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to last a long time
examples: She seems to make her money go a long way.
A small amount of this paint goes a long way (= covers a large area).
I find that a little of Jerry's company can go a long way (= I quickly get tired of being with him).

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to help very much/a little in achieving something
examples: The new law goes a long way towards solving the problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to have made a lot of progress
examples: We've come a long way since the early days of the project.
The study of genes has come a long way in recent years.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to need to make a lot of progress before you can achieve something
examples: She still has a long way to go before she's fully fit.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that there is no definite answer to a question
examples: ‘How long will it take?’ ‘How long's a piece of string?’

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: relating to a longer period in the future
examples: This measure inevitably means higher taxes in the long run.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used to describe what will happen a long, short, etc. time in the future
examples: Such a development seems unlikely, at least in the short term (= it will not happen for quite a long time).
In the longer term, children of depressed mothers are more likely to suffer from childhood depression.
In the long term, our efforts will pay off.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: it makes no real difference which of two possible choices you make

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to say that the reasons for something are complicated and you would prefer not to give all the details

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to reject something or treat it as not important; to stop dealing with a problem
examples: He tends to deal with disputes by kicking them into the long grass.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used when you are telling somebody the essential facts about something or what effect it will have, without explaining all the details

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: the power and/or authority of something
examples: There is no escape from the long arm of the law.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: (to have) an unhappy or disappointed expression
examples: He took one look at her long face and said ‘What’s wrong?’
The news for the company isn't good, judging from the long faces in the boardroom.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: old or too old

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: an attempt or a guess that is not likely to be successful but is worth trying
examples: It's a long shot, but it just might work.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: used when you are saying that you will get to the point of what you are saying quickly, without including all the details
examples: To cut a long story short, we didn’t get home until 3 in the morning!
Anyway, long story short: we had this argument and I haven't seen him since.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: used to say hello to somebody you have not seen for a long time

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: not nearly; not at all
examples: It's not over yet—not by a long chalk.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to consider a problem or possibility very carefully and without hurrying
examples: We need to take a long, hard look at all the options.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to consider what is likely to happen or be important over a long period of time rather than only considering the present situation
examples: As pension funds are investing for members’ retirements, they can take the long view.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that has existed or lasted for a long time
examples: a long-standing relationship
Long-standing grievances were aired at the meeting.
The country’s long-standing relationship with the US was finally under strain.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: over a long period of time
examples: to benefit/affect somebody long-term
It is unclear if this shift will continue long-term.
We need to think long-term (= think about what will happen over a long period of time) if we want to get any serious results.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: over a long period of time
examples: to benefit/affect somebody long-term
It is unclear if this shift will continue long-term.
We need to think long-term (= think about what will happen over a long period of time) if we want to get any serious results.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having been the particular thing mentioned for a long time
examples: his long-time colleague

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to turn your eyes in a particular direction
examples: SEE ALSO forward-looking
Look closely and tell me what you see.
If you look carefully you can just see our house from here.
‘Has the mail come yet?’ ‘I'll look and see.’
Look! I'm sure that's Jennifer Lawrence!
Don't look now, but there's someone staring at you!
She looked at me and smiled.
I got up and looked out of the window.
She looked across to the other side of the room.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to try to find somebody/something
examples: Where have you been? We've been looking for you.
Are you still looking for a job?
We’re looking for someone with experience for this post.
They are always looking for ways to save money.
I can't find my book—I've looked everywhere.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to pay attention to something
examples: Look at the time! We're going to be late.
Can't you look where you're going?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to seem; to appear
examples: SEE ALSO good-looking
You look great!
The garden looks nice.
Don't worry—it looks worse than it is.
The film looks likely to offend many people.
That book looks interesting.
That looks like an interesting book.
It doesn't look like fun to me.
You made me look a complete fool!
That looks an interesting book.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have a particular appearance
examples: That photograph doesn't look like her at all.
‘What does your cousin look like?’ ‘He's tall and thin with brown hair.’
You look as though you slept badly.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to seem likely to happen or be true
examples: It looks like rain (= it looks as if it's going to rain).
It doesn't look as if we'll be moving after all.
It looks to me as though the company is in real trouble.
They don’t look like they’re trying to win.
It looks to me like they have a plan.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to face a particular direction
examples: The house looks east.
The hotel looks out over the harbour.
The kitchen looks onto the garden.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used in a shop to say that you are not ready to buy something
examples: ‘Can I help you?’ ‘I'm just looking, thank you.’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to try to find ways of doing something
examples: The government is looking to reduce inflation.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be considered bad behaviour or bad manners
examples: It looks bad not going to your own brother's wedding.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to show that something bad might happen
examples: He's had another heart attack; things are looking bad for him, I'm afraid.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to show success or that something good might happen
examples: This year's sales figures are looking good.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to protest about something
examples: Now look here, it wasn't my fault.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to give an example that proves what you are saying or makes it clearer
examples: Look how lazy we've become.
Be careful climbing that ladder. Look what happened last time.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to say that something is exactly what somebody needs and so they do not need to consider any other options
examples: Those looking for an enjoyable evening need look no further than the hotel's nightclub.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to look at somebody in a careful or critical way

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to (not) have your normal healthy appearance
examples: You're not looking yourself today (= you look tired or ill/sick).

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to become more and more successful
examples: Her first novel was published in 2007 and since then she hasn't looked back.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: not attractive

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: judging by the appearance of somebody/something
examples: To look at him you'd never think he was nearly fifty.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to appear as a large shape that is not clear, especially in a frightening way
examples: A dark shape loomed up ahead of us.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to appear serious and and likely to happen soon
examples: There was a crisis looming.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be frightening and make you worried because something seems hard to avoid
examples: The prospect of war loomed large.
The issue looms large in political campaigns nationwide.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a shape like a curve or circle made by a line curving right round
examples: The road went in a huge loop around the lake.
Duclair is a small town on a loop of the River Seine.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of rope, wire, etc. in the shape of a curve or circle
examples: He tied a loop of rope around his arm.
Make a loop in the string.
a belt loop (= on trousers, etc. for holding a belt in place)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a long, narrow piece of film or tape on which the pictures and sound are repeated continuously
examples: The film is on a loop.
His mind kept turning in an endless loop.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a set of instructions that is repeated again and again until a particular condition is satisfied

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a complete circuit for electrical current

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a railway line or road that leaves the main track or road and then joins it again

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the business centre of the US city of Chicago

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: part of a group of people that is dealing with something important; not part of this group
examples: A lot of people want to be in the loop on this operation.
Lawton had gradually been cut out of the loop on legal reviews.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to shock or surprise somebody
examples: The result of the election knocked most people for a loop.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not securely fixed where it should be; able to become separated from something
examples: a loose button/tooth
Check that the plug has not come loose.
One of the bricks feels slightly loose.
Darien shook his arm loose.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not tied together; not held in position by anything or contained in anything
examples: She usually wears her hair loose.
She tucked a loose strand of hair behind her ear.
The potatoes were sold loose, not in bags.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: free to move around without control; not tied up or shut in somewhere
examples: The sheep had got out and were loose on the road.
The horse had broken loose (= escaped) from its tether.
The animals ran loose without collars or leashes.
During the night, somebody had cut the boat loose from its moorings.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not fitting closely
examples: OPPOSITE tight
On long flights, wear loose clothing and comfortable shoes.
a loose shirt

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not tightly packed together; not solid or hard
examples: loose soil
a fabric with a loose weave

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not strictly organized or managed
examples: a loose alliance/coalition/federation
a loose association of artists, writers and composers

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not exact; not very careful
examples: This is only a loose translation as I am not fluent in Japanese.
This book is an antidote for much of the loose thinking in the world of today.
The committees work within fairly loose guidelines.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: having or involving an attitude to sexual relationships that people consider to be morally wrong
examples: a young man of loose morals

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: not in any player’s control
examples: He pounced on a loose ball.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: having too much liquid in it
examples: a baby with loose bowel movements

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: suddenly there was a lot of noise, arguing, fighting, etc.
examples: There was a loud bang and then all hell broke loose.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to separate yourself or somebody/something from a group of people or their influence, etc.
examples: The organization broke loose from its sponsors.
He cut himself loose from his family.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to remain calm; to not worry
examples: It's OK—hang loose and stay cool.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to talk too much, especially about things that are private

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be slightly strange in your behaviour

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to do something or to happen in a way that no one controls
examples: Teenagers need a place to let loose.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to make a noise or remark, especially in a loud or sudden way
examples: She let loose a stream of abuse.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to free somebody/something from whatever holds them/it in place
examples: She let her hair loose and it fell around her shoulders.
Who's let the dog loose?

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to give somebody complete freedom to do what they want in a place or situation
examples: He was at last let loose in the kitchen.
A team of professionals were let loose on the project.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to treat somebody/something in a way that shows that you feel no responsibility or respect for themWord Origin
examples: Middle English loos ‘free from bonds’, from Old Norse lauss, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch and German los.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: (in the UK) a man of high rank in the nobility (= people of high social class), or somebody who has been given the title ‘lord’ as an honour
examples: COMPARE lady
She's married to a lord.
The head of the successful construction group became a lord in 1984.
They entered a huge hall filled with lords and ladies.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: (in the UK) the title used by a lord
examples: Lord Beaverbrook
He was made a peer and took the title Lord Northcliffe.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a title used for some high official positions in the UK
examples: SEE ALSO Sea Lord
the Lord Chancellor
the Lord Mayor
Lord Justice Slade

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (in the UK) a title of respect used when speaking to a judge, bishop or some male members of the nobility (= people of high social class)
examples: COMPARE lady

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a powerful man in medieval Europe, who owned a lot of land and property
examples: SEE ALSO drug lord
a feudal lord
the lord of the manor

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a title used to refer to God or Christ
examples: Love the Lord with all your heart.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a title used to refer to Christ

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: (in the UK) the part of Parliament whose members are not elected by the people of the country
examples: SEE ALSO the Law Lords
The Lords has/have not yet reached a decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the building where members of the House of Lords meet

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: very drunk

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to show that you are surprised, annoyed or worried about something
examples: Good Lord, what have you done to your hair!

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to emphasize what you are saying
examples: Lord knows, I tried to teach her.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not know the answer to something
examples: ‘Why did she say that?’ ‘Lord knows!’

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: any particular year after the birth of ChristWord Origin
examples: Old English hlāford, from hlāfweard ‘bread-keeper’, from a Germanic base (see loaf (noun), ward). Compare with lady.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large vehicle for carrying heavy loads by road
examples: a lorry driver
a lorry load of frozen fish
Emergency food supplies were brought in by lorry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: goods that fell off the back of a lorry were probably stolen. People say or accept that they came ‘off the back of a lorry’ to avoid saying or asking where they really came from.Word Origin
examples: mid 19th cent.: perhaps from the given name Laurie.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be unable to find something/somebody
examples: SYNONYM mislay
I've lost my keys.
The tickets seem to have got lost.
She lost her husband in the crowd.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to have something/somebody taken away from you, especially as a result of an accident, dying, etc.
examples: She lost a leg in a car crash.
Some families lost everything (= all they owned) in the flood.
She lost her baby (= had a miscarriage) three months into the pregnancy.
They lost both their sons (= they were killed) in the war.
The ship was lost at sea (= it sank).
Many people lost their lives (= were killed).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have to give up something; to fail to keep something/somebody
examples: He's lost his job.
You will lose your deposit if you cancel the order.
Sit down or you'll lose your seat.
The government has lost control of the city.
We cannot afford to lose any more senior members of staff.
The average business loses 20 per cent of its customers every year.
You risk losing your house if you do not keep up the payments.
The company has lost a lot of business to its competitors.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to no longer have something, or have less of something than you had before, especially as a result of getting older
examples: to lose your hair/teeth
to lose your sight/eyesight/hearing/memory
There's new hope for people trying to lose weight.
I've lost ten pounds since I started this diet.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have less and less of a quality or ability, especially until you no longer have any of it
examples: She seemed to have lost interest in food.
to lose faith/confidence
He lost his nerve at the last minute.
At that moment he lost his balance and fell.
The train was losing speed.
He never lost the ability to make people laugh.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be defeated; to fail to win a competition, a court case, an argument, etc.; to cause somebody to be defeated
examples: So far they haven't lost a game.
to lose a race/an election/a battle/a war
We lost to a stronger team.
He lost by less than 100 votes.
We lost the game by three points.
They lost on penalties to (= because they scored fewer penalties than) Spain.
Many believe the incident lost them the election.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to fail to keep something you want or need, especially money; to cause somebody to fail to keep something
examples: The business is losing money.
Poetry always loses something in translation.
You have nothing to lose by telling the truth.
What do we lose by working with them?
We lost on that deal.
The company stands to lose financially if this deal falls through.
His carelessness lost him the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to fail to get, hear or understand something
examples: His words were lost (= could not be heard) in the applause.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be no longer understood by somebody
examples: I'm afraid you've lost me there.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to escape from somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM evade
We managed to lose our pursuers in the darkness.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to waste time or an opportunity
examples: We lost twenty minutes changing a tyre.
Hurry—there's no time to lose!
He lost no time in setting out for London.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if a watch or clock loses or loses time, it goes too slowly or becomes a particular amount of time behind the correct time
examples: OPPOSITE gain
This clock loses two minutes a day.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be unable to stop yourself from crying, laughing, etc.; to become crazy
examples: Then she just lost it and started screaming.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of no longer having something or as much of something; the process that leads to this
examples: I want to report the loss of a package.
Insure your instrument against loss or damage.
weight loss
hearing/memory loss
The closure of the factory will lead to a number of job losses.
When she died I was filled with a sense of loss.
He suffered a loss of confidence.
loss of earnings/income (= the money you do not earn because you are prevented from working)
The loss of her job was a terrible blow.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: money that has been lost by a business or an organization
examples: OPPOSITE profit
The company has announced net losses of $1.5 million.
The banks incurred huge losses.
We made a loss on (= lost money on) the deal.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the death of a person
examples: He is mourning the loss of his wife.
the tragic loss of a child
Enemy troops suffered heavy losses.
The drought caused widespread loss of life.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the disadvantage that is caused when somebody leaves, or when a useful or valuable object is taken away; a person who causes a disadvantage by leaving
examples: SEE ALSO dead loss
Her departure is a big loss to the school.
She will be a great loss to the company.
She wouldn't be able to attend the lecture, which was no great loss.
His death is a sad loss to all who knew him.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a failure to win a contest
examples: Brazil’s 2–1 loss to Argentina

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not knowing what to say or do
examples: His comments left me at a loss for words.
I'm at a loss what to do next.
We are at a loss to understand his actions.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in a way that loses you money
examples: We are now operating at a loss.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that if somebody chooses not to do something, they will not obtain a benefit they could have had
examples: If people can't appreciate how great this film is, it's their loss.
I can see you don't trust me. Well, that's your loss

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to stop doing something that is not successful before the situation becomes even worse
examples: I decided to cut my losses and move back to England.
He decided to cut his losses and sell the shares before they sank further.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the state of being less respected by other people or looking stupid because of something you have done
examples: Failure to pass the exams means a massive loss of face for the students and their parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: unable to find your way; not knowing where you are
examples: We always get lost in London.
We're completely lost.
We got lost in the woods.
I was tired, hungry and hopelessly lost.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that cannot be found or brought back
examples: SEE ALSO long-lost
I'm still looking for that lost file.
a lost cat/dog/pet
Your invitation must have got lost in the post.
Report all instances of lost or stolen cards immediately.
Along with flight delays, lost luggage is the most common cause for passenger complaint.
Without a form of backup, this data would be lost forever.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: that cannot be obtained; that cannot be found or created again
examples: Piracy is costing film studios millions in lost revenues.
The strike cost them thousands of pounds in lost business.
lost sales/profits/earnings
She's trying to recapture her lost youth.
a poignant and bittersweet tale of lost love
He regretted the lost (= wasted) opportunity to apologize to her.
the lost art of letter-writing

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: unable to deal successfully with a particular situation
examples: I felt so lost after my mother died.
We would be lost without your help.
He's a lost soul (= a person who does not seem to know what to do, and seems unhappy).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: unable to understand something because it is too complicated
examples: They spoke so quickly I just got lost.
Hang on a minute—I'm lost.
I was a little lost at first but quickly caught on to what was happening in this elaborate series.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: there is still some hope of making a bad situation better
examples: All is not lost—we still haven’t tried the banks for a loan.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be so surprised, confused, etc. that you do not know what to say

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be giving all your attention to something so that you do not notice what is happening around you
examples: to be lost in thought

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be not understood or noticed by somebody
examples: His jokes were completely lost on most of the students.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be giving all your attention to something so that you do not notice what is happening around you
examples: When he’s listening to music he’s lost to the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a rude way of telling somebody to go away, or of refusing something
examples: Tell him to get lost.
‘Lend us the car, won’t you?’ ‘Get lost!’

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to stop expecting to find somebody alive

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to do something quickly or very often because you wish you had started doing it sooner
examples: I’ll have to work hard now to make up for lost time.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: they do not like each other
examples: There's no love lost between her and her in-laws.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large number or amount
examples: ‘How many do you need?’ ‘A lot.’
Have some more cake. There's lots left.
He has invited nearly a hundred people but a lot aren't able to come.
I have a lot to do today.
She still has an awful lot (= a very large amount) to learn.

a lottery ticket

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: They shared a love of learning.
her love for her garden

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person, a thing or an activity that you like very much
examples: Take care, my love.

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: COMPARE duck

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: They're all volunteers, working for the love of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 10

examples: For the love of God, tell me what he said!

definitions.label: Meaning 11

examples: Give my love to Mary when you see her.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: loving somebody very much

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a hard task that you do because you want to, not because it is necessary
examples: Writing the book was a labour of love.

definitions.label: Meaning 14

examples: Lots of love, Jenny

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.label: Meaning 16

examples: Her mother was a lovely woman.

examples: It's lovely and warm in here.

a low wall/building/table
The fence is too low.
a low range of hills
low clouds
flying at low altitude

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: OPPOSITE high
low back pain
the lower slopes of the mountain
temperatures in the low 20s (= no higher than 21–23°)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not high at the neck
examples: SEE ALSO low-cut
a dress with a low neckline

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: OPPOSITE high

lower prices/costs

low-tar cigarettes

examples: The reservoir was low after the long drought.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

low marks/grades
a low standard of living

the lower classes of society

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 12

examples: SYNONYM disreputable

definitions.label: Meaning 13

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.definition: used to ask somebody if they have been successful with something
examples: ‘Any luck?’ ‘No, they're all too busy to help.’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in the way that chance decides what will happen
examples: As luck would have it, the train was late.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to express sympathy for somebody
examples: Bad luck, Helen, you played very well.
It's hard luck on him that he wasn't chosen.
What rotten luck it had to happen now!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have no money because of a period of bad luck
examples: In the movie they play two jazz musicians who are down on their luck.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to wish somebody success with something
examples: The best of luck with your exams.
Good luck! I hope it goes well.
‘I'm going to try giving up social media for a year.’ ‘Good luck with that (= I don't think you will succeed).’

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to encourage somebody who has not been successful at something
examples: Never mind— better luck next time.
If you didn't win a prize, better luck next time.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: because you believe it will bring you good luck, or because this is a traditional belief
examples: Take something blue. It's for luck.
I always carry it with me, just for luck.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: for no particular reason
examples: I gave the mixture one more stir for luck.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not mind what somebody does as it does not affect you, but you hope they will be successful
examples: It's not something I would care to try myself but if she wants to, good luck to her.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that you feel sorry for them
examples: ‘Failed again, I'm afraid.’ ‘Oh, hard luck.’

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to show you are not surprised something bad has happened to you, because you are not often lucky
examples: Just my luck to arrive after they had left.
Just my luck to get the broken chair!

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody has been lucky or successful
examples: On a Sunday I didn’t expect to find him at his desk but my luck was in.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: the fact that chance decides something, in a way that you cannot control
examples: To a large extent the life you have depends on who your parents were; it’s just the luck of the biological draw.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to show that you are disappointed because something you were hoping for did not happen
examples: ‘Were you chosen for the team?’ ‘No such luck!’

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: when you take pot luck, you choose something or go somewhere without knowing very much about it, but hope that it will be good, pleasant, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO potluck
It's pot luck whether you get good advice or not.
You're welcome to stay to supper, but you'll have to take pot luck (= eat whatever is available).

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to take a risk because you have successfully avoided problems in the past
examples: You didn't get caught last time, but don't push your luck!

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: used to show sympathy for somebody that something bad that has happened to
examples: ‘I failed by one point.’ ‘That's tough luck.’

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used to show that you do not feel sorry for somebody who has a problem
examples: ‘If you take the car, I won't be able to go out.’ ‘Tough luck!’

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to do something that involves risk or luck, hoping to succeed
examples: My grandparents emigrated to Canada to try their luck there.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to show that you are disappointed about something
examples: I shall have to miss the party, worse luck!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having good luck
examples: SYNONYM fortunate
His friend was killed and he knows he is lucky to be alive.
She was lucky enough to be chosen for the team.
You were lucky (that) you spotted the danger in time.
In terms of my career I feel incredibly lucky.
You can think yourself lucky you didn't get mugged.
She counted herself lucky that she still had a job.
Mark is one of the lucky ones—he at least has somewhere to sleep.
the lucky winners
He was among the lucky ones whose works were approved.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: being the result of good luck
examples: It was lucky for us that we were able to go.
Lucky for her, a police car was passing.
It is lucky (that) neither were killed in the accident.
That was the luckiest escape of my life.
a lucky guess
A lucky find on the edge of the Cotswolds is helping archaeologists discover what life was like in Roman Britain.
I had a lucky break when I left school getting a job on local radio.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: bringing good luck
examples: a lucky charm
The team thinks of me as their lucky mascot.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have good luck
examples: She hopes that some day she'll get lucky and win the jackpot.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to meet somebody new and have sex with them
examples: Mike's hoping to get lucky tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to show that you think somebody is lucky to have something, be able to do something, etc.
examples: ‘I'm off to Paris.’ ‘Lucky you!’

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have good luck
examples: We certainly struck it lucky with the weather.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to feel very grateful and lucky about something
examples: Just thank your lucky stars you weren’t in the house at the time.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used when you have failed to do something twice and hope that you will succeed the third time

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that something that they are expecting probably will not happen
examples: ‘I was hoping to get a ticket for Saturday.’ ‘You'll be lucky.’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that they will probably not get what they are hoping for, and may not deserve it

definitions.definition: the fact of enjoying special and expensive things, particularly food and drink, clothes and places
examples: a life of unimaginable luxury
Now we'll be able to live in luxury for the rest of our lives.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that is expensive and pleasant but not essential
examples: SYNONYM extravagance

It was a luxury if you had a washing machine in those days.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a pleasure or an advantage that you do not often have
examples: We had the luxury of being able to choose from four good candidates for the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in easy, comfortable conditions, and enjoying the advantages of being rich
examples: We spent two weeks in the hotel living in the lap of luxury.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: He got mad and walked out.
She's mad at me for being late.
They're pretty mad about being lied to.
That noise is driving me mad.
He'll go mad when he sees the damage.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: liking something/somebody very much; very interested in something
examples: He's always been mad about kids.
to be mad on tennis
Scott's mad for peanuts.
football-mad boys
She's completely power-mad.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: done without thought or control; wild and excited
examples: The crowd made a mad rush for the exit.

The four companies are in a mad scramble for market share.
The team won and the fans went mad.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: suffering from rabies
examples: SYNONYM rabid (3)

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: Love him or hate him, the man's got mad skills.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: very angry

examples: I had to run like mad to catch the bus.

definitions.label: Meaning 10

examples: He's mad keen on planes.

definitions.label: Meaning 12

examples: Old English gemǣd(e)d ‘maddened’, participial form related to gemād ‘mad’, of Germanic origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a type of large thin book with a paper cover that you can buy every week or month, containing articles, photographs, etc., often on a particular topic; a similar collection of articles, etc. that appears regularly online
examples: a weekly/monthly magazine
a magazine article/interview/story/feature/piece
an online magazine
a literary/news magazine

a magazine editor/publisher/journalist/reporter

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a radio or television programme that is about a particular topic
examples: a regional news magazine on TV
a magazine programme/program

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the part of a gun that holds the bullets before they are fired
examples: He took the machine gun and a spare magazine.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a room or building where weapons, explosives and bullets are stored
examples: Those buildings are ammunition magazines.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to keep a building, a machine, etc. in good condition by checking or repairing it regularly
examples: The house is large and difficult to maintain.

examples: SYNONYM keep

examples: SYNONYM insist

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to control or be in charge of a business, a team, an organization, land, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO stage-manage
to manage a business/factory/bank/hotel/soccer team
to manage a department/project
I think that Forestry Tasmania manages the forest.
The units in some areas are poorly maintained and badly managed.
We need people who are good at managing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to succeed in doing something, especially something difficult
examples: I don't know exactly how we'll manage it, but we will, somehow.
Can you manage another piece of cake? (= eat one)
We managed to get to the airport in time.
How did you manage to persuade him?
She somehow managed to escape through the window.
He always manages to say the wrong thing.
They managed to find a place to stay.
We couldn't have managed without you.
‘Need any help?’ ‘No, thanks. I can manage.’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to succeed in achieving or producing something
examples: In spite of his disappointment, he managed a weak smile.
Davies manages light humour without seeming silly.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be able to solve your problems, deal with a difficult situation, etc.
examples: SYNONYM cope
She's 82 and can't manage on her own any more.
How do you manage without a car?
I can manage without a dishwasher.
I don’t know how she manages on her own with four kids.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be able to live or survive without having much money, support, sleep, etc.
examples: young families who are just about managing
She was finding it difficult to manage financially.
He has to manage on less than £100 a week.
Many find it difficult to manage on their weekly income.
He generally managed on five hours' sleep a night
Everyone will just have to manage with less.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to use money, time, information, etc. in a sensible way
examples: Don't tell me how to manage my affairs.
a computer program that helps you manage data efficiently
This enables pension funds to manage risk.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be able to do something at a particular time
examples: Let's meet up again—can you manage next week sometime?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to keep somebody/something under control; to be able to deal with somebody/something
examples: It's like trying to manage an unruly child.
Can you manage that suitcase?
She manages horses better than anyone I know.
I really liked the chapter about how to manage stress.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to control how land is used, so that it is used in a sensible way
examples: The landowners manage their land to provide habitat for the desired species.
All the timber comes from sustainably managed forests.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activity of running and controlling a business or similar organization
examples: SEE ALSO event management
a career in management
hotel/project management
a management training course
the day-to-day management of the business
The report blames bad management.
Effective financial management is essential.
The company's top-down management style made decision-making slow and inflexible.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the people who run and control a business or similar organization
examples: The management is/are considering closing the factory.
The shop is now under new management.
junior/middle/senior management
the bank's/airline's/hospital's management
a management decision/job
A new board and management team took over.
My role is to act as a mediator between employees and management.
Most managements are keen to avoid strikes.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act or skill of dealing with people or situations in a successful way
examples: SEE ALSO self-management
classroom management
time management (= the way in which you organize how you spend your time)
Security is all about risk management.
a waste management system/company/plan
management of staff/patients/resources
Diet plays an important role in the management of heart disease.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who is in charge of running a business, a shop or a similar organization or part of one
examples: SEE ALSO actor-manager
a bank/hotel manager
the sales/marketing/human resources manager
a fund/portfolio/asset manager
The company always needs project managers.
I'm a senior manager in a multinational company.
a meeting of area managers
If you have any questions, speak to your manager.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who deals with the business affairs of an actor, a musician, etc.
examples: The comedian is unavailable for comment, according to her manager.
The band's manager said that the gig sold out in hours.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who trains and organizes a sports team
examples: the new manager of Italy
He will be the club's caretaker manager until a new manager is appointed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who is good at managing resources
examples: She's a good manager who never throws any food away.
TV ads depicted the candidate as a would-be efficient manager of the US economy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the authority to do something, given to a government or other organization by the people who vote for it in an election
examples: It is undemocratic to govern an area without an electoral mandate.
The election victory gave the party a clear mandate to continue its programme of reform.
a mandate for an end to the civil war

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the period of time for which a government is given power
examples: The presidential mandate is limited to two terms of four years each.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an official order given to somebody to perform a particular task
examples: The bank had no mandate to honour the cheque.
They accused him of acting without a mandate.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the power given to a country to govern another country or region, especially in the past
examples: The Cook Islands mandate was given to New Zealand.
The mandate ran until 1947.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: required by law
examples: SYNONYM compulsory
The offence carries a mandatory life sentence.
It is mandatory for blood banks to test all donated blood for the virus.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to show something clearly, especially a feeling, an attitude or a quality
examples: SYNONYM demonstrate
Social tensions were manifested in the recent political crisis.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to appear or become easy to notice
examples: SYNONYM appear
The symptoms of the disease manifested themselves ten days later.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to control or influence somebody/something, often in a dishonest way so that they do not realize it
examples: She uses her charm to manipulate people.
As a politician, he knows how to manipulate public opinion.
They managed to manipulate us into agreeing to help.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to control, use or change something with skill
examples: to manipulate the gears and levers of a machine
Computers are very efficient at manipulating information.
genetically manipulated organisms
digitally manipulated images

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move a person’s bones or joints into the correct positionWord Origin
examples: early 19th cent.: back-formation from manipulation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: behaviour that controls or influences somebody/something, often in a dishonest way so that they do not realize it
examples: Advertising like this is a cynical manipulation of the elderly.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the control or use of something in a way that shows skill
examples: data manipulation
manipulation of images

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the skill or act of moving a person's bones or joints into the correct position
examples: manipulation of the bones of the back

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: behaviour that is considered to be polite in a particular society or culture
examples: SEE ALSO table manners
to have good/bad manners
It is bad manners to talk with your mouth full.
He has no manners (= behaves very badly).
She could at least have the good manners to let me know she won’t be able to attend.
These children need to learn some manners.
Now sit down and eat and mind your manners!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the way that something is done or happens
examples: She answered in a businesslike manner.
All claims must be settled in a professional and timely manner.
The manner in which the decision was announced was extremely regrettable.
The eye works in a similar manner to a camera.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the way that somebody behaves towards other people
examples: SEE ALSO bedside manner
to have an aggressive/a friendly/a relaxed manner
His manner was polite but cool.
She behaved in a threatening manner towards her mother.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the habits and customs of a particular group of people
examples: the social morals and manners of the seventeenth century

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: many different types of people or things
examples: The problem can be solved in all manner of ways.
He enjoyed interacting with all manner of different people.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: in a style that is typical of somebody/something
examples: a painting in the manner of Raphael

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: if you think about it in a particular way; true in some but not all ways
examples: All these points of view are related, in a manner of speaking.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: as if something is natural for you and you have done it many times in the past
examples: She adapted to life on the estate as if to the manner born.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: what kind of…
examples: What manner of man could do such a terrible thing?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make goods in large quantities, using machines
examples: SYNONYM mass-produce
manufactured goods
This company manufactures the equipment used to make contact lenses.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to invent a story, an excuse, etc.
examples: a news story manufactured by an unscrupulous journalist

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to produce a substance
examples: Vitamins cannot be manufactured by our bodies.
Plants use the sun's light to manufacture their food.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the business or industry of producing goods in large quantities in factories, etc.
examples: Many jobs in manufacturing were lost during the recession.
The company has established its first manufacturing base in Europe.
manufacturing industry

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a copy of a book, piece of music, etc. before it has been printed
examples: an unpublished/original manuscript
I read her poems in manuscript.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a very old book or document that was written by hand before printing was invented
examples: medieval illuminated manuscripts

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used with plural nouns and verbs, especially in negative sentences or in more formal English, to mean ‘a large number of’. Also used in questions to ask about the size of a number, and with ‘as’, ‘so’ and ‘too’.
examples: NOTE AT much
We don't have very many copies left.
You can't have one each. We haven't got many.
Many people feel that the law should be changed.
Many of those present disagreed.
How many children do you have?
There are too many mistakes in this essay.
He made ten mistakes in as many (= in ten) lines.
New drivers have twice as many accidents as experienced drivers.
Don't take so many.
I've known her for a great many (= very many) years.
Even if one person is hurt that is one too many.
It was one of my many mistakes.
a many-headed monster

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used with a plural verb to mean ‘most people’
examples: a government which improves conditions for the many

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used with a singular noun and verb to mean ‘a large number of’
examples: Many a good man has been destroyed by drink.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show surprise that the number of people or things involved is so large
examples: There were as many as 200 people at the lecture.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be slightly drunk

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to show that something happens often
examples: Many's the time I heard her use those words.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a drawing or plan of the earth’s surface or part of it, showing countries, towns, rivers, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO Ordnance Survey
a map of France
a street map of Miami
a map of the area/region/world/route
to read a/the map (= understand the information on a map)
large-scale maps
Can you find Black Hill on the map?
to be marked/plotted/shown on a map
I'll draw you a map of how to get to my house.
Click here to download a map.
an interactive map

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a diagram to show the positions of things over an area
examples: SEE ALSO heat map
an electron density map

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a diagram to show the position of genes on a chromosome
examples: a physical and genetic map of the entire human genome

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: lacking organization; in a confused state
examples: Oil prices were all over the map last week, but they seem to be more stable now.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: very far away or remote
examples: Although the town was completely off the map, I was glad that I made the effort to visit.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something famous or important
examples: This chicken dish put the chef firmly on the map.
The exhibition has helped put the city on the map.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to destroy or remove somebody/something completelyWord Origin
examples: early 16th cent.: from medieval Latin mappa mundi, literally ‘sheet of the world’, from Latin mappa ‘sheet, napkin’ + mundi ‘of the world’ (genitive of mundus).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: lasting a long time and requiring a lot of effort, concentration, etc.
examples: a marathon journey lasting 56 hours
a marathon legal battle
a marathon five-set tennis match
The painting would be completed in one marathon session.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to walk with stiff regular steps like a soldier
examples: Quick march! (= the order to start marching)
Soldiers were marching up and down outside the government buildings.
They marched 20 miles to reach the capital.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to walk somewhere quickly in a determined way
examples: She marched over to me and demanded an apology.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to walk through the streets in a large group in order to protest about something
examples: SYNONYM demonstrate
They were marching for peace.
We marched peacefully through the streets.
Hundreds of people marched in support of the teachers' pay claim.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to force somebody to walk somewhere with you
examples: The guards marched the prisoner away.
She was marched out of the door and into a waiting car.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be ordered to leave a place, a job, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to order somebody to leave a place, their job, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to behave in a different way from other people; to have different attitudes or ideas
examples: She was a gifted and original artist who marched to a different drummer.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the empty space at the side of a written or printed page
examples: the left-hand/right-hand margin
a narrow/wide margin
notes scribbled in the margin

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the amount of time, or number of votes, etc. by which somebody wins something
examples: He won by a narrow margin.
She beat the other runners by a margin of ten seconds.
Members voted by a margin of 7–1 to become a public limited company.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the difference between the cost of buying or producing something and the price that it is sold for
examples: What are your average operating margins?
a gross margin of 45 per cent

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an extra amount of something such as time, space, money, etc. that you include in order to make sure that something is successful
examples: SEE ALSO margin of error
a safety margin
The narrow gateway left me little margin for error as I reversed the car.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the extreme edge or limit of a place
examples: the eastern margin of the Indian Ocean

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the part that is not included in the main part of a group or situation
examples: SYNONYM fringe
people living on the margins of society

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an amount that is added to a basic wage, paid for special skill or responsibilityWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Latin margo, margin- ‘edge’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: small and not important
examples: SYNONYM slight
a marginal improvement in weather conditions
The story will only be of marginal interest to our readers.
The difference between the two estimates is marginal.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: relating to or resulting from small changes
examples: All three companies reported marginal revenue growth.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not part of a main or important group or situation
examples: marginal groups in society
Welsh was considered a marginal language.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: won or lost by a very small number of votes and therefore very important or interesting as evidence of public opinion
examples: a marginal seat/constituency

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: written in the margin of a page
examples: marginal notes/comments

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: that cannot produce enough good crops to make a profitWord Origin
examples: late 16th cent.: from medieval Latin marginalis, from margo, margin- ‘edge’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the sea and the creatures and plants that live there
examples: marine life
a marine biologist (= a scientist who studies life in the sea)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with ships or trade at seaWord Origin
examples: Middle English (as a noun in the sense ‘seashore’): from Old French marin, marine, from Latin marinus, from mare ‘sea’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to write or draw a symbol, line, etc. on something in order to give information about it
examples: The flood level is marked by a white line on the wall.
Items marked with an asterisk can be omitted.
Prices are marked on the goods.
The teacher marked her absent (= made a mark by her name to show that she was absent).
Why have you marked this wrong?
Do not open any mail marked ‘Confidential’.
Certain words were marked as important.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give marks to students’ work
examples: COMPARE grade
I hate marking exam papers.
I spend at least six hours a week marking.
If you don't hand your homework in on time, I won't mark it.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a mark on something in a way that damages it or makes it look less good; to become damaged or be made to look less good in this way
examples: A large purple scar marked his cheek.
The surfaces are made from a material that doesn't mark.
The paperweight had fallen onto the desk, badly marking the surface.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to show the position of something
examples: SYNONYM indicate
Yellow arrows mark the way.
The cross marks the spot where the body was found.
The route has been marked in red.
The boundary was marked with a dotted line.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to celebrate or officially remember an event that you consider to be important
examples: a ceremony to mark the 50th anniversary of the end of the war
The event marked a milestone in the hotel's success story.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be a sign that something new is going to happen
examples: This agreement marks the start of a new phase in international relations.
This speech may mark a change in government policy.
‘Lyrical Ballads’ conveniently marks the beginning of nineteenth-century poetry.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to give somebody/something a particular quality or character
examples: SYNONYM characterize
a life marked by suffering
The town is still deeply marked by the folk memory of the Depression.
He was marked as an enemy of the poor.
Christianity has indelibly marked the culture and consciousness of Europe.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to pay careful attention to something
examples: There'll be trouble over this, mark my words.
You mark what I say, John.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to stay close to an opponent in order to prevent them from getting the ball
examples: SEE ALSO marking
Hughes was marking Taylor.
Our defence had him closely marked.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to pass the time while you wait for something more interesting
examples: I'm just marking time in this job—I'm hoping to get into journalism.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make marching movements without moving forwards

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to remind somebody of something they should consider in a particular case
examples: She hasn't had much success yet. Mark you, she tries hard.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
