examples: Price is not always an accurate marker of quality.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a pen with a thick felt tip
examples: SEE ALSO Magic Marker™

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who marks students’ work or exam papers

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a player who stays close to a player on the other team in order to stop them getting the ball

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to do something that sets a standard for your competitors or shows what you intend to do or achieve in the future
examples: The reigning champions laid down a marker with a 36–0 defeat of their opponents.
The prime minister has put down a marker for a Washington visit in May.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an occasion when people buy and sell goods; the open area or building where they meet to do this
examples: SEE ALSO farmers’ market
a fruit/flower/fish market
an antiques market
an indoor/a street market
market stalls/traders
We buy our fruit and vegetables at the market.
Thursday is market day.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: business or trade, or the amount of trade in a particular type of goods
examples: SEE ALSO labour market
the world market in coffee
They have increased their share of the market by 10 per cent.
The firm will expand its size to claim more market share.
the property/housing/job market (= the number and type of houses, jobs, etc. that are available)
They have cornered the market in sportswear (= sell the most).
New companies have entered the market.
The big players still dominate the market.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a particular area, country or section of the population that might buy goods
examples: SEE ALSO common market
The Chinese market has opened up recently.
Expansion into the global market brings more risk.
They supply beef to the domestic market.
The young, health-conscious female consumer is our target market.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the number of people who want to buy something
examples: SYNONYM demand
a growing/declining market for second-hand cars
There's not much of a market for tourist art on the island.
New Zealand is competing in an international market for medical graduates.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: people who buy and sell goods in competition with each other
examples: SEE ALSO black market
The market will decide if the TV station has any future.
a market-based/market-led/market-driven economy
innovative products at the forefront of market trends

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the business of buying and selling shares in companies and the place where this happens; a stock exchange
examples: SEE ALSO bear market
the futures market
a market crash
The market closed weaker.
The markets reacted quickly to the negative publicity.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a situation in which there is a lot of a particular item for sale, so that prices are low and people buying have a choice
examples: In a buyer's market, the commodity is plentiful and so its price is not high.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: interested in buying something
examples: I'm not in the market for a new car at the moment.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: available for people to buy
examples: to put your house on the market
The house came on the market last year.
There are hundreds of different brands on the market.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: available to buy without any limits

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to buy and sell stocks and shares in order to make a profit
examples: He is a skilled investor who knows how to play the market—and win.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to charge such a high price for your goods, services, etc. that nobody wants to buy them
examples: Some leading UK firms are pricing themselves out of the market.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a situation in which people selling something have an advantage, because there is not a lot of a particular item for sale, and prices can be kept high
examples: In a seller’s market, demand exceeds supply, and prices are high.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to stop something from being sold
examples: The slimming pills were taken off the market.
Thousands of egg products were taken off the shelves following the health scare.

the education marketplace

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the legal relationship between two people who are married to each other
examples: SEE ALSO arranged marriage
a happy/an unhappy marriage
All of her children's marriages ended in divorce.
She has two children by a previous marriage.
This is his second marriage.
Same-sex marriages are now recognized in many countries.

examples: They don't believe in marriage.

Public support for gay marriage has risen.
They strongly disapprove of sex outside marriage.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: Their marriage took place in a local church.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a combination of two things
examples: The new collection is a marriage of fashion and technology.
the marriage between a young team and an experienced coach

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: when somebody is related to you by marriage, they are married to somebody in your family, or you are married to somebody in their family
examples: Jane and I are related by marriage.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: permission to marry somebody, especially a woman
examples: He asked the general for his daughter's hand in marriage.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a husband or wife
examples: OPPOSITE unmarried
a married man/woman
Is he married?
a happily/an unhappily married couple
She's married to John.
Sam and Chris are getting married on Saturday.
How long have you been married?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with marriage
examples: Are you enjoying married life?
Her married name (= the family name of her husband) is Jones.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very involved in something so that you have no time for other activities or interests
examples: My brother is married to his job.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become the husband or wife of somebody; to get married to somebody

I don't want to marry Robert.
We got married in a small village church.
Dali and Gala were married in a civil ceremony in Paris.
He never married.
I guess I'm not the marrying kind (= the kind of person who wants to get married).
They married young.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to perform a ceremony in which two people get married
examples: They were married by the local priest.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to find a husband or wife for somebody, especially your daughter or son

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to combine two different things, ideas, etc. successfully
examples: SYNONYM unite

The focus for business should be how to marry economic efficiency with social justice.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: people who marry quickly, without really getting to know each other, may discover later that they have made a mistake

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: late Middle English: from Old French, or from Latin martialis, from Mars, Mart-. Mars is the god of war in Roman mythology.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that you wear over your face to hide it, or to frighten or entertain other people
examples: The robbers wore stocking masks.
The kids were all wearing animal masks.
In the second part of the play, the actors take off their masks.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that you wear over part or all of your face in order to protect it
examples: SEE ALSO gas mask
a surgical/gas mask
a fencing mask

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thick cream made of various substances that you put on your face and neck in order to improve the quality of your skin
examples: a face mask

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a manner or an expression that hides your true character or feelings
examples: He longed to throw off the mask of respectability.
Her face was a cold, blank mask.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large amount of a substance that does not have a definite shape or form
examples: She saw a large dark mass in the water.
The hill appeared as a black mass in the distance.
a mass of snow and rocks falling down the mountain
The sky was full of dark masses of clouds.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a large amount or quantity of something
examples: a mass of blonde hair
I began sifting through the mass of evidence.
Both titles give readers a mass of information.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a large number of people or things grouped together, often in a confused way
examples: I struggled through the mass of people to the exit.
The page was covered with a mass of figures.
a chaotic mass of ideas

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a large number or amount of something
examples: SYNONYM lots
There were masses of people in the shops yesterday.

There is masses of cake left over from the party.

examples: government attempts to suppress dissatisfaction among the masses
a TV programme that brings science to the masses
the image of America with arms open wide to the world's huddled masses

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the most; the majority
examples: The reforms are unpopular with the mass of teachers and parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: SEE ALSO biomass
calculating the mass of a planet
a mass of 46.3 kg

examples: The game was a 10–0 massacre for our team.

definitions.definition: very large, heavy and solid
examples: a massive rock
the massive walls of the castle

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: extremely large or serious

These farmers grow crops on a massive scale.
He suffered a massive heart attack.
Their house is massive.
They have a massive great house.

The band's new album was a massive hit.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very successful or important
examples: This band is going to be massive.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a man who has people working for him, often as servants in his home
examples: They lived in fear of their master.
the exploitation of slaves by their former masters

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is in charge of an organization or group
examples: SEE ALSO harbour master
His political masters are all old right-wing politicians.
Many nations were trying to shake off their colonial masters.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is able to control something
examples: SEE ALSO puppet master

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: SEE ALSO grandmaster
a master of disguise
a master of her craft
a master of the serve-and-volley game
a master at managing money

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a famous painter who lived in the past
examples: SEE ALSO old master
an exhibition of work by the French master, Monet
the great masters of Impressionism
This portrait is the work of an acknowledged master.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a second university degree, or, in Scotland, a first university degree, such as an MA
examples: SEE ALSO MA
He has a Master's in Business Administration.
She holds a master's degree in journalism.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a person who has a master’s degree
examples: a Master of Arts/Science

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the owner of an animal, especially a dog or horse
examples: COMPARE mistress

Even the animals knew their masters were excited.
The horses watched their masters placidly.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a male teacher at a school, especially a private school
examples: COMPARE headmaster
the physics master

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the captain of a ship that transports goods

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a version of a recording from which copies are made
examples: the master copy

definitions.label: Meaning 12

a tennis match
a league match

to win/lose a match
I'll probably watch the match on TV.

Ireland took the match (= won) 2–1 .

examples: I was no match for him at tennis.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the members, or the number of members, of a group, a club, an organization, etc.
examples: The membership has/have not yet voted.
The club has a membership of more than 500.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official note from one person to another in the same organization
examples: to write/send a memo
She circulated a memo to the staff.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an account written by somebody, especially somebody famous, about their life and experiencesExtra Examples
examples: O'Connor published a childhood memoir.
He has published a long memoir about those years.
She describes in her memoirs how she coped with her mother's death.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a written account of somebody’s life, a place, or an event, written by somebody who knows it well
examples: his brief memoir of his father's life
the market for political memoirs

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: worth remembering or easy to remember, especially because of being special or unusual
examples: SYNONYM unforgettable
The holiday provided many memorable moments.
a truly memorable occasion/event
Her novels are full of memorable characters.
Olivier gives a memorable performance as Hamlet.
memorable lines/lyrics/phrases
The city is memorable for its fantastic beaches.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a statue, stone, etc. that is built in order to remind people of an important past event or of a famous person who has died
examples: a war memorial (= in memory of soldiers who died in a war)
a memorial to victims of the Holocaust

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that will continue to remind people of somebody/something
examples: The painting will be a lasting memorial to a remarkable woman.
a memorial of my husband

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a ceremony that is held to remember somebody who has died or an important past event
examples: a memorial for victims of the air crash
They are holding a memorial for it.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: your ability to remember things
examples: SEE ALSO photographic memory
I have a bad memory for names.
People have short memories (= they soon forget).
He had a long memory for people who had disappointed him.
He had a great memory for detail.
She can recite the whole poem from memory.
He suffered memory loss for weeks after the accident.
Are you sure? Memory can play tricks on you.
The drugs had a severe effect on her short-term memory.
I quickly committed the number of the car to memory (= learned and remembered it).
Culture is the unit of collective memory, keeping the past alive.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the period of time that a person or group of people is able to remember events
examples: SEE ALSO folk memory
There hasn’t been peace in the country in my memory.
It was the worst storm in recent memory.
This hasn't happened within living memory (= nobody alive now can remember it).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thought of something that you remember from the past
examples: SYNONYM recollection
Her poems are often based on childhood memories.
I have vivid memories of my grandparents.
My mother has fond memories of those days.
I have many happy memories of working there.
The snow outside makes summer feel like a distant memory.
What is your earliest memory?
The photos bring back lots of good memories.
This music evokes painful memories.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: what is remembered about somebody after they have died
examples: Her memory lives on (= we still remember her).
Their behaviour insults the memory of those who died for this country.
They held a feast to honour the memory of Patroclus, his slain comrade.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the part of a computer where information is stored; the amount of space in a computer for storing information
examples: SEE ALSO flash memory
32 gigabytes of memory
Have you got enough memory available to run the program?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if something is etched on your heart, memory, etc. you remember it because it has made a strong impression on you

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have a very bad memory; to forget things easily

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if I remember correctly

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: intended to show respect and remind people of somebody who has died
examples: He founded the charity in memory of his late wife.
The statue was erected to the memory of my father.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to say or do something that makes somebody remember something
examples: Maybe these letters will help to jog your memory.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with or happening in the mind; involving the process of thinking
examples: the mental process of remembering
Do you have a mental picture of what it will look like?
The actor doesn't match the mental image I had of the character.
I made a mental note to talk to her about it.
He has a complete mental block (= difficulty in understanding or remembering) when it comes to physics.
These musicians have prodigious mental capacities.
The experience caused her huge amounts of mental suffering.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with the state of health of the mind or with the treatment of illnesses of the mind
examples: COMPARE psychiatric
a mental disorder/illness
He had a history of mental problems.
She was suffering from physical and mental exhaustion.
The analysis of dreams can reveal details of a person's mental state.
a mental hospital/patient

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: crazy
examples: Watch him. He's mental.
My dad will go mental (= be very angry) when he finds out.
We were just losing so much money—it was mental.
It was mental, but a brilliant ending to the film.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to write or speak about something/somebody, especially without giving much information
examples: SEE ALSO above-mentioned
Sorry, I won't mention it again.
The newspaper failed to mention a word of Johnson's speech.
The doctor mentioned the possibility of going to Nairobi for special treatment.
The disease is rarely mentioned by Western media.
Now that you mention it, she did seem to be in a strange mood.
Nobody mentioned anything to me about it.
Did she mention where she was going?
You mentioned in your letter that you might be moving abroad.
He failed to mention that he was the one who started the fight.
Did I mention going to see Vicky on Sunday?
The cruise visits most places mentioned in the article.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to refer to somebody/something as being interesting, especially as a possible candidate for a job or position
examples: His name has been mentioned as a future MP.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used as a polite answer when somebody has thanked you for something
examples: SYNONYM you’re welcome
‘Thanks for all your help.’ ‘Don't mention it.’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to introduce extra information and emphasize what you are saying
examples: He has two big houses in this country, not to mention his villa in France.
I admired her confidence, not to mention the fact that she was intelligent and well spoken.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an experienced person who advises and helps somebody with less experience over a period of time
examples: COMPARE mentee
She was a friend and mentor to many young actors.
His former coach had remained his mentor throughout his career.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an experienced person in a company, university, etc. who trains and advises new employees or students
examples: Regular meetings between mentor and trainee help guide young engineers through their early years.
The company runs a mentor programme.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a list of the food that is available at a restaurant or to be served at a meal
examples: SEE ALSO tasting menu
May we have the menu?
to ask for/look at the menu
the lunch/dinner menu
What's on the menu (= for dinner) tonight?
The chef put together a special menu of drinks and dishes employing chocolate.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a list of possible choices that are shown on a computer screen
examples: SEE ALSO drop-down menu
a pull-down/pop-up menu
When highlighted information is clicked, a pop-up menu appears.
I clicked on a menu item called ‘connect to server’.
a menu option/button

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who buys and sells goods in large quantities, especially one who imports and exports goods
examples: SEE ALSO builders’ merchant
a coal/wine merchant
Venice was once a city of rich merchants.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who sells goods to the public, especially through a store
examples: The credit cards are accepted by 10 million merchants worldwide.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who likes a particular activity
examples: a speed merchant (= somebody who likes to drive fast)
noise merchants (= for example, a band who make a lot of noise)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who predicts that things will go very badly
examples: The doom merchants who said television would kill off the book were wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person who predicts that things will go very badly
examples: The prophets of doom who said television would kill off the book were wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a kind or forgiving attitude towards somebody that you have the power to harm or right to punish
examples: SYNONYM humanity
to ask/beg/plead for mercy
They showed no mercy to their hostages.
God have mercy on us.
The troops are on a mercy mission (= a journey to help people) in the war zone.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an event or a situation to be grateful for, usually because it stops something unpleasant
examples: It's a mercy she wasn't seriously hurt.
His death was a mercy (= because he was in great pain).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not able to stop somebody/something harming you because they have power or control over you
examples: I'm not going to put myself at the mercy of the bank.
We were at the mercy of the weather.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be happy that a situation that is bad is not as bad as it could have been
examples: Well, at least you weren't hurt. I suppose we should be grateful for small mercies.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to leave somebody/something in a situation that may cause them to suffer or to be treated badly
examples: privatized companies left to the mercy of market forces
I’ll leave you to the tender mercies of these ladies!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to put yourself in a situation where you must rely on somebody to be kind to you and not harm or punish youWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French merci ‘pity’ or ‘thanks’, from Latin merces, merced- ‘reward’, in Christian Latin ‘pity, favour, heavenly reward’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used when you want to emphasize how small, unimportant, etc. somebody/something is
examples: It took her a mere 20 minutes to win.
A mere 2 per cent of their budget has been spent on publicity.
He seemed so young, a mere boy.
You've got the job. The interview will be a mere formality.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used when you are saying that the fact that a particular thing is present in a situation is enough to have an influence on that situation
examples: His mere presence (= just the fact that he was there) made her feel afraid.
The mere fact that they were prepared to talk was encouraging.
The mere thought of eating made him feel sick.
The merest (= the slightest) hint of smoke is enough to make her feel ill.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used meaning ‘only’ or ‘simply’ to emphasize a fact or something that you are saying
examples: It is not merely a job, but a way of life.
He said nothing, merely smiled and watched her.
They agreed to go merely because they were getting paid for it.
I'm merely stating what everybody knows anyway.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to combine or make two or more things combine to form a single thing
examples: The banks are set to merge next year.
The two groups have merged to form a new party.
His department will merge with mine.
The villages expanded and merged into one large town.
Fact and fiction merge together in his latest thriller.
His department will be merged with mine.
The company was formed by merging three smaller firms.
Merge multiple text files into one master file.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: if two things merge, or if one thing merges into another, the differences between them gradually disappear so that it is impossible to separate them
examples: The hills merged into the dark sky behind them.
The figures gradually merged into the darkness.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to behave quietly when you are with a group of people so that they do not notice youWord Origin
examples: mid 17th cent. (in the sense ‘immerse oneself’): from Latin mergere ‘to dip, plunge’; the legal sense is from Anglo-Norman French merger.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of joining two or more organizations or businesses into one
examples: If the merger goes through, thousands of jobs will be lost.
a merger between the two banks
our proposed merger with the university
There are local companies ripe for merger or acquisition.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of being good and of deserving praise or reward
examples: SYNONYM worth
a work of outstanding artistic merit
The plan is entirely without merit.
I want to get the job on merit.
He was awarded a certificate of merit for his piano playing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a good feature that deserves praise or reward
examples: SYNONYM strength
We will consider each case on its (own) merits (= without considering any other issues, feelings, etc.).
They weighed up the relative merits of the four candidates.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a grade in an exam or for a piece of work at school or university that is very good
examples: COMPARE distinction (5)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a special mark or award given as a reward for good behaviour at school
examples: Other schools already have merit systems in place that reward good behaviour and attitudes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a dirty or untidy state
examples: The room was in a mess.
The kids made a mess in the bathroom.
‘What a mess!’ she said, surveying the scene after the party.
My hair's a real mess!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a situation that is full of problems, usually because of a lack of organization or because of mistakes that somebody has made
examples: The economy is in a mess.
a financial mess
I feel I've made a mess of things.
How did this whole mess start?
Let's try to sort out the mess.
How do we get out of this mess?
The biggest question is how they got into this mess in the first place.
That’s another fine mess you’ve got us into.
The entire event is a sorry mess.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is dirty or whose clothes and hair are not tidy
examples: You're a mess!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who has serious problems and is in a bad mental condition
examples: When my wife left me I was a total mess.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the excrement (= solid waste matter) of an animal, usually a dog or cat

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a lot of something
examples: There's a mess of fish down there, so get your lines in the water.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a building or room in which members of the armed forces have their meals
examples: the officers’ mess

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a written or spoken piece of information, etc. that you send to somebody or leave for somebody when you cannot speak to them yourself
examples: SEE ALSO error message
There were no messages for me at the hotel.
I never got your message.
We've had an urgent message saying that your father's ill.
Jenny's not here at the moment. Can I take a message?
I left a message on her voicemail.
I've been trying to get you all day—don't you ever listen to your messages?
Messages of support have been arriving from all over the country.
a televised message from the president to the American people
A radio message was sent out to all ships in the area.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of information sent in electronic form, for example by email or mobile phone
examples: SEE ALSO direct message
an email/a text/an SMS message
There were four messages in my inbox.
He sent me a message.
I turned on my cell phone to check my messages.
Fans post messages on her website.
I keep getting an error message when I try to connect to the internet.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an important moral, social or political idea that a book, speech, etc. is trying to communicate
examples: SEE ALSO mixed message
a film with a strong religious message
The campaign is trying to get the message across to young people that drugs are dangerous.
The clear message coming from the government is that they are getting tough on crime.
I think this movie sends the wrong message to her young fans.
He uses his art to convey a political message.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a piece of information that is sent from the brain to a part of the body, or from a part of the body to the brain
examples: The message arrives in your brain in a fraction of a second.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: shopping
examples: to do the messages
to go for the messages
You can leave your messages (= the things that you have bought) here.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to understand what somebody is trying to tell you indirectly
examples: When he started looking at his watch, I got the message and left.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: stating/not stating the official view of the political party or organization you representWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French, based on Latin missus, past participle of mittere ‘send’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a type of solid mineral substance that is usually hard and shiny and that heat and electricity can travel through, for example tin, iron and gold
examples: SEE ALSO base metal
a piece/sheet of metal
a metal pipe/bar/box/plate
a heap of scrap metal
a roof of sheet metal
The frame is made of metal.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: (to go) at full speed; (to drive) with the accelerator of the car pressed to the floor
examples: We drove through the night flat-out, with the pedal to the metal.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to use as much effort as possible; with as much effort as possible
examples: I'm still putting the pedal to the metal here at work.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a word or phrase used to describe somebody/something else, in a way that is different from its normal use, in order to show that the two things have the same qualities and to make the description more powerful, for example She has a heart of stone; the use of such words and phrases
examples: COMPARE simile
a game of football used as a metaphor for the competitive struggle of life
the writer’s striking use of metaphor

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a particular way of doing something
examples: SEE ALSO barrier method
Which method is the most effective?
traditional/alternative methods
a scientific method of data analysis
a reliable method of measuring blood pressure
the best method for arriving at an accurate prediction of the costs
Developing new methods to keep insects out of food packages is critical.
to use/employ/apply a method
to devise/propose/adopt a method
He's quite critical of modern teaching methods.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the quality of being well planned and organized
examples: There's very little method in his approach.
We have to apply some method to this investigation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: there is a reason for somebody’s behaviour and it is not as strange or as stupid as it seemsWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (in the sense ‘prescribed medical treatment for a disease’): via Latin from Greek methodos ‘pursuit of knowledge’, from meta- (expressing development) + hodos ‘way’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a set of methods and principles used to perform a particular activity
examples: recent changes in the methodology of language teaching
research methodologies

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring length; a hundred centimetres
examples: a 50-metre swimming pool
Every few metres the cat stopped and turned to look at me.
Over 3 700 square metres of office space is available.
The huge sculpture is made of 500 cubic metres of ice.
an athlete running at 10 metres per second

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used in the name of races
examples: She came second in the 200 metres.
the 4 × 100 metre(s) relay

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the arrangement of strong and weak stresses in lines of poetry that produces the rhythm; a particular example of this
examples: She knows a lot about verse metre.
poems in a variety of metres
the hexameter, the epic metre of Homer

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the part of something that is at an equal distance from all its edges or sides; a point or a period of time between the beginning and the end of something
examples: SEE ALSO monkey in the middle
a lake with an island in the middle
This chicken isn't cooked in the middle.
Her car was stuck in the middle of the road.
The phone rang in the middle of the night.
You can’t leave in the middle of the meeting!
His picture was right/bang (= exactly) in the middle of the front page.
I have a pain in the middle of my back.
Low temperatures in the middle of winter can kill some trees.
Take a sheet of paper and draw a line down the middle.
I should have finished by the middle of the week.
I like a story with a beginning, a middle and an end.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person’s waist
examples: SEE ALSO middle-of-the-road
He grabbed her around the middle.
I’ve put on weight around the middle.
The work features a stuffed goat with a rubber tyre around its middle.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be involved in an argument or fight between two other people or groups
examples: When they quarrel, I am often caught in the middle.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be busy doing something
examples: They were in the middle of dinner when I called.
I'm in the middle of writing a difficult letter.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a place that is a long way from other buildings, towns, etc.
examples: She lives on a small farm in the middle of nowhere.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to divide something into two equal parts; to divide into two equal parts
examples: The country was split down the middle over the strike (= half supported it, half did not).
Divide the cake down the middle.
It would seem the community has divided down the middle, with some favouring expansion and some dead set against it.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: 12 o’clock at night
examples: She heard the clock strike midnight.
They had to leave at midnight.
At/on the stroke of midnight fireworks lit up the sky.
We have to catch the midnight train.
Let’s have a midnight feast tonight (= a secret meal that children like to have in the middle of the night).
They whiled away the midnight hours playing cards.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a very dark blue colour

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to study or work until late at night

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to leave a place suddenly and secretly, especially at night, usually in order to avoid paying money that you owe to somebodyWord Origin
examples: Old English midniht (see mid-, night).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the middle part of something
examples: SYNONYM middle
Such beauty was unexpected in the midst of the city.
The house is set in the midst of large gardens.
She appeared from the midst of the crowd.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: among or with them/us/it/you
examples: There is a traitor in our midst.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: while something is happening or being done; while you are doing something
examples: a country in the midst of a recession
She discovered it in the midst of sorting out her father's things.
She alone remained calm in the midst of all the confusion.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used when showing that something is or was possible
examples: He might get there in time, but I can't be sure.
It might not be too late to save the building.
I know Vicky doesn't like the job, but I mightn't find it too bad.
The pills might have helped him, if only he'd taken them regularly.
He might say that now (= it is true that he does), but he can soon change his mind.
He might, if he chose, retire and live in luxury for the rest of his days.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used as the past tense of may when reporting what somebody has said
examples: He said he might come tomorrow.
Zheng said she might not stay in the city for long.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to make a polite suggestion
examples: You might try calling the help desk.
I thought we might go to the zoo on Saturday.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to ask permission politely
examples: Might I use your phone?
If I might just say something…

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to ask for information
examples: How might the plans be improved upon?
And who might she be?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to show that you are annoyed about something that somebody could do or could have done
examples: I think you might at least offer to help!
Honestly, you might have told me!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that you are not surprised by something
examples: I might have guessed it was you!
Her film was full of magical effects, as you might expect.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that an important point has been made
examples: ‘And where is the money coming from?’ ‘You might well ask!’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to say that something seems the best thing to do in the situation that you are in, although you may not really want to do it
examples: If no one else wants it, we might as well give it to him.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to say that there is no real difference between two things that you might do
examples: If you are going to have sugar, you may as well have a bar of chocolate.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the movement every year of large numbers of birds or animals from one place to another
examples: the seasonal migration of blue whales
the migration routes of birds

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the movement of people to a new country or area in order to find work or better living conditions
examples: migration from rural to urban areas
It was one of the largest mass migrations in US history.
Net migration— more people moving to the state than leaving—accounts for about two thirds of the population gain.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of moving programs, etc. from one computer system to another; the fact of changing from one computer system to another

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not severe or strong
examples: a mild form of the disease
a mild case of flu
The symptoms were mild.
a mild punishment/criticism

Everyone should have the right to speak their mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: to be remembered for a long time
examples: One of his paintings in particular sticks in my mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: to make you forget about something unpleasant for a short time
examples: SYNONYM distract
Painting helped take her mind off her troubles.

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: in my opinion
examples: It was a ridiculous thing to do, to my mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: a particular way of thinking about thingsWord Origin
examples: Old English gemynd ‘memory, thought’, of Germanic origin, from an Indo-European root meaning ‘revolve in the mind, think’, shared by Sanskrit manas and Latin mens ‘mind’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: of or belonging to the person writing or speaking
examples: That's mine.
He's a friend of mine (= one of my friends).
She wanted one like mine (= like I have).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: my home
examples: Let's go back to mine after the show.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

She wanted one like mine (= like I have).

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who works in a mine taking out coal, gold, diamonds, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO coal miner
Rescuers are trying to save miners trapped underground after a gas explosion.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a substance that is naturally present in the earth and is not formed from animal or vegetable matter, for example gold and salt. Some minerals are also present in food and drink and in the human body and are essential for good health.
examples: COMPARE vegetable
a country rich in mineral resources
mineral deposits/extraction
the recommended intake of vitamins and minerals
Low bone mineral density is linked with vitamin deficiency.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sweet drink with various different tastes that has bubbles of gas in it and does not contain alcohol
examples: Soft drinks and minerals sold here.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very small in size or amount; as small as possible
examples: COMPARE maximal
The work was carried out at minimal cost.
There's only a minimal amount of risk involved.
The damage to the car was minimal.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to reduce something, especially something bad, to the lowest possible level
examples: OPPOSITE maximize
Good hygiene helps to minimize the risk of infection.
Costs were minimized by using plastic instead of leather.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to try to make something seem less important than it really is
examples: SYNONYM play down
He always tried to minimize his own faults, while exaggerating those of others.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make something small, especially on a computer screen
examples: OPPOSITE maximize
Minimize any windows you have open.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used after amounts to show that the amount is the lowest possible
examples: OPPOSITE maximum
You'll need £200 minimum for your holiday expenses.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used after amounts to show that the amount is the lowest possible
examples: OPPOSITE maximum
You'll need £200 minimum for your holiday expenses.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of getting coal and other minerals from under the ground; the industry involved in this
examples: SEE ALSO data mining
coal/diamond/gold/tin mining
a mining company/community/engineer
Mining is prohibited in the National Park.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a senior member of the government who is in charge of a government department or a branch of one
examples: SEE ALSO first minister
the Minister of Education
She became minister of education in 2016.
A new minister of defence had been appointed.
a meeting of EU Foreign Ministers
senior ministers in the Cabinet
cabinet/government ministers
the finance/defence/interior/justice minister
The health minister announced £10 billion in extra funding.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a trained religious leader
examples: COMPARE pastor
a Methodist minister
He was ordained minister of a small rural congregation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person, lower in rank than an ambassador, whose job is to represent their government in a foreign countryWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in sense (2); also in the sense ‘a person acting under the authority of another’): from Old French ministre (noun), ministrer (verb), from Latin minister ‘servant’, from minus ‘less’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a government department that has a particular area of responsibility
examples: The Ministry of Defence has issued the following statement.
A ministry spokesperson defended the measures.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: ministers of religion, especially Protestant ministers, when they are mentioned as a group
examples: He was an excellent candidate for the Baptist ministry.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the spiritual work or service of a Christian or group of Christians; the period of time spent serving the Church
examples: The church provides a valuable ministry to a growing population.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not very large, important or serious
examples: OPPOSITE major
The new plan involves widening a minor road through the valley.
Both the driver and the passenger suffered minor injuries.
You may need to undergo minor surgery.
Most of these youths are in prison for minor offences.
minor modifications/adjustments
There may be some minor changes to the schedule.
Women played a relatively minor role in the organization.
The minor characters in the story are all well drawn.
When you drive a classic car, you expect a few minor problems.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: based on a scale in which the third note is a semitone / half step higher than the second note
examples: COMPARE major
the key of C minor

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the smaller part of a group; less than half of the people or things in a large group
examples: OPPOSITE majority
Only a small minority of students is/are interested in politics these days.
Only a tiny minority of products is/are affected.
For a minority, the decision was a disappointment.
That's very much a minority view.
Minority interest groups have gained disproportionate influence.
You are definitely among the minority.
minority shareholders in the bank
to have a minority stake in a company

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small group within a community or country that is different because of race, religion, language, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO BAME
the rights of ethnic/racial minorities
There is a large German-speaking minority in the east of the country.
persecuted/oppressed minorities
minority languages
The school is 95 per cent minority (= 95 per cent of children are not white Americans but from different groups).
minority neighborhoods (= where no or few white people live)
minority groups/populations/leaders

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the state of being under the age at which you are legally an adult
examples: COMPARE majority (4)
When his minority ended he had to fight to reclaim his property.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to form less than half of a large group
examples: Men are in the minority in this profession.
We are in the minority on this issue.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be the only person to have a particular opinion or to vote a particular wayWord Origin
examples: late 15th cent. (in sense (3)): from French minorité or medieval Latin minoritas, from Latin minor ‘smaller’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act or event that does not follow the laws of nature and is believed to be caused by God
examples: SYNONYM wonder
the miracle of rising from the grave

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a lucky thing that happens that you did not expect or think was possible
examples: SYNONYM wonder
an economic miracle
a miracle cure/drug
It's a miracle (that) nobody was killed in the crash.
It would take a miracle to make this business profitable.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a very good example or product of something
examples: SYNONYM wonder
The car is a miracle of engineering.
A colony of bees is a miracle of organization.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to achieve very good results
examples: Her exercise programme has worked miracles for her.
You can work miracles with very little money if you follow our home decoration tips.
He performed miracles to get everything ready in time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of special flat glass that reflects images, so that you can see yourself when you look in it
examples: SEE ALSO rear-view mirror
He looked at himself in the mirror.
Remember to look in the mirror (= in a car, when driving) before signalling.
the bathroom mirror

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that shows what something else is like
examples: The face is the mirror of the soul.
Dickens' novels are a mirror of his times.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a website that is a copy of another website but that has a different address on the internet

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the fact of hiding the truth with information that is not important or relevant
examples: There's a lot of smoke and mirrors in the financing of this film.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very unhappy or uncomfortable
examples: We were cold, wet and thoroughly miserable.
Don't look so miserable!
She knows how to make life miserable for her employees.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: making you feel very unhappy or uncomfortable
examples: SYNONYM depressing
miserable housing conditions
I spent a miserable weekend alone at home.
What a miserable day! (= cold and wet)
The play was a miserable failure.
These people live in miserable conditions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: always unhappy, unfriendly and in a bad mood
examples: SYNONYM grumpy
He was a miserable old devil.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: too small in quantity
examples: SYNONYM paltry
How can anyone live on such a miserable wage?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: great physical or mental pain
examples: SYNONYM distress
Fame brought her nothing but misery.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very poor living conditions
examples: SYNONYM poverty
The vast majority of the population lives in utter misery.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that causes great physical or mental pain
examples: the miseries of unemployment
the sheer misery of homelessness
the country's economic misery

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who is always unhappy and complaining
examples: Don't be such an old misery!
Old misery guts here doesn’t want to go out.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that makes somebody else feel very unhappy
examples: My old boss used to make my life a misery.
His constant criticism made her life a misery.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to kill a creature because it has an illness or injury that cannot be treated
examples: In the end we asked the vet to put the poor creature out of its misery.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to stop somebody worrying by telling them something that they are anxious to know
examples: Put me out of my misery—did I pass or didn't I?
Oh, put her out of her misery—tell her who won.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: giving the wrong idea or impression and making you believe something that is not true
examples: SYNONYM deceptive
misleading information/advertisements
It would be seriously misleading to suggest that television has no effect on children.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be or arrive too late for something
examples: If I don't leave now I'll miss my plane.
Sorry I'm late—have I missed anything?
‘Is Ann there?’ ‘You've just missed her (= she has just left).’
You'd better hurry—you don't want to miss the bus.
If you miss the deadline, you'll have to pay a fine.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to fail to be or go somewhere
examples: She hasn't missed a game all year.
You missed a good party last night (= because you did not go).
‘Are you coming to the school play?’ ‘I wouldn't miss it for the world.’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to fail to do something
examples: You can't afford to miss meals (= not eat meals) when you're in training.
You have to miss a turn (= to not play when it is your turn in a game).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to not take the opportunity to do something
examples: The sale prices were too good to miss.
It was an opportunity not to be missed.
She missed the opportunity to take part.
Jackson never missed a chance to serve as teacher and mentor.
The film is a real missed opportunity—it could have been so much better.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to fail to hit, catch, reach, etc. something
examples: How many goals has he missed this season?
The bullet missed her by about six inches.
It was a joke that missed its target.
The company has missed all its targets this year.
She threw a plate at him and only narrowly missed.
She narrowly missed hitting him.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to fail to hear, see or notice something
examples: The hotel is the only white building on the road—you can't miss it.
Don't miss next week's issue!
I missed her name.
No one will want to miss this film.
Your mother will know who's moved in—she doesn't miss much.
When you painted your bedroom, you missed a bit (= of the wall) under the window.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to fail to understand something
examples: He completely missed the joke.
You're missing the point (= failing to understand the main part) of what I'm saying.
I think I must have missed something because none of this makes any sense.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to feel sad because you can no longer see somebody or do something that you like
examples: PAST TENSE, PAST PARTICIPLE OF miss
I still miss her a lot.
Your father misses you dreadfully.
She will be greatly missed when she leaves.
Anne, who died on 22 July, will be sadly missed by all who knew her.
What did you miss most when you were in France?
I'm really going to miss Cheri's cooking.
I don't miss getting up at six every morning!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to notice that somebody/something is not where they/it should be
examples: When did you first miss the necklace?
Let’s go for a quick drink—nobody will miss us.
We seem to be missing some students this morning.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to avoid something unpleasant
examples: SYNONYM escape
If you go now you should miss the crowds.
He fell and just missed knocking the whole display over.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to not work correctly because the petrol does not burn at the right time

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody has a sudden feeling of fear, excitement, etc.
examples: My heart missed a beat when I saw who it was.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody notices every opportunity to gain an advantage

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to succeed/fail in achieving or guessing something
examples: He blushed furiously and Robyn knew she had hit the mark.
The film misses the mark because it just isn't believable.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be unable to take advantage of something because you are too late
examples: If you don't buy now, you may find that you've missed the boat.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to make a mistake
examples: Unless I miss my guess, your computer needs a new hard drive.
If you miss your guess, you lose 10 points.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a weapon that is sent through the air and that explodes when it hits the thing that it is aimed at
examples: SEE ALSO ballistic missile
nuclear missiles
a missile base/site

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an object that is thrown at somebody to hurt them
examples: SYNONYM projectile
Missiles including stones and bottles were thrown at the police.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that cannot be found or that is not in its usual place; that has been removed, lost or destroyed
examples: SYNONYM lost
I never found the missing piece.
Cases with missing data are excluded from the report.
My gloves have been missing for ages.
Two files have gone missing.
Our cat's gone missing again.
The book has two pages missing.
The book has two missing pages,
He didn't notice there was anything missing from his room until later on.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not at home; not found
examples: a missing four-year-old girl
They still hoped to find their missing son.
a woman who went missing three months ago
Posters of missing persons lined the walls.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not present after an accident, battle, etc. but not known to have been killed
examples: SEE ALSO MIA
He was reported missing, presumed dead.
Many soldiers were listed as missing in action.
It was six hours before the seamen were discovered missing.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not included, often when it should have been
examples: Fill in the missing words in this text.
There were several candidates missing from the list.
What is missing from the production is any sense of emotional commitment.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an important official job that a person or group of people is given to do, especially when they are sent to another country
examples: She led a recent trade mission to China.
Thomas More toured Antwerp on a diplomatic mission for the king.
It was too late to launch a rescue mission.
They undertook a fact-finding mission in the region.
a mercy mission to aid homeless refugees

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of people doing such a job; the place where they work
examples: He is the head of the British mission in Berlin.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the work of teaching people about Christianity, especially in a foreign country; a group of people doing such work
examples: Gandhi’s attitude to mission and conversion
a Catholic mission in Africa
She took up a position as a school teacher at St Peter's mission in Montana.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a building or group of buildings used by a Christian mission

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: particular work that you feel it is your duty to do
examples: SYNONYM vocation
Her mission in life was to work with the homeless.
We are committed to the mission of helping students realize their full potential.
You can tell by the determined way he talks that he is a man with a mission.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an important job that is done by a soldier, group of soldiers, etc.
examples: The squadron flew on a reconnaissance mission.
The military are fulfilling an important peacekeeping mission.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a flight into space
examples: a US space mission
He's been on several shuttle missions over the last decade.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a task or journey that is very difficult and takes a long time to complete
examples: It's a mission to get there.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used when you have successfully completed what you have had to do
examples: Mission accomplished, we headed for home.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a difficult or impossible task
examples: Many regard this task as mission impossible.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an action or an opinion that is not correct, or that produces a result that you did not want
examples: It's easy to make a mistake.
Don't worry, we all make mistakes.
You are making a big mistake.
Leaving school so young was the biggest mistake of my life.
a terrible/serious/huge mistake
It’s a common mistake (= one that a lot of people make).
You must try to learn from your mistakes.
He is determined not to repeat the mistakes of his predecessors.
This letter is addressed to someone else—there must be some mistake.
I made the mistake of giving him my address.
It would be a mistake to ignore his opinion.
It was a big mistake on my part to have trusted her.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a word, figure, etc. that is not said or written down correctly
examples: SYNONYM error
It's a common mistake among learners of English.
Her essay is full of spelling mistakes.
If students correct their own mistakes, learning improves.
The waiter made a mistake (in) adding up the bill.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to show that you are sure about the truth of what you have just said
examples: This is a strange business and no mistake.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: by accident; without intending to
examples: I took your bag instead of mine by mistake.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: thinking that something is something else
examples: Children may eat pills in mistake for sweets.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to emphasize what you are saying, especially when you want to warn somebody about something
examples: Make no mistake (about it), this is one crisis that won’t just go away.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if two or more substances or things mix or you mix them, they combine, usually in a way that means they cannot easily be separated
examples: Oil and water do not mix.
Oil does not mix with water.
Grief mixed with fear and rage as the people surveyed the ruins of their homes.
Mix all the ingredients together in a bowl.
If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
I don't like to mix business with pleasure (= combine social events with doing business).
Smith often mixed sand into her paint to create a textured surface.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to prepare something by combining two or more different substances
examples: With this range of paints, you can mix your own colours.
Be sure to mix the solution properly .
Why don't you mix a cocktail for our guests?
Why don't you mix our guests a cocktail?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if two or more things, people or activities do not mix, they are likely to cause problems or danger if they are combined
examples: Children and fireworks don't mix.
These pills won't mix well with alcohol.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to meet and talk to different people, especially at social events
examples: SYNONYM socialize
We've worked together for years but never mixed socially.
They don't mix much with the neighbours.
She mixed happily with the other children.
I don't really mix with people my own age.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to combine different recordings of voices and/or instruments to produce a single piece of music
examples: Up to eight tracks can be mixed simultaneously.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be/become involved in something, especially something illegal or dishonest
examples: Don't tell me you're mixed up in all of this?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be/become friendly with or involved with somebody that other people do not approve of
examples: He got mixed up with a crowd who were into drugs and crime.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to combine things in different ways for different purposes
examples: You can mix and match courses to suit your requirements.
This mix-and-match approach will appeal to a variety of players.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to argue with somebody or cause trouble

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to do something differently from the way it is usually done
examples: The show has been the same for ten years, so it’s time to mix it up.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: consisting of different qualities or elements
examples: SEE ALSO ready-mixed
a mixed diet
beaches with mixed sand and shingle

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having both good and bad qualities or feelings
examples: I still have mixed feelings about going to Brazil (= I am not sure what to think).
I listened to her story with mixed emotions.
These studies have produced mixed results.
The results were decidedly mixed.
The weather has been very mixed recently.
Having a famous father can be a mixed blessing.
The play was given a mixed reception by the critics (= some liked it, some did not).
The film met with a mixed reaction from viewers and critics.
British athletes had mixed fortunes in yesterday's competition.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: consisting of different kinds of people, for example, people from different races and cultures
examples: an ethnically mixed community
people of mixed race
a mixed marriage (= between two people of different races or religions)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: consisting of different types of the same thing
examples: a mixed salad
I served chicken with mixed vegetables.
a mixed woodland of ash, oak and birch
The students in the class are of mixed ability (= different levels of ability).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: of or for both males and females
examples: a mixed school
I'd rather not talk about it in mixed company.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a combination of different things
examples: SEE ALSO dolly mixture

The city is a mixture of old and new buildings.
We listened to the news with a mixture of surprise and horror.
Anger is often caused by frustration or embarrassment, or a mixture of the two.
pastries filled with a mixture of nuts, sugar and rose water

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a substance made by mixing other substances together
examples: SEE ALSO cough mixture
Spread the cake mixture into a greased baking tin.
Add the eggs to the mixture and beat well.
Gradually fold the flour into the egg mixture.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a combination of two or more substances that mix together without any chemical reaction taking place
examples: COMPARE compound
Exposures to chemical mixtures have produced unexpected effects.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of mixing different substances togetherWord Origin

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large crowd of people, especially one that may become violent or cause trouble

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: the surface of the moon
the first man to walk on the moon

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: SEE ALSO full moon
a crescent moon

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: Politicians promise the moon before an election, but things are different afterwards.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with principles of right and wrong behaviour
examples: a moral issue/dilemma
traditional moral values
a decline in moral standards
moral and ethical questions
The basic moral philosophies of most world religions are remarkably similar.
He was a deeply religious man with a highly developed moral sense.
The newspapers were full of moral outrage at the weakness of other countries.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: based on your own sense of what is right and fair, not on legal rights or duties
examples: SYNONYM ethical
moral responsibility/duty/authority
We have a moral imperative to help whenever we can.
I make no moral judgement on this decision.
Governments have at least a moral obligation to answer these questions.
Children learn to develop their own moral code for adulthood.
The job was to call on all her diplomatic skills and moral courage (= the courage to do what you think is right).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: following the standards of behaviour considered acceptable and right by most people
examples: SYNONYM good
He led a very moral life.
a very moral person
We try to teach our students to be conscientious, moral young people.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: able to understand the difference between right and wrong
examples: Children are not naturally moral beings.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to claim that your side of an argument is morally better than your opponents’ side; to argue in a way that makes your side seem morally better
examples: I was angry with his blatant attempt to take the moral high ground.
