definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small animal that is covered in fur and has a long thin tail. Mice live in fields, in people’s houses or where food is stored.
examples: SEE ALSO dormouse
a house mouse
The stores were overrun with rats and mice.
She crept upstairs, quiet as a mouse.
He was a weak little mouse of a man.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small device that is moved by hand across a surface to control the movement of the cursor on a computer screen
examples: Use the mouse to drag the icon to a new position.
I prefer a wireless mouse.
The keyboard and mouse are wireless devices.
Click the left mouse button twice to highlight the program.
With simple mouse clicks, the viewer can navigate the room.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to play a cruel game with somebody in your power by changing your behaviour very often, so that they become nervous and do not know what to expect
examples: He thought the police were playing some elaborate game of cat and mouse and waiting to trap him.
Young car thieves enjoy playing cat and mouse with the police.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: people enjoy themselves more and behave with greater freedom when the person in charge of them is not thereWord Origin
examples: Old English mūs, (plural) mȳs, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch muis and German Maus, from an Indo-European root shared by Latin and Greek mus.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the opening in the face used for speaking, eating, etc.; the area inside the head behind this opening
examples: SEE ALSO foot-and-mouth disease
She opened her mouth to say something.
His mouth twisted into a wry smile.
Their mouths fell open (= they were surprised).
Don't talk with your mouth full (= when eating).
The creature was foaming/frothing at the mouth.
Cover your mouth when you cough.
The adult bird drops the worms into the mouths of the hungry chicks.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person considered only as somebody who needs to be provided with food
examples: Now there would be another mouth to feed.
The world will not be able to support all these extra hungry mouths.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the place where a river joins the sea
examples: A number of industries sprang up around the mouth of the river.
Pelicans are found close to river mouths.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the entrance or opening of something
examples: SEE ALSO goalmouth
the mouth of a cave/pit
Up ahead was the tunnel mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a particular way of speaking
examples: SEE ALSO loudmouth
He has a foul mouth on him!
Watch your mouth! (= stop saying things that are rude and/or offensive)

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: having the type or shape of mouth mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO open-mouthed
a wide-mouthed old woman
a narrow-mouthed cave

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: having a particular way of speaking
examples: SEE ALSO foul-mouthed
a rather crude-mouthed individual

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if you say somebody is all mouth, you mean that they talk a lot about doing something, but are, in fact, not brave enough to do it

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: having rich parents

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody seems to be innocent, kind, etc. when they are not really

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: because people tell each other and not because they read about it
examples: The news spread by word of mouth.
The restaurant does not advertise, but relies on word of mouth for custom.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: unhappy and depressed

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to have a mass of small bubbles in and around its mouth, especially because it is sick or angry
examples: The dog started foaming at the mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be very angry

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: given by somebody who is directly involved and therefore likely to be accurate

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be bad at keeping secrets

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to talk too much, especially about your own abilities and achievements

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: somebody feels nervous or frightened about something
examples: My heart was in my mouth as I opened the envelope.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to not talk about something to somebody because it is a secret or because it will upset or annoy them
examples: I've warned them to keep their mouths shut about this.
Now she's upset—why couldn't you keep your mouth shut?
The athletes were warned to keep their mouths shut about politics.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to make you feel upset or ashamed afterwards
examples: The whole business left a bad taste in my mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to spend all the money you earn on basic needs such as food without being able to save any money
examples: SEE ALSO hand-to-mouth

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to refuse or criticize something that is given to you for nothing
examples: I’m never one to look a gift horse in the mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: used when you realize that you have said something that you should not have said

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to be soft and very good to eat
examples: They serve steaks that just melt in your mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: used when a small child has just said something that seems very wise or clever

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to say or do something that upsets, offends or embarrasses somebody
examples: I really put my foot in my mouth with Ella—I didn't know she'd split up with Tom.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to support what you say by doing something practical; to show by your actions that you really mean something

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to suggest that somebody has said something when in fact they have not
examples: He felt after the interview that the police officers had been trying to put words into his mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to talk too much, in a way that is not sensible

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to talk about something in a way that shows that you are too proud of it

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to talk about something that is private or secret

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: a rude way of telling somebody to be quiet or stop talking

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to take away somebody’s job so that they are no longer able to earn enough money to live

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to say what somebody else was going to say
examples: I was about to say we should cancel the trip, but she took the words right out of my mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to be careful what you say in order not to offend somebody or make them angryWord Origin
examples: Old English mūth, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch mond and German Mund, from an Indo-European root shared by Latin mentum ‘chin’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to change position or make somebody/something change position in a way that can be seen, heard or felt
examples: Don't move—stay perfectly still.
The bus was already moving when I jumped onto it.
The ball was really moving (= moving fast) when it reached him.
He could hear someone moving around in the room above.
Phil moved towards the window.
You can hardly move in this pub on Saturdays (= because it is so crowded).
You can't move for books in her room.
Temperatures will drop as the cold front moves down across France.
I can't move my fingers.
We moved our chairs a little nearer.
She moved the ball toward the opponent's goal.
He moved his arm away from his face.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to change the place where you live, have your work, etc.
examples: We don't like it here so we've decided to move.
The company's moving to Scotland.
People move from place to place today in ever greater numbers.
She's been all on her own since her daughter moved away.
We moved house last week.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody change from one job, class, etc. to another
examples: SYNONYM transfer
I'm being moved to the New York office.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to change the position of a piece
examples: It's your turn to move.
She moved her queen.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to leave, begin something, etc. quickly
examples: Let's move—it's time we went shopping.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to change; to change something
examples: SYNONYM shift
The government has not moved on this issue.
Things have moved on a lot since the days when I was young.
Let's move the meeting to Wednesday.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make progress in the way or direction mentioned
examples: SYNONYM progress
Time is moving on.
Share prices moved ahead today.
After that, things moved forward at lightning speed
Things are not moving as fast as we hoped.
Things certainly move fast in the blogosphere.
Finally things are moving in the right direction.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to take action; to do something
examples: SYNONYM act
The police moved quickly to dispel the rumours.
The firm has moved to reassure customers that they will continue to provide good service.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to cause somebody to have strong feelings, especially of sympathy or of being sad
examples: SEE ALSO moving
We were deeply moved by her plight.
Grown men were moved to tears at the horrific scenes.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to cause somebody to do something
examples: SYNONYM prompt
She felt moved to address the crowd.
He works when the spirit moves him (= when he wants to).

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to sell goods; to be sold
examples: How quickly can we move this stock?
These copies are moving fast—they'll soon be sold out.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to suggest something formally so that it can be discussed and decided
examples: SYNONYM put forward
The Opposition moved an amendment to the Bill.
I move that a vote be taken on this.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a rude way of telling somebody to hurry
examples: If you get your ass in gear, we can make it out of here tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to begin, leave, etc. quickly
examples: It's late—we'd better get moving.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to cause something to make progress
examples: The new director has really got things moving.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: in the future, starting from now
examples: We have a very solid financial position going forward.
The strategy going forward is still undecided.
Moving forward, we need to have a real plan.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to change and develop your ideas, way of working, etc. so that you do what is modern and what is expected
examples: Many complained that the Royal Family had failed to move with the times.

definitions.label: Meaning 18

examples: If you move your ass, we can make it out of here tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to do everything you possibly can in order to achieve something

definitions.definition: to do something more quickly because there is not much time
examples: Move it! We’re going to be late!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act of moving the body or part of the body
examples: hand/eye movements
She observed the gentle movement of his chest as he breathed.
Loose clothing gives you greater freedom of movement.
Power comes from the forward movement of the entire body.
Troy watched her every movement.
There was a sudden movement in the undergrowth.
The dance combined colour, movement and music.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an act of moving from one place to another or of moving something from one place to another
examples: SEE ALSO pincer movement
enemy troop movements
laws to allow free movement of goods and services
the mass movement of herds of wildebeest

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: SEE ALSO civil rights movement

the labour movement
the civil rights movement
the Romantic movement (= for example in literature)
to build/join/support a movement
She led a movement for women's rights.
a mass movement for change

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person’s activities over a period of time, especially as watched by somebody else
examples: The police are keeping a close watch on the suspect's movements.
to track/monitor somebody's movements

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a slow steady change in what people in society do or think
examples: SYNONYM trend
We see a big movement away from cash.
a movement towards greater sexual equality

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: progress, especially in a particular task
examples: It needs cooperation from all the countries to get any movement in arms control.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a change in amount
examples: There has been no movement in oil prices.
We have no further movement to make on the offer.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: any of the main parts that a long piece of music is divided into
examples: the slow movement of the First Concerto

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: an act of emptying waste material from the bowels; the waste material that is emptiedWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: via Old French from medieval Latin movimentum, from Latin movere ‘to move’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a series of moving pictures recorded with sound that tells a story, watched at a movie theater or on a television or other device
examples: SYNONYM film
You'll love this movie.
Let's watch a movie tonight.
Have you seen the latest Miyazaki movie?
to rent/download a movie
to make a horror movie
a movie starring Jennifer Lawrence
a famous movie director
the Hollywood movie industry
a movie studio

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: when you go to the movies, you go to a movie theater to see a movie
examples: Let's go to the movies.
This weekend at the movies I felt like a kid again.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: movies as an art or an industry
examples: I've always wanted to work in the movies.
Is it glamorous like in the movies?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: causing strong, often sad, feelings about somebody/something
examples: a deeply moving experience
a moving story/speech

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: changing from one place or position to another
examples: the moving parts of a machine
fast-moving water
a moving target

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used with uncountable nouns, especially in negative sentences to mean ‘a large amount of something’, or after ‘how’ to ask about the amount of something. It is also used with ‘as’, ‘so’ and ‘too’.
examples: I don't have much money with me.
‘Got any money?’ ‘Not much.’
How much water do you need?
How much is it (= What does it cost)?
Take as much time as you like.
There was so much traffic that we were an hour late.
I've got far too much to do.
I lay awake for much of the night.
There was much discussion about the reasons for the failure.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the same
examples: Please help me get this job—you know I would do as much for you.
‘Roger stole the money.’ ‘I thought as much.’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that something is difficult to do
examples: No dessert for me, thanks. It was as much as I could do to finish the main course.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not fair or not reasonable
examples: It's a bit much calling me at three in the morning.
The noise from next door is getting a bit much.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to treat something/somebody as very important
examples: He always makes much of his humble origins.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that there is little difference between two things
examples: I won, but there wasn't much in it (= our scores were nearly the same).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not a good…
examples: He's not much of a tennis player.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to introduce something positive or definite
examples: I'll say this much for him—he never leaves a piece of work unfinished.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a situation or experience that is too difficult to deal with
examples: It all proved too much for him.

Heavy rain caused thick, deep mud on the site.
mud bricks/huts (= made of dried mud)
nests made of mud or clay

examples: Oh well, that's all as clear as mud, then.

2 multiplied by 4 is/equals/makes 8 (= 2 × 4  =  8).

If you are cooking for more people, just multiply up the quantities.

expectant/new/young/teenage mums
stay-at-home/working mums

examples: municipal elections/councils
municipal workers
the Los Angeles Municipal Art Gallery

definitions.definition: to scream loudly and for a long time, especially in order to protest about somethingWord Origin
examples: Old English morthor, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch moord and German Mord, from an Indo-European root shared by Sanskrit mará ‘death’ and Latin mors; reinforced in Middle English by Old French murdre.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the crime of killing somebody deliberately
examples: SYNONYM homicide
He was found guilty of murder.
She has been charged with the attempted murder of her husband.
Who is responsible for this brutal murder?
to commit (a) murder
He was arrested on suspicion of murder.
a murder case/investigation/charge/trial
The rebels were responsible for the mass murder of 400 civilians.
the families of the murder victims
What was the murder weapon?
The play is a murder mystery.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to describe something that is difficult or unpleasant
examples: It's murder trying to get to the airport at this time of day.
It was murder (= very busy and unpleasant) in the office today.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to do whatever you want without being stopped or punished
examples: They let their children get away with murder!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to scream loudly and for a long time, especially in order to protest about somethingWord Origin
examples: Old English morthor, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch moord and German Mord, from an Indo-European root shared by Sanskrit mará ‘death’ and Latin mors; reinforced in Middle English by Old French murdre.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of body tissue that you make tight and relax in order to move a particular part of the body; the tissue that forms the muscles of the body
examples: SEE ALSO abductor (2)
a calf/neck/thigh muscle
All of this put strain on the heart muscle.
to pull/tear/strain a muscle
He poses and flexes his muscles in the mirror.
This exercise will work the muscles of the lower back.
Contract and relax the muscles in your fingers a few times.
She tried to relax her tense muscles.
He felt every muscle in his body tighten.
He didn't move a muscle (= stood completely still).
Lift weights to build muscle.
muscle fibre/tissue/mass

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: physical strength
examples: He's an intelligent player but lacks the muscle of older competitors.
I exerted every ounce of my miserable muscle power.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the power and influence to make others do what you want
examples: to exercise political/industrial/financial muscle
The countries tried to flex their collective muscle.
This show gives the artist the chance to flex his creative muscle.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a building in which objects of artistic, cultural, historical or scientific interest are kept and shown to the public
examples: SEE ALSO folk museum
a museum of modern art
a science museum
They visited museums and galleries throughout the city.
He's the director of a new museum.
The items will go on display at the museum next year.
a museum director/curator
Her prints are in major museum collections.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: sounds that are arranged in a way that is pleasant or exciting to listen to. People sing music or play it on instruments.
examples: SEE ALSO absolute music
I like any kind of pop or dance music.
He plays traditional Asian music.
People often choose to listen to music that suits their moods and activities.
She could hear music playing somewhere.
to stream/share/download music
to write/compose music
to perform/record music
Every week they get together to make music (= to play music or sing).
the popularity of Mozart’s music
It was a charming piece of music.
The poem has been set to music (= music has been written for it)
Birmingham's live music scene
music lovers/fans
Every summer he runs a three-day music festival.
The band released a music video on YouTube today.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the art of writing or playing music
examples: He studied music in Moscow.
a career in music
a music teacher
music lessons
the music business/industry

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the written or printed signs that represent the sounds to be played or sung in a piece of music
examples: SEE ALSO sheet music
Can you read music (= understand the signs in order to play or sing a piece of music)?
I had to play it without the music.
The music (= the paper or book with the musical notes on it) was still open on the piano.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to accept and deal with criticism or punishment for something you have done
examples: The others all ran off, leaving me to face the music.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: news or information that you are very pleased to hearWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French musique, via Latin from Greek mousikē (tekhnē) ‘(art) of the Muses’, from mousa ‘muse’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with music; containing music
examples: musical styles/tastes
to have exceptional musical talent
He was one of the greatest musical talents of all time.
a first-rate musical performance
a musical production/entertainment
a diverse range of musical genres
She had a brilliant career in musical theatre.
A jazz band provided the musical accompaniment to the meal.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: with a natural skill or interest in music
examples: OPPOSITE unmusical
She's very musical.
a highly musical nation
I grew up in a very musical family.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: pleasant to listen to, like music
examples: a musical voice
The language often sounds musical.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who plays a musical instrument or writes music, especially as a job
examples: a jazz/rock/classical musician
She has been a professional musician for over 25 years.
The competition recognizes talented young musicians.
A group of local musicians entertained the guests.
The pipes were played by Irish musician, John Burney.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to say that something is necessary or very important (sometimes involving a rule or a law)
examples: All visitors must report to reception.
Cars must not park in front of the entrance (= it is not allowed).
I must ask you not to do that again.
You mustn't say things like that.
I must go and get the kids from school.
I must admit (= I feel that I should admit) I was surprised it cost so little.
Must you always question everything I say? (= it is annoying)
‘Do we have to finish this today?’ ‘Yes, you must.’

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that something is likely or logical
examples: You must be hungry after all that walking.
He must have known (= surely he knew) what she wanted.
I'm sorry, she's not here. She must have left already (= that must be the explanation).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to recommend that somebody does something because you think it is a good idea
examples: You simply must read this book.
We must get together soon for lunch.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody may do something but you do not really want them to
examples: ‘Can I smoke?’ ‘If you must.’
It's from my boyfriend, if you must know.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to tell people that something is so good or interesting that they should see, read, get it, etc.
examples: Sydney is one of the world's must-see cities.
The magazine is a must-read in the show business world.
This is on my must-do list.
a must-have for any fan

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: in certain situations it is necessary for you to do something that you do not like or enjoyWord Origin
examples: Old English mōste, past tense of mōt ‘may’, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch moeten and German müssen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to describe feelings that two or more people have for each other equally, or actions that affect two or more people equally
examples: mutual respect/understanding
mutual support/aid
They parted by mutual consent.
I don't like her, and I think the feeling is mutual (= she doesn't like me either).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: shared by two or more people
examples: We met at the home of a mutual friend.
They soon discovered a mutual interest in music.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: of or belonging to the speaker or writer
examples: Where's my passport?
My feet are cold.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used in exclamations to express surprise, etc.
examples: My goodness! Look at the time.
Oh my! What are we going to do?
My my Megan, I do believe you 're jealous!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used when speaking to somebody, to show love
examples: my dear/darling/love

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used when speaking to somebody that you consider to have a lower status than you
examples: My dear girl, you're wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used when the speaker or writer is also the person affected by an action
examples: I cut myself on a knife.
I wrote a message to myself.
I found myself unable to speak.
I haven't been feeling myself recently (= I have not felt well).
I needed space to be myself (= not influenced by other people).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the fact that the speaker is doing something
examples: I'll speak to her myself.
I myself do not agree.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: alone; without anyone else
examples: I live by myself.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: without help
examples: I painted the room all by myself.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: for the speaker or writer alone to have or use; not shared
examples: I had a whole pizza to myself.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: difficult to understand or explain; strange
examples: He died in mysterious circumstances.
the mysterious disappearance of his wife
Fate works in mysterious ways.
the events that led up to her mysterious death by drowning
A mysterious illness is affecting all the animals.
The whole thing was very mysterious.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: seeming strange or secret
examples: The gardens looked dark and mysterious in the twilight.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: strange and interesting because you do not know much about them
examples: SYNONYM enigmatic
She meets a mysterious stranger who offers to help her.
Her last years remain somewhat mysterious.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not saying much about something, especially when other people want to know more
examples: He was being very mysterious about where he was going.
Why are they being so mysterious?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that is difficult to understand or to explain
examples: It is one of the great unsolved mysteries of this century.
Their motives remain a mystery.
She tried to solve the mystery of the boy's sudden death.
It's a complete mystery to me why they chose him.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is strange and interesting because you do not know much about them or it
examples: He's a bit of a mystery.
There was a mystery guest on the programme.
The mystery man's identity remains hidden.
a mystery disease/illness/virus
a mystery tour (= when you do not know where you are going)
My sister is a complete mystery to me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of being difficult to understand or to explain, especially when this makes somebody/something seem interesting and exciting
examples: Mystery surrounds her disappearance.
His past is shrouded in mystery (= not much is known about it).
The dark glasses give her an air of mystery.
She’s a woman of mystery.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a story, a film or a play in which crimes and strange events are only explained at the end
examples: He is the author of several murder mysteries.
The film is based on Daphne DuMaurier's mystery novel, ‘Rebecca’.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: secret religious ceremonies; secret knowledge
examples: the teacher who initiated me into the mysteries of mathematics

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a religious belief that cannot be explained or proved in a scientific way
examples: the mystery of creation

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a story from ancient times, especially one that was told to explain natural events or to describe the early history of a people; this type of story
examples: SYNONYM legend
ancient Greek myths
a creation myth (= that explains how the world began)
the heroes of myth and legend

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that many people believe but that does not exist or is false
examples: SYNONYM fallacy
It is time to dispel the myth of a classless society (= to show that it does not exist).
Contrary to popular myth, women are not worse drivers than men.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the thin hard layer covering the outer tip of the fingers or toes
examples: SEE ALSO fingernail
Stop biting your nails!
nail clippers

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small thin pointed piece of metal with a flat head, used for joining pieces of wood together or hanging things on a wall
examples: COMPARE screw
She hammered the nail in.
He knocked the nail into the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to fight in a very determined way for what you want
examples: The residents are fighting tooth and nail to stop the new development.
She fought tooth and nail to keep custody of the children.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: showing no fear, sympathy or kind behaviour

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to say something that is exactly right

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: something that makes the end or failure of an organization, somebody’s plans, etc. more likely to happen
examples: This latest defeat is another nail in the government's coffin.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: without delay
examples: They're good customers who always pay on the nail.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: very strong and able to deal successfully with difficult conditions or situations
examples: She's almost 90 but she's still as tough as nails.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not wearing any clothes
examples: SYNONYM bare
She was clutching the sheet around her naked body.
Her blonde hair fell over her naked shoulders.
He was naked from the waist up.
They often wandered around the house stark naked (= completely naked).
They found him half naked and bleeding to death.
The prisoners were stripped naked.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: with nothing to cover it
examples: SYNONYM bare
a naked light
a naked sword
Mice are born naked (= without fur).
a naked flame

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: expressed strongly and not hidden
examples: naked aggression
Revealed: the naked truth about your favourite soap stars.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: unable to protect yourself from being harmed, criticized, etc.
examples: SYNONYM helpless
He still felt naked and drained after his ordeal.
Never had he felt so completely naked.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the normal power of your eyes without the help of an instrument
examples: The planet should be visible with/to the naked eye.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a word or words that a particular person, animal, place or thing is known by
examples: SEE ALSO assumed name
What's your name?
What is/was the name, please? (= a polite way of asking somebody’s name)
Please write your full name and address below.
Leave your name and number (= phone number) and we'll call you later.
Are you changing your name when you get married?
She uses her married name at work.
The singer's real name is Bob Rich.
His full name was William Augustus Grove.
His father was a painter of the same name.
Do you know the name of this flower?
Rubella is just another name for German measles.
The company reopened under a new name.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a reputation that somebody/something has; the opinion that people have about somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO good name
She first made her name as a writer of children's books.
He's made quite a name for himself (= become famous).
The college has a good name for languages.
This kind of behaviour gives students a bad name.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having a name or a reputation of the kind mentioned, especially one that is known by a lot of people
examples: SEE ALSO household name
a big-name company
brand-name goods

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a famous person
examples: SEE ALSO no-name (1)
He is a big name in the world of rock music.
Some of the biggest names in the art world were at the party.
The event attracted many famous names from the past.
The movie needs some names in it, if it’s going to be successful.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be called something
examples: The dog was an ugly brute, answering to the name of Spike.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody has a lot of a particular quality
examples: ‘Patience’ is my middle name!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an important person

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: using the name of somebody/something
examples: She asked for you by name.
The principal knows all the students by name.
I only know her by name (= I have heard about her but I have not met her).
The head teacher knows every child in the school by name.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: who is called
examples: a young actor by the name of Tom Rees

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to use offensive words about somebody
examples: Stop calling me names!

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to criticize or say bad things about somebody in public, in a way that is unfair
examples: The paper has dragged his name through the mud.
They feel their agency has been dragged through the mud by the press.
Football's good name is being dragged through the dirt.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to mention famous people you know or have met in order to impress others
examples: RELATED NOUN name-dropping
She found him rather irritating to talk to; all he did was drop names.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to apply for a place at a school, in a competition, etc. for somebody or yourself
examples: Have you entered your name for the quiz yet?
They’ve already put his name down for Eton College.
Have you put your name down for the school play?

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: when a person already has a bad reputation, it is difficult to change it because others will continue to blame or suspect him/her

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to discover or invent something which then becomes known by your name
examples: Henry Hudson gave his name to New York's Hudson River.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to use a name that may not be your real one
examples: a thief who goes by the name of ‘The Cat’
He goes by the name of Jonno.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: if something has your name on it, or there is something with your name on it, it is intended for you
examples: He took my place and got killed. It should have been me—that bullet had my name on it.
Are you coming for dinner this evening? I've got a steak here with your name on it!

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to describe a situation which exists in reality but that is not officially recognized
examples: He runs the company in all but name.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: used especially in questions to show that you are angry, surprised or shocked
examples: What in God's name was that noise?
Where in the name of Heaven have you been?

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: for somebody; showing that something officially belongs to somebody
examples: We reserved two tickets in the name of Brown.
The car is registered in my name.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: using the authority of somebody/something; as a representative of somebody/something
examples: I arrest you in the name of the law.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to give a reason or an excuse for doing something, often when what you are doing is wrong
examples: crimes committed in the name of religion

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: officially recognized but not existing in reality
examples: He's party leader in name only.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to let it be known in public that you support or agree with something
examples: I am more than happy to lend my name to this campaign.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to have a place named after you

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody is not liked or popular because of something they have done
examples: Your name’s mud around here at the moment!
If you tell our secret your name will be mud round here.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to give the names of the people involved in something, especially something wrong or illegal
examples: He has accused the government of corruption and claims he is prepared to name names.
Detectives believe that a hitman was sent to silence the witness before he could name names.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: the most important aspect of an activity; the most important quality needed for an activity
examples: Hard work is the name of the game if you want to succeed in business.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is well known and respected in a particular field
examples: Miyazaki is still a name to conjure with among anime fans.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: used when you mention a name that you think is difficult to remember or pronounce
examples: He comes from Tighnabruaich—now there's a name to conjure with!

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to know or remember what somebody/something is called
examples: I recognize the tune but I can't put a name to it.
I nodded, desperately trying to put a name to the face.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to have a name that sounds funny
examples: He rejoiced in the name of Owen Owen.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: what is important is what people or things are, not what they are called

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to show a lack of respect when using somebody’s name or when talking about them
examples: Have you been taking my name in vain again?
to take the Lord's name in vain

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to have or own something
examples: an Olympic athlete with five gold medals to his name
She doesn’t have a penny/cent to her name (= she is very poor).

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: using a name that may not be your real name
examples: The room was booked under a false name.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: what is important is what people or things are, not what they are called

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to show a lack of respect when using somebody’s name or when talking about them
examples: Have you been taking my name in vain again?
to take the Lord's name in vain

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to have or own something
examples: an Olympic athlete with five gold medals to his name
She doesn’t have a penny/cent to her name (= she is very poor).

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: using a name that may not be your real name
examples: The room was booked under a false name.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to introduce more exact and detailed information about something that you have just mentioned
examples: We need to concentrate on our target audience, namely women aged between 20 and 30.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a description of events
examples: SYNONYM story
a gripping narrative of their journey up the Amazon
a collection of personal narratives
She has woven a strong personal narrative filled with lively anecdotes.
a historical narrative of the United States
The film lacks a coherent, compelling narrative.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the part of a novel that tells the story, rather than the dialogue
examples: The novel contains too much dialogue and not enough narrative.
The book is written in the style of first-person narrative.
interruptions to the narrative flow

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a way of explaining events to illustrate a set of aims or values
examples: a new narrative about economic globalization
How do we construct a new narrative about economic globalization?
Politicians create narrative from scant facts on a daily basis.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: measuring a short distance from one side to the other, especially in relation to length
examples: OPPOSITE broad
Stray dogs wander the steep narrow lanes of the old town.
The road soon became narrower and steeper.
a narrow bed/doorway/shelf
Tall narrow windows admit only slivers of light.
narrow shoulders/hips
There was only a narrow gap between the bed and the wall.
Farming is confined to a narrow strip of land between the mountains and the sea.
the narrow confines of prison life

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: only just achieved or avoided
examples: a narrow victory
She was elected by a narrow majority.
He had a narrow escape when his car skidded on the ice.
He lost the race by the narrowest of margins.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: limited in variety or numbers
examples: SYNONYM restricted
The shop sells only a narrow range of goods.
She only has a narrow circle of friends.
The exhibition is disappointingly narrow in scope.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: limited in a way that ignores important issues or the opinions of other people
examples: OPPOSITE broad
narrow interests
She has a very narrow view of the world.
I found the focus of the debate too narrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: limited in meaning; exact
examples: OPPOSITE broad
I am using the word ‘education’ in the narrower sense.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the honest and morally acceptable way of living
examples: His wife is trying to keep him on the straight and narrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very bad or unpleasant
examples: He had a nasty accident.
The news gave me a nasty shock.
I got a nasty surprise when I opened the door and saw who was there.
I had a nasty feeling that he would follow me.
This coffee has a nasty taste.
Don't buy that coat—it looks cheap and nasty.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: unkind; unpleasant
examples: SYNONYM mean
She's always making nasty remarks about people.
the nastier side of her character
He has a nasty temper.
Life has a nasty habit of repeating itself.
That was a nasty little trick.
Some of these reality TV shows can be downright nasty. .
Don't be so nasty to your brother.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: dangerous or serious
examples: a nasty bend (= dangerous for cars going fast)
a nasty injury
gang warfare of a thoroughly nasty kind

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: offensive; in bad taste
examples: SEE ALSO video nasty
to have a nasty mind
nasty jokes

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to start making threats or become violent
examples: You'd better do what he says or he'll turn nasty.
After the game, things turned nasty and there were fights in the streets.
Things could turn nasty if we're not careful.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to become bad or unpleasant
examples: It looks as though the weather is going to turn nasty again.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make you feel upset or ashamed afterwards
examples: The whole business left a bad taste in my mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a person who is unpleasant, unkind or dishonest
examples: Don’t trust him; he’s a nasty piece of work.
He's a thoroughly nasty piece of work.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a country considered as a group of people with the same language, culture and history, who live in a particular area under one government
examples: SEE ALSO rainbow nation
European/Arab/Asian nations
The African nations have been particularly affected.
Developing nations need affordable access to drugs and medication.
Fewer and fewer people in industrialized nations actually know where their food comes from.
Leaders of the nations signed a declaration of support.
This is an important moment in our nation's history.
Germans celebrated yesterday in Berlin, the nation's capital.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: all the people in a country
examples: SYNONYM population
The entire nation, it seemed, was watching TV.
They are a nation of food lovers.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with a particular nation; shared by a whole nation
examples: Decide whether it would be better to advertise in a national or a local newspaper.
national and international news
national and regional politics
decisions made at a local rather than national level
a national election
a coach for the national basketball team
The protection of public health is a matter of national security.
It is in the national interest to have a public enquiry.
The national average is just over two children per family.
They are afraid of losing their national identity.
These buildings are part of our national heritage.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: owned, controlled or paid for by the government
examples: a national airline/museum/theatre
the National Health Service

examples: a nationwide campaign

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the place where you were born and lived for the first years of your life
examples: SEE ALSO native speaker
your native land/country/city
Her native language is Korean.
It is a long time since he has visited his native Chile.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with the place where you have always lived or have lived for a long time
examples: native Berliners

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: connected with the people who originally lived in a country before other people, especially white people, came there
examples: The native peoples depend on the forest for their livelihoods.
The island's native population began disappearing due to exposure to diseases.
native art
The festival is a celebration of native art and culture.
a record of Native American life

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: existing naturally in a place
examples: SYNONYM indigenous
the native plants of America
native species
The tiger is native to India.
Some animals are in danger because their native habitat is being destroyed.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: that you have naturally without having to learn it
examples: SYNONYM innate
native cunning
He had to rely on his native wit.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: found in a pure state
examples: native gold/silver/copper
Native copper was probably the first metal to be made into tools and weapons.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: designed for or built into a particular system, especially using the language or computer code associated with a particular computer or processor
examples: Native apps still generally perform better than web apps, but the gap is shrinking.
Early programmers worked in native computer code or machine language.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to try to live and behave like the local people
examples: You will be able to meet local people, eat local food and ‘go native’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: existing in nature; not made or caused by humans
examples: COMPARE supernatural
the natural world (= of trees, rivers, animals and birds)
We should respect animals and the natural environment, which is their home.
a country’s natural resources (= its coal, oil, forests, etc.)
wildlife in its natural habitat
The natural beauty of flowers inspired Monet's experiments in colour.
All the materials used are natural.
My hair soon grew back to its natural colour (= after being dyed).
The clothes are available in warm natural colours.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having little or no processing
examples: natural yogurt (= with no flavour added)
I try to eat a sugar-free, natural food diet.
Natural treatments have no unwanted side effects.
We made bread with a natural raising agent.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: normal; as you would expect
examples: COMPARE unnatural
to die of natural causes (= not by violence, but normally, of old age)
Singing for her was as natural as breathing.
He thought social inequality was all part of the natural order of things.
She was the natural choice for the job.
It's only natural to worry about your children.
It's perfectly natural for you to feel annoyed.
It's natural that he would want to see his own son.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to describe behaviour or abilities that are part of the character that a person or an animal was born with
examples: the natural agility of a cat
the natural processes of language learning
She has a natural ability with children.
Daniel's natural talent is for engineering.
It was my natural instinct to defend myself.
When body temperature is beginning to fall there is a natural tendency to fall asleep.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: having an ability that you were born with
examples: He's a natural leader.
She's a natural rebel.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: relaxed and not pretending to be somebody/something different
examples: It's difficult to look natural when you're feeling nervous.
There's something really natural about her.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: related by blood
examples: His natural mother was unable to care for him so he was raised by an aunt.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: born to parents who are not married
examples: SYNONYM illegitimate
She was a natural daughter of King James II.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: based on human reason alone
examples: I am a firm believer in human rights and natural law.
It goes against natural justice to punish a child for the crimes of its parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used after the name of a note to show that the note is neither sharp nor flat. The written symbol is (♮).
examples: B natural

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that you would expect
examples: SYNONYM of course
Naturally, I get upset when things go wrong.
After a while, we naturally started talking about the children.
‘Did you complain about the noise?’ ‘Naturally.’
It was late, so naturally her mother was worried.
We heard a loud crash, so naturally we went outside to investigate.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: without special help, treatment or action by somebody
examples: naturally occurring chemicals
plants that grow naturally in poor soils
The enzyme is naturally present in garlic.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: as a normal, logical result of something
examples: This leads naturally to my next point.
The topic arose naturally in the conversation.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in a way that shows or uses abilities or qualities that a person or an animal is born with
examples: to be naturally artistic
a naturally gifted athlete
Most birds are naturally timid.
She was naturally gifted when it came to music.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in a relaxed and normal way
examples: Just act naturally.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if something comes naturally to you, you are able to do it very easily and very well
examples: Making money came naturally to him.
We were simply doing what came naturally.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: all the plants, animals and things that exist in the universe that are not made by people
examples: Take time to appreciate the beauties of nature.
man-made substances not found in nature
A lot of nature conservation is about protecting habitats.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the way that things happen in the physical world when it is not controlled by people
examples: SEE ALSO Mother Nature
The forces of nature are constantly reshaping our world.
It is impossible to change the laws of nature.
Her illness was Nature's way of telling her to do less.
Is genius the result of nature or nurture?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the usual way that a person or an animal behaves that is part of their character
examples: SEE ALSO good nature
She is very sensitive by nature.
It's not in his nature to be unkind.
It was against her nature to tell lies.
We appealed to his better nature (= his kindness).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the basic qualities of a thing
examples: the changing nature of society
It's difficult to define the exact nature of the problem.
His work explores the nature of the mother-child relationship.
My work is very specialized in nature.
The future by its very nature is uncertain.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a type or kind of something
examples: His books were mainly of a scientific nature.
Don't worry about things of that nature.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: having the type of character or quality mentioned
examples: a good-natured man

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not natural; not moral
examples: Murder is a crime against nature.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: (to return to) a simple kind of life in the country, away from cities
examples: When you’re camping, you can get back to nature.
We built our house in the country because we wanted to get back to nature.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the need to go to the toilet

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a person with a very strong personality who is full of energy, very determined and difficult for others to resist
examples: Gerard is a force of nature, continually pursuing his target when everyone else is ready to give up.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: the power of the wind, rain, etc., especially when it causes damage or harm
examples: They were fighting a losing battle against the forces of nature.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: similar to something; a type of something; in the style of something
examples: His speech was in the nature of an apology.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: in the way that things usually happen
examples: In the nature of things, young people often rebel against their parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to allow natural processes to happen, without trying to stop or change them (used especially in the context of illness)
examples: The midwife must judge when to let nature take its course and when to intervene.
When the dog responded so badly to the treatment, we decided to let nature take its course.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the navy of a country
examples: a naval base/officer/battle
the country’s naval forces

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the skill or the process of planning a route for a ship or other vehicle and taking it there
examples: a maker of in-car navigation systems
an expert in navigation

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the movement of ships or aircraft
examples: the right of navigation through international waters

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the way that you move around a website or the internet when you are looking for information
examples: The site was redesigned to improve navigation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at a short distance away from somebody/something
examples: Do you live near here?
Go and sit nearer (to) the fire.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a short period of time from something
examples: My birthday is very near Christmas.
I’ll think about it nearer (to) the time (= when it is just going to happen).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used before a number to mean ‘approximately’, ‘just below or above’
examples: Share prices are near their record high of last year.
Profits fell from $11 million to nearer $8 million.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: similar to somebody/something in quality, size, etc.
examples: Nobody else comes near her in intellect.
He's nearer 70 than 60.
This colour is nearest (to) the original.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: close to a particular state
examples: a state near (to) death
She was near to tears (= almost crying).
We came near to being killed.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: close to you in time or distance
examples: Help was at hand.
The property is ideally located with all local amenities close at hand.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be fairly accurate in a guess, statement, etc.
examples: Such guesses are thought to be close to the mark.
‘The Times’ was nearer the mark when it said…

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: having a lot of importance and interest for somebody

definitions.definition: near in position; not far away
examples: Her mother lived in a nearby town.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: almost; not quite; not completely
examples: The bottle's nearly empty.
I've worked here for nearly two years.
It's nearly time to leave.
The audience was nearly all men.
He's nearly as tall as you are.
They're nearly always late.
She very nearly died.
It's nearly impossible to get tickets for her gigs.
Sales have nearly doubled this year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: much less than; not at all
examples: It's not nearly as hot as last year.
There isn't nearly enough time to get there now.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: almost; almost completely
examples: The first stage is pretty nearly finished.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: tidy and in order; carefully done or arranged
examples: She kept her desk extremely neat.
You've got very neat handwriting!
neat rows of books
She was wearing a neat black suit.
They sat in her neat and tidy kitchen.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: liking to keep things tidy and in order; looking tidy or doing things in a tidy way
examples: Try and be neater!
He had a neat methodical mind.
By nature he was clean and neat.
Don't be a neat freak. Relax. A little clutter won't kill you.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: small, with an attractive shape or appearance
examples: SYNONYM trim
her neat figure
The puppies’ ears should be neat and in proportion to the head.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: simple but clever
examples: a neat explanation
a neat solution to the problem
The film has a lot of neat tricks and clever editing.
We can't put people and events into neat little boxes.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: good; excellent
examples: It's a really neat movie.
We had a great time—it was pretty neat.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not mixed with water or anything else
examples: neat whisky

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to say that something cannot be avoided
examples: The number of places available is necessarily limited.
Servants necessarily had close contact with their employers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that something is possibly true but not definitely or always true
examples: Biggest doesn't necessarily mean best.
It isn't necessarily true that sugar is bad for you.
The more expensive articles are not necessarily better.
‘We're going to lose.’ ‘Not necessarily.’
The views in this article do not necessarily reflect those of the college.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that is needed for a purpose or a reason
examples: SYNONYM essential
It may be necessary to buy a new one.
It doesn't seem necessary for us to meet.
Food is necessary for survival.
I'll make the necessary arrangements.
Radical change was a necessary step for reform.
If necessary, you can contact me at home.
Only use your car when absolutely necessary.
Changes can easily be made where necessary.
He has the expertise necessary to make it work.
I was determined not to stay in hospital for any longer than was strictly necessary.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that must exist or happen and cannot be avoided
examples: SYNONYM inevitable
This is a necessary consequence of progress.
A necessary condition for a steep fall in demand is a widespread collapse in confidence.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing that is bad or that you do not like but that you must accept for a particular reason
examples: The loss of jobs is regarded as a necessary evil in the fight against inflation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the fact that something must happen or be done; the need for something
examples: We recognize the necessity for a written agreement.
We were discussing the necessity of employing more staff.
There had never been any necessity for her to go out to work.
There is absolutely no necessity for you to be involved.
This is, of necessity, a brief and incomplete account.
He is changing job out of necessity, not because he particularly wants to.
These animals don't like water but will swim if the necessity arises.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that you must have and cannot manage without
examples: Many people cannot even afford basic necessities such as food and clothing.
Air-conditioning is an absolute necessity in this climate.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a situation that must happen and that cannot be avoided
examples: Living in London, he felt, was an unfortunate necessity.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to manage to gain an advantage from something that you have to do and cannot avoid
examples: She decided to make a virtue of necessity and combined a business trip to Paris with a visit to her cousins there.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a difficult new problem forces people to think of a solution to itWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French necessite, from Latin necessitas, from necesse ‘be needful’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the part of the body between the head and the shoulders
examples: He tied a scarf around his neck.
I woke up with a stiff neck.
Giraffes have very long necks.
She craned (= stretched) her neck to get a better view.
He broke his neck in the fall.
Somebody's going to break their neck (= injure themselves) on these steps.
The hairs on the nape of my neck stood on end.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the part of a piece of clothing that fits around the neck
examples: SEE ALSO cowl neck
He wore a casual shirt with an open neck.
Her dress had three buttons at the neck undone.
What neck size do you take?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having the type of neck mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO open-necked
a round-necked sweater

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a long narrow part of something
examples: the neck of a bottle
the narrow neck of land between the lake and the sea
the neck of a guitar

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the neck of an animal, cooked and eaten
examples: neck of lamb

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have a lot of something to deal with
examples: We're up to our neck in debt.
He's in it (= trouble) up to his neck.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a combination of confidence and lack of respect
examples: I didn't think she would have the brass neck to do that.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to watch closely what somebody is doing in a way that makes them feel anxious and/or annoyed
examples: I can’t get any work done with you breathing down my neck.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: if a person or an animal wins a race by a neck, they win it by a short distance

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: roughly holding the back of an animal’s or person’s neck
examples: She grabbed him by the scruff of the neck and threw him out.
The cat picked up her kitten by the scruff of its neck.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be shouted at or punished because of something that you have done

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a difficult problem or responsibility that it seems impossible to solve or get rid of
examples: My debts are a millstone around my neck.
Unemployment was an economic millstone around the country’s neck.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: level with somebody in a race or competition
examples: COMPARE nip and tuck
The cyclists were neck and neck as they approached the final lap.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: a particular place or area
examples: He's from your neck of the woods (= the area where you live).
What are you doing in this neck of the woods?

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is very annoying
examples: That man's a pain in the neck!

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to risk losing your job, damaging your reputation, etc. by doing or saying something
examples: It's not a matter that I'm prepared to put my head on the block for.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to risk being killed or injured in order to do something
examples: I'm not going to risk my neck playing rugby with you!

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to rescue somebody from a very difficult situation
examples: He's out to save his own political neck.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to try to avoid death, punishment, etc., especially by leaving others in an extremely difficult situation
examples: To save his own skin, he lied and blamed the accident on his friend.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to do or say something when there is a risk that you may be wrong
examples: I’ll stick my neck out and say that Bill is definitely the best candidate for the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: when you say that you will wring somebody’s neck, you mean that you are very angry or annoyed with them
examples: When he was late again I wanted to wring his neck.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to require something/somebody because they are essential or very important, not just because you would like to have them
examples: Do you need any help?
It's here if you need it.
Don't go—I might need you.
They badly needed a change.
We desperately need hard facts on this disease.
Food aid is urgently needed.
What do you need your own computer for? You can use ours.
She needs more time to recover.
People need income not handouts.
More new housing is needed in the city.
I don't need your comments, thank you.
I need to get some sleep.
He needs to win this game to stay in the match.
You don't need to leave yet, do you?
You need to know how toxic the product is.
This shirt needs to be washed.
This shirt needs washing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to show what you should or have to do
examples: All you need to do is complete this form.
I didn't need to go to the bank after all—Mary lent me the money.
You may well need to look outside your preferred area to find affordable accommodation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be crazyWord Origin
examples: Old English nēodian (verb), nēod, nēd (noun), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch nood and German Not ‘danger’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small thin piece of steel that you use for sewing, with a point at one end and a hole for the thread at the other
examples: SEE ALSO pins and needles
a needle and thread
the eye (= hole) of a needle
Can you thread this needle?
a packet of small needles

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a long thin piece of plastic or metal with a point at one end that you use for knitting. You usually use two together.
examples: Vera's knitting needles clicked away.
a circular needle
a needle holding two stitches

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a very thin, pointed piece of steel used on the end of a syringe for putting a drug into somebody’s body, or for taking blood out of it
examples: a hypodermic needle
a needle inserted into the abdomen
Using dirty needles was a significant factor in the spread of the disease.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a thin piece of metal on a scientific instrument that moves to point to the correct measurement or direction
examples: The compass needle was pointing north.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the thin, hard, pointed leaf of a pine tree
examples: A soft blanket of pine needles covered the forest floor.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the very small pointed piece of metal that touches a record that is being played in order to produce the sound
examples: SYNONYM stylus
She lowered the needle onto the record.
The gramophone needle stuck in a groove.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: (to be) very anxious or excited while you are waiting to find out something or see what will happen
examples: I've been on pins and needles all week waiting for the results.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a thing that is almost impossible to find
examples: Searching for one man in this city is like looking for a needle in a haystack.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: bad or harmful
examples: OPPOSITE positive
The crisis had a negative effect on trade.
Government cuts will have a negative impact on public services.
The whole experience was definitely more positive than negative.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: containing a word such as ‘no’, ‘not’, ‘never’, etc.
examples: OPPOSITE affirmative (2)
a negative form/sentence

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: expressing the answer ‘no’
examples: OPPOSITE affirmative
His response was negative.
They received a negative reply.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: considering only the bad side of something/somebody; having no enthusiasm or hope
examples: OPPOSITE positive
Scientists have a fairly negative attitude to the theory.
The developers' proposal received negative feedback from neighbours.
‘He probably won't show up.’ ‘Don't be so negative.’
She's been rather negative about the idea.
He was too negative in his thinking.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not showing any evidence of a particular substance or medical condition
examples: OPPOSITE positive
Her pregnancy test was negative.
Negative results are not a guarantee of a safe water supply.
He tested negative for HIV infection.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: containing or producing the type of electricity that is carried by an electron
examples: OPPOSITE positive
a negative charge/current
the negative terminal of a battery

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: less than zero
examples: OPPOSITE positive
a negative trade balance
The industry suffered negative growth (= a decline) throughout the decade.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: showing light and shade, or colours, in the opposite way to the original
examples: In a negative image of the photograph, dark is light and right is left.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to fail to take care of somebody/something
examples: She denies neglecting her baby.
The buildings had been neglected for years.
Don’t neglect your health.
Local communities have been neglected in favour of private sector interests.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to not give enough attention to something
examples: Dance has been neglected by television.
She has neglected her studies.
They are neglecting their duty as elected representatives.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to fail or forget to do something that you ought to do
examples: SYNONYM omit
You neglected to mention the name of your previous employer.
