definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to try to reach an agreement by formal discussion
examples: The government will not negotiate with terrorists.
We have been negotiating for more pay.
They have refused to negotiate on this issue.
a strong negotiating position
negotiating skills
to negotiate between the two sides

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to arrange or agree something by formal discussion
examples: to negotiate a deal/contract/treaty/settlement
We successfully negotiated the release of the hostages.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to successfully get over or past a difficult part on a path or route
examples: The climbers had to negotiate a steep rock face.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: formal discussion between people who are trying to reach an agreement
examples: peace/trade/contract negotiations
They begin another round of negotiations today.
to enter into/open/begin negotiations
to continue/resume/conclude negotiations
They were conducting secret negotiations with Spain.
The rent is a matter for negotiation between the landlord and the tenant.
A contract is prepared in negotiation with our clients.
The issue is still under negotiation.
The price is generally open to negotiation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who lives next to you or near you
examples: We've had a lot of support from all our friends and neighbours.
Our next-door neighbours are very noisy.
She's been a very good neighbour to me.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a country that is next to or near another country
examples: What is Britain's nearest neighbour?
Consider Canada, our neighbor to the north.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is standing or located next to another person or thing
examples: Stand quietly, children, and try not to talk to your neighbour.
The tree fell slowly, its branches caught in those of its neighbours.
She leaned over to her nearest neighbour and whispered something.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: any other human
examples: We should all love our neighbours.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a district or an area of a town; the people who live there
examples: We grew up in the same neighbourhood.
a poor/quiet/residential neighbourhood
an old working-class neighbourhood
Manhattan is divided into distinct neighborhoods.
the neighbourhood police
He shouted so loudly that the whole neighbourhood could hear him.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the area that you are in or the area near a particular place
examples: SYNONYM vicinity
We searched the surrounding neighbourhood for the missing boy.
It was a car from outside the immediate neighbourhood.
Houses in the neighbourhood of Paris are extremely expensive.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: approximately; not exactly
examples: It cost in the neighbourhood of $500.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: located or living near or next to a place or person
examples: a neighbouring house
neighbouring towns
a neighbouring farmer

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not one nor the other of two things or people
examples: Neither answer is correct.
Neither of them has/have a car.
They produced two reports, neither of which contained any useful suggestions.
‘Which do you like?’ ‘Neither. I think they're both ugly.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: any of the long fibres that carry messages between the brain and parts of the body, enabling you to move, feel pain, etc.
examples: the optic nerve
He's off work with a trapped nerve in his neck.
Every nerve in her body was tense.
The illness kills nerve cells and causes chronic fatigue.
Pain occurs when the nerve fibres are damaged.
Signals are transmitted from the nerve endings to the brain.
The disease can also cause nerve damage.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: feelings of worry or stress
examples: Even after years as a singer, he still suffers from nerves before a performance.
I need something to calm my nerves.
to settle/soothe/steady your nerves
Everyone's nerves were on edge (= everyone felt tense).
He lives on his nerves (= is always worried).
By the end of the meal her nerves were completely frayed.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the courage to do something difficult or dangerous
examples: SYNONYM guts
It took a lot of nerve to take the company to court.
I was going to have a go at parachuting but lost my nerve at the last minute.
He held his nerve to win the final set 6–4.
Investors largely kept their nerve and stayed with the company.
It was an amazing journey which tested her nerves to the full.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a way of behaving that other people think is rude or not appropriate
examples: SYNONYM cheek
I don't know how you have the nerve to show your face after what you said!
He's got a nerve asking us for money!
‘Then she demanded to see the manager!’ ‘What a nerve!’
He had some nerve to insult Mina's cooking.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be very nervous
examples: By the time of the interview, I was a bundle of nerves.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to annoy somebody
examples: That music is starting to get on my nerves.
It really gets on my nerves when people talk loudly on the phone in public.
His endless whining really gets on my nerves.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be able to remain calm in a difficult or dangerous situation
examples: You need nerves of steel to be a good poker player.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to mention a subject that makes somebody feel angry, upset, embarrassed, etc.
examples: You touched a raw nerve when you mentioned his first wife.
My remarks about divorce had unwittingly touched a raw nerve.
The article struck a raw nerve as it revived unpleasant memories.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to try as hard as you can to do something
examples: He strained every nerve to snatch victory from defeat.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to have a strong effect
examples: His work strikes a nerve with people who are attracted to nostalgia.
It seems I struck a nerve with my last post about cell phones.
Nissan may well strike a popular nerve here.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: an attempt to defeat your opponents by putting pressure on them so that they lose courage or confidence
examples: The union has been fighting a war of nerves with the management over pay.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: anxious about something or afraid of something
examples: OPPOSITE confident
I felt really nervous before the interview.
I get so nervous before exams.
I was too nervous to say anything.
Consumers are very nervous about the future.
The horse may be nervous of cars.
He had been nervous about inviting us.
a nervous laugh/glance/smile (= one that shows that you feel anxious)
By the time the police arrived, I was a nervous wreck.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: easily worried or frightened
examples: She was a thin, nervous girl.
He's not the nervous type.
She was of a nervous disposition.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: connected with the body’s nerves and often affecting you mentally or emotionally
examples: a nervous condition/disorder/disease
She was in a state of nervous exhaustion.
There is danger of her going into nervous shock.
He was full of nervous energy, like a racehorse who hadn't run in a while.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be very easily frightened; to be very nervousWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (in the senses ‘containing nerves’ and ‘relating to the nerves’): from Latin nervosus ‘sinewy, vigorous’, from nervus ‘sinew’; related to Greek neuron ‘nerve’. Senses (1) and (2) date from the mid 18th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a hollow place or structure that a bird makes or chooses for laying its eggs in and sheltering its young
examples: sparrows building a nest of twigs and dry grass

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a place where insects or other small creatures live and produce their young
examples: a wasps’ nest
a nest of mice
The snake will attack if disturbed inside its nest.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a secret place which is full of bad people and their activities
examples: a nest of thieves

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the home, thought of as the safe place where parents bring up their children
examples: SEE ALSO empty nest
to leave the nest (= leave your parents’ home)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a group or set of similar things that are made to fit inside each other
examples: a nest of tables

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make yourself richer, especially at somebody else's expense, by spending money on yourself that should be spent on somebody/something else

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to become able to fly and leave its nest

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to leave home and live somewhere else
examples: Her children have flown the nest.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a difficult situation in which a lot of people get very angry
examples: His letter to the papers stirred up a real hornets' nest.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a discovery that seems interesting but is found to have no value

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a very complicated situation
examples: This area of the law is a veritable mare’s nest.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: material that is made of string, thread or wire twisted or tied together, with small spaces in between; a piece of this material used for a particular purpose
examples: SEE ALSO drift net
Unfortunately the animals are often caught in fishing nets.
She's always peering through the net curtains, spying on the neighbours.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the frame covered in net that forms the goal
examples: to kick the ball into the back of the net
She shot the ball past the goalkeeper and into an empty net.
Kane finally found the net in the 78th minute.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the piece of net between the two players that the ball goes over
examples: She hit her second serve straight into the net.
to hit the ball over the net

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a piece of ground with a net around it, used for practising batting and bowling
examples: He practised bowling all morning in the nets.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the internet
examples: He spends his time playing computer games and surfing the net.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a network of radios or computers that are connected to each other
examples: A call on the radio net went out that there had been a crash.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to consider a lot of different people, activities, possibilities, etc. when you are looking for something
examples: It’s worth casting your net wide when applying for your first job.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: when somebody/something slips through the net, an organization or a system fails to find them and deal with them
examples: We tried to contact all former students, but one or two slipped through the net.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to consider a wide range of possibilities or cover a large area, especially to try to find somebody/something
examples: They have spread their net far and wide in the search for a new team coach.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to consider or include a larger range of options or possibilities, especially when searching for something
examples: It's time to widen the net in the search for a suitable candidate.

definitions.definition: a complicated system of roads, lines, tubes, nerves, etc. that are connected to each other and operate together
examples: a rail/road/canal network
The new rail services will form a network connecting the capital and major cities.
Europe's mobile phone networks are controlled by five dominant players.
a network of veins
an extensive network of underground tunnels

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a closely connected group of people, companies, etc. that exchange information, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO social network (2)
They have one of the most efficient distribution networks in Europe.

to build/create/develop a network
She has a supportive network of close friends.
Expand your network of contacts beyond your usual circles.

definitions.definition: a number of computers and other devices that are connected together so that equipment and information can be shared
examples: SEE ALSO LAN

Users can access data across a network.
The files are accessible over a network.
You can print and scan from your device via a wireless network.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a group of radio or television stations in different places that are connected and that broadcast the same programmes at the same time
examples: the four big US television networks

The show was first aired on the cable network Showtime.
He's chairman of a network of radio stations.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the situation in many British companies, government departments and branches of the armed forces where people give jobs to former students of the school or university that they went to
examples: Recruiting staff used to be done by means of the old boy network.
Most of the managers were chosen by the old boy network and many of them turned out to be incompetent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not supporting or helping either side in a disagreement, competition, etc.
examples: SYNONYM impartial
Journalists are supposed to be politically neutral.
I didn't take my father's or my mother's side; I tried to remain neutral.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not belonging to any of the countries that are involved in a war; not supporting any of the countries involved in a war
examples: neutral territory/waters
Switzerland was neutral during the war.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: deliberately not expressing any strong feeling
examples: ‘So you told her?’ he said in a neutral tone of voice.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not affected by something
examples: SEE ALSO gender-neutral
He believes that technology is morally neutral until it is applied.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not very bright or strong, such as grey or light brown
examples: a neutral colour scheme
Neutral tones will give the room a feeling of space.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: neither acid nor alkaline

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: having neither a positive nor a negative electrical charge
examples: the neutral wire in a plug

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: in a place that has no connection with either of the people or sides who are meeting and so does not give an advantage to either of them
examples: We decided to meet on neutral ground.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not at any time; not on any occasion
examples: You never help me.
He'll never forget her.
He has never been abroad.
She had never seen so much snow.
She left the country, vowing never to return again.
‘Would you vote for him?’ ‘Never.’
‘I work for a company called Orion Technology.’ ‘Never heard of them.’
Never in all my life have I seen such a horrible thing.
Never ever tell anyone your password.
Never before has English cuisine been so stylish.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a negative statement instead of ‘not’
examples: I never knew (= didn't know until now) you had a twin sister.
I never realized just how easy it is.
Someone might find out, and that would never do (= that is not acceptable).
He never so much as smiled (= did not smile even once).
Most people have never even heard of Iggy.
‘I told my boss exactly what I thought of her.’ ‘You never did!’ (= ‘Surely you didn't!’)
‘You took my bike.’ ‘No, I never.’
Never fear (= Do not worry), everything will be all right.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that nothing is impossible
examples: Many thought the book could not become a movie, but with Hollywood never say never.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: on hire purchase (= by making payments over a long period)
examples: to buy a new car on the never-never

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to express surprise or disapproval
examples: Well, I never! Fancy getting married and not telling us!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: despite something that you have just mentioned
examples: SYNONYM nonetheless
There is little chance that we will succeed in changing the law. Nevertheless, it is important that we try.
Our defeat was expected but it is disappointing nevertheless.
The old system had its flaws, but nevertheless it was preferable to the new one.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not existing before; recently made, invented, introduced, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO brand new
Have you read her new novel?
We retrain staff to use the new technology.
The company is trialling a new security system.
Have you seen Danielle's new baby?
a new addition to the family (= a baby)
The school secretary wants to introduce new ways of doing things in the office.
This idea isn't new.
The latest model has over 100 new features.
Check out the band's new album.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that is new
examples: It was a good mix of the old and the new.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: recently bought
examples: Let me show you my new dress.
The car still looks new.
They are very proud of their spanking new kitchen.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not used or owned by anyone before
examples: A second-hand car costs a fraction of a new one.
They are building 500 new houses in the town.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: different from the previous one
examples: I like your new hairstyle.
When do you start your new job?
He's made a lot of new friends.
Do you have her new phone number?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: already existing but not seen, experienced, etc. before; not familiar
examples: This is a new experience for me.
I'd like to learn a new language.
the discovery of a new star
Scientists have identified an entirely new species.
Manga is drawing in a whole new generation of readers.
to try/learn/do something new
Our system is probably new to you.
Hard work is nothing new to Bill.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not yet familiar with something because you have only just started, arrived, etc.
examples: You're new here, aren't you?
New arrivals should have their passports ready for inspection.
We offer intensive training to all new recruits.
I should tell you, I'm completely new to this kind of work.
I am new to the town.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: just beginning or beginning again
examples: a new day
It was a new era in the history of our country.
She went to Australia to start a new life.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used in compounds to describe something that has recently happened
examples: He was enjoying his new-found freedom.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: modern; of the latest type
examples: the new morality
They called themselves the New Romantics.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: having fresh energy, courage or health
examples: Since he changed jobs he's looked like a new man.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: only recently produced or developed
examples: The new buds are appearing on the trees now.
new potatoes (= ones dug from the soil early in the season)

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a situation or society that changes in a way that is meant to improve people’s lives but is often a source of extra problems
examples: the brave new world of technology
the architects' vision of a brave new world of pristine concrete

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to make a new discovery or do something that has not been done before
examples: SEE ALSO groundbreaking
Her architectural designs have broken new ground.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to improve something by introducing new ideas and making people more interested in it
examples: The results of their research have breathed new life into the debate.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to describe a situation in which everybody suddenly realizes that they were wrong to believe that somebody/something was very good, important, etc.
examples: Is this artist's white canvas a case of the emperor's new clothes or is it something beautiful, even moving?
Soon investors will realize that the emperor has no clothes and there will be a big sell-off in stocks.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: in very good condition, as it was when it was new
examples: I've had your coat cleaned—it's as good as new now.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that something has become very fashionable and can be thought of as replacing something else
examples: Brown is the new black.
Comedy is the new rock and roll.
Fifty is the new forty.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: new members or employees, especially young ones, with new ideas or ways of doing things
examples: This company badly needs to bring in some new blood.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: a person who has just started to work for an organization, department, etc., especially in a senior job, and who is likely to make a lot of changes
examples: Well, you know what they say—a new broom sweeps clean.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: a person who is new to a place, an organization, etc.
examples: Despite his six years in politics, he was still regarded by many as the new kid on the block.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: a situation that used to be unusual but is now what you should expect
examples: This is not a temporary blip—this is the new normal.
Scientists say these weather patterns could be the new normal for Florida.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: used to say that you have not heard a particular idea, piece of information, joke, etc. before
examples: ‘Have you come across this before?’ ‘No, it's a new one on me.’

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to change the way that a situation appears
examples: What you have told us puts a different complexion on the situation.
The joke took on a rather serious complexion when the police became involved.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to behave in a worse way than ever before
examples: The government has stooped to an all-time low with this policy.
Reality TV has sunk to new lows.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: (you cannot) successfully make people change their ideas, methods of work, etc., when they have had them for a long time

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to change your way of life to become a better, more responsible person

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: used as a friendly greeting
examples: Hi! What's new?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: recently
examples: a newly qualified doctor
a newly created job
a newly independent republic

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: new information about something that has happened recently
examples: What's the latest news?
Have you heard the news? Pat's leaving!
That's great news.
Tell me all your news.
Do you want the good news or the bad news first?
saddened/shocked/surprised by the news

Have you had any news of Patrick?
Any news on the deal?
He gave me some news about the office move.
Messengers brought news that the battle had been lost.
It's news to me (= I haven't heard it before).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: reports of recent events that appear in newspapers or on television, radio or the internet
examples: SEE ALSO fake news
national/international/local news
a news story/item/report
a TV/radio news bulletin
news media/coverage

breaking news (= news that is arriving about events that have just happened)
The wedding was front-page news.
News of a serious road accident is just coming in.
Is there any news on the car bomb attack?
I'm not interested in news about celebrities.
She is always in the news.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a regular television or radio broadcast of the latest news
examples: SEE ALSO the shipping news
to listen to/watch the news
Can you put the news on?
the nine o’clock news
I saw it on the news.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person, thing or event that is considered to be interesting enough to be reported as news
examples: Pop stars are always news.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be likely to cause problems
examples: Central heating is bad news for indoor plants.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be likely to be helpful or give an advantage
examples: The cut in interest rates is good news for homeowners.
The good news is that there's still plenty of money available.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be the first to tell somebody some bad news
examples: There's no easy way to break the news.
The police had to break the news to the boy's parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if there were bad news we would hear it, so as we have heard nothing, it is likely that nothing bad has happened
examples: I still haven't heard anything about the job, but no news is good news.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a report containing news of the activities of a club or organization that is sent regularly to all its members
examples: Our sailing club produces a monthly newsletter.
a church newsletter

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a set of large printed sheets of paper, or a website, containing news, articles, advertisements, etc. and published every day or every week; the organization responsible for producing this
examples: SEE ALSO paper
a daily/weekly newspaper
a local/national newspaper
an online newspaper
a tabloid/broadsheet newspaper
a newspaper article/report/headline
a newspaper cutting/clipping
a newspaper editor/reporter/columnist
newspapers and news websites
British newspapers and their websites carried no photos of the event.
Which newspaper do you read?
to publish/own/print a newspaper
The newspaper reported on Friday that the boy had been found.
I read about it in the newspaper.
The company is considering up to 4000 job losses, according to The Times newspaper.
She works for the local newspaper (= the company that produces it).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: paper taken from old newspapers
examples: Wrap all your glasses in newspaper.
Use old newspaper to wipe windows clean and dry.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: coming straight after somebody/something in time, order or space
examples: The next train to Baltimore is at ten.
The next six months will be the hardest.
The next chapter deals with the post-war situation.
Who's next?
The woman in the next room was talking in a very loud voice.
The parcel will arrive in the next few days.
I fainted and the next thing I knew I was in the hospital.
Round here, you leave school and next thing you know you're married with three kids.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the Monday, week, etc. immediately following
examples: Next Thursday is 12 April.
Next time I'll bring a book.
I'm going away next month.
Next month's rent is due today.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to encourage somebody who has not been successful at something
examples: Never mind— better luck next time.
If you didn't win a prize, better luck next time.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if a situation changes from one day to the next, it is uncertain and not likely to stay the same each day
examples: I never know what to expect from one day to the next.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the average person
examples: I can enjoy a joke as well as the next man, but this is going too far.

examples: SYNONYM subtle

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.definition: to be pleasant or polite to somebody, especially when you do not really want to

definitions.definition: used to show you are pleased when something good has happened or somebody has said something funny
examples: You got the job? Nice one!

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to show you are pleased when somebody has done something well
examples: You did a good job today. Nice work, James!

examples: They spotted a niche in the market, with no serious competition.

examples: SYNONYM nook

examples: Within each niche, similar animals avoid competing with each other.

examples: We took a picnic lunch to the river and made a day of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the morning after an evening of drinking
examples: Drink plenty of water the morning after the night before, and learn from experience.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: at all times of the day and night (used to emphasize that something happens very often or that it happens continuously)
examples: She talks about him morning, noon and night.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: all the time; continuously
examples: The machines are kept running night and day.
The store is open day and night.

definitions.label: Meaning 13

examples: ‘Night night, sleep tight!’

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: an evening that you spend enjoying yourself away from home
examples: They enjoy a night out occasionally.

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.label: Meaning 17

definitions.definition: used when you cannot give a clear answer to a question
examples: ‘Are you enjoying it?’ ‘Yes and no.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having or showing fine personal qualities that people admire, such as courage, honesty and care for others
examples: OPPOSITE ignoble
a noble leader
noble ideals
He died for a noble cause.
She died in a noble cause.
It was very noble of you to go so far to take him home.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: belonging to a family of high social rank (= belonging to the nobility)
examples: SYNONYM aristocratic
He was a young man of noble birth.
one of the noblest families in Portugal
Intermarriage between the noble families means that all the counts are related.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very impressive in size or quality
examples: SYNONYM splendid
a noble building

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not anyone; no person
examples: Nobody knew what to say.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if you nod, nod your head or your head nods, you move your head up and down to show agreement, understanding, etc.
examples: I asked him if he would help me and he nodded.
‘Ready?’ She nodded at me and we set off.
Her head nodded in agreement.
He nodded his head sympathetically.
She nodded approval.
Everyone nodded their agreement.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move your head down and up once to say hello or goodbye to somebody or to give them a sign to do something
examples: The president nodded to the crowd as he passed in the motorcade.
She nodded at him to begin speaking
to nod a greeting

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move your head in the direction of somebody/something to show that you are talking about them/it
examples: I asked where Steve was and she nodded in the direction of the kitchen.
She nodded towards his suitcase. ‘Going somewhere?’ she asked.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to let your head fall forward when you are sleeping in a chair
examples: He sat nodding in front of the fire.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to only know somebody/something slightlyWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (as a verb): perhaps of Low German origin; compare with Middle High German notten ‘move about, shake’. The noun dates from the mid 16th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sound, especially when it is loud, unpleasant or frightening
examples: SEE ALSO white noise
There was a rattling noise coming from the back of the car.
What's that noise?
I heard a loud noise and turned around.
Don't make a noise.
They were making too much noise.
I was woken by the noise of a car starting up.
There was constant background noise from the motorway.
Measures are needed to reduce noise levels.
We had to shout above the noise of the traffic.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: extra electrical or electronic signals that are not part of the signal that is being broadcast or transmitted and which may damage it
examples: Place the devices as close as possible to the sensors to reduce noise in the signal.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: information that is not wanted and that can make it difficult for the important or useful information to be seen clearly
examples: There is some noise in the data which needs to be reduced.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an important person

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to complain loudly
examples: I will continue to make as much noise as I can to support the scheme.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to talk in an indirect way about something that you think you might do
examples: The company has been making noises about closing several factories.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to complain about something

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to make remarks of the kind mentioned, even when that is not what you really think
examples: He made all the right noises at the meeting yesterday (= said what people wanted to hear).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: making a lot of noise
examples: noisy children/traffic/crowds
He was kept awake by noisy neighbours.
a noisy protest (= when people shout)
The kids were even noisier than the dogs.
The engine is very noisy at high speed.
They are a small but noisy pressure group (= they attract attention to their ideas by frequent discussion and argument in public and in the media).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: full of noise
examples: a noisy classroom/office
People find it difficult to concentrate in noisy environments such as open-plan offices.
The streets were very noisy throughout the night.
The party was getting a bit noisy.
It was so noisy I couldn't hear myself speak.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to formally suggest that somebody/something should be chosen for an important role, prize, position, etc.
examples: SYNONYM propose
She has been nominated for the presidency.
He was nominated (as) best actor.
I nominated Paul to take on the role of treasurer.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to choose somebody to do a particular job
examples: SYNONYM appoint
I have been nominated to the committee.
The president wanted to nominate him as as successor.
She was nominated to speak on our behalf.
Each office will nominate a representative to sit on the committee.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to choose a time, date or title for something
examples: SYNONYM select
1 December has been nominated as the day of the election.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of suggesting or choosing somebody as a candidate in an election, or for a job or an award; the fact of being suggested for this
examples: Membership of the club is by nomination only.
He won the nomination as Democratic candidate for the presidency.
They opposed her nomination to the post of Deputy Director.
He has had nine Oscar nominations.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who has been formally suggested for a job, a prize, etc.
examples: He was chosen as the party's presidential nominee.
an Oscar nominee

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person in whose name money is invested in a company, etc.
examples: They were acting through nominees.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: without the aim of making a profit
examples: an independent non-profit organization
The centre is run on a non-profit basis.
The charity is non-profit-making.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not one of a group of people or things; not any
examples: None of these pens works/work.
We have three sons but none of them lives/live nearby.
We saw several houses but none we really liked.
Tickets for Friday? Sorry we've got none left.
He told me all the news but none of it was very exciting.
‘Is there any more milk?’ ‘No, none at all.’
Everybody liked him but none (= nobody) more than I.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to refuse to accept something
examples: I offered to pay but he was having none of it.
They pretended to be enthusiastic about my work but then suddenly decided they wanted none of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: only
examples: None but he knew the truth.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: despite this fact

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize who or what somebody/something is, when this is surprising
examples: Her first customer was none other than Mrs Obama.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: despite this fact
examples: SYNONYM nevertheless
The book is too long but, nonetheless, informative and entertaining.
The problems are not serious. Nonetheless, we shall need to tackle them soon.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: ideas, statements or beliefs that you think are silly or not true
examples: SYNONYM rubbish (3)
Reports that he has resigned are nonsense.
You're talking nonsense!
‘I won't go.’ ‘Nonsense! You must go!’
It's nonsense to say they don't care.
The idea is an economic nonsense.
Ministers have dismissed the rumours of a bribery scandal as nonsense.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: spoken or written words that have no meaning or make no sense
examples: a book of children’s nonsense poems
Most of the translation he did for me was complete nonsense.
The whole article seemed like complete nonsense to me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: silly or unacceptable behaviour
examples: SEE ALSO no-nonsense
The new teacher won't stand for any nonsense.
I can't wait for this nonsense to end so that we can all be friends again.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to reduce the value of something by a lot; to make something seem silly
examples: If people can bribe police officers, it makes a complete nonsense of the legal system.
The unemployment figures make nonsense of talk of an economic recovery.
This decision makes absolute nonsense of all our hard work.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that something is stupid or not true

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: 12 o’clock in the middle of the day
examples: SYNONYM midday
We should be there by noon.
The conference opens at 12 noon on Saturday.
the noon deadline for the end of hostilities
I'm leaving on the noon train.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: at all times of the day and night (used to emphasize that something happens very often or that it happens continuously)
examples: She talks about him morning, noon and night.
The work continues morning, noon and night.
It's all she talks about, morning, noon and night.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: and not
examples: She seemed neither surprised nor worried.
He wasn't there on Monday. Nor on Tuesday, for that matter.
Not a building nor a tree was left standing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used before a positive verb to agree with something negative that has just been said
examples: She doesn't like them and nor does Jeff.
‘I'm not going.’ ‘Nor am I.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: and not
examples: She seemed neither surprised nor worried.
He wasn't there on Monday. Nor on Tuesday, for that matter.
Not a building nor a tree was left standing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used before a positive verb to agree with something negative that has just been said
examples: She doesn't like them and nor does Jeff.
‘I'm not going.’ ‘Nor am I.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a situation or a pattern of behaviour that is usual or expected
examples: SYNONYM rule (4)
The new design is a departure from the norm.
Older parents seem to be the norm rather than the exception nowadays.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: standards of behaviour that are typical of or accepted within a particular group or society
examples: social/cultural norms
She considered people to be products of the values and norms of the society they lived in.
accepted norms of behaviour

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a required or agreed standard, amount, etc.
examples: detailed education norms for children of particular ages
The government claims that background radioactivity is well below international norms.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: typical, usual or ordinary; what you would expect
examples: quite/perfectly (= completely) normal
Her temperature is normal.
They are just quiet, normal people.
It's normal to feel tired after such a long trip.
It is now regarded as normal for women to work outside the home.
He should be able to lead a perfectly normal life.
Divorce is complicated enough in normal circumstances, but this situation is even worse.
Under normal circumstances, I would say ‘yes’.
In the normal course of events I wouldn't go to that part of town.
Statistically, in a normal distribution, 68 per cent of the scores fall fairly close.
The unemployment rate was above normal levels.
Temperatures are expected to be in the normal range for May.
We are open during normal office hours.
It is normal practice to inform somebody if you want to leave early.
My day began in the normal way, and then I received a very strange phone call.
During normal conditions the road is clear of stones and mud.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not suffering from any mental or physical disorder
examples: People who commit such crimes aren't normal.
Rebecca was born a normal, healthy baby.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in the way that is normal or usual; as often happens
examples: Everyone blamed me as per usual.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: usually; in normal circumstances

He didn't eat as much as he normally does.
It normally takes 20 minutes to get there.
The track is normally used by farmers and their goats.
Normally, there was a background hum of noise.
They played at venues not normally associated with classical music.
to function/operate/develop normally
The data were not normally distributed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in the usual or ordinary way
examples: Her heart is beating normally.
Just try to behave normally.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the direction that is on your left when you watch the sun rise; one of the four main points of the compass
examples: COMPARE east
Which way is north?
cold winds coming from the north
Mount Kenya is to the north of (= further north than) Nairobi.
views of distant mountains to north and south

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the northern part of a country, a region or the world
examples: birds migrating from the north
Houses are less expensive in the North (= of England) than in the South.
They wanted to escape the cold of the north.
The main road ran across the north of the island.
There's been a severe earthquake in the north of the country.
Edinburgh was called the Athens of the North.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the north-east states of the US which fought against the South in the American Civil War
examples: Some delegates from Virginia voted to join the North.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the richer and more developed countries of the world, especially in Europe and North America
examples: The North refused to commit itself to safeguarding species diversity.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: located in the north or facing north; connected with or typical of the north part of the world or a region
examples: the northern slopes of the mountains
the northern part of Syria
northern Scotland
a northern accent
He grew up in the northern city of Lille.
a concert of Northern European music
This week marks the height of summer in the northern hemisphere.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the part of the face that sticks out above the mouth, used for breathing and smelling things
examples: SEE ALSO Grecian nose
She had dark eyes and a long narrow nose.
He broke his nose in the fight.
She wrinkled her nose in disgust.
He pressed his nose up against the window.
Try to breathe through your nose.
He blew his nose (= cleared it by blowing strongly into a handkerchief).
a blocked/runny nose
Stop picking your nose! (= removing dirt from it with your finger)
He held his nose as he passed the stinking dustbins.
He held his nose and voted for the bill anyway.
He pushed his glasses up the bridge of his nose (= the hard part near the top).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the type of nose mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO hard-nosed
red-nosed
large-nosed

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the front part of a plane, spacecraft, etc.
examples: Heat detectors are fitted in the nose of the missile.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a special ability for finding or recognizing something
examples: SYNONYM instinct
As a journalist, she has always had a nose for a good story.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a sense of smell
examples: a dog with a good nose
Good noses can always smell a fight brewing.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a smell that is characteristic of a particular wine
examples: SYNONYM bouquet
This Cote de Beaune has a good nose, with apricot and raisin aromas.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: by only a small amount (used mostly when talking about horse racing)
examples: He lost his first race by a nose but won the next three.
Glen's Diamond was declared the winner by a nose from the 11–4 favourite.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to do something when you are angry that is meant to harm somebody else but that also harms you

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be guided by your sense of smell

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to go straight forward
examples: The garage is a mile ahead up the hill—just follow your nose.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to act according to what seems right or reasonable, rather than following any particular rules

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if you say that people have their noses in the trough, you mean that they are trying to get a lot of money for themselves

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to annoy somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to defeat somebody
examples: We have to give him a bloody nose in the election.
Voters gave the government a bloody nose in the local elections.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be reading
examples: She always has her nose in a book.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be reading something and giving it all your attention
examples: Peter always has his nose in a book.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to look around a place; to look for something in a place
examples: I’ll have a nose round and see what I can find.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody is not upset or annoyed about something because it does not affect them in a bad way

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to avoid doing anything wrong or illegal
examples: Since leaving prison, he's managed to keep his nose clean.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to try not to become involved in things that should not really involve you

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to work hard for a long period of time without stopping

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to make somebody do everything you want; to control somebody completely

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that suggests that you think that you are better than somebody or that something is not good enough for you
examples: SYNONYM look down on somebody
People who live in that area tend to look down their noses at their poorer neighbours.
They tend to look down their noses at people who drive small cars.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: if cars, etc. are nose to tail, they are moving slowly in a long line with little space between them
examples: The traffic was nose to tail for miles.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: exactly
examples: The budget should hit the $136 billion target on the nose.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to pay too much money for something

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: very obvious

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to try to become involved in something that should not involve you
examples: He’s always poking his nose into other people’s business.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: a polite way of referring to the fact that a woman is going to the toilet
examples: I'm just going to powder my nose.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to upset or annoy somebody, especially by not giving them enough attention

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to keep reminding somebody in an unkind way of their past mistakes

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to make a rude sign with your thumb on your nose; to show that you have no respect for somebody/something
examples: The company just thumbs its nose at the legislation on pollution.
They thumb their noses at all of our traditions.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to refuse something, especially because you do not think that it is good enough for you
examples: The children turn up their noses at almost everything I cook.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: if something is under somebody’s nose, it is very close to them but they cannot see it
examples: I searched everywhere for the letter and it was under my nose all the time!

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: if something happens under somebody’s nose, they do not notice it even though it is not being done secretly
examples: The police didn't know the drugs ring was operating right under their noses.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: in a way that is not friendly and suggests that you think that you are better than other people
examples: She walked in with her nose in the air, ignoring everyone.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used with be, do or have to form the negative of verbs; used to form the negative of modal verbs like can or must
examples: She did not/didn’t see him.
It’s not/It isn’t raining.
It's cold, isn't it?
Don't you eat meat?
I can't see from here.
He must not go.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to give the following word or phrase a negative meaning, or to reply in the negative
examples: He warned me not to be late.
I was sorry not to have seen them.
Not everybody agrees.
They had still not decided.
‘Who's next?’ ‘Not me.’
‘What did you do at school?’ ‘Not a lot.’
It's not easy being a parent (= it's difficult).
It's not every day you get to meet a famous actor.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used after hope, expect, believe, etc. to give a negative reply
examples: ‘Will she be there?’ ‘I hope not.’
‘Is it ready?’ ‘I'm afraid not.’
‘Does he know?’ ‘I believe not.’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show a negative possibility
examples: I don't know if he's telling the truth or not.
Whether you succeed or not depends on the how skilled you are.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not want something or will not allow something
examples: ‘Some more?’ ‘Not for me, thanks.’
‘Can I throw this out?’ ‘Certainly not.’

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: even less than
examples: She was standing not three feet in front of me.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to suggest that the opposite of the following word or phrase is true
examples: This could all happen in the not too distant future (= soon).
His view on the matter was not a million miles away from (= close to) mine.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the opposite of a statement
examples: Well, that sounds like a fun evening—not!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used for emphasis to mean ‘no thing or person’
examples: He didn't speak to me—not one word.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to politely accept thanks or to agree to something
examples: ‘Thanks a lot.’ ‘Not at all.’
‘Will it bother you if I smoke?’ ‘Not at all.’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something else is also true
examples: She not only wrote the text but also selected the illustrations.
He not only read the book, but also remembered what he had read.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to state that you are not suggesting something
examples: She hasn't written—not that she said she would.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: deserving to be noticed or to receive attention; important
examples: SYNONYM striking
a notable success/achievement/example
His eyes are his most notable feature.
The town is notable for its ancient harbour.
With a few notable exceptions, everyone gave something.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used for giving a good or the most important example of something
examples: SYNONYM especially
The house had many drawbacks, most notably its price.
This argument has been put forward by many politicians, most notably by the Prime Minister and the Foreign Secretary.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to a great degree
examples: SYNONYM remarkably
This has not been a notably successful project.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a short piece of writing to help you remember something
examples: Please make a note of the dates.
She made a mental note (= decided that she must remember) to ask Alan about it.
Note to self (= a mental instruction): book more holidays.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a short informal letter
examples: SEE ALSO suicide note
Just a quick note to say thank you for a wonderful evening.
She left a note for Ben on the kitchen table.
He wrote a note to his parents saying he was leaving.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: information that you write down when somebody is speaking, or when you are reading a book, etc.
examples: He sat taking notes of everything that was said.
Can I borrow your lecture notes?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: detailed information that is kept about a particular person, topic or situation
examples: Patients' medical notes have gone missing.
He kept notes on the birds, mammals, reptiles and plants he saw on walks.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: information about a performance, an actor’s career, a piece of music, etc. printed in a special book or on a record cover, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO liner note
The booklet has full notes on each artist.
The catalogue contains detailed notes on each painting.
The sleeve notes include a short biography of the performers on this recording.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a short comment on a word or passage in a book
examples: SEE ALSO footnote
a new edition of ‘Hamlet’, with explanatory notes
See note 3, page 259.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a piece of paper money
examples: a £5 note
We only exchange notes and traveller's cheques.
a thick wad of notes

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a single sound of a particular length and pitch (= how high or low a sound is), made by the voice or a musical instrument; the written or printed sign for a musical note
examples: SEE ALSO blue note
He played the first few notes of the tune.
high/low notes
I played a lot of wrong notes because I was so nervous.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a particular quality in something, for example in somebody’s voice or the atmosphere at an event; a comment on something with a particular quality
examples: SYNONYM air
There was a note of amusement in his voice.
It's good to finish on a positive note.
On a more serious note (= speaking more seriously)…
On a slightly different note (= changing the subject slightly), let’s talk about…
The year ended on an optimistic note.
As a side note, the entire festival is free.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: an official document with a particular purpose
examples: SEE ALSO credit note
a sick note from your doctor
The buyer has to sign a delivery note as proof of receipt.
Students returning to school after absence must bring a note from their parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: an official letter from the representative of one government to another
examples: an exchange of diplomatic notes

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if two or more people compare notes, they each say what they think about the same event, situation, etc.
examples: We saw the play separately and compared notes afterwards.
Let's compare notes on our experiences.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to do, say or write something that is suitable/not suitable for a particular occasion
examples: It is a bizarre tale and the author hits just the right note of horror and disbelief.
Unfortunately, the president struck the wrong note in his speech, ignoring the public mood.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: of importance or of great interest
examples: a scientist of note
The museum contains nothing of great note.
The frescoes are worthy of note.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to express feelings or opinions of a particular kind
examples: She sounded a note of warning in her speech.
The touch of cynicism struck a slightly sour note.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to pay attention to something and be sure to remember it
examples: Take note of what he says.
Under the new rules the penalty for illegal play is increased. Players take note.
He took careful note of the suspicious-looking man in the corner of the bar.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a short piece of writing to help you remember something
examples: Please make a note of the dates.
She made a mental note (= decided that she must remember) to ask Alan about it.
Note to self (= a mental instruction): book more holidays.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a short informal letter
examples: SEE ALSO suicide note
Just a quick note to say thank you for a wonderful evening.
She left a note for Ben on the kitchen table.
He wrote a note to his parents saying he was leaving.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: information that you write down when somebody is speaking, or when you are reading a book, etc.
examples: He sat taking notes of everything that was said.
Can I borrow your lecture notes?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: detailed information that is kept about a particular person, topic or situation
examples: Patients' medical notes have gone missing.
He kept notes on the birds, mammals, reptiles and plants he saw on walks.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: information about a performance, an actor’s career, a piece of music, etc. printed in a special book or on a record cover, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO liner note
The booklet has full notes on each artist.
The catalogue contains detailed notes on each painting.
The sleeve notes include a short biography of the performers on this recording.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a short comment on a word or passage in a book
examples: SEE ALSO footnote
a new edition of ‘Hamlet’, with explanatory notes
See note 3, page 259.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a piece of paper money
examples: a £5 note
We only exchange notes and traveller's cheques.
a thick wad of notes

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a single sound of a particular length and pitch (= how high or low a sound is), made by the voice or a musical instrument; the written or printed sign for a musical note
examples: SEE ALSO blue note
He played the first few notes of the tune.
high/low notes
I played a lot of wrong notes because I was so nervous.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a particular quality in something, for example in somebody’s voice or the atmosphere at an event; a comment on something with a particular quality
examples: SYNONYM air
There was a note of amusement in his voice.
It's good to finish on a positive note.
On a more serious note (= speaking more seriously)…
On a slightly different note (= changing the subject slightly), let’s talk about…
The year ended on an optimistic note.
As a side note, the entire festival is free.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: an official document with a particular purpose
examples: SEE ALSO credit note
a sick note from your doctor
The buyer has to sign a delivery note as proof of receipt.
Students returning to school after absence must bring a note from their parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: an official letter from the representative of one government to another
examples: an exchange of diplomatic notes

examples: We saw the play separately and compared notes afterwards.

examples: a scientist of note

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small book of plain paper for writing notes in
examples: The police officer wrote the details down in his notebook.
She kept a notebook (= wrote notes in it) during the trip.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small book for students to write their work in

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a small computer that can work with a battery and be easily carried
examples: SYNONYM laptop

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not anything; no single thing
examples: There was nothing in her bag.
There's nothing you can do to help.
The doctor said there was nothing wrong with me.
Nothing else matters to him apart from his job.
It cost us nothing to go in.
He's five foot nothing (= exactly five feet tall).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very little; something that is not at all important or interesting
examples: We did nothing at the weekend.
‘What's that in your pocket?’ ‘Oh, nothing.’
I know next to nothing (= almost nothing) about art.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be a person for whom somebody has no feelings
examples: I used to love her but she's nothing to me any more.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have no connection with somebody/something
examples: Get out! It's nothing to do with you (= you have no right to know about it).
That has nothing to do with what we're discussing.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: without payment
examples: SYNONYM free
She's always trying to get something for nothing.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: with no reward or result
examples: All that preparation was for nothing because the visit was cancelled.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have much less of a particular quality than somebody/something
examples: I'm quite a fast worker, but I've got nothing on her!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to have no information that could show somebody to be guilty of something

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used as a polite way of replying when somebody thanks you for doing something, to show that you were happy to do it
examples: ‘Thanks for all your help.’ ‘It was nothing—I enjoyed it.’

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: for a very good reason
examples: Not for nothing was he called the king of rock and roll.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: only; no more/less than
examples: Nothing but a miracle can save her now.
I want nothing but the best for my children.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: extremely; very
examples: The trip was nothing if not varied.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how great or extreme something is
examples: It was nothing less than a disaster.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: not at all like
examples: It looks nothing like a horse.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: not nearly; not at all
examples: I had nothing like enough time to answer all the questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: not a great amount of something; nothing of great value or importance
examples: There's nothing much in the fridge.
I got up late and did nothing much all day.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: (it’s) very easy
examples: You'll soon learn. There's nothing to it really.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to be willing to do anything to get what you want, even if it is dishonest or wrong
examples: She’ll stop at nothing to make money.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: romantic words
examples: to whisper sweet nothings in somebody’s ear

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: there is no other action to take except the one mentioned
examples: There was nothing else for it but to resign.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: something is/was not true
examples: There was a rumour she was going to resign, but there was nothing in it.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to say that you enjoy something very much
examples: There's nothing like a brisk walk on a cold day!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to see or hear somebody/something; to become aware of somebody/something
examples: People were making fun of him but he didn't seem to notice.
The first thing I noticed about the room was the smell.
I began to notice something strange.
You can't fail to notice the poverty of the region.
to barely/hardly/scarcely notice something
Most people never notice these details.
I couldn’t help noticing (that) she was wearing a wig.
He won't even notice I'm gone.
Did you notice how Rachel kept looking at her watch?
I noticed them come in.
I didn't notice him leaving.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to pay attention to somebody/something
examples: Notice the way the bridge is supported by its suspension cables.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to get attention from other people
examples: She wears those strange clothes just to get herself noticed.

definitions.definition: to formally or officially tell somebody about something
examples: SYNONYM inform
Competition winners will be notified by post.
You must notify us in writing if you wish to cancel your subscription.
The police must be notified of the date of the demonstration.
The date of the demonstration must be notified to the police.
Members have been notified that there will be a small increase in the fee.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an idea, a belief or an understanding of something
examples: a political system based on the notions of equality and liberty
She had only a vague notion of what might happen.
He has no notion of the difficulty of the problem.
The author challenges preconceived notions of storytelling.
She dismissed the very notion of compromise.
I have to reject the notion that greed can be a good thing.
I haven't the faintest notion how to get there.
I don't have any romantic notions about rural living.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: well known for being bad
examples: a notorious criminal
a location made notorious by battles between local gangs
The country is notorious for its appalling prison conditions.
The bar has become notorious as a meeting-place for drug dealers.
an area which is notorious as a centre for drug trafficking

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a story long enough to fill a complete book, in which the characters and events are usually imaginary
examples: SEE ALSO dime novel
to write/publish/read a novel
detective/historical/romantic novels
the novels of Jane Austen
Her latest novel is set in Cornwall.
a best-selling novel
Highsmith's debut novel was a bestseller in 1949.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the type of literature that novels represent
examples: The novel is the most adaptable of all literary forms.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who writes novels
examples: a romantic/historical novelist

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the 11th month of the year, between October and DecemberExtra Examples
examples: She was born in November.
The meeting is on the fifth of November/November the fifth.
The meeting is on November fifth.
We went to Japan last November.
I arrived at the end of November.
last November's election
It was a cold November night.
The competition will be held in New Delhi from November 19th to November 22nd.
In November 1945 he travelled from Moscow to Leningrad.
The report came five years after the floods of November 2000.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: (at) the present time
examples: Where are you living now?
They now have everything they wanted.
We now know the truth.
It's too late now.
It's been two weeks now since she called.
I can tell you right now that you're wrong.
I didn't receive the letter but it hardly matters now.
From now on I'll be more careful.
He should be home by now.
I've lived at home up till now.
That's all for now.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: at or from this moment, but not before
examples: Start writing now.
I am now ready to answer your questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to show that you are annoyed about something
examples: Now they want to tax food!
What do you want now?
It's broken. Now I'll have to get a new one.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to get somebody’s attention before changing the subject or asking them to do something
examples: Now, listen to what she's saying.
Now, the next point is quite complex.
Now come and sit down.
Now let me think…

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: from time to time; occasionally
examples: Every now and again she checked to see if he was still asleep.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when turning to a fresh activity or subject
examples: And now for some travel news.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show in a mild way that you do not approve of something
examples: Now now, that's enough noise.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: at one time… at another time…
examples: Her moods kept changing—now happy, now sad.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: this is the only opportunity somebody will have to do something

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to show in a mild way that you do not approve of something

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used when making a suggestion or an offer
examples: Now then, who wants to come for a walk?

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used when you are annoyed because somebody is always asking questions or interrupting you
examples: ‘Yes, but Dad…’ ‘Now what?’

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not know what to do next in a particular situationWord Origin
examples: Old English nū, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch nu, German nun, from an Indo-European root shared by Latin nunc and Greek nun.
