definitions.definition: at the present time, in contrast with the past
examples: Nowadays most kids prefer going online to reading books.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not in or to any place
examples: I had nowhere to live, so I was sleeping on my sister's couch.
There was nowhere for me to sit.
‘Where are you going this weekend?’ ‘Nowhere special.’
She doesn't want to stay there but she has nowhere else to go.
Nowhere do plants flourish with such vigour as they do in tropical rainforests.
This animal is found in Australia, and nowhere else.
Nowhere is the effect of government policy more apparent than in agriculture.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a sudden and surprising way
examples: A huge flock of sheep seemed to appear from nowhere.
The attack came from nowhere.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make no progress or have no success; to not enable somebody to make progress or have success
examples: We discussed it all morning but got nowhere.
Talking to him will get you nowhere.
His career was going nowhere fast.
The campaign over pay and conditions was getting nowhere.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have no successful result for somebody
examples: This discussion is leading us nowhere.
Often there are discoveries which lead nowhere.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a place that is a long way from other buildings, towns, etc.
examples: She lives on a small farm in the middle of nowhere.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: far from; not at all
examples: The job doesn't pay anywhere near enough for me.
Older cars are nowhere near as fuel-efficient as modern cars.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: far from; not at all
examples: Older cars are nowhere near as fuel-efficient as modern cars.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: impossible for anyone to find or see
examples: I wanted to talk to him but he was nowhere to be found.
The children were nowhere to be seen.
A peace settlement is nowhere in sight (= is not likely in the near future).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: using, producing or resulting from nuclear energy
examples: a nuclear power plant/station
China and India only produce a very small percentage of their electricity from nuclear facilities.
the nuclear industry
nuclear-powered submarines
a nuclear reactor
nuclear waste/fuel

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with weapons that use nuclear energy
examples: nuclear weapons/arms
a nuclear bomb/missile/warhead
a nuclear explosion/attack/war
the country’s nuclear capability (= the fact that it has nuclear weapons)
The country is developing a nuclear weapons program.
They aim to discourage the country from developing its nuclear weapons program further.
They argued in favour of keeping a nuclear deterrent (= nuclear weapons that are intended to stop an enemy from attacking).
The opponents are campaigning for nuclear disarmament.
Years of threats by the U.S. have done nothing to curb these states' nuclear ambitions (= attempts to develop nuclear weapons).
Russia's huge nuclear arsenal

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: of the nucleus (= central part) of an atom
examples: nuclear particles
a nuclear reaction

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a word or symbol that represents an amount or a quantity
examples: SYNONYM figure
Think of a number and multiply it by two.
a high/low number
even numbers (= 2, 4, 6, etc.)
odd numbers (= 1, 3, 5, etc.)
You owe me 27 dollars? Make it 30, that's a good round number.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used before a figure to show the position of something in a series
examples: They live at number 26.
The song reached number 5 in the charts.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a set of figures that is used to identify something or communicate by phone, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO 800 number
Ask for the customer's name and phone number.
Customers can reach us by calling an 0800 number (= a free phone number in the UK).
I'm sorry, I think you have the wrong number (= wrong phone number).
Call this number and ask to speak to John.
What is your account number, please?
Can I have your credit card number?
Please give your landline and mobile phone numbers.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a quantity of people or things
examples: A large number of people have applied for the job.
In a small number of cases the illness is fatal.
The number of homeless people has increased dramatically.
The total number of students has doubled in the last six years.
Huge numbers of (= very many) animals have died.
A number of (= some) problems have arisen.
I could give you any number of (= a lot of) reasons for not going.
Use a pedometer to count the number of steps you take.
Our aim is to reduce the number of road accidents.
This year we have increased the number of events from six to ten.
We were eight in number (= there were eight of us).
Nurses are leaving the profession in increasing numbers.
Sheer weight of numbers (= the large number of soldiers) secured them the victory.
The course will have to be repeated owing to pressure of numbers (= too many students).
staff/student numbers

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a group or quantity of people
examples: one of our number (= one of us)
The prime minister is elected by MPs from among their number.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the version of a magazine, etc. published on a particular day, in a particular month, etc.
examples: SYNONYM issue
the October number of ‘Vogue’
The back numbers of ‘The Times’ were kept in a basement.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a song or dance, especially one of several in a performance
examples: They sang a slow romantic number.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a thing, such as a dress or a car, that is admired
examples: She was wearing a black velvet number.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the form of a word, showing whether one or more than one person or thing is being talked about
examples: The word ‘men’ is plural in number.
The subject of a sentence and its verb must agree in number.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: following a set of simple instructions identified by numbers
examples: painting by numbers

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: following closely the accepted rules for doing something

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: an easy job; a pleasant situation that other people would like
examples: It’s all right for him—he’s got a very cushy number.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to know what somebody is really like and what they plan to do
examples: He thinks he can fool me but I've got his number.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: the time has come when you will die or lose everything

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: a way of considering an activity, etc. that considers only the number of people doing something, things achieved, etc., not with who or what they are
examples: MPs were playing the numbers game as the crucial vote drew closer.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: a person who does the same job as you in another organization
examples: The Foreign Secretary is currently having talks with his opposite number in the White House.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: being in a group makes you safer and makes you feel more confident

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: being in a group gives you more power
examples: There's strength in numbers, so encourage your friends and family to join us.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: the combined power, strength or influence of a group
examples: They won the argument by sheer weight of numbers.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

advice on diet and nutrition
to study food science and nutrition

definitions.label: Meaning 2

art objects from the ancient world

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being forced to do something because it is your duty, or because of a law, etc.
examples: You are under no obligation to buy anything.
She did not feel under any obligation to tell him the truth.
I don't want people coming to see me out of a sense of obligation.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something which you must do because you have promised, because of a law, etc.
examples: SYNONYM commitment
legal/professional/financial obligations

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to force somebody to do something, by law, because it is a duty, etc.
examples: Parents are obliged by law to send their children to school.
I felt obliged to ask them to dinner.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to help somebody by doing what they ask or what you know they want
examples: Call me if you need any help—I'd be happy to oblige.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of watching somebody/something carefully for a period of time, especially to learn something

an observation post/tower (= a place from where somebody, especially an enemy, can be watched)
an observation deck (= a room or platform at the top of a tall building which provides views of the surrounding area)
his close observations of animal life in its natural setting

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a comment, especially based on something you have seen, heard or read
examples: SYNONYM remark

her witty observations on life

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to watch somebody/something carefully, especially to learn more about them
examples: He observes keenly, but says little.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a remark
examples: She observed that it was getting late.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: Will the rebels observe the ceasefire?

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: Do they observe Christmas?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who watches somebody/something

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who attends a meeting, lesson, etc. to listen and watch but not to take part
examples: A team of British officials were sent as observers to the conference.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who watches and studies particular events, situations, etc. and is therefore considered to be an expert on them

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to completely fill your mind so that you cannot think of anything else, in a way that is not normal

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be always talking or worrying about a particular thing, especially when this annoys other people
examples: SEE ALSO self-obsessed
I think you should try to stop obsessing about food.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state in which a person’s mind is completely filled with thoughts of one particular thing or person in a way that is not normal
examples: Her fear of flying is bordering on obsession.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or thing that somebody thinks about too much
examples: Fitness has become an obsession with him.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 5

jobs that have traditionally been occupied by men

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a large amount of somethingWord Origin

definitions.label: Meaning 1

last October's election
the October issue of the magazine

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: strange or unusual
examples: COMPARE peculiar
They're very odd people.
There's something odd about that man.
That painting looks very odd.

examples: an odd-looking house

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is different from others or does not fit easily into a group or set
examples: At school he was always the odd man out.

definitions.label: Meaning 10

examples: Middle English (in the numerical sense): from Old Norse odda-, found in combinations such as odda-mathr ‘third or odd man’, from oddi ‘angle’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 12

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say that you are willing to do something for somebody
examples: The kids offered to do the dishes.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make something available for sale or use
examples: The hotel offers excellent facilities for families.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to provide the opportunity for something; to provide access to something

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to show that you are ready to resist or attack somebody/something

definitions.label: Meaning 6

to get/grow old

a little old lady
She was a woman grown old before her time (= who looked older than she was).
He was beginning to look old.
Tom was the last surviving member of the older generation of the family.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: old people
examples: The old feel the cold more than the young.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: having existed or been used for a long time
examples: OPPOSITE new
old habits
He always gives the same old excuses.
This carpet's getting pretty old now.
a beautiful old farmhouse

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: former; belonging to past times or a past time in your life
examples: Things were different in the old days.
I went back to visit my old school.
Old and Middle English
People are still clinging to the old ways of thinking.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to refer to something that has been replaced by something else
examples: OPPOSITE new
We had more room in our old house.
Mum and Dad bought us a fridge and gave us their old telly.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: known for a long time
examples: COMPARE recent
She's an old friend of mine (= I have known her for a long time).
We're old rivals.
It's always the same old faces.
The album includes both new titles and old favourites.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to show kind feelings or a lack of respect
examples: Good old Dad!
You poor old thing!
I hate her, the silly old cow!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: any item of the type mentioned (used when it is not important which particular item is chosen)
examples: Any old room would have done.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: in a careless or untidy way
examples: The books were piled up all over the floor any old how.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: very old; ancient

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be behaving in the same bad way as before
examples: He had soon spent all the money and was up to his old tricks.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a person who is very similar to their mother or father in the way that they look or behave

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: if you do something for old times’ sake, you do it because it is connected with something good that happened to you in the past

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to dismiss somebody from their job; to end a relationship with somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: an earlier period of time in your life or in history that is seen as better/worse than the present
examples: That was in the bad old days of rampant inflation.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: a great age
examples: She finally learned to drive at the grand old age of 70.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: a man who is respected in a particular profession that he has been involved in for a long time
examples: James Lovelock, the grand old man of environmental science

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to enjoy yourself very much

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used to give an amount, a measurement, etc. using older or more traditional units that may be more familiar to some people
examples: The fish measured 29 centimetres (that's a foot in old money).

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: money that is earned very easily, for something that needs little effort
examples: The job only took about an hour—it was money for old rope.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: an older person who behaves in a stupid way is worse than a younger person who does the same thing, because experience should have taught him or her not to do it

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: in or since past times
examples: in days of old
We know him of old (= we have known him for a long time).

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used by older men of the middle and upper classes as a friendly way of addressing another man

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: very much older than somebody (especially used to suggest that a romantic or sexual relationship between the two people is not appropriate)

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: old enough to behave in a more sensible way than you actually did

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: used to describe a young person who acts in a more sensible way than you would expect for a person of their age

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: what usually happens
examples: It's the same old story of a badly managed project with inadequate funding.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: an old idea or belief that people now know is not correct

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: an old-fashioned person who likes to do things as they were done in the past
examples: SEE ALSO old school

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: an age that is considered to be very old
examples: He lived to the ripe old age of 91.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to hurt or punish somebody who has harmed or cheated you in the past
examples: ‘Who would do such a thing?’ ‘Maybe someone with an old score to settle.’
An embittered Charlotte is determined to settle accounts with Elizabeth.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: (you cannot) successfully make people change their ideas, methods of work, etc., when they have had them for a long time

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: very strong and able to deal successfully with difficult conditions or situations
examples: She’s almost 90 but she’s still as tough as old boots.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not modern; no longer fashionable
examples: SYNONYM dated
old-fashioned clothes/styles/methods/equipment

The Winnedumah Hotel has old-fashioned charm.
His clothes were curiously old-fashioned.
Critics regarded her films as hopelessly old-fashioned.
The whole room looked old-fashioned.
The hotel is quaint and old-fashioned.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: believing in old or traditional ways; having traditional ideas
examples: My parents are old-fashioned about relationships and marriage.
She wants to be an old-fashioned mother, staying at home and looking after the children.
Call me old-fashioned, but I still believe in good manners.
She's somewhat old-fashioned in her attitudes.
He seemed too old-fashioned and formal.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: simple, traditional and good quality
examples: At heart, it's just a good old-fashioned detective story.
What's needed is some good old-fashioned common sense.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: a picture on a wall
There's a mark on your skirt.
the diagram on page 5
Put it down on the table.
He had been hit on the head.
She climbed on to the bed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: supported by somebody/something
examples: She was standing on one foot.
Try lying on your back.
Hang your coat on that hook.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to show a means of transport
examples: He was on the plane from New York.
to travel on the bus/tube/coach
I came on my bike.
a woman on horseback

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: by means of something; using something
examples: She played a tune on her guitar.
The information is available on the internet.

What's on TV?
The programme's on Channel 4.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to show a day or date
examples: He came on Sunday.
We meet on Tuesdays.
on May the first/the first of May
on the evening of May the first
on one occasion
on your birthday

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to describe an activity or a state
examples: to be on business/holiday/vacation
The book is currently on loan.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show direction
examples: on the left/right
He turned his back on us.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: at or near a place
examples: a town on the coast
a house on the Thames

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to show the basis or reason for something
examples: a story based on fact

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: immediately after something
examples: On arriving home I discovered they had gone.
Please report to reception on arrival.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: about something/somebody
examples: a book on South Africa

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to show that somebody belongs to a group or an organization
examples: to be on the committee/staff/jury/panel
Whose side are you on (= which of two or more different views do you support)?

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: eating or drinking something; using a drug or a medicine regularly
examples: He lived on a diet of junk food.

definitions.label: Meaning 14

to be on a low wage

definitions.definition: at some time in the past
examples: I once met your mother.
He once lived in Zambia.
This book was famous once, but nobody reads it today.
She remembers once travelling with her father to Kilkenny.
I famously once said that I was a fighter and not a quitter.

It was once thought to be the best hotel in Europe.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used in negative sentences and questions, and after if to mean ‘ever’ or ‘at all’
examples: He never once offered to help.
If she once decides to do something, you won't change her mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: suddenly

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: immediately; without delay
examples: Come here at once!

definitions.label: Meaning 8

I can't do two things at once.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: Just for once he arrived on time.
Can't you be nice to each other just this once?

definitions.label: Meaning 10

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: one more time; another time
examples: Once again the train was late.

definitions.label: Meaning 12

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: after an unpleasant experience you are careful to avoid something similar

definitions.label: Meaning 14

a one-bedroomed apartment
I'll see you at one (= one o'clock).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used in formal language or for emphasis before hundred, thousand, etc., or before a unit of measurement
examples: It cost one hundred and fifty pounds.
He lost by less than one second.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used for emphasis to mean ‘a single’ or ‘just one’
examples: PAST TENSE, PAST PARTICIPLE OF win
There's only one thing we can do.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person or thing, especially when they are part of a group
examples: One of my friends lives in Brighton.
One place I'd really like to visit is Bali.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used for emphasis to mean ‘the only one’ or ‘the most important one’
examples: He's the one person I can trust.
Her one concern was for the health of her baby.
It's the one thing I can't stand about him.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when you are talking about a time in the past or the future, without actually saying which one
examples: I saw her one afternoon last week.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the same
examples: They all went off in one direction.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used for emphasis instead of a or an
examples: That was one hell of a game!
She's one snappy dresser.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used with a person’s name to show that the speaker does not know the person
examples: SYNONYM certain (5)

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: in agreement; all together
examples: We spoke as one on this matter.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to feel that you completely agree with somebody/something, or that you are part of something
examples: a place where you can feel at one with nature

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a return to the situation you were in at the beginning of a project, task, etc., because you have made no real progress
examples: If this suggestion isn't accepted, we'll be back to square one.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be the only person to have a particular opinion or to vote a particular way

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that a particular person does something and that you believe other people do too
examples: I, for one, would prefer to postpone the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to understand or guess something immediately
examples: ‘Oh, so she’s his sister!’ ‘Got it in one!’

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to get an advantage over somebody/something
examples: I'm not going to let them get one over on me!

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to do something better than somebody else or than you have done before

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody/something has different roles, contains different things or is used for different purposes
examples: SEE ALSO all-in-one

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: first one person or thing, and then another, and then another, up to any number or amount

definitions.label: Meaning 20

definitions.label: Meaning 21

definitions.label: Meaning 22

definitions.label: Meaning 23

definitions.label: Meaning 24

definitions.label: Meaning 25

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the number 1
examples: Do you want one or two?
There's only room for one person.
One more, please!
a one-bedroomed apartment
I'll see you at one (= one o'clock).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used in formal language or for emphasis before hundred, thousand, etc., or before a unit of measurement
examples: It cost one hundred and fifty pounds.
He lost by less than one second.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used for emphasis to mean ‘a single’ or ‘just one’
examples: PAST TENSE, PAST PARTICIPLE OF win
There's only one thing we can do.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person or thing, especially when they are part of a group
examples: One of my friends lives in Brighton.
One place I'd really like to visit is Bali.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used for emphasis to mean ‘the only one’ or ‘the most important one’
examples: He's the one person I can trust.
Her one concern was for the health of her baby.
It's the one thing I can't stand about him.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when you are talking about a time in the past or the future, without actually saying which one
examples: I saw her one afternoon last week.
One day (= at some time in the future) you'll understand.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the same
examples: They all went off in one direction.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used for emphasis instead of a or an
examples: That was one hell of a game!
She's one snappy dresser.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used with a person’s name to show that the speaker does not know the person
examples: SYNONYM certain (5)
He worked as an assistant to one Mr Ming.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: in agreement; all together
examples: We spoke as one on this matter.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to feel that you completely agree with somebody/something, or that you are part of something
examples: a place where you can feel at one with nature

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a return to the situation you were in at the beginning of a project, task, etc., because you have made no real progress
examples: If this suggestion isn't accepted, we'll be back to square one.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be the only person to have a particular opinion or to vote a particular way

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that a particular person does something and that you believe other people do too
examples: I, for one, would prefer to postpone the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to understand or guess something immediately
examples: ‘Oh, so she’s his sister!’ ‘Got it in one!’

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to get an advantage over somebody/something
examples: I'm not going to let them get one over on me!

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to do something better than somebody else or than you have done before
examples: SYNONYM outdo
She did well this year and next year she hopes to go one better.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody/something has different roles, contains different things or is used for different purposes
examples: SEE ALSO all-in-one
She's a mother and company director in one.
It's a public relations office, a press office and a private office all in one.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: first one person or thing, and then another, and then another, up to any number or amount
examples: The bills kept coming in, one after another.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: everyone
examples: Happy New Year to one and all!

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that somebody is famous
examples: Here she is, the one and only Rihanna!

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used for emphasis to mean ‘the same’
examples: I never realized Ruth Rendell and Barbara Vine were one and the same (= the same person using two different names).

definitions.label: Meaning 23

examples: I went through the items on the list one by one.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: a few
examples: We've had one or two problems—nothing serious.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: having an advantage over somebody

examples: I've been going there every summer since the year one.

Training is part of our ongoing career development program.

examples: SEE ALSO spring onion
Chop the onions finely.
French onion soup
slice/fry/peel an onion
Pile golden caramelized onions on top of mashed potatoes.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to show that something faces in a particular direction
examples: The window looked out onto the terrace.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: allowing things or people to go through; not closed or blocked
examples: OPPOSITE closed
A wasp flew in the open window.
She had left the door wide open.
The castle gates swung open.
The door burst open and the children rushed in.
She held the door open for them.
In spite of the snow, the roads remained open.
The mountain pass is kept open all year.
open borders
Borders between the countries are open and passports are not required.
Taylor headed the ball into the open goal.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: with eyelids or lips apart
examples: OPPOSITE closed
She had difficulty keeping her eyes open (= because she was very tired).
He was breathing through his open mouth.
She stared at him, her mouth hanging open.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: spread out; with the edges apart
examples: OPPOSITE closed
The flowers are all open now.
The book lay open on the table.
She put the money into his open hand.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not fastened or covered, so that things can easily come out or be put in
examples: Leave the envelope open.
The bag burst open and everything fell out.
I tried to pry open the locket.
The children ripped open the presents excitedly.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not fastened
examples: Her coat was open.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not surrounded by anything; not closed in
examples: open country/countryside (= without forests, buildings, etc.)
a city with a lot of parks and wide open spaces
driving along the open road (= part of a road in the country, where you can drive fast)
We left port and headed for the open sea.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: with no cover or roof on
examples: an open drain
people working in the open air (= not in a building)
The hall of the old house was open to the sky.
an open wound (= with no skin covering it)
They were living in a tent, cooking their meals on an open fire.
She sliced open the side of her thumb cutting up a tomato.
an open flame

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if a shop, bank, business, etc. is open, it is ready for business and will allow customers or visitors to come in
examples: OPPOSITE closed
Is the museum open on Sundays?
The new store will be open in the spring.
I declare this festival open.
The bank is open for business again.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: if a competition, meeting, etc. is open, anyone can enter, attend it, etc.
examples: an open debate/championship/scholarship
She was tried in open court (= the public could go and listen to the trial).
The debate was thrown open to the audience.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: if a competition, building, etc. is open to particular people, those people can enter it
examples: OPPOSITE closed
The competition is open to young people under the age of 18.
The house is not open to the public.
The car park is only open to residents.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be available and ready to use
examples: OPPOSITE closed
Is the offer still open?
I want to keep my Swiss bank account open.
What options are open to us?
My advice is to keep your options open.
We have kept the door open for future discussions.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if a phone line or other channel of communication is open, it is ready to take calls, receive requests, etc.
examples: OPPOSITE closed
Lines are open 8 am to 7 pm weekdays.
It is important to keep communication channels open.
Nominations are now open for this year's Design Awards.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: likely to suffer something such as criticism, injury, etc.
examples: SYNONYM vulnerable
The system is open to abuse.
He has laid himself wide open to political attack.
Kasparov had left his bishop open (= not protected, in a game of chess).

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: known to everyone; not kept hidden
examples: an open quarrel
We need more open government, starting with a Freedom of Information Act.
their open display of affection
His eyes showed open admiration as he looked at her.
One more border skirmish could lead to open war.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: honest; not keeping thoughts and feelings hidden
examples: SYNONYM frank
a frank and open discussion
She was always open with her parents.
He was quite open about his reasons for leaving.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: willing to listen to and think about new ideas
examples: He was in an open frame of mind.
They are very open to new ideas.
I'm open to suggestions for what you would like to do in our classes.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: not yet finally decided or settled
examples: The race is still wide open (= anyone could win).
Which route is better remains an open question (= it is not decided).
In an interview try to ask open questions (= to which the answer is not just ‘yes’ or ‘no’).

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: allowing something; making something possible
examples: The price is not open to negotiation.
Some phrases in the contract are open to interpretation.
What she means precisely is open to debate.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: that does not have to be used on a particular day
examples: I have an open ticket, so I can travel any day I like.
I didn't know how long I would be staying so I bought an open return.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: with wide spaces between the threads
examples: an open weave

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: produced with the tongue in the lowest possible position
examples: COMPARE close2 (16)

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: if something is an open secret, many people know about it, although it is supposed to be a secret

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to open suddenly or violently; to make something open in this way
examples: The door burst open.
Firefighters burst the door open and rescued them.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: (to provide) the means of getting or reaching something; (to create) the opportunity for something
examples: The agreement will open the door to increased international trade.
Our courses are the door to success in English.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to be willing to listen to or accept new ideas or suggestions
examples: Try to keep an open mind until you've heard all the facts.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to listen or look out for somebody/something that you might hear or see

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to look for somebody/something while you are doing other things
examples: Police have asked residents to keep an eye out for anything suspicious.
I walked around the store, keeping an eye out for bargains.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to avoid making a decision now so that you still have a choice in the future
examples: At the moment I'm keeping my options open and applying for as many different jobs as possible.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: available to buy without any limits

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: if you describe somebody or their life as an open book, you mean that you can easily understand them and know everything about them

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: an invitation to somebody to visit you at any time

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: if something is an open invitation to criminals, etc., it encourages them to commit a crime by making it easier
examples: Leaving your camera on the seat in the car is an open invitation to thieves.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: fully aware of the possible problems or results of a particular course of action
examples: I went into this with my eyes open so I guess I only have myself to blame.

definitions.definition: if you welcome somebody with open arms, you are extremely happy and pleased to see themWord Origin

definitions.definition: a space or hole that somebody/something can pass through
examples: We could see the stars through an opening in the roof.
It looks like the opening to a small cave.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the beginning or first part of something
examples: OPPOSITE ending
The movie has an exciting opening.
a brilliant opening sequence
It's such a brave opening to a book.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a ceremony to celebrate the start of a public event or the first time a new building, road, etc. is used
examples: the official opening of the new hospital
the opening of the Olympic Games
the state opening of Parliament
tickets for the opening ceremony
The gallery has scheduled a grand opening for June 29.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act or process of making something open or of becoming open
examples: COMPARE closing
the opening of a flower
the opening of the new play
Late opening of supermarkets is common in Britain now.
She heard footsteps and the opening and closing of the door.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a job that is available
examples: SYNONYM vacancy
There are several openings in the sales department.
We will keep you informed of any job openings.
She is the strongest candidate to fill this opening.
Most openings in the mills were for single women.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a good opportunity for somebody
examples: Winning the competition was the opening she needed for her career.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: part of a piece of clothing that is made to open and close so that it can be put on easily
examples: The skirt has a side opening.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: without hiding any feelings, opinions or information
examples: Can you talk openly about sex with your parents?
The men in prison would never cry openly (= so that other people could see).

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: SEE ALSO soap opera
Puccini’s operas
to go to the opera
an opera singer
light/grand opera

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a company that performs opera; a building in which operas are performed
examples: the Vienna State Opera

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to work in a particular way
examples: Most domestic freezers operate at below −18°C.
Solar panels can only operate in sunlight.
Some people can only operate well under pressure.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to use or control a machine or make it work
examples: What skills are needed to operate this machinery?
They use a remotely operated camera.
The doors can be manually operated in the event of fire.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to manage a business, organization or service
examples: The airline currently operates flights to 25 countries.
By last year, the chain was operating 388 stores in 47 states.
He started and operated a successful technology business.
The company operates public transport services across the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to work, especially in a particular way or from a particular place
examples: A new late-night service is now operating.
They plan to operate from a new office in Edinburgh.
Retailers operate in a fast-paced environment.
The business operates on a cooperative basis.
We operate independently from our sister companies.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be used or working; to use something or make it work
examples: The regulation operates in favour of married couples.
He believes that sinister forces are operating.
France operates a system of subsidized loans to dairy farmers.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to cut open somebody’s body in order to remove a part that has a disease or to repair a part that is damaged
examples: Surgeons operated last night.
We will have to operate on his eyes.
She was operated on the next day.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be involved in military activities in a place
examples: Troops are operating from bases in the north.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of cutting open a part of a person’s body in order to remove or repair a damaged part
examples: Will I need to have an operation?

He had an operation to remove a growth.
an operation on her lung to remove a tumour
Doctors performed an emergency operation for appendicitis last night.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an organized activity that involves several people

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person that you are playing or fighting against in a game, competition, argument, etc.

a political opponent

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is against something and tries to change or stop it
examples: opponents of abortion
opponents of the regime

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a time when a particular situation makes it possible to do or achieve something
examples: SYNONYM chance

There’ll be plenty of opportunity for relaxing once the work is done.
At least give him the opportunity of explaining what happened.

a business/an investment opportunity

I would definitely go if the opportunity arose.
a window of opportunity (= a period of time when the circumstances are right for doing something)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to disagree strongly with somebody’s plan, policy, etc. and try to change it or prevent it from succeeding
examples: COMPARE propose
This party would bitterly oppose the re-introduction of the death penalty.
He threw all those that opposed him into prison.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: He intends to oppose the prime minister in the leadership election.

definitions.definition: disagreeing strongly with something and trying to stop it
examples: He was strongly opposed to modernism in art.
She remained bitterly opposed to the idea of moving abroad.
They are totally opposed to abortion.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very different from something
examples: Our views are diametrically opposed on this issue.
The two sets of values seemed mutually opposed.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to make a contrast between two things
examples: 200 attended, as opposed to 300 the previous year.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: on the other side of a particular area from somebody/something and usually facing them
examples: Answers are given on the opposite page.
We live further down on the opposite side of the road.
It's not easy having a relationship when you live at opposite ends of the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: facing the speaker or somebody/something that has been mentioned
examples: I could see smoke coming from the windows of the house directly opposite.
He sat down in the chair opposite.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: as different as possible from something

a story about a pair of young boys from opposite extremes of society

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: The Foreign Secretary is currently having talks with his opposite number in the White House.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the other sex
examples: He found it difficult to talk to members of the opposite sex.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have different aims that cannot be achieved together without causing problems
examples: There are different considerations, often pulling in different directions.

definitions.label: Meaning 13

definitions.label: Meaning 15

a steady fall in overall crime rates
an overall result/impact/aim/strategy

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to succeed in dealing with or controlling a problem that has been preventing you from achieving something
examples: She overcame injury to win the Olympic gold medal.
The two parties managed to overcome their differences on the issue.
He finally managed to overcome his fear of flying
He overcame a strong temptation to run away.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to defeat somebody
examples: In the final game Sweden easily overcame France.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to affect somebody very strongly
examples: SYNONYM overwhelm
Her parents were overcome with grief at the funeral.
Overcome by curiosity, the boy looked through the window.
The dead woman had been overcome by smoke.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to fail to see or notice something
examples: SYNONYM miss
He seems to have overlooked one important fact.
In my hurry to finish the exam I had overlooked part of one of the questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to see something wrong or bad but decide to ignore it
examples: SYNONYM turn a blind eye (to something)
We could not afford to overlook such a serious offence.
He’s so friendly people are prepared to overlook his faults.
I was prepared to overlook her mistakes this time.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if a building, etc. overlooks a place, you can see that place from the building
examples: a restaurant overlooking the lake
Our back yard is overlooked by several houses.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to not consider somebody for a job or position, even though they might be suitable
examples: SYNONYM pass over
She's been overlooked for promotion several times.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: too; very
examples: SYNONYM excessively
I'm not overly fond of pasta.
We think you are being overly optimistic.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: during or for the night
examples: We stayed overnight in London after the theatre.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: suddenly or quickly
examples: Don't expect it to improve overnight.
She became famous overnight.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with foreign countries, especially those separated from your country by the sea or ocean
examples: COMPARE home
The firm is expanding into overseas markets.
overseas development/trade
overseas visitors/students
This was her first overseas trip as prime minister.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with foreign countries, especially those separated from your country by the sea or ocean
examples: COMPARE home
The firm is expanding into overseas markets.
overseas development/trade
overseas visitors/students

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to watch somebody/something and make sure that a job or an activity is done correctly
examples: SYNONYM supervise
United Nations observers oversaw the elections.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if something overturns, or if somebody overturns it, it turns into a position in which the top of it is where the bottom of it normally is or on its side
examples: The car skidded and overturned.
He stood up quickly, overturning his chair.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to officially decide that a legal decision, etc. is not correct, and to make it no longer legally recognized
examples: to overturn a decision/conviction/verdict
His sentence was overturned by the appeal court.
He hopes that councillors will overturn the decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show that a belief or an idea is not correct
examples: She completely overturned my preconceptions about film stars.
This argument seems convincing, but is easily overturned.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have such a strong emotional effect on somebody that it is difficult for them to resist or know how to react
examples: SYNONYM overcome
She was overwhelmed by feelings of guilt.
The beauty of the landscape overwhelmed me.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to defeat somebody completely
examples: SYNONYM overpower
The army was overwhelmed by the rebels.
He totally overwhelmed the Spaniard, 6–2, 6–3,6–2, in the final.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be so bad or so great that a person cannot deal with it; to give too much of a thing to a person
examples: We were overwhelmed by requests for information.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to cover somebody/something completely
examples: The wave broke through the wall and overwhelmed the town.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very great or very strong; so powerful that you cannot resist it or decide how to react
examples: The evidence against him was overwhelming.
The overwhelming majority of those present were in favour of the plan.
an overwhelming sense of loss
She had the almost overwhelming desire to tell him the truth.
You may find it somewhat overwhelming at first.
There was overwhelming support for our policies.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have to pay somebody for something that you have already received or return money that you have borrowed
examples: She still owes her father £3 000.
I'm still owed three days' leave.
He owes more money than he can afford to pay.
Exactly how much do we owe?
She still owes £3 000 to her father
The country owes billions of dollars to foreign creditors.
Most hospitals owe money to pharmaceutical companies for medicines and equipment.
How much do I owe you for the groceries?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to feel that you ought to do something for somebody or give them something, especially because they have done something for you
examples: I owe a debt of gratitude to all my family.
You owe it to your staff to be honest with them.
I owe a duty to my family.
You owe me a favour!
Thanks for sticking up for me—I owe you one (= I owe you a favour).
I think you owe us an explanation.
I think we're owed an apology.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to exist or be successful because of the help or influence of somebody/something
examples: He owes his success to hard work.
The play owes much to French tragedy.
I owe everything to him.
The town owes its existence to the minerals that lie below the mountains.
I owe him everything.
I knew that I owed the surgeon my life.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have to obey and support somebody who is in a position of authority or power
examples: All serfs owed allegiance to a lord.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something belongs to or is connected with somebody
examples: It was her own idea.
I saw it with my own eyes (= I didn't hear about it from somebody else).
Is the car your own?
Your day off is your own (= you can spend it as you wish).
He desperately wants to live his own life (= be independent and do whatever he wants).
Our children are grown up and have children of their own.
For reasons of his own (= particular reasons that perhaps only he knew about), he refused to join the club.
The accident happened through no fault of her own.
He wants to come into the business on his own terms.
I need a room of my own.
I have my very own room at last.
their own personal/unique/private beliefs
He was determined to go his own way.
I was almost completely in my own little world.
Most people want to live in their own homes as they age.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: done or produced by and for yourself
examples: She makes all her own clothes.
He has to cook his own meals.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have the opportunity to show how good or useful you are or something is
examples: When the traffic's this bad, a bicycle really comes into its own.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: bad people often seem to have good luck

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to do something to somebody in return for harm they have done to you; to get revenge
examples: I'll get my own back on him one day, I swear!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to have your own opinion and make your own decisions without being influenced by other people
examples: She has a mind of her own and isn't afraid to say what she thinks.
My computer seems to have a mind of its own!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to remain in a strong position when somebody is attacking you, competing with you, etc.
examples: Business isn't good but we're managing to hold our own.
She can hold her own against anybody in an argument.
The patient is holding her own although she is still very sick.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: because of your personal qualifications or efforts, not because of your connection with somebody else
examples: She sings with a rock band, but she's also a jazz musician in her own right.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to like talking a lot or too much, usually without wanting to listen to other people
examples: She’s much too fond of the sound of her own voice.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: alone; without anyone else
examples: I'm all on my own today.
She lives on her own.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: without help
examples: He did it on his own.

a passive observer of events
She wore a passive expression on her face as if she didn’t care what happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with the form of a verb used when the subject is affected by the action of the verb, for example He was bitten by a dog.
examples: COMPARE active

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official document that identifies you as a citizen of a particular country, and that you may have to show when you enter or leave a country
examples: a valid passport
a fake passport
a South African passport
to issue/confiscate a passport
I was stopped as I went through passport control (= where passports are checked).
EU passport holders
a passport photo

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that makes something possible or enables you to achieve something
examples: SYNONYM key
The only passport to success is hard work.
The gold medal is his passport into professional boxing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a series of letters, numbers, etc. that you must type into a computer or computer system in order to be able to use it
examples: Enter a username and password to get into the system.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a secret word or phrase that you need to know in order to be allowed into a place
examples: You must give the password before they'll let you in.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: gone by in time
examples: PAST TENSE, PAST PARTICIPLE OF pass
in past years/centuries
in times past
The time for discussion is past.
The days are long past when people worked at the same company all their lives.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: gone by recently; just ended
examples: in the past year/month/week
I've seen her several times over the past few days.
The past month has been really busy at work.
This past summer I worked at a theatre.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: belonging to an earlier time
examples: From past experience I'd say he'd probably forgotten the time.
past and present students of the college
Let's forget about who was more to blame—it's all past history.
I warned her not to repeat her past mistakes.
past events
Americans hold past presidents in high regard.
He is reluctant to speak about his past life as a professional musician.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a minister in charge of a Christian church or group, especially in some Nonconformist churches
examples: He was ordained a pastor in the Lutheran Church.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small area of something, especially one which is different from the area around it
examples: a black dog with a white patch on its back
a bald patch on the top of his head
damp patches on the wall
patches of dense fog
We sat in a patch of shade under a tree.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small piece of material that is used to cover a hole in something or to make a weak area stronger, or as decoration
examples: I sewed patches on the knees of my jeans.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a piece of material that you wear over an eye, usually because the eye is damaged
examples: SEE ALSO eyepatch
He had a black patch over one eye.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a piece of material that you sew onto clothes as part of a uniform
examples: He wears a patch from his employer, Verizon.
It has a UPS patch sewn on the right shoulder.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a piece of material that people can wear on their skin to help them to stop smoking
examples: nicotine patches

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a small piece of land, especially one used for growing vegetables or fruit
examples: a vegetable patch
We had a strawberry patch beside the greenhouse.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an area that somebody works in, knows well or comes from
examples: He knows every house in his patch.
She has had a lot of success in her home patch.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a period of time of the type mentioned, usually a difficult or unhappy one
examples: SEE ALSO purple patch
to go through a bad/difficult/sticky patch

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a small piece of code (= instructions that a computer can understand) which can be added to a computer program to improve it or to correct a fault
examples: Follow the instructions below to download and install the patch.
Update and apply all security patches to your browser, as soon as possible.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be much less good, attractive, etc. than somebody/something else
examples: This book isn’t a patch on her others.
She was no great beauty. Not a patch on Martha.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official right to be the only person to make, use or sell a product or an invention; a document that proves this
examples: to apply for/obtain/take out a patent on an invention
The device was protected by patent.
patent applications/laws
the US Patent Office

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a way or track that is built or is made by the action of people walking
examples: SEE ALSO bridle path
a dirt/gravel/concrete path
Follow the path through the woods.
They walked along the cliff path to the next town.
The path led up a steep hill.
a coastal path

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a plan of action or a way of achieving something
examples: SYNONYM pathway (2)
Her sister followed a different career path.
There is no easy path to success.
Here are some pointers to set you on the right path.
The company cannot continue on its current path.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a line along which somebody/something moves; the space in front of somebody/something as they move
examples: SYNONYM way
Three men blocked her path.
He threw himself into the path of an oncoming vehicle.
We're trying to get people out of the path of the storm.
The avalanche forced its way down the mountain, crushing everything in its path.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if a lot of people beat a path to somebody’s door, they are all interested in something that person has to sell, or can do or tell them
examples: Top theatrical agents are beating a path to the teenager's door.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if somebody crosses somebody’s path or their paths cross, they meet by chance
examples: I hope I never cross her path again.
Our paths were to cross again many years later.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make somebody believe something that is not true

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: (to choose, etc.) the easiest way of doing something

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: an easy life that is full of pleasure but that causes you harm in the end

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to make it easier for somebody/something to develop or make progress
examples: These negotiations are intended to smooth the path to a peace treaty.
We’re trying to smooth the way for women who want to resume their careers.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a track that serves as a path
examples: They came out of the woods and onto a pathway.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a plan of action or way of achieving something
examples: SYNONYM path (2)
We help students define and develop a clear career pathway.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a route formed by a chain of nerve cells along which electrical signals travel from one part of the body to another
examples: neural pathways

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the ability to stay calm and accept a delay or something annoying without complaining
examples: She has little patience with (= will not accept or consider) such views.
People have lost patience with (= have become annoyed about) the slow pace of reform.
I have run out of patience with her.
My patience is wearing thin (= I do not have much patience left).
Teaching children with special needs requires patience and understanding.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the ability to spend a lot of time doing something difficult that needs a lot of attention and effort
examples: It takes time and patience to photograph wildlife.
I don't have the patience to do jigsaw puzzles.
Our patience was finally rewarded and we got the band's autographs.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a card game for only one player

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the quality of being extremely patient and not complaining
examples: You need the patience of Job to deal with some of our customers.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel impatient
examples: His stubbornness would try the patience of a saint.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who is receiving medical treatment, especially in a hospital
examples: cancer/AIDS/heart patients
critically ill/elderly patients
Hospitals are treating more patients than ever before.
patients receiving/undergoing treatment
patients with heart disease
patient care/safety

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who receives treatment from a particular doctor, dentist, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO private patient
He's one of Dr Shaw's patients.
He only takes private patients.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the person or thing that is affected by the action of the verb. In the sentence ‘I started the car’, the patient is car.
examples: COMPARE agent

definitions.definition: the act of going to different parts of a building, an area, etc. to make sure that there is no trouble or crime
examples: Security guards make regular patrols at night.
a police car on patrol

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of soldiers, vehicles, etc. that patrol an area
examples: a naval/police patrol
a patrol car/boat

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a group of about six Boy Scouts or Girl Guides / Girl Scouts that forms part of a larger group

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who gives money and support to artists and writers
examples: Frederick the Great was the patron of many artists.
He was a great patron of the arts and helped to establish the Baltimore Museum.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a famous person who supports an organization such as a charity and whose name is used in the advertisements, etc. for the organization
examples: the official patron of the college
The Duchess of Cornwall is to be patron of the new Unicorn Theatre for Children.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who uses a particular shop, restaurant, etc.
examples: Patrons are requested not to smoke.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the regular way in which something happens or is done
examples: SEE ALSO holding pattern
changing patterns of urban life
We have no way of predicting next year's weather patterns.
behaviour/sleep/growth patterns
stress/intonation/speech patterns
Wages in both sectors have followed a similar pattern.
The studies show different patterns of distribution.
The music contains repeated rhythmic patterns.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an excellent example to copy
examples: This system sets the pattern for others to follow.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a regular arrangement of lines, shapes, colours, etc. for example as a design on material, carpets, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO willow pattern
a pattern of diamonds and squares
a shirt with a floral pattern
complex geometric patterns

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a design, set of instructions or shape to cut around that you use in order to make something
examples: a knitting pattern
She bought a dress pattern and some material.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a small piece of material, paper, etc. that helps you choose the design of something
examples: SYNONYM sample
wallpaper patterns

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to stop talking or doing something for a short time before continuing
examples: Anita paused for a moment, then said: ‘All right’.
The woman spoke almost without pausing for breath (= very quickly).
I paused at the door and looked back.
Pausing only to pull on a sweater, he ran out of the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop a video, etc. for a short time using the pause button
examples: She paused the movie to go and answer the door.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to stop talking or doing something for a short time before continuing
examples: Anita paused for a moment, then said: ‘All right’.
The woman spoke almost without pausing for breath (= very quickly).
I paused at the door and looked back.
Pausing only to pull on a sweater, he ran out of the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop a video, etc. for a short time using the pause button
examples: She paused the movie to go and answer the door.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give somebody money for work, goods, services, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO low-paid
Who's paying?
I'll pay for the tickets.
You have to pay extra for a single room.
Many consumers are willing to pay more for better service.
Let me pay you for your time.
Her parents paid for her to go to Canada.
Would you mind paying the taxi driver?
She's paid $200 a day.
Let me pay the bill.
Are you paying by card?
to pay (in) cash
She pays £200 a week for this apartment.
I don't pay you to sit around all day doing nothing!
I pay him £10 to clean the car.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give somebody money that you owe them
examples: to pay a fee/bill/fine/debt
to pay your rent
Everyone has to pay their taxes.
The union paid all her legal costs.
Membership fees should be paid to the secretary.
He still hasn't paid me the money he owes me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to give or provide a particular amount of money for the work that somebody does
examples: Software firms generally pay well (= pay high salaries).
jobs that pay less than £10 an hour
I need to get a job that pays better.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used with some nouns to show that you are giving or doing the thing mentioned
examples: Most of the students weren't paying attention.
The director paid tribute to all she had done for the charity.
He paid a visit to Japan last year.
The film pays homage to classic Hollywood musicals.
I'll pay you a visit when I'm next in town.
He's always paying me compliments.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to produce a profit; to result in some advantage for somebody
examples: It's hard to make farming pay.
Crime doesn't pay.
It pays to keep up to date with your work.
It would probably pay you to hire an accountant.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to suffer or be punished for your beliefs or actions
examples: You'll pay for that remark!
He will pay dearly for what he did.
Many people paid with their lives (= they died).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to cost/pay a lot of money

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a lot of trouble
examples: There'll be hell to pay when he finds out.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to pay careful attention to somebody/something
examples: They gave little heed to the rumours.
I paid no heed at the time but later I had cause to remember what he’d said.
Small businesses would be wise to take heed of the warnings contained in the Chancellor’s speech.
She took little heed of her surroundings.
They paid no heed to the advice.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the person who provides the money for something can also control how it is spent

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to give no attention to somebody/something
examples: People call him names sometimes, but he doesn't pay them any mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to treat somebody with great respect in order to gain favour with them

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to work hard and gain experience, so that you deserve success or respect
examples: As a young actor, he paid his dues in small roles.
She is incredibly qualified and has paid her dues to become president.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to do what is required or expected of you
examples: Vick paid his dues (= completed his punishment), and since being released from prison has been a model citizen.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to save as much money as it cost
examples: The rail pass will pay for itself after about two trips.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something cost(s) a lot of money, especially if the money is wasted
examples: I paid good money for this jacket, and now look at it—it's ruined!

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to suffer because of bad luck, a mistake or something you have done
examples: He looked terrible this morning. I think he's paying the penalty for all those late nights.
They're now paying the price for past mistakes.
She thinks that any inconvenience is a price worth paying for living in such a beautiful place.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to visit somebody or to send a message of good wishes as a sign of respect for them
examples: Many came to pay their last respects (= by attending somebody's funeral).

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to pay too much money for something

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to make enough money to pay what it costs to keep it going
examples: The bridge is still not paying its way.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to pay for everything yourself without having to rely on anyone else’s money

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to borrow money from one person to pay back what you owe to another person; to take money from one thing to use for something else

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: used for saying that there is very little difference between two or more things that you can chooseWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in the sense ‘pacify’): from Old French paie (noun), payer (verb), from Latin pacare ‘appease’, from pax, pac- ‘peace’. The notion of ‘payment’ arose from the sense of ‘pacifying’ a creditor.
