definitions.definition: the act of paying somebody/something or of being paid
examples: SEE ALSO non-payment
What method of payment do you prefer?
payment in cash/by cheque
They asked for payment in advance.
There will be a penalty for late payment of bills.
to receive/accept/demand/withhold payment
payment for goods/services
The public has right of access, on payment of a fee.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sum of money paid or expected to be paid
examples: SEE ALSO balance of payments
a cash payment
It's important to make the payments on time.
to receive/accept/demand/withhold a payment
interest payments
They've never missed a mortgage payment.
He agreed to make ten monthly payments of £50.
They are finding it difficult to meet the payments on their car.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a reward or an act of thanks for something you have done
examples: SYNONYM recompense
Is this all the payment I get for my efforts?
We'd like you to accept this gift in payment for your kindness.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: after something has been paid
examples: Entry is only allowed on payment of the full registration fee.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a situation or a period of time in which there is no war or violence in a country or an area
examples: world peace
The two communities live together in peace.
The countries have been at peace for more than a century.
peace talks/negotiations
the peace process
a peace treaty/accord/agreement/deal
The negotiators are trying to make peace between the warring factions.
The fragile peace between North and South is threatened.
He is critical of US efforts to restore peace to the country.
to bring/promote/achieve/ensure peace
A UN force has been sent to keep the peace (= to prevent people from fighting).
After years of war, the people long for a lasting peace.
the peace movement (= that tries to prevent war by protesting, persuading politicians, etc.)
the Peace of Utrecht, 1713 (= the agreement ending the war)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of being calm or quiet
examples: She lay back and enjoyed the peace of the summer evening.
I would work better if I had some peace and quiet.
I need to check that she is all right, just for my own peace of mind (= so that I do not have to worry).
He never really felt at peace with himself.
I felt calm and at peace.
Her father is at peace (= dead) now.
They were charged with disturbing the peace (= behaving in a noisy and violent way).
He just wants to be left in peace (= not to be disturbed).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the state of living in friendship with somebody without arguing
examples: SEE ALSO breach
They simply can't seem to live in peace with each other.
They live together in peace despite their differences.
She felt at peace with the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to say nothing although you would like to give your opinion

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to end an argument with somebody, usually by saying you are sorry
examples: He made peace with his brother when their father was dying.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when somebody is complaining that they have a lot of work to doWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French pais, from Latin pax, pac- ‘peace’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not involving a war, violence or argument
examples: a peaceful protest/demonstration
a peaceful resolution to the war
They hope for a peaceful settlement of the dispute.
The only way ahead was via diplomatic and peaceful means.
people of different religions living in peaceful coexistence
The time without her in the house had been blissfully peaceful.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: quiet and calm; not worried or upset in any way
examples: SYNONYM tranquil
a peaceful atmosphere
peaceful sleep
It's so peaceful out here in the country.
She lives a peaceful existence in a mountain village.
He had a peaceful life.
a peaceful place
You looked so peaceful that we didn't want to wake you.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: trying to create peace or to live in peace; not liking violence or argument
examples: SYNONYM peaceable
a peaceful religion/society
The aims of the organization are wholly peaceful.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the point when somebody/something is best, most successful, strongest, etc.
examples: SYNONYM height
Traffic reaches its peak between 8 and 9 in the morning.
the peaks and troughs of married life
She's at the peak of her career.
Membership of the club has fallen from a peak of 600 people in 2006.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the pointed top of a mountain; a mountain with a pointed top
examples: a mountain peak
snow-capped/jagged peaks
The climbers made camp halfway up the peak.
We looked up at the rocky peaks towering above us.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: any narrow and pointed shape, edge, etc.
examples: Whisk the egg whites into stiff peaks.
He combed his hair into a peak.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the stiff front part of a cap that sticks out above your eyesWord Origin
examples: mid 16th cent.: probably a back-formation from peaked, variant of dialect picked ‘pointed’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: (especially in the past, or in poorer countries) a farmer who owns or rents a small piece of land
examples: peasant farmers
a peasant family
peasant revolts

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is rude, behaves badly or has little education
examples: SYNONYM lout

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: strange or unusual, especially in a way that is unpleasant or makes you worried
examples: COMPARE odd
a peculiar smell/taste
The meat tasted rather peculiar.
There was something peculiar in the way he smiled.
I had a peculiar feeling we'd met before.
He died in very peculiar circumstances.
For some peculiar reason, she refused to come inside.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: belonging or relating to one particular place, situation, person, etc., and not to others
examples: a humour that is peculiar to American sitcoms
a species of bird peculiar to Asia
He has his own peculiar style which you'll soon get used to.
the family’s peculiar importance in the affair
the peculiar properties of mercury

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: slightly ill
examples: I don’t think I’ll eat anything—I’m feeling a bit peculiar.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that ‘funny’ is being used with the meaning of ‘strange’Word Origin
examples: late Middle English (in the sense ‘particular’): from Latin peculiaris ‘of private property’, from peculium ‘property’, from pecu ‘cattle’ (cattle being private property). The sense ‘strange’ dates from the early 17th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who is the same age or who has the same social status as you
examples: She enjoys the respect of her peers.
A peer review system is being introduced to help teachers who are experiencing difficulty.
Children are worried about failing in front of their peers.
Peer pressure is strong among young people (= they want to be like other people of the same age).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: (in the UK) a member of the nobility or the House of Lords
examples: SEE ALSO hereditary peer
MPs and peers from all parties met to discuss the issue.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an instrument made of plastic or metal used for writing with ink (= coloured liquid for writing, etc.)
examples: SEE ALSO ballpoint pen
an ink pen
Let me grab a pen.
to use pen and paper
pen and ink
a message written in red pen (= using a red pen)
a new book from the pen of (= written by) Zadie Smith

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small piece of land surrounded by a fence in which farm animals are kept
examples: a sheep pen

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a penitentiary (= a prison)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: people who write books, poems, etc. have a greater effect on history and human affairs than soldiers and wars

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to write or start to write something

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a small mistake in something that you write or say
examples: Sorry, it was a slip of the pen—I meant to write ‘pheasants’, not ‘peasants’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a punishment for breaking a law, rule or contract
examples: SEE ALSO death penalty
to impose a penalty
Assault carries a maximum penalty of seven years' imprisonment.
The penalty for travelling without a ticket is £200.
Contractors who fall behind schedule incur heavy financial penalties.
Harsher penalties are being imposed for crimes involving firearms.
a penalty clause in a contract
You can withdraw money from the account at any time without penalty.
The Romans prohibited the teaching of the Torah on penalty of death.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a disadvantage suffered as a result of something
examples: One of the penalties of fame is loss of privacy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a disadvantage given to a player or a team when they break a rule
examples: He incurred a ten-second penalty in the first round.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a chance to score a goal or point without any defending players, except the goalkeeper, trying to stop it; the goal or point that is given if it is successful. This chance is given because the other team has broken the rules.
examples: Two minutes later Ford equalized with a penalty.
We were awarded a penalty after a late tackle.
I volunteered to take the penalty (= be the person who tries to score the goal/point)
He missed a penalty in the last minute of the game.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to suffer because of bad luck, a mistake or something you have done
examples: He looked terrible this morning. I think he's paying the penalty for all those late nights.
They're now paying the price for past mistakes.
She thinks that any inconvenience is a price worth paying for living in such a beautiful place.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a narrow piece of wood, or a metal or plastic case, containing a black or coloured substance, used for drawing or writing
examples: SEE ALSO eyebrow pencil
I'll get a pencil and paper.
coloured pencils
I need to sharpen my pencil.
She scribbled a note in pencil.
margin notes in pencil
Each picture was carefully drawn with pencil and then colour was added.
a pencil drawing/sketch

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small British coin and unit of money. There are 100 pence in one pound (£1).
examples: He had a few pennies in his pocket.
That will be 45 pence, please.
They cost 20p each.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a British coin in use until 1971. There were twelve pennies in one shilling and twenty shillings in a pound.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a cent
examples: The fee ranges from a few pennies to $30 or more.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: all of the money
examples: We collected £700 and every penny went to charity.
She’s on a high salary but I’m sure she deserves every penny.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that since you have started to do something, it is worth spending as much time or money as you need to in order to complete it

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: no money at all
examples: It didn't cost a penny.
He has never paid me a penny.
She hasn’t got a penny to her name.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody has finally understood or realized something that they had not understood or realized before
examples: I had to explain the joke to her a couple of times before the penny dropped.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody what they are thinking about

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to try to spend as little money as possible

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a lot of money
examples: I bet that cost you a pretty penny.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: people say ‘spend a penny’ to avoid saying ‘use the toilet’

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to appear when they are not welcome or not wanted, especially when this happens regularly

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: very common and therefore not valuable
examples: Teachers of history are ten a penny.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: human beings; men, women and children
examples: At least ten people were killed in the crash.
There were a lot of people at the party.
Many young people are out of work.
older people
They are just ordinary people.
Millions of working people are struggling.
It is important to involve local people in the project.
poor/rich people
people of faith (= people who are religious)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: humans in general; everyone
examples: We want to change the way people think.
People want fresh, local food.
He wanted to help people fulfil their potential.
She tends to annoy people.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: all the people who live in a particular place or belong to a particular country, race, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO townspeople
the American/French people
black/white people
people of colour (= people who are not white)
the indigenous peoples of Mexico

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: men and women who work in a particular type of job or are involved in a particular area of activity
examples: a meeting with business people and bankers
These garments are intended for professional sports people.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the ordinary citizens of a country rather than those who govern or have a special position in society
examples: SEE ALSO little people
the life of the common people
It was felt that the government was no longer in touch with the people.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the men, women and children that a person leads
examples: The king urged his people to prepare for war.
the story of the Zulu leader who died while attempting to free his people

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the men and women who work for you or support you
examples: I've had my people watching the house for a few days.
Our people are all highly trained and motivated.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: guests or friends
examples: I'm having people to dinner this evening.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the men, women and children that you are closely related to, especially your parents, grandparents, etc.
examples: She's spending the holidays with her people.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to please everyone by changing your attitudes or opinions to suit different people

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be understood or used in different ways by different people

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a man/woman who understands and supports ordinary people
examples: He is not only a statesman, but also a man of the people.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: when you say of all people, you are emphasizing that somebody is the person you would most or least expect to do something
examples: She of all people should know the answer to that.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: you should not criticize other people, because they will easily find ways of criticizing youWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Anglo-Norman French poeple, from Latin populus ‘populace’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a powder made from dried berries (called peppercorns), used to give a hot, spicy taste to food
examples: SEE ALSO black pepper
Season with salt and pepper
freshly ground pepper
sirloin steak with a pepper sauce

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a hollow fruit, usually red, green or yellow, eaten as a vegetable either raw or cooked
examples: He gave me a great recipe for stuffed peppers.
peppers stuffed with meat and rice

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to express the cost or amount of something for each person, number used, distance travelled, etc.
examples: Rooms cost £50 per person, per night.
60 miles per hour
France consumes around 200 000 tonnes of cocoa per year.
This country has a higher crime rate per 100 000 of the population than most other European countries.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: following something that has been decided
examples: The work was carried out as per instructions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in the way that is normal or usual; as often happens
examples: Everyone blamed me as per usual.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to understand or think of somebody/something in a particular way
examples: SYNONYM see
This discovery was perceived as a major breakthrough.
She did not perceive herself as disabled.
A science degree and artistic interests are often perceived as incompatible.
They were widely perceived to have been unlucky.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to notice or become aware of something
examples: I perceived a change in his behaviour.
She perceived that all was not well.
The patient was perceived to have difficulty in breathing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the number, amount or rate of something, expressed as if it is part of a total that is 100; a part or share of a whole
examples: What percentage of the population is/are overweight?
A high percentage of the female staff are part-time workers.
a large/small/low percentage
The figure is expressed as a percentage.
The results were analysed in percentage terms.
Interest rates are expected to rise by one percentage point (= a unit of one per cent).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a share of the profits of something
examples: He gets a percentage for every car sold.
The artist's agent receives commission on a percentage basis.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an idea, a belief or an image you have as a result of how you see or understand something
examples: a campaign to change public perception of the police
There is a general public perception that standards in schools are falling.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the way you notice things, especially with the senses
examples: Everyone's perception of reality is slightly different.
visual perception

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the ability to understand the true nature of something
examples: SYNONYM insight
She showed great perception in her assessment of the family situation.
They have little perception of how ordinary people live their lives.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having everything that is necessary; complete and without faults or weaknesses
examples: in perfect condition
He smiled, revealing a perfect set of teeth.
Well I'm sorry—but nobody's perfect (= used when somebody has criticized you).
In a perfect world, everybody would have everything they needed.
What's your idea of the perfect partner?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: completely correct; exact and accurate
examples: SEE ALSO letter-perfect
She speaks perfect English.
a perfect fit/match
What perfect timing!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the best of its kind
examples: a perfect example of the painter’s early style
the perfect crime (= one in which the criminal is never discovered)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: excellent; very good
examples: The weather was perfect.
I have this dress that would just look perfect on you!

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: exactly right for somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM ideal
Hawaii is the perfect place for a honeymoon.
She's the perfect candidate for the job.
You and Jeff are perfect for each other.
‘Will 2.30 be OK for you?’ ‘Perfect, thanks.’

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: total; complete
examples: I don't know him—he's a perfect stranger.
I have a perfect right to ask you—and you have the right not to answer.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: connected with the form of a verb that consists of part of the verb have with the past participle of the main verb, used to express actions completed by the present or a particular point in the past or future
examples: SEE ALSO future perfect
‘I have eaten’ is the present perfect tense of the verb ‘to eat’, ‘I had eaten’ is the past perfect and ‘I will have eaten’ is the future perfect.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that something is what you would like to happen or what should happen, but you know it cannot
examples: In an ideal world we would be recycling and reusing everything.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a way of encouraging people by telling them that if you do an activity regularly and try to improve your skill, you will become very good at itWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French perfet, from Latin perfectus ‘completed’, from the verb perficere, from per- ‘through, completely’ + facere ‘do’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: completely
examples: It's perfectly normal to feel like this.
It's perfectly good as it is (= it doesn't need changing).
I thought he'd be upset, but he seems perfectly fine.
You know perfectly well what I mean.
To be perfectly honest, I didn't want to go anyway.
He stood perfectly still until the danger had passed.
‘Do you understand?’ ‘Perfectly.’
How perfectly awful!
They’re perfectly within their rights to ask to see the report.
He is perfectly suited to the role.
Sparkling wine is a perfectly acceptable alternative to champagne.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a perfect way
examples: The TV works perfectly now.
This dress fits perfectly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to entertain an audience by playing a piece of music, acting in a play, etc.
examples: to perform a song/dance/play
The play was first performed in 2007.
Visiting artists will perform their music and poetry.
I'm looking forward to seeing you perform.
I'd love to see them perform live (= in a live show, not a recording).
What do you like about performing on stage?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to do something, such as a piece of work, task or duty
examples: SYNONYM carry out
She performs an important role in our organization.
A computer can perform many tasks at once.
to perform a function/duty
to perform an analysis/a test/an experiment
to perform a ceremony/ritual
to perform an operation/a procedure/surgery
The procedure was performed safely on ten patients.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to work or function well or badly
examples: The engine seems to be performing well.
The company has been performing poorly over the past year.
England's players perform better for their clubs than for their country.
to perform admirably/brilliantly/strongly
She performed less well in the second test.
They gather information on how businesses are performing.
If Bale performs (= performs well) then I believe Wales can win.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to achieve very good results
examples: Her exercise programme has worked miracles for her.
You can work miracles with very little money if you follow our home decoration tips.
He performed miracles to get everything ready in time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of performing a play, concert or some other form of entertainment
examples: SEE ALSO command performance
The performance starts at seven.
an evening performance
They put on performances for the tourists.
This was one of the band's rare live performances.
They gave a performance of Ravel’s String Quartet
a series of performances by the Kirov Ballet

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the way a person performs in a play, concert, etc.
examples: She gave the greatest performance of her career.
Both actors deliver outstanding performances.
an excellent/a fine/an impressive performance

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: how well or badly you do something; how well or badly something works
examples: COMPARE pay-for-performance
the country's strong economic performance over the last two years
It was an impressive performance by the French team.
He criticized the recent poor performance of the company.
Her academic performance has been inconsistent.
Profits continue to grow, with strong performances in South America and the Far East.
The team has continued to improve performance.
This machine delivers excellent performance at a very competitive price.
to measure/evaluate the performance of somebody/something
high-performance (= very powerful) cars
performance indicators (= things that show how well or badly something is working)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act or process of performing a task, an action, etc.
examples: She has shown enthusiasm in the performance of her duties.
He did not want a repeat performance of the humiliating defeat he had suffered.
The party are dreading a repeat performance of their defeat in the last election.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an act that involves a lot of effort or trouble, sometimes when it is not necessary
examples: SYNONYM carry-on
It's such a performance getting the children off to school in the morning.
He always goes through the whole performance of checking the oil and water even if we’re in a hurry.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: possibly
examples: SYNONYM maybe
‘Are you going to come?’ ‘Perhaps. I'll see how I feel.’
Perhaps he's forgotten.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used when you want to make a statement or opinion less definite
examples: LANGUAGE BANK AT impersonal
This is perhaps his best novel to date.
He had a difficult upbringing, which perhaps explains why he behaves like that.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used when making a rough estimate
examples: a change which could affect perhaps 20 per cent of the population

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used when you agree or accept something unwillingly, or do not want to say that you think something is bad
examples: ‘You could do it yourself.’ ‘Yeah, perhaps.’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used when making a polite request, offer or suggestion
examples: Perhaps it would be better if you came back tomorrow.
I think perhaps you've had enough to drink tonight.
Perhaps you’d like to have a shower before the others arrive.
Perhaps you would be good enough to let him know we are on our way.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a particular length of time
examples: SEE ALSO cooling-off period
a long/an extended period
a short/brief period
a period of transition/uncertainty/expansion
a period of two years/six months/four weeks
a two-year/six-month/four-week period
All these changes happened over a period of time.
A year-to-year lease has no fixed time period.
The offer is available for a limited period only.
This compares with a 4% increase for the same period last year.
The project will run for a six-month trial period.
The hall will be closed over a 2-year period.
We know little of her life during that period.
The aim is to reduce traffic at peak periods.
Tomorrow will be cold with sunny periods.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a length of time in the life of a particular person or in the history of a particular country
examples: Which period of history would you most like to have lived in?
This textbook covers the post-war period.
The church dates from the Norman period.
We are currently studying the early medieval period.
Like Picasso, she too had a blue period.
Most teenagers go through a period of rebelling.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a length of time which is a division of an era. A period is divided into epochs.
examples: the Jurassic period
Dinosaurs died out during the Cretaceous period.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: any of the parts that a day is divided into at a school, college, etc. for study
examples: ‘What do you have next period?’ ‘French.’
a free/study period (= for private study)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the flow of blood each month from the body of a woman who is not pregnant
examples: COMPARE menstruation
period pains
monthly periods
When did you last have a period?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the mark ( . ) used at the end of a sentence and in some abbreviations, for example e.g.Word Origin
examples: late Middle English (denoting the time during which something, especially a disease, runs its course): from Old French periode, via Latin from Greek periodos ‘orbit, recurrence, course’, from peri- ‘around’ + hodos ‘way, course’. The sense ‘portion of time’ dates from the early 17th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: lasting for a long time or for all time in the future; existing all the time
examples: OPPOSITE temporary
She was unable to find a permanent job.
Holiday camps employ only a very small number of permanent staff.
They are now living together on a permanent basis.
The accident has not done any permanent damage.
a permanent fixture (= a person or an object that is always in a particular place)
a permanent resident of the United States
She doesn't intend to make London her permanent home.
The gallery hosts various exhibitions and a permanent collection.
We decided to make the arrangement permanent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that lasts for a long time or for all time in the future; in a way that exists all the time
examples: OPPOSITE temporarily
The stroke left his right side permanently damaged.
She had decided to settle permanently in France.
This door is kept permanently locked.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of allowing somebody to do something, especially when this is done by somebody in a position of authority
examples: You must ask permission for all major expenditure.
After much persuasion, permission was granted to speak to the refugees at the camp.
The school has been refused permission to expand.
All minors must seek parental permission to marry.
No official permission has been given for the event to take place.
You shouldn't rent out your property without seeking permission from your mortgage lender.
He had to get permission from his parents to audition for the show.
She took the car without permission.
With your permission, I'd like to say a few words.
poems reprinted by kind permission of the author

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an official written statement allowing somebody to do something
examples: SEE ALSO planning permission
The publisher is responsible for obtaining the necessary permissions to reproduce illustrations.
The report recommends that all planning permissions for quarrying in national parks should expire in ten years.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to do something or to allow something to happen
examples: Mobile phones are not permitted in the examination room.
We were not permitted any contact with each other.
Visitors are not permitted to take photographs.
The owners have been unwilling to permit the use of their land.
There are fines for exceeding permitted levels of noise pollution.
Jim permitted himself a wry smile.
The bill was designed to permit new fathers to take time off work.
She would not permit herself to look at them.
Permit me to offer you some advice.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something possible
examples: We hope to visit the cathedral, if time permits.
I'll come tomorrow, weather permitting (= if the weather is fine).
The password permits access to all files on the hard disk.
The length of the report does not permit a detailed discussion of the problems.
Cash machines permit you to withdraw money at any time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to do something or to allow something to happen
examples: Mobile phones are not permitted in the examination room.
We were not permitted any contact with each other.
Visitors are not permitted to take photographs.
The owners have been unwilling to permit the use of their land.
There are fines for exceeding permitted levels of noise pollution.
Jim permitted himself a wry smile.
The bill was designed to permit new fathers to take time off work.
She would not permit herself to look at them.
Permit me to offer you some advice.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something possible
examples: We hope to visit the cathedral, if time permits.
I'll come tomorrow, weather permitting (= if the weather is fine).
The password permits access to all files on the hard disk.
The length of the report does not permit a detailed discussion of the problems.
Cash machines permit you to withdraw money at any time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to continue to do something despite difficulties or opposition, in a way that can seem unreasonable
examples: Why do you persist in blaming yourself for what happened?
She persisted in her search for the truth.
He persisted with his questioning.
‘So, did you agree or not?’ he persisted.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to continue to exist
examples: The belief that the earth was flat persisted for many centuries.
If the symptoms persist, consult your doctor.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: determined to do something despite difficulties, especially when other people are against you and think that you are being annoying or unreasonable
examples: How do you deal with persistent salesmen who won't take no for an answer?
a persistent offender (= a person who continues to commit crimes after they have been caught and punished)
She can be very persistent when she wants something.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: continuing for a long period of time, or repeated frequently, especially in a way that is annoying and cannot be stopped
examples: SYNONYM unrelenting
Persistent heavy rain held up work on the bridge for more than a week.
The most common symptom is a persistent cough.
I can’t take much more of this persistent criticism.
He resigned over persistent rumours of his affair with an actress.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

He's a fascinating person.
What is she like as a person?

She's the only person I can talk to about my problems.
Gary was the last person I expected to see when I answered the doorbell.
I had a letter from the people who used to live next door.
I'm not really a city person (= I don't really like cities).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a human, especially one who is not identified

The price is $40 per person.
This vehicle is licensed to carry 4 persons. (= in a notice)

The virus is spread from person to person.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person working in the area of business mentioned; a person connected with the thing mentioned
examples: a salesperson
a spokesperson

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: any of the three classes of personal pronouns. The first person (I/we) refers to the person(s) speaking; the second person (you) refers to the person(s) spoken to; the third person (he/she/it/they) refers to the person(s) or thing(s) spoken about.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if you have or carry something about/on your person, you carry it about with you, for example in your pocket
examples: Relatives of the dead man were traced through an address found on his person.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to treat everyone in the same way, without being influenced by their importance, wealth, etc.
examples: Death is no respecter of persons.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: if you do something in person, you go somewhere and do it yourself, instead of doing it by letter, asking somebody else to do it, etc.
examples: He had to pick up his welfare cheque in person.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: in the form or shape of somebody
examples: Help arrived in the person of his mother.
The firm has an important asset in the person of the sales director.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: your own; not belonging to or connected with anyone else
examples: The novel is written from personal experience.

a personal preference/view
Her art is deeply personal.
intensely/highly personal

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: between individual people who know each other
examples: Having good personal relationships is the most important thing for me.
She is a personal friend of mine.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: connected with a person’s private life, rather than their job or official position
examples: I try not to let work interfere with my personal life.
personal information/data/details (= information about you that not everyone can know)

I'd like to talk to you about a personal matter.
Please keep personal phone calls to a minimum.
I'd rather not talk about it, it's personal.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: done by a particular person rather than by somebody who is acting for them
examples: The President made a personal appearance at the event.
I shall give the matter my personal attention.
She takes a personal interest in the work of the charity.
The Principal has little personal contact with the students.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: made or done for a particular person rather than for a large group of people or people in general
examples: We offer a personal service to all our customers.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: referring to a particular person’s character, appearance, opinions, etc. in a way that is offensive
examples: Try to avoid making personal remarks.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: Get up close and personal with the koalas at the San Diego Zoo.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the various aspects of a person’s character that combine to make them different from other people

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: We need someone with lots of personality to head the project.

examples: SYNONYM celebrity

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: Their son is a real personality.

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: All emails will be answered personally.

definitions.definition: in a way that is connected with one particular person rather than a group of people

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in a way that is intended to be offensive
examples: I'm sure she didn't mean it personally.

examples: Have you had any dealings with any of the suspects, either personally or professionally?

definitions.label: Meaning 6

the personnel department/manager

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: She was aware that she was losing all sense of perspective.

examples: The artist plays with perspective to confuse the eye.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: a perspective of the whole valley

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: Middle English: from Latin petitio(n-), from petit- ‘aimed at, sought, laid claim to’, from the verb petere.

Names were picked at random out of a hat.
to pick your nose (= put your finger inside your nose to remove dried mucus)
to pick your teeth (= use a small sharp piece of wood or plastice to remove pieces of food from your teeth)
The dogs picked the bones clean (= ate all the meat from the bones).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to play a musical instrument, especially a guitar, by pulling the strings with your fingers

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be angry with somebody about something and want to discuss it with them

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to choose only those things that you like or want very much
examples: You have to take any job you can get—you can't pick and choose.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to ask somebody a lot of questions about something because they know more about the subject than you do
examples: I need to pick your brains: what can you tell me about credit unions?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to deliberately start a fight or an argument with somebody
examples: He had drunk too much and was ready to pick a fight with anyone who crossed his path.
She tried to pick a quarrel with me.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to find the weak points in something such as a plan, suggestion, etc.
examples: It was easy to pick holes in his arguments.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to open a lock without a key, using something such as a piece of wire
examples: The burglars must have picked the lock on the back door.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to steal something from somebody’s pocket without them noticing
examples: RELATED NOUN pickpocket
The back pocket on a pair of jeans is the easiest one to pick.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to criticize somebody, or their work or ideas, very severely

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to criticize somebody, or their work or ideas, very severely
examples: Their case was torn to shreds by the defence lawyer.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to pay for something
examples: The company picked up the tab for his hotel room.
The government will continue to pick up college fees for some students.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to return or to help somebody return to a normal situation, particularly after a shock or a disaster
examples: You cannot live your children's lives for them; you can only be there to pick up the pieces when things go wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to go faster
examples: The train began to pick up speed.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to return to an earlier situation or way of life after a period doing something else

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to walk carefully, choosing the safest, driest, etc. place to put your feet
examples: She picked her way delicately over the rough ground.
We picked our way carefully over the jagged rocks.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to choose a horse, etc. that you think is most likely to win a race
examples: He's very good at picking winners.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to make a very good choice

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: offering somebody an ideal opportunity to gain an advantage
examples: This is an opportunity ripe for the picking.
The Raiders' defense is ripe for the picking.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a painting or drawing, etc. that shows a scene, a person or thing
examples: He likes books with lots of pictures in them.
A picture of flowers hung on the wall.
The children were drawing pictures of their pets.
She wanted a famous artist to paint her picture (= a picture of herself).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a photograph
examples: to take a picture
We had our picture taken in front of the hotel.
The picture shows the couple together on their yacht.
She posted a picture of the two of them on her Facebook page.
Have you got any pictures of your trip?
The star shared the picture on Twitter.
to upload/send/tweet a picture

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an image on a television screen
examples: harrowing television pictures of the famine
You are looking at live pictures of midtown Manhattan.
poor picture quality

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a description that gives you an idea in your mind of what something is like
examples: We've only got scraps of information, not the full picture.
The writer paints a gloomy picture of the economy.
a bleak/grim picture of the future
a clear/an accurate/a complete picture of these events
The police are trying to build up a picture of what happened.
From news reports a picture emerges of a country in crisis.
The TV report painted a much rosier picture of the employment situation than research shows to be the case.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a mental image or memory of something
examples: I have a vivid picture of my grandfather smiling down at me when I was very small.
He uses imagery to form mental pictures within the mind of the reader.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the general situation relating to somebody/something
examples: Just a few years ago the picture was very different.
The overall picture for farming is encouraging.
The documentary was interesting but it didn't give the full picture.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a film
examples: SEE ALSO motion picture
The movie won nine Academy Awards, including Best Picture.
I believe her husband's in pictures (= he acts in movies or works in the movie industry).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the cinema
examples: Shall we go to the pictures tonight?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: very pretty
examples: She’s as pretty as a picture.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to look very beautiful or special
examples: The garden looks a picture in the summer.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to look extremely healthy, guilty, unhappy, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: the situation as a whole
examples: Right now forget the details and take a look at the big picture.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to understand a situation, especially one that somebody is describing to you
examples: ‘I pretended that I hadn't heard.’ ‘I get the picture.’

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: involved/not involved in a situation
examples: Morris is likely to win, with Jones out of the picture now.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to describe somebody/something in a particular way; to give a particular impression of somebody/something
examples: The report paints a vivid picture of life in the city.
Journalists paint a grim picture of conditions in the camps.

examples: Just to put you in the picture—there have been a number of changes here recently.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of something that has been cut or separated from the rest of it; a standard amount of something

a piece of wood/metal
a large piece of land
a piece of cake
a piece of cheese/meat/bread
I've got a piece of grit in my eye.
a small/little/tiny piece of something
He cut the pizza into bite-sized pieces.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one of the bits or parts that something breaks into
examples: There were tiny pieces of glass all over the road.
The boat had been smashed to pieces on the rocks.
The building was blown to pieces.
tear/rip something to pieces
The vase lay in pieces in the floor.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: one of the parts that something is made of
examples: SEE ALSO one-piece
He took the clock to pieces.
a missing piece of the puzzle
The bridge was taken down piece by piece.
She's been doing a 500-piece jigsaw.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a single item of a particular type, especially one that forms part of a set
examples: SEE ALSO chimney piece
a piece of equipment/furniture
a piece of clothing/luggage
a piece of machinery
a 28-piece dinner service

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used with many uncountable nouns to describe a single example or an amount of something
examples: a piece of information/evidence/advice/news/legislation
a piece of software
This is a superb piece of work.
It was an interesting piece of research.
The building is a piece of history (= of historical interest or importance).
Isn't that a piece of luck?
You should eat at least two pieces of fruit a day.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a single item of writing, art, music, etc. that somebody has produced or created; a short item of writing from a longer work
examples: SEE ALSO conversation piece
a piece of music/art
a fine piece of writing
They performed pieces by Bach and Handel.
The painting is a companion piece to (= is closely related to and intended to be displayed with) an earlier work.
They have some beautiful pieces (= works of art, etc.) in their home.
She read a piece from ‘Alice in Wonderland’.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an article in a newspaper or magazine or a broadcast on television or radio
examples: SEE ALSO hit piece
The Washington Post ran a series of opinion pieces criticizing the policy.
Did you see her piece about the internet in the paper today?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a coin of the value mentioned
examples: a 50p piece
a five-cent piece

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: one of the small figures or objects that you move around in games such as chess

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a part or share of something
examples: companies seeking a piece of the market

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a gun

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a short distance
examples: She lives down the road a piece from here.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: small objects or items of various kinds
examples: She stuffed all her bits and pieces into a bag and left.
I just need to get a few bits and pieces at the supermarket.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to use bombs or other weapons to destroy somebody/something completely
examples: The plane was blown to pieces when the bomb exploded.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to become very old and in bad condition because of long use
examples: SYNONYM fall apart
Our car is falling to pieces, we've had it so long.
My old dictionary is falling to pieces.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to stop working; to be destroyed
examples: He's worried the business will fall to pieces without him.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to tell somebody that you think their behaviour is bad or are angry with them

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to be so upset or afraid that you cannot manage to live or work normally
examples: After his wife died he just went to pieces.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: used to say that there is no definite answer to a question
examples: ‘How long will it take?’ ‘How long's a piece of string?’

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: safe; not damaged or hurt, especially after a journey or dangerous experience
examples: They were lucky to get home in one piece.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: a person who is unpleasant, unkind or dishonest
examples: Don’t trust him; he’s a nasty piece of work.
He's a thoroughly nasty piece of work.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: all the same or similar
examples: The houses are all of a piece.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: all at the same time
examples: The house was built all of a piece in 1754.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to criticize somebody, or their work or ideas, very severely

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to return or to help somebody return to a normal situation, particularly after a shock or a disaster
examples: You cannot live your children's lives for them; you can only be there to pick up the pieces when things go wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: a thing that is very easy to do

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: a share of the available money or benefits that you believe you have a right to
examples: The company is demanding a larger slice of the corporate pie.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: a thing that is very easy to do

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: used to express the fact that you admire somebody or find them funny, often when they have done something that surprises you
examples: You're some piece of work, Jack, do you know that?

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: a share or role in an interesting or exciting activity, especially one that makes money
examples: Foreign firms will all want a piece of the action if the new airport goes ahead.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to say exactly what you feel or think

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: the person or thing that is responsible for all the trouble in a situation
examples: It’s hard to identify the real villain of the piece in this case.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an animal with pink, black or brown skin, short legs, a broad nose and a short curly tail. Pigs are kept on farms for their meat (called pork) or live in the wild.
examples: SEE ALSO boar
a pig farmer
Pigs were grunting and squealing in the yard.
to breed/rear pigs

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an unpleasant or offensive person; a person who is dirty or greedy
examples: Arrogant pig!
Don't be such a pig!
The greedy pig's eaten all the biscuits!
She made a pig of herself with the ice cream (= ate too much).
He's a real male chauvinist pig (= a man who does not think women are equal to men).
We cooked up a load of pasta and all made pigs of ourselves.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an offensive word for a police officer

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to do something badly; to make a mess of something

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if you buy a pig in a poke, you buy something without seeing it or knowing if it is good enough
examples: Buying from a catalogue can mean buying a pig in a poke.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a difficult or unpleasant thing or task
examples: I've had a pig of a day.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show that you do not believe something will ever happen
examples: ‘With a bit of luck, we'll be finished by the end of the year.’ ‘Yes, and pigs might fly!’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a number of things that have been placed on top of each other
examples: a pile of clothes/paper
I found it in a pile of documents on his desk.
The hats were stacked in neat piles.
I've sorted the books into three separate piles.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a mass of something that is high in the middle and wider at the bottom than at the top
examples: SYNONYM heap
piles of dirty washing
The house was reduced to a pile of rubble.
He threw the remaining stones onto the pile.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a lot of something
examples: He made a pile of cash on the sale of his house.
He walked out leaving a pile of debt behind him.
I have got piles of work to do.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the short threads, pieces of wool, etc. that form the soft surface of carpets and some types of cloth such as velvet
examples: a deep-pile carpet
Corduroy is the poor man’s velvet; its pile is made of cotton rather than silk or satin.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a large wooden, metal or stone post that is fixed into the ground and used to support a building, bridge, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a large impressive building
examples: a Victorian pile built as a private hospital
her family's ancestral pile

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in the least/most important position in a group of people or things
examples: It’s been 20 years since a British player was top of the pile.
The government is doing little to help those on the bottom of the social pile.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to make a lot of money
examples: The family made its pile from oil.
I bet they made an absolute pile out of the deal.

examples: SEE ALSO chill pill
a vitamin pill

pill-popping (= the act of taking too many pills or using illegal drugs)
The doctor prescribed her some pills to help her sleep.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a pill that some women take to prevent them becoming pregnant
examples: SEE ALSO mini-pill
the contraceptive pill
to be/go on the pill
Her doctor put her on the pill at 16.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an annoying person

definitions.definition: a fact or an event that is unpleasant and difficult to accept
examples: The election defeat was a bitter pill for the party to swallow.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to do something that makes an unpleasant situation seem less unpleasant
examples: SYNONYM sugar-coat

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who operates the controls of an aircraft, especially as a job
examples: SEE ALSO automatic pilot
an airline pilot
a fighter/helicopter pilot
The accident was caused by pilot error.
The pilot bailed out as the aircraft crashed into the ocean.
He has his own plane and a pilot's licence.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person with special knowledge of a difficult area of water, for example, the entrance to a harbour, whose job is to guide ships through it

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a single television programme that is made in order to find out whether people will like it and want to watch further programmes

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a small flame that burns all the time, for example on a gas boiler, and lights a larger flame when the gas is turned onWord Origin
examples: early 16th cent. (denoting a person who steers a ship): from French pilote, from medieval Latin pilotus, an alteration of pedota, based on Greek pēdon ‘oar’, (plural) ‘rudder’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a short thin piece of stiff wire with a sharp point at one end and a round head at the other, used especially for fastening together pieces of cloth when sewing
examples: SEE ALSO bobby pin
Use pins to keep the patch in place while you sew it on.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a short thin piece of stiff wire with a sharp point at one end and an item of decoration at the other, worn as jewellery
examples: SEE ALSO tiepin
a diamond pin

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a piece of jewellery with a pin on the back of it, that can be fastened to your clothes

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a type of badge that is fastened with a pin at the back
examples: He supports the group and wears its pin on his lapel.
an American flag lapel pin

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a piece of steel used to support a bone in your body when it has been broken
examples: The pin in her spine will have to be changed as she grows.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: one of the metal parts that stick out of an electric plug and fit into a socket
examples: a 2-pin plug

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a wooden or plastic object that is like a bottle in shape and that players try to knock down in games such as bowling
examples: SEE ALSO ninepins

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a stick with a flag on top of it, placed in a hole so that players can see where they are aiming for
examples: The ball stopped five feet short of the pin.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a person’s legs
examples: He’s not as quick on his pins as he used to be.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a small piece of metal on a hand grenade that stops it from exploding and is pulled out just before the hand grenade is thrown

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: (to be) very anxious or excited while you are waiting to find out something or see what will happen
