In the 1880s, he spent several years as a pioneer missionary in north China.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who is the first to study and develop a particular area of knowledge, culture, etc. that other people then continue to develop
examples: SYNONYM trailblazer
a pioneer in the field of microsurgery
a computer pioneer
a pioneer aviator
a pioneer design (= one that introduces new ideas, methods, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one of the first people to go to a particular area in order to live and work there
examples: Early pioneers settled on both sides of the Maple River.
the pioneer spirit
In the 1880s, he spent several years as a pioneer missionary in north China.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a tube through which liquids and gases can flow
examples: SEE ALSO drainpipe
Both hot and cold water pipes should be properly insulated.
steel/copper pipes
a burst pipe
The house was blown apart by an explosion, caused by a leaking gas pipe.
PVC pipe is commonly used in building and construction.
a drainage/sewage pipe
Insulation may reduce the danger of pipes bursting in winter.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a narrow tube with a bowl at one end, used for smoking tobacco
examples: SEE ALSO peace pipe
to smoke a pipe
He puffed on his pipe.
pipe tobacco
He knocked out his pipe in the big glass ashtray.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a musical instrument in the shape of a tube, played by blowing
examples: SEE ALSO pan pipes

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: any of the tubes from which sound is produced in an organ

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a musical instrument played especially in Scotland. The player blows air into a bag held under the arm and then slowly forces the air out through pipes to produce a noise.Word Origin
examples: Old English pīpe ‘musical tube’, pīpian ‘play a pipe’, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch pijp and German Pfeife, based on Latin pipare ‘to peep, chirp’, reinforced in Middle English by Old French piper ‘to chirp, squeak’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a series of pipes that are usually underground and are used for carrying oil, gas, etc. over long distances
examples: There are plans to lay a gas pipeline through the region.
The pipeline runs through central Mozambique.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that is in the pipeline is being discussed, planned or prepared and will happen or exist soon
examples: Important new laws are already in the pipeline.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: (especially in the past) a person on a ship who attacks other ships at sea in order to steal from them
examples: There were reports that a pirate ship had come looking for treasure in the cove.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who makes illegal copies of books, computer programs, etc., in order to sell them
examples: a pirate edition
software pirates

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or an organization that broadcasts illegally
examples: a pirate radio station

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large deep hole in the ground
examples: SEE ALSO snake pit
We dug a deep pit in the yard.
The body had been dumped in a pit.
The human mind is a dark, bottomless pit.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a deep hole in the ground from which minerals are dug out
examples: a chalk/gravel pit

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a place underground where coal is dug
examples: SEE ALSO open-pit
pit closures
He went down the pit (= started work as a miner) when he left school.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a small shallow hole in the surface of something, especially a mark left on the surface of the skin by some disease, such as chickenpox
examples: SEE ALSO pitted

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a hard shell containing the nut or seed in the middle of some types of fruit
examples: a peach pit

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a place near the track where cars can stop for fuel, new tyres, etc. during a race
examples: SEE ALSO pit stop

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the place in a theatre just in front of the stage where the orchestra sits and plays for an opera, a ballet, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO mosh pit

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: an armpit (= the part of the body under the arm where it joins the shoulder)

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the area of a stock exchange where a particular product is traded
examples: COMPARE floor
the corn pit

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be very bad or the worst example of something

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a thing or situation which seems to have no limits or seems never to end
examples: There isn't a bottomless pit of money for public spending.
the bottomless pit of his sorrow

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: the bottom of the stomach where people say they feel strong feelings, especially fear
examples: He had a sudden sinking feeling in the pit of his stomach.
I felt a sickening feeling in the pit of my stomach when I saw the ambulance.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an area of ground specially prepared and marked for playing a sports game
examples: a football pitch
a cricket/rugby/hockey pitch
an artificial pitch
After the game fans invaded the pitch.
The rugby tour was a disaster both on and off the pitch (= they lost their matches and the players behaved badly while on tour, getting bad news reports).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: how high or low a sound is, especially a musical note
examples: SEE ALSO perfect pitch
A basic sense of rhythm and pitch is essential in a music teacher.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the degree or strength of a feeling or activity; the highest point of something
examples: a frenetic pitch of activity
Speculation has reached such a pitch that a decision will have to be made immediately.
to reach a high pitch of excitement

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: talk or arguments used by a person trying to sell things or persuade people to do something
examples: an aggressive sales pitch
the candidate’s campaign pitch
Each company was given ten minutes to make its pitch.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an act of throwing the ball; the way in which it is thrown

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a black sticky substance made from oil or coal, used on roofs or the wooden boards of a ship to stop water from coming through

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a place in a street or market where somebody sells things, or where somebody performs in order to entertain people outdoors

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a place in a campsite where you can put up one tent or park one caravan, etc.
examples: Pitches to rent from only £15 per night.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the movement of a ship up and down in the water or of an aircraft in the air
examples: COMPARE roll

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the degree to which a roof slopes
examples: The pitch of the roof is 45 degrees.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make a determined effort to get something or to persuade somebody of something
examples: He made a pitch to black voters in Alabama.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to cause somebody’s plans to fail or to destroy their chances of getting somethingWord Origin
examples: noun senses 1 to 5 and noun senses 7 to 9 Middle English (as a verb in the senses ‘thrust (something pointed) into the ground’ and ‘fall headlong’): perhaps related to Old English picung ‘stigmata’, of unknown ultimate origin. The sense development is obscure. noun sense 6 Old English pic (noun), pician (verb), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch pek and German Pech; based on Latin pix, pic-.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to show that you are disappointed about something
examples: SYNONYM shame
It's a pity that you can't stay longer.
‘I've lost it!’ ‘Oh, what a pity.’
What a pity that she didn't tell me earlier.
This dress is really nice. Pity it's so expensive.
Oh, that's a pity.
It would be a great pity if you gave up now.
It seems a pity to waste this food.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sad feeling caused by the pain and troubles of others
examples: I took pity on her and lent her the money.
I beg you to have pity on him.
I don't want your pity.
a look/feeling/surge of pity
I could only feel pity for what they were enduring.
He had no pity for her.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: unfortunately
examples: ‘Was the bicycle insured?’ ‘No, more's the pity!’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a particular position, point or area
examples: Keep your purse in a safe place.
I can't be in two places at once.
They organized several demonstrations in public places.
I happened to be in the right place at the right time.
Is this the place where it happened?
This would be a good place for a picnic.
There is a time and place for these questions, but not right here and now.
If you're looking for a new service provider, this list is a good place to start.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a particular city, town, building, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO watering place
I can't remember all the places we visited in Thailand.
I used to live in York and I'm still fond of the place.
The police searched the place.
Let's get out of this place!
We were looking for a place to eat.
a place to live/stay
Please write your full name and date and place of birth.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a building or an area of land used for a particular purpose
examples: SEE ALSO dwelling place
The town has many excellent eating places.
I couldn't find a parking place anywhere.
churches and other places of worship
He can usually be contacted at his place of work.
They seem to have no fixed employment or place of residence.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a particular area on a surface, especially on a person’s body
examples: He broke his arm in three places.
The paint was peeling off the wall in places.
The footbath is bumpy in places.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a point in a book, speech, piece of music, etc., especially one that somebody has reached at a particular time
examples: She had marked her place with a bookmark.
Excuse me, I seem to have lost my place.
The audience laughed in all the right places.
The film is scary in places.
This is one of the few places in his work where he mentions his childhood.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the natural or correct position for something
examples: Is there a place on the form to put your address?
There is a place to sign and date at the bottom of the form.
Put it back in its place when you've finished with it.
He remembered the saying ‘A place for everything and everything in its place.’

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a position, seat, etc., especially one that is available for or being used by a person or vehicle
examples: Come and sit here—I've saved you a place.
I don't want to lose my place in the line.
Would you like to change places with me so you can see better?
I've set a place for you at the table.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: an opportunity to take part in something, especially to study at a school or university or on a course
examples: She's been offered a place at Bath to study Business.
There are very few places left on the course.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the position of being a member of a sports team
examples: She has won a place in the Olympic team.
He lost his place in the first team.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a position among the winners of a race or competition; a position in the next stage of a competition
examples: She took third place.
He finished in third place.
Victory earned them a place in the final.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: the role or importance of somebody/something in a particular situation, usually in relation to others
examples: He is assured of his place in history.
They felt that they had no place in society and nowhere to go.
It took her a while to find her place in the world.
Anecdotes have no place in (= are not acceptable in) an academic essay.
Accurate reporting takes second place to lurid detail.
My father believed that people should know their place (= behave according to their social position).
It's not your place (= your role) to give advice.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a house or flat; a person’s home
examples: What about dinner at my place?
I'm fed up with living with my parents, so I'm looking for a place of my own.
I thought I’d better clean the place up.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a suitable or safe area for somebody to be
examples: These streets are no place for a child to be out alone at night.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: the position of a figure after a decimal point
examples: SEE ALSO decimal place
Convert the decimal to a percentage by moving the decimal point two places to the right.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used as part of a name for a short street or square
examples: 66 Portland Place

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: everywhere
examples: New restaurants are appearing all over the place.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: not neat or tidy; not well organized
examples: Your calculations are all over the place (= completely wrong).

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to be getting more and more successful in your life or career
examples: a young architect who’s really going places

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to behave in a very confident way that annoys other people, for example by telling them what to do
examples: She was acting as if she owned the place.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to be feeling happy, sad, worried, etc. about something; to be in a good, bad, unhappy, etc. state
examples: I'm happy now. I'm in a good place.
Me and Ed are in a good space right now.
The economy is in a better place than it was a year ago.
He was in a bad place, mentally and emotionally.
She was in a dark place after her mother's death.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to be able to take advantage of opportunities when they come
examples: His success was down to being in the right place at the right time.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: in a situation where you have to choose between two things, both of which are unpleasant

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to be in somebody else’s situation
examples: I'm perfectly happy—I wouldn't change places with anyone.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: if something complicated or difficult to understand falls or slots into place, it becomes organized or clear in your mind
examples: Then I found his diary and it all began to fall into place.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: friends, people, etc. in positions of power and influence
examples: He has friends in high places.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to be replaced by somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM give way to
Houses and factories gave place to open fields as the train gathered speed.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to be very dear to somebody
examples: He'll always have a place in my heart.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody’s intentions are kind and sincere even though they sometimes do the wrong thing

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: used to introduce a piece of advice you are giving to somebody
examples: If I were in your place, I'd resign immediately.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: used at the end of a sentence to talk about why something was done or whether it should have been done or not
examples: I still don't understand why you chose that name in the first place.
I should never have taken that job in the first place.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: used at the beginning of a sentence to introduce the different points you are making in an argument
examples: Well, in the first place he has all the right qualifications.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: in my, your, etc. situation
examples: I wouldn't like to be in your place.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: in the correct position; ready for something
examples: Carefully lay each slab in place.
The receiver had already clicked into place.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: working or ready to work
examples: All the arrangements are now in place for their visit.
How long has the import ban been in place?

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: in one exact place, without moving in any direction
examples: Running in place is good exercise.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: instead of somebody/something
examples: You can use milk in place of cream in this recipe.
He was unable to come to the ceremony, but he sent his son to accept the award in his place.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: an unusual or unpleasant event is not likely to happen in the same place or to the same people twice

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: to look extremely clean and neat

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: not in the correct place
examples: Some of these files seem to be out of place.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: not suitable for a particular situation
examples: Her remarks were out of place.
I felt completely out of place among all these successful people.

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: a position in which you are comfortable or have an advantage over other people

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: the position in which something is most easily seen, that is given to the most important thing in a particular group
examples: The photo was given pride of place on the mantelpiece.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel stupid or embarrassed for showing too much confidence
examples: At first she tried to take charge of the meeting but I soon put her in her place.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: to imagine that you are in somebody else’s situation
examples: Of course I was upset—just put yourself in my place.

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: to stay indoors during an emergency in order to protect yourself and others
examples: Residents of the city have been ordered to shelter in place for at least the next three weeks.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: to happen, especially after previously being arranged or planned
examples: The film festival takes place in October.
We may never discover what took place that night.

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: to replace somebody/something
examples: She couldn't attend the meeting so her assistant took her place.
Computers have taken the place of typewriters in most offices.

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: to go to the physical position that is necessary for an activity
examples: Take your places for dinner.

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: to take or accept the status in society that is correct or that you deserveWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French, from an alteration of Latin platea ‘open space’, from Greek plateia (hodos) ‘broad (way)’.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: the time when you must continue with what you have decided to do, because it is not possible to get back to an earlier situation
examples: We have passed the point of no return.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: used to say that you accept that somebody else is right when they have disagreed with you or criticized you
examples: Point taken. Let's drop the subject.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: to show that you are better than somebody, especially by making clever remarks, for example in an argument
examples: He was always trying to score points off his teachers.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: a subject that makes you feel angry or upset when it is mentioned
examples: It's a sore point with Sue's parents that the children have not been baptized yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: to allow or do something that is not usually acceptable, especially because of a particular situation
examples: I was hoping they would stretch a point and let me stay on for a while.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: expressed in a simple, clear way without any extra information or feelings
examples: SYNONYM pertinent
The letter was short and to the point.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to a degree that can be described as something
examples: He was rude to the point of being aggressive.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: to some extent; to some degree but not completely
examples: I agree with you up to a point.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that somebody says or writes giving their opinion or stating a fact
examples: SEE ALSO talking point
She made several interesting points in the article.
I take your point (= understand and accept what you are saying).
He's just saying that to prove a point (= to show his idea is right).
OK, you've made your point!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the main or most important idea in something that is said or done
examples: The point is you shouldn't have to wait so long to see a doctor.
I wish he would get to the point (= say it quickly).
I'll come straight to the point: we need more money.
Do you see my point (= understand)?
I think I missed the point (= did not understand).
You have a point (= your idea is right)—it would be better to wait till this evening.
‘There won’t be anywhere to park.’ ‘Oh, that’s a (good) point.’ (= I had not thought of that)
It just isn't true. That's the whole point (= the only important fact).
I thought the whole point was getting the same amount done with less effort.
‘He's been married before.’ ‘That's beside the point’ (= not important).
I know it won't cost very much but that's not the point (= not the important thing).
The point behind the film was to help people understand the motivations of the criminals.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the purpose or aim of something
examples: What's the point of all this violence?
‘Why don't you try again?’ ‘What's the point?’
The point of the lesson is to compare the two countries.
I don't see the point of doing it all again.
There's no point in getting angry.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a particular detail or fact
examples: SEE ALSO action point
Can you explain that point again?
Summarize the main points of the argument.
I should like to highlight the key points.
An important point has been missed out.
You raise an interesting point.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a particular quality or feature that somebody/something has
examples: SEE ALSO selling point
Tact is not one of her strong points.
Read the manual to learn the program's finer points (= small details).
Living in Scotland has its good points but the weather is not one of them.
One of the hotel's plus points (= good features) is that it is very central.
There is not a single weak point in his essay.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a particular time or stage of development
examples: SEE ALSO end point
We had reached the point when there was no money left.
The climber was at the point of death when they found him.
At one point he looked like winning.
Many people suffer from mental illness at some point in their lives.
At this point in time we just have to wait.
At this point I don't care what you decide to do.
Up to that point we were living in London.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a particular place or area
examples: SEE ALSO entry point
I'll wait for you at the meeting point in the arrivals hall.
the point at which the river divides
Draw a line from point A to point B.
No parking beyond this point.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: one of the marks of direction around a compass
examples: the points of the compass (= N, S, E, W, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: an individual unit that adds to a score in a game or sports competition
examples: SEE ALSO break point
to win/lose a point
Australia finished 20 points ahead.
Players score points for finding words not found by any other player.
You get bonus points for answering the mystery question.
They won on points (= by scoring more points rather than by completely defeating their opponents).

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a mark or unit on a scale of measurement
examples: SEE ALSO boiling point
The party's share of the vote fell by ten percentage points.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a unit of credit towards an award or benefit
examples: Applicants are awarded points on criteria such as education, skills and knowledge of English.
Let children trade their earned points for privileges, like extra playtime.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: the sharp, thin end of something
examples: SEE ALSO ballpoint
the point of a pencil/knife/pin

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a narrow piece of land that stretches into the sea
examples: The ship sailed around the point.
Pagoda Point

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: a small round mark used in writing, especially the mark that separates a whole number from the part that comes after it
examples: SEE ALSO bullet point
two point six (2.6)
a decimal point
We broadcast on ninety-five point nine (95.9) FM.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: a very small dot of light or colour
examples: The stars were points of light in the sky.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: a place in a wall, etc. where a piece of equipment can be connected to electricity
examples: a power/shaver/telephone point

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: the hard tops of the toes of a kind of shoe that a ballet dancer balances on

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: a piece of track at a place where a railway line divides that can be moved to allow a train to change tracks

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: a unit of measurement for the size of letters in printing or on a computer screen, etc.
examples: Change the text to 10 point.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to repeat an idea, argument, etc. many times to emphasize it, especially when it has already been mentioned or understood
examples: I don’t want to belabour the point, but it’s vital you understand how important this is.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: a clear example of the problem, situation, etc. that is being discussed
examples: Many professions feel they deserve higher pay, and nurses are a case in point.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: the more complicated or detailed aspects of something
examples: She seems at ease discussing the finer points of foreign policy.
He learnt the finer points of cricket during a trip to London.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: used when you have to decide something or say what you really think
examples: When it comes to the point, he always changes his mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used to say what is true in a situation
examples: In point of fact, she is their adopted daughter.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to continue to repeat or explain something that has already been said and understood
examples: I understand what you’re saying—there’s no need to labour the point.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to be or make sure you do something because it is important or necessary
examples: I made a point of closing all the windows before leaving the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: a matter about which there may be difference of opinion or a lack of understanding
examples: Whether this should be enforced by law or not is a moot point.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: used to say that something is more important than something else
examples: I couldn't do the job—I've never been to Spain and, more to the point, I don't speak Spanish.
More to the point, did they get away?

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something that is expressed clearly and directly, especially a criticism
examples: Not to put too fine a point on it, I think you are lying.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: appropriate or relevant to the situation
examples: The quotation was directly on point.
Let's stay on point.
None of the replies was on point.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: perfect; exactly right for the occasion
examples: The music here is totally on point.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to be close to doing something; to be going to do something very soon
examples: SYNONYM be about to do something
I was just on the point of calling you.
We were on the point of giving up.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: a place where you go or a person that you speak to when you are dealing with an organization
examples: The receptionist is the first point of contact most people have with the clinic.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: a place where a journey starts

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: an idea, a theory or an event that is used to start a discussion, an activity, etc.
examples: The author takes Freud's dream theories as the point of departure for his essay.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: a thing that somebody considers to be very important for their honour or reputation

examples: He was always trying to score points off his teachers.

examples: I was hoping they would stretch a point and let me stay on for a while.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to a degree that can be described as something

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a sharp end
examples: SEE ALSO pointy
a pointed chin
pointed teeth
Llamas have long, pointed ears.
the pointed arches used in medieval buildings
a pointed instrument

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: aimed in a clear and often critical way against a particular person or their behaviour
examples: a pointed comment/remark
His words were a pointed reminder of her position.
His questions were starting to sound very pointed.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a substance that causes death or harm if it gets into the body
examples: Some mushrooms contain a deadly poison.
How did he die? Was it poison?
The dog was killed by rat poison (= poison intended to kill rats).
to hunt with poison arrows
bombs containing poison gas
She had laced his drink with poison.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an idea, a feeling, etc. that is extremely harmful
examples: the poison of racial hatred

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that different people like different things; what one person likes very much, another person does not like at all

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody what alcoholic drink they would likeWord Origin
examples: Middle English (denoting a harmful medicinal draught): from Old French poison ‘magic potion’, from Latin potio(n-) ‘potion’, related to potare ‘to drink’.

examples: SYNONYM toxic
poisonous chemicals/fumes/plants
a poisonous substance

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: producing a poison that can cause death or illness if the animal or insect bites you
examples: SYNONYM venomous
poisonous snakes

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: extremely unpleasant or unfriendly
examples: a poisonous person
the poisonous atmosphere in the office

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long thin straight piece of wood or metal, especially one with the end placed in the ground, used as a support
examples: SEE ALSO barber’s pole
a tent pole
a ski pole
a curtain pole

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: either of the two points at the opposite ends of the line on which the earth or any other planet turns
examples: SEE ALSO magnetic pole (1)
the North/South Pole
The meridian is an imaginary line drawn from pole to pole.
The north magnetic pole lies to the west of the geographic North Pole.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: either of the two ends of a magnet, or the positive or negative points of an electric battery
examples: SEE ALSO magnetic pole (2)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: either of two opposite or very different extremes
examples: Their opinions were at opposite poles of the debate.
an artistic compromise between the poles of abstraction and representation

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be widely separated; to have no interests that you share
examples: Her own friends were poles apart from his.
In temperament, she and her sister are poles apart.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to refer to the difficult way to the top of a profession

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to refuse to get involved with somebody/something or in a particular situation
examples: Personally, I wouldn’t touch him or his business with a ten-foot pole.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: crazyWord Origin
examples: noun sense 1 and up the pole. late Old English pāl (in early use without reference to thickness or length), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch paal and German Pfahl, based on Latin palus ‘stake’. noun senses 2 to 4 and be poles apart. late Middle English: from Latin polus ‘end of an axis’, from Greek polos ‘pivot, axis, sky’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official organization whose job is to make people obey the law and to prevent and solve crime; the people who work for this organization
examples: SEE ALSO kitchen police
Get out of the house or I'll call the police.
Contact the police if you see anything suspicious.
The police arrested three men and took them for questioning.
Police are investigating the break-in.
Armed police soon arrived on the scene.
traffic/transport police
Hundreds of police in riot gear struggled to control the violence.
a police car
the police investigation into the killings

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a male police officer
examples: a plain-clothes/uniformed policeman
A policeman arrested the suspect at the scene of the crime.
An off-duty policeman chased after the man.
A policeman was called to the house just after midnight.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a plan of action agreed or chosen by a political party, a business, etc.
examples: the present government’s policy on education
The company has adopted a firm policy on shoplifting.
The new managers are expected to implement new policies.
We have tried to pursue a policy of neutrality.
We have a policy of refusing to comment on such matters.
This marked the beginning of a more open policy towards the rest of the world.
US foreign/economic policy
The document does not represent government policy.
He implemented an aggressive monetary policy to stimulate the economy.
They have had a significant change in policy on paternity leave.
This would be a radical shift in policy.
a policy adviser/decision
a policy statement/objective/initiative/document

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a principle that you believe in that influences how you behave; a way in which you usually behave
examples: She is following her usual policy of ignoring all offers of help.
Honesty is the best policy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a written statement of a contract of insurance
examples: Check the terms of the policy before you sign.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having or showing good manners and respect for the feelings of others
examples: SYNONYM courteous
Please be polite to our guests.
Our waiter was very polite and helpful.
We were all too polite to object.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: socially correct but not always sincere
examples: I don't know how to make polite conversation.
The performance was greeted with polite applause.
She greeted me with a quick hello and a polite smile.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: from a class of society that believes it is better than others
examples: ‘Bum’ is not a word we use in polite company.
The scandal outraged polite society.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the state, government or public affairs
examples: a monarch without political power
He was a political prisoner (= one who was put in prison for holding opinions that the government thought dangerous).
a period of political stability
a political situation/crisis
The police force is facing intense political pressure to reopen the investigation.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with the different groups working in politics, especially their policies and the competition between them
examples: a political party/leader/opponent
What are your political sympathies?
Peace organizations are being used as fronts for political agendas.
a successful political career
the right to participate in political processes.
the US political system

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: interested in or active in politics
examples: She became very political at university.
I'm not a political animal (= person who is interested in politics).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: connected with power, status, etc. within an organization, rather than with matters of principle
examples: I suspect that he was dismissed for political reasons.
We have no intention of getting political.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person whose job involves politics, especially as an elected member of parliament, etc.
examples: democratically elected politicians
prominent/senior/leading politicians
Opposition politicians have called for fresh elections.
a local politician (= one who works in local government)
a career politician (= one who has spent most of their life in politics)
a journalist who exposed corrupt politicians

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is good at using different situations in an organization to try to get power or advantage for himself or herself
examples: Marcos was a consummate politician: energetic and ruthless.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activities involved in getting and using power in public life, and being able to influence decisions that affect a country or a society
examples: SEE ALSO party politics
world/international politics
domestic/national/local politics
progressive/radical politics
She is aiming for a career in politics.
a major figure in British politics
Have you considered going into politics (= trying to become a Member of Parliament, Congress, etc.)?
The economy has been the major issue in electoral politics.
This issue is beyond partisan politics (= when people strongly support one party or another).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: matters connected with getting or using power within a particular group or organization
examples: SEE ALSO identity politics
I don't want to get involved in office politics.
the internal politics of the legal profession
racial/gender/sexual politics (= connected with relationships of power between different groups in society)
the politics of identity/race/gender
the politics of fear/envy/division/hate (= when people are influenced by fear, envy, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person’s political views or beliefs
examples: His politics are extreme.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the study of government and politics
examples: a degree in Politics

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a system of political beliefs; a state of political affairs
examples: A politics of the future has to engage with new ideas.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of questioning people who are representative of a larger group in order to get information about the general opinion
examples: SYNONYM survey
to carry out/conduct a poll
A recent poll suggests some surprising changes in public opinion.
A nationwide poll revealed different food preferences in the North and the South.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of voting at an election; the process of counting the votes
examples: The final result of the poll will be known tomorrow.
Thursday is traditionally the day when Britain goes to the polls (= when elections are held).
Polls close (= voting ends) at 9 p.m.
Their defeat at the polls came as a big shock.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the number of votes given in an election
examples: SYNONYM ballot
Labour is ahead in the poll.
They gained 20 per cent of the poll.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of making air, water, soil, etc. dirty; the state of being dirty
examples: air/water pollution
to reduce pollution levels
new pollution control technologies

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: substances that make air, water, soil, etc. dirty
examples: beaches covered with pollution
The new buses emit no more pollution than the average car.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: harmful or annoying levels of noise, or of artificial light at night
examples: Heavy traffic flow is a major source of noise pollution in urban areas.
The government has announced plans to tackle light pollution.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small area of still water, especially one that is artificial
examples: a fish pond

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the Atlantic Ocean
examples: He's relatively unknown on this side of the pond.
Critics across the pond have been queuing up to heap praise on the movie.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an important person (in a small community)Word Origin
examples: Middle English: alteration of pound ‘a place where stray animals are kept’; commonly used in dialect in the same sense.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an area of water that has been created for people to swim in
examples: SEE ALSO infinity pool
an indoor/outdoor pool
Does the hotel have a pool?
relaxing by the pool

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the building that contains a public pool

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a small area of still water, especially one that has formed naturally
examples: SEE ALSO rock pool
freshwater/thermal pools

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a small amount of liquid or light lying on a surface
examples: The body was lying in a pool of blood.
a pool of light
The water ran down out of their clothes and formed a pool on floor.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a supply of things or money that is shared by a group of people and can be used when needed
examples: SEE ALSO car pool
a pool of cars used by the firm’s sales force
a pool car

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a group of people available for work when needed
examples: a pool of cheap labour
I started my career in the typing pool (= a group of people who shared a company’s typing work) over 40 years ago.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a game for two people played with 16 balls on a table, often in pubs and bars. Players use cues (= long sticks) to try to hit the balls into pockets at the edge of the table.
examples: COMPARE billiards
a pool table
to shoot (= play) pool
Do you play pool?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a form of gambling in the UK in which people try to win money by saying what the results of football matches will be
examples: He does the pools every week.
a pools winner

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having very little money; not having enough money for basic needs
examples: OPPOSITE rich

We aim to help the poorest families.
It's among the poorer countries of the world.
This is a relatively poor neighbourhood.
Andrew grew up desperately poor.
They were so poor that they couldn't afford to feed their family.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: people who have very little money
examples: OPPOSITE the rich

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: deserving sympathy
examples: Have you heard about poor old Harry? His wife's left him.
It's hungry—the poor little thing.
‘I have stacks of homework to do.’ ‘Oh, you poor thing.’
Some poor soul will have to clean the house after the party.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not good; of a quality that is low or lower than expected
examples: SEE ALSO piss-poor
the party’s poor performance in the election
The food was of very poor quality.
She's been in poor health for some time now.
The cottage was in poor physical condition.
It was raining heavily and visibility was poor.
poor food/light/soil
to have a poor opinion of somebody (= to not think well of somebody)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not good at something
examples: a poor swimmer
a poor judge of character
She's a good teacher but a poor manager.
a poor sailor (= somebody who easily gets sick at sea)
Many companies are poor at dealing with telephone complaints.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: having very small amounts of something
examples: OPPOSITE rich
a country poor in natural resources
soil poor in nutrients
There's very little soil here and it's poor in quality.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to finish a long way behind the winner in a race, competition, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is similar to but of a lower quality than a particular famous person or thing
examples: Sparkling white wine is the poor man's champagne.

definitions.definition: costing a particular amount for each one
examples: We can charge $50 a pop.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: liked or enjoyed by a large number of people
examples: OPPOSITE unpopular
Andalucia is a popular tourist destination.
an extremely/immensely popular TV show
This annual event is wildly popular.
This is one of our most popular designs.
The use of case studies has become increasingly popular in higher education.
These policies are unlikely to prove popular with middle-class voters.
I'm not very popular with my parents (= they are annoyed with me) at the moment.
Pizza is more popular among younger adults.
‘Our dog got into the neighbour's garden again!’ ‘You'll be popular.’

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: right or appropriate for the taste and knowledge of ordinary people
examples: popular music/songs/culture/fiction
This story has been widely reported in the popular press.
The band's success is largely due to the popular appeal of the lead singer.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: shared by a large number of people
examples: There's a popular misconception that it's a difficult instrument to play.
Contrary to popular belief, women cause fewer road accidents than men.
Popular opinion was divided on the issue.
By popular demand, the tour has been extended by two weeks.
Their story has captured the popular imagination.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: connected with the ordinary people of a country
examples: The party still has widespread popular support.
a share of the popular vote
The regime was overthrown by a popular uprising.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the view or belief that most people hold
examples: Conventional wisdom has it that riots only ever happen in cities.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being liked, enjoyed or supported by a large number of people
examples: the increasing popularity of cycling
The band's growing popularity landed them a US tour.
Her novels have gained in popularity over recent years.
to win/lose popularity with the students
Their music still enjoys widespread popularity among teenagers.
At the height of his popularity, he was the highest paid television star in history.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: all the people who live in a particular area, city or country; the total number of people who live there
examples: One third of the world’s population consumes/consume two thirds of the world’s resources.
The country has a total population of 65 million.
The entire population of the town was at the meeting.
countries with ageing populations
Muslims make up 55 per cent of the population.
an increase in population
areas of dense/sparse population (= where many/not many people live)
The population is increasing at about 6 per cent per year.
population growth/density

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a particular group of people or animals living in a particular area
examples: the adult/student/working population
the rural/urban population
The disease is relatively uncommon in the general population.
The prison population (= the number of people in prison) is continuing to rise.
He was accused of war crimes against the civilian population.
Oil spillages are disastrous for fish populations.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a collection of items being statistically analysed
examples: When populations are small, random events can lead them to behave atypicallly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a town or city with a harbour, especially one where ships load and unload goods
examples: a container/fishing ports
Rotterdam is a major port.
the port city of Gdansk
the Black Sea ports

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a place where ships load and unload goods or shelter from storms
examples: SEE ALSO airport
a naval port
a container/ferry port
The ship spent four days in port.
They reached port at last.
port of entry (= a place where people or goods can enter a country)
the port authorities

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a strong sweet wine, usually dark red, that is made in Portugal. It is usually drunk at the end of a meal.
examples: SEE ALSO tawny port

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a glass of port

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the side of a ship or aircraft that is on the left when you are facing forward
examples: COMPARE starboard
the port side

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a place on a computer where you can attach another piece of equipment, often using a cable
examples: SEE ALSO parallel port
the modem port

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: if you are in great trouble, you take any help that is offeredWord Origin
examples: noun senses 1 to 2 Old English, from Latin portus ‘haven, harbour’, reinforced in Middle English by Old French. noun senses 3 to 4 shortened form of Oporto, a major port in Portugal from which the wine is shipped. noun sense 5 mid 16th cent.: probably originally the side containing an entry port or facing the port (quayside) for loading. noun sense 6 Old English (in the sense ‘gateway’), from Latin porta ‘gate’; reinforced in Middle English by Old French porte. The later sense ‘opening in the side of a ship’ led to the general sense ‘opening’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thin flat case used for carrying documents, drawings, etc.
examples: I left my portfolio on the train.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a collection of photographs, drawings, etc. that you use as an example of your work, especially when applying for a job
examples: She spent most of last year getting her portfolio together.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a set of shares owned by a particular person or organization
examples: an investment/share portfolio
a portfolio manager

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the particular area of responsibility of a government minister
examples: the defence portfolio
a ministerial portfolio
She resigned her portfolio.
He was asked to join as a minister without portfolio (= one without responsibility for a particular government department).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the range of products or services offered by a particular company or organization
examples: a portfolio of wines

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one part of something larger
examples: a substantial/significant portion of the population
Only a small portion of the budget is spent on books.
The central portion of the bridge collapsed.
You give this portion of the ticket to the inspector and keep the other.
She could recite large portions of Shakespeare.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an amount of food that is large enough for one person
examples: a generous portion of meat
She cut the cake into six small portions.
You should eat several portions of fruit a day.
Do you serve children’s portions?
This particular type of fish has less than 200 calories per portion.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a part of something that is shared with other people
examples: SYNONYM share
You must accept a portion of the blame for this crisis.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a painting, drawing or photograph of a person, especially of the head and shoulders
examples: SEE ALSO self-portrait
a portrait of his wife
a full-length portrait
He had his portrait painted in uniform.
a portrait painter

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a detailed description of somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM depiction
a portrait of life at the French court
The film paints a portrait of a man consumed with jealousy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the way of printing a document in which the top of the page is one of the shorter sides
examples: COMPARE landscape (4)
You can print landscape and portrait pages in the same document.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to show somebody/something in a picture; to describe somebody/something in a piece of writing
examples: SYNONYM depict
The painting portrays the duke’s third wife.
He was one of the first to portray animals from the New World.
His war poetry vividly portrays life in the trenches.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to describe or show somebody/something in a particular way, especially when this does not give a complete or accurate impression of what they are like
examples: SYNONYM represent
Throughout the trial, he portrayed himself as the victim.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to act a particular role in a film or play
examples: SYNONYM play
Her father will be portrayed by Jim Broadbent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to create a threat, problem, etc. that has to be dealt with
examples: to pose a threat/risk/challenge/danger
the threat posed by terrorism
Obesity poses real risks to health and happiness.
The task poses no special problems.
to pose a hazard/obstacle/barrier

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to ask a question, especially one that needs serious thought
examples: The new play poses some challenging questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to sit or stand in a particular position in order to be painted, drawn or photographed
examples: The delegates posed for a group photograph.
They posed briefly for pictures before driving off.
She was only too delighted to pose for the cameras.
He was persuaded to pose for his portrait.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to pretend to be somebody in order to trick other people
examples: The gang entered the building posing as workmen.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to dress or behave in a way that is intended to impress other people
examples: I saw him out posing in his new sports car.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the place where somebody/something is located
examples: Where would be the best position for the lights?
From his position on the cliff top, he had a good view of the harbour.
She looked down over the scene from a raised position.
These plants will grow well in a sheltered position.
The hotel stands in an elevated position looking out over the lake.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the place where somebody/something is meant to be; the correct place
examples: He took up his position by the door.
Is everybody in position?
The dancers all got into position.
She was learning to change her hand from first to third position (= on the strings of a violin).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the way in which somebody is sitting or standing, or the way in which something is arranged
examples: SEE ALSO lotus position
a sitting/standing/kneeling position
My arms were aching so I shifted (my) position slightly.
The soldiers had to stand for hours without changing position.
Keep the box in an upright position.
Make sure that you are working in a comfortable position.
She moved the seat into a reclining position.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the situation that somebody is in, especially when it affects what they can and cannot do
examples: The company's financial position is not certain.
The company hopes to maintain its position as market leader.
What would you do in my position?
This put him and his colleagues in a difficult position.
This recent sale puts us in a strong position.
to be in a position of power/strength/authority
I'm afraid I am not in a position to help you.
You are in no position to complain.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an opinion on or an attitude towards a particular subject
examples: She has made her position very clear.
to change/reconsider/shift your position
the party’s position on education reforms
My parents always took the position that early nights meant healthy children.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a person or organization’s level of importance when compared with others
examples: the position of women in society
the company’s dominant position in the world market
Atkins occupies a remarkable position in the history of photography.
Wealth and position (= high social status) were not important to her.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a job
examples: SYNONYM post
He held a senior position in a large company.
I should like to apply for the position of Sales Director.
They are advertising for a clinic coordinator and hope to fill the position by June.
We need more women in leadership positions.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a place in a race, competition, or test, when compared to others
examples: SEE ALSO pole position
United's 3–0 win moved them up to third position.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the place where somebody plays and the responsibilities they have in some team games
examples: What position does he play?
Nakata had to play out of position when the defender was injured.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a place where a group of people involved in fighting have put men and guns
examples: They attacked the enemy positions at dawn.
The defence stuck firmly to its position.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: good or useful
examples: OPPOSITE negative
The tests have so far yielded positive results.
The contributions have a positive impact on the lives of hundreds of children.
Overseas investment has had a positive effect on exports.
His family have been a very positive influence on him.
The only positive outcome of that day was that our country came together.
to make a positive contribution to a discussion

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: expressing agreement or support
examples: OPPOSITE negative
It's always nice to get positive feedback.
We've had a very positive response to the idea.
The company expects a positive reaction to these new products.
There were some overwhelmingly positive reviews.
I should probably say something positive.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: directed at dealing with something or producing a successful result
examples: OPPOSITE negative
We must take positive steps to deal with the problem.
In the last few years, positive changes have been made.
It will require positive action by all in the industry.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: thinking about what is good in a situation; feeling confident and sure that something good will happen
examples: OPPOSITE negative
a positive attitude/outlook
the power of positive thinking
She tried to be more positive about her new job.
On the positive side, profits have increased.
The report ended on a positive note.
There were times when it was difficult to remain positive.
Analysts remain positive on the outlook for the shares over the long term.
Another positive sign is that many companies have recently raised their dividend payouts.
The goal was to create a positive image of older workers.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: showing clear evidence that a particular substance or medical condition is present
examples: OPPOSITE negative
a positive pregnancy test
The athlete tested positive for steroids.
If your test results are positive, it means that blood was detected.
to be HIV positive
The test proved positive.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: completely sure that something is correct or true
examples: I can't be positive about what time it happened.
She was positive that he had been there.
I'm absolutely positive it was him.
‘Are you sure?’ ‘Positive.’

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: giving clear and definite proof or information
examples: SYNONYM conclusive
The results show a positive correlation between exercise and self-esteem.
We have no positive evidence that she was involved.
This is proof positive that he stole the money.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: complete and definite
examples: SYNONYM absolute
He has a positive genius for upsetting people.
It was a positive miracle that we survived.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: expressing something that is true, did happen, etc.; not containing words such as ‘no’, ‘not’, ‘never’, etc.
examples: OPPOSITE negative (2)

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: greater than zero
examples: OPPOSITE negative

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have or own something
examples: He was charged with possessing a shotgun without a licence.
I'm afraid this is the only suitcase I possess.
The gallery possesses a number of the artist's early works.
Belgium was the first European country to possess a fully fledged rail network.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to have a particular quality or feature
examples: I'm afraid he doesn't possess a sense of humour.
workers who possess the requisite skills for the task
He credited her with a maturity she did not possess.
Isaak 's songwriting possesses a timeless quality.
Young adults possess incredible purchasing power.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have a powerful effect on somebody and control the way that they think, behave, etc.
examples: A terrible fear possessed her.
I was possessed by a desire to tell her everything.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make somebody do something that seems strange or unreasonable
examples: What possessed him to say such a thing?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that you own or have with you at a particular time
examples: SYNONYM belongings
Prisoners were allowed no personal possessions.
One of Jane's most prized possessions was her photo album.
The ring is one of her most treasured possessions.
Please make sure you have all your possessions with you when leaving the plane.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of having or owning something
examples: SEE ALSO vacant possession
The possession of a passport is essential for foreign travel.
They had exclusive possession of the property as tenants.
On her father's death, she came into possession of (= received) a vast fortune.
You cannot legally take possession of the property (= start using it after buying it) until three weeks after the contract is signed.
The manuscript is just one of the treasures in their possession.
The gang was caught in possession of stolen goods.
drug possession
weapons/firearms possession

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the state of having control of the ball
examples: to win/get/lose possession of the ball
The home team had most of the possession in the first half.
The team was struggling to retain possession of the ball.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the state of having illegal drugs or weapons with you at a particular time
examples: She was charged with possession.
They were charged with unlawful possession of firearms.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a country that is controlled or governed by another country
examples: The former colonial possessions are now independent states.
the country's overseas possessions

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the situation when somebody’s mind is believed to be controlled by the Devil or by an evil spirit

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: if you already have or control something, it is difficult for somebody else to take it away from you, even if they have the legal right to itWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French, from Latin possessio(n-), from the verb possidere, from potis ‘able, capable’ + sedere ‘sit’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that may happen or be true; the fact that something might happen or be true, but is not certain
examples: OPPOSITE impossibility
Bankruptcy is a real possibility if sales don't improve.
What had seemed impossible now seemed a distinct possibility.
Reaching the final seems a remote possibility.
There's a strong possibility that it will rain.
There is now no possibility that she will make a full recovery.
We cannot exclude the possibility that another person may have been involved.
I have considered the possibility that she is dead.
He refused to rule out the possibility of a tax increase.
There is a real possibility of war.
The company has raised the possibility of legal action.
I am excited about the possibility of going to the Olympics.
This is a one-year appointment, with the possibility of renewal for an additional year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one of the different things that you can do in a particular situation
examples: The possibilities are endless.
Selling the house is just one possibility that is open to us.
We have to investigate every possibility.
Police are considering a wide range of possibilities.
to exhaust all the possibilities
She explored the possibility of studying in the US.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that gives you a chance to achieve something
examples: SYNONYM opportunity
There are countless possibilities for future research.
The course offers a range of exciting possibilities for developing your skills.
In a bookshop, the possibilities for browsing are endless.
Career possibilities for women are much greater than they were fifty years ago.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if something has possibilities, it can be improved or made successful
examples: The house is in a bad state of repair but it has possibilities.
He was the first to see the possibilities of the plan.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: possible/not possible
examples: A successful outcome is not beyond the realms of possibility.
It is not beyond the bounds of possibility that we'll all meet again one day.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that can be done or achieved
examples: OPPOSITE impossible
New technology has made it possible to communicate more easily.
It is possible to get there by bus.
It's just not physically possible to finish all this by the end of the week.
Would it be possible for me to leave a message for her?
This wouldn't have been possible without you.
I'd like the money back by next week if possible.
Try to avoid losing your temper if at all possible (= if you can).
Use public transport whenever possible (= when you can).
The doctors did all that was humanly possible to save him.
We spent every possible moment on the beach.
Expansion was made possible by the investment of government money.
This film was better than I thought possible.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that might exist or happen but is not certain to
examples: the possible side effects of the drug
a possible future president
Frost is possible, although unlikely, at this time of year.
It is quite possible that the river will flood again.
It's just possible that I gave them the wrong directions.
‘You might be wrong, of course!’ ‘It’s possible, but I doubt it.’
With the possible exception of the Beatles, no other band has become so successful so quickly.
‘Do you think he’ll resign?’ ‘Anything’s possible where he’s concerned.’
a possible outcome/effect/consequence
We have to look at every possible scenario.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: reasonable or acceptable in a particular situation
examples: There are several possible explanations.
Please suggest possible ways in which you would improve the existing program.
a possible solution
One possible cause/reason is…

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used after adjectives to emphasize that something is the best, worst, etc. of its type
examples: It was the best possible surprise anyone could have given me.
Don't leave your packing until the last possible moment.
Jacobs faces the maximum possible sentence of five years imprisonment.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: as quickly, much, soon, etc. as you can
examples: We will get your order to you as soon as possible.
Try to give as much detail as possible in your answer.
She did as much as possible to help him.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a situation in which you have all the possible advantages/disadvantages together
examples: In the best of all possible worlds, you should be able to develop your career and enjoy a rewarding family life.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the benefits of two or more completely different situations that you can enjoy at the same time
examples: If you enjoy the coast and the country, you'll get the best of both worlds on this walk.
Maybe in the best of all possible worlds things would be different.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a situation in which you have all the possible disadvantages at the same timeWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French, or from Latin possibilis, from posse ‘be able’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to say that something might exist, happen or be true, but you are not certain
examples: SYNONYM perhaps
It was possibly their worst performance ever.
She found it difficult to get on with her, possibly because of the difference in their ages.
‘Will you be around next week?’ ‘Possibly.’
‘I’m sure he didn’t mean to be rude.’ ‘Quite possibly (= you may be right), but the damage has been done.’
Last year, his mother died, possibly due to heart failure.
a popular but possibly dangerous type of extreme diet

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used with can/could to emphasize that you are surprised, annoyed, etc. about something
examples: You can't possibly mean that!
How could you possibly think that I had anything to do with it!
He turned out to be the nicest guy you could possibly imagine.
What could possibly go wrong?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used with could to ask somebody politely to do something

definitions.label: Meaning 5

the practice of medicine
clinical/medical practice

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be/become less good at doing something than you were because you have not spent time doing it recently
examples: Don't ask me to speak French! I'm out of practice.
If you don't play regularly you soon get out of practice.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in reality
examples: Prisoners have legal rights, but in practice these rights are not always respected.
The idea sounds fine in theory, but would it work in practice?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a way of encouraging people by telling them that if you do an activity regularly and try to improve your skill, you will become very good at itWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from practise, on the pattern of pairs such as advise, advice.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to do an activity or train regularly so that you can improve your skill
examples: You need to practise every day.
She's practising for her piano exam.
I've been practising my serve for weeks.
She diligently practised her violin every day.
He usually wants to practise his English on me.
I learned hairdressing by practising on my sister.
Practise reversing the car into the garage.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to work as a doctor, lawyer, etc.
examples: There are over 50 000 solicitors practising in England and Wales.
She practised as a barrister for many years.
He was banned from practising medicine.
She practised law for more than a decade.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to do something regularly as part of your normal behaviour
examples: to practise self-restraint/safe sex
Do you still practise your religion?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to do the things yourself that you tell other people to doWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French practiser or medieval Latin practizare, alteration of practicare ‘perform, carry out’, from practica ‘practice’, from Greek praktikē, feminine (used as a noun), of praktikos ‘concerned with action’, from prattein ‘do, act’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who works in a profession, especially medicine or law
examples: SEE ALSO family practitioner
dental practitioners
a qualified practitioner

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who regularly does a particular activity, especially one that requires skill
examples: one of the greatest practitioners of science fiction

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: words that show that you approve of and admire somebody/something
examples: THIRD PERSON OF pray
The team coach singled out two players for special praise.
His teachers are full of praise for the progress he's making.
His latest movie has won high praise from the critics.
He received widespread praise for his performance from fans on social media.

to deserve/earn/garner praise
We have nothing but praise for the way they handled the investigation.
She wrote poems in praise of freedom.
She left with their praises ringing in her ears.
They always sing his praises (= praise him very highly).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the expression of thanks to or respect for God

joyous singing and praise to God
Praise be (to God)! (= expressing belief or joy)

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to hope very much that something will happen
examples: We're praying for good weather on Saturday.

examples: to say your prayers
prayers for the sick

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a fixed form of words that you can say when you speak to God
examples: SEE ALSO Lord’s Prayer

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act or habit of praying
examples: They knelt in prayer.
