spiritual healing through prayer
a national day of prayer

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a religious meeting that takes place regularly in which people say prayersExtra Examples
examples: Muslims attend Friday prayers at the mosque.
Students are required to attend prayers twice a week.
We had family prayers before breakfast.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a thing that you hope for very much
examples: My prayer is that one day he will walk again.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: with only a very slight chance of successWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French preiere, based on Latin precarius ‘obtained by entreaty’, from prex, prec- ‘prayer’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give a religious talk in a public place, especially in a church during a service
examples: She preached to the congregation about forgiveness.
The minister preached a sermon on the parable of the lost sheep.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to tell people about a particular religion, way of life, system, etc. in order to persuade them to accept it
examples: to preach the word of God
He preached the virtues of capitalism to us.
She preached about the benefits of a healthy lifestyle.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to give somebody advice on moral standards, behaviour, etc., especially in a way that they find annoying or boring
examples: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to preach.
You're preaching at me again!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to do the things yourself that you tell other people to do

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to speak to people in support of views that they already hold
examples: I realize I may be preaching to the choir, but I think he's gorgeous.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to happen before something or come before something/somebody in order
examples: the years preceding the war

She preceded me in the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to go in front of somebody
examples: She preceded him out of the room.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to do or say something to introduce something else
examples: She preceded her speech with a vote of thanks to the committee.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official action or decision that has happened in the past and that is seen as an example or a rule to be followed in a similar situation later
examples: The ruling set a precedent for future libel cases.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a similar action or event that happened earlier
examples: historical precedents
There is no precedent for a disaster of this scale.
Such protests are without precedent in recent history.
The achievements of this period were without precedent in history.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the way that things have always been done
examples: SYNONYM tradition
to break with precedent (= to do something in a different way)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: rare and worth a lot of money
examples: SEE ALSO precious metal
a precious vase

precious metals

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: valuable or important and not to be wasted
examples: Clean water is a precious commodity in that part of the world.
You're wasting precious time!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: loved or valued very much
examples: SYNONYM treasured
precious memories/possessions
You are infinitely precious to me.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show you are angry that another person thinks something is very important
examples: I didn't touch your precious car!

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: very formal, exaggerated and not natural in what you say and do
examples: SYNONYM affected

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: clear and accurate
examples: SYNONYM exact
precise details/instructions/measurements
Can you give a more precise definition of the word?
I can be reasonably precise about the time of the incident.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something happens at a particular time or in a particular way
examples: We were just talking about her when, at that precise moment, she walked in.
Doctors found it hard to establish the precise nature of her illness.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: taking care to be exact and accurate, especially about small details
examples: SYNONYM meticulous
a skilled and precise worker
small, precise movements
We've tried to make the process as precise as possible.
She's rather prim and precise.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that you are giving more detailed and accurate information about something you have just mentioned
examples: The shelf is about a metre long—well, 98cm, to be precise.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: exactly
examples: They look precisely the same to me.
That's precisely what I meant.
It's not clear precisely how the accident happened.
The meeting starts at 2 o'clock precisely.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: accurately; carefully
examples: to describe something precisely
She pronounced the word very slowly and precisely.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something is very true or obvious
examples: It's precisely because I care about you that I don't like you staying out late.
The children are precisely the ones who will suffer if they get divorced.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you agree with a statement, especially because you think it is obvious or is similar to what you have just said
examples: ‘It's not that easy, is it?’ ‘No, precisely.’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to show that you are giving more detailed and accurate information about something you have just mentioned
examples: The problem is due to discipline, or, more precisely, the lack of discipline, in schools.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of being exact, accurate and careful
examples: SYNONYM accuracy
Her writing is imaginative but lacks precision.
He chose his words with precision.
done with mathematical precision

precision instruments/tools

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an animal that kills and eats other animals
examples: Some animals have no natural predators.
the relationship between predator and prey

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or an organization that uses weaker people for their own advantage
examples: to protect domestic industry from foreign predators

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who did a job before somebody else
examples: The new president reversed many of the policies of his predecessor.
his immediate predecessor in the post
my predecessor at the Ministry of Defence

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing, such as a machine, that has been followed or replaced by something else
examples: This computer has a larger memory than its predecessor.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say that something will happen in the future

She predicted (that) the election result would be close.
He predicted (that) it would be a smash hit.
It was predicted that inflation would continue to fall.
The trial is predicted to last for months.
This figure is predicted to rise to one billion by the year 2015.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if something is predictable, you know in advance that it will happen or what it will be like
examples: a predictable result
The ending of the book was entirely predictable.
The disease follows a highly predictable pattern.
In March and April, the weather is much less predictable.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: behaving or happening in a way that you would expect and therefore boring
examples: He's very nice, but I find him rather dull and predictable.
Rock music is getting so predictable these days.
She had been in a number of predictable sitcoms.

definitions.definition: a statement that says what you think will happen; the act of making such a statement
examples: The results of the experiment confirmed our predictions.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: mostly; mainly
examples: She works in a predominantly male environment.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to like one thing or person better than another; to choose one thing rather than something else because you like it better

I much prefer jazz to rock music.
I prefer quality to quantity.

I prefer my coffee black.

Would you prefer me to stay?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to accuse somebody formally of a crime so that there can be a trial in court
examples: Police have brought a charge of dangerous driving against the man.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a greater interest in or desire for somebody/something than somebody/something else
examples: It's a matter of personal preference.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: a study of consumer preferences

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: Preference will be given to graduates of this university.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: rather than somebody/something
examples: She was chosen in preference to her sister.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being pregnant
examples: SEE ALSO ectopic pregnancy

unplanned/unwanted pregnancies
the increase in teenage pregnancies

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a baby or young animal developing inside her/its body

a heavily pregnant woman (= one whose baby is nearly ready to be born)
to get/become/fall pregnant
He got his girlfriend pregnant and they're getting married.
She's six months pregnant.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: full of a quality or feeling
examples: Her silences were pregnant with criticism.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an occasion when nobody speaks, although people are aware that there are feelings or thoughts to express
examples: There was a pregnant pause before she replied.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an unreasonable dislike of or preference for a person, group, custom, etc., especially when it is based on their race, religion, sex, etc.
examples: a victim of racial prejudice
Their decision was based on ignorance and prejudice.
There is little prejudice against workers from other EU states.
I must admit to a prejudice in favour of British universities.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: without affecting any other legal matter
examples: They agreed to pay compensation without prejudice (= without admitting guilt).

definitions.label: Meaning 1

preliminary results/findings/enquiries
the preliminary rounds of the contest
pilot studies preliminary to a full-scale study

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: one of the country’s premier chefs
the Premier League/Division

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: the basic premise of her argument

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: a monthly premium of £6.25

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: You have to pay a high premium for express delivery.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if something is at a premium, there is little of it available and it is difficult to get
examples: Space is at a premium in a one-bedroomed apartment.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: at a higher than normal price
examples: Shares are selling at a premium.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to think that somebody/something is particularly important or valuable
examples: The company places a high premium on initiative.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act or process of getting ready for something or making something ready

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: things that you do to get ready for something or make something ready
examples: The country is making preparations for war.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: a pharmaceutical preparation
preparations for the hair and skin

definitions.label: Meaning 1

The college prepares students for a career in business.
The training has prepared me to deal with any medical issue.
We all set about preparing for the party.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make yourself ready to do something or for something that you expect to happen
examples: I had no time to prepare.
The whole class is working hard preparing for the exams.
The police are preparing themselves for trouble at the demonstration.
I had been preparing myself for this moment.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: He was in the kitchen preparing lunch.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make it possible or easier for something to be achieved
examples: The committee will prepare the ground for next month's meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: willing to do something
examples: OPPOSITE unwilling

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: done, made, written, etc. in advance
examples: The police officer read out a prepared statement.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell somebody to take a particular medicine or have a particular treatment; to write a prescription for a particular medicine, etc.
examples: Valium is usually prescribed to treat anxiety.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say what should be done or how something should be done

definitions.definition: an official piece of paper on which a doctor writes the type of medicine you should have, and which enables you to get it from a chemist's
examples: The doctor gave me a prescription for antibiotics.

prescription drugs/medication(s)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: medicine that your doctor has ordered for you
examples: The pharmacist will make up your prescription.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of prescribing medicine
examples: The prescription of drugs is a doctor's responsibility.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a plan or a suggestion for making something happen or for improving it
examples: a prescription for happiness

definitions.label: Meaning 1

Your presence is requested at the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of being in a particular place or thing
examples: OPPOSITE absence

definitions.definition: a group of people, especially soldiers, who have been sent to a place to deal with a particular situation
examples: The government is maintaining a heavy police presence in the area.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person or spirit that you cannot see but that you feel is near
examples: She felt a presence behind her.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the quality of making a strong impression on other people by the way you talk or behave; a person who has this quality
examples: a man of great presence

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: when something exists in a particular place

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to do something to make people very aware of the fact that you are there; to have a strong influence on a group of people or a situation
examples: She’s only been here a couple of weeks but she is already making her presence felt.

the present owner of the house

You can’t use it in its present condition.

definitions.definition: being in a particular place

The mistake was obvious to all those present.
There were 200 people present at the meeting.
Most fathers wish to be present at the birth of their child.
Simply to be physically present was all that was required.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: existing in a particular place or thing
examples: OPPOSITE absent
The threat of force was always present.
the ever present risk of pollution
Levels of pollution present in the atmosphere are increasing.
Analysis showed that traces of arsenic were present in the body.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that all the things or people who should be there are now there

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used after being rude or critical about somebody to say that the people you are talking to are not included in the criticism
examples: The people in this office are so narrow-minded, present company excepted, of course.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a meeting at which something, especially a new product or idea, or piece of work, is shown to a group of people
examples: The sales manager will give a presentation on the new products.
Several speakers will be making short presentations.
The conference will begin with a keynote presentation by a leading industry figure.
a slide/video/multimedia presentation

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of showing something or of giving something to somebody
examples: The trial was adjourned following the presentation of new evidence to the court.
The presentation of prizes began after the speeches.
The Mayor will make the presentation (= hand over the gift) herself.
Members will be admitted on presentation of a membership card.
a presentation copy (= a free book given by the author or publisher)
a presentation ceremony/evening

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the way in which something is offered, shown, explained, etc. to others
examples: Improving the product's presentation (= the way it is wrapped, advertised, etc.) should increase sales.
I admire the clear, logical presentation of her arguments.
The main emphasis of the training will be on presentation skills.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the series of computer slides (= images) that are shown with the talk when somebody gives a presentation at a meeting
examples: I've put my presentation on a memory stick.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a ceremony or formal occasion during which a gift or prize is given
examples: the school's annual presentation evening

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a performance of a play, etc. in a theatre

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the position in which a baby is lying in the mother’s body just before birthWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: via Old French from late Latin praesentatio(n-), from Latin praesentare ‘place before’ (in medieval Latin ‘present as a gift’), from praesent- ‘being at hand’, present participle of praeesse, from prae ‘before’ + esse ‘be’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at the time you are speaking or writing; now
examples: SYNONYM currently
The crime is presently being investigated by the police.
These are the courses presently available.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to show that something happened after a short time
examples: Presently, the door opened again and three men stepped out.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to show that something will happen soon
examples: SYNONYM shortly
She'll be here presently.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of keeping something in its original state or in good condition
examples: building/environmental/food preservation
a preservation group/society
The council has placed a preservation order on the building.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of making sure that something is kept
examples: The central issue in the strike was the preservation of jobs.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the degree to which something has not been changed or damaged by age, weather, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO self-preservation
The paintings were in an excellent state of preservation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to keep a particular quality, feature, etc.; to make sure that something is kept
examples: He was anxious to preserve his reputation.
Efforts to preserve the peace have failed.
She managed to preserve her sense of humour under very trying circumstances.
He was insistent on preserving the integrity of the brand.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to keep something in its original state in good condition
examples: a perfectly preserved 14th century house
Is he really 60? He's remarkably well preserved.
We need knowledgeable gallery curators to preserve great masterpieces for posterity.
This vase has been preserved intact.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to prevent something, especially food, from decaying (= being destroyed by natural processes) by treating it in a particular way
examples: Wax polish preserves wood and leather.
preserved lemons
olives preserved in brine
an attempt to preserve the corpse from decomposition

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to keep somebody/something alive, or safe from harm or danger
examples: SYNONYM save
The society was set up to preserve endangered species from extinction.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to lead or be in charge of a meeting, ceremony, etc.
examples: the presiding judge
They asked if I would preside at the committee meeting.
The party presided over one of the worst economic declines in the country's history (= it was in power when the decline happened).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the job of being president of a country or an organization; the period of time somebody holds this job
examples: the current holder of the EU presidency
She hopes to be the first woman elected to the presidency of the United States.
He was a White House official during the Bush presidency.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the leader of a republic, for example the US
examples: SEE ALSO vice-president (1)
Several presidents attended the funeral.
the President of the United States
President Trump is due to visit the country next month.
Do you have any comment, Mr President?
France elected a new president in 2017.
Ford became president following Nixon's resignation.
She should run for president.
former South African president, Nelson Mandela
He was sworn in as President on August 31.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the person in charge of some organizations, clubs, colleges, etc.
examples: to be made president of the students’ union
She travels extensively in her role as President of the World Wide Fund for Nature.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the person in charge of a bank or a commercial organization
examples: SEE ALSO vice-president (2)
the bank president
the president of Columbia Pictures

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the position or activities of a president
examples: a presidential campaign/candidate/election
a presidential system of government
a presidential year (= one in which the people vote for the next president of the country)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: newspapers and magazines
examples: SEE ALSO gutter press
the local/national/foreign press
the popular/tabloid press (= newspapers with a lot of pictures and stories about famous people)
the music/sporting press (= newspapers and magazines about music/sport)
The mainstream press is ignoring this story.
Unlike the American, the British press operates on a national scale.
The case has been widely reported in the press.
the freedom of the Press/press freedom (= the freedom to report any events and express opinions)
The event is bound to attract wide press coverage (= it will be written about in many newspapers).
According to French press reports, three people have been killed.
a White House press briefing

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the journalists and photographers who work for newspapers and magazines
examples: The Press was/were not allowed to attend the trial.
She has been harassed by the press, who desperately need a story.
He told the press that there had been ‘further progress’.
She told them not to talk to the press.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the type or amount of reports that newspapers write about somebody/something
examples: The airline has had a bad press recently (= journalists have written unpleasant things about it).
The demonstration got very little press.
His latest novel didn't get (a) very good press (= was not praised in the media).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a machine for printing books, newspapers, etc.; the process of printing them
examples: SEE ALSO printing press
We were able to watch the books rolling off the presses.
These prices are correct at the time of going to press.
a story that is hot off the press (= has just appeared in the newspapers)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a business that prints and publishes books
examples: Oxford University Press

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a piece of equipment that is used for creating pressure on things, to make them flat or to get liquid from them
examples: SEE ALSO French press™
a trouser press
a garlic press

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: an act of pushing something with your hand or with a tool that you are holding
examples: He gave the bell another press.
Those shirts need a press (= with an iron).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a large number of people or things competing for space or movement
examples: SYNONYM throng
the press of bodies all moving the same way
Among the press of cars he glimpsed a taxi.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a large cupboard, usually with shelves, for holding clothes, books, etc.Word Origin
examples: noun Middle English: from Old French presse (noun), presser (verb), from Latin pressare ‘keep pressing’, frequentative of premere.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of trying to persuade or to force somebody to do something
examples: SEE ALSO peer pressure
The pressure for change continued to mount.
We are determined to keep up the pressure on the other member states.
There is intense pressure on her to resign.
In every society there is strong pressure to conform.
Do you feel any pressure to dress in a certain way?
We must bring pressure to bear on our government to reverse this decision.
The company is facing increasing pressure from shareholders
The government eventually bowed to popular pressure (= they agreed to do what people were trying to get them to do).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: difficulties and worries that are caused by the need to achieve or to behave in a particular way
examples: You need to be able to handle pressure in this job.
She was unable to attend because of the pressure of work.
How can anyone enjoy the pressures of city life?
The economic pressures on small businesses are intense.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the force or weight with which something presses against something else
examples: The nurse applied pressure to his arm to stop the bleeding.
The barriers gave way under the pressure of the crowd.
Last year he had brain surgery to relieve pressure from a blood clot.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the force produced by a particular amount of gas or liquid in a container or a limited space; the amount of this
examples: SEE ALSO blood pressure
air/water pressure
Check the tyre pressure (= the amount of air in a tyre) regularly.
a pressure gauge (= an instrument used for measuring the pressure of a liquid or a gas)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the effect that something has on the way a situation develops, especially when this causes problems
examples: This puts upward pressure on prices.
The high unemployment rate was exerting downward pressure on wage growth.
These measures are intended to relieve the pressure on the prison system.
They raised the starting threshold for income tax to ease the pressure on family budgets.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the force of the atmosphere on the earth’s surface
examples: SEE ALSO atmospheric
A band of high/low pressure is moving across the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to force or to try to persuade somebody to do something
examples: Advertisements put pressure on girls to be thin.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: if a liquid or a gas is kept under pressure, it is forced into a container so that when the container is opened, the liquid or gas escapes quickly
examples: Draught beer is pumped out of the barrel under pressure.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: being forced to do something
examples: The director is under increasing pressure to resign.
Hospital staff are coming under pressure to work longer hours.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: made to feel anxious about something you have to do
examples: The team performs well under pressure.
He's felt under pressure since his wife had the operation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: respected and admired as very important or of very high quality
examples: a prestigious award
a highly prestigious university
My parents wanted me to go to a more prestigious university.
the city’s most prestigious and exclusive hotel
The Gold Cup is one of the most prestigious events in the racing calendar.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to say that you think that something is probably true
examples: Presumably this is where the accident happened.
You'll be taking the car, presumably?
I couldn't concentrate, presumably because I was so tired.
Presumably you’ll be leaving the children at home.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to suppose that something is true, although you do not have actual proof
examples: SYNONYM assume
They are very expensive, I presume?
‘Is he still abroad?’ ‘I presume so.’
I presumed (that) he understood the rules.
Little is known of the youngest son; it is presumed that he died young.
I presumed him to be her husband.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to accept that something is true until it is shown not to be true, especially in court
examples: Twelve passengers are missing, presumed dead.
In English law, a person is presumed innocent until proved guilty.
We must presume innocence until we have proof of guilt.
We must presume them to be innocent until we have proof of guilt.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to accept something as true or existing and to act on that basis
examples: The course seems to presume some previous knowledge of the subject.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that shows a lack of respect by doing something that you have no right to do
examples: I wouldn't presume to tell you how to run your own business.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to behave in a particular way, in order to make other people believe something that is not true
examples: I'm tired of having to pretend all the time.
Of course I was wrong; it would be hypocritical to pretend otherwise.
He pretended to his family that everything was fine.
We pretended (that) nothing had happened.
She pretended (that) she was his niece.
I pretended to be asleep.
He pretended not to notice.
She didn't love him, though she pretended to.
She pretended an interest she did not feel.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to imagine that something is true as part of a game
examples: They didn't have any real money so they had to pretend.
Let’s pretend (that) we’re astronauts.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to claim to be, do or have something, especially when this is not true
examples: I can't pretend to any great musical talent.
I don’t pretend (that) I know much about the subject, but…
The book doesn't pretend to be a great work of literature.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to some extent; fairly
examples: The game was pretty good.
I'm pretty sure I'll be going.
It's pretty hard to explain.
I'm going to have to find a new apartment pretty soon.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very
examples: That performance was pretty impressive.
Things are looking pretty good!
The idea sounds pretty cool.
We were pretty disappointed with the quality of the food.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be in a good situation, especially when others are not
examples: With profits at record levels, the company’s certainly sitting pretty this year.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: almost; almost completely
examples: One dog looks pretty much like another to me.
He goes out pretty well every night.
The first stage is pretty near finished.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to exist or be very common at a particular time or in a particular place
examples: We were horrified at the conditions prevailing in local prisons.
Those beliefs still prevail among certain social groups.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be accepted, especially after a struggle or an argument
examples: Justice will prevail over tyranny.
Fortunately, common sense prevailed.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to defeat an opponent, especially after a long struggle
examples: In a one-sided final, Spain prevailed against title-holder Croatia 40–34.
They wasted two penalties but still prevailed 2–1.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the fact of existing or being very common at a particular time or in a particular place
examples: an increase in the prevalence of smoking among young people

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to stop somebody from doing something; to stop something from happening
examples: The accident could have been prevented.
Maddie would have joined the army if an injury had not prevented her.
The government took steps to prevent a scandal.
He is prevented by law from holding a licence.
Nothing would prevent him from speaking out against injustice.
Nothing would prevent him speaking out against injustice.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of stopping something bad from happening
examples: accident/crime prevention
the prevention of disease
a fire prevention officer
a drug prevention programme

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: it is better to stop something bad from happening rather than try to deal with the problems after it has happened
examples: Prevention is better than cure, so start looking after your heart now.
Prevention is better than cure, so start taking care of yourself.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening or existing before the event or object that you are talking about
examples: SYNONYM prior
No previous experience is necessary for this job.
The car has only had one previous owner.
She is his daughter from a previous marriage.
I was unable to attend because of a previous engagement.
The judge will take into consideration any previous convictions.
We dealt with this in a previous chapter.
We had met on two previous occasions.
Most previous studies have focused on the elderly.
Today's teens are more health conscious than previous generations.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: immediately before the time you are talking about
examples: SYNONYM preceding
the previous year/month/week/night
I couldn't believe it when I heard the news. I'd only seen him the previous day.
He went jogging on Friday, despite the doctor’s warnings the previous day.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at a time before the time that you are talking about
examples: The building had previously been used as a hotel.
As previously reported, the couple separated in May.
The book contains a number of photographs not previously published.
I had visited them three days previously.
a previously unknown species

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an animal, a bird, etc. that is hunted, killed and eaten by another
examples: The lion will often stalk its prey for hours.
birds of prey (= birds that kill for food)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is harmed or tricked by somebody, especially for dishonest purposes
examples: Elderly people are easy prey for dishonest salesmen.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be killed and eaten by another animal or bird
examples: Many small birds and rodents fall prey to the domestic cat.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be harmed or affected by something bad
examples: Since the attack, she had fallen prey to irrational fears.
She knew she must not fall prey to his charm.
The new government has fallen prey to corruption and fraud.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the amount of money that you have to pay for something
examples: SEE ALSO asking price
Boat for sale, price £8 000
house/oil/share prices
rising/falling prices
to increase/lower/reduce prices
We will have to raise ticket prices.
The company has announced that it is cutting prices.
In the past year, house prices have fallen.
The price of crude oil has risen over the last few months.
to charge a high/reasonable/low price for something
to pay/charge a price for something
He managed to get a good price for the car.
Retail prices for food at the supermarket rose just under two per cent in the first quarter.
Can you give me a price for the work (= tell me how much you will charge)?
Children over five must pay (the) full price for the ticket.
I'm only buying it if it's the right price (= a price that I think is reasonable).
How much are these? They don't have a price on them.
Most new technology comes down in price with time.
a rise/an increase/a fall/a drop in price
They sell quality art supplies at discount prices.
I don't think you'll be able to sell it for that price.
price rises/increases/hikes/cuts

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the unpleasant things that you must do or experience in order to achieve something or as a result of achieving something
examples: Criticism is part of the price of leadership.
Loneliness is a high price to pay for independence in your old age.
Giving up his job was a small price to pay for his children's happiness.
The team paid a heavy price for its lack of preparation.
Being recognized wherever you go is the price you pay for being famous.
His success came at a high price.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the numbers that tell you how much money you will receive if the horse that you bet on wins the race
examples: SYNONYM odds
Six to one is a good price for that horse.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: whatever the cost or the difficulties may be
examples: We want peace at any price.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: costing a lot of money
examples: You can buy strawberries all year round, but at a price.
Food is available, at a price.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: involving something unpleasant
examples: He'll help you—at a price!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: extremely valuable or important

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: so good or useful that the cost does not seem too much
examples: To buy all the recommended equipment is expensive, but as an investment for the future it is cheap at the price.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: you can persuade anyone to do something by giving them more money or something that they want

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to say that no amount of money would persuade you to do or to sell something
examples: I wouldn't work for her again—not at any price!

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to suffer because of bad luck, a mistake or something you have done
examples: He looked terrible this morning. I think he's paying the penalty for all those late nights.
They're now paying the price for past mistakes.
She thinks that any inconvenience is a price worth paying for living in such a beautiful place.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: an amount of money that is offered for capturing or killing somebody
examples: Ever since he killed the gang’s leader, there has been a price on his head.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to say how much money something valuable is worth
examples: They haven't yet put a price on the business.
You can't put a price on that sort of loyalty.
You can't put a price on happiness.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say that you think that something you have achieved may not be worth all the problems and difficulties it causes
examples: What price fame and fortune?

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to say that something seems unlikely
examples: What price England winning the World Cup?

definitions.label: Meaning 1

Their reputation for fairness is a matter of pride.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: The new sports stadium is the pride of the town.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

Her pride was hurt.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: SEE ALSO high priest
a Hindu/Buddhist priest

primary education

definitions.label: Meaning 4

the royal princes

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: SEE ALSO crown princess

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a moral rule or a strong belief that influences your actions
examples: He has high moral principles.
Stick to your principles and tell him you won't do it.
I refuse to lie about it; it's against my principles.
He doesn't invest in the arms industry on principle.
She refuses to allow her family to help her as a matter of principle.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a law, a rule or a theory that something is based on
examples: The same principles apply to both humans and animals.
an important legal principle
‘You learn general principles from studying particular things,’ he asserts.
the basic principles of car maintenance
There are three fundamental principles of teamwork.
to learn the basic/general principles of something
the principles of justice/law
the principles and practice of writing reports
draft principles for the management of shared natural resources

Discussing all these details will get us nowhere; we must get back to first principles (= the most basic rules).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a belief that is accepted as a reason for acting or thinking in a particular way
examples: The welfare of the child is the guiding principle of the family courts.

the principle that free education should be available for all children

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a general or scientific law that explains how something works or why something happens
examples: O'Sullivan was among the first chemists to apply scientific principles to brewing beer.
the principle that heat rises

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if something can be done in principle, there is no good reason why it should not be done although it has not yet been done and there may be some difficulties
examples: In principle there is nothing that a human can do that a machine might not be able to do one day.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: in general but not in detail
examples: They have agreed to the proposal in principle but we still have to negotiate the terms.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: I'm printing a copy of the document for you.

examples: They printed 30 000 copies of the book.

examples: The photo was printed in all the national newspapers.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: Print your name and address clearly in the space provided.

the prison population (= the total number of prisoners in a country)

a prison guard

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 2

There have been mounting protests at the treatment of asylum seekers by the government.
The director resigned in protest at the decision.
People rioted in the streets in protest.
protests over plans to close the museum
She accepted the charge without protest.
The workers staged a protest against the proposed changes in their contracts.
They have decided not to attend the Bonn conference as a protest.
The strike began the day before as a protest against the proposed cuts.
The building work will go ahead, despite protests from local residents.
The country has undergone two weeks of protests by workers and students.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: unwillingly and after expressing disagreement
examples: She wrote a letter of apology but only under protest.
The strikers returned to work, but under protest.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who makes a public protest
examples: SYNONYM demonstrator
Thousands of protesters marched through the city.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a system of fixed rules and formal behaviour used at official meetings, usually between governments
examples: a breach of protocol
the protocol of diplomatic visits

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the first or original version of an agreement, especially a treaty between countries, etc.; an extra part added to an agreement or treaty
examples: the first Geneva Protocol
It is set out in a legally binding protocol which forms part of the treaty.
The dates were agreed under a protocol to the climate convention.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a set of rules that control the way data is sent between computers

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a plan for performing a scientific experiment or medical treatmentWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (denoting the original minute of an agreement, forming the legal authority for future dealings relating to it): from Old French prothocole, via medieval Latin from Greek prōtokollon ‘first page, flyleaf’, from prōtos ‘first’ + kolla ‘glue’. Sense 1 derives from French protocole, the collection of set forms of etiquette to be observed by the French head of state, and the name of the government department responsible for this (in the 19th cent.).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling pleased and satisfied about something that you own or have done, or are connected with
examples: SEE ALSO house-proud
proud parents
the proud owner of a new car
The girls have made me extremely proud.
Your achievements are something to be proud of.
Barry was proud of the fact that he had never missed a day's work in his life.
He was proud of himself for not giving up.
I feel very proud to be a part of the team.
I'm proud to say it's now been 17 days since I last smoked.
We are proud to present this award to you.
She was proud that her daughter had so much talent.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: causing somebody to feel proud
examples: This is the proudest moment of my life.
It was a proud day in the nation’s history
The car had been his proudest possession.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: feeling that you are better and more important than other people
examples: SYNONYM arrogant
She comes across as proud and arrogant.
He was too proud now to be seen with his former friends.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: having respect for yourself and not wanting to lose the respect of others
examples: They were a proud and independent people.
Don't be too proud to ask for help.
What has become of this once proud nation?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: beautiful, tall and impressive
examples: SEE ALSO pride
The sunflowers stretched tall and proud to the sun.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: very proud/pleased
examples: Now he's passed his driving test, he's as proud as Punch.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to use facts, evidence, etc. to show that something is true
examples: OPPOSITE disprove
They hope this new evidence will prove her innocence.
‘I know you're lying.’ ‘Prove it!’
He felt he needed to prove his point (= show other people that he was right).
Are you just doing this to prove a point?
What are you trying to prove?
I certainly don't have anything to prove—my record speaks for itself.
The prosecution has failed to prove its case.
She continued to prove her worth to the team.
Just give me a chance and I'll prove it to you.
This proves (that) I was right.
She was determined to prove everyone wrong.
In this country, you are innocent until proved guilty.
You've just proved yourself to be a liar.
This just proves what I have been saying for some time.
Can it be proved that he did commit these offences?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: if something proves dangerous, expensive, etc. or if it proves to be dangerous, etc., you discover that it is dangerous, etc. over a period of time
examples: SYNONYM turn out (1)
The strategy has proved successful.
The new system has proved popular with our clients.
It was proving extremely difficult to establish the truth.
I have some information that may prove useful.
The opposition proved too strong for him.
The play proved a great success.
Shares in the industry proved a poor investment.
His lack of experience may prove a problem in a crisis.
The promotion proved to be a turning point in his career.
Their fears proved to be groundless.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show other people how good you are at doing something or that you are capable of doing something
examples: He constantly feels he has to prove himself to others.
She wants a chance to prove herself.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to show other people that you are a particular type of person or that you have a particular quality
examples: He proved himself determined to succeed.
She proved herself to be a skilful negotiator.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to swell (= become larger or rounder) before being baked because of the action of yeast
examples: SYNONYM rise

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: people say that something is the exception that proves the rule when they are stating something that seems to be different from the normal situation, but they mean that the normal situation remains true in general
examples: Most electronics companies have not done well this year, but ours is the exception that proves the rule.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give something to somebody or make it available for them to use
examples: SYNONYM supply
Please provide the following information.
The exhibition provides an opportunity for local artists to show their work.
She did not provide any evidence to substantiate the claims.
The hospital has a commitment to provide the best possible medical care.
Please answer questions in the space provided.
Refreshments will be provided.
We are here to provide a service for the public.
We are here to provide the public with a service
He provided us with a lot of useful information.
We provide financial support to low-income families.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to state that something will or must happen
examples: SYNONYM stipulate
The final section provides that any work produced for the company is thereafter owned by the company.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of the areas that some countries are divided into with its own local government
examples: the provinces of Canada
the central province of Ghor

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: all the parts of a country except the capital city
examples: The show will tour the provinces after it closes in London.
a shy young man from the provinces

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person’s particular area of knowledge, interest or responsibility
examples: Such decisions are normally the province of higher management.
I'm afraid the matter is outside my province (= I cannot or need not deal with it).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with one of the large areas that some countries are divided into, with its own local government
examples: provincial assemblies/elections

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with the parts of a country that do not include the capital city, especially when these are regarded as lacking culture or modern ideas
examples: a provincial town
It was all very dull and provincial—I longed for the city.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: unwilling to consider new or different ideas or things
examples: SYNONYM narrow-minded
In spite of his education and travels, he has remained very provincial.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of supplying somebody with something that they need or want; something that is supplied
examples: housing provision
The government is responsible for the provision of healthcare.
There is no provision for anyone to sit down here.
The provision of specialist teachers is being increased.
Several companies are responsible for the provision of cleaning services.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: preparations that you make for something that might or will happen in the future
examples: He had already made provisions for (= planned for the financial future of) his wife and children before the accident.
You should make provision for things going wrong.
Small businesses are advised to make adequate provisions against bad debts.
The plans for developing the area include provision for both water and field sports.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: supplies of food and drink, especially for a long journey
examples: We have enough provisions to last us two weeks.
We went into town to stock up on provisions.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a condition or an arrangement in a legal document
examples: The same provisions apply to foreign-owned companies.
Under the provisions of the lease, the tenant is responsible for repairs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to cause a particular reaction or have a particular effect
examples: The announcement provoked a storm of protest.
The article was intended to provoke discussion.
Dairy products may provoke allergic reactions in some people.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say or do something that you know will annoy somebody so that they react in an angry way
examples: SYNONYM goad
Be careful what you say—he's easily provoked.
The lawyer claimed his client was provoked into acts of violence by the defendant.
An attack on their city will only provoke them to retaliate.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: relating to psychiatry or to mental illness
examples: COMPARE mental
psychiatric disorders
a psychiatric hospital/nurse/patient
psychiatric treatment

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with a person’s mind and the way in which it works
examples: the psychological development of children
Abuse can lead to both psychological and emotional problems.
Her symptoms are more psychological than physical (= imaginary rather than real).
Victory in the last game gave them a psychological advantage over their opponents.
a psychological novel (= one that examines the minds of the characters)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with the study of psychology
examples: psychological research
A psychological study of refugee children came up with some worrying results.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the best time to do something in order for it to be successful
examples: The trick is in finding the (right) psychological moment to ask him for more money.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a scientist who studies and is trained in psychology
examples: SEE ALSO social psychologist
to see a psychologist
to go to a psychologist
an educational psychologist
a clinical psychologist (= one who treats people with mental disorders or problems)
I made an appointment with the school psychologist.
a child psychologist
a sports psychologist

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the scientific study of the mind and how it influences behaviour
examples: COMPARE pop psychology
clinical/educational/child/sport psychology
Kevin has a masters degree in psychology.
She's a professor of psychology at Harvard University.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the kind of mind that somebody has that makes them think or behave in a particular way
examples: the psychology of small boys
I help the actors understand the psychology of their characters.
The answers we give will reflect our own psychology.
Watching the shoppers at the sales gave her a first-hand insight into crowd psychology.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: how the mind influences behaviour in a particular area of life
examples: the psychology of interpersonal relationships

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a building where people go to drink and meet their friends. Pubs serve alcoholic and other drinks, and often also food.
examples: We're all going to the pub after work.
They've gone down the pub for a drink.
They spent the whole evening in the pub.
He is one of the regulars at the pub.
I got home from the pub just after 11.
a pub lunch
the landlord of the local pub
The Elm Tree will remain a traditional village pub.
We are holding a pub quiz in the bar on Tuesday night.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with ordinary people in society in general
examples: The campaign is designed to increase public awareness of the issues.
Levels of waste from the factory may be a danger to public health.
Public safety must come first.
Why would the closure of hospitals be in the public interest (= useful to ordinary people)?
The government had to bow to public pressure.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: provided, especially by the government, for the use of people in general
examples: OPPOSITE private
a public education system
a public library

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: connected with the government and the services it provides
examples: OPPOSITE private
public money/spending/funding
He spent much of his career in public office (= working in the government).
the public purse (= the money that the government can spend)
The rail industry is no longer in public ownership (= controlled by the government).
Schools are worried about public spending cuts.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: known to people in general
examples: Details of the government report have not yet been made public.
a public figure (= a person who is well known because they are often on the television, radio, etc.)
She entered public life (= started a job in which she became known to the public) at the age of 25.
This latest scandal will not have done their public image (= the opinion that people have of them) any good.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: open to people in general; intended to be seen or heard by people in general
examples: There is a ban on smoking in public places.
A public meeting to discuss the issue will be held tomorrow night.
The company was forced to issue a public apology.
The painting will be put on public display next week.
This may be the band's last public appearance together.
The reception and other public areas have been refurbished.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: where there are a lot of people who can see and hear you
examples: OPPOSITE private
Let's go somewhere a little less public.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be something that everyone knows, especially in a particular community or group
examples: Their relationship is common knowledge.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to tell people about something that is a secret
examples: A court order failed to stop her going public with the story.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to start selling shares on the stock exchange

definitions.label: Meaning 10

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of printing a book, a magazine, etc. and making it available to the public; a book, a magazine, etc. that has been published
examples: specialist publications
the publication date
The study is published this week as an advance online publication.
He has written for various publications.
the publication of his first novel
He resigned following the publication of a damning report.
I am delighted to celebrate the publication of this book.
a list of recent publications on this subject
Her article has been accepted for publication in the June issue of the journal.
Her work has appeared in a wide variety of mainstream publications.
the publication by the European Commission of an agriculture information pack

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of printing something in a newspaper, report, etc. so that the public knows about it
examples: The Home Secretary attempted to get an injunction to prevent publication, but was unsuccessful.
a delay in the publication of the exam results
The newspaper continues to defend its publication of the photographs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the attention that is given to somebody/something by newspapers, television, etc.
examples: good/bad/adverse publicity
There has been a great deal of publicity surrounding his disappearance.
The trial took place amid a blaze of (= a lot of) publicity.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the business of attracting the attention of the public to something/somebody; the things that are done to attract attention
examples: She works in publicity.
There has been a lot of advance publicity for her new film.
publicity material
a publicity campaign
The band dressed up as the Beatles as a publicity stunt.
He’s in charge of the publicity for next year’s festival.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to produce a book, magazine, CD-ROM, etc. and sell it to the public
examples: to publish a book/novel/magazine/paper
The first edition was published in 2007.
He works for a company that publishes reference books.
Most of our titles are also published on CD-ROM.
The book was first published in 1960.
This essay was originally published in German.
Many plays were published anonymously.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to print a letter, an article, etc. in a newspaper or magazine
examples: to publish a story/letter/comment/review
to publish an article/interview
Pictures of the suspect were published in all the daily papers.
The editors published a full apology in the following edition.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make information available to the public
examples: SYNONYM release
to publish work/research/results
The findings of the committee will be published on Friday.
The study was published online.
according to the information published on their website
The report will be published on the internet.
The team's report will be published in the journal on 18 August.
This data set is based on a previously published report.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have your work printed and sold to the public
examples: University teachers are under pressure to publish.
He has published extensively on medieval education.
She hasn't published anything for years.
She has recently published her memoirs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the profession or business of preparing and printing books, magazines, CD-ROMs, etc. and selling or making them available to the public
examples: SEE ALSO desktop publishing
a job in publishing
a publishing house/company

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take hold of something and use force in order to move it or try to move it towards yourself
examples: You push and I'll pull.
Don't pull so hard or the handle will come off.
He got hold of the end and pulled.
I pulled on the rope to see if it was secure.
He pulled at her coat sleeve.
Stop pulling her hair!
She pulled the cord and the parachute opened.
She pulled him gently towards her.
He smiled and pulled her closer.
Pull the door shut.
She pulled the straps tight.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to remove something from a place by pulling
examples: If these weeds are not pulled, they will spread rapidly .
He pulled a knife and stabbed the man.
Pull the plug out.
to pull out a gun/knife
She pulled off her boots.
James pulled his shirt over his head, letting it fall to the floor.
They were still pulling bodies from the rubble.
She he was spotted in the water and pulled to safety.
He pulled a gun on me (= took out a gun and aimed it at me).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move somebody/something in a particular direction by pulling
examples: Pull your chair nearer the table.
I pulled up a seat next to her.
He pulled on his sweater.
She took his arm and pulled him along.
The sun was too bright so I pulled the blinds down.
Mary pulled the blanket up over her head.
He was the only living person pulled from the rubble that night .
She pulled on her boots and hurried off.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to hold or be attached to something and move it along behind you
examples: In this area oxen are used to pull carts.
a car pulling a trailer
The horses pulling the wagon stopped suddenly.
Ponies were used to pull the coal trucks.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to move your body or a part of your body in a particular direction, especially using force
examples: He tried to kiss her but she pulled away.
The dog snapped at her and she quickly pulled back her hand.
John pulled himself free and ran off.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to open or close curtains, etc.
examples: SYNONYM draw
Pull the curtains—it's dark outside.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to damage a muscle, etc. by using too much force
examples: to pull a muscle/ligament/tendon
He pulled a hamstring in training.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to move a switch, etc. towards yourself or down in order to operate a machine or piece of equipment
examples: Pull the lever to start the motor.
Don't pull the trigger!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to move or make a vehicle move to the side
examples: The wheel is pulling to the left.
She pulled the car to the right to avoid the dog.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to work hard and use a lot of power
examples: The old car pulled hard as we drove slowly up the hill.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to use oars to move a boat along
examples: They pulled towards the shore.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to attract the interest or support of somebody/something
examples: They pulled in huge crowds on their latest tour.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to attract somebody sexually and get them to spend the evening with you
examples: He can still pull the girls.
She's hoping to pull tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to succeed in playing a trick on somebody, committing a crime, etc.
examples: He's pulling some sort of trick on you.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to cancel an event; to stop showing an advertisement, etc.
examples: The gig was pulled at the last moment.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to perform two roles or functions at the same time
examples: This device can pull double duty as a decent laptop and an adequate tablet.
She deserves credit for serving double duty as a host and performer.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to start being more careful in your behaviour, especially by spending less money than before
examples: Small businesses have had to pull their horns in during the recession.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that it is very difficult to make somebody do something
examples: It's like pulling teeth trying to get him to talk.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to criticize somebody, or their work or ideas, very severely

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to improve your situation yourself, without help from other people

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to produce an expression on your face to show that you do not like somebody/something or in order to make somebody laugh
examples: What are you pulling a face at now?
Do you think it’s funny to make faces behind my back?

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to trick somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to have different aims that cannot be achieved together without causing problems
examples: There are different considerations, often pulling in different directions.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to succeed in doing something difficult by making an extra effort or doing something clever or surprising
examples: We managed to pull it out of the bag despite not being at our best for most of the game.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to play a joke on somebody, usually by making them believe something that is not true

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: used to show that you do not believe what somebody has just said

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to make the greatest effort possible to achieve something

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to put an end to somebody’s project, a plan, etc.
examples: The television company pulled the plug on the series after only five episodes.
They decided to pull the plug on the project.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to express something less strongly than you are able to, for example to avoid upsetting or shocking somebody
examples: Her articles certainly don't pull any punches.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to suddenly produce something as a solution to a problem

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to make use of your place or status in society or at work to make somebody do what you want

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to take help or support away from somebody suddenly

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to try to improve your performance, work, behaviour, etc.
examples: You're going to have to pull your socks up.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to use your influence in order to get an advantage for somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to control events or the actions of other people

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to suddenly move from your house and go to live somewhere else
examples: He pulled up stakes and went back to France.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to work as hard as everyone else in a job, an activity, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12

She's hoping to pull tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 14

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.label: Meaning 16

definitions.label: Meaning 17

definitions.label: Meaning 20

definitions.label: Meaning 22

definitions.label: Meaning 23

definitions.label: Meaning 24

definitions.label: Meaning 26

definitions.label: Meaning 27

definitions.label: Meaning 29

definitions.label: Meaning 30

definitions.label: Meaning 32

definitions.label: Meaning 33

definitions.label: Meaning 34

definitions.label: Meaning 35

definitions.label: Meaning 1

an abnormally high pulse rate

Fear sent her pulse racing (= made it beat very quickly).

definitions.label: Meaning 2

the throbbing pulse of the drums

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: pulse waves
sound pulses

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make water, air, gas, etc. flow in a particular direction by using a pump or something that works like a pump
examples: The engine is used for pumping water out of the mine.
The heart pumps blood around the body.
It took ages to pump out the cellar (= pump the water out of it) after the flood.
The lake had been pumped dry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to flow in a particular direction as if it is being forced by a pump
examples: Blood was pumping out of his wound.
The shock sent adrenalin pumping through her veins.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move something quickly up and down or in and out
examples: He kept pumping my hand up and down.
I pumped the handle like crazy.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to move quickly up and down or in and out
examples: She sprinted for the line, legs pumping.
My heart was pumping with excitement.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to try to get information from somebody by asking them a lot of questions
examples: See if you can pump him for more details.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to fill somebody with something, especially drugs
examples: They pumped her full of painkillers.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to remove the contents of somebody’s stomach using a pump, because they have swallowed something harmful
examples: He had his stomach pumped after taking an overdose.

He keeps pushing himself to get better.
