examples: The prime minister pressed the panic button yesterday as Britain’s economy plunged deeper into crisis.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to do exactly the right things to please somebody
examples: a new satirical comedy show that pushes all the right buttons

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to spend a lot of money on enjoying yourself or celebrating something
examples: SYNONYM splash out (on something)

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to attempt to go beyond what is allowed or thought to be possible
examples: We aim to push the boundaries of what we can achieve.
She pushes her physical limits through various endurance challenges.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to go beyond the limits of what is allowed or thought to be possible
examples: He is a performer who consistently pushes the envelope of TV comedy.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to take a risk because you have successfully avoided problems in the past
examples: You didn't get caught last time, but don't push your luck!

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to force somebody to lose control of their behaviour, usually after a particular event or series of events
examples: No one knows exactly what caused his breakdown, but losing his job may have pushed him over the edge.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to react in a sudden or extreme way to something unexpected that has frightened you
examples: The prime minister pushed the panic button yesterday as Britain's economy plunged deeper into crisis.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to try to forget about something unpleasant
examples: I tried to push the thought to the back of my mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move something into a particular place or position
examples: Put the cases down there, please.
Did you put sugar in my coffee?
Put your hand up if you need more paper.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move something into a particular place or position using force
examples: He put his fist through a glass door.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to cause somebody/something to go to a particular place
examples: Her family put her into a nursing home.
It was the year the Americans put a man on the moon.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to attach or fix something to something else
examples: We had to put new locks on all the doors.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to write something or make a mark on something
examples: Put your name here.
Friday at 11? I'll put it in my diary.
I couldn't read what she had put.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to bring somebody/something into the state or condition mentioned
examples: I was put in charge of the office.
The incident put her in a bad mood.
Put yourself in my position. What would you have done?
I tried to put the matter into perspective.
Don't go putting yourself at risk.
I am determined to put things right.
It was time to put their suggestion into practice.
This new injury will put him out of action for several weeks.
He put Ray on guard with a gun.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something feel something or be affected by something
examples: Her new job has put a great strain on her.
They put pressure on her to resign.
It's time you put a stop to this childish behaviour.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to express or state something in a particular way
examples: She put it very tactfully.
Put simply, we accept their offer or go bankrupt.
Simply put, the film is a masterpiece.
I was, to put it mildly, annoyed (= I was extremely angry).
Putting it bluntly, the project was a disaster.
He was too trusting—or, to put it another way, he had no head for business.
The meat was—how shall I put it?—a little overdone.
As T.S. Eliot puts it…
She had never tried to put this feeling into words.
Can you help me put this letter into good English, please?
I thought you put your points very well.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to give or attach a particular level of importance, trust, value, etc. to something
examples: Our company puts the emphasis on quality.
He put a limit on the amount we could spend.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to consider somebody/something to belong to the class or level mentioned
examples: I'd put her in the top rank of modern novelists.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to throw the shot

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say that you think somebody is capable of doing something wrong, illegal, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to have many sexual partners

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to suggest something to somebody to see if they can argue against it
examples: I put it to you that you are the only person who had a motive for the crime.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to persuade somebody to believe something that is not true
examples: Don't try to put one over on me!

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to force somebody to experience something difficult or unpleasant
examples: They really put me through it (= asked me difficult questions) at the interview.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used when comparing or contrasting somebody/something with a group of other people or things to mean ‘combined’ or ‘in total’
examples: Your department spent more last year than all the others put together.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to stop just talking about something and actually do it, show it, etc.Word Origin
examples: Old English (recorded only in the verbal noun putung), of unknown origin; compare with dialect pote ‘to push, thrust’ (an early sense of the verb put).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a game, etc. that you have to think about carefully in order to answer it or do it
examples: a crossword puzzle
a book of puzzles for children

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that is difficult to understand or explain
examples: SYNONYM mystery
The deeper meaning of the poem remains a puzzle.
The detectives were beginning to solve the murder. All the pieces in the puzzle were falling neatly into place.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a picture printed on cardboard (= very thick, stiff card) or wood, that has been cut up into a lot of small pieces of different shapes that you have to fit together againWord Origin
examples: late 16th cent. (as a verb): of unknown origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an exam that you have passed or a course of study that you have successfully completed
examples: academic/educational/professional/vocational qualifications
a coaching/teaching/nursing qualification
He left school with no formal qualifications.
to have qualifications
to gain/get/obtain/possess/achieve qualifications
In this job, experience counts for more than paper qualifications.
Too many school-leavers lack basic qualifications in English and Maths.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a skill or type of experience that you need for a particular job or activity
examples: What qualifications do radio presenters require?
Previous teaching experience is a necessary qualification for this job.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: information that you add to a statement to limit the effect that it has or the way it is applied
examples: SYNONYM proviso
I accept his theories, but not without certain qualifications.
The plan was approved without qualification.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the fact of passing an exam, completing a course of training or reaching the standard necessary to do a job or take part in a competition
examples: Nurses in training should be given a guarantee of employment following qualification.
A victory in this game will earn them qualification for the World Cup.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having passed the exams or completed the training that are necessary in order to do a particular job; having the experience to do a particular job
examples: a qualified teacher
a qualified instructor/accountant/nurse/doctor
qualified staff/personnel
to be highly qualified
to be suitably/fully qualified
She's extremely well qualified for the job.
I'm not qualified to teach in state schools.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the practical knowledge or skills to do something
examples: I don't know much about it, so I don't feel qualified to comment.
I'm not technically qualified to say anything.
His supporters say he is uniquely qualified to lead the country out of the crisis.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: limited in some way
examples: The plan was given only qualified support.
The project was only a qualified success.
It was met with qualified enthusiasm.
The proposals received heavily qualified approval.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to reach the standard of ability or knowledge needed to do a particular job, for example by completing a course of study or passing exams
examples: How long does it take to qualify?
He qualified as a doctor last year.
She spent seven years qualifying in law.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give somebody the skills and knowledge they need to do something
examples: This training course will qualify you for a better job.
The test qualifies you to drive heavy vehicles.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be of a high enough standard to enter a competition; to defeat another person or team in order to enter or continue in a competition
examples: He failed to qualify.
South Korea qualified for the finals when they beat Italy 6–1.
They qualified for the World Cup.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have or give somebody the right to do something
examples: To qualify, you must have lived in this country for at least three years.
If you live in the area, you qualify for a parking permit.
In order to qualify for scholarships, students must demonstrate potential for academic excellence.
Your educational background, interests and family history are some of the things that might qualify you.
Paying a fee doesn't automatically qualify you for membership.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have the right qualities to be described as a particular thing
examples: Do you think this dress qualifies as evening wear?
It's an old building, but that doesn't qualify it as an ancient monument!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to add something to a previous statement to make the meaning less strong or less general
examples: I want to qualify what I said earlier—I didn't mean he couldn't do the job, only that he would need supervision.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to describe another word in a particular way
examples: In ‘the open door’, ‘open’ is an adjective qualifying ‘door’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the standard of something when it is compared to other things like it; how good or bad something is
examples: SEE ALSO air quality
Improving the quality of care for nursing home residents is a priority.
When costs are cut product quality suffers.
The soil here is of poor quality.
The food is fresh and of good quality.
His goal was of top quality.
goods of a high quality
high-quality goods
a decline in water quality
We have seen a marked improvement in the quality of service provided.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a high standard
examples: SYNONYM excellence
We aim to provide quality at reasonable prices.
They need to decrease costs while maintaining quality.
contemporary writers of quality
Get it right, even if it takes time; it's quality not quantity that matters.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing that is part of a person’s character, especially something good
examples: personal qualities such as honesty and generosity
to have leadership qualities
She has all the qualities of a good teacher.
It's hard to find people with the right qualities for the job.
He has a lot of good qualities.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a feature of somebody/something, especially one that makes them different from somebody/something else
examples: the special quality of light and shade in her paintings
His voice has a rich, melodic quality.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a newspaper that deals seriously with issues and has a high standard of editing and commentWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in the senses ‘character, disposition’ and ‘particular property or feature’): from Old French qualite, from Latin qualitas (translating Greek poiotēs), from qualis ‘of what kind, of such a kind’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount or a number of something
examples: a large/small quantity of something
vast/huge quantities of food
enormous/massive/considerable/substantial quantities of something
a product that is cheap to produce in large quantities
Lamb is consumed in large quantities in rural areas.
Is it available in sufficient quantity?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the measurement of something by saying how much of it there is
examples: The data is limited in terms of both quality and quantity.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a large amount or number of something
examples: The police found a quantity of drugs at his home.
I was overwhelmed by the sheer quantity of information available.
She felt daunted by the quantity of books she was expected to read for the course.
Their latest album isn't selling in anything like the quantities that their first one did.
A quantity of jewellery was taken during the burglary.
It's cheaper to buy goods in quantity.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person or thing whose qualities or abilities are not yet knownWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French quantite, from Latin quantitas (translating Greek posotēs), from quantus ‘how great, how much’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of four equal parts of something
examples: a quarter of an hour/a century
a quarter of a mile/million
Almost a quarter of respondents reported employment discrimination.
three quarters of all potential customers
The programme lasted an hour and a quarter.
Cut the apple into quarters.
The theatre was about three quarters full.
He completed his last work a quarter century ago.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a period of 15 minutes either before or after every hour
examples: It’s (a) quarter to four now—I’ll meet you at (a) quarter past.
It's quarter of four now—I'll meet you at quarter after.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a period of three months, used especially as a period for which bills are paid or a company’s income is calculated
examples: The rent is due at the end of each quarter.
Our gas bill for the last quarter was much higher than usual.
Sales were down 10% in the first quarter of 2009.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a district or part of a town
examples: the historic quarter of the city
As a student in Paris, she loved the Latin quarter.
The robbery took place in a normally quiet quarter of the town.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person or group of people, especially as a source of help, information or a reaction
examples: Support for the plan came from an unexpected quarter.
The news was greeted with dismay in some quarters.
The move was met with complaints from all quarters (= from everyone).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a coin of the US and Canada worth 25 cents

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: rooms that are provided for soldiers, servants, etc. to live in
examples: We were moved to more comfortable living quarters.
the servants'/officers' quarters

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the period of time twice a month when we can see a quarter of the moon
examples: The moon is in its first quarter.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: one of the four periods of time into which a game of American football is divided
examples: Ford scored the winning touchdown early in the fourth quarter.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring weight, a quarter of a pound; 4 ounces

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring weight, 28 pounds in the UK or 25 pounds in the US; a quarter of a hundredweight

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: kind treatment of an enemy or opponent who is in your power
examples: SYNONYM mercy
His rivals knew that they could expect no quarter from such a ruthless adversary.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: very near
examples: fighting at close quarters

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the female ruler of an independent state that has a royal family
examples: She was crowned queen at the age of fifteen.
kings and queens
the Queen of Norway
Queen Victoria

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the wife of a king
examples: Henry VII and his queen, Elizabeth of York
The King and Queen of Denmark attended the wedding.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a woman, place or thing that is thought to be one of the best in a particular group or area
examples: SEE ALSO drama queen
the queen of fashion
a movie queen
Venice, queen of the Adriatic

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a woman or girl chosen to perform official duties at a festival or celebration
examples: SEE ALSO beauty queen
a carnival queen
a May queen (= at a festival to celebrate the coming of spring)
a homecoming queen
She was nominated for prom queen in high school.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the most powerful piece used in the game of chess that can move any number of squares in any direction

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a playing card with the picture of a queen on it

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a large female insect that lays eggs for the whole group
examples: a queen bee

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: an offensive word for a gay man who behaves like a woman
examples: SEE ALSO drag queen

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the person considered to be the best, most famous or successful in a particular place or area of activityWord Origin
examples: Old English cwēn, of Germanic origin; related to quean ‘badly behaved woman or girl’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a question, especially one asking for information or expressing a doubt about something
examples: Our assistants will be happy to answer your queries.
If you have a query about your insurance policy, contact our helpline.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a question mark to show that something has not been finished or decided
examples: Put a query against Jack's name—I'm not sure if he's coming.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long search for something, especially for some quality such as happiness
examples: the quest for happiness/knowledge/truth
He set off in quest of adventure.
a quest narrative/novel/story

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sentence, phrase or word that asks for information
examples: SEE ALSO indirect question
You didn't answer my question.
You will have the opportunity to ask questions.
Does anyone have any questions?
I would now like to pose two questions:…
That's a very interesting question.
The question is, how much are they going to pay you?
The big question is, why did they do it?
The question arises as to whether or not he knew of the situation.
The key question of what caused the leak remains unanswered.
Can I ask you a question about your first novel?
He put a question to the minister about the recent reforms.
I hope the police don't ask any awkward questions.
This is a difficult question to answer.
The short answer to your question is yes.
The government doesn’t have the answers to these difficult questions.
In an interview try to ask open questions that don't just need ‘Yes’ or ‘No’ as an answer.
I paid cash, no questions asked.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a task or request for information that is intended to test your knowledge or understanding, for example in an exam or a competition
examples: Question 3 was very difficult.
I couldn't do Question 6.
You must answer all ten questions.
In the exam there's sure to be a question on energy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a matter or topic that needs to be discussed or dealt with
examples: This is an issue that raises many important questions.
Let's look at the question of security.
Finally we shall deal with the question of cost.
The question that needs to be addressed is one of funding.
Questions remain about how she was appointed.
The case raises serious questions about the company's conduct.
Which route is better remains an open question (= it is not decided).
The film doesn't answer all the questions it raises.
The research is asking the wrong questions.
The new play poses some challenging questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: doubt or not being certain about something
examples: His suitability for the job is open to question.
Her honesty is beyond question.
Her version of events was accepted without question.
This case brings into question the whole purpose of the law.
The authenticity of the painting has been thrown into question.
The safety of the system has recently come into question.
His ability has never been called into question.
I did have some questions as to his motive in coming.
She's a great dancer, there's no question about that.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody want to ask a question that has not yet been answered
examples: All of which begs the question as to who will fund the project.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to talk about something as if it were definitely true, even though it might not be
examples: These assumptions beg the question that children learn languages more easily than adults.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show that you do not know the answer to a question
examples: ‘How much is all this going to cost?’ ‘Good question!’

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: that is being discussed
examples: On the day in question we were in Cardiff.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: in doubt; uncertain
examples: The future of public transport is not in question.
His sincerity is not in question.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to say that something is not difficult to predict, explain, do, etc.
examples: It's merely a question of time before the business collapses.
It's just a question of deciding what you really want.
Now it's just a question of getting the wording right.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a matter about which there may be difference of opinion or a lack of understanding
examples: Whether this should be enforced by law or not is a moot point.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a matter about which there may be difference of opinion or a lack of understanding
examples: Whether this should be enforced by law or not is a moot question.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: impossible or not allowed and therefore not worth discussing
examples: Another trip abroad this year is out of the question.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to ask somebody to marry you

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: there is/was no possibility of something
examples: There was no question of his/him cancelling the trip so near the departure date.

to fill out a questionnaire

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: done with speed; taking or lasting a short time
examples: SEE ALSO double quick
a quick look/check/search
She gave him a quick glance.
Let's take a quick break.
There's no quick fix for this problem.
Just a quick note to say thanks for lunch yesterday.
Let me just ask one quick question.
Thanks for the quick response.
These cakes are very quick and easy to make.
Would you like a quick drink?
It's quicker by train.
Are you sure this is the quickest way?
Have you finished already? That was quick!
His quick thinking saved her life.
He fired three shots in quick succession.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: moving or doing something fast
examples: a quick learner
The kids were quick to learn.
She was quick (= too quick) to point out the mistakes I'd made.
Don't be too quick to dismiss science fiction.
Don't be so quick to judge unless you know all the facts.
Her quick hands suddenly stopped moving.
Try to be quick! We're late already.
Once again, his quick wits (= ability to think quickly) got him out of an awkward situation.
He's a quick study (= he learns quickly).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: happening very soon or without delay
examples: We need to make a quick decision.
The company wants quick results.
The doctor said she'd make a quick recovery.

The archers poured a rain of arrows on the enemy.

examples: He goes jogging every morning, rain or shine.
We work outside every day, rain or shine.

examples: SEE ALSO acid rain
There will be rain in all parts tomorrow.
The rain was falling more heavily now.
Rain is forecast for the weekend.
Don't go out in the rain.
It's pouring with rain (= raining very hard).
heavy/torrential/pouring/driving rain
The rain poured down.
It looks like rain (= as if it is going to rain).
A light rain began to fall.
I think I felt a drop of rain.
Typically, we get nearly 5 inches of rain in June.
rain clouds/showers
I remember too the sound of the rain on the tin roof.
Sleet, snow, and rain lashed down.
Some people sheltered from the rain in shop doorways.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: The rains come in September.
The monsoon rains started early this year.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to lift or move something to a higher level
examples: OPPOSITE lower1
She raised the gun and fired.
He raised a hand in greeting.
She raised her eyes from her work.
He slowly raised his head up.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move somebody/something/yourself to a standing, sitting or vertical position
examples: OPPOSITE lower1
Somehow we managed to raise her to her feet.
He raised himself up on one elbow.
The security man raised the barrier for me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to increase the amount or level of something
examples: to raise prices/taxes
We need to raise public awareness of the issue.
How can we raise standards in schools?
They raised their offer to $500.
Don't tell her about the job until you know for sure—we don't want to raise her hopes (= make her hope too much).
I've never heard him even raise his voice (= speak louder because he was angry).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to bring or collect money or people together; to manage to get or form something
examples: SEE ALSO fundraiser
We are raising money for charity.
They are holding a quiz to help raise funds for the club.
The event raised over £30 000 for cancer research.
He set about raising an army.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to mention something for people to discuss or somebody to deal with
examples: SYNONYM broach
The book raises many important questions.
I'm glad you raised the subject of money.
I have raised this issue with the environmental health office.
Local residents have raised concerns about late-night noise.
You raise some interesting points.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to cause or produce a feeling or reaction
examples: to raise doubts in people’s minds
The plans for the new development have raised angry protests from local residents.
It wasn't an easy audience but he raised a laugh with his joke.
It had been a difficult day but she managed to raise a smile.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make something happen or appear
examples: SEE ALSO fire-raiser
She raised the alarm when he failed to return home.
The horses' hooves raised a cloud of dust.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to care for a child or young animal until it is able to take care of itself
examples: COMPARE bring somebody up
She raised five children on her own.
They were both raised in the South.
kids raised on a diet of hamburgers
They raised her (as) a Catholic.
I was born and raised a city boy.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to breed (= keep and produce young from) particular farm animals; to grow particular crops
examples: Farmers cleared the land in order to raise cattle.
They raise corn, soybeans and alfalfa on 460 acres.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to end the limits on somebody/something
examples: to raise a blockade/ban/siege

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to contact somebody and speak to them by radio or phone
examples: We managed to raise him on his mobile phone.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to make somebody who has died come to life again
examples: SYNONYM resurrect
Christians believe that God raised Jesus from the dead.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to make a higher bet than another player in a card game
examples: I'll raise you another hundred dollars.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to multiply an amount by itself a particular number of times
examples: 3 raised to the power of 3 is 27 (= 3 × 3 × 3).

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to build something
examples: Our priority will be to raise a boundary wall and prevent trespassing.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to create a document such as an invoice or a petition
examples: They have been raising a petition against the war.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to make somebody angry
examples: Her controversial article is bound to raise hackles.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to do nothing to help somebody
examples: The children never lift a finger to help around the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to do nothing to help somebody
examples: The children never raised a finger to help around the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to increase the level of something, especially demands or sums of money
examples: His ex-wife has upped the ante in her alimony suit against him.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to set a new, higher standard of quality or performance
examples: OPPOSITE lower1
The factory has raised the bar on productivity, food safety and quality.
This latest computer game raises the bar for interface design.
The awards go to people who have truly raised the bar.
Perhaps the new admission requirements raised the bar too high.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to show that you think something is bad or are surprised by something
examples: Eyebrows were raised when he arrived without his wife.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to hold up your glass and wish somebody happiness, good luck, etc. before you drink

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to hit or threaten to hit somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to protest angrily, especially in a way that causes trouble for somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to produce or make somebody produce a lot of noise in a building, for example by shouting or cheering
examples: Their cheers raised the roof.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to expect more/less from a situation
examples: If they can’t afford such a big house, they’ll just have to lower their sights a little.
After failing to get into university, he lowered his sights and got a job in a shop.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel more cheerful or brave
examples: SYNONYM cheer up
The sunny weather raised my spirits a little.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to increase/decrease the amount of excitement, emotion, etc. in a situation
examples: His angry refusal to agree raised the temperature of the meeting.
The government tried to lower the political temperature by agreeing to some of the demands.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: if something unpleasant rears its head or rears its ugly head, it appears or happensWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old Norse reisa; related to the verb rear.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large public meeting, especially one held to support a particular idea or political party
examples: SEE ALSO pep rally
to attend/hold a rally
a peace/protest rally
a mass rally in support of the strike

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a race for cars, motorcycles, etc. over public roads
examples: the Monte Carlo rally
rally driving
He will join the team at the rally next week.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a series of hits of the ball before a point is scored
examples: That was a great rally!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an act of returning to a strong position after a period of difficulty or weakness
examples: SYNONYM recovery
After a furious late rally, they finally scored.
a rally in shares on the stock market

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: done, chosen, etc. without somebody deciding in advance what is going to happen, or without any regular pattern
examples: the random killing of innocent people
a random sample/selection (= in which each thing has an equal chance of being chosen)
The information is processed in a random order.
I find and play a lot of random stuff—Bach, blues, bebop.
He grabbed a random pair of jeans and an old red shirt.
She dodged the random items that were on the concrete floor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not known or not identified
examples: Some random guy gave me a hundred bucks.
You don’t want some random dude telling you how to live your life.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing or person that is random is strange and does not make sense, often in a way that interests you or makes you laugh
examples: Mom, you are so random!
The humour is great because it's just so random and unhinged from reality.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a variety of things of a particular type
examples: The hotel offers a wide range of facilities.
Librarians need a broad range of skills.
There is a full range of activities for children.
This material is available in a huge range of colours.
a narrow/limited range of options
Voters support parties for a whole range of reasons.
The textbook covers a wide range of topics.
Employees across a range of occupations were surveyed.
We have reached agreement over a range of issues.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set of products of a particular type
examples: SEE ALSO mid-range
our new range of hair products
We are looking to expand our product range.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the limits between which something varies
examples: Most of the students are in the 17–20 age range.
It's difficult to find a house in our price range (= that we can afford).
There will be an increase in the range of 0 to 3 per cent.
Prices vary only within a narrow range.
This was outside the range of his experience.
This car is beyond the range of most people's pockets.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the extent of somebody's knowledge or abilities
examples: I think she has quite a limited range as an actor.
The range of his knowledge is impressive.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the area covered by or included in something
examples: Her sculptures explore the range of human experience.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the distance over which something can be seen or heard
examples: The child was now out of her range of vision (= not near enough for her to see).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the distance over which a gun or other weapon can hit things
examples: SEE ALSO close-range
These missiles have a range of 300 miles.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the distance that a vehicle will travel before it needs more fuel

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a line or group of mountains or hills
examples: the great mountain range of the Alps

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: an area of land where people can practise shooting or where bombs, etc. can be tested
examples: SEE ALSO driving range
a shooting range
A device was exploded at the main nuclear testing range.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a large piece of equipment that can burn various fuels and is kept hot all the time, used for cooking, especially in the past

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a large piece of equipment for cooking food, containing an oven and gas or electric rings on top
examples: Cook the meat on a low heat on top of the range.
Many chefs prefer to cook on a gas rather than an electric range.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a large open area for keeping cows, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: from only a short distance away
examples: SEE ALSO close-range
The president was shot at close range.
She scored from close range.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: near enough to be reached, seen or heard
examples: He shouted angrily at anyone within range.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: too far away to be reached, seen or heard
examples: The cat stayed well out of range of the children.
She hid away in her house, out of range of prying eyes.
Don't shoot yet—he's still out of range.
I listened, but the voices were just out of hearing range.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the position, especially a high position, that somebody has in a particular organization, society, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO ranking
She was not used to mixing with people of high social rank.
He rose through the ranks to become managing director.
Within months she was elevated to ministerial rank.
Promotion will mean that I’m immediately above him in rank.
Barons are the lowest rank of the nobility.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the position that somebody has in the army, navy, police, etc.
examples: He was soon promoted to the rank of captain.
He rose steadily through the ranks and retired as a lieutenant-colonel.
officers of junior/senior rank
officers and other ranks (= people who are not officers)
The colonel was stripped of his rank (= was given a lower position, especially as a punishment).
a military commander similar in rank to a modern general

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the position of ordinary soldiers rather than officers; the army
examples: He served in the ranks for most of the war.
He rose from the ranks (= from being an ordinary soldier) to become a warrant officer.
a campaign to attract more women into the military ranks

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the degree to which somebody/something is of high quality
examples: a painter of the first rank
Britain is no longer in the front rank of world powers.
The findings are arranged in rank order according to performance.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the members of a particular group or organization
examples: We have a number of international players in our ranks.
At 50, he was forced to join the ranks of the unemployed.
There were serious divisions within the party's own ranks.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a line or row of soldiers, police, etc. standing next to each other
examples: They watched as ranks of marching infantry passed the window.
They fired at random into the enemy ranks.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a line or row of people or things
examples: SEE ALSO taxi rank
massed ranks of spectators
The trees grew in serried ranks (= very closely together).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a number that gives the position of a member of a set of numbers

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to fail to remain in line
examples: The police broke ranks and started hitting people with their batons.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to refuse to support the group or the organization of which they are members
examples: Large numbers of MPs felt compelled to break ranks over the issue.
He broke ranks with his fellow Republicans and opposed the war.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: if a group of people close ranks, they work closely together to defend themselves, especially when they are being criticized
examples: It's not unusual for the police to close ranks when one of their officers is being investigated.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if soldiers close ranks, they move closer together in order to defend themselves

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to make use of your place or status in society or at work to make somebody do what you wantWord Origin
examples: noun Middle English (in the sense ‘row of things’): from Old French ranc, of Germanic origin; related to ring

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: rapid change/expansion/growth/development
a rapid rise/increase/decline in sales
The patient made a rapid recovery.
a rapid pulse/heartbeat
The guard fired four shots in rapid succession.
Work proceeded at a rapid pace.
The disease is spreading at a rapid rate.
We try hard to provide a rapid response to requests.
Rapid economic growth pushed unemployment to relatively low levels.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very quickly; at a great rate
examples: to increase/spread/expand rapidly
to change/develop/evolve rapidly
a rapidly growing economy
Crime figures are rising rapidly.
It rapidly became apparent that there were insufficient officers to maintain control.
The technology is rapidly changing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not done, seen, happening, etc. very often
examples: a rare disease/occurrence/event
This weekend, visitors will get a rare chance to visit the private apartments.
It's extremely rare for it to be this hot in April.
It is rare to find such loyalty these days.
On the rare occasions when they met he hardly even dared speak to her.
The bacteria can cause infection and, in rare cases, blindness.
The current exhibition offers a rare opportunity to see his original drawings.
In a rare moment of candour, she admitted that mistakes had been made.
It was a rare (= very great) honour to be made a fellow of the college.
Most documentaries, with few rare exceptions, aren't worth purchasing.
Serious crime is a relatively rare occurrence here.
Cold spells in Britain are becoming increasingly rare.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: existing only in small numbers and therefore valuable or interesting
examples: a rare book
a rare coin/stamp
a rare breed
a rare plant/bird/animal
This species is extremely rare.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: cooked for only a short time so that the inside is still red
examples: COMPARE well done
‘How would you like your steak?’ ‘Rare.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not very often
examples: She is rarely seen in public nowadays.
The term is rarely used today.
Irish coins minted before 1100 are rarely found.
I only rarely get a chance to go to the theatre.
We rarely agree on what to do.
a rarely performed play
Rarely has a debate attracted so much media attention.
You will rarely, if ever, have to wait longer than an hour.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small animal with a long tail, that looks like a large mouse, usually considered a pest (= an animal which is disliked because it destroys food or spreads disease)
examples: SEE ALSO brown rat
rat poison
The police are all over town. He’s caught, like a rat in a trap.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an unpleasant person, especially somebody who treats their partner or friends badly, for example by leaving them or cheating them
examples: You mean he just walked out on her after fifteen years? What a rat!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to talk about people who leave an organization, a company, etc. that is having difficulties, without caring about the people who are left

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to suspect that something is wrong about a situationWord Origin
examples: Old English ræt, probably of Romance origin; reinforced in Middle English by Old French rat. The verb dates from the early 19th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a measurement of the speed at which something happens
examples: SEE ALSO burn rate
Figures published today show another fall in the rate of inflation.
Most people walk at an average rate of five kilometres an hour.
The number of reported crimes is increasing at an alarming rate.
At the rate you work, you'll never finish!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a measurement of the number of times something happens or something does something during a particular period
examples: SEE ALSO birth rate
We have seen a reduction in the crime rate over the last 12 months.
a high success/failure rate
the youth unemployment rate
His pulse rate dropped suddenly.
a high/low/rising rate of unemployment
Local businesses are closing at the rate of three a year.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a fixed amount of money that is charged or paid for something
examples: SEE ALSO bank rate
advertising/insurance/postal rates
A rise in interest rates tends to reduce inflation.
The euro exchange rate is strengthening.
He argued for a reduction in the top tax rate.
We offer special reduced rates for students.
to cut/reduce/increase/raise interest rates
a low/high hourly rate of pay
the basic rate of tax (= the lowest amount that is paid by everyone)
We had to borrow money at a high rate of interest.
a fixed-rate mortgage (= one in which the amount of money paid back each month is fixed for a particular period)
a premium-rate phone number (= one that costs more than the usual rate to call)

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: SEE ALSO first-rate

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that a particular fact is true despite what has happened in the past or what may happen in the future
examples: Well, that's one good piece of news at any rate.
I may be away on business next week but at any rate I'll be back by Friday.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to show that you are being more accurate about something that you have just said
examples: He said he'll be coming tomorrow. At any rate, I think that's what he said.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show that what you have just said is not as important as what you are going to say
examples: There were maybe 60 or 70 people there. At any rate, the room was packed.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: very quickly
examples: She's getting through her winnings at a rate of knots.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to say what will happen if a particular situation continues to develop in the same way
examples: At this rate, we'll soon be bankrupt.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the usual amount of money paid for goods or services at a particular time
examples: They pay slightly more than the going rate.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

Figures published today show another fall in the rate of inflation.
Most people walk at an average rate of five kilometres an hour.
The number of reported crimes is increasing at an alarming rate.
At the rate you work, you'll never finish!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a measurement of the number of times something happens or something does something during a particular period
examples: SEE ALSO birth rate
We have seen a reduction in the crime rate over the last 12 months.
a high success/failure rate
the youth unemployment rate
His pulse rate dropped suddenly.
a high/low/rising rate of unemployment
Local businesses are closing at the rate of three a year.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a fixed amount of money that is charged or paid for something

advertising/insurance/postal rates
A rise in interest rates tends to reduce inflation.

He argued for a reduction in the top tax rate.
We offer special reduced rates for students.
to cut/reduce/increase/raise interest rates
a low/high hourly rate of pay
the basic rate of tax (= the lowest amount that is paid by everyone)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to mean ‘fairly’ or ‘to some degree’, often when you are disappointed, surprised or expressing slight criticism
examples: rather odd/strange/unusual
a rather large sum of money
A rather small number of people turned up.
They took a rather different approach.
I thought it was a rather good idea.
The instructions were rather complicated.
She fell and hurt her leg rather badly.
I didn't fail the exam; in fact I did rather well!
It was a rather difficult question.
It was rather a difficult question.
He looks rather like his father.
The patient has responded to the treatment rather better than expected.
He was conscious that he was talking rather too much.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used with a verb to make a statement sound less strong
examples: I've always rather liked Charlie.
I rather suspect we're making a mistake.
We were rather hoping you'd be able to do it by Friday.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to correct something you have said, or to give more accurate information
examples: She worked as a secretary, or rather, a personal assistant.
In the end he had to walk—or rather run—to the office.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to introduce an idea that is different or opposite to the idea that you have stated previously
examples: The walls were not white, but rather a sort of dirty grey.
The problem is not in the whole system, but rather in one small part.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: instead of somebody/something
examples: I think I'll have a cold drink rather than coffee.
Why didn't you ask for help, rather than trying to do it on your own?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used for saying that you would not like to do something that another person is going to do
examples: ‘I'm going climbing tomorrow.’ ‘Rather you than me!’

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: would prefer to
examples: She'd rather die than give a speech.
‘Do you want to come with us?’ ‘No, I'd rather not.’
Would you rather walk or take the bus?
‘Do you mind if I smoke?’ ‘Well, I'd rather you didn't.’
Personally, I'd rather see the money and resources going into education.
I'd rather have a simple product that actually works than something fancy that's just not reliable.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a measurement of how good, popular, important, etc. somebody/something is, especially in relation to other people or things
examples: SEE ALSO credit rating
The poll gave an approval rating of 39 per cent for the president.
Education has been given a high-priority rating by the new administration.
‘The Big Bang Theory’ was the network show with the highest rating.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set of figures that show how many people watch or listen to a particular television or radio programme, used to show how popular a programme is
examples: The show has gone up in the ratings.
The BBC is currently ahead in the ratings war.
Bringing her on the show was a cynical attempt to boost the ratings.
His new sitcom was a ratings success.
It has been ousted from top spot in the TV ratings.
The network's prime-time ratings are up 150 per cent.
The programme's ratings have dipped sharply.
The ratings went shooting up overnight.
The show continues to garner high ratings.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a number or letter that shows which groups of people a particular film is suitable for
examples: SEE ALSO movie rating
The film was given a 15 rating by British censors.
The movie carries an R rating.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a sailor in the navy who is not an officer

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the relationship between two groups of people or things that is represented by two numbers showing how much larger one group is than the other
examples: The school has a very high teacher-student ratio.
What is the ratio of men to women in the department?
The ratio of applications to available places currently stands at 100:1.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: based on reason rather than emotions
examples: a rational argument/choice/decision
rational analysis/thought
There is no rational explanation for his actions.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: able to think clearly and make decisions based on reason rather than emotions
examples: SYNONYM reasonable
No rational person would ever behave like that.
Try to be rational about it.
Humans are essentially rational beings.
She said that she had not been fully rational when she signed the form.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not cooked
examples: raw meat
raw eggs/vegetables
These fish are often eaten raw.
The tigers were fed raw chicken bones.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in its natural state; not yet changed, used or made into something else
examples: raw sewage
raw sugar/milk/cotton
Iron ore is the main raw ingredient in steel.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not yet organized into a form in which it can be easily used or understood
examples: This information is only raw data and will need further analysis.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: powerful and natural; not trained or showing control
examples: songs full of raw emotion
the raw power of imagination
He started with nothing but raw talent and determination.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: red and painful because the skin has been damaged
examples: There were raw patches on her feet where the shoes had rubbed.
His throat was raw and painful.
The skin on her feet had been rubbed raw.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: new to a job or an activity and therefore without experience or skill
examples: a raw beginner
raw recruits (= for example, in the army)

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: very cold
examples: a raw north wind
It had been a wet, raw winter.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: honest, direct and sometimes shocking
examples: a raw portrayal of working-class life
raw language (= containing many sexual details)

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the fact of somebody being treated unfairly
examples: Older workers often get a raw deal.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a narrow line of light, heat or other energy
examples: PLURAL OF ray
The last of the sun's rays shone on the grass.
Ultraviolet rays damage the skin.
The windows were shining in the reflected rays of the setting sun.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small amount of something good or of something that you are hoping for
examples: SYNONYM glimmer
There was just one small ray of hope.
The one ray of light in this whole affair is that justice has been done.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a sea fish with a large broad flat body and a long tail, that is used for food

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the second note of a major scale

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to sit or lie in the sun, especially in order to get a suntan

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a person or thing that makes life brighter or more cheerful
examples: My nephew is a little ray of sunshine.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to arrive at the place that you have been travelling to
examples: They didn't reach the border until after dark.
The beach can only be reached by boat.
I hope this letter reaches you.
We finally reached our destination.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to come to somebody’s attention
examples: The rumours eventually reached the President.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to increase to a particular level, speed, etc. over a period of time
examples: The conflict has now reached a new level of intensity.
Daytime temperatures can reach 40°C.
This tree can reach a height of 24 metres.
Her popularity reached its peak in the late 1990s.
Over half the candidates failed to reach the expected standard.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to arrive at a particular point or stage of something after a period of time
examples: We have a good chance of reaching the final.
His parents have not yet reached retirement age.
The problem has now reached crisis point.
I have reached the stage in my career where I need a change.
The negotiations have reached deadlock.
I'd just like to reach the end of the chapter.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to achieve a particular aim
examples: SYNONYM arrive at
Politicians again failed to reach an agreement.
The two men reached the same conclusion.
They have yet to reach a decision.
In the end we reached a compromise.
The jury was unable to reach a verdict.
We will not stop until we have reached our goal.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to stretch your hand towards something in order to touch it, pick it up, etc.
examples: She reached inside her bag for a pen.
I reached out to pat the dog.
He reached into his pocket and pulled out his phone.
She reached blindly for the light switch.
He reached across the table to squeeze her hand.
He reached out his hand to touch her.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be able to stretch your hand far enough in order to touch something, pick something up, etc.
examples: ‘Grab the end of the rope.’ ‘I can't reach that far!’
Can you reach the light switch from where you're sitting?
I can't reach the top shelf.
She had arranged her desk so that she could reach everything easily.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to stretch your hand out or up in order to get something for somebody
examples: Can you reach that box down for me?
Can you reach me down that box?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be big enough, long enough, etc. to arrive at a particular point
examples: The carpet only reached halfway across the room.
His hair reached down to the middle of his back.
Is the cable long enough to reach the socket?
Her skirt almost reached the ground.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to communicate with somebody, especially by phone
examples: Do you know where I can reach him?
You can reach me at this number.
No one at the company could be reached for comment.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be seen or heard by somebody
examples: Through the internet we are able to reach a wider audience.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: somebody hears about something, especially when other people already know about it
examples: News of his affair eventually reached her ears.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to change or behave in a particular way as a result of or in response to something
examples: I nudged her but she didn't react.
You never know how he is going to react.
He would have reacted in the same way.
Local residents have reacted angrily to the news.
The market reacted by falling a further two points.
The army has reacted to the situation by increasing investment in recruitment.
Her family reacted with horror when she told them.
Residents have reacted with fury to the news.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to become ill after eating, breathing, etc. a particular substance
examples: Some patients may react adversely.
People can react badly to certain food additives.
People react differently to these drugs.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to experience a chemical change when coming into contact with another substance
examples: Silicon reacts chemically like carbon.
Iron reacts with water and air to produce rust.
When an acid and an alkali react together the result is a salt and water.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: what you do, say or think as a result of something that has happened
examples: to provoke/cause/get a reaction
a positive/negative/adverse reaction
What was his reaction to the news?
Often our actions are based upon an emotional reaction to what someone has done or said to us.
A spokesman said the changes were not in reaction to the company's recent losses.
The initial reaction of the White House was favourable.
It's just another knee-jerk reaction from sections of the media.
My immediate reaction was one of shock.
There has been a mixed reaction to her appointment as director.
The decision provoked an angry reaction from local residents.
I tried shaking him but there was no reaction.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a change in people’s attitudes or behaviour caused by disapproval of the attitudes, etc. of the past
examples: The return to traditional family values is a reaction against the permissiveness of recent decades.
Her rebellious attitude is just a reaction against her strict upbringing.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a response by the body, usually a bad one, to a drug, chemical substance, etc.
examples: If you have a bad reaction, discontinue use immediately.
to have an allergic reaction to a drug
Adverse reactions to certain foods can take a few days to manifest.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the ability to move quickly in response to something, especially if in danger
examples: a skilled driver with quick reactions

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a chemical change produced by two or more substances acting on each other
examples: SEE ALSO addition reaction
a chemical reaction
a nuclear reaction
To perform the test, add five drops of the solution to the compound and then observe the reaction.
the reaction of oxygen with other atoms
the reaction of chlorine atoms and ozone

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a force shown by something in response to another force, which is of equal strength and acts in the opposite direction
examples: Action and reaction are equal and opposite.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: opposition to social or political progress or change
examples: The forces of reaction made change difficult.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to look at and understand the meaning of written or printed words or symbols
examples: SEE ALSO sight-read
She's still learning to read.
Some children can read and write before they go to school.
I can't read your writing.
Can you read music?
I'm trying to read the map.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to go through written or printed words, etc. in silence or speaking them to other people
examples: SEE ALSO proofread
I'm going to go to bed and read.
The book is very easy to read.
He liked reading to his grandchildren.
to read a book/magazine/newspaper
to read an article/a report/a letter/a blog/a review
Have you read any Steinbeck (= novels by him)?
one of the most widely read books in the world
I have read every single post in this entire thread.
I didn't have time to read the novel.
I just finished reading your recent article.
He read the poem aloud.
Go on—read it to us.

She read us a story.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to discover or find out about somebody/something by reading
examples: I read about the accident in the local paper.
I read that he had resigned.
I read somewhere that women are starting companies at record rates.
I can't remember where I read it.
That's the most ridiculous thing I have ever read!
Don't believe everything you read in the papers.
I read the reviews on the internet.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to guess what somebody else is thinking
examples: Tell me what you want—I can't read your mind!

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to look at the movements of somebody’s lips to learn what they are saying
examples: SEE ALSO lip-read

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to understand something in a particular way
examples: SYNONYM interpret
How do you read the present situation?
Silence must not always be read as consent.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have something written on it; to be written in a particular way
examples: The sign read ‘No admittance’.
I’ve changed the last paragraph. It now reads as follows…

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to give a particular impression when read
examples: Generally, the article reads very well.
The poem reads like (= sounds as if it is) a translation.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to show a particular weight, pressure, etc.
examples: What does the thermometer read?

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to get information from a measuring instrument
examples: A man came to read the gas meter.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to hear and understand somebody speaking on a radio set
examples: ‘Do you read me?’ ‘I'm reading you loud and clear.’

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to replace one word, etc. with another when correcting a text
examples: For ‘madam’ in line 3 read ‘madman’.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to study a subject, especially at a university
examples: I read English at Oxford.
She's reading for a law degree.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to take information from a disk
examples: My computer can't read the CD-ROM you sent.
to read a file into a computer

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to look for or discover a meaning in something that is not openly stated
examples: Reading between the lines, I think Clare needs money.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to understand easily what somebody is thinking or feeling

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to listen carefully to what you are saying
examples: Read my lips: no new taxes (= I promise there will be no new taxes).

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to tell somebody with force that they must not do something

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to accept something without discussing it
examples: Can we take it as read that you want the job?
