examples: SEE ALSO sight-reader
an avid reader of science fiction
a fast/slow reader
And so, dear reader, our tale comes to its end.
The reader is left to draw his or her own conclusions.
There are many examples to help the reader understand the usefulness of this approach.
Johnson also reminds his readers that ‘the New York School’ was much more than a geographical label.
Readers interested in this period of British history will find much of value in this book.
The book invites young readers to examine the issues.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who reads a particular newspaper, magazine, etc.
examples: readers’ letters
Are you a ‘Times’ reader?
regular readers of this magazine
Readers of this blog will know my views on the matter.
Alert readers may have noticed the misprint in last week's column.
The magazine asked readers to nominate their favourite celebrities.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an easy book that is intended to help people learn to read their own or a foreign language
examples: a series of graded English readers

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a senior teacher at a British university just below the rank of a professor
examples: She is Reader in Music at Edinburgh.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an electronic device that reads data stored in one form and changes it into another form so that a computer can perform operations on it
examples: SEE ALSO card reader

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a machine that produces on a screen a large image of a text stored on a microfiche or microfilmWord Origin
examples: Old English rǣdere ‘interpreter of dreams, reader’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: quickly and without difficulty
examples: SYNONYM freely
All ingredients are readily available from your local store.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a way that shows you do not object to something
examples: SYNONYM willingly
Most people readily accept the need for laws.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activity of somebody who reads
examples: My hobbies include reading and painting.
He needs more help with his reading.
Are you any good at map reading?
He enjoys reading and going to the cinema.
reading glasses (= worn when reading)
a reading lamp/light (= one that can be moved to shine light onto something that you are reading)
She has a reading knowledge of German (= she can understand written German).
After extensive reading on the subject she set to work on an article.
He's done a lot of reading about the history of race relations.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an act of reading something
examples: A closer (= more detailed) reading of the text reveals just how desperate he was feeling.
We are all expected to attend the reading of her will.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: books, articles, etc. that are intended to be read
examples: reading material
reading matter
a series of reading books for children
a reading list (= a list of books, etc. that students are expected to read for a particular subject)
further reading (= at the end of a book, a list of other books that give more information about the same subject)
The report makes for interesting reading (= it is interesting to read)
The article is not exactly light reading (= it is serious and requires effort and concentration to understand).
His article should be compulsory reading for law students.
Her assigned reading for English class was ‘Great Expectations’.
a list of suggested reading on this topic

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the particular way in which you understand a book, situation, etc.
examples: SYNONYM interpretation
Those conclusions are based on a literal reading of the text.
My own reading of events is less optimistic.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the amount or number shown on an instrument used for measuring something
examples: Meter readings are taken every three months.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an event at which something is read to an audience for entertainment; a piece of literature that is read at such an event
examples: He was invited to give a poetry reading as part of the literary festival.
The evening ended with a reading from her latest novel.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a short section from a holy text that is read to people as part of a religious service
examples: The reading today is from the Book of Daniel.
readings from the Koran

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: one of the stages during which a bill (= a proposal for a new law) must be discussed and accepted by a parliament before it can become law
examples: The bill looks like it will be given a second reading.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: fully prepared for what you are going to do and able to start it immediately
examples: Just a minute—I'm almost ready.
Are you nearly ready?
‘Shall we go?’ ‘I'm ready when you are!’
I'm just getting the kids ready for school.
Right, we're ready to go.
We were getting ready to go out.
She's always ready to help.
Volunteers were ready and waiting to pack the food in boxes.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the experience, attitude, etc. that you need in order to be able to deal with something
examples: Her husband wants to start a family, but she isn't ready.
I’m not sure if Karen is ready for marriage yet.
I was twenty years old and ready for anything.
He is clearly not ready to take on such an important role.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: completed and available to be used
examples: Come on, dinner's ready!
The new building should be ready by 2020.
Can you help me get everything ready for the party?
The contract will be ready to sign in two weeks.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: available to be used easily and immediately
examples: SEE ALSO readily
All the relevant records are easily available ready to hand.
a ready supply of wood
a ready source of income

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: willing and quick to do or give something
examples: I was very angry and ready for a fight.
She's always ready with advice.
He's always ready and willing to help.
Don't be so ready to believe the worst about people.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: likely to do something very soon
examples: SYNONYM on the point of
She looked ready to collapse at any minute.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: needing something as soon as possible
examples: Right, I'm ready for bed.
After the long walk, we were all ready for a drink.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: quick and clever
examples: She has great charm and a ready wit.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to prepare for something; to prepare something for something
examples: to make ready for the President’s visit

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: what you say to tell people to start a race

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: ready to start
examples: The show is just about ready to roll.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: actually existing or happening and not imagined or pretended
examples: a real danger/risk/threat/concern
All the characters are based on real people.
It wasn't a ghost; it was a real person.
pictures of animals, both real and mythological
In the movies guns kill people instantly, but it's not like that in real life.
Politicians seem to be out of touch with the real world.
The growth of violent crime is a very real problem.
There's no real possibility of them changing their minds.
We have a real chance of success.
By the end of it I had a real sense of achievement.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not false or artificial
examples: Are those real flowers?
real leather
Pinocchio wanted to be a real live boy.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: actual or true, rather than what appears to be true
examples: Tell me the real reason.
The real story is even more amazing.
Judy Garland's real name was Frances Ethel Gumm.
The real problem is a lack of investment in infrastructure.
The real issue was whether the accused knew the goods were stolen.
The real question here is how he is going to accomplish this.
See the real Africa on one of our walking safaris.
I couldn't resist the opportunity to meet a real live celebrity.
I do my best to hide my real feelings from others.
The only real complaint I have about the film is that it's a little too slow.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: having all the important qualities that it should have to deserve to be called what it is called
examples: She never had any real friends at school.
his first real kiss
I had no real interest in politics.
He was making a real effort to be nice to her.
These measures have made a real difference to peoples lives
She has not shown any real regret for what she did.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a state or quality
examples: He looks a real idiot.
This accident could have produced a real tragedy.
Her next play was a real contrast.
This is a real privilege.
It's been a real challenge, but we're determined to succeed.
He made a real cock-up of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: when the effect of such things as price rises on the power of money to buy things is included in the sums
examples: Real wage costs have risen by 10 per cent in the past year.
The real value of the country's exports has grown little since the 1970s.
This represents a reduction of 5 per cent in real terms.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: what somebody claims it is or serious
examples: This is not a fire drill—it's for real.
He managed to convince voters that he was for real.
I don’t think her tears were for real.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that they are behaving in a stupid or unreasonable way

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to act in an honest and natural way

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the person who really controls an organization, a country, etc. in contrast to the person who is legally in charge
examples: The president’s wife was suspected of being the real power behind the throne.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: something that is what somebody claims it is and that has value, not a copy
examples: It's an American flying jacket, the real McCoy.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: actually what somebody claims that something is
examples: Are you sure it's the real thing (= love), not just infatuation?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: accepting in a sensible way what it is actually possible to do or achieve in a particular situation
examples: a realistic assessment/approach/view
We have to be realistic about our chances of winning.
It is not realistic to expect people to spend so much money.
It would not be realistic for the Government to demand a pay freeze in the sector at this point.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: sensible and appropriate; possible to achieve
examples: SYNONYM feasible
a realistic prospect/chance/possibility
a realistic alternative/option
The important thing is to have realistic expectations about what you can and can't accomplish.
We must set realistic goals.
a realistic target
If you want to retain good employees, you have to pay a realistic salary.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: representing things as they are in real life
examples: a realistic portrayal/depiction/picture
She made a very realistic drawing of a horse.
We try to make these training courses as realistic as possible.
The realistic graphics really bring the game to life.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the true situation and the problems that actually exist in life, in contrast to how you would like life to be
examples: She refuses to face reality.
You're out of touch with reality.
The reality is that there is not enough money to pay for this project.
They seemed to have the perfect marriage but the reality was very different.
I'm having a hard time adjusting to the reality of this situation.
He needs to accept the reality that his time in this job is over.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that is actually experienced or seen, in contrast to what people might imagine
examples: SEE ALSO virtual reality
Will time travel ever become a reality?
The paperless office is still far from being a reality.
As children they experienced the harsh realities of life.
This decision reflects the realities of the political situation.
Politicians should not ignore economic realities for short-term political gain.
It took five years to make her idea a reality.
Money is the key to turning dreams into a reality.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: television/shows, etc. that use real people (not actors) in real situations, presented as entertainment
examples: a reality TV star
the reality show ‘Survivor’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that a situation is different from what has just been said or from what people believe
examples: Outwardly she seemed confident but in reality she felt extremely nervous.
In reality, human beings and dinosaurs never lived on earth at the same time.
The media portray her as happy and successful, but in reality she has a difficult life.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of becoming aware of something
examples: SYNONYM awareness
As realization dawned, he went pale.
the sudden realization of what she had done
There is a growing realization that changes must be made.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of achieving a particular aim, etc.
examples: SYNONYM achievement
It was the realization of his greatest ambition.
the realization of political goals

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of selling something that you own, such as property, in order to get the money that you need for something

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of producing a sound, play, design, etc.; or the thing that is produced

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to understand or become aware of a particular fact or situation
examples: I didn’t realize (that) you were so unhappy.
The moment I saw her, I realized something was wrong.
I finally came to realize that he would never change.
It is important to realize that there are still potential problems.
I don't think you realize how important this is to her.
They hadn't realized just how much time it would take.
Many families fail to realize the importance of a well-balanced diet
Only later did she realize her mistake.
I hope you realize the seriousness of this crime.
The situation was more complicated than they had at first realized.
They managed to leave without any of us realizing.
There was a cheer when it was realized that everyone was safely back.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to achieve something important that you very much want to do
examples: to realize your dream
We try to help all students realize their full potential (= be as successful as they are able to be).
She never realized her ambition of becoming a professional singer.
He has fully realized the promise which he showed.
He finally realized a life long ambition.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if somebody’s fears are realized, the things that they are afraid will happen, do happen
examples: His worst fears were realized when he saw that the door had been forced open.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to sell things that you own, for example property, in order to get the money that you need for something
examples: SYNONYM convert

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be sold for a particular amount of money
examples: SYNONYM make
The paintings realized $2 million at auction.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to produce something that can be seen or heard, based on written information or instructions
examples: The stage designs have been beautifully realized.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb
examples: That's a really good idea.
It's really hard to find a decent job these days.
It all went really well.
This is a really nice place.
Things are looking really bad for him.
It's really important that I speak with her right away.
a really hot fire
I'm really sorry.
She was driving really fast.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something you are saying or an opinion you are giving
examples: I really want to go home now.
I want to help—I really do.
You really need to forget all about her.
Now I really must go.
I really don't mind.
He really likes you.
I really enjoyed the film.
I really, really hope you're right.
I really and truly am in love this time.
I really love it here.
I am really looking forward to seeing the film.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to express interest in or surprise at what somebody is saying
examples: ‘We're going to Japan next month.’ ‘Oh, really?’
‘She's resigned.’ ‘Really? Are you sure?’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say what is actually the fact or the truth about something
examples: What do you really think about it?
Tell me what really happened.
They are not really my aunt and uncle.
I can't believe I am really going to meet the princess.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used, often in negative sentences, to reduce the force of something you are saying
examples: I don't really agree with that.
It doesn't really matter.
I don't really know what to expect.
‘Did you enjoy the book?’ ‘Not really’ (= ‘no’ or ‘not very much’).
We’ve done well, really.
I don't really have a choice.
He never really recovered from the scandal.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used in questions and negative sentences when you want somebody to say ‘no’
examples: Do you really expect me to believe that?
I don't really need to go, do I?
He doesn't really have a clue about what's going on, does he?
Is that how you're really going to do it?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show that you think something that somebody has done is bad
examples: Really, you could have told us before.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an area of activity, interest or knowledge
examples: in the realm of literature
At the end of the speech he seemed to be moving into the realms of fantasy.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a country ruled by a king or queen
examples: SYNONYM kingdom
The Crown maintains armed forces for the defence of the realm.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: possible/not possible
examples: A successful outcome is not beyond the realms of possibility.
It is not beyond the bounds of possibility that we'll all meet again one day.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at or near the back of something
examples: front and rear windows
the rear entrance of the building

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at or near the back of something
examples: front and rear windows
the rear entrance of the building

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a cause or an explanation for something that has happened or that somebody has done
examples: He said no but he didn't give a reason.
She gave no reasons for her decision.
I have no particular reason for doubting him.
There were a number of reasons behind her departure.
We aren't going for the simple reason that we can't afford it.
Job satisfaction is the main reason people remain in jobs or careers.
The only reason your parents are doing this is because they care so much for you.
Give me one good reason why I should help you.
I'd like to know the reason why you're so late.
For some reason (= one that I don't know or don't understand) we all have to come in early tomorrow.
For this reason, it's important to have friends who will support you.
These rules are there for a very good reason.
The man attacked me for no apparent reason.
Sometimes I cry for no reason at all.
She resigned for personal reasons.
For obvious reasons the data is not complete.
He wants to keep them all in his office for reasons best known to himself.
people who, for whatever reason, are unable to support themselves
For reasons of security the door is always kept locked.
‘Why do you want to know?’ ‘No reason’ (= I do not want to say why).
‘Why did she do that?’ ‘She must have her reasons’ (= secret reasons which she does not want to tell).
He was excused by reason of (= because of) his age.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a fact that makes it right or fair to do something
examples: They have reason to believe she is lying.
We have every reason (= have very good reasons) to feel optimistic.
You have no reason to accuse him of laziness.
She has good reason to be concerned.
There is no reason at all to doubt it.
There is no reason why we should agree to this.
This result gives us all the more reason for optimism.
He has every reason for feeling excited.
She complained, with reason (= rightly), that she had been underpaid.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the power of the mind to think in a logical way, to understand and have opinions, etc.
examples: Only human beings are capable of reason (= of thinking in a logical way, etc.).
to lose your reason (= become mentally ill)
the conflict between faith and reason

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: what is possible, practical or right
examples: I can't get her to listen to reason.
Why can't they see reason?
Look, you're supposed to be the voice of reason here.
Keith appears to be open to reason (= to be willing to accept sensible advice).
He's looking for a job and he's willing to do anything within reason.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: it must be clear to any sensible person who thinks about it
examples: It stands to reason that they'll leave if you don't pay them enough.
It stands to reason that she wouldn't want them to find out about her personal problems.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if there is no rhyme or reason to something or it happens without rhyme or reason, it happens in a way that cannot be easily explained or understood
examples: Suddenly, without rhyme or reason, his mood changed.
There's no rhyme or reason to the new opening hours.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: fair, practical, and sensible
examples: OPPOSITE unreasonable
It is reasonable to assume that he knew beforehand that this would happen.
As life expectancy increases, it is reasonable to expect that the retirement age will increase too.
It seems reasonable to conclude that their claims are unfounded.
Is it not reasonable for the government to look for savings and efficiencies?
Be reasonable! We can't work late every night.
The prosecution has to prove beyond (a) reasonable doubt that he is guilty of murder.
We have reasonable grounds for believing that you are responsible.
Any reasonable person would have done exactly as you did.
You must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the information that you provide is correct.
It seems a perfectly reasonable request to make.
If companies expect work during personal time, it's only reasonable to allow personal time at work.
I considered the evidence in order to decide what is fair and reasonable in the circumstances.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: acceptable and appropriate in a particular situation
examples: The police apparently thought this explanation perfectly reasonable.
The judge said they had a reasonable expectation of privacy relating to the information concerned.
He made us a reasonable offer for the car.
You must submit your claim within a reasonable time.
It can even be done as a class project in a reasonable amount of time.
The adviser must take reasonable care to ensure that the information is correct

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not too expensive
examples: SYNONYM fair
We sell good-quality food at reasonable prices.
He believes NASA can reach Mars at a reasonable cost.
If the price is reasonable, we'll buy it.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: fairly good, but not very good
examples: SYNONYM average
Most people here have a reasonable standard of living.
The hotel was reasonable, I suppose (= but not excellent).
There's a reasonable chance that he'll come.
The furniture is in reasonable condition.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to a degree that is fairly good but not very good
examples: The instructions are reasonably straightforward.
She seems reasonably happy in her new job.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a logical and sensible way
examples: We tried to discuss the matter calmly and reasonably.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a fair way
examples: He couldn't reasonably be expected to pay back the loan all at once.
The apartments are reasonably priced (= not too expensive).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of thinking about things in a logical way; opinions and ideas that are based on logical thinking
examples: What is the reasoning behind this decision?
This line of reasoning is faulty.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say or do something that makes somebody less frightened or worried
examples: SYNONYM put/set somebody’s mind at ease/rest
They tried to reassure her, but she still felt anxious.
The doctor reassured him that there was nothing seriously wrong.
She needed to be reassured of his love for her.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who fights against the government of their country
examples: rebel forces
Armed rebels advanced towards the capital.
Some parts of the country fell into rebel hands.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who opposes somebody in authority over them within an organization, a political party, etc.
examples: A number of Tory rebels are planning to vote against the government.
The Education Secretary has made further concessions to the back-bench rebels.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who does not like to obey rules or who does not accept normal standards of behaviour, dress, etc.
examples: I've always been the rebel of the family.
He was a rebel in his teens but he’s a respectable citizen these days.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an attempt by some of the people in a country to change their government, using violence
examples: SYNONYM uprising
The north of the country rose in rebellion against the government.
The army put down the rebellion.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: opposition to authority within an organization, a political party, etc.
examples: Some members are in rebellion against proposed cuts in spending.
The prime minister faces a rebellion from junior members of her party.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: opposition to authority; being unwilling to obey rules or accept normal standards of behaviour, dress, etc.
examples: Teenage rebellion often starts in the home.
rebellion against their parents
The band refused to go on stage and rebellion began to stir in the audience.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to build or put something together again
examples: After the earthquake, the people set about rebuilding their homes.
He rebuilt the engine using parts from cars that had been scrapped.
It could take ten years for the area to completely rebuild after the hurricane.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something/somebody complete and strong again
examples: When she lost her job, she had to rebuild her life completely.
attempts to rebuild the shattered post-war economy
After the divorce, it took me a long time to rebuild my confidence.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to remember something
examples: SYNONYM recollect
She could not recall his name.
Many years later Muir recalled his days at Glasgow University.
I cannot recall a time when the country faced such serious problems.
'I may have; I don't recall,' she said.
If I recall correctly, he lives in Luton.
I can't recall meeting her before.
I vaguely recall seeing the film.
I seem to recall receiving an email from a reader a while ago.
I seem to recall him mentioning a brother once.
He recalled that she always came home late on Wednesdays.
He later recalled that he had met her once.
Can you recall exactly what happened?
I can vividly recall where and when I saw them.
‘It was on a Thursday in March,’ he recalled.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody think of something
examples: SYNONYM evoke
The poem recalls Eliot's ‘The Waste Land’.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to order somebody to return
examples: Both countries recalled their ambassadors.
He was recalled to military duty.
They have both been recalled to the Welsh squad (= selected as members of the team after a time when they were not selected).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to ask for something to be returned, often because there is something wrong with it
examples: The company has recalled all the faulty hairdryers.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of paper or an electronic document that shows that goods or services have been paid for
examples: Can I have a receipt, please?
Do you need a receipt for that?
We will email the receipt to you.
I kept the receipt, so I can return it if you don't like it.
to make out (= write) a receipt
They have to submit receipts to support all expenditure.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of receiving something
examples: You will get an automatic reply to your email confirming receipt.
to acknowledge receipt of a letter
The goods will be dispatched on receipt of an order form.
Are you in receipt of any state benefits?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: money that a business, bank or government receives
examples: net/gross receipts

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to get or accept something that is sent or given to you
examples: I was delighted to receive your letter.
She received many messages of support.
Police had received information about a planned post office robbery.
to receive payment/thanks
He received an award for bravery from the police.
I received a phone call from her a few weeks later.
I received a lovely email from Tina.
The programme's website received many complaints from listeners.
The service receives no money from the local council.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to experience or be given a particular type of treatment or attention
examples: Her work has not received the attention it deserves.
She received urgent hospital treatment.
All our staff receive training on dealing with customers.
We have received overwhelming support from the local community.
We received a warm welcome from our hosts.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to form an idea or impression of somebody/something as a result of what you see, experience, etc.
examples: I did not receive the impression that he was afraid.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be injured in a particular way
examples: Several of the passengers received severe injuries.
She received only minor cuts and bruises.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to react to something new, in a particular way
examples: The play was well received by the critics.
The speech was warmly received by the audience.
The proposals have been received with great enthusiasm.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to welcome or entertain a guest, especially formally
examples: He was received as an honoured guest at the White House.
We were received with great cordiality.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to officially recognize and accept somebody as a member of a group
examples: Three young people were received into the Church at Easter.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to change broadcast signals into sounds or pictures on a television, radio, etc.
examples: to receive programmes via satellite
a device for sending and receiving electronic signals

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be able to hear a radio message that is being sent by somebody
examples: I'm receiving you loud and clear.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to buy or accept goods that you know have been stolen

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be the player that the server hits the ball to
examples: She won the toss and chose to receive.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be the person that an action, etc. is directed at, especially an unpleasant one
examples: She found herself on the receiving end of a great deal of criticism.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the part of a phone that you hold close to your mouth and ear
examples: COMPARE handset
to pick up/lift/put down/replace the receiver

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of radio or television equipment that changes broadcast signals into sound or pictures
examples: COMPARE transmitter
a satellite/GPS receiver
To change channel, select the desired number on the receiver unit.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is chosen by a court to be in charge of a company that is bankrupt
examples: They had to lay off 200 staff and call in the receivers.
The company has been put in the hands of the receiver.
A receiver was appointed by the court to handle the company’s affairs.
The company remained in the hands of the receiver.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who receives something
examples: Molly's more of a giver than a receiver.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person who buys or accepts stolen goods, knowing that they have been stolen

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a player who plays in a position in which the ball can be caught when it is being passed forward
examples: SEE ALSO wide receiver

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that happened or began only a short time ago
examples: a recent study/report/survey
a recent event/development/discovery
The Prime Minister discussed the issue during his most recent visit to Poland.
There have been many changes in recent years.
in recent months/weeks/days
a relatively recent phenomenon
It is only in the recent past that these problems have arisen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not long ago
examples: a recently published book
a recently released report
The company recently announced plans to lay off one-fifth of its workforce.
She recently completed a follow-up study of participants.
We received a letter from him recently.
Until recently they were living in York.
I haven't seen them recently (= it is some time since I saw them).
Have you used it recently (= in the recent past)?
It's only recently that it's become a problem.
Her father died recently at age 79.
Public meetings were held recently to discuss the proposals.
The company has recently signed a deal with a major bank.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the area inside the entrance of a hotel, an office building, etc. where guests or visitors go first when they arrive
examples: COMPARE front desk
Please report to reception on arrival.
You can leave a message with reception.
the reception area
We arranged to meet in reception at 6.30.
I've left the keys at reception.
I've been on reception (= working there) the whole morning.
the reception desk

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a formal social occasion to welcome somebody or celebrate something
examples: a wedding reception
They held a reception for the Japanese trade delegation at the White House.
Are you having a big reception after the wedding?
A champagne reception was held at the Swallow Hotel.
They hosted a reception for 75 guests.
We met at a reception.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the type of welcome that is given to somebody/something
examples: The reception from critics and audiences was at best lukewarm
The band got a rapturous reception from the crowd.
Her latest album has met with a mixed reception from fans.
the book's reception by reviewers
Delegates gave him a warm reception as he called for more spending on education.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the quality of radio and television signals that are broadcast
examples: good/bad reception
There was very poor reception on my phone.
Television reception is very good in this area.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the act of receiving or welcoming somebody
examples: The locals provided facilities for the reception of children from the war zone.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the first class at school for children aged 4 or 5
examples: My son is in reception.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a difficult time for the economy of a country, when there is less trade and industrial activity than usual and more people are unemployed
examples: SEE ALSO double-dip recession
How do you assess the impact of the current recession on manufacturing?
The economy is in deep recession.
policies to pull the country out of recession
These industries have been hard hit by recession.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the movement backwards of something from a previous position
examples: the gradual recession of the floodwater

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: a recipe for chicken soup
vegetarian recipes
a recipe book

This recipe calls for 120g of butter.
a collection of 100 delicious recipes from top chefs
I tried some recipes from this book.
The dish is made to a (= according to) traditional Italian recipe.
The jam is based on a 14th century recipe.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a method or an idea that seems likely to have a particular result
examples: SYNONYM formula
His plans are a recipe for disaster.
What's her recipe for success?
a recipe for failure/chaos/trouble

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who receives something
examples: recipients of awards

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to think something or have an opinion about something
examples: I reckon (that) I’m going to get that job.
He'll be famous one day. What do you reckon (= do you agree)?
It's worth a lot of money, I reckon.
‘They'll never find out.’ ‘You reckon?’ (= I think you may be wrong about that)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be generally considered to be something
examples: Children are reckoned to be more sophisticated nowadays.
It was generally reckoned a success.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to expect to do something
examples: We reckon to finish by ten.
He wasn’t reckoning to pay so much.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to calculate an amount, a number, etc.
examples: I could see him reckoning the cost as I spoke.
The age of the earth is reckoned at about 4.6 billion years.
My debts were reckoned at $12 000.
They reckon (that) their profits are down by at least 20%.
It is generally reckoned that about half of all job vacancies are never advertised publicly.
The journey was reckoned to take about two hours.
The trip was reckoned to take over two days.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is well known and respected in a particular field
examples: Miyazaki is still a name to conjure with among anime fans.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when you mention a name that you think is difficult to remember or pronounce
examples: He comes from Tighnabruaich—now there's a name to conjure with!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is well known and respected in a particular field
examples: Miyazaki is still a name to reckon with among anime fans.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of remembering who somebody is when you see them, or of identifying what something is
examples: SEE ALSO name recognition
He glanced briefly towards her but there was no sign of recognition.
the automatic recognition of handwriting and printed text by computer

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of accepting that something exists, is true or is official
examples: a growing recognition that older people have potential too
There is a general recognition of the urgent need for reform.
to seek international/official/formal recognition as a sovereign state
The government granted full diplomatic recognition to the republics.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: public praise and reward for somebody’s work or actions
examples: She gained only minimal recognition for her work.
He received the award in recognition of his success over the past year.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to change so much that you can hardly recognize it
examples: The town has changed beyond recognition since I was last here.
Capitalism has been reformed almost out of all recognition.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to know who somebody is or what something is when you see or hear them or it, because you have seen or heard them or it before
examples: I recognized him as soon as he came in the room.
Do you recognize this tune?
You might not recognize the name but you'll know her face.
I recognized the voice immediately.
I recognized her by her red hair.
I recognized him from the photo in the paper.
He recognized the man as one of the police officers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to admit or to be aware that something exists or is true
examples: SYNONYM acknowledge
They recognized the need to take the problem seriously.
Most of us recognize the importance of diet.
The government does recognize the value of the arts in this country.
You must recognize the fact that the situation has changed.
Drugs were not recognized as a problem then.
Drugs were not recognized to be a problem then.
Nobody recognized how urgent the situation was.
We recognized that the task was not straightforward.
It is widely recognized that driver fatigue is a problem on motorways.
It was recognized that this solution could only be temporary.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to accept and approve of somebody/something officially
examples: The UK has refused to recognize the new regime.
These qualifications are recognized throughout the EU.
internationally recognized human rights
The court explicitly recognized the group's right to exist.
The organization has not been officially recognized as a trade union.
Such crimes are recognized by international law as crimes against humanity.
He is recognized to be their natural leader.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be thought of as very good or important by people in general
examples: The book is now recognized as a classic.
She's a recognized authority on the subject.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to give somebody official thanks for something that they have done or achieved
examples: His services to the state were recognized with the award of a knighthood.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell somebody that something is good or useful, or that somebody would be suitable for a particular job, etc.
examples: The hotel's new restaurant comes highly recommended (= a lot of people have praised it).
Can you recommend a good hotel?
I recommend the book to all my students.
She was recommended for the post by a colleague.
This game is recommended for children aged 12 and above.
The guidelines recommend low-fat dairy products as excellent sources of calcium

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to advise a particular course of action; to advise somebody to do something
examples: The report recommended a 10% pay increase.
It is dangerous to exceed the recommended dose.
a recommended price of $50
He recommended reading the book before seeing the movie.
I recommend using the latest version of the browser.
My doctor recommended against surgery.
Medical guidelines recommend against using this drug to treat migraines.
I recommend that he see a lawyer.
I recommend that he should see a lawyer.
It is strongly recommended that the machines should be checked every year.
We'd recommend you to book your flight early.
Can you recommend how much we should charge?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something seem attractive or good
examples: SYNONYM commend
This system has much to recommend it.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official suggestion about the best thing to do
examples: to accept/reject a recommendation
Her report lists numerous recommendations for the improvement of safety.
The committee made recommendations to the board on teachers' pay and conditions.
The major recommendation is for a change in the law.
recommendations on the use of vaccines
The commission will make recommendations on how to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases.
We will be implementing all the recommendations from the report.
The council will follow any recommendations made by the fire investigators.
We accept the 16 recommendations of the report.
I had the operation on the recommendation of my doctor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of telling somebody that something is good or useful or that somebody would be suitable for a particular job, etc.
examples: It's best to find a builder through personal recommendation.
We chose the hotel on their recommendation (= because they recommended it).
Here's the list of my top restaurant recommendations.
The girl lived up to her mother’s recommendation of being ‘good with children’.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a formal letter or statement that somebody would be suitable for a particular job, etc.
examples: SYNONYM testimonial
The company gave her a glowing recommendation.
Will you write me a recommendation letter?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of changing or improving the condition of something or the way it works; the process of putting something back into the state it was in before
examples: the reconstruction of the educational system
the post-war reconstruction of Germany
a reconstruction period

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the activity of building again something that has been damaged or destroyed
examples: the reconstruction of the sea walls

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a copy of something that no longer exists
examples: The doorway is a nineteenth-century reconstruction of Norman work.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an act of acting out events that are known to have happened, in order to try and get more information or better understanding about what happened, especially a crime
examples: Last night police staged a reconstruction of the incident.
The police have staged a reconstruction of the events leading up to the murder.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: (in the US) the period after the Civil War when the southern states returned to the US and laws were passed that gave rights to African Americans

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a written account of something that is kept so that it can be looked at and used in the future
examples: You should keep a record of your expenses.
medical/dental records
It was the worst flood since records began.
According to official records, there were 21 murders in the city that year.
Last summer was the wettest on record.
people who leave no trace in the historical record (= written documents that provide evidence about the past)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the best result or the highest or lowest level that has ever been reached, especially in sport
examples: She holds the world record for the 100 metres.
to break the record (= to achieve a better result than there has ever been before)
to set a new record
There was a record number of candidates for the post.
I got to work in record time.
The UK's biggest banks made record profits last year.
Unemployment has reached a record high (= the highest level ever).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the facts that are known about somebody/something’s past behaviour, character, achievements, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO track record
The airline has a good safety record.
The report criticizes the government's record on housing.
He has an impressive record of achievement.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: rocks, fossils, the parts of buildings and objects found in the ground, etc. that provide evidence about the past
examples: Fossil records suggest that the region was covered in water until relatively recently.
evidence in the geological record
This period of barbarian rule is poorly represented in the archaeological record.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the fact of having committed crimes in the past
examples: Does he have a record?
teenagers with a criminal record

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a thin, round piece of plastic on which music, etc. is recorded
examples: SEE ALSO vinyl (2)
to play a record
a record collection

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a piece or collection of music released as a record, or on CD, the internet, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO album (2)
a record company (= one which produces and sells records)
They released their first record in 1963.
The band had a hit record in 1973.
His new record is available on CD or as a download.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to show that you want what you are saying to be officially written down and remembered
examples: Just for the record I would like to clarify something my colleague said earlier.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a point that you are making, so that the person you are speaking to takes notice
examples: And, for the record, he would be the last person I'd ask.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: in a way that keeps repeating a statement or opinion in an annoying way
examples: I hate sounding like a broken record, but I have to say again, we must do more to help.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: something that has been recorded as being true

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if you tell somebody something off the record, it is not yet official and you do not want them to repeat it publicly
examples: Strictly off the record, some members of staff will have to be made redundant.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to say something publicly or officially so that it may be written down and repeated
examples: He didn't want to go on the record as either praising or criticizing the proposal.
I should like to place on record my sincere thanks to all those who have given support.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to give people the correct information about something in order to make it clear that what they previously believed was in fact wrong
examples: To put the record straight, I do not support that idea and never have done.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to get well again after being ill, hurt, etc.
examples: He's still recovering from his operation.
She spent many weeks in hospital recovering from her injuries.
He has fully recovered from the shoulder surgery.
She remains in serious condition, but is expected to recover.
The victim is recovering well at home.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to return to a normal state after an unpleasant or unusual experience or a period of difficulty
examples: It can take many years to recover from the death of a loved one.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to get back the same amount of money that you have spent or that is owed to you
examples: SYNONYM recoup
He is unlikely to ever recover his legal costs.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to get back or find something that was lost, stolen or missing
examples: The police eventually recovered the stolen paintings.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to win back a position, level, status, etc. that has been lost
examples: SYNONYM regain

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to get back the use of your senses, control of your emotions, etc.
examples: SYNONYM regain
It took her a few minutes to recover consciousness.
to recover your sight

examples: My father has made a full recovery from the operation.
to make a remarkable/quick/speedy/slow recovery

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of improving or becoming stronger again
examples: The government is forecasting an economic recovery.
The economy is showing signs of recovery.
a recovery in consumer spending

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the action or process of getting something back that has been lost or stolen
examples: There is a reward for information leading to the recovery of the missing diamonds.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the room in a hospital where patients are kept immediately after an operation
examples: Your mother is now in recovery.
After the operation she was taken to the recovery room.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

recycled materials

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to use the same ideas, methods, jokes, etc. again
examples: He recycled all his old jokes.

She went red as a beet.

definitions.definition: to make something less or smaller in size, quantity, price, etc.; to become less or smaller in size, quantity, etc.
examples: Reduce speed now (= on a sign).

to reduce costs/numbers
a reduced rate/price
They will require car makers to reduce emissions of carbon dioxide by 30%.
Costs have been reduced by 20% over the past year.
The number of employees was reduced from 40 to 25.
The skirt was reduced to £10 in the sale.
Towards the coast, the hills gradually reduce in size.
The number of search engines has reduced substantially over the last few years.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: if you reduce a liquid or a liquid reduces, you boil it so that it becomes less in quantity

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to lose weight by limiting the amount and type of food that you eat
examples: a reducing plan

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to add one or more electrons to a substance or to remove oxygen from a substance
examples: COMPARE oxidize

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the state of being poorer than you were before. People say ‘living in reduced circumstances’ to avoid saying ‘poor’.Word Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Latin reducere, from re- ‘back, again’ + ducere ‘bring, lead’. The original sense was ‘bring back’ ; this led to ‘bring to a different state’, then ‘bring to a simpler or lower state’ (hence sense (2)); and finally ‘diminish in size or amount’ (sense (1), dating from the late 18th cent.).

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: COMPARE oxidation

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: a red wine reduction

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to send somebody/something to somebody/something for help, advice or a decision
examples: My doctor referred me to a specialist.
The company says it has referred the matter to its lawyers.
The case was referred to the Court of Appeal.
May I refer you to my letter of 14 May?
Patients should be referred to a specialist pain clinic.
If you are referred urgently by your GP, a specialist should see you within two weeks.
She was referred for evaluation and treatment.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the official who controls the game in some sports
examples: SEE ALSO assistant referee
He was sent off for arguing with the referee.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who gives information about your character and ability, usually in a letter, for example when you are applying for a job
examples: The principal often acts as a referee for his students.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is asked to settle an argument
examples: to act as a referee between the parties involved

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person who reads and checks the quality of an academic article before it is published
examples: All papers are sent out to external referees.

definitions.definition: the act of looking at something for information
examples: SEE ALSO point of reference
A copy of the booklet is given to the employee for reference.
Keep the list of numbers near the phone for easy reference.
I wrote down the name of the hotel for future reference (= because it might be useful in the future).
The library contains many popular works of reference (= books that contain facts and information).
We provided reference materials about our Greek vase collection.
Reference to the guide shows that the word has been used in the latter sense.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a number, word or symbol that shows where something is on a map, or where you can find a piece of information
examples: The map reference is Y4.
It is essential that an accurate grid reference is given.
Please quote your reference number when making an enquiry.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the act of asking somebody for help or advice
examples: The emergency nurse can treat minor injuries without reference to a doctor.
The decision was made without reference to local managers.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a letter written by somebody who knows you, giving information about your character and abilities, especially to a new employer
examples: I'm sure she'll give you a good reference.
We will take up references (= contact the people who provided them) after the interview.
We'll need a reference from your current employer.
She asked him to provide a reference for her.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a person who agrees to write a reference, for you, for example when you are applying for a job
examples: SYNONYM referee
My previous boss will act as a reference for me.
His former employer agreed to act as a reference for him.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a note in a book that tells you where a particular piece of information comes from
examples: There is a list of references at the end of each chapter.
For references, see Section D above.
References to previous research are listed in an appendix.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say what you are talking or writing about
examples: With reference to your letter of July 22…
I am writing with reference to your job application.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an occasion when all the people of a country can vote on an important issue
examples: Switzerland decided to hold a referendum on joining the EU.
The changes were approved by referendum.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to show the image of somebody/something on the surface of something such as a mirror, water or glass
examples: His face was reflected in the mirror.
She looked into the water and saw her face reflected there.
She could see herself reflected in his eyes.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to throw back light, heat, sound, etc. from a surface
examples: The windows reflected the bright afternoon sunlight.
This material absorbs the sound, and doesn’t reflect it.
When the sun's rays hit the earth, a lot of the heat is reflected back into space.
The sun reflected dully off the stone walls.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show or be a sign of the nature of something or of somebody’s attitude or feeling
examples: Our newspaper aims to reflect the views of the local community.
His music reflects his interest in African culture.
This year's figures simply reflect the fact that we have fewer people out of work.
Does popular culture reflect reality or distort it?
They are constantly revising the dictionary to reflect changes in language.
Her remarks accurately reflect the views of most of us.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to think carefully and deeply about something
examples: Before I decide, I need time to reflect.
She was left to reflect on the implications of her decision.
William had little time to reflect upon these episodes.
On the way home he reflected that the interview had gone well.
She reflected how different it could have been.
‘It could all have been so different,’ she reflected.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something appear to be good, bad, etc. to other people
examples: This incident reflects badly on everyone involved.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an image in a mirror, on a shiny surface, on water, etc.
examples: He admired his reflection in the mirror.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the action or process of sending back light, heat, sound, etc. from a surface
examples: There is reflection of heat from the metal surface.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a sign that shows the state or nature of something
examples: Your clothes are often a reflection of your personality.
This account is only a pale reflection of the true state of affairs.
The increase in crime is a sad reflection on (= shows something bad about) our society today.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: careful thought about something, sometimes over a long period of time
examples: SEE ALSO self-reflection
A week off would give him time for reflection.
She decided on reflection to accept his offer after all.
It may be that, on mature reflection, you decide to cancel the plan.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: your written or spoken thoughts about a particular subject or topic
examples: a book of her reflections on childhood

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an account or a description of something
examples: The article is an accurate reflection of events that day.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: change that is made to a social system, an organization, etc. in order to improve or correct it
examples: a government committed to reform
economic/electoral/constitutional, etc. reform
the reform of the educational system
reforms in education
far-reaching/major/sweeping reforms

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: change that is made to a social system, an organization, etc. in order to improve or correct it
examples: a government committed to reform
economic/electoral/constitutional, etc. reform
the reform of the educational system
reforms in education
far-reaching/major/sweeping reforms

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: shelter or protection from danger, trouble, etc.
examples: A further 300 people have taken refuge in the US embassy.
The region was a place of refuge for outlaws and bandits.
They were forced to seek refuge from the fighting.
As the situation at home got worse she increasingly took refuge in her work.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a place, person or thing that provides shelter or protection for somebody/something
examples: The marshes are a wetland refuge for seabirds, waders and wild fowl.
He regarded the room as a refuge from the outside world.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a building that provides a temporary home for people in need of shelter or protection from somebody/something
examples: The best option for a female victim of domestic abuse is to contact a women's refuge.
During the great fire of 1871 the church served as a refuge for the homeless.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an area in the middle of a road where you can stand and wait for cars to go past until it is safe for you to crossWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French, from Latin refugium, from Latin re- ‘back’ + fugere ‘flee’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who has been forced to leave their country or home, because there is a war or for political, religious or social reasons
examples: There has been a steady flow of refugees from the war zone.
political/economic refugees
a refugee camp

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act of saying or showing that you will not do, give or accept something
examples: SEE ALSO first refusal
the refusal of a request/an invitation/an offer
a blunt/flat/curt refusal
His refusal to discuss the matter is very annoying.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to get back something you no longer have, especially an ability or a quality
examples: I struggled to regain some dignity.
The party has regained control of the region.
She paused on the edge, trying to regain her balance.
She soon regained her composure.
He did not regain consciousness (= wake up after being unconscious) for several days.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to get back to a place that you have left
examples: They finally managed to regain the beach.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to think about somebody/something in a particular way
examples: They regarded people outside their own town with suspicion.
Her work is very highly regarded.
He regards himself as a patriot.
Capital punishment was regarded as inhuman and immoral.
She is widely regarded as the current leader's natural successor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to look at somebody/something, especially in a particular way
examples: SYNONYM contemplate
He regarded us suspiciously.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: relating to or in connection with somebody/something
examples: I have little information as regards her fitness for the post.
As regards the first point in your letter…

examples: They regarded people outside their own town with suspicion.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: relating to or in connection with somebody/something
examples: I have little information as regards her fitness for the post.
As regards the first point in your letter…

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: paying no attention, even if the situation is bad or there are difficulties
examples: The weather was terrible but we carried on regardless.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a method or system of government, especially one that has not been elected in a fair way
examples: a fascist/totalitarian/military, etc. regime
an oppressive/brutal regime

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a method or system of organizing or managing something
examples: Our tax regime is one of the most favourable in Europe.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a set of rules about food and exercise or medical treatment that you follow in order to stay healthy or to improve your health
examples: a dietary regime

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large area of land, usually without exact limits or borders
examples: mountainous/coastal regions
the northern/southern/central, etc. region
This is one of the most densely populated regions of North America.
There are more than two million people living in the region.
Many new species have been discovered in the Amazon region.
Businesses across the region are supporting the project.
The plant is found throughout the western region of the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one of the areas that a country is divided into, that has its own customs and/or its own government
examples: Bilbao is the largest city in the Basque region in northern Spain.
The country is divided into 17 autonomous regions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: all of a country except the capital city
examples: People in the regions should not have to travel to London to fly to the United States.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a part of the body, usually one that has a particular character or problem
examples: pains in the abdominal region

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used when you are giving a number, price, etc. to show that it is not exact
examples: SYNONYM approximately
He earns somewhere in the region of €50 000.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: of or relating to a region
examples: services available at a local and regional level
the conflict between regional and national interests
a regional assembly/council/government
a regional director/manager
national initiatives for regional development
a regional office/centre/agency

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to record your/somebody’s/something’s name on an official list
examples: You can also register online.
to register a birth/marriage/death
to register a company/trademark
The site has 114 million registered users.
a registered charity
We expect about 50 per cent of registered voters to vote in the election.
The police has registered a case against the company.
The regulations require doctors and patients to register in a database.
The ship was registered in Panama.
Six other families were also registered at the same address.
to register at a hotel
She is officially registered disabled.
They encouraged all eligible citizens to register as voters.
He then registered the name as a trademark.
to register with a doctor/dentist
All childminders should be registered with the local authority.
About 700 people registered for the conference.
The drug has not been registered for use in Australia.
More than 5 000 people registered to take part in the contest.
78 per cent reported that they were registered to vote.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make your opinion known officially or publicly
examples: China has registered a protest over foreign intervention.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if a measuring instrument registers an amount or something registers an amount on a measuring instrument, the instrument shows or records that amount
examples: The thermometer registered 32°C.
The earthquake registered 3 on the Richter scale.
The stock exchange has registered huge losses this week.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to show or express a feeling
examples: Her face registered disapproval.
Shock registered on everyone's face.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to notice something and remember it; to be noticed
examples: He barely registered our presence.
I told her my name, but it obviously didn't register.
He vaguely registered that the women had gone.
Slowly, my mind began to register where I was: in the hospital.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to send something by mail, paying extra money to protect it against loss or damage
examples: Can I register this, please?
a registered letter

definitions.definition: the act of making an official record of something/somebody
examples: the registration of letters and parcels
the registration of students for a course
registration fees
the registration of a child’s birth

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a document showing that an official record has been made of something
examples: COMPARE logbook
my Democratic party registration
the information on the registration roll
I traced my family history using the civil registration records.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the series of letters and numbers that are shown on a number plate at the front and back of a vehicle to identify it
examples: The police are looking for a black car with German registration plates.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the time when a teacher looks at the list of students on the class register and checks that the students are presentWord Origin
examples: mid 16th cent.: from medieval Latin registratio(n-), based on Latin regerere ‘enter, record’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to feel sorry about something you have done or about something that you have not been able to do
examples: If you don't do it now, you'll only regret it.
The decision could be one he lives to regret.
I soon came to regret my action.
‘I've had a wonderful life,’ she said, ‘I don't regret a thing.’
She regretted the words the moment they were out of her mouth.
He bitterly regretted ever having mentioned it.
I never regretted dropping out of college.
I deeply regret what I said.
I regret that I never got to meet him in person.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say in a polite or formal way that you are sorry or sad about a situation
examples: The airline regrets any inconvenience.
The president said that his country deeply regretted the incident.
The United States regrets the loss of innocent civilian lives.
I regret that I am unable to accept your kind invitation.
I very much regret that I cannot be with you this evening.
We regret to inform you that your application has not been successful.
I regret to say that we cannot let you have the picture.
It is to be regretted that so many young people leave school without qualifications.
