definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: following a pattern, especially with the same time or space in between each thing and the next
examples: OPPOSITE irregular
regular breathing
a regular pulse/heartbeat
A light flashed at regular intervals.
There is a regular bus service to the airport.
regular meetings/visits
We also hold a regular monthly meeting.
The equipment is checked on a regular basis.
She writes a regular column for a national newspaper.
a regular geometric pattern

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: done or happening often
examples: OPPOSITE irregular
Do you take regular exercise?
I'm still in regular contact with friends I met at university.
Domestic violence is a regular occurrence in some families.
a painter whose work is a regular feature of the Summer Exhibition
The key to good anti-virus software is regular updates.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: doing the same thing or going to the same place often
examples: regular readers/customers/users
She is a regular contributor to many journals and magazines
regular offenders (= against the law)
He was a regular visitor to her house.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: changing their form in the same way as most other verbs and nouns
examples: OPPOSITE irregular
The past participle of regular verbs ends in ‘-ed’.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: usual
examples: I couldn't see my regular doctor today.
On Monday he would have to return to his regular duties.
It's important to follow the regular procedure.
He was mistaken for one of the regular crew.
the last match of the regular season

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: of a standard size
examples: Regular or large fries?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: ordinary; without any special or extra features
examples: Do you want regular or diet cola?
I just want to buy a regular white shirt—nothing fancy.
He's just a regular guy who loves his dog.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: having an even shape
examples: OPPOSITE irregular
a face with regular features
He flashed a smile, showing two rows of white, regular teeth.
Her face was perfectly regular.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: lasting or happening over a long period
examples: The need to earn a regular income restricted the time he could spend pursuing his real interests.
She couldn't find any regular employment.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: belonging to or connected with the permanent armed forces or police force of a country
examples: OPPOSITE irregular
the regular army
regular soldiers

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used for emphasis to show that somebody/something is an exact or clear example of the thing mentioned
examples: The whole thing was a regular disaster.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: very regularly; happening at the same time in the same way
examples: He is home by six every day, regular as clockwork.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at regular intervals or times
examples: We meet regularly to discuss the progress of the project.
the introduction of direct, regularly scheduled flights to Beijing
The water in the fish tank should be changed regularly.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: often
examples: I go there quite regularly.
He admitted that he regularly used drugs.
The couple regularly attended Mass.
As Home Secretary he had regularly visited Belfast.
She appeared regularly at the Metropolitan Opera.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in an even or balanced way
examples: The plants were spaced regularly, about 50 cm apart.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to control something by means of rules
examples: The department is responsible for regulating the insurance industry.
The activities of credit companies are regulated by law.
The government accepts whaling in principle as long as it is carefully regulated.
It is up to the regulating authority to put the measures into effect.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to control the speed, pressure, temperature, etc. in a machine or system
examples: This valve regulates the flow of water.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an official rule made by a government or some other authority
examples: too many rules and regulations
fire/building regulations
the strict regulations governing the sale of weapons
To comply with government hygiene regulations, there must be a separate sink for hand washing.
It's against safety regulations to fix these doors open.
Under the new regulations spending on office equipment will be strictly controlled.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: controlling something by means of rules
examples: SEE ALSO self-regulation
the voluntary regulation of the press

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or an organization that officially controls an area of business or industry and makes sure that it is operating fairly
examples: Ofgas, the gas industry regulator
banking regulators

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a device that controls something such as speed, temperature or pressure
examples: a pressure regulator

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having the power to control an area of business or industry and make sure that it is operating fairly
examples: regulatory bodies/authorities/agencies
regulatory procedures

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of helping somebody to have a normal, useful life again after they have been very ill or in prison for a long time
examples: a drug rehabilitation centre
the rehabilitation of offenders

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of starting to consider that somebody is good or acceptable after a long period during which they were considered bad or unacceptable
examples: the rehabilitation of Magritte as an artist

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of returning a building, place or area of activity to its previous good condition
examples: the rehabilitation of the steel industry

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the period during which a king, queen, emperor, etc. rules
examples: By the end of his reign, the vast empire was in decline.
The house was built during the reign of Henry VIII.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the period during which somebody is in charge of an organization, a team, etc.
examples: Sir Alex Ferguson's reign at Manchester United
The story only came out during the final days of his reign as Chief Executive.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a feeling, an idea, etc. stronger
examples: The experience reinforced my sense of loss.
Such jokes tend to reinforce racial stereotypes.
The climate of political confusion has only reinforced the country's economic decline.
Success in the talks will reinforce his reputation as an international statesman.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make a structure or material stronger, especially by adding another material to it
examples: All buildings are now reinforced to withstand earthquakes.
reinforced plastic/steel/concrete
The door was built of oak, heavily reinforced with iron.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to send more people or equipment in order to make an army, etc. stronger
examples: The UN has undertaken to reinforce its military presence along the borders.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to refuse to accept or consider something
examples: to reject an argument/a hypothesis/a notion/a plan
to reject a claim/an offer/a request/an application
The bank has the option of accepting or rejecting this offer.
The prime minister rejected any idea of reforming the system.
The proposal was firmly rejected.
School officials flatly rejected the proposal.
All our suggestions were rejected out of hand.
The Government rejected calls for an inquiry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to refuse to accept somebody for a job, position, etc.
examples: Please reject the following candidates…
I've been rejected by all the universities I applied to.
Some applicants were rejected outright.
We considered offering him the job, but finally rejected him.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to decide not to use, sell, publish, etc. something because its quality is not good enough
examples: Imperfect articles are rejected by our quality control.
The book was at first rejected by publishers.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to not accept a new organ after a transplant operation, by producing substances that attack the organ
examples: Her body has already rejected two kidneys.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to fail to give a person or an animal enough love or care
examples: The lioness rejected the smallest cub, which died.
When her husband left home she felt rejected and useless.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of refusing to accept or consider something
examples: Her proposal met with unanimous rejection.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of refusing to accept somebody for a job, position, etc.
examples: a rejection letter (= a letter in which you are told, for example, that you have not been accepted for a job)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the decision not to use, sell, publish, etc. something because its quality is not good enough
examples: I've had letters of rejection from several publishers.
Everyone from George Orwell to J. K. Rowling has had rejection slips (= formal notice from a publisher that a book, etc. is rejected).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the failure of somebody's body to accept a new organ after a transplant operation
examples: He had a second lung transplant after rejection of the first.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: failure to give a person or an animal enough love or care
examples: painful feelings of rejection

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: show or make a connection between two or more things
examples: SYNONYM connect
I found it difficult to relate the two ideas in my mind.
In the future, pay increases will be related to productivity.
Attempts to relate studies on animals to those on humans are not really comparing like with like.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give a spoken or written report of something; to tell a story
examples: Then he related a story about his days working in a research laboratory.
She relates her childhood experiences in the first chapters.
He related the facts of the case to journalists.
She related how he had run away from home as a boy.
The story relates that an angel appeared and told him to sing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with something/somebody in some way
examples: OPPOSITE unrelated
The amount of protein you need is directly related to your lifestyle.
Much of the crime in this area is related to drug abuse.
Parental unemployment was not significantly related to youth unemployment for the total sample.
These problems are closely related.
a related issue
a related question/subject/matter
links on the website to related articles
institutions engaged in similar or related activities
education and training and other related topics
In related news, the star was rushed to a Los Angeles hospital on Wednesday night.
He was suffering from a stress-related illness.
These two incidents are closely related to each other.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in the same family
examples: We're distantly related.
Are you related to Margaret?
He claims to be distantly related to the British royal family.
The Logans and the Fishers were related by marriage.
We were closely related by blood.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: belonging to the same group
examples: related species
related languages
The llama is related to the camel.
All the bees in the colony are genetically related.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the way in which two people, groups or countries behave towards each other or deal with each other
examples: SEE ALSO industrial relations
diplomatic/international/foreign relations
US-Chinese relations
teacher-student relations
Relations with neighbouring countries are under strain at present.

I remember thinking what a brilliant idea that was.
I remember reading something in the paper about that.
I remember watching the film on television.
I can still vividly remember my grandfather teaching me to play cards.
I seem to remember the film being genuinely scary.
I can't remember his taking a single day off work.
I remember (that) we used to go and see them most weekends.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to bring back to your mind a fact, piece of information, etc. that you knew
examples: You were going to help me with this. Remember?
If I remember correctly, you were supposed to collect the keys on your way here.
I'm sorry—I can't remember your name.
I can't remember a time when I didn't feel this way.
He couldn't remember the words to any of the songs.
Can you remember how much money we spent?
He was trying to remember where he had parked his car the night before.
Remember that we're going out tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to keep an important fact in your mind
examples: Remember (that) you may feel sleepy after taking the pills.
It is important to remember that exercise and a balanced diet are the foundation of any successful fitness plan.
The thing to remember is that all of this will take time.
You have to remember that he is still recovering from injury.
You need to remember that the court has a very wide discretion in such cases.
It should be remembered that the majority of accidents happen in the home.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to not forget to do something; to actually do what you have to do
examples: Remember to call me when you arrive!
Remember to keep your doors and windows locked—even if you're in the back garden.
Please remember to include a contact telephone number.
I must remember to check which day they are due to start.
Just remember to take your mosquito repellent.
Did you remember your homework (= to bring it)?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to think about somebody with respect, especially when saying a prayer
examples: SYNONYM commemorate
a church service to remember the war dead

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to give money, a present, etc. to somebody/something
examples: My aunt always remembers my birthday (= by sending a card or present).
His grandfather remembered him (= left him money) in his will.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be famous or known for a particular thing that you have done in the past
examples: He is best remembered as the man who brought jazz to England.
She is best remembered for her first book, ‘In the Ditch’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to help somebody remember something, especially something important that they must do
examples: I'm sorry, I've forgotten your name. Can you remind me?
That (= what you have just said, done, etc.) reminds me, I must get some cash.
‘You need to finish that essay.’ ‘Don't remind me (= I don't want to think about it).’
‘Don't forget the camera.’ ‘Remind me about it nearer the time.’
I loved her and wanted to remind her of that.
Your advertisements should remind people of your great location.
Remind me to phone Alan before I go out.
Passengers are reminded that smoking is not allowed on this train.
The paper reminded its readers that 4,500 soldiers were killed on the first day of the Normandy landings.
Members are reminded that the club's annual general meeting will take place on Thursday.
The bathroom mirror constantly reminds me that I am getting old.
He likes to remind everyone that he is a US senator.
I have to keep reminding myself that things could be much worse.
Can someone remind me what I should do next?
‘You had an accident,’ he reminded her.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that makes you think about or remember somebody/something, that you have forgotten or would like to forget
examples: The sheer size of the cathedral is a constant reminder of the power of religion.
The incident served as a timely reminder of just how dangerous mountaineering can be.
The article concludes with a chilling reminder that the disease can strike anyone at any time.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a letter or note informing somebody that they have not done something
examples: If an invoice is not paid within seven days, we automatically send out a reminder.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: far away from places where other people live
examples: SYNONYM isolated
a remote village/island/location/region
a remote community
a remote part of the country
a remote beach
one of the remotest areas of the world
The area is remote, mountainous, and roadless.
The site is remote from major population centres.
The farmhouse is remote from any other buildings.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: far away in time
examples: SYNONYM distant
in the remote past/future
a remote ancestor (= who lived a long time ago)
There are many facts about the remote past and the remote future that we cannot know.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not closely related
examples: SYNONYM distant
a remote cousin

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: that you can connect to from far away, using an electronic link
examples: a remote terminal/database/server

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: very different from something
examples: His theories are somewhat remote from reality.
A novel should not be too remote from the experiences of its readers.
Jane felt remote from what was going on around her.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not very friendly or interested in other people
examples: SYNONYM aloof
When he spoke, his voice was cold and remote.
He somehow remains a remote figure.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not very great
examples: SYNONYM slight
There is still a remote chance that they will find her alive.
I don't have the remotest idea what you're talking about.
At that time, a new school building was just a remote dream.
a fairly remote possibility

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of taking somebody/something away from a particular place
examples: Clearance of the site required the removal of a number of trees.
the removal of a tumour
Allegations of abuse led to the removal of several children from their families.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of getting rid of something
examples: stain removal
the removal of trade barriers

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of dismissing somebody from their job
examples: SYNONYM dismissal
events leading to the removal of the president from office

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an act of taking furniture, etc. from one house to another
examples: house removals
a removal company/firm
When are the removal men coming?
the collection's temporary removal to storage

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take somebody/something away from a place
examples: Illegally parked vehicles will be removed.
He removed his hand from her shoulder.
Three children were removed from the school for persistent bad behaviour.
Remove the pan from the heat and continue to stir the sauce.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take off clothing, etc. from the body
examples: She removed her glasses and rubbed her eyes.
Passengers no longer have to remove their shoes during security checks.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to get rid of something unpleasant, dirty, etc.; to make something disappear
examples: She has had the tumour removed.
She had surgery to remove the two tumours.
to remove problems/obstacles/objections
Considerable progress has been made in removing barriers to trade within the EU.
The news removed any doubts about the company's future.
This comment has been removed by a moderator.
The police instructed the author to remove the offending material from the website.
She asked for her name to be removed from the list of candidates.
It was impossible to remove the stain from the tablecloth.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to dismiss somebody from their position or job
examples: The elections removed the government from power.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be very different from something; to not be connected with something
examples: Many of these books are far removed from the reality of the children's lives.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: belonging to a different generation
examples: He's my cousin's son so he's my first cousin once removed.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to cause somebody/something to be in a particular state or condition
examples: SYNONYM make
to render something harmless/useless/ineffective
Hundreds of people were rendered homeless by the earthquake.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give somebody something, especially in return for something or because it is expected
examples: They rendered assistance to the disaster victims.
to render a service to somebody
to render somebody a service
It was payment for services rendered.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to present something, especially when it is done officially
examples: SYNONYM furnish
The committee was asked to render a report on the housing situation.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to express or perform something
examples: He stood up and rendered a beautiful version of ‘Summertime’.
The artist has rendered the stormy sea in dark greens and browns.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to express something in a different language
examples: SYNONYM translate
The Italian phrase can be rendered as ‘I did my best’.
It's a concept that is difficult to render into English.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to cover a wall with a layer of plaster or cement

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make fat liquid by heating it; to melt somethingWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French rendre, from an alteration of Latin reddere ‘give back’, from re- ‘back’ + dare ‘give’. The earliest senses were ‘recite’, ‘translate’, and ‘give back’ (hence ‘represent’ and ‘perform’); ‘hand over’ (hence ‘give help’ and ‘submit for consideration’); ‘cause to be’; and ‘melt down’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to begin something again after it stopped or was interrupted
examples: SYNONYM resume
The army renewed its assault on the capital.
We have to renew our efforts to attract young players.
The annual dinner is a chance to renew acquaintance with old friends.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something legally acceptable for a further period of time
examples: to renew a licence/lease/subscription/contract
How do I go about renewing my passport?
I'd like to renew these library books (= arrange to borrow them for a further period of time).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to emphasize something by saying or stating it again
examples: SYNONYM reiterate
to renew an appeal/a request/a complaint
Community leaders have renewed calls for a peaceful settlement.
The project is to go ahead following renewed promises of aid from the UN.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to change something that is old or damaged and replace it with something new of the same kind
examples: The wiring in your house should be renewed every ten to fifteen years.
Our bones normally renew themselves constantly.
The paintwork will need renewing every five years.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: famous and respected
examples: SYNONYM celebrated
a renowned author
We asked for advice from the renowned legal expert, Sam Pincher.
It is renowned as one of the region's best restaurants.
She is renowned for her patience.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of money that you regularly pay so that you can use a house, room, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO ground rent
I earn just about enough to pay the rent.
How much rent do you pay for this place?
The landlord has put the rent up again.
The landlord charged them a month's rent in advance.
a high/low/fair rent
He was evicted for rent arrears.
What's the average rent for homes in your part of town?
The rent on the two-bedroom flat was £250 a week.
The supply of housing at affordable rents became inadequate.
The property is available at a rent of £55,000 per annum.
a rent book (= used to record payments of rent)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the amount of money that you pay to use something for a particular period of time

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a torn place in a piece of material or clothing

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: available to rentWord Origin
examples: noun senses 1 to 2 Middle English: from Old French rente, from a root shared by render. noun sense 3 mid 16th cent.: from obsolete rent ‘pull to pieces, lacerate’, variant of rend.

examples: COMPARE hire
the world’s largest car rental company
a rental car
a minimum rental period of three months

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a house, car or piece of equipment that you can rent
examples: ‘Is this your own car?’ ‘No, it's a rental.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to fix something that is broken, damaged or torn
examples: to repair a car/television
to repair a road/wall/building/bridge
to repair a hole/crack/leak
to repair an injury/a hernia/a tear/a defect
to repair a ligament/tendon/cartilage
He has had surgery to repair the damage.
His surgically repaired knee is bothering him.
It's almost 15 years old. It isn't worth having it repaired.
We need to get the roof repaired.
the budget for maintaining and repairing equipment
The human body has an amazing capacity to repair itself.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say or do something in order to improve a bad or unpleasant situation
examples: SYNONYM right (5)
to repair relations/a relationship
It was too late to repair the damage done to their relationship.
The home team did well to repair a bad start.
They moved quickly to repair relations between themselves and the US.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say or write something again or more than once
examples: to repeat a question/a claim/an assertion/a warning
to repeat a phrase/mantra
She repeated the word several times.
I'm sorry—could you repeat that?
She kept repeating his name softly over and over again.
The opposition have been repeating their calls for the president's resignation.
Are you prepared to repeat these allegations in court?
I mentioned it before, but it bears (= is worth) repeating.
Do say if I'm repeating myself (= if I have already said this).
He's fond of repeating that the company's success is all down to him.
‘Are you really sure?’ she repeated.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something that you have already said
examples: The claims are, I repeat, totally unfounded.
Nor, to repeat, can these changes be avoided.
I am not, repeat not, travelling in the same car as him!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to say something that somebody else has said, especially in order to learn it
examples: The teacher's statement is then repeated by the students.
Listen and repeat each sentence after me.
Can you repeat what I've just said word for word?
‘We were both asleep and didn’t hear anything,’ she repeated.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to tell somebody something that you have heard or been told by somebody else
examples: I don't want you to repeat a word of this to anyone.
The rumour has been widely repeated in the press.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to do or produce something again or more than once
examples: to repeat a mistake/process
to repeat an experiment/exercise
Organizers are hoping to repeat the success of last year's event.
He won his first Monaco Grand Prix in 1994 and repeated the feat in 1995, 1997 and 1999.
The treatment should be repeated every two to three hours.
They are hoping to repeat last year's victory.
These offers are unlikely to be repeated.
The programmes will be repeated next year.
to repeat a class/year/grade (= in a school, to take a class/year/grade again)
Lift and lower the right leg 20 times. Repeat with the left leg.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to happen more than once in the same way
examples: History has a strange way of repeating itself.
This phrase is repeated at intervals throughout the song.
a repeating pattern/design
A single note repeated over and over again, throbbing in my head.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: if food repeats, you can taste it for some time after you have eaten it
examples: Do you find that onions repeat on you?

definitions.definition: to be used instead of somebody/something else; to do something instead of somebody/something else
examples: SYNONYM take over (from something)

to replace a battery/light bulb

definitions.definition: to put something back in the place where it was before
examples: I replaced the cup carefully in the saucer.
to replace the handset (= after using the phone).

replacement windows

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who replaces another person in an organization, especially in their job
examples: We need to find a replacement for Sue.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to take part in a sports event for a particular country, city, etc.
examples: He's been chosen to represent Scotland in next year's World Cup Finals.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be a symbol of something
examples: SYNONYM symbolize
Each colour on the chart represents a different department.
Wind direction is represented by arrows.
The artist uses doves to represent peace.
It is not clear what these symbols were intended to represent.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be something
examples: SYNONYM constitute
This contract represents 20% of the company's annual revenue.
The final figure represents a 12% increase on the number of new jobs created the previous year.
They're investing in low-carbon technologies that represent value for money.
He got rid of anyone who represented a threat to his authority.
This role represents a unique opportunity to further your career in healthcare.
The peace plan represents (= is the result of) weeks of negotiation.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be present in something to a particular degree
examples: Women and men were represented equally on the teams.
Women are disproportionately represented among welfare recipients.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be an example or expression of something
examples: SYNONYM be typical of
The project represents all that is good in the community.
Those comments do not represent the views of us all.
The book purported to represent the lives of ordinary people.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to show somebody/something, especially in a picture
examples: SYNONYM depict
The carvings represent a hunting scene.
The map represents Italy in the 12th century.
The results are represented in fig.3 below.
The Egyptian goddess is represented as a woman with cow's horns.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to present or describe somebody/something in a particular way, especially when this may not be fair
examples: The king is represented as a villain in the play.
The risks were represented as negligible.
The film represents women as victims.
The film accurately represents the atmosphere of the post-war period.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make a formal statement to somebody in authority to make your opinions known or to protest
examples: They represented their concerns to the authorities.
He admitted falsely representing to police officers that the car had been stolen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of presenting somebody/something in a particular way; something that shows or describes something
examples: SYNONYM portrayal
the negative representation of single mothers in the media
The snake swallowing its tail is a representation of infinity.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of having representatives who will speak or vote for you or act in your place
examples: SEE ALSO proportional representation
The green movement lacks effective representation in Parliament.
The accused was not allowed legal representation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: formal statements made to somebody in authority, especially in order to make your opinions known or to protest
examples: We have made representations to the prime minister, but without success.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who has been chosen to speak or vote for somebody else or for a group of people, or to take the place of somebody else
examples: Our elected representatives in government should be doing something about this.
Management are obliged to consult with union representatives about changes to conditions.
The actor's legal representatives have strongly denied the allegations.
He was the Queen's representative at the ceremony.
a representative of the UN
The committee includes representatives from industry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who works for a company and travels around selling its products
examples: a sales representative
She's our representative in France.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is typical of a particular group
examples: The singer is regarded as a representative of the youth of her generation.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (in the US) a member of the House of Representatives, the Lower House of Congress; a member of the House of Representatives in the lower house of a state parliamentWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French representatif, -ive or medieval Latin repraesentativus, from the verb repraesentare ‘exhibit’, from re- (expressing intensive force) + praesentare ‘to present’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a copy of a picture, piece of text, etc.
examples: It is illegal to reproduce these worksheets without permission from the publisher.
The photocopier reproduces colours very well.
This material can be reproduced without payment.
All illustrations are reproduced by kind permission of the Mercury Gallery.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to produce something very similar to something else in a different medium or context; to make something happen again in the same way
examples: The atmosphere of the novel is successfully reproduced in the movie.
Unfortunately, he was never able to reproduce this level of performance in a competition.
I was able to reproduce the same results with subsequent tests.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if people, plants, animals, etc. reproduce or reproduce themselves, they produce young
examples: Most reptiles reproduce by laying eggs on land.
cells reproducing themselves (= making new ones)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act or process of producing babies, young animals or plants
examples: sexual reproduction
They are studying reproduction in shellfish.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act or process of producing copies of a document, book, picture, etc.
examples: Use a black pen on white paper to ensure good reproduction.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of recorded sound
examples: Digital recording gives excellent sound reproduction.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a thing that has been reproduced, especially a copy of a work of art
examples: They have a catalogue with colour reproductions of the paintings for sale.
reproduction furniture (= furniture made as a copy of an earlier style)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a country that is governed by a president and politicians elected by the people and where there is no king or queen
examples: SEE ALSO banana republic
newly independent republics
Mary McAleese has been the President of the Republic of Ireland since 1997.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the opinion that people have about what somebody/something is like, based on what has happened in the past
examples: to have a good/bad reputation
to build/earn a reputation
She soon established a reputation as a first-class cook.
The company enjoys an international reputation for quality of design.
a politician with a reputation for honesty
I'm aware of Mark's reputation for being late.
He has the reputation of being a hard worker.
to damage/tarnish/ruin somebody’s reputation
The weather in England is living up to its reputation (= is exactly as expected).
She is, by reputation, very difficult to please.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the action of asking for something formally and politely; a thing that you formally ask for
examples: a request for information
They made a request for further aid.
He submitted a request to adopt a flexible working routine.
to grant a request
to refuse/decline/reject/deny a request
She went to the wedding at her mother's request (= because her mother had asked her to go).
He was there at the request of his manager (= because his manager had asked him to go).
The writer's name was withheld by request (= because the writer asked for this to be done).
Application forms are available on request.
She left her address with a request that any mail should be sent on to her.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an instruction to a computer to perform a task
examples: When the software has finished processing the request, a download window pops up.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a song or tune that somebody asks to have played on a radio programme
examples: The next request is from a listener in Aberdeen.
a radio request programme

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to need something; to depend on somebody/something
examples: These pets require a lot of care and attention.
Deciphering the code requires an expert.
This condition requires urgent treatment.
Do you require anything else? (= in a shop/store, for example)
These plants absolutely require shade.
True marriage requires us to show trust and loyalty.
The situation required that he be present.
The situation required that he should be present.
Lentils do not require soaking before cooking.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody do or have something, especially because it is necessary according to a particular law or set of rules
examples: I just require a signature on the form.
The wearing of seat belts is required by law.
‘Hamlet’ is required reading (= must be read) for this course.
Several students failed to reach the required standard.
What exactly is required of a receptionist (= what are they expected to do)?
All candidates will be required to take a short test.
All adults are legally required to pay the tax.
We require that you comply with the following rules:…
The law requires that everyone wear a seat belt.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that you need or want
examples: the basic requirements of life
a software solution to meet your requirements
All products can be customized to suit your specific requirements.
Our immediate requirement is extra staff.
These goods are surplus to requirements (= more than we need).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that you must have in order to do something else
examples: to meet/fulfil/satisfy the requirements
What is the minimum entry requirement for this course?
Banks now face stricter regulatory requirements.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to save somebody/something from a dangerous or harmful situation
examples: The coastguard rescued six people from the sinking boat.
The woman was rescued from her burning home by firefighters.
You rescued me from an embarrassing situation.
The house was rescued from demolition.
He rescued a child from drowning.
The hostages were rescued and brought to safety.
The shelter rescues stray dogs.
She had despaired of ever being rescued alive.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a careful study of a subject, especially in order to discover new facts or information about it
examples: SEE ALSO action research
scientific/medical/academic research
They are raising money for cancer research.
to do/conduct/undertake research
I've done some research to find out the cheapest way of travelling there.
He has carried out extensive research into renewable energy sources.
Recent research on deaf children has produced some interesting findings about their speech.
Research on animals has led to some important medical advances.
According to recent research, more people are going to the movies than ever before.
Their latest research project will be funded by the government.
Are you hoping to get a research grant?
a research fellow/assistant/scientist
a research institute/centre/laboratory
The research findings were published in the Journal of Environmental Quality.

researchers in psychology

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to look like or be similar to another person or thing
examples: She closely resembles her sister.
So many hotels resemble each other.
The plant resembles grass in appearance.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an arrangement for a seat on a plane or train, a room in a hotel, etc. to be kept for you
examples: COMPARE booking
I'll call the restaurant and make a reservation.
We have a reservation in the name of Grant.
I had to cancel my hotel reservation.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a feeling of doubt about a plan or an idea
examples: SYNONYM misgiving
I have serious reservations about his ability to do the job.
They support the measures without reservation (= completely).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an area of land in the US that is kept separate for Native Americans to live in

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (in India) the policy of keeping a fixed number of jobs or places in schools, colleges, etc. for people who are members of scheduled castes, scheduled tribes or other backward classesWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (denoting the Pope's right of nomination to a benefice): from Old French, or from late Latin reservatio(n-), from reservare ‘keep back’, ‘keep back’, from re- ‘back’ + servare ‘to keep’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a supply of something that is available to be used in the future or when it is needed
examples: SEE ALSO gold reserve
cash/foreign currency reserves
large oil and gas reserves
reserve funds
He discovered unexpected reserves of strength.
The country has the world's largest reserves of coal.
The company has substantial reserves of capital.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of land that is a protected area for animals, plants, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO game reserve
a wildlife/forest reserve

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an area of land in the US that is kept separate for Native Americans to live in

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the quality that somebody has when they do not talk easily to other people about their ideas, feelings, etc.
examples: SYNONYM reticence
She found it difficult to make friends because of her natural reserve.
Jaime always talked to people without reserve.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a feeling that you do not want to accept or agree to something, etc. until you are quite sure that it is all right to do so
examples: Any contract should be treated with reserve until it has been checked.
She trusted him without reserve (= completely).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an extra player who plays in a team when one of the other players is injured or not available to play

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a team that is below the level of the main team

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: an extra military force, etc. that is not part of a country’s regular forces, but is available to be used when needed
examples: the Army Reserve
the reserve police

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: the lowest price that somebody will accept for something, especially something that is sold at an auction
examples: The painting failed to reach to its reserve and was withdrawn from the sale.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: available to be used in the future or when needed
examples: The money was being kept in reserve for their retirement.
200 police officers were held in reserve.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to live in a particular place
examples: He returned to Britain in 1939, having resided abroad for many years.
Their passports do not give them the right to reside in Britain.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a house, especially a large or impressive one
examples: a desirable family residence for sale (= for example, in an advertisement)
10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister’s official residence.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of living in a particular place
examples: SEE ALSO hall of residence
They were not able to take up residence in their new home until the spring.
Please state your occupation and place of residence.
The flag flies when the Queen is in residence.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: permission to live in a country that is not your own
examples: They have been denied residence in this country.
a residence permit

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: having an official position in a particular place such as a college or university
examples: creative writing classes given by the writer in residence

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who lives in a particular place or who has their home there
examples: SEE ALSO permanent resident
a resident of the United States
The proposals sparked concern among local residents.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who is staying in a hotel
examples: The hotel restaurant is open to non-residents.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a doctor working in a hospital in the US who is receiving special advanced training
examples: COMPARE registrar

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: COMPARE registrar

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: suitable for living in; consisting of houses rather than factories or offices
examples: a quiet residential area

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: requiring a person to live at a particular place; offering living accommodation
examples: a residential language course
a residential home for the elderly
residential care for children

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small amount of something that remains at the end of a process
examples: pesticide residues in fruit and vegetables

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the part of the money, property, etc. of a person who has died that remains after all the debts, gifts, etc. have been paid
examples: The residue of the estate was divided equally among his children.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to officially tell somebody that you are leaving your job, an organization, etc.
examples: She was forced to resign due to ill health.
He resigned as manager after eight years.
Two members resigned from the board in protest.
Some judges have threatened to resign over this issue.
My father resigned his directorship last year.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of giving up your job or position; the occasion when you do this
examples: a letter of resignation
There were calls for her resignation from the board of directors.
Further resignations are expected.
The defeat led to his resignation as team manager.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a letter, for example to your employers, to say that you are giving up your job or position
examples: to offer/hand in/tender your resignation
We haven't received his resignation yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of being willing to accept a difficult or unpleasant situation that you cannot change
examples: They accepted their defeat with resignation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to refuse to accept something and try to stop it from happening
examples: SYNONYM oppose
They are determined to resist pressure to change the law.
People naturally resist change.
The bank strongly resisted cutting interest rates.
Residents who oppose the plans are threatening to resist.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to fight back when attacked; to use force to stop something from happening
examples: He tried to pin me down, but I resisted.
She was charged with resisting arrest.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to stop yourself from having something you like or doing something you very much want to do
examples: I finished the cake. I couldn't resist it.
The Chancellor resisted the temptation to raise business taxes.
I found the temptation to miss the class too hard to resist.
She could hardly resist the urge to turn and run.
He couldn't resist showing off his new car.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to not be harmed or damaged by something
examples: A healthy diet should help your body resist infection.
The castle was built to resist attack.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: dislike of or opposition to a plan, an idea, etc.; the act of refusing to obey
examples: As with all new ideas it met with resistance.
There has been a lot of resistance to this new law.
Resistance to change has nearly destroyed the industry.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of using force to oppose somebody/something
examples: SEE ALSO passive resistance
There were a number of episodes of armed resistance during the early years of occupation.
The defenders put up a strong resistance.
The demonstrators offered little or no resistance to the police.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the power not to be affected by something
examples: AIDS lowers the body's resistance to infection.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a force that stops something moving or makes it move more slowly
examples: wind/air resistance (= in the design of planes or cars)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the opposition of a substance or device to the flow of an electrical current
examples: COMPARE reactance

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a secret organization that resists the authorities, especially in a country that an enemy has control of
examples: resistance fighters

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: (to choose, etc.) the easiest way of doing somethingWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from French résistance, from late Latin resistentia, from the verb resistere ‘hold back’, from re- (expressing opposition) + sistere ‘stop’ (reduplication of stare ‘to stand’).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a definite decision to do or not to do something
examples: Have you made any New Year's resolutions (= for example, to give up smoking from 1 January)?
She made a resolution to visit her relatives more often.
I made a New Year resolution to give up smoking.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a formal statement of an opinion agreed on by a committee or a council, especially by means of a vote
examples: SEE ALSO joint resolution
to pass/adopt/approve a resolution
The UN Security Council unanimously adopted a resolution calling for a halt to hostilities.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of solving or settling a problem, argument, etc.
examples: SYNONYM settlement
dispute/conflict resolution
The government is pressing for an early resolution of the dispute.
Hopes of a peaceful resolution to the conflict were fading.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the quality of being resolute or determined
examples: The reforms owe a great deal to the resolution of one man.
Her resolution never faltered.
She showed great resolution in her dealings with management.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the power of a computer screen, printer, etc. to give a clear image, depending on the size of the dots (= marks) that make up the image
examples: SEE ALSO high-resolution
The graphics look fine, even at low resolution.
The higher the resolution, the sharper the image.
a monitor capable of a 1 024 by 768 pixel resolution

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to find an acceptable solution to a problem or difficulty
examples: SYNONYM settle
to resolve an issue/a dispute/a conflict/a crisis
Attempts are being made to resolve the problem of security in schools.
Both sides met in order to try to resolve their differences.
We hope to resolve the matter as soon as possible.
Everything is being done to resolve the situation.
The dispute has not been fully resolved.
Be patient and the situation may resolve itself.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make a definite decision to do something
examples: He resolved not to tell her the truth.
He resolved to do something to help the children he had met.
She resolved that she would never see him again.
We had resolved on making an early start.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to reach a decision by means of a formal vote
examples: It was resolved that the matter be referred to a higher authority.
They resolved that the matter be referred to a higher authority.
The committee unanimously resolved that the party chairman should step down.
The Supreme Council resolved to resume control over the national press.
The board of directors has called a meeting to resolve on the merger.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a place where a lot of people go on holiday
examples: seaside/mountain resorts
They spent a month at a fashionable ski resort in Switzerland.
a popular tourist resort
a popular holiday resort
the resort town of Byron Bay
destination resorts such as Atlantis in the Bahamas

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of using something, especially something bad or unpleasant, because nothing else is possible
examples: SYNONYM recourse
There are hopes that the conflict can be resolved without resort to violence.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the first or last course of action that you should or can take in a particular situation
examples: Strike action should be regarded as a last resort, when all attempts to negotiate have failed.
In the last resort (= in the end) everyone must decide for themselves.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a supply of something that a country, an organization or a person has and can use, especially to increase their wealth
examples: SEE ALSO human resources
the exploitation of minerals and other natural resources
They promote the use of renewable resources like soybean oil.
water/mineral/energy resources
The school does the best it can with limited resources (= money).
a valuable/precious/scarce resource
Think carefully about how you allocate resources.
We agreed to pool our resources (= so that everyone gives something).
Police have had to devote more resources to these cases.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that can be used to help achieve an aim, especially a book, equipment, etc. that provides information for teachers and students
examples: The website is an invaluable educational resource.
This is an online resource for anyone interested in digital design.
The library is a vast resource for historians of medieval France.
Time is your most valuable resource, especially in examinations.
resource books for teachers
a library resource centre

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: personal qualities such as courage and imagination that help you deal with difficult situations
examples: He has no inner resources and hates being alone.
She is someone of considerable personal resources.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong feeling of approval of somebody/something because of their good qualities or achievements
examples: SEE ALSO self-respect
I have the utmost respect for her and her work.
They feel a deep and mutual respect for each other.
It was a noble effort that deserves respect.
She soon earned the respect of her colleagues.
You did a great job. Respect! (= used to praise somebody)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: polite behaviour towards or care for somebody/something that you think is important
examples: OPPOSITE disrespect
to show a lack of respect for authority
They have a deep respect for the natural world.
He has no respect for her feelings.
Everyone has a right to be treated with respect.
A two-minute silence was held as a mark of respect.
Out of respect for my friend, I didn't say anything.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a particular aspect or detail of something
examples: In this respect we are very fortunate.
This has been a difficult year in many respects.
There was one respect, however, in which they differed.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: about; relating to
examples: A writ was served on the firm in respect of their unpaid bill.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in payment for something
examples: money received in respect of overtime worked

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to visit somebody or to send a message of good wishes as a sign of respect for them
examples: Many came to pay their last respects (= by attending somebody's funeral).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used when you are going to disagree, usually quite strongly, with somebody
examples: With all due respect, the figures simply do not support you on this.
With all due respect, I think you've misunderstood what he said.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: in connection with
examples: The two groups were similar with respect to income and status.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong feeling of approval of somebody/something because of their good qualities or achievements
examples: SEE ALSO self-respect
I have the utmost respect for her and her work.
They feel a deep and mutual respect for each other.
It was a noble effort that deserves respect.
She soon earned the respect of her colleagues.
You did a great job. Respect! (= used to praise somebody)

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: in connection with
examples: The two groups were similar with respect to income and status.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: belonging or relating separately to each of the people or things already mentioned
examples: They are each recognized specialists in their respective fields.
the respective roles of men and women in society

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in the same order as the people or things already mentioned
examples: Julie and Mark, aged 17 and 19 respectively

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to give a spoken or written answer to somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM reply
I asked him his name, but he didn't respond.
The government did not respond to our questions.
She never responded to my letter.
‘I'm not sure,’ she responded.
When asked about the company's future, the director responded that he remained optimistic.
He responded with a question.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to do something as a reaction to something that somebody has said or done
examples: SYNONYM react
How did they respond to the news?
to respond to a call/need/demand
The public is responding positively to these changes.
to respond favourably/enthusiastically
The government responded by banning all future demonstrations.
The audience responded with enthusiasm.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to react quickly or in the correct way to something/somebody
examples: The car responds very well to the controls.
You can rely on him to respond to a challenge.
Our company is small enough to respond quickly.
He tried to move but his body wouldn't respond.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to improve as a result of a particular kind of treatment
examples: The infection did not respond to the drugs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a spoken or written answer
examples: SEE ALSO total physical response
She made no response.
We have asked for a meeting and we are awaiting a response.
I received an immediate response to my request.
Here's a quick response to your question.
I am writing in response to your enquiry.
Jack just nodded in response.
We sent out over 1 000 letters but the response rate has been low (= few people replied).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a reaction to something that has happened or been said
examples: SEE ALSO immune response
The news provoked an angry response.
to elicit/trigger/evoke a response
When I suggested changes, I got a very positive response.
I knocked on the door but there was no response.
There has been little response to our appeal for funds.
The product was developed in response to demand.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a part of a church service that the people sing or speak as an answer to the part that the priest sings or speaks
examples: The congregation sang the responses.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a duty to deal with or take care of somebody/something, so that you may be blamed if something goes wrong
examples: to be in a position of responsibility
It's time for someone to take responsibility and get the job done.
She assumed responsibility for recruitment.
We are recruiting a sales manager with responsibility for the European market.
They have responsibility for ensuring the rules are enforced.
The responsibility for doing this rests with the department managers.
It is their responsibility to ensure the rules are enforced.
parental rights and responsibilities
She is no longer able to fulfil her responsibilities.
I did it on my own responsibility (= without being told to and being willing to take the blame if it had gone wrong).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: blame for something bad that has happened
examples: SEE ALSO diminished responsibility
The bank refuses to accept responsibility for the mistake.
Nobody has claimed responsibility for the bombing.
It is for the court to decide who bears responsibility.
We take full responsibility for any errors in the text.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a moral duty to do something or to help or take care of somebody because of your job, position, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO corporate responsibility
We want to instil a sense of personal responsibility in children.
She feels a strong sense of responsibility towards her employees.
We have a responsibility to our shareholders.
I think we have a moral responsibility to help these countries.
The media has abdicated its reponsibility to report the facts.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having the job or duty of doing something or taking care of somebody/something, so that you may be blamed if something goes wrong
examples: Mike is responsible for designing the entire project.
Even where parents no longer live together, they each continue to be responsible for their children.
The management team is directly responsible for the day-to-day operations of the company.
I'd like to talk to whoever is responsible here.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: being able to be blamed for something
examples: Who's responsible for this mess?
He is mentally ill and cannot be held responsible for his actions.
We will ensure that anyone found responsible for the accident is held accountable.
Everything will be done to bring those responsible to justice.
You mustn't feel responsible in any way.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: being the cause of something
examples: Cigarette smoking is responsible for about 90 per cent of deaths from lung cancer.
He believes that man-made carbon dioxide is directly responsible for global warming.
Hormonal changes may be partly responsible for these mood swings.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: that you can trust and rely on
examples: SYNONYM conscientious
The child should be accompanied by a parent or other responsible adult.
We need to teach our children to act as responsible citizens.
the importance of using medicines in a responsible manner
Clare has a mature and responsible attitude to work.
The firm specializes in socially responsible investments.
They are not very responsible with money.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: needing somebody who can be trusted and relied on; involving important duties
examples: a responsible position

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: having to report to somebody/something with authority or in a higher position and explain to them what you have done
examples: The Council of Ministers is responsible to the Assembly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the part of something that remains
examples: Take what you want and throw the rest away.
The country enjoys friendly relations with the rest of the world.
How would you like to spend the rest of the day?
I'm not doing this job for the rest of my life.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the people or things that remain; the others
examples: The first question was difficult, but the rest were pretty easy.
Don't blame Alex. He's human, like the rest of us.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a period of relaxing, sleeping or doing nothing after a period of activity
examples: SEE ALSO bed rest
I had a good night's rest.
We stopped for a well-earned rest.
to have/take a rest from all your hard work
Try to get some rest—you have a busy day tomorrow.
There are no matches tomorrow, which is a rest day, but the tournament resumes on Monday.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an object that is used to support or hold something
examples: an armrest (= for example on a seat or chair)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a period of silence between notes; a sign that shows a rest between notes

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used at the end of a list to mean everything else that you might expect to be on the list
examples: He wants a big house and an expensive car and all the rest of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that the actual amount or number of something is much higher than somebody has stated
examples: ‘It cost 250 pounds…’ ‘And the rest, and the rest!’

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: not moving
examples: At rest the insect looks like a dead leaf.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: dead and therefore free from trouble or worry. People say ‘at rest’ to avoid saying ‘dead’.
examples: She now lies at rest in the churchyard.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to stop moving
examples: The car crashed through the barrier and came to rest in a field.
His eyes came to rest on Clara's face.
The ball rolled down the hill and came to rest against a tree.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: apart from that; considering other matters
examples: The book has some interesting passages about the author's childhood. For the rest, it is extremely dull.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to stop talking about something because they are annoying you
examples: Give it a rest! You’ve been complaining all day.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to stop doing something for a while

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to bury somebody. People say ‘to lay somebody to rest’ to avoid saying ‘to bury’ somebody.
examples: George was laid to rest beside his parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to stop something by showing it is not true
examples: The announcement finally laid all the speculation about their future to rest.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used when somebody is complaining that they have a lot of work to do

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to do or say something to make somebody stop worrying about something
examples: SYNONYM reassure

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used when you are telling a story to say that you do not need to tell the end of it, because everyone knows it alreadyWord Origin
examples: noun senses 3 to 5 Old English ræst, rest (noun), ræstan, restan (verb), of Germanic origin, from a root meaning ‘league’ or ‘mile’ (referring to a distance after which one rests). noun senses 1 to 2 late Middle English: from Old French reste (noun), rester (verb), from Latin restare ‘remain’, from re- ‘back’ + stare ‘to stand’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a place where you can buy and eat a meal
examples: COMPARE cafe
We're going to try this Italian restaurant that just opened.
They stopped at a fast-food restaurant on the way to the concert.
We had a meal in a restaurant.
We went to my favourite restaurant to celebrate.
a restaurant chain/owner

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the work of repairing and cleaning an old building, a painting, etc. so that its condition is as good as it originally was
examples: restoration work
The palace is closed for restoration.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of bringing back a system, a law, etc. that existed previously
examples: the restoration of diplomatic relations between the two countries
the restoration of democracy/the monarchy

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of returning something to its correct place, condition or owner
examples: the restoration of the Elgin marbles to Greece

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the time in Britain after 1660 when, following a period with no king or queen, Charles II became king
examples: Restoration comedy/poetry (= written during and after this time)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to bring back a situation or feeling that existed before
examples: The measures are intended to restore public confidence in the economy.
Order was quickly restored after the riots.
Such kindness restores your faith in human nature (= makes you believe most people are kind).
The operation restored his sight (= made him able to see again).
Peace has now been restored to the area.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to bring somebody/something back to a former condition, place or position
examples: He is now fully restored to health.
We hope to restore the garden to its former glory (= make it as beautiful as it used to be).
This cream claims to restore your skin to its youthful condition.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to repair a building, work of art, piece of furniture, etc. so that it looks as good as it did originally
examples: Her job is restoring old paintings.
The house has been lovingly restored to the way it looked in 1900 when it was built.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to bring a law, tradition, way of working, etc. back into use
examples: SYNONYM reintroduce
to restore ancient traditions
Some people argue that the death penalty should be restored.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to give something that was lost or stolen back to somebody
examples: The police have now restored the painting to its rightful owner.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a rule, a fact, an idea, etc. that limits or controls what people can do
examples: The government has imposed export restraints on some products.
social restraints on drinking alcohol

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of controlling or limiting something because it is necessary or sensible to do so
examples: The unions are unlikely to accept any sort of wage restraint.
They said that they would fight without restraint (= completely freely) for what they wanted.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of behaving calmly and with control
examples: SYNONYM self-control
The police appealed to the crowd for restraint.
He exercised considerable restraint in ignoring the insults.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the use of physical force to control somebody who is behaving in a violent way
examples: the physical restraint of prisoners

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a type of seat belt or safety device
examples: Children must use an approved child restraint or adult seat belt.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to limit the size, amount or range of something
examples: Speed is restricted to 30 mph in towns.
We restrict the number of students per class to ten.
Fog severely restricted visibility.
Having small children tends to restrict your freedom.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop somebody/something from moving or acting freely
examples: SYNONYM impede
The long skirt restricted her movements.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to control something with rules or laws
examples: Access to the club is restricted to members only.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to allow yourself or somebody to have only a limited amount of something or to do only a particular kind of activity
examples: I restrict myself to one cup of coffee a day.
Why don't you restrict yourself to setting down the facts?
I'm restricting myself to one glass of wine a day.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a rule or law that limits what you can do or what can happen
examples: import/speed/travel restrictions
to impose/place a restriction on something
The government has agreed to lift restrictions on press freedom.
There are no restrictions on the amount of money you can withdraw.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of limiting or controlling somebody/something
examples: sports clothes that prevent any restriction of movement
A diet to lose weight relies on calorie restriction in order to obtain results.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a thing that limits the amount of freedom you have
examples: the restrictions of a prison

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that is caused or produced because of something else
examples: And did your intervention produce the desired result?
to yield/achieve a result
The company's failure was a direct result of bad management.
This book is the result of 25 years of research.
The end result (= the final one) of her hard work was a place at medical school.
He made one big mistake, and, as a result, lost his job.
She died as a result of her injuries.
The farm was flooded, with the result that the crop was lost.
He decided to get involved, with disastrous results.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the final score or the name of the winner in a sports event, competition, election, etc.
examples: the election results
The announcer was reading out the football results.
They will announce the result of the vote tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a victory or a success
examples: We badly need to get a result from this match.
This was a great result for us.
He left. Result! (= used when you are happy something has happened)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the mark or grade you get in an exam or in a number of exams
examples: Have you had your results yet?
When do you get your exam results?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the information that you get from a scientific test or piece of research
examples: Other research has yielded similar results.
The doctor will explain your blood test results.
a positive/negative test result
the results of a study
The results of our experiment indicate that environmental factors play a part.
The results obtained were compared with previous results.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the information that you get from a computer search
examples: My search produced several thousand results.
The user can control how the search results are displayed.
the first page of search results

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: things that are achieved successfully
examples: The project is beginning to show results.
a coach who knows how to get results from his players
For best results, defrost fully before use.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the amount of profit or loss made by a business over a particular period of time
examples: Companies are required by law to report their financial results on a quarterly basis.
The company will publish its interim results (= before the final results are known) on Monday.
The corporation is expected to announce improved results for the last quarter.
