definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if you resume an activity, or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after being interrupted
examples: to resume talks/negotiations
She resumed her career after an interval of six years.
The noise resumed, louder than before.
There is no sign of the peace talks resuming.
He got back in the car and resumed driving.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to go back to the seat or place that you had before
examples: He resumed his seat opposite her.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to keep something; to continue to have something
examples: SYNONYM preserve
to retain your independence
He struggled to retain control of the situation.
The house retains much of its original charm.
She retained her tennis title for the third year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to continue to hold or contain something
examples: These plants will need a soil that retains moisture during the summer months.
This information is no longer retained within the computer's main memory.
She has a good memory and finds it easy to retain facts.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: if a member of the public retains somebody such as a lawyer, he or she pays money regularly or in advance so the lawyer, etc. will do work for him or her
examples: You will be paid a retaining fee.
You will need to retain the services of a lawyer.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to leave your job and stop working, especially because you have reached a particular age or because you are ill; to tell somebody they must stop doing their job
examples: He is retiring next year after 30 years with the company.
The company's official retiring age is 65.
Lots of teachers like me expected to retire on a full pension.
She was forced to retire early from teaching because of ill health.
She retired from politics after her second term in office.
My dream is to retire to a villa in France.
He has no plans to retire as editor of the magazine.
She was retired on medical grounds.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to stop competing during a game, race, etc., usually because you are injured
examples: She fell badly, spraining her ankle, and had to retire.
He retired hurt in the first five minutes of the game.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to leave a place, especially to go somewhere quieter or more private
examples: The jury retired to consider the evidence.
After dinner he likes to retire to his study.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to move back from a battle in order to organize your soldiers in a different way

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to go to bed
examples: I retired late that evening.
to retire to bed/for the night

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make a player or team have to stop their turn at batting
examples: He retired twelve batters in a row.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having retired from work
examples: a retired doctor/teacher/officer/general
He is a recently retired judge.
Dad is retired now.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the fact of stopping work because you have reached a particular age; the time when you do this
examples: At 60, he was now approaching retirement.
Susan is going to take early retirement (= retire before the usual age).
retirement age
This year we have seen the retirements of several senior personnel.
a retirement pension

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the period of your life after you have stopped work at a particular age
examples: He provided for a comfortable retirement by selling the business.
We all wish you a long and happy retirement.
Up to a third of one's life is now being spent in retirement.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of stopping a particular type of work, especially in sport, politics, etc.; the period of your life after a career in sport, politics, etc.
examples: He announced his retirement from football.
She came out of retirement to win two gold medals at the championships.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a movement away from a place or an enemy because of danger or defeat
examples: Napoleon’s retreat from Moscow
The army was in full retreat (= retreating very quickly).
to sound the retreat (= to give a loud signal for an army to move away)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an act of trying to escape from a particular situation to one that you think is safer or more pleasant
examples: SYNONYM escape
Is watching television a retreat from reality?
her retreat into a fantasy world of her own

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an act of changing a decision because of criticism or because a situation has become too difficult
examples: The Senator made an embarrassing retreat from his earlier position.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a quiet, private place that you go to in order to get away from your usual life
examples: a country retreat

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a period of time when somebody stops their usual activities and goes to a quiet place for prayer and thought; an organized event when people can do this
examples: He went into retreat and tried to resolve the conflicts within himself.
He went on a Buddhist retreat.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to go away or back quickly, especially to avoid something unpleasant
examples: I decided to beat a hasty retreat.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a movement away from a place or an enemy because of danger or defeat
examples: Napoleon’s retreat from Moscow
The army was in full retreat (= retreating very quickly).
to sound the retreat (= to give a loud signal for an army to move away)

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: SYNONYM escape

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to bring or get something back, especially from a place where it should not be
examples: SYNONYM recover
She bent to retrieve her comb from the floor.
The dog retrieved the ball from the water.
The police have managed to retrieve some of the stolen money.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to find and get back data or information that has been stored in the memory of a computer
examples: to retrieve information from the database
The program allows you to retrieve items quickly by searching under a keyword.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a bad situation better; to get back something that was lost
examples: You can only retrieve the situation by apologizing.
Employers are anxious to retrieve the investment they have made in training their employees.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to come or go back from one place to another
examples: I waited a long time for him to return.
returning emigrants/exiles/refugees (= who are coming home after being away)
She's returning to Australia tomorrow after six months in Europe.
He had recently returned to this country after living in Spain.
I had to return to the store to look for my purse.
I returned from work to find the house empty.
People were returning home for the weekend.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to bring, give, put or send something back to somebody/something
examples: We had to return the hairdryer to the store because it was faulty.
I must return some books to the library.
The court ordered him to return the children to their mother.
Completed questionnaires should be returned to this address.
He refused to return our money.
I returned the letter unopened.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to come back again
examples: SYNONYM reappear
The following day the pain returned.
There's a chance the cancer will return.
Confidence returned and prices started to rise.
The bad weather has returned with a vengeance.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to start discussing a subject you were discussing earlier, or doing an activity you were doing earlier
examples: He returns to this topic later in the report.
She looked up briefly then returned to her sewing.
The doctor may allow her to return to work next week.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to go back to a previous state
examples: Train services have returned to normal after the strike.
The land has returned to its natural state.
Many find returning to civilian life difficult.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to do or give something to somebody because they have done or given the same to you first; to have the same feeling about somebody that they have about you
examples: to return a smile/gaze/greeting
If you assist people when they ask for help, it is more likely they will return the favour.
She phoned him several times but he was too busy to return her call.
It's time we returned their invitation (= invite them to something as they invited us first).
You were both wonderful!’ ‘So were you!’ we said, returning the compliment.
to return a kiss (= to kiss somebody with the same enthusiasm with which they kiss you)
He did not return her love.
to return fire (= to shoot at somebody who is shooting at you)

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to hit the ball back to your opponent during a game
examples: to return a service/shot

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to give a decision about something in court
examples: The jury returned a verdict of not guilty.
The inquest returned a verdict of accidental death.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to elect somebody to a political position
examples: She was returned as MP for Edgbaston in the last election.
He was returned to Parliament with an increased majority.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to give or produce a particular amount of money as a profit or loss
examples: to return a high rate of interest
Last year the company returned a loss of £157 million.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make something known to somebody
examples: SYNONYM disclose
to reveal a secret
Her expression revealed nothing.
A series of flashbacks reveal the details of the tragedy.
The identity of the buyer has not been revealed.
The survey reveals some worrying statistics.
The doctors did not reveal the truth to him.
The report reveals that the company made a loss of £20 million last year.
It was revealed that important evidence had been suppressed.
Officers could not reveal how he died.
Salted peanuts were recently revealed to be the nation's favourite snack.
He has been revealed as a traitor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to show something that previously could not be seen
examples: SYNONYM display
He laughed, revealing a line of white teeth.
The door opened to reveal a cosy little room.
X-rays revealed a fracture.
Excavations at these sites have revealed impressive stone structures.
She crouched in the dark, too frightened to reveal herself.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a fact that people are made aware of, especially one that has been secret and is surprising
examples: SYNONYM disclosure
startling/sensational revelations about her private life
He was dismissed after revelations that confidential files were missing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of making people aware of something that has been secret
examples: SYNONYM disclosure
The company's financial problems followed the revelation of a major fraud scandal.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that is considered to be a sign or message from God
examples: These events were seen as a divine revelation.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be a completely new or surprising experience; to be different from what was expected
examples: His performance in the race today was a revelation to everyone.
My trip to Texas was a revelation.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that you do in order to make somebody suffer because they have made you suffer
examples: She is seeking revenge for the murder of her husband.
The bombing was an act of revenge for the shooting of two young boys.
The bombing was in revenge for the assassination.
He swore to take (his) revenge on his political enemies.
revenge attacks/killings

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the defeat of a person or team that defeated you in a previous game
examples: The team wanted to get revenge for their defeat earlier in the season.
This was sweet revenge for our defeat earlier in the season.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the money that a government receives from taxes or that an organization, etc. receives from its business
examples: SYNONYM receipt
The government is currently facing a shortfall in tax revenue.
Advertising revenue finances the commercial television channels.
a slump in oil revenues
The company's annual revenues rose by 30%.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to change something completely so that it is the opposite of what it was before
examples: Falling birth rates may reverse the trend towards early retirement.
to reverse a procedure/process
The government has failed to reverse the economic decline.
It is sometimes possible to arrest or reverse the disease.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to change a previous decision, law, etc. to the opposite one
examples: SYNONYM revoke
The Court of Appeal reversed the decision.
The policy is likely to be reversed if there is a change of government.
to reverse a judgement

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to turn something the opposite way around or change the order of something around
examples: Writing is reversed in a mirror.
You should reverse the order of these pages.
To solve the puzzle, simply reverse the order of the numbers.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to exchange the positions or functions of two things
examples: It felt as if we had reversed our roles of parent and child.
She used to work for me, but our situations are now reversed.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to admit you were wrong or to stop having a particular position in an argument
examples: He has reversed himself on a dozen issues.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: when a vehicle or its driver reverses or the driver reverses a vehicle, the vehicle goes backwards
examples: COMPARE back
He reversed around the corner.
She reversed into a parking space.
Caution! This truck is reversing.
Now reverse the car.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make a phone call that will be paid for by the person you are calling, not by you
examples: I want to reverse the charges, please.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a report in a newspaper or magazine, or on the internet, television or radio, in which somebody gives their opinion of a book, play, film, product, etc.; the act of writing this kind of report
examples: SEE ALSO rave review
a book review
She gave the film a glowing review.
mixed/negative/bad reviews
a positive/favourable review
an online review of the restaurant
He submitted his latest novel for review.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an act of looking again at something you have studied or written, especially in order to prepare for an exam
examples: We need to do the review for the test tomorrow.
I should have time for a quick review of my notes before the test.
We'll have time at the end of class for review.
There is a grammar review section at the end of each unit.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an examination of something, with the intention of changing it if necessary
examples: SEE ALSO judicial review
The government has embarked on a systematic review of transport policy.
MPS have called for an independent review.
The proposals are available for review online.
The terms of the contract are under review.
His parole application is up for review next week.
a review board/panel
a pay/salary review

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an examination of all the relevant information on a subject or on a series of events
examples: SEE ALSO peer review
to conduct/undertake a review of customer complaints
to publish a review of recent cancer research
a comprehensive review of current scientific knowledge on the subject
a thorough review of relevant materials
The literature review suggests a number of areas for further study.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a ceremony that involves an official inspection of soldiers, etc. by an important visitorWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (as a noun denoting a formal inspection of military or naval forces): from obsolete French reveue, from revoir ‘see again’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to change your opinions or plans, for example because of something you have learned
examples: I can see I will have to revise my opinions of his abilities now.
The government may need to revise its policy in the light of this report.
I realised that I would have to revise my life plan.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to change something, such as a book or an estimate, in order to correct or improve it
examples: a revised edition of a textbook
I'll prepare a revised estimate for you.
This revised version of his play has only two acts.
They should create a revised marketing plan.
We may have to revise this figure upwards.
The growth forecast has been revised down.
Of the original 200, that was revised to 100, only about 50 people showed up.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to prepare for an exam by looking again at work that you have done
examples: I can't come out tonight. I have to revise.
I spent the weekend revising for my exam.
I'm revising Geography today.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a change or set of changes to something
examples: He made some minor revisions to the report before printing it out.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of changing something, or of examining something with the intention of changing it
examples: The system is in need of revision.
a revision of trading standards
Their educational policies are due for revision.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of learning work for an exam
examples: Have you started your revision yet?
a revision class/course/timetable

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an improvement in the condition or strength of something
examples: the revival of trade
an economic revival
a revival of property values

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the process of something becoming or being made popular or fashionable again
examples: a religious revival
Jazz is enjoying a revival.
a revival of interest in folk music

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a new production of a play that has not been performed for some time
examples: a revival of Peter Shaffer’s ‘Equus’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become, or to make somebody/something become, conscious or healthy and strong again
examples: The flowers soon revived in water.
The economy is beginning to revive.
The paramedics couldn't revive her.
This movie is intended to revive her flagging career.
Attempts to revive him failed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something start being used or done again
examples: This quaint custom should be revived.
She has been trying to revive the debate over equal pay.
The poor trade figures have revived fears of higher interest rates.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to produce again a play, etc. that has not been performed for some time
examples: This 1930s musical is being revived at the National Theatre.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an attempt, by a large number of people, to change the government of a country, especially by violent action
examples: SEE ALSO counter-revolution
a socialist revolution
the outbreak of the French Revolution in 1789
The shooting and killing of thirty people started a revolution.
The country appears to be on the brink of revolution.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a great change in conditions, ways of working, beliefs, etc. that affects large numbers of people
examples: SEE ALSO agrarian revolution
a cultural/social/scientific, etc. revolution
the sexual revolution of the 1960s
the digital/technological revolution
They led the electronics revolution but have been left behind by the IT revolution.
A revolution in information technology is taking place.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a complete circular movement around a point
examples: SEE ALSO revolve
The disk rotates at up to 500 revolutions per minute.
The revolution of the earth around the sun takes one year.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with political revolution
examples: a revolutionary leader
revolutionary uprisings

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: involving a great or complete change
examples: a revolutionary idea
a time of rapid and revolutionary change
revolutionary advances in medicine
The effects of technological development are revolutionary.
At the time this idea was revolutionary.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that you are given because you have done something good, worked hard, etc.
examples: a financial reward
a reward for good behaviour
You deserve a reward for being so helpful.
Winning the match was just reward for the effort the team had made.
They're playing the game more for the love of sport than for financial reward.
The company is now reaping the rewards of their investments.
Top corporate jobs are not without their rewards.
The appointment was widely seen as a reward for his loyalty.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an amount of money that is offered to somebody for helping the police to find a criminal or for finding something that is lost
examples: A £100 reward has been offered for the return of the necklace.
Anyone wanting to claim the reward should contact the city police.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the reward for acting in a moral or correct way is the knowledge that you have done so, and you should not expect more than this, for example praise from other people or paymentWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Anglo-Norman French, variant of Old French reguard ‘regard, heed’, also an early sense of the English word.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: speech or writing that is intended to influence people, but that is not completely honest or sincere
examples: the rhetoric of political slogans
Her speech was just empty rhetoric.
His speech was dismissed as mere rhetoric by the opposition.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the art of using language in speech or writing in a special way that influences or entertains people
examples: SYNONYM eloquence

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong regular repeated pattern of sounds or movements
examples: SEE ALSO delta rhythm
to dance to the rhythm of the music
I listened to the steady rhythm of her breathing.
music with a fast/slow/steady rhythm
I love these jazz rhythms.
abnormal heart rhythms
He can't seem to play in rhythm.
The boat rocked up and down in rhythm with the sea.
a dancer with a natural sense of rhythm (= the ability to move in time to a fixed beat)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a regular pattern of changes or events
examples: SEE ALSO biorhythm
the rhythm of the seasons
biological/body rhythms
Lack of sleep can upset your daily rhythm.
You'll soon get into a rhythm.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: short, narrow white or brown grain grown on wet land in hot countries as food; the plant that produces this grain
examples: SEE ALSO jollof rice
a grain of rice
boiled/steamed/fried rice
long-/short-grain rice
sticky/basmati/wild rice
brown rice (= without its outer layer removed)
rice paddies (= rice fields)
a spicy rice dish
rice flour/noodles/cakes
There is no need to keep the rice field flooded.
The dish is served with rice.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a lot of money or property
examples: SEE ALSO cash-rich
She's one of the richest women in the world.
to get/grow/become rich
Nobody gets rich from writing nowadays.
She longed to be rich and famous.
He was born in a rich and powerful family.
to be filthy/stinking (= extremely) rich

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: people who have a lot of money or property
examples: OPPOSITE the poor
It's a favourite resort for the rich and famous.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: producing a lot of wealth so that many of its people can live at a high standard
examples: OPPOSITE poor
the richest countries/economies/nations

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: containing or providing a large supply of something
examples: OPPOSITE poor
Oranges are rich in vitamin C.
The area is rich in wildlife.
Russia is hugely rich in oil and gas.
The animation is amazingly rich in detail.
The country is rich in natural resources.
His novels are a rich source of material for the movie industry.
iron-rich rocks
the exceptionally rich fishing grounds of the North Pacific
Several major US companies have set up in the country in order to tap into the rich vein of talent available.
Ours is a world rich with possibilities.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: very interesting and full of variety
examples: the region’s rich history and culture
She leads a rich and varied life.
a culturally rich nation
the rich architectural heritage of India
This story emphasizes the rich African tradition of oral history.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: containing a lot of fat, butter, eggs, etc. and making you feel full quickly
examples: a rich, creamy sauce
a rich chocolate cake
The chocolate orange fondant was too rich for me.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: containing the substances that make it good for growing plants in
examples: SYNONYM fertile
a rich, well-drained soil
rich farming land

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: Try and get rid of your visitors before I get there.
The problem is getting rid of nuclear waste.
I can't get rid of this headache.
We got rid of all the old furniture.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.definition: a gun with a long barrel which you hold to your shoulder to fire
examples: SEE ALSO air rifle
a hunting rifle
an assault rifle

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: true or correct as a fact
examples: OPPOSITE wrong
Did you get the answer right?
‘What's the right time?’ ‘10.37.’
That's exactly right.
‘David, isn't it?’ ‘Yes, that's right.’
It was Monday you went to see Angie, right?
Let me get this right (= understand correctly)—you want us to do an extra ten hours' work for no extra pay?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: correct in your opinion or judgement
examples: OPPOSITE wrong

They're absolutely right to be cautious.
‘It's not easy.’ ‘Yeah, you're right.’

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: morally good or acceptable; correct according to law or a person’s duty

I don't know, it just doesn't seem right.
On some level this just feels right.
You were quite right to criticize him.
It's only right to warn you of the risk.
It's right that he should be punished.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in a normal or good enough condition

I don't feel quite right today (= I feel ill).
Things aren't right between her parents.
If only I could have helped put matters right.
That sausage doesn't smell right.
The meat doesn't taste right to me.
We talk about the reasons why something doesn't look right.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: socially fashionable or important
examples: She knows all the right people (= for example, people who can help her in her career).
They make sure that their children go to the right schools.
I wore the best clothes and was seen in all the right places.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: of, on or towards the side of the body that is towards the east when a person faces north
examples: OPPOSITE left
your right hand/arm/foot/leg
My right eye is weaker than my left eye.
Keep on the right side of the road.
Take a right turn at the intersection.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something bad
examples: You made a right mess of that!
I felt a right idiot.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be able to take advantage of opportunities when they come
examples: His success was down to being in the right place at the right time.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to start a relationship well/badly
examples: I seem to have got off on the wrong foot with the new boss.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make somebody pleased with you/annoyed with you

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody is willing to give up a lot in order to have or do something that they really want
examples: I'd have given my right arm to have been there with them.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be a sensible person

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to have found a very good or successful way of living, doing something, etc.
examples: He's certainly got the right idea—retiring at 55.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody’s intentions are kind and sincere even though they sometimes do the wrong thing

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to do, say or write something that is suitable/not suitable for a particular occasion
examples: It is a bizarre tale and the author hits just the right note of horror and disbelief.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: (not) mentally normal
examples: Who in their right mind would want to marry a murderer?

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: having the power to do something gives you the right to do it
examples: Their foreign policy is based on the principle that ‘might is right’.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: younger or older than 40, 50, etc. years of age

definitions.label: Meaning 20

definitions.label: Meaning 21

definitions.label: Meaning 22

definitions.label: Meaning 23

definitions.label: Meaning 24

Shortages eventually led to food riots.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a collection of a lot of different types of the same thing
examples: The garden was a riot of colour.
The market was a riot of unfamiliar sounds and smells.
A riot of emotions raged through her.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or an event that is very funny
examples: The movie is a laugh riot.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to tell somebody with force that they must not do something

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to behave in a way that is violent and/or not under control
examples: SYNONYM rampage

definitions.label: Meaning 7

She ripped the letter open.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to remove something quickly or violently, often by pulling it

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to copy sound or video files from a website or CD on to a computer

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to change text or images into a form in which they can be displayed on a screen or printed

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: When she gets angry with her boyfriend, she really lets rip at him.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to destroy something; to criticize somebody very strongly

definitions.label: Meaning 9

The flood waters were rising fast.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: OPPOSITE set
The sun rises in the east.
It was almost dark and the moon was just rising.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to become more successful, important, powerful, etc.

He rose to prominence in the 90s.
to rise to fame/power
You could rise to the top if you work hard.
He rose to the rank of general.
She has risen to a position of great responsibility.

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: SYNONYM get up

They rose from the table.
She rose to her feet.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to end a meeting

The House (= members of the House of Commons) rose at 10 p.m.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: SYNONYM get up
The wind is rising—I think there's a storm coming.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 10

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to begin to fight against your government or leader or against a foreign army
examples: The peasants rose in revolt.

definitions.label: Meaning 13

examples: Mountains rose in the distance.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: if land rises, it slopes upwards
examples: The ground rose steeply all around.

definitions.label: Meaning 15

examples: The Thames rises in the Cotswold hills.

definitions.label: Meaning 16

definitions.label: Meaning 17

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the possibility of something bad happening at some time in the future; a situation that could be dangerous or have a bad result
examples: SEE ALSO high-risk
The health risks are very low.
a high risk of failure
a serious/significant risk of something
The study found a slightly increased risk of cancer in this group.
Steps have been taken to reduce the risk of any trouble.
Use filters or boil water to minimize the risk of infection.
Smoking can increase the risk of developing heart disease.
There is still a risk that the whole deal will fall through.
The chemicals pose little risk (= are not dangerous) to human health.
a calculated risk (= one that you think is small compared with the possible benefits)
Trying new things can be a gamble, but it's worth the risk.
Patients should be made aware of the risks involved with this treatment.
Make sure you understand the risks and benefits.
Cigarette smoking is a risk factor for this disease.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is likely to cause problems or danger at some time in the future
examples: SEE ALSO security risk
Those old boxes in the corridor are a fire risk.
a safety/health risk
The group was considered to be a risk to national security.
Pollutants in the river pose a real risk to the fish.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or business that a bank or an insurance company is willing/unwilling to lend money or sell insurance to because they are likely/unlikely to pay back the money, etc.
examples: With five previous claims, he's now a bad insurance risk.
He's a good insurance risk.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in danger of something unpleasant or harmful happening
examples: As with all diseases, certain groups will be more at risk than others.
If we go to war, innocent lives will be put at risk.
Journalists in the zone are at serious risk of being kidnapped.
Adults were also at risk from epidemics.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to introduce something that may sound stupid or may offend somebody
examples: At the risk of showing my ignorance, how exactly does the internet work?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: with the possibility of harming yourself/somebody/something
examples: He dived in to save the dog at considerable risk to his own life.
He saved the child at considerable risk to himself.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to do something even though you have been warned about the possible dangers and will have to take responsibility for anything bad that happens
examples: Persons swimming beyond this point do so at their own risk (= on a notice).
Valuables are left at their owner's risk (= on a notice).
The building is unsafe—enter at your own risk.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be or put yourself in a situation in which something bad could happen to you
examples: People who are overweight run a risk of a heart attack or stroke.
We don't want to run the risk of losing their business.
Investment is all about running risks.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to do something even though you know that something bad could happen as a result
examples: That's a risk I'm not prepared to take.
You have no right to take risks with other people's lives.

the sound of waves rolling in to the shore

She rolled her jeans to her knees.

definitions.label: Meaning 10

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to wrap or cover somebody/something/yourself in something
examples: Roll the meat in the breadcrumbs.
He rolled himself up in the blanket.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to move or make something move from side to side
examples: COMPARE pitch
He walked with a rolling gait.
The ship was rolling heavily to and fro.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to make a long continuous sound
examples: rolling drums

to roll your r’s (= by letting your tongue vibrate with each ‘r’ sound)

definitions.label: Meaning 14

examples: They had to repeat the scene because the cameras weren't rolling.

definitions.label: Meaning 16

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: approximately but not exactly
examples: Sales are up by roughly 10 per cent.
We live roughly halfway between here and the coast.
They all left at roughly the same time.
Roughly speaking, we receive about fifty letters a week on the subject.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: using force or not being careful and gentle
examples: He pushed her roughly out of the way.
‘What do you want?’ she demanded roughly.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a way that does not leave a smooth surface
examples: roughly plastered walls

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a shape like a circle or a ball
examples: SEE ALSO round-eyed
a round plate
These glasses suit people with round faces.
The fruit are small and round.
Rugby isn't played with a round ball.
the discovery that the world is round
The child was watching it all with big round eyes (= showing interest).
a T-shirt with a round neck
a coin with a round hole in the centre
The tower was perfectly round.
They sat at a large round table.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having a curved shape
examples: the round green hills of Donegal
Put both the surname and publication date in round brackets.
She had a small mouth and round pink cheeks.
Choose shoes with a flat sole and round toes.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a round figure or amount is one that is given as a whole number, usually one ending in 0
examples: SEE ALSO year-round
Make it a round figure—say forty dollars.
Two thousand is a nice round number—put that down.
Well, in round figures (= not giving the exact figures) we've spent twenty thousand so far.
The total was a round $30 million in Australian dollars.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a way that you follow to get from one place to another
examples: SEE ALSO en route
Which is the best route to take?
Motorists are advised to find an alternative route.
a coastal route
the quickest route from Florence to Rome
Mark showed me the quickest route to the hospital on foot.
a key route through the city centre
The shortest route home is along the shore.
The alley would take them on a more direct route to the Old City.
an escape route
Thousands of people lined the parade route.
People gathered at points along the route to wave and cheer .

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a fixed way along which a bus, train, etc. regularly travels or goods are regularly sent
examples: SEE ALSO rural route
The house is not on a bus route.
shipping/supply routes
a cycle route (= a path that is only for cyclists)
Eventually, the main rail routes will be unable to carry any more trains.
Only one company operates on this route.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a particular way of achieving something
examples: to go down/take/follow a particular route
Some people decided to go down the of violent protest.
This is not a route I would choose to take.
the route to success
There are a number of routes to qualifying as a social worker.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used before the number of a main road in the US
examples: Route 66

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the normal order and way in which you regularly do things
examples: to settle/get/fall into a routine
We are trying to get the baby into a routine for feeding and sleeping.
In school, I quickly fell into the routine.
Make exercise a part of your daily routine.
A pressing work project had disrupted his normal sleep routine.
There's never a bad time to begin a new exercise routine.
We clean and repair the machines as a matter of routine.
Don't cut back on your regular fitness routine.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a situation in which life is boring because things are always done in the same way
examples: She needed a break from routine.
He tries to escape the dull routine of his office life.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a series of movements, jokes, etc. that are part of a performance
examples: to do/perform a dance routine
We need some new material for our routine.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a list of instructions that enable a computer to perform a particular taskWord Origin
examples: late 17th cent. (denoting a regular course or procedure): from French, from route ‘road’, from Old French rute ‘road’, from Latin rupta (via) ‘broken (way)’, feminine past participle of rumpere.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with or belonging to the king or queen of a country
examples: COMPARE regal
the royal family
the royal household/court
a royal wedding
a royal palace
During the Second World War the royal couple played a prominent role.
by royal appointment (= a sign used by companies that supply goods to the royal family)
She took the opportunity to meet members of the British royal family.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used in the names of organizations that serve or are supported by a king or queen
examples: the Royal Navy
the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: impressive; suitable for a king or queen
examples: SYNONYM splendid
We were given a royal welcome.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move your hand, a cloth, etc., backwards and forwards over a surface while pressing it
examples: He sat up on the hard bunk and rubbed his eyes.
She rubbed her chin thoughtfully.
He rubbed a hand wearily over his eyes.
Rub the surface with sandpaper before painting.
The cat rubbed itself against my legs.
I rubbed at the stain on the cloth.
Animals had been rubbing against the trees.
Rub the surface smooth.
She rubbed her hair dry quickly with a towel.
I rubbed a clear patch on the window with my fingers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to press two surfaces against each other and move them backwards and forwards; to be pressed together and move in this way
examples: She rubbed her hands in delight.
In some cultures, people traditionally greet each other by rubbing noses.
She rubbed her hands together in effort to warm them.
He made a fire by rubbing sticks together.
It sounded like two pieces of wood rubbing together.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move backwards and forwards many times against something while pressing it, especially causing pain or damage
examples: The back of my shoe is rubbing.
The wheel is rubbing on the mudguard.
Their perpetually wet clothes rubbed against their skin.
The horse's neck was rubbed raw (= until the skin came off) where the rope had been.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to spread a liquid or other substance over a surface while pressing it
examples: She rubbed the lotion into her skin.
Rub salt over the fish before cooking.
Put a little cream onto each hand and rub it in well.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be very poor, stupid, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to keep reminding somebody in an unkind way of their past mistakes

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make a difficult experience even more difficult for somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to meet and spend time with a famous person, socially or as part of your job
examples: He’s rubbing shoulders with stars all the time.
She had been rubbing elbows with celebrities.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to make somebody annoyed or angry, often without intending to, by doing or saying something that offends them
examples: She tends to rub people up the wrong way.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong substance that can be stretched and does not allow liquids to pass through it, used for making tyres, boots, etc. It is made from the liquid (= sap) inside a tropical plant or is produced using chemicals.
examples: SEE ALSO foam rubberfoam
a ball made of rubber
a rubber tree
a rubber plantation
My legs were like rubber - I could hardly walk.
I don't like the smell of burning rubber.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small piece of rubber or a similar substance, used for removing pencil marks from paper; a piece of soft material used for removing chalk marks from a blackboard or pen from a whiteboard

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a condom (= a thin rubber tube that a man wears over his penis during sex to stop a woman from becoming pregnant or to protect against disease)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: (in some card games or sports) a competition consisting of a series of games or matches between the same teams or players

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to drive very fast

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the point at which something is tested and you really find out whether it is successful or true
examples: Here's where the rubber meets the road: will consumers actually buy the product?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: things that you throw away because you no longer want or need them
examples: SEE ALSO garbage
a rubbish bag/bin
a rubbish dump/heap/tip
The streets were littered with rubbish.
garden/household rubbish
The rubbish is collected on Tuesdays.
Weeks have gone by without a rubbish collection, and the stench is terrible.
He is supporting a campaign to encourage people to recycle their rubbish.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that you think is of poor quality
examples: I thought the play was rubbish!
The film was absolute/complete rubbish.
Do we have to listen to this rubbish music?
They said I was a rubbish boss.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: comments, ideas, etc. that you think are stupid or wrong
examples: SYNONYM nonsense
Rubbish! You're not fat.
You're talking a load of rubbish.
It's not rubbish—it's true!
He described the claims as utter rubbish and nonsense.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having or showing a lack of respect for other people and their feelings
examples: SYNONYM impolite
a rude comment/remark
He started swearing and using rude words.
There’s no need to be rude!
She is bossy, rude and arrogant.
a rude waiter
I don’t wish to be rude, but I have another appointment in five minutes.
I don't mean to sound rude, but I have no idea what you're talking about.
The man was downright rude to us.
Why are you so rude to your mother?
She was very rude about my driving.
He's always rude to me about my singing.
It's rude to speak when you're eating.
How rude of me not to offer you something to drink!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with sex or the body in a way that people find offensive or embarrassing
examples: a rude gesture
Someone made a rude noise.
The joke is too rude to repeat.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: sudden, unpleasant and unexpected
examples: Those expecting good news will get a rude shock.
If the players think they can win this match easily, they are in for a rude awakening.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: made in a simple, basic way
examples: SYNONYM primitive
rude shacks

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: looking or feeling very healthyWord Origin
examples: Middle English (in sense (4), also ‘uncultured’): from Old French, from Latin rudis ‘unwrought’ (referring to handicraft), figuratively ‘uncultivated’; related to rudus ‘broken stone’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a game played by two teams of 13 or 15 players, using an oval ball which may be kicked or carried. Teams try to put the ball over the other team’s line.
examples: to play a game of rugby
Kids from six years old play mini rugby at the club.
a rugby club/match/player/team
the Ireland rugby captain

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to damage something so badly that it loses all its value, pleasure, etc.
examples: SYNONYM spoil (1)
The bad weather ruined our trip.
That one mistake ruined his chances of getting the job.
My new shoes got ruined in the mud.
The crops were ruined by the late frost.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something lose all their money, their position, etc.
examples: If she loses the court case it will ruin her.
The country was ruined by the war.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a statement of what may, must or must not be done in a particular situation or when playing a game
examples: SEE ALSO gag rule
She laid down strict rules for her tenants, including prompt payment of rent.
the rules of golf/tennis/football
to follow/obey a rule
to break/violate a rule
to enforce/apply a rule
You can't just change the rules to suit yourself.
It's against all the rules and regulations.
These products are banned under international rules.
This explains the rules under which the library operates.
the unwritten rules of adult society (= that everyone understands)
the rules of procedure/conduct (= saying how something must be done)
New rules governing pensions come into effect next year.
Normal competition rules apply.
According to the rules of the game, you have to miss a turn.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a statement of what is possible according to a particular system, for example the grammar of a language
examples: the basic rules of grammar
What is the rule for forming plurals?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a statement of what you are advised to do in a particular situation
examples: SEE ALSO golden rule
The first rule is to make eye contact with your interviewer.
Follow these few simple rules and you won't go far wrong.
There are no hard and fast rules for planning healthy meals.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a habit; the normal state of things; what is true in most cases
examples: He makes it a rule never to borrow money.
Cold winters here are the exception rather than the rule (= are rare).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the government of a country or control of a group of people by a particular person, group or system
examples: SEE ALSO home rule
military/civilian/democratic rule
The 1972 Act imposed direct rule from Westminster.
The country was still under colonial rule.
majority rule (= government by the political party that most people have voted for)

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a measuring instrument with a straight edge
examples: SEE ALSO slide rule

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: usually but not always
examples: I go to bed early as a rule.
As a general rule, vegetable oils are better for you than animal fats.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to change the rules to suit a particular person or situation
examples: Couldn't they just bend the rules and let us in without a ticket?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: people say that something is the exception that proves the rule when they are stating something that seems to be different from the normal situation, but they mean that the normal situation remains true in general
examples: Most electronics companies have not done well this year, but ours is the exception that proves the rule.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: if somebody plays by their own rules or makes other people play by their rules, they set the conditions for doing business or having a relationship
examples: If he wanted a loan he would have to play by the bank's rules.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to deal fairly and honestly with people

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: the condition in which all members of society, including its political leaders, accept the authority of the law
examples: Democracy and the rule of law are yet to be firmly established in the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a practical method of doing or measuring something, usually based on past experience rather than on exact measurement
examples: As a rule of thumb, you should cook a chicken for 20 minutes for each pound of weight.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: the standards of behaviour that most people accept or that actually operate in a particular area of life or business

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to follow the rules of your job in a very strict way in order to cause delay, as a form of protest against your employer or your working conditions
examples: SEE ALSO work-to-rule

definitions.definition: an official decision made by somebody in a position of authority, especially a judge
examples: The court will make its ruling on the case next week.
The company intends to appeal against the ruling that it was negligent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of information, or a story, that people talk about, but that may not be true
examples: to start/spread a rumour
There are widespread rumours of job losses.
Some malicious rumours are circulating about his past.
I heard a rumour that they are getting married.
Many of the stories are based on rumour.
Rumour has it (= people say) that he was murdered.
I thought she was leaving the company, but perhaps it may be just a rumour.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move using your legs, going faster than when you walk
examples: Can you run as fast as Mike?
They turned and ran when they saw us coming.
She came running to meet us.
I had to run to catch the bus.
The dogs ran off as soon as we appeared.
He ran home in tears to his mother.
The children spent the morning running around in the park.
She can run really fast.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to travel a particular distance by running
examples: SEE ALSO mile
Who was the first person to run a mile in under four minutes?
I ran four miles today.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to run as a sport
examples: She used to run when she was at college.
I often go running before work.
Try to run round the block a few times every morning.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to take part in a race
examples: SEE ALSO runner (1)
He will be running in the 100 metres tonight.
There are only five horses running in the first race.
to run a marathon
Farah ran a fine race to take the gold medal.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make a race take place
examples: The Derby will be run in spite of the bad weather.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to hurry from one place to another
examples: SEE ALSO rat run
I've spent the whole day running around after the kids.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be in charge of a business, campaign, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO running (2)
to run a hotel/store/language school
He has no idea how to run a business.
Stop trying to run my life (= organize it) for me.
The shareholders want more say in how the company is run.
a badly run company
Both candidates have run a good campaign.
state-run industries

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to make a service, course of study, etc. available to people
examples: SYNONYM organize
The college runs summer courses for foreign students.
The programme will be jointly run with NASA in the US.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to travel on a particular route
examples: Buses to Oxford run every half hour.
All the trains are running late (= are leaving later than planned).
Trains between London and Brighton run throughout the day.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make buses, trains, etc. travel on a particular route
examples: They run extra trains during the rush hour.
The transport company is concerned about the cost of running more buses.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to operate or function; to make something do this
examples: Stan had the chainsaw running.
Our van runs on (= uses) diesel.
Could you run the engine for a moment?

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: when a computer program or system runs or somebody runs it, it operates
examples: You may find that some apps are running slowly.
There are too many programs running on your computer.
You need to have antivirus software running on your PC.
The app runs on all Android devices.
You can run the program overnight.
My PC runs Windows 10.
Don't forget to run a final spellcheck.
What applications were you running when the problem occurred?

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if a recording on a tape runs or somebody runs it, it plays
examples: He didn't know the tape was still running.
Run the tape, please.
Can you run the tape back a few minutes?

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to own and use a vehicle or machine
examples: I can't afford to run a car on my salary.

definitions.label: Meaning 15

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move or to do something with great speed, often too fast

the sound of rushing water
Don't rush off, I haven't finished.
I've been rushing around all day trying to get everything done.
The children rushed out of school.
Firefighters rushed to the scene and extinguished the blaze.
When I fell forwards onto the ice, Michael came rushing to my aid, helping me up giving me an encouraging smile.
His wife immediately rushed to his defence (= defended him against attack or criticism).
Beachgoers rushed to the rescue of three boys as they were pulled out to sea in a rip tide.
My college years seemed to rush past.
She rushed back upstairs.
People rushed to buy shares in the company.
We had to rush our meal.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to transport or send somebody/something somewhere with great speed
examples: Ambulances rushed the injured to the hospital.
Relief supplies were rushed in.
He was rushed home immediately.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to do something or to make somebody do something without thinking about it carefully
examples: We have to be careful not to rush to judgment.

Let us not rush headlong into this crazy project without careful consideration.
Don't rush me. I need time to think about it.
I'm not going to be rushed into anything.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to flow strongly
examples: The water rushed in through the hole in the ship's hull.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to try to attack or capture somebody/something suddenly
examples: A group of prisoners rushed an officer and managed to break out.
Fans rushed the stage after the concert.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to run into somebody who has the ball

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to move forward and gain ground by carrying the ball and not passing it

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to give a lot of attention to somebody, especially to a student because you want them to join your fraternity or sorority
examples: He is being rushed by Sigma Nu.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be extremely busy; to have too many things to do

definitions.label: Meaning 10

examples: We were glad she let us know she was safe.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

examples: SYNONYM careful
a safe driver

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 15

examples: Colleagues regard him as a safe pair of hands.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being safe and protected from danger or harm
examples: a place where children can play in safety
He was kept in custody for his own safety.
measures to ensure patient safety
His behaviour endangered the safety of the public.
The police are concerned for the safety of the 12-year-old boy who has been missing for three days.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the state of not being dangerous
examples: I'm worried about the safety of the treatment.
a local campaign to improve road safety
People worry about food safety (= food that could be harmful to health).
breaches of fire safety regulations
safety standards/measures/precautions
safety concerns/issues
The airline has an excellent safety record.
a safety hazard (= something that is not safe)
a safety officer (= somebody whose job is to ensure safety)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a place where you are safe
examples: They reached safety seconds before the building was engulfed in flames.
I managed to swim to safety.
We watched the lions from the safety of the car.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a device that stops a gun from being fired or a machine from working by accident

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: (in American football) a defending player who plays in a position far away from the other team

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: safety is the most important thing
examples: When cycling on the roads, remember: safety first.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: being in a group makes you safer and makes you feel more confidentWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French sauvete, from medieval Latin salvitas, from Latin salvus ‘safe’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to travel on water using sails or an engine
examples: to sail into harbour
The dinghy sailed smoothly across the lake.
The ferry sails from Newhaven to Dieppe.
one of the first people to sail around the world
The flotilla will sail north to Hawaii.
to sail the Atlantic
In his young days he had sailed the seas.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to control or travel on a boat with a sail, especially as a sport
examples: We spent the weekend sailing off the south coast.
Do you go sailing often?
the first woman to sail solo around the world
She sails her own yacht.
He managed to sail the boat between the rocks.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to begin a journey on water
examples: We sail at 2 p.m. tomorrow.
He sailed for the West Indies from Portsmouth.
The ferry sails for Southampton at 5.30.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to move quickly and smoothly in a particular direction; (of people) to move in a confident manner
examples: clouds sailing across the sky
The ball sailed over the goalie's head.
She sailed past, ignoring me completely.
An owl sailed silently out of the branches.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to take a risk by doing something that is dangerous or that may be illegalWord Origin
examples: Old English segel (noun), seglian (verb), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch zeil and German Segel (nouns).

a sailing club
the college rowing and sailing teams

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one of the regular times that a ship leaves a port
examples: There are six sailings a day.
What time is the next sailing?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be simple and free from trouble

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who works on a ship as a member of the crew
examples: a crew of two officers and 13 sailors
The vessels are manned by 1  300 sailors.
His father was a US Navy sailor.
Many soldiers, sailors and airmen lost their lives.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who sails a boat
examples: My parents were keen sailors.
The three missing men were experienced sailors.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who rarely/often becomes sick at seaWord Origin
examples: mid 17th cent.: variant of obsolete sailer.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person that the Christian Church recognizes as being very holy, because of the way they have lived or died
examples: SEE ALSO patron saint
St John
St Valentine’s Day
The children were all named after saints.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a very good, kind or patient person
examples: SEE ALSO plaster saint
She's a saint to go on living with that man.
His behaviour would try the patience of a saint.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a mixture of raw vegetables such as lettuce, tomato and cucumber, usually served with other food as part of a meal
examples: SEE ALSO Caesar salad
All main courses come with salad or vegetables.
Is cold meat and salad OK for lunch?
a side salad (= a small bowl of salad served with the main course of a meal)
a salad bowl (= a large bowl for serving salad in)
a salad sandwich
Toss the salad with the dressing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: meat, fish, cheese, etc. served with salad
examples: a chicken/tuna/seafood/egg salad

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: raw or cooked vegetables, etc. that are cut into small pieces, often mixed with mayonnaise and served cold with other food
examples: SEE ALSO fruit salad
potato salad
a pasta salad

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: any green vegetable, especially lettuce, that is eaten raw in a salad
examples: salad plants/leaves
baby octopus served with salad greens

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the time when you are young and do not have much experience of lifeWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French salade, from Provençal salada, based on Latin sal ‘salt’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: money that employees receive for doing their job, especially professional employees or people working in an office, usually paid every month
examples: COMPARE wage
an annual salary of $40 000
The average monthly salary for an unskilled worker is $550.
She's on a salary of £24 000.
She earned a six-figure salary.
a 9 per cent salary increase
He gets a basic salary plus commission.
base salary
Chemical engineering grads are expected to get the biggest starting salaries.
the closure of final salary pension schemes
We have no money to pay staff salaries.
The CEO received a salary of $1 million.
The average annual salary for those jobs was $90 721.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act or the process of selling something
examples: SEE ALSO bill of sale
regulations governing the sale of alcoholic beverages
The product has been withdrawn from sale.
I haven't made a sale all week.
She gets 10 per cent commission on each sale.
They charge a fee of 3 to 5 per cent of the sale price .
We gave them our sales pitch (= our explanation of why they should buy something).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the number of items sold
examples: They have to boost sales to make a profit.
Retail sales fell in November by 10 per cent.
ticket/car sales
The company has seen record sales over the past year.
Online sales were up by 12 per cent.
the sales figures for May

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the part of a company that deals with selling its products
examples: a sales and marketing director
She works in sales.
She works in the sales department.
He's a sales manager for a hotel group.
The Weldon Group has a 6 000 strong sales force.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an occasion when a shop or business sells its products at a lower price than usual
examples: SEE ALSO fire sale
The sale starts next week.
the January sales
I bought a coat in the sales.
a half-price sale on all bed linen
The airline is selling one third of all its seats at the sale price.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: an occasion when goods are sold, especially an auction
examples: SEE ALSO bake sale
a contemporary art sale
a major sale of paintings

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: available to be bought, especially from the owner
examples: I'm sorry, it's not for sale.
They've put their house up for sale.
an increase in the number of stolen vehicles being offered for sale
a ‘for sale’ sign
The land has come up for sale again.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: available to be bought, especially in a shop
examples: Tickets are on sale from the booking office.
The new model goes on sale next month.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: being offered at a reduced price
examples: All video equipment is on sale today and tomorrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: supplied with the agreement that any item that is not sold can be sent back without having to be paid for
examples: The novels are delivered to outlets on a sale or return basis.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a white substance that is added to food to make it taste better or to preserve it. Salt is obtained from mines and is also found in seawater. It is sometimes called common salt to show that it is different from other chemical salts. Its chemical name is sodium chloride.
examples: SEE ALSO rock salt
Pass the salt, please.
a pinch of salt (= a small amount of it)
Season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with salt to taste.
Avoid adding table salt to your food.
salt and vinegar crisps

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a chemical formed from a metal and an acid
examples: SEE ALSO acid salt
mineral salts

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a substance that looks or tastes like salt
examples: SEE ALSO smelling salts
bath salts (= used to give a pleasant smell to bath water)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very fast and easily
examples: He got through the housework like a dose of salts.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make a difficult experience even more difficult for somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a very good and honest person that you can always depend on

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be careful about believing that something is completely true
examples: If I were you, I’d take everything he says with a pinch of salt.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: deserving respect, especially because you do your job well
examples: Any teacher worth her salt knows that.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: exactly the one or ones referred to or mentioned; not different
examples: We have lived in the same house for twenty years.
Our children go to the same school as theirs.
She's still the same fun-loving person that I knew at college.
This one works in exactly the same way as the other.
They promise to meet again in the exact same place six months later.
They both said much the same thing.
He used the very same (= exactly the same) words.
I resigned last Friday and left that same day.
I was relieved and sad at the same time.
Gary and I look more or less the same age.
I recognized a lot of the same people.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: exactly like the one or ones referred to or mentioned
examples: I bought the same car as yours (= another car of that type).
She was wearing the same dress that I had on.
The same thing happened to me last week.
Most parents tend to raise their children in much the same way they were raised
Other countries don't suffer from the same kinds of health problems we do.
Older adults may not get the same level of protection from the vaccine.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that a situation has not changed at all
examples: ‘How's it going?’ ‘Oh, same old, same old.’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that a situation or the excuses, products or entertainment being offered have not improved at all
examples: It's the same old story  —budget cuts and government neglect.
The band's new album includes the same old stuff they've been playing forever.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a number of people or things taken from a larger group and used in tests to provide information about the group
examples: The interviews were given to a random sample of students.
The survey covers a representative sample of schools.
a sample survey
The current study has a larger sample size than earlier studies.
We studied a large population sample.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small amount of a substance taken from a larger amount and tested in order to obtain information about the substance
examples: a blood/urine/tissue/DNA sample
Samples of the water contained pesticide.
A small sample of blood must be tested by a doctor.
to collect/obtain/take a sample
We analyzed samples from more than a dozen common tree species.
Her sample contained traces of the banned steroid.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a small amount or example of something that can be looked at or tried to see what it is like
examples: ‘I'd like to see a sample of your work,’ said the manager.
a free sample of shampoo
Would you like a sample of the fabric to take home?
We looked at sample books to choose the fabric.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a piece of recorded music or sound that is used in a new piece of music
examples: ‘Candy’ includes a swirling sample from a Walker Brothers song.
