examples: SEE ALSO dust sheet
Have you changed the sheets (= put clean sheets on the bed)?
He slid between the sheets and closed his eyes.
white bed sheets

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of paper for writing or printing on, etc. usually in a standard size
examples: SEE ALSO balance sheet
a clean/blank sheet of paper (= with no writing on it)
a sheet of A4
Start each answer on a fresh sheet.
Pick up one of our free information sheets at reception.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a flat thin piece of any material, normally square or rectangular
examples: SEE ALSO baking sheet
a sheet of glass/plastic/plywood/steel
sheet metal (= metal that has been made into thin sheets)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a wide flat area of something, covering the surface of something else
examples: SEE ALSO ice sheet
The road was covered with a sheet of ice.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a large moving mass of fire or water
examples: a sheet of flame
The rain was coming down in sheets (= very heavily).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a rope or chain fastened to the lower corner of a sail to hold it and to control the angle of the sail

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a record of your work or behaviour that does not show any mistakes or bad things that you have done
examples: No government operates with a completely clean sheet.
They kept a clean sheet in the match (= no goals were scored against them).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a flat board, made of wood, metal, glass, etc., fixed to the wall or forming part of a cupboard, bookcase, etc., for things to be placed on
examples: SEE ALSO top-shelf
I helped him put up some shelves in his bedroom.
The book I wanted was on the top shelf.
supermarket shelves
store shelves
The product should hit store shelves by August.
library shelves
empty shelves
the powerful retailers who control what products get shelf space

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing like a shelf in shape, especially a piece of rock sticking out from a cliff or from the edge of a mass of land under the sea

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: that can be bought immediately and does not have to be specially designed or ordered
examples: COMPARE off the peg
I bought this package off the shelf.
Some courses can be bought off the shelf as self-contained study packages.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not wanted by anyone; not used

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: considered to be too old to get married

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to stop something from being sold
examples: The slimming pills were taken off the market.
Thousands of egg products were taken off the shelves following the health scare.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the hard outer part of eggs, nuts, some seeds, and some animals
examples: SEE ALSO eggshell
We collected shells on the beach.
snail/oyster/clam shells
walnut shells
earrings made out of coconut shell
the shell of a turtle

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: any object that looks like the shell of a snail or sea creature
examples: pasta shells

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a strong feeling of surprise as a result of something happening, especially something unpleasant; the event that causes this feeling
examples: SEE ALSO culture shock
I got a terrible shock the other day.
When I added up the cost it gave me quite a shock.
The news of my promotion came as a shock.
The price came as something of a shock.
She stared at him in shock for a moment.
He's still in a state of shock.
If you think the job will be easy, you're in for a shock.
The party has hardly recovered from the shock of its defeat in May.
She still hadn't got over the shock of seeing him again.
This must be quite a shock for you all.
Her sudden death was a huge shock to the many people who knew her.
Losing in the first round was a shock to the system (= it was more of a shock because it was not expected).
The team suffered a shock defeat in the first round.
Neighbours expressed shock at the news.
He spoke of his shock at the attitude of the two men.
Her shock at finding Elizabeth there was obvious.
It was a shock to find an ambulance outside his house.
It was a bit of a shock for audiences to see him in such a different role.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a serious medical condition, usually the result of injury in which a person has lost a lot of blood and they are extremely weak
examples: SEE ALSO shell shock
Many passengers were treated for shock.
She was taken to hospital suffering from shock.
Others seemed in shock, waiting to be told what to do next.
He isn’t seriously injured but he is in a state of shock.
He had gone into shock and was shaking violently.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a violent shaking movement that is caused by an explosion, earthquake, etc.
examples: COMPARE aftershock
The shock of the explosion could be felt six miles away.
The bumper absorbs shock on impact.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a sudden flow of electricity through a part of the body, causing pain and sometimes death
examples: Don't touch that wire or you'll get a shock.
He gave himself a mild shock while changing a light bulb.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a thick mass of hair on a person’s head
examples: She's a large plump woman with a shock of red hair.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when you pretend to be shocked by something that is not really very serious or surprising
examples: SEE ALSO shock-horror
The article reports on a celebrity who—shock horror—has gained weight!

examples: The figure he came up with was really just a shot in the dark.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to show what is right, appropriate, etc., especially when criticizing somebody’s actions
examples: You shouldn't drink and drive.

A present for me? You shouldn't have! (= used to thank somebody politely)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used for giving or asking for advice
examples: You should stop worrying about it.
Should I call him and apologize?
I should wait a little longer, if I were you.
‘She doesn't think she'll get a job.’ ‘She should worry, with all her qualifications (= she does not need to worry).’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that you expect something is true or will happen
examples: We should arrive before dark.
I should have finished the book by Friday.
The roads should be less crowded today.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that something that was expected has not happened
examples: It should be snowing now, according to the weather forecast.
The bus should have arrived ten minutes ago.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used as the past form of shall when reporting what somebody has said
examples: He asked me what time he should come. (= His words were: ‘What time shall I come?’)
I said (that) I should be glad to help.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used after that when something is suggested or arranged
examples: She recommended that I should take some time off.
In order that training should be effective it must be planned systematically.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used with I and we to give opinions that you are not certain about
examples: I should imagine it will take about three hours.
‘Is this enough food for everyone?’ ‘I should think so.’
‘Will it matter?’ ‘I shouldn't think so.’

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used for expressing strong agreement
examples: ‘I know it's expensive but it will last for years.’ ‘I should hope so too!’
‘Nobody will oppose it.’ ‘I should think not!’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to refuse something or to show that you are annoyed at a request; used to express surprise about an event or a situation
examples: Why should I help him? He's never done anything for me.
How should I know where you've left your bag?
I got on the bus and who should be sitting in front of me but Tony!

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that something would surprise them or make them laugh if they saw or experienced it
examples: You should have seen her face when she found out!

definitions.label: Meaning 11

examples: I'm anxious that we should allow plenty of time.
I find it astonishing that he should be so rude to you.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used with I and we in polite requests
examples: I should like to call my lawyer.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used after I or we instead of would for describing what you would do if something else happened first
examples: If I were asked to work on Sundays, I should resign.

examples: If you should change your mind, do let me know.

examples: The village lay just around the shoulder of the hill.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to treat somebody in a way that is not friendly

definitions.label: Meaning 11

examples: Stop trying to put the blame on somebody else’s shoulders.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to start working very hard at a particular task
examples: Everyone is going to have to put their shoulder to the wheel.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to meet and spend time with a famous person, socially or as part of your job
examples: He’s rubbing shoulders with stars all the time.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to describe a person who listens to your problems and gives you sympathy
examples: He was a fatherly shoulder to cry on when things went wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: physically close to somebody
examples: The large crowd stood shoulder to shoulder in the stands.

definitions.label: Meaning 18

examples: Your dinner comes with a choice of two sides.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: one of the two halves of an animal that has been killed for meat

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: a television channel
examples: What's on the other side?

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to support and agree with somebody
examples: I'm definitely on your side in this.
Whose side are you on anyway?

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: the boyfriend or girlfriend of somebody who is already married or in a steady sexual relationship with somebody else
examples: Is he your bit on the side?

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to choose between two possible choices

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to show too much of a good quality in order to avoid showing too little
examples: I thought it was better to err on the side of caution (= to be too careful rather than take a risk).

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: moving to the left and then to the right and then back again
examples: He shook his head slowly from side to side.
The ship rolled from side to side.
The cat sat with its tail twitching from side to side.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: from or living in a poor area or part of town

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to make somebody pleased with you/annoyed with you

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to be in a bad mood for the whole day for no particular reason

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: said about people who never seem happy with what they have and always think they could be happier in a different place or situation

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to have something as an advantage that will make it more likely that you will achieve something
examples: She may not win this year, but she does have youth on her side.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to know where you can get an advantage for yourself

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to be forced to change from feeling pleased or satisfied to feeling disappointed or annoyed
examples: He’ll be laughing on the other side of his face when he reads my letter.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to fail to give your friends, family, etc. the help and support they expect, or to behave in a way that makes them disappointed
examples: You can always rely on Maggie—she’d never let the side down.
I felt I was letting the side down by not going to the wedding.

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to be cheerful or positive about a bad situation, for example by thinking only of the advantages and not the disadvantages
examples: Look on the bright side. You managed to do more than I did.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to stay with somebody, especially in order to take care of them

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: in or from all directions; everywhere
examples: We realized we were surrounded on all sides.
Disaster threatens on every side.
She was bombarded with questions from all sides.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: slightly too big, small, high, etc.
examples: These shoes are a little on the tight side.
Don’t you think you’re a bit on the short side to play basketball?

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: used to introduce the good points about somebody/something, especially after the bad points have been mentioned
examples: On the credit side, she’s always willing to work very late.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: on the woman’s side of the family

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: out of your way
examples: I left my bags on one side.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: to be dealt with later
examples: I put his complaint to one side until I had more time.
Leaving that to one side for a moment, are there any other questions?

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: younger or older than 40, 50, etc. years of age

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: being especially careful; taking no risks
examples: I took some extra cash just to be on the safe side.

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: in addition to your main job
examples: a mechanic who buys and sells cars on the side

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: secretly or illegally
examples: He's married but he has a girlfriend on the side.

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: served at the same time as the main part of the meal, but on a separate plate

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: in trouble with the police

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: the aspect of a situation that is the opposite of or contrasts with the one you have been talking about

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: with the top part turned to the top; in the correct, normal position
examples: OPPOSITE upside down
I dropped my toast, but luckily it fell right side up.

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: close together and facing in the same direction
examples: There were two children ahead, walking side by side.
The two sat side by side on the bench.

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: together, without any difficulties
examples: We have been using both systems, side by side, for two years.
The two communities exist happily side by side.

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: used to refer to either of two opposite opinions on an issue
examples: The two countries are often on opposite sides of the fence when it comes to climate change.
There are arguments on both sides of the aisle.

definitions.label: Meaning 54
definitions.definition: to laugh a lot at somebody/something

definitions.label: Meaning 55
definitions.definition: to express support for somebody in an argument
examples: She didn't think it was wise to take sides in their argument.

definitions.label: Meaning 56
definitions.definition: to speak to somebody in private, especially in order to warn or tell them about something

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: before a particular time, event, age, etc.
examples: They aren't likely to arrive this side of midnight.

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: a person or thing that repeatedly annoys somebody or stops them from doing something

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody can wait for something to happen or can wait before doing something

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: used to talk about two ways of looking at the same situationWord Origin
examples: Old English sīde ‘left or right part of the body’, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch zijde and German Seite, probably from a base meaning ‘extending lengthways’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take and then let out a long deep breath that can be heard, to show that you are disappointed, sad, tired, etc.
examples: He sighed deeply at the thought.
She sighed with relief that it was all over.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say something with a sigh
examples: ‘Oh well, better luck next time,’ she sighed.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a long sound like a sigh
examples: the sighing of the wind through the trees
branches sighing in the wind

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take and then let out a long deep breath that can be heard, to show that you are disappointed, sad, tired, etc.
examples: He sighed deeply at the thought.
She sighed with relief that it was all over.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say something with a sigh
examples: ‘Oh well, better luck next time,’ she sighed.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a long sound like a sigh
examples: the sighing of the wind through the trees
branches sighing in the wind

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the ability to see
examples: SYNONYM eyesight
to lose your sight (= to become blind)
She has very good sight.
The disease has affected her sight.
He has very little sight in his right eye.
It's important that you have regular sight tests.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of seeing somebody/something
examples: She kept sight of him in her mirror.
She caught sight of a car in the distance.
After ten days at sea, we had our first sight of land.
The mere sight of him makes me want to scream.
The sight of him hobbling off so early in the match depressed everyone.
He laughed quietly to himself at the sight.
I have been known to faint at the sight of blood.
The soldiers were given orders to shoot on sight (= as soon as they saw somebody).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the area or distance within which somebody can see or something can be seen
examples: SEE ALSO line of sight
There was no one in sight.
They stole everything in sight.
The end is in sight (= will happen soon).
The goats ate everything in sight.
At last we came in sight of a few houses.
A bicycle came into sight on the main road.
They marched on and by the following afternoon the enemy was within sight.
He sprinted ahead as they came within sight of the finishing line.
Leave any valuables in your car out of sight.
Keep out of sight (= stay where you cannot be seen).
She never lets her daughter out of her sight (= always keeps her where she can see her).
Get out of my sight! (= Go away!)
The boat disappeared from sight.
The house was hidden from sight behind some trees.
He won't let the children leave his sight.
Her father was nowhere in sight.
The cricket ground was situated within sight of both village pubs.
They waited until the enemy was in plain sight.
He strode by, in full sight of the guards.
He didn't shoot until he had a clear sight of the goal.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a thing that you see or can see
examples: Roadside stalls are a common sight in the city.
It's a spectacular sight as the flamingos lift into the air.
The museum attempts to recreate the sights and sounds of wartime Britain.
He was a sorry sight, soaked to the skin and shivering.
The bird is now a rare sight in this country.
He became a familiar sight on the streets of Oxford.
The gardens were a beautiful sight to behold in the twilight.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the interesting places, especially in a town or city, that are often visited by tourists
examples: We're going to Paris for the weekend to see the sights.
The next day I did the sights of the city.
It's best if you can get someone local to show you the sights.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a person or thing that looks silly, untidy, unpleasant, etc.
examples: She looks a sight in that hat!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a device that you look through to aim a gun, etc. or to look at something through a telescope, etc.
examples: He had the deer in his sights now.
to align the sights on the target
Even as a young actress, she always had Hollywood firmly in her sights (= as her final goal).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: when you first begin to consider something
examples: At first sight, it may look like a generous offer, but always read the small print.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: when you see somebody/something for the first time
examples: It was love at first sight (= we fell in love the first time we saw each other).
We fell in love with the house at first sight.
He looked at first sight like a tourist.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to hate, etc. somebody/something very much
examples: I can't stand the sight of him!
We've shared an office for too long and we're sick of the sight of each other.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to appear, especially when moving gradually closer from a long way off
examples: A ship hove into sight.
Like a galleon in full sail, Cara hove into view.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: in somebody’s opinion
examples: We are all equal in the sight of God.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to recognize somebody without knowing them well

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to become no longer able to see somebody/something
examples: They finally lost sight of land.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to stop considering something; to forget something
examples: We must not lose sight of our original aim.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: not pleasant to look at
examples: You should have seen him in his swimming trunks—not a pretty sight!

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: impossible for anyone to find or see
examples: I wanted to talk to him but he was nowhere to be found.
The children were nowhere to be seen.
A peace settlement is nowhere in sight (= is not likely in the near future).

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say somebody will quickly be forgotten when they are no longer with you

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to expect more/less from a situation
examples: If they can’t afford such a big house, they’ll just have to lower their sights a little.
After failing to get into university, he lowered his sights and got a job in a shop.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to decide that you want something and to try very hard to get it
examples: She's set her sights on getting into Harvard.
I had set my sights on a career in journalism.
He says he wants to win the trophy, but I think he's setting his sights too high.
She has her sights set on becoming a writer.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: very much better; much too good, etc.
examples: She's done a darn sight better than I have.
It's worth a damn sight more than I thought.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: a person or thing that you are pleased to see; something that is very pleasant to look at

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: if you buy something sight unseen, you do not have an opportunity to see it before you buy it
examples: I bought it, sight unseen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an event, an action, a fact, etc. that shows that something exists, is happening or may happen in the future
examples: SYNONYM indication
Looking back, I should have seen the signs.
a clear/visible sign
an encouraging sign
a positive sign
The fact that he didn't say ‘no’ immediately is a good sign.
If I had noticed the warning signs, none of this would have happened.
Early signs point to business improving.
This move will be seen as a sign of weakness.
Bankers say they can definitely detect signs of a recovery.
Headaches may be a sign of stress.
There is no sign of John anywhere.
Soldiers swarmed the city looking for any sign of her.
There was no sign of life in the house (= there seemed to be nobody there).
Her work is showing some signs of improvement.
I hope this incident isn't a sign of things to come.
Get this test if you have signs and symptoms of diabetes.
He is reading the signs all wrong.
Call the police at the first sign of trouble.
The gloomy weather shows no sign of improving.
There is little sign of this happening in the immediate future.
If an interview is too easy, it's a sure sign that you haven't got the job.
There were no outward signs that anything was wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of paper, wood or metal that has writing or a picture on it that gives you information, instructions, a warning, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO lawn sign
to put up/post a sign
to carry/hold a sign
a street/stop sign
a shop/pub sign
a traffic sign
The sign read ‘No Fishing’.
The sign on the wall said ‘Now wash your hands’.
There was a 'Closed' sign in the window.
Follow the signs for the city centre.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a movement or sound that you make to tell somebody something
examples: SEE ALSO V-sign
He gave a thumbs-up sign (= to show approval/agreement).
She was waiting for some kind of sign from him.
At a sign from her, the band would start to play.
He gave a slight bow as a sign of respect.
She shook her head in a desperate sign to tell the child to remain silent.
She nodded as a sign for us to sit down.
Three blasts on the whistle was the sign for visitors to leave.
to make the sign of the cross (= an act of moving one hand in the shape of a cross, done by Christians to show respect for God or by a priest to bless somebody/something)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a mark used to represent something, especially in mathematics
examples: SEE ALSO call sign
a plus/minus sign (= +/−)
a dollar/pound sign (= $/£)
the sign for ‘square root’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a star sign (= one of the twelve signs of the zodiac)
examples: What sign are you?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: something that you feel shows what things are like now, especially how bad they are
examples: The increasing number of people owning guns is an alarming sign of the times.

definitions.definition: a movement or sound that you make to give somebody information, instructions, a warning, etc.
examples: SYNONYM sign
a danger/warning/distress signal
At an agreed signal they left the room.
She made an impatient signal to him, but he ignored her.
He thought he had heard the referee's signal to proceed.
The siren was a signal for everyone to leave the building.
We spotted the scout's signal that four enemy soldiers were coming towards us.
Wait for the signal from the leader of your group.
When I give the signal, run!
All I get is a busy signal when I dial his number (= his phone is being used).
hand signals (= movements that cyclists make with their hands to tell other people that they are going to stop, turn, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of equipment that uses different coloured lights to tell drivers to go slower, stop, etc., used especially on railways and roads
examples: The traffic signals were on red.
a stop signal
Delays are occurring as a result of signal failure on the northbound line.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a series of electrical waves that carry sounds, pictures or messages, for example to a radio, television or mobile phone
examples: SEE ALSO time signal
radio signals
TV signals
a digital signal
a high-frequency signal
a radar signal
to emit a signal
to detect/pick up signals
I couldn't get a signal on my phone.
The signal is received by three different antennas at slightly different times.
The satellite is used for transmitting signals around the world.
The signal from the transmitter seems to have been boosted.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an event, an action, a fact, etc. that shows that something exists or is likely to happen
examples: SYNONYM indication
The rise in inflation is a clear signal that the government's policies are not working.
The court has given a strong signal that it disagrees with the government's position.
Chest pains can be a warning signal of heart problems.
Reducing prison sentences would send the wrong signals to criminals.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: your name as you usually write it, for example at the end of a letter
examples: SEE ALSO e-signature
Someone had forged her signature on the cheque.
They collected 10 000 signatures for their petition.
He was attacked for having put his signature to the deal.
Can you witness my signature on my will, please?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of signing something
examples: Two copies of the contract will be sent to you for signature.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a particular quality that makes something different from other similar things and makes it easy to recognize
examples: Bright colours are his signature.
The signature flavours of Thai cookery are coriander and lime.
Each song bears the signature of its performer.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the importance of something, especially when this has an effect on what happens in the future
examples: a decision of major political significance
The new drug has great significance for the treatment of the disease.
They discussed the statistical significance of the results.
We should be fully aware of the significance of television in shaping our ideas.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the meaning of something
examples: COMPARE insignificance
She couldn't grasp the full significance of what he had said.
Do these symbols have any particular significance?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: large or important enough to have an effect or to be noticed
examples: COMPARE insignificant
There are no significant differences between the two groups of students.
Your work has shown a significant improvement.
a significant increase/decrease/reduction/loss
a significant amount/number/part/portion
significant change/progress
The results of the experiment are not statistically significant.
These views are held by a significant proportion of the population.
The 1992 reform made very significant contributions to the development of many rural areas.
The drug has had no significant effect on stopping the spread of the disease.
Asthma has a significant impact on the life and well-being of children affected by this disease.
The offender was assessed as posing a significant risk to others.
It is significant that girls generally do better in examinations than boys.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having a particular meaning
examples: The fact that her remarks were leaked to the media in advance is highly significant.
It is significant that he changed his will only days before his death.
This year's event is particularly significant as it takes place on the centenary of his birth.
rituals which are deeply significant to Christians
November 16th will always be an especially significant day for us, thanks to the birth of our second grandchild.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having a special or secret meaning that is not understood by everyone
examples: SYNONYM meaningful
a significant look/smile

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that is large or important enough to have an effect on something or to be noticed
examples: significantly higher/lower/larger/smaller
The two sets of figures are not significantly different.
to differ/vary/change significantly
significantly greater/better
significantly more/less/fewer
Profits have increased significantly over the past few years.
The high school dropout rate has significantly decreased since then.
The risks can be significantly reduced by paying close attention to diet and lifestyle.
Your decision will significantly affect your future.
These services will significantly improve the quality of life for older people in the area.
Einstein contributed significantly to the early development of quantum mechanics.
Food prices are significantly lower in the US.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a way that has a particular meaning
examples: Significantly, he did not deny that there might be an election.
Perhaps significantly, many of their illegal activities were not considered as crime.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a way that has a special or secret meaning
examples: She paused significantly before she answered.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a complete lack of noise or sound
examples: SYNONYM quiet
Their footsteps echoed in the silence.
A scream broke the silence of the night.
I need absolute silence when I'm working.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a situation when nobody is speaking
examples: an embarrassed/awkward/uncomfortable silence
a moment’s stunned silence
I got used to his long silences.
They finished their meal in total silence.
She lapsed into silence again.
There was a deafening silence (= one that is very noticeable).
a two-minute silence in honour of those who had died
Her accusations reduced him to silence.
He’s not one to suffer in silence! (= to suffer without telling somebody)
There was a moment of uncomfortable silence.
They observed a two-minute silence in memory of the children.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a situation in which somebody refuses to talk about something or to answer questions
examples: She broke her public silence in a TV interview.
The company's silence on the subject has been taken as an admission of guilt.
the right to silence (= the legal right not to say anything when you are arrested)
There is a conspiracy of silence about what is happening (= everyone has agreed not to discuss it).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a situation in which people do not communicate with each other by letter or phone
examples: The phone call came after months of silence.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a situation when people do not say anything, but feel embarrassed or uncomfortable

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an occasion when nobody speaks, although people are aware that there are feelings or thoughts to express
examples: There was a pregnant pause before she replied.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: it is often best not to say anythingWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old French, from Latin silentium, from silere ‘be silent’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: where there is little or no sound; making little or no sound
examples: SYNONYM quiet
At last the traffic fell silent.
The streets were silent and deserted.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not speaking
examples: to remain/stay/keep silent
As the curtain rose, the audience fell silent.
He gave me the silent treatment (= did not speak to me because he was angry).
Half the room went silent and turned to see what was happening.
They huddled together in silent groups.
The mayor was silent for a moment.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not expressed with words or sound
examples: a silent prayer/protest
They nodded in silent agreement.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: written but not pronounced
examples: The ‘b’ in ‘lamb’ is silent.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: with pictures but no sound
examples: a silent film/movie
stars of the silent screen

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not talking very much
examples: SYNONYM quiet
He's the strong silent type.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: not giving information about something; refusing to speak about something
examples: The report is strangely silent on this issue.
the right to remain silent (= the legal right not to say anything when you are arrested)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: fine soft thread produced by silkworms
examples: The caterpillar spins the silk around its entire body.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a type of fine smooth cloth made from silk thread; a piece of this cloth
examples: SEE ALSO watered silk
a silk dress/blouse/scarf/tie/sari
silk stockings
made of pure silk
Her skin was as smooth as silk.
fine silks produced in Italy

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: thread made of silk used for sewing

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: clothes made of silk, especially the coloured shirts worn by people riding horses in a race (= jockeys)
examples: ladies in silks and satins

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a type of lawyer who represents the government (= a King’s Counsel / Queen’s Counsel)
examples: to take silk (= to become this type of lawyer)

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: (you won't) succeed in making something good out of material that does not seem very good at allWord Origin
examples: Old English sioloc, seolec, from late Latin sericum, neuter of Latin sericus, based on Greek Sēres, the name given to the inhabitants of the Far Eastern countries from which silk first came overland to Europe.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: showing a lack of thought, understanding, or judgement
examples: SYNONYM foolish
a silly idea/question/name
That was a silly thing to do!
It sounds silly, I know, but think about it.
Her work is full of silly mistakes.
‘I can walk home.’ ‘Don't be silly—it's much too far!’
The answers they give are plain silly.
You silly boy!
It would have been silly to pretend that I wasn't upset.
It would be silly of me to say no.
How silly of me to expect them to help!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: stupid or embarrassing, especially in a way that is more typical of a child than an adult
examples: SYNONYM ridiculous
a silly sense of humour
a silly game
He would never dance in case he looked silly.
I feel silly in these clothes.
She had a silly grin on her face.
This is getting silly! I think we had all better calm down.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not practical or serious
examples: We had to wear these silly little hats.
Why worry about a silly thing like that?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: extremely bored
examples: I remember being bored stiff during my entire time at school.
She enjoys it. Everyone else is bored silly.
He walked along, bored out of his mind.
She was alone all day and bored to death.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to drink, laugh, shout, etc. so much that you cannot behave in a sensible way

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not to treat a situation seriously, especially in order to cheat somebody
examples: Don't play silly games with me; I know you did it.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to behave in a stupid and annoying way
examples: Stop playing silly buggers and give me a hand with this!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a chemical element. Silver is a shiny, grey-white precious metal used for making coins, jewellery, beautiful objects, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO sterling silver
a silver ring/chain
made of solid silver
a silver mine

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a shiny grey-white colour
examples: SEE ALSO silvery
There was a streak of silver in her hair.
the shimmering silver of the moon

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: dishes, beautiful objects, etc. that are made of silver
examples: Thieves stole £5 000 worth of silver.
They've had to sell the family silver to pay the bills.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: coins that are made of silver or a metal that looks like silver
examples: I need £2 in silver for the parking meter.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a medal that is given to the person or the team that wins the second prize in a race or competition
examples: She won silver in last year's championships.
The team won two silvers and a bronze.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: having rich parents

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to give somebody money so that they will do you a favour, especially tell your fortune

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: every sad or difficult situation has a positive side

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: if you are given something on a silver platter, you do not have to do much to get it
examples: These rich kids expect to have it all handed to them on a silver platter.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: like somebody/something but not exactly the same
examples: OPPOSITE different
We have very similar interests.
The experiment was repeated, with similar results.
I came across a similar situation last year.
The brothers look very similar.
The three portraits are remarkably similar.
My teaching style is similar to that of most other teachers.
The case is strikingly similar to another case from the 1990s.
The two houses are similar in size.
All the narratives follow a similar pattern.
The disease attacks the immune system in a similar way to AIDS.
She easily won today, and hopes to carry on in a similar vein tomorrow.
Stir the paint with a piece of wood or something similar.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of being similar to somebody/something but not exactly the same
examples: SYNONYM resemblance
The report highlights the similarity between the two groups.
She bears a striking similarity to her mother.
There is some similarity in the way they sing.
In this work we can observe the stylistic similarity with Beethoven.
The results also showed the similarity of the two groups.
They are both doctors but that is where the similarity ends.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a feature that things or people have that makes them like each other
examples: SYNONYM resemblance
a study of the similarities and differences between the two countries
similarities in/of style
The karate bout has many similarities to a boxing match.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in almost the same way
examples: It is a little cheaper than other similarly sized cars.
He has a similarly impressive record in the sport.
Husband and wife were similarly successful in their chosen careers.
The different groups of women in the study responded similarly.
All sections of society were similarly affected by the war.
Phosphorus behaves similarly to nitrogen.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that two facts, actions, statements, etc. are like each other
examples: LANGUAGE BANK AT contrast
The United States won most of the track and field events. Similarly, in swimming, the top three places went to Americans.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not complicated; easy to understand or do
examples: SYNONYM easy
a simple solution/explanation/question/task/example
You will soon see that what once seemed impossible is now simple for you.
This machine is very simple to use.
The game is supposed to be simple for anyone to play.
It's too simple to blame the lack of manufacturing jobs on the last government.
Give the necessary information but keep it simple.
It would be much simpler for me to go there myself and sort things out.
We lost because we played badly. It's as simple as that.
If you enjoy your workout, you'll want to do it. It's that simple.
It all sounds simple enough.
Let me make it simple —this is going to take years to do.
These are bad guys, plain and simple.
The answer is really quite simple.
There must be a simpler way of doing this.
In simple terms, the more saturated fat something contains, the less healthy it is.
a relatively simple process

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: basic or plain without anything extra or unnecessary
examples: OPPOSITE fancy
simple but elegant clothes
We had a simple meal of soup and bread.
The accommodation is simple but spacious.
The simple things in life are often the best.
He was pleased to live the simple life and enjoy nature around him.
simple pleasures, like reading and walking
The engine design is elegantly simple.
contemporary furniture that is simple in design

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used before a noun to emphasize that it is exactly that and nothing else
examples: We cannot ignore the simple fact that the country cannot sustain the current level of economic growth.
The simple truth is that we just can't afford it.
It's a simple matter of giving them enough to eat.
It was a matter of simple survival.
It's nothing to worry about—just a simple headache.
I had to do it for the simple reason that (= because) I couldn't trust anyone else.
A simple majority is all that is required.
The simple act of eating raises your metabolism.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: consisting of only a few parts; not complicated in structure
examples: simple forms of life, for example amoebas
a simple machine
a simple sentence (= one with only one verb)
a simple model of a business market

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: ordinary; not special
examples: I'm a simple country girl.
The poem describes simple young soldiers in the Civil War.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not very intelligent; not mentally normal
examples: He's not mad—just a little simple.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to describe the present or past tense of a verb that is formed without using an auxiliary verb, as in She loves him (= the simple present tense) or He arrived late (= the simple past tense)

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used after the noun that it refers to in order to emphasize that there is nothing but the thing you have just mentioned involved in something
examples: It's laziness, pure and simple.
The man wants revenge, pure and simple.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how easy or basic something is
examples: SYNONYM just
To order, simply click here.
This is not to suggest we simply ignore the problem.
She says that the company was simply trying to protect its business.
Simply add hot water and stir.
The runway is simply a strip of grass.
Fame is often simply a matter of being in the right place at the right time.
You can enjoy all the water sports, or simply lie on the beach.
We are simply saying research is good.
Most internet users simply want information.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a way that is easy to understand
examples: The book explains grammar simply and clearly.
Anyway, to put it simply, we still owe them £2 000.
Simply put, electronic music is anything made using technology.
Put simply, cells contain an inbuilt mechanism which determines their lifespan.
Simply stated, the time for major reform is now.
It is in many ways a simple story, simply told.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a way that is natural and plain
examples: The rooms are simply furnished.
They live simply (= they do not spend much money).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a statement
examples: SYNONYM absolutely
You simply must see the play.
You simply have to come with us.
He simply refused to believe it.
The view is simply wonderful!
That is simply not true!
This information is simply wrong.
Her behaviour is simply unacceptable.
I haven't seen her for simply ages.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to introduce a summary or an explanation of something that you have just said or done
examples: I don't want to be rude, it's simply that we have to be careful who we give this information to.
He was loud, vulgar and arrogant—quite simply the rudest man I've ever met!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to create particular conditions that exist in real life using computers, models, etc., usually for study or training purposes
examples: Computer software can be used to simulate conditions on the seabed.
Role-playing is a useful way of simulating real-life situations.
The device simulates conditions in space quite closely.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be made to look like something else
examples: a gas heater that simulates a coal fire

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to pretend that you have a particular feeling
examples: SYNONYM feign
I tried to simulate surprise at the news.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a situation in which a particular set of conditions is created artificially in order to study or experience something that could exist in reality
examples: a computer simulation of how the planet functions
a simulation model
An important part of training is role-play and the simulation of court cases.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of pretending that something is real when it is not
examples: the simulation of concern

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: at the same time as something else
examples: The game will be broadcast simultaneously on TV and radio.
The slowdown of the US economy occurred simultaneously with a downturn in Europe.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an offence against God or against a religious or moral law
examples: SEE ALSO deadly sin
to commit a sin
Confess your sins to God and he will forgive you.
God forgives our sins.
The Bible says that stealing is a sin.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of breaking a religious or moral law
examples: SEE ALSO sinful
a life of sin
Believers are called on to turn away from sin and embrace a life of prayer.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an action that people think is very bad
examples: SEE ALSO cardinal sin
It's a sin to waste taxpayers' money like that.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that something that somebody does is like a punishment
examples: She works with us in Accounts, for her sins!

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to hide the real situation or facts when these are not good or pleasant
examples: She was dressed in loose comfortable clothes that hid a multitude of sins.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to live together and have a sexual relationship without being married

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that somebody is very unhappy or uglyWord Origin
examples: noun Old English synn (noun), syngian (verb); probably related to Latin sons, sont- ‘guilty’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: from a time in the past until a later past time, or until now
examples: She's been off work since Tuesday.
We've lived here since 2006.
I haven't eaten since breakfast.
He's been working in a bank since leaving school.
Since the party she had only spoken to him once.
‘They've split up.’ ‘Since when?’
That was years ago. I've changed jobs since then.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used when you are showing that you are angry about something
examples: Since when did he ever listen to me?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: showing what you really think or feel
examples: SYNONYM genuine
a sincere apology
a sincere attempt to resolve the problem
sincere regret
Please accept our sincere thanks.
We offer our sincere sympathy to the two families.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: saying only what you really think or feel
examples: SYNONYM honest
He seemed sincere enough when he said he wanted to help.
She is never completely sincere in what she says about people.
I think he is sincere in his desire to keep the economy growing.
his refusal to be sincere about his feelings

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act of singing
examples: Let's have a sing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who sings, or whose job is singing, especially in public
examples: SEE ALSO carol singer
She's a wonderful singer.
a pop/country/folk singer
He trained as an opera singer.
the band's lead singer
a singer in a German rock band
a singer of classical Javanese songs
She became a singer with various local bands.
His main ambition is to become a singer songwriter.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activity of making musical sounds with your voice
examples: the beautiful singing of birds
the singing of hymns/songs/carols
choral singing
There was singing and dancing all night.
a singing teacher
She has a beautiful singing voice.
The sound of singing came from the kitchen.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: only one
examples: He sent her a single red rose.
a single-sex school (= for boys only or for girls only)
All these jobs can now be done by one single machine.
We won by a single point.
They cloned a lamb from a single cell taken from an adult sheep.
the European single currency, the euro
a single honours degree (= for which you study only one subject)
It was the work of a single individual.
The statue was carved out of a single piece of wood.
You can switch between the single player and the multiplayer games.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: intended to be used by only one person
examples: COMPARE double
a single room
The jail housed 860 prisoners in single cells.
a single sheet (= large enough for a single bed)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not married or having a romantic relationship with somebody
examples: SEE ALSO single parent
a single person/woman/man
The apartments are ideal for single people living alone.
Are you still single?
She remained single till her death.
Young people are staying single for longer.
The film stars Bening as a single mother with a teenage son.
I'm a single father and take my kids to school every morning.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a single ticket, etc. can be used for travelling to a place but not back again
examples: COMPARE return (7)
a single ticket
How much is the single fare to Glasgow?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you are referring to one particular person or thing on its own
examples: Unemployment is the single most important factor in the growing crime rates.
We eat rice every single day.
Every single one of her so-called friends had turned their backs on her.
I couldn't understand a single word she said!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: immediately; with only a quick look
examples: She is able to take in complex information at a single glance.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in one single attempt or try
examples: She blew out the candles in a single go.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: (in) one line, one behind the other
examples: They made their way in single file along the cliff path.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to go down below the surface or towards the bottom of a liquid or soft substance
examples: The ship sank to the bottom of the sea.
The submarine sank after an explosion.
We're sinking!
The wheels started to sink into the mud.
The little boat sank beneath the waves.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to damage a boat or ship so that it goes below the surface of the sea, etc.
examples: The battleship was sunk by a torpedo.
Bombs sank all four carriers.
Five brothers all died when their ship was sunk.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move downwards, especially by falling or sitting down
examples: SYNONYM collapse
I sank into an armchair.
She sank back into her seat, exhausted.
The old man had sunk to his knees.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to move slowly downwards
examples: The sun was sinking in the west.
The sun had sunk below the horizon.
The foundations of the building are starting to sink.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to decrease in amount, volume, strength, etc.
examples: The pound has sunk to its lowest recorded level against the dollar.
He is clearly sinking fast (= getting weaker quickly and will soon die).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to become quieter
examples: SYNONYM fade
Her voice sank to a whisper.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to make a deep hole in the ground
examples: SYNONYM drill
to sink a well/shaft/mine

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to place something in the ground by digging
examples: SEE ALSO sunken
to sink a post into the ground

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to prevent somebody or somebody’s plans from succeeding
examples: I think I've just sunk my chances of getting the job.
If the car breaks down, we'll be sunk (= have serious problems).

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to hit a ball into a hole in golf or snooker
examples: He sank a 12-foot putt to win the match.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to drink something quickly, especially a large amount of alcohol
examples: They sank three pints each in 10 minutes.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be in a state of unhappiness or deep thought
examples: She just sat there, sunk in thought.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to talk about people who leave an organization, a company, etc. that is having difficulties, without caring about the people who are left

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody suddenly feels sad or depressed about something
examples: My heart sank when I saw how much work there was left.
She watched him go with a sinking heart.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to agree to forget about your disagreements
examples: We need to sink our differences and present a united opposition to the plan.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: an unpleasant feeling that you get when you realize that something bad has happened or is going to happen
examples: I had a horrible sinking feeling when I saw the ambulance outside the house.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to be in a situation where you will either succeed by your own efforts or fail completely
examples: The new students were just left to sink or swim.
In a situation like this, you either sink or swim.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to have such low moral standards that you do something very bad
examples: Stealing from your friends? How could you sink so low?
I can't believe that anyone would sink to such depths.
With this article the newspaper has sunk to a new low.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to behave in a worse way than ever before
examples: The government has stooped to an all-time low with this policy.
Reality TV has sunk to new lows.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used as a polite way of addressing a man whose name you do not know, for example in a shop or restaurant
examples: COMPARE ma’am
Good morning, sir. Can I help you?
Are you ready to order, sir?
‘Thank you very much.’ ‘You're welcome, sir. Have a nice day.’

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used at the beginning of a formal business letter when you do not know the name of the man or people that you are dealing with
examples: Dear Sir/Sirs
Dear Sir or Madam

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a title that is used before the first name of a man who has received one of the highest British honours (= a knight), or before the first name of a baronet
examples: COMPARE lady
Sir Paul McCartney
Thank you, Sir Paul.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used as a form of address to a man in a position of authority, especially in the armed forces
examples: ‘Report to me tomorrow, corporal!’ ‘Yes, sir!’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used as a form of address by children in school to a male teacher
examples: COMPARE miss
Please, sir, can I open a window?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: certainly not
examples: We will never allow that to happen! No sir!

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something is true
examples: That's a fine car you have. Yes sir!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a girl or woman who has the same mother and father as another person
examples: SEE ALSO cousin sister
She's my sister.
an older/a younger sister
a big/little sister
a kid sister
my twin sister
We're sisters.
the Brontë sisters—Charlotte, Emily and Anne
Do you have any brothers or sisters?
He married the sister of his best friend.
She's the sister of the bride.
Joe's sister Mary lives in Seattle.
My best friend has been like a sister to me (= very close).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used for talking to or about other members of a women’s organization or other women who have the same ideas, purpose, etc. as yourself
examples: They supported their sisters in the dispute.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a senior female nurse who is in charge of a hospital ward
examples: SEE ALSO charge nurse

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a female member of a religious group, especially a nun
examples: Sister Mary
the Sisters of Charity

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: (in the US) a member of a sorority (= a club for a group of female students at a college or university)
examples: Carolyn's sorority sisters at Indiana University

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used by black people as a form of address for a black woman

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a thing that belongs to the same type or group as something else
examples: our sister company in Italy
a sister ship

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to rest your weight on your bottom with your back straight, for example on/in a chair
examples: SEE ALSO sit down
She sat and stared at the letter in front of her.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

The drawers slide in and out easily.
She slid her hand along the rail.
You can slide the front seats forward if necessary.
The automatic doors slid open.
Quietly, she slid the drawer shut.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: SYNONYM slip
He slid into bed.
She slid out while no one was looking.
The man slid the money quickly into his pocket.
He slid a shy look at Claire.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: Shares slid to a 10-year low.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

The economy is sliding rapidly downhill.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

slightly higher/lower/larger/smaller

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to slide a short distance by accident so that you fall or nearly fall
examples: She slipped and landed flat on her back.

She got on her feet and ran towards the door, slipping and sliding.
He slipped on a bar of soap in the shower room.
She slipped over on the ice and broke her leg.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to slide out of position or out of your hand
examples: My hand slipped as I was slicing the bread and I cut myself.
His hat had slipped over one eye.
The fish slipped out of my hand.
The child slipped from his grasp and ran off.
She was careful not to let her control slip.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to go somewhere quickly and quietly, especially without being noticed
examples: SYNONYM creep
She slipped out of the house before the others were awake.
I slipped away before the end of the performance.
The ship slipped into the harbour at night.
A guard was posted at the door, in case anyone tried to slip in.
She knew that time was slipping away.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to put something somewhere quickly, quietly or secretly
examples: Anna slipped her hand into his.
He slipped the letter back into its envelope.
He beat three defenders before slipping the ball past the goalkeeper.
She slipped her head around the door.
I managed to slip a few jokes into my speech.
I managed to slip in a few jokes.
He slipped the ring onto her finger.
They'd slipped some money to the guards.
They'd slipped the guards some money.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to fall to a lower level; to become worse
examples: Standards have slipped in the last few years.
His popularity has slipped recently.
The director never lets the tension slip.
That's three times she's beaten me—I must be slipping!
A defeat would see them slip down the rankings.
Already the Conservatives are slipping in the polls.
Pre-tax profits slipped from $3.9 million to $3.7 million,.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to pass into a particular state or situation, especially a difficult or unpleasant one
examples: He began to slip into debt.
The patient had slipped into a coma.
We seem to have slipped behind schedule.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to put clothes on or to take them off quickly and easily
examples: to slip into/out of a dress
to slip your shoes on/off
He slipped a coat over his sweatshirt.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to get free; to make something/somebody/yourself free from something
examples: The ship had slipped its moorings in the night.
The dog slipped its collar.
The animal had slipped free and escaped.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to give somebody information that is supposed to be secret
examples: I happened to let it slip that he had given me £1 000 for the car.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to miss or fail to use an opportunity
examples: Don't let the chance to work abroad slip through your fingers.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: (to become) out of control
examples: She said nothing in case her temper slipped out of gear.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be easy to say or pronounce
examples: It's not a name that exactly trips off the tongue, is it?

definitions.label: Meaning 13

examples: I’m sorry I didn’t tell you. It completely slipped my mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 14

definitions.label: Meaning 15

examples: an advertising slogan
a campaign slogan

definitions.label: Meaning 1

a grassy slope

definitions.definition: an area of land that is part of a mountain or hill
examples: the eastern slopes of the Andes
ski slopes

examples: a steep slope
a gentle slope

the angle of slope

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: She realized he was on the slippery slope towards a life of crime.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: I missed the fast train and had to get the slow one (= the one that stops at all the stations).

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 6

a bunch of sweet-smelling flowers
His breath smelt of garlic.
When he did come home, he smelled of alcohol.
The house smelt of cedar wood and fresh polish.
What does the perfume smell like?

The crisp air smells like clean hay.

The dog had smelt a rabbit.
I could smell alcohol on his breath.
Snow fell so that you could almost smell the cold.
Can you smell something burning?
As she came downstairs, she smelled bacon cooking.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

I can't smell anything because I've got a bad cold.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to put your nose near something and breathe in so that you can discover or identify its smell

Smell this and tell me what you think it is.
I bent down to smell the flowers.
He leaned in closer and smelled the perfume she was wearing.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have an unpleasant smell
examples: The drains smell.
Does my breath smell?
He hadn't washed for days and was beginning to smell.
After a few days, the meat began to smell.
It smells in here.
It smells awful in here.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to feel that something exists or is going to happen
examples: He smelt danger.
I can smell trouble.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the grey, white or black gas that is produced by something burning
examples: SEE ALSO second-hand smoke
cigarette/tobacco smoke
Plumes of black smoke could be seen rising from the area.
The explosion sent a huge cloud of smoke into the sky.
Clouds of thick black smoke billowed from the car's exhaust.
His eyes were smarting from the smoke from the fire.
The smoke from their cigarettes curled upwards.
The majority of people who die in fires die of smoke inhalation.
Check your smoke detectors for dead batteries.
The witch disappeared in a puff of smoke.
I can definitely smell smoke.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an act of smoking a cigarette
examples: Are you coming outside for a smoke?
He's in the back garden having a smoke.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: London, or another large city

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to try to trick somebody or lie to somebody, particularly by saying something is better than it really is

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be completely burnt
examples: The whole house went up in smoke.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if your plans, hopes, etc. go up in smoke, they fail completely
examples: Hopes of an early end to the dispute have gone up in smoke.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: if something bad is being said about somebody/something, it usually has some truth in it

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the fact of hiding the truth with information that is not important or relevant
examples: There's a lot of smoke and mirrors in the financing of this film.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: Old English smoca (noun), smocian (verb), from the Germanic base of smēocan ‘emit smoke’; related to Dutch smook and German Schmauch.

He's trying to stop smoking.
She started smoking at university.
to take up/quit smoking
the harmful effects of cigarette smoking
Your GP can provide advice on smoking cessation.
the introduction of the smoking ban in pubs, restaurants, and hotels

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: completely flat and even, without any rough areas or holes
examples: OPPOSITE rough
the smooth surface of the metal
a lotion to make your skin feel soft and smooth
The water was as smooth as glass.
a paint that gives a smooth, silky finish
Over the years, the stone steps had worn smooth.
They noticed her perfectly smooth white skin.
The new motorway surfaces were smooth as silk.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: without any solid pieces
examples: Mix the flour with the milk to form a smooth paste.
Once the mixture is smooth, spread it over the cake.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: happening or continuing without any problems
examples: They are introducing new measures to ensure the smooth running of the business.
a fairly smooth transition to democracy
They could not ensure a smooth transfer of political power.
The project got off to a remarkably smooth start.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: even and regular, without sudden stops and starts
examples: The car's improved suspension gives you a smoother ride.
The plane made a smooth landing.
She swung herself over the gate in one smooth movement.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: very polite and pleasant, but in a way that is often not very sincere
examples: SYNONYM smarmy
I don't like him. He's far too smooth for me.
He's something of a smooth operator.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: pleasant and not bitter
examples: This coffee has a smooth, rich taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: nice to hear, and without any rough or unpleasant sounds

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be simple and free from troubleWord Origin
examples: Old English smōth, probably of Germanic origin, though no cognates are known. The verb dates from Middle English.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a reptile with a very long thin body and no legs. There are many types of snake, some of which are poisonous.
examples: SEE ALSO coral snake
a snake coiled up in the grass
a poisonous/deadly snake
Venomous snakes spit and hiss when they are cornered.
snake venom
There has been an increase in snake bite cases.
He writhed and hissed like a snake.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who pretends to be your friend but who cannot be trusted
examples: I came to realize that he's just a snake in the grass.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to break something suddenly with a sharp noise; to be broken in this way
examples: The wind had snapped the tree in two.
He snapped a twig off a bush.
Suddenly, the rope snapped.
The branch she was standing on must have snapped off.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take a photograph
examples: A passing tourist snapped the incident.
She seemed oblivious to the crowds of photographers snapping away.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move, or to move something, into a particular position quickly, especially with a sudden sharp noise
examples: The lid snapped shut.
His eyes snapped open.
He snapped to attention and saluted.
The plastic pieces snap together to make a replica of a dinosaur.
She snapped the bag shut.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to speak or say something in an impatient, usually angry, voice
examples: ‘Don't just stand there,’ she snapped.
I was tempted to snap back angrily at him.
He snapped a reply.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to try to bite somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM nip
The dogs snarled and snapped at our heels.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to suddenly be unable to control your feelings any longer because the situation has become too difficult
examples: My patience finally snapped.
When he said that, something snapped inside her.
And that did it. I snapped.
I guess he just snapped.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to fasten a piece of clothing with a snap

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to start play by passing the ball back between your legs
examples: Time will not be resumed until the ball is snapped on the next play.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to shout at somebody in an angry way, especially without reason

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make a sharp noise by moving your second or third finger quickly against your thumb, to attract somebody’s attention, or to mark the beat of music, for example
examples: He snapped his fingers for the waiter to bring more wine.
He snapped his fingers and the waiter came running.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make an effort to stop feeling unhappy or depressed; to help somebody to stop feeling unhappy
examples: You've been depressed for weeks. It's time you snapped out of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used, especially in orders, to tell somebody to start working harder or more quicklyWord Origin
examples: late 15th cent. (in the senses ‘make a sudden audible bite’ and ‘quick sharp biting sound’): probably from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German snappen ‘seize’; partly imitative.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: small soft white pieces (called flakes) of frozen water that fall from the sky in cold weather; this substance when it is lying on the ground
examples: Snow was falling heavily.
We had snow in May this year.
The snow was beginning to melt.
Heavy snow is expected tomorrow.
Children were playing in the snow.
She saw them trudging through the snow towards the house.
We got over 100 inches of snow last winter.
There was almost a foot of snow on the ground.
20 cm of snow were expected today.
The snow didn't settle (= stay on the ground).
The snow and ice caused a number of traffic accidents.
Last week's cold temperatures were accompanied by rain and snow.
Her skin was as white as snow.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an amount of snow that falls in one particular place or at one particular time
examples: the first snows of winter
the snows of Everest

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: extremely clean, pure, etc.Word Origin
examples: Old English snāw, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch sneeuw and German Schnee, from an Indo-European root shared by Latin nix, niv- and Greek nipha.
