definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to such a great degree
examples: Don't look so angry.
There's no need to worry so.
Why has it taken so long?
That wasn't so bad, was it?
She spoke so quietly (that) I could hardly hear her.
What is it that's so important it can't wait five minutes?
He was so impressed that he jumped up and down with excitement.
She gets so caught up in her fame that she neglects her true friends.
It was so incredibly cheap it was unbelievable.
I'm not so stupid as to believe that.
Would you be so kind as to lock the door when you leave?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very; extremely
examples: I'm so glad to see you.
The girls looked so pretty in their summer dresses.
I was pleased that so many people turned up.
We have so much to do.
It's so good to have you back.
We've worked so hard to get to this point.
They came so close to winning.
You're going to Harvard! That's so great!
Their attitude is so very English.
The article was just so much (= nothing but) nonsense.
I am so pleased with this new book.
He sat there ever so quietly.
I do love it so.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not to the same degree
examples: I haven't enjoyed myself so much for a long time.
I have never felt so humiliated in my entire life.
It wasn't so good as last time.
It's not so easy as you'd think.
He was not so quick a learner as his brother.
It's not so much a hobby as a career (= more like a career than a hobby).
Off she went without so much as (= without even) a ‘goodbye’.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show the size, amount or number of something
examples: The fish was about so big (= said when using your hands to show the size).
There are only so many (= only a limited number of) hours in a day.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to refer back to something that has already been mentioned
examples: ‘Is he coming?’ ‘I hope so.’
‘Did they mind?’ ‘I don't think so.’
If she notices, she never says so.
I might be away next week. If so, I won't be able to see you.
We are very busy—so much so that we won't be able to take time off this year.
Programs are expensive, and even more so if you have to keep altering them.
I hear that you're a writer—is that so (= is that true)?
George is going to help me, or so he says (= that is what he says but I am not sure if I believe him).
They asked me to call them and I did so (= I called).
She leaked the story to the media and, in so doing, helped bring down the president.
He thinks I dislike him but that just isn't so.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: also
examples: Times have changed and so have I.
‘I prefer the first version.’ ‘So do we.’
Temperatures are rising in Canada, and so too are the annual blueberry harvests.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to agree that something is true, especially when you are surprised
examples: ‘You were there, too.’ ‘So I was—I'd forgotten.’
‘There's another one.’ ‘So there is.’

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used, often with a negative, before adjectives and noun phrases to emphasize something that you are saying
examples: He is so not the right person for you.
That is so not cool.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used, especially by children, to say that what somebody says is not the case and the opposite is true
examples: ‘You're not telling the truth, are you?’ ‘I am, so!’

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used when you are showing somebody how to do something or telling them how something happened
examples: Stand with your arms out, so.
So it was that he finally returned home.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used at the end of a list to show that it continues in the same way
examples: We discussed everything—when to go, what to see and so on.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to give an important extra reason why something is true
examples: His achievement is remarkable; all the more so because he had no help at all.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used after a number, an amount, etc. to show that it is not exact
examples: There were twenty or so (= about twenty) people there.
We stayed for an hour or so.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: with the intention of doing something
examples: We went early so as to get good seats.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to show that you accept something and will not try to change it or cannot change it
examples: If he doesn't want to be involved, then so be it.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to show that you have finished talking about something
examples: So much for the situation in Germany. Now we turn our attention to France.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to suggest that something has not been successful or useful
examples: So much for that idea!

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: in such a way that
examples: The programme has been so organized that none of the talks overlap.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to introduce the word that people usually use to describe something
examples: artists from the so-called ‘School of London’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to put something in liquid for a time so that it becomes completely wet; to become completely wet in this way
examples: I usually soak the beans overnight.
If you soak the tablecloth before you wash it, the stains should come out.
He soaked the cloth with petrol.
Leave the apricots to soak for 20 minutes.
I'm going to go and soak in the bath.
Soak the clothes in cold water.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something completely wet
examples: SYNONYM drench
A sudden shower of rain soaked the spectators.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to enter or pass through something
examples: Blood had soaked through the bandage.
The rain had soaked through every layer of his clothing.
Water dripped off the table and soaked into the carpet.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to obtain a lot of money from somebody by making them pay very high taxes or prices
examples: He was accused of soaking his clients.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a substance that you use with water for washing your body
examples: SEE ALSO soft soap
Wash the affected area with soap and water.
a bar/cake of soap
soap bubbles
Avoid using perfumed soaps on sensitive skin.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a soap opera (= a story about the lives and problems of a group of people that is broadcast every day or several times a week on television or radio)
examples: soaps on TV
She's a US soap star.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: if the value, amount or level of something soars, it rises very quickly
examples: soaring costs/prices/temperatures
Air pollution will soon soar above safety levels.
Unemployment has soared to 18 per cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to rise quickly and smoothly up into the air
examples: The rocket soared (up) into the air.
Her spirits soared (= she became very happy and excited).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to fly very high in the air or remain high in the air
examples: an eagle soaring high above the cliffs

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be very high or tall
examples: soaring mountains
The building soared above us.
The cliffs soared upward.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: when music soars, it becomes higher or louder
examples: soaring strings

definitions.definition: if you make a song and dance about something, you complain or talk about it too much when this is not necessary
examples: She gives generously to charity without making a song and dance about it.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a long explanation about something, or excuse for somethingWord Origin
examples: Old English sang, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch zang and German Sang, also to sing.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a short time from now; a short time after something else has happened
examples: She sold the house soon after her husband died.
Soon afterwards, he joined a youth theatre group.
I'd love to meet up again sometime soon.
I soon realized the mistake.
See you soon!
More success soon followed.
We’ll be home soon./We’ll soon be home.
I'll be back soon.
It soon became clear that the programme was a failure.
He promises to visit again soon.
Coming soon to a cinema/theater near you: 'War of the Wizards II'.
He moved in with a friend and soon found work.
The two men soon discovered they had much in common.
The trial is expected to start soon.
Soon thereafter (= soon after that), she returned to Tanzania.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: early; quickly
examples: SEE ALSO asap
How soon can you get here?
We'll deliver the goods as soon as we can.
Please send it as soon as possible.
Do you really have to go so soon?
It's too soon to say what caused this.
Next Monday is the soonest we can deliver.
The sooner we set off, the sooner we will arrive.
All too soon the party was over.
They arrived home sooner than expected.
The note said, ‘Call Bill soonest’ (= as soon as possible).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used in negative sentences and questions to refer to the near future
examples: Will she be back anytime soon?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that you would equally well like to do something as do something else that has been suggested
examples: I'd just as soon stay at home as go out tonight.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to prefer to do something (than do something else)
examples: She'd sooner share a house with other students than live at home with her parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a bad situation will pass or be forgotten most quickly if nothing more is said about it

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that something was, or will be, done immediately

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that something happens immediately after something else
examples: No sooner had she said it than she burst into tears.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: very soon; as soon as possible
examples: ‘When shall I tell him?’ ‘The sooner the better.’

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: at some time in the future, even if you are not sure exactly when
examples: Sooner or later you will have to make a decision.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: after a short time rather than after a long time
examples: We urged them to sort out the problem sooner rather than later.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: clever and complicated in the way that it works or is presented
examples: highly sophisticated computer systems
Medical techniques are becoming more sophisticated all the time.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having a lot of experience of the world and knowing about fashion, culture and other things that people think are socially important
examples: COMPARE naive
the sophisticated pleasures of city life
Mark is a smart and sophisticated young man.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: able to understand difficult or complicated ideas
examples: a sophisticated audience

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling sad and ashamed about something that has been done
examples: We're very sorry about the damage to your car.
I'm sorry about the mess—I haven't had a chance to tidy up yet.
She is obviously deeply sorry for what she has done.
We are sorry for the delay and hope the train will be moving again shortly.
He says he's really sorry for taking the car without asking.
She was sorry that she'd lost her temper.
I am so sorry that this happened.
If you say you're sorry we'll forgive you.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: feeling sad and showing sympathy
examples: I'm sorry that your husband lost his job.
We're sorry to hear that your father's in hospital again.
I was sorry to see him go.
No one is sorrier than I am about what happened.
I am sorry about the way Dad treated you.
I'm sorry about your mother. I do hope she'll soon be feeling better.
I'm very sorry for your loss (= expressing sympathy when somebody has died).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: feeling disappointed about something and wishing you had done something different or had not done something
examples: She was sorry that she'd lost contact with Mary.
I'll make you sorry you were ever born!
You'll be sorry if I catch you!
I was genuinely sorry to be leaving college.
She was almost sorry to stop work.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very sad or bad, especially making you feel pity or disapproval
examples: The business is in a sorry state.
They were a sorry sight when they eventually got off the boat.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be sad or feel sympathy for somebody
examples: He decided to help Jan as he felt sorry for her.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that it is wiser to be too careful than to act too quickly and do something you may later wish you had not
examples: She decided to avoid travelling at night. Better safe than sorry.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to feel unhappy; to be sad about yourself because you are suffering
examples: Stop feeling sorry for yourself and think about other people for a change.
Mitch felt slightly sorry for himself.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when you are apologizing for something
examples: I'm sorry, I forgot.
Oh, I'm sorry. Have I taken the one you wanted?
I'm sorry. I can't make it tomorrow.
I'm sorry to interrupt but there's an urgent call for you.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used for disagreeing with somebody or politely saying ‘no’
examples: I'm sorry, I don't agree.
I'm sorry, I'd rather you didn't go.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used for introducing bad news
examples: I'm sorry to have to tell you you've failed.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used for saying that something is disappointing
examples: He didn't accept the job, I'm sorry to say.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a group or type of people or things that are similar in a particular way
examples: SYNONYM kind
‘What sort of music do you like?’ ‘Oh, all sorts.’
This sort of problem is quite common./These sorts of problems are quite common.
He's the sort of person who only cares about money.
The sort/sorts of people who are having large families in the US and Ireland are very similar.
For dessert there's a fruit pie of some sort (= you are not sure what kind).
Most people went on training courses of one sort or another (= of various types) last year.
There were snacks—peanuts, olives, that sort of thing.
There are all sorts of activities (= many different ones) for kids at the campsite.
What sort of price did you want to pay? (= approximately how much)
What sort of time do you call this? (= I'm very angry that you have come so late.)
Statements like these are not the sort of stuff you'd expect from one of Australia's most powerful women.
Tracey has been causing her mother all sorts of problems (= many different ones).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a particular type of person
examples: My brother would never cheat on his wife; he's not that sort.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the process of putting data in a particular order
examples: to do a sort

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that you think somebody’s behaviour is very strange or unusual but that everyone is different and likes different things
examples: ‘They spent their honeymoon mountain climbing.’ ‘Oh well, it takes all sorts!’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that the situation is very different from what has been said
examples: ‘I was terrible!’ ‘You were nothing of the sort.’

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used when you are saying that something is not a good example of a particular type of thing
examples: He offered us an apology of sorts.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: ill or upset
examples: She was tired and out of sorts by the time she arrived home.
Are you feeling all right? You look a bit out of sorts.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to some extent but in a way that you cannot easily describe
examples: She sort of pretends that she doesn't really care.
‘Do you understand?’ ‘Sort of.’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used for describing something in a not very exact way
examples: I had a sort of feeling that he wouldn't come.
She was jumping around like some sort of kangaroo.
They're a sort of greenish-blue colour.
I was glad about it afterwards, in a funny sort of way.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the spiritual part of a person, believed to exist after death
examples: He believed his immortal soul was in peril.
The howling wind sounded like the wailing of lost souls (= the spirits of dead people who are not in heaven).
'Repent now if you want to save your soul,' he cried.
a prayer for the soul of the deceased
They believe that ghosts are the wandering souls of the departed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person’s inner character, containing their true thoughts and feelings
examples: music that soothes your soul
The eyes are the windows to the soul.
There was a feeling of restlessness deep in her soul.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the spiritual and moral qualities of humans in general
examples: SYNONYM psyche
the dark side of the human soul
In my view, fine art feeds the mind and soul.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: strong and good human feeling, especially that gives a work of art its quality or enables somebody to recognize and enjoy that quality
examples: It was a very polished performance, but it lacked soul.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a perfect example of a good quality
examples: He is the soul of discretion.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a person of a particular type
examples: She's lost all her money, poor soul.
You're a brave soul.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a person
examples: There wasn't a soul in sight (= nobody was in sight).
Don't tell a soul (= do not tell anyone).
a village of 300 souls (= with 300 people living there)

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a type of music that expresses strong emotions, made popular by African American musicians
examples: a soul singer

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to tell somebody your deepest and most private feelings

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: with all your energy
examples: She committed herself body and soul to fighting for the cause.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to show respect when you are talking about somebody who is dead

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: good for you, even if it seems unpleasant
examples: ‘Want a ride?’ ‘No thanks. Walking is good for the soul.’

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: with a lot of energy and enthusiasm
examples: They threw themselves heart and soul into the project.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to stay alive with just enough of the food, clothing, etc. that you need
examples: SYNONYM survive
They barely have enough money to keep body and soul together.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: the liveliest and funniest person at a party, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to do anything, even something really bad or dishonest, in return for money, success or powerWord Origin
examples: Old English sāwol, sāw(e)l, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch ziel and German Seele.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that you can hear
examples: SYNONYM noise
a loud/soft/faint sound
a high/low sound
a buzzing/hissing/popping sound
He crept into the house trying not to make a sound.
She heard the sound of footsteps outside.
the different sounds and smells of the forest
He could hear the sound of several voices.
The sound of children playing in the garden woke me.
A strange sound from the room next door startled her.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: continuous rapid movements (called vibrations) that travel through air or water and can be heard when they reach a person’s or an animal’s ear
examples: Sound travels more slowly than light.
aircraft that can fly faster than the speed of sound
Sound carries well over calm water.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: what you can hear coming from a television, radio, etc., or as part of a film
examples: SEE ALSO surround sound
Could you turn the sound up/down?
The sound quality of the tapes was excellent.
Is the sound turned on? I can't hear anything.
Even with the sound turned off, television is distracting.
They were known for producing DVDs with good picture and sound.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the effect that is produced by the music of a particular singer or group of musicians
examples: I like their sound.
Franz Ferdinand have a great sound that's their own.
The Moog synthesizer created a whole new sound.
The band developed a formidable live sound.
We experimented with different sounds.
He has a sound unlike any other guitarist.
Most of their songs have the sound of the sixties about them.
He produces a good clean sound on his flute.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the idea or impression that you get of somebody/something from what somebody says or what you read
examples: They had a wonderful time by the sound of it.
From the sound of things you were lucky to find him.
They're consulting a lawyer? I don't like the sound of that.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a narrow passage of water that joins two larger areas of water
examples: SYNONYM strait
Plymouth Sound

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to like talking a lot or too much, usually without wanting to listen to other people
examples: She’s much too fond of the sound of her own voice.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: near enough to be able to hear something
examples: a house within sound of the sea

examples: SEE ALSO alphabet soup
a bowl /cup of soup
chicken/vegetable/tomato soup
a soup spoon/bowl/plate
a tin/packet of soup
a can/package of soup
He ladled out three bowls of soup.
tinned/packet soups
canned/packaged soups

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: from beginning to end
examples: She told me the whole story from soup to nuts.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in trouble
examples: We're all in the soup now.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a place, person or thing that you get something from
examples: renewable energy sources
These fish are widely used as a food source.
Your local library will be a useful source of information.
What is their main source of income?
Tourism is a major source of revenue for the area.
The tiny window was the only source of light.
Funding came from a wide variety of sources.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person, book or document that provides information, especially for study, a piece of written work or news
examples: SEE ALSO primary source
He refused to name his sources.
Government sources indicated yesterday that cuts may have to be made.
Intelligence sources say they now believe he is dead.
This information comes from a very reliable source.
According to industry sources, these prices are likely to rise.
Proper attribution of source material is extremely important.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that causes or provides something
examples: The Irish landscape has long been a source of inspiration to artists.
Sporting success is a great source of national pride.
a potential source of conflict
a constant source of irritation

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the place where a river or stream starts
examples: the source of the Nile

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: at the place or the point that something comes from or begins
examples: Is your salary taxed at source (= by your employer)?
It is better to deal with such problems at source.
Under the PAYE system, employees' income is taxed at source.

warmer weather coming from the south

views of distant mountains to north and south

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: He fell asleep, in spite of himself.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to divide, or to make something divide, into two or more parts
examples: SEE ALSO split somebody up
He was a member of the team that split the atom in 1932.
The Turkish invasion of the northern part of Cyprus ended with the island split in two.
Split the coconut in half.
She split the class into groups of four.
Each chapter is split into two parts.
The results split neatly into two groups.
Slate splits easily into thin sheets.
If the nail you use is too big, there's a chance that the wood will split.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to divide something into two or more parts and share it between different people, activities, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO split something up
She split the money she won with her brother.
The two men agreed to split the proceeds.
We share a house and split all the bills.
His time is split between the London and Paris offices.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to divide, or to make a group of people divide, into smaller groups that have very different opinions
examples: The committee split over government subsidies.
His candidacy split the Republican vote.
The sect split from the Mormon church more than a hundred years ago.
The party is deeply split on this issue.
The poll found the public evenly split on the issue.
The community was split down the middle on this.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to tear, or to make something tear, along a straight line
examples: Her dress had split along the seam.
Don't tell me you've split another pair of pants!
The cushion split open and sent feathers everywhere.
He split the packet open and poured out a handful of peanuts.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to cut somebody’s skin and make it bleed
examples: She split her head open on the cupboard door.
She fell downstairs and split her head open.
How did you split your lip?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to leave somebody and stop having a relationship with them
examples: SEE ALSO split up (with somebody)
The singer split with his wife last June.
She intends to split from the band at the end of the tour.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to leave a place quickly
examples: Let's split!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: (when discussing a price, etc.) to agree on an amount that is at an equal distance between the two amounts that have been suggested
examples: I offered €200 but he wanted €300. In the end, we split the difference and I paid him €250.
I wanted to leave early and Ian wanted to leave late, so we split the difference and left at noon.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: The country was split down the middle over the strike (= half supported it, half did not).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to cover, or to make something cover, a larger and larger area
examples: There is no evidence that the cancer has spread.

A strong wind spread the flames.
Using too much water could spread the stain.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: The valley spread out beneath us.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to put a layer of a substance onto the surface of something; to be able to be put onto a surface

pieces of toast spread with butter
If the paint is too thick, it will not spread evenly.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to open something that has been folded so that it covers a larger area than before
examples: The bird spread its wings.
a bird with its wings spread wide

Sue spread the map out on the floor.
We spread the rug out on the floor.
He spread the blanket over the straw and went to sleep.
He had a newspaper spread open on his knee.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to arrange objects so that they cover a large area and can be seen easily
examples: Papers had been spread out on the desk.

He shuffled the cards and spread them in a fan.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: SEE ALSO pinch (3)

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 10

definitions.label: Meaning 11

examples: Rumours of his death spread like wildfire.

examples: They have spread their net far and wide in the search for a new team coach.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 10

definitions.label: Meaning 11

definitions.label: Meaning 12

examples: Stand the ladder up against the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a song that has been recorded by many different singersWord Origin
examples: Middle English (denoting a flag raised on a pole as a rallying point, the authorized exemplar of a unit of measurement, or an upright timber): shortening of Old French estendart, from estendre ‘extend’; in sense (5), influenced by the verb stand.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a level of quality, especially one that people think is acceptable
examples: SEE ALSO standard of living
There has been a fall in living standards.
safety/quality standards
Who sets the standard for water quality?
A number of Britain's beaches fail to meet European standards on cleanliness.
to improve/raise standards
He failed to reach the minimum standard and did not qualify.
We aim to maintain high standards of customer care.
The standard of this year's applications is very low.
The quality of the image was below the standard I had hoped for.
The work was done to a professional standard.
Her work is not up to standard (= of a good enough standard).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a level of quality that is normal or acceptable for a particular person or in a particular situation
examples: You'd better lower your standards if you want to find somewhere cheap to live.
It was a simple meal by Eddie's standards.
The equipment is slow and heavy by modern standards.
His latest film is well below his usual standards.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a level of behaviour that somebody considers to be morally acceptable
examples: SEE ALSO double standard
a man of high moral standards
Some people have no standards.
The government must uphold basic standards of decency.
My grandparents are always complaining about falling standards.
the advertising standards watchdog

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a unit of measurement that is officially used; an official rule used when producing something
examples: SEE ALSO gold standard
a reduction in the weight standard of silver coins
industry standards

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a flag that is used during official ceremonies, especially one connected with a particular military group
examples: the royal standard

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a song that has been recorded by many different singersWord Origin
examples: Middle English (denoting a flag raised on a pole as a rallying point, the authorized exemplar of a unit of measurement, or an upright timber): shortening of Old French estendart, from estendre ‘extend’; in sense (5), influenced by the verb stand.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: done from a position in which you are standing rather than sitting or running
examples: a standing jump/start
The speaker got a standing ovation (= people stood up to clap after the speech).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: existing or arranged permanently, not formed or made for a particular situation
examples: a standing army
a standing charge (= an amount of money that you pay regularly in order to use a service, such as gas or water)
a standing committee
It’s a standing joke (= something that a group of people regularly laugh at).
We have a standing invitation to visit them anytime.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: from an initial position in which none of the necessary elements are in place
examples: The space project went from a standing start to the moon in ten years.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large ball of burning gas in space that we see as a point of light in the sky at night
examples: SEE ALSO dark star
There was a big moon and hundreds of stars were shining overhead.
Sirius is the brightest star in the sky.
We camped out under the stars.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an object, a decoration, a mark, etc., usually with five or six points, whose shape represents a star
examples: a horse with a white star on its forehead
a sheriff’s star
I've put a star by the names of the girls in the class.
Liz deserves a gold star for all her hard work.
a four-star general

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a mark that represents a star and tells you how good something is, especially a hotel or restaurant
examples: three-/four-/five-star hotels
What star rating does this restaurant have?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a famous and excellent singer, performer, sports player, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO all-star
pop/rock/Hollywood/TV stars
a football/tennis/sports star
She acts well but she hasn't got star quality.
Get used to her face as she is a rising star.
She's a former child star.
He's so good—I'm sure he'll be a big star.
The best models receive star treatment.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person who has the main part, or one of the main parts, in a film, play, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO star turn
The star of the show was a young Italian singer.
The show has plenty of guest stars appearing each week.
She was the star of many popular television series.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is the best of a group
examples: a star student
Paula is the star of the class.
He was the star performer at the championships.
The star prize is a weekend for two in Paris.
The monkey was the star attraction (= the best or most popular act) at the show.
Through high school he was a track star.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to show that you feel very grateful for something that somebody has done or that you think they are wonderful
examples: Thanks! You're a star!

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a description of what somebody thinks is going to happen to somebody in the future, based on the position of the stars and planets when they were born
examples: SYNONYM horoscope
Do you read your stars in the paper?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to try to be successful at something that is difficult

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to see flashes of light in front of your eyes, usually because you have been hit on the head

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: if somebody has stars in their eyes, they have dreams of becoming famous, especially as an actor, singer, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to feel very grateful and lucky about something
examples: Just thank your lucky stars you weren’t in the house at the time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to look at somebody/something for a long time
examples: I screamed and everyone stared.
I stared blankly at the paper in front of me.
They stared up at the hole in the ceiling.
He sat staring into space (= looking at nothing).
I was staring into her beautiful blue eyes.
She looked at them with dark staring eyes.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to describe something that you have failed to see, even though it was obvious and should have been easy to see
examples: The answer was staring us in the face but we never saw it until it was too late.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be certain to happen
examples: Defeat was staring them in the face.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be unable to avoid something
examples: They were staring defeat in the face.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: unpleasant; real, and impossible to avoid
examples: SYNONYM bleak
The author paints a stark picture of life in a prison camp.
The government faced a stark choice between civil war and martial law.
The remains of the building stand as a stark reminder of the fire.
He now faces the stark reality of life in prison.
The stark truth is that there is not enough money left.
The stark fact is that even with more time, we still couldn’t raise enough money.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very different from something in a way that is easy to see
examples: SYNONYM clear
stark differences
Social divisions in the city are stark.
The good weather was in stark contrast to the storms of previous weeks.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: looking severe and without any colour or decoration
examples: I think white would be too stark for the bedroom.
The hills stood stark against the winter sky.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: complete and total
examples: SYNONYM utter
The children watched in stark terror.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to begin doing or using something
examples: I start work at nine.
He's just started a new job.
The kids start school next week.
I only started (= began to read) this book yesterday.
We need to start (= begin using) a new jar of coffee.
It's a long story. Where shall I start?
Can you start (= a new job) on Monday?
It started to rain.
I was starting to feel tired.
Mistakes were starting to creep in.
She started laughing.
Suddenly things started happening.
It's time you started on your homework.
Let's start by reviewing what we did last week.
If you want to find out more, this website is a good place to start.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to begin happening; to make something begin happening
examples: Work is due to start this weekend.
What time does the show start?
Have you any idea where the rumour started?
Who started the fire?
I'm ready to start the process of writing.
Do you start the day with a good breakfast?
You're always trying to start an argument.
The news started me thinking.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: when you start a machine or a vehicle or it starts, it begins to operate
examples: SEE ALSO jump-start
Start the engines!
He started the recording.
I can't get the car started.
The car won't start.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to begin to exist; to make something begin to exist
examples: The company started in 1894 in Pennsylvania.
There are a lot of small businesses starting up in that area.
She started a business while she was still at school.
I decided to start a fashion blog.
They want to start a family (= to have children).
He decided to start up his own film festival.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to begin from a particular place, amount or situation; to begin in a particular way
examples: The trail starts just outside the town.
Hotel prices start at €80 for a double room.
A sentence always starts with a capital letter.
The evening started badly when the speaker failed to turn up.
The best professional musicians start young.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to begin, or to begin something such as a career, in a particular way that changed later
examples: She started as a secretary but ended up running the department.
It started as a hobby and grew from there.
The company started out with 30 employees.
I started off as a dishwasher making 25 cents an hour.
He started life as a teacher before turning to journalism.
She started her career working for the BBC.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to begin a journey; to leave
examples: SYNONYM set off
What time are we starting tomorrow?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to begin to move in a particular direction
examples: I started after her (= began to follow her) to tell her the news.
He started for the door, but I blocked his way.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to move suddenly and quickly because you are surprised or afraid
examples: SYNONYM jump
The sudden noise made her start.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody not to complain or be critical
examples: Don't start! I told you I'd be late.
Don't you start! It's hard enough managing the kids, without you complaining too.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make something start happening; to make sure that something continues to happen

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to start a relationship well/badly
examples: I seem to have got off on the wrong foot with the new boss.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to begin doing something
examples: It's nearly ten o'clock. Let's get started.
It's already late, so I think we should get started.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to start a relationship well/badly
examples: I seem to have started off on the wrong foot with the new boss.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to cause trouble

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used when you are giving the first and most important reason for something
examples: To start with it’s much too expensive…

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: at the beginning
examples: The club had only six members to start with.
I'll have melon to start with.
She wasn't keen on the idea to start with.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to blame somebody for beginning a fight or an argument
examples: ‘Stop fighting, you two!’ ‘He started it!’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to suffer or die because you do not have enough food to eat; to make somebody suffer or die in this way
examples: The animals were left to starve to death.
pictures of starving children
The new job doesn't pay as much but we won't starve!
She's starving herself to try to lose weight.
Many of the prisoners looked half starved.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not having something that you need
examples: SEE ALSO cash-starved
supply-starved rebels

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to feel very hungry
examples: When's the food coming? I'm starving!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a country considered as an organized political community controlled by one government
examples: SEE ALSO chief of state
the Baltic States
European Union member states

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an organized political community forming part of a country
examples: SEE ALSO Gulf States (2)
the states of Victoria and Western Australia
The hurricane swept across the southern states of the US.
Both candidates have been campaigning in key battleground states.
She decided to return to her home state of Ohio.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the government of a country
examples: matters/affairs of state
people who are financially dependent on the state
a state-owned company
They wish to limit the power of the State.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the mental, emotional or physical condition that a person or thing is in
examples: a confused mental state
a confused state of mind
anxieties about the state of the country’s economy
The government has declared a state of emergency in the flooded regions.
Given the current state of knowledge, it will take years to find a solution.
A report condemned the state of prisoners' cells.
water in a liquid state
He was in a terrible state by the time he got home.
She was in a state of shock.
The building is in a bad state of repair (= needs to be repaired).
He was in a state of permanent depression.
You're not in a fit state to drive.
Look at the state of you! You can't go out looking like that.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the formal ceremonies connected with high levels of government or with kings and queens
examples: SEE ALSO lying-in-state
The president was driven in state through the streets.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the United States of America
examples: I've never been to the States.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be/become excited or anxious
examples: She was in a real state about her exams.
He made a mistake and got into a terrible state about it.
Jane was in a terrible state after losing her job.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be dirty or untidy
examples: What a state this place is in!
How did the carpet get into that state?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: (in the Roman Catholic Church) having been forgiven by God for the wrong or evil things you have done
examples: He died in a state of grace.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a situation
examples: This state of affairs can no longer be ignored.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: the stage that has been reached in a process, etc. which has not yet been completed
examples: What is the current state of play in the peace talks?

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: the score in a sports match, especially in cricketWord Origin
examples: Middle English (as a noun): partly a shortening of estate, partly from Latin status ‘manner of standing, condition’, from stare ‘to stand’. The current verb senses date from the mid 17th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: something that you say or write that gives information or an opinion
examples: Are the following statements true or false?
The article contained several false statements.
He made a rather misleading statement.
Is that a statement or a question?
I didn't agree with her statement about education.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a formal or official account of facts or opinions
examples: SYNONYM declaration
a joint/a written/an official statement
A government spokesperson made a statement to the press.
The court heard witness statements from several people.
The prosecution delivered a brilliant opening statement.
The government will issue a statement on the policy change today.
In a statement released yesterday, the company denied the allegations.
He gave a statement (= a written account of facts about a crime, used in court if legal action follows) in which he said he saw two men.

definitions.definition: to no longer continue to do something; to make somebody/something no longer do something
examples: Can't you just stop?
That phone never stops ringing!
Don't you ever stop talking?
Please stop crying and tell me what's wrong.
She criticizes everyone and the trouble is, she doesn't know when to stop.
Stop me (= make me stop talking) if I'm boring you.
Stop it! You're hurting me.
Mike immediately stopped what he was doing.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to end or finish; to make something end or finish
examples: When is this fighting going to stop?
The bus service stops at midnight.
Has it stopped raining yet?
Doctors couldn't stop the bleeding.
The referee was forced to stop the game because of heavy snow.
She called on both sides to stop the violence.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to prevent somebody from doing something; to prevent something from happening
examples: I want to go and you can't stop me.
efforts to stop the spread of the disease
There's no stopping us now (= nothing can prevent us from achieving what we want to achieve).
You can't stop people (from) saying what they think.
They tried to stop me from leaving.
There's nothing to stop you from accepting the offer.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to end an activity for a short time in order to do something
examples: I'm hungry. Let's stop for lunch.
We stopped for the night in Port Augusta.
We stopped to admire the scenery.
People just don't stop to think about the consequences.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to no longer be working or functioning; to make something be no longer working or functioning
examples: Why has the engine stopped?
What time is it? My watch has stopped.
I felt as if my heart had stopped.
Can you stop the printer once it’s started?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to stay somewhere for a short time, especially at somebody’s house
examples: I'm not stopping. I just came to give you this message.
Can you stop for tea?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to prevent money from being paid
examples: to stop a cheque (= tell the bank not to pay it)
Employees of the failed company will have their wages stopped from tomorrow.
Dad threatened to stop £1 a week from our pocket money if we didn't clean our rooms.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to block, fill or close a hole, an opening, etc.
examples: Stop up the other end of the tube, will you?
I stopped my ears but still heard her cry out.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be willing to do anything to get what you want, even if it is dishonest or wrong
examples: She’ll stop at nothing to make money.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to stop measuring time in a game or an activity that has a time limit

definitions.label: Meaning 12

examples: The question stopped Alice in her tracks.

The agency provided me with a steady stream of work.
a constant stream of enquiries
Most of the letter consisted of a stream of abuse.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a continuous flow of video or sound sent over the internet; a continuous flow of computer data or instructions
examples: You can listen to the live audio stream.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a group of students of the same age and level of ability in some schools
examples: She was put into the fast stream.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be in operation or available
examples: The new computer system comes on stream next month.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a public road in a city or town that has houses and buildings on one side or both sides
examples: SEE ALSO backstreet
I was just walking along the street when it happened.
She lives just up the street here.
The bank is just across the street.
He is used to being recognized in the street.
Workers took to the streets in protest.
It's not safe to walk the streets at night.
It's a medieval town, with narrow cobbled streets.
a crowded/residential/quiet/deserted street
92nd Street
10 Downing Street
You can find these shops on every street corner.
The council promised better street lighting and cleaner streets.
a street map/plan of York
My office is at street level (= on the ground floor).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the ideas and opinions of ordinary people, especially people who live in cities, which are considered important
examples: The feeling I get from the street is that we have a good chance of winning this election.
The word on the street is that it's not going to happen.
Opinion on the street was divided.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an average or ordinary person, either male or female
examples: Politicians often don't understand the views of the man in the street.
What really matters to the man and woman in the street?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: enjoying a comfortable way of life with plenty of money

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: without a home; outside, not in a house or other building
examples: the problems of young people living on the streets
If it had been left to me I would have put him out on the street long ago.
She was thrown onto the street.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: working as a prostitute

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: much better or more advanced than somebody/something else
examples: a country that is streets ahead in the control of environmental pollution
Beth is streets ahead of all the other students in her year.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that it seems easy to make money in a place

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: very suitable for you because it is something that you know a lot about or are very interested in
examples: This job seems right up your street.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of being physically strong
examples: OPPOSITE weakness (1)
He pushed against the rock with all his strength.
It may take a few weeks for you to build up your strength again.
She gradually regained strength in her legs.
He had a physical strength that matched his outward appearance.
She didn't have the strength to walk any further.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the ability that something has to resist force or hold heavy weights without breaking or being damaged
examples: SEE ALSO industrial-strength
the strength of a rope
The panels are reinforced with steel for extra strength.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of being brave and determined in a difficult situation
examples: OPPOSITE weakness (2)
During this ordeal he was able to draw strength from his faith.
She has a remarkable inner strength.
You have shown great strength of character.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the power and influence that somebody/something has
examples: OPPOSITE weakness (2)
Political power depends upon economic strength.
Their superior military strength gives them a huge advantage.
to negotiate from a position of strength
The rally was intended to be a show of strength by the socialists.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: how strong or deeply felt an opinion or a feeling is
examples: the strength of public opinion
This view has recently gathered strength (= become stronger or more widely held).
I was surprised by the strength of her feelings.
I have been overwhelmed by the strength of feeling that people have about this issue.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a quality or an ability that a person or thing has that gives them an advantage
examples: OPPOSITE weakness (3)
The ability to keep calm is one of her many strengths.
the strengths and weaknesses of an argument
The new weapon's strength lies in its accuracy.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: how strong a natural force or a signal is
examples: the strength of the sun
wind strength
the strength and direction of the tide
The phone company aims to improve signal strength within buildings.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: how strong a particular taste or substance is
examples: Add more curry powder depending on the strength required.
a range of beers with different strengths (= with different amounts of alcohol in them)
a packet of double-strength mints
These wines vary in strength between 11° and 15°.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: how strong a country’s currency is in relation to other countries’ currencies
examples: OPPOSITE weakness (4)
the relative strength of the euro against the dollar
The euro has continued to gain strength.
the continuing strength of the pound

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the number of people in a group, a team or an organization
examples: The strength of the workforce is about to be doubled from 3 000 to 6 000.
The team will be back at full strength (= with all the best players) for the next match.
The Korean team was not up to strength for the final.
The protesters turned out in strength (= in large numbers).
These cuts have left the local police force under strength (= with fewer members than it needs).

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to become more and more successful
examples: Since her appointment the department has gone from strength to strength.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: because somebody has been influenced or persuaded by something
examples: I got the job on the strength of your recommendation.
She hopes to secure a recording contract on the strength of these songs.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: the quality of being strong because you have a great variety of good people, ideas, etc. that can contribute to the success of something
examples: The French team does not have the strength in depth that the Australians have.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: being in a group gives you more power
examples: There's strength in numbers, so encourage your friends and family to join us.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: a person that you can rely on to help, protect and comfort you when you are in trouble
examples: He was a tower of strength to his sisters when their father died.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become more powerful or effective; to make somebody/something more powerful or effective
examples: Her position in the party has strengthened in recent weeks.
The move is clearly intended to strengthen the president's position as head of state.
The new evidence will strengthen their case.
The new manager has strengthened the side by bringing in several younger players.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to become physically stronger
examples: The exercises are designed to strengthen your stomach muscles.
Repairs are necessary to strengthen the bridge.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a feeling, an opinion or a relationship stronger; to become stronger
examples: This temporary setback merely strengthened her resolve.
Their attitude only strengthened his resolve to fight on.
The experience of bereavement can strengthen family ties.
His determination only strengthened in the face of this opposition.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to become stronger
examples: The wind had strengthened overnight.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to become stronger; to make a currency or an economy stronger
examples: OPPOSITE weaken
Yesterday the pound strengthened against the dollar.
The fall in unemployment is a sign of a strengthening economy.
The measures should help create jobs and strengthen the economy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: pressure or worry caused by the problems in somebody’s life
examples: SEE ALSO post-traumatic stress disorder
emotional/mental stress
to suffer from stress
to relieve/reduce/alleviate stress
Things can easily go wrong when people are under stress.
The incident has caused enormous stress and anxiety to my family.
She failed to withstand the stresses and strains of public life.
stress-related illnesses
stress management (= dealing with stress)
The release of the stress hormone cortisol is part of the human stress response.
Stress is often a factor in the development of long-term sickness.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: physical pressure put on something that can damage it or make it lose its shape
examples: When you have an injury you start putting stress on other parts of your body.
Little is known about the effects of water stress on plants.
The building was condemned because of the damage caused by excessive heat stress.
Different organisms react differently to environmental stress (= damage to the environment caused by human activity or natural events).
a stress fracture of the foot (= one caused by such pressure)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an extra force used when pronouncing a particular word or syllable
examples: COMPARE intonation
We worked on pronunciation, stress and intonation.
There's a stress on the second syllable.
In ‘strategic’ the stress falls on the second syllable

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: special importance given to something
examples: She lays great stress on punctuality.
I think the company places too much stress on cost and not enough on quality.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: extra force used when making a particular sound in music

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: illness caused by difficult physical conditions
examples: Those most vulnerable to heat stress are the elderly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make something longer, wider or looser, for example by pulling it; to become longer, etc. in this way
examples: Is there any way of stretching shoes?
Stop stretching your sleeves like that!
This sweater has stretched.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to become bigger or longer when you pull it and return to its original shape when you stop
examples: The jeans stretch to provide a perfect fit.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to pull something so that it is smooth and tight
examples: Stretch the fabric tightly over the frame.
Striped awnings had been stretched across the courtyard.
Make sure that the rope is stretched tight.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to put your arms or legs out straight and contract your muscles
examples: He stretched and yawned lazily.
Andrea turned out the light and stretched full-length on the bed.
The exercises are designed to stretch and tone your leg muscles.
It was impossible to bend or stretch my legs.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to put out an arm or a leg in order to reach something
examples: She stretched across the table for the butter.
She stretched up to reach the top shelf.
I stretched out a hand and picked up the book.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to spread over an area of land
examples: SYNONYM extend
Fields and hills stretched out as far as we could see.
The traffic jam seemed to stretch for miles.
A line of cars stretched into the distance.
The flat landscape stretched to the horizon.
Beyond the mountains stretches a vast desert.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to continue over a period of time
examples: The town's history stretches back to before 1500.
to stretch back years/decades/generations/centuries
The training stretches over a period of 16 months.
Endless summer days stretched out before us.
The talks look set to stretch into a second week.
The future stretched out endlessly in front of me.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be enough to buy or pay for something
examples: I need a new car, but my savings won't stretch to it.
There are lots of things I’d like to buy, but our budget just won’t stretch that far.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to make use of a lot of your money, supplies, time, etc.
examples: The influx of refugees has stretched the country's resources to the limit.
We can't take on any more work—we're fully stretched as it is.
The budget is already stretched to breaking point.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to increase your lead over somebody in a game or competition
examples: A minute later, Kelly stretched their lead to eight points.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to make use of all somebody’s skill, intelligence, etc.
examples: I need a job that will stretch me.
She was never really stretched at school.
The book really stretches your imagination.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to use something in a way that would not normally be considered fair, acceptable, etc.
examples: He admitted that he had maybe stretched the truth a little (= not been completely honest).
The play's plot stretches credulity to the limit.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to change the rules to suit a particular person or situation
examples: Couldn't they just bend the rules and let us in without a ticket?

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to go for a short walk after sitting for some time
examples: It was good to get out of the car and stretch our legs.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to allow or do something that is not usually acceptable, especially because of a particular situation
examples: I was hoping they would stretch a point and let me stay on for a while.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that must be obeyed exactly
examples: strict rules/regulations
There are strict guidelines on how the work is to be carried out.
The head teacher imposed very strict discipline.
She's on a very strict diet.
He told me in the strictest confidence (= on the understanding that I would tell nobody else).
He expected strict adherence to his rules.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: demanding that rules, especially rules about behaviour, should be obeyed
examples: a strict teacher/parent/disciplinarian
I had a very strict upbringing.
She's very strict about things like homework.
They were always very strict with their children.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: obeying the rules of a particular religion, belief, etc. exactly
examples: a strict Muslim
a strict vegetarian

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very exact and clearly defined
examples: It wasn’t illegal in the strict sense (of the word).
They insisted on their strict legal rights.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: with a lot of control and rules that must be obeyed
examples: She was brought up very strictly.
The industry is strictly regulated.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something happens or must happen in all circumstances
examples: SYNONYM absolutely
Smoking is strictly forbidden.
My letter is, of course, strictly private and confidential.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in all details; exactly
examples: This is not strictly true.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something only applies to one particular person, thing or situation
examples: SYNONYM purely
We'll look at the problem from a strictly legal point of view.
I know we're friends, but this is strictly business.
Their relationship is strictly platonic.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if you are using words or rules in their exact or correct sense
examples: Strictly speaking, the book is not a novel, but a short story.
Using the word in that context is not, strictly speaking, correct.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to hit somebody/something hard or with force
examples: The ship struck a rock.
The child ran into the road and was struck by a car.
The tree was struck by lightning.
Warplanes struck several targets in the city.
He fell, striking his head on the edge of the table.
He was struck in the head by a bullet.
The stone struck her on the forehead.
The oar struck against something hard.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to hit somebody/something with your hand or a weapon
examples: She struck him in the face.
He struck the table with his fist.
Who struck the first blow (= started the fight)?
Did she ever strike you?
He struck her two blows on the leg.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to hit or kick a ball, etc.
examples: He walked up to the penalty spot and struck the ball firmly into the back of the net.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to attack somebody/something, especially suddenly
examples: The lion crouched ready to strike.
Police fear that the killer may strike again.
The guerrillas struck with deadly force.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to happen suddenly and have a harmful or damaging effect on somebody/something
examples: Two days later tragedy struck.
Disaster struck again when their best player was injured.
The area was struck by an outbreak of cholera.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to come into somebody’s mind suddenly
examples: An awful thought has just struck me.
I was struck by her resemblance to my aunt.
One thing that really struck me was how calm he appeared.
It suddenly struck me how we could improve the situation.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to give somebody a particular impression
examples: Another part of his comment struck me.
His reaction struck me as odd.
She strikes me as a very efficient person.
How does the idea strike you?
It strikes me that nobody is really in favour of the changes.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to refuse to work because of an argument over pay or conditions
examples: Over 100 000 civil servants are set to strike on Tuesday.
Drivers are threatening to strike over pay.
The union has voted to strike for a pay increase of 6%.
Striking workers picketed the factory.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to fall on a surface
examples: The windows sparkled as the sun struck the glass.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to put somebody suddenly into a particular state
examples: to be struck dumb/deaf/blind

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to rub something such as a match against a surface so that it produces a flame; to produce a flame when rubbed against a rough surface
examples: to strike a match on a wall
The sword struck sparks off the stone floor.
The matches were damp and he couldn't make them strike.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to show the time by making a ringing noise, etc.
examples: SYNONYM chime
Did you hear the clock strike?
Four o’clock had just struck.
The clock has just struck three.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to produce a musical note, sound, etc. by pressing a key or hitting something
examples: She struck a chord on the piano and the children began to sing.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to discover gold, oil, etc. by digging or drilling
examples: They had struck oil!

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to go somewhere with great energy or purpose
examples: We left the road and struck off across the fields.
He struck out (= started swimming) towards the shore.
The German army struck deep into northern France.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be impressed or interested by somebody/something; to like somebody/something very much
examples: I was struck by her youth and enthusiasm.
We're not very struck on that new restaurant.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to argue in an aggressive way and force somebody to agree on the best possible price or arrangement

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: if a remark, etc. hits/strikes home, it has a strong effect on somebody, in a way that makes them realize what the true facts of a situation are
examples: Her face went pale as his words hit home.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to suddenly be in a successful situation, especially one that makes you rich
examples: The band really hit pay dirt with their last album.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to do, say or write something that is suitable/not suitable for a particular occasion
examples: It is a bizarre tale and the author hits just the right note of horror and disbelief.
Unfortunately, the president struck the wrong note in his speech, ignoring the public mood.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to hit the wooden frame of the goal in the game of football (soccer), instead of scoring a goal
examples: She hit the woodwork twice before scoring.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: an unusual or unpleasant event is not likely to happen in the same place or to the same people twice

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to express feelings or opinions of a particular kind
examples: She sounded a note of warning in her speech.
The touch of cynicism struck a slightly sour note.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to manage to find a way of being fair to two things that are opposed to each other; to find an acceptable position that is between two things
examples: We need to strike a balance between these conflicting interests.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to make an agreement with somebody in which both sides have an advantage
examples: Perhaps we could strike a bargain.
The United States has struck a historic deal with India.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to do something in support of/against a belief, principle, etc.
examples: He felt that they had struck a blow for democracy.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to say or do something that makes people feel sympathy or enthusiasm
examples: The speaker had obviously struck a chord with his audience.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to make somebody be afraid, etc.
examples: The sound of gunfire struck fear into the hearts of the villagers.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to find or do something that brings you a lot of success or money
examples: He has struck gold with his latest novel.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: if a remark, etc. strikes/hits home, it has a strong effect on somebody, in a way that makes them realize what the true facts of a situation are
examples: His face went pale as her words struck home.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to get a lot of money, especially suddenly or unexpectedly

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to have good luck
examples: We certainly struck it lucky with the weather.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to have a strong effect
examples: His work strikes a nerve with people who are attracted to nostalgia.
It seems I struck a nerve with my last post about cell phones.
Nissan may well strike a popular nerve here.

definitions.label: Meaning 34

examples: The band really struck pay dirt with their last album.

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to hold your body in a particular way to create a particular impression
examples: to strike a dramatic pose
He strikes an attitude of bravery and lonely defiance.

definitions.label: Meaning 36

examples: It is a bizarre tale and the author strikes just the right note of horror and disbelief.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to make use of an opportunity immediately
