How does the idea strike you?
It strikes me that nobody is really in favour of the changes.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to refuse to work because of an argument over pay or conditions
examples: Over 100 000 civil servants are set to strike on Tuesday.
Drivers are threatening to strike over pay.
The union has voted to strike for a pay increase of 6%.
Striking workers picketed the factory.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to fall on a surface
examples: The windows sparkled as the sun struck the glass.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to put somebody suddenly into a particular state
examples: to be struck dumb/deaf/blind

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to rub something such as a match against a surface so that it produces a flame; to produce a flame when rubbed against a rough surface
examples: to strike a match on a wall
The sword struck sparks off the stone floor.
The matches were damp and he couldn't make them strike.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to show the time by making a ringing noise, etc.
examples: SYNONYM chime
Did you hear the clock strike?
Four o’clock had just struck.
The clock has just struck three.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to produce a musical note, sound, etc. by pressing a key or hitting something
examples: She struck a chord on the piano and the children began to sing.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to discover gold, oil, etc. by digging or drilling
examples: They had struck oil!

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to go somewhere with great energy or purpose
examples: We left the road and struck off across the fields.
He struck out (= started swimming) towards the shore.
The German army struck deep into northern France.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be impressed or interested by somebody/something; to like somebody/something very much
examples: I was struck by her youth and enthusiasm.
We're not very struck on that new restaurant.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to argue in an aggressive way and force somebody to agree on the best possible price or arrangement

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: if a remark, etc. hits/strikes home, it has a strong effect on somebody, in a way that makes them realize what the true facts of a situation are
examples: Her face went pale as his words hit home.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to suddenly be in a successful situation, especially one that makes you rich
examples: The band really hit pay dirt with their last album.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to do, say or write something that is suitable/not suitable for a particular occasion
examples: It is a bizarre tale and the author hits just the right note of horror and disbelief.
Unfortunately, the president struck the wrong note in his speech, ignoring the public mood.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to hit the wooden frame of the goal in the game of football (soccer), instead of scoring a goal
examples: She hit the woodwork twice before scoring.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: an unusual or unpleasant event is not likely to happen in the same place or to the same people twice

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to express feelings or opinions of a particular kind
examples: She sounded a note of warning in her speech.
The touch of cynicism struck a slightly sour note.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to manage to find a way of being fair to two things that are opposed to each other; to find an acceptable position that is between two things
examples: We need to strike a balance between these conflicting interests.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to make an agreement with somebody in which both sides have an advantage
examples: Perhaps we could strike a bargain.
The United States has struck a historic deal with India.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to do something in support of/against a belief, principle, etc.
examples: He felt that they had struck a blow for democracy.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to say or do something that makes people feel sympathy or enthusiasm
examples: The speaker had obviously struck a chord with his audience.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to make somebody be afraid, etc.
examples: The sound of gunfire struck fear into the hearts of the villagers.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to find or do something that brings you a lot of success or money
examples: He has struck gold with his latest novel.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: if a remark, etc. strikes/hits home, it has a strong effect on somebody, in a way that makes them realize what the true facts of a situation are
examples: His face went pale as her words struck home.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to get a lot of money, especially suddenly or unexpectedly

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to have good luck
examples: We certainly struck it lucky with the weather.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to have a strong effect
examples: His work strikes a nerve with people who are attracted to nostalgia.
It seems I struck a nerve with my last post about cell phones.
Nissan may well strike a popular nerve here.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to suddenly be in a successful situation, especially one that makes you rich
examples: The band really struck pay dirt with their last album.

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to hold your body in a particular way to create a particular impression
examples: to strike a dramatic pose
He strikes an attitude of bravery and lonely defiance.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to do, say or write something that is suitable/not suitable for a particular occasion
examples: It is a bizarre tale and the author strikes just the right note of horror and disbelief.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to make use of an opportunity immediately

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: near enough to be reached or attacked easily; near enough to reach or attack something easily
examples: The beach is within striking distance.
The cat was now within striking distance of the duck.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: interesting and unusual enough to attract attention
examples: SYNONYM marked
a striking feature
She bears a striking resemblance to her older sister.
In striking contrast to their brothers, the girls were both intelligent and charming.
The similarities between the two cases are striking.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very attractive, often in an unusual way
examples: SYNONYM stunning
striking good looks
She was undoubtedly a very striking young woman.
That hat looks very striking.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: long, thin material used for tying things together, made of several threads that have been twisted together; a piece of string used to fasten or pull something or keep something in place
examples: SEE ALSO drawstring
a piece/length/ball of string
He wrapped the package in brown paper and tied it with string.
The key is hanging on a string by the door.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set or series of things that are joined together, for example on a string
examples: a string of pearls
The molecules join together to form long strings.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a series of things or people that come closely one after another
examples: The band had a string of hits in the nineties.
He owns a string of racing stables.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a series of characters (= letters, numbers, etc.)
examples: to key in/enter a search string

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a tightly stretched piece of wire, nylon, or catgut on a musical instrument, that produces a musical note when the instrument is played
examples: Play it on the G string.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the group of musical instruments in an orchestra that have strings, for example violins; the people who play them
examples: COMPARE brass
The opening theme is taken up by the strings.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: any of the tightly stretched pieces of nylon or natural gut in a racket, used for hitting balls in tennis and some other sports

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: special conditions or limits
examples: Major loans like these always come with strings.
It's a business proposition, pure and simple. No strings attached.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: (too much under) the influence and control of somebody
examples: The British prime minister is too apt to cling to Washington's apron strings.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to have more than one skill or plan that you can use if you need to
examples: The exhibition shows that he has other strings to his artistic bow.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that there is no definite answer to a question
examples: ‘How long will it take?’ ‘How long's a piece of string?’

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to use your influence in order to get an advantage for somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to control events or the actions of other peopleWord Origin
examples: Old English streng (noun), of Germanic origin; related to German Strang, also to strong. The verb (dating from late Middle English) is first recorded in the senses ‘arrange in a row’ and ‘fit with a string’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long narrow piece of paper, metal, cloth, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO magnetic strip
a strip of material
Cut the meat into strips.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a long narrow area of land, sea, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO airstrip
the Gaza Strip
a tiny strip of garden
The islands are separated by a narrow strip of water.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the uniform that is worn by the members of a sports team when they are playing
examples: Juventus in their famous black and white strip
the team’s away strip (= that they use when playing games away from home)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an act of taking your clothes off, especially in a sexually exciting way and in front of an audience
examples: SEE ALSO striptease
to do a strip
a strip show

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a street that has many shops, stores, restaurants, etc. along it
examples: Sunset Strip

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a series of drawings inside boxes that tell a story and are often published in newspapers

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to speak angrily to somebody who has done something wrongWord Origin
examples: noun senses 1 to 2 and noun senses 5 to 6 late Middle English: from or related to Middle Low German strippe ‘strap, thong’, probably also to stripe. noun senses 3 to 4 Middle English (as a verb): of Germanic origin; related to Dutch stropen. Sense (3) of the noun arose in the late 20th cent., possibly from the notion of clothing to which a player “strips” down.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to try very hard to achieve something
examples: We encourage all members to strive for the highest standards.
They were always striving towards perfection.
striving against corruption
Newspaper editors all strive to be first with a story.
She strove to find a solution that was acceptable to all.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act of hitting a ball, for example with a bat or racket
examples: What a beautiful stroke!
He won by two strokes (= in golf, by taking two fewer strokes than his opponent).
He played some powerful backhand strokes throughout the game.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a single movement of the arm when hitting somebody/something
examples: His punishment was six strokes of the cane.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a single successful action or event
examples: SEE ALSO masterstroke
Your idea was a stroke of genius.
It was a stroke of luck that I found you here.
It was a bold stroke to reveal the identity of the murderer on the first page.
She never does a stroke (of work) (= never does any work).
I had a sudden stroke of inspiration.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a sudden serious illness when a blood vessel (= tube) in the brain bursts (= breaks open) or is blocked, which can cause death or the loss of the ability to move or to speak clearly
examples: to have/suffer a stroke
The stroke left him partly paralysed.
Smoking increases the risk of stroke.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: any of a series of repeated movements in swimming or rowing
examples: She took a few more strokes to reach the bank.
He swam with long powerful strokes.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a style of swimming
examples: SEE ALSO backstroke
Butterfly is the only stroke I can't do.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the person who sets the speed at which everyone in a boat rows

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: an act of moving your hand gently over a surface, usually several times
examples: He gave the cat a stroke.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a mark made by moving a pen, brush, etc. once across a surface
examples: to paint with fine brush strokes
At the stroke of a pen (= by signing something) they removed thousands of people from the welfare system.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: each of the sounds made by a clock or bell giving the hours
examples: At the first stroke it will be 9 o'clock exactly.
on the stroke of three (= at 3 o’clock exactly)

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: with a single immediate action
examples: They threatened to cancel the whole project at a stroke.
They lost half their fortune at a stroke.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to make somebody make a mistake or hesitate in what they are doing
examples: My speech was going well until I was put off my stroke by an interruption.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a lot of physical power so that you can lift heavy weights, do hard physical work, etc.
examples: He's strong enough to lift a car!
strong muscles
She wasn't a strong swimmer (= she could not swim well).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having great power
examples: Stay indoors in the middle of the day, when the sun is strongest.
a strong wind
a strong magnet/current

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having a powerful effect on the body or mind
examples: a strong drug
His imagery made a strong impression on the critics.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: having a lot of power or influence
examples: a strong leader
What the country needs right now is a strong government.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: people who are rich or powerful

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: difficult to attack or criticize
examples: There is strong evidence of a link between exercise and a healthy heart.
You have a strong case for getting your job back.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: very powerful and difficult for people to fight against or defeat
examples: a strong team
The proposal aroused strong opposition.
The temptation to tell her everything was very strong.
He exerts an extremely strong influence on his classmates.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: very powerful
examples: strong support for the government
People have strong feelings about this issue.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: holding an opinion or a belief very seriously
examples: SYNONYM firm
a strong supporter of the government
a strong opponent
She has long been one of the strongest advocates of sanctions.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: easy to see, hear, feel or smell; very great or intense
examples: a strong smell
a strong feeling of nausea
a strong voice (= loud)
strong colours
a face with strong features (= large and easy to notice)
She spoke with a strong Australian accent.
He was under strong pressure to resign.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: having a lot of taste
examples: OPPOSITE mild (4)
strong cheese
You'll need to use plenty of strong French mustard.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: containing a lot of a substance
examples: strong black coffee

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: not easily broken or damaged; made well
examples: The box looks strong enough.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: not easily upset or frightened; not easily influenced by other people
examples: SEE ALSO headstrong
You need strong nerves to ride a bike in London.
Every child needs to develop a strong sense of identity.
It's difficult, I know. But be strong!
a strong personality
She’s had a strong will since she was a baby.
We must stand strong in the face of adversity.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: likely to succeed or happen
examples: a strong candidate for the job
You're in a strong position to negotiate a deal.
There's a strong possibility that we'll lose the game.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: having existed for a long time and functioning well; difficult to destroy
examples: a strong marriage
The college has strong links with local industry.
I know that their relationship is growing stronger every day.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: having a value that is high or increasing
examples: strong share prices
The country is currently experiencing particularly strong economic growth.
The euro is getting stronger against the dollar.
This news helped keep the dollar relatively strong today.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: in a safe financial position
examples: Their catering business remained strong despite the recession.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: good at something; done well
examples: The play has a very strong cast.
The actors give extremely strong performances.
Mathematics was never my strong point (= I was never very good at it).

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: great in number
examples: There was a strong police presence at the demonstration.
Sales were surprisingly strong in the second half of the year.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used after numbers to show the size of a group
examples: a 5 000-strong crowd
The crowd was 5 000 strong.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: not easily affected by disease; healthy
examples: These vitamins are meant to keep you healthy and strong.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: having a lot of force, often causing offence to people
examples: The movie has been criticized for strong language (= swearing).

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: forming the past tense and past participle by changing a vowel, not by adding a regular ending, for example sing, sang, sung

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: used to describe the way some words are pronounced when they have stress. For example, the strong form of and is /ænd/.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: used to say that you think what somebody has said is unfair or too critical

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: something that gives somebody an advantage over other people in a particular situation

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to be good at something
examples: I'm not very strong on dates (= I can't remember the dates of important events).

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to have a lot of something
examples: The report was strong on criticism, but short on practical suggestions.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to be a subject that somebody knows a lot about
examples: I'm afraid geography is not my strong suit.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to make your feelings clear in an aggressive way, especially your sexual feelings towards somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to continue to be healthy, active or successful
examples: My grandmother is 90 and still going strong.
The business is still going strong.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to be able to see or do unpleasant things without feeling sick or upset
examples: You need a strong stomach to go on the giant roller coaster.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that shows definite and serious opinions or beliefs
examples: a strongly worded protest
He was strongly opposed to the idea.
This is an issue I feel strongly about.
This decision was strongly criticized by both sides.
Nearly all of them strongly agree that education is the key to success.
I strongly disagree with this statement.
We believe strongly in the importance of taking personal responsibility for our own actions.
We strongly urge the British government to take the necessary action.
I strongly suspect that this whole story is fictional.
The company says it strongly believes in the importance of organic agriculture.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to a great degree or extent
examples: Health spending is strongly linked to the country's wealth.
These conclusions are strongly supported by a recent study.
Interest is already very high and advance booking is strongly recommended.
She was strongly influenced by his views.
The evidence strongly suggests that he did not commit the crime.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a way that is easy to notice
examples: The room smelt strongly of polish.
These works are strongly reminiscent of earlier paintings.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: with a lot of power or force
examples: a light shining strongly
He finished strongly in a time of 38 minutes, 44 seconds.
The market rebounded strongly in the second half of the year.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in a way that means something cannot be easily broken or damaged
examples: a strongly built boat

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with the way in which something is built or organized
examples: Storms have caused structural damage to hundreds of homes.
structural changes in society
a structural survey (= an examination of a building to check for any damage to the walls, roof, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the way in which the parts of something are connected together, arranged or organized; a particular arrangement of parts
examples: the structure of the building
changes in the economic structure of society
Bees have a complex social structure.
the grammatical structures of a language
the structure of proteins/DNA

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that is made of several parts, especially a building
examples: a stone/brick/wooden structure
She used sand and rocks to build elaborate structures on the beach.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the state of being well organized or planned with all the parts linked together; a careful plan
examples: Your essay needs (a) structure.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to try very hard to do something when it is difficult or when there are a lot of problems
examples: life as a struggling artist (= one who is very poor)
Shona struggled for breath.
a country struggling for independence
The firm is struggling to cope with the demand for its products.
Local workers were still struggling to find employment.
Most social enterprises struggle to survive.
We're already struggling to keep up with demand.
They struggled just to pay their bills.
She struggled for 10 years to achieve success as an actress.
I was unemployed and struggling financially.
The housing market continues to struggle.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move somewhere or do something with difficulty
examples: I struggled up the hill with the heavy bags.
Paul struggled out of his wheelchair.
She had to struggle into the tight dress.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to fight against somebody/something in order to prevent a bad situation or result
examples: Chloe continued to struggle, but her eyes began to close.
He struggled against cancer for two years.
We should all struggle against injustice.
I have been struggling with injury for a couple of years
I am struggling with the same issues that other people are.
Lisa struggled with her conscience before talking to the police.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to fight somebody or try to get away from them
examples: I struggled and screamed for help.
James was hit in the mouth as he struggled with the raiders.
How did she manage to struggle free?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to compete or argue with somebody/something, especially in order to get something
examples: rival leaders struggling for power
countries struggling with each other for economic and military advantage

examples: SEE ALSO mature student
a college/university student
a graduate student
a medical/law student
international students (= who come to study from other countries)
She's a student at Oxford.
He's a third-year student at the College of Art.
a student loan (= money lent to students to pay for their studies)
He is here on a student visa.
a plan to reduce student debt
student fees (= to pay for the cost of teaching)
a student nurse/teacher
a dramatic increase in student numbers

definitions.definition: a person who is studying at a school, especially a secondary school
examples: COMPARE pupil
a 15-year-old high school student
a teacher who engages her students

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is very interested in a particular subject
examples: a keen student of human nature

definitions.definition: a room where radio or television programmes are recorded and broadcast from, or where music is recorded
examples: a television/recording studio
a studio audience (= one in a studio, that can be seen or heard as a programme is broadcast)
She has released eight studio albums.

definitions.definition: a place where films are made or produced
examples: The tour guide is showing a group of tourists around a movie studio.
a film studio

a studio executive

examples: a dance studio

examples: early 19th cent.: from Italian, from Latin studium ‘painstaking application’.

definitions.definition: the activity of learning or gaining knowledge, either from books or by examining things in the world
examples: SEE ALSO self-study
a room set aside for private study
academic/literary/scientific study
It is important to develop good study skills.
Physiology is the study of how living things work.

definitions.definition: a particular person’s learning activities, for example at a college or university
examples: to continue your studies

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: business/media/American studies

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to refer to a substance, material, group of objects, etc. when you do not know the name, when the name is not important or when it is obvious what you are talking about
examples: SEE ALSO foodstuff
What's all that sticky stuff on the carpet?
The chairs were covered in some sort of plastic stuff.
This wine is good stuff.
I don't know how you can eat that stuff!
They sell stationery and stuff (like that).
Where's all my stuff (= my possessions)?
Could you move all that stuff off the table?
I want to buy some expensive tech stuff.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to refer in a general way to things that people do, say, think, etc.
examples: Peter's article had lots of interesting stuff in it.
There's still a lot of cool stuff happening in Manchester.
I've got loads of stuff to do today.
I like reading and stuff.
The band did some great stuff on their first album.
This is all good stuff. Well done!
I don't believe in all that stuff about ghosts.
What's all this ‘Mrs Smith’ stuff? Call me Anna.
He's done so much stuff and been so many interesting places.
I've read a whole bunch of stuff by different people over the past few days.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the most important feature of something; something that something else is based on or is made from
examples: SEE ALSO hot stuff
The trip was magical; the stuff of which dreams are made.
Parades and marches were the very stuff of politics in the region.
Connor's story is the stuff of legend.
the stuff of dreams/nightmares
Let’s see what stuff you’re made of (= what sort of person you are).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have a stronger character and to be more determined in dealing with problems than other people
examples: Many would have given up, but Tim was made of sterner stuff.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody not to worry about small details or things that are not important

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to do what you are good at or what you have been trained to do
examples: Some members of the team are just not doing their stuff (= doing as well as they should).
The medicine has clearly done its stuff.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: something that is so easy to do or understand that it is thought to be not very serious or only suitable for children
examples: That was kids' stuff compared with what lies ahead.
The movie is pure kids' stuff from beginning to end.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to know a lot about a particular subject or job

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to not care at all about something

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to proudly show your ability, especially at dancing or performing
examples: strutting your stuff to the latest chart hits

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that something is stupid or not trueWord Origin
examples: Middle English (denoting material for making clothes): shortening of Old French estoffe ‘material, furniture’, estoffer ‘equip, furnish’, from Greek stuphein ‘draw together’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a problem or temporary failure when you are on the way to achieving something
examples: There were good reasons for the team's first-round stumble against Los Angeles.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an act of falling or almost falling, especially because you hit your foot against something
examples: After a slight stumble backwards, he regained his balance.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a mistake that causes you to stop when you are reading, speaking or playing music
examples: verbal stumbles

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a person or an animal unconscious for a short time, especially by hitting them on the head
examples: SYNONYM knock out
The fall stunned me for a moment.
The animals are stunned before slaughter.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to surprise or shock somebody so much that they cannot think clearly or speak
examples: SYNONYM astound
Her words stunned me—I had no idea she felt that way.
The guests were stunned into silence.
The company stunned investors with its third profits warning in five months.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to impress somebody very much
examples: SYNONYM amaze
They were stunned by the view from the summit.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: extremely attractive or impressive
examples: SYNONYM beautiful
You look absolutely stunning!
a stunning view of the lake
His performance was simply stunning.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that surprises or shocks you very much
examples: He suffered a stunning defeat in the election.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: showing a lack of thought or good judgement
examples: SYNONYM foolish
a stupid mistake/question/idea
It was a pretty stupid thing to do.
You've been warned, so don't do anything stupid.
I was stupid enough to believe him.
It was stupid of you to get involved.
That was just plain stupid!
We made some incredibly stupid business mistakes.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: slow to learn or understand things; not clever or intelligent
examples: He'll manage—he isn't stupid.
Forgetting my notes made me look stupid.
She always makes me feel really stupid.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you are annoyed with somebody/something
examples: I can't get the stupid thing open!
Get your stupid feet off the chair!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the particular way in which something is done
examples: SEE ALSO lifestyle
a wide range of musical styles
They want a wide range of learning resources to suit different learning styles.
a management style
a style of management
furniture to suit your style of living
His aggressive style of play sometimes gets him in trouble.
I really enjoy playing this style of music.
I like your style (= I like the way you do things).
Caution was not her style (= not the way she usually behaved).
I'm surprised he rides a motorbike—I'd have thought big cars were more his style (= what suited him).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a particular design of something, especially clothes
examples: SEE ALSO hairstyle
We stock a wide variety of styles and sizes.
Have you thought about having your hair in a shorter style?
a style that was popular in the 1950s

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of being fashionable in the clothes that you wear
examples: style-conscious teenagers
My husband has no sense of style.
Short skirts are back in style (= fashionable).
They still refer to her as a style guru and a trend-setter.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the quality of being attractive and made or done to a high standard
examples: The hotel has been redecorated but it's lost a lot of its style.
This movie is all surface style and no substance.
She does everything with style and grace.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the features of a book, painting, building, etc. that make it typical of a particular author, artist, historical period, etc.
examples: a style of architecture
a fine example of Gothic style
The film has a unique visual style.
He developed a distinctive style of painting.
a parody written in the style of Molière
The palace was rebuilt in the same style.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the correct use of language
examples: It's not considered good style to start a sentence with ‘but’.
Please follow house style (= the rules of spelling, etc. used by a particular publishing company).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: having the type of style mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO family-style
Italian-style gardens
a buffet-style breakfast

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the long, thin part of a flower that carries the stigma

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to stop somebody from behaving in the way they want to
examples: She didn’t want me to go with her to the party in case I cramped her style.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: in an impressive way
examples: She always celebrates her birthday in style.
He won the championship in great style.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing or person that is being discussed, described or dealt with
examples: Walker's work has been the subject of much debate.
a subject of discussion/conversation
Nelson Mandela is the subject of a new biography.
The incident is currently the subject of a police investigation.
books on many different subjects
I have nothing more to say on the subject.
a magazine article on the subject of space travel
How did we get onto the subject of marriage?
I wish you'd change the subject (= talk about something else).
We seem to have got off the subject we're meant to be discussing.
a subject for debate/discussion
The university runs a wide range of research programmes in different subject areas.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an area of knowledge studied in a school, college, etc.
examples: Biology is my favourite subject.
Which subjects are you studying?
The college offers a wide range of subjects.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that is the main feature of a picture or photograph, or that a work of art is based on
examples: Focus the camera on the subject.
Classical landscapes were a popular subject with many 18th century painters.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person or thing being used to study something, especially in an experiment
examples: We need male subjects between the ages of 18 and 25 for the experiment.

examples: a gesture of submission

His response was one of resistance, not submission.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of giving a document, proposal, etc. to somebody in authority so that they can study or consider it; the document, etc. that you give
examples: When is the final date for the submission of proposals?
They prepared a report for submission to the council.
The deadline is 1 October and late submissions will not be marked.
Many diploma courses require the submission of a project.

definitions.definition: a statement that is made to a judge in court
examples: All parties will have the opportunity to make submissions relating to this case.

examples: to submit an application/a claim/a proposal
Completed projects must be submitted by 10 March.
She submitted her report to the committee.
Articles should be submitted electronically as email attachments.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to accept the authority, control or greater strength of somebody/something; to agree to something because of this
examples: SYNONYM give in (to somebody/something)
She refused to submit to threats.
He submitted himself to a search by the guards.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to say or suggest something
examples: Counsel for the defence submitted that the evidence was inadmissible.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who pays money, usually once a year, to receive regular copies of a magazine or newspaper or have access to it online
examples: subscribers to ‘New Scientist’
Subscribers to the magazine can take advantage of this special offer.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who pays to receive a service
examples: subscribers to cable television

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who gives money regularly to help the work of an organization such as a charity
examples: subscribers to Oxfam

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of money that you pay regularly to receive a service, be a member of a club, support a charity or receive regular copies of a newspaper or magazine; the act of paying this money
examples: an annual subscription
a subscription to Netflix
a monthly subscription to Oxfam
to take out a subscription to ‘Newsweek’
to cancel/renew a subscription
Copies are available by subscription.
Subscriptions are due annually by the end of January.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of people paying money for something to be done
examples: A statue in his memory was erected by public subscription.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening or coming after something else
examples: OPPOSITE previous
subsequent generations
Subsequent events confirmed our doubts.
Developments on this issue will be dealt with in a subsequent report.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: afterwards; later; after something else has happened
examples: The original interview notes were subsequently lost.
Subsequently, new guidelines were issued to all employees.
He subsequently became chairman of the party.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: money that is paid by a government or an organization to reduce the costs of services or of producing goods so that their prices can be kept low
examples: agricultural subsidies
to reduce the level of subsidy

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a type of solid, liquid or gas that has particular qualities
examples: a sticky substance
a chemical/radioactive/hazardous substance
Some frogs produce toxic substances in their skin.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a drug, especially an illegal one
examples: illegal/controlled substances
He was disqualified from competing after testing positive to a banned substance.
Adolescent substance use remains high in the United States.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the quality of being based on facts or the truth
examples: The commission's report gives substance to these allegations.
There is some substance in what he says.
It was malicious gossip, completely without substance.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the most important or main part of something
examples: Love and guilt form the substance of his new book.
The real substance of the report was in the third part.
I agreed with what she said in substance, though not with every detail.
There seems to be no difference in substance between the two procedures.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: importance
examples: SYNONYM significance
matters of substance
Nothing of any substance was achieved in the meeting.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a rich and powerful man or womanWord Origin
examples: Middle English (denoting the essential nature of something): from Old French, from Latin substantia ‘being, essence’, from substant- ‘standing firm’, from the verb substare.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: large in amount, value or importance
examples: SYNONYM considerable
substantial sums of money
a substantial change
Substantial numbers of people support the reforms.
He ate a substantial breakfast.
There are substantial differences between the two groups.
Their share of the software market is substantial.
We were able to see a substantial improvement.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: large and solid; strongly built
examples: a substantial house
a street of substantial Victorian villas

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very much; a lot
examples: SYNONYM considerably
The costs have increased substantially.
The plane was substantially damaged in the crash.
The company’s profits have been substantially lower this year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: mainly; in most details, even if not completely
examples: What she says is substantially true.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or thing that you use or have instead of the one you normally use or have
examples: a meat substitute
a substitute family
Paul's father only saw him as a substitute for his dead brother.
The course teaches you the theory but there's no substitute for practical experience.
The local bus service was a poor substitute for their car.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a player who replaces another player in a sports game
examples: He was brought on as (a) substitute after half-time.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an act of using one person or thing in the place of another
examples: Two substitutions were made during the game.
the substitution of low-fat spreads for butter
the substitution of butter with low-fat spreads

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not very obvious or easy to notice
examples: subtle colours/flavours/smells, etc.
There are subtle differences between the two versions.
The fragrance is a subtle blend of jasmine and sandalwood.
She's been dropping subtle hints about what she'd like as a present.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: behaving or organized in a clever way, and using indirect methods, in order to achieve something
examples: I decided to try a more subtle approach.
a subtle plan
a subtle use of lighting in the play

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: good at noticing and understanding things
examples: The job required a subtle mind.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an area where people live that is outside the centre of a city
examples: SEE ALSO garden suburb
a suburb of London
a London suburb
They live in the suburbs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in or connected with a suburb
examples: suburban areas
a suburban street
life in suburban London

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: boring and ordinary
examples: a suburban lifestyle

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to achieve something that you have been trying to do or get; to have the result or effect that was intended
examples: OPPOSITE fail (1)
Our plan succeeded.
Whether we succeed or fail depends on ingenuity and luck.
He succeeded in getting a place at art school.
I tried to discuss it with her but only succeeded in making her angry (= I failed and did the opposite of what I intended).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be successful in your job, earning money, power, respect, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO success
You will have to work hard if you are to succeed.
She doesn't have the ruthlessness required to succeed in business.
He had hoped to succeed as a violinist.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to come next after somebody/something and take their/its place or position
examples: SYNONYM follow
Who succeeded Kennedy as President?
Their early success was succeeded by a period of miserable failure.
Strands of DNA are reproduced through succeeding generations.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to gain the right to a title, property, etc. when somebody dies
examples: SEE ALSO succession
She succeeded to the throne (= became queen) in 1558.
He had no right to succeed to the tenancy when his father died.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: when you are successful in one area of your life, it often leads to success in other areasWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French succeder or Latin succedere ‘come close after’, from sub- ‘close to’ + cedere ‘go’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the fact that you have achieved something that you want and have been trying to do or get
examples: The company has achieved considerable success in this market.
Initially the venture enjoyed a fair amount of success.
I didn't have much success in finding a job.
I tried a second time, but without success.
Confidence is the key to success.
Their plan will probably meet with little success.
The success or failure of the project was now in the students' control.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the fact of becoming rich or famous or of getting a high social position
examples: What's the secret of your success?
They didn't have much success in life.
She was surprised by the book's success (= that it had sold a lot of copies).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person or thing that has achieved a good result and been successful
examples: The party was a great success.
a resounding/tremendous/phenomenal success.
The book proved a huge commercial success.
He's proud of his daughter's successes.
He was determined to make a success of the business.
She wasn't a success as a teacher.
It is important to learn from both successes and failures.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: when you are successful in one area of your life, it often leads to success in other areas

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a very great success
examples: The evening was a resounding success.
The latest Disneyland has been a roaring success.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the pleasant feeling of being successfulWord Origin
examples: mid 16th cent.: from Latin successus, from the verb succedere ‘come close after’, from sub- ‘close to’ + cedere ‘go’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: achieving your aims or what was intended
examples: The experiment was entirely successful.
We congratulated them on the successful completion of the project.
He's always been highly successful in his work.
They were successful in winning the contract.
No one can be successful at everything.
I wasn't very successful at keeping the news secret.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having become popular and/or made a lot of money
examples: OPPOSITE unsuccessful
The play was very successful on Broadway.
a successful actor/businessman
She has had a long and successful career in television.
The company has had another successful year.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: in a way that achieves your aims or what was intended
examples: She had already successfully completed these courses.
They successfully defended their championship title.
Companies have to be able to compete successfully in international markets.
This arrangement has operated successfully for the past six years.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a number of people or things that follow each other in time or order
examples: SYNONYM series
a succession of visitors
He's been hit by a succession of injuries since he joined the team.
She has won the award for the third year in succession.
They had three children in quick succession.
The gunman fired three times in rapid succession.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the regular pattern of one thing following another thing
examples: the succession of the seasons
the succession of images on a screen

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of taking over an official position or title; the right to take over an official position or title, especially to become the king or queen of a country
examples: He became chairman in succession to Bernard Allen.
She's third in order of succession to the throne.
a line of succession

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: following immediately one after the other
examples: SYNONYM consecutive
This was their fourth successive win.
Successive governments have tried to tackle the problem.
There has been low rainfall for two successive years.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person or thing that comes after somebody/something else and takes their/its place
examples: COMPARE predecessor
Who's the likely successor to him as party leader?
Their latest release is a worthy successor to their popular debut album.
He chose as his successor a relative newcomer to the organization.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the great degree of something
examples: This issue was of such importance that we could not afford to ignore it.
Why are you in such a hurry?
It's such a beautiful day!
Such is the elegance of this typeface that it is still a favourite of designers.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: of the type already mentioned
examples: They had been invited to a Hindu wedding and were not sure what happened on such occasions.
He said he didn't have time or made some such excuse.
She longed to find somebody who understood her problems, and in him she thought she had found such a person.
We were second-class citizens and they treated us as such.
Accountants were boring. Such (= that) was her opinion before meeting Ian!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: of the type that you are just going to mention
examples: There is no such thing as a free lunch.
Such advice as he was given (= it was not very much) has proved almost worthless.
The knot was fastened in such a way that it was impossible to undo.
The damage was such that it would cost thousands to repair.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: and similar things or people
examples: The centre offers activities like canoeing and sailing and such.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: as the word is usually understood; in the exact sense of the word
examples: The new job is not a promotion as such, but it has good prospects.
‘Well, did they offer it to you?’ ‘No, not as such, but they said I had a good chance.’

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: for example
examples: Wild flowers such as primroses are becoming rare.
‘There are loads of things to do.’ ‘Such as?’ (= give me an example)

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: of a kind that; like
examples: Opportunities such as this did not come every day.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that there is not much of something or that it is of poor quality
examples: The food, such as it was, was served at nine o'clock.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to take liquid, air, etc. into your mouth by using the muscles of your lips
examples: to suck the juice from an orange
She was noisily sucking up milk through a straw.
He sucked the blood from a cut on his finger.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to keep something in your mouth and pull on it with your lips and tongue
examples: The baby sucked at its mother's breast.
He sucked at the wound on his hand.
She sucked on a mint.
She sucked a mint.
Stop sucking your thumb!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to take liquid, air, etc. out of something
examples: The pump sucks air out through the valve.
Greenfly can literally suck a plant dry.
The machine sucks up mud and stones from the bottom of the pond.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to pull somebody/something with great force in a particular direction
examples: The canoe was sucked down into the whirlpool.
The mud had sucked him in up to his waist.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that something is very bad
examples: COMPARE rock
Their new album sucks.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to get from somebody/something all the money, help, information, etc. they have, usually giving nothing in return
examples: By earning millions from racing and giving pennies back, the bookmakers are sucking the sport dry.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that the only way to know if something is suitable is to try it

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to accept something bad and deal with it well, controlling your emotions

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to tell or show somebody how to do something that they can already do well, and probably better than you canWord Origin
examples: Old English sūcan (verb), from an Indo-European imitative root; related to soak.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: happening or done quickly and unexpectedly
examples: News of his sudden and unexpected death came as a great shock.
a sudden change in temperature
There were several sudden bursts of gunfire outside.
It was only decided yesterday. It's all been very sudden.
Don't make any sudden movements.
His death was very sudden.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: quickly and unexpectedly
examples: All of a sudden someone grabbed me around the neck.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: quickly and unexpectedly
examples: I suddenly realized what I had to do.
I suddenly became aware of just how late it was.
She took ill and died suddenly at her home.
You might suddenly find yourself in dire need of cash.
A pedestrian suddenly appeared in front of the taxi.
I tried to sit up but I suddenly felt dizzy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a claim against a person or an organization in court about something that they have said or done to harm you
examples: They threatened to sue if the work was not completed.
to sue somebody for breach of contract
to sue somebody for $10 million (= in order to get money from somebody)
to sue somebody for damages
He threatened to sue the company for negligence.
The water authority was successfully sued over his illness.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to formally ask for something, especially in court
examples: to sue for divorce
The rebels were forced to sue for peace.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be badly affected by a disease, pain, sad feelings, a lack of something, etc.
examples: I hate to see animals suffering.
The country has suffered greatly at the hands of its corrupt government.
to suffer from a disorder/a disease/an illness/a condition
patients suffering from depression/cancer
Increasing numbers of children are suffering from mental health problems.
He suffers from asthma.
The economy is still suffering badly from a lack of demand.
to suffer with depression/a cold
He made a rash decision and now he is suffering for it.
The lead actor had to suffer for his art by losing 10kg for the role.
Women continue to suffer in silence under the repressive regime.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to experience something unpleasant, such as injury, defeat or loss
examples: to suffer a stroke/heart attack
Victims suffered severe injuries in the accident.
The company suffered huge losses in the last financial year.
Crops suffered serious damage as a result of the floods.
The party suffered a humiliating defeat in the general election.
His mother died young, and his sister suffered the same fate (= his sister also died young).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to become worse
examples: His school work is suffering because of family problems.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be very impatient with people that you think are stupid
examples: She was a forceful personality who didn't suffer fools gladly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: physical or mental pain
examples: Death finally brought an end to her suffering.
This war has caused widespread human suffering.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: feelings of pain and unhappiness
examples: The hospice aims to ease the sufferings of the dying.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: enough for a particular purpose; as much as you need
examples: OPPOSITE insufficient
Allow sufficient time to get there.
One dose should be sufficient.
These reasons are not sufficient to justify the ban.
Our budget is hardly sufficient to pay people, let alone buy any new equipment.
Is £100 sufficient for your expenses?
The salary proved sufficient for his needs.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: enough for a particular purpose; as much as you need
examples: OPPOSITE insufficiently
The following day she felt sufficiently well to go to work.
By 1995, bald eagles had recovered sufficiently to be removed from the endangered list.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sweet substance, often in the form of white or brown crystals, made from the juices of various plants, used in cooking or to make tea, coffee, etc. sweeter
examples: SEE ALSO barley sugar
Do you take sugar (= have it in your tea, coffee, etc.)?
Serve the cake warm or cold, sprinkled with sugar.
This juice contains no added sugar.
a sugar bowl
a sugar plantation/refinery
He stirred another spoonful of sugar into his tea.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the amount of sugar that a small spoon can hold or that is contained in a small cube, added to tea, coffee, etc.
examples: How many sugars do you take in coffee?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: any of various sweet substances that are found naturally in plants, fruit, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO blood sugar
fruit sugars
Fruit juices contain natural sugars.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a way of addressing somebody that you like or love
examples: See you later, sugar.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to put forward an idea or a plan for other people to think about
examples: SYNONYM propose
I'd like to suggest a different explanation for the company's decline.
The designer is known for suggesting innovative ideas to her clients.
He thought long and hard, but no answer suggested itself.
A solution immediately suggested itself to me (= I immediately thought of a solution).
I strongly suggest (that) you don't get involved.
I suggested going in my car.
It has been suggested that bright children take their exams early.
It has been suggested that bright children should take their exams early.
‘We could go for a drive,’ Nate suggested hopefully.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to tell somebody about a suitable person, thing, method, etc. for a particular job or purpose
examples: SYNONYM recommend
Who would you suggest for the job?
She suggested Paris as a good place for the conference.
She suggested John as chairman.
Can you suggest a better way of doing it?
May I suggest a white wine with this dish, Sir?
There is a suggested donation of $5 to attend the show.
Can you suggest how I might contact him?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to put an idea into somebody’s mind; to make somebody think that something is true
examples: SYNONYM indicate
All the evidence suggests (that) he stole the money.
Recent studies suggest the possibility of a cure for the disease.
Some believe that organic foods offer no health benefits, but this research suggests otherwise.
The symptoms suggest a minor heart attack.
The stage lighting was used to suggest a beach scene.
What do these results suggest to you?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to state something indirectly
examples: SYNONYM imply
Are you suggesting (that) I’m lazy?
I’m not suggesting (that) she was responsible for the accident.
I would never suggest such a thing.
It is not far-fetched to suggest a connection between them.
You're not seriously suggesting that is a plausible explanation?
I do not mean to suggest that the poem is purely biographical.
I am merely suggesting that there is more than one way to view this matter.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an idea or a plan that you mention for somebody else to think about
examples: Can I make a suggestion?
Do you have any suggestions?
I would like to offer a suggestion.
He rejected my suggestion as impractical.
The report offers suggestions for improvement to policy.
I'd like to hear your suggestions for ways of raising money.
We welcome any comments and suggestions on these proposals.
Are there any suggestions about how best to tackle the problem?
He agreed with my suggestion that we should change the date.
We are open to suggestions (= willing to listen to ideas from other people).
We need to get it there by four. Any suggestions?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a reason to think that something, especially something bad, is true
examples: SYNONYM hint
A spokesman dismissed any suggestion of a boardroom rift.
There is no suggestion of any impropriety.
There was no suggestion that he was doing anything illegal.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: putting an idea into people’s minds by connecting it with other ideas
examples: Most advertisements work through suggestion.
the power of suggestion

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a slight amount or sign of something
examples: SYNONYM trace
She looked at me with just a suggestion of a smile.
He spoke English with a suggestion of a French accent.
Her eyes contained a strong suggestion of mischief.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: because somebody suggested it
examples: At his suggestion, I bought the more expensive printer.
At the suggestion of his boss, he resigned.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of killing yourself deliberately
examples: SEE ALSO assisted suicide
to commit suicide
an attempted suicide (= one in which the person survives)
a suicide bomber (= who expects to die while trying to kill other people with a bomb)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a course of action that is likely to destroy your career, position in society, etc.
examples: It would have been political suicide for him to challenge the allegations in court.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who commits suicideWord Origin
examples: mid 17th cent.: from modern Latin suicida ‘act of suicide’, suicidium ‘person who commits suicide’, from Latin sui ‘of oneself’ + caedere ‘kill’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a set of clothes made of the same cloth, including a jacket and trousers or a skirt
examples: SEE ALSO dinner suit
He was wearing a grey business suit.
He is dressed in a formal black suit.
They won't let you into the restaurant without a suit and tie.
a two-/three-piece suit (= of two/three pieces of clothing)
a pinstripe suit

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set of clothing worn for a particular activity
examples: SEE ALSO bathing suit
a diving suit
a suit of armour
His parents had bought him a new suit of clothes for the occasion.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: any of the four sets that form a pack of cards
examples: The suits are called hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a claim or complaint against somebody that a person or an organization can make in court
examples: SEE ALSO paternity suit
to file/bring a suit against somebody
a divorce suit

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person with an important job as a manager in a company or organization, especially one who is thought to work mainly with financial matters or to have a lot of influence
examples: We can leave the detailed negotiations to the suits.
He’s a ‘suit’, not a ‘creative’.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be a subject that somebody knows a lot about
examples: I'm afraid geography is not my strong suit.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to play a card of the same suit that has just been played

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to act or behave in the way that somebody else has just done

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: not wearing any clothesWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Anglo-Norman French siwte, from a feminine past participle of a Romance verb based on Latin sequi ‘follow’. Early senses included ‘attendance at a court’ and ‘legal process’; senses (1) to (3) derive from an earlier meaning ‘set of things to be used together’. The verb sense ‘make appropriate’ dates from the late 16th cent.

definitions.definition: right or appropriate for a particular purpose or occasion
examples: OPPOSITE unsuitable
a suitable candidate
a suitable habitat/location/site
This programme is not suitable for children.
a suitable place for a picnic
The documentary is particularly suitable for classroom use.
I don't have anything suitable to wear for the party.
Would now be a suitable moment to discuss my report?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a set of rooms, especially in a hotel
examples: SEE ALSO edit suite
a hotel/private/honeymoon suite
a suite of rooms/offices

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set of matching pieces of furniture
examples: a bathroom/bedroom suite
a three-piece suite with two armchairs and a sofa

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a piece of music made up of three or more related parts, for example pieces from an opera
examples: Stravinsky’s Firebird Suite

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a set of related computer programs
examples: a suite of software development tools

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of money
examples: SEE ALSO capital sum
You will be fined the sum of £200.
a large sum of money
The judge awarded them an undisclosed six-figure sum in damages.
Huge sums have been invested in this project.
The team has raised substantial sums for local charities.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the number you get when you add two or more numbers together
examples: The sum of 7 and 12 is 19.
Calculate the sum of the following figures.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: all of something, especially when you think that it is not very much
examples: This is the sum of my achievements so far.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a simple problem that involves calculating numbers
examples: to do a sum in your head
I was good at sums at school.
If I've got my sums right, I should be able to afford the rent.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be better or more effective as a group than you would think just by looking at the individual members of the group
examples: The team is greater than the sum of its parts.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to introduce a short statement of the main points of a discussion, speech, etc.
examples: In sum, we have no chance of winning the case.

definitions.definition: to give a summary of something
examples: This essay briefly summarizes some of our approaches.

To summarize, the main conclusions are as follows…
The findings are summarized in Table 4.
The main findings of this research are summarized below.
The research has been usefully summarized in an article by Greenwood.
The argument can be summarized as follows:…

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a short statement that gives only the main points of something, not the details
examples: SEE ALSO executive summary
a news summary
The following is a summary of our conclusions.
What follows is a brief summary of the findings.
He has provided a useful summary of the main categories.
a two-page summary of a government report
The book provides useful summaries of the arguments.
In summary, this was a disappointing performance.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the warmest season of the year, coming between spring and autumn
examples: SEE ALSO Indian summer
We're going away in the summer.
in the summer of 2019
this/next/last summer
two summers ago
It's very hot here in summer.
late/early summer
It is now high summer (= the hottest part of summer).
during the long hot summer
a cool/wet summer
I managed to get six weeks' work over the summer.
Sales will take place throughout the spring and summer.
a summer’s day
She was wearing a light summer dress.
The house is now open to the public during the summer months.
the summer holidays/vacation/break

Are you looking for a summer job?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: you must not take too seriously a small sign that something is happening or will happen in the future, because the situation could changeWord Origin
examples: Old English sumor, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch zomer, German Sommer, also to Sanskrit samā ‘year’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the highest point of something, especially the top of a mountain
examples: We reached the summit at noon.
This path leads to the summit.
the summit of his career

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an official meeting or series of meetings between the leaders of two or more governments at which they discuss important matters
examples: a summit in Moscow
a summit conference

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the star that shines in the sky during the day and gives the earth heat and light
examples: The sun was shining and birds were singing.
the sun’s rays
The sun rises highest in the sky during the summer.
the rising/setting sun
The sun was just setting.
A pale wintry sun shone through the clouds.
The vampire is killed by the first rays of the morning sun.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the light and heat from the sun
examples: SYNONYM sunshine
the warmth of the afternoon sun
The sun was blazing hot.
This room gets the sun in the mornings.
We sat in the sun.
The harvested crop is dried in the hot Indian sun.
They've booked a holiday in the sun (= in a place where it is warm and the sun shines a lot).
We did our best to keep out of the sun.
Her face had obviously caught the sun (= become red or brown) on holiday.
Too much sun ages the skin.
I was driving westwards and I had the sun in my eyes (= the sun was shining in my eyes).
Patients are advised to avoid sun exposure for six weeks.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: any star around which planets move

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make good use of opportunities, good conditions, etc. while they last

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a position in which you are comfortable or have an advantage over other people

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you are talking about a very large number of things
examples: We talked about everything under the sun.
I’ve been called all the names under the sun!
There is nothing new under the sun (= in the world).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: when the sun rises or sets
examples: I get up with the sun.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: It's Sunday today, isn't it?
She went to a cooking class last Sunday.
Are you busy next Sunday?
Sunday morning/afternoon/evening
We'll see each other at Sunday's party.
I work Sunday to Thursday.
I work Sundays to Thursdays.
We'll meet on Sunday (= next Sunday).
We met on Sunday (= last Monday).
We'll meet Sunday.
The office is closed on Sundays (= every Sunday).
The office is closed Sundays.
He was born on a Sunday.
I always do yoga on a Sunday (= every Sunday).

‘When did the accident happen?’ ‘It was the Sunday (= the Sunday of the week we are talking about).’
Come back Sunday week (= a week after next Sunday).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a newspaper published on a Sunday

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something will never happen or will take a very long time
examples: You won't find it, not in a month of Sundays.
It is possible to learn to skydive in Britain, but with our weather it might take a month of Sundays to do it.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: your best clothes
examples: I put on my Sunday best for the occasion.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: extremely good
examples: a super meal
We had a super time in Italy.
‘The pilot did a super job,’ a passenger said afterwards.
She was super (= very kind) when I was having problems.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: excellent; of very good quality
examples: a superb player
The car's in superb condition.
His performance was absolutely superb.
You look superb.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: better in quality than somebody/something else; greater than somebody/something else
examples: OPPOSITE inferior
vastly superior
superior intelligence
Liverpool were clearly the superior team.
This model is technically superior to its competitors.
She felt socially superior to most of her neighbours.
The enemy won because of their superior numbers (= there were more of them).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: higher in rank, importance or position
examples: OPPOSITE inferior
my superior officer
superior status
a superior court of law

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: showing by your behaviour that you think you are better than others
examples: SYNONYM arrogant
a superior manner
He always looks so superior.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: of very good quality; better than other similar things
examples: superior apartments
The hotel offers superior accommodation and leisure facilities.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large shop that sells food, drinks and goods used in the home. People choose what they want from the shelves and pay for it as they leave.
examples: I only shop at this supermarket.
It is the fifth largest supermarket chain in the UK.
An increasing amount of organic produce is to be found on supermarket shelves.
a supermarket checkout/aisle
a supermarket trolley

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be in charge of somebody/something and make sure that everything is done correctly, safely, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO unsupervised
to supervise building work
Who is supervising?
She supervised the children playing near the pool.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the work or activity involved in being in charge of somebody/something and making sure that everything is done correctly, safely, etc.
examples: Very young children should not be left to play without supervision.
The drug should only be used under medical supervision.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a meeting between a student and their tutor or supervisor that involves teaching and discussion of the student's work
examples: SYNONYM tutorial (1)
I have weekly supervisions.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who supervises somebody/something
examples: I have a meeting with my supervisor about my research topic.
All work is done under the guidance of a supervisor.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that is added to something else to improve or complete it
examples: vitamin/dietary supplements (= vitamins and other foods eaten in addition to what you usually eat)
Industrial sponsorship is a supplement to government funding.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an extra separate section, often in the form of a magazine, that is sold with a newspaper
examples: the Sunday colour supplements
Our special supplement is packed with ideas for healthy hair.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a book or a section at the end of a book that gives extra information or deals with a special subject
examples: the supplement to the Oxford English Dictionary
a supplement to the main report
You can use these books as supplements to the basic English course.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an amount of money that you pay for an extra service or item, especially in addition to the basic cost of a holiday
examples: SYNONYM surcharge
There is a £10 supplement for a single room.
There is a supplement on rooms with a sea view.
Safety deposit boxes are available at a supplement.
