definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount of something that is provided or available to be used
examples: SEE ALSO money supply
Advances in agriculture increased the food supply.
Demand for skilled labour outstrips supply.
We ordered a month's supply of oil.
We cannot guarantee adequate supplies of raw materials.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the things such as food, medicines, fuel, etc. that are needed by a group of people, for example an army or expedition
examples: Our supplies were running out.
food and medical supplies for refugees

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the act of supplying something; the fact of receiving something that is being supplied
examples: SEE ALSO water supply
the electricity/energy/gas supply
The storm disrupted the town's power supply.
A stroke is caused by disruption to the blood supply to the brain.
the supply of goods and services
a contract for the supply of timber

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not existing in large enough quantities to satisfy demand
examples: Basic foodstuffs were in short supply.
Sunshine will be in short supply for the west coast.
Safe drinking water is in desperately short supply.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to help or encourage somebody/something by saying or showing that you agree with them/it
examples: SYNONYM back
to support an idea/a view
The party fully supports new welfare reform bill.
Efforts to reduce waste are strongly supported by environmental groups.
The majority of ordinary citizens did not support the war.
If you raise it at the meeting, I'll support you.
The government supported the unions in their demand for a minimum wage.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give or be ready to give help to somebody if they need it
examples: an organization that supports people with AIDS
She supported her husband through many difficult times.
The company will support customers in Europe (= solve their problems with a product).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to like a particular sports team, watch their games, etc.
examples: Which team do you support?
Who do you support?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to help or encourage something to be successful by giving it money
examples: SYNONYM sponsor
The project was supported by grants from various charities.
A number of famous actors actively supported the campaign.
Several major companies are supporting the project.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to provide everything necessary, especially money, so that somebody/something can live or exist
examples: He struggles to support his family.
She supported herself through college by working as a waitress in a local bar.
He turned to crime to support his drug habit.
The atmosphere of Mars could not support life.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to help to show that something is true
examples: SYNONYM corroborate
Current data support this hypothesis.
There is no evidence to support his claims.
The witness's story was not supported by the evidence.
He said the figures were questionable and not well supported.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to hold somebody/something in position; to prevent somebody/something from falling
examples: a platform supported by concrete pillars
Support the baby's head when you hold it.
She walked carefully down the stairs, supported by her grandson.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to perform in a pop or rock concert before the main performer
examples: They were supported by a local Liverpool band.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to allow a particular program, language or device to be used with it
examples: This digital audio player supports multiple formats.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who supports a political party, an idea, etc.
examples: a strong/loyal/staunch/ardent supporter
Labour supporters
The magazine is free to members and supporters.
About a hundred of his supporters rallied to demand justice.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who supports a particular sports team
examples: SYNONYM fan
I'm an Arsenal supporter.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: encouraging somebody or giving them help or sympathy
examples: a supportive family
She was very supportive during my father's illness.
a mutually supportive relationship
He was strongly supportive of my career.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to think or believe that something is true or possible (based on the knowledge that you have)
examples: Getting a visa isn't as simple as you might suppose.
Prices will go up, I suppose.
I don't suppose for a minute that he'll agree (= I'm sure that he won't).
It's reasonable to suppose that he left the note after he tried to call her.
Why do you suppose he resigned?
I suppose all the tickets have been sold now, have they?
There is no reason to suppose she's lying.
I suppose you think it's funny, do you? (= showing anger).
She had supposed him (to be) very rich.
I had supposed his wife a younger woman.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to make a statement, request or suggestion less direct or less strong
examples: I could take you in the car, I suppose (= but I don't really want to).
‘Can I borrow the car?’ ‘I suppose so’ (= Yes, but I'm not happy about it).
What I’m saying, I suppose, is that she’s not really suitable for the job.
I don’t suppose (that) I could have a look at your newspaper, could I?
Suppose we take a later train?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to pretend that something is true; to imagine what would happen if something were true
examples: Suppose flights are fully booked on that day—which other day could we go?
Let us suppose, for example, that you are married with two children.
Let's suppose for a moment that these four points are correct.
The theory supposes the existence of life on other planets.
Suppose him (to be) dead—what then?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be expected or required to do/be something according to a rule, a custom, an arrangement, etc.
examples: What am I supposed to do?
You're supposed to buy a ticket, but not many people do.
I thought we were supposed to be paid today.
The engine doesn't sound like it's supposed to.
You were supposed to be here an hour ago!
Oops—that wasn't supposed to happen.
How was I supposed to know you were waiting for me?
‘Yes and no.’ ‘What is that supposed to mean?’ (= showing that you are annoyed)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be generally believed or expected to be/do something
examples: I haven't seen it myself, but it's supposed to be a great movie.
This combination of qualities is generally supposed to be extremely rare.
She's supposed to have had hundreds of lovers.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to not be allowed to do something
examples: You're not supposed to walk on the grass.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: according to what is generally thought or believed but not known for certain
examples: SYNONYM allegedly
The novel is supposedly based on a true story.
a poem supposedly written by Shakespeare
Police have found the supposedly stolen car.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to put an end, often by force, to a group or an activity that is believed to threaten authority
examples: SYNONYM quash
The rebellion was brutally suppressed.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to prevent something from being published or made known
examples: The police were accused of suppressing vital evidence.
This information had been deliberately suppressed.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to prevent yourself from having or expressing a feeling or an emotion
examples: to suppress a smile
She was unable to suppress her anger.
He had suppressed the painful memories of his childhood.
He could hardly suppress his surprise.
Her face was charged with barely suppressed anger.
She was unable to suppress a giggle.
The disloyal thought was instantly suppressed.
He couldn't suppress the excitement in his voice.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to prevent something from growing, developing or continuing
examples: drugs that suppress the appetite

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: highest in rank or position
examples: the Supreme Commander of the armed forces
the supreme champion
It is an event in which she reigns supreme.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very great or the greatest in degree
examples: to make the supreme sacrifice (= die for what you believe in)
a supreme effort
She smiled with supreme confidence.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: confident that you know something or that you are right
examples: SYNONYM certain
‘Is that John over there?’ ‘I'm not sure’.
You don't sound very sure.
I'm pretty sure (that) he'll agree.
Are you sure you don't mind?
I’m sure he’s still alive.
I hope you are sure of your facts.
Are you sure about that?
Ask me if you're not sure how to do it.
I'm not sure whether I should tell you this.
not exactly/entirely/absolutely/really sure
I still wasn't even sure who I was talking to.
I like this bit, but I'm not so sure about that one.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: certain that you will receive something or that something will happen
examples: You're always sure of a warm welcome there.
We could not be sure of financial support.
England must win this game to be sure of qualifying for the World Cup.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: certain to do something or to happen
examples: The exhibition is sure to be popular.
It's sure to rain.
You’re sure to get lost if you don’t keep to the path.
She's sure to be picked for the team.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: that can be trusted or relied on
examples: It's a sure sign of economic recovery.
There's only one sure way to do it.
He is a sure bet for the presidential nomination (= certain to succeed).
I told my friends that our winning was a sure thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: steady and confident
examples: We admired her sure touch at the keyboard.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to do something
examples: Be sure to give your family my regards.
Be sure to check out our website.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: without doubt
examples: No one knows for sure what happened.
I think he'll be back on Monday, but I can't say for sure.
One thing is for sure—it's not going to be easy.
‘Will you be there?’ ‘For sure.’

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: something that is likely to happen, to succeed or to be suitable
examples: He's a good bet to earn a spot on the US team.
Clothes are a safe bet as a present for a teenager.
The movie looks like a sure bet for Best Film.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to do something in order to be certain that something else happens
examples: Make sure (that) no one finds out about this.
They scored another goal and made sure of victory.
Our staff will do their best to make sure you enjoy your visit.
To make doubly sure they would not be disturbed she turned the key in the lock.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to check that something is true or has been done
examples: She looked around to make sure that she was alone.
I think the door's locked, but I'll just go and make sure.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: very confident
examples: She seems very sure of herself.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say ‘yes’ to a suggestion or request
examples: ‘Are you coming?’ ‘Sure thing.’

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to admit that something is true
examples: He is intelligent, to be sure, but he's also very lazy.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to show that you are almost certain of what you are saying and want other people to agree with you
examples: Surely we should do something about it?
It's surely only a matter of time before he is found, isn't it?
Surely by now, things could be organized better?
Oil prices will surely have some impact on trade.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used with a negative to show that something surprises you and you do not want to believe it
examples: Surely you don't think I was responsible for this?
‘They're getting married.’ ‘Surely not!’
They won't go, surely?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: without doubt; certainly
examples: NOTE AT course
He knew that if help did not arrive soon they would surely die.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say ‘yes’ to somebody or to agree to something

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: making slow but definite progress
examples: We'll get there slowly but surely.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the outside or top layer of something
examples: We need a flat, smooth surface to play the game on.
an uneven road surface
a broad leaf with a large surface area
Surface water (= rainwater that has collected on the surface of a road) made driving conditions hazardous.
Teeth have a hard surface layer called enamel.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the top layer of an area of water or land
examples: the earth's surface
These plants float on the surface of the water.
We could see fish swimming just below the surface.
Alligators lurk beneath the surface of the swamp.
The earth’s surface temperature is rising.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the flat upper part of a piece of furniture, that is used for working on
examples: SEE ALSO work surface
She's cleaned all the kitchen surfaces.
You'll need a large smooth surface for rolling out the pastry.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the outer appearance of a person, thing or situation; the qualities that you see or notice, that are not hidden
examples: Rage bubbled just below the surface of his mind.
She gives the impression of being rather conventional, but under the surface she is wildly eccentric.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: when not thought about deeply or carefully and completely; when not looked at carefully
examples: It seems like a good idea on the surface but there are sure to be problems.
On the surface, he appeared unchanged.
On the surface his words were funny, but I detected a lot of anger behind them.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to deal with, understand, or find out about only a small part of a subject or problem
examples: We left feeling that we had just scratched the surface of this fascinating country.
The investigation barely scratched the surface of the city's drug problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a sudden increase of a strong feeling
examples: SYNONYM rush
She felt a sudden surge of anger.
a surge of excitement

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sudden increase in the amount or number of something
examples: SEE ALSO upsurge
a surge in consumer spending
We are having trouble keeping up with the recent surge in demand.
A last-minute surge in ticket sales saved the show from closure.
After an initial surge of interest, there has been little call for our services.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a sudden, strong movement forward or upwards
examples: SEE ALSO storm surge
a tidal surge
A surge of people poured through the gates.
Police struggled to control the sudden surge forward by the demonstrators.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a sudden increase in the flow of electrical power through a system
examples: An electrical surge damaged the computer's disk drive.
The National Grid was hit by a huge power surge.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a doctor who is trained to perform surgery (= medical operations that involve cutting open a person’s body)
examples: COMPARE physician
a brain/heart surgeon
Surgeons performed two operations on him yesterday.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: medical treatment of injuries or diseases that involves cutting open a person’s body and often removing or replacing some parts; the branch of medicine connected with this treatment
examples: SEE ALSO brain surgery
major/minor surgery
to undergo heart/knee/shoulder surgery
He will require surgery on his left knee.
The doctor had to perform emergency surgery to the patient's head.
She's a specialist in reconstructive and cosmetic surgery.
The president is to undergo minor surgery to remove a small growth from his hand.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a place where a doctor, dentist or vet sees patients
examples: a doctor’s/dentist’s/vet's surgery

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the time during which a doctor, dentist or vet is available to see patients
examples: morning/afternoon/evening surgery
surgery hours
Is there a surgery this evening?
He holds surgery from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a time when people can meet their Member of Parliament to ask questions and get help
examples: a constituency surgery

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used in or connected with surgery
examples: surgical procedures
a surgical ward (= for patients having operations)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an amount that is extra or more than you need
examples: SEE ALSO army surplus
food surpluses
Wheat was in surplus that year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the amount by which the amount of money received is greater than the amount of money spent
examples: COMPARE deficit
a surplus of £400 million
The balance of payments was in surplus last year (= the value of exports was greater than the value of imports).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an event, a piece of news, etc. that is unexpected or that happens suddenly
examples: What a nice surprise!
I have a surprise for you!
a surprise attack
There are few surprises in this year's budget.
It comes as no surprise to learn that they broke their promises.
Her letter came as a complete surprise.
‘The appointment came as a pleasant surprise to me,’ she says.
The announcements came as something of a surprise to them.
There are lots of surprises in store for visitors to the gallery.
He was there on a surprise visit to the troops.
Life’s full of surprises.
She likes springing surprises on people.
Visitors to the gallery are in for a few surprises.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a feeling caused by something happening suddenly or unexpectedly
examples: a look of surprise
She looked up in surprise.
He gasped with surprise at her strength.
They couldn't conceal their surprise at seeing us together.
I got a surprise when I saw the bill.
To everyone's surprise, the plan succeeded.
Much to my surprise, I passed.
Imagine our surprise when he walked into the room!
When we went inside we got a nasty surprise.
The decision has been greeted with surprise.
They expressed surprise at the outcome.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the use of methods that cause feelings of surprise
examples: A successful campaign should have an element of surprise.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show that something is not a surprise to you, as you could easily have predicted that it would happen or be true
examples: One of the candidates was the manager's niece, and surprise, surprise, she got the job.
Bob turned up half an hour late, surprise surprise.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used when giving somebody a surprise
examples: Surprise, surprise! Look who's here!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to happen unexpectedly so that somebody is slightly shocked; to surprise somebody
examples: His frankness took her by surprise.
The storm took us completely by surprise.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to attack or capture somebody/something unexpectedly or without warning
examples: The police took the burglars by surprise.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling or showing surprise
examples: COMPARE unsurprised
a surprised look
She looked surprised when I told her.
I was surprised at how quickly she agreed.
I'm surprised at you, behaving like that in front of the kids.
They were surprised to find that he'd already left.
You shouldn’t be surprised (that) he didn’t come.
Don't be surprised if I pretend not to recognize you.
‘Will she cancel the party?’ ‘I wouldn't be surprised.’
You’d be surprised how many people voted for him.
He was pleasantly surprised to discover that he was no longer afraid.
to be a little/a bit/quite surprised
She seemed somewhat surprised at his reaction.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: causing surprise
examples: LANGUAGE BANK AT contrast
It’s not surprising (that) they lost.
The frequency of such bad weather is hardly surprising given how far north we are.
A surprising number of people came.
We had a surprising amount in common.
It's surprising what people will do for money.
It’s surprising how many people applied for the job.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to admit that you have been defeated and want to stop fighting; to allow yourself to be caught, taken prisoner, etc.
examples: SYNONYM give in (to somebody/something)
The rebel soldiers were forced to surrender.
He surrendered voluntarily to his enemies.
The hijackers eventually surrendered themselves to the police.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to give up something/somebody when you are forced to
examples: SYNONYM relinquish
He agreed to surrender all claims to the property.
They surrendered their guns to the police.
The defendant was released to await trial but had to surrender her passport.
The dictator surrendered power to Parliament.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be all around something/somebody
examples: Tall trees surround the lake.
the membranes surrounding the brain
The garden is surrounded by a wall.
As a child I was surrounded by love and kindness.
I loved being surrounded by enthusiastic young people.
The lake is surrounded with trees.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move into position all around somebody/something, especially so as to prevent them from escaping; to move somebody/something into position in this way
examples: Police surrounded the building.
They've surrounded the building with police.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be closely connected with something/somebody
examples: publicity surrounding the divorce
the controversy/circumstances surrounding his death
The report explores the issues surrounding the case.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to choose to have particular people or things near you all the time
examples: I like to surround myself with beautiful things.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: that is near or around something
examples: Oxford and the surrounding area
From the top of the hill you can see all the surrounding countryside.
the immediately surrounding area
The college tries to respond to the needs of the surrounding community.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of carefully watching a person suspected of a crime or a place where a crime may be committed
examples: SYNONYM observation
The police are keeping the suspects under constant surveillance.
surveillance cameras/equipment

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an investigation of the opinions, behaviour, etc. of a particular group of people, which is usually done by asking them questions
examples: A recent survey showed 75 per cent of those questioned were in favour of the plan.
The survey revealed/found that…
to conduct/carry out/do/complete a survey
According to the survey, many young adults have experimented with drugs of some kind.
Another national survey conducted last year found the same result.
Roughly half of survey respondents express strong interest in additional education.
The results of the survey come as no surprise to us.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of examining and recording the measurements, features, etc. of an area of land in order to make a map or plan of it
examples: an aerial survey (= made by taking photographs from an aircraft)
A geological survey revealed the presence of oil beneath the ground.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an examination of the condition of a house, etc., usually done for somebody who is thinking of buying it
examples: a detailed structural survey

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a general study, view or description of something
examples: a comprehensive survey of modern music
a historical survey of children's clothing

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the state of continuing to live or exist, often despite difficulty or danger
examples: the struggle/battle/fight for survival
His only chance of survival was a heart transplant.
Exporting is necessary for our economic survival.
Continued trade in these products is a threat to the survival of the species.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that has continued to exist from an earlier time
examples: SYNONYM relic
The ceremony is a survival from pre-Christian times.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the principle that only the people or things that are best adapted to their environment will continue to exist

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to continue to live or exist
examples: She was the last surviving member of the family.
Of the six people injured in the crash, only two survived.
Many of these teachers are struggling to survive financially.
He must betray his friend in order to survive.
The children had to survive by begging and stealing.
‘How are you these days?’ ‘Oh, surviving.’
Don't worry, it's only a scratch—you'll survive.
Some strange customs have survived from earlier times.
I can't survive on £40 a week (= it is not enough for my basic needs).
They spent two months in the jungle, surviving on small animals and fruit.
He survived as party leader until his second election defeat.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to continue to live or exist despite a dangerous event or time
examples: Her 5-year-old son miraculously survived the crash.
He only survived the attack because he was wearing body armour.
Many birds didn't survive the severe winter.
The company managed to survive the crisis.
Few buildings survived the war intact.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to live or exist longer than somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM outlive
She survived her husband by ten years.
He is survived by his wife and two sons (= he has just died but they are still alive).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who continues to live, especially despite being nearly killed or experiencing great danger or difficulty
examples: the sole/only survivor of the massacre
The plane crashed in an area of dense jungle. There were no survivors.
There are only a few survivors from the original team (= members who remain in it while others have been replaced).
She'll cope. She's one of life's great survivors (= somebody who deals very well with difficult situations).
A movie has been made about the last remaining survivor of the tribe.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have an idea that something is probably true or likely to happen, especially something bad, but without having definite proof
examples: As I had suspected all along, he was not a real policeman.
If you suspect a gas leak, do not strike a match or even turn on an electric light.
Suspecting nothing, he walked right into the trap.
I didn’t want the neighbours suspecting anything.
I began to suspect (that) they were trying to get rid of me.
I strongly suspect (that) this whole story is fictional.
She had no reason to suspect (that) Sylvia had not been telling the truth.
I suspect (that) she might be lying.
It was suspected that the drugs had been brought into the country by boat.
She suspected him to be an impostor.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to have an idea that somebody is guilty of something, without having definite proof
examples: He resigned after being suspected of theft.
He is not suspected of any involvement in the recent attacks.
He was wrongly suspected of the crime.
They arrested four men suspected of links to an extremist group.
I suspected her of damaging the equipment.
The drug is suspected of causing over 200 deaths.
Whom do the police suspect?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to feel that something is not completely right, legal or honest, without having any proof; to not trust something
examples: I suspected her motives in offering to help.
He dealt through a broker whose honesty he had no reason to suspect.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to hang something from something else
examples: A lamp was suspended from the ceiling.
Her body was found suspended by a rope.
A boat was suspended on wires from the rafters.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to officially stop something for a time; to prevent something from being active, used, etc. for a time
examples: Production has been suspended while safety checks are carried out.
The constitution was suspended as the fighting grew worse.
In the theatre we willingly suspend disbelief (= temporarily believe that the characters, etc. are real).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to officially delay something; to arrange for something to happen later than planned
examples: The introduction of the new system has been suspended until next year.
to suspend judgement (= delay forming or expressing an opinion)

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to officially prevent somebody from doing their job, going to school, etc. for a time, as a punishment or while a complaint against them is investigated
examples: The police officer was suspended while the complaint was investigated.
She was suspended from school for a week.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to float in liquid or air without moving
examples: Small droplets are held suspended in the atmosphere.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of officially removing somebody from their job, school, team, etc. for a period of time, usually as a punishment
examples: suspension from school

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of delaying something for a period of time, until a decision has been taken
examples: These events have led to the suspension of talks.
Many movies require the viewer to engage in a willing suspension of disbelief.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the system of springs, etc. by which a vehicle is supported on its wheels and that makes it more comfortable to ride in when the road surface is not even
examples: the front/rear suspension
The new model is fitted with computer-controlled suspension.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a liquid with very small pieces of solid matter floating in it; the state of such a liquid
examples: The suspension was passed through a filter to separate out the solid particles.
The material carried in suspension by the tide is deposited on the shore.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a feeling that somebody has done something wrong, illegal or dishonest, even though you have no proof
examples: SEE ALSO suspect
They drove away slowly to avoid arousing suspicion.
He was arrested on suspicion of murder.
I have a sneaking suspicion that she's not telling the truth.
My suspicions were confirmed when police raided the property.
She was reluctant to voice her suspicions.
His resignation seemed only to fuel suspicions.
It’s time to confront him with our suspicions.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a feeling or belief that something is true, even though you have no proof
examples: I have a horrible suspicion that we've come to the wrong station.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the feeling that you cannot trust somebody/something
examples: Their offer was greeted with some suspicion.
Water from shallow wells should be regarded with suspicion, as it may be contaminated.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a small amount of something
examples: SYNONYM hint
His mouth quivered in the suspicion of a smile.
Wasn’t there even a suspicion of truth in what he said?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: too good, honest, etc. to have done something wrong, illegal or dishonest
examples: Nobody who was near the scene of the crime is above suspicion.
They thought the head teacher was beyond suspicion.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if the finger of blame/suspicion points or is pointed at somebody, they are suspected of having committed a crime, being responsible for something, etc.
examples: The inquiry pointed the finger of blame at the driver of the crashed coach.
The finger of suspicion was pointed at the chicken served for lunch.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: suspected of doing something wrong, illegal or dishonest
examples: The whole family is currently under suspicion of her murder.
A number of doctors came under suspicion of unethical behaviour.
He fell under suspicion of tax evasion.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling that somebody has done something wrong, illegal or dishonest, without having any proof
examples: They became suspicious of his behaviour and contacted the police.
a suspicious look
You have a very suspicious mind (= you always think that people are behaving in an illegal or dishonest way).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: making you feel that something is wrong, illegal or dishonest
examples: Didn't you notice anything suspicious in his behaviour?
She died in suspicious circumstances.
Police are not treating the fire as suspicious.
It might look suspicious if we arrived together.
It was all very suspicious.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not willing or able to trust somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM sceptical
I was suspicious of his motives.
Many were suspicious of reform.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to provide enough of what somebody/something needs in order to live or exist
examples: Which planets can sustain life?
I only had a little chocolate to sustain me on my walk.
The love and support of his family sustained him during his time in prison.
When she lost her job they could no longer sustain their expensive lifestyle.
The soil was so badly eroded it could no longer sustain crop production.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make something continue for some time without becoming less
examples: SYNONYM maintain
She managed to sustain everyone's interest until the end of her speech.
Kangaroos can sustain high speeds over long distances.
the sustaining pedal of a piano (= that allows a note to continue sounding for a long time)
This relationship would be very difficult to sustain.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to experience something bad
examples: SYNONYM suffer
to sustain damage/an injury/a defeat
The company sustained losses of millions of dollars.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to provide evidence to support an opinion, a theory, etc.
examples: SYNONYM uphold
The evidence is not detailed enough to sustain his argument.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to support a weight without breaking or falling
examples: SYNONYM bear
The ice will not sustain your weight.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to decide that a claim, etc. is true or legally valid
examples: SYNONYM uphold
The court sustained his claim that the contract was illegal.
Objection sustained! (= said by a judge when a lawyer makes an objection in court)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: involving the use of natural products and energy in a way that does not harm the environment
examples: sustainable forest management
an environmentally sustainable society
This type of farming is simply not sustainable any more.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: that can continue or be continued for a long time
examples: OPPOSITE unsustainable
sustainable economic growth
Unfortunately, this level of output is not sustainable.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make food, drink, etc. go down your throat into your stomach
examples: Always chew food well before swallowing it.
I had a sore throat and it hurt to swallow.
The pills should be swallowed whole.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move the muscles of your throat as if you were swallowing something, especially because you are nervous
examples: She swallowed hard and told him the bad news.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to take somebody/something in or completely cover them/it so that they/it cannot be seen or exist separately any longer
examples: I watched her walk down the road until she was swallowed by the darkness.
Large areas of countryside have been swallowed up by towns.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to use up something completely, especially an amount of money
examples: Most of my salary gets swallowed (up) by the rent and bills.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to accept that something is true; to believe something
examples: I found her excuse very hard to swallow.
He told her a pack of lies, but she swallowed it whole.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to hide your feelings
examples: to swallow your doubts
You're going to have to swallow your pride and ask for your job back.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to accept offensive remarks, criticisms, etc. without complaining or protesting
examples: I was surprised that he just sat there and swallowed all their remarks.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a fact or an event that is unpleasant and difficult to accept
examples: The election defeat was a bitter pill for the party to swallow.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: very pleased with yourself
examples: SYNONYM smug
She looked like a cat that’s swallowed the canary. She was almost purring with pleasure.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to use rude or offensive language, usually because you are angry
examples: She fell over and swore loudly.
I don't like to hear children swearing.
He heard her swear under her breath.
She was shouting, swearing, and acting in an aggressive manner towards the staff
Why did you let him swear at you like that?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make a serious promise to do something
examples: He swore revenge on the man who had killed his father.
I solemnly swear (that) it will never happen again.
I swear (that) I’ll never leave you.
He swore solemnly that he would never hit her again.
She made him swear not to tell anyone.
He left, swearing never to return.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to promise that you are telling the truth
examples: She swore (that) she’d never seen him before.
I could have sworn (= I am sure) I heard the phone ring.
I swear to God I had nothing to do with it.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make a public or official promise, especially in court
examples: Witnesses were required to swear on the Bible.
Are you willing to stand up in court and swear that you don't recognize him?
Remember, you have sworn to tell the truth.
Barons had to swear an oath of allegiance to the king.
I swear by Almighty God to tell the truth.
They refused to swear allegiance to the new ruler.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to make somebody promise not to tell something to anyone
examples: SEE ALSO sworn
Everyone was sworn to secrecy about what had happened.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to say that something is definitely true
examples: He swore blind that he’d already paid back the money he owed me.
He swore blind that you knew all about it.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to often use very rude or offensive languageWord Origin
examples: Old English swerian of Germanic origin; related to Dutch zweren, German schwören, also to answer.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of clothing for the upper part of the body, made of wool or cotton, with long sleeves
examples: SYNONYM jumper (1)
She wore jeans and a sweater.
He was wearing a cashmere sweater over his shirt.
She has knitted me beautiful sweaters and socks.
a grey merino wool turtleneck sweater

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to clean a room, surface, etc. using a broom (= a type of brush on a long handle)
examples: to sweep the floor
Chimneys should be swept regularly.
I don't have to sweep and mop every day.
Don't just stand around—grab a broom and sweep up.
The showroom had been emptied and swept clean.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to remove something from a surface using a brush, your hand, etc.
examples: She swept the crumbs into the wastebasket.
He swept the leaves up into a pile.
She swept the clothes onto the floor and invited him to sit down.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move or push somebody/something suddenly and with a lot of force
examples: The little boat was swept out to sea.
Their tent was swept away in the storm.
She let herself be swept along by the crowd.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to move suddenly and/or with force over an area or in a particular direction
examples: Rain swept in through the broken windows.
A fire swept through the store on Tuesday night.
Strong winds regularly sweep the islands.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to move quickly and/or smoothly, especially in a way that impresses or is intended to impress other people
examples: Without another word she swept out of the room.
Two police motorcycles swept through the village.
A pair of golden eagles swept across the sky.
She swept past the photographers without a glance.
He swept into the lead with an almost perfect performance.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to move something, especially your hand or arm, quickly and smoothly in a particular direction
examples: He rushed to greet her, sweeping his arms wide.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to suddenly affect somebody strongly
examples: A wave of tiredness swept over her.
Memories came sweeping back.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to spread quickly
examples: Rumours of his resignation swept through the company.
the latest craze sweeping the nation

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to move over an area, especially in order to look for something
examples: His eyes swept around the room.
The car headlights swept across the front of the building.
Searchlights swept the sky.
She swept the crowd with her binoculars.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to move, or move something, over a surface, touching it lightly
examples: Her dress swept the ground as she walked.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to brush, comb, etc. your hair in a particular direction
examples: Her hair was swept back from her face.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to form a long, smooth curve
examples: The hotel gardens sweep down to the beach.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to win all the games in a series of games against another team or all the parts of a contest
examples: The Blue Jays have a chance to sweep the series.
New Jersey swept Detroit last season.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to win all the prizes, etc. in a competition

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to make somebody fall suddenly and deeply in love with you
examples: She’s waiting for some hero to come and sweep her off her feet.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to win an election by a large number of votes; to make somebody win an election with a large number of votes

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to win a contest easily
examples: Macron swept to victory in 2017.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to try to stop people from finding out about something wrong, illegal, embarrassing, etc. that has happened or that you have done
examples: An earlier report, implicating the government, had been conveniently swept under the carpet.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: containing, or tasting as if it contains, a lot of sugar
examples: OPPOSITE sour
a cup of hot sweet tea
sweet food
I had a craving for something sweet.
roast duck with a sweet and sour sauce
sweet sherry
This wine is too sweet for me.
I found the dessert a bit sweet for my taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having a pleasant smell
examples: SYNONYM fragrant
a sweet-smelling rose
The air was sweet with incense.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having a pleasant sound
examples: a sweet voice

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: pleasant and not containing any harmful substances
examples: the sweet air of a mountain village

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: making you feel happy and/or satisfied
examples: Goodnight. Sweet dreams.
I can't tell you how sweet this victory is.
He played a sweet shot onto the final green (= in golf).
an act of sweet revenge

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: attractive
examples: SYNONYM cute
His sister's a sweet young thing.
You look sweet in this photograph.
We stayed in a sweet little hotel on the seafront.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: She gave him her sweetest smile.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move through water by moving your arms and legs, without touching the bottom
examples: I can't swim.
The boys swam across the lake.
We swam out (= away from land) to the yacht.
They spent the day swimming and sunbathing.
I've only just learned to swim.
I have always found it easy to swim underwater.
They are too far out to swim to shore.
Can you swim backstroke yet?
How long will it take her to swim the Channel?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to spend time swimming for pleasure
examples: I go swimming twice a week.
We always went swimming together in our indoor pool.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move through or across water
examples: Sharks must swim or die.
A shoal of fish swam past.
Ducks were swimming around on the river.
A beaver swam vigorously upstream.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be covered with a lot of liquid
examples: The main course was swimming in oil.
Her eyes were swimming with tears.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to seem to be moving around, especially when you are ill or drunk
examples: The pages swam before her eyes.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to feel confused and/or as if everything is turning round and round
examples: His head swam and he swayed dizzily.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be in a situation where you will either succeed by your own efforts or fail completely
examples: The new students were just left to sink or swim.
In a situation like this, you either sink or swim.

definitions.definition: the sport or activity of swimming
examples: Swimming is a good form of exercise.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move backwards or forwards or from side to side while hanging from a fixed point; to make something do this
examples: His arms swung as he walked.
As he pushed her, she swung higher and higher (= while sitting on a swing).
A set of keys swung from her belt.
He sat on the stool, swinging his legs.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move from one place to another by holding something that is fixed and pulling yourself along, up, etc.
examples: The gunshot sent monkeys swinging away through the trees.
He swung himself out of the car.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move or make something move with a wide curved movement
examples: A line of cars swung out of the palace gates.
He swung his legs over the side of the bed.
The door swung open.
She let the door swing shut behind her.
She swung the door open.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to change or make somebody/something change from one opinion, mood, etc. to another
examples: The state has swung from Republican to Democrat.
His emotions swung between fear and curiosity.
The game could swing either way (= either side could win it).
I managed to swing them round to my point of view.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to turn or change direction suddenly; to make something do this
examples: She swung back to face him.
The bus swung sharply to the left.
He swung the camera around to face the opposite direction.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to try to hit somebody/something
examples: She swung at me with the iron bar.
He swung another punch in my direction.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to succeed in getting or achieving something, sometimes in a slightly dishonest way
examples: We're trying to swing it so that we can travel on the same flight.
Is there any chance of you swinging us a couple of tickets?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to have a strong rhythm

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: if a party, etc. is swinging, there are a lot of people there having a good time

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: when somebody says there’s no room to swing a cat, they mean that a room is very small and that there is not enough space

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to affect the result of something in one way rather than another
examples: In an interview, smart presentation can swing the balance in your favour.
New evidence swung the balance against the prosecution.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be bisexual (= sexually attracted to both men and women)

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to really try to achieve something great, even when it is not reasonable to expect to be so successful
examples: entrepreneurs who think big and swing for the fences
Investors need to manage risk and not swing for the fences.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to start doing something quickly and with a lot of energy
examples: The ambulance crew swung into action to resuscitate the patient.
The rescue operation swung into action immediately.
The emergency services swung into action as soon as the disaster was reported.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to pretend to be ill when in fact you are not, especially to avoid work
examples: I don't think there's anything wrong with her—she's just swinging the lead.

examples: We're in the process of switching over to a new system of invoicing.

He switched over from acting to journalism.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to exchange one thing for another
examples: SYNONYM swap

I see you've switched the furniture around (= changed its position).
Do you think she'll notice if I switch my glass with hers?
We asked them if they would switch places with us.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: SYNONYM swap
I can't work next weekend—will you switch with me?
Have you been able to switch your shift with anyone?
Can we switch our shifts around?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person, an object, an event, etc. that represents a more general quality or situation
examples: The vase is decorated with religious symbols.
The new school stands as a symbol of hope for a better future.
Mandela became a symbol of the anti-apartheid struggle.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sign, number, letter, etc. that has a fixed meaning, especially in science, mathematics and music
examples: the mathematical symbol for infinity
Hotels that display this symbol offer activities for children.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: containing symbols, or being used as a symbol
examples: He shook his fist in a symbolic gesture of defiance.
The ceremony has a deep symbolic meaning.
The new regulations are largely symbolic (= they will not have any real effect).
The dove is symbolic of peace.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: kind to somebody who is hurt or sad; showing that you understand and care about their problems
examples: a sympathetic listener
a sympathetic response
She was very sympathetic when I was sick.
I did not feel at all sympathetic towards Kate.
I'm here if you need a sympathetic ear (= somebody to talk to about your problems).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: showing that you approve of somebody/something or that you share their views and are willing to support them
examples: He was speaking to a highly sympathetic audience.
to be sympathetic to the party’s aims
Russian newspapers are largely sympathetic to the president.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: easy to like
examples: OPPOSITE unsympathetic
a sympathetic character in a novel
I don't find her a very sympathetic person.
The character's faults actually make him more sympathetic.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the feeling of being sorry for somebody; showing that you understand and care about somebody’s problems
examples: to express/feel sympathy for somebody
I have no sympathy for Jan—it's all her own fault.
I wish he'd show me a little more sympathy.
Our heartfelt sympathy goes out to the victims of the war.
Shops were closed out of sympathy for the victims.
May we offer our deepest sympathies on the death of your wife.
I would like to extend our sincere sympathies to his family at this sad time.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the act of showing support for or approval of an idea, a cause, an organization, etc.
examples: The seamen went on strike in sympathy with (= to show their support for) the dockers.
Her sympathies lie with the anti-abortion lobby.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: friendship and understanding between people who have similar opinions or interests
examples: There was no personal sympathy between them.
He has a total lack of sympathy for young people.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: happening because something else has happened
examples: Share prices slipped in sympathy with the German market.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not agreeing with or not wanting to support somebody/somethingWord Origin
examples: late 16th cent.: via Latin from Greek sumpatheia, from sumpathēs, from sun- ‘with’ + pathos ‘feeling’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a change in your body or mind that shows that you are not healthy
examples: Symptoms include a headache and sore throat.
If symptoms persist, consult your doctor.
to experience symptoms of anxiety and depression
to show/develop symptoms of illness
to relieve/alleviate symptoms

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a sign that something exists, especially something bad
examples: SYNONYM indication
The rise in inflation was just one symptom of the poor state of the economy.
Their relationship was obviously failing, but they just ignored the symptoms.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a set of physical conditions that show you have a particular disease or medical problem
examples: SEE ALSO AIDS
PMS or premenstrual syndrome
This syndrome is associated with frequent coughing.
This syndrome mostly affects women in their forties.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a set of opinions or a way of behaving that is typical of a particular type of person, attitude or social problem
examples: SEE ALSO tall poppy syndrome
With teenagers, be prepared for the ‘Me, me, me!’ syndrome (= they think of themselves first).
This phenomenon has become known as the ‘Californian syndrome’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of combining separate ideas, beliefs, styles, etc.; a mixture or combination of ideas, beliefs, styles, etc.
examples: the synthesis of art with everyday life
a synthesis of traditional and modern values

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the natural chemical production of a substance in animals and plants
examples: protein synthesis
the synthesis of nucleic acids

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the artificial production of a substance that is present naturally in animals and plants
examples: the synthesis of penicillin

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the production of sounds, music or speech by electronic means
examples: SEE ALSO speech synthesis

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an organized set of ideas or theories or a particular way of doing something
examples: SEE ALSO binary
reform of the country's education system
the criminal justice system
the healthcare system
the legal/financial/political system
Systems are in place for dealing with complaints.
a system of government

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a group of things, pieces of equipment, etc. that are connected or work together
examples: SEE ALSO Copernican system
They installed a security system but it failed.
How does the system work?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a set of computer equipment and programs that are used together
examples: SEE ALSO distributed system
to develop a new computer system
We're designing a voice-recognition system.
computerized information systems

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a human or an animal body, or a part of it, when it is being thought of as the organs and processes that make it function
examples: SEE ALSO central nervous system
Wait until the drugs have passed through your system.
the male reproductive system
Returning to work after a long break can be a terrible shock to the system (= a big change that is difficult to deal with).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the rules or people that control a country or an organization, especially when they seem to be unfair because you cannot change them
examples: SEE ALSO the spoils system
You can't beat the system (= you must accept it).
You have to learn how to work the system if you want to succeed.
young people rebelling against the system

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that everything is working well or that everything is ready for something to happen or be successful
examples: The firm struggled to generate much business at the start, but now it's all systems go.
Last weekend's heavy snowfall means it's all systems go for the ski season.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to do something so that you no longer feel a very strong emotion or have a strong desire
examples: I was very angry with him, but now I feel I've got it out of my system.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: done according to a system or plan, in a complete, efficient or determined way
examples: OPPOSITE unsystematic
a systematic approach to solving the problem
a systematic attempt to destroy the organization
The prisoner was subjected to systematic torture.
the systematic analysis of the risks involved

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an informal shirt, usually with short sleeves (= arms) no collar or buttons, or just a few buttons at the top
examples: He was wearing a faded pair of blue jeans and an old T-shirt.
a sleeveless/long-sleeved T-shirt

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of furniture that consists of a flat top supported by legs
examples: SEE ALSO bird table
We sat at a round table in the corner.
They were sitting around the kitchen table.
She took a seat at the end of the table.
My father always sits at the head of the table.
A table for two, please (= in a restaurant).
I'd like to book a table for dinner tonight (= in a restaurant)
to set the table
to lay the table (= to put the plates, knives, etc. on it for a meal)
to clear the table (= take away the dirty plates, etc. at the end of a meal)
He questioned her next morning over the breakfast table (= during breakfast).
a pool/billiard/snooker table

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the people sitting at a table for a meal or to play cards, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO round-table
He kept the whole table entertained with his jokes.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a list of facts or numbers arranged in a special order, usually in rows and columns
examples: SEE ALSO periodic table
a table of contents (= a list of the main points or information in a book, usually at the front of the book)
The table below shows how prices have changed over the past 20 years.
He showed the price fluctuations in a statistical table.
See Table XII for population figures.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a list of sports teams, countries, schools, etc. that shows their position in a competition, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO league table
If Arsenal win this game they'll go to the top of the table.
the bottom of the table
United are second in the table.
The team will be lucky to finish the season mid-table.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a list showing the results when a number is multiplied by a set of other numbers, especially 1 to 12, in turn
examples: Do you know your six times table?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to contribute something useful to a discussion, project, etc.
examples: What Hislop brought to the table was real commitment and energy.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to join formal discussions about something
examples: Different countries come to the table with differing expectations about what they can achieve.

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to tell somebody honestly what your plans, ideas, etc. are

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: if a topic is off the table at a formal discussion, people are not willing or allowed to discuss it
examples: Some issues were so controversial they were taken off the table.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: offered to people so that they can consider or discuss it
examples: Management have put several new proposals on the table.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: not going to be discussed or considered until a future date

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to change a situation so that you are now in a stronger position than the person who used to be in a stronger position than you

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to serve food to people, for example at a formal meal

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to work serving food to people in a restaurantWord Origin
examples: Old English tabule ‘flat slab, inscribed tablet’, from Latin tabula ‘plank, tablet, list’, reinforced in Middle English by Old French table.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a small computer that is easy to carry, with a large touch screen and usually without a physical keyboard
examples: The company has launched its latest 10-inch tablet.
Consumers show a growing preference for tablets and smartphones over PCs and laptops.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a small round solid piece of medicine that you swallow
examples: SYNONYM pill
Take two tablets with water before meals.
I took the tablets prescribed by my doctor.
The drug is now available in tablet and capsule form.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an amount of a substance in a small, round, solid piece
examples: water purification tablets

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a flat piece of stone that has words written on it, especially one that has been fixed to a wall in memory of an important person or event
examples: SYNONYM plaque
The school has a memorial tablet engraved with the name of the founder.
We can be very flexible—our entry requirements are not set in tablets of stone (= they can be changed).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a piece of soap

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a number of pieces of paper for writing or drawing on, that are fastened together at one edge
examples: SEE ALSO graphics tablet

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem or situation
examples: The government is determined to tackle inflation.
I think I'll tackle the repairs next weekend.
Firefighters tackled a blaze in a garage last night.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to speak to somebody about a problem or difficult situation
examples: SYNONYM confront
I tackled him about the money he owed me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: He was tackled just outside the penalty area.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make an opponent fall to the ground in order to stop them running
examples: He can run fast and tackle hard.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to deal with somebody who is violent or threatening you
examples: He tackled a masked intruder at his home.

examples: They tried all kinds of tactics to get us to go.
This was just the latest in a series of delaying tactics.
The manager discussed tactics with his team.
Confrontation is not always the best tactic.
It's time to try a change of tactic.

examples: COMPARE strategy

tactical planning
to have a tactical advantage

definitions.label: Meaning 3

tactical weapons/missiles
tactical nuclear weapons

definitions.label: Meaning 4

He put name tags on all his shirts.
a gift tag (= tied to a present)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an electronic device that can be attached to a person, animal or object so that police, researchers, etc. know where the person, etc. is
examples: The police use electronic tags to monitor the whereabouts of young offenders on probation.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a name or phrase that is used to describe a person or thing in some way
examples: They are finally ready to drop the tag ‘the new Beatles’.
The ‘lucky’ tag stuck for years.
The president made several jokes in an attempt to shake off his ‘humourless’ tag.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: SEE ALSO question tag

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a set of letters or symbols that are put before and after a piece of text or data in order to identify it or show that it is to be treated in a particular way

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7
