definitions.definition: the part that sticks out at the back of the body of a bird, an animal or a fish, which the animal can move from side to side or up and down
examples: SEE ALSO ponytail
The dog ran up, wagging its tail.
My dog loves to chase his tail.
The male has beautiful tail feathers.
It was black from its nose to the tip of its tail.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having the type of tail mentioned
examples: a white-tailed eagle

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the back part of a plane, spacecraft, etc.
examples: The plane's tail section had broken off.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a part of something that sticks out at the back like a tail
examples: the tail of a kite

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the last part of something that is moving away from you
examples: SEE ALSO tail end
the tail of the procession
the truck at the tail of our convoy

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a long jacket divided at the back below the waist into two pieces that become narrower at the bottom, worn by men at very formal events
examples: COMPARE dinner jacket
The men all wore top hat and tails.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the side of a coin that does not have a picture of the head of a person on it, used as one choice when a coin is tossed to decide something
examples: COMPARE heads

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a person who is sent to follow somebody secretly and find out information about where that person goes, what they do, etc.
examples: The police have put a tail on him.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be unable to understand something
examples: I couldn't make head nor tail of what he was saying.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be very busy but in fact achieve very little

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody which side of a coin they think will be facing upwards when it is tossed in order to decide something by chance

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if cars, etc. are nose to tail, they are moving slowly in a long line with little space between them
examples: The traffic was nose to tail for miles.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: following behind somebody very closely, especially in a car
examples: There’s been a white van sitting on my tail for the past ten miles.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: an unpleasant feature that comes at the end of a story, an event, etc. and makes it less good, successful, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to describe a situation in which the most important aspect is being influenced and controlled by somebody/something that is not as important

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to run away from a fight or dangerous situation
examples: When they heard the sirens, they turned tail and ran.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: feeling ashamed or unhappy because you have been defeated or punishedWord Origin
examples: Old English tæg(e)l, from a Germanic base meaning ‘hair, hairy tail’; related to Middle Low German tagel ‘twisted whip, rope's end’. The early sense of the verb (early 16th cent.) was ‘fasten to the back of something’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to carry or move something from one place to another
examples: Remember to take your coat when you leave.
I forgot to take my bag with me when I got off the bus.
Shall I take my host family a gift?
Can you take my suit to the dry-cleaner's?
You need to take your laptop to the technician.
Don't forget to take a present for Catherine's new baby.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to go with somebody from one place to another, especially to guide or lead them
examples: It's too far to walk—I'll take you by car.
A boy took us to our room.
I'm taking the kids swimming later.
The boys were taken to see their grandparents most weekends.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make somebody/something go from one level, situation, etc. to another
examples: Her energy and talent took her to the top of her profession.
The new loan takes the total debt to $100 000.
I'd like to take my argument a stage further.
He believes he has the skills to take the club forward.
We'll take the matter forward at our next meeting (= discuss it further).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to need or require a particular amount of time
examples: The process took about a year.
The journey to the airport takes about half an hour.
It takes about half an hour to get to the airport.
That cut is taking a long time to heal.
The official seemed to take hours to examine my passport.
That should only take you ten minutes.
It took her three hours to repair her bike.
It'll take her time to recover from the illness.
It'll take time (= take a long time) for her to recover from the illness.
I need a shower—I won't take long.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to photograph somebody/something
examples: to take a picture/photo/shot of somebody/something
to have your picture/photo taken

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to use a form of transport, a road, a path, etc. to go to a place
examples: to take the bus/train
to take a cab/plane
Take the second road on the right.
It's more interesting to take the coast road.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to put your hands or arms around somebody/something and hold them/it; to reach for somebody/something and hold them/it
examples: I passed him the rope and he took it.
Free newspapers: please take one.
Can you take (= hold) the baby for a moment?
He took her hand/took her by the hand (= held her hand, for example to lead her somewhere).
She took the child in her arms and kissed him.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to remove something/somebody from a place or a person
examples: Will you take your books off the table?
The sign must be taken down.
He took some keys out of his pocket.
My name had been taken off the list.
She was playing with a knife, so I took it away from her.
She was playing with a knife, so I took it off her.
The new sports centre will take the pressure off the old one.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to remove something without permission or by mistake
examples: Someone has taken my scarf.
Did the burglars take anything valuable?
All she had taken was her passport and driving licence.
The storms took the lives of 50 people.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to get something from a particular source
examples: The scientists are taking water samples from the river.
The machine takes its name from its inventor.
Part of her article is taken straight (= copied) out of my book.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to sit down in or use a chair, etc.
examples: Are these seats taken?
Come in; take a seat.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to eat, drink, etc. something
examples: Do you take sugar in your coffee?
The doctor has given me some medicine to take for my cough.
He started taking drugs (= illegal drugs) at college.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to find out and record something; to write something down
examples: The police officer took my name and address.
Did you take notes in the class?

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to do an exam or a test
examples: When did you take your driving test?

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to study a subject at school, college, etc.
examples: She is planning to take a course in web design.
Last year I started taking yoga classes.
How many subjects are you taking this year?

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to use a particular course of action in order to deal with or achieve something
examples: We need to take a different approach to the problem.
The government is taking action to combat drug abuse.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used with nouns to say that somebody is doing something, performing an action, etc.
examples: to take a look
to take a break
to take a shot at somebody/something
to take a step/walk/stroll
to take a bath/shower/wash
to take a bite/drink/sip
to take a deep breath
We will take a decision on the matter next week.
She's taken a nasty fall and has her leg in plaster.
Experts have urged ministers to take the necessary steps to resolve the issue.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to test or measure something
examples: to take somebody’s temperature
I need to have my blood pressure taken.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to capture a place or person; to get control of something
examples: The rebels succeeded in taking the town.
The state has taken control of the company.
The militants took the city from government forces.
The rebels took him prisoner.
He was taken prisoner by the rebels.
The bank robbers took several employees hostage.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to choose, buy or rent something
examples: I'll take the grey jacket.
We took a room at the hotel for two nights.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to buy a newspaper or magazine regularly
examples: We take the ‘Express’.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to accept or receive something
examples: If they offer me the job, I'll take it.
She was accused of taking bribes.
I'll take the call in my office.
I take full responsibility for my actions.
Why should I take the blame for somebody else's mistakes?
If you choose deceit, then you must take the consequences of your actions.
If you take my advice you'll have nothing more to do with him.
Will you take $10 for the book (= will you sell it for $10)?
The store took (= sold goods worth) $100 000 last week.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to act in response to an opportunity
examples: When the bus stopped for fuel, we took the opportunity to get something to eat.
England failed to take their chances and had to settle for a draw.
He isn't afraid to take risks.
Take the initiative and fill your life with exciting experiences.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to accept somebody as a customer, patient, etc.
examples: The school doesn't take boys (= only has girls).
The dentist can't take any new patients.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to experience or be affected by something
examples: The school took the full force of the explosion.
Can the ropes take the strain (= not break)?
The team took a terrible beating.
I'm afraid your husband has taken a turn for the worse.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to be able to bear something
examples: She can't take criticism.
I don't think I can take much more of this heat.
I find his attitude a little hard to take.
It was clear that she wasn't going to take any nonsense.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to react to something/somebody in a particular way
examples: He took the criticism surprisingly well.
These threats are not to be taken lightly.
I wish you'd take me seriously.
I was being sarcastic but you took my comment literally.
She took it in the spirit in which it was intended.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to understand or consider something in a particular way
examples: How am I supposed to take that remark?
Taken overall, the project was a success.
She took what he said as a compliment.
What did you take his comments to mean?

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to consider somebody/something to be somebody/something, especially when you are wrong
examples: Even the experts took the painting for a genuine Van Gogh.
Of course I didn't do it! What do you take me for (= what sort of person do you think I am)?
I took the man with him to be his father.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to have a particular feeling, opinion or attitude
examples: My parents always took an interest in my hobbies.
Don't take offence (= be offended) at what I said.
I took a dislike to him.
He takes the view that children are responsible for their own actions.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to reduce one number by the value of another
examples: SYNONYM subtract
Take 5 from 12 and you're left with 7.
80 take away 5 is 75.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: used to introduce somebody/something as an example
examples: Lots of couples have problems in the first year of marriage. Take Ann and Paul.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to have or start to have a particular form, position or state
examples: Our next class will take the form of a debate.
The new president takes office in January.
The home side had a chance to take the lead.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to need or require something in order to happen or be done
examples: It only takes one careless driver to cause an accident.
It doesn't take much to make her angry.
He didn't take much persuading (= he was easily persuaded).

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to use something in order to work
examples: The buses have been adapted to take biofuel.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to wear a particular size in shoes or clothes
examples: What size shoes do you take?

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to have enough space for something/somebody; to be able to hold or contain a particular quantity
examples: The bus can take 60 passengers.
The tank takes 50 litres.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: to be the teacher or leader in a class or a religious service
examples: The head teacher usually takes us for French.
Mr Perkins took the morning service.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: to go over or around something
examples: The horse took the first fence well.
He takes bends much too fast.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: to kick or throw the ball from a fixed or agreed position
examples: to take a penalty/free kick/corner

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: to use a particular method to find out people’s opinions
examples: to take a vote/poll/survey

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: to be successful; to work
examples: The skin graft failed to take.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to have or require something when used in a sentence or other structure
examples: The verb ‘rely’ takes the preposition ‘on’.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not care if somebody accepts or rejects your offer

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody does not have a strong opinion about something
examples: Dancing? I can take it or leave it.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: to have the qualities, ability, etc. needed to be successful

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: used to say that you cannot trust somebody to behave well in public
examples: You haven’t spilled your coffee again! I can’t take you anywhere!

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: to accept something/somebody without wishing it/them to be different or without thinking about it/them very much in advance
examples: She takes life as it comes.

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: to suppose; to assume
examples: I take it you won't be coming to the party?

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that what you are going to say is the truth
examples: Take it from me—he'll be a millionaire before he's 30.

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: to make somebody physically or mentally tired
examples: Looking after small children really takes it out of you.

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: to decide to do something without asking permission or advice

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: to need a lot of effort or time; to be very difficult to do

definitions.label: Meaning 54
definitions.definition: used as an exclamation when you are hitting somebody or attacking them in some other wayWord Origin
examples: late Old English tacan ‘get (especially by force), capture’, from Old Norse taka ‘grasp, lay hold of’, of unknown ultimate origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a story created using the imagination, especially one that is full of action and adventure
examples: SEE ALSO fairy tale
a coming-of-age/morality tale
The story is a classic tale of love and betrayal.
Dickens’ ‘A Tale of Two Cities’
His latest book is a delightful children’s tale about talking animals.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an exciting spoken description of an event, which may not be completely true
examples: I love listening to his tales of life at sea.
I've heard tales of people seeing ghosts in that house.
She regaled us with tales of her wild youth.
The team's tale of woe continued on Saturday (= they lost another match).
Her experiences provide a cautionary tale (= a warning) for us all.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to survive a difficult or dangerous experience so that you can tell others what really happened

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an old idea or belief that people now know is not correct

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to give some information that is different from what you expect or have been told
examples: These drugs are widely believed to be effective medications. The data, however, tell a different story.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to explain itself, without needing any further explanation or comment
examples: Her face told its own story.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to tell somebody about something that another person has done wrong
examples: RELATED NOUN telltale

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a natural ability to do something well
examples: The festival showcases the talent of young musicians.
to possess/have exceptional musical talent
The team is known for nurturing raw talent.
a man of many talents
She displayed her talent for comedy at the event.
She showed considerable talent for getting what she wanted.
a talent contest/competition (= in which people perform, to show how well they can sing, dance, etc.)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: people or a person with a natural ability to do something well
examples: to nurture/develop young talent
We are losing our top talent to other countries who pay more.
He is a great talent.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: people who are sexually attractive
examples: He likes to spend his time chatting up the local talent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a natural ability to do something well
examples: a talented player/musician/artist
Some of these young musicians are incredibly talented.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to say things; to speak in order to give information or to express feelings, ideas, etc.
examples: Stop talking and listen!
We talked on the phone for over an hour.
Who were you talking to just now?
Ann and Joe aren't talking to each other right now (= they refuse to speak to each other because they have argued).
Watch the scene where Don talks to himself in the mirror while shaving.
We looked around the school and talked with the principal.
They talk a lot about the inspiration for their music.
When they get together, all they talk about is football.
What are you talking about? (= used when you are surprised, annoyed and/or worried by something that somebody has just said)
I don't know what you're talking about (= used to say that you did not do something that somebody has accused you of).
to talk openly/freely/publicly about something
She started talking loudly to her friends about the film they'd just seen.
Mary is talking of looking for another job.
We often talked of the war.
We talked ourselves hoarse, catching up on all the news.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to discuss something, usually something serious or important
examples: This situation can't go on. We need to talk.
The two sides in the dispute are finally willing to talk.
Talk with your doctor before radically changing your diet.
Is there anything you'd like to talk about?
We want to talk to people about this issue.
to talk politics

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to say words in a language
examples: The baby is just starting to talk.
Alex can't talk yet—he's only just one year old.
We couldn't understand them because they were talking in Chinese.
Are they talking Swedish or Danish?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to say things that are/are not sensible
examples: She talks a lot of sense.
You're talking rubbish!
See if you can talk some sense into him (= persuade him to be sensible).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize an amount of money, how serious something is, etc.
examples: We're talking £500 for three hours' work.
Do you know what this will cost? We’re talking megabucks here.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to talk about a person’s private life
examples: SYNONYM gossip
Don't phone me at work—people will talk.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to give information to somebody, especially unwillingly
examples: The police questioned him but he refused to talk.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to try and persuade somebody to stop behaving in a stupid way, sometimes using rough or violent methods
examples: Try and talk some sense into her before she makes the wrong decision.
Where would I be without you to knock some sense into my head?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to have knowledge about something from your own experience
examples: I’ve lived in China, so I know what I’m talking about.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that they should not criticize somebody else for something because they do the same things too
examples: ‘George is so careless with money.’ ‘Look who's talking!’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: people who have a lot of money have more power and influence than others

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used when you like what somebody has suggested very much

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: people say speak/talk of the devil when somebody they have been talking about appears unexpectedly
examples: Well, speak of the devil—here's Alice now!

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to say something that you should not because it is the wrong situation or because it offends somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be able to communicate easily with another person because you share similar opinions and experience

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something
examples: Talk about mean! She didn't even buy me a card.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to talk to somebody about sex in order to make them sexually excited

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to talk in a way that sounds convincing, but may not be sincere
examples: The senior managers talk a good game about customer relations, but really they don't care about the customer.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to talk too much, especially about things that are boring or not important

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used when you are going to say more about a subject that has already been mentioned

Ann and Joe aren't talking to each other right now (= they refuse to speak to each other because they have argued).

Mary is talking of looking for another job.
We often talked of the war.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

See if you can talk some sense into him (= persuade him to be sensible).

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the particular quality that different foods and drinks have that allows you to recognize them when you put them in your mouth
examples: a sweet/salty/bitter/sour taste
I don't like the taste of olives.
This dish has an unusual combination of tastes and textures.
The soup has very little taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the sense you have that allows you to recognize different foods and drinks when you put them in your mouth
examples: I've lost my sense of taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a small quantity of food or drink that you try in order to see what it is like
examples: Just have a taste of this cheese.
Do you want a taste?

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a short experience of something
examples: This was my first taste of live theatre.
Although we didn't know it, this incident was a taste of things to come.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person’s ability to choose things that people recognize as being of good quality or appropriate
examples: He has very good taste in music.
They've got more money than taste.
She's famous for her impeccable taste and style.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: what a person likes or prefers
examples: You can adapt the recipe to suit your personal taste.
That trip gave me a taste for foreign travel.

He has very expensive taste in clothes.
The colour and style is a matter of personal taste
Modern art is not to everyone's taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a thing that you do not like much at first but gradually learn to like
examples: Abstract art is an acquired taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be offensive and not at all appropriate
examples: Most of his jokes were in very poor taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be appropriate and not at all offensive
examples: The love scenes are all done in the best possible taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make you feel upset or ashamed afterwards
examples: The whole business left a bad taste in my mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: the same bad treatment that you have given to others
examples: Let the bully have a taste of his own medicine.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say how difficult it is to understand why somebody likes somebody/something that you do not like at all
examples: She thinks he's wonderful—oh well, there's no accounting for taste.

definitions.label: Meaning 13

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a place, building or set of buildings where journeys by train, bus or boat begin or end
examples: a railway/bus/ferry terminal

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a piece of equipment, usually consisting of a keyboard and a screen that joins the user to a central computer system
examples: SEE ALSO data terminal

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a point at which connections can be made in an electric circuit
examples: a positive/negative terminal

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to end; to make something end
examples: Your contract of employment terminates in December.
The agreement was terminated immediately.
to terminate a pregnancy (= to perform or have an abortion)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to end a journey
examples: OPPOSITE originate (3)
This train terminates at London Victoria.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the conditions that people offer, demand or accept when they make an agreement, an arrangement or a contract
examples: peace terms
They failed to agree on the terms of a settlement.
These are the terms and conditions of your employment.
Under the terms of the agreement, their funding of the project will continue until 2025.
We are negotiating terms for the development of the site.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: conditions that you agree to when you buy, sell, or pay for something; a price or cost
examples: to buy something on easy terms (= paying for it over a long period)
My terms are £20 a lesson.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a way of expressing yourself or of saying something
examples: We wish to protest in the strongest possible terms (= to say we are very angry).
I'll try to explain in simple terms.
The letter was brief, and couched in very polite terms.
She spoke of you in glowing terms (= expressing her admiration of you).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to have a good, friendly, etc. relationship with somebody
examples: I had no idea that you and he were on such intimate terms (= were such close friends).
He is still on excellent terms with his ex-wife.
I'm on first-name terms with my boss now (= we call each other by our first names).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be willing to be polite or friendly towards somebody, especially after an argument
examples: She's not been on speaking terms with her uncle for years.
Are they speaking to each other again yet?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to reach an agreement with somebody; to find a way of living or working together
examples: The enemy was eventually forced to come to terms.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to accept something unpleasant by learning to deal with it
examples: She is still coming to terms with her son's death.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a statement containing two words that contradict each other’s meaning
examples: A ‘nomad settlement’ is a contradiction in terms.
The idea is almost a contradiction in terms.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: clearly and strongly
examples: I told him what I thought of him in no uncertain terms.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to show what aspect of a subject you are talking about or how you are thinking about it
examples: The job is great in terms of salary, but it has its disadvantages.
This title ranks alongside the Olympics in terms of importance.
What does this mean in terms of cost?
In terms of cost—how much were you thinking of charging?
In terms of extra staff—how many will we need?
In practical terms this law may be difficult to enforce.
The decision was disastrous in political terms.
He's talking in terms of starting a completely new career.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: having the same advantages and disadvantages as somebody else
examples: Can our industry compete on equal terms with its overseas rivals?

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: according to the conditions that you or somebody else decides
examples: I'll only take the job on my own terms.
I'm not doing it on your terms.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to refer to an area of land when you are mentioning its natural features, for example, if it is rough, flat, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO all-terrain
difficult/rough/mountainous terrain
They walked for miles across steep and inhospitable terrain.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very unpleasant; making you feel very unhappy, upset or frightened
examples: a terrible experience
What terrible news!
I've just had a terrible thought.
It was a terrible thing to happen to someone so young.
That’s a terrible thing to say!
It smells terrible in here.
It must have been terrible to witness the accident.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: causing great harm or injury; very serious
examples: a terrible accident
He had suffered terrible injuries.
I'll have to stay with her—she's in a terrible state.
The storm was terrible and caused a lot of damage.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: unhappy or ill
examples: I feel terrible—I think I'll go to bed.
You look terrible, you'd better sit down.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: of very bad quality; very bad
examples: a terrible meal
Your driving is terrible!
I have a terrible memory for names.
Cyclists claim that most city streets are in terrible condition.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to show the great extent or degree of something bad
examples: a terrible mistake
to be in terrible pain
The room was in a terrible mess.
It was a terrible tragedy.
I had a terrible job (= it was very difficult) to persuade her to come.
You’ll be in terrible trouble if you’re late again.
Sometimes the pain is so terrible I can't sleep.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: very
examples: I'm terribly sorry—did I hurt you?
It's terribly important for parents to be consistent.
I’m not terribly interested in politics.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very much; very badly
examples: I miss him terribly.
They suffered terribly when their son was killed.
The experiment went terribly wrong.
Would you mind terribly if I didn’t come today?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: excellent; wonderful
examples: I feel absolutely terrific today!
She's doing a terrific job.
You look terrific in that dress.
He was really terrific when I was in trouble.
That’s terrific news!
So nobody’s coming. Terrific!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: very large; very great
examples: I've got a terrific amount of work to do.
We drove along at a terrific speed.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel extremely frightened
examples: Flying terrifies her.
Stop it! You’re terrifying the children!
He terrified employees at the bank into handing over cash.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: land that is under the control of a particular country or political leader
examples: enemy/disputed/foreign territory
occupied territories
They have refused to allow UN troops to be stationed in their territory.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an area that one person, group, animal, etc. considers as their own and defends against others who try to enter it
examples: Blackbirds will defend their territory against intruders.
She seems to regard that end of the office as her territory.
Each of these gangs has its own territory.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an area of activity, especially one that is familiar/unfamiliar or somebody's particular responsibility
examples: This type of work is uncharted territory for us.
Legal problem's are Andy's territory.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an area of a town, country, etc. that somebody has responsibility for in their work or another activity
examples: Our representatives cover a very large territory.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a particular type of land
examples: unexplored territory

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a country or an area that is part of the US, Australia or Canada but is not a state or province
examples: Guam and American Samoa are US territories.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be a normal and accepted part of a particular job, situation, etc.
examples: She has to work late most days, but in her kind of job that goes with the territory.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: in a place that has no connection with either of the people or sides who are meeting and so does not give an advantage to either of them
examples: We decided to meet on neutral ground.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: in a place that has no connection with either of the people or sides who are meeting and so does not give an advantage to either of them
examples: We decided to meet on neutral territory.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a feeling of extreme fear
examples: a feeling of sheer/pure terror
Her eyes were wild with terror.
People fled from the explosion in terror.
He lives in terror of (= is constantly afraid of) losing his job.
Some women have a terror of losing control in the birth process.
The very name of the enemy struck terror into their hearts.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person, situation or thing that makes you very afraid
examples: These street gangs have become the terror of the neighbourhood.
The terrors of the night were past.
Death holds no terrors for (= does not frighten or worry) me.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: violent action or the threat of violent action that is intended to cause fear, usually for political purposes
examples: SYNONYM terrorism
a campaign of terror
terror tactics/groups
The president declared a war on terror (= a campaign against the use of terror).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a person (usually a child) or an animal that causes you trouble or is difficult to control
examples: Their kids are real little terrors.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the use of violent action in order to achieve political aims or to force a government to act
examples: an act of terrorism
the fight against terrorism
The government has sworn to do everything in its power to combat terrorism.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person who takes part in terrorism
examples: The terrorists are threatening to blow up the plane.
a terrorist attack/bomb/group

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an examination of somebody’s knowledge or ability, consisting of questions for them to answer or activities for them to perform
examples: SEE ALSO cloze test
an IQ/a fitness test
a test on irregular verbs
Students take standardized tests in English and maths.
to do a test
to pass/fail a test
a good mark in the test
a good score on the test

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a medical examination to discover what is wrong with you or to check the condition of your health
examples: SEE ALSO blood test
The hospital is doing some tests.
We'll need to perform a series of tests.
screening tests for cancer
Three athletes were sent home after failing drugs tests.
The pregnancy test was positive.
negative/positive test results

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an experiment to discover whether or how well something works, or to find out more information about it
examples: SEE ALSO acid test
the results of laboratory tests
to conduct a nuclear test
Tests have shown high levels of pollutants in the water.
I'll run a diagnostic test to determine why the server keeps crashing.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a situation or an event that shows how good, strong, etc. somebody/something is
examples: The local elections will be a good test of the government's popularity.
He saw their separation as a test of the strength of their love.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a cricket or rugby match played between the teams of two different countries, usually as part of a series of matches on a tour
examples: They played well in the first Test against South Africa.
He will be first choice for the opening test against the All Blacks.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to put somebody/something in a situation that will show what their or its true qualities are
examples: His theories have never really been put to the test.
The latest pay dispute has really put her management skills to the test.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to prove to be good, popular, etc. over a long period of time
examples: Whether this new technology will stand the test of time remains to be seen.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to teach students only what is necessary in order to pass a particular test, rather than help them develop a range of skillsWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (denoting a container used to treat gold or silver alloys or ore): via Old French from Latin testu, testum ‘earthen pot’, variant of testa ‘jug, shell’. The verb dates from the early 17th cent.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make a statement that something happened or that something is true, especially as a witness in court
examples: She refused to testify against her husband.
There are several witnesses who will testify for the defence.
He was summoned to testify before a grand jury about his role in the affair.
Evans testified to receiving $200 000 in bribes.
He testified (that) he was at the theatre at the time of the murder.
‘I was approached by a man I did not recognize,’ she testified.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to say that you believe something is true because you have evidence of it
examples: Too many young people are unable to write or spell well, as employers will testify.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to express your belief in God publiclyWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Latin testificari, from testis ‘a witness’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a thing that shows that something else exists or is true
examples: SYNONYM testament
This increase in exports bears testimony to the successes of industry.
The pyramids are an eloquent testimony to the ancient Egyptians' engineering skills.
His thick, swollen fingers bore testimony to a lifetime of toil.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a formal written or spoken statement saying what you know to be true, usually in court
examples: a sworn testimony
Her claim was supported by the testimony of several witnesses.
Can I refuse to give testimony?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activity of testing somebody/something in order to find something out, see if it works, etc.
examples: nuclear testing
testing and assessment in education

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: any form of written material
examples: SEE ALSO plain text
a computer that can process text
printed text
Highlight the area of text on screen and press the ‘delete’ key.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of writing that you have to answer questions about in an exam or a lesson
examples: SYNONYM passage
Read the text carefully and then answer the questions.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a written message that you send using a mobile phone
examples: She sent me a text to say she would be late.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the main printed part of a book or magazine, not the notes, pictures, etc.
examples: My job is to lay out the text and graphics on the page.
She wrote the text for a book of photographs.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the written form of a speech, a play, an article, etc.
examples: The newspaper had printed the full text of the president's speech.
Can you act out this scene without referring to the text?
The filmed version of Henry V stays close to the original text.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a book, play, etc., especially one that is being studied
examples: SEE ALSO set text
a literary text
sacred/religious/ancient texts

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a book that teaches a particular subject and that is used especially in schools and colleges
examples: medical texts

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a sentence or short passage from the Bible that is read out and discussed by somebody, especially during a religious serviceWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old Northern French texte, from Latin textus ‘tissue, literary style’ (in medieval Latin, ‘Gospel’), from text- ‘woven’, from the verb texere.

examples: a school/medical/history textbook

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the way a surface, substance or piece of cloth feels when you touch it, for example how rough, smooth, hard or soft it is
examples: the soft texture of velvet
She uses a variety of different colours and textures in her wall hangings.
The method used will vary with the soil texture and climate.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the way food or drink tastes or feels in your mouth, for example whether it is rough, smooth, light, heavy, etc.
examples: The two cheeses were very different in both taste and texture.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the way that different parts of a piece of music or literature are combined to create a final impression
examples: the rich texture of the symphony
a piece of music with a dense choral texture

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to introduce the second part of a comparison
examples: I'm older than her.
There was more whisky in it than soda.
He loves me more than you do.
It was much better than I'd expected.
You should know better than to behave like that.
I'd rather email than phone, if that's OK by you.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used for comparing amounts, numbers, distances, etc.
examples: It never takes more than an hour.
It's less than a mile to the beach.
There were fewer than twenty people there.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used in expressions showing that one thing happens straight after another
examples: No sooner had I sat down than there was a loud knock on the door.
Hardly had we arrived than the problems started.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: except
examples: I don't know any French people other than you.
We're going away in June but other than that I'll be here all summer.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: different or in a different way from; not
examples: I have never known him to behave other than selfishly.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to tell somebody that you are grateful for something
examples: I must write and thank Mary for the present.
In his speech, he thanked everyone for all their hard work.
She said goodbye and thanked us for coming.
There's no need to thank me—I enjoyed doing it.
I'd like to take this opportunity to thank everyone I've worked with over the years.
The organizing committee wish to thank their sponsors and all who helped.
I would like to thank you all most sincerely.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used when you are saying who or what is responsible for something
examples: I have my parents to thank for my success.
Largely we have science to thank for our longer, healthier lives.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that you are annoyed and do not want them to do something
examples: I'll thank you to mind your own business.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that you are pleased about something
examples: Thank God you're safe!
‘Thank goodness for that!’ she said with a sigh of relief.
Thank heavens I've found my keys.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to feel very grateful and lucky about something
examples: Just thank your lucky stars you weren’t in the house at the time.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody will not be pleased or will be annoyed about something
examples: John won't thank you for interfering.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to show that you are pleased that something good has happened or that something bad has been avoided
examples: SYNONYM fortunately
There was a fire in the building, but thankfully no one was hurt.
Thankfully, the house was empty when I got home.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in a pleased or grateful way
examples: At the end of a busy day, I just sink thankfully into bed.
I accepted the invitation thankfully.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to show that you are grateful to somebody for something they have done
examples: ‘How are you?’ ‘Fine, thanks (= thanks for asking).’
Thanks for lending me the money.
Many thanks for your support.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a polite way of accepting something that somebody has offered you
examples: ‘Would you like a coffee?’ ‘Oh, thanks.’
‘Here's the change.’ ‘Thanks very much.’
‘Do you want to come with us?’ ‘I’d love to, thanks.’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a polite way of refusing something that somebody has offered you
examples: ‘Would you like some more?’ ‘No thanks.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used for referring to a person or thing that is not near the speaker or as near to the speaker as another
examples: Look at that man over there.
How much are those apples at the back?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used for referring to somebody/something that has already been mentioned or is already known about
examples: I was living with my parents at that time.
That incident changed their lives.
Have you forgotten about that money I lent you last week?
That dress of hers is too short.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to refer to somebody/something that has already been mentioned or is easily understood
examples: There were three questions. The first two were relatively easy but the third one was hard.
There was an accident here yesterday. A car hit a tree and the driver was killed.
The heat was getting to be too much for me.
The nights are getting longer.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to refer to somebody/something that is the only, normal or obvious one of their kind
examples: the Mona Lisa
the Nile
the Queen
What's the matter?
The phone rang.
I patted her on the back.
How's the (= your) baby?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used when explaining which person or thing you mean
examples: the house at the end of the street
The people I met there were very friendly.
It was the best day of my life.
You're the third person to ask me that.
Friday the thirteenth
Alexander the Great

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to refer to a thing in general rather than a particular example
examples: He taught himself to play the violin.
The dolphin is an intelligent animal.
They placed the African elephant on their endangered list.
I heard it on the radio.
I'm usually out during the day.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used with adjectives to refer to a thing or a group of people described by the adjective
examples: With him, you should always expect the unexpected.
the unemployed
the French

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used before the plural of somebody’s last name to refer to a whole family or a married couple
examples: Don't forget to invite the Jordans.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used with a unit of measurement to mean ‘every’
examples: My car does forty miles to the gallon.
You get paid by the hour.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: enough of something for a particular purpose

One thing is for sure—it will be a memorable evening!
The main thing to remember is to switch off the burglar alarm.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the general situation, as it affects somebody
examples: Things haven't gone entirely to plan.
I wish things could have been different.
Hi, Jane! How are things?
As things stand at present, he seems certain to win.
All things considered (= considering all the difficulties or problems), she's done very well.
They're trying to change things for the better.
Things have changed over the last few years.
He's happy with the way things have worked out.
Why do you make things so difficult for yourself?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a quality or a concept
examples: Reality and truth are not the same thing.
The two of them have one thing in common—they never give up.
The good thing about this job is all the travelling.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: what is needed or socially acceptable
examples: You need something to cheer you up—I know just the thing!
to say the right/wrong thing
The best thing to do is to apologize.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that something is important or real
examples: I don't understand why these corny films are still a thing in 2020.
I'm not sure that ‘modular techno music’ is really a thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used with negatives to mean ‘anything’ in order to emphasize what you are saying
examples: I haven't got a thing to wear!
She hasn't had a thing to eat all day.
There wasn't a thing we could do to help.
Ignore what he said—it doesn't mean a thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: all that can be described in a particular way
examples: She loves all things Japanese.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a living creature
examples: All living things are composed of cells.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to talk to or about a person or an animal, to show how you feel about them
examples: SEE ALSO bright young thing
You silly thing!
You must be starving, you poor things.
The cat's very ill, poor old thing.
The baby's a pretty little thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if the conditions stay the same; if other conditions are the same
examples: All things being equal, we should finish the job tomorrow.
All other things being equal, the bigger fighter should win.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used when you do not want to complete a list
examples: She likes nice clothes and things like that.
I've been busy shopping and things.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: as was shown or proved by later events
examples: I didn't need my umbrella, as it turned out (= because it didn't rain).

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: as was shown or proved by later events
examples: As things turned out, the weather—and the whole weekend—were perfect.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to please everyone by changing your attitudes or opinions to suit different people

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to be understood or used in different ways by different people

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to be socially acceptable behaviour

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to be lucky that…
examples: It's a good thing we got here early.
It's a good thing you remembered to turn off the gas!

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used to say that although something seems to be bad, it could have good results
examples: We didn't want the press to get hold of the story, but it might be no bad thing.
It's no bad thing to express your anger.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to have found a job, situation or style of life that is pleasant or easy

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to imagine that you can see or hear something that is in fact not there

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: people say chance would be a fine thing to show that they would like to do or have the thing that somebody has mentioned, but that they do not think that it is very likely

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: a situation in which somebody only just wins or loses, for example in a competition or an election
examples: Mr Taylor’s election defeat was a close-run thing.
The invasion never happened but it was a close-run thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: a situation in which success or failure is equally possible
examples: We got him out in the end, but it was a close thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to have the same result or meaning

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to do what you want to do or what interests you, without thinking about other people; to be independent

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to have a powerful emotional effect on somebody
examples: That song just does things to me.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: early in the morning/late in the evening
examples: I need the report on my desk first thing Monday morning.
I took the dog for a walk last thing before going to bed.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: the most important matters must be dealt with first
examples: We have a lot to discuss, but, first things first, let's have a cup of coffee!

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: used to introduce one of two or more reasons for doing something
examples: ‘Why don't you get a car?’ ‘Well, for one thing, I can't drive!’

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to have something arranged in the way that you want, even though other people want it to be arranged differently
examples: The German team weren't going to let the English have everything their own way.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to have a strong like or dislike of somebody/something in a way that seems strange or unreasonable
examples: She has a thing about men with beards.

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to be sexually attracted to somebody; to like something very much
examples: Liz has always had a thing for guys in bands.
He has a thing for the new girl in the office.
Jamie has a thing for fast cars.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: in the way that things usually happen
examples: In the nature of things, young people often rebel against their parents.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: B is very different from A, for example it is more difficult, serious or important
examples: Romance is one thing; marriage is quite another.
It's one thing to tease your sister, but it's another to hit her.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: it isn’t something that you really enjoy or are interested in

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: it is something that only a particular group understands
examples: You wouldn't know what it means—it's a girl thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: to know/tell somebody some useful, interesting or surprising information about somebody/something
examples: She's been married five times, so she knows a thing or two about men!

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: to make something seem more important than it really is

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: a situation in which you are successful, but which could also have ended badly
examples: Phew! That was a near thing! It could have been a disaster.
We won in the end but it was a near thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to know nothing at all about something/somebody
examples: We’ve lived next to him for years, but we still don’t know the first thing about him.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: not considered socially acceptable
examples: It wouldn't be quite the thing to turn up in running gear.

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: not healthy or normal

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not want to discuss or think about something bad or unpleasant that has happened, but just accept it
examples: It wasn't your fault. It was just one of those things.

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: used to complain that a lot of unpleasant things keep happening to you

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: used to suggest that the way one event or action leads to others is so obvious that it does not need to be stated
examples: He offered me a ride home one night, and, well, one thing led to another and now we're married!

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: used before mentioning a worry or problem you have with something
examples: I'd love to come—the only thing is I might be late.

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: to work, study, etc. too hard or for too long
examples: He's been overdoing things recently.
I overdid it in the gym and hurt my back.

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: to take a risk because you have successfully avoided problems in the past
examples: You didn't get caught last time, but don't push your luck!

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: to take a risk because you have successfully avoided problems in the past
examples: Don't push things—we don't want it all to go wrong now.

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: actually what somebody claims that something is
examples: Are you sure it's the real thing (= love), not just infatuation?

definitions.label: Meaning 54
definitions.definition: the way things seem to be organized; the way somebody wants everything to be organized
examples: My personal problems are not really important in the overall scheme of things.
This small annoyance isn't much in the grand scheme of things.
I don't think marriage figures in his scheme of things.

definitions.label: Meaning 55
definitions.definition: the way things are likely to develop in the future
examples: Are solar-powered cars the shape of things to come?
This new system could be the shape of things to come.

definitions.label: Meaning 56
definitions.definition: used to say ‘yes’ to a suggestion or request
examples: ‘Are you coming?’ ‘Sure thing.’

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: to relax and avoid working too hard or doing too much
examples: The doctor told me to take it easy for a few weeks.
I like to take things easy when I’m on holiday.

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: to not think about what will happen in the future
examples: I don't know if he'll get better. We're just taking it one day at a time.

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: to not think about what will happen in the future
examples: I don't know if he'll get better. We're just taking things one day at a time.

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: there is only one possible course of action

definitions.label: Meaning 61
definitions.definition: used to say that you should accept an unpleasant situation or event because you cannot change it

definitions.label: Meaning 62
definitions.definition: a situation or an activity of the type mentioned
examples: She really didn't want to be involved in the whole family thing.

definitions.label: Meaning 63
definitions.definition: used to introduce an important fact, reason or explanation
examples: I'm sorry my assignment isn't finished. The thing is, I've had a lot of other work this week.

definitions.label: Meaning 64
definitions.definition: used to introduce a problem about something/somebody
examples: The thing with Karl is, he's always late.

definitions.label: Meaning 65
definitions.definition: used to refer to ghosts and other supernatural things that cannot be explained
examples: There are mysterious lights in the sky and things that go bump in the night.

definitions.label: Meaning 66
definitions.definition: to do what people or society expect, especially in a difficult situation
examples: He did the decent thing and resigned.

definitions.label: Meaning 67
definitions.definition: used to say that, although something is pleasant, you do not want to have too much of it

definitions.label: Meaning 68
definitions.definition: because you have been busy with various problems, events or things you had to do
examples: I completely forgot her birthday, what with one thing and another.

definitions.label: Meaning 69
definitions.definition: to arrange something in a particular way, especially by being clever
examples: Can you work it so that we get free tickets?

definitions.label: Meaning 70
definitions.definition: to arrange something in a particular way, especially by being clever
examples: Can you work things so that we get Friday afternoon off?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to have a particular idea or opinion about something/somebody; to believe something
examples: SEE ALSO well thought of
Do you really think (that) he'll win?
I thought I heard a scream.
I didn't think people were allowed to park here.
Am I right in thinking that you used to live here?
I think this is their house, but I'm not sure.
He ought to resign, I think.
That's my opinion, but you might think otherwise (= have a different opinion).
We'll need about 20 chairs, I should think.
I can't help thinking (that) things could have been different.
It was once thought that the sun travelled around the earth.
Well, I like it. What do you think?
What did you think about the idea?
What did you think of the film?
‘Is he any good?’ ‘I don't think so.’
‘Will we make it in time?’ ‘I think so.’
I think it highly unlikely that I'll get the job.
She thought him kind and generous.
It was better than I thought possible.
I thought it a good idea to go with him.
He's thought to be one of the richest men in Europe.
I think of this place as my home.
She is thought of as a possible director.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to use your mind to consider something, to form connected ideas, to try to solve problems, etc.
examples: Are animals able to think?
Let me think (= give me time before I answer).
Stop and think for a moment before making any decisions.
I'm sorry, I wasn't thinking (= said when you have upset or offended somebody accidentally).
I can't tell you now—I'll have to think about it.
The government needs to think carefully about the issues raised.
All he ever thinks about is money.
He was trying to think what to do.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to have ideas, words or images in your mind
examples: You're very quiet. What are you thinking?
I was just thinking what a long way it is.
‘I must be crazy,’ she thought.
‘What can I do now?’ he thought frantically.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to form an idea of something; to imagine something
examples: We couldn't think where you'd gone.
Just think how nice it would be to see them again.
I hate to think what would have happened if we hadn't arrived.
I like to think (that) he would help if I needed it.
I can’t think (that) he would be so stupid.
If I'm home late, my mother always thinks the worst.
Just think—we'll be lying on the beach this time tomorrow.
Try to think yourself into the role.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to expect something
examples: I never thought (that) I’d see her again.
The job took longer than we thought.
You'd think she'd have been grateful for my help (= but she wasn't).
I never thought you would carry out your threat.
Who would have thought to find you here?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to think in a particular way or on a particular subject
examples: Let's think positive.
You need to think big (= aim to achieve a lot).
If you want to make money, you've got to think money.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used in questions to show that you are angry or surprised
examples: What do you think you're doing?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to make something you say sound less definite or more polite
examples: I thought we could go out tonight.
Twenty guests are enough, I would have thought.
Do you think you could open the window?
‘You've made a mistake.’ ‘I don't think so.’

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to intend something; to have a plan about something
examples: I think I'll go for a swim.
I'm thinking in terms of about 70 guests at the wedding.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to remember something; to have something come into your mind
examples: I didn't think (= it did not occur to me) to tell her.
I can't think where I put the keys.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to behave in a very confident way that annoys other people, for example by telling them what to do
examples: She was acting as if she owned the place.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used when you suddenly remember something or realize that it might be important
examples: Come to think of it, he did mention seeing you.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to say that you and another person must both be very clever because you have had the same idea or agree about something

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say very strongly that you do not agree with something, or that something is not possible
examples: Me? Fail? I don't think so.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used to draw attention to a fact that is not obvious or has not previously been mentioned
examples: It was a difficult situation, when you think about it.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: used to say that you hope or believe that something is true
examples: I like to think I'm broad-minded.
I’d like to think that you were helping me because you wanted to, not because you felt you had to.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: that is what I expected or suspected
examples: ‘He said he'd forgotten.’ ‘I thought as much.’

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used when you are thinking or trying to remember something
examples: Now let me see—where did he say he lived?

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to consider it right or acceptable to do something; to decide or choose to do something
examples: You must do as you think fit (= but I don't agree with your decision).
The newspaper did not see fit to publish my letter (= and I criticize it for that).

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to say or think bad things about somebody
examples: Don't speak ill of the dead.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to consider a situation again and perhaps change your idea or intention
examples: You really should think again about that.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to say what your thoughts are as you have them

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to have a higher opinion of somebody
examples: She has behaved appallingly—I must say I thought better of her.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to decide not to do something after thinking further about it
examples: SYNONYM reconsider
Rosie was about to protest but thought better of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to form your own opinions and make decisions without depending on others

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to say or think bad things about somebody
examples: I wouldn't want them to think ill of me.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to consider an activity to be normal and not particularly unusual or difficult
examples: She thinks nothing of walking thirty miles a day.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: used as a polite response when somebody has said sorry to you or thanked you

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to be able to think and react to things very quickly and effectively without any preparation

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to think about something, or how to do something, in a way that is new, different or shows imagination

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to think in a clear or logical way
examples: The drugs were affecting her and she couldn't think straight.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to think carefully before deciding to do something
examples: You should think twice about employing someone you've never met.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to have a very good, poor, etc. opinion of somebody/something
examples: He thinks the world of his daughter.
I don't think much of her idea.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: used to show that you are surprised or shocked by something
examples: To think that my mother wrote all those books and I never knew!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the process of thinking about something
examples: SEE ALSO critical thinking
I had to do some quick thinking.
She believes in encouraging creative thinking in the classroom.
He had some serious thinking to do.
With good, clear thinking one can arrive at an answer.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: ideas or opinions about something
examples: What is the current thinking on this question?
I disagree with that kind of thinking.
She explained the thinking behind the campaign.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in my opinion

examples: We were hungry and thirsty.
Digging is thirsty work (= makes you thirsty).

I'm really thirsty.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having a strong desire for something
examples: SYNONYM hungry (5)
He is thirsty for power.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: dry; in need of water

definitions.definition: between the ages of 30 and 39

I think you'll find these more comfortable than those.

examples: There was a court case resulting from this incident.
The boy was afraid and the dog had sensed this.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: doing things very carefully and with great attention to detail
examples: She's very thorough and conscientious.
He was determined to be thorough in his research.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how bad or annoying somebody/something is
examples: SYNONYM complete
Everything was in a thorough mess.

definitions.definition: very much; completely
examples: We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves.
I'm thoroughly confused.
a thoroughly professional performance
I can thoroughly recommend it.
I felt thoroughly ashamed of myself.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: completely and with great attention to detail
examples: Wash the fruit thoroughly before use.
The work had not been done very thoroughly.

definitions.definition: despite the fact that
examples: SYNONYM although

Though she gave no sign, I was sure she had seen me.
His clothes, though old and worn, looked clean and of good quality.

examples: The tide turned for the Canadian at the start of the second set.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: arranged neatly and with everything in order
examples: OPPOSITE untidy
a tidy desk
She keeps her flat very tidy.
I like everything to be neat and tidy.

The place has never looked so tidy.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: OPPOSITE untidy
I'm a tidy person.
He is obsessively tidy.
tidy habits

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: SYNONYM considerable
It must have cost a tidy sum.
a tidy profit

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to attach or hold two or more things together using string, rope, etc.; to fasten somebody/something with string, rope, etc.
examples: PAST TENSE, PAST PARTICIPLE OF tie
She tied the newspapers in a bundle.
He had to tie her hands together.
They tied him to a chair with cable.
I tie back my hair when I'm cooking.
The box was tied with plastic string.
His hands were tied behind his back.
Shall I tie the package or tape it?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to fasten something to or around something else
examples: She tied a label on to the suitcase.
Anything which might be blown over was tied down or moved inside.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to make a knot in a piece of string, rope, etc.
examples: to tie a ribbon
Can you help me tie my tie?
Tie the cords neatly.
Can you tie a bow tie?
He tied his shoes (= the laces on his shoes) with a double knot.
Tie up your shoelaces!
I tied a knot in the rope.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be closed or fastened with a knot, etc.
examples: The skirt ties at the waist.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to connect or link somebody/something closely with somebody/something else
examples: Pay increases are tied to inflation.
Their company's future is closely tied to our own.
The house is tied to the job, so we'll have to move when I retire.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to limit somebody's freedom to act and make them unable to do everything they want to
examples: to be tied by a contract
I want to work but I'm tied to the house with the baby.
Carers can be completely tied to their homes.
I don't want to be tied to coming home at a particular time.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have the same number of points
examples: SYNONYM draw
England tied 2–2 with Germany in the first round.
They tied for second place.
The scores are tied at 3–3.
Last night's vote was tied.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to join notes with a tie

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: (too much under) the influence and control of somebody
examples: The British prime minister is too apt to cling to Washington's apron strings.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to tie somebody’s hands and feet together so that they cannot move or escape

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to prevent somebody from doing what they want by creating rules, limits, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be unable to do what you want to do because of rules, promises, etc.
examples: I really wish I could help but my hands are tied.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to become or make somebody very confused
examples: I got myself tied up in knots when I tried to explain the legal system to them.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to get married

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to get very drunkWord Origin
examples: Old English tīgan (verb), tēah (noun), of Germanic origin.

examples: He kept a tight grip on her arm.

examples: OPPOSITE loose

examples: We have a very tight budget.

examples: to keep tight control over something

examples: The rope was stretched tight.

He drew the cord tighter with a jerk.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: with things or people packed closely together, leaving little space between them
examples: There was a tight group of people around the speaker.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: SEE ALSO uptight

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: SYNONYM constricted

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: SEE ALSO tight-knit

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: curving suddenly rather than gradually
examples: The driver slowed down at a tight bend in the road.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

examples: SYNONYM close2
a tight race

definitions.label: Meaning 12

examples: SYNONYM mean

definitions.label: Meaning 13

examples: SYNONYM tipsy

definitions.label: Meaning 14

examples: SEE ALSO airtight

definitions.label: Meaning 15

examples: She’ll always help if you’re in a tight spot.
