definitions.label: Meaning 16

examples: It’s essential to keep a tight rein on public spending.

definitions.label: Meaning 17

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: The rope holding the boat suddenly tightened and broke.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: SEE ALSO standard time

examples: His injuries will take a long time to heal.
It took them a long time to get home.
Did you have to wait a long time to see the doctor?
I lived in Egypt for a time.
I was only there for a short time.
The early morning is the best time of day.
Her parents died a long time ago.

Mr Curtis was the manager in my time (= when I was working there).

definitions.label: Meaning 7

examples: SEE ALSO old-time

the violent times we live in (= the present period of history)
in times of trouble
The business was successful, even during difficult times.
Times are hard for the unemployed.
Times have changed since Grandma was young.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: an occasion when you do something or when something happens
examples: Every time I hear that song I feel happy.
It doesn't matter if you don't win every time (= every time you play).
Next time you're here let's have lunch together.
He failed his driving test three times.
He's determined to pass this time.
When was the last time you saw her?
I see her two or three times a week.
How many times (= how often) do I have to tell you not to do that?
I remember one time (= once) we had to abandon our car in the snow.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: an event or occasion that you experience in a particular way
examples: Did you have a good time in Spain?
They're having a hard time dealing with her illness.
I had an awful time in the hospital.
Mike and I shared some really good times.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: how long somebody takes to run a race or complete an event
examples: The winner's time was 11.6 seconds.
She completed the 500 metres in record time (= faster than any previous runner).
one of the fastest times ever

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: the number of beats (= units of rhythm) in a bar of music
examples: This piece is in four-four time.
a slow waltz time
The conductor beat time with a baton.

definitions.label: Meaning 12

examples: SEE ALSO big time

Clap your hands to keep time (= sing or move with the correct speed and rhythm).

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to say that something should have happened before now

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: if you do something against time, you do it as fast as you can because you do not have much time
examples: They're working against time to try and get people out of the rubble alive.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: earlier/later than was expected
examples: We finished 15 minutes ahead of time.
The plane took off an hour behind time.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: having advanced or new ideas that other people use or copy later

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: during the whole of a particular period of time
examples: The letter was in my pocket all the time (= while I was looking for it).

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: very often; repeatedly
examples: She leaves the lights on all the time.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: always
examples: Our representatives are ready to help you at all times.
Hot water is available at all times.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: even when the circumstances are very good
examples: He's never very happy at the best of times—he'll be much worse now!

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: at one time; together
examples: She was laughing and crying at the same time.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to introduce a fact that is different and must be considered
examples: You have to be firm, but at the same time you should try and be sympathetic.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: separately or in groups of two, three, etc. on each occasion
examples: We had to go and see the principal one at a time.
She ran up the stairs two at a time.
He surfs the internet for hours at a time.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: at the age you are (especially when you are not young)
examples: Eyesight doesn't get any better at my time of life.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: sometimes
examples: He can be really bad-tempered at times.
The rain will become heavy at times in the afternoon.
He can be rather moody at times.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to mark or follow the rhythm of music, by waving a stick, tapping your foot (= hitting it against the floor), etc.
examples: She beat time with her fingers.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: happening before you were born or can remember or before you lived, worked, etc. somewhere
examples: ‘Were you taught by Professor Pascal?’ ‘No, he was before my time.’

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: before the usual time in somebody’s life when something happens
examples: SYNONYM prematurely
She got old before her time.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: old-fashioned in your ideas, methods, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: to be able to take advantage of opportunities when they come
examples: His success was down to being in the right place at the right time.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to still be alive after the time when you were expected to die
examples: He’s been living on borrowed time ever since his last heart attack.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to be doing something that other people are likely to soon stop you from doing
examples: According to the latest opinion polls, the government is living on borrowed time.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: used to encourage somebody who has not been successful at something
examples: Never mind— better luck next time.
If you didn't win a prize, better luck next time.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to wait for the right time to do something
examples: He decided to bide his time until he got an opportunity to talk to her alone.

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to do something in order to delay an event, a decision, etc.
examples: The negotiators kept the gunman talking to buy time for the hostages.

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: to say or decide that it is time for something to finish

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: a very difficult or unpleasant job or time
examples: I've had a devil of a job finding you.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: to spend time in prison

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: whenever there is a choice
examples: I don't really like cities—give me the countryside every time.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: if you do something for old times’ sake, you do it because it is connected with something good that happened to you in the past

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: for a short period of time but not permanently
examples: You can leave your suitcase here for the time being.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: beginning on that day; from that time
examples: From that time forth she gave me endless friendship and encouragement.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: occasionally but not regularly
examples: She has to work at weekends from time to time.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: to delay something so that you can have more time to make a decision, deal with a problem, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: to deliberately make a situation difficult and unpleasant for somebody
examples: They really gave me a hard time at the interview.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: used to say that you prefer a particular thing or person to the one that has just been mentioned
examples: We don't go out much. Give me a quiet night in front of the TV any day!

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: to have no difficulties or problems
examples: He’s had an easy time of it since he married Lucy.

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: to enjoy yourself very much

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: to like and be interested in somebody/something
examples: I've always had a lot of time for Mary.

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: to dislike somebody/something
examples: I have no time for lazy people like Steve.

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: to have many problems or difficulties to deal with; to not be successful
examples: He’s had a thin time of it since losing his job.

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: to enjoy yourself very much

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: to have nothing to do or not be busy

definitions.label: Meaning 54
definitions.definition: to enjoy yourself very much; to have a very good time
examples: The kids had a whale of a time at the theme park.

definitions.label: Meaning 55
definitions.definition: when enough time has passed
examples: SYNONYM eventually

In the course of time, I began to understand.

definitions.label: Meaning 56
definitions.definition: when the time is appropriate, usually after a long period
examples: I have no doubt that she’ll tell us in the fullness of time.

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: early; with enough time so that you are not in a hurry
examples: Get to the airport in good time.

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: used to say that something will be done or will happen at the appropriate time and not before
examples: Be patient, Emily! All in good time.

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: at the very last moment; just before something bad happens, so that you manage to avoid it, but only just
examples: They escaped from the smoke-filled house just in the nick of time.

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: so soon or so quickly that it is surprising
examples: The kids will be leaving home in no time.

definitions.label: Meaning 61
definitions.definition: a long time ago in the past
examples: In olden times people would gather in town squares to gossip and exchange stories.

definitions.label: Meaning 62
definitions.definition: how and when you want to, even though this might annoy other people
examples: He always does the work, but in his own sweet time.
She just ignores all the criticism and continues on her own sweet way.

definitions.label: Meaning 63
definitions.definition: when you are ready and not sooner
examples: Don't hassle him! He'll do it in his own good time.

definitions.label: Meaning 64
definitions.definition: in your free time and not when you usually work or study

definitions.label: Meaning 65
definitions.definition: after a period of time when a situation has changed
examples: SYNONYM eventually

You'll get used to the work in time.

definitions.label: Meaning 66
definitions.definition: not late; with enough time to be able to do something
examples: Will we be in time for the six o'clock train?
The ambulance got there just in time (= to save somebody's life).

definitions.label: Meaning 67
definitions.definition: used to say that you think somebody should do something soon
examples: It's about time you cleaned your room!

definitions.label: Meaning 68
definitions.definition: used to say that something will definitely happen, although you are not sure when
examples: It's only a matter of time before they bring out their own version of the software.

examples: SYNONYM hint
handy tips for buying a computer
useful tips on how to save money
Here are my top tips for interview success.
The blog offered various beauty tips.
His money tips and tricks could save a typical family up to £6 000 a year.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a secret or expert piece of advice about what the result of a competition, etc. is likely to be, especially about which horse is likely to win a race
examples: a hot tip for the big race

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: secret information that somebody gives, for example to the police, to warn them about an illegal activity that is going to happen or has happened
examples: The man was arrested after an anonymous tip.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a small amount of extra money that you give to somebody, for example somebody who serves you in a restaurant
examples: to leave a tip
He gave the waiter a generous tip.
Someone put a dollar in the tip jar.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the thin, pointed end of something
examples: SEE ALSO fingertip
the tips of your fingers
the tip of your nose
the northern tip of the island

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a small part that fits on or over the end of something
examples: SEE ALSO felt-tip pen
a walking stick with a rubber tip

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a place where you can take rubbish and leave it

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: an untidy place
examples: SYNONYM dump
Their flat is a tip!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: if a word or name is on the tip of your tongue, you are sure that you know it but you cannot remember it

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: only a small part of a much larger problem
examples: This figure represents only the tip of the iceberg, since as many as 90% of cases go unreported.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: feeling that you would like to sleep or rest; needing rest
examples: SYNONYM weary
to be/look/feel tired
I'm too tired even to think.
They were cold, hungry and tired out (= very tired).
He still felt really tired and wanted to stay in bed.
I'm still a bit tired from the journey.
I take the bus when my legs get tired from walking.
We were both so dead tired that we kept falling asleep.
She was tired after a long day at the office.
tired feet

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: feeling that you have had enough of somebody/something because you no longer find them/it interesting or because they make you angry or unhappy
examples: I'm sick and tired of all the arguments.
She had grown heartily tired of his company.
She was tired of hearing about their trip to India.
I'm really tired of people complaining about us.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: boring because it is too familiar or has been used too much
examples: He always comes out with the same tired old jokes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of soft paper, used especially as a handkerchief
examples: a box of tissues
He wiped his nose on a tissue.
She grabbed a wad of tissues from the box and soaked up the spilt wine.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a collection of cells that form the different parts of humans, animals and plants
examples: SEE ALSO soft tissue
muscle/brain/lung tissue
scar tissue

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very thin paper used for wrapping and packing things that break easily

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a story, an excuse, etc. that is full of liesWord Origin
examples: late Middle English: from Old French tissu ‘woven’, past participle of tistre, from Latin texere ‘to weave’. The word originally denoted a rich material, often interwoven with gold or silver threads, later (mid 16th cent.) any woven fabric, hence the sense of ‘intricacy’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the name of a book, poem, painting, piece of music, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO working title
What's title of her new book?
a book/album title
Some of his song titles and lyrics have also attracted criticism.
His poems were published under the title of ‘Love and Reason’.
the title track from their latest CD (= the song with the same title as the disc)
She has sung the title role in ‘Carmen’ (= the role of Carmen in that opera).
The title character (= the person mentioned in the name of the book, play, etc.) is a native of Colombia.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a particular book or magazine
examples: The company publishes twenty new titles a year.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a word in front of a person’s name to show their rank or profession, whether or not they are married, etc.
examples: The present duke inherited the title from his father.
Give your name and title (= Mr, Miss, Ms, Dr, etc.).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a name that describes a job
examples: The official title of the job is ‘Administrative Assistant’.
What is your name and job title?
Bessie Smith earned the title ‘Empress of the Blues’.
In 2017, Brooks assumed the title of chairman.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the position of being the winner of a competition, especially a sports competition
examples: She has won three world titles.
He'll be defending his title at this week's French Open.
the world heavyweight title
the league/division/national title
a title fight (= in boxing)

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the legal right to own something, especially land or property; the document that shows you have this right
examples: He claims he has title to the land.

examples: I walked to the office.
It fell to the ground.
It was on the way to the station.
He's going to Paris.
my first visit to Africa
He pointed to something on the opposite bank.
Her childhood was spent travelling from place to place.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: as far as something
examples: The meadows lead down to the river.
Her hair fell to her waist.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: located in the direction mentioned from something
examples: Place the cursor to the left of the first word.
There are mountains to the north.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to show the person or thing that receives something
examples: He gave it to his sister.
I'll explain to you where everything goes.
I am deeply grateful to my parents.
Who did she address the letter to?
To whom did she address the letter?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to show the end or limit of a range or period of time
examples: a drop in profits from $105 million to around $75 million
I'd say he was 25 to 30 years old (= approximately 25 or 30 years old).
I like all kinds of music from opera to reggae.
We only work from Monday to Friday.
I watched the programme from beginning to end.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: before the start of something
examples: How long is it to lunch?
It's five to ten (= five minutes before ten o'clock).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: reaching a particular state
examples: The vegetables were cooked to perfection.
He tore the letter to pieces.
She sang the baby to sleep.
The letter reduced her to tears (= made her cry).
His expression changed from amazement to joy.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to show the person or thing that is affected by an action
examples: She is devoted to her family.
What have you done to your hair?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to show that two things are attached or connected
examples: Attach this rope to the front of the car.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to show a relationship between one person or thing and another
examples: She's married to an Italian.
the Japanese ambassador to France
the key to the door
the solution to this problem

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: directed towards; in connection with
examples: It was a threat to world peace.
She made a reference to her recent book.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to introduce the second part of a comparison or ratio
examples: I prefer walking to climbing.
The industry today is nothing to what it once was.
We won by six goals to three.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to show a quantity or rate
examples: COMPARE per
There are 2.54 centimetres to an inch.
This car does 30 miles to the gallon.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: in honour of somebody/something
examples: a monument to the soldiers who died in the war

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: one of the five small parts that stick out from the foot; any similar part on the foot of an animal or bird
examples: the big/little toe (= the largest/smallest toe)
I stubbed my toe on the step.
Can you touch your toes? (= by bending over while keeping your legs straight)
She wiggled her fingers and toes thoughtfully.
She stood on her toes and kissed him.
They are ground birds with long toes and claws.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the part of a sock, shoe, etc. that covers the toes
examples: He kicked the earth with the toe of his boot.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having the type or number of toes mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO pigeon-toed
open-toed sandals
a three-toed sloth

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to refuse to do something or to change your mind about something
examples: They dug their toes in and would not lower the price.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to start doing something very carefully to see if it will be successful or not
examples: We decided to dip a toe in the computer games market.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: covering your whole body
examples: We were covered from head to foot in mud.
She was dressed from head to toe in red.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: completely; all over
examples: She was dressed in green from top to toe.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to make sure that somebody is ready to deal with anything that might happen by doing things that they are not expecting
examples: Surprise visits help to keep the staff on their toes.
The threat of inspections kept us all on our toes.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel embarrassed or uncomfortable
examples: SEE ALSO toe-curling
The man's broad smile made her toes curl.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to offend or annoy somebody, especially by getting involved in something that is their responsibility
examples: I don’t want to tread on anybody’s toes so I’ll keep quiet.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: with or near to somebody/something else; with each other
examples: We grew up together.
Get all the ingredients together before you start cooking.
Stay close together—I don't want anyone to get lost.
Do you want to get together (= meet) again next week?
Together they climbed the dark stairs.
The two sides need to work together to solve this dispute.
They worked closely together over the next few years.
They seem to get on perfectly well together.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: so that two or more things touch or are joined to or combined with each other
examples: He rubbed his hands together in satisfaction.
She nailed the two boards together.
Mix the sand and cement together.
All the parts fit together perfectly.
Taken together, these factors are highly significant.
He has more money than the rest of us put together.
Four small tiles set together form a complete design.
The two countries together account for almost half the company's total sales.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in a close relationship, for example a marriage
examples: They split up after ten years together.
My son and his girlfriend are living together now.
My ex-wife and I are getting back together again.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: at the same time
examples: They both spoke together.
All together now: ‘Happy birthday to you…’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in or into agreement
examples: After the meeting the two sides in the dispute were no closer together.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: for hours, days, etc. without stopping
examples: She sat for hours together just staring into space.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: including
examples: Together with the Johnsons, there were 12 of us in the villa.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: in addition to; as well as
examples: Our meal arrived, together with a bottle of red wine.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a large bowl attached to a pipe that you sit on or stand over when you get rid of waste matter from your body
examples: Have you flushed the toilet?
I need to go to the toilet (= use the toilet).
a toilet seat
the toilet bowl
toilet facilities
Do you need the toilet?
The girl asked if she could use the toilet.
The hotels usually have modern showers and toilets.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a room containing a toilet
examples: Every flat has its own bathroom and toilet.
Who's in the toilet?
There was a communal toilet on the landing for the four flats.
There is a separate downstairs toilet.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a room or small building containing several toilets, each in a separate smaller room
examples: public toilets
toilet facilities
Could you tell me where the ladies' toilet is, please?
The toilets are located in the entrance area.
a disabled toilet (= for disabled people)
His new duties included cleaning the toilets.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the process of washing and dressing yourself, arranging your hair, etc.Word Origin
examples: mid 16th cent.: from French toilette ‘cloth, wrapper’, diminutive of toile ‘cloth, web’, from Latin tela ‘web’. The word originally denoted a cloth used as a wrapper for clothes; then (in the 17th cent.) a cloth cover for a dressing table, the articles used in dressing, and the process of dressing, later also of washing oneself (sense (4)). In the 19th cent. the word came to denote a dressing room, and, in the US, one with washing facilities; hence, a lavatory (early 20th cent.).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of being willing to accept or tolerate somebody/something, especially opinions or behaviour that you may not agree with, or people who are not like you
examples: SEE ALSO zero tolerance
She had no tolerance for jokes of any kind.
religious tolerance
a reputation for tolerance towards refugees

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the ability to suffer something, especially pain, difficult conditions, etc. without being harmed
examples: tolerance to cold
Tolerance to alcohol decreases with age.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the amount by which the measurement of a value can vary without causing problems
examples: They were working to a tolerance of 0.0001 of a centimetre.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to allow somebody to do something that you do not agree with or like
examples: SYNONYM put up with somebody/something
Their relationship was tolerated but not encouraged.
This sort of behaviour will not be tolerated.
She refused to tolerate being called a liar.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to accept somebody/something that is annoying, unpleasant, etc. without complaining
examples: SYNONYM put up with somebody/something
There is a limit to what one person can tolerate.
I don't know how you tolerate that noise!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be able to be affected by a drug, difficult conditions, etc. without being harmed
examples: She tolerated the chemotherapy well.
Few plants will tolerate sudden changes in temperature.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: money that you pay to use a particular road or bridge
examples: SEE ALSO e-toll
motorway tolls
a toll bridge
the possibility of imposing tolls on some motorways

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the amount of damage or the number of deaths and injuries that are caused in a particular war, disaster, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO death toll
the war’s growing casualty toll
Every hour, the news bulletin reported the mounting toll of casualties.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the sound of a bell ringing with slow, regular sounds

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a charge for a phone call that is calculated at a higher rate than a local call

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have a bad effect on somebody/something; to cause a lot of damage, deaths, pain, etc.
examples: Illness had taken a heavy toll on her.
The recession is taking its toll on the housing markets.
The pressure of fame can take a terrible toll.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a soft fruit with a lot of juice and shiny red skin that is eaten as a vegetable either raw or cooked
examples: SEE ALSO cherry tomato
a bacon, lettuce, and tomato sandwich
sliced/chopped tomatoes
tomato plants
tomato sauce/soup/juice
tomato paste/puree
sun-dried tomatoes
Demonstrators threw rotten tomatoes at the car.
It smells great, like ripe tomatoes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: I'm off now. See you tomorrow.
She's leaving tomorrow.
They arrive a week tomorrow/tomorrow week (= after a week, starting from tomorrow).

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: COMPARE tonne
What have you got in this bag? It weighs a ton (= is very heavy).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring the size of a ship. 1 ton is equal to 100 cubic feet.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a lot
examples: They've got tons of money.
I've still got tons to do.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: 100, especially when connected with a speed of 100 miles per hour
examples: He was caught doing a ton.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: very heavily; very severely
examples: Disappointment hit her like a ton of bricks.
They came down on him like a ton of bricks (= criticized him very severely).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the quality of somebody’s voice, especially expressing a particular emotion
examples: speaking in hushed/low/clipped/measured, etc. tones
a conversational tone
a tone of surprise
Don't speak to me in that tone of voice (= in that unpleasant way).
There's not need to take that tone (= speak critically or rudely) with me—it's not my fault we're late.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the general character and attitude of something such as a piece of writing, or the atmosphere of an event
examples: The overall tone of the book is gently nostalgic.

The film takes a sudden shift in tone in the final minutes.
The newspaper said voters had been turned off by the negative tone of the campaign.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

examples: the full rich tone of the trumpet
the sweet tone of the flute

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a shade of a colour
examples: SEE ALSO earth tone
a carpet in warm tones of brown and orange

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: how strong and tight your muscles or skin are
examples: how to improve your muscle/skin tone

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a sound heard on a phone line
examples: SEE ALSO ringtone
the dialling tone
the dial tone
Please speak after the tone (= for example as an instruction on an answering machine).
I keep getting the engaged tone.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: one of the five longer intervals in a musical scale, for example the interval between C and D or between E and F♯
examples: COMPARE semitone

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the pitch (= how high or low a sound is) of a syllable in speaking
examples: a rising/falling tone

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a particular pitch pattern on a syllable in languages such as Chinese, that can be used to recognize the difference in meanings

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: having the type of tone mentioned
examples: a bright-toned soprano
olive-toned skin

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the soft part in the mouth that moves around, used for tasting, swallowing, speaking, etc.
examples: He clicked his tongue to attract their attention.
She ran her tongue over her lips.
It's very rude to stick your tongue out at people.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the tongue of some animals, cooked and eaten
examples: a slice of ox tongue

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a language
examples: SEE ALSO mother tongue
None of the tribes speak the same tongue.
I tried speaking to her in her native tongue.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a particular way of speaking
examples: SEE ALSO silver tongue
He has a sharp tongue.
I'll thank you to keep a civil tongue in your head (= speak politely).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: speaking in the way mentioned
examples: sharp-tongued

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a long, narrow piece of leather under the laces on a shoe

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: something that is long and narrow and like a tongue in shape
examples: a tongue of flame

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to stop yourself from saying something that might upset somebody or cause an argument, although you want to speak
examples: I didn't believe her explanation but I bit my tongue.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: said to somebody, especially a child, who stays silent when expected to speak, for example after being asked a question
examples: What's the matter? Cat got your tongue?

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be able to speak or express your opinion

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to pronounce a difficult word correctly
examples: He was having trouble getting his tongue around my name.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to talk too much, especially about things that are private

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to say nothing although you would like to give your opinion

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to make somebody talk more freely than usual
examples: A bottle of wine had loosened Harry's tongue.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: if a word or name is on the tip of your tongue, you are sure that you know it but you cannot remember it

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be easy to say or pronounce
examples: It's not a name that exactly trips off the tongue, is it?

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to cause people to start talking/people are talking about somebody’s private affairs
examples: His sudden resignation set tongues wagging.
This is a small island and tongues are beginning to wag.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: a small mistake in something that you write or say
examples: Did I call you Richard? Sorry, Robert, just a slip of the tongue.
I didn't mean to say that—it was just a slip of the tongue.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to be careful what you say in order not to offend somebody or make them angry

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: if you say something with your tongue in your cheek, you are not being serious and mean it as a jokeWord Origin
examples: Old English tunge, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch tong, German Zunge, and Latin lingua.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: on or during the evening or night of today
examples: Will you have dinner with me tonight?
It's cold tonight.
I don't expect to see him until late tonight.
I will be out of town tonight and tomorrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: on or during the evening or night of today
examples: Will you have dinner with me tonight?
It's cold tonight.
I don't expect to see him until late tonight.
I will be out of town tonight and tomorrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring weight, equal to 1 000 kilograms
examples: COMPARE ton
a record grain harvest of 236m tonnes
a 17-tonne truck

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used before adjectives and adverbs to say that something is more than is good, necessary, possible, etc.
examples: He's far too young to go on his own.
She was much too big to be carried.
This is too large a helping for me/This helping is too large for me.
Is it too much to ask for a little quiet?
The dress was too tight for me.
It's too late to do anything about it now.
Accidents like this happen all too (= much too) often.
It’s too soon to say if he’ll survive.
It’s only too easy for them to deny responsibility.
The room was a bit too cramped for the three of us.
For most people treatment is just too expensive.
You can never have too many friends.
Some patients had to wait too long for an appointment.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: also; as well
examples: SEE ALSO me-too
Can I come too?
When I've finished painting the bathroom, I'm going to do the kitchen too.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: very
examples: I'm not too sure if this is right.
I'm just going out—I won't be too long.
Mary will be only too glad to help.
She's none too (= not very) clever.
potential customers who will not be too pleased about your lack of attention.
It's unlikely anyone's going to be too concerned about a little thing like that.
Our roads aren't too bad.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to comment on something that makes a situation worse
examples: She broke her leg last week—and on her birthday too!

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to emphasize something, especially your anger, surprise or agreement with something
examples: ‘He did apologize eventually.’ ‘I should think so too!’
‘She gave me the money.’ ‘About time too!’

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to need more skill or strength than you have; to be more difficult, annoying, etc. than you can bear

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that there is no doubt about something
examples: ‘We need to stick together.’ ‘Too right!’
‘I'll have to do it again.’ ‘Too right you will.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an instrument such as a hammer, screwdriver, saw, etc. that you hold in your hand and use for making things, repairing things, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO machine tool
garden tools
a cutting tool
Always select the right tool for the job.
craftsmen using traditional tools
a set of tools

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a thing that helps you to do your job or to achieve something
examples: research tools like questionnaires
a marketing/management tool
The internet can be a powerful teaching tool.
a useful/valuable tool
Some of them carried the guns which were the tools of their trade (= the things they needed to do their job).
the effectiveness of interest rates as an economic tool
An email newsletter can be a very effective communication tool.
They need to use all the tools at their disposal.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who is used or controlled by another person or group
examples: The prime minister was an unwitting tool of the president.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a penis

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to stop work; to go on strike

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: not intelligent
examples: He's not exactly the sharpest tool in the box, is he?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: any of the hard white structures in the mouth used for biting food
examples: SEE ALSO buck teeth
I've just had a tooth out at the dentist's.
to brush/clean your teeth
tooth decay
She answered through clenched teeth (= opening her mouth only a little because of anger).
The cat sank its teeth into his finger.
She had to have a tooth pulled (= removed).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a narrow, pointed part that sticks out of an object
examples: SEE ALSO fine-tooth comb
the teeth on a saw
The teeth of the cog should fit into these grooves.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having many weapons

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to show your teeth in an aggressive and threatening way
examples: The dog bared its teeth and growled.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: if you do something by the skin of your teeth, you only just manage to do it
examples: He escaped defeat by the skin of his teeth.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to do something that gives you your first experience of a particular type of work
examples: She cut her teeth on local radio.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to grow a new tooth

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to say that you should punish somebody by doing to them what they have done to you or to somebody else
examples: They advocate a justice system that works on the principle of an eye for an eye.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to fight in a very determined way for what you want
examples: The residents are fighting tooth and nail to stop the new development.
She fought tooth and nail to keep custody of the children.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to become very enthusiastic about something that you have started to do so that you are unlikely to stop until you have finished

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to put a lot of effort and enthusiasm into something that is difficult enough to keep you interested
examples: Choose an essay topic that you can really get your teeth into.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used when you are saying that you want something very much
examples: I'd give my eye teeth to own a car like that.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to press or hit your teeth together because you feel angry; to feel very angry and upset about something, especially because you cannot get what you want
examples: He'll be gnashing his teeth when he hears that we lost the contract.
The news caused great wailing and gnashing of teeth.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to bite your teeth tightly together
examples: She gritted her teeth against the pain.
‘Stop it!’ he said through gritted teeth.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be determined to continue to do something in a difficult or unpleasant situation
examples: It started to rain harder, but we gritted our teeth and carried on.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to like food that contains a lot of sugar

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to be powerful and effective

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to express anger or surprise
examples: Hell’s teeth, I promised I’d be back by two.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: despite problems, opposition, etc.
examples: The new policy was adopted in the teeth of fierce criticism.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: in the direction that a strong wind is coming from
examples: They crossed the bay in the teeth of a howling gale.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to treat somebody badly or fail to give them help when they need it

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: something that hurts somebody/something emotionally; a great disappointment
examples: The job losses are a kick in the teeth for the union.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to say something that is not true at all
examples: The witness was clearly lying through his teeth.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: used to say that it is very difficult to make somebody do something
examples: It's like pulling teeth trying to get him to talk.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: old or too old

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: involving opposition or competition that is violent and without sympathy
examples: nature, red in tooth and claw

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel physically uncomfortable
examples: Just the sound of her voice sets my teeth on edge.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the highest part or point of something
examples: SEE ALSO rooftop
She was standing at the top of the stairs.
The title is right at the top of the page.
Write your name at the top.
He filled my glass to the top.
We climbed to the very top of the hill.
Snow was falling on the mountain tops.
He was completely bald on the top of his head.
I was out of breath when I reached the top.
the top of the milk (= the cream that rises to the top of a bottle of milk)
The wind was blowing in the tops of the trees.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the upper flat surface of something
examples: SEE ALSO desktop (2)
Can you polish the top of the table?

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a piece of clothing worn on the upper part of the body
examples: SEE ALSO crop top
I need a top to go with this skirt.
a tracksuit/bikini/pyjama top
He was wearing a blue hooded top.
She wore a pink skirt with a matching top.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a thing that you put on the end of something to close it
examples: Where's the top of this pen?
a bottle with a screw top

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the highest or most important rank or position
examples: They finished the season at the top of the league.
He's at the top of his profession.
We have a lot of things to do, but packing is at the top of the list.
The company needs to make a change at the top.
She is determined to make it to the top (= achieve fame or success).
He worked his way to the top in just a few short years.
The album shot straight to the top of the charts.
The issue has recently risen to the top of the agenda.
I would not have gone into boxing if I didn't think I could reach the top.
This decision came from the top.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the end of a street, table, etc. that is furthest away from you or from where you usually come to it
examples: I'll meet you at the top of Thorpe Street.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the leaves of a plant that is grown mainly for its root
examples: Remove the green tops from the carrots.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used after an amount of money, time, etc. to show that it is the highest, longest, etc. possible
examples: It couldn't have cost more than £50, tops.
It'll take a couple of hours, tops.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a person or thing of the best quality
examples: Among sports superstars she’s (the) tops.
In the survey the Brits come out tops for humour.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a child’s toy that turns round on a point when it is moved very quickly by hand or by a string
examples: She was so confused—her mind was spinning like a top.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: high up/low down in the structure of an organization or a society
examples: These workers are at the bottom of the economic heap.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: in the highest position or rank in a profession or career

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: as loudly as possible
examples: She was screaming at the top of her voice.
I was shouting at the top of my voice but she couldn't hear me.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to get very angry

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: in the least/most important position in a group of people or things
examples: It’s been 20 years since a British player was top of the pile.
The government is doing little to help those on the bottom of the social pile.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to win a contest or an argument
examples: In most boardroom disputes he tends to come out on top.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: going to every part of a place in a very careful way
examples: We cleaned the house from top to bottom.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: completely; all over
examples: She was dressed in green from top to toe.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to be too much for somebody to manage or deal with
examples: All this extra work is getting on top of him.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to manage to control or deal with something
examples: How will I ever get on top of all this work?

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: just guessing or using your memory, without taking time to think carefully or check the facts
examples: I can't remember the name off the top of my head, but I can look it up for you.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: on the highest point or surface
examples: a cake with cream on top
Stand on top and look down.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: in a leading position or in control
examples: She remained on top for the rest of the match.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: in addition
examples: Look, here's 30 dollars, and I'll buy you lunch on top.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: on, over or covering something/somebody
examples: Books were piled on top of one another.
There was a vase on top of the bookcase.
Many people were crushed when the building collapsed on top of them.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: in addition to something
examples: He gets commission on top of his salary.
On top of everything else, my car's been stolen.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: very close to something/somebody
examples: We were all living on top of each other in that tiny apartment.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: in control of a situation
examples: Do you think he's really on top of his job?
Work tends to pile up if I don’t keep on top of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: very happy or proud

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: done with too much acting, emotion or effort
examples: His performance is completely over the top.
an over-the-top reaction

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to go back to the beginning of a song, piece of music, etc. and repeat it
examples: OK, everybody, let's take it from the top.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: with little or no hair on the head
examples: He's starting to get a little thin on top (= he's losing his hair).
He's going bald on top.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: used to talk about a person’s intelligence
examples: He hasn't got much up top (= he isn't very intelligent).
It’s what’s up top (= how intelligent you are) that matters.

examples: SYNONYM flip
Let's toss a coin.
There's only one ticket left—I'll toss you for it.
We tossed up to see who went first.
He had to toss up between (= decide between) paying the rent or buying food.

examples: She just tossed her head and walked off.

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 5

examples: early 16th cent.: of unknown origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: being the amount or number after everyone or everything is counted or added together
examples: Their total cost was $18 000.

the total profit/sales/revenue/income/expenditure/value

The total student population at Cambridge University is around 13,000 students.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: SYNONYM complete

They wanted a total ban on handguns.
The evening was a total disaster.
I can't believe you'd tell a total stranger about it!

They lived with an almost total lack of information about what was happening.
She maintained total artistic control over a project.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to put your hand or another part of your body onto somebody/something
examples: Don't touch that plate—it's hot!
Can you touch your toes? (= bend and reach them with your hands)
I touched him lightly on the arm.
Do not touch anything with your bare hands.
He has hardly touched the ball all game.
I must do some more work on that article—I haven't touched it all week.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be or come so close together that there is no space between
examples: Make sure the wires don't touch.
Their faces were almost touching.
Don't let your coat touch the wet paint.
His coat was so long it was almost touching the floor.
The dancer’s feet hardly seemed to touch the ground.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move something, especially in such a way that you damage it; to hit or harm somebody
examples: I told you not to touch my things.
He said I kicked him, but I never touched him!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel upset or emotional
examples: Her story touched us all deeply.
What he said really touched my heart.
I had been touched by his kindness to my aunts.
It truly touches me to know that I am holding in my hand a piece of paper used by someone who lived in 1745.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to affect somebody/something
examples: These are issues that touch us all.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to eat, drink or use something
examples: You've hardly touched your food.
He hasn't touched the money his aunt left him.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be as good as somebody in skill, quality, etc.
examples: No one can touch him when it comes to interior design.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to reach a particular level, etc.
examples: The speedometer was touching 90.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to become connected with or work with a situation or person
examples: Everything she touches turns to disaster.
His last two movies have been complete flops and now no studio will touch him.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be seen on somebody’s face for a short time
examples: A smile touched the corners of his mouth.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to have a small amount of a particular quality
examples: His hair was touched with grey.
Some of her poems are touched with real genius.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to upset somebody by reminding them of something they are particularly sensitive about

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to mention a subject that makes somebody feel angry, upset, embarrassed, etc.
examples: You touched a raw nerve when you mentioned his first wife.
My remarks about divorce had unwittingly touched a raw nerve.
The article struck a raw nerve as it revived unpleasant memories.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to not hurt somebody physically in any way

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to refuse to get involved with somebody/something or in a particular situation
examples: Personally, I wouldn’t touch him or his business with a bargepole.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to say or do something that makes people feel sympathy or enthusiasm
examples: The speaker had obviously struck a chord with his audience.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to make contact with somebody again

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to reach the ground at the bottom of an area of water
examples: I put my feet down and touched bottom.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to reach the worst possible state or condition
examples: Her career really touched bottom with that movie.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to say or do something that makes people feel sympathy or enthusiasm
examples: The speaker had obviously touched a chord with his audience.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to show too much respect for somebody of a higher class, especially because you are anxious about what they think of you

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used when talking about your previous good luck or your hopes for the future, to avoid bringing bad luck
examples: I've been driving for over 20 years and never had an accident—touch wood!

definitions.definition: very close
examples: We came within touching distance of winning the cup.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

the toxic atmosphere that now exists in political life

cuddly/stuffed toys

a toy shop/store

definitions.label: Meaning 2

executive toys

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to find or discover somebody/something by looking carefully for them/it
examples: SYNONYM track down
We finally traced him to an address in Chicago.
I have been unable to trace the letter you mentioned.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to find the origin or cause of something
examples: She could trace her family tree back to the 16th century.
The leak was eventually traced to a broken seal.
The police traced the call (= used special electronic equipment to find out who made the phone call) to her ex-husband's number.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to describe a process or the development of something
examples: Her book traces the town's history from Saxon times to the present day.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to draw a line or lines on a surface
examples: She traced a line in the sand.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to follow the shape or outline of something
examples: He traced the route on the map.
A tear traced a path down her cheek.
She lightly traced the outline of his face with her finger.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to copy a map, drawing, etc. by drawing on tracing paper (= paper that you can see through) placed over itWord Origin
examples: verb Middle English (first recorded as a noun in the sense ‘path that someone or something takes’): from Old French trace (noun), tracier (verb), based on Latin tractus ‘drawing, draught’, from trahere ‘draw, pull’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: rails (= metal bars) that a train moves along
examples: railway/railroad tracks
We crossed the rail/train track.
India has thousands of miles of track.
Many branch lines were closed, and the tracks lifted.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a track with a number at a train station that a train arrives at or leaves from
examples: The train for Chicago is on track 9.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a piece of ground with a special surface for people, cars, etc. to have races or to drive on
examples: SEE ALSO dirt track (2)
a race track
a Formula One Grand Prix track (= for motor racing)
a running track

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the sport of running on a track
examples: He loves sports and participates in track and basketball.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a rough path or road, usually one that has not been built but that has been made by people walking there
examples: SEE ALSO cart track
a muddy track through the forest
a dirt track

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: marks left by a person, an animal or a moving vehicle
examples: We followed the bear's tracks in the snow.
Leading away into the bushes were fresh rabbit tracks.
tyre tracks
The beach is criss-crossed with animal tracks.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the path or direction that somebody/something is moving in
examples: SEE ALSO fast track
He switched tracks and went back to college.
Police are on the track of (= searching for) the thieves.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a recording of one song or piece of music
examples: a track from their latest album
The album kicks off with the title track (= a song with the same name as the album).
The opening track is sweet and sentimental.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: part of a computer disk or tape that music or information can be recorded on
examples: a sixteen track recording studio
She sang on the backing track.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the soundtrack of a film or video
examples: SEE ALSO laugh track
The film is available with French and Spanish audio tracks.
There is a commentary track by the director.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: a long, thin, straight piece of metal, wood or plastic that a curtain hangs from and moves along

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a continuous belt of metal plates around the wheels of a large vehicle such as a bulldozer that allows it to move over the ground
examples: SEE ALSO Caterpillar track™

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: going in the right direction again after a mistake, failure, etc.
examples: I tried to get my life back on track after my divorce.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be doing the right thing in order to achieve a particular result
examples: Curtis is on track for the gold medal.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to try and hide what you have done, because you do not want other people to find out about it
examples: He had attempted to cover his tracks by making her death appear like suicide.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: from or living in a poor area or part of town

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: close to catching or finding the person or thing that you have been running after or searching for

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to have/not have information about what is happening or where somebody/something is
examples: Bank statements help you keep track of where your money is going.
I lost all track of time (= forgot what time it was).

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to leave a place, especially to go home
examples: It’s getting late—I’d better make tracks.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: far away from other people, houses, etc.
examples: They live miles off the beaten track.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: thinking or behaving in the right/wrong way
examples: We haven’t found a cure yet—but we are on the right track.
The new manager successfully got the team back onto the right track.
The police were on the wrong track when they treated the case as a revenge killing.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to suddenly make somebody stop by frightening or surprising them; to suddenly stop because something has frightened or surprised you
examples: The question stopped Alice in her tracks.
Suddenly he stopped dead in his tracks: what was he doing?
The disease was stopped in its tracks by immunization programmes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activity of buying and selling or of exchanging goods or services between people or countries
examples: SEE ALSO balance of trade
international/foreign/global/world trade
the international trade in oil
the illegal trade in wildlife
the arms/drugs trade
The Senate has approved a trade agreement with Latin American nations.
Trade between the two countries has increased.
an international trade barrier to GM food
Market prices and trade liberalization have increased prices.
trade negotiations/talks
Public support for the current trade policy is declining.
a bilateral trade deal

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a particular type of business
examples: SEE ALSO rag trade
the building/food/tourist trade
He works in the retail trade (= selling goods in shops/stores).
the fur/book trade

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a particular area of business and the people or companies that are connected with it
examples: SEE ALSO stock-in-trade
They offer discounts to the trade (= to people who are working in the same business).
a trade magazine/journal
Their company is respected and well known in the trade.
It's a trade association that represents all segments of the dairy industry.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the amount of goods or services that you sell
examples: SYNONYM business
Trade was very good last month.
All around the pyramids, salespeople were doing a roaring trade in souvenirs.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a job, especially one that involves working with your hands and that requires special training and skills
examples: He was a carpenter by trade.
When she leaves school, she wants to learn a trade.
She was surrounded by the tools of her trade (= everything she needs to do her job).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to sell a lot of something very quickly
examples: The ice-cream vendors were doing a roaring trade.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a person who can do many different types of work, but who perhaps does not do them very well

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to look for customers, passengers, etc. in order to do business
examples: taxis plying for trade outside the theatre

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to do your work or business
examples: This is the restaurant where he plied his trade as a cook.
Drug dealers openly plied their trade in front of children.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the clever ways of doing things, known and used by people who do a particular job or activityWord Origin
examples: late Middle English (as a noun): from Middle Low German, literally ‘track’, of West Germanic origin; related to tread. definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: Attention to detail is Anthea’s trademark.

new laws on Sunday trading (= shops being open on Sundays)

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a belief, custom or way of doing something that has existed for a long time among a particular group of people; a set of these beliefs or customs
examples: religious/cultural/ancient traditions
This region is steeped in tradition.
The company has a long tradition of fine design.
The company has continued its tradition of innovation.
The British are said to love tradition (= to want to do things in the way they have always been done).
They broke with tradition (= did things differently) and got married quietly.
By tradition, children play tricks on 1 April.
According to tradition, a tree grew on this spot.
There's a tradition in our family that we have a party on New Year's Eve.
He's a politician in the tradition of (= similar in style to) Kennedy.
a native culture expressed almost wholly through an oral tradition (= that is only spoken and not written down)

his country's rich folk traditions
His work has earned him a central place in the African American literary tradition.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: being part of the beliefs, customs or way of life of a particular group of people, that have not changed for a long time
examples: traditional dress/music/art/culture/dance
It's traditional in America to eat turkey on Thanksgiving Day.
traditional values/practices/beliefs
Acupuncture has long been a part of traditional Chinese medicine.
Janet makes cheese by traditional methods.
Cinema poses a threat to traditional art forms.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: following older methods and ideas rather than modern or different ones
examples: SYNONYM conventional
a traditional method/way of doing something
traditional methods of teaching
a traditional approach/view
Their marriage is very traditional.
the traditional female role of homemaker
He was raised in a traditional patriarchal family.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the vehicles that are on a road at a particular time
examples: There's always a lot of traffic at this time of day.
There are currently delays of 40 minutes due to heavy traffic.
She left home early to avoid the rush-hour traffic.
The road will be closed to through traffic for eight weeks.
The car veered across the road into the path of oncoming traffic.
They were stuck in traffic and missed their flight.
a plan to reduce traffic congestion
traffic police (= who control traffic on a road or stop drivers who are breaking the law)
She was badly injured in a road traffic accident.
The delay is due simply to the volume of traffic.
We got used to the constant noise of the traffic.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the movement of ships, trains, aircraft, etc. along a particular route
examples: SEE ALSO air traffic control
transatlantic traffic
The line is used by both passenger and freight traffic.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the movement of people or goods from one place to another
examples: commuter/freight/passenger traffic
the traffic of goods between one country and another

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the movement of messages and signals through an electronic communication system
examples: the computer servers that manage global internet traffic
web/network traffic
Telecom operators have upgraded their networks to improve their capacity as data traffic increases.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: illegal trade in something
examples: the traffic in firearms

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a very sad event or situation, especially one that involves death
examples: It's a tragedy that she died so young.
Tragedy struck the family when their son was hit by a car and killed.
The whole affair ended in tragedy.
Investigators are searching the wreckage of the plane to try to find the cause of the tragedy.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a serious play with a sad ending, especially one in which the main character dies; plays of this type
examples: COMPARE comedy
Shakespeare’s tragedies
Greek tragedy
Revenge tragedies were very popular in Elizabethan England.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: making you feel very sad, usually because somebody has died or suffered a lot
examples: He was killed in a tragic accident at the age of 24.
Cuts in the health service could have tragic consequences for patients.
It would be tragic if her talent remained unrecognized.
a rather tragic story

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: connected with tragedy (= the style of literature)
examples: a tragic actor/hero

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long line or series of marks that is left by somebody/something
examples: a trail of blood
tourists who leave a trail of litter everywhere they go
The hurricane left a trail of destruction behind it.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a track, sign or smell that is left behind and that can be followed, especially in hunting
examples: SEE ALSO vapour trail
The hounds were following the fox's trail.
The police are still on the trail of the escaped prisoner.
Fortunately the trail was still warm (= clear and easy to follow).
The trail had gone cold.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a path through the countryside
examples: SEE ALSO national trail
a trail through the forest

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a route that is followed for a particular purpose
examples: a tourist trail (= of famous buildings)
politicians on the campaign trail (= travelling around to attract support)

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be the first to do or to discover something that others follow
examples: COMPARE trailblazer
The department is blazing a trail in the field of laser surgery.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to start a journey
examples: The following spring I hit the road.

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: something that confuses you so that you see, understand, remember, etc. things in the wrong way
examples: One of the problems of old age is that your memory can start to play tricks on you.

examples: SEE ALSO hat-trick

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a way of doing something that works well; a good method

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the cards that you play or win in a single part of a card game
examples: SEE ALSO three-card trick

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: I don't know what it was that did the trick, but I am definitely feeling much better.

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: He'll try every trick in the book to stop you from winning.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to have an idea, some plans, etc. that you keep ready to use if it becomes necessary
examples: I have a few tricks up my sleeve.

definitions.label: Meaning 11

He's in trouble with the police.

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: The police were expecting trouble after the match.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: illness or pain

definitions.label: Meaning 6
