examples: a cattle truck

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a vehicle that is open at the back, used for carrying goods, soldiers, animals, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO breakdown truck
a delivery/farm truck
a dump/tow/armoured truck
They heard a truck pull up outside.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a vehicle for carrying things, that is pulled or pushed by hand

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to refuse to deal with somebody; to refuse to accept or consider something
examples: We in this party will have no truck with illegal organizations.
Dave wants no truck with change. For him, things are just fine as they are.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: connected with facts rather than things that have been invented or guessed
examples: OPPOSITE untrue
Indicate whether the following statements are true or false.
Can you prove that what you say is true?
All the rumours turned out to be true.
Is it true she's leaving?
It is certainly true that money can't buy you happiness.
I think it would be true to say that the show was a success.
That's not strictly (= completely) true.
The novel is based on a true story.
Unfortunately, these findings do not hold true (= are not valid) for women and children.
Exercise can help in the development of social skills, and this is especially true for kids playing team sports.
The music is dull and uninspiring, and the same is true of the acting.
You never spoke a truer word (= used to emphasize that you agree with what somebody has just said).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: real or exact, especially when this is different from how something seems
examples: the true face of war (= what it is really like rather than what people think it is like)
This project demonstrates the true value of teamwork.
The true cost of these experiments to the environment will not be known for years to come.
He reveals his true character to very few people.
I did not realize the true nature of their relationship.
She was unable to hide her true feelings for him.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having the qualities or characteristics of the thing mentioned
examples: It was true love between them.
He's a true gentleman.
The painting is a masterpiece in the truest sense of the word.
He is credited with inventing the first true helicopter.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to admit that a particular fact or statement is correct, although you think that something else is more important
examples: It's true that he could do the job, but would he fit in with the rest of the team?
It's perfectly true that I didn't help much, but I was busy.
‘We could get it cheaper.’ ‘True, but would it be as good?’
True enough, but that doesn't tell the whole story.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: showing respect and support for a particular person or belief in a way that does not change, even in different situations
examples: a true friend
She has always been true to herself (= done what she thought was good, right, etc.).
He was true to his word (= did what he promised to do).
Many were executed for remaining true to their principles.
Knights swore to be true to their lord.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: being an accurate version or copy of something
examples: The movie is not true to the book.
The painting is a true likeness of her.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: straight and accurate
examples: His aim was true (= he hit the target).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to become reality
examples: Winning the medal was like a dream come true.
All her wishes came true.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to give the impression of being sincere/true or not sincere/true
examples: It may seem a strange story but it rings true to me.
His expressions of support rang rather hollow.
His promise rang hollow.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to say that you cannot believe that something is as good as it seems
examples: ‘I'm afraid you were quoted the wrong price.’ ‘I thought it was too good to be true.’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: that you have used or relied on in the past successfully
examples: a tried and true method for solving the problem

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: your real character, rather than the one that you usually allow other people to see
examples: It was only after they got married that he showed himself in his true colours.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody is behaving in the way that you expect them to behave, especially when this is annoying
examples: True to form, she managed to upset everyone before leaving.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: seeming real rather than invented
examples: I don’t think the characters are very true to life.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that a particular statement, feeling, etc. is sincere or real
examples: She truly believes that none of this is her fault.
I'm truly sorry that things had to end like this.
I felt truly at home.
I do care. Truly, I do!
Does she truly love him?
He could never truly forgive her.
He truly wants to improve the town.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a particular quality
examples: The results are truly amazing.
It's a truly remarkable movie.
a truly great work of art
a truly memorable occasion
a truly magnificent performance

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that a particular description is accurate or correct
examples: a truly democratic system of government
Well, really and truly, things were better than expected.
He started the first truly international ballet company.
They truly understand what we're going through.
a brand that is truly global

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: completely
examples: By that time we were well and truly lost.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used at the end of a formal letter before you sign your name

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: I/me
examples: Steve came first, Robin second, and yours truly came last.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the belief that somebody/something is good, sincere, honest, etc. and will not try to harm or trick you
examples: Our partnership is based on trust.
This is a relationship built on mutual trust.
It has taken years to earn their trust.
We worked hard to gain the trust of local people.
Talking openly with your team helps to build trust.
Her trust in him was unfounded.
If you put your trust in me, I will not let you down.
I want to thank all those people who have placed their trust in me.
She will not betray your trust (= do something that you have asked her not to do).
He was appointed to a position of trust (= a job involving a lot of responsibility, because people trust him).
This is a serious breach of trust.
The company has to earn the trust and confidence of consumers again.
There is a lack of trust between the two countries.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the belief that something is true or correct or that you can rely on it
examples: We place so much trust in computers that it gets a little scary.
Voters need to have trust in the voting system.
Public trust in science is harmed by inaccurate journalism.
If I were you, I would not place too much trust in their findings.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an arrangement by which an organization or a group of people has legal control of money or property that has been given to somebody, usually until that person reaches a particular age; an amount of money or property that is controlled in this way
examples: SEE ALSO blind trust
He set up a trust for his children.
The money will be held in trust until she is 18.
Our fees depend on the value of the trust.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: an organization or a group of people that invests money that is given or lent to it and uses the profits to help a charity
examples: SEE ALSO hospital trust
a charitable trust

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a group of companies that work together illegally to reduce competition, control prices, etc.
examples: anti-trust laws

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: being taken care of by somebody
examples: The family pet was left in the trust of a neighbour.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to believe what somebody says even though you do not have any proof or evidence to show that it is trueWord Origin
examples: Middle English: from Old Norse traust, from traustr ‘strong’; the verb from Old Norse treysta, assimilated to the noun.

definitions.definition: a person or an organization that has control of money or property that has been put into a trust for somebody
examples: The bank will act as trustees for the estate until the child is 18.

definitions.definition: a member of a group of people that controls the financial affairs and decides the policy of a charity or other organization
examples: the board of trustees

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the true facts about something, rather than the things that have been invented or guessed
examples: Do you think she's telling the truth?
We are determined to get at (= discover) the truth.
She had only spoken the truth.
So now you know the truth.
I knew the truth would come out in the end.
The truth is that there are no easy answers.
The truth of the matter is we can’t afford to keep all the staff on.
The sad truth is that, at 72, he is past his prime.
The simple truth is that new roads just encourage more traffic.
I don't think you are telling me the whole truth about what happened.
These documents reveal the truth about his past.
The awful truth about his disappearance finally dawned on her.
Only recently has the truth behind the killings emerged.
It’s the gospel truth! (= completely true)
I honestly don't know, and that's the truth.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the quality or state of being based on fact
examples: OPPOSITE falsity
There is no truth in the rumours.
There is not a grain of truth in what she says.
His version of events does contain an element of truth.
You must be prepared to prove the truth of these allegations.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a fact that is believed by most people to be true
examples: COMPARE untruth
universal truths
She was forced to face up to a few unwelcome truths about her family.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: if you say that somebody has been economical with the truth, you mean that they left out some important facts, but you do not want to say that they were lying

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to say something that is not completely true
examples: I wasn’t exactly lying when I said I hadn’t seen her—I was just bending the truth a little.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody the true facts about a situation, especially when these are not known by other people
examples: If the truth be known, I was afraid to tell anyone.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the true facts about a situation
examples: She laughed and chatted but was, in truth, not having much fun.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a time when somebody/something is tested, or when important decisions are made
examples: The moment of truth is when the trainee pilots take over the controls of the plane.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to say that a fact or comment is completely false
examples: She thinks I don’t like her but nothing could be further from the truth.
I know you think she's mean, but nothing could be further from the truth.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used when admitting something
examples: To tell you the truth, I'll be glad to get home.
I got a bit big-headed, to tell the truth.
To tell you the truth, I'm rather dreading his return.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to say that things that actually happen are often more surprising than stories that are invented

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say that people will find out the true facts about a situation even if you try to keep them secretWord Origin
examples: Old English trīewth, trēowth ‘faithfulness, constancy’ (see true, -th).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make an attempt or effort to do or get something
examples: I don't know if I can come but I'll try.
What are you trying to do?
I tried hard not to laugh.
You haven’t even tried to find it.
Don’t try to do it too quickly.
I kept trying to remember where I had seen him before.
I was just trying to help!
She was desperately trying to stay afloat.
She tried her best to solve the problem.
Just try your hardest.
I tried calling him but there was no answer.
Just try getting a plumber at the weekend!
He tried and tried but he could not climb out.
Please try again later.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to use, do or test something in order to see if it is good, suitable, etc.
examples: Have you tried this new coffee? It's very good.
‘Would you like to try some raw fish?’ ‘Why not? I'll try anything once!’
I'd like to try something new.
I'm having a caffeine-free week. You should try it.
Have you ever tried windsurfing?
Try these shoes for size—they should fit you.
She tried the door, but it was locked.
The treatment has not yet been tried on patients.
John isn't here. Try phoning his mobile.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to examine evidence in court and decide whether somebody is innocent or guilty
examples: He was tried for murder.
The case was tried before a jury.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to try as hard as you can (to do something)
examples: She did her damnedest to get it done on time.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to do as much as you can to try to achieve something

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that although somebody has not succeeded in something, they have tried very hard
examples: They haven't won a game yet, but it isn't for want of trying.
They lost the game, but not for lack of trying.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that you should accept an unpleasant situation or event because you cannot change it

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: that you have used or relied on in the past successfully
examples: a tried and tested method for solving the problem

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to try as hard as you can (to do something)
examples: She tried her damnedest to get it done on time.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to do something such as an activity or a sport for the first time

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to behave badly towards somebody or try to get something from them, even though you know this will make them angry
examples: Children often try it on with new teachers.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to try to start a sexual relationship with somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to do something that involves risk or luck, hoping to succeed
examples: My grandparents emigrated to Canada to try their luck there.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel impatient
examples: His stubbornness would try the patience of a saint.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an extremely large wave in the sea caused, for example, by an earthquake
examples: COMPARE tidal wave
A tsunami early warning system was set up in Hawaii.
The tsunami caused immeasurable damage.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long, hollow pipe made of metal, plastic, rubber, etc., through which liquids or gases move from one place to another
examples: SEE ALSO cathode ray tube
He had to be fed through a feeding tube for several months.
She poured the liquid down the tube.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a hollow object in the shape of a pipe or tube
examples: SEE ALSO inner tube
the cardboard tube from the centre of a toilet roll
I put the poster back into its tube.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a long, narrow container made of soft metal or plastic, with a lid (= cover), used for holding thick liquids that can be forced out of it by pressing
examples: a tube of toothpaste
a tube of glue

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a can of beer
examples: a tube of lager

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a part inside the body that is like a tube in shape and through which air, liquid, etc. passes
examples: SEE ALSO fallopian tube
bronchial tubes
The oesophagus is the tube leading from the throat to the stomach.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: the underground railway system in London
examples: I often travel on the tube
We came by tube.
a tube station/train
She caught the wrong tube (= tube train).

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the television

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a small tube placed in a child’s ear in order to drain liquid from it when there is an infection

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to fail
examples: The education system is going down the tubes.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the day of the week after Monday and before Wednesday
examples: It's Tuesday today, isn't it?
She started work last Tuesday.
Are you busy next Tuesday?
Tuesday morning/afternoon/evening
We'll discuss this at Tuesday's meeting.
I work Tuesday to Friday.
I work Tuesdays to Fridays.
We'll meet on Tuesday (= next Tuesday).
We met on Tuesday (= last Tuesday).
We'll meet Tuesday.
The museum is closed on Tuesdays (= every Tuesday).
The museum is closed Tuesdays.
He was born on a Tuesday.
I always do yoga on a Tuesday (= every Tuesday).
I went to Paris on Thursday, and came back the following Tuesday.
‘When did the accident happen?’ ‘It was the Tuesday (= the Tuesday of the week we are talking about).’
Come back Tuesday week (= a week after next Tuesday).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the act of teaching something, especially to one person or to people in small groups
examples: She received private tuition in French.
The course involves six hours of individual tuition per week.
I studied dance for two years under her expert tuition.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the money that you pay to be taught, especially in a college or university
examples: The scholarship pays the tuition fees but students still need to find money for accommodation, meals and books.
He won't be able to finish his education unless someone pays his tuition.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a series of musical notes that are sung or played in a particular order to form a piece of music
examples: SEE ALSO signature tune
to sing/whistle a tune
He was humming a familiar tune.
I can play a few tunes on the piano.
I don't know the title but I recognize the tune.
It was a catchy tune (= easy to remember).
a football song sung to the tune of (= using the tune of) ‘When the saints go marching in’
a show/dance/pop tune

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be/not be singing or playing the correct musical notes to sound pleasant
examples: None of them could sing in tune.
The piano is out of tune.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be/not be in agreement with somebody/something; to have/not have the same opinions, feelings, interests, etc. as somebody/something
examples: These proposals are perfectly in tune with our own thoughts on the subject.
The President is out of tune with public opinion.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be the person who controls a situation

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to express a different opinion or behave in a different way when your situation changes
examples: Wait until it happens to him—he'll soon change his tune.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to do whatever somebody tells you to

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the person who provides the money for something can also control how it is spent

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to behave in a different way from other people; to have different attitudes or ideas
examples: She was a gifted and original artist who marched to a different drummer.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to change your opinion about somebody/something or your attitude towards somebody/something

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how much money something has cost
examples: The hotel has been refurbished to the tune of a million dollars.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a passage built underground, for example to allow a road or railway to go through a hill, under a river, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO wind tunnel
a railway/railroad tunnel
the Channel Tunnel
the tunnel entrance/walls/ceiling
They have been digging underground tunnels in the mountains since the 1960s.
A gust of wind passed through the tunnel.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an underground passage made by an animal or natural processes
examples: The badger sett had twelve entrances to what must have been a labyrinth of tunnels.
The tunnel opened out into a large cavern.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that shows you are nearly at the end of a long and difficult time or situation
examples: For the first time since the start of his treatment, we can now see light at the end of the tunnel.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move or make something move around a central point
examples: The wheels of the car began to turn.
I can't get the screw to turn.
The blades of the helicopter were turning slowly.
I turned the knob and pushed the door open.
He turned the key in the lock.
She turned the wheel sharply to the left.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move your body or part of your body so as to face or start moving in a different direction
examples: SEE ALSO turn over
We turned and headed for home.
She turned to look at me.
He turned back to his work.
I turned away and looked out of the window.
He turned his back to the wall.
I turned my face to the sky.
She turned her head away.
I only turned my back for a second.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to move something so that it is in a different position or facing a different direction
examples: SEE ALSO turn something over
She turned the chair on its side to repair it.
Turn the sweater inside out before you wash it.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to change the direction you are moving or travelling in; to make something change the direction it is moving in
examples: He turned into a narrow street.
We turned down a dark alleyway.
Turn left at the traffic lights.
The man turned the corner and disappeared.
I turned the car into the car park.
The pilot attempted to turn the aircraft towards a wooded area.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to bend or curve in a particular direction
examples: The road turns to the left after the church.
After a while the path turns sharply right.
The river turns north at this point.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if you turn a page of a book or magazine, you move it so that you can read the next page
examples: He sat turning the pages idly.
Turn to p.23.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to change into a particular state or condition; to make something do this
examples: The leaves were turning brown.
They say her hair turned white overnight.
I could feel my face turn red with embarrassment.
The weather has turned cold.
He turned nasty when we refused to give him the money.
He decided to turn professional.
The heat turned the milk sour.
She turned a deathly shade of white when she heard the news.
He's a lawyer turned politician (= he used to be a lawyer but is now a politician).

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to aim or point something in a particular direction
examples: Police turned water cannon on the rioters.
He turned the gun on himself.
She looked at him then turned her attention back to me.
His thoughts turned to his dead wife.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to start to come in or go out
examples: The tide is turning—we'd better get back.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make or let somebody/something go into a particular place or state
examples: They turned the horse into the field.
to turn the dogs loose

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to fold something in a particular way
examples: She turned down the blankets and climbed into bed.
He turned up the collar of his coat and hurried out into the rain.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to perform a movement by moving your body in a circle
examples: to turn cartwheels/somersaults

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: if a game turns or somebody turns it, it changes the way it is developing so that a different person or team starts to win

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to reach or pass a particular age or time
examples: She turns 21 in June.
It's turned midnight.

definitions.label: Meaning 15

Is anything up? You can tell me.

definitions.label: Meaning 13

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to be somebody’s duty or responsibility; to be for somebody to decide
examples: It's not up to you to tell me how to do my job.
Shall we eat out or stay in? It's up to you.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be of poor quality; to not be very good
examples: His work isn't up to much.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: facing problems or opposition
examples: Teachers are up against some major problems these days.
She's really up against it (= in a difficult situation).

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: moving upwards and downwards
examples: The boat bobbed up and down on the water.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: in one direction and then in the opposite direction
examples: She was pacing up and down in front of her desk.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: sometimes good and sometimes bad
examples: My relationship with him was up and down.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: if you swear up and down that something is true, you say that it is definitely true

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: working; being used
examples: By that time the new system should be up and running.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: appearing in front of somebody in authority for a judgement to be made about something that you have done
examples: He came up before the local magistrate for speeding.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: on offer for something
examples: The house is up for sale.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: being considered for something, especially as a candidate

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: willing to take part in a particular activity

definitions.label: Meaning 26

definitions.definition: physically or mentally capable of something

definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that they must be patient and wait to find out about something later
examples: We'll just have to wait and see—there's nothing we can do at the moment.
a wait-and-see policy
‘Where are we going?’ ‘Wait and see!’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to serve food to people, for example at a formal meal

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to say that you are about to tell somebody something that is surprising
examples: They're off on a trip, to—wait for it—the Maldives!

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody not to start doing something yet, but to wait until you tell them

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to wait for a short time
examples: Can you wait a second while I make a call?
Hey! Wait a minute! I'll come with you!

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used when you have just noticed or remembered something, or had a sudden idea
examples: Wait a minute—this isn't the right key.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to take care of somebody’s needs so well that they do not have to do anything for themselves
examples: He seems to expect me to wait on him hand and foot.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to work serving food to people in a restaurant

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to show that you are very excited about telling or showing something to somebody
examples: Wait till you see what I've found!

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: used to threaten to punish somebody or do something bad to them
examples: Wait till I get my hands on him!

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: used to suggest that you should all start doing what you have been discussing

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to do something now rather than later
examples: If the car needs cleaning, what are you waiting for?

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: used to emphasize a threat, warning or promise
examples: I'll be famous one day, just you wait!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person whose job is to serve customers at their tables in a restaurant, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO dumb waiter
I'll ask the waitress for the bill.
Waiter, could you bring me some water?
He was working as a waiter in a small restaurant in New York.
She complained to the head waiter.
A waiter serves them drinks.
He was trying to attract the waiter's attention to get the bill.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to stop sleeping; to make somebody stop sleeping
examples: SEE ALSO asleep
I always wake early in the summer.
Tom woke with a start and lifted his head.
What time do you usually wake up in the morning?
I woke up an hour earlier than I wanted to.
They woke to a clear blue sky.
I woke to the sound of heavy rain outside.
She had just woken from a deep sleep.
He woke up to find himself alone in the house.
The woman woke to see the defendant in her bedroom.
I was woken by the sound of someone moving around.
Try not to wake the baby up.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody remember something or feel something again
examples: The incident woke memories of his past sufferings.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody to become aware of what is really happening in a situation, especially when this is something unpleasantWord Origin
examples: verb Old English (recorded only in the past tense wōc), also partly from the weak verb wacian ‘remain awake, hold a vigil’, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch waken and German wachen; compare with watch.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to move or go somewhere by putting one foot in front of the other on the ground, but without running
examples: The baby is just learning to walk.
He may not be able to walk again.
‘How did you get here?’ ‘I walked.’
He walked slowly away from her.
The door opened and Jo walked in.
She missed the bus and had to walk home.
He turned and walked away.
He started to walk away from me, but quickly returned.
People walking past were staring at him.
You don't mind walking back, do you?
It looks like a nice place to walk around.
He walks over to the window and looks out.
I just happened to be walking by.
We walked along in silence for a while.
I ignored him and walked on.
I always walk to school.
Taking a deep breath, she walked into the room.
He immediately got up and walked out of the room.
I walked in the door and looked around.
He walked out the door, got in his car, and drove off.
He greeted her as she walked through the door.
I was walking down the street when I suddenly felt ill.
The school is within easy walking distance of the train station.
They walked the dark streets of Los Angeles.
Children here walk several miles to school.
She walked the short distance to her flat.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to spend time walking for pleasure
examples: I like an active holiday, so I walk.
She's started to go walking.
We're going walking in the mountains this summer.
I walked across Scotland with a friend.
They love walking the moors.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to go somewhere with somebody on foot, especially in order to make sure they get there safely
examples: He always walked her home.
I walked him to the corner of the street.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to take an animal for a walk; to make an animal walk somewhere
examples: They walk their dogs every day.
She walked the horse around the ring.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to disappear; to be taken away
examples: Lock up any valuables. Things tend to walk here (= be stolen).

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to appear

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: when a batsman walks, he/she leaves the field without waiting for the umpire to say that he/she is out
examples: He knew he was out, so he walked.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to reach first base without having to do anything because the pitcher failed to throw the ball correctly four times and you didn't try to hit it; to enable a batter to walk
examples: He walked 60 times in 57 games.
Despite walking one batter, Jackson showed solid control of the pitch.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to be taking a risk

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to feel very happy
examples: Most couples feel they are walking on air on their wedding day.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to get married

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to do things that are difficult, without learning the basic skills first

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to be in a difficult situation in which you do not have much freedom of action and need to be extremely careful about what you do
examples: The government is walking a difficult tightrope in wanting to reduce interest rates without pushing up inflation.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: to walk around the area that they are responsible for
examples: We have two officers walking the beat after midnight.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: to be in a difficult or dangerous situation where you could easily make a mistake
examples: He was walking a fine line between being funny and being rude.
She often seems to tread a thin line between success and failure.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to be allowed to leave court, etc., without receiving any punishment
examples: She was acquitted and walked free from court.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: to go somewhere on foot instead of in a vehicle
examples: It’s not very far. We can easily walk it.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to easily achieve something that you want
examples: It's not a difficult exam. You'll walk it!

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to make somebody walk so far or so fast that they are very tired
examples: I hope I haven’t walked you off your feet.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to stop working in order to go on strike

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: (in the past) to walk along a board placed over the side of a ship and fall into the sea, as a punishment

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to walk around the streets of a town or city
examples: Is it safe to walk the streets alone at night?

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to feel proud and confident

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to act in a way that shows people you are really good at what you do, and not just good at talking about it
examples: You can talk the talk but can you walk the walk?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long, solid structure that rises straight up from the ground, made of stone, brick or concrete, that surrounds, divides or protects an area of land
examples: SEE ALSO drystone wall
to build a wall
a brick/concrete wall
The fields were divided by stone walls.
He sat on the wall and watched the others playing.
The enemy set up camp just outside the city walls.
a private garden hidden behind high walls
They quickly climbed over the wall and ran off.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: any of the sides of a building or room
examples: SEE ALSO cavity wall
She leaned against the wall.
Colourful abstract paintings hung on the walls.
He drilled a hole in the wall.
Books lined the walls.
I'm going to paint the walls white and the ceiling pink.
the row of tables along the back wall
Pictures covered the walls.
the wall between the living room and the dining room

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: something that forms a barrier or stops you from making progress
examples: SEE ALSO fourth wall
The boat struck a solid wall of water.
The investigators were confronted by a wall of silence.
a solid wall of fog

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: the outer layer of something hollow such as an organ of the body or a cell of an animal or a plant
examples: the abdominal wall
the wall of an artery
Heating food breaks down plant cell walls so they can release more of their nutrients.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a space on a social media website where you can share messages, photos, etc. with other users
examples: She posted a pink baby romper on her Facebook wall, announcing they were expecting a girl.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to keep trying to do something that will never be successful
examples: Trying to reason with them was like banging my head against a brick wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to be so full of energy or so excited that you cannot keep still
examples: The kids have been bouncing off the walls all day.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be unable to make any progress because there is a difficulty that stops you

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a person who watches others without being noticed
examples: I'd love to be a fly on the wall when he tells her the news.
fly-on-the-wall documentaries (= in which people are filmed going about their normal lives as if the camera were not there)

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to fail because of lack of money
examples: Many firms have gone to the wall in this recession.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used when you are describing a situation in which there are signs that something is going to have problems or that it is going to be a failure
examples: It is amazing that not one of them saw the handwriting on the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to be in a difficult situation in which you are forced to do something but are unable to make the choices that you would like
examples: We had our backs to the wall with no choice but to sell.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to reach a point when you cannot continue or make any more progress
examples: We hit a wall and we weren't scoring.

What do you do when you hit the wall at work?

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: unusual or slightly crazy
examples: Some of his ideas are really off the wall.
off-the-wall ideas

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: used when you are talking about keeping something secret
examples: Don't let this go further than these four walls (= Don't tell anyone else who is not in the room now).

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: crazy or angry
examples: That noise is driving me up the wall.
I mustn't be late or Dad will go up the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: used to warn people to be careful what they say because other people may be listening

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used when you are describing a situation in which there are signs that something is going to have problems or that it is going to be a failure
examples: It is amazing that not one of them saw the writing on the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to walk slowly around or to a place, often without any particular sense of purpose or direction
examples: She wandered aimlessly around the streets.
We wandered back towards the car.
The child was found wandering the streets alone.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to move away from the place where you ought to be or the people you are with
examples: SYNONYM stray
The child wandered off and got lost.
How could you let him wander off like that?
They had wandered from the path into the woods.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to stop being directed on something and to move without much control to other ideas, subjects, etc.
examples: SYNONYM drift
It's easy to be distracted and let your attention wander.
Try not to let your mind wander.
Her thoughts wandered back to her youth.
Don’t wander off the subject—keep to the point.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to move slowly from looking at one thing to looking at another thing or in other directions
examples: She let her gaze wander.
His eyes wandered towards the photographs on the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to go in a curve instead of following a straight course
examples: The road wanders along through the hills.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

examples: We'll want more furniture for the new office.

The plants want watering daily.
The cake mixture wants to be smooth and light.
The plants want to be watered daily.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to need somebody to be present in the place or for the purpose mentioned
examples: SEE ALSO wanted
She's wanted immediately in the director's office.
Excuse me, you're wanted on the phone.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to give advice to somebody, meaning ‘should’ or ‘ought to’
examples: If possible, you want to avoid alcohol.
He wants to be more careful.
You don't want to do it like that.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to feel sexual desire for somebody
examples: ‘I want you so much,’ she whispered in his ear.
Alice, please don't leave me. I want you. I need you. I can't live without you.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to lack something
examples: SYNONYM be short of
He doesn't want courage.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have or want to have the advantages of two different situations or ways of behaving that are impossible to combine
examples: You can't have it both ways. If you can afford to go out all the time, you can afford to pay off some of your debts.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to refuse to accept something
examples: I offered to pay but he was having none of it.
They pretended to be enthusiastic about my work but then suddenly decided they wanted none of it.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to refuse to deal with somebody; to refuse to accept or consider something
examples: We in this party will have no truck with illegal organizations.
Dave wants no truck with change. For him, things are just fine as they are.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to take no interest in something because you do not care about it or it is too much trouble
examples: I've tried to ask her advice, but she doesn't want to know (= about my problems).
‘How much was it?’ ‘You don't want to know’ (= it is better if you don't know).

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to want to be free of somebody/something that has been annoying you or that you do not want
examples: Are you trying to say you want rid of me?

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if you never waste anything, especially food or money, you will always have it when you need it

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody in a rude or angry way why they are there or what they want you to doWord Origin
examples: Middle English: the noun from Old Norse vant, neuter of vanr ‘lacking’; the verb from Old Norse vanta ‘be lacking’. The original notion of “lack” was early extended to “need” and from this developed the sense ‘desire’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1

examples: PAST TENSE OF wear
the Second World War
the threat of (a) nuclear war
to win/lose a/the war
the war between England and Scotland
England's war with Scotland

How long have they been at war?
a war hero/veteran
More troops are being despatched to the war zone.
the theatre of war (= the area in which fighting takes place)

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a situation in which there is aggressive competition between groups, companies, countries, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO class war

They launched a trade war against France.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a fight or an effort over a long period of time to get rid of or stop something unpleasant
examples: The government has declared war on drug dealers.
Our two countries work together in fighting the war on terrorism.
We seem to be winning the war against crime.
a war against drug abuse

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: in some situations any type of behaviour is acceptable to get what you want

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to have been injured in a fight or an accident
examples: You look like you've been in the wars—who gave you that black eye?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: an attempt to defeat your opponents by putting pressure on them so that they lose courage or confidence
examples: The union has been fighting a war of nerves with the management over pay.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a bitter argument over a period of time between two or more people or groups
examples: the political war of words over tax

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a separate room or area in a hospital for people with the same type of medical condition
examples: a maternity/surgical/psychiatric/children’s ward
He worked as a nurse on the children's ward.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: (in the UK) one of the areas into which a city or town is divided and which elects and is represented by a member of the local council

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person, especially a child, who is under the legal protection of a court or another person (called a guardian)
examples: The child was made a ward of court.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a building where large quantities of goods are stored, especially before they are sent to shops to be sold
examples: Police are investigating a fire at a furniture warehouse.
He's a warehouse manager for an import company.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activity of fighting a war, especially using particular weapons or methods
examples: SEE ALSO biological warfare
air/naval/guerrilla warfare
countries engaged in warfare

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the activity of competing in an aggressive way with another group, company, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO class warfare
gang warfare
The debate soon degenerated into open warfare.
warfare between gangs

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody has almost guessed the answer to something or that they have almost found somebody/something that has been hidden
examples: Keep guessing—you're getting warmer.

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 1

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to take care of somebody/something for a short time
examples: Could you watch my bags for me while I buy a paper?
It's OK, I can watch the baby for a while.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to be careful about something
examples: Watch yourself! (= be careful, because you're in a dangerous situation)

Watch your head on the low ceiling.
I have to watch every penny (= be careful what I spend).
Hey, watch where you're going!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to pay attention to a situation so that you notice any changes
examples: We're watching the situation very carefully.
This election is being closely watched in the region.
The food retail sector is one to watch.
We'll watch for any developments.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to observe somebody's activities without their knowledge, especially over a period of time
examples: He didn't know he was being watched by the authorities.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to be careful about what you say in order not to upset or offend somebody
examples: Watch your language, young man!
The referee told the players to mind their language.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to walk carefully

definitions.label: Meaning 8

definitions.label: Meaning 9

examples: She'd better watch her back if she wants to hold onto the top job.

definitions.label: Meaning 10

examples: I can't tell you any more right now, but watch this space.

definitions.definition: to give reasons for not being in favour of something; to criticize something
examples: She immediately poured cold water on his plans to expand the business.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to try to settle an argument

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: a person who seems to be quiet or shy may surprise you by knowing a lot or having deep feelings

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: to find out what the situation is before doing something or making a decision

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: to keep yourself in the same place in deep water by moving your arms and legs

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: to make no progress while you are waiting for something to happen
examples: I decided to tread water until a better job came along.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: used to say that something, especially criticism, has no effect on somebody/something
examples: I can't tell my son what to do; it's water off a duck's back with him.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: when a pregnant woman’s waters break, the liquid in her womb passes out of her body just before the baby is born

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: you can give somebody the opportunity to do something, but you cannot force them to do it if they do not want toWord Origin
examples: Old English wæter (noun), wæterian (verb), of Germanic origin; related to Dutch water, German Wasser, from an Indo-European root shared by Russian voda (compare with vodka), also by Latin unda ‘wave’ and Greek hudōr ‘water’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a raised line of water that moves across the surface of the sea, ocean, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO tidal wave
Huge waves were breaking on the shore.
Surfers flocked to the beach to ride the waves.
the gentle sound of waves lapping
The wind made little waves on the pond.
Children were playing in the waves.
Seagulls bobbed on the waves.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the form that some types of energy such as heat, sound, light, etc. take as they move
examples: SEE ALSO airwaves
electromagnetic/gravity/ultrasonic waves

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a movement of your arm and hand from side to side
examples: She declined the offer with a wave of her hand.
With a wave and a shout he ran down the road to meet us.
He gave us a wave as the bus drove off.
She managed a wave to her disappointed supporters as she left.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a continuous movement that looks like a wave on the sea, made by a large group of people, especially people watching a sports game, when one person after another stands up, raises their arms, and then sits down again

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a sudden increase in a particular activity or feeling
examples: SEE ALSO brainwave
Insurgents launched a wave of attacks against the security forces.
Wave after wave of attacks rocked the city.
a wave of protests/strikes/scandals
a wave of violence/unrest
There has been a new wave of bombings since the peace talks broke down.
A wave of fear swept over him.
A wave of panic spread through the crowd.
Guilt and horror flooded her in waves.
Exhaustion hit him in a wave.
Three hundred employees lost their jobs in the latest wave of redundancies.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a large number of people or things suddenly moving or appearing somewhere
examples: SEE ALSO new wave
Wave after wave of aircraft passed overhead.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: if a person’s hair has a wave or waves, it is not straight but slightly curly
examples: SEE ALSO permanent wave

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the sea
examples: life on the waves (= life at sea)

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a situation in which somebody is very successful, happy, etc.
examples: They’ve been on the crest of the wave ever since their election victory.
She is on the crest of a wave at the moment following her Olympic success.
They are riding the crest of the wave at the moment.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to be very active in a way that makes people notice you, and that may sometimes cause problems

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to enjoy or be supported by the particular situation or quality mentioned
examples: Schools are riding a wave of renewed public interest.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a method, style or manner of doing something
examples: SEE ALSO third way
I prefer to do things the easy way.
I love him and I think he feels the same way.
I'm sure we can find a way to make this work.
Using the subway is the only way to avoid the traffic.
That's no way to speak to your mother!
I'm not happy with this way of working.
It's not what you say, it's the way that you say it.
I hate the way she always criticizes me.
I told you we should have done it my way!
She dresses in the same way as her sister.
Infectious diseases can be acquired in several ways.
In this way, we can track the storms as they move across the ocean.
It works in the way you'd expect.
New technology has radically changed the way in which this work is done.
She writes in a way that is easy to understand.
I generally get what I want one way or another (= by some means).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a particular manner or style of behaviour
examples: They grinned at her in a friendly way.
It was not his way to admit that he had made a mistake.
Don't worry, if she seems quiet—it's just her way.
He was showing off, as is the way with adolescent boys.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the typical way of behaving and living of a particular group of people
examples: After ten years I'm used to the strange British ways.
She always said that the old ways were the best.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a route or road that you take in order to reach a place
examples: to ask somebody the way
Do you know the way?
Can you tell me the way to Leicester Square?
the best/quickest/shortest way from A to B
We went the long way round.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the route along which somebody/something is moving; the route that somebody/something would take if there was nothing stopping them/it
examples: SEE ALSO right of way
Get out of my way! I'm in a hurry.
Riot police with shields were blocking the demonstrators' way.
Unfortunately they ran into a snowstorm along the way.
We fought our way through the dense vegetation.
We will eventually find a way out of the crisis.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a road, path or street for travelling along
examples: SEE ALSO freeway
There's a way across the fields.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used in the names of streets
examples: 106 Headley Way

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a particular direction; in a particular direction
examples: SEE ALSO each way
Which way did they go?
We just missed a car coming the other way.
Look both ways (= look left and right) before crossing the road.
Make sure that sign's the right way up.
The pipe could be moved a few inches either way.
Kids were running this way and that (= in all directions).
They decided to split the money four ways (= between four different people).
Which way (= for which party) are you going to vote?

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a means of going into or leaving a place, such as a door or gate
examples: SEE ALSO companionway
the way in/out
They escaped out the back way.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a distance or period of time between two points
examples: A little way up on the left is the Museum of Modern Art.
We had to go a long way before we found a place to eat.
September was a long way off.
You came all this way to see us?
The area's wine industry still has a way to go to full maturity.
We still have a ways to go.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: an area, a part of a country, etc.
examples: I think he lives somewhere over Greenwich way.
I'll stop by and see you next time I'm down your way.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: a particular aspect of something
examples: SYNONYM respect
I have changed in every way.
It's been quite a day, one way and another (= for several reasons).

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: a particular condition or state
examples: The economy's in a bad way.
I don't know how we're going to manage, the way things are.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: on the other side of the street, etc.
examples: Music blared from the open window of the house across the way.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: during the whole journey/period of time
examples: She didn't speak a word to me all the way back home.
the whole way to Arizona
This bus doesn't go all the way so you'll have to change.
I watched the movie the whole way through.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: completely; as much as it takes to achieve what you want
examples: I'm fighting him all the way.
You can feel that the audience is with her all the way.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: as you make progress with something
examples: You'll learn something along the way.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: used to say that things often happen in a particular way, especially when it is not convenient

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: however you choose to look at a situation

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: to behave or do things in a particular manner because it is part of your character
examples: It's not his fault he's so pompous—he was born that way.

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: to be easy compared with what came before
examples: It's all downhill from here. We'll soon be finished.

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: to become worse or less successful
examples: It's been all downhill for his career since then, with four defeats in five games.
I started work as a journalist and it was downhill all the way for my health.

definitions.label: Meaning 23
definitions.definition: to be easy compared with what came before
examples: It's downhill all the way from here. We'll soon be finished.

definitions.label: Meaning 24
definitions.definition: to become worse or less successful
examples: I started work as a journalist and it was downhill all the way for my health.
It's been all downhill for his career since then, with four defeats in five games.

definitions.label: Meaning 25
definitions.definition: to have habits or opinions that you have had for a long time and that you do not want to change
examples: Grandma is so set in her ways.

definitions.label: Meaning 26
definitions.definition: to have nearly achieved something and be going to achieve it soon
examples: She is well on the way to recovery.
He is well on the way to establishing himself among the top ten players in the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 27
definitions.definition: by a great amount
examples: He was the best by a long way.

definitions.label: Meaning 28
definitions.definition: used to introduce a comment or question that is not directly related to what you have been talking about
examples: By the way, I found that book you were looking for.
What's the time, by the way?
Oh by the way, if you see Jackie, tell her I'll call her this evening.

definitions.label: Meaning 29
definitions.definition: by a route that includes the place mentioned
examples: SYNONYM via
The artist recently arrived in Paris from Bulgaria by way of Vienna.
She came to TV by way of drama school.

definitions.label: Meaning 30
definitions.definition: as a form of something; for something; as a means of something
examples: He received £600 by way of compensation from the company.
She rolled her eyes by way of an answer and left.

definitions.label: Meaning 31
definitions.definition: to start to live or behave in a different way from before
examples: He was in trouble with the police as a teenager but now he’s completely changed his ways.
Your father is unlikely to change his ways now.

definitions.label: Meaning 32
definitions.definition: to gradually achieve something or move somewhere by being determined and using a lot of effort
examples: She clawed her way to the top of her profession.
Slowly, he clawed his way out from under the collapsed building.

definitions.label: Meaning 33
definitions.definition: to remove things that are stopping the progress or movement of something
examples: The ruling could clear the way for extradition proceedings.

definitions.label: Meaning 34
definitions.definition: to happen to you by chance, or when you were not expecting it
examples: He took the first job that came his way.
Have any interesting articles come your way recently?

definitions.label: Meaning 35
definitions.definition: to have two opposite effects or results

definitions.label: Meaning 36
definitions.definition: used to say that it does not matter which one of two possibilities happens, is chosen or is true
examples: Was it his fault or not? Either way, an explanation is due.
We could meet today or tomorrow—I don't mind one way or the other.

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: in all directions
examples: Her hair tumbled every which way.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: to move along carefully, for example when it is dark, by touching walls, objects, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: to be careful about how you do things, usually because you are in a situation that you are not familiar with
examples: She was new in the job, still feeling her way.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: to discover the right route (to a place)
examples: I hope you can find your way home.

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: to come to a place or a situation by chance or without intending to
examples: He eventually found his way into acting.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: to become used to doing something/to lose the habit of doing something
examples: The women had got into the way of going up on the deck every evening.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: to prevent somebody from doing something; to prevent something from happening
examples: He wouldn't allow emotions to get in the way of him doing his job.

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: to get or do what you want, especially when somebody has tried to stop you
examples: She always gets her own way in the end.

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: to break or fall down
examples: The pillars gave way and a section of the roof collapsed.
Her numb leg gave way beneath her and she stumbled clumsily.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: to stop resisting somebody/something; to agree to do something that you do not want to do
examples: He refused to give way on any of the points.

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: to allow somebody/something to be or go first
examples: Give way to traffic already on the roundabout.

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: to allow yourself to be very strongly affected by something, especially an emotion
examples: Flinging herself on the bed, she gave way to helpless misery.

definitions.label: Meaning 49
definitions.definition: to be replaced by something
examples: The storm gave way to bright sunshine.
As he drew nearer, his anxiety gave way to relief.

definitions.label: Meaning 50
definitions.definition: to have full sexual intercourse with somebody

definitions.label: Meaning 51
definitions.definition: to have known each other for a long time
examples: We go back a long way, he and I.

definitions.label: Meaning 52
definitions.definition: to last a long time
examples: She seems to make her money go a long way.
A small amount of this paint goes a long way (= covers a large area).
I find that a little of Jerry's company can go a long way (= I quickly get tired of being with him).

definitions.label: Meaning 53
definitions.definition: to help very much/a little in achieving something
examples: The new law goes a long way towards solving the problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 54
definitions.definition: to make a special effort to do something
examples: He would always go out of his way to be friendly towards her.
She went out of her way to help them.

definitions.label: Meaning 55
definitions.definition: to do as you choose, especially when somebody has advised you against it
examples: It's best to let her go her own way if you don't want a fight.
He's always gone his own way when it comes to design.

definitions.label: Meaning 56
definitions.definition: to end a relationship with somebody
examples: When the business was sold they went their separate ways.
They decided to go their separate ways after being together for five years.
When we finished school, we all went our separate ways.

definitions.label: Meaning 57
definitions.definition: to go in a different direction from somebody you have been travelling with

definitions.label: Meaning 58
definitions.definition: to travel in the same direction as somebody
examples: I'm going your way—I'll walk with you.

definitions.label: Meaning 59
definitions.definition: to go well for you; to be in your favour
examples: By the third round he knew the fight was going his way.

definitions.label: Meaning 60
definitions.definition: to die

definitions.label: Meaning 61
definitions.definition: by having an unpleasant experience or by making mistakes
examples: She won't listen to my advice so she'll just have to learn the hard way.
He learned about the dangers of drugs the hard way.

definitions.label: Meaning 62
definitions.definition: to have made a lot of progress
examples: We've come a long way since the early days of the project.
The study of genes has come a long way in recent years.

definitions.label: Meaning 63
definitions.definition: to be a sensible person

definitions.label: Meaning 64
definitions.definition: to have or want to have the advantages of two different situations or ways of behaving that are impossible to combine
examples: You can't have it both ways. If you can afford to go out all the time, you can afford to pay off some of your debts.

definitions.label: Meaning 65
definitions.definition: used to say in an angry way that although you are not happy about something that somebody has said, you are not going to argue
examples: Oh OK, then. Have it your own way!

definitions.label: Meaning 66
definitions.definition: to have something arranged in the way that you want, even though other people want it to be arranged differently
examples: The German team weren't going to let the English have everything their own way.

definitions.label: Meaning 67
definitions.definition: to need to make a lot of progress before you can achieve something
examples: She still has a long way to go before she's fully fit.

definitions.label: Meaning 68
definitions.definition: used to say that something often happens in a particular way, especially when it is out of your control
examples: First love affairs have a way of not working out.
Fate has a way of changing the best of plans.

definitions.label: Meaning 69
definitions.definition: to be good at dealing with somebody/something
examples: He has a way with small children.
She has a way with words (= is very good at expressing herself).

definitions.label: Meaning 70
definitions.definition: to persuade somebody to have sex with you

definitions.label: Meaning 71
definitions.definition: used to explain what you would do if you had total control over something
examples: If I had my way, smoking would be banned completely.

definitions.label: Meaning 72
definitions.definition: of any type
examples: I don't approve of violence in any shape or form.
I can't stand insects in any shape or form.
I do not condone bullying in any way, shape or form.

definitions.label: Meaning 73
definitions.definition: on a large/small scale
examples: The new delivery service has taken off in a big way.
Many people are investing in a small way in the stock market.
He then started spending money in a big way.

definitions.label: Meaning 74
definitions.definition: (to be/become) pregnant

definitions.label: Meaning 75
definitions.definition: used to show that a statement has more than one meaning
examples: With the first goal he used his head in more ways than one.

definitions.label: Meaning 76
definitions.definition: used to say what normally happens in a particular situation
examples: In the ordinary way, she's not a nervous person.

definitions.label: Meaning 77
definitions.definition: how and when you want to, even though this might annoy other people
examples: He always does the work, but in his own sweet time.
She just ignores all the criticism and continues on her own sweet way.

definitions.label: Meaning 78
definitions.definition: to some extent; not completely
examples: In a way it was one of our biggest mistakes.

definitions.label: Meaning 79
definitions.definition: in a manner that is appropriate to or typical of a person or thing but that may seem unusual to other people
examples: I expect she does love you in her own way.
The building is very attractive in its own way.
He was attractive in his own way.

definitions.label: Meaning 80
definitions.definition: stopping somebody from moving or doing something
examples: You'll have to move—you're in my way.
I left them alone, as I felt I was in the way.
There were several rocks in the way.

definitions.label: Meaning 81
definitions.definition: used in questions and negative sentences to talk about the types of something that are available
examples: There isn't much in the way of entertainment in this place.

definitions.label: Meaning 82
definitions.definition: to avoid somebody
examples: Let's keep out of her way while she's in such a bad mood.

definitions.label: Meaning 83
definitions.definition: to be familiar with a place, subject, etc.

definitions.label: Meaning 84
definitions.definition: to make a lot of money easily and feel very pleased about it

definitions.label: Meaning 85
definitions.definition: to get yourself into or out of a situation by lying

definitions.label: Meaning 86
definitions.definition: to deliberately avoid seeing somebody/something
examples: Prison officers know what's going on, but look the other way.

definitions.label: Meaning 87
definitions.definition: to become lost
examples: We lost our way in the dark.
She lost her way in the fog.

definitions.label: Meaning 88
definitions.definition: to forget or move away from the purpose or reason for something
examples: I feel that the project has lost its way.
This project seems to have lost its way.

definitions.label: Meaning 89
definitions.definition: to allow somebody/something to pass; to allow somebody/something to take the place of somebody/something
examples: Make way for the Lord Mayor!
Tropical forest is felled to make way for grassland.

definitions.label: Meaning 90
definitions.definition: to move or get somewhere; to make progress
examples: Will you be able to make your own way to the airport (= get there without help, a ride, etc.)?
Is this your plan for making your way in the world?

definitions.label: Meaning 91
definitions.definition: to stop behaving badly

definitions.label: Meaning 92
definitions.definition: (to take/find) an acceptable course of action that avoids two extreme positions

definitions.label: Meaning 93
definitions.definition: used to show that you are certain about something
examples: It was the wrong decision—there are no two ways about it.

definitions.label: Meaning 94
definitions.definition: used to say that there is no possibility that you will do something or that something will happen
examples: ‘Do you want to help?’ ‘No way!’
No way am I going to drive them there.
There's no way we could afford that sort of money.

definitions.label: Meaning 95
definitions.definition: during the journey
examples: He stopped for breakfast on the way.
She grabbed her camera and bag on her way out.

definitions.label: Meaning 96
definitions.definition: going or coming
examples: I'd better be on my way (= I must leave) soon.
The letter should be on its way to you.
Then he went off on his merry way.

definitions.label: Meaning 97
definitions.definition: not yet born
examples: They've got three kids and one on the way.

definitions.label: Meaning 98
definitions.definition: to make it possible for somebody to do something or for something to happen
examples: The agreement could open the way for the country to pay off its debts.

definitions.label: Meaning 99
definitions.definition: in the opposite position, direction or order
examples: I think it should go on the other way round.

definitions.label: Meaning 100
definitions.definition: the opposite situation
examples: I didn't leave you. It was the other way round (= you left me).

definitions.label: Meaning 101
definitions.definition: in a safe place where somebody/something cannot be hurt or injured or do any damage to somebody/something
examples: She put the knife in a drawer, out of harm’s way.
I prefer the children to play in the garden where they’re out of harm’s way.

definitions.label: Meaning 102
definitions.definition: no longer stopping somebody from moving or doing something
examples: I moved my legs out of the way so that she could get past.
I didn't say anything until Dad was out of the way.

definitions.label: Meaning 103
definitions.definition: finished; dealt with
examples: Our region is poised for growth once the election is out of the way.

definitions.label: Meaning 104
definitions.definition: used in negative sentences to mean ‘unusual’
examples: She had obviously noticed nothing out of the way.

definitions.label: Meaning 105
definitions.definition: not on the route that you planned to take
examples: I'd love a ride home—if it's not out of your way.

definitions.label: Meaning 106
definitions.definition: a point at which two people or groups of people decide to separate
examples: These events led to a final parting of the ways.

definitions.label: Meaning 107
definitions.definition: to create a situation in which somebody will be able to do something or something can happen
examples: This decision paved the way for changes in employment rights for women.

definitions.label: Meaning 108
definitions.definition: to make enough money to pay what it costs to keep it going
examples: The bridge is still not paying its way.

definitions.label: Meaning 109
definitions.definition: to pay for everything yourself without having to rely on anyone else’s money

definitions.label: Meaning 110
definitions.definition: to walk carefully, choosing the safest, driest, etc. place to put your feet
examples: She picked her way delicately over the rough ground.
We picked our way carefully over the jagged rocks.

definitions.label: Meaning 111
definitions.definition: to make somebody annoyed or angry, often without intending to, by doing or saying something that offends them
examples: She tends to rub people up the wrong way.

definitions.label: Meaning 112
definitions.definition: to realize or admit that you have done something wrong and decide to change your behaviour
examples: Will they realize the error of their ways before it is too late?

definitions.label: Meaning 113
definitions.definition: to find that it is possible or convenient to do something
examples: Small builders cannot see their way clear to take on many trainees.

definitions.label: Meaning 114
definitions.definition: to get an idea of what is likely to happen before deciding what to do

definitions.label: Meaning 115
definitions.definition: to do something first so that other people can follow

definitions.label: Meaning 116
definitions.definition: to make it easier for somebody/something to develop or make progress
examples: These negotiations are intended to smooth the path to a peace treaty.
We’re trying to smooth the way for women who want to resume their careers.

definitions.label: Meaning 117
definitions.definition: to (not) prevent somebody from doing something
examples: If you believe you can make her happy, I won't stand in your way.
He wanted to go to college and would let nothing stand in his way.

definitions.label: Meaning 118
definitions.definition: to be bisexual (= sexually attracted to both men and women)

definitions.label: Meaning 119
definitions.definition: to end a difficult situation by choosing the simplest solution even if it is not the best one
examples: He took the easy way out and didn’t go to the meeting.
