Who are you to tell me I can't park here?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the person or people who; any person who
examples: Whoever says that is a liar.
Send it to whoever is in charge of sales.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that it does not matter who, since the result will be the same
examples: Come out of there, whoever you are.
I don't want to see them, whoever they are.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used in questions to mean ‘who’, expressing surprise
examples: Whoever heard of such a thing!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: full; complete
examples: Let's forget the whole thing.
Jenna was my best friend in the whole world.
It seems I've spent my whole life travelling.
The whole family will be there.
But that's not the whole story, is it?
He spent the whole day writing.
We drank a whole bottle each.
I went through the whole process with them.
My whole body ached.
The whole country (= all the people in it) mourned her death.
The school is keen to involve the whole community in this project.
She wasn't telling the whole truth.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how large or important something is
examples: I'm going to be talking about a whole range of things today.
We are going to have a whole bunch of people over tomorrow night.
I can't afford it—that's the whole point.
We offer a whole variety of weekend breaks.
I think the whole idea is ridiculous.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: not broken or damaged
examples: SYNONYM (all) in one piece
Owls usually swallow their prey whole (= without biting it into small pieces).
Peel the small onions, but leave them whole.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very much; a lot
examples: I'm feeling a whole lot better.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a large number or amount
examples: There were a whole lot of people I didn't know.
I lost a whole lot of money.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: everything; all of something
examples: I've sold the whole lot.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: a completely different thing
examples: Now that's a whole 'nother question.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to give more information about a person or thing

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used in questions to ask the reason for or purpose of something
examples: Why were you late?
Tell me why you did it.
‘I would like you to go.’ ‘Why me?’
Why oh why do people keep leaving the door open?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used in questions to suggest that it is not necessary to do something
examples: Why get upset just because you got one bad grade?
Why bother to write? We'll see him tomorrow.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to give or talk about a reason
examples: That's why I left so early.
I know you did it—I just want to know why.
The reason why the injection needs repeating every year is that the virus changes.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used in questions to mean ‘why’, expressing surprise
examples: Why ever didn't you tell us before?

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to make or agree to a suggestion
examples: Why not write to her?
‘Let's eat out.’ ‘Why not?’
Why don't we go together?

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: measuring a large distance from one side to the other
examples: OPPOSITE narrow
It's a wide, fast-flowing river.
The river gets quite wide here.
He wore a jacket with wide lapels.
Her face broke into a wide grin.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: measuring a particular distance from one side to the other
examples: How wide is that stream?
It's about 2 metres wide.
The road was just wide enough for two vehicles to pass.
The road was only wide enough for only one vehicle at a time.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: including a large number or variety of different people or things; covering a large area
examples: a wide range/choice/variety/selection of goods
The company offers a wide array of services to businesses.
Her music appeals to a wide audience.
It's the best job in the whole wide world.
Experts believe the project could bring positive benefits to the wider community.
The contributors to this volume represent a wide spectrum of opinion on the subject.
Publication on the internet makes the material accessible to a wider public for the first time.
He is a manager with a wide experience of industry.
Jenny has a wide circle of friends.
The incident has received wide coverage in the press.
The festival attracts people from a wide area.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: very big
examples: The Australians won by a wide margin.
There are wide variations in prices.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: general; not only looking at details
examples: the wider aims of the project
We are talking about education in its widest sense.
You can't just look at it in terms of the immediate problem. You've got to see it in a wider context.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: fully open
examples: She stared at him with wide eyes.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: far from the point aimed at
examples: Her shot was wide (of the target).
Her shot fell just wide of the target.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: happening or existing in the whole of a country, etc.
examples: a nationwide search
We need to act on a Europe-wide scale.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to not go too near somebody/something; to avoid somebody/something
examples: He gave the dog a wide berth.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: not accurate
examples: Their predictions turned out to be wide of the mark.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: by a lot of people; in or to many places
examples: The term is widely used in everyday speech.
The idea is now widely accepted.
There is still no word on when the service will become widely available.
The film is widely regarded as a masterpiece.
The company is widely acknowledged as a leader in the field.
He is widely recognized as the founder of modern anatomy.
Her remarks were widely reported in the media.
a widely held belief
The 2012 Olympic Games were widely considered a success.
He was not widely known outside China.
the most widely distributed species of lizards in North America
The ruling party was widely expected to win the elections.
It is widely believed that the bank may move its headquarters to Frankfurt.
a widely publicized murder case
The president was widely criticized for his response to the disaster.
He has travelled widely in Asia.
Her books are widely read (= a lot of people read them).
He's an educated, widely read man (= he has read a lot of books).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to a large degree; a lot
examples: Standards vary widely.
The two men have widely different views on the question.
There are widely divergent opinions about who is responsible.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to become wider; to make something wider
examples: Her eyes widened in surprise.
Jasmine's eyes widened with disbelief.
Here the stream widens into a river.
The road gradually widens out.
They may have to widen the road to cope with the increase in traffic.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to become larger in degree or range; to make something larger in degree or range
examples: Another concern is the widening gap between rich and poor.
We plan to widen the scope of our existing activities by offering more language courses.
The legislation will be widened to include all firearms.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to consider or include a larger range of options or possibilities, especially when searching for something
examples: It's time to widen the net in the search for a suitable candidate.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: existing or happening over a large area or among many people
examples: The storm caused widespread damage.
The plan received widespread support throughout the country.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a woman whose husband or wife has died and who has not married again
examples: SEE ALSO black widow
She gets a widow’s pension.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the measurement from one side of something to the other; how wide something is
examples: The terrace runs the full width of the house.
It's about ten metres in width.
The carpet is available in different widths.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a piece of material of a particular width
examples: You'll need two widths of fabric for each curtain.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the distance between the two long sides of a swimming pool
examples: How many widths can you swim?

definitions.label: Meaning 1

the wife of the Italian ambassador

his former/future wife

At that time there was an increase in the number of working wives.

definitions.label: Meaning 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

examples: wild animals/birds/flowers

wild mushrooms/rice

a wild boar

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: in its natural state; not changed by people
examples: the destruction of forests and other wild lands
wild moorland

definitions.label: Meaning 3

definitions.label: Meaning 4

definitions.label: Meaning 6

definitions.label: Meaning 7

definitions.label: Meaning 8

examples: SYNONYM stormy

definitions.label: Meaning 9

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to say that something has happened in a way that somebody did not expect at all
examples: Never in my wildest dreams did I think I'd meet him again.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to grow or develop freely without any control
examples: The ivy has run wild.

I just let my imagination run wild and come up with as many ideas as I can.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: if children or animals run wild, they behave as they like because nobody is controlling them
examples: Those boys have been allowed to run wild.
They annoy the neighbours because they let their children run wild.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to go through a period of wild behaviour while young, especially having a lot of romantic or sexual relationships
examples: He wants to leave home, sow his wild oats and learn about life.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to say that nothing would persuade somebody to go somewhere or do something they do not want to doWord Origin
examples: Old English wilde, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch and German wild.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: animals, birds, insects, etc. that are wild and live in a natural environment
examples: policies designed to protect wildlife

a wildlife habitat
a wildlife refuge/sanctuary

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to want or like
examples: Call it what you will, it's still a problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to want or like
examples: Call it what you will, it's still a problem.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not objecting to doing something; having no reason for not doing something

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: ready or pleased to help and not needing to be persuaded; done or given in an enthusiastic way
examples: OPPOSITE unwilling
a willing participant/accomplice
a willing buyer/seller
She's very willing.
willing helpers/volunteers
her willing acceptance of the responsibility
their willing participation in the plan

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to show that you are ready to help, work hard, etc. if necessary

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: you intend to do good things but you are too lazy, weak or busy to actually do them

definitions.definition: the quality of being happy and ready to do something
examples: Success in studying depends on a willingness to learn.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to be the most successful in a competition, race, battle, etc.
examples: Which team won?
to win an election
to win a game/race/war/battle
She loves to win an argument.
to win at cards/chess
France won by six goals to two against Denmark.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to get something as the result of a competition, race, election, etc.
examples: PAST TENSE, PAST PARTICIPLE OF win
Britain won five gold medals.
He won £3 000 in the lottery.
How many states did the Republicans win?
Everyone who takes part wins a small prize.
to win an award/a title
The Conservatives won the seat from Labour in the last election.
You've won yourself a trip to New York.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to achieve or get something that you want, especially by your own efforts
examples: They are trying to win support for their proposals.
The company has won a contract to supply books and materials to schools.
She won the admiration of many people in her battle against cancer.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to be successful against somebody/something
examples: Despite strong opposition, the ruling party carried the day.
Teamwork and persistence can still win the day.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to win something very easily

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to make somebody love you

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: whether you succeed or fail
examples: Win or lose, we'll know we've done our best.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to become famous or successful

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to express sympathy for somebody who has been disappointed about something

to open/close the window

definitions.label: Meaning 5

definitions.label: Meaning 37
definitions.definition: to talk about how the world could be changed to be a better place
examples: We stayed up all night, setting the world to rights.

definitions.label: Meaning 38
definitions.definition: a state in which things are strange, mysterious or secret; a state that exists on the dividing line between two things
examples: the twilight world of the occult
The dissidents lived in a twilight world of hushed voices and secret meetings.
the twilight zone between living and merely existing
They lived in the twilight zone on the fringes of society.

definitions.label: Meaning 39
definitions.definition: to relax and watch people in a public place
examples: We sat outside a cafe, watching the world go by.
I love just watching the world go by.

definitions.label: Meaning 40
definitions.definition: the way that most people behave; the way that things happen, which you cannot change
examples: The rich and powerful make the decisions—that's the way of the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 41
definitions.definition: used to express dislike, surprise or shock, especially at changes in people’s attitudes or behaviour
examples: When I listen to the news these days, I sometimes wonder what the world is coming to.

definitions.label: Meaning 42
definitions.definition: used to say that you cannot do something, even though you really want to
examples: With the best will in the world I could not describe him as a good father.

definitions.label: Meaning 43
definitions.definition: everyone; a large number of people

definitions.label: Meaning 44
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how different two things are
examples: His new luxury mansion was a world away from the tiny house where he was born.

definitions.label: Meaning 45
definitions.definition: there is no limit to the opportunities open to you
examples: With talent like that, the world is her oyster.

definitions.label: Meaning 46
definitions.definition: used to emphasize how much difference there is between two things
examples: There's a world of difference between liking someone and loving them.

definitions.label: Meaning 47
definitions.definition: everywhere in the world
examples: People are basically the same the world over.
Scientists the world over have been waiting for this breakthrough.

definitions.label: Meaning 48
definitions.definition: a situation in which you have all the possible disadvantages at the same timeWord Origin
examples: Old English w(e)oruld, from a Germanic compound meaning ‘age of man’; related to Dutch wereld and German Welt.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: affecting all parts of the world
examples: an increase in worldwide sales
The show has a worldwide audience of 115 million viewers.
a worldwide terrorist network
The story has attracted worldwide attention.
a worldwide shortage of qualified engineers
The company employs 28 000 people worldwide.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a long, thin creature with a soft body and no bones or legs
examples: SEE ALSO earthworm
birds looking for worms
Worms burrow down through the soil.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: long, thin creatures that live inside the bodies of humans or animals and can cause illness
examples: SEE ALSO hookworm
The dog has worms.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the young form of an insect when it looks like a short worm
examples: SEE ALSO glow-worm
This apple is full of worms.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a computer program that is a type of virus and that spreads across a network by copying itself

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a person you do not like or respect, especially because they have a weak character and do not behave well towards other people

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: if you open up a can of worms, you start doing something that will cause a lot of problems and be very difficult

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: the person who takes the opportunity to do something before other people will have an advantage over them

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: a person who is normally quiet and does not complain will protest when the situation becomes too hard to bearWord Origin
examples: Old English wyrm (noun), of Germanic origin; related to Latin vermis ‘worm’ and Greek rhomox ‘woodworm’.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: thinking about unpleasant things that have happened or that might happen and therefore feeling unhappy and afraid
examples: Don't look so worried!
I'm not worried about her—she can take care of herself.
Doctors are worried about the possible spread of the disease.
People are really worried about losing their jobs.
He is extremely worried for her safety.
I was worried for my family.
We're not too worried by these results.
The police are worried that the man may be armed.
I was worried you wouldn't come.
Where have you been? I've been worried sick (= extremely worried).
Try not to get worried.
His worried parents were waiting for him when he got home.
She gave me a worried look.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to tell somebody that you were worried because you had not understood what they had said correctly
examples: You had me worried for a moment—I thought you were going to resign!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to keep thinking about unpleasant things that might happen or about problems that you have
examples: Don't worry. We have plenty of time.
Stop worrying, Dad—it'll be fine.
Don't worry about me. I'll be all right.
He's always worrying about his weight.
Never mind—it's nothing to worry about.
That's not something you need to worry about.
You can stay here tonight, so you don't have to worry about walking home in the dark.
There's no point in worrying over things you can't change.
She's my sister, and I worry for her safety.
She began to worry for her friend.
I worry that I won't get into college.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to make somebody/yourself anxious about somebody/something
examples: What worries me is how I am going to get another job.
That prospect worried investors.
Don't worry yourself about it—I'll deal with it.
He's worried himself sick (= become extremely anxious) about his daughter.
Where have you been? I've been worrying myself silly (= been extremely anxious) all evening.
It worries me that he hasn't come home yet.
It worried me to think what might happen.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to annoy or upset somebody
examples: SYNONYM disturb
The noise never seems to worry her.
Don't keep worrying him with a lot of silly questions.
I didn't want to worry you with all the details.
Don't worry the driver with unnecessary requests.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to attack animals, especially sheep, by running after and/or biting them

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: it is not important; it does not matter
examples: Not to worry—I can soon fix it.
Not to worry—no harm done.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: of poorer quality or lower standard; more unpleasant
examples: The rooms were awful and the food was worse.
The weather got worse during the day.
I've been to far worse places.
The film was no worse than many others he made in the 1930s.
The interview was much worse than he had expected.
The area seemed almost worse than the city he had left.
There's nothing worse than going out in the cold with wet hair.
It's much worse for the parents than it is for the child.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: more serious or severe
examples: They were trying to prevent an even worse tragedy.
The crisis was getting worse and worse.
Don't tell her that—you'll only make things worse.
Could things get any worse?
Never mind—it could be worse (= although the situation is bad, it is not as bad as it might have been).
The situation was worse than he had imagined.
It's not just the government's poor ratings in the opinion polls. It's worse than that.
Killing someone is considered morally worse than letting them die.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: more ill or unhappy
examples: If he gets any worse, we'll call the doctor.
He told her she'd let them down and she felt worse than ever.
She seems worse than she was yesterday.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to say that somebody is not really as angry or as aggressive as they sound

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to lose a fight, competition, etc. or suffer more compared with others

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a terrible thing that could happen
examples: At the last minute the hero saves her from a fate worse than death.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to get even worse

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to show that you are disappointed about something
examples: I shall have to miss the party, worse luck!

definitions.definition: the practice of showing respect for God or a god, by saying prayers, singing with others, etc.; a ceremony for this
examples: an act/a place of worship
morning/evening worship (= a church service in the morning/evening)
The tradition of ancestor worship stretches back thousands of years.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a strong feeling of love and respect for somebody/something
examples: SYNONYM adoration
What she feels for him is akin to worship.

definitions.definition: a polite way of addressing or referring to a magistrate or mayorWord Origin

It's not the worst idea I've ever heard.
What's the worst thing that could happen?
What she said confirmed my worst fears (= proved they were right).
This is every parent's worst nightmare.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to be the cause of your own problems
examples: Her indecisiveness makes her her own worst enemy.
Some dancers become their own worst enemies, criticizing themselves for every imperfection.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having a value in money, etc.
examples: Our house is worth about £100 000.
How much is this painting worth?
to be worth a bomb/packet/fortune (= a lot of money)
It isn't worth much.
If you answer this question correctly, it's worth five points.
This order is potentially worth millions of pounds to the company.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to recommend the action mentioned because you think it may be useful, pleasant, etc.
examples: The museum is certainly worth a visit.
This idea is well worth considering.
It's so unimportant it's hardly worth mentioning.
It's worth making an appointment before you go.
It's always worth paying the extra £3 for next-day delivery.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: important, good or pleasant enough to make somebody feel satisfied, especially when difficulty or effort is involved
examples: SEE ALSO worthwhile
Was it worth the effort?
The new house really wasn't worth all the expense involved.
The job involves a lot of hard work but it's worth it.
The trip was expensive but it was worth every penny.
The film is definitely worth seeing.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: having money and possessions of a particular value
examples: He's worth £10 million.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: it is better to keep something that you already have than to risk losing it by trying to get much more

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: with great energy, effort and purpose
examples: He was rowing for all he was worth.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in order to get as much as you can from somebody/something
examples: She is milking her success for all it's worth.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that what you are saying is only your own opinion or suggestion and may not be very helpful
examples: I prefer this colour, for what it's worth.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: not worth doing because it is against the rules or because it might cause you to lose your job
examples: SEE ALSO jobsworth
It's more than my job's worth to let you in without a ticket.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: the advantages to be gained from doing something are not great enough, considering the effort or cost involved
examples: If the price goes up again, he may decide that the game’s not worth the candle.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: having no value, especially legally, or because one of the people involved has no intention of doing what they said they would

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: deserving respect, especially because you do your job well
examples: Any teacher worth her salt knows that.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: very useful or valuable
examples: A good mechanic is worth his weight in gold.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: interesting or useful for somebody to do
examples: It will be worth your while to come to the meeting.
He'll do the job if you make it worth his while (= pay him well).

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: important, pleasant, interesting, etc.; worth spending time, money or effort on
examples: It was in aid of a worthwhile cause (= a charity, etc.)
a worthwhile discussion/job
The smile on her face made it all worthwhile.
We all felt we had done something worthwhile for the local community.
High prices in the UK make it worthwhile for buyers to look abroad.
It is worthwhile to include really high-quality illustrations.
It didn't seem worthwhile writing it all out again.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having the qualities that deserve somebody/something
examples: OPPOSITE unworthy
Very few of his ideas are worthy of further attention.
A number of the report's findings are worthy of note.
No composer was considered worthy of the name until he had written an opera.
a worthy champion (= one who deserved to win)
He felt he was not worthy of her.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: having qualities that deserve your respect or attention
examples: SYNONYM deserving
The money we raise will be going to a very worthy cause.
a worthy member of the team
We thought it was a worthy enough objective.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: having good qualities but not very interesting or exciting
examples: her worthy but dull husband
He's a very worthy man, I suppose, but he's very dull.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: typical of what a particular person or thing might do, give, etc.
examples: He gave a speech that was worthy of Martin Luther King.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: deserving, or suitable for, the thing mentioned
examples: trustworthy
roadworthy

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used in polite offers or invitations
examples: Would you like a sandwich?
Would you have dinner with me on Friday?

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say what you like, love, hate, etc.
examples: I'd love a coffee.
I'd be only too glad to help.
I'd hate you to think I was criticizing you.
I'd rather come with you.
I'd rather you came with us.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used as the past form of will when reporting what somebody has said or thought
examples: He said he would be here at eight o'clock (= His words were: ‘I will be there at eight o'clock.’).
She asked if I would help.
They told me that they probably wouldn't come.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used for talking about the result of an event that you imagine
examples: She'd look better with shorter hair.
If you went to see him, he would be delighted.
Hurry up! It would be a shame to miss the beginning of the play.
She'd be a fool to accept it (= if she accepted).

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used for describing a possible action or event that did not in fact happen, because something else did not happen first
examples: If I had seen the advertisement in time, I would have applied for the job.
They would never have met if she hadn't gone to Emma's party.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used for saying why somebody does something
examples: She burned the letters so that her husband would never read them.
He worked hard in order that he would pass all his exams.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used for saying what you want to happen
examples: I wish that you'd be quiet for a minute.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to show that somebody/something was not willing or refused to do something
examples: She wouldn't change it, even though she knew it was wrong.
My car wouldn't start this morning.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to ask somebody politely to do something
examples: Would you mind leaving us alone for a few minutes?
Would you open the door for me, please?

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to give opinions that you are not certain about
examples: I would imagine the job will take about two days.
I'd say he was about fifty.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to give advice
examples: I wouldn't have any more to drink, if I were you.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used for talking about things that often happened in the past
examples: SYNONYM used to
When my parents were away, my grandmother would take care of me.
He'd always be the first to offer to help.

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used for talking about behaviour that you think is typical
examples: ‘She said it was your fault.’ ‘Well, she would say that, wouldn't she? She's never liked me.’

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used to express a strong wish
examples: Would that he had lived to see it.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to show that you are very surprised or impressed by somebody/something
examples: Wow! You look terrific!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to cover something completely in paper or other material, for example when you are giving it as a present
examples: SEE ALSO gift-wrap
He spent the evening wrapping up the Christmas presents.
individually wrapped chocolates
Each apple was wrapped in paper.
The cheese is cut and wrapped in plastic.
fish and chips wrapped up in newspaper

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to cover something/somebody in material, for example in order to protect it/them
examples: SEE ALSO shrink-wrapped
Wrap the meat in foil before you cook it.
I wrapped the baby up in a blanket.
He tossed her a towel. ‘Wrap yourself in that.’
She wrapped herself up in a long shawl.
I wrapped a blanket around the baby.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to put something around something/somebody
examples: A scarf was wrapped around his neck.
The nurse wrapped a bandage tightly around my ankle.
His arms were wrapped around her waist.
He wrapped his arms tightly around her waist.
He wrapped his hands around my neck and tried to strangle me.
She's got a towel wrapped around her head.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to cause a word or text to be carried over to a new line as the end of the previous line is reached by the writer; to be carried over in this way
examples: How can I wrap the text around?
The text wraps around if it is too long to fit the screen.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to be so involved with somebody/something that you do not pay enough attention to other people or things
examples: SYNONYM absorbed
They are completely wrapped up in their children.
She was so wrapped up in her work that she didn’t realize how late it was.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to persuade somebody to do anything that you want
examples: She has always been able to wrap her parents around her little finger.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the joint between the hand and the arm
examples: She's broken her wrist.
He wore a copper bracelet on his wrist.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a warning or mild punishment
examples: We're hoping that she gets off with a slap on the wrist from the judge.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to make letters or numbers on a surface, especially using a pen or a pencil
examples: In some countries children don't start learning to read and write until they are six.
Please write in pen on both sides of the paper.
I haven't got anything to write with.
Write your name at the top of the paper.
The teacher wrote the answers on the board.
The ‘b’ had been wrongly written as a ‘d’.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: to produce something in written form so that people can read, perform or use it, etc.
examples: to write a novel/song/computer program
to write an article/essay
Who was ‘The Grapes of Wrath’ written by?
Which opera did Verdi write first?
He hopes to write a book about his experiences one day.
She had to write a report on the project.
The text is very well written.
The play was originally written for British television.
I wanted to travel and then write about it.
He writes for the ‘New Yorker’ (= works as a writer).
No decision has been made at the time of writing.
She wrote him several poems.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: to put information, a message of good wishes, etc. in a letter or an email and send it to somebody
examples: Bye! Don't forget to write.
I'm writing to enquire about language courses.
She wrote to him in France.
I wrote a letter to the Publicity Department.
I wrote the Publicity Department a letter.
She wrote that they were all fine.
Write me while you're away.
He wrote me that he would be arriving Monday.
They wrote thanking us for the present.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to state the information or the words mentioned
examples: The author writes that this theory has now been disproved.
Ancient historians wrote of a lost continent beneath the ocean.
She wrote of her life in Africa.
‘Of all my books,’ wrote Dickens, ‘I like this the best.’

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: to put information in the appropriate places on a form
examples: to write (out) a cheque
The doctor wrote her a prescription for more antibiotics.
I'll write you out a receipt.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to record data in the memory of a computer
examples: An error was reported when he tried to write data to the file for the first time.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to work correctly or in the way mentioned
examples: This pen won't write.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: to be very obvious to other people from the expression on somebody’s face
examples: Guilt was written all over his face.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to show clearly the quality mentioned or the influence of the person mentioned
examples: It was a performance with star quality written all over it.
This essay has got Mike written all over it.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: not especially good; ordinary
examples: The team’s performance was nothing to write home about.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: having no value, especially legally, or because one of the people involved has no intention of doing what they said they would

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used when you are stating that there is nothing more that can be said about something or that something is completely finished
examples: We were doing well but we ran out of money and that’s all she wrote.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a person whose job is writing books, stories, articles, etc.
examples: SEE ALSO staff writer
Who's your favourite writer?
a travel/cookery/science fiction writer
a freelance feature writer for ‘Time’ magazine
writers of poetry/fiction
the first Russian writer to win the Nobel Prize for Literature
She left her job to become a full-time writer.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a person who has written a particular thing
examples: the writer of this letter
I used to be a prolific letter writer.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: a person who forms letters in a particular way when they are writing
examples: a messy writer

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the activity of writing, in contrast to reading, speaking, etc.
examples: Our son’s having problems with his reading and writing (= at school)
a writing case (= containing paper, pens, etc.)
Every morning the children do writing.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the activity of writing books, articles, etc., especially as a job
examples: SEE ALSO songwriting
Only later did she discover a talent for writing.
I wanted to try out a new style of writing.
creative writing
feminist/travel writing
He is leaving the band to concentrate on his writing.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: books, articles, etc. in general
examples: The review is a brilliant piece of writing.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: words that have been written or painted on something
examples: There was writing all over the desk.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: the particular way in which somebody forms letters when they write
examples: SYNONYM handwriting
Who's this from? I don't recognize the writing.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a group of pieces of writing, especially by a particular person or on a particular subject
examples: His experiences in India influenced his later writings.
the writings of Hegel
His writings on complex subjects are clear and definitive.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: in the form of a letter, document, etc. (that gives proof of something)
examples: All telephone reservations must be confirmed in writing.
Could you put your complaint in writing?
You must get it in writing.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when you are describing a situation in which there are signs that something is going to have problems or that it is going to be a failure
examples: It is amazing that not one of them saw the writing on the wall.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: expressed in writing rather than in speech
examples: Having a written record of what I've done is very valuable.
written instructions
The council is inviting written submissions from the public before June 19.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: involving writing rather than speaking or practical skills
examples: a written test
Students must submit one or more pieces of written work for assessment.
written communication skills

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: in the form of a letter, document, etc. and therefore official
examples: No portion of this site may be copied without express written consent.
You must give written permission before this information can be shared.
a written apology
a written contract
In a written statement, the government has denied the claims.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: language expressed in writing rather than in speech
examples: the permanence of the written word

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: not right or correct
examples: OPPOSITE right
I got all the answers wrong.
He was driving on the wrong side of the road.
Sorry, I must have dialled the wrong number.
You're holding the camera the wrong way up!
That picture is the wrong way round.
I soon realised I'd taken a wrong turn.
He got all his calculations wrong.
The information is just plain wrong.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not right about something/somebody
examples: SYNONYM mistaken
I think she lives at number 44, but I could be wrong.
You were wrong about Tom; he's not married after all.
We were wrong to assume that she'd agree.
She would prove him wrong (= prove that he was wrong) whatever happened.
Correct me if I'm wrong (= I may be wrong) but didn't you say you two knew each other?
If you think I'm happy, you're dead wrong.
You think you've beaten me but that's where you're wrong.
‘I thought this might interest you because I know you like boxing.’ ‘You're not wrong (= you are absolutely right). I love boxing.’

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: causing problems or difficulties; not as it should be
examples: Is anything wrong? You look worried.
‘What's wrong?’ ‘Oh, nothing.’
There's something wrong with the printer.
I have something wrong with my foot.
The doctor could find nothing wrong with him.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: not suitable, right or what you need
examples: He's the wrong person for the job.
She's simply wrong for this job.
I realized that it was the wrong thing to say.
Most people think that the country is heading in the wrong direction.
It was his bad luck to be in the wrong place at the wrong time (= so that he got involved in trouble without intending to).
We don't want this document falling into the wrong hands.
She's all wrong for you.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: not morally right or honest
examples: This man has done nothing wrong.
It is wrong to tell lies.
It's morally wrong to kill somebody.
It was wrong of me to get so angry.
What's wrong with eating meat?
There's nothing inherently wrong with this type of nostalgia.
It is wrong that he should not be punished for what he did.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: to support somebody/something that is not successful

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: to have the wrong idea about how to get or achieve something
examples: You're barking up the wrong tree if you're expecting us to lend you any money.

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: from or living in a poor area or part of town

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: to start a relationship well/badly
examples: I seem to have got off on the wrong foot with the new boss.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: to make somebody pleased with you/annoyed with you

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: to be in a bad mood for the whole day for no particular reason

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: to understand something in the wrong way

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to do, say or write something that is suitable/not suitable for a particular occasion
examples: It is a bizarre tale and the author hits just the right note of horror and disbelief.
Unfortunately, the president struck the wrong note in his speech, ignoring the public mood.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: almost correct
examples: Your guess wasn't far out at all.
They weren't far out with their estimate of 100 000.
You're not far wrong when you say he's the richest guy in town.

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: younger or older than 40, 50, etc. years of age

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: thinking or behaving in the right/wrong way
examples: We haven’t found a cure yet—but we are on the right track.
The new manager successfully got the team back onto the right track.
The police were on the wrong track when they treated the case as a revenge killing.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: in trouble with the police

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: to make somebody annoyed or angry, often without intending to, by doing or saying something that offends them
examples: She tends to rub people up the wrong way.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: to be offended by a remark that was not intended to be offensive
examples: She always takes things the wrong way.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a piece of land next to or around your house where you can grow flowers, fruit, vegetables, etc., usually with a lawn (= an area of grass)
examples: SEE ALSO backyard (1)
They have a gorgeous old oak tree in their front yard.
My next-door neighbor was watering her yard.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an area outside a building, usually with a hard surface and a surrounding wall
examples: SEE ALSO backyard (2)
The prisoners were made to line up in the prison yard.
The children were playing in the yard at the front of the school.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an area of land used for a special purpose or business
examples: SEE ALSO knacker’s yard
a boat yard

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a unit for measuring length, equal to 3 feet (36 inches) or 0.9144 of a metre
examples: They still live within yards of each other.
a beautiful white dress with yards and yards of fabric
The accident happened less than 50 yards from his home.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a long piece of wood fastened to a mast that supports a sail on a boat or ship

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that if you allow some people a small amount of freedom or power they will see you as weak and try to take a lot more

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: everything, or a situation which includes everything
examples: When Dan cooks dinner he always goes the whole nine yards, with three courses and a choice of dessert.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: yes

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used when you are commenting on what somebody has just said
examples: ‘We're off to France soon.’ ‘Oh yeah? When's that?’
‘I'm going to be rich one day.’ ‘Oh yeah?’ (= I don't believe you.)

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to say that you do not believe what somebody has just said, disagree with it, or are not interested in it
examples: ‘You'll be fine.’ ‘Yeah, right.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the period from 1 January to 31 December, that is 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months
examples: SEE ALSO leap year
Elections take place every year.
I lost my job earlier this year.
next/last year
She died the following year.
Three million tourists visit Yellowstone every year.
She was born in the year 1865.
The crowd was much smaller than in previous years.
In the past few years, she has become one of our top-selling authors.
The museum is open all year round (= during the whole year).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a period of twelve months, measured from any particular time
examples: SEE ALSO gap year
It's exactly a year since I started working here.
She gave up teaching three years ago.
They got married two years later.
The autobiography could only be published 100 years after his death.
I hope to retire in two years' time.
Where do you think you will be five years from now?
Seeds can live in the soil for many years.
in the first year of their marriage
Production has declined in recent years.
His early years were spent in San Francisco.
We have high hopes for the coming year (= the next twelve months).
the pre-war/war/post-war years (= the period before/during/after the war)
I have happy memories of my years in Poland (= the time I spent there).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: age; time of life
examples: He was 14 years old when it happened.
She looks young for her years.
They were both only 20 years of age.
a twenty-year-old man
He died in his sixtieth year.
She's getting on in years (= is no longer young).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a period of twelve months connected with a particular activity
examples: SEE ALSO academic year
the tax/fiscal year
the school year

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: a level that you stay in for one year; a student at a particular level
examples: We started German in year seven.
She was in my year at school.
The project is the work of a group of year-seven pupils.
The first years do French.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a long time
examples: It's years since we last met.
They haven't seen each other for years and years.
That's the best movie I've seen in years.
It's the first time we've met in years.
We've had a lot of fun over the years.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: at some time in the future
examples: There are certain to be more job losses further down the road.
Will this movie still be funny a few years down the road?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: the last years of somebody’s life

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: a very long time
examples: We've known each other for donkey's years.
I met him once, but that was donkey’s years ago.
This technology has been around for donkey's.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: a person or thing that people decide is the best in a particular field in a particular year
examples: He was chosen as TV personality of the year.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that you will/would never do something
examples: I'd never have thought of that in a million years.

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used in polite expressions to describe somebody as ‘very old’
examples: He was a man of advanced years.
Even at my advanced age I still know how to enjoy myself!

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel or look older
examples: The illness put years on him.
His wife's death has put years on him.

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: the desire for new sexual experience that is thought to be felt after seven years of marriage

definitions.label: Meaning 15
definitions.definition: since a very long time ago
examples: I've been going there every summer since the year dot.

definitions.label: Meaning 16
definitions.definition: to make somebody feel or look younger
examples: That haircut takes years off her.
Careful make-up and styling can take years off you.

definitions.label: Meaning 17
definitions.definition: the time when a new century/year starts
examples: It was built at the turn of the century.
The team are unbeaten since the turn of the year.

definitions.label: Meaning 18
definitions.definition: every year for many years
examples: People return year after year.

definitions.label: Meaning 19
definitions.definition: as the years pass; each year
examples: Year by year their affection for each other grew stronger.

definitions.label: Meaning 20
definitions.definition: every year

definitions.label: Meaning 21
definitions.definition: any particular year after the birth of Christ

definitions.label: Meaning 22
definitions.definition: each year, compared with the last year
examples: Spending has increased year on year.
a year-on-year increase in spending

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: to shout loudly, for example because you are angry, excited, frightened or in pain
examples: He yelled at the other driver.
She yelled at the child to get down from the wall.
They yelled with excitement.
She yelled out in pain.
‘Be careful!’ he yelled.
The crowd yelled encouragement at the players.
He yelled out her name.
He yelled for help.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having the colour of lemons or butter
examples: pale yellow flowers
a bright yellow waterproof jacket
Her teeth were rather yellow.
She wore a pale yellow dress.
The leaves turn yellow in November.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: an offensive word used to describe the light brown skin of people from some East Asian countries

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: easily frightened
examples: SYNONYM cowardly

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used to answer a question and say that something is correct or true
examples: ‘Is this your car?’ ‘Yes, it is.’
‘Are you coming? Yes or no?’

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to show that you agree with what has been said
examples: ‘I enjoyed her latest novel.’ ‘Yes, me too.’
‘It's an excellent hotel.’ ‘Yes, but (= I don't completely agree) it's too expensive.’
In reply to his question, most of them answered yes.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to disagree with something negative that somebody has just said
examples: ‘I've never met her before.’ ‘Yes, you have.’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to agree to a request or to give permission
examples: ‘Dad, can I borrow the car?’ ‘Yes, but be careful.’
We're hoping that they will say yes to our proposals.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to accept an offer or invitation
examples: ‘Would you like a drink?’ ‘Yes, please/thanks.’

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used for asking somebody what they want
examples: Yes? How can I help you?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used for replying politely when somebody calls you
examples: ‘Waiter!’ ‘Yes, sir?’

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used to show that you have just remembered something
examples: Where did I put the keys? Oh yes—in my pocket!

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to encourage somebody to continue speaking
examples: ‘I’m going to Paris this weekend.’ ‘Yes…’

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: used to show that you do not believe what somebody has said
examples: ‘Sorry I'm late—the bus didn't come.’ ‘Oh yes?’

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to emphasize what you have just said
examples: Mrs Smith has just won £2 million—yes!—£2 million!

definitions.label: Meaning 12
definitions.definition: used to show that you are excited or extremely pleased about something that you have done or something that has happened
examples: ‘They've scored another goal.’ ‘Yes!!’

definitions.label: Meaning 13
definitions.definition: used to show that you are impatient or annoyed about something
examples: ‘Hurry up—it's late.’ ‘Yes, yes—I'm coming.’

definitions.label: Meaning 14
definitions.definition: used when you cannot give a clear answer to a question
examples: ‘Are you enjoying it?’ ‘Yes and no.’

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: on the day before today
examples: A company spokeswoman said yesterday that no final decision had been made yet.
yesterday morning/afternoon/evening
The company yesterday announced a $40 million deal.
To think I was lying on a beach only the day before yesterday.
I can remember our wedding as if it were yesterday.
They arrived yesterday.
Where were you yesterday morning?
Figures released yesterday show 4,944 people were awaiting surgery.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to say that you are not stupid enough to believe what somebody is telling you
examples: Oh yeah? I wasn't born yesterday, you know.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used in negative sentences and questions to talk about something that has not happened but that you expect to happen
examples: I haven't received a letter from him yet.
I didn't receive a letter from him yet.
‘Are you ready?’ ‘No, not yet.’
We don't yet know what really happened.
We have yet to decide what action to take (= We have not decided what action to take).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: now; as soon as this
examples: Don't go yet.
We don't need to start yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to emphasize an increase in number or amount or the number of times something happens
examples: snow, snow and yet more snow
yet another diet book
Prices were cut yet again (= once more, after many other times).

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used to emphasize that something is the best, longest, etc. thing of its kind made, produced, written, etc. until now/then
examples: the most comprehensive study yet of his music
It was the tallest building yet constructed anywhere.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: from now until the period of time mentioned has passed
examples: He'll be busy for ages yet.
They won't arrive for at least two hours yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used to say that something could, might, etc. happen in the future, even though it seems unlikely
examples: We may win yet.
She could yet surprise us all.

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to emphasize an increase in the degree of something (= how bad, important, etc. it is)
examples: SYNONYM even
a recent and yet more improbable theory

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: until now or until a particular time in the past
examples: an as yet unpublished report
As yet little was known of the causes of the disease.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to say that while one thing is good, another thing is even better
examples: You can see and, better yet, hear the effects of these changes on their website.
I wanted to make my parents proud by becoming a lawyer or, better yet, a doctor.

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: not now but probably quite soon
examples: I can't give you the money just yet.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: used to comment on something that was almost successful but in fact failedWord Origin
examples: Old English gīet(a), of unknown origin.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the total amount of crops, profits, etc. that are produced
examples: a high crop yield
a reduction in milk yield
This will give a yield of 10% on your investment.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the total amount of crops, profits, etc. that are produced
examples: a high crop yield
a reduction in milk yield
This will give a yield of 10% on your investment.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used as the subject or object of a verb or after a preposition to refer to the person or people being spoken or written to
examples: You said you knew the way.
I thought she told you.
Can I sit next to you?
I want both of you to help.
I don't think that hairstyle is you (= it doesn't suit your appearance or personality).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used with nouns and adjectives to speak to somebody directly
examples: You girls, stop talking!
You stupid idiot!

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used for referring to people in general
examples: You learn a language better if you visit the country where it is spoken.
It's a friendly place—people come up to you in the street and start talking.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: you, your family and your close friends
examples: I wish you and yours all the best for the year ahead!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: having lived or existed for only a short time; not fully developed
examples: OPPOSITE old
Young babies need to be wrapped up warmly.
a young country
Caterpillars eat the young leaves of this plant.
It's a young wine, not really up to drinking yet.
The night is still young (= it has only just started).
Small businesses, especially young ones, tend to operate on a tight budget.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: not yet old; not as old as others
examples: OPPOSITE old
young people
They sent many young men and women off to war.
My son's thirteen but he's young for his age (= not as developed as other boys of the same age).
I'm too young to remember much about the 1990s.
They married young (= at an early age).
My mother died young.
She looks much younger than her 39 years.
I don't know how families with young children manage to cope.
a young girl/boy/adult/person
In his younger days he played rugby for Wales.
I am the youngest of four sisters.
talented young football players
I met the young Michelle Obama at Princeton.
Her grandchildren keep her young (= keep her feeling young).

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: consisting of young people or young children; with a low average age
examples: They have a young family.
a young audience
This cottage would be perfect for a couple with a young family.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: suitable or appropriate for young people
examples: SYNONYM youthful
young fashion
The clothes she wears are much too young for her.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: used to show that you are angry or annoyed with a particular young person
examples: I think you owe me an apology, young lady!

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: used before or after a person’s name to show the difference between them and an older relative
examples: COMPARE elder
the younger Kennedy
William Pitt the younger

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: used to say that people seem to be doing something at a younger age than they used to, or that they seem younger because you are now older
examples: The band's fans are getting younger.
Why do police officers seem to be getting younger?

definitions.label: Meaning 8
definitions.definition: used when you are commenting that time is passing and that you are growing older
examples: We need to start thinking about our retirement. We’re not getting any younger, you know.

definitions.label: Meaning 9
definitions.definition: used to describe a young person who acts in a more sensible way than you would expect for a person of their age

definitions.label: Meaning 10
definitions.definition: thinking and behaving like a young person even when you are old
examples: My father is 76 but he’s still young at heart.
He's over 70, but he's young at heart.

definitions.label: Meaning 11
definitions.definition: young people should enjoy themselves as much as possible, because they will have to work and worry later in their livesWord Origin
examples: Old English g(e)ong, of Germanic origin; related to Dutch jong and German jung, also to youth; from an Indo-European root shared by Latin juvenis.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: a young person or a child
examples: The camp is for youngsters aged 8 to 14.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: of or belonging to the person or people being spoken or written to
examples: I like your dress.
Excuse me, is this your seat?
The bank is on your right.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: of or belonging to people in general
examples: Dentists advise you to have your teeth checked every six months.
In Japan you are taught great respect for your elders.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used to show that somebody/something is well known or often talked about
examples: This is your typical English pub.
You and your bright ideas!

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: used in some titles, especially those of royal people
examples: Your Majesty
Your Excellency

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: of or belonging to you
examples: Is that book yours?
Is she a friend of yours?
My hair is very fine. Yours is much thicker.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used at the end of a letter before signing your name
examples: Yours sincerely/faithfully
Sincerely Yours
Yours Truly

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: your home
examples: Let's go back to yours after the show.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: you, your family and your close friends
examples: I wish you and yours all the best for the year ahead!

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: used when the person or people being spoken to both cause and are affected by an action
examples: Have you hurt yourself?
You don't seem quite yourself today (= you do not seem well or do not seem as happy as usual).
Enjoy yourselves!

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: used to emphasize the fact that the person who is being spoken to is doing something
examples: Do it yourself—I don't have time.
You can try it out for yourselves.
You yourself are one of the chief offenders.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: used instead of ‘you’ in order to sound polite or formal (although some people do not consider this use to be correct)
examples: We sell a lot of these to people like yourself.
‘And yourself,’ he replied, ‘How are you?’

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: to act naturally
examples: Don't act sophisticated—just be yourself.

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: alone; without anyone else
examples: How long were you by yourself in the house?

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: without help
examples: Are you sure you did this exercise by yourself?

definitions.label: Meaning 7
definitions.definition: for only you to have or use; not shared
examples: I'm going to be away next week so you'll have the office to yourself.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: the time of life when a person is young, especially the time before a child becomes an adult
examples: He had been a talented musician in his youth.
She regrets that she spent her youth travelling and not studying.
to relive/recapture your youth
He joked that being good at cards was the sign of a misspent youth (= having wasted his time when he was young).

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: the quality or state of being young
examples: She brings to the job a rare combination of youth and experience.
His youth gives him an advantage over the other runners.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: young people considered as a group
examples: the nation’s youth
Many people think the youth of today are not taught proper standards of behaviour.
training for unemployed youth
an increase in youth unemployment
contemporary youth culture
a youth worker (= somebody who works with young people)
Youth and adults tend to see things very differently.

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: a young man
examples: The fight was started by a gang of youths.

definitions.label: Meaning 1
examples: Five, four, three, two, one, zero… We have lift-off.

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: a temperature, pressure, etc. that is equal to zero on a scale
examples: It was ten degrees below zero last night (= −10°C).
The thermometer had fallen to zero.

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: the lowest possible amount or level; nothing at all
examples: I rated my chances as zero.
zero inflation

definitions.label: Meaning 1
definitions.definition: an area or a region with a particular feature or use
examples: SEE ALSO danger zone
a war/combat/demilitarized/exclusion zone
a danger zone
a pedestrian zone (= where vehicles may not go)
They have called for a 100-mile buffer zone (= protected area) around the island to protect the seals.
an earthquake zone

definitions.label: Meaning 2
definitions.definition: one of the areas that a larger area is divided into for the purpose of organization
examples: postal charges to countries in zone 2

definitions.label: Meaning 3
definitions.definition: an area or a part of an object, especially one that is different from everything that is around it
examples: SEE ALSO crumple zone
When the needle enters the red zone the engine is too hot.
the erogenous zones of the body

definitions.label: Meaning 4
definitions.definition: one of the parts that the earth’s surface is divided into by imaginary lines that are parallel to the equator
examples: the northern/southern temperate zone

definitions.label: Meaning 5
definitions.definition: in a state in which you feel confident and are performing at your best
examples: SEE ALSO comfort zone
When I'm in the zone, writing is the most satisfying thing in the world.

definitions.label: Meaning 6
definitions.definition: a state in which things are strange, mysterious or secret; a state that exists on the dividing line between two things
examples: the twilight world of the occult
The dissidents lived in a twilight world of hushed voices and secret meetings.
the twilight zone between living and merely existing
They lived in the twilight zone on the fringes of society.
